e398e8b0-629a-4c63-901f-a0f74af0fd2b.Text:
Gain access to the two upcoming major story expansions for Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader and save with the bundle price!

1. Void Shadows

The first story expansion is all about the Rogue Trader's voidship, the life of its crew, and the threats lurking in its holds. Dive into a new epic story integrated into the main narrative, battle new enemies, and recruit a new companion — a death cult assassin. Explore new decks of your voidship, unlock new upgrade options, and master the mechanics of void combat. Meet new members of your crew on the bridge, such as the Astropath, the chirurgeon, and others. - The events of this story will be reflected in the game's epilogue. - This expansion offers 15 hours of gameplay.

2. Lex Imperialis

The second story expansion sees the Lord Captain join forces with a new companion — a member of the Adeptus Arbites. As the past of House von Valancius begins to present itself in a new light, the Rogue Trader faces difficult decisions that may affect the future of the entire Koronus Expanse. Over the course of this story, you will get a chance to learn more about the collection of the Imperial Tithe, otherwise known as the Grand Harvesting. Interfere with this fundamental process of the Imperium at your own peril. Discover new areas, game mechanics, and archetypes — and of course, encounter new horrors of the Immaterium. - This expansion likewise offers 15 hours of gameplay.

28fc52a2-c96f-4445-9028-365134b10cba.Text:
Some objects in the game can be interacted with in a special way. They are marked with specific icons — some icons allow you to study objects, others will transfer the character to neighbouring locations or launch a small event. These icons become visible when your character is standing close enough to the interactive object.
Click [LMB] on the icon to perform the associated action. Some interactive objects, such as doors or chests, are not always marked with icons, but the cursor changes when you hover over them. Hover your cursor over the object. If the cursor changes, the object is interactable.

Swapping weapon sets in combat does not cost {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g}.

98deb96d-afc7-42c5-903f-6c7fd83342e2.Text:
An Arbitrator with the Subductor specialisation has the passive ability, {g|f:613246cc28464ade9845da9b30dc65c3}Ruthless Suppression{/g}, which grants the Arbitrator and their familiar immunity to {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hits{/g} and increases the Arbitrator and their familiar's critical hit chance if there are 2 or more enemies in a 2-cell radius around the Arbitrator. Whenever an enemy adjacent to the Arbitrator gets up from being {g|Encyclopedia:ProneEffect}prone{/g}, that enemy provokes an {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunityFullGlossary}attack of opportunity{/g} from the Arbitrator.
The Subductor's active abilities are only available with a shield equipped.
The {g|f:8c7d2be4225745e4911eb3c53c603b76}Assault Onslaught{/g} ability allows the Arbitrator to dash through allies and enemies in a straight line for up to 5 cells without provoking attacks of opportunity. Each enemy they pass through must pass an Agility resistance test or fall prone until the start of that enemy's next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.
The Subductor's {g|f:1c5f4edca9f64fe0911bc946e0b4ea4a}Shield Bash{/g} deals more damage to prone or {g|Encyclopedia:ImmobilisedEffect}immobilised{/g} enemies and scores guaranteed critical hits against them.
Enemies affected by the Subductor's {g|f:f6a60b4556214528b0ce295c4f69306e}Stalwart Defence{/g} deal less damage and suffer more damage from the Subductor's counter-attacks.

0808bad8-9ba5-4568-9dc8-743999aad357.Text:
An Arbitrator with the Vigilant specialisation has the passive ability, {g|f:e9fc0a90ebe8458a86c9b7db9f6770b3}Swift Justice{/g}, which causes enemies attacked by the Arbitrator or their familiar to suffer the {g|f:3a4b8214c73240de911a805fe645e624}swift justice{/g} effect until the start of the Arbitrator's next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. The Arbitrator's shotgun attacks deal more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} to those enemies.
With a shotgun equipped, the Vigilant gains access to unique shotgun attacks. Each of them costs 2 AP and does not spend ammunition.
{g|f:def7164545244af28d52cd38d0502525}Double Slug{/g} allows the Arbitrator to make two {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacksGlossary}single shots{/g} against the target.
{g|f:027e75ab89364049b844a720feca85ec}Grisly Adjudication{/g} increases shotgun {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g} and inflicts {g|Encyclopedia:BleedingEffect}bleeding{/g} on targets {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g}.
{g|f:2162ce26f6db4cd1b748a4105c364ddb}Fulminating Shot{/g} deals less damage but reduces the {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g}, and block of targets in its {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area of effect{/g} for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}, regardless of whether they were hit or not.

df8ea9cc-b9d9-49ef-9d74-b1a4f5c0d502.Text: Armour protects the character from incoming {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}. Light and {g|Encyclopedia:MediumArmour}medium armour{/g} types are both available to you at the moment. The armour stat indicates what percent of incoming damage from an enemy attack it can absorb. The type of armour also influences the chances that the character wearing it will pass a {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} test — the higher the dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g}, the lower the chance to dodge an enemy attack. A character in {g|Encyclopedia:LightArmour}light armour{/g} dodges attacks more often, but takes more damage when hit. Medium armour absorbs more damage if the character is hit, but reduces their mobility and ability to dodge attacks. Some {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} allow characters to use different types of armour more effectively.

415d1037-8e73-4262-92af-5527981de93c.Text:
You can gain a better understanding of what transpired in combat by checking the combat log. All actions performed by your character, their companions, and enemies are recorded in the combat log in the bottom right corner of the screen.
Click [RMB] on an event or an action to learn more about it.

e23160b6-e03f-4233-afb2-f10b0502ec5a.Text: Certain types of weapons let you make {g|Encyclopedia:BurstAttacks}burst{/g} attacks. When performing a melee burst attack, the character makes several strikes against a single target. If the first strike hits the target, all subsequent strikes automatically hit. If the first strike is dodged or parried, all subsequent strikes are automatically dodged or parried. When performing a ranged burst attack, the character fires several successive shots with different trajectories. Most of these shots are concentrated in the centre of the selected attack cone; therefore, the more enemies there are in the centre of this area, the more of them will be damaged if the attack is successful. All shots fired after the first one are less accurate and have a higher chance of deviating from the central line. Burst shots are particularly effective against clusters of enemies. Be careful: burst shots can hit allies if they are standing in the direction of the attack.

7fb1fa3a-aef9-417c-9d27-ec297cb990ed.Text: Argenta is the warrior of the Adepta Sororitas and a Soldier. She is an expert with {g|Encyclopedia:BurstAttacks}burst{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} weapons and weapons that deal damage in an area. Another of Argenta's strengths is her mobility in combat. {g|f:7a76af1ef02c4699b62db147e2b9a172}Run and Gun{/g} is a unique Soldier {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}. Using it grants the Soldier extra {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}movement points{/g} and reduces the cost of their next attack by −1 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action point{/g}. The Soldier will also suffer a −10 {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g} to their {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} for this attack. {g|f:7a76af1ef02c4699b62db147e2b9a172}Run and Gun{/g} also allows the Soldier to perform an additional attack with a ranged weapon, which is a handy tool if you want to make more than one attack with them on their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. {g|f:8638221f9caf46649cefcbd7574804d1}Revel in Slaughter{/g} is a Soldier ability which can be used once for each 3 enemies the Soldier kills in a single battle. Each activation of this ability increases the Soldier's Ballistic Skill, {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hit chance, and critical damage{/g}. This {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g} stacks and lasts until the end of combat.

10c56826-cc2d-4f72-96ab-26ef7a4e98b2.Text: Change your point of view! Move the camera using the [{bind|CameraUp}], [{bind|CameraDown}], [{bind|CameraLeft}], [{bind|CameraRight}] keys or by using the arrow keys on your keyboard. Rotate the camera using the [{bind|CameraRotateLeft}], [{bind|CameraRotateRight}] keys or the mouse wheel.

8fbf1f88-a871-47e8-86a2-3aff5448f5bc.Text:
Open the cargo management screen to learn more about the cargo on your flagship: the amount, the types, and the percentage of cargo being filled up.
On the cargo tab, you can see details about the items packed in each cargo slot. If you need to use an item that is already packed, move that item back to your inventory.
Cargo is needed when trading with merchants. You will meet them soon.

c965a127-4701-40a3-9c75-c03b592d4968.Text: At the moment, it is impossible to remove trophies from cargo since communication with the flagship hasn't been established.

8b206f8f-cbae-4385-8569-a6d7eef730b8.Text:
You have packed an important piece of equipment as cargo — characters cannot equip items from the ship's cargo!
Transfer the weapon from cargo back to your inventory and equip it — you will need it at this stage of the game. Later on, you will be able to use cargo to trade with merchants.

c3d89bff-65bf-43f8-a8f2-8deb4a7f8acf.Text: Cassia is an Officer and your ship's Navigator. She strikes foes with energies of the warp and supports the party by making her allies stronger. {g|f:9c78e44bf8ff44a9afff8370c673c9ad}Voice of Command{/g} is an Officer {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} that increases an ally's characteristics for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g} and also allows the Officer to use their other Officer archetype abilities on that ally from any distance. The higher the Officer's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}Fellowship{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} is, the more the target's characteristics are increased. An Officer can use {g|f:9c78e44bf8ff44a9afff8370c673c9ad}Voice of Command{/g} again on the same ally only after 2 rounds have passed since its first application. {g|f:5bfccf14d8604ae1a041fb347fb8f19f}Bring It Down!{/g} is an Officer ability that lets them immediately grant an {g|Encyclopedia:ExtraTurn}extra turn{/g} to an ally. During that extra turn, the ally does not gain any {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}movement points{/g}, but they do gain 2 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g} which can be spent on making an attack or using abilities or consumables. If the ally is under the effect of {g|f:9c78e44bf8ff44a9afff8370c673c9ad}Voice of Command{/g} and destroys an enemy before the end of the Officer's turn, the ally will be granted extra {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetails}momentum{/g} for this kill. {g|f:e8164ac219f44e69b95de4853569da3b}Lidless Stare{/g} is a unique damaging ability that assails all targets in a wide cone in front of the Navigator with warp energies. The damage dealt is based on the Navigator's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} bonus. All creatures targeted by this ability must pass a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} or become {g|Encyclopedia:Stun}stunned{/g}.

d21463d7-fea0-4df9-af2c-a517aca42411.Text:
In your travels, you will come across containers, crates, and other objects in the environment that you can search. Inside, you can find a variety of loot — from things that are of no use to a Rogue Trader (but may still pique a merchant's interest) to new equipment and important plot items.
Click [LMB] on a container to open it.
You will also encounter locked containers. To open such a container, your party members will have to pass the associated {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}.

30c6c710-bb9e-4245-b4cf-28c7a91d5ed6.Text:
In combat, you can significantly increase the animation speed of your enemies and allies. To do so, hold the assigned key ([SPACE] by default).
In the options menu, you can enable this option to speed up animations automatically or disable it.

4fde63b1-820b-4954-8f08-a8f3ab98be3f.Text:
You have met the Mercenary Steward. Talk to him. Through the corresponding dialogue options, you will be able to create up to 2 mercenaries for other group members to control.
As the group leader, you will be redirected to the character creation screen. There, you will be able to give these mercenaries names and customise them, choosing their backgrounds, archetypes, and various other parameters.
Once the mercenaries are created, their models will appear in the game world. At first, they will be controlled by you. Go to the character assignment menu to grant each group member the ability to control the corresponding mercenary.
If your group consists of more than 3 players and there are still not enough characters for everybody, keep playing. As the story unfolds, new companions will soon join your party, and each group member will be able to pick a character for themselves.
Warning! If you skip the dialogue with the Mercenary Steward, you will not be able to return to him later.

dd16b229-acd0-4f98-85f9-c6ada01d905d.Text:
All group members except the leader can use [LMB] in ground combat to highlight the icon of an ability or a consumable item on the panel at the bottom of the screen.
Additionally, they can use [LMB] to highlight choices in dialogues and book events, showing other group members which option they would like to select.
Note: though each group member can express their opinion, it is up to the group leader to make the final decision.

51914511-0dec-4cd1-8dc8-428f1462024b.Text:
In dialogues and book events, you can use [LMB] + [ALT] to highlight a text line to show other group members which option you would like to choose.
Note: though each group member can express their opinion, it is up to the group leader to make a decision.

11eda7cb-1e0a-4341-b378-cfacefecb753.Text:
Each group member can use [ALT] + [LMB] to highlight a selected object, such as:
-<indent=5%>a unit (in combat and out of combat)</indent>
-<indent=5%>a cell on the battlefield (in ground and space combat)</indent>
-<indent=5%>an object on the map (including location map, system map, and the Koronus Expanse map)</indent>

dc710ca5-8042-4a68-b5cc-4bf0078e0a6c.Text:
During ground or space combat, you can use [LMB] + [ALT] to highlight a selected object to emphasise it for other group members will focus on it. You can highlight:
-<indent=5%>a creature model</indent>
-<indent=5%>an icon on the abilities panel</indent>
-<indent=5%>a cell on the battlefield</indent>

96b9fda3-2622-48d0-9d4a-dec3dd4fde8e.Text: While playing in co-op mode, you can highlight a cell, a creature, a line of dialogue, an object on the map, or an ability icon to emphasise it for other group members. They will hear the ping and see that object highlighted on their screens. This can be used in zones where you can directly control your characters, in ground and space combat, in dialogues and book events, and on various maps.

2773983d-6b66-4729-a89d-380d96cadcaa.Text:
While playing in co-op mode, you can highlight a cell, a creature, a dialogue line, or an icon on the abilities panel to emphasise it for other group members. To do so, hover the cursor over the object and click [LMB] while holding [ALT]. The other group members will hear the ping and see that object highlighted on their screens.
This can be used in zones where you can directly control your characters, on system maps, and on the Koronus Expanse map.

419d7b03-f23a-49b3-99e6-9d55f74cd8c0.Text: Interaction in Dialogues and Book Events

bccbb24f-ec5e-464f-bcf2-caa7656e9aa5.Text: Interaction During Ground and Space Combat

88c0511d-d2ba-4e58-8ffd-5ec4d4751e13.Text:
Use {g|Encyclopedia:DetailsOfTheCoverGlossary}cover{/g} to avoid enemy attacks.
Cover that a character can hide behind are marked with a shield (or a shield with a skull). When standing close to them, the character will automatically take up an advantageous position — in this case, the chance that enemy attacks will hit the cover and not the character behind them increases.
The character will not receive a {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} if attacked from a side not protected by their current cover.

55d90ef7-f04d-476a-bcee-2016fe2bf629.Text: Full and partial covers give you the opportunity to avoid enemy attacks. {g|Encyclopedia:DetailsOfTheCoverGlossary}Full cover{/g}, indicated by a skull on the shield, reduces the chance to be hit by 60%. Partial cover reduces it by 35%. At the same time, the chance to hit a character behind cover may vary depending on the difficulty of the game you choose. Some cover can be destroyed by {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacks}melee attacks{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attacks{/g}, and other {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}. Destructible cover has a durability bar above it. {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacks}Single shot{/g} can penetrate through any cover.

3726b301-57dc-4814-b1d0-4d2dff95b7ac.Text:
The higher a character's {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} score, the easier it is for them to succeed on {g|Encyclopedia:Test}tests{/g}. Skill scores depend on the character's respective characteristic scores, skill advancements on level ups, and any {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} the character's equipment might offer.
To succeed on various tests during gameplay, develop different skills for your character and their companions.

fa4eea83-4b39-4d25-b792-f4cf63ec6458.Text: Your character is about to make a {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLogic}Logic{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}. In dialogue and during exploration, you will often make various skill tests, and their result might determine how successful your character's efforts are, make hidden dialogue options appear, or reveal new information. The success of the test is determined by rolling a 100-sided die. Each skill test has a difficulty of up to 100 (including negative values). To succeed, you must roll a value equal to or less than the sum of both the stated difficulty and the value of the skill used for the test. For example, you are attempting a test with difficulty of −10. Your character's Logic skill score is 40. 40 − 10 = 30 Therefore, to succeed on the Logic skill test, you must roll a 30 or less. Any result above 30 will mean failure. Note that difficulty is calculated from greater to lower values. The greater the difficulty value, the easier it is to pass the test (it is easier to succeed on a difficulty 40 test than on a difficulty 10 test).

6d1ac33f-2e3e-41f2-8819-bf355d8d1746.Text:
{g|Encyclopedia:BurningEffect}Burning{/g} surfaces, electricity, toxic fumes, and other hazardous environmental effects can deal damage to your party or inflict ongoing {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffect}negative effects{/g}.
Use a {g|ib:Medikit}medikit{/g} to stop such effects.

925ccd12-280c-417d-a4b6-d463ca3f86a4.Text: One of the available dialogue options requires making a {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}. Unlike with passive tests, which are made automatically, in this case you can decide whether or not to select an option, the consequences of which will depend on the result of the associated test. Success or failure affects how the dialogue develops — depending on the context, you might change the course of the conversation, alter the character's attitude, or perform an action whose consequences will only become apparent later. Hover your cursor over the dialogue option that requires a skill test, and you will see a tooltip detailing your chances of success. The number after the skill's name indicates the difficulty of the test. Once your character starts travelling with allies, the party member with the highest score in the applicable skill will be selected for each test.

117d3d89-4b38-4766-982b-dc69352c1488.Text: Your characters' skills reflect their knowledge and capabilities. Some dialogues automatically initiate passive {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}tests{/g} — if such a test succeeds, new information will be revealed or a hidden dialogue option will unlock. If your character is travelling with allies, the party member with the highest score in the applicable skill is selected for each given passive skill test.

6d0854b7-adcf-4863-b09b-a0c4d796f1c2.Text:
You are in a dialogue — here you can learn more about current events, influence the character you are speaking to, or even alter the course of the game's narrative. Your character's personal story depends on the dialogue choices you make.
Available dialogue options are displayed on the right. Select a reply by clicking [LMB] on it or pressing the corresponding digit on your keyboard.

6058be98-b3e2-4d30-b8ee-1064c1cbdf17.Text:
The combat {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} of characters differ depending on their archetype. Available abilities are located at the bottom right of the screen on the abilities panel. To read the full description of the ability, hover your cursor over its icon or click [RMB] on it.
Click [LMB] on the icon to use the ability. Before the ability is used, you will get to review its estimated outcome while hovering your cursor over a character or an area of your choosing. You will also see the ability's {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area of effect{/g}, and each character in this area will have a number displayed over them denoting the probability of being successfully affected. If the ability's {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g} is guaranteed to work, the ability's icon is displayed instead of a number. When you are ready to use the ability, click [LMB] again to confirm your choice.
During your adventures, your characters will gain new abilities and {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} as their power grows. You can view the full list of available abilities and talents on the features tab in the character menu [{bind|OpenCharacterScreen}].

f7d9cc37-6036-4153-8405-472d6cba14a6.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}Action points{/g} (AP) are used to perform attacks and use {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} in combat. Their amount is displayed on the abilities panel at the bottom of the screen. Each attack or ability has a certain AP cost. At the start of each {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, a character's AP is restored to its maximum value. The higher a character's {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g} rank, the more AP they have.

8d06a9b8-a1fb-4985-a0c1-71133d13f5da.Text: To {g|Encyclopedia:SpeedSpace}speed{/g} up enemies' actions, hold [{bind|SpeedUpEnemies}] during their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g} to make the battle proceed at a faster pace.

78c99da1-c6a7-4b0e-89ee-6e04a8eb0d1b.Text: Characters with melee weapons can make an {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunity}attack of opportunity{/g} if an opponent in an adjacent cell initiates movement. It can also be triggered by some {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}. All characters with melee weapons, including members of your party, can make attacks of opportunity. The chance to hit and deal {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} is calculated just like a normal attack.

52003f15-11ef-43dd-b22c-5ac08ece0549.Text: Your character has just landed a critical hit that deals increased damage equal to the character's {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamage}critical damage{/g} stat. Characters' critical damage is 150% of their normal damage by default, however certain {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}, effects, and {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} can increase it. Certain weapons have their own critical damage stat, which is added to the character's total stat value during attack.

e5dd947d-822a-49aa-aae3-612ef325b0f7.Text:
Your character has lost consciousness — their {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} have been reduced to 0!
The character can no longer participate in combat nor can they be resuscitated by any means. They will regain consciousness after the battle and receive a {g|Encyclopedia:Traumas}trauma{/g}, which can be healed by resting on the ship or in certain other places suitable for rest.

fc8e4061-b149-486c-b98e-cbd366b0b5c6.Text:
Be careful! Companions can get hurt by your {g|Encyclopedia:BurstAttacks}burst{/g} attacks or {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attacks{/g}.
To avoid {g|Encyclopedia:FriendlyFire}friendly fire{/g}, keep an eye on the trajectory of the shots and the area of {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g} of area attacks and melee burst attacks.

3a413e52-85e0-49d3-8ae0-db364bf504bc.Text:
Before taking an action in combat, you can evaluate its effectiveness with a hologram.
Click [LMB] on the battlefield to place a hologram in that location. Select actions and {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} to see their expected outcomes. The action will be displayed as if used from the hologram's location to let you assess whether you have picked an effective position for the action you are planning to take.
Click [LMB] again to confirm your choice. Click [RMB] or press the [ESC] key to cancel it.

115d914a-2b8a-4906-ad53-75e0714c2a5b.Text:
You can use the hologram to gauge the effectiveness of your intended actions in combat before taking them.
Click [LMB] on any accessible cell on the battlefield to place the character's hologram there. Select an {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} or a {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacks}single-shot{/g} attack to see the expected outcome. The action will be displayed as if used from the hologram's location to let you assess whether you have picked an effective position for the action you are planning to take. The hologram also lets you see if the enemy will be within your {g|Encyclopedia:LineOfSight}line of sight{/g} after you move to the selected cell.
Click [LMB] again to confirm your choice and execute the selected action. Click [RMB] anywhere on the battlefield or press the [ESC] key to cancel it.

f2f134cc-1142-41cd-9d35-e54d9e5e079d.Text: All combatants act in {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turns{/g} and their order is determined by an initiative roll. The order of turns is displayed on the left side of the screen from bottom to top: the character at the very bottom goes first, then the one above them, and so on.

fc0f4ece-04a9-4dc8-9596-1129e9c7766d.Text:
You can use a {g|ib:Medikit}medikit{/g} to restore your party members' {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} in battle, treat an {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injury{/g}, or get rid of certain {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffect}negative effects{/g} (if the character is injured or suffering such an {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g}). If the character has a medikit equipped, its icon will be displayed on the bottom left. If no such icon is present, open your inventory and equip a medikit by double-clicking [LMB] on it. To use a medikit, select its icon at the bottom of the screen, then click [LMB] on the character who requires treatment or their portrait. A character can only use a medikit on a target they are adjacent to.
Medikits can only be used by characters who have the {g|f:9aefa8d7db3349358e23b2106578353b}Field Medic{/g} feature, {g|f:37363b46061e46218f40e01ed81e9189}Base Skill: Medicae{/g}, or have taken the {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g} skill advancement at least once. A {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} determines the number of wounds restored.
Each medikit holds 2 or more charges, with 1 charge being consumed per use. Once used, medikits disappear from the panel on the bottom of the screen, so remember to equip your characters with new medikits regularly.
Note that healing, just like most actions, spends the character's {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g} in combat.

848bb8de-d732-41e2-b1c4-1d265b1b6c36.Text:
This character is using a melee weapon. {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacks}Melee attacks{/g} require the character to be adjacent to the enemy. To make a melee attack, click [LMB] on the {g|f:be721a48e3614ddbb86bf18503511c2c}Strike{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, then on the enemy you wish to attack. Unlike {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacks}single shots{/g}, melee attacks hit automatically with no need for a roll. The enemy will try to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} the attack if they are using a melee weapon of their own.
Melee weapons can be used to make {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attacks{/g} — all creatures in the area will suffer damage unless they succeed on a dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} (or a parry test if they are armed with a melee weapon). Damage dealt by melee weapons depends on the weapon's parameters and the attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g} score.

f4317f8b-c6ed-42a1-9f9f-68f4578eae9e.Text:
Your new companion is a Warrior. Abelard specialises in melee combat and drawing the enemy's attacks.
{g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g} is a unique Warrior {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} that works only when they are using a melee weapon and is not considered an attack action. Use {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g} to close the distance between you and the enemy and deal damage. Click [LMB] on the ability's icon and choose a direction to charge in. If an enemy is in the direct path of {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g}, Abelard will attack them and will still be able to use an attack action afterward if he has not used one this {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.
Note that {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g} can only be used if the character is 2 or more cells away from their target.

03d2314d-ef84-416c-8a2b-e5adbd34ee94.Text: Your character has just missed! To increase {g|Encyclopedia:HitChance}hit chance{/g}, equip your character with a decent weapon and place them on a vantage point. {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}Abilities{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} that improve the {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} characteristic will help you hit more often in close combat. For improved marksmanship, learn talents that increase the {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} characteristics.

f416ef03-1b4b-4c8e-815b-5814818beef5.Text:
All battles in the game are {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}-based and take place on a grid. On their turn, a character can move, attack, and use their {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}.
Select a cell within the highlighted area and double-click [LMB] on it to move the character there.

1507d9f0-f732-4196-b109-93f60f5dccd7.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}Movement points{/g} ({g|Encyclopedia:MovementPointsSpace}MP{/g}) determine how far a character can move on their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. 1 MP corresponds to one cell on the battlefield. Moving diagonally is more costly — every second diagonal cell uses 2 MP. At the beginning of each turn, movement points are restored to their maximum value. Note that once a character starts moving, this action can no longer be cancelled.

8290dea0-bdf2-4237-bb7d-a9326b7e4b16.Text:
Your character is afflicted with a {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effect{/g}!
Such effects can hinder a character's ability to fight, pass {g|Encyclopedia:Test}tests{/g}, or use weapons and items.
To learn more about a negative effect, hover your cursor over its icon above the character on the battlefield and hold [TAB]. You can also examine active negative effects in the character menu or by hovering your cursor over the effect's icon next to the character's portrait. A negative effect's description can help you understand how long the effect will last and how you might be able to get rid of it.

6796ce67-e243-468e-ad72-c1768cac531c.Text:
The order in which actions are taken in combat matters. Your character can only move around the battlefield before they take an attack action.
Once a character attacks, they lose their remaining {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}movement points{/g}, unable to move until the start of their next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. There is a way around this, however, if, for example, the character has some way of gaining movement points after attacking.

61735246-105c-477f-89e8-05559577d8cb.Text: Some shots are able to pierce enemies through and deal {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} not only to them but also to the characters standing behind them. The {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g} parameter is found on most weapons and affects how much damage the target takes as well as determines the chance of {g|Encyclopedia:Overpenetration}overpenetration{/g}. Some weapons have the overpenetration parameter, which depends on the type of weapon, the value of the weapon's {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g} parameter, and the character's {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}. In case of overpenetration, characters standing behind the target will receive less damage.

4e81ec2c-cf67-4503-93f3-887049738556.Text: Whenever a target is {g|Encyclopedia:PushGlossary}pushed{/g}, it can collide with walls, another character, or other obstacles. Collision damage is reduced by {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} and is calculated differently than regular damage. Note that if a target collides with another character, both will suffer collision damage. That character also cannot {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} the collision.

5bea4872-2eec-41af-bc21-5fb3bc2cc3ce.Text: You've run out of ammo! To continue shooting, you need to {g|Encyclopedia:Reload}reload{/g} the weapon. Use the reload action on the weapons panel at the bottom of the screen to replenish ammo and keep fighting. Like with most actions in combat, you need to spend {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g} to reload. Ammo supply is unlimited for your character and party, so you can reload whenever the need arises.

1318a52b-e89f-41ef-99dd-bb71fe9bf202.Text: Characters with melee weapons block adjacent enemies' ability to perform attacks with ranged weapons. Pistols and shotguns are an exception to this rule — those can be fired at point-blank range.

d9dbd6f0-9c32-4fbb-8985-50a146e3877a.Text:
To survive in the grim darkness of the far future, you will have to face enemies of all kinds and fight for your life. These hints and tutorials will familiarise you with the combat system of Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader.
Click the button at the top of the screen to start the battle.

db0cefe4-dd01-4801-b723-65c6fc839980.Text: The character is {g|Encyclopedia:Stun}stunned{/g} and is forced to skip one {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}! While stun is active, the character cannot {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, or perform {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunity}attacks of opportunity{/g}. When attacking a stunned target, enemies gain hit {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g}.

0a829dfd-7796-45fc-a2af-891db76bd00b.Text: To use the unique {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} called {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic acts{/g} or {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measures{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetails}momentum{/g} is required. Depending on the actions of your party in combat, the momentum bar will increase or decrease. A high momentum value allows a character to use a {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g}. A low value grants access to {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measures{/g}. Both abilities can completely change the course of a battle, but every party member can either use one or the other and only once in a single combat.

7de7c298-cd96-489b-98bc-f9c5e08bd0b6.Text: When you're ready to end your {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, press [{bind|Pause}] or click the end turn button on the bottom right of the screen.

955994aa-dbe7-40ee-99db-a15b9ef6f1ce.Text:
You will encounter enemies with various {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and features. An icon next to an enemy's portrait indicates that they are under the influence of some kind of {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g}. Click [RMB] on the effect's icon to see more details.
If you wish to learn more about an enemy, click [RMB] on their portrait or the enemy themselves.

31df20fb-ad52-4af7-b8a8-ca664bdeefe7.Text:
Trophies on the right side of the trophy window go to your inventory — such items can be used or equipped by your characters. Trophies on the left are packed up as cargo and sent to your ship, which can later be used to trade with various factions.
You can move trophies from one side of the window to the other by dragging them over using [LMB]. Alternatively, you can use the buttons at the bottom to mass transfer all trophies to the cargo or inventory section of the trophy window and vice versa. Click "Collect all" or press [SPACE] to transfer the trophies from both sides of the trophy window to the corresponding windows.

56910c54-b08d-48a4-9953-9af866563846.Text: Defeated enemies have no further need for their former belongings, but you can discover valuable trophies among them. Click [LMB] on a defeated enemy to inspect what is left of them.

cb63fd8e-7f9b-4395-b37b-997b67fd1354.Text: You have obtained heavy armour. Unlike light and {g|Encyclopedia:MediumArmour}medium armour{/g}, heavy armour provides the ability to deflect damage. {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}Deflection{/g} is a unique heavy armour stat that reduces damage taken by a specified flat amount. Heavy armour has a higher armour rating than medium and {g|Encyclopedia:LightArmour}light armour{/g}, but also usually has a higher {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g}, making it harder to dodge an enemy attack while wearing it . Only characters with the {g|f:684c766dc9c24fcf856dc1d6f01d9290}Heavy Armour Proficiency{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talent{/g} can wear heavy armour.

af7a3957-8bbc-429c-aa59-57da9418af74.Text:
You can hover your cursor over {g|Encyclopedia:GlossaryLink}highlighted{/g} words to learn more about them. The tooltips that appear can help you better understand the world of the game or its mechanics.
Words are highlighted when they first appear in a text — scroll up the dialogue box to see the desired highlighted term again.

af1b8dfd-b189-4546-91ec-bde522d892a1.Text: Idira is armed with a special staff that allows a psyker to unleash {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPowers}psychic powers{/g} against enemies. In the future, you will encounter staves that only a psyker versed in a certain discipline can use. For example, you might find a staff that lets a psyker use Inferno, but to do so, they must first have the pyromancy psychic discipline learned.

1b10f4ac-eeec-4874-928b-95a8353b4439.Text: Idira is a psyker and an Operative. As an Operative, she can study opponents and identify their weaknesses, and her psyker {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} allow her to deal damage to them. {g|f:502b9195c84c42c5b180f3f63ed7955c}Analyse Enemies{/g} is an Operative ability which applies the {g|Encyclopedia:Exploit}exploit{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g} to all enemies within the Operative's {g|Encyclopedia:LineOfSight}line of sight{/g} at the start of each of the Operative's {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turns{/g}. The Operative can also use this ability against a specific enemy to inflict several stacks of this effect. The higher the Operative's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerIntelligence}Intelligence{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} is, the more exploit stacks will be inflicted. Whenever the Operative hits a target with an exploit applied to them, the attack deals additional damage. The amount of extra damage depends on the target's number of exploit stacks and the Operative's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g}. {g|f:197b8a8a12b0442db7ffee1067cf3d97}Expose Weakness{/g} is an Operative ability which they can use against a single enemy who is under the exploit effect. This ability reduces the enemy's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g}, and armour. The amount of reduction depends on the number of active exploits on the enemy and the Operative's Perception.

b6982eae-9079-44ff-81ff-b5b5009613b9.Text:
When a psyker reaches a new level, they can choose to learn new {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPowers}psychic powers{/g} and psyker {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} instead of archetype {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and talents.
Psychic powers and talents are categorised based on disciplines. Until a psyker learns at least one psychic power from a discipline, they cannot acquire talents from that discipline. To learn higher level psyker powers, a psyker must first learn at least one psychic power that is one level lower from the same discipline, and they also must have a sufficiently high {g|Encyclopedia:PsyRating}psy rating{/g}. A psyker can increase their psy rating instead of choosing a new talent.

99d4edbd-209d-4f9b-bd3a-e9a47b68c9e8.Text:
You have gotten new items! All items are added to your inventory. You can open it by pressing [{bind|OpenInventory}] or clicking on the bag icon on the right side of the screen.
On the inventory screen, weapons, armour, and other items can be equipped or interacted with in other ways. {g|ib:Medikit}Medikits{/g} can be used to replenish {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} and heal injuries.

4e74a9ea-eac4-4e10-8908-05fc04250155.Text: You can switch between party members using the arrows at the top of the inventory screen or clicking [LMB] on a character's portrait. Item descriptions contain comparisons with any corresponding items already equipped by the character.

761fe4f3-916f-4a35-b315-47f535d713fe.Text: To equip new weapons or armour, open your inventory from [{bind|OpenInventory}] and double-click [LMB] on the item. Alternatively, you can hold [LMB] and drag the item to the right slot (it will become highlighted once you start dragging the item). To view the parameters of an item, hover your cursor over its icon and wait for the information window to appear. Another way to view details about an item is to click [RMB] on its icon, then select Info.

0a8d92e6-40bb-4ee7-961f-8f4851c739a7.Text:
Kibellah has a remarkable background. As a {g|f:9b090810169e4a42b22afd5995d3720d}Death Cult assassin{/g}, she can use a special ability called {g|f:6d4c042a5a71482d87c6087fb0a3a245}Raining Blood{/g}. When used, it causes the target of Kibellah's next melee attack to explode in a burst of blood, covering the floor and any enemies behind the target.
The affected enemies suffer additional damage.
Kibellah can also use a special throwable consumable item called a {g|ib:3a4eebf212974ba68d6867981c240b1b}blood phial{/g} to spill even more blood on the battlefield.

ecb88a05-a10c-413a-8c97-a1005de79fa7.Text: Kibellah is a Bladedancer. Bladedancers are incredibly skilled sword fighters who can devastate enemies using two special attacks: {g|f:de2fa09b36314b2dafe09c3e8354d214}Blade Dance{/g} and {g|f:c3d6e29e74e440a79cb243e4e93e0501}Death From Above{/g}. The {g|f:de2fa09b36314b2dafe09c3e8354d214}Blade Dance{/g} ability allows the Bladedancer to make several light strikes against random adjacent targets. If there is only one adjacent target, all the strikes are directed against that target. If two swords are equipped, the Bladedancer deals significantly more strikes. {g|f:c3d6e29e74e440a79cb243e4e93e0501}Death From Above{/g} allows the Bladedancer to swiftly leap to a selected cell and, upon landing, deal damage to all adjacent targets. This ability can be used multiple times per turn, but each use requires a charge to be spent. The Bladedancer gains charges by killing their enemies. The Bladedancer's main characteristics are Weapon Skill, Agility, and Strength. Weapon Skill enhances their melee attacks and defence in close combat. Agility increases their dodge chance and makes their abilities more efficient, for example, increasing the number of strikes made with {g|f:de2fa09b36314b2dafe09c3e8354d214}Blade Dance{/g}. Strength increases their damage dealt with swords. Note: most of the Bladedancer's abilities can only be used with a sword equipped. Some abilities, available through progression, cost wounds instead of AP.

c273fc7b-eb28-4bdc-bbc4-c75520780f51.Text: You can advance the level of your character and companions! Prevailing in battles, exploring the Koronus Expanse, and completing quests earns you {g|Encyclopedia:ExperiencePoints}experience points{/g}. Once you have accumulated enough experience, your character gains a new level. Click on the arrows symbol on a character's portrait to open the {g|Encyclopedia:CharacterLevel}level up{/g} screen. Each level gained offers your characters new progression options, which include new {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} improvements, and other enhancements. Your companions gain new levels at the same time as your character. Even if they are not included in the active party during your journeys, you can always increase their level later.

fadf7fc0-0bed-49ef-a5e6-f270f5e15dc1.Text: You can open the map using [{bind|OpenMap}] to orient yourself.

994d7880-9404-47f2-82f5-c40b4b164ab6.Text:
Here is a map of your voidship — it consists of several parts, between which you can travel. Some parts are not yet available, but over time your character will be able to access them.
Click [LMB] on the active part of the voidship to move there.

4c2029fa-c2d8-4ed0-9950-13da2b97f486.Text: Marazhai is a Drukhari and a Dracon of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest. Marazhai does not use human weapons and can wear either Drukhari armour or — if he learns the required feature — Aeldari armour. Marazhai's unique {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} deals {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g}-based damage to Marazhai himself and inflicts the {g|Encyclopedia:BleedingEffect}bleeding{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g} on him. While Marazhai is bleeding, he gains +3 {g|Encyclopedia:Resolve}resolve{/g}, and he can also obtain other {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} as his power grows. Marazhai is also an Assassin. Assassins have a unique parameter called {g|Encyclopedia:Lethality}lethality{/g}, whose value can change over the course of combat and is equal to either the Assassin's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} or their {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g} (whichever is greater). Assassins have a passive keystone ability called Seek the {g|Encyclopedia:Opening}Opening{/g}, which allows them to see their enemy's weak spots. If the Assassin attacks a target from a side that has an opening, the attack will be particularly effective and deal additional damage equal to 10% of the target's maximum {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}. The active keystone ability, Aim for the Opening, allows the Assassin to create additional openings on the side closest to them.

d8056202-ac2c-43c1-837e-531995626d27.Text:
In order to open locked doors, clear rubble, coerce machine spirits, and overcome other challenges you can also use consumable items.
To open the door in front of you, use a {g|ib:Consumable_MeltaCharge}melta charge{/g}. On a successful {g|Encyclopedia:SkillDemolition}Demolition{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}, the door will be blown apart, allowing you to proceed.

fed22ff2-d762-44c4-95f2-499620a1bcb8.Text: Move your character by clicking [LMB] on a spot on the screen. A symbol will appear, and your character will move toward it. If the spot you chose is inaccessible, the symbol will appear in the closest accessible location.

a1b78488-acab-4e88-9e1f-c184637dc69d.Text: You have received a new, more efficient weapon for your character. To upgrade your equipment, open the inventory [{bind|OpenInventory}]. You can either hold [LMB] and drag the new item to a weapon slot or double-click [LMB] on the item's icon. You will find and purchase new equipment often on your travels, so do not forget to update your characters' equipment in order to make them more powerful.

57a3cf80-04f8-4d29-8d51-5d2d091ee3c6.Text:
As the game's story unfolds, you will see notifications at the top of the screen indicating that the status of your current objective has been updated and that new information has been added to your journal. You can open the journal by pressing [{bind|OpenJournal}] or clicking [LMB] on the notification at the top of the screen.
Journal entries help you keep track of current events and guide your character on their journey. The quests tab tracks the progress of the main story — here you can find information about any quests you have accepted and their current status. Use the journal to help yourself understand where to go on the next steps of your adventure.
The rumours and contracts sections also contain important information — you will learn more about them later.

7b80f0db-b435-4459-bc06-96dbae4f74db.Text: The Rogue Trader's familiar has its own maintenance stations located on the flagship and in your residence on Dargonus. Through corresponding upgrade kits, those stations can gain up to three levels of improvement. The upgrades are permanent, so even if you decide to change your archetype, thus changing your familiar, the stations remain improved.

dc075b3c-66e2-4d7f-baac-2bb50550e212.Text:
Idira has joined your party, which now consists of several characters. To select one character, click [LMB] on their portrait. To select multiple characters, hold [LMB] and drag a box around them.
To select the entire party and issue commands to all your characters at once, press [{bind|SelectAllCharacters}].

907dc36c-a502-45de-8a32-03d411d47ce7.Text: Pasqal is an Operative like Idira, but he is also a member of the fellowship of Tech-Priests, which grants him additional options, advantages, and unique capabilities. One of Pasqal's mechadendrites allows him to hold his two-handed Tech-Priest's axe and a {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} weapon at the same time. Equip a second weapon in his mechadendrite slot on the inventory screen [{bind|OpenInventory}]. {g|f:95cdd5f42ef5480d9fadd9e0acee641b}Machine Spirit Communion{/g} is Pasqal's special {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} which reduces {g|Encyclopedia:Recoil}recoil{/g} and boosts {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g} of allies' weapons in an area. All enemies in the same area will suffer opposite effects. {g|f:0b8058ef3f33406faebea94ee7967d66}Machine Spirit Banishment{/g} is one of Pasqal's special abilities, which reduces the damage dealt by the target's attacks for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}. Targets with the {g|f:ed0acc1731834a89bda8cc52ec769e3d}Reject the Flesh{/g} feature suffer {g|Encyclopedia:ShockDamage}shock damage{/g}. If the target is a mechanism or a machine, this damage is doubled and its characteristics are reduced until the end of combat.

3e5af6a5-304b-49a6-96a3-d143d23ed765.Text: Equipment, weapons, and other items can be found at vendors of various factions throughout the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}. To trade with them, {g|Encyclopedia:ProfitFactor}profit factor{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Reputation}reputation{/g} are required. They are not spent on purchases, but their level (one or both at once) affects the range of goods available to you. Reputation is a measure of the Rogue Trader's relationship with the different factions of the Koronus Expanse. The higher the reputation with a faction, the wider the range of goods available from its representative. To increase your reputation with a particular faction, complete their orders and transfer valuable cargo to their representatives.

0e301847-2dbd-4610-a046-5eed0086eeeb.Text: Profit factor is a measure of your status, wealth, and power as a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}. Its value is determined by your trade connections, income of your holdings, and treasury reserves. The value of your profit factor is displayed on the reputation tab in the character menu [{bind|OpenCharacterScreen}]. While travelling, your character will use profit factor for buying items and completing colonial projects. Profit factor is not spent on purchases and transactions — instead, its level determines your ability to conclude trade transactions. Profit factor can grow or diminish. Its growth is primarily influenced by major trade deals, and its decrease by investments in colonial projects.

3b32786e-1d41-492f-85aa-6145cb655136.Text:
Your character has received a temporary {g|Encyclopedia:PositiveEffect}positive effect{/g} from an ally! Such effects enhance your character's capabilities in combat in some way.
To learn more about the {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g} you have gained, hover your cursor over the effect's icon next to the character's portrait.

50eee8af-6d85-49a5-b3d0-5b3986d83e00.Text:
You have found a new staff!
Psykers can use staves to channel new {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPowers}psychic powers{/g} and their variations in the form of {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic acts{/g} or {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measures{/g}. The staff's wielder follows the usual rules when using these new powers in combat.
Furthermore, each such staff has its own power level which affects the potency, {g|Encyclopedia:Range}range{/g}, and other parameters of the associated psychic powers.

8920c31a-7855-4d18-900d-9b9d075a4da2.Text:
Remember to advance the level of your character and their companions — they always receive new {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} and improve their {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skills{/g} and characteristics.
Click on the arrows symbol on a character's portrait to open the {g|Encyclopedia:CharacterLevel}level up{/g} screen.

486a9edd-e21e-4bd4-86d9-516e78c67b0d.Text: Your character just succeeded on a passive {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAwareness}Awareness{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}! Such tests allow your party to discover hidden passages, stashes, items, and other obscure details. Improving the Awareness {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} for your character and their companions will let you find more concealed objects while exploring.

10cd9632-db9a-4509-bf00-d25be300aff1.Text:
A shield is equipped in one hand but occupies the slot in both weapon sets.
Every shield has a chance to block an enemy's attack. If a hit in a burst attack is blocked, all subsequent hits are also blocked.
{g|f:1c5f4edca9f64fe0911bc946e0b4ea4a}Shield Bash{/g} allows the wielder to attack an enemy, using the shield.
The {g|f:f6a60b4556214528b0ce295c4f69306e}Stalwart Defence{/g} ability increases the wielder's chance to block attacks of multiple enemies. If such an attack is blocked, the wielder can counter-attack the corresponding enemy, using their main weapon.

5cfd0a52-5bca-4f89-8bef-64d6bc851283.Text: To attack, first click [LMB] on the {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacks}single shot{/g} icon on the weapons panel at the bottom of the screen. Hover the cursor over an enemy — a tooltip will appear showing your chances of {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hitting{/g} that enemy and the possible damage you can deal on a successful hit. Click [LMB] on the enemy to fire. The amount of damage your characters deal depends on the parameters of the weapon they are using. The effectiveness of the shot depends on the distance between the character and their enemy — when you target an enemy with a single shot, you will see two areas denoting the weapon's effective and maximum firing {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranges{/g}.

d14ae2ec-dc73-4ca5-8cba-dd8ffa2602c0.Text: Certain {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} in the game are considered attack actions and can only be used once per {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g} unless affected by specific {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} or other abilities a character might have. If a character performs an attack action, they will not be able to attack again and will lose their remaining {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}movement points{/g} until the start of their next turn.

5b14b410-3af9-4846-ba02-f2c4fcc5d864.Text:
To make attacks and use {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} in combat, a character must spend {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g} (or AP). Their total is displayed on the panel at the bottom of the screen.
Every attack or ability has a certain AP cost associated with it. The number of squares next to the icons of attack actions and other abilities indicates their AP cost.
At the start of each character's {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, their AP are restored to their maximum value.

a4ea940a-e82d-4076-b5e0-239444b5bdbc.Text: A true expert in the strategies of the Vigilant, Proctor Solomorne Anthar of the Adeptus Arbites excels in tactical combat, using a shield and a shotgun. His loyal cyber-mastiff Glaito is always by his side, ready to cover his back. Through years, Glaito has become Solomorne's comrade-in-arms, not just a familiar. So, whenever an enemy deals damage to Glaito, the Arbitrator's {g|f:cd8984dc4b2043c18278c317e2e309e5}Fury{/g} grows. Then, the {g|f:2de518e4ecaa4cba86aef0a703dc7e42}Torrent of Fury{/g} ability allows him to unleash his righteous anger upon his enemies, dealing increased damage.

9cff87d7-8636-4557-97b5-56c5ae41f358.Text:
You have found an item that can only be equipped by characters of a certain conviction rank. You can open the character menu to see which conviction your character follows.
Note that both your character and their companions have their own convictions. You can check what conviction a character adheres to on the biography tab in the character menu [{bind|OpenCharacterScreen}].
Convictions change in direction and rank based on how the game's story develops and during important plot decisions.

431cbae6-5f1f-48b0-874f-1bd709d8a2d9.Text: Sometimes your character will have to make tough decisions based on their values, interests, and goals. Such decisions affect their convictions. This can develop in three directions: Dogmatic, Iconoclast, Heretical. Each includes five ranks — the higher the rank, the more zealously the character follows their convictions, and the more noticeably the world around them reacts to their actions and decisions. Promotion through the ranks of each of the three directions opens up access to new dialogue lines, events, unique {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}, and also changes the attitude of others toward your character. Also, some items can only be equipped by characters with certain convictions. When one of the conviction branches reaches rank III: Votary, it becomes the character's main focus. When that happens, the other two conviction branches cannot be raised above rank II: Adherent. Your character's allies have convictions of their own, as well.

f4b197cb-7f3b-4cf9-b00f-b34a3afca316.Text: One of your {g|SoulmarkTypesGlossary}conviction{/g} branches has reached rank II, Adherent. Once it reaches rank III, Votary, it becomes the character's main conviction. After that, you will still be able to choose dialogue options referring to other conviction branches, but those branches cannot be raised above rank II, Adherent.

6e0cf45e-9392-447a-9760-6f7f8cab43ba.Text: When placing the {g|f:b1e24d15bb6841d89b9873829f7b3ba5}Rear{/g} or {g|f:bc99e6ba256f45368bc6bc529e59effd}Backline{/g} {g|f:e4e45f74936c4740b7bc03013f6991ba}Combat Tactics{/g} area, you can press {bind|FlipZoneStrategist} to turn this area 90 degrees.

5a97239e-6dbb-4621-85d3-c93994cae3fe.Text:
There is a trap up ahead! Order your character to disable it. If a character enters a trapped area or fails the {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} to disarm it, the trap will trigger, dealing {g|Encyclopedia:DamageTypesGlossary}damage{/g} and inflicting {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injuries{/g} on all characters within its {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area of effect{/g}.
Sometimes you will see a trap marked with a red area and a connecting dotted line. This line leads to the mechanism that controls the trap. Hover your cursor over the mechanism — if the cursor changes to a trap icon, the trap can be disarmed by interacting with the mechanism. Click [LMB] on the mechanism to attempt the disarm test. If you have your entire party selected, the character with the highest relevant {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} score will go to disarm the trap. If a trap is marked with a red area without a dotted line, simply approach the trap and click on it to attempt the disarm test.
Different skills are used to disarm different types of traps.

32b0f4d3-82f4-4667-bae2-1eeed54ec0a1.Text: While fighting, your character can lose some of their {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}. Your character has suffered an {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injury{/g} after being attacked by Kunrad — this happens when a character receives damage that exceeds 50% of their {g|Encyclopedia:MaxWounds}maximum wounds{/g} within one {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g} (the exact percentage of wounds a character must lose for this to happen may vary depending on the difficulty of the game you choose). Injuries reduce the character's {g|Encyclopedia:Resolve}resolve{/g}. When a character initially suffers an injury, it is considered a fresh injury during the first three rounds. Once three rounds have passed, a fresh injury becomes an old injury. A fresh injury can be healed using a {g|ib:Medikit}medikit{/g} without passing any {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}tests{/g}. Old injuries can be healed with a medikit, but they require the character administering the treatment to pass a {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g} skill test to succeed. Use medikits to restore wounds and heal injuries. Note that when a character loses all of their wounds, they fall {g|Encyclopedia:UnconsciousEffect}unconscious{/g}.

574b3f1c-d349-482d-bfe1-97257a114587.Text:
Once the combat is over, the wounds of all party members are replenished automatically, but any {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injuries{/g} they may have sustained remain — those can be healed with a medikit.
Medikits can only be used by characters who have the {g|f:9aefa8d7db3349358e23b2106578353b}Field Medic{/g} feature, {g|f:37363b46061e46218f40e01ed81e9189}Base Skill: Medicae{/g}, or have taken {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g} skill advancement at least once. Whenever a character uses a medikit in battle, a {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} determines the number of {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} that will be restored as a result.
Abelard can heal your character's injury. Click [LMB] on Abelard's portrait, select the medikit on the panel at the bottom left of the screen, then use it on your character. Abelard needs to be standing right next to your character for him to administer the treatment.

21ac618e-13ac-4623-b851-5bd5a0d345ce.Text: Once a character has suffered a certain number of {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injuries{/g}, these injuries are replaced with a {g|Encyclopedia:Traumas}trauma{/g}. Make use of medikits in time to treat injuries to avoid characters suffering traumas. Removing traumas is a more difficult task — they can only be healed by resting on the ship or in certain other places suitable for rest.

984639d1-27dd-4875-a6a4-d06b3dfe87f4.Text: Combat begins with the tactical phase, during which characters cannot attack or take other actions but may try to take up advantageous positions. Select a character by clicking [LMB] on their portrait at the top of the screen, then click [LMB] on the cell you want the character to move to. Red cells are areas inaccessible to the character. During the tactical phase, each character in the party may move up to their maximum {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}movement points{/g} but cannot position themselves adjacent to an enemy. Press [{bind|Pause}] to start the battle.

332693d4-b988-4fab-b612-e873893b7d31.Text:
Ulfar is a Space Wolf, a mighty Space Marine. His proportions instil respect in his allies and fear in his foes, but because Ulfar takes up 4 cells instead of 1, certain mechanics may work differently for him.
Ulfar does not use {g|Encyclopedia:DetailsOfTheCoverGlossary}cover{/g} or conventional human armour and weapons.
Ulfar's unique {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} allows him, once per combat, instead of losing consciousness due to having his {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} reduced to 0, to become incapacitated for 2 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}rounds{/g}.
While in this state, Ulfar cannot be targeted by attacks or suffer damage, and he also counts as full cover for his allies.
Once 2 rounds have passed, Ulfar can act again and regains 50% of his {g|Encyclopedia:MaxWounds}maximum wounds{/g}.
Furthermore, Ulfar is an Arch-Militant. An Arch-Militant's keystone ability allows them to gain a stack of {g|f:7f7d109653f24774939f758d094b8812}versatility{/g} each time they make an attack whose type is different from the previous one the Arch-Militant used.
For the purposes of this ability, attack types are: {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacks}single shot{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacks}melee attack{/g} (single-target or {g|Encyclopedia:BurstAttacksGlossary}burst{/g}), area melee attack, area {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} attack, and ranged burst attack.
For each stack of this {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g} on the Arch-Militant, their {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} are increased by +5.
If the Arch-Militant accumulates 4 or more stacks of this effect, their attacks start dealing an additional +<u>(3 × Arch-Militant's WS {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g})</u>% or +<u>(3 × Arch-Militant's BS bonus)</u>% damage (whichever is greater).

9d9b949b-b731-4ed8-a90f-68c42797e436.Text:
You have gained access to {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic acts{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measures{/g}! These {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} can sometimes turn the tide of events even in the most hopeless battle. But remember: {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measures{/g} not only help in combat, but also have negative consequences. Study the abilities carefully before using them.
Both are unique to each class and develop as characters {g|Encyclopedia:CharacterLevel}level up{/g}.

4825f0cc-1f93-4035-9e45-4686d0a7e7fb.Text:
You have found a consumable item!
Grenades, stimulants, medikits, and other consumables can be placed in quick access slots. To do this, double-click on such an item [LMB] or drag it to a highlighted slot by holding [LMB]. Each consumable item has a certain number of uses, which is indicated in the item's description.
As with most actions in combat, using consumable items spends the character's {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g}.

104b8ae3-2b30-45de-b2b4-75e690627e24.Text:
Psykers are dangerous not only to their enemies, but to everyone around them (including themselves).
When using {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPowers}psychic powers{/g}, the psyker and their allies can be subjected to {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPhenomena}psychic phenomena{/g} that reduce the level of the party's {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetails}momentum{/g}.
Each use of psychic powers thins the veil between realspace and the warp, increasing {g|Encyclopedia:VeilThickness}veil degradation{/g}. When its value reaches 15, each subsequent use of psychic powers has the possibility of triggering {g|Encyclopedia:PerilsOfWarp}perils of the warp{/g}, a random and dangerous event with unpredictable consequences.

511b7e0d-b1c8-4b02-8365-0c95ceaf5d4d.Text: Yrliet is a xenos, one of the Asuryani. She is a Ranger who follows the Path of the Outcast, and her skills in ranged combat are without equal. Yrliet does not use human weapons and can wear either Aeldari armour or — if she learns the required feature — Drukhari armour. Yrliet's unique {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} instantly ends her {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. However, at the start of her next turn, she will make an attack that always hits its target.

a06acd6e-a95a-418b-86fc-dba827bb1e18.Text: Suffers {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} at the start of each {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. The effect can be removed by any source of healing.

8aa25f27-901c-41a4-9a50-b1521bba36df.Text: Deals fire {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} to the target every {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.

e90e2f82-a22f-4236-8f4e-e344e7d52e02.Text: Increases the creature's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} by +<u>N</u> until the end of combat.

a8956375-340a-4118-9d19-cc378e175859.Text: Each stack reduces {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} by −1 and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} by −10%.

cc15bdcb-2c16-4119-811c-898ab3b578e1.Text: Reduces the creature's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} by −{uip|Dodge|c6372a830a0b47b4b6fa9fc1a4351cdd} until the end of combat.

04f6ae46-fad6-426a-9345-bfd97d244e8a.Text: Increases the creature's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} by +{uip|Dodge|a48288ec76f9441993ed99bf94230a60} until the end of combat.

6b70995d-e4f8-4a69-bc6f-ba1e714c2904.Text: The creature's {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g} have been increased until the end of combat. Current MP: {uip|MP|a536a73c7e7543c9bcd66ac8442b6e9a}.

2a05848e-cf46-4224-92d5-e9a81027d983.Text: Allies always {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} shots from allies' attacks.

2ab8b0c8-f584-4df7-81f1-294141fccb5f.Text: Each stack of burst of disease increases {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} by +7.

357f7dc7-dc82-4679-8654-240a06b6ffce.Text:
Grants the ability to improve their {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreXenos}Lore (Xenos){/g} skill even if their background or {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g} does not allow it.
<indent=5%>+5 to {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g}</indent>

fd7c71c3-71cc-469a-8f66-f78a3381fe78.Text: This {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} costs {uip|WoundCost|a84ce6cbf09447b3970f7b4df0b7f109} {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} to use. The character removes the blinded, immobilised, prone, slowed, staggered, and stunned effects from themselves. This ability can be used even while stunned or prone. If the character has no negative effects to remove, they instead gain +1 AP and +4 MP on the current turn. This ability can only be used once per combat and cannot be used during the first round.

65e7465b-9b04-496a-ac17-3bfc65bfad53.Text:
Mere survival in the grim darkness of the far future is no easy task, to thrive in it — a next to impossible one. But some manage to go beyond and become {g|Encyclopedia:CareerTiersGlossary}Exemplars{/g}. Not only do Exemplars possess extraordinary knowledge in their given archetypes, but they have also reached the pinnacle of mastery, transcending what is thought to be possible.
Core focus: additional {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} from previous archetypes, new Exemplar talents.

3ad9f288-3f21-4c72-a8c2-03c29f1082d6.Text: Grants +1 additional {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g} at the 10th and 20th Exemplar rank.

f2ff776e-4419-403e-adc9-9f5c1d5a4121.Text: Enemies gain no {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeSuperiority}melee superiority{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} against this character.

f53906d6-03c7-49bc-93a9-2d91f4909edc.Text: The character may improve this {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} even if their {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g} or origin does not allow it.

51fbd0e7-fe51-4850-9085-8972b84e95db.Text: The character can also re-roll failed {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}tests{/g} (+1 attempt for each test).

b25b894d-dd39-4ff5-b592-47c3cc23daa7.Text: The character may improve any trained {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristic{/g} even if their {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g} or origin does not allow it.

3c883af1-b6f0-4ea0-9058-60711f50c320.Text: After the first incoming attack each enemy performs during this creature's turn within a 1-cell radius, they perform a strike against that enemy in response.

200bbad1-a4be-4e3f-b364-abdd91c2bdf9.Text: An additional attack with the second weapon will suffer no penalties or increased cost if the first attack was either an axe's {g|f:a270dbb75ea44128b951b5d18d0b6bed}Sweep{/g} or a hammer or mace's {g|f:bd5f109c46684a09b07fb13743d2a6d7}Harsh Shove{/g} ability.

a8ffba14-8b42-4fd0-b8c2-43ccdfaf9184.Text: Flame weapon attacks cost −1 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g} less to use (1 AP minimum).

a00aef13-1171-40fb-8136-a891070900ef.Text: Enemies {g|Encyclopedia:ImmobilisedEffect}immobilised{/g} or {g|Encyclopedia:SlowedEffect}slowed{/g} by this character's webber have their {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} reduced by −{uip|Debuff|ea3131acef5645c3a8eaba942fe404a9} while this effect lasts.

08f6b70a-6414-4c5d-a366-ee000e1efc1f.Text: Enemies suffer a −20% {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} against las weapon attacks.

8bd043c7-4aca-4315-81ae-ec25ee98913c.Text: The axe's {g|f:a270dbb75ea44128b951b5d18d0b6bed}Sweep{/g} and the hammer or mace's {g|f:bd5f109c46684a09b07fb13743d2a6d7}Harsh Shove{/g} ability costs −1 AP less (but no less than 1).

18f78317-0dc8-4192-9004-237434a4877e.Text: The wielder gains +5% {g|Encyclopedia:BlockChance}block{/g} and deals +50% more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} with {g|f:1c5f4edca9f64fe0911bc946e0b4ea4a}Shield Bash{/g}.

92a81b7b-d74b-40a9-bb4d-4d6225249e4c.Text:
Whenever the wielder successfully {g|Encyclopedia:BlockChance}blocks{/g} an attack, they immediately use {g|f:1c5f4edca9f64fe0911bc946e0b4ea4a}Shield Bash{/g} against the attacker, if possible.
If the wielder makes a counter-attack triggered by {g|f:f6a60b4556214528b0ce295c4f69306e}Stalwart Defence{/g}, the {g|f:1c5f4edca9f64fe0911bc946e0b4ea4a}Shield Bash{/g} follows that counter-attack.

01cd41ab-cdfb-47d6-98bd-54f01615e539.Text: Whenever the wielder successfully uses {g|f:1c5f4edca9f64fe0911bc946e0b4ea4a}Shield Bash{/g}, they regain +2 {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}. If they move, they will not provoke {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunityFullGlossary}attacks of opportunity{/g} from the target until the end of their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.

035c3bbd-cad2-47f5-9f8b-6f84391b310f.Text: The wielder gains +{uip|Damage|b090c98714c84716a2c6b586c6228f26} {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} if a shield is in their current weapon set.

ed714f0a-6b56-4ae4-9863-f4c45ccba89f.Text: The wielder gains +{uip|Damage|d77cb4ca64674dcba20f225998828e78} {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}.

7a1db175-5e16-411d-b50e-a5032a5a88fb.Text: A shield only occupies the slot in a single weapon set.

284cc94e-b4f2-478b-9967-721eb6144fa9.Text: Solid projectile weapon attacks gain +2 minimum {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}.

7759bde6-638c-4009-8fe6-72fe4c34ceb0.Text: Increases {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} by half of the character's level (rounded up).

0f7d0aa5-518c-4e17-a056-83184c65e2b6.Text:
{g|Encyclopedia:CareerExecutionerGlossary}Executioners{/g} are specialists in inflicting enduring and excruciating pain on all enemies around them, exploiting it to quickly eradicate their adversaries.
Core focus: {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}-over-time effects, {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} damage, {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effects{/g}, crowd control, large number of {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}.

979e22e0-890c-4554-82e0-187f973df8fe.Text:
Warriors are combatants boasting exceptional {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} prowess, capable of dealing high damage in close quarters combat and withstanding heavy amounts of damage. They also excel at drawing enemies' attention from less defended allies.
Core focus: melee, movement and {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g}, taunts, soaking damage.

88dd56a4-5b39-4ce2-9691-8b982110da5f.Text:
The {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warrior{/g} moves in a straight line and launches a {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee attack{/g} against any target in the Warrior's path. This attack does not count toward the limit of the Warrior's {g|Encyclopedia:AttacksPerTurn}attacks per turn{/g}.
There must be at least 2 free cells between the Warrior and the target to use {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g}.

4015878d-03b8-4c4d-82ed-c420aaf85b38.Text: Until the {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warrior{/g}'s next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, they gain +{uip|TOU|4d2f2a839d2340388d45cf4cf66c947b} {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} and +{uip|THP|4d2f2a839d2340388d45cf4cf66c947b} {g|Encyclopedia:TemporaryWounds}temporary wounds{/g}.

cef41f94-8d87-491a-a939-130bf155dacb.Text:
The {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warrior{/g} gathers all their might for a crushing strike. Their next {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee attack{/g} pushes the enemy away. The distance of the {g|Encyclopedia:PushGlossary}push{/g} is equal to {uip|Push|93d58dfeb6c648858c130e0a902f6ed6} cells.
This {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} cannot be used with a heavy rock saw.

6bd60a02-bf88-4e61-a590-4a918e98fb7d.Text: The {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warrior{/g} unleashes a terrifying scream, drawing the attention of their enemies and becoming a {g|Encyclopedia:PriorityTarget}priority target{/g} for any enemy who fails a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} for 3 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}rounds{/g}.

0c63e281-b092-4cf8-8a14-198737af29be.Text: Bonus armour against the selected target

7bb57314-6b94-4a51-ab62-06b449d9fea4.Text: Bonus damage from melee attacks against the selected target

25515f77-b2c8-438c-8107-9f818a1e5fc1.Text:
For one {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}, the Warrior stays on their feet, even if their {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} reach zero. The Warrior also strikes back when receiving attacks and guards allies in a 3-cell radius around them, jumping in and striking enemies with preemptively, making enemy attacks 50% easier to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}.
! Requires a {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapon.

046517f9-09c6-4170-9825-88814ecac714.Text:
{g|Encyclopedia:CareerHunterGlossary}Bounty Hunters{/g} are methodical killers who leave trails of dead bodies in their wake. A Bounty Hunter chooses their next target before the previous one has even realised it's dead.
Core focus: {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hits{/g}, defence reduction, killing key targets, repositioning.

7ec55513-3d9c-44c2-9be5-65fd669681f0.Text:
The Officer immediately grants an ally an {g|Encyclopedia:ExtraTurn}extra turn{/g} with 2 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g} and no {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}.
