Each shot in a burst is subject to the rules governing {g|Encyclopedia:OverpenetrationFullGlossary}overpenetration{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:PushGlossary}push{/g}.

a42fa219-f579-4e6a-8589-31eff716816a.Text: Operatives support the party and weaken the enemy's defences. Their keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:502b9195c84c42c5b180f3f63ed7955c}Analyse Enemies{/g}, automatically inflicts one stack of the {g|Encyclopedia:Exploit}exploit{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} on every enemy in the Operative's {g|Encyclopedia:LineOfSight}line of sight{/g} at the start of each of the Operative's {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turns{/g}.

289ccc68-ba0f-4716-9d9e-0378ebd9e80b.Text: If an Operative attacks a target afflicted with an {g|Encyclopedia:Exploit}exploit{/g}, the attack will deal (5 × {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g})% more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}, which is further increased by 10% for each exploit on the target. All exploits on the target are then removed. An Operative can also use {g|f:502b9195c84c42c5b180f3f63ed7955c}Analyse Enemies{/g} actively to apply (1 + {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerIntelligence}Intelligence{/g} bonus / 2) exploits on an enemy. The Operative's second keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:fbdba5fe2a264c25bada29aecd64049a}Expose Weakness{/g}, removes all exploits from an enemy to reduce their {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} by −(10 + exploit stacks × Perception bonus)% until the start of the Operative's next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. The Operative's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} inflicts 1 exploit on every enemy in combat, then the Operative attacks a target, landing a guaranteed {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g}. The target suffers a −30% {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g} to their dodge and armour until the end of combat. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: Intelligence, Perception, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAwareness}Awareness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreXenos}Lore (Xenos){/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreImperium}Lore (Imperium){/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillTechUse}Tech-Use{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLogic}Logic{/g}. Operatives can become {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAssassinGlossary}Assassins{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerHunterGlossary}Bounty Hunters{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerExecutionerGlossary}Executioners{/g}, or {g|Encyclopedia:CareerStrategistGlossary}Grand Strategists{/g}.

ea719f05-c920-466a-b3d3-477ce54d83df.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:CareerBladedancerGlossary}Bladedancers{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAdeptGlossary}Operatives{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warriors{/g} can become Assassins, killers who excel in delivering devastating blows and dodging enemy attacks. Assassins have a unique parameter called {g|Encyclopedia:Lethality}lethality{/g}, whose value can change over the course of combat. Its base value is equal to either the Assassin's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} or their {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g} (whichever is greater).

b7c12ce9-9960-4317-9a43-f8f02bb6cc0f.Text: Assassins have a passive keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} called {g|f:74a1e39f3d0c4cab828d49d4acd54851}Seek the Opening{/g}, which allows them to see their enemy's weak spots. If the Assassin attacks a target from a side that has an {g|Encyclopedia:Opening}opening{/g}, the attack will be particularly effective and deal additional {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} equal to 10% of the target's {g|Encyclopedia:MaxWounds}maximum wounds{/g}. Their active keystone ability, {g|f:e2af8c0124f94ca5b9a8b3f91982908a}Aim for the Opening{/g}, allows the Assassin to create additional openings on the side of an enemy closest to them. The Assassin's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} makes an attack against a target. This attack always {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hits{/g} and deals +50% more damage as well as additional damage equal to 25% of the target's missing {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}. For this attack, the Assassin's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:ParryReduction}parry reduction{/g} are doubled. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAwareness}Awareness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCoercion}Coercion{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAthletics}Athletics{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCarouse}Carouse{/g}.

bda7f42e-edaf-4b91-8c01-005c3a20cc94.Text: Bladedancers are swift and deadly masters of the sword, specialising in delivering flurries of rapid strikes with their keystone ability {g|f:e955823f54d24088ae1fdefe88d3684d}Blade Dance{/g}. This ability allows the Bladedancer to make several melee strikes against random adjacent targets.

97a069be-add5-4321-89ab-ff0bf47a3838.Text: The second keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:c3d6e29e74e440a79cb243e4e93e0501}Death From Above{/g}, allows the Bladedancer to jump a short distance and, upon landing, deal damage to all adjacent enemies. This ability can be used multiple times per turn, but each use requires a charge to be spent. These charges are gained through killing enemies. {g|f:c3d6e29e74e440a79cb243e4e93e0501}Death From Above{/g} significantly improves the Bladedancer's mobility and grants them the ability to perform a quick series of kills. The Bladedancer's heroic act is a deadly sequence of jumps and strikes. The Bladedancer jumps toward the target using {g|f:c3d6e29e74e440a79cb243e4e93e0501}Death From Above{/g}, then attacks that target with a sword, and finally repeats that combination multiple times against random targets within range. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAthletics}Athletics{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAwareness}Awareness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCarouse}Carouse{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillDemolition}Demolition{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}. Bladedancers can become {g|Encyclopedia:CareerVeteranGlossary}Arch-Militants{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAssassinGlossary}Assassins{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerExecutionerGlossary}Executioners{/g}, or {g|Encyclopedia:CareerTacticianGlossary}Master Tacticians{/g}.

71efacfe-8427-42d1-8967-ba73f761171d.Text: Executioners are masters of damage-over-time effects, including all bleeding, burning, and toxin effects. For example, the {g|f:47f5b3809fba409b9d27611ef0a77cd3}Scourging Strikes{/g} ability allows the Executioner to inflict bleeding on any targets hit with melee attacks. {g|f:4f04773685be45c29927c6740ccf64d8}Forced Repentance{/g} makes damage-over-time effects even more destructive when inflicted on targets that are already suffering the same effects. Finally, {g|f:5c06542194b74ecc922b92f3543703d2}Where It Hurts{/g} detonates the damage-over-time effects on a target, instantly dealing an incredible amount of damage.

8c716395-7fda-4132-87c9-04d70f6bd7f3.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warriors{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerBladedancerGlossary}Bladedancers{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAdeptGlossary}Operatives{/g} can become Executioners, masters of damage-over-time effects. The first keystone ability, {g|f:47f5b3809fba409b9d27611ef0a77cd3}Scourging Strikes{/g}, allows the Executioner to inflict bleeding on any targets hit with melee attacks, making it so that their enemies are constantly suffering from damage-over-time effects. The second keystone ability is called {g|f:4f04773685be45c29927c6740ccf64d8}Forced Repentance{/g}. Whenever the Executioner inflicts a damage-over-time effect on a target which is already suffering from an effect of the same type, {g|f:4f04773685be45c29927c6740ccf64d8}Forced Repentance{/g} makes the target immediately suffer an additional instance of damage from the initial effect. Additionally, all subsequent damage-over-time effects of this type on that target have their level increased until the end of combat. When the Executioner uses their third keystone ability called {g|f:5c06542194b74ecc922b92f3543703d2}Where It Hurts{/g}, their next attack makes the target immediately suffer several instances of the damage-over-time effects inflicted on it previously. After that, these effects are removed. The Executioner's heroic act immediately inflicts bleeding, burning, and toxin on all enemies in combat while also significantly increasing the level of these effects. Now, time is on your side, and your enemies ripe for the picking. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerIntelligence}Intelligence{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAthletics}Athletics{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreXenos}Lore (Xenos){/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreImperium}Lore (Imperium){/g}.

2f50fc3a-3b03-441b-b0db-b0ad1628b41a.Text: A Warrior relies on their superior skills in {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} combat. The Warrior keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g}, provides them with both great mobility on the battlefield and a way to land an extra {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} in combat.

5c254446-f427-4c58-97fd-6a071ce6ae4d.Text: The Warrior's second keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:4d2f2a839d2340388d45cf4cf66c947b}Endure{/g}, grants them {g|Encyclopedia:TemporaryWounds}temporary wounds{/g} and +({g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} / 2) {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g}. The Warrior's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} instantly restores all their {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}, grants them +(2 × {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} bonus) {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}, and removes the attack limit for the current {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g}, Toughness, Agility. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCoercion}Coercion{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAthletics}Athletics{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCarouse}Carouse{/g}. Warriors can become {g|Encyclopedia:CareerVeteranGlossary}Arch-Militants{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAssassinGlossary}Assassins{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerExecutionerGlossary}Executioners{/g}, or {g|Encyclopedia:CareerVanguardGlossary}Vanguards{/g}.

ead521b7-9f39-471d-97f3-4994801bbfed.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:CareerMarksmanGlossary}Soldiers{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAdeptGlossary}Operatives{/g} can become Bounty Hunters, slayers of their {g|Encyclopedia:Prey}prey{/g} who specialise in breaching the enemy's defences and scoring critical {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hits{/g}.

13ffb14b-d66e-42bd-a9cf-094338facbed.Text: Bounty Hunters are able to see the {g|Encyclopedia:DifficultyTier}difficulty tier{/g} of their enemies, which can vary from I to VII. The Bounty Hunter's keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:802d21391d2f4573bfff126023df39bb}Hunt Down the Prey{/g}, has 3 charges. By spending a charge, they can inflict the {g|Encyclopedia:Prey}prey{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} on an enemy. If a Bounty Hunter kills their prey, they gain {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} that last until the end of combat and depend on the enemy's difficulty tier: Tiers I–II: {g|Encyclopedia:TemporaryWounds}temporary wounds{/g} equal to 25% of the Bounty Hunter's {g|Encyclopedia:MaxWounds}maximum wounds{/g}. Tiers III–IV: +(5 × prey's difficulty tier)% {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical damage{/g} and +(2 × prey's difficulty tier)% critical hit chance. Tiers V–VII: all of the aforementioned bonuses. These bonuses stack. The Bounty Hunter's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} allows them to attack all of the Bounty Hunter's prey within their {g|Encyclopedia:LineOfSight}line of sight{/g} at once. These attacks always {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} and always score critical hits. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAwareness}Awareness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreXenos}Lore (Xenos){/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAthletics}Athletics{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillDemolition}Demolition{/g}.

a1463a5e-03e2-4bdb-bbe5-c851c95654ab.Text: Officers inspire their comrades-in-arms and grant them additional opportunities to impact the course of battle. The Officer keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:9c78e44bf8ff44a9afff8370c673c9ad}Voice of Command{/g}, increases an ally's {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g} by +(5 + 2 × Officer's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}Fellowship{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g}) for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}. An ally affected by this ability can also be targeted by the Officer's other abilities from any distance.

cc8c7513-2430-4fdd-8c85-38c71cd8156a.Text: The Officer's second keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:5bfccf14d8604ae1a041fb347fb8f19f}Bring It Down!{/g}, instantly grants an ally an {g|Encyclopedia:ExtraTurn}extra turn{/g} with 0 {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g} and 2 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}. If this ally is also under the {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} of {g|f:9c78e44bf8ff44a9afff8370c673c9ad}Voice of Command{/g} and kills an enemy by the end of the Officer's {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, the ally will also gain (2 × Officer's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}FEL{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g}) {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetailsGlossary}momentum{/g}. The Officer's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} instantly grants an ally an extra turn with full MP and AP. The ally also has no limit on attacks until the end of this extra turn. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: Fellowship, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillPersuasion}Persuasion{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCoercion}Coercion{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCommerce}Commerce{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreImperium}Lore (Imperium){/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCarouse}Carouse{/g}. Officers can become {g|Encyclopedia:CareerVanguardGlossary}Vanguards{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerStrategistGlossary}Grand Strategists{/g}, or {g|Encyclopedia:CareerTacticianGlossary}Master Tacticians{/g}.

0b9a616a-d63c-428e-a1b2-c2a1d216a1ad.Text: Soldiers sow panic in the enemy ranks from afar. Their keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:7a76af1ef02c4699b62db147e2b9a172}Run and Gun{/g}, grants them +(2 + {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} / 2) {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g} and lets them make one more attack per {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. This attack will cost −1 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g} less. However, from the moment the Soldier activates this ability and until the end of their next turn, the Soldier becomes winded. While winded, they suffer a −10 {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} and cannot use {g|f:7a76af1ef02c4699b62db147e2b9a172}Run and Gun{/g}.

13ba4e42-e432-45bc-a58f-6b97039ed99d.Text: The Soldier's second keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:530b6d2cefef42f180b90c7bdbb99f90}Revel in Slaughter{/g}, immediately removes the winded effect, but can only be used once the Soldier has killed 3 enemies this battle. Once used, the ability grants the Soldier a number of {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} until the end of combat: +10 {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}, +(5 + 2 × {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} bonus)% {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical damage{/g}, and +Agility bonus% critical {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit chance{/g}. The Soldier's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} instantly {g|Encyclopedia:Reload}reloads{/g} their weapon and allows them to make a number of extra attacks equal to their weapon's {g|Encyclopedia:RateOfFire}rate of fire{/g} (minimum 2), using the weapon attack that normally costs the least {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}. These attacks do not spend AP. Until the end of their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, the Soldier's first attack against each new enemy automatically scores a critical hit. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: Ballistic Skill, Agility, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerIntelligence}Intelligence{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAwareness}Awareness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillDemolition}Demolition{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAthletics}Athletics{/g}. Soldiers can become {g|Encyclopedia:CareerVeteranGlossary}Arch-Militants{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerHunterGlossary}Bounty Hunters{/g}, or {g|Encyclopedia:CareerTacticianGlossary}Master Tacticians{/g}.

bf8ae537-2fd4-47ca-8ad8-3192b3c51ce0.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:CareerLeaderGlossary}Officers{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAdeptGlossary}Operatives{/g}, but also Arbitrators and psykers (both sanctioned and unsanctioned), can become {g|Encyclopedia:CareerOverseerGlossary}Overseers{/g}. Their tactics and capabilities are determined by their selected familiar.

914cc4a0-4566-4bd2-9909-cddb97229bfa.Text: The Overseer's keystone feature, selected from several options, allows them to control a familiar. Each option determines which familiar they can control. The familiar is a supplementary unit with its own set of {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}. It does not count toward the party character limit. By default, a familiar is controlled by its Overseer and cannot act on its own in combat. The Overseer's ability, {g|f:374265cc61d5475898f17ac969795f7c}Reactivate{/g}, allows them to restore {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} to a deactivated familiar, thus bringing it back into combat. Although it costs 3 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g} and can only be used once every 2 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}rounds{/g}, it can completely change the course of a battle if used wisely. The Overseer's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} brings their familiar to full wounds (even if it is deactivated) and reduces the cost of the Overseer's next three abilities by −1 AP. Also, it activates the familiar's unique passive bonus. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}Fellowship{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerIntelligence}Intelligence{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g}. Skills: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAwareness}Awareness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCarouse}Carouse{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCoercion}Coercion{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillTechUse}Tech-Use{/g}.

35ea1d86-5935-48e8-9e91-67e810704222.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:CareerLeaderGlossary}Officers{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAdeptGlossary}Operatives{/g} can become Grand Strategists, keen commanders who divide the battlefield into key zones that provide various benefits.

7f4a91dc-936c-4c05-9c0f-6d09b48bcbf0.Text: Grand Strategists have a set of keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} categorised as {g|f:e4e45f74936c4740b7bc03013f6991ba}Combat Tactics{/g}: {g|f:7cdf3a1dd3b5477096e008492e738587}Frontline{/g}, {g|f:bc99e6ba256f45368bc6bc529e59effd}Backline{/g}, and {g|f:b1e24d15bb6841d89b9873829f7b3ba5}Rear{/g}. Each of these designates an area of the battlefield that will have specific interactions with the rest of the Grand Strategist's abilities, while also granting various {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} to allies and imposing {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalties{/g} on enemies. The Grand Strategist can use their {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} on one of these areas. At the start of the Grand Strategist's next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, each ally who is in the area when this turn begins gains an {g|Encyclopedia:ExtraTurn}extra turn{/g} with 1 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g} and 2 {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}. For every enemy who is killed in the area between when the heroic act is used and when the extra turns begin, the number of AP is increased by +1 (up to a maximum of 3) and MP by +2 (up to a maximum of 6). Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}Fellowship{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerIntelligence}Intelligence{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillPersuasion}Persuasion{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCommerce}Commerce{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillDemolition}Demolition{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLogic}Logic{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillTechUse}Tech-Use{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreImperium}Lore (Imperium){/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreXenos}Lore (Xenos){/g}.

c0775537-6839-4beb-a20e-ec7b248340bd.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:CareerBladedancerGlossary}Bladedancers{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerLeaderGlossary}Officers{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:CareerMarksmanGlossary}Soldiers{/g} can become Master Tacticians, cunning combatants who make the most out of their party's strengths.

3ebdc079-bfac-4498-a354-1736ecd297d9.Text: The Master Tactician's passive keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:b669fe2c03a240fca1b3b2429ca87414}Tactical Advantage{/g}, grants the Master Tactician stacks of a unique {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} by the same name whenever they or their allies gain {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetailsGlossary}momentum{/g}. The Master Tactician is granted a number of stacks equal to 20% of the momentum gained (i.e. 1 stack for every 5 momentum). The Master Tactician starts combat with a number of stacks equal to their Fellowship {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g}. The Master Tactician's active keystone ability, {g|f:7989c6e3109841329aee9e4546138395}Press the Advantage{/g}, empowers their next attack, making it deal +4% more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} for each stack of {g|f:b669fe2c03a240fca1b3b2429ca87414}tactical advantage{/g} on the Master Tactician, then removes half of these stacks (rounded up). The Master Tactician's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} lets them select a 3×3 area on the battlefield. All of the Master Tactician's allies (including the Master Tactician themselves) who have {g|Encyclopedia:LineOfSight}line of sight{/g} to at least one enemy within the selected area and can {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} at least one enemy with the weapon they are currently wielding immediately make a single attack against a random enemy they can target within this area. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}Fellowship{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillDemolition}Demolition{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillPersuasion}Persuasion{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreImperium}Lore (Imperium){/g}.

df60c508-00ae-4f40-b5bf-5e0f160c7d9a.Text:
After completing their second-tier {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g}, characters gain access to their third-tier archetype, which has a unique progression path.
This is their chance to pick up more {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} from the first two previously mastered archetypes, improve their {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skills{/g} even further, gain additional {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}, and select 5 new talents from a special list.

a00214df-5579-4c8d-8711-6b9c497ae311.Text: These {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} are more powerful than regular {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g} talents, and most of them are versatile — only a few of them require that certain conditions are met (such as the character having access to {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g} or {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerPowersGlossary}psychic powers{/g}).

2bad5654-8d47-427e-95a9-31118c704939.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:CareerLeaderGlossary}Officers{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warriors{/g} can become Vanguards, living bulwarks who draw enemy fire upon themselves.

ad253aa5-63df-4f4a-b4c5-cb02ba8a57e8.Text: The Vanguard's passive keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:fc83a8ac57e54db59c3bb70083dc385c}Unyielding Beacon{/g}, lets them accumulate stacks of a unique {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} by the same name, which they gain whenever they are attacked. Each stack increases the Vanguard's {g|Encyclopedia:Resolve}resolve{/g} by +1 up to a maximum of +15. Their allies within a 2-cell radius around them receive 1/5 of this {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g}. The Vanguard can also gain {g|Encyclopedia:TemporaryWounds}temporary wounds{/g} based on the number of stacks until the start of their next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. If a Vanguard has fewer remaining temporary {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} than {g|f:fc83a8ac57e54db59c3bb70083dc385c}unyielding beacon{/g} stacks at the start of their turn, the number of temporary wounds becomes equal to the number of stacks even if the Vanguard had no temporary wounds at all at the start of their turn. The Vanguard's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} allows them to attack enemies whenever they attack the Vanguard's allies within 3 cells of the Vanguard. The Vanguard likewise retaliates against anyone who attacks the Vanguard themselves. Both of these effects last until the start of the Vanguard's next turn. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}Fellowship{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAthletics}Athletics{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCarouse}Carouse{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillPersuasion}Persuasion{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCoercion}Coercion{/g}.

afbae6a4-4708-4447-889a-d0bf57418534.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:CareerBladedancerGlossary}Bladedancers{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:CareerMarksmanGlossary}Soldiers{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warriors{/g} can become Arch-Militants, versatile experts who utilise different types of weapons to maximum efficiency.

f77fd9b0-8599-4537-8e3b-d74f3644a5b2.Text: The Arch-Militant's passive keystone {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, {g|f:7f7d109653f24774939f758d094b8812}Versatility{/g}, grants them a stack of versatility each time they make an attack whose type is different from the one previously used by the Arch-Militant. For the purposes of this ability, attack types are: {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacks}single shot{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacks}melee attack{/g} (single-target or {g|Encyclopedia:BurstAttacksGlossary}burst{/g}), area melee attack, area {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} attack, and ranged burst attack. For each stack of this {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} on the Arch-Militant, their {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} are increased by +5. If the Arch-Militant accumulates 4 or more stacks of this effect, their attacks start dealing an additional +(3 × Weapon Skill {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g})% or +(3 × Ballistic Skill bonus)% {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} (whichever is greater). The Arch-Militant's {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} lets them make 1 more {g|Encyclopedia:AttacksPerTurn}attack per turn{/g} until the end of combat, including the {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g} when the heroic act is used. The first attack after the heroic act is used and the first attack the Arch-Militant makes on each of their subsequent turns costs 0 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}. Key {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}: Weapon Skill, Ballistic Skill, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}Skills{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAwareness}Awareness{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCarouse}Carouse{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillAthletics}Athletics{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SkillDemolition}Demolition{/g}.

f8e8e0f3-93cc-43ca-95d9-9228e001bcab.Text: In many ways, a trade protectorate is built on the Rogue Trader's pursuit of profit in the Koronus Expanse. They seek out planets rich in certain resources and absorb them into their trade infrastructure by making use of extractiums. An extractium is a machinery complex that includes everything one needs to exploit natural resources in any corner of the Expanse. You can acquire extractiums by reclaiming colonies, completing projects, fulfilling contracts, and trading with merchants. Resources mined by extractiums can be used to fulfil contracts — special quests listed on a separate tab of your journal. Contracts reward additional resources and other means to further develop your protectorate.

184fd851-17ac-4e6e-9757-41f4637cba77.Text: A substantial part of a Rogue Trader's fortune depends on the efficiency and welfare of their colonies. House von Valancius has already established four colonies, which its new heir must now reclaim: Janus, Kiava Gamma, Dargonus, and Vheabos VI. As you progress through the story, you will also have an opportunity to add a new colony to your domain — Foulstone. Developing colonies requires completing projects that predominantly involve constructing improvements or assisting various factions. These projects grant unique rewards, faction {g|Encyclopedia:Reputation}reputation{/g}, or {g|Encyclopedia:SoulmarkTypesGlossary}conviction{/g} points. They are also the primary method of increasing your {g|Encyclopedia:ProfitFactorFullGlossary}profit factor{/g}. Completing projects takes time, so the colonies will notify the Rogue Trader when a project is complete and deliver the rewards to your ship. You can claim these rewards in the colony management menu. Each colony has its own unfolding story — a chronicle that significantly impacts the colony's development and offers special rewards or effects. Chronicles are updated during important milestones in a colony's growth. Unique events can also occur in colonies, which will either offer {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} or demand the Rogue Trader's direct intervention in order to deal with the threats facing the populace.

e2e94054-ee84-4d16-bff9-a5e141a2b9b3.Text:
The combat log displays detailed information about characters' actions and their outcomes.
It is your primary tool for assessing combat-related data on attacks, abilities, and test rolls.

c4e06299-2343-45ae-bf35-849e97aaf098.Text: You can select any line in the combat log to learn more about the factors that impact the effectiveness of actions performed by your enemies and your party, such as sources of additional damage, enhanced protection, or modified hit chances.

a1dd1a8c-89b7-4bb4-8f90-8f44e7b9e64c.Text: Characters can receive various temporary or permanent effects that influence, either beneficially or adversely, the affected character's condition. Such effects can be loosely categorised into three groups: -Damage-over-time effects -{g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}Characteristic{/g} and parameter modifiers -Control effects There are two broad categories of {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effects{/g}: common and unique. You can learn more about their differences and specific examples by consulting the relevant encyclopedia entry.

b41bc8de-d5c3-4a09-9f05-bc4184707805.Text:
A damage-over-time {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} deals a certain amount of damage to the afflicted character at the start of their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.
Such effects can be removed by using items or {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}.
For example, the {g|Encyclopedia:BleedingEffect}bleeding{/g} effect deals damage at the start of each of the character's turns and lasts indefinitely, but bleeding can be removed with a medikit.
Some damaging status effects: {g|Encyclopedia:ToxinEffect}toxin{/g}, bleeding, {g|Encyclopedia:BurningEffect}burning{/g}, etc. have a number indicating its power.
For example, burning (4) means that this effect will deal 4 damage every turn, until it is removed.
This number can be modified by a variety of {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}, abilities, or equipment that can increase or decrease the power of the effect.
You cannot stack the same effect, but stronger sources of the effect override weaker when applied.
For example, if a creature currently suffering from burning (5) is attacked with a flamer with burning (6), it will suffer burning (6) effect. If it is attacked after that with a flamer with burning (3), it will still have burning (6) effect.
{g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}Characteristic{/g} and parameter modifiers can reduce or boost certain character stats. They generally last a limited time and are removed after a certain number of {g|Encyclopedia:Round}rounds{/g} have passed or at the end of combat. An example of such an effect is {g|Encyclopedia:BlindedEffect}blinded{/g}, which reduces the character's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} by −30 and their {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} chance by −30%.
1 is the lowest possible value of a characteristic. No effect can reduce a characteristic below 1.
Control effects rob the character of the ability to perform certain actions.
These effects always have a limited duration.
For example, the {g|Encyclopedia:ImmobilisedEffect}immobilised{/g} effect prevents the character from moving.

b266f23c-a6f9-4dd8-a891-0f1e334b655e.Text: Critical hit allows the character to deal increased {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} to the enemy. If a character scores a critical hit, the target takes 150% of the attacker's normal damage by default, but some {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}, effects, and {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} could increase this amount. The chance to score a critical hit depends on the character's critical hit chance. The base chance is 10% for {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} attacks and 0% for {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee attacks{/g}.

8fbfc490-2c7b-40da-9a1d-d53915d53880.Text: When firing a {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} weapon, critical hit chance increases by 1% for every 1% increased hit chance above 95%. While in {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g}, critical hit chance increases by 1% for every 1 point difference between the attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristic{/g} and that of their target. Critical {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} also depends on the properties of the selected weapon. Critical damage is calculated before defences are considered and is added alongside other percentage-based damage modifiers, not multiplied.

7ee06d50-3472-431f-ae23-8a3988d299b0.Text: The damage received from attacks with {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} or {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapons as well as from other {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} is calculated in the same way. There are several factors involved. The damage that a character inflicts is affected by the parameters of the weapon used, the character's abilities, and also active effects. The target's {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} directly reduces received damage by its value, but deflection can be reduced by {g|Encyclopedia:DeflectionNegation}deflection negation{/g}. Damage is also reduced by the target's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} applied as a flat percentage (for example, if the target has 56 armour, incoming damage will be reduced by 56%), but armour also can be reduced by {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}.

d643e663-344f-409b-ac09-2a6143200626.Text:
{g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}Armour{/g} rating and {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} can protect the character in the event of a {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g}. Armour rating is calculated as a percentage, while {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} deflection is represented using positive integer values. After calculating the damage, damage deflection is first subtracted, and then the damage is further reduced based on the percentage value of the armour rating.
Weapon parameters such as {g|Encyclopedia:DeflectionNegation}deflection negation{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g} can reduce the value of armour and deflection. However, penetration can never lower defences below zero.

f24a1586-5c33-4027-878c-e5d30bbf89e7.Text: The formula for {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage calculation{/g}, taking into account protection from {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}, looks like this: damage = (damage calculation with all multipliers − ({g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} − {g|Encyclopedia:DeflectionNegation}deflection negation{/g})) × (1 − ({g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} − {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}/100)). Damage {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalties{/g}, including {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical damage{/g}, are added together before damage protection is calculated.

876af2f4-1268-4d35-8e5d-9c55a4198b1a.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}Damage{/g} is divided into three groups: physical, energy, and irreducible. Each of them includes several additional types.

f726259a-9dcc-436f-8f43-483f5e3caf90.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:PhysicalDamage}Physical damage{/g} is usually dealt by projectiles or {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapons. Its types are: -Impact: anything capable of inflicting blunt force {g|Encyclopedia:Traumas}trauma{/g} like blunt weapons, unarmed strikes, bolts, and explosions. -{g|Encyclopedia:RendingDamage}Rending{/g}: anything with a sharp edge like bladed weapons and sharp projectiles like shuriken. -Piercing: any piercing projectiles like bullets or needle ammo. -Power: {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} inflicted by a field that disrupts the molecular bonds of matter and is usually used in power weapons, such as a power sword, power maul, or power axe.{br} {g|Encyclopedia:EnergyDamage}Energy damage{/g} is usually dealt by various chemical substances, fire, electricity, and energy beams. Its types are: -Fire: anything that ignites the target. -Shock: anything that electrocutes the target. -Toxic: anything that deals damage with poison, corrosive acid, etc. -Thermal: anything that uses beams of energy, plasma, or disintegrates the target.{br} {g|Encyclopedia:IrreducibleDamage}Irreducible damage{/g} ignores {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g}. Its types are: -Warp: any kind of exposure to the energies of the warp. -Mental: anything that damages the nervous system of organic targets. Non-organic targets like machines and physical {g|Encyclopedia:DetailsOfTheCoverGlossary}cover{/g} are immune. -Machine: anything that affects exclusively machines and technology. Organic targets and non-mechanical physical objects are immune.{br} There's also a special damage type called {g|Encyclopedia:DirectDamage}direct damage{/g} that cannot be reduced by the target's parameters or {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g}.

7b1f63c4-1209-446d-a571-d41d2dd1f97f.Text: Damage is calculated with the formula: damage = ((damage calculation with all multipliers − ({g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} − {g|Encyclopedia:DeflectionNegation}deflection negation{/g})) × (1 − ({g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} − {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}) / 100)). Firstly, damage calculation with all multipliers is performed. Modifiers (e.g. +2, −3, +4) are added to the damage — they are indicated in the description of the weapon or the selected {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}. Then percentage multipliers (+20%, +35%, −10%) are applied — for example, damage is increased by a certain percentage in case of a {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hit{/g} or a plasma weapon overheating. Some enemies also have their own unique percentage-based damage {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g}. From this resulting amount, the deflection value is subtracted, taking into account deflection negation (these values are expressed as positive integers, e.g. 2, 4, 5). Then the damage mitigation from armour is subtracted, taking into account armour penetration (expressed as a percentage, e.g. 20%, 50%). The damage value is always rounded down (down to zero).

43c976ef-0755-423e-a0b8-01e072a66c45.Text: A character hiding behind cover has a chance to avoid enemy {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} attacks. Full cover, indicated by a skull on the shield, reduce the chance to {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} the character by 60%. Partial cover reduces the chance to hit by 35%. Although, the chance to hit a character behind cover may vary depending on the difficulty of the game you choose and can be altered by certain {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}, and effects.

cd630505-014b-401e-8bed-7e3852e8b2a5.Text: When enemies from the opposite side of a character's cover attack them, the character must pass a cover {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}. If successful, the character avoids {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from the attack — however, if the cover can be destroyed, it will take damage instead of the character. Cover cannot protect the character from {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee attacks{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}Area attacks{/g} (including those from melee weapons) can completely obliterate destructible cover. Full and partial cover provide differing chances for attack avoidance. Partial cover protects a character from attacks originating at least one cell away from the partial cover, but not directly next to it. Full cover protects a character from one side. To make an attack from behind full cover, the character must be at its very edge. During a {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} attack, they automatically step out onto an unoccupied cell nearby, make an attack, and return back to cover. Enemies can shoot at a character behind full cover only if they can see the space the character is on or the space they are stepping out onto to make their attacks.

3a432a7d-4933-4452-9466-490c4b07c68b.Text: A parameter that helps negate {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} attacks. If the character is attacked, they will automatically try to dodge the attack — no matter the weapon. Base dodge chance is (30 + target's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} − attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g})%. Total dodge chance can be further affected by {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and effects that grant {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} or penalties to the target's dodge or the attacker's dodge reduction. For ranged attacks, base dodge reduction is equal to the attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g} score. For melee attacks, base dodge reduction is increased by half of the attacker's Agility score. When dodging an {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attack{/g} made by a ranged weapon, the character can only move up to three cells in order to leave the affected area — only in this case can a dodge be successful. If for some reason the character is unable to leave the affected area, they automatically take grazing {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} damage.

79301735-511a-417c-8d83-3a11272ce5c4.Text: Voidship weapons can only fire within certain arcs determined by the slot where the weapon is mounted and its {g|Encyclopedia:FiringRangeSpace}firing range{/g}.

308b7aec-501e-402f-8c32-10014e10c6ff.Text: A weapon mounted on the {g|Encyclopedia:ProwSpace}prow{/g} fires forward while weapons installed on the ship's {g|Encyclopedia:PortSpace}port{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:StarboardSpace}starboard{/g} sections fire sideways. {g|Encyclopedia:DorsalSpace}Dorsal{/g}-mounted weapons have the best {g|Encyclopedia:FiringArcSpace}firing arc{/g} of 270 degrees, but only special light versions of {g|Encyclopedia:MacroCannonsSpace}macro-cannons{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:LanceWeaponSpace}lance weapons{/g} can be installed in this particular slot.

5de8f60d-a9a7-4a7a-9b02-02d8f59e8da5.Text: In combat, characters can attack from a distance with firearms or fight up close using {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapons. There are three types of {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} attacks: {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacksGlossary}single shot{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:BurstAttacksGlossary}burst{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attack{/g}. When attacking with a firearm, the character must make a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristic{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}. For this test, the distance between the shooter and the target, the effective range of the weapon, as well as {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} that affect {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit chance{/g} (items, {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}, and some {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}) are taken into account. If successful, the target will try to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} the attack — the chance of a successful dodge will depend on the target's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g}, the shooter's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g}, and other factors that influence the dodge and {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g} parameters. Also, if the target is behind {g|Encyclopedia:DetailsOfTheCoverGlossary}cover{/g}, it will give them an additional chance to avoid the attack. If the target fails to dodge or take cover, they suffer {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}. Melee weapons can make single attacks, melee burst attacks, and area attacks. If a character attacks a target with a melee weapon, the target will attempt to both dodge and {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} the attack. The higher the attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} is compared to that of their target, the higher the chance is that the attack will not be parried and the target will suffer damage. Similarly, the higher the attacker's Perception and Agility are, the easier it is for them to damage the target in spite of their attempt to dodge. When making a melee burst attack, if the first strike hits the target, all subsequent strikes automatically hit. If the first strike is dodged or parried, all subsequent strikes are automatically dodged or parried.

365aba11-dbfe-4e03-a026-b241f4459ffd.Text: At the start of each battle, all characters in combat are separated into allied and enemy groups with 2 to 4 characters in each. An allied group's {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g} alternates with an enemy group's turn. A character's {g|Encyclopedia:InitiativeGlossary}initiative{/g} determines which group of allies or enemies they are assigned to. The higher a character's initiative, the higher the chances of being added to a group that is closer to the start of the initiative tracker, therefore allowing them to act first in combat. The first to act is the group whose average initiative (total initiative divided by the number of characters in the group) is the highest. Initiative is calculated using the following formula: ({g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} + {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g} bonus / 2 + (from 1 to 10))

96abc9e3-4542-4ca2-8733-966fe1bd8e6e.Text: If a character attacks a target with a melee weapon, the target may attempt to both {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} the attack and, if they are also using a melee weapon, {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} it. The higher the attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristic{/g} score is, the easier it is for them to ignore the target's parry attempt. The higher the attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} are, the easier it is for them to ignore the target's dodge attempt.

7369b249-52b3-4dfd-a7b1-73af4f2ff018.Text: The chance to successfully {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} is (20 + target's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} + parry {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} − (attacker's Weapon Skill + {g|Encyclopedia:ParryReduction}parry reduction{/g}))%. If an ally with a melee weapon is near the target or the attacking character, {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeSuperiority}melee superiority{/g} is activated, which gives: 1) +10 to attacker's Weapon Skill for each ally with a melee weapon near the target 2) +10 to target's Weapon Skill for each ally with a melee weapon next to the attacker. The base chance to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} such an attack is (30 + target's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} − attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g})%. Total dodge chance can be further affected by {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and effects that grant bonuses or penalties to the target's dodge or the attacker's dodge reduction. The target takes {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} if they fail to dodge or parry the attack. Melee {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attacks{/g} are made in the same way as single-target attacks, but {g|Encyclopedia:Test}tests{/g} against each target in the affected area are made separately. Damage from area attacks is inflicted on all targets in the affected area, both allies and enemies.

53658a43-5c09-4c32-834a-3bbdd6b437dd.Text: Mercenaries are special characters that you can create and add to your party. While playing in co-op mode, you can either control one of the Rogue Trader's companions or create a unique mercenary for yourself. Once you have reached the beginning of Chapter 1, you can bolster your party with mercenaries by speaking to the High Factotum aboard your voidship. Mercenary recruitment is essentially the same as creating a brand-new character.

710a912d-d82c-48ec-a329-a3de7c9c681a.Text:
A recruited mercenary automatically starts at the same level and experience as the Rogue Trader's party, though they do not come with equipment.
You can change any of the mercenary's {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} using the retraining system similar to the one available to your main character.
There is no limit on the number of mercenaries you can have. However, in Chapter 1, the number of characters you can have in your party is limited to 3, not including your main character. Certain events in Chapter 1 can increase this limit to a maximum of 5.
Each time you recruit a mercenary, your {g|Encyclopedia:ProfitFactorFullGlossary}profit factor{/g} decreases by −1.

d2bba327-8140-460f-9a93-5556d9c04a92.Text: With momentum, your party members can use unique {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} called {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic acts{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measures{/g}. In battle, the level of momentum changes depending on the actions of characters. If the momentum gauge reaches 175 or more, any party member can use a heroic act. If momentum drops below 25, your party will gain the ability to use desperate measures, which has a number of {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effects{/g}. At the beginning of each combat, the momentum of the party starts at 100. The maximum momentum of the party is 200, the minimum is 0.

7c44e24c-75b2-45a9-8d20-1e8c0a81e592.Text: The first use of a {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} in combat costs 75 points of momentum — with each subsequent use, the cost increases by 25 points. Each party member has a {g|Encyclopedia:Resolve}resolve{/g} stat — its base value is equal to the {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}Fellowship{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristic{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g}, but it can change due to various {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}, and effects. Resolve is used to calculate the accrual and loss of momentum. The value of momentum constantly changes during combat. For example, the following events may affect it: 1) At the start of a {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g} for a character that has not yet used a heroic act or {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measure{/g} in combat, the party's momentum is increased by that character's resolve. 2) When killing an enemy, the party gains momentum equal to (attacker's resolve × {g|Encyclopedia:DifficultyTier}difficulty tier{/g} of the defeated enemy). The difficulty tier depends on the strength of the enemy. 3) If the {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} of one of the party members drops below 0, the entire party loses momentum equal to (resolve of the fallen ally × 10).

187d549d-5995-47de-a09a-97f522b05df8.Text:
Under the influence of negative effects, your character's chances of survival are reduced: they receive {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalties{/g} to their {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skills{/g}, or actions, and may also suffer {g|Encyclopedia:DirectDamage}direct damage{/g} each {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.
When a character is subject to any {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g}, a corresponding icon will appear next to their portrait.
There are two broad categories of negative effects: common and unique.

872b1347-70ae-4b5c-bc49-e21f0aecd29a.Text:
Common negative effects include:
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:BurningEffect}Burning{/g}: suffers {g|Encyclopedia:FireDamage}fire damage{/g} each {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:BleedingEffect}Bleeding{/g}: suffers {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} at the start of each {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:ToxinEffect}Toxin{/g}: at the start of every turn, the affected target must pass a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} to remove this {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} or suffer damage.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:FatiguedEffect}Fatigued{/g}: each stack grants a −10 {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g}, Toughness, and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} and −1 {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}movement point{/g}.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:DisturbedEffect}Disturbed{/g}: each stack grants a −10 penalty to {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerFellowship}Fellowship{/g}.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:PerplexedEffect}Perplexed{/g}: each stack grants a −10 penalty to {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerIntelligence}Intelligence{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g}.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:BlindedEffect}Blinded{/g}: suffers a −30 penalty to Ballistic Skill and Weapon Skill, as well as a −30% penalty to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g}.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:StaggeredEffect}Staggered{/g}: suffers a −20 penalty to Weapon Skill, Ballistic Skill, Strength, Toughness, and Agility.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:SlowedEffect}Slowed{/g}: movement points are reduced by −3.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:CalmedWarpEffect}Psy dampening{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:PsyRating}psy rating{/g} is reduced by −1.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:Stun}Stunned{/g}: while stunned, a character cannot parry, dodge, or make {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunityFullGlossary}attacks of opportunity{/g}.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:ImmobilisedEffect}Immobilised{/g}: immobilised targets do not regain movement points at the beginning of their turn and cannot use {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} that move them or add movement points.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:CantAttackEffect}Cannot attack{/g}: cannot use weapons.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:PsychosomaticTraumaEffect}Psychosomatic trauma{/g} cannot use {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerPowersGlossary}psychic powers{/g}.</indent>
-<indent=5%>{g|Encyclopedia:ProneEffect}Prone{/g}: cannot act and suffers a −30 penalty to parry and dodge.</indent>
All other negative effects are considered unique — they are not nearly as commonly encountered. These unique effects are generally applied by specific abilities of characters or enemies.

567b914d-7ae0-42dc-a40d-2543c03746f3.Text: Most non-area {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} weapon attacks have a chance to cause overpenetration. When this happens, the attack will also {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} the creatures and objects behind the intended target, although the damage to targets beyond the first is usually lower.

8c85f768-a4b0-4654-882a-c58255183721.Text: This chance depends on the weapon's overpenetration value (usually 50%), the weapon's {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}, and the target's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g}. The chance equals (overpenetration + armour penetration − target's armour)%. The {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} to the next target is equal to (previous percentage × original damage to first target) but cannot be higher than 100% of the original damage. Overpenetration can trigger after the second target (although the chance is reduced by the armour of both the second and the first targets). Overpenetration can happen as long as the chance is higher than 0%, being reduced by the armour of every next target {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g}. All overpenetration attacks are resolved separately, which may lead to some of them being {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hits{/g} or triggering {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} or effects multiple times. Some {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}, talents, and weapon properties can increase the chances of overpenetration, for example, the {g|Encyclopedia:CareerHunterGlossary}Bounty Hunter{/g}'s {g|f:e92f1c119dd64d3981fd750a56e5aab2}Piercing Shot{/g} increases it by a whole 100%. This might raise the overpenetration chance to higher than 100%, which means that the overpenetration will pierce through a higher number of enemies in a line before their armour will reduce the chances below 100%.

fe352a18-30b0-4baa-8731-9b05447872ff.Text: Profit factor (PF) is a measure of a Rogue Trader's wealth and power, the aggregated value of their income, treasury reserves, and exalted status. Profit factor acts as a replacement for conventional currency and is used for all of the Rogue Trader's purchases from grenades to planetary improvements. Buying items does not reduce your profit factor. Rather, its value serves as a threshold that determines your access to certain purchases and opportunities.

806ab694-2ee6-4dc2-ae53-cc468b3828dd.Text: Profit factor is a numerical value that can increase or, on rarer occasions, decrease. -PF can never drop below 0. -If an action requires you to reduce your PF below 0, that action becomes unavailable. -PF has no upper limit. You can increase your profit factor by: -Completing story quests -Selecting certain dialogue options -Fulfilling contracts -Completing colony projects You can cause your profit factor to decrease by: -Completing story quests -Selecting certain dialogue options -Fulfilling contracts -Launching colony projects

4926eebc-37e0-4cea-aa24-a7a152a25033.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerPowersGlossary}Psychic powers{/g} are special {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} available only to psykers. They allow psykers to reach into the warp and use it in various ways. Just like normal abilities, they are used in combat, can be taken when levelling up (instead of {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g} abilities), and some of them can be considered attacks. The main differences from normal abilities is that they can only be taken by a psyker, are separated into unique disciplines, and using them will degrade the {g|Encyclopedia:VeilThickness}veil{/g} between reality and the warp. The worse the degradation, the higher the chance psychic powers will trigger {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPhenomena}psychic phenomena{/g} or even {g|Encyclopedia:PerilsOfWarp}perils of the warp{/g}.

5dc33c29-ebdd-4e6d-8ec9-56b8f7dcaa71.Text:
There are different disciplines of {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerPowersGlossary}psychic powers{/g} — for example, pyromancy allows the psyker to control and create fire, {g|Encyclopedia:BurningEffect}burning{/g} opponents to ash, whereas biomancy allows the psyker to control biological processes inside living creatures, empowering and healing the psyker's allies.
When the psyker selects a new {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} from an {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g}, the psyker can instead select a new psychic power or discipline. When the psyker takes a new discipline, they also gain the basic power of that discipline. Psychic powers have levels — in order to select a high-level psychic power, the psyker must know a psychic power of a lower level from the same discipline and must have a high enough {g|Encyclopedia:PsyRating}psy rating{/g} (that can be increased instead of selecting a {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talent{/g} if the psyker's level is high enough).
All psychic powers are inherently dangerous, as reaching into the warp can cause {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPhenomena}psychic phenomena{/g}, unnerving manifestations that reduce the {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetailsGlossary}momentum{/g} of the party. Basic psychic powers are called minor psychic powers. They only have a chance to trigger psychic phenomena and increase {g|Encyclopedia:VeilThickness}veil degradation{/g} by +1.
But some psychic powers are far more dangerous than others — those powers are called major psychic powers and cause psychic phenomena far more often, additionally increasing veil degradation by +3. Using these psychic powers when the veil degradation is 15 or greater is very dangerous and can trigger {g|Encyclopedia:PerilsOfWarp}perils of the warp{/g}.
Some psychic powers are bound to a psychic focus in a psyker's staff — those psychic powers, usually major psychic powers, require a psyker to wield a specific staff and have {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measure{/g} versions. Their power scales significantly based on the quality of the staff. Using a desperate measure from a staff will always trigger perils of the warp.

a764afc9-502c-4b48-9083-759c9b7f7583.Text: Some {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} (for example, a {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warrior{/g}'s {g|f:93d58dfeb6c648858c130e0a902f6ed6}Forceful Strike{/g}) and weapons (for example, thunder hammers) can push targets away from the character. The targets will be pushed in a direct line away from the character. Should the pushed target collide with an obstacle or another creature, both the target that was pushed away and the target they collide with will take {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} (if they can take damage at all). The damage is equal to (2 × the distance the target should have travelled) regardless of how much the target actually travelled during the push. This damage ignores {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} but can be reduced by other means (for example, with the {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} property of {g|Encyclopedia:HeavyArmour}heavy armour{/g}). The maximum push distance is 5 cells.

83b42bda-6d6b-4449-9251-0f2b76fcadbd.Text:
Some {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} can further modify the {g|Encyclopedia:PushGlossary}collision{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} or other effects caused by a character's pushes. Should two push effects happen at the same time (for example, using the {g|f:bd5f109c46684a09b07fb13743d2a6d7}Harsh Shove{/g} ability of a hammer together with a {g|f:93d58dfeb6c648858c130e0a902f6ed6}Forceful Strike{/g}), the distances will stack.
Larger creatures are harder to push away. Creatures that occupy four squares on the battlefield travel half the distance of any push, while larger creatures cannot be pushed at all.

b3d2682c-05e6-429a-83fb-fff7fe1ec0ba.Text: Some {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} weapons allow you to make {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attacks{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} multiple targets at once. When making such an attack, the character makes a hit {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} for each target according to the rules governing {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacksGlossary}single shots{/g} — {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from such attacks is taken by both enemies and allies caught in the affected area. If the hit test fails against one or more targets, those targets will still take {g|Encyclopedia:GrazingHit}grazing hit{/g} damage. This is equal to 50% of normal damage but can be increased by {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}.

59002452-776e-4ef4-9933-03769a4713ca.Text: During most {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attacks{/g}, the trajectory of the projectile is calculated from the centre of the affected area. If there is no {g|Encyclopedia:DetailsOfTheCoverGlossary}cover{/g} between the centre of the affected area and the target, they will not be able to take cover. Area attacks still take into account the effective {g|Encyclopedia:Range}range{/g} of the weapon and the distance to the target when calculating the chance to {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g}. If the enemy is behind cover, they have a chance to use it — partial cover gives a 35% chance to avoid an attack, full cover increases it to 60%. In addition, this chance can change depending on the character's {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} as well as positive and {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effects{/g}. If the target takes cover, they take {g|Encyclopedia:GrazingHit}grazing hit{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}, but can still avoid damage entirely if they successfully {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}. Base dodge chance is (30 + target's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} − attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g})%. Total dodge chance can be further affected by abilities and effects that grant {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} or penalties to the target's dodge or the attacker's dodge reduction. With a successful dodge, the enemy can completely avoid damage and leave the area of effect — the maximum distance of such a dodge is three cells. If for some reason the target dodges but cannot leave the area, they automatically take grazing hit damage.

42df542d-ac6d-4ec2-9d22-3734e3032628.Text: Every {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} weapon has two firing areas determined by the weapon's range parameters: effective range and maximum range. The maximum range parameter denotes the farthest possible distance for hitting a target. The effective range parameter is equal to 50% of the weapon's maximum range and indicates the distance at which firing the weapon would be the most optimal.

6b364192-e4a2-4dd3-ad2e-58bdaa2dcb2b.Text:
A character cannot target another character with a {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacksGlossary}single shot{/g} or a {g|Encyclopedia:BurstAttacksGlossary}burst{/g} if their target is outside their weapon's maximum range.
Effective and maximum ranges vary for different weapons.
A ranged attack against a target within the weapon's effective range suffers no {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalties{/g} due to the target's distance.
When making a ranged attack against a target between the weapon's maximum effective range and maximum range:
-<indent=5%>Single shots' chance to {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} is reduced by half compared to attacks made against targets within the effective range.</indent>
-<indent=5%>Burst shots' chance to follow the central trajectory is reduced by half, and the number of possible deviation trajectories is doubled due to the expanded cone of fire.</indent>

415b6a2c-4143-4fcd-ad1c-c626828990ce.Text: In addition to the {g|Encyclopedia:HullIntegritySpace}hull{/g}, a voidship has a number of components such as weapons, engines, and other ship parts. Most components can be replaced with ones of the same type, should you happen to procure them. You can make such replacements at any time outside combat.

8a731a1d-7136-4b8f-8d6a-9d47d70849d3.Text:
There are many ways to obtain new ship components — you can collect them as spoils of war, receive during certain events, collect them as rewards from your colonies, or purchase them from a {g|Encyclopedia:VendorsAndReputationGlossary}merchant{/g} in the Furibundus System, as long as you have sufficiently high reputation with their faction.
Apart from replaceable components, your voidship also has two system components — elements of the ship's structure that cannot be replaced but can be upgraded.
There is one more limitation: you cannot install two weapons of the same type in the {g|Encyclopedia:ProwSpace}prow{/g} slots.

eedc3a2a-9aec-4784-b767-9a18d57f3e7c.Text: Your {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} carries a stockpile of {g|Encyclopedia:ScrapSpace}scrap{/g} — spare parts and materials that can be used for repairs. Scrap can be spent on repairing your ship's {g|Encyclopedia:HullIntegritySpace}hull integrity{/g} after a battle, improving system {g|Encyclopedia:ShipComponentsGlossary}components{/g}, or adapting the ship's posts.

e1cbca22-300c-4bd2-ae21-0b43adeb2e2d.Text:
You can collect {g|Encyclopedia:ScrapSpace}scrap{/g} from destroyed enemy ships and from a few other sources.
If you find yourself in desperate need of scrap to make repairs, you can dismantle an upgrade from one of the system {g|Encyclopedia:ShipComponentsGlossary}components{/g} and receive a portion of the scrap you spent on the upgrade.

ea98d48f-1b5e-4b8a-a997-04297a06251d.Text: There are three types of voidship weapons: {g|Encyclopedia:LanceWeaponSpace}lance weapons{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:MacroCannonsSpace}macro-cannons{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:TorpedoLaunchersSpace}torpedo tubes{/g}.

f35854cc-8623-482f-be9c-560fa71a8ce8.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:LanceWeaponSpace}Lance weapons{/g} have high range and damage, but they are unwieldy and thus often have a smaller {g|Encyclopedia:FiringArcSpace}firing arc{/g}. Lance weapons can be installed on the ship's {g|Encyclopedia:ProwSpace}prow{/g}, and their lighter versions in the {g|Encyclopedia:DorsalSpace}dorsal{/g} slot. Lance weapons fire several short pulses, but the target's armour is applied only once to the whole attack. This makes lance weapons especially effective against heavily armoured targets such as large ships. {g|Encyclopedia:MacroCannonsSpace}Macro-cannons{/g} have shorter range but there are usually more of them, and each of their shots is counted independently. Thick armour can drastically reduce the damage macro-cannons can deal. {g|Encyclopedia:TorpedoLaunchersSpace}Torpedo tubes{/g} fire torpedo salvos, which act as separate entities on the battlefield. You can control torpedoes' movement the following round after they are fired. Torpedoes, just like ships, can be fired at. However, torpedoes have no {g|Encyclopedia:HullIntegritySpace}hull integrity{/g} — instead, whenever a {g|Encyclopedia:TorpedoSalvoSpace}salvo{/g} is hit with any weapon, one torpedo gets destroyed, thus reducing the salvo's potential damage. Torpedoes can deal two types of damage: direct and area. When a torpedo salvo collides with a target, each remaining torpedo in the salvo attacks it with the same chance of successfully hitting the target as a regular ship weapon would have. If the torpedo hits, it explodes, dealing high damage but only to the target itself. If the torpedo misses, it detonates outside the target's hull, dealing reduced area damage both to the target and all other objects in a 1-cell radius. Torpedoes can also be detonated manually using a self-destruct command, resulting in the effect as when a torpedo misses its target.

c202de84-7487-4b39-ba54-25f87c703765.Text: A type of {g|Encyclopedia:Range}ranged{/g} attack aimed at a single target. Such shots cannot {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} opponents standing between the shooter and their target, but in the case of a miss, successful {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, or successful {g|Encyclopedia:OverpenetrationFullGlossary}overpenetration{/g}, they can {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} characters behind the main target (both enemies and allies). When a character attacks with a single shot, they roll to hit one target with a base success chance of (30 + {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g})%. After the roll, any {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} that increase hit chance are added to the result. This chance is halved if the enemy is farther than the effective range of the weapon (usually half the maximum range).

598d3caa-b315-4316-a542-be4530dcde55.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}Hit chance{/g} cannot be greater than 95%. Every 1% increased hit chance above 95% transforms into an increased 1% chance to score a {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hit{/g}. If the enemy is behind {g|Encyclopedia:DetailsOfTheCoverGlossary}cover{/g}, they have a chance to successfully use it — partial cover gives a 35% chance to avoid an attack, full cover increases it to 60%. In addition, this chance can change depending on characters' {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} as well as positive and {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effects{/g}. If the target fails to take cover, it will try to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} the attack. Base dodge chance is (30 + target's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} − attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g})%. Total dodge chance can be further affected by abilities and effects that grant {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} or penalties to the target's dodge or the attacker's dodge reduction. The target takes {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} if it fails to take cover or dodge the single-shot attack.

3268b3d9-094e-4e94-aa4b-7dab10503c2e.Text: Your characters will find themselves in situations that {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} their {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skills{/g}. For the purposes of such tests, the game simulates a 100-sided die roll. For a character to pass a characteristic or {g|Encyclopedia:SkillTestsGlossary}skill test{/g}, they must roll a number less than their corresponding characteristic or skill score. Every test also has a difficulty associated with it, which acts as a modifier to the relevant characteristic or skill score.

fbd5bbb6-1f7e-42f0-9c42-70a8bf92f3f6.Text:
Let's say a character is attempting to disarm a trap. The difficulty of this test is −10, and the character's Demolition skill is 50.
The game simulates the die roll, the result of which is 75.
Since the character needed to roll a 40 or lower to pass (Demolition + difficulty modifier = 50 + (−10)), and the roll result is 75, which is greater than 40, the test has been failed.
If the character had rolled a 17 on the die, since 17 < 40, the test would have been passed.

7d944db3-53c6-41a6-b376-fd0e50fe8cba.Text: The convictions system tracks your decisions and alters your Rogue Trader in terms of both narrative and gameplay. Convictions have a large impact on how the game's story unfolds and how it will end. They also offer various mechanical {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} to characters. Your Rogue Trader can gain conviction points by selecting certain options during dialogues, exploration events, and colony development. When one of the conviction branches reaches rank III: Votary, it becomes the character's main focus. When that happens, the other two conviction branches cannot be raised above rank II: Adherent.

6c5f5161-8c08-4191-9e1d-5c58b23b624b.Text: Each {g|Encyclopedia:SoulmarkTypesGlossary}conviction{/g} branch has 5 ranks. Once your character has accumulated enough points to advance to a new conviction rank, they will receive a {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} — usually a passive or active {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}. There are three conviction branches that embody certain role-playing philosophies. {g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkFaith}Dogmatic{/g}: the path of the Imperial Creed, saving Humanity by destroying all that is unknown, unorthodox, and alien. {g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkHope}Iconoclast{/g}: the path of an idealist who believes that even in a cruel universe there is place for nobility and compassion. {g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkCorruption}Heretical{/g}: the path of Chaos and the corruption of the soul. This particular conviction grows both from the decisions you make as well as from using corrupted items and gaining forbidden knowledge. Certain items in the game have additional properties that only become available to those with a specific conviction or a specific conviction and rank.

befe0341-5e83-47bb-8a93-33940db486ec.Text: When attacking, ship weapons first try to hit the target. Hit chance is determined by the ship's auspex and reduced by the target's {g|Encyclopedia:EvasionSpace}evasion{/g}.
