Many ships in the game have 0 evasion, but certain xenos ships might have some evasion score, and relatively small targets such as torpedo salvos always have high evasion.

e66dc27b-a1eb-4fd6-b467-a1f35d056b4b.Text: When a hit is confirmed, there is a chance that the attack scores a critical hit and deals double damage. This chance can be affected by the ship's auspex. If the target has active {g|Encyclopedia:VoidshipShieldsGlossary}shields{/g}, some damage from the incoming attack will be absorbed by them. The damage that was not absorbed is then reduced by a flat amount based on armour, and finally the target's {g|Encyclopedia:HullIntegritySpace}hull{/g} suffers the remainder of the attack's damage.

a12853f5-0b06-4ed4-b0d4-95fbbc2cd4a2.Text: Voidships have tremendous mass and therefore a large amount of inertia. They cannot stop or accelerate instantly — these processes take time. As a result, each ship must travel a certain distance on its turn and can only end its turn during the end phase, when most of its movement is done. The end movement zone is highlighted as the solid-coloured area of the {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g}'s movement.

9748f598-05ba-40ee-b9e5-1d87b51188c1.Text: Ending Your Turn in Space Combat

0c7ab3dc-f0e5-4c92-ae94-78312eac587a.Text: The size of the end movement zone (and the acceleration zone — the initial phase of the ship's movement, where certain abilities can be used) depends on the engine installed on the ship. Some engines are more dynamic and therefore have expanded end movement and acceleration zones (one such engine is installed on the ship at the start of the game), while other models offer increased {g|Encyclopedia:SpeedSpace}speed{/g}, allowing the ship to move farther in a single turn.

b88c1744-9729-4a86-b3a2-3413e567409c.Text: Ending Your Turn in Space Combat

01adc73a-7807-4d10-9189-b22ad27297c5.Text: Ships in combat act in turns based on their priority. The smaller the ship, the higher its priority — small ships get to act earlier than large ones. The Rogue Trader's {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} has a lower priority than enemy ships as they tend to anticipate your arrival and therefore act first. However, the opposite can also occur if you manage to get the drop on your adversaries.

ed76dbc5-9d22-445e-a10e-63f93b8a66a0.Text: As you improve your ship's capabilities, you will be able to increase its priority by selecting certain features, allowing you to act before your enemies do.

ada3e785-992c-4124-be74-cabfc08d788a.Text: While controlling the Rogue Trader's {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} in combat, a total of 6 posts, representing various ship systems, are available for you to manage. As you level up your ship, you can select new abilities that your posts can use. Each post can have up to two basic abilities. These can be used each round, but they have a random {g|Encyclopedia:Cooldown}cooldown{/g} time and each post can only activate one of its abilities per round.

bbe8251e-8a7d-4ed9-a27c-77c562daa8b7.Text:
In addition to basic abilities, each post can have one {g|Encyclopedia:UltimateAbilities}ultimate ability{/g}. Such abilities require time to charge. The gauge gradually fills each round of combat, at the end of combat, and during certain events outside combat. You can have multiple ultimate abilities from different posts charged up at once, but only one of them can be used in a single battle.
It is advisable to assign one of your companions to each post as the officer in charge. A specific skill or some other condition is required for each post, but your companions have special features that can improve some of your ship's abilities.

1b690a61-f9ee-42d2-a631-03f2efa1e01f.Text:
When psykers reach deeper into the warp to power their {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}, there is always the chance of the Empyrean bleeding into our reality, a factor that is invariably destructive and damaging.
At the beginning of the combat, veil degradation is usually 0. Veil degradation increases by +1 for each use of minor {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerPowersGlossary}psychic power{/g} and by +3 for each use of major psychic power, and decreases by −1 each {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}.

21459649-d263-43a5-bacb-8f21c83ae3af.Text: While veil degradation is 14 or less: -Minor psychic powers have a (5 + {g|Encyclopedia:PsyRating}psy rating{/g})% chance to trigger {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPhenomena}psychic phenomena{/g}. -Major psychic powers have a (20 + 4 × psy rating)% chance to trigger psychic phenomena. -Sanctioned psykers using minor psychic powers have a ((5 + psy rating) / 2)% chance to trigger psychic phenomena. -Sanctioned psykers using major psychic powers have a (10 + 2 × psy rating)% chance to trigger psychic phenomena.{br} After veil degradation reaches 15: -Chances of triggering psychic phenomena quadruples. -Major psychic powers may trigger {g|Encyclopedia:PerilsOfWarp}perils of the warp{/g}. -Unsanctioned psykers using minor psychic powers have a (20 + 4 × psy rating)% chance to trigger psychic phenomena. -Unsanctioned psykers using major psychic powers have a (20 + psy rating + veil degradation)% chance to trigger psychic phenomena whenever perils of the warp do not occur. -Sanctioned psykers using minor psychic powers have a (10 + 2 × psy rating)% chance to trigger psychic phenomena. -Sanctioned psykers using major psychic powers have a (10 + psy rating + veil degradation)% chance to trigger psychic phenomena whenever perils of the warp do not occur.

c40a4905-5f4e-47e6-9784-f359b986fcd6.Text: The Rogue Trader can procure various items of interest from several factions in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}. The key dealers you will encounter in the game are representatives from one of five factions: the Drusians, the Explorators, the Kasballica Mission, the Fellowship of the Void, and the Imperial Navy. The Rogue Trader will build business relationships with them over the course of the entire game. The game also features a small number of special merchants who are not affiliated with these five factions.

05cdc0a9-55ea-4c5b-bc75-03efa9c64fbe.Text:
You can improve your reputation with merchants by turning in full loads of various cargo.
You do not spend any resources when purchasing items from merchants, but you do need to meet either one or both of the following conditions: a certain level of {g|Encyclopedia:ProfitFactorFullGlossary}profit factor{/g} and reputation rank.
Items can only be purchased when all of the requirements for doing so are satisfied.
Starting from Chapter 2, the Rogue Trader will be able to contact merchants by speaking to the High Factotum on the voidship's bridge.

355f9250-556c-4538-8bdf-64ec7f1df472.Text: Most ships in the Imperium utilise void shields — energy fields that protect the vessel from enemy fire. For every point of damage absorbed by a shield, it loses one point of its charge. Your void shield has 4 sectors distributed along the sides of the ship. Each sector has its own independent charge, and if one of them is depleted, that {g|Encyclopedia:ShieldSectorSpace}shield sector{/g} will no longer be able to absorb damage even if the rest of the shields are intact.

0a0f716c-3a2a-4d0a-9018-9509b841179f.Text:
The shield charge does not recover automatically mid-combat, but it is fully replenished between battles and can be recharged using the {g|f:bd61b300bcd84e06a80c8cf3b699c78b}Restart Shields{/g} ability.
Shields do not always absorb the entirety of the damage dealt to the ship. Depending on how much charge a shield sector has, it might absorb all of the damage, half of it, or none at all. The more charge a shield sector has, the higher the chance of it absorbing damage. A fully charged shield is guaranteed to absorb all the damage it can. When the charge is at 50% or higher, the shield absorbs either all or half of the damage. When the charge is at 50% or lower, the shield absorbs either half or no damage.

4a9334a9-bc98-43e1-ad2e-b2128061f305.Text:
Armour is a parameter a character or an object can have that reduces incoming {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} by a certain percentage.
Armour is always expressed as a percentage. If a character with 30% armour would suffer 9 damage, they instead only suffer 6, and if they would suffer 300, they would only suffer 210.
If 300 damage would be dealt to a character with 90% armour, the character only suffers 30 damage.

f4026cd5-7cec-4bee-bfc4-c5b10e9879c1.Text:
The value of a character's or object's armour can change due to equipment or the effects of certain {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}.
When calculating the {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from an attack, a target's armour parameter can be reduced by the attack's {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}.
Armour penetration can never reduce a target's armour below 0%.

30658b41-15a4-4dc3-8e42-f5095f77ea8e.Text: Travel between systems takes place on the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} map. First, the ship's Navigator surveys the warp around the current system in search of other systems and possible routes leading to them. Doing so earns you Navigator's insight, a resource that can be spent on charting new routes or lowering the danger level of existing ones. You can also receive {g|Encyclopedia:NavigatorsInsight}Navigator's insight{/g} by resolving certain events that occur in the warp.

78bde35d-e665-4aec-b91e-e200e09b15e1.Text: Four types of warp routes exist in the game: green (safe), yellow (unsafe), orange (dangerous), and red (deadly). The colour of the route affects the frequency and difficulty of warp events that can happen when traversing it. For example, green routes have next to no adverse occurrences, while red routes bode the most perilous of encounters. Sometimes a warp event can cause an incursion on your ship, to which you will have to react either by using certain items or intervening personally.

3b6f975c-a494-4cd3-be35-64b7dbb6f335.Text: Whenever a character loses a large portion of their {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}, they might suffer permanent {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effects{/g} known as {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injuries{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Traumas}traumas{/g}. If a character's wounds are reduced to 0, they lose consciousness and suffer a trauma that applies substantial {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalties{/g} to their {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g} depending on what kind of trauma it ends up being. If a character loses N% of their non-temporary {g|Encyclopedia:MaxWounds}maximum wounds{/g} in a single combat {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}, they suffer an injury. Each injury reduces a character's {g|Encyclopedia:Resolve}resolve{/g}.

fa711804-f8ae-48eb-b7ad-51b0582535c7.Text: Upon receiving K {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injuries{/g}, all injuries are removed from the character and they suffer a {g|Encyclopedia:Traumas}trauma{/g} instead. For the first M {g|Encyclopedia:Round}rounds{/g} (or (M × 6) seconds out of combat), an injury is considered fresh. Once this period of time passes, the fresh injury turns into an old injury. Different types of injuries can be healed by different means. The variables N, K, and M change depending on the game difficulty. On Daring difficulty, these variables are equal to 50/3/3, respectively. Traumas can be removed by: -Resting on the ship or in certain other places suitable for rest. Traumas are healed the moment the character enters the bridge. No specific actions (such as sleeping, speaking to chirurgeons, or waiting for time to pass) are required. Your party may find itself unable to return to the ship, but the area you are in could have some means of resting or recovering such as a {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}medicae{/g} station, a healer, or simply a place suitable for respite. In this scenario, you can heal your characters via an interaction of some sort, such as a dialogue or a button. -Using rare and expensive consumable items. Injuries can be removed by: -Resting on the ship or in certain other places suitable for rest. -Using rare and expensive consumable items. -Using a medikit automatically removes one fresh injury. If there are no fresh injuries on the target, the character administering the treatment makes a Medicae skill {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} (difficulty 0). If they succeed, they remove one old injury.

b7952b46-3a3a-4b45-aac5-860435c3cec3.Text: Each of the wearer's critical {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hits{/g} made with a {g|Encyclopedia:RangeAreaAttacksGlossary}ranged weapon{/g} increases their {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapon {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical damage{/g} by +{unit_stat|WarhammerStrength|bonus} until the end of combat.

aec32a1e-a560-47c7-af5f-bc264b220ee2.Text: Mimic fibres blend the colouration of the wearer into their surroundings. The cloak grants the wearer +10% {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}.

68a7347b-d359-4b7c-9213-ad8eb997e095.Text: While the wearer is adjacent to {g|Encyclopedia:DetailsOfTheCoverGlossary}full cover{/g}, their {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} chance is calculated without considering enemies' {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g} value.

dc29fd6f-dd9a-4a8f-934d-e63ea5d686f6.Text: The wearer's {g|f:e8164ac219f44e69b95de4853569da3b}Lidless Stare{/g} ability no longer deals damage to the affected allies. Instead, those allies gain {unit_stat|WarhammerFellowship|bonus} temporary wounds.

beaf6a42-ea94-4551-9a72-193fffb96d72.Text: The wearer gains the {g|f:e8e9fbe8696e4820b84c733ceba629af}Get Back in the Fight!{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} that costs 0 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}.

a6c006b1-8d50-45d9-8266-e659f63dd82f.Text: Whenever the wearer {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodges{/g} an enemy ranged attack, they immediately perform a single attack with the equipped {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapon on a random adjacent enemy. This attack has +35% {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:ParryReduction}parry reduction{/g} and can only be performed three times in a single {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}.

43579fca-1bcc-433d-a100-fb8ba73d61c2.Text: Whenever the wearer makes an {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attack{/g}, this attack deals additional {g|Encyclopedia:DirectDamage}direct damage{/g} equal to the target's {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g}.

f84ec2e2-0b68-44e8-ae60-05318d5d2968.Text:
Grants the wearer a +5 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:SkillPersuasion}Persuasion{/g}.
Whenever the wearer is affected by an ally's {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, they gain +3% {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} until end of combat. Stacks.

0d0e0a39-9595-4cff-93a7-0310bb8bf7bf.Text:
The wearer of this cape is immune to {g|Encyclopedia:BurningEffect}burning{/g}.
Also, whenever the wearer ends their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, burning is removed from all adjacent allies.

b63f319c-84d7-43ab-8280-b299037079ef.Text:
Whenever the wielder suffers {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}, 1 charge of this effect is removed to prevent that damage.
If there are no charges left, damage is not prevented and the wielder becomes {g|Encyclopedia:StaggeredEffect}staggered{/g} until the end of combat.

a1a9c533-b763-4e87-8c53-7c418bb33e26.Text:
The wielder gains 3 charges of a holo-field at the start of combat. Whenever the wielder suffers {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}, 1 charge of the holo-field is removed to prevent this damage.
If there are no charges left, damage is not prevented and the wielder becomes {g|Encyclopedia:StaggeredEffect}staggered{/g} until the end of combat

6efea028-f2bc-4243-a370-54744c4d6b93.Text:
Whenever the wearer deals damage with a {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee attack{/g}, they gain +{uip|THP|fb13409a1d7b4784b229adddf99d59ec} temporary {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}.
The wielder's melee attacks deal +{uip|Damage|fb13409a1d7b4784b229adddf99d59ec}% more damage.

565e0127-ec12-4e5f-96cb-0d65028065e1.Text: The wearer gains a +15% {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} against enemies that dealt damage to the wearer this {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}.

4df0418e-e01d-4e5f-905c-3841a121cf22.Text: The wearer becomes the least {g|Encyclopedia:PriorityTarget}priority target{/g} as long as they have no enemies or allies adjacent.

b10cf756-931b-4890-9a6c-1e628e5dd956.Text: Whenever the wielder performs a {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} or a {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measure{/g}, they gain +2 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}, +6 {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}, and {uip|THP|a70164cbc0e54e168449793ecc448367} temporary {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}.

One of its worlds is marked with an unknown symbol.

edadd6c0-b4f4-4a89-911f-bf74270a05f6.Text: Whenever the wearer starts their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g} with no enemies adjacent, they gain +6 {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}.

23ab07cd-67fa-46f0-911d-6a7fb7c71149.Text:
Whenever the wearer fails to {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} an attack, they can re-roll the parry {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} once.
If they wield dual {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapons, they can re-roll the parry test twice.

ac15254b-844e-4ed6-9304-37bba52fe708.Text: A marvellous compact weapon in the form of a ring that allows the wearer to fire a {g|f:501282c1591440c3a208c57e92094945}Laser Shot{/g} once per combat.

a2bbdd14-c81b-4155-9ec8-39d2f75ce27a.Text: A marvellous compact weapon in the form of a ring that allows the wearer to fire a {g|f:795d08dee468444aa7594ccd70cce165}Melta Scorching Shot{/g} once per combat.

8e3b8386-e257-4485-8295-59890e4d02f5.Text: Fires a short stream of flame, damaging enemies in a line.

69de200d-82fb-4b5b-9186-fa2d38db9f69.Text: This device grants the wielder a +15 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCarouse}Carouse{/g}.

2d57f87a-968c-499f-82e3-be446306bb91.Text: The wearer's {g|Encyclopedia:DeadeyeShot}deadeye shot{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hits{/g} triggers {g|f:197b8a8a12b0442db7ffee1067cf3d97}Expose Weakness{/g} against the affected enemy until the end of combat.

9eefc7a3-6103-43a6-bf2f-9aa49dcbdcfd.Text: A marvellous compact weapon in the form of a ring that allows the wearer to fire a {g|f:0d179aa9276c4780a95e77801d6c77d5}Flamer Shot: Stream{/g} once per combat.

4899d3a7-f486-42e6-b24b-e320dbe8a74f.Text: The wearer's {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee attack{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} is increased by +{uip|Damage|8e23a4f43526479d85322b8ce69b1214}.

11c5434e-b11a-4518-bf02-d5cbda253a5a.Text: This scroll grants the owner a +15 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreImperium}Lore (Imperium){/g}.

242cc238-302f-4e98-ac41-fb7890e17c77.Text: A marvellous compact weapon in the form of a ring that allows the wearer to fire an {g|f:d22f788b9bb44ab0addf08575d131036}Inferno Pistol Shot{/g} once per combat.

3335de2b-5cbd-4104-a3f3-f36707a3d58b.Text:
Each time the wearer uses a minor {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerPowersGlossary}psychic power{/g}, all allies affected by this power gain +1 stack of the thick luck effect.
Thick luck allows those affected to re-roll a failed attack or a {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} or {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} attempt and is then removed.

86ba9f8a-2035-4fa5-9266-1af815487a8f.Text:
At the start of every combat, the wearer's allies gain {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} equal to the wearer's {g|Encyclopedia:PsyRating}psy rating{/g}.
Whenever an ally suffers any {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} and loses non-temporary {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}, this effect is removed from that ally.

15092619-665b-4fc2-99d9-5746fff75dbb.Text: Once per {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, when the wearer scores a {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hit{/g} with a pistol, the next attack with a pistol costs 0 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}.

f10bb2cf-b679-48c7-8787-b95745aa24fa.Text: This cogitator grants the owner a +10 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLogic}Logic{/g}.

da7781bc-51fd-4ede-8459-1b18a801b40a.Text: Grants a +20 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreWarp}Lore (Warp){/g} and a −10 {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance tests{/g}.

a8161368-5943-464e-83f3-4881dd0d6a72.Text: This tome is full of terrifying descriptions recounting heretical magic experiments and twisted laws of the warp. Although it contains forbidden knowledge, to read through it is to welcome hideous visions into one's head.

4051e3de-5610-4c99-b7d5-150fb99ab5d8.Text: Whenever the wearer {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hits{/g} an enemy with a {g|Encyclopedia:DeadeyeShot}deadeye shot{/g}, it reduces the enemy's {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} by −1 and applies +1 {g|Encyclopedia:Exploit}exploit{/g} until the end of combat. Stacks up to 3 times.

376c43c1-65ae-4e48-912d-1ec393254064.Text: Grants +10 to {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLoreWarp}Lore (Warp){/g}, but the wielder suffers +{uip|Damage|2339239546f843d5ad3b0ed2065483f8}% more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from psychic and Navigator powers.

494b7f26-3b5f-49e7-9448-7c549253f0d7.Text: After triggering a {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPhenomena}psychic phenomenon{/g}, the wearer immediately restores {uip|Wounds|2fad967b07a043969528c310d52d43ac} {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} and gains +{unit_stat|PsyRating} {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}. After triggering {g|Encyclopedia:PerilsOfWarp}perils of the warp{/g}, the wearer immediately gains +1 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g}.

2d986f16-783e-4bab-84a8-f77f839cff8b.Text: Monastery of the Order of the Hammer

5adcc75b-e028-4b54-9a81-df8636c15350.Text: Our survey detected a long-deserted outpost of the Adeptus Mechanicus on the planet. Several useful devices, either abandoned or forgotten by the Tech-Priests, are now in your possession.

2ae3f8a9-69ae-4147-b137-3052953808ed.Text: A smuggler's cache was found on the planet's surface. As a Rogue Trader, you can claim ownership and confiscate its contents.

9842b4b7-c90b-41d9-976c-680442b6b49c.Text: The survey detected a wrecked Imperial voidship. Its crew is lost, but the remaining cargo can still prove useful to the children of the Imperium.

48f06244-54e2-4ce5-9365-e19235e9ccd2.Text: Ruined xenos structures on the planet's surface contain many curious artefacts. They can be yours... if you are willing to risk your soul's purity.

3514e333-ba8c-4946-ab52-53a3d1b3e896.Text: The character has already used a desperate measure this round

8e9f19eb-d9bf-466b-b0ba-0cad4454e13f.Text: This character can no longer use heroic acts or desperate measures this combat

99c9bc70-d445-4bd3-b418-56936f653106.Text: The Warrant of Trade issued to all Rogue Traders grants not only the permission to go beyond the Imperium's borders but also to deal with who or whatever might be out there with the full authority of the Senatorum Imperialis, the High Lords. Many Rogue Traders use the Warrant to conquer or colonise newly discovered planets, taking up the role of Imperial Commander, thus pushing the Imperium's borders ever outward. Others use the Warrant to gain exclusive trade rights with newly discovered cultures, earning for themselves unimaginable riches and establishing the foundation of powerful noble lines. The Warrant also elevates the recipient to the absolute highest of ranks to which an Imperium servant may hope to rise, granting him equivalent status with the likes of Imperial Commanders, Inquisitors, and Space Marine Chapter Masters.

bd060f51-3a92-4cc3-899d-63b6c18e97d5.Text: Make use of cover to minimise damage to your characters.

8c1d3e19-063b-4c76-9ea7-6c015ee17a57.Text: You can select answers in dialogues using the number keys on your keyboard.

7fcd303e-8bce-4cc8-9434-90c4e3b0082d.Text: You can use a character's portrait as the target for an ability.

44b43651-6343-44a2-96f9-99a38a8a2978.Text: There is an obstacle between the attacker and the target

22de3e82-783d-40f5-a85f-cd16a196a951.Text: Can only be used on enemies

0ea9eeab-6bed-4623-ae01-0939296aa44c.Text: Can only be used on non-party members

2b8fb57f-a9cc-4d8f-ab1c-e9fae5a12fad.Text: [UI draft] Target's {text} must be lower or equal to {description}

7591ead2-4ed4-44ce-ba8c-374af46cd438.Text: // Some upgrades can be blocked due to your previous choices

49d73478-723f-4f4a-b16d-e2c07989238e.Text: Efficiency improves the productivity of buildings.

53eb5cb8-b451-43e7-a837-a96e3e7673d5.Text: All unsaved progress will be lost

96b9b4dd-d230-4109-8284-0dbf7620ce25.Text: Press enter to restart the application and switch controls. Or connect a gamepad to continue.

ffcdf027-ca5b-44dc-8b7c-6f0ae4177600.Text: Gamepad disconnected. You have to restart the game application if you want to use a keyboard and mouse. All unsaved progress will be lost.

0f9056e9-384e-4e32-a2af-26a65e621ee4.Text: There are no quests available in this location

75f76d6a-cd18-4bc8-b40b-e7eb584c3e04.Text: Enabling this option records your in-game keystrokes in the game log that is attached to a bug report. If you are having problems with the game's response to keyboard input, enable this option, press the problematic keys, and then submit a bug report.

4881d836-3711-4950-977a-22ce35e49b19.Text: You can not change equipment in combat

39929c24-4423-4c27-a6bc-857178e9d6b3.Text: The combat skills of this creature are extremely noteworthy. They gain large {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:ParryReduction}parry reduction{/g}.

7bc10979-294c-47a0-a6dc-d73dfa6894b0.Text: A veteran of many battles, this creature's {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skills{/g} are significant. They gain bonuses to damage, {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:ParryReduction}parry reduction{/g}.

13fc1f5b-d7da-46c5-9b57-7ef6c5897183.Text: This creature has limited combat experience, and is expendable in most cases. They gain small {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:ParryReduction}parry reduction{/g}.

d1bfbe14-0601-4112-919c-68500190d3d6.Text: An {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injury{/g} received from a trap or a sudden large amount of {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}. If not removed with a medikit, it will turn into an old injury. Too many injuries reduce the character's {g|Encyclopedia:Resolve}resolve{/g} and cause {g|Encyclopedia:Traumas}traumas{/g}. Visit the voidship or use medikit to remove the injury.

bc41346d-03c5-4bc2-931b-af2d3b57d808.Text: An {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injury{/g} that wasn't healed in time. It can be healed with a medikit, but it requires passing a {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g} skill {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} to succeed. Too many injuries reduce the character's {g|Encyclopedia:Resolve}resolve{/g} and cause {g|Encyclopedia:Traumas}traumas{/g}. Visit the voidship or try to use medikit to remove the injury.

ec6592f8-0aa2-47cd-b955-afda8b5c212c.Text:
The Rogue Trader and their allies gain a +20% chance to save a combat stimulant or a medikit after using it.{br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkCorruption}Heretical{/g} — Follower -//

5fcf1919-644b-48e7-b13f-263034b75cde.Text:
Any {g|Encyclopedia:PsychicPhenomena}psychic phenomena{/g} increase the {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetailsGlossary}momentum{/g} of the Rogue Trader's party by +<u>(2 to 10)</u> instead of decreasing it by −<u>(1 to 5)</u>.{br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkCorruption}Heretical{/g} — Votary -//

c651199c-c78a-4453-857f-9675f226d263.Text:
Once per battle the Rogue Trader may choose an ally (including themselves) and grant them a +20 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to all their {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g} for 2 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}rounds{/g}. After the {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g} fades, the target falls {g|Encyclopedia:ProneEffect}prone{/g}.{br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkCorruption}Heretical{/g} — Fanatic -//

2cd17b1f-d498-45fe-bf3a-d62e4ffb213d.Text:
The Rogue Trader and their allies gain a +10% chance to survive with 1 {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wound{/g} instead of falling {g|Encyclopedia:UnconsciousEffect}unconscious{/g}.{br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkFaith}Dogmatic{/g} — Follower -//

c9e87eef-b466-46ab-9a70-4bbc641b66db.Text:
In the first {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g} of combat, all {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hits{/g} scored by the Rogue Trader's party inflict {g|Encyclopedia:BurningEffect}burning{/g} (10). In addition, all {g|Encyclopedia:FireDamage}fire damage{/g} suffered by enemies is increased by +1 for each rank of {g|Encyclopedia:SoulmarkTypesGlossary}Conviction{/g} — {g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkFaith}Dogmatic{/g}.{br}
///Dogmatic — Adherent -//

645fb471-37c3-48ce-b5cd-f9d6c113c98a.Text:
Any {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetailsGlossary}momentum{/g} expenditure by the Rogue Trader and their allies, including {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic acts{/g}, is reduced by −20%.{br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkFaith}Dogmatic{/g} — Votary -//

c765cb98-364f-4759-96f9-08e8747e32ff.Text:
Once per battle the Rogue Trader may choose an ally (including themselves). For 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g} all the target's weapon attacks ignore enemies' {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g}.{br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkFaith}Dogmatic{/g} — Fanatic -//

ddccd597-47f1-4b34-857e-945ea06f2df8.Text:
The Rogue Trader and two random allies start combat with temporary {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} equal to <u>(their own {g|Encyclopedia:Resolve}resolve{/g})</u>.{br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkHope}Iconoclast{/g} — Follower -//

c8a39016-7ef1-41d8-bc3f-85fc853e5639.Text:
In the first {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g} of every combat, the Rogue Trader and their allies gain +<u>(2 + Rogue Trader's {g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkHope}Iconoclast{/g} rank)</u> additional {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}.{br}
///Iconoclast — Adherent -//

467027e3-8699-44aa-a92e-9618eba5e7e8.Text:
The Rogue Trader and their allies spend 30 less {g|Encyclopedia:MomentumWithDetailsGlossary}momentum{/g} when activating a {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g}.{br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkHope}Iconoclast{/g} — Votary -//

2332b9bb-d604-45d1-a500-6d9f87d96d1b.Text:
Any attacks from allies that may {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} other allies will be {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodged{/g} if possible. Any allied {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} that may target an ally and has a {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} will be resisted by allies. {br}
///{g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkHope}Iconoclast{/g} — Zealot -//

1aeb164a-07ac-4849-b505-6dc98a5d26e0.Text: Grants +100% critical {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit chance{/g} until the next {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hit{/g} is scored.

682c64da-175f-45d1-a587-bbf6a49fd2ac.Text: Grants +10% {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit chance{/g} against xenos and daemons.

24ecb65f-7ebd-4112-8f52-89a8fdc20c1b.Text: Any {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} dealt by the character is increased by 10%.

63fbd4b3-6fc0-4c5a-9d2c-d540cd6c525b.Text: Grants a +10 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to all Lore {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skills{/g} — Warp, Xenos, and Imperium, and +10 to {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g}.

5b7af04b-3b47-4962-b9dd-fc070f826667.Text: An attack that deals <u>(10 × {g|Encyclopedia:SoulMarkCorruption}Heretical{/g} rank)</u> {g|Encyclopedia:WarpDamage}warp damage{/g} in a cone pattern. Does not count toward the limit of attacks per {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.

2b7a2ace-fc10-4e33-91e9-7f1d12593751.Text:
Whenever a vessel is inside this cloud of gas and dust, its aiming and firing capabilities are reduced. This cloud also conceals the vessel's position, making it more difficult for its enemies to hit that vessel. Specifically, the Rogue Trader's {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} also has its {g|Encyclopedia:SpeedSpace}speed{/g} reduced.
{g|Encyclopedia:EvasionSpace}Evasion{/g}: +30%
{g|Encyclopedia:ManoeuvrabilitySpace}Manoeuvrability{/g}: −1
Speed: −3 (the Rogue Trader's flagship only)
Hit chance: −25%
Range: −3

0270d675-5824-4de0-9c08-05516528e18f.Text:
Once per round, each vessel in the {g|Encyclopedia:AsteroidField}asteroid field{/g} suffers {g|Encyclopedia:HullIntegritySpace}hull{/g} damage. Torpedoes immediately detonate upon reaching it. Lastly, attack craft deal more damage in the asteroid field.
Damage: <u>(from 8 to 24)</u>
Attack craft damage: +25%

fad90afd-b273-409e-b1ba-7756a7788fdc.Text:
In the {g|Encyclopedia:AsteroidField}asteroid field{/g}, attack craft deal more damage.
Attack craft damage: +25%

765d0ebd-eee2-4228-88b9-c5a612c5e8d7.Text:
Whenever a vessel enters this {g|Encyclopedia:AnomalousZone}anomalous zone{/g}, its shields are fully restored and their strength increased. Upon entering the zone, two random weapons on the vessel are disabled until the end of this round. Additionally, there is a chance of an internal fire.
Shields: +20%

f7ac0b55-b5db-47cc-a743-5f00fd31690c.Text:
This cloud of explosive gas enhances the capabilities of {g|Encyclopedia:MacroCannonsSpace}macro-cannons{/g} but increases the incoming damage. Whenever a vessel inside this {g|Encyclopedia:AnomalousZone}anomalous zone{/g} makes an attack, it suffers damage.
Macro-cannons range: +5 cells
Macro-cannons damage: +20%
Incoming damage: +25%
Damage: <u>(from 2 to 6)</u>

95407510-6379-428a-9631-aefdb13552b8.Text: During the next combat, your {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g}'s {g|Encyclopedia:PortSpace}port{/g} side {g|Encyclopedia:MacroCannonsSpace}macro-cannons{/g} will be unavailable.

da599b62-3fc1-4f3f-b7c1-cdd926288493.Text: The {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} suffers −15% less damage during warp encounters.

8b798b8d-3d03-417f-a308-e04006daf163.Text: Through the Warp and the Stars

bbd90bba-9e04-40e9-92eb-108cc9114945.Text:
The crew fears possible punishment at the hands of the Drukhari and therefore serves more diligently.
There is a 50% chance to gain an additional shot while attacking with the ship's {g|Encyclopedia:MacroCannonsSpace}macro-cannons{/g}.

2db4333a-f4f6-46c6-b95a-6b5c7bd5a5c7.Text:
The crew is terrified of the massacre carried out by the Drukhari.
The chances for a successful attack with the ships's {g|Encyclopedia:MacroCannonsSpace}macro-cannons{/g} are reduced by −20%.

1187dc30-dc9d-4c57-b630-9330bd02f3da.Text:
The crew knows about the Drukhari hunting grounds and does not want to end up there.
There is a 15% chance to gain an additional shot while attacking with the ship {g|Encyclopedia:MacroCannonsSpace}macro-cannons{/g}.

8b4d0aa1-99eb-4c14-8ebc-6b3f9c7855d7.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:SpeedSpace}Speed{/g} is reduced by −2. {g|Encyclopedia:ManoeuvrabilitySpace}Manoeuvrability{/g} is reduced by −1.

2efed7f8-b469-4f09-8a4a-33d3e485fbf7.Text: The {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g}'s weapons have a +10% bonus to critical hit chance.

ed82dc9b-a5a3-4059-95bf-d113bd01473b.Text: Craft bay ships have to return to the {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} to recharge.

cedec9d8-b91b-4f0c-9c6f-1e6d1c27449d.Text: The interior of this ship is on fire. The ship suffers <u>(from 5 to 10)</u> {g|Encyclopedia:SpaceBattleDamageGlossary}damage{/g} each round.

769a1c3a-7b6d-43ee-b57c-b3cb89b79258.Text: Once per combat, when the {g|Encyclopedia:HullIntegritySpace}hull integrity{/g} of the {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} drops below 50%, the weakest void {g|Encyclopedia:ShieldSectorSpace}shield sector{/g} is fully restored.

8d3e25b2-720f-446f-a1a6-98055d92fea4.Text:
Over its centuries-old history, the {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} of the von Valancius dynasty has undergone many modifications.
Learn new combat manoeuvres, develop officer posts, and improve flagship abilities at every rank to dominate the void in the Expanse.

4b3a0fc1-45bd-48a2-bac9-b0b0b80746df.Text: "Lord Cap'n, the augurs have detected Aeldari ships! Combat is imminent! Our more experienced officers advise piercing their multi-charge shields with a series of consecutive attacks."

43b1a1b4-6f23-47b6-b8f0-8550d410c177.Text: "I can say from experience that we won't crack their defences from far off, their shields are too tough. We will have to close in and fire practically at point-blank range."

606a392f-0afc-42fe-a9a7-7891fc8e4b8e.Text: "Throne damn it! Xenos bastards, dead ahead! We just had to run into Drukhari ships..."

102a917d-5b48-4a5d-9b5a-8e88d15575e0.Text: Enemy creatures within the area suffer a {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}. They also cannot use any {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerPowersGlossary}psychic powers{/g}.

ac6bb5c9-43ae-486a-bef8-072d806715f3.Text: Allied creatures within the area gain {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}.

9ecd18e0-ff07-4ae4-9fee-891f6535b130.Text: The warp currents make creatures suffer a {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g} to their {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:MovementPoints}MP{/g}.

fc900274-d842-4475-96f9-f399d3a95aee.Text: The warp currents grant creatures {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} to their {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}.

1e240205-3d4c-403c-baa2-8af019154b59.Text: To open the door, interact with the icon above the cogitator — the character with the highest {g|Encyclopedia:SkillLogic}Logic{/g} will make the {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}. If this test fails, the door will remain closed. A particularly bad result of a Logic test can cause the door to become permanently stuck and impossible to open.

60332c42-c8e5-4ae6-b213-a2d4bcae5417.Text: Press {console_bind|FuncAdditional} to highlight objects your character can interact with.

1f2657f3-7369-43ef-934c-29b1b2f6804f.Text:
Some objects in the game can be interacted with in a special way. They are marked with specific icons — some icons allow you to study objects, others will transfer the character to neighbouring locations or launch a small event. These icons become visible when your character is standing close enough to the interactive object.
You can interact with such objects using {console_bind|Confirm}. If there are multiple interactive objects next to the character, you can switch between them with {console_bind|LeftUp}/{console_bind|RightUp}.
Some interactive objects, such as doors or chests, are not always marked with icons. Move your character closer to the object. If it is highlighted, the object is interactable.
You can also bring up the cursor using {console_bind|LeftStickButton} and hover over icons or highlighted objects with it. Use the cursor to interact with objects by pressing {console_bind|Confirm}.

9cdef806-e9c4-4bc6-8eeb-8db259d414ad.Text:
A new rumour has been added to your journal! Travel to the designated place on the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} map to see if there is any truth to it.
To review known rumours, open the journal from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom} and select the Rumours section by pressing {console_bind|LeftUp}/{console_bind|RightUp}.

d8129e33-cba6-496f-bfbc-cf3d25b8365f.Text:
In combat, a character may need to use different kinds of weapons, which can be prepared in advance. Hold {console_bind|RightBottom} to open your inventory and prepare different weapon sets. To switch to a different weapon set in combat, hold {console_bind|Func01}.
Swapping weapon sets in combat does not cost {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g}.

e5277ad3-4467-4608-bb99-d7e5c49b6b47.Text:
You can gain a better understanding of what transpired in combat by checking the combat log. All actions performed by your character, their companions, and enemies are recorded in the combat log in the bottom right corner of the screen.
Hold {console_bind|RightUp} to bring up the combat log and choose an entry that interests you. To read the entry in more detail, hold {console_bind|RightStickButton}.

212934a9-70ee-448a-a72d-224aec9c2378.Text:
Change your point of view! Move, rotate, and zoom the camera using {console_bind|RightStick}. Press {console_bind|RightStickButton} to switch between different camera control modes.
Press {console_bind|RightStickButton} to re-centre the camera on the character.

6cba8e72-034a-4d9d-a608-43d145344a15.Text:
In your travels, you will come across containers, crates, and other objects in the environment that you can search. Inside, you can find a variety of loot — from things that are of no use to a Rogue Trader (but may still pique a merchant's interest) to new equipment and important plot items.
Approach the object and press {console_bind|Confirm}. If there are multiple objects nearby, select the one you need using {console_bind|LeftUp}/{console_bind|RightUp}.
You will also encounter locked containers. To open such a container, your party members will have to pass the associated {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}.

85db5121-97ff-48d5-89a3-d74603d1cc54.Text: You can manage your colonies remotely using the colony management screen, which can be opened from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom}.

8c45f6af-fc56-48fe-916f-f60952bfdf7c.Text:
An important event has occurred in one of your protectorate's colonies which calls for the Rogue Trader's personal attention.
You can visit the colony and complete the event at any time. You can find information about all current events demanding your involvement on the colony management screen. Open it from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom}.

040e3396-c93d-47a5-993d-3a027c822c04.Text:
In combat, you can significantly increase the animation speed of your enemies and allies. To do so, hold {console_bind|FuncAdditional}.
In the options menu, you can enable this option to speed up the animations automatically or disable it.

2f9224e1-e2fa-4bb3-9b06-a41067999744.Text:
All group members except the leader can use {console_bind|Confirm} in ground combat to highlight the icon of an ability or a consumable item on the panel at the bottom of the screen.
Additionally, they can use {console_bind|Confirm} to highlight choices in dialogues and book events to show other group members which option they would like to select.
Note: though each group member can express their opinion, it is up to the group leader to make the final decision.

e1a1b637-9638-480f-8750-fee7274b3e80.Text:
In dialogues and book events, you can use {console_bind|Confirm} + {console_bind|LeftUp} to highlight a text line to show other group members which option you would like to choose.
Note: though each group member can express their opinion, it is up to the group leader to make a decision.

50a8cb9d-3cb0-4946-8c34-3ee870199486.Text:
Each group member can use {console_bind|Confirm} + {console_bind|LeftUp} to highlight a selected object, such as:
-<indent=5%>a unit (in combat and out of combat)</indent>
-<indent=5%>a cell on the battlefield (in ground and space combat)</indent>
-<indent=5%>an object on the map (including location map, system map, and the Koronus Expanse map)</indent>

b52654fc-2448-49dd-9027-dd5dcf5e304d.Text:
During ground or space combat, you can use {console_bind|Confirm} + {console_bind|LeftUp} to highlight a selected object to emphasise it for other group members. You can highlight:
-<indent=5%>a creature model</indent>
-<indent=5%>an icon on the abilities panel</indent>
-<indent=5%>a cell on the battlefield</indent>

c1d0cc72-62ce-4d84-badb-63bb04ba546a.Text: While playing in co-op mode, you can highlight a cell, a creature, a line of dialogue, an object on the map, or an ability icon to emphasise it for other group members. They will hear the ping and see that object highlighted on their screens. This can be used in zones where you can directly control your characters, in ground and space combat, in dialogues and book events, and on various maps.

78309ab3-f5d9-4606-8a53-2eb1d4f3ea96.Text:
While playing in co-op mode, you can highlight a cell, a creature, a dialogue line, or an icon on the abilities panel to emphasise it for other group members. To do so, hover the cursor over the object and press {console_bind|Confirm} while holding {console_bind|LeftUp}. The other group members will hear the ping and see that object highlighted on their screens.
This can be used in zones where you can directly control your characters, on system maps, and on the Koronus Expanse map.

833dde22-fbd2-4275-8572-22f1052716ff.Text: One of the available dialogue options requires making a {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}. Unlike with passive skill tests which are made automatically, you can decide whether or not to select an option, the consequences of which depend on the result of the associated test. Success or failure affects how the dialogue develops — depending on the context, you might change the course of the conversation, alter the character's attitude, or perform an action whose consequences will only become apparent later. Select the dialogue option that requires a skill test to display a tooltip detailing your chances of success. The number after the skill's name indicates the difficulty of the test. Once your character starts travelling with allies, the party member with the highest score in the applicable skill will be selected for each test.

469aab3f-bac5-4706-85ce-c49e15c777f1.Text:
You are in a dialogue — here you can learn more about current events, influence the character you are speaking to, or even alter the course of the game's narrative. Your character's personal story depends on the dialogue choices you make.
Available dialogue options are displayed on the right. Select a reply with {console_bind|LeftStickY}/{console_bind|DPadVertical}, then confirm your choice using {console_bind|Confirm}.

a69c303e-b1ef-4e7b-a6ba-fd8624e438ab.Text:
The combat {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} of characters differ depending on their {g|Encyclopedia:Career}archetype{/g}. Available abilities are located at the bottom of the screen on the abilities panel. To read the full description of the ability, activate the abilities panel by pressing {console_bind|Func02}, select the ability, then hold {console_bind|RightStickButton} to open its complete description. A single press of {console_bind|RightStickButton} brings up a quick preview of the description.
Press {console_bind|Confirm} on the icon to use the ability. Before the ability is used, you will get to review its estimated outcome while targeting a character or an area of your choosing. You will also see the ability's {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area of effect{/g}, and each character in this area will have a number displayed over them denoting the probability of being successfully affected. If the ability's effect is guaranteed to work, the ability's icon is displayed instead of a number. When you are ready to use the ability, press {console_bind|Confirm} again to confirm your choice.
During your adventures, your characters will gain new abilities and {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} as their power grows. You can view the full list of available abilities and talents on the features tab in the character menu, which can be opened from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom}.

cbf89d95-721c-4c2b-8e03-45a49a1a7576.Text:
Many characters have entered the fray this time around.
To speed up enemies' animations, you can hold {console_bind|FuncAdditional} during their turn.

2ef92d25-6e8b-4d32-a6c9-39c9e733b8cc.Text:
Before taking an action in combat, you can evaluate its effectiveness with a hologram.
Pressing {console_bind|Confirm} on the battlefield once will place a hologram in that location. Select actions and {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} to see the expected outcome of their use. The action will be displayed as if used from the hologram's location to let you assess whether you have picked an effective position for the action you are planning to take. Press {console_bind|Confirm} on the target again to confirm your choice or press {console_bind|Decline} to cancel it.

dcda0bae-fb9a-4829-a5fa-da9ec30fbfa1.Text:
You can use the hologram to gauge the effectiveness of your intended actions in combat before taking them.
Select a cell on the battlefield and press {console_bind|Confirm} to place the character's hologram there. Select an {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} or a {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacksGlossary}single-shot{/g} attack to see the expected outcome. The action will be displayed as if used from the hologram's location to let you assess whether you have picked an effective position for the action you are planning to take. The hologram also lets you see if the enemy will be within your {g|Encyclopedia:LineOfSight}line of sight{/g} after you move to the selected cell.
Press {console_bind|Confirm} again to confirm your choice and execute the selected action. Press {console_bind|Decline} to cancel it.

c5abd687-fde9-4822-aa6f-9da5e64e2b35.Text:
You can use a {g|ib:Medikit}medikit{/g} to restore your party members' {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} in battle, treat an {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injury{/g}, or get rid of certain {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effects{/g} (if the character is injured or suffering such an {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g}). If the character has a medikit equipped, its icon will be displayed on the bottom left. If no such icon is present, open your inventory and equip a medikit. To use it, select its icon using {console_bind|DPadVertical} and confirm the selection with {console_bind|Confirm}. Then target the character who requires treatment and press {console_bind|Confirm}. A character can only use a medikit on a target they are adjacent to.
Medikits can only be used by characters who have the {g|f:9aefa8d7db3349358e23b2106578353b}Field Medic{/g} feature, {g|f:37363b46061e46218f40e01ed81e9189}Base Skill: Medicae{/g}, or have taken the {g|Encyclopedia:SkillMedicae}Medicae{/g} skill advancement at least once. A Medicae {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} determines the number of wounds restored.
Each medikit holds 2 or more charges, with 1 charge being consumed per use. Used medikits disappear from the panel on the bottom of the screen, so remember to equip your characters with new medikits regularly.
Note that healing, just like most actions, spends the character's {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g} in combat.

eb81ccdd-981e-4403-a4a7-483f654a7c4d.Text:
Your new companion is a {g|Encyclopedia:CareerFighterGlossary}Warrior{/g}. Abelard specialises in {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} combat and drawing the enemy's attacks.
{g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g} is a unique Warrior {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} that works only when they are using a melee weapon and is not considered an attack action. Use {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g} to close the distance between you and the enemy and deal {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}. Press {console_bind|Func02} to switch to ability selection. Then select {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g}, press {console_bind|Confirm}, and choose a direction to charge in. If an enemy is in the direct path of {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g}, Abelard will attack them and will still be able to use an attack action afterward if he has not used one this {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.
Note that {g|f:4955b43454f6488f82892e166c76c995}Charge{/g} can only be used if the character is 2 or more cells away from their target.

443b3046-fac8-4d9a-92fa-8342e800b284.Text:
This character is using a {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapon. {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacks}Melee attacks{/g} require the character to be adjacent to the enemy. To make a melee attack, choose the {g|f:be721a48e3614ddbb86bf18503511c2c}Strike{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g}, using {console_bind|DPadHorizontal}, and confirm your choice with {console_bind|Confirm}. Then choose the enemy you wish to attack and press {console_bind|Confirm}. Unlike {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacksGlossary}single shots{/g}, melee attacks {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} automatically with no need for a roll. The enemy will try to {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} the attack if they are using a melee weapon of their own.
Melee weapons can be used to make {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area attacks{/g} — all creatures in the area will suffer {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} unless they succeed on a dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} (or a parry test if they are armed with a melee weapon). Damage dealt by melee weapons depends on the weapon's parameters and the attacker's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerStrength}Strength{/g} score.

e45fb8ee-3160-4e8d-82f9-21bb2bb4f21b.Text:
All battles in the game are {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}-based and take place on a grid. On their turn, a character can move, attack, and use their {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}.
Select a cell within the highlighted area and press {console_bind|Confirm} twice to move the character there.

7642cf7e-c228-4b4d-be8f-feaba6097e8a.Text:
Your character is afflicted with a {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effect{/g}!
Such {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effects{/g} can hinder a character's ability to fight, pass {g|Encyclopedia:Test}tests{/g}, or use weapons and items.
Press {console_bind|LeftStickButton} to activate the {g|Encyclopedia:InitiativeGlossary}initiative{/g} panel on the left, select a character using {console_bind|DPadVertical}, and press {console_bind|Func01} to see what effects are currently on them. In the character information window that opens, select the effect and press {console_bind|RightStickButton} to learn more about it. A negative effect's description can help you understand how long the effect will last and how you might be able to get rid of it.

ca16bf0e-35dd-42ba-b4c1-c475bbf79a59.Text: You've run out of ammo! To continue shooting, you need to {g|Encyclopedia:Reload}reload{/g} the weapon. Press {console_bind|DPadHorizontal} and select the reload action on the weapons panel at the bottom left to replenish ammo and keep fighting. Like with most actions in combat, you need to spend {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}action points{/g} to reload. Ammo supply is unlimited for your character and party, so you can reload whenever the need arises.

0ec11211-029e-4437-be9d-09148fee298e.Text:
To survive in the grim darkness of the far future, you will have to face enemies of all kinds and fight for your life. These hints and tutorials will familiarise you with the combat system of Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader.
Press {console_bind|FuncAdditional} to start the battle.

2f7afaa8-4347-46fc-bde9-c896bfd7d106.Text: When you're ready to end your {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, press {console_bind|FuncAdditional}.

4ead9576-f95e-4ac0-b129-5cc3f7706510.Text: You will encounter enemies with various {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and features. An icon next to an enemy's portrait indicates that they are under the influence of some kind of {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g}. Press {console_bind|LeftStickButton} to activate the {g|Encyclopedia:InitiativeGlossary}initiative{/g} panel on the left. Then select an enemy using {console_bind|DPadVertical} and press {console_bind|Func01}. In the character information window that opens, select the effect and press {console_bind|RightStickButton} to learn more about it.

05cacb2e-f4bb-4655-9a89-f60caaf032ba.Text:
Standard scanning could not reveal a route to the selected system, but you can still get there by spending points of Navigator's {g|Encyclopedia:Insight}insight{/g} to plot a guaranteed direct path.
Use {g|Encyclopedia:NavigatorsInsight}Navigator's insight{/g} to chart the course. To do this, select the system, then press and hold {console_bind|Func01}.

fa07b63a-db99-4bee-bb90-fbb7570b3240.Text:
Trophies on the right side of the trophy window go to your inventory — such items can be used or equipped by your characters. Trophies on the left are packed up as cargo and sent to your ship, which can later be used to trade with various factions.
You can move trophies manually from one side of the window to the other. To do this, select a trophy and press {console_bind|Confirm}. Alternatively, you can mass transfer all trophies to the cargo (press {console_bind|LeftUp}) or inventory (press {console_bind|RightUp}) section of the trophy window or vice versa. Hold {console_bind|Func01} to transfer the trophies from both sides of the trophy window to the corresponding windows.

f5077e89-0bf6-4cb4-a9f9-a2db0135ca58.Text: Defeated enemies have no further need for their former belongings, but you can discover valuable trophies among them. Approach a defeated enemy and press {console_bind|Confirm} to inspect what is left of them.

0234d9d6-fb42-449a-b200-2c9750f48630.Text: Defeated enemies have no further need for their former belongings, but you can discover valuable trophies among them. Approach a defeated enemy and press {console_bind|Confirm}.

549c3b9b-2b36-47d8-810c-d82b1d139d1b.Text:
If you place trophies on the right side of the window, they will go to your party's inventory.
Anything placed on the left side will be packed as cargo containers to be traded to various factions at a later time.
You can either move items between the two sections manually by selecting them and pressing {console_bind|Confirm} or use the respective buttons to mass transfer items to cargo or your inventory.

fc30c417-6d3d-444d-a283-c5b751f5499b.Text:
The {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} is a vast region of space where you will travel between different star systems. In each system, unique events can occur. By steering your {g|Encyclopedia:FlagshipSpace}flagship{/g} toward them, you can explore planets, study anomalies, and interact with other ships.
To switch to the map of the entire Koronus Expanse, press and hold {console_bind|FuncAdditional}.

b2e54845-732c-4ac9-b2aa-4e1ae950743d.Text:
Travel between systems is fraught with mortal peril and takes place in another dimension known as the warp. Only a Navigator can plot a course through the warp to other star systems.
Press {console_bind|Func01} to have the ship's Navigator chart new routes to the system you have selected.

8b435dfa-981e-4a74-b00b-34b704e90cc6.Text: To initiate travel to the selected system, press {console_bind|Confirm}.

fa09e105-3888-481b-8530-2257af397c62.Text:
To get to another system, you must pass through the warp.
Your Navigator must first survey your surroundings and tell you which systems you can choose as your next destination.
Press {console_bind|Func01} to see what routes you can take.

104d7ce3-3210-4f15-ad8b-3e9d47629040.Text: Select the system you wish to visit using {console_bind|LeftStick} and press {console_bind|Confirm} to travel there.

03e968bf-d95d-45a1-a7a5-8d928e4941c5.Text:
Highlighted words can help you better understand the world of the game or its mechanics. Press {console_bind|Func02} to switch to description view mode. You can switch between words using {console_bind|LeftStick}/{console_bind|DPadFull}.
Words are highlighted when they first appear in a text — use {console_bind|RightStickY} in the dialogue box to see the desired highlighted term again.

c06ff26c-a796-4db2-8fc0-b436d9e9679f.Text:
You have gotten new items! All items are added to your inventory. You can open it from quick access by holding {console_bind|RightBottom}, selecting the inventory icon using {console_bind|DPadFull}, and then releasing {console_bind|RightBottom}.
Weapons, {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g}, and other items can be equipped or interacted with in some other way. {g|ib:Medikit}Medikits{/g} can be used to replenish {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g} and heal {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injuries{/g}.

93091de9-a19d-4898-b26e-3a0040a7b8a7.Text: You can switch between party members by holding {console_bind|LeftBottom}, selecting a character using {console_bind|DPadFull}/{console_bind|LeftStick}, and then releasing {console_bind|LeftBottom}. Item descriptions contain comparisons with any corresponding items already equipped by the character.

4ba2c1d2-c34b-4d75-98fe-e9cf28e00edd.Text: To equip new weapons or {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g}, open your inventory from quick access, select the item using {console_bind|DPadFull}/{console_bind|LeftStick}, press {console_bind|Func01}, then select Equip. Alternatively, you can select the equipment slot where you would like to equip your new gear, press {console_bind|Confirm}, and then select the item from the list. To view the parameters of an item, select it and press {console_bind|RightStickButton}.

390f0d24-3ead-4ba7-9d27-044df81b9510.Text:
To equip new weapons or {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g}, open your inventory from quick access, select the item using {console_bind|DPadFull}/{console_bind|LeftStick}, press {console_bind|Func01}, and then select Equip. Alternatively, you can choose an equipment slot that contains gear you would like to replace, press {console_bind|Confirm}, then select an item from the list.
To view the parameters of an item, select it and press {console_bind|RightStickButton}. You can learn even more about the item by holding {console_bind|RightStickButton}.

a77c9e70-b730-49ec-a685-7cf995099ea7.Text:
You can switch between party members by holding {console_bind|LeftBottom}, selecting a character using {console_bind|DPadFull}/{console_bind|LeftStick}, and then releasing {console_bind|LeftBottom}.
While viewing equipment descriptions, you will be presented with comparisons between the selected equipment and any corresponding items already equipped by the currently selected character.

d3774c88-7aeb-4556-815e-e3f7563332f8.Text: You can advance the level of your character and their companions! Prevailing in battles, exploring the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}, and completing quests earns you {g|Encyclopedia:ExperiencePoints}experience points{/g}. Once you have accumulated enough experience, your character gains a new level. Hold {console_bind|RightBottom}, select the {g|Encyclopedia:CharacterLevel}level up{/g} icon, then release {console_bind|RightBottom} to open the level up screen. Each level gained offers your characters new progression options, which include new {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} improvements, and other enhancements. Your companions gain new levels at the same time as your character. Even if they are not included in the active party during your journeys, you can always increase their level later.

71666098-53f0-4a74-97e3-7fe4fc608a83.Text: You can open the map by holding {console_bind|FuncAdditional} to orient yourself.

b3b84daa-1700-4c22-98e2-8159e082082b.Text:
Here is a diagram of your voidship — it consists of several parts, between which you can travel. Some parts are not yet available, but over time your character will gain access to them.
Use {console_bind|RightStickY}/{console_bind|DPadVertical} to select the compartment you wish to go to and press {console_bind|Confirm}.

65e1df7b-fcc2-4007-a9e1-3ba5aa1b6ea3.Text:
Move your character using {console_bind|LeftStick} in free mode.
You can also bring up the cursor with {console_bind|LeftStickButton}, move it to a spot on the screen, and press {console_bind|Confirm}. A symbol will appear, and your character will move toward it. If the spot you chose is inaccessible, the symbol will appear in the closest accessible location.

a2558a6a-c8d2-4fdd-9a32-22d7bc7213e9.Text: You have received a new, more efficient weapon for your character. To upgrade your equipment, hold {console_bind|RightBottom}, select the inventory icon in the menu, then release {console_bind|RightBottom}. Equip the new item to a weapon slot by selecting the weapon's icon in the party's inventory with {console_bind|DPadFull}, then press {console_bind|Confirm}. You can also equip items by selecting the appropriate equipment slot and pressing {console_bind|Confirm}. Select the item you wish to equip in the list that appears. You will find and purchase new equipment often on your travels, so do not forget to update your characters' equipment in order to make them more powerful.

a3d757a9-5056-4213-a1ac-57b85961dd5d.Text:
As the game's story unfolds, you will see notifications at the top of the screen indicating that the status of your current objective has been updated and that new information has been added to your journal. You can open the journal from quick access. Hold {console_bind|RightBottom}, use {console_bind|DPadFull}/{console_bind|LeftStick} to select Journal, then release {console_bind|RightBottom}.
Journal entries help you keep track of current events and guide your character on their journey. The quests tab tracks the progress of the main story — here you can find information about any quests you have accepted and their current status. Use the journal to remind yourself about the next step of your adventure.
The rumours and contracts sections also contain important information — you will learn more about them later.

ef38569f-d154-4f1d-b4d8-be72e6e46c87.Text:
Idira has joined your party, which now consists of several characters. There character selection menu allows you to switch between characters — press and hold {console_bind|LeftBottom}. While moving, all party members follow the character you have selected.
If you wish to move only one character or leave a party member somewhere, you can separate that character from the party by pressing {console_bind|Func02} in the character selection menu.

c856aa9a-1e92-4d5c-8ad0-491814d6ee55.Text: Pasqal is an {g|Encyclopedia:CareerAdeptGlossary}Operative{/g} like Idira, but he is also a member of the fellowship of Tech-Priests, which grants him additional options, advantages, and unique capabilities. One of Pasqal's mechadendrites allows him to hold his two-handed Tech-Priest's axe and a ranged weapon at the same time. Equip a second weapon in his mechadendrite slot on the inventory screen, which can be navigated to from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom}. {g|f:95cdd5f42ef5480d9fadd9e0acee641b}Machine Spirit Communion{/g} is Pasqal's special {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} which reduces the {g|Encyclopedia:Recoil}recoil{/g} and boosts the {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeReduction}dodge reduction{/g} of allies' weapons in an area. All enemies in the same area will suffer opposite effects. {g|f:0b8058ef3f33406faebea94ee7967d66}Machine Spirit Banishment{/g} is one of Pasqal's special abilities, which reduces the damage dealt by the target's attacks for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}. Targets with the {g|f:ed0acc1731834a89bda8cc52ec769e3d}Reject the Flesh{/g} feature suffer {g|Encyclopedia:ShockDamage}shock damage{/g}. If the target is a mechanism or a machine, this damage is doubled and its {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g} are reduced until the end of combat.

9af40623-8c13-4f91-ba2c-c836ef7b4537.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:ProfitFactorFullGlossary}Profit factor{/g} is a measure of your status, wealth, and power as a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}. Its value is determined by your trade connections, income of your holdings, and treasury reserves. The value of your profit factor is displayed on the reputation tab in the character menu, which can be opened from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom}. While travelling, your character will use profit factor for buying items and completing colonial projects. Profit factor is not spent on purchases and transactions — instead, its level determines your ability to make a trade deal. Profit factor can grow or diminish. Its growth is primarily influenced by major trade deals, and its decrease by investments in colonial projects.

f45eeb01-c393-42c6-800c-cf902fbe0413.Text:
Planets in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} are teeming with valuable resources. Before these resources can be harvested, however, an extractium needs to be set up on the world's surface.
Select the resource mining icon on the planet view, then press {console_bind|Confirm} to confirm the deployment of an extractium. You can see how many extractiums you have available at the bottom of the screen.

c4cb731b-6cb1-4400-8b95-4db34588b2a4.Text:
New contracts are now available in the journal!
Contracts are requests issued by your colonies. By fulfilling them, you can obtain resources, increase your {g|Encyclopedia:ProfitFactorFullGlossary}profit factor{/g}, or receive unique items. Sometimes fulfilling contracts offered by one colony can affect the productivity of your other colonies.
From quick access, {console_bind|RightBottom}, open the journal and select the Contracts section by pressing {console_bind|LeftUp}/{console_bind|RightUp}.

071b525c-f748-4bf7-acb3-70d00652fac2.Text: Fulfilling contracts costs a certain amount of resources or a share of your {g|Encyclopedia:ProfitFactorFullGlossary}profit factor{/g}. A contract's description contains both the costs associated with it and the reward you will receive. You can fulfil a contract by selecting it in the journal and pressing {console_bind|Func01}. Contracts that are ready to be fulfilled are marked with a yellow symbol.

e12375b4-3d34-42b0-9579-806839425cb8.Text:
Your character has received a temporary {g|Encyclopedia:PositiveEffect}positive effect{/g} from an ally! Such {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effects{/g} enhance your character's capabilities in combat in some way.
Press {console_bind|LeftStickButton} to activate the {g|Encyclopedia:InitiativeGlossary}initiative{/g} tracker, select the character using {console_bind|DPadVertical}, and press {console_bind|Func01}. In the character information window that opens, select the {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatuses}effect{/g} and press {console_bind|RightStickButton} to learn more about it.

cf07935d-83dd-4609-b34f-a22f352b1079.Text:
Remember to advance the level of your character and their companions — they always receive new {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Talent}talents{/g} and improve their {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skills{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Characteristic}characteristics{/g}.
When a character is ready to advance to the next level, the corresponding option will appear in quick access {console_bind|RightBottom}.

aadf6570-0159-4410-8958-0097468f28b6.Text:
On your travels, you will hear many rumours. Those of them that are deserving of the Rogue Trader's attention are logged in the journal.
Sometimes rumours are just that. Other times there is truth to them, and in some cases there may be even more. To verify a rumour, travel to the place indicated in the rumour's description.
To review known rumours, open the journal from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom} and select the Rumours section by pressing {console_bind|LeftUp}/{console_bind|RightUp}.

0a80f6bf-c277-4586-bfaf-8ccf3adda086.Text: Each of the ship's weapons has a separate attack action. You can activate the attacks panel using {console_bind|Func01}. Once you have selected an ability to attack an enemy with, the weapon's {g|Encyclopedia:FiringArcSpace}firing arc{/g} will be displayed.

630945d6-6401-480e-abc7-1f8ad55f7d70.Text:
Select an attack action on the attacks panel and press {console_bind|Confirm} to confirm your selection. Each turn, you can use each of the ship's attacks once.
Manoeuvre your ship in battle and attack with different weapons to make the most out of your ship's capabilities.

1e32ef8a-9040-4efe-bb78-463ddd9608a5.Text: To move the ship, select an accessible cell on the battlefield and press {console_bind|Confirm}. Once you do, you will see a hologram of the ship that will allow you to evaluate the efficiency of future attacks and actions from that position just as you would in regular combat. Press {console_bind|Confirm} again to confirm your choice and command the ship to move. Alternatively, you can press {console_bind|Decline} to remove the hologram.

8a77ce48-11b9-4e20-b5df-41a403fd0c00.Text:
Think of posts as your "ammo clip" of abilities and attacks in space battles.
{g|Encyclopedia:PostSpace}Post{/g} abilities are unlocked as you level up your ship.
You can assign up to two basic abilities and one {g|Encyclopedia:UltimateAbilities}ultimate ability{/g} to every post.
Each round, you can use only one ability from each post.
The cooldown times of abilities are determined randomly after each use and can take up to 3 rounds.
To use a post's ability, activate the posts panel using {console_bind|Func02}, select the ability you wish to use, and press {console_bind|Confirm} to use the ability or choose a target.

15bda449-ba6e-4b48-866c-3cc2600ef263.Text: The ship has reached the end movement zone. To end your turn, press {console_bind|FuncAdditional}.

838d7f9c-d2f5-4760-962e-ae6b440e80b2.Text: Long-range attacks against Drukhari ships are less effective due to the Shadow Field that surrounds them. Try changing your tactics by attacking them at close range — that way you can deal more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} and crush the enemy. Press {console_bind|LeftStickButton} to activate the {g|Encyclopedia:SpaceBattleInitiativeGlossary}priority{/g} panel on the left, select an enemy ship, and press {console_bind|Confirm} to learn how its passive abilities work.

4fa0bdbe-8225-407c-a2d3-a1c82e4eeeff.Text:
You have received new equipment for your ship!
Open the voidship management screen from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom} and select the newly acquired component. To install the equipment, select the desired compartment or item and press {console_bind|Confirm}.

441bbe57-0b3e-4884-a0f6-a9c55e18758e.Text:
Your ship has reached a new level!
On the development tab of the voidship management screen, you can improve the abilities and upgrades you already have or choose new ones. For quick navigation, select the level up option from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom}.

93112776-cf4c-4eca-910d-1f1b985a2259.Text: You can enter cursor mode to make more precise adjustments to the trajectory of your ship's movement. To do this, press {console_bind|LeftStickButton}.

3cab0388-4bd5-4e0c-87cc-3fdb0629d991.Text: Enemy attacks can penetrate your {g|Encyclopedia:VoidshipShieldsGlossary}shields{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} your ship's {g|Encyclopedia:HullIntegritySpace}hull{/g}. This damage remains after the battle is over and must be repaired. Open the voidship management screen from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom} to make repairs to your ship.

09866d45-ca2a-4a64-ac61-c0473cfc799c.Text:
You do not have enough readily available {g|Encyclopedia:ScrapSpace}scrap{/g} to repair your ship, but you still have options if you are willing to sacrifice some of your ship's upgrades.
Open the voidship management screen from quick access {console_bind|RightBottom} and choose a component. Press {console_bind|Confirm} and select Downgrade. The current level of the component will be lowered as it is stripped from the ship and turned into spare scrap — a portion of the original investment — that can be used to repair your ship.

501acd44-b712-4b87-915f-b2c84bb29238.Text:
One of the voidships in battle has gained a new {g|Encyclopedia:CommonStatusesGlossary}effect{/g}!
Press {console_bind|LeftStickButton} to activate the {g|Encyclopedia:SpaceBattleInitiativeGlossary}priority{/g} panel on the left and select a ship to see what effects are currently on them. To learn more about an effect, press {console_bind|Confirm}.

345cfeb5-836e-4795-b2ea-61a8cde205fb.Text: To attack, first select the {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacksGlossary}single shot{/g} icon on the weapons panel using {console_bind|DPadHorizontal}. Target an enemy — a tooltip will appear showing your chances of {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hitting{/g} that enemy and the possible {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} you can deal on a successful hit. Press {console_bind|Confirm} when selecting the enemy to fire. The amount of damage your characters deal depends on the parameters of the weapon they are using. The effectiveness of the shot depends on the distance between the character and their enemy — when you target an enemy with a single shot, you will see two areas denoting the weapon's effective and maximum firing ranges.

05314da0-c034-4ef1-9583-200fc99ae22c.Text:
You have found an item that can only be equipped by characters of a certain {g|Encyclopedia:SoulmarkTypesGlossary}conviction{/g} rank. You can open the character menu to see which conviction your character follows.
Note that both your character and their companions have their own convictions. You can check what conviction a character adheres to on the biography tab in the character menu. To navigate to this menu, open quick access by holding {console_bind|RightBottom}, select the character icon, then release {console_bind|RightBottom}.
Convictions change in direction and rank based on how the game's story develops and during important plot decisions.

de5156aa-f14f-4b04-940d-55cc10faaf3e.Text: Each star system contains objects you can interact with. Such objects are marked as points of interest. Move your ship to a point of interest using {console_bind|LeftStick}, then press {console_bind|Confirm} to initiate the event or open the planet view. You can cancel your movement order using {console_bind|Decline}.

3881ca3c-72b7-4eb8-b0ae-f69fed4bf550.Text: Some interactive objects, such as doors or chests, are not always marked with icons. You can press {console_bind|FuncAdditional} to highlight such objects.

5259527e-32d3-4450-930d-655160686087.Text:
There is a trap up ahead! Order your character to disable it. If a character enters a trapped area or fails the {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} to disarm it, the trap will trigger, dealing {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} and inflicting {g|Encyclopedia:Injury}injuries{/g} on all characters within its {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area of effect{/g}.
Sometimes you will see a trap marked with a red area and a connecting dotted line. This line leads to the mechanism that controls the trap. Approach the mechanism — if it becomes highlighted, the trap can be disarmed by interacting with the mechanism. Press {console_bind|Confirm} to attempt the disarm test. If all characters are selected as a group using quick access {console_bind|RightBottom}, the character with the highest relevant {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} score will go to disarm the trap. If you have a character selected separately from the rest of the party, that character will try to disarm the trap on their own.
