bc307436-6a12-4dfe-bfde-09663f6695e2.Text: But though her heart ached for home, she could not leave her elantach. Rejected by her kin and deprived of a spirit stone and protection from the filthy claws of Slaanesh, the Aeldari withered away like a bird in a cage. Yrliet was to be found more often in meditation, trying to escape her suffocating reality. Each time her search for strength in the depths of her soul took longer and longer.

ada7d334-1d4c-41dc-94a4-991a1f47d601.Text: Yrliet Lanaevyss remained a prisoner of Commorragh, in soul and body, until the end of her days. Her re-education was put in the hands of the best Wyches, and her body was given over to the finest masters of flesh. Soon enough, the Child of Asuryan corrupted her own spirit stone, proving to her dark kin that she was one of them.

9456a3d0-058c-40e3-ba0a-6ea8efbf9c0e.Text: Hatred and disdain for her kin who had rejected her and taken away her home filled Yrliet Lanaevyss's soul with venom. For a time, she accompanied the Rogue Trader, but the Path of the Outcast only led to oblivion. Everything changed when a mysterious xenos in motley garb arrived uninvited on the von Valancius flagship and offered her an opportunity. A new role awaited her — but the chroniclers of the Imperium know nothing of it.

ac9d057e-bf03-497f-8c79-c30699e30397.Text: Marazhai Aezyrraesh died by the Rogue Trader's hand, but the mark he left on the Lord Captain's soul never disappeared. Poisoned by the venom that was injected into {mf|his|her} veins by {mf|his|her} skilled and sadistic lover, over the years {name} was consumed more and more by a haunting and insatiable thirst for heinous pleasures, heedless of the suffering of others.

772c0f7b-fa7a-47ad-b0cb-8a3a27d34193.Text: Though they had once been allies, Marazhai never mentioned his human patron from the von Valancius dynasty again. The forces that {name} now served were too terrifying and repulsive even for the unholy xenos.

285d12bf-ac79-45f8-82b8-19c941d5014f.Text: Resisting the temptations that besieged him, Calligos Winterscale returned to his domain and began to piece together the shattered remains of his protectorate. Until his dying day, his actions and thoughts were dedicated to saving abandoned worlds and protecting survivors. Alas, he was not able to achieve much in the time he was allotted. He breathed his last breath on the same throne that he refused to leave for decades, adamantly refusing augmetics that would restore mobility and power to his legs.

2ea35cae-75b2-4496-96ce-2465f4536c7b.Text: Some whispered of a special, dark, and wicked bond between the Rogue Trader and Marazhai... of xenos ships secretly docking with the von Valancius flagship, of bloody nights full of screaming victims and delirious laughter shared between maniacs, of macabre traces of the orgies the lovers left behind.

6e09b66f-bc32-451b-93aa-59fec3152cfe.Text: Though he left, Marazhai never could fully part with the Rogue Trader, as their unbreakable bond went beyond simple passions. The inhuman was seen many times in realspace at the side of the Lord Captain, who had forced the indomitable Marazhai to recognise {mf|him|her} as an equal. Bloody orgies aboard the dynasty's flagship spawned bloodcurdling legends. There were also whispers of mysterious attacks on von Valancius enemies by Aezyrraesh's subordinates.

4efa2d8a-df5b-40ee-9e64-1300feaf805b.Text: Marazhai Aezyrraesh, exile from Commorragh and murderer of his own Kabal, did not remain in the Rogue Trader's retinue for long. Broken by his many losses and unable to cope with the bitterness of his unfulfilled ambitions, the Drukhari found rapture in another role. People say he left the flagship of the von Valancius dynasty in the company of a mysterious and colourful xenos — the same one who took Yrliet Lanaevyss on the same day. The Imperium's chronicles know nothing of the fate of Marazhai. Only the Laughing God Cegorach knows that with the disappearance of the Asuryani and Drukhari, in the depths of the Webway two new Harlequin masques were born.

6ff0c236-7c86-4779-832d-b604575bc9e8.Text:
The Mercatum Tabula Officiale unlocked a sea of possibilities for Jae Heydari. She left the Kasballica Mission and became an independent agent. Choosing one's destiny is a unique gift that ordinary mortals would never dare dream of, but Jae was no ordinary mortal. She found new friends, skilfully danced along the knife's edge between trade and piracy, stole from the strong, granted mercy to the weak, and even bought a couple of modest planets — and she never, ever betrayed herself.
Half a century later, her life was tragically cut short — a weak and little-known Rogue Trader dynasty, led by a young and ambitious leader, ambushed and captured Jae Heydari in order to appropriate her wealth. The von Valancius fleet's strike was lightning-fast, but Mistress Heydari could not be saved — she died in the hands of her avaricious captors.

e3b90264-f1d8-4c92-8304-c908dc003ad0.Text: Enjoying the privileges of the Mercatum Tabula Officiale, Jae Heydari found her way into the heart of the Expanse's underworld. She became known as the Baroness of Shadows — having amassed so much wealth and influence, she came to control the economic fate of the sector. Even the most powerful figures in the Expanse were forced to reckon with her... reckon with and despise her. For a long time, Jae was able to thwart the attempts on her life, until one day she disappeared. But many continued to believe that she still rules the Expanse from shadows even deeper than before.

0d0a566d-9f47-43e6-86ed-27a7291f2c13.Text: The Harlequin known as Nocturne of Oblivion visited the Expanse once again. Sneaking onto Dargonus, he came to the Rogue Trader's palace and left {mf|him|her} a special gift: a case of Aeldari crafting, unmistakably ancient and precious, adorned with the rune of an eye inside a triangle. Only the Lord Captain knew what it contained. The Harlequin candidly warned {mf|him|her} that he was drawing the von Valancius dynasty into "a deadly dance, a shaking doom, that all will freeze within the threads of terror's loom." Then he promptly departed, and not without reason — a few hours later, assassins from the Dark City appeared, following his trail, and were mercilessly killed. Their armour bore the sign of the Kabal of the Black Heart.

1220344e-3683-4904-97d0-1f8fbf1353a0.Text: Jae Heydari basked in the Rogue Trader's light for many years, trying to make the most of such illustrious patronage. Alas, her appetites were insatiable, and two decades later, she brazenly attempted a coup. It was a failure, and she found herself on the executioner's block. Before the end, she bestowed one of her famous smiles on the thronging rabble in farewell.

9cb1b8e2-4a48-423d-8f35-dfab37ba9e02.Text: After accepting a position as the Rogue Trader's right hand, Jae Heydari received several worlds to oversee. But after several years of peace and prosperity, she once again began bending the law to see if it would break. Within a decade, her crimes had exceeded the limits of the Imperium's patience, and she became a wanted woman. For the rest of her life, she was forced to hide from those who wanted vengeance... and her head.

870f58e4-35a1-4dcf-a899-0865c08f9aed.Text: Though the chronicles mention one Vackemo, a boarder who served under an unknown Rogue Trader.

ab6f9ff5-1d41-421c-871c-86ef56ac74e7.Text: Jae Heydari died in the sewers of Footfall among the void rats, wretches, and thugs. Her body was found torn to pieces in a stinking canal next to the remains of her gang and the corpse of the Cold Trader Falco. An arm augmetic had been driven into his throat, its gilded fingers curled in an obscene gesture.

94e538a3-83cc-4690-9a41-d416ae977360.Text: In her journeys with the Rogue Trader, Cassia Orsellio experienced all the hardships and delights of the galaxy. The invaluable experience and new knowledge helped her to finally conquer her fears and accept herself and her powers. The Lady Navigator became Novator of her House, tasked with addressing the consequences of Tisiphone's rule and the chaos that followed her disappearance. For the duration of her reign, she patiently worked on uniting the feuding branches of the House, forging alliances and expanding the influence of House Orsellio.

c2425cc1-4286-4ff7-80d1-8812873d7e5c.Text: After bidding farewell to her elantach, Yrliet made her way to her surviving kin.

eee8d1f5-5ed0-47ea-afc0-2bb0ad8d1f71.Text: Many lost their lives, but those who survived the crisis became hardened veterans and pillars of the House. Most of those fortunate souls were young and brave, too few among them were old and wise.

4e77cf6e-e54e-4750-b45d-6d5fd19c2c17.Text: Yrliet followed a new Path, the Path of the Warrior. She only hoped she would never be forced to raise her weapon against the mortals who had become her true brothers and sisters in arms.

7da9fba9-7e63-4fac-8f66-973a12b76db5.Text: The elantach {mf|him|her}self put an end to this torment. Not willing to see Yrliet wither away in an alien world, {mf|he|she} persuaded the Aeldari to leave the Expanse. It seems that some things are just not meant to be, and a happy union between a mon-keigh and an Aeldari warrior is one of them.

d18de47a-8b8a-4a3f-8e9a-9f75d6b61c7b.Text: Cassia's heart was ground to dust by her lover's betrayal. Trembling in terror and avoiding the touch of the one she had once called her Lord Captain, she opened her Third Eye and disappeared in a horrendous manifestation of Empyrean might.

61822cf0-845d-43f8-aea2-7fece480d4f4.Text: A note was found on her body — the confession of a girl from the underhive, who by some miracle had managed to break free from her destiny, who had found fame, riches, and even a person she was bold enough to love. Yet, as fate would have it, her fame, thrones, and love turned out to be lies, just like her foolish hope of escaping her destiny, which doomed her to die alone in the dark without a crumb of food or a drop of water.

967c5d61-12fa-4311-8de0-c1ed2be3dda6.Text: In her final moments, she tried to break into the world of the one she called her elantach, to understand how a betrayal so vile could ripen in the heart of one so dear to her. The things she saw there were so heinous that the heart of valiant Yrliet stopped beating that very instant.

c6b8033f-3848-49f6-a6d8-f7eb2a8d14d6.Text: Their love was like a candle flame: warm, tremulous, insatiable, and... quickly extinguished. When Cassia took the throne as Novator, love gave way to duty. Some praised their doomed love over glasses of amasec, while others cursed it and spat in disgust. Yet, even after entering an arranged dynastic marriage and passing on her precious genes, Cassia kept in contact with the only person she had ever fully loved until her dying day.

b4393433-a038-43a0-a8a3-4fe53bc0d8dc.Text: Their love was delicate and selfless. The Lord Captain and the Lady Navigator wordlessly understood and accepted each other's feelings. Even after Cassia ascended the throne as Novator, she spurned all claims on her hand and heart, remaining loyal to her first and only love. As the years passed, mutations transformed her body, but the bond between the Lord Captain and the Lady Navigator endured and they continued to find solace and consolation in each other.

b55d2542-da3f-4493-96c2-ed4c8db65181.Text: Novator Cassia Orsellio and Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius were joined in matrimony, securing a powerful alliance. Sadly, their countless concerns and responsibilities prevented the spouses from seeing much of one other, keeping them apart for months and sometimes years at a time. Although no passion or love kindled in their union, they held one other in genuine esteem.

0318c87f-cb79-40c6-9101-a764fcaa5a5c.Text: Hieronymus Doloroso remained the most revered priest in the Cult of Saint Drusus. He turned no one away, hearing confessions from pirates, bilge rats, deserters, and beggars alike. It might have been one of those undeserving wretches who infected him with the rare form of leprosy that robbed him of his sight. Yet his heart could always see the corruption in the souls of his repenting children.

e3ff2095-3e6d-419c-a3c3-d608bb8eca2a.Text: Yet the conflict between the Imperium and the head of the von Valancius dynasty could not but affect the young order. Some sisters demanded that Argenta denounce her former commander.

852f14d7-e36b-4497-9f43-ebb3b04055ac.Text: Unable to choose between the order she had created and the person without whom she could not have completed her journey, she stepped down from her position and went into exile. Despite everything, love for her among the people of the Expanse only grew. Argenta would be the heroine of songs and tales for centuries to come, a radiant angel who would appear in the darkest hour to protect innocents from the forces of darkness.

06e11b86-69b4-4f98-8c98-2aac1ca3d25d.Text: Rumours said that Argenta was lured there under false pretences by her former allies. It may have even been {name} von Valancius {mf|him|her}self, unwilling to kill her off or tolerate her raging desire to cleanse the Expanse of heresy. No one knows the truth, but many gave a sigh of relief after her disappearance.

38453575-ebca-48fd-92da-55525aadf247.Text: Since then, there have been incessant pilgrimages in search of Salis Prime. Legend has it that the renowned Argenta wanders the ancient ship, awaiting the hero of purest heart to whom she will bestow the One Star, and mercilessly slaying those in whom she detects even a sliver of darkness. No one knows whether the legend is true, yet of the thousands who have tried to enter the ancient ship, not one has returned alive.

92c467f7-1078-42f5-90a3-da49823c4119.Text: Most of the miracles came down to technology refusing to obey xenos and heretics, turning against them and leading them to their demise. Several non-human or non-Imperium worlds were set back in their development, as their inhabitants saw any machine as a potential threat.

2dc7d4dc-01d1-4572-85fe-21ca0451014b.Text: Most of the miracles came down to machines coming to life to save someone from danger, damaged shuttles safely reaching the ground even without engines, or cogitators suddenly addressing their operators with words of encouragement and support, scaring them speechless.

e0fca6bb-4c25-46f6-8953-e83f1a6088be.Text: Such "miracles" were as bizarre as they were terrifying and often resulted in death and destruction.

726bc3b9-f2b9-4f9f-a6f1-6c0326b9e000.Text: There were many who wanted to find the source of these strange phenomena, yet Nomos were sufficiently cautious to avoid apprehension.

14a6e5f8-7407-49a6-8927-cfaf16d5cda0.Text: The truth of the fate of the Aeldari Yrliet Lanaevyss, whom the Rogue Trader handed over to the servants of the Ordo Xenos, was kept hidden from the uninitiated.

5df3b38e-ba25-4449-ac15-20ead565481e.Text: Idira did not remain a servant of the von Valancius dynasty for long. Her travels with the Lord Captain had changed her. She was as lively and talkative as ever, but she had also developed a tendency toward rumination. Idira was now sometimes seen in a place she had barely visited before — the ship's chapel — deep in thought or prayer. Curiously, the warp phenomena that haunted her became less and less frequent. Yet Idira did not seem reassured by this and ultimately decided to go into exile — a pilgrimage, she called it — to protect people from herself. Her trail disappeared somewhere in the Expanse, yet the memory of her lives on.

76ed09aa-6c34-4004-a7e9-ba00bc1235bd.Text: The sisters of the Order of the One Star, founded by Argenta, another companion of the Lord Captain, often mentioned Idira in their sermons as an example of a transgressor who found the light.

aa57f158-03fd-4e04-89f6-a90a5ea35157.Text: The Expanse is full of strange stories, yet one of the most bizarre tales emerged in the wake of Rogue Trader von Valancius's rise to prominence. According to the legend, on every world the Rogue Trader visited, people or objects would suddenly vanish without a trace if they found themselves in the same room as a mirror, even an utterly ordinary one.

172f4ef6-641d-407f-8ea6-1d4e42f7c872.Text: Uralon the Cruel was not an advisor to the Rogue Trader for long. During a session of vile worship with his {mf|master|mistress}, he was struck by a vision that was equally frightening and awe-inspiring. The terror instilled in the heart of the hardened heretic was so profound and incomprehensible that Uralon promptly embarked on a journey. The Eye of Terror itself was his goal. There he hoped to find someone who could interpret the vision that had overwhelmed him. No one could say if fate would ever lead him back to the Expanse, or if the Rogue Trader would accept him if it did.

c6d802f2-ca81-445d-85c4-4afc14e35683.Text: When enemies came down on the von Valancius protectorate from all sides, young Evayne was the only one to not take part in the savage assault, choosing instead to take in many refugees who had been stained by their service to the betrayer of Humanity.

e707e605-2c83-4045-ae98-25c69da9510f.Text: Noble preachers of the Creed performed acts of heroism to protect von Valancius servants from destruction at the hands of the vengeful attackers. Thousands of innocents were evacuated on pilgrim ships to new worlds to seek shelter in young colonies.

88785253-9605-4a81-acd2-6da4b7b29307.Text: When wrathful rivals attacked the von Valancius protectorate, the Explorators did not forget their bonds of alliance, choosing to save... the things they deemed worthy of salvation — extensive libraries, sacred mechanisms, and manufacturing complexes.

7f311815-1f57-4d69-a364-4adfbc55bd2f.Text: The news from the Expanse was met with deep concern in the Imperium. Some began speaking of a punitive campaign, though they quickly fell silent. A lone ship broke through the Great Rift, carrying a letter to Dargonus bearing the Inquisition's seal. But what the letter contained, and who penned it... is better left unknown.

0a4d1eee-cd91-4a9e-9628-2125ae524397.Text: After fleeing the retinue of the corrupted Rogue Trader, Yrliet Lanaevyss disappeared without a trace. However, soon after, high-standing nobles on von Valancius planets who displayed their loyalty to the Ruinous Powers too openly started dying. Each was slain by a single clean shot, and the assassin was never found.

2cad2e93-8ea3-4934-9ec8-78cbc4fc40a6.Text: Across many systems, power was seized by heresiarchs and pirate leaders. When they failed to find a common enemy, they turned their weapons on each other, and the Expanse sank into even darker depths of bloody anarchy.

57535631-4d52-4ce0-8a46-9aa0ef9898ac.Text: Returning with his magnificent trophy, Xavier Calcazar solemnly handed the regalia of the Warden of the Expanse to the Rogue Trader. He did not call off the martial law he had declared at the start of the crisis — the Lord Inquisitor had had enough of the disorder that reigned in the Expanse and wanted to make sure that power remained firmly in one trusted pair of hands. As for himself, he wanted to embark as soon as possible on a search for the next C'tan Shard, but fate did not allow him to continue this grand quest.

0d22ae72-d5e8-4949-953b-e39d8a191f04.Text: Vladaym Tocara, former crime lord and smuggler, managed surprisingly well in the role of janitor. Climbing the hierarchical ladder, he eventually obtained a pardon and became an administrator of high standing on Dargonus. His business acumen, shrewdness, and willingness to get his hands dirty brought success to his operations, but he was unable to enjoy the fruits of his labour — until the end of his days, he resided in modest quarters and avoided any luxury, afraid of being accused of corruption and, in his own words, "thrown for a loop."

5e184e8a-3392-4d13-90ab-038a5d0526f5.Text: In Epitaph's orbit, the von Valancius flagship took a last stand against the creature that had once been its Lord Captain. The crew met grizzly ends to the last man at the frigid hands of the former Rogue Trader when {mf|he|she} broke onto the bridge from the cold void.

26805f72-634e-4db5-ae8e-663a5acefcb5.Text: Idira showed her treacherous nature and almost brought about the demise of the Rogue Trader's ship.

069eca52-f8fd-4cc1-be79-6d33de756280.Text: Among honest servants of the Imperium, the case would become one of the Expanse's most common cautionary tales about the danger of unsanctioned psykers.

05f1b75d-5da0-4c63-9c61-5d2bdbf17505.Text: Heinrix van Calox, former Interrogator of the Ordo Xenos, left the path ordained for him and denounced the Holy Inquisition in order to remain with his beloved. Chroniclers to this day cannot agree on the reason for his betrayal: was it a flaw in his character? Some hidden taint that poisoned the soul of a once faithful subject of the Imperium? Or was it a sentiment so profound that the God-Emperor's numb servants could never comprehend it?

5450a5e3-51b0-49f2-9561-e7a4a445bade.Text: Novator Cassia shut herself in her chambers for many days. When she emerged, she wielded the most fearsome weapon House Orsellio had ever seen. She had transformed the Starway Atlas itself into an instrument of destruction. With it, she was able to exterminate the various xenos encroaching on her House. After celebrating her victory, to everyone's astonishment she suddenly decided to continue the research that Novator Tisiphone had started, though it was no secret that she had held it in great contempt in the past. The Novator knew that the Starway Atlas was slowly becoming twisted, that the xenos would doubtless return, and that she had a duty to protect her House.

13803b13-6917-4208-b765-f86c17f36378.Text: Tired, afraid, and angered by their own weakness without the Atlases, the Navigators rose up against the Novator.

7b582c75-8545-4984-bc12-3e854075abab.Text: Heinrix van Calox, traitor to the Imperium and breaker of the sacred oaths of the Inquisition, did not survive his last journey with the betrayer of Humanity for whom he had renounced his duty. {name} von Valancius, now vassal to an ancient horror, took his life. She destroyed her former lover not for trying to kill her but for appealing to her mind and heart.

a4ec3e9e-06a5-48f1-afe3-c3a8a050eab7.Text: Idira Tlass, who was never able to subdue the whispers in her head, fell back on her old crutches of prohibited stimulants and amasec. People often saw her talking to an imaginary "Theodora" or deliriously muttering to herself in a dark corner. One day she was found with a hole in her head, sitting at the desk where Theodora von Valancius had died. She held an autopistol in one hand and in the other an open bottle of Flame of Purity wine — Lady Theodora's libation of choice.

4928fa5c-a027-4ff3-9ed5-57421ea6a98a.Text: By a twist of fate, when the Rogue Trader joined the Koronus Conclave, Heinrix van Calox became the Lord Captain's commanding officer. He gleefully took advantage of every opportunity to chastise and order the Rogue Trader around.

aefb634a-ecaf-4409-8d1e-2b5049cfb0a9.Text: The Lord Inquisitor found a most loyal ally in Incendia Chorda. She gladly became a lethal instrument of retribution in van Calox's hands, knowing no rest.

45bdf238-ccbf-4cc0-9087-0be679af323b.Text: Novator Cassia mustered all the might of her House and set off for distant stars. Ensnared by Cassia's Starway Atlas, not a single Navigator could ignore the call to battle. The Novator launched a retaliatory strike on mysterious assassins — xenos in motley garb. Disaster struck during the victorious campaign's triumphal celebration — the Novator lost her mind. In a fit of madness, she destroyed the Starway Atlas and disappeared in a hideous manifestation of the Immaterium. Most of her subjects died that very day, connected to the Atlas by their spiritual bonds. The Orsellio name fell into oblivion along with them.

e9ce9386-b575-4bb9-87f3-5dafdb232642.Text: Lacking an iron will and an aptitude for command, Novator Cassia was not able to build a sufficient bulwark around her rule, and disgruntled members of House Orsellio decided to rebel. They set out to depose Lady Cassia and install a worthy protector on the throne instead. Their plan only half worked — to avenge Cassia's death, the Rogue Trader brutally crushed everyone who bore the Orsellio name.

dbcccf94-5552-4096-a583-d665a59dda45.Text: Years later, House Orsellio was racked by a wave of brutal murders. Unknown assailants butchered Navigators, gouging the Atlases from their chests.

146b95b9-4f58-4bc9-ab4b-2cfb2f804a7d.Text: After the battle on Epitaph, Argenta was firmly set on the path of a Sister Repentia. Her former fervour and zeal gave way to grim, cold resignation. She longed for death, yet death seemed to flee before the former companion of the Lord Captain... Or, perhaps, she just could not find a worthy opponent. So things carried on, until one day, while fighting heretics on an uncharted world, Argenta threw herself into a massive inferno to strike down a horrendous warp spawn. Her comrades saw only shadows in the fire and heard the beast's dying bellow. The flames burned for several days. When they finally subsided, Argenta's body was found among the charred rubble, lifeless but untouched by the fire. In one hand she held her chainsword, in the other — a shard of the golden Aquila she had always kept close ever since arriving in the Expanse.

0372502b-07f5-4711-8310-c33c6ad98dad.Text: The Starway Atlas, which contained the memories of Tisiphone and the Setthala clan, lost its power. House Orsellio's Navigators once again had to rely on skill alone in the depths of the Immaterium.

2e51dc78-2dc4-4066-81d8-1829b5d78ead.Text: Despite scandalous rumours about a love affair with the Rogue Trader, Lady Navigator Cassia continued to accompany her lover among the stars of the Expanse for a time.

ffd072ff-3648-47e5-8668-b32c110a9d7c.Text: Cassia crushed the rebellion with an iron fist. She desperately tried to bring her House back from ruin and recreate the Atlas that had been so unwisely destroyed, but fate was not on her side. She eventually left the post of Novator and passed the unwanted title to a young heir.

e88c9e2e-477e-4247-9c9e-60ef138bbaa7.Text: The Lord Inquisitor delved deeper and deeper into dangerous and obscure fields of study. Having succeeded in shackling one ancient beast, he now wanted to repeat his success. The Imperium would never be safe while its enemies yet lived.

6cf9da1c-7213-4f42-8a8c-a16700a713be.Text: House Orsellio did not dare oppose the Rogue Trader and became embroiled in a bloody internecine war for power. Its members and genetic bounty were wiped out in the fighting, the House collapsed, and it was eventually assimilated into other more influential Navigator Houses. Lady Cassia did not make any attempts to save her House from oblivion.

13bdedc2-d339-41e8-aab9-9194942ca790.Text: House Orsellio did not dare oppose the Rogue Trader, and its struggle to determine a new Novator did not last long. It soon fell victim to a series of bloody assassinations. Some said the perpetrators were mysterious xenos in motley garb who brutally slaughtered their victims, gouging the Atlases from their chests. The fall of House Orsellio was quick, bloody, and mysterious. Lady Cassia did not intervene to stop the massacre.

84d1bccc-2213-4696-be19-b265f2ae7459.Text: The entire Expanse knew of the bond between Jae and the Rogue Trader. The smuggler accompanied her Lord Captain on many dangerous adventures, and their passion for each other burned as fiercely as on the first day they met. Yet as soon as a journey ended, Jae would disappear, sometimes without any notice. No matter how much she enjoyed the Rogue Trader's company, the accomplished smuggler never allowed their relationship to turn into something more. The only master Jae Heydari would ever need was Jae Heydari.

8d8cb484-9f2a-459b-88dc-5d9e1fd47f96.Text: Once known for her passionate nature, after meeting the Lord Captain Jae firmly refused to share her favour with all others who sought it. After the many adversities they had braved together, her heart belonged to the Rogue Trader. Decades later, a glorious ship was built on Kiava Gamma, which became the new flagship of House von Valancius. The proud vessel was named the Lady Jae.

149b9b2f-20e1-46a9-80f1-6df46e293acb.Text: The person known as Mercy never forgot the humiliation he suffered at the hands of Jae Heydari. Everyone she ever showed affection for would mysteriously die in some tragic way, and the sorrow of never-ending loss poisoned her heart. Only one person escaped this fate, and {mf|his|her} name was {name} von Valancius.

463b6c06-3b3a-45c2-afb0-043c54e6b9b0.Text: Even the momentous events on Epitaph could not silence the call in Argenta's soul for the mysterious relic she so eagerly sought. The Sister of Battle left the Rogue Trader's retinue and embarked on a solitary pilgrimage in search of Salis Prime. Her fate after that is unknown.

e0715a30-d301-4f7f-89eb-7906aa0307f1.Text: The xenos Marazhai Aezyrraesh vanished without a trace after his powerful patron betrayed the unholy alien into the hands of the Holy Inquisition.

0d7b251e-d131-4ed5-82e5-fbd7db6ca6e0.Text: The retribution that Nocturne of Oblivion promised the Rogue Trader arrived when relentless Aeldari avengers swept down on the von Valancius protectorate. In their wake, several Harlequin Troupes performed the monstrous and mesmerisingly bloody Melody of Coals Fading in the Night that bathed Janus in the sorrow and fury of the playwright in a horned mask.

e0d88873-1034-4cb8-9742-2e31410aca11.Text: For many years, old Ryzza presided over the captains of the Fellowship. At the end of her life, she once again took the helm of a ship and led an unprecedented attack on the mother squadron of the Cognisance Fleet, during which the attackers managed to seize a dozen transport ships loaded with the Omnissiah's sacred gifts.

723822c7-0d16-42bc-b8c4-c775a9312ea1.Text: Inquisitor Heinrix van Calox continued to serve the Imperium and vanished under mysterious circumstances several years later. After receiving a signal encrypted with Inquisition codes, he travelled to an unknown distant world from which he never returned.

12560900-d614-4ec1-a1cb-2b486515306a.Text: The esteemed Ulfar left the Rogue Trader's retinue and set out alone in search of his glorious pack. The Stormbiters tried to locate the defiant Wolf, but to no avail. He was forever lost in the darkness of the Expanse.

ff84cc62-471d-478c-936c-d5914e26fd2d.Text: When the Rogue Trader's apostasy became apparent, the Imperial Navy fulfilled its duty and fought the von Valancius dynasty. The Battle of Dargonus ended in resounding defeat, and the surviving ships fled to distant systems. Disheartened but not broken, the captains vowed to rebuild their force and planned raids into the apostate territory.

41065cd6-c9e2-4b37-843d-e289881a6334.Text: However, the hunters were often struck by a peculiar blindness. After all, there were many former friends and business partners among the people they were sent to pursue.

6e4a5482-b72d-4ec1-ba17-48ebe61ebf6c.Text: The crucial reason for the defeat was the extraordinarily high percentage of captains who betrayed their oaths and defected to the Rogue Trader's side. Overnight, {mf|he|she} acquired a battle-ready fleet of {mf|his|her} own.

6b4d9cb5-84fe-4325-87e8-bab98439ad8c.Text: Chartist Captain Austerius Thorfast founded the Thorfast and Companions Merchant Company, excelling in trade and acquiring a substantial escort fleet. After three decades, he travelled to the Maw to return to the Imperium in hopes of obtaining the fabled Warrant of Trade. It is not known how this venture ended.

bea704b6-fd7f-4c3e-b8c3-3a699ea626a8.Text: Dargonus was subjected to horrific pillaging, millions were put to death, and blood ran through the streets. After the von Valancius treasures were stolen, the abode of the traitor to Humanity was bombed with cyclonic torpedoes from orbit. The once glorious world was lost.

b5ddf146-f605-4895-9c1c-e172cb023718.Text: After Ryzza's death, her place was taken by a quiet man who simply called himself a Useful Acquaintance and was prone to coining his own nonsensical words. Few guessed that this scrawny fellow had been Ryzza's first mate, who possessed an iron will and a truly monstrous nature. On his quiet orders, the pirates conducted brazen and violent raids.

9ff77931-e995-4fbf-91c4-5803160c011c.Text: Kiava Gamma prepared to fight back, but the battle was brief. The servants of the Adeptus Mechanicus conspired with their fellow adepts in the avenging fleet, stabbing the planet's garrison in the back. The world was captured quickly, and the unharmed sacred workshops were turned over to the disciples of the Omnissiah.

91e65c7d-d386-4f95-96ff-ce4b7b3500b9.Text: After the obliteration of Dargonus, the surviving forces of the renegade Rogue Trader gathered on Janus. Here the second major battle was fought, and the backbone of the treasonous dynasty was broken. In a three-day battle, the tank tracks drove the abomination banners into the mud and the heretics were burned along with the crops, their weapons drowned in the irrigation canals. Fertilised with the ashes of the apostates, the fields yielded a bountiful harvest for many seasons to come.

7a9a6ad1-f299-4d87-9098-277f1dc1d9b5.Text: An ungodly massacre took place on Foulstone in the last days of the von Valancius protectorate. Millions of pilgrims blindly rejected the news of the Rogue Trader's apostasy and tried to fight back against the forces loyal to the Imperium, until holy statues crumbled under the volleys of macro-cannons and innumerable pious souls perished with the betrayer's name on their lips.

12798161-3c95-494d-b0fd-ef1dfa9293e9.Text: Vheabos VI was swiftly overrun by the avenging force. Its mines became the final place of exile for the servants of the disgraced Rogue Trader.

b92e6ec7-dcc7-4823-8c01-7c2dfc6ea8b0.Text: Humanity was exploring the Expanse, and Dargonus became the capital for the brave starfarers and pioneers. It was from here that expeditions departed into the uncharted wilderness and here they returned bearing wondrous trophies. Captains, cartographers, and scribes flocked here to exchange news.

1eb81172-3a6f-4207-92ad-7a6327b67095.Text: The voracious and shameless nobility of the Expanse flocked to Dargonus in search of the forbidden pleasures. Its librariums harboured dangerous volumes and its dark corners harboured dangerous people. The rule of law could not reach the tops of the spires, shrouded in a veil of sinister and mystical rumours.

2b7cd6db-53ea-488c-9a2c-358f25ec746e.Text: Dargonus became the bastion of order in the Expanse. From here, punitive expeditions were dispatched to tainted worlds, and entire spires were occupied by officials and bureaucrats of the Imperium. On many planets, the expression "a man from Dargonus" soon came to mean a fearsome inspector with the power to impose punishment.

3d6b3e2d-6d93-4376-84fd-ed8118f5737a.Text: The mines of Vheabos VI grew deeper and deeper, and soon the planet became the darkest and most frightening colony of the Expanse, the final stop for the exiled and the damned. The brutal, hardened inhabitants of the death world feared neither humans nor xenohorrors, knew no mercy, and were known as the most fearsome fighters in the sector, who had traded their lives for the right to leave the eternal darkness of the mines.

f33519b4-39de-4164-a70f-7324e3bcfd4b.Text: Over time, Vheabos VI became the largest pirate den in the Expanse. From here the void skulkers set out on their raids, and this was where they stored their loot and licked their wounds, knowing that not even the Imperial Navy would risk setting foot on the formidable Vheabos.

0fd70899-0e54-4b84-91ab-e5d15480ab39.Text: The harsh Vheabos VI became a land of trials capable of testing one's righteousness. The repentant and the zealous alike flocked there to be purified and toughened by its poisonous atmosphere. In the ominous halls of the Fortress of Penance, the Grim Guard was established, an order of crusaders who guarded the purity of the Expanse, renowned for their tenacity and feared for their unyielding fanaticism.

43f4965c-25f6-4293-9e14-7d682482f2d5.Text: The Kasballica Mission thrived on the riches it acquired in its deals with the Rogue Trader. The organisation expanded to new markets, built up a mercenary army and fleet, and was ready to defend the legitimacy of its business from the authorities. Those foolish enough to deny it that right died quick, brutal, and unexplained deaths.

6ca5ba05-0869-4d3a-91f6-7171de8bd5ab.Text: The enthroned Null Caliph drew millions of pilgrims and granted the planet hallowed status. Its sacred calculation continued for centuries, and the foremost sages of the Adeptus Mechanicus travelled to the world so they could attempt to divine its meaning.

cc99b352-1a81-4e0e-93ff-279796d85298.Text: The subjugation of Null Caliph left the Adeptus Mechanicus in awe. Kneeling before the chained demigod, they lost their resolve and no longer interfered in the governance of the colony. With ever increasing boldness, the Rogue Trader's viceroys gained access to sacraments inaccessible to the laity and handed them over to their {mf|master|mistress}.

fbfe32ed-60f2-4726-b624-83be09398270.Text: The parasitic demigod was no more. Freed from the tyranny of Null Caliph, Kiava Gamma surged with new life. Spires grew, manufactorums multiplied, and greedy transports jostled at the docks. Only occasionally, a mysterious data-ghost manifested in the noosphere of the sacred workshops and proclaimed with dismay: "Error! Calculation interrupted!" But no one knew what calamity it was trying to prevent.

b5123680-58b8-41d1-918c-bf397d36c27d.Text: Treasures and influence quickly corrupted the supreme hierarchs of Foulstone, turning them into a coterie of venal egotists anointed by greed. As they did dirty deeds under the cover of holy vestments, their power steadily grew. It is hardly surprising that a few years later the hierarchs of Foulstone recognised the blood relationship between their patrons the von Valancius dynasty and Saint Cognatius himself.

12b08599-53f0-415e-85ce-059f198121fc.Text: Converted into a comet shrine, Foulstone's moon spread the word of Saint Cognatius throughout the Expanse. Protecting worlds from attacks by the enemies of Humanity, its servants asked for neither money nor power, but only the relics left by their blessed patron. The wise handed them over with reverence, while the haughty learned how heavy the Hammer of Foulstone was.

3dce316b-7ccf-40da-907a-fec54ea47dfb.Text: The Order of the Hammer grew in power and prominence thanks to the Rogue Trader's patronage. So widespread was the reverence for Cognatius that he supplanted Drusus the Warrior on his pedestal as the most honoured saint in the Expanse. The Drusian cult did not forgive this, and feuds broke out between the clergies, but the warlike servants of the Hammer were not afraid of bloodshed.

96531ce2-1638-47db-8f53-de308333f50c.Text: The fate of the Pure-Voiced Prophet, guardian of the hallowed Crucible, was a sad one. After visiting seven worlds and bestowing the blessing of transformation upon them, he perished at the hands of bloodthirsty Drukhari pirates along with his retinue and the priceless relic.

165b0482-6c71-4026-8468-42cfd9528ae1.Text: Bleeding from hundreds of wounds, Master Helmsman Ravor led the ship to ram the ominous tomb. A crushing blow split the sinister xenos edifice, but even that was not enough to defeat the C'tan.

92e0c5f0-8107-47ce-88bc-545d277dbd06.Text: High Factotum Janris Danrok fell, shielding the Vox Master from devastating blows with his corpulent body. Honed by many years of calculations, his mind correctly predicted there was no hope of victory or salvation, and so spreading the news of the terrible disaster to others was the only thing that mattered.

9e4b903a-3af5-49bd-b671-86f4cfcc496c.Text: Vigdis Surri Otta of the Toliman line was on every vox-frequency carrying the news of the heinous treason that had been committed. Her voice did not tremble with horror when she uttered the terrible words, "Rogue Trader von Valancius has betrayed Humanity." Then she fell silent.

92cbc955-12cf-4da6-a94b-fcc55f4195b0.Text: The mysterious entity named Nomos left the von Valancius ship but not the Expanse. Rumours about machines behaving strangely and worryingly potent tech-miracles emerged every year on dozens of worlds.

f1c72f04-22b2-438d-a7ef-fcb723726695.Text: Janus became a melting pot for cultures from hundreds of worlds, taking in refugees from across the entire Expanse in its darkest hour. It became a stronghold and a symbol of hope. After the crisis passed, the refugees started to return to their home planets and to reclaim the lost worlds, thus earning Janus the proud name — the Home of the Reconquista.

cd7d1b69-950d-4453-891a-15d9aed72e53.Text: The dark rule of the seekers of the forbidden was established on Janus. While terrified serfs toiled in the fields, in the lofty castles, wise renegades studied the knowledge of the xenos, learned their filthy language, and embraced their culture. The mists born of irrigation devices hid the evil work from the righteous.

46a39447-8d57-416a-8860-69a1e3e8e3f6.Text: Despite grim expectations, the coexistence of humans and the Aeldari did not lead to enmity. Janus had faced many trials, and the struggle against them brought the two peoples together. They did not develop an affection for one another, but they learned to speak with no weapons in their hands. More than one dangerous xenophile schism was born on Janus.

9d812830-a170-4a37-bb52-91feeaeecaf2.Text: The ruthlessness with which Cassia persecuted dissent did not go unnoticed. Jae Heydari met with her former companion twice and appealed to her mercy. Their second meeting ended in a deadly quarrel, and it was soon discovered that Kasballica Mission ships were helping the Orsellio dissidents to escape reprisal. Cassia publicly swore revenge on Lady Heydari for betraying her former friendship.

7de1b808-fc36-4303-827b-14d5ad331374.Text: Blessed Sister Argenta spent many cycles looking for Ulfar to try to save him from his despair. When she caught up with him on a bloody path littered with bodies of enemies of Humanity, she begged Ulfar to become a paladin of the Order of the One Star, promising hope and companionship. But the Lone Wolf did not heed the words of the good sister.

27a07905-d67d-4036-b6ac-300818530c72.Text: Marazhai and Yrliet's fleets often hunted together. Their kin wondered how the two captains were getting along. The Outcast and the former Dracon bonded over the horrors they had both experienced — the incursions in the Immaterium during their journeys with the Rogue Trader had left a grim mark on their souls.

63a18cc3-815b-4454-8c9e-3271e38271dd.Text: Interrogation revealed that the most likely instigator was the esteemed Seneschal Werserian, outraged by the execution of several crew members. However, Abelard denied his involvement even when questioned by the Rogue Trader.

eb73c8e7-3322-4139-9d72-601e0c23211d.Text: Abelard found himself at her side that day. He could have walked away, but he stayed by Idira's side until the last second, trying to keep her mind from collapsing. His body was never found after the incident.

8a8d9e8d-fda0-46e9-baee-f8d17f3612c0.Text: It is rumoured that the true cause of Thorbald Ironhide's demise was treachery. Faced with a superior enemy, the Space Wolves called on their allies for help, but a nearby squadron of the Cognisance Fleet withdrew, defiantly broadcasting that "The blood debt to Archmagos Amarnat is not forgotten."

cde7740a-02fb-412b-8ab2-9221bd2dad53.Text: The austere House Sauerback found protection in the Cult of Saint Drusus. Donating their riches to those in need, they became grim and fierce champions of faith, leading the rabble in the fight against evil.

502fcf82-b0ec-4e2a-95ed-3e56f682e566.Text: Rumour has it that Yrliet and Pasqal met again among the alien stars. A band of Aeldari warriors were trying to protect an ancient planetary edifice of their people from the covetous servants of the Omnissiah. Upon learning that Yrliet was leading the xenos, Pasqal personally descended to the planet and struck down his former comrade-in-arms. Her death did not stir any feelings in his metallic heart.

d2d6efa2-d2b2-4e36-9fa2-0438fc02a789.Text: Years later, Marazhai's name resounded through the Expanse once more. His gang had intercepted Astartia Werserian's ship. Her head was delivered to Abelard with a note informing him that it was "a gift from an old acquaintance in remembrance of a glorious past." Abelard's grief sent him on a six-year-long hunt for the despicable xenos, which, sadly, was unsuccessful.

99836212-297f-4384-9d7b-125ce181cff8.Text: It is said that the xenos Marazhai travelled to these dark sectors to hunt down and exterminate the beast more than once, but each time he limped back in a sorry state. He was proud of his experience, however, and believed that one day he would succeed.

b86eab75-16cc-4194-a5b3-e8b28b0765fa.Text: The Order of the One Star joined the rebellion against the Inquisitor turned apostate. It is said that it was the hand of Prelate Argenta that ended the life of a despicable traitor, though she was greatly saddened by the deed.

9ef2915b-debe-45e5-bfb1-feb8976eef54.Text: Only in the brief moments of Cassia Orsellio's visits did the old Idira resurface from under the impassive mask. Cassia's Navigator's powers enabled her to fill her old friend's mind with emotions, but they always faded soon after the Navigator's departure.

17e389e0-b312-4b15-963d-9afcf2b68b00.Text: Shortly before her death, Idira vanished from her post. Jae disappeared with her. When Jae returned many cycles later, she declared that Idira's last days had been full of joy and adventure, and that her greatest pleasure had been watching the void whales play.

1fbdde23-e6f3-4d0b-940c-72b215d6d0ba.Text: Decades later, Tech-Interrogator Brasswhisper confronted a cartel of Cold Traders who had defiled the Adeptus Mechanicus regalia and executed a powerful criminal named Torra. This act plunged Jae Heydari into grief and rage. In retaliation, she arranged the assassination of Magos Abel Haneumann, a pure-hearted and harmless servant of the Omnissiah.

ac98e7ad-455c-4cf2-ba4c-0ea72a1702c1.Text: The circumstances of Xavier Calcazar's death are not known. It is rumoured that the Lord Inquisitor was slain in a duel by an Angel of the Emperor, who shouted the names of his brothers in the Inquisitor's face and then stamped on his head with a sabaton.

c6715287-9160-4f2c-9997-01b37758d45a.Text: Seeing a true champion of the Dark Gods in the Rogue Trader, the Word Bearers established themselves in the von Valancius demesne. Thousands of scribes scratched away on data-slates, slowly losing their minds as they recorded the words of unholy teachings, and thousands of voxes broadcast the Word Bearers' hideous sermons across the Expanse.

0baa9033-4b53-4813-9fd9-27f8c914f0cc.Text: When the Lady Navigator's service came to an end, Cassia left the Rogue Trader and returned to House Orsellio's embrace. It was rumoured that a new Novator would soon take the throne and the House would be reborn after years of silence. Alas, the inauguration did not come to pass, as the discord within the House flared up and turned into a fratricidal war. Lady Cassia died at its outset, taking the lives of many loyalists and renegades with her. The other Navigator Houses made efforts to scatter the remains of the once great House Orsellio and to absorb what little was left of it.

d5665d38-e42f-4417-9a7c-16f516dde4b8.Text: But before the great slaughter could make the planet's irrigation canals run red with blood, the Farseer Muaran emerged from the forests to address the avengers. Having convinced his kin to stay their hand, he and his people departed Janus.

aa3e089f-2d30-4b59-acc1-31569904d390.Text: However, the participants of the cannibalistic feasting soon came to regret their rapacity. After rallying around Marazhai Aezyrraesh, the surviving warriors of the Reaving Tempest delivered a surprise counter-attack. Many of the plundering Kabals lost so many fighters that they in turn became tempting prey for vultures. By throwing this bloody carrion to the scavengers, the Reaving Tempest seized its chance to survive and return to its former strength.

7e874ba0-fc13-427d-ba3b-c6dde1a8a24b.Text: The alliance between the von Valancius dynasty and the Kabal of the Black Heart, forged over the cooling corpse of Marazhai Aezyrraesh, was short-lived and the fruits of the union poisoned. By setting nefarious xenos against {mf|his|her} enemies, the Rogue Trader also left {mf|himself|herself} vulnerable to daggers in the back. More than once or twice, the Drukhari made attempts to secretly eliminate the Lord Captain and seize control of the dynasty. Abandoning hope of a lasting alliance, the Rogue Trader answered the inhumans' deviousness with {mf|his|her} own, treacherously slaying many Kabalite warriors and claiming the richest trophies.

60f36ad6-4d23-4806-b153-e9aa638f65af.Text: In the same year that Jae Heydari ceased appearing in public, a magnificent and heavily fortified mansion, popularly known as the Tower of Sunset, was built on Dargonus. No one knows to whom the Rogue Trader granted this palace, but {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} visited the mansion with surprising frequency.

cad1f807-7eb8-491a-951b-13a535ab97d6.Text: Jocasta Sauerback was stunned by her Lord Captain's treason. However, her own oath of loyalty forbade her from turning her weapons against the one she served. Therefore, the Master-at-Arms resigned from her position and summoned two of her trusted, armed bodyguards. The loyal servants carried out Jocasta's last orders and helped her solve her conundrum with no loss of honour.

9d77cf58-3c40-4d3b-acd0-8713b8bcdbe8.Text: The hour of the Rogue Trader's treason found Zacchary Weisz in his chapel. He had been listening to the warp for many days, trying to discern an elusive voice speaking from the Immaterium. He felt an odd certainty that he had to hear and decipher that message. The moment the alarm was raised on the flagship, he heard it at last. It was his own voice shouting about the Lord Captain's betrayal. The Empyrean's insidious currents had seized his yet-to-be-spoken words and carried them into the past. Realising that he was hopelessly late, Weisz shouted into the warp as loudly as he could. He prayed that this time he would succeed in warning his past self.

3b05170e-b3ad-4fa1-a080-fd0f9578f66f.Text: Jocasta Sauerback carried on in her service as Master-at-Arms, maintaining order on the decks with maul and noose. Over the years, she took several husbands, and her descendants came to be named Sauerbacks of the Void: a lesser offshoot of the eminent aristocratic clan from the capital world.

0f3bdcd9-3e80-4673-9ac2-35c38c0950da.Text: The foulness that festered in the depths of Kiava Gamma was patient. Its tentacles crept into workshop after workshop, capturing Magos after Magos. The words of binharic mantras were distorted and the algorithmic catechism was compromised. Beneath the shell of iron, a vile worm gnawed at the world's heart.

a7ede6d7-c219-4761-9174-41e01c8e2c5c.Text: Jocasta Sauerback served as Master-at-Arms for years, but eventually her zeal faded. It appeared that, having tried every form of violence in existence, she no longer derived out of any of them the joy it had once held. Jocasta humbly submitted her resignation and went back to her home on the capital world.

4cc60c4b-b04c-4791-bd61-fc43f3a47ecd.Text: Jocasta Sauerback served as the Rogue Trader's Master-at-Arms for many years. At the head of a horde of frenzied enforcers, she landed on worlds and boarded stations to replenish the ship's crew with new captives. If any dared resist, she would beat them to death with her merciless maul. Those who submitted to her were never seen again. Each landing and boarding added scars to her stern face, until it disappeared completely behind a riot of old wounds with only a pair of eyes on it, ablaze with hatred. She earned the fearsome sobriquet: the Lady of Scars.

a0195e84-37d4-4819-b5e1-873c0111d9dc.Text: Zacchary Weisz, Choirmaster of the Astropaths, turned his shame and repentance into an iron chain binding his soul. Cold and detached, he would never again take a personal apprentice or become close with a subordinate. He dedicated himself to impeccable service, unfailingly carrying out the Lord Captain's orders and surviving at least seven incidents that wiped out the entire Astropathic Choir.

095e4c8a-ca09-4ab4-9f5a-59203c31ef40.Text: After many years, Zacchary Weisz mustered the courage to take personal apprentices again. He searched throughout the Expanse for Astropaths whose masters were harsh and cruel to them, and recruited them into his Choir. He gathered a cast of talented men and women by his side, and was their guardian and mentor. Weisz died defending his wards from cursed words spewed by the Immaterium. Sealing the sound of those words in his mind, he preferred a horrible death to a repetition of his shameful past mistakes.

c1e9033a-ec6e-410e-a744-8abef0331772.Text: As years passed, Zacchary Weisz's obsession and his dark proclivities grew ever more apparent. His Choir was replenished with captive Astropaths from worlds and ships ransacked by the Rogue Trader. A ghostly gathering of souls taken by the warp would surround him as he sat behind an organ of living flesh and played upon it a symphony of despair, the Immaterium his only audience.

3ed56b78-a860-4e4e-88ab-de461e7aaa79.Text: A handful of prisoners— all that remained of the Congregation of the Ravenous Star — were left on a minor planet with few supplies. The survivors included only children and old men and women whose appearance had the fewest distortions. Not one of the true monsters had been spared... Or so it seemed. The genetic aberration had all but faded away in the blood of the survivors, only to reveal itself again in their offspring. Soon, purple chitin-covered children were born under the greedy light of alien stars, and went on to carry the truth of the Many-Armed Emperor on the tips of their sting-like tongues.

7c6434eb-dafa-4e28-aeb5-3bbf443ebed6.Text: A loyal servant of the Undying Emperor, Kibellah did not forgive the Rogue Trader for {mf|his|her} betrayal of Humanity. They met in battle, and Kibellah's steady hand dealt an inescapable mortal blow... Only for her to realise that she had been mistaken. The Undying One was not death itself. {name} von Valancius was.

82cc5715-2b72-458a-b6a6-49a83de4e04c.Text: However, none in the Expanse were the wiser as to the true and greater horror of her fate. Devastated by the treachery of the one she loved, Kibellah's suffering was so ruinous that reality itself gave way under her feet. Ever since then, a rumour spread through the Expanse of a terrifying creature of the warp that took the shape of a maiden in scarlet and manifested itself to diviners and fortune-tellers. It commanded them to tell it the fate of its beloved Domin, and then murdered them in cruel and unholy ways. The dead flesh of its victims bore the carved image of a card from the Emperor's Tarot: the Monster.

cea9bb61-fc3a-495f-83f2-346e686c5cbc.Text: Vizsier Kibellah of the Bloodspun Web performed a great reading of the Emperor's Tarot, and the card of the Knight showed her cult a new path and a new teaching. Kibellah raised a generation of proud and fervent warriors, and led the scarlet-and-black army out of the shadows, to descend upon a multitude of worlds and hound the faithless in the name of the Undying Emperor. Rivers of spilt unclean blood drenched the soils of worlds where the Bloodspun Web's seeds had sprouted. Planetary rulers outlawed and hunted down the death cultists, to the point of starting full-blown wars, but their armies were hopelessly outmatched by a host led by the Vizsier's will and her powerful foresight guided by the Emperor's Tarot.

d9e9d7de-bfc6-4b92-8eb1-52096e8170ee.Text: Vizsier Kibellah of the Bloodspun Web guided her cult along its old paths and remained faithful to tradition. As before, Bloodspun Web cultists led ascetic lives and brought death to those who had been marked by the Undying One. However, nothing is unchanging. A momentous event profoundly impacted the Bloodspun Web: the discovery and miraculous return of a lost relic, a card from the Emperor's Tarot. The Vizsier performed a reading, and the Emperor showed her a new goal: to put the blessed deck back together. Only in its entirety could it reveal the great and dark future that awaited the Koronus Expanse. The Bloodspun Web read the portents, and the holy search commenced.

bea36bac-880c-4d58-82a3-5353cbb0579f.Text: The nobility of the Expanse appreciated the idyllic conditions of the pearl-like paradise world. White castles rose above the agri-complexes and their mud, and the shining knights of Janus gifted the sector with many a hero who covered themselves in glory.

d20884a4-5d33-43b0-8035-790c451f7a89.Text: Vizsier Kibellah of the Bloodspun Web performed a great reading of the Emperor's Tarot, and a card, the Lord of Swords, showed her cult a new path and a new teaching. The spinners vested themselves in gold, painted their faces with blood, came to the upper decks, and took the power and respect they were owed as the Undying One's chosen servants. The spinners surrounded the Domin with a barrier of sharp blades, becoming {mf|his|her} guard of honour and the ship's new gentry. Proud officers bent their stiff necks before them. Commoners filled their cups with their blood. The Bloodspun Web extended a thread to each of the dynasty's worlds, picking new recruits among those bearing marks of strong and noble blood. The Vizsier's reading portended grim changes, and the Bloodspun Web was making sure it would have the numbers and the weapons to face what was to come.

e9f9ddd5-5baa-4cf9-940c-3b07ad9f27cf.Text: Second Spinner Kibellah of the Bloodspun Web served the Vizsier and the Domin loyally — but over the years, alarming changes transformed her further and further. Caught in a tangle of doubts, Kibellah began to neglect the Emperor's Tarot, for its readings were terrifying, contradictory, and enigmatic. The Undying One gave her a different kind of signs through her dreams, and Kibellah killed ever more often, sending souls to the Emperor in their dozens and hundreds. She took a vow of silence and never spoke again. Her armour crusted over with rust and gore. There were whispers of her insanity among the crew, but no one would dare stand up to the sacred bodyguard of the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself}.

3d68f7e9-33a1-492a-9d7d-bf5d1129166d.Text: Kibellah's vision of a new path made her give in to the feeling that had sparked between her and the Domin. She shunned her role as bodyguard and companion to become something greater for the Lord Captain. The Bloodspun Web's threads trembled as a new duty descended on it. From then on, a Domin could find among the Undying One's servants, not only a loyal protector, but also a sacred spouse.

a8eac0ca-f052-4ed0-85fc-8f69294f82f4.Text: Everyone on the ship knew about the liaison between Kibellah and her Domin, but they also knew it would never turn into anything greater. Reluctantly, Kibellah grew distant from the Lord Captain, content with her role as her beloved's bodyguard and keeping her feelings confined to her own heart. As painful as that decision was, she saw no other path that the Tenets of the Bloodspun Web could lead her down.

22c44713-f109-4b6d-8c03-b5f652d8af15.Text: The body of Second Spinner Kibellah disappeared, and none were the wiser as to where — while her soul remained beside the throne of the Undying Emperor. Legends speak of a dark figure that sometimes disembarks from the von Valancius flagship in ports. They say it is a woman who no longer has a soul. They say bloodless corpses are found in the ports' slums sometime after the ship departs... Many untrustworthy legends are told and retold in ports across the Koronus Expanse.

3032932c-aab3-4ad7-ba36-73fa6fefebc0.Text: Many marvelled at the tolerance with which Kibellah regarded the Rogue Trader's obvious signs of apostasy. But the day came when the Undying One revealed to Kibellah that it was time for the Domin to depart.

d795ded2-6268-4816-af1a-35829249a8c6.Text: Mattis Erebis was a loyal and dutiful servant of the Rogue Trader. Because of his vehement faith in the Undying Emperor, he was permitted to join the Bloodspun Web. A decade and a half later, having risen to the rank of the Web's Fourth Spinner, he died honourably during an assignment, and his soul passed on to the Undying One. The Vizsier composed an enigmatic and profound quatrain in his memory.

9218af34-e110-4394-bcc0-f3912ba22fda.Text: Mattis Erebis was a loyal and dutiful servant of the Rogue Trader. He went on to become an outstanding bridge officer and a true void wolf. He visited many systems and worlds in the Koronus Expanse, but never set foot on his native Dargonus or saw his family again.

67f3865f-b89a-45ca-8b67-ce17a55a6d0c.Text: Mattis Erebis was a loyal and dutiful servant of the Rogue Trader. His faith in the Undying Emperor entangled him in the Bloodspun Web, but the young man was soon horrified at what the death cult had become under his sister's leadership. Mattis saw the changes she had made as blasphemous against the Emperor, and dared to speak out publicly against her. He met a grim fate. The Vizsier opened his veins with her own hand, tasted his lifeless blood, and made a reading of the Emperor's Tarot with it.

5c7fa5c4-3fea-4cd4-89f8-e25ae22e0f1a.Text: Dargonus continued to grow for two decades until a terrifying rebellion put a decisive end to its prosperity. A genetic abomination known as the Genestealer Cult infiltrated the hives of Dargonus and tried to take over the world. Millions were exterminated in purges and street battles destroyed many hives, setting Dargonus back centuries and depriving it of its chance to become the capital of the Expanse.

976a7eba-27b1-451e-b5dc-5f8e2f705447.Text: The secret of the Genestealer Cult infestation in the Koronus Expanse was laid bare. A wave of purges rolled across many worlds, with enraged rabble and planetary guards massacring thousands of those whose appearance diverged from true human form. Most of them were, of course, ordinary abject genetic misfits and luckless rejects, but their lives were a small price for the sector's purity.

5b2db5f3-eb41-4d14-8f79-c950b72bcbe2.Text: The fact that the von Valancius flagship had been infected with the Genestealer Cult's corruption was kept secret. The Rogue Trader's prestige and reputation had to be protected from harm, and all that remained was to hope that no new seeds of aberration were sprouting in other dark corners of the Koronus Expanse.

7f822cd6-adec-49d8-9dbd-a922489bd4b7.Text: With a passion that bordered on depravity, Kibellah gave in to the feeling that had sparked between her and the Domin. Years passed, but her attraction to the Lord Captain did not fade — and neither did her beauty, nourished by bathing in the blood of young maidens. The affair was ripe with dark passions and jealousy. Kibellah took many a life out of a suspicion that the person was eclipsing her in the Domin's eyes. However, their love was only strengthened by the blood offerings made to it.

ffec4ed4-ff4e-451b-9647-b19aa0f73b74.Text: She came up on the bridge in ceremonial dress, recited a prayer, and tried to execute the Undying One's bidding. The outcome was a foregone conclusion. Kibellah was struck down, and the Lord Captain's throne was encrusted with her still-alive, bleeding body. Using unholy sorcery to hold life within her dying flesh, the Domin prevented the soul of {mf|his|her} once faithful companion from passing on to the Undying One.

814badb7-92d3-4c36-8464-7f6ee5702d79.Text: After spending the watch in reflection and meditation, Kibellah made up her mind. She came up on the bridge in ceremonial dress and presented the Domin with a steel chest fastened by a chain. The chain was made of broken blades that had belonged to Kibellah, and the chest contained the Emperor's Tarot deck. As part of rejecting the Undying One's will, Kibellah also disowned His relic, and never touched His cards again.

906b5890-68ce-4af9-95be-ba3b0275fe12.Text: There were whispers among the crew that one of Mistress Sauerback's children had Werserian blood in him. Something of the noble features particular to that family could be discerned in the young man's genteel face. Whether it was true — whether Jocasta's resolute, uncompromising nature could have, and had, attracted the venerable Seneschal — remained a mystery.

4e86651b-7730-4f18-a39a-e811f8ed90e2.Text: She took up the position of the warden of one of the capital world's hives, and reconciled with her cousin Macharius, albeit only after a while. The reconciliation was, at any rate, easy to overlook during gatherings of capital-world nobility, where Jocasta and Macharius would waste no opportunity to have a ferocious row.

502a9d4e-e305-46da-81c9-65e2e855af9e.Text: Since the Sauerback family had been wiped out as punishment for their treason, Jocasta believed she could not start a family and give life to an heir. She devoted herself to her faith in the God-Emperor, and took a major temple on the capital world under her care. She developed a reputation as a strict but pious matron, and died at an advanced age. No one was around to accept her last words save for the golden image of the God-Emperor installed in her chambers.

b137fc1c-0dce-4d06-bac8-3290e0b5f716.Text: Dark legends say that the firstborn in whom the Domin and Kibellah's blood commingled was not raised in the Lord Captain's chambers but at the temple of the Undying One, as the child had been promised to the Bloodspun Web in their infancy. They grew up unaware of their noble bloodline, but aware of their duty, for the Undying One is duty itself.

ac37075f-9f28-4334-8b2d-bd762723cf36.Text: Although the Bloodspun Web provided the Inquisition with many deadly agents, the contradictions between the Undying Emperor's whispers and the will of the Lord Inquisitor slowly grew as the years went by. Eventually, the death cult splintered apart, and rivers of blood were spilt. A number of the Undying One's servants renounced their Vizsier and founded a new cult bound by absolute loyalty to the Inquisition, which they named Shadows of the Throne. Contrary to expectations, Vizsier Kibellah was not angered by the schism — instead, she saw the new teaching as another thread of service to the Undying Emperor. Until the end of his days, Lord Inquisitor van Calox wondered just how much sincerity there was in the hearts of the renegades who had agreed to serve under his command.

a3efd855-da57-4838-a050-1eaf94bd2281.Text: Dargonus grew and prospered until it became the capital of the Koronus Expanse. The planet was like a giant magnet whose pull held together the worlds of the Expanse, absorbing the treasures and vices of the sector.

53124e8f-e41b-4ad6-bb48-5e6ecddb8023.Text: At a time when Idira Tlass was preparing to accept her fate, she found guidance where she least expected it — in the wisdom of the Bloodspun Web. The words of Vizsier Kibellah, who had come to know death better than any mortal soul, helped Idira look to her future not without regret, but without fear. For many years afterward, there was an empty table in the common area of the officers' deck that had an intricate labyrinth carved into the tabletop. None of the crew sat at that table out of respect for the quiet and candid conversations once shared at it by a psyker and a servant of the Undying Emperor.

97ff7272-453e-4ac6-a411-3b459576a301.Text: Novator Cassia and Vizsier Kibellah were brought closer by their common burden of assuming a high position of power at a young age. Though their friendship was short-lived, as it could not overcome the gravity of their duties and the differences between the worlds to which they belonged, they exchanged gifts out of respect for each other and to honour the memories of the journeys they had shared. Cassia used Kibellah's blood to paint an incredible piece which became a relic of the Bloodspun Web. Kibellah, in turn, assigned one of her best spinners to act as Cassia's bodyguard. Many years later, this spinner was rumoured to have ended Cassia's life on the Novator's own orders when her body could no longer resist the strain of mutation.

ed094764-06fa-471d-a3a5-80b90fae4350.Text: Not a soul knows how many enemies Marazhai faced in his lifetime, but what is known is the name of his last opponent. Once he had left the Rogue Trader's retinue, there was nothing to stop him from testing the warrior that had long since caught his curiosity — Vizsier Kibellah, the bladedancer. In turn, there was nothing to stop her from executing the Undying Emperor's will by exterminating the xenos. Both spent years preparing for this fight, studying each other from the shadows. Their dance took place on a remote world, and bountiful was the offering of blood it left upon the surface. The victor of that battle never appeared in the Koronus Expanse again, and thus the outcome remains unknown.

dc796f64-caa2-44b8-a00b-9bcb247652ff.Text: With her newly acquired power and resources, Jae Heydari expended a great deal of effort to put an end to the Cult of the Bloodspun Web. The ease with which she sent assassins after the spinners and spread damning propaganda betrayed her strong vested interest. Many thought her actions reckless and expected a retaliatory strike to be delivered before long, but... it never came. With the cards of the Emperor's Tarot spread before her in the darkness, Vizsier Kibellah performed one reading after another, but, as much as it troubled her, she could find no command to end the life of her brazen adversary. Thus, the blade remained sheathed.

f0c79ced-b642-40f3-8739-07e76253377d.Text: For a time, Commorragh's streets were abuzz with tales of a mon-keigh accompanied by a leashed beast who exacted his perverse justice, but these rumours soon died down. However, around that time, a new gladiator entered the arena — a muscular Wrack with a dog's head sewn onto its body. It died while trying to climb the Archon's stand during a show.

f159753a-f522-4cb0-b15f-acd1a11e971b.Text: Solomorne remained on Vheabos VI, struggling long and hard to wrestle back control over himself from his own tumultuous rage. It was not to last, however. One day, Marshal Strachs came to impound a valuable Arbites asset — the cyber-mastiff — only to be attacked by Solomorne. At the Marshal's command, Glaito tore his master to pieces.

cd05839e-af21-42e4-ba65-316c3edf0de1.Text:
Voidfarers shared grim tales about the von Valancius flagship. Monsters dwelt in the bowels of the vessel, they whispered, and from time to time, the servants of those monsters descended to worlds and stations to spread corruption. These rumours were suppressed as criminal slander... but that made them no less true.
Many generations later, a great rebellion of genetic abomination shook the Expanse. Mutants born of the profane xenodisease revolted at the call of their fearsome four-armed Angel. Dargonus, the glorious capital of the von Valancius dynasty, was lost. Cleansed of genetic abomination once before, it was now tainted by it again — this time forever. After becoming a breeding ground for mutants, Dargonus proclaimed its faith in the Many-Armed Emperor. On a high throne in the Rogue Trader's palace, a scaled saint from the distant stars slumbered. In his dreams, he spoke to his progenitor and sensed that he was approaching.

029f2483-45e4-4bf3-80a6-48507824c34a.Text: Witnessing the Rogue Trader's treachery did not surprise Proctor Solomorne Anthar, who always assumed the worst and trusted no one save for his cyber-mastiff. The Arbitrator felt a grim satisfaction as his final moments brought him proof of the correctness of his chosen path. After shooting Glaito, preferring to end his companion's life himself over leaving him to die painfully or suffer an even worse fate, Solomorne faced his former comrade in arms, and died before he could land a single blow.

0a6de4d7-f925-42bd-a65a-798adba271d6.Text: After being demoted to the status of a patrolman, Solomorne Anthar took up duty on the lower levels of Dargonus. The shabby precinct the former Arbitrator was assigned to soon rivalled the von Valancius palace in safety, drawing the envy of the enforcers and ultimately signing his death warrant. One fateful day, finding himself cornered by a gang of criminals, Solomorne requested backup, but no one came to his aid.

eb6c0d87-4317-4ef4-ad55-1a81f3897de8.Text: All traces of the former Arbitrator have been lost in the darkness of history. Following his summary expulsion, he never set foot on a von Valancius world again, nor did he seek out a patron in other systems. A century later, a void wanderer was heard speaking of an uncharted world on the outskirts of the Expanse, where one could find an unmarked grave alongside the metal frame of a cybernetic animal, which stood over it like a headstone.

eb922256-01cb-4e57-846a-b931c55c20a0.Text: Kiava Gamma washed off the stain of its former defilement and became known as a pious and productive world. Hard work and inquisitive study of the mysteries of Technology glorified the Deus Mechanicus.

b6a2ef01-829a-426c-9f29-45f311dbd4dd.Text: Years later, Solomorne Anthar became Marshal and quickly tightened the requirements for all Arbitrators. They were now expected to be beyond any reproach whatsoever in both thought or deed, as well as ascetic to a religious degree. Under their great Marshal's leadership, the Arbites became the true bearers of the Emperor's divine light; however, the lack of new recruits from across the Maw would also doom them to extinction. After Solomorne's death, the Arbitrators continued to do their duty honourably, until they, too, passed away one by one, leaving the Koronus Expanse without their ever-vigilant oversight.

ae312657-00ad-4bfd-bde2-3b260e7ba073.Text: After becoming Marshal several years later, Solomorne Anthar began to reform the laws of the Expanse, seeking to imbue them with a spirit of justice. His approach led to a severalfold increase in workload for the Adeptus Arbites; Solomorne's solution to this was to assemble a so-called "Lex Imperialis militia," which recruited only the most honourable subjects of the Imperium. This in turn resulted in a conflict between the original Arbites and Marshal Anthar, which escalated into a war that went on for decades and claimed hundreds of lives.

6c1766ab-11d0-4c7b-b890-11de5c60e245.Text: When his time came to take the reins of the Adeptus Arbites, Marshal Anthar began his watch by immediately executing any who would not obey him without question. His next step was to formulate a new Lex Koronus, written in the blood of criminals. The sacred tome was put on display at what was now called the Palace of Punishment. Marshal Anthar sent death squads after any who did not uphold the latest version of the Lex Koronus. These merciless raids came to epitomise the oppressive terror of the new and monstrous face of the law in the Expanse.

f4c1119e-0731-4112-beba-f1325d8c71ad.Text: Following the transition of power at the Adeptus Arbites, Solomorne rejoined its ranks, where he remained in service for the rest of his life. Implacable and incorruptible, Solomorne was thrice offered the position of an Arbites Marshal, which he refused every time. Toward the end of his life, Anthar, though still a humble Proctor, wielded an authority surpassing that of all his superior officers. This was likely the reason for the final — and the only successful — attempt on his life.

79e9a552-f391-4b12-baa2-e5d4883c916d.Text: Solomorne Anthar remained in the ranks of the Adeptus Arbites, straying ever more from the letter of the law in favour of its spirit. On one occasion, several years later, he refused to collect tithe from one of the fringe worlds, as this would have condemned its people to death by starvation. Aware of the Proctor's long-standing ties with the Rogue Trader, the Marshal decided not to take the risk of having the freethinker executed. Instead, he sent Solomorne on an impossible mission, thereby spelling his death sentence.

dc8cad28-fca8-4d3d-8166-b56bdc9b0cae.Text: After joining the ranks of the reformed Adeptus Arbites, Solomorne rallied some of the Arbitrators around him. Together, they terrorised entire worlds and disembowelled planetary governors' families as a lesson to any who breached the law by even one iota. The new Marshal tried to put an end to the rampant heresy, but the brief fight that ensued resulted in the Marshal being overpowered and given to Glaito to be eaten alive. By the time the Arbites elected their new leader, their organisation was all but a shadow of its former self. Meanwhile, Solomorne had become captain of a ship, the Blood Tribute. The vessel would continue to dole out his perverse justice for decades, until it finally perished in a particularly horrific warp storm, much to the relief of the Expanse's inhabitants.

19b6bca2-2ea3-4ab7-a4dd-98cad489ccc7.Text: After exterminating the last of the Arbites in the Expanse, Solomorne Anthar realised he was now the sector's sole wielder of the Lex Imperialis. He placed upon himself a great mission to wipe out crime, and spent years cleansing the Expanse of lawlessness as he hunted down Shadow Barons and pirate captains. Impeccably loyal to the Emperor and His Law, the former Proctor came to symbolise the implacability of justice to all inhabitants of the Expanse.

4c07f2be-64fe-4858-8e37-3d278121ca7f.Text: Solomorne Anthar did not stay idle for long, as his sense of justice would not allow him to sit back and merely observe the growing lawlessness around him. He and Glaito disappeared for many years, after which a rumour began to spread throughout the Expanse of an Invisible Judge who came for the most ruthless of criminals and struck them down. There was no hiding from him on void stations or in the depths of hive worlds. Dozens of bounties were put on the Invisible Judge, only for him to escape every manhunt unscathed. It was said the faceless avenger was able to show up in different corners of the sector at the same time, and even to change his appearance. Whether these apparitions were the Invisible Judge's successors, his imitators, or sorcerous illusions remains unknown.

fabbc6ed-6e1d-49c7-bc51-881f04936ba9.Text: Having dealt with the Adeptus Arbites, Solomorne Anthar became the Rogue Trader's personal investigator. Whenever {name} von Valancius wanted to track someone down, {mf|he|she} would send Solomorne and his faithful dog. There was no hiding from them, and Glaito's jaws were relentless in tearing apart the dynasty's enemies. When the cyber-mastiff's body became possessed by a daemon lured there by his master's devastating fury, Anthar merely smiled a wry smile, pleased that his beast was now even more deadly and invincible than before.

6b400819-e4f2-4d01-a760-6b068af8e438.Text: The romantic bond between Solomorne Anthar and {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius withstood every test, but it was not to last.
