Though death had claimed the Arbitrator, his love for the Rogue Trader immortalised him, as many among the Expanse's nobility followed Proctor Anthar's example in choosing an influential person as the object of their adoration and swearing romantic fidelity to them alongside their vows of service. The expression "to love each other like {name} and Solomorne" was soon taken up to describe any relationship where love surpassed duty and could not be broken even by the scheming of powerful suzerains and commanders.

71b191fb-a70c-40ee-89e0-615134db2144.Text: Kiava Gamma washed off the stain of its former defilement, but not the dark memory of it. The sacred halls were never silent, and production rates became the supreme law. The glory of the Imperium was forged in the blood and sweat of its toilers, and the millstones of the manufactorums ground the workers down by the thousand. Even in death, the souls of its servants dared not step away from their machines.

29e8e2dd-3dc9-46f4-98f0-9e92da2e5f40.Text: A multitude of agreements bound the Imperial Navy to the von Valancius dynasty. Captains were eager to patrol the protectorate, knowing they would be richly rewarded. Competing ships were lost to "pirate attacks" and subjected to harsh inspections. Many officers quietly entered the dynasty's service, receiving a salary and title in exchange for their excellent skills. Worthy admirals valued their new friends and enjoyed more gold on their uniforms.

a293982c-b1a5-4270-a10b-feb429ee30c6.Text:
After accepting the Rogue Trader's proposal and becoming {mf|his|her} worthy consort, Solomorne never let anyone stand between him and his love again.
Once, Solomorne went on a pirate hunt and came back accompanied by three orphans of a delicate age — captives whom he had rescued. He and the Rogue Trader developed an affection for the youngsters, and took it upon themselves to raise them. Under their wise and devoted care, the three children grew up to become adults of great talent, whose deeds astounded the Koronus Expanse on many occasions. And although the love between the Arbitrator and the Lord Captain was no longer theirs alone, they never felt a lack of it.

ca959eba-ded9-4f91-97fe-c11fb9f4c42b.Text: On Epitaph, Solomorne witnessed his beloved betray Humanity, and for the first time ever, the Arbitrator's face was wet with tears. The unimaginable grief burst the devastated Proctor's heart before an even more terrible fate could befall him.

b52e5c9a-5b93-42c7-97db-486e6d260702.Text: Abelard Werserian and Solomorne Anthar spent most of their infrequent meetings playing regicide, to which the Seneschal had introduced the Proctor. Meticulously recorded by Abelard's adjutant, their games soon found their way into collections of the best ones ever played in the Expanse, and were later referenced by many a noble regicide aficionado. When First Officer Werserian passed away before he could finish the last match in a long series of draws, Solomorne attended his funeral in full dress and regalia, and placed a regicide piece on his grave.

f8c7fc02-e2ca-4be7-9e63-643f22ea24ba.Text: The antagonism between the Baroness of Shadows and the Marshal of the Expanse became the stuff of legends. Thousands of people found themselves entangled in their respective leader's battle of wits. Where some hid, others searched for them; where some ran, others pursued them. It is known for a fact that there were two things the adversaries never did even once: meet in person or threaten one another's nearest and dearest.

58d7bb63-9c5b-46bb-b9e5-c578710083b8.Text: The struggle between the Baroness of Shadows and the Marshal of the Expanse became the largest-ever conflict between the underworld and the law. One after another, the bandits' lairs fell to the Marshal's forces, until one day, an explosion destroyed the Palace of Justice, along with most of the Arbites. In the full-scale war that ensued, Arbitrators exterminated entire families of the Baroness's people, paying no mind to collateral damage. After years of being dragged into the internecine carnage, the sector's inhabitants found themselves cursing both sides alike.

9ef75c1d-6758-4428-8051-463ca074a295.Text: Duty demanded that Magos Haneumann and Marshal Anthar part ways. During their last meeting, Pasqal made a few final modifications to Glaito's design, increasing the cyber-mastiff's service life severalfold. Whether the gift had any impact on Solomorne is uncertain, but on more than one occasion, having his faithful dog at his side would turn out to be his salvation in even the darkest of days.

64c942e2-5cef-4ff3-ae68-891c1cb5ddb3.Text: The protracted search for a Marshal had so weakened the Adeptus Arbites that their new leader had to spend the rest of their life restoring order within the organisation. While the Arbites were busy dealing with their internal problems, lawlessness and disobedience flourished throughout the Expanse.

9a0eb737-202c-4707-86af-6070f740777f.Text: After the trial of Prefect Vultur and Marshal Strachs, the Rogue Trader ordered the Arbites to find a new commander and forget about House von Valancius. The Marshal appointed years later was so frightened by the fate of their predecessor that they never dared say a word against the dynasty's decisions. Once every criminal's worst nightmare, the Arbites of the Expanse gradually declined into just another law-enforcement clan, indistinguishable from the many thousands like it.

4a9d7bac-d269-441a-a174-67951a09fe28.Text: After the Adeptus Arbites were outlawed throughout the Expanse, a few of their members surrendered to the Rogue Trader, while many others went into hiding. The remainder either died in shows of resistance or made attempts to band together, eventually coalescing into the pirate gang known as the Lex Voidis. Under the pretext of restoring the rule of law, they unleashed horror and destruction on countless von Valancius worlds.

a8e6b17b-2b46-4d6c-b44c-dbdf93e2db0e.Text: Solomorne Anthar, House von Valancius's faithful watchdog, tracked down the Lex Voidis flagship and carried out the last sentence on the Adeptus Arbites in the Koronus Expanse.

fed6c847-e965-4cf8-8d26-039c6395225d.Text: Kiava Gamma grew and new manufactorums were founded, until disturbing reports started to trickle in many years later. It seemed that someone had secretly taken control of the colony, shrouding it in a tangle of conspiracy. Neither enquiries nor threats to Tech-Priests or executions helped. Someone in the shadows was weaving their web and making secret plans.

b00490cf-513a-465e-a18a-b448728790ba.Text: During the purges within the ranks of the Arbites, no one who fell even slightly short of the strict stipulations of the Lex Imperialis was spared. Those that remained, the best of the best, could no longer perform the entire spectrum of Arbites duties, being unable to arrive in time wherever their vigilance was required. Not one of the thousands of candidates seeking to replenish the ranks of the new and flawless servants of the Lex Imperialis managed to pass the entrance trials. Eventually, the Arbites Koronus, as it came to be called, became a closed order of lawmen that administered their own brand of justice. The order's history ended with the death of its last member.

2ecaefba-acef-467a-b827-016ff6e17045.Text: The former prefect was sentenced to tithe accounting duty for the rest of her life. For several years, she inhabited a tiny room stacked with papers, until one day, she felt the life going out of her withered body. She assembled her few subordinates and meticulously handed over her various responsibilities. Her final words were: "This completes the reading of the list. Rank two clerk Inscribia Vultur is hereby stepping down for death-related reasons."

f2ac2d34-0030-475b-bb1a-d123e7c7d16c.Text: High Overseer Gregoras Strachs of Vheabos VI rendered his duties with a zeal unfathomable to the common mind. Under his leadership, the penal world became a paragon of order and a place of incarceration that criminals feared more than death. Strachs spent his final years in a small, damp room disturbingly reminiscent of a jail cell. He declined every award and honour for his assiduous service, and preferred solitude to any kind of company.

80f0fbc9-f90a-44a7-8e7a-669bc7ec54f0.Text: The only exception was Solomorne Anthar, who visited his former superior whenever he had the chance. The contents of their long conversations are unknown, but their outcome was the same every time: a gloomy and unmistakable mark of regret on each of the two dour men's faces.

0b0d0528-2fb2-4ad7-9056-f33c0ebf2f8c.Text: Maive's rule as governor of Thassera was as short as it was memorable. Incapable of turning down any common folk suffering under the nobility's oppression, she focused her every effort on helping those in need, thus incurring the aristocracy's wrath. False accusations of sorcery were concocted against the governor, and, being uninitiated in the art of plotting and scheming, Maive walked right into the trap. The Phesmophorius took the young woman in its embrace, and all that remained of her memory was a handful of mournful songs, hummed in secret by a few grateful commoners.

aeae4b18-846c-4b64-9d26-bad67c9b5500.Text: The Rogue Trader's servo-skull-penned autobiography became a landmark of literature in the Expanse. In an ironic twist, the numerous manual copies made during the memoir's distribution littered it with so many distortions and reinterpretations that, centuries later, no widely available version of the text contained even a single word of truth. The original publication has become an object of speculative trade among enterprising collectors, and secret underground auctions are sometimes held, in which noble buyers are prepared to part with entire worlds and voidships just for the chance to possess a manuscript of such incredible value.

6b8054e2-661c-4d75-8684-ba9e58006899.Text: The Rogue Trader asserted {mf|his|her} right to the Leethus tithe. All of it, down to the last crumb, was spent in the name of the Imperium. Cathedrals were erected; fortresses were built to defend against Humanity's enemies; entire new armies were recruited and equipped. However, other dynasties soon branded House von Valancius as a tithe usurper, thenceforth refusing to pay the sacred tribute, and the already shaky peace between the Rogue Traders was damaged beyond all repair.

763fb885-c415-47b4-b472-5f7179b9c07f.Text: In the end, the Cult of the Fatal Thirst did not recover from the daemons' bloodbath in the arena. After losing all of its Succubi, it became an easy target, and soon the entire arena, along with its spectators, died in a sudden and surprisingly rapid dimensional collapse, sending the screaming xenos souls right into the maw of She Who Thirsts.

46195a3f-9bc7-40c0-9f97-17e667752cdb.Text: The tithe taken from Leethus was a lifeline for many dying worlds in the Expanse. The Rogue Trader spared no expense in helping not only {mf|his|her} own protectorate, but the neighbouring stars as well. Not everyone was understanding of such charity, but the role of House von Valancius in saving entire systems was beyond any doubt. After a time, some worlds began objecting to the volume of aid they were receiving, while others altogether balked at paying their tithe. In the end, all too many of them came to waste their precious gift of life on bloody revolts and senseless infighting.

026ad017-8c2d-4906-9c2e-379b98ace981.Text: The unimaginable wealth that was the Koronus Expanse's tithe became the foundation of the Rogue Trader's absolute power. Mercenary armies were prepared to kiss the feet of the owner of such immense treasure. Architects erected palaces in {mf|his|her} honour. Traders preferred Dargonus as the place to sell their most valuable artefacts. Sinister opulence flowed into the residences of {mf|him|her} whose greed the dark gods smiled upon. The feasts and the sacrifices never ceased for a moment. Trade elsewhere was gutted, and other dynasties had no choice but to either bend the knee or decline and disappear, for the Expanse now belonged to one person alone.

5d4af068-0cac-4827-9b31-a13403aa804b.Text: Following Leethus's destruction, its tithe ended up in the tenacious grip of the Administratum. The clerks stashed the wealth of the Koronus Expanse away in warehouses. A few years later, a decision was made to transport the tribute across the Maw, where the barges carrying the immense wealth were lost without a trace.

4f73b443-b78a-4db0-bf52-4eb7e7028d98.Text: Following the destruction of Leethus, Rogue Trader von Valancius directed part of its tithe toward restoring Koronus Expanse worlds that had suffered from xenos, heretics, and the horrors of the void. Many of them only survived thanks to that aid, although the broad gesture was met with scant understanding by aristocrats. Some years later, the worlds to which the tithe had been distributed were struck by a ghastly disease that came to be known as the Leethus Curse. Whether it truly was related to the tithe or a mere attempt to slander the Expanse's protector forever remained a mystery.

ecb6296e-913b-4b7a-b39b-f929f93ea818.Text: {name} von Valancius took a percentage of the tithe as payment for {mf|his|her} help to the Arbites. The resources were used to construct a void station, the Gem of the Dynasty, a true ornament of the Koronus Expanse. The monumental structure remained standing for centuries after its creator's death.

3b89f4a2-e496-45cd-a586-e85e04a12f5d.Text: As the sole owner of the Leethus tithe, the Rogue Trader was able to turn {mf|his|her} greatest ambitions into reality; however, the colossal wealth soon became a curse for the von Valancius dynasty. Frauds and tricksters of all kinds swarmed Dargonus, seeking to use their cunning to obtain even a small fraction of its fabulous wealth; pirates assembled flotillas, hoping to sack the dynasty's treasury; and even formerly loyal comrades and subjects soon leapt on every opportunity for embezzlement. Much like the rusty winds of Leethus had done before them, corruption and scheming soon began gnawing away at the appropriated tithe.

709ee283-07da-448d-a765-1b15c5c54aa8.Text: Maive settled into life aboard the flagship surprisingly quickly, and her kindness and gentle nature touched the hearts of the crew. One dashing officer made his romantic interest known, but Maive spurned his advances, hiding behind high collars and shawls the disfiguring marks of the dark ritual that had taken place on Thassera. When Maive's suitor at last secured her consent to marry, little did he know that he was walking into a blood-soaked nightmare: just before the ceremony, his bride-to-be transformed into a Chaos spawn. To the cries of horror and despair, the creature gorged itself on shattered hopes until it was slain by the arriving enforcers. It is said that, as the creature lay bleeding, it tried to sing a surprisingly tender tune and called out to someone named Daen.

713b43d3-c5d6-45d2-bd3c-55ab5649b4c5.Text: After the Rogue Trader left the Necron systems, the path to them was closed. The gates leading to the Tomb Worlds remained under the control of the Lord Captain, and there was no telling if {mf|he|she} was protecting Humanity from the dangers lurking beyond them, or if {mf|he|she} had simply made {mf|himself|herself} the sole proprietor of the terrifying technologies and secrets of the xenos.

14d57ec5-c73d-4315-a8d7-0a43938ddc8f.Text: As they were leaving the Necron systems, Nomos destroyed every Tomb World of the ancient xenos. Some eternal strife had awakened within the young deity, demanding that the planets of the undead be obliterated.

51639055-fb04-4768-997a-f0a3b4d8171b.Text: Before leaving the Necron systems, Lord Inquisitor Calcazar ordered the conquered deity to destroy every Tomb World. Thus perished another threat to Humanity in the sector, along with the hidden clues it held about the nature of the monster brought into the Imperium's service.

6fe98e05-0697-4704-af1b-04e630bd4234.Text: Janus was conquered, the xenos spirits were exorcised, and the wilderness was subdued. The fields grew until they covered the entire planet, and billions of tons of provisions were harvested there. Janus had become the breadbasket of the Expanse, and to threaten it would be to condemn millions to starvation.

952c9840-e3fc-4cb1-bac0-e03d46797112.Text: Vistenza Vyatt's reign was long and bloody. The Prince of Pleasure bestowed the secrets of metamorphoses upon her, and Janus's nature was transformed. An endless string of serfs was sent into her palace, their blood, flesh, and souls consumed in experimentation or endless revelry. Over the years, Vistenza's body became covered in scales, becoming long and sinuous. She no longer left her lair, which was filled with specimens of delicious degradation and corrupted wisdom.

92a286ba-3c72-495d-a1f0-b03f91187f49.Text: Muaran's secret rule bore poisonous fruit. Repeated rebellions broke out in the agri-complexes as the serfs felt they were being manipulated by a force hostile to Humanity. Devoid of sympathy for humans, the Aeldari developed a plan to control and eliminate the unruly, terrorising them in the night. Janus bent under the yoke of inhuman occupation.

6bc26a76-8fd6-4ae4-8d3c-4a84c7949f87.Text: Five years after the Epitaph campaign, Vheabos VI died out as a result of an unknown scourge that came from beneath the ground. Convicts and overseers were poisoned, mangled, or just disappeared. However, the slave barracks were quickly repopulated, for there was no shortage of outcasts and criminals in the Expanse.

a0797309-fee8-40fd-85fb-01c3edb40f46.Text: Somewhere on the underside of reality lay Commorragh, woven from manifold other dimensions and illuminated as always with the light of stolen suns, its streets ever filled with screams and agony. Any misfortune experienced by the Dark City became another scar on its appalling face, lost among thousands of other vile blemishes. As long as pain pulsed in its blood-soaked spires, the insatiable and unshakeable Commorragh continued its flight through the Webway, along with its unchanging ruler, the leader of the Kabal of the Black Heart and the most dangerous of all Drukhari — Asdrubael Vect.

4002943c-7e56-4160-bf86-6e5133423e6c.Text: Incendia Chorda never returned from her expedition through the dimensional gate with Rogue Trader von Valancius. Her dynasty lost its leader.

2d6e05ac-0be4-4d48-9194-30d78c7065ee.Text: The savage Calligos Winterscale never returned from the campaign he embarked on with the Rogue Trader. No one knew the cause of the indomitable warrior's demise.

17d2d3a3-c862-4b30-8bdb-db9528d232e7.Text: The protectorate became engulfed in a brutal fight for the throne that made Calligos's violent deeds seem tame in comparison.

8a698352-ebe5-4cf8-a834-1d3ec9d245f7.Text: The Imperial Navy was wary of the rise of the von Valancius. They saw themselves as dogs guarding the flock of the Emperor's subjects, and there was a new master of the pack. Therefore, the dynasty was watched with utmost diligence, and the admirals feared that one day they would have to go to war against the Rogue Trader.

fcd202a9-36e7-4e77-8cf5-fc36ccb4bfb4.Text: Liege Tocara, under a secret oath of loyalty to the Rogue Trader, slowly but surely corrupted the station. During the restoration of the magnificent statue of the God-Emperor, his craftsmen introduced faults in the structure that were invisible to the naked eye. Yet, years later, Astropaths noticed that the light of the Astronomican was greatly dimmed around Footfall.

22d6a0d7-75d9-4a6e-bb65-cd61dcb2927f.Text: Vladaym Tocara ended his days as a maintenance servitor on a janitorial team, losing his life due to an error by a technomat who sent him to clean a compartment scheduled for decompression. The technomat received a penance of seven electro-whippings and a fine equal to his annual pay as punishment for negligent handling of property.

d99e8263-4a70-4177-94e7-d25ac90e1711.Text: Vladaym Tocara spent six Terran years in the position of janitor, and then senior janitor, before one day dying after accidentally getting stuck in a compartment scheduled for decompression. Vladaym's coworkers insisted that he would have definitely known about the planned procedure.

e1aee877-67d2-4cf0-8fa8-323a4a0081d6.Text: Even after Incendia's death, Footfall could not find peace. Religious leaders and commanders of confessional units kept up the order she had established with zeal. A great tribunal, akin to the one that Incendia held, now took place every Terran year. And every year it was preceded by the rioting of exhausted and embittered citizens.

0f042168-a9ae-463d-a6b9-68b7fd142706.Text: Having walked a thorny path by the Rogue Trader's side, Yrliet met her end on an altar as an offering to She Who Thirsts. Her soul was wounded by the Lord Captain's monstrous betrayal, but the suffering did not last long — the dark deity soon consumed her.

3b4ddf0e-b8ed-4168-bd84-ca6e9b19b635.Text: Marazhai Aezyrraesh, also known as the Tempest's Doom, spent several years with the Rogue Trader, filling the entire crew with terror. However, with time, his restless and ambitious nature got the better of him. Having grown weary of the company of mon-keigh, the Drukhari left the ship.

cd1661b7-98a8-4982-8169-72fd612fbe84.Text: After the victory on Epitaph, Argenta left the Rogue Trader. An insatiable flame burned brighter and brighter in her soul, hungry for vengeance, and so the sister embarked on her own personal crusade. At first, she hunted and exterminated the remaining followers of the Final Dawn, then she pursued those who had abetted them, and then anyone in whom she saw a hint of heresy. Even when she directed her wrath against entire cities, no power could stop Argenta, clad in her sacred armour. She left a trail of fire and blood across the Expanse, a trail that ended on Salis Prime. No one knows why the sister returned for a third time to the planet where she had found her relic, but, after descending to its surface, she mysteriously vanished.

20e8b2d6-32d8-4909-8e4b-a9f882b60bce.Text: Many members of the conclave perished during the tragic events that accompanied the return of the Messiah of Discontinuing the Cycle. The hierarchical chain raised Magos Dominus Opticon-22 to the highest circle of leadership. He remained there for more than a century until he was deposed and disposed of, charged with attempting to revive the anathematised schism.

647003f9-e3ae-4e6f-a8d1-8de90d8bad65.Text: The dimensional gate leading to the Necron Tomb Worlds was sealed, and not a soul knew what transpired on the other side. But now and then, rumours came from the fringes of systems settled by Humanity, rumours of sickle-shaped ships that appeared and disappeared suddenly, without showing any signs of hostility... yet.

48dc9ec4-9e4c-4e80-99cf-f53e4728dcc4.Text: The corrupted harvest from Janus was reaped in Footfall's agro-chapels. The food cooked from it sowed the seeds of corruption among the station's citizens and bred voracity in all things. Hedonistic cults appeared seemingly out of nowhere all over the station, the most prominent among them being the Cult of the Blessed Harvest. It took it upon itself to cultivate tainted crops so that everyone could taste the fruit of true faith.

248ec448-01c6-43a2-8df0-c09d38a9e5db.Text: When the news of the Rogue Trader's betrayal reached the inhabited systems, it was the Navy's grim duty to exact retribution on the protectorate. It was they who defeated the fleet in Dargonus's orbit and carried out the purge of the capital world. All across the Expanse, patrols hunted for the ships bearing the once glorious crest of von Valancius.

fb8e6fe7-32f3-4503-af0a-764aaddf98cf.Text: Master Helmsman Ravor diligently executed his duties until his dying day without once succumbing to sleep's sweet embrace. Only when a piece of shell penetrated the bridge's armoured hull and was stopped by the stern officer's unyielding chest did he finally know rest, leaning against his trusty helm.

07be1f50-7b11-4f74-b6a7-1abb4c8882ea.Text: The first command that Ryzza issued after her miraculous rescue on Footfall was the complete extermination of all worshippers of the Dark Gods among the Fellowship of the Void. The old pirate wanted to find another way for her people to survive. The former renegades hoped to live by the law working as mercenaries and traders. When it seemed they were finally on the path to a peaceful life, the Imperial Navy conducted a flash raid and destroyed all their ships. Those who survived the bloodbath were publicly hanged.

f2ee69f3-b674-41f2-a7f4-ae8520a7fde8.Text: As their enemies' activities ramped up, the Fellowship of the Void required more powerful allies. Old Ryzza, with other pirates following suit, embraced the blasphemous doctrine of the Dark Gods, and her ships became immune to the damage caused by harsh warp storms. If prior accusations of the pirates' widespread worship of the Ruinous Powers had been wildly exaggerated, with every passing year they became closer to the truth.

3fbd3dd9-beee-45d9-88d5-8fee45517915.Text: The shrewd Gaprak family found patronage among the servants of the Omnissiah. Many of its members were granted the posthumous honour of becoming servo-skulls, and Vicent Gaprak even rose to the rank of Magos.

fc1bbb76-91e7-4390-9e03-b8ad26f2c665.Text: The nauseating breath of Grandfather Nurgle poisoned the sermons of Reverend Hieronymus. Preaching the omnipresence of rot and taint, he no longer called for purification but tormented the souls of his flock instead. Fallen into despair and craving solace, his people were willing to bow to any force that could promise peace and relief from their suffering.

173bfba8-f238-4019-a7ba-b3bf53c4e617.Text: Abelard Werserian witnessed the monstrous "ascension" of his {mf|lord|lady} and led the futile attempt to destroy the C'tan Shard. He died with Theodora's name on his lips — no longer deeming {name} von Valancius worthy of being his Lord Captain, he devoted his last desperate act to the one he had revered all his life.

b4632b1f-4deb-4a37-8d1a-89f558c50bfb.Text: Vladaym, who had formerly stayed clear of those suspected of heresy and dealings with corrupted goods, changed his mind with time. The Mission's ships not only brought contraband to different worlds, but they also transferred suspicious individuals clutching books bound in strange hide. Not everyone liked it, but no one was brave enough to challenge the orders of the terrifying Vackemo.

917ede18-b7ea-4f83-aa5e-e03263388b15.Text: The Drusians who tried to oppose the corruption were slaughtered and banished from Footfall. Yet many preachers were enticed by the absence of authority. Staining their black robes with wine and blood, they started giving mock pardons and imposing penances on their new heretic brethren.

c4b9169d-49b4-44a2-bf45-e3fe414cfb1a.Text: Strict abidance by the law and devotion to the Imperial Creed brought great renown to the Rogue Trader. Every planetary turn on every world in the sector, thousands of prayers were offered up to the Golden Throne praising the name of the Guardian of the Koronus Expanse.

7fa9a2bd-3c24-4e7d-b5c0-2502da9186e0.Text: The unholy blessing of the Dark Gods fell on the shoulders of the Rogue Trader, showing everyone that {mf|he|she} was their champion, destined to bring the Expanse under their rule. But it is well known that the favour of the lords of the warp is fickle.

c735c125-c9ad-4716-8f14-86ef3bb28371.Text: The honour of leading the restoration of the statue of the God-Emperor was bestowed upon none other than Gordei Skatov.

3e931b6a-8b9b-446e-85e8-93d79d78fd13.Text: Pulled between various forces that were desperate to control the Rogue Trader, {mf|His|Her} {mf|Lord|Lady}ship managed to walk the fine line between fanaticism, heresy, and becoming a heartless monster. Each force was either an ally or an enemy, but none were {mf|his|her} master. {name} von Valancius served only {mf|him|her}self and {mf|his|her} dynasty. Everything else was either a resource or a trophy.

2cc6935f-021d-4436-aeeb-bc75a4d18e55.Text: The nobility on Dargonus lost all its power when neighbours of the protectorate, enraged by the Rogue Trader's betrayal, came to tear it asunder.

a3a48230-5423-4565-ab6d-ef4d2894c889.Text: The Farseer Muaran led the now sparse army of those who had once been given sanctuary on Janus into battle. Their time in the den of evil had taken too many of them and filled Muaran's soul with despair. The Aeldari's sorcery was powerless, and he heard only the mocking laughter of She Who Thirsts as he watched the souls of his kin be consumed by the insatiable deity. Then he too vanished into her hideous maw.

bda9c020-1114-44f5-87d7-b0b52577462c.Text: The Drivestem family used their connections in the Kasballica Mission and became calculating and unscrupulous dealers who spurned the law. Few noticed the change.

53a5868c-dfcb-49f4-aa76-2b3ace16332e.Text: The Imperium could not forgive such insolent deviation from the order prescribed by Holy Terra. The von Valancius dynasty was accused of the seditious formation of their own empire. An invasion fleet gathered in the Calixis Sector, and the lifespan of the young utopia was as short as its creator's.

f8841de0-36d4-4e0f-99d4-e035aaff3ad1.Text: Gazing upon the drained and crippled worlds, the Rogue Trader saw innumerable opportunities for the growth of {mf|his|her} dynasty. From the ashes of decades of relative peace, a new ambitious power was set to rise.

e2a4afc9-bef5-41a6-a87d-cab65d6c91ac.Text: Having tamed a deity, the von Valancius dynasty became the dominant power in the Expanse. Of course, news of the horrible monster that {name} von Valancius was using to terrorise the entire sector would sooner or later reach the Imperium and prompt a punitive expedition, but... the Rogue Trader was given plenty of time to prepare.

fe7d1c2a-7cd6-45a1-bcd4-dc8a28503329.Text: The entire Expanse heard of the Rogue Trader's betrayal. {mf|His|Her} punishment was swift. Retaliatory strikes fell on the von Valancius protectorate from all sides, obliterating it in the blink of an eye. But did that trouble its former ruler? Unlikely...

77d71239-a2d9-447e-ba39-576ed6bb14cc.Text: After losing Ryzza and her closest associates, the Fellowship of the Void soon fell into a bloody and messy succession crisis. The fighting was so brutal, there could be no doubt that whoever came out of it the victor would be a much greater threat to the Expanse than the reckless deceased pirate ever was.

ce3b7b55-51d6-4d28-938d-b35727903d5e.Text: As the years passed, Master Helmsman Ravor's ill temper became even more unbearable. Continuing his never-ending watch on the bridge, he tormented any member of the crew whom he deemed not sufficiently diligent in fulfilling their duties. Holding the helm with his many hands, he woefully pronounced grim prophecies, filling hearts with despair.

800e4ee1-627a-44dc-acc6-a9596503af2c.Text: Poorhouses opened by the order of the Rogue Trader saved many hungry and homeless from death. Unfortunately, this disrupted the station's delicate ecosystem. No longer freezing to death in empty compartments or tormented by epidemics, those who lived in poverty on Footfall began to choke the station, leading to a sharp rise in crime: organ traders, illegal augmetic specialists, and savage gangs of Anvers proliferated.

d2e6cb73-70df-4884-9b86-c741550bb5c7.Text: The unit bearing the name Abel Haneumann was granted a pardon for his participation in the schism. Abel spent the rest of his days in monastic solitude on station Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17. Not bothered by unwanted voices, he gave himself fully to the passion of statistical augury and the creation of binharic harmonics. His liturgies were performed in machine cathedrals and were regarded as beautiful hymns to the Omnissiah, even if somewhat unorthodox due to a certain liveliness not characteristic of mechanist hymns to the Deus Mechanicus.

795cb130-89a5-4c71-9338-31643ebd3686.Text: The unit bearing the name Abel Haneumann did not follow Pasqal. No longer needed by his ambitious comrade, he was discarded and left behind. While en route to station Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17, Abel was captured by pirates and forced to toil as a technomat. The day the Imperial Navy destroyed his pirate ship prison marked the end of his silent torment.

f5e61058-ad07-4fcb-b5fa-e3a44f04a615.Text: With the backing of the Kasballica Mission, Octaviana became the new Liege of Footfall. All those who opposed her leadership died in an accident when promethium canisters on the Adeptus Amasecus suddenly detonated in the middle of negotiations between crime lords about the station's future. Octaviana was unharmed. She had left the ship several minutes before the explosion... purely by chance. She opened a new bar on an asteroid previously known as the Liege's palace.

13f7b3b1-a208-4aed-ade3-48ae7f063fb8.Text: The Edge of Daybreak, the Greater Daemon who turned Eufrates II into his lair, provided guidance and counsel to {mf|His|Her} {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, revealing the intricate will of the Lord of Change and warning {mf|him|her} about threats. This remained so until the Path changed and {name} von Valancius and the Edge of Daybreak became enemies vying for power in the Expanse. In the raging warp, nothing is forever, and no alliance is strong.

80d9e40b-46c1-42a3-8f04-f93cb39e7692.Text: No longer secluded and forlorn, Foulstone turned into the spiritual centre of the Expanse, clad in gold and power. Rulers went there to be anointed for greatness, criminals for penance, and the righteous for encouragement, and there was no end to them in sight.

506e8fbe-66c1-4454-954b-b5876eea16d7.Text: Of course, the corrupting influence of the Rogue Trader tainted each spark of faith that was kindled on Foulstone, turning the zealots into tools and the gullible into traitors. Donning the masks of piety, despicable demagogues lead their flock into the abyss of heresy.

35292f51-ab78-4d41-9611-073851688ce4.Text: The Farseer Muaran led his kin in battle against the mon-keigh. He was not able to overcome his hatred for them, and he washed the bitterness of loss from his heart with blood before leaving the transformed Lilaethan behind.

7bda3e82-ba4d-4d90-a79a-e4055a13a57e.Text: The Drusian preachers dwelling on the station turned into grim ascetics, ridden with ulcers and swelling with disease. Many voidsmen looking for redemption were attracted to the new forbidding image of the cult. Rumours abounded that the recurring technical breakdowns poisoning entire asteroids were the work of the Drusians, who led their flock through suffering to faith. A new faith.

c57535bb-f97f-4879-b6c5-265e017c2038.Text: Naturally, the servants of the von Valancius dynasty and people under the Rogue Trader's protection were safe from the Fellowship of the Void's attacks... mostly.

8291b800-6bea-4682-a25b-022518d8f78a.Text: After returning to the place where {mf|his|her} path as a Rogue Trader had begun, {name} von Valancius founded a new capital on Rykad Minoris, asserting {mf|his|her} right to rule over any manifestation of the warp's horror in the Koronus Expanse.

df73d314-cdb7-4741-a407-3b0e3fb7c223.Text: The new regime on Footfall was less harsh than Chorda's dictatorship, but it still managed to give the station the appearance of a lawful colony of the Imperium. After years of persecution, the crime lords realised that it was more profitable to make thrones legally, and so they installed themselves in high-ranking positions among the station's wardens and bureaucrats. But this change only increased their greed and thirst for blood.

efa65f11-9d0d-4cd4-8fee-cdd8ea6985d0.Text: Incendia Chorda's crusade put an end to the existence of this corrupted place. With heavy losses, her fleet broke into the system, defeated the warp spawn there, and bombed every world to ash with cyclonic torpedoes. A decade later, the warp tear in realspace closed.

e9e851a5-1719-48fa-a5c1-85bc4c48422b.Text: Brave House Werserian returned to its roots and engaged in void trade. Their renowned ship, the Lady Theodora, embarked on many grand voyages and took part in astounding expeditions to the limits of uncharted systems.

47b4f872-42ee-4fc8-b364-1ba775c6932a.Text: However, close friendship with the von Valancius dynasty did not stop pirate squadrons from pillaging the protectorate's treasures when fleets of outraged neighbours arrived to take their vengeance.

a5835fbf-54f3-4682-bed4-9c32af748239.Text: Realising that things were changing in the Expanse, Kasballica agents limited their appetites and restricted their trade to goods of moderate risk. They secretly turned the most dangerous trophies over to the Inquisition, alongside information about their suspicious suppliers. Information about this shadowy alliance was tightly controlled.

c7f79ff2-8214-4ccd-8736-c97bad3783af.Text: When news of the death of the master of flesh reached him, Shairenkhei sent what was left of the Aeldari ships to the most distant stars of the Expanse. There, hidden from human eyes with xenotech and sorcery, the Aeldari carried on their humble existence and even managed to establish a few contacts among trusted mon-keigh, who helped the xenos in return for knowledge and technology.

c8d912c1-01b8-4ff3-ab29-272f466217f8.Text: When the von Valancius protectorate perished under the retaliatory strikes of resentful citizens of the Expanse, many servants of the Rogue Trader found sanctuary and a new way of life in this powerful organisation. The Kasballica Mission did not forget the kindness shown to it.

482d08c4-df38-48fa-a480-c4e58e83e823.Text: Memories of the adversity they suffered and of their fallen home filled the hearts of both commoners and nobles with hatred for the Ruinous Powers. That loathing fuelled the building of a kingdom of intolerance and strict order on New Rykad. Proclaiming prayers to the Emperor, they kept vigilant watch for any signs of corruption in their home and surrounding colonies and regularly embarked on "purging campaigns" on nearby colonies that resembled military invasions.

be3e1852-f6ce-4755-84f2-0190e4c4c7d2.Text: The corrupted harvest from Janus was eradicated from Footfall's agro-chapels, but some of it remained in underground nurseries. The starving were ready to commit heinous acts for a handful of food, or even a sip of fermented rotgut. Illegal drinks made from the fruits of Janus sparked sinister rage and a thirst for violence in the hearts of the peasantry, spawning riots and stirring up the worst vices of the common folk.

1fe718da-30e8-4b08-927b-4a8d71e5122d.Text: The schism of Discontinuing the Cycle engulfed the entire Cognisance Fleet, and soon the civil war was over. Disregarding the commandments of their forefathers, the Explorators started down a dangerous path of new comprehension, creation, and revision of procedures and algorithms. The fleet was united once more, and in its unity, it was ready to stare down any horrors standing in the way of the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation.

278cc538-eb3e-4127-8b5c-333a328722ca.Text: Cassia Orsellio died on Epitaph, and her death became the undoing of her noble House. In her last moments, tormented by fear and sorrow, she let out a scream so full of despair that every Navigator of her bloodline heard it. Echoing her cry, they all lost their minds in that instant and became loathsome monstrosities. House Orsellio fell, and its inhabitants were buried in the ruins.

462849d4-3298-483e-b063-db80ffeb5858.Text: By some bizarre miracle, Marazhai Aezyrraesh managed to survive the Rogue Trader's betrayal on Epitaph. Even more fortuitously, he was picked up by a Drukhari raiding ship and delivered to Commorragh. Acting strangely calm and quiet, the former Dracon of the Reaving Tempest was granted an audience with one of the Archons of the Kabal of the Black Heart. What they discussed that day is unknown, but Marazhai left the Archon's palace with an armed squad and embarked on a hunt for a secret trophy.

3448ac1c-aa9a-4179-ab83-7b214886ca34.Text: This sacred relic was gifted to House von Valancius as a sign of the Ecclesiarchy's rare trust.

dad3477d-257e-4020-bbf8-b870948e8161.Text: The coat of arms of House von Valancius, which has become the symbol of mercy and hope for the billions of the Rogue Trader's subjects.

917d9947-9404-4f6c-bac0-d78fefa6e70d.Text: The heir to the von Valancius dynasty, who cravenly refused the great honour of accepting the Warrant of Trade, was mercifully let go. After {name} was transported by shuttle to the surface of Rykad Minoris, {mf|his|her} trail was lost forever. If Theodora's successor was not tracked down by Kunrad Voigtvir's assassins, {mf|he|she} most likely was consumed by the fires of the monstrous events that were to befall the hive world...

b7a970cf-0b32-4a55-a204-3d398e7fcdeb.Text: Swayed by the promises of the xenos infestation, {name} von Valancius received the Genestealer's Kiss and joined the Congregation of the Ravenous Star. {mf|He|She} let the sweetness of genetic perfection into {mf|his|her} flesh, and let the songs of the blessed Angel into {mf|his|her} mind. As {mf|he|she} spread the Ravenous Star's teachings across worlds, ships, and stations, {mf|he|she} prayed for the Day of Liberation, the day the heavenly host of the Many-Armed Emperor arrives in the Expanse. On that glorious day of triumph, the Rogue Trader, as the first of His saints, will be greatly rewarded for {mf|his|her} piety and loyalty.

ac063328-5649-4eae-8619-cb604f03a350.Text: Wet the altar with Ryzza's blood

e2494dc4-7ab7-49d3-92e0-bccd709f914d.Text: Place Yrliet's spirit stone on the altar

49879ef3-44fe-4fdc-820e-fe17783de68b.Text: The shattered weapon clearly has a significant role to play in the future preordained by the Weaver of Destinies. To part with any of the shards would mean losing the trust of the Rogue Trader's patron.

7716046d-b2b3-477e-ad7a-409735f11f53.Text: Retain the sword shards for the future

79e63eaf-c3af-45ac-98dd-416a47f3dbb9.Text: The Rogue Trader was told to "seek the Second Dawn" — presumably meaning another sword shard.

d193b15f-b148-4282-813b-a11d021c4a4f.Text: A future champion of Chaos needs followers. There is only one way to prove the Rogue Trader's might to {mf|his|her} servants — by committing acts against mortals and in the name of Chaos.

59fe6f50-bc79-4fef-bd32-b969a18a7b26.Text: Become a god to your subjects

5387d5d4-10d9-484b-b907-99d41f47edd1.Text: The Rogue Trader's power has reached the point where {mf|he|she} can appeal directly to {mf|his|her} patron.

ccdff4f1-3887-4cb1-9c29-8d3d03535791.Text: Take the sword shards to the altar of Chaos

172b00f9-3afe-46e7-acfb-8c3fc36a3a3d.Text: The Dawns will only accept a worthy aspirant — those who do not show proper zeal in serving the Weaver of Destinies will be rejected.

acbaf3e0-5012-4a1c-bdd4-de199bd304b6.Text: The Rogue Trader will be revealed, but until that moment {mf|he|she} must hide {mf|his|her} true intentions.

75961052-159e-440f-aff6-4c941164135f.Text: Follow the plan of the servants of the corpse emperor until the right moment

5ae646b4-c5a6-4484-b7c7-fa0f8a6fd411.Text: Vog and Haik prophesied the discovery of the Third Dawn in the hands of a "preacher." Sooner or later, the threads of fate will lead the Rogue Trader to him.

e5eab086-4f44-458c-9b4a-6fa1faa56fcc.Text: Wait for fate to lead you to the "iron world"

7ca8e439-f566-4193-8e80-62438296059f.Text: An alliance with Chaos requires sacrifices — destroy the Space Wolves who dare to oppose the will of Chaos, and then destroy the one intended for the great destiny of becoming the gateway to the Edge of Daybreak.

bd276ca4-7251-41e6-8c6a-6628861ef833.Text: Offer up a sacrifice to the Weaver of Destinies

8c94de96-fd9f-48fd-8aa3-4982758f3039.Text: The hour has struck — the name "Sameth" will serve as the key to the Rogue Trader's future.

4059a017-3e53-4440-a1d6-51febc1a26bd.Text: Speak the forbidden name to Uralon the Cruel

b79aea9d-77a9-4db7-86bc-6dc391257267.Text: The champion of Chaos can bow to the Edge of Daybreak, or defeat it to obtain an ancient treasure in which the Greater Daemon will be sealed. The choice is up to the Rogue Trader.

f407a279-eef6-4fdd-91a1-87fff577cd96.Text: Rogue Trader von Valancius bowed down before the forces of Chaos and fulfilled the prophecy of the Edge of Daybreak, spoken by him at their first meeting.

f1448abb-b654-440a-bfd8-08745df9dd2c.Text: The powerful warp entity promised the Rogue Trader might and power if {mf|he|she} managed to become the new champion of Chaos.

46adda1d-25c6-486e-b295-02014763b46e.Text: Kunrad Voigtvir, the Master of Whispers serving the von Valancius dynasty, has graciously offered to escort the dynasty heir to Lord Captain Theodora.

40935273-a6a2-40eb-b7b6-1ab452835095.Text: An automaton has suffered an unknown malfunction and is now attacking people. The deranged machine must be stopped!

961053d4-6fa6-490c-b529-3cb52f8da6bc.Text: Kunrad Voigtvir has decided to remain at the scene of the servitor incident to personally investigate the cause. Theodora von Valancius is at the orrery: she must not be kept waiting.

7372d3f9-f914-4ca6-bdea-b3d68cbe1621.Text: The officers' deck is under attack by an unknown enemy, so Arch-Militant Mort has left to clear the way to the lift leading to the upper decks. The officer has not returned yet, so it is time to find out the cause of the delay.

5b109406-6b22-46d1-871e-5170aa7d04fe.Text: While the Lord Captain and her officers are busy crushing the revolt, someone needs to find Edelthrad — the dynasty heir particularly favoured by Lady Theodora.

74e5d48c-86a2-45f0-b38c-405723d46003.Text: Discover the whereabouts of Edelthrad the heir

57e89103-3c22-4ac5-9c03-4b6dd59788dd.Text: The Warrant Chamber has opened its doors for the dynasty heir. It is time to make sure the sacred Warrant of Trade is safe.

cccabf9c-ac19-48f4-a741-175f4540945c.Text: The weapon offered by Seneschal Abelard Werserian should be kept at the ready.

861cfc27-4016-499d-8c97-9bdd7f86ffcb.Text: Seneschal Abelard Werserian has offered medical assistance. Accepting it would be a wise choice.

4504ffcf-4d2f-435a-a6bd-c885e697346f.Text: No one must reach the Warrant. A simple order to the Sentinel cogitator will lock the chamber.

70b1132d-0939-412e-afac-6d1a7fce8321.Text: The Navigator's untimely demise would spell disaster for the voidship when making a warp jump. Whatever is happening on the other decks, it is imperative to reach the Navigator's Sanctum and see what has happened to the vessel's warp guide.

bdb52252-e549-49ed-8cce-1523019c791b.Text: Idira, a psyker in Theodora von Valancius's service, speaks of ill omens related to the Navigator's fate. The warp guide must be protected at all costs.

81d78060-4043-42d5-9ad4-176b37aa2fa8.Text: The enemies in the Navigator's Sanctum have been eliminated, but the warp guide's condition gives cause for concern.

9bb7be16-343f-4127-a718-d77dca7ad5bc.Text: A servo-skull from the Warrant Chamber has relayed Edelthrad's message: the heir is alive and gathering people loyal to the dynasty to storm the bridge. It is vital to make it to this meeting to unite forces with Edelthrad and confront Kunrad.

2f4e49cc-0580-4f69-bee3-d88fb05ed2b2.Text: Make it to the meeting with the heir

4ed0a226-5556-4b12-a219-4380420b6350.Text: A separate lift leads to Theodora von Valancius's personal quarters.

5baddb44-1d57-4859-af31-79a5dbc3713b.Text: Theodora von Valancius vanished right after leaving the officers' deck. What could be behind her disappearance?

af0a9968-7916-4931-88ec-98d98048249f.Text: Edelthrad's reckless bravery cost him his life: he died trying to disrupt Kunrad's ritual. Put the creature the psyker has turned into out of its misery.

37294897-df8b-4a2a-a7d5-35d80e9cd05c.Text: Edelthrad was going to confront Kunrad and his heretics on the bridge. He will need all the help he can get for the counter-attack to succeed.

85115347-9643-400e-a1ef-75010754c15b.Text: The Master Helmsman must be found in order to begin the translation from the warp. He is the only person capable of coordinating the crew and guiding the voidship out of this perilous dimension.

674d347b-73df-44be-b27d-8c8eee11f983.Text: It is customary for the Lord Captain to preside on the bridge. Lady Theodora is dead — only her heir possesses the right to take her place at the helm.

cf8bc00a-7614-4d9a-acd4-09bdf567d270.Text: The bridge over the lower deck is impassable. An alternative way to the rendezvous point must be found.

812e90c0-2e0d-4676-97f9-2ea0e3d7da5d.Text: The crew need more powerful weapons for the coming battle. Maybe something suitable can be found on the officers' deck.

75072e0c-9943-44fc-8a53-45555bcb826e.Text: The door to the mess deck is stuck. There must be a way to open it.

b55d9718-7929-49b3-b17c-2ea62565d458.Text: The door leading to the main promenade is sealed shut. Explosives will be able to deal with the obstacle.

814f2d0a-173f-45c4-b7ba-2e0342757bdf.Text: Theodora von Valancius and Edelthrad are dead, and {name} has been declared the new Rogue Trader. The newly crowned Lord Captain will face new challenges at the helm of the powerful von Valancius dynasty and protectorate.

b9692caf-cb2a-4b75-b214-13eb6f6792a8.Text: Rogue Trader Theodora von Valancius desires to personally meet with the person recently brought aboard her flagship. A storm is brewing over the dynasty, so the Lord Captain has something important to share with her heir — if she ever gets the chance.

c84d709f-ea4c-4b4f-b4b5-a967b39db46e.Text: {n}This portly man's body is riddled with {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g}. About half a dozen of them are plainly visible, and the crude stitch marks on the uncovered areas of skin suggest that he has even more implants on the inside. However, he moves with uncanny agility as he offers you a deep and dignified bow.{/n}

75613516-29cc-40d1-8e84-421ada2b6f00.Text: {n}This portly man's body is riddled with {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g}. About half a dozen of them are plainly visible, and the crude stitch marks on the uncovered areas of skin indicate that he has even more implants on the inside. However, he moves with uncanny agility as he opens his arms to you in a welcoming gesture.{/n}

5707d47f-b9a6-42b0-b6eb-7019fd9be311.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, what an honour this is! The whole of Footfall is talking about your arrival! I am Reinheld Razzimus, head of the local Armourers' Guild. I'd be delighted to show you samples of our goods, if you wish?"

18f39da9-9c3e-425a-8236-8782ec885e88.Text: "Honoured {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g}, bless us in the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s name." {n}Reinheld humbly bows his head and nods solemnly along with the binharic prayer pouring out of Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-system.{/n}

e933cd76-321a-4ec3-9f3a-2c6de6cb1370.Text: "Greetings, greetings! The Footfall Armourers' Guild is happy to offer its wares!"

86bfc773-8333-4f0f-87ec-81954903670d.Text: "In a nutshell, Old Reinheld and his lads manufacture anything that shoots, burns, or otherwise hurts living things. Our goods are more of the 'plain, simple, and reliable' sort, but it's all about the service! I give every new client a smile. Bulk buyers might even get a hug. Right, I almost forgot — we also accept all kinds of simple weaponry for recycling, and we can take on individual orders if we get enough raw material. We put our hearts into what we do, and we do it well!"

2647e84e-87fe-48f6-8146-f078b7d45cbe.Text: "My Guild can't rightly claim to have distinguished clients such as yourself, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We make weapons for the undiscerning public. Still, we'll gladly accept any weapon scraps you might have for recycling — and take on individual orders, if you so wish!"

944503e7-1f22-4051-8b53-bbc4f5fe3e7c.Text: "Fresh faces in my shop! This is a joyous occasion! I'm the head of the Footfall Armourers' Guild, everyone calls me Old Reinheld! Would you like to see the best guns on the station?"

e5c7bd59-e93b-4d87-9f7a-5b0cd474cffa.Text: "Blessed are the armourers, for there can be no Imperium without them."

c40df208-3b55-46ba-9abf-bd02ce162a29.Text: "I assure you that, even in light of recent events, our stock has suffered no losses." {n}He scowls.{/n} "Some brawny lads came by to enforce a new ban — said we were not to sell anything more dangerous than a peashooter to ordinary customers. It's their way of fighting piracy, you see. But surely this ban doesn't apply to a client as estimable as yourself, now, does it?" {n}He gives you a conspiratorial wink.{/n}

1263feb8-0ec9-4e9c-9e3d-b234a267e859.Text: [if you see it bug report please] All fundi receive a +50% productivity bonus.

2ff8df1b-3b26-473c-b525-878dbcc9812a.Text: [if you see it bug report please] Affects the percentage of the colony's goods that make it to the protectorate.

2301055f-024e-4561-8abb-2a76ee40ffbb.Text: [if you see it bug report please] Accessibility

0dab9044-1c4e-4c31-8284-9946b59aabeb.Text: [if you see it bug report please] Current population (thousand people)

dc39b3a2-e814-4e7d-8008-9181c5ee7c33.Text: [if you see it bug report please] People

fa9d106f-10da-4f34-8f7d-3ecacf8b7df6.Text: [if you see it bug report please] Population

259eaf0c-ccaf-4752-b3f3-4f0ed406b323.Text: [if you see it bug report please] Free space for construction.

315dd165-9645-4557-9f56-36b7b46c40e9.Text: [if you see it bug report please] Space

afde645f-9be1-4b68-9c58-719bad497bf8.Text: [if you see it bug report please] Space

7604b0f2-513c-4b93-a5af-84b168b6c45a.Text: [if you see it bug report please] This building is not operational in the alpha version.

5124fe6c-cb4a-4f3f-ba23-e926f25d9659.Text: [if you see it bug report please] All extractiums receive a +50% productivity bonus.

80e574c4-9e4b-4743-97e9-f4b222ff2c1f.Text: [if you see it bug report please] The protectorate's building resources.

20775ead-c891-4e69-b7b6-52fd6aecbf8e.Text: [if you see it bug report please] BP

7695a246-f2d4-455d-b5cb-85e70a9e66b4.Text: [if you see it bug report please] Building Points (BP)

c41a97dd-7d53-4cf2-9656-2e7f58cc3fea.Text: "I am writing to inform you that two days ago, the discharge was interrupted by a raid launched by the Anvers gang. In the attack, three loader servitors were put out of commission. Furthermore, one cargo container, serial number FVDA1-16165, was stolen along with its contents."

fa9a80e5-f85f-44ca-b7cc-57abf793a653.Text: "No more playing it safe! Are we going to keep scaring Shadow Quarter lowlifes and hunting on our own doorstep forever? It's time to pay a visit to the rich scumbags in the Atrium! We meet tomorrow, after the second shift."

dd7645a9-0312-4a19-81ec-56057ead29d1.Text: Restore the colony at any cost

437c04bc-2f13-4286-ac16-9fbbf10b1f74.Text: Reinstate Vheabos VI as a penal world

68680c51-a421-4ed8-9e64-7adc81b3aa9e.Text: Turn the planet into a world of blood-soaked pleasures, following the Drukhari's idea

7b8097ca-1bb7-4e8f-8517-9d09e237b8db.Text: Evacuate the people and destroy the world

b10eaaa0-c45e-4788-a817-bf17cd1cae01.Text: Destroy the world along with the traitors

bdbceb0e-209c-4cad-abd8-435149fa9dbd.Text: The sanctified mountain extractiums have been obliterated by Drukhari orbital strikes. The valves that shut off the gas wells were destroyed, and the atmosphere was poisoned by toxic fumes. The meagre population of the world has sullied itself by grovelling before blasphemous inhumans. Vheabos VI is ready to accept its fate.

cdfd5ade-300d-4050-8c10-61c3a7a31f9e.Text: The restoration of the crippled Vheabos VI has begun. Hundreds of Tech-Priests and thousands of the Omnissiah's pilgrims will answer the Astropathic call. Together, singing the litanies of reconstruction and re-ignition, they will purify the atmosphere, restore the extractiums, and heal the wounds of their machine spirits. But this path will be long and costly for the von Valancius dynasty.

10eae983-39bf-4907-85a9-5727b9bd0b55.Text: By the Questors' reckoning, the average life expectancy of a worker on Vheabos VI is one month. With a filtration mask and a hundred detox tablets, this can be extended to a year. This is more than long enough for the convicts sent to the planet to work off the cost of their transport.

63e6a28c-cc85-4f6e-a379-c1736e89b82f.Text: Blood will continue to flow on Vheabos VI, but now the gladiator fights will be watched not by blasphemous xenos but by zealous servants of the Rogue Trader whose diligent toil has earned them a bit of entertainment.

59d3479e-159d-44b6-bba8-8fac596f090a.Text: The heretics, who chose to become the plaything of ungodly xenos over a righteous death, have been given another chance. The ranks of the ship's landing crews have swelled with hardened and brutal fighters, alarming many of the vessel's pious inhabitants.

93f39030-6164-4d58-8367-6274d4cb3c3a.Text: Subjected to merciless bombardment, the defiled world perished along with the tainted souls of its population. The hearts of the entire crew were set aflame by the glorious sight.

4cda980d-8beb-40ec-a439-b81628273bf5.Text: The ship called the Seven Bloody Stigmata vanished during a warp jump, though some have managed to decipher the stray Astropathic messages and determine that the legendary vessel may be in the Rikatus System.

bd6b5e17-f26c-48c2-8170-c88ebac21736.Text: Lost Void Cruiser Found in Rikatus System

59f679b8-c807-41bf-9a7b-c98319d21815.Text: "I am a serious client who is interested in bigger deals. Think you can you surprise me?"

6434cee1-e57d-4993-9bde-7006ffba81cc.Text: [Give her a purse heavy with thrones] "I would be very surprised indeed. And I would be eager to purchase it."

b117cf96-a807-4820-8e3f-703d50acf9c1.Text: "I would say that the information, the ship, and the cargo reek of murder, plunder, and dishonour. I have no interest in such things."

c5127969-5ffc-4bd1-b824-81f879be70c2.Text: "I would put a weapon to Ryzza's head and suggest that she tell me everything."

15188231-19c1-438a-8911-714335877955.Text: {n}Ryzza lowers her voice.{/n} "Let's see. Ever heard of the Seven Bloody Stigmata? One lucky birdie, that void cruiser — she plundered dozens of {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} worlds throughout the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}. But the Seven Bloody Stigmata disappeared during a warp jump on her way back from a raid, a good five hundred years ago, and nobody knows where fate left her adrift and what spoils she carries in her hold."

902755cf-4c67-4a7b-8cde-2aa71d2b2acb.Text: "Only one mad {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} who appeared on Footfall after the vanishing had a guess as to the location of the Seven Bloody Stigmata's resting place, but he died shortly afterward. Such a tragic tale."

419026db-cb27-4eb1-a7ef-8e2a6236ffdb.Text: "Now what if I told you that old Ryzza has heard a rumour about where the Seven Bloody Stigmata last stopped? Just imagine the score that the lucky finder of this cruiser could take — not just the treasure, but the ship itself too. What do you say — would you be surprised if Ryzza were to have this information?"

c63867e2-0321-480c-b3c0-5a32442199ce.Text: {n}Ryzza nods in agreement.{/n} "That would be very wise." {n}She leans closer to you and whispers,{/n} "Some {g|Encyclopedia:Astropath}Astropaths{/g} sometimes hear an odd message echoing in their heads. 'Seven stigmata... assist... stoke.'"

c416c744-55fc-40f0-84db-ed24f66cb142.Text: "That would be a real shame. Because if Ryzza divulged such valuable information for free, it'd make her associates very upset. But they're hard people, and they'd try to get over the feeling by doing what hard people do."

0f40432a-fb48-46d5-8d02-f151be96ce9c.Text: "I understand. You must be a {mf|man|woman} of extraordinary luck — after all, only the lucky ones can afford to keep their hands clean in the Koronus Expanse."

3c46c050-a521-48b4-9b1b-c1101b549d48.Text: {n}Ryzza gives you a calculating look and says tentatively,{/n} "I take it we're talking about something more substantial than a shipment of lasguns or a hold packed with obscura? I can't offer you anything at the moment, but I'll remember that you asked. I'll let my associates know."

001e8ba0-8a0c-44c2-8dcb-fd33460d8310.Text: "But let me warn you right now — they are a cautious bunch, and they don't make deals with just anybody. Only a buyer with truly phenomenal wealth could pique their interest."

5743b0ab-b486-4cc2-b236-e706eb2d5884.Text: "Mysterious, right? Stoke what? Yes, few still remember the orbital {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g} factory Stoker VII in the Rikatus system, and it was a proper pirate den once. It was... up until one fateful day when the factory stopped responding to communication and ships heading to its coordinates started disappearing."

bdc4f2ec-ec4d-4e21-98a8-c44746323711.Text: "And so the Stoke became history, and those who receive messages from the Seven Bloody Stigmata either can't decipher them or don't want to try their luck by poking their heads into that forsaken place. But you definitely have luck on your side, don't you?"

cc66cc3c-71cc-45c0-91f8-1f4f81ef7528.Text: The Arbitrator inflicts +{uip|Damage|6a4c3b65dff840e0aab5966ffe8aa7ba} stacks of the {g|f:f5c2bdd369324a0d9b7809782a7ae508}death sentence{/g} effect on an enemy. Each stack increases the enemy's chance to be {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critically hit{/g} by +1% and reduces their {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} by −2. Whenever a target under this effect suffers {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from an attack, it suffers +1 stack of {g|f:f5c2bdd369324a0d9b7809782a7ae508}death sentence{/g}. The effect lasts until the start of the Arbitrator's next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.

207d0db3-ab94-44d7-950a-0000fdca11e0.Text: Each stack increases this creature's chance to be {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critically hit{/g} by +1% and reduces its {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerPerception}Perception{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} by −2.

1abb8942-6425-425d-9831-58d280e6f860.Text: For 1 round, the Arbitrator and their allies gain immunity to the {g|Encyclopedia:ProneEffect}prone{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Stun}stunned{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:ImmobilisedEffect}immobilised{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:CantAttackEffect}cannot attack{/g} effects, as well as to all types of forced movement. Enemies must pass a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} with a −{uip|Damage|376ff1a6c0274b4e9564935e1ae9a383} penalty or become immobilised until the Arbitrator's next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.

49d008f6-2a56-42fe-b737-733de7093c6a.Text: In the Name of the Lex Imperialis!

3b214703-7dc3-47de-9dd8-c072d622552b.Text: The Arbitrator chooses a cell within a 6-cell radius. All enemies within a 3-cell radius around the Arbitrator must make a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} with a −{uip|Damage|b6e6d67ba6cb4fae9bd717b1b05b15fa} {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g}. On a failed test, if possible, they immediately move to the designated cell.

770f3e8d-466f-4f64-b6d1-7f16e1cd2c77.Text:
The Arbitrator dashes through allies and enemies in a straight line for up to 5 cells without provoking {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunityFullGlossary}attacks of opportunity{/g}. Each enemy they dash through must pass an {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerAgility}Agility{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} or fall {g|Encyclopedia:ProneEffect}prone{/g} until the start of that enemy's next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}.
! This {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} can only be used with a shield equipped.

0508b222-df3a-43c3-9cba-ca61e8f25d9f.Text:
The Arbitrator chooses an enemy within a 6-cell radius. This cell must be on the same side as the Arbitrator's shield. The {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from that enemy's next successful attack against the Arbitrator will be reduced by −50% and redirected toward the enemy closest to the Arbitrator shielded side.
! This {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} can only be used with a shield equipped.

254ff58b-0505-4691-8430-da0bf739c6c5.Text: This shotgun attack reduces the {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:BlockChance}block{/g} of targets in its {g|Encyclopedia:AreaOfEffect}area of effect{/g} by −{uip|Damage|2162ce26f6db4cd1b748a4105c364ddb}% for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}, regardless of whether they were {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} or not. {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}Damage{/g} from this attack is reduced by half.

49a7578b-8885-4272-a20c-0ae6822214d8.Text: This shotgun attack has +{uip|Penetration|027e75ab89364049b844a720feca85ec}% additional {g|Encyclopedia:ArmourPenetration}armour penetration{/g} and inflicts {uip|Bleed|027e75ab89364049b844a720feca85ec} levels of {g|Encyclopedia:BleedingEffect}bleeding{/g} on targets {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g}.

411206e0-b73c-4dd5-b151-a3014ce1a7de.Text: This shotgun attack allows the Arbitrator to make two {g|Encyclopedia:SingleRangedAttacksGlossary}single shots{/g} against the target.

1cf01558-84fe-4ebc-8b18-d0ba944e9bf6.Text: The Adeptus Arbites are the implacable and unbribable keepers of the Lex Imperialis, the sole and sacred law of the Imperium. They exact a merciless and terrifying punishment upon any who dare violate the sacred tithe, the tribute every Imperium world must pay in the name of its continued existence.

b738f530-09b3-477c-97d8-08066ca2b0a6.Text: If there are 2 or more enemies in a 2-cell radius around the Arbitrator, no {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hits{/g} can be scored against the Arbitrator or their familiar, and the Arbitrator and their familiar's critical hit chance is increased by +{uip|Damage|613246cc28464ade9845da9b30dc65c3}%. Whenever an enemy adjacent to the Arbitrator gets up from being {g|Encyclopedia:ProneEffect}prone{/g}, that enemy provokes an {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunityFullGlossary}attack of opportunity{/g} from the Arbitrator.

2612415d-72d3-4c5b-b678-7d2dd104a617.Text: An Arbitrator's order is the voice of the Lex Imperialis. Your squad was in charge of collecting the sacred tithe from debtors and suppressing any resistance shown. Your commands bellow with unshakeable confidence honed by years of service, making allies and offenders alike comply, for none dare protest when you give voice to your will. Hundreds of criminals have fallen to their knees and begged for mercy upon hearing your deafening order to surrender. All of them faced swift and harsh judgement.

666f545f-47a9-4b4d-a3ba-850143e3f8b0.Text: The Arbitrator gains the {g|f:2533d30143ec4008ae7c1b0c0919a3ad}Castigated!{/g} and {g|f:6a4c3b65dff840e0aab5966ffe8aa7ba}Death Sentence{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g} and can select {g|f:b6e6d67ba6cb4fae9bd717b1b05b15fa}That's an Order!{/g} and {g|f:376ff1a6c0274b4e9564935e1ae9a383}In the Name of the Lex Imperialis!{/g} through progression.

3e6f7967-d674-4e75-ba30-308d411f5376.Text: Whenever the Arbitrator {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hits{/g} an enemy from a distance of 2 cells or further, that enemy must pass a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} with a −{uip|Damage|2ec8e80ae4184b409a3d242fcaf0db17} penalty or suffer the {g|Encyclopedia:CantAttackEffect}cannot attack{/g} effect for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}. If the Arbitrator's attack hits multiple enemies, this effect is applied to the enemy closest to the Arbitrator.

75d9ad5f-4bf3-4be4-909d-e912cfbe7113.Text: The shield of the Adeptus Arbites separates the law from the lawless, and the truth from the detestable lie. Before your ascension, you were part of a squad tasked with keeping crowds from rioting and dangerous criminals from escaping. As long as you have your shield, you are prepared to face any threat and push it back outside the perimeter.

05a43de4-9808-4d43-b039-27470d22e3c2.Text:
The Arbitrator gains the {g|f:8c7d2be4225745e4911eb3c53c603b76}Assault Onslaught{/g} and {g|f:613246cc28464ade9845da9b30dc65c3}Ruthless Suppression{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}abilities{/g}.
{g|f:1c5f4edca9f64fe0911bc946e0b4ea4a}Shield Bash{/g} now deals +{uip|ShieldDamageBonus|3ef2ffb9a92b4e4b9cde5371644e95d1}% more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} and scores guaranteed {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical hits{/g} against {g|Encyclopedia:ProneEffect}prone{/g} or {g|Encyclopedia:ImmobilisedEffect}immobilised{/g} enemies.
Enemies suffering the {g|f:f6a60b4556214528b0ce295c4f69306e}stalwart defence{/g} effect deal −{uip|DamageReduction |3ef2ffb9a92b4e4b9cde5371644e95d1}% less damage, and the Arbitrator's counter-attacks against them deal +{uip|DamageBonus|3ef2ffb9a92b4e4b9cde5371644e95d1}% more damage.

070c48bd-aaf9-45c5-b766-1813ea1ad043.Text: Enemies {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} by the Arbitrator or their familiar deal −{uip|Damage|2533d30143ec4008ae7c1b0c0919a3ad}% less {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}. Does not stack.

64ed3b28-49c9-4d34-90c3-776df2e32fd0.Text: This creature suffers +{uip|Damage|e9fc0a90ebe8458a86c9b7db9f6770b3}% more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from the Arbitrator's shotgun attacks.

0b64aad7-159d-48d7-a4e8-f6d0d8323ed3.Text: Enemies attacked by the Arbitrator or their familiar suffer the {g|f:3a4b8214c73240de911a805fe645e624}swift justice{/g} effect until the start of the Arbitrator's next {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}. The Arbitrator's shotgun attacks deal +{uip|Damage|e9fc0a90ebe8458a86c9b7db9f6770b3}% more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} to those enemies.

a35cf24d-a131-4b24-af87-4cb26bc31915.Text: For every target, there is a bullet. Your former squad was responsible for eradicating heretics who had defied the Lex Imperialis. You learned to utilise different ammo types to best suit a given situation or take down a specific enemy. By choosing your arsenal wisely and targeting the leaders of the resistance, you always completed your objective in the God-Emperor's name.

8a2802bd-b01f-49cb-b382-24cca6b4d5de.Text: The Arbitrator gains the {g|f:e9fc0a90ebe8458a86c9b7db9f6770b3}Swift Justice{/g} ability and can use {g|f:2162ce26f6db4cd1b748a4105c364ddb}Fulminating Shot{/g} with shotguns. In addition, they can select the {g|f:def7164545244af28d52cd38d0502525}Double Slug{/g} and {g|f:027e75ab89364049b844a720feca85ec}Grisly Adjudication{/g} shotgun attacks through progression.

5534dfbc-0ecb-44b2-987c-4e64a110d01d.Text: The Arbitrators can wield two-handed shotguns in one hand.

826af4b2-677b-44b6-b2f8-84473b7fc1ff.Text: The Arbitrator can {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} incoming attacks with a ranged weapon. To calculate the parry chance, the Arbitrator's {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerBallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} is used instead of {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g}. The Arbitrator can make {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunityFullGlossary}attacks of opportunity{/g} with a ranged weapon that they can use in {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee range{/g}.

5e9199dd-c44d-474b-a251-36824e0c845c.Text: The Arbitrator's successful attacks reduce enemies' {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} by −{uip|ArmourPenalty|cd4ba7fabdd84963831c5f66af65d726}% for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}. Does not stack.

ee1cfed4-7008-4e77-9b59-d425632a7782.Text: The Arbitrator's attacks made on others' {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turns{/g} deal +{uip|DamageBonus|3b54a01fdbcb4031a47fab20f93a3a98}% more damage. The target of such an attack must pass a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} or become {g|Encyclopedia:ImmobilisedEffect}immobilised{/g} for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}.

7d201a67-b4f7-42ea-9745-3a63bd31fa9e.Text: The Arbitrator gains {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g} equal to half their equipped shield's {g|Encyclopedia:BlockChance}block{/g}.

2cfb2abc-8486-4600-85b5-57d9e084d276.Text: Once per {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, the Arbitrator can throw a grenade that does not deal {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} on impact. That action costs 0 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}AP{/g} and does not count toward the {g|Encyclopedia:AttacksPerTurn}attack limit per turn{/g}.

c8a5e4ee-39ae-484f-b3ce-898c97d8558d.Text: {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}Resistance tests{/g} have a −<u>(Arbitrator's {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCoercion}Coercion{/g} / 10)</u> {g|Encyclopedia:Penalty}penalty{/g}. Does not stack.

fae1db93-3caa-424e-ae30-de6bb2cff5af.Text: Whenever an enemy adjacent to the Arbitrator fails a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} for the first time in a {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}, that enemy provokes an {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunityFullGlossary}attack of opportunity{/g} from the Arbitrator. If multiple enemies fail this {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g} at the same time, the attack of opportunity is triggered against one of them randomly.

cec2dfbe-73f5-446f-ae8c-c2b259790e6e.Text: Allies in a 3-cell radius around the Arbitrator deal +{uip|Damage|3394e59a3d87445ca99a3b8bead0b315}% more {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g}. Does not stack.

f91d117b-3b6c-42ef-bf50-a21eb3a90121.Text: During the tactical phase, the Arbitrator can be placed in a cell adjacent to an enemy.

cb1c8067-ad11-41f5-acd2-6619648dca03.Text: As long as the Arbitrator has more than 90% {g|Encyclopedia:HitPoints}wounds{/g}, they are immune to the following {g|Encyclopedia:NegativeEffectTypesGlossary}negative effects{/g}: {g|Encyclopedia:BlindedEffect}blinded{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:DisturbedEffect}disturbed{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:FatiguedEffect}fatigued{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:PerplexedEffect}perplexed{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:SlowedEffect}slowed{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:StaggeredEffect}staggered{/g}.

26cd846a-0d3c-4efa-9b22-55ed88cc997d.Text: After the Arbitrator uses a {g|Encyclopedia:HeroicAct}heroic act{/g} or a {g|Encyclopedia:DesperateMeasure}desperate measure{/g}, they gain +{uip|Coercion|3227585cd33e4cd6b7cb24f2c23492be} to {g|Encyclopedia:SkillCoercion}Coercion{/g} and +{unit_stat|WarhammerWillpower|bonus}% {g|Encyclopedia:BlockChance}block{/g} until the end of combat.

7015b751-caf7-45cc-a473-74fa15222fb4.Text: With a one-handed shock baton or a one-handed power maul equipped, the Arbitrator gains +10% to {g|Encyclopedia:Parry}parry{/g} and reduces the {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWeaponSkill}Weapon Skill{/g} of enemies {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} with this weapon by −10 until the end of combat (does not stack). This weapon also deals +25% more {g|Encyclopedia:CritChancesAndCritDamageGlossary}critical damage{/g}.

98ae0f58-2224-496c-b947-33cfb8936292.Text: Enemies {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit{/g} by the Arbitrator must pass a {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g} or fall {g|Encyclopedia:ProneEffect}prone{/g} for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}.

98dbea5b-696a-4e7b-92e0-0c845b7f0993.Text: The cyber-eagle has {uip|EagleArmor|fe156ca111b8485cb947f85384152a07}% {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} and {uip|EagleDeflection|fe156ca111b8485cb947f85384152a07} {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g}. Its {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} is increased by +30%.

58291f78-96fb-43d5-8b62-10491bbcbfc2.Text: At the start of combat and whenever the {g|Encyclopedia:CareerOverseerGlossary}Overseer{/g} ends their {g|Encyclopedia:Turn}turn{/g}, the cyber-eagle starts {g|f:ec56854df2e84ef196a49079a43b5211}soaring{/g}. While {g|f:ec56854df2e84ef196a49079a43b5211}soaring{/g}, it regains +10% of its {g|Encyclopedia:MaxWounds}maximum wounds{/g} at the start of each {g|Encyclopedia:Round}round{/g}.

7839f805-b4b6-4cb9-aa5f-fd2b3b0698f1.Text: The cyber-mastiff has {uip|Armour|267ea941490e468aa0b6e262ea6fd171}% {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} and {uip|Deflection|267ea941490e468aa0b6e262ea6fd171} {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g}. Its {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} is increased by +15%.

46b12200-d6eb-4e84-82d2-fd484a62ffaa.Text: While moving, the cyber-mastiff never triggers {g|Encyclopedia:AttackOfOpportunityFullGlossary}attacks of opportunity{/g}.

3c93a328-3214-473a-abc4-7686098a1830.Text: The familiar's attacks ignore the target's {g|Encyclopedia:BlockChance}block{/g}.

62496a80-2759-460c-afab-f416c4deb266.Text: The psyber-raven has {uip|RavenArmor|36c3b6aec151475aa701bd920cbf227a}% {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} and {uip|RavenDeflection|36c3b6aec151475aa701bd920cbf227a} {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g}. Its {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} is increased by +20%.

bba583be-b554-4de0-92b3-32d7a6d502d5.Text: The servo-skull swarm has {uip|ArmorBonus|7b088e5f02c74a828f0b0d19bc04cee1}% {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerArmourGlossary}armour{/g} and {uip|DeflectionBonus|7b088e5f02c74a828f0b0d19bc04cee1} {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g}. Its {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} is increased by +20%.

2f79eb65-a5a9-43b5-ab39-159a8784b3fc.Text: The target gains +{uip|ChanceBonus|6f1395647e8b4f6cb47bce10d7cccd2f}% increased {g|Encyclopedia:HitSequenceGlossary}hit chance{/g} on their next attack, {g|Encyclopedia:DodgeGlossary}dodge{/g} on their next dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Test}test{/g}, and chance of success on their next {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance test{/g}. These {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} disappear independently from each other after being successfully applied.

0bcdef0a-8bd0-4ceb-8628-f49d30e86408.Text:
The Navigator decreases {g|Encyclopedia:VeilThickness}veil degradation{/g} by −{unit_stat|WarhammerWillpower|bonus} points.
All allies gain +{unit_stat|WarhammerWillpower|bonus} {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}deflection{/g} against all {g|Encyclopedia:WarpDamage}warp damage{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerPowersGlossary}psychic powers{/g} until the end of the Navigator's next turn.

1cfdc8fc-dbdf-48bd-8d12-a04901862629.Text: Allies suffer −{uip|PerceptionBonus|2d5c8abfc6ff4b2fa09971935817ebc7}% less {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from Navigator powers and gain +{uip|ChanceBonus|2d5c8abfc6ff4b2fa09971935817ebc7} to {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance tests{/g} against them.

ee9609ad-a899-4e1b-a425-848466e8d66c.Text: Allies suffer −{unit_stat|WarhammerPerception|stat}% less {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from Navigator powers and gain +{uip|ResistanceBonus|2d5c8abfc6ff4b2fa09971935817ebc7} to {g|Encyclopedia:ResistanceTest}resistance tests{/g} against them.

7bdc6921-4801-4933-9ede-3551450747a9.Text: The target ally gains +{uip|StatBonus|8b97251d56204c40904d06c927930572} to their {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerWillpower}Willpower{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:WarhammerToughness}Toughness{/g} until the end of the combat.

62bd760f-73ff-4dad-b8b7-311b77c4fb1e.Text: This {g|Encyclopedia:Ability}ability{/g} can only target allies that have at least one {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttacksGlossary}melee{/g} weapon in one of their weapon sets.
