8ef0fa4c-6983-42f6-a778-980358e96a1c.Text: A bit of rest and some good food authorised by the Lord Captain have made a great difference in the Astropaths' struggle against the warp's machinations.

0e30aac1-6a12-4aea-b763-6069f5f05333.Text: Without the protection of a powerful psyker, the souls of the ritual participants are defenceless against the harrowings of the warp terrors.

f2ec481d-3970-4b8d-ae19-5005986742cc.Text: With each fallen Astropath, the warp's power grows.

69657119-3ca5-43a7-a902-58e8d3fc1471.Text: The psychic protection provided by the Rogue Trader fills the participants of the ritual with courage.

a6f4a49e-75dc-4eb4-bb37-0b7592f7b29b.Text: The warp sees you. The warp knows you. The warp is coming for you.

a76bfcfa-1ae8-42e0-b8b9-f94d1018d00e.Text: "How did you like serving under Lady Theodora?"

f6ec60f9-e3f9-4771-a90f-cdbabf7d00ff.Text: "I was worried the maker of that confession might be dangerous. Explain yourself."

5bf22ca1-97f9-420d-b233-7ad1b0ca1fab.Text: "That odd noise inside the chapel. Does it not bother you?"

4427ff6e-1cb3-48e0-9cd9-c4778e699d3a.Text: "I have witnessed the death of one of your Astropaths. What happened?"

e57cc5c8-5143-4292-a110-1addd2b798a6.Text: "We will speak later, Choirmaster. I have business to attend to."

b110ee4f-a89e-406e-8540-b9264ad8338c.Text: "I am confused. So how old are you?"

34c740aa-f41a-4451-ad59-399f4272b7dd.Text: "I was led by curiosity. So what was your confession about?"

6ef0d408-34ef-4a18-b0f0-381e48cdeee6.Text: "So if you wanted to hide certain information from me, you could?"

a45197c4-df80-405e-a78f-a3b3ee06d721.Text: "I felt there was anguish in that confession. I wanted to help."

51d04bf4-ecc1-45c4-8884-13543bea9673.Text: "If something happens to your Choir, where can I find new Astropaths?"

1cff3175-ecc6-414f-be0b-00f6464d1aca.Text: "I will get to the bottom of that message."

4f90d918-d245-4487-bd62-3190a9274c0e.Text: Showed concern for the ship's choir by providing them with supplies.

861c7cfe-7446-41ca-a276-384b69b8183e.Text: "If your machine knows the meaning of the symbols, why can't it decode the messages itself?"

7a254027-364d-484e-b0d5-80dedfea1bf3.Text: [Point to the mechanical drum] "What device is this?"

acdd3851-eff0-4786-afca-0217ddecca6f.Text: {n}Choirmaster Zacchary Weisz, a tall old man in a long green robe, stands motionless in front of a cogitator. The closer you approach, the clearer you can hear his continuous unintelligible whisper. You are about to call his name when he falls silent sharply and turns toward you first. {/n} "Lord Captain."

d2b4d835-5b02-45ab-98c3-03c177c9850e.Text: "A visit from the Rogue Trader is an honour for us." {n}Like other {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropaths{/g} at the chapel, the Choirmaster's eyes are bandaged over with time-worn scrolls of sacred manuscripts. Nevertheless, you cannot shake the feeling that his otherworldly glowing gaze is studying you keenly.{/n} "How can I be of use, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"

ff22ce9a-21e7-421b-a9cd-b27c1ff4b3ce.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. To what do I owe the honour of your visit?"

8a54be43-088b-48c6-8f70-de2bb8867911.Text: "Something is afoot on the other side of the {g|Encyclopedia:Maw}Maw{/g}, Lord Captain. Something infinitely sinister. Something disastrous. The scraps of mental images that reach us from the Imperium carry the mark of doom. The images emanating from there are like a beast baring its teeth."

ac891d0f-18d5-499a-b0de-64a984611e06.Text: "I know a couple of places where you can get new Astropaths." {n}Idira grins maliciously.{/n} "That's of course if you don't insist on them being all classy and proper like this fried-eyed bunch."

d9c08bee-940f-43b3-b14f-7441ed80512a.Text: "I have no doubt of that, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

b0688b36-e7a2-4e2c-8ffb-bfee0cfa813d.Text: "One can never be too prudent — I of all people should know that. Thank you for your vigilance. I must give more thought to what I can do for the living. That is the best way to repay one's debt to the dead, if indeed it is at all repayable."

225b977e-46d7-41c6-b4a2-3c58ad6fe78b.Text: "To us Astropaths, this place is our cradle and our grave, Lord Captain. You are at the conflux of every secret missive, every order of prime importance, every scheme being plotted behind the scenes. You are at a place where each of your loyal Astropaths is ready to lay down their life for crumbs of information, if that is your wish."

4c2f33b6-be45-4d26-a723-5ca0a631b442.Text: "Of course, Lord Captain. Is there something specific you would like to know?"

be3b6011-c9a4-4c4f-a5a4-c12623c26758.Text: {n}The wrinkled face and drooping corners of the mouth look focused yet courteous at the same time.{/n} "My name is Zacchary Weisz, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I am the Choirmaster of the Astropathic Choir. I was posted to this ship soon after my Soul Binding ritual on {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Holy Terra{/g}. You might say I have been serving House von Valancius all my life."

1074924e-047b-4824-8f97-d225c51d3d34.Text: "I served her for two decades, and never knew another Lord Captain before your ascension. With her, I had been through..." {n}The Choirmaster falls silent, as though briefly transported in his mind to another place. A shadow of regret creeps onto his face.{/n} "...many things."

7d6f1c93-520d-44d3-b517-45b7dfb0c001.Text: "On the contrary, Lord Captain. It is a mental focusing technique used by your flagship's Choir, one that I invented myself. This music was written by an Astropath. What my charges and I hear in it is not what ordinary people hear. Its true depth and beauty cannot be fathomed without the Emperor's blessing. The music protects our minds from rudimentary thoughts, purifies, and sharpens them. But above all else, it serves as a beacon of sorts amid the tumultuous Sea of Souls, a thread to lead us home from the deadly maze."

17bc15f7-9976-4280-83ac-017628fa9748.Text: {n}The Choirmaster sighs and makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n} "May the God-Emperor rest his soul and protect him from the {g|Encyclopedia:ChaosGlossary}Ruinous Powers'{/g} tenacious claws. That was the fifth one this month. Our younger voices cannot handle the warp storms raging in the Expanse, and end up losing their minds." {n}He adds, barely audibly,{/n} "If they are lucky..."

dc04020a-919e-4d2d-aad4-d8129d6cd923.Text: "Goodbye, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The Choirmaster follows you with his otherworldly glowing gaze as you leave, then turns back to the cogitator.{/n}

e1f61de6-f3e8-4238-b107-3934926adacc.Text: "How odd." {n}He grimaces, as though with pain.{/n} "Odd that you should have listened to my confession, and odd that you should choose to approach me afterward. Why?"

be714ac7-a49f-47cf-bded-3f169dc4122b.Text: "Astropaths seldom die of old age, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Unless one thinks of the inexorable drain our service is on our life forces as an old age of sorts. More often, the warp claims us in its cruel ways, and I have... lost many a fellow." {n}He rubs the bridge of his nose, looking tired.{/n}

0f95c7ae-770e-47c6-a07f-6ed5c7820fdf.Text: "My confession made you anxious on my account, resulting in a waste of your time, for which I apologise. I am thankful for your consideration." {n}He smiles a bittersweet smile.{/n}

a3c426ae-c689-40e9-866a-43bd67e933b3.Text: "Death always keeps close to Astropaths, and its punishments for arrogance and weaknesses are severe. I have seen my fellows die, and at times the memories are exceedingly hard to bear. Sadly, almost every Choir has a story like that... and a survivor who has carried their ghosts with them ever since." {n}Weisz lets out a ragged breath.{/n} "My apologies, but I cannot continue worrying at these old wounds. Directing a Choir requires a clear and firm state of mind."

e35fee7b-a1ce-41b4-b65e-9642ed7a0a45.Text: "Lady Theodora had a good understanding of my significance within the overall mechanism of the ship's services." {n}Poorly concealed irritation creeps into the expression of regret on his face.{/n} "Which, however, did not stop her from neglecting my warnings."

06701427-eb4c-4351-83c9-9f115480032a.Text: {n}The light emanating from beneath the bandages flickers with strange hues as the Choirmaster clutches his temple. His expression shifts in a way you are well familiar with. It is the look of one who has glimpsed the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}grim signs{/d} that evil has left upon your soul.{/n}

08eac5c1-a96e-412f-9255-4a95197bd11c.Text: "My apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I sensed... a strangeness in you, and my mind reached out of its own accord. I did not see much, but what I did see was enough. It grieves me to know that this... mark... weighs on you so. Trust me, I am well acquainted with the oppressive burden of doom."

cb6efaf7-620f-4644-a6fa-82203cfb8f55.Text: {n}Weisz gives you a polite smile.{/n} "I would assume that you know the answer already, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. You have walked a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}similar road{/d} yourself, even though you took a different turn than I."

23a44f2b-b67a-4c3f-a27a-9b55ee5beb4e.Text: "Regrettably for us all, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, Astropathic messages are not ciphered dispatches, but rather psychic imprints containing information. Only an Astropath can read the entirety of something created through the medium of the warp. Furthermore, as messages pass through the Immaterium, they might become distorted by malevolent intent. It falls to your servants alone to shield their mind with faith and separate the true meaning from the influence of the Ruinous Powers."

d3eb4f3d-389f-408b-91e8-d87fedf556e9.Text: "If my calculations are correct, having factored in our movements through the warp, then I turned thirty-four a month and a half ago." {n}There is a pause. You can't quite decide if the old man in front of you is joking, but there is not the slightest hint of a smile on his face.{/n}

29471612-de4f-4acf-8953-94a2ccb9a68e.Text: {n}You have heard accounts of disturbances in the warp affecting psykers, especially Astropaths, who delve most deeply into the Immaterium. But there have been more and more alarming stories of late. {g|Encyclopedia:CicatrixMaledictumGlossary}Something is raging in the warp{/g}, something that poses a particular threat to those with psychic powers.{/n}

0b442d51-002f-43a0-85c9-b5478c851fd6.Text: {n}The warp is unpredictable and perilous — one can only sympathise with Astropaths whose duty compels them to plunge their minds into the depths of the Immaterium.{/n}

0b63d892-2cee-464c-8e34-1765a60eb458.Text: {n}Sanctioning is a brutal procedure, one which robs every Astropath of the gift of sight. But in return, they gain a new kind of vision that allows them to see what ordinary people cannot.{/n}

af26e0a5-f0a9-4516-b7ce-cc37d40e78df.Text: {n}The alien glow that filters through from beneath Weisz's bandages leaves you wondering if he actually can see you, or is he just skilfully pretending?{/n}

c07b8504-228e-45cd-8d26-7c657fc0e5fe.Text: "I do not recommend even considering such an option. Unsanctioned psykers are gateways for the {g|Encyclopedia:ChaosGlossary}Archenemy{/g}'s forces, for all the claims to the contrary made by those less knowledgeable on the issue."

187746fd-d3dd-46c9-a23c-6f8bbc427f3d.Text: "The compiler matches the images in the message against its data and forwards the results to the central {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} and myself so that I can begin the ritual of decoding. I know of no other Choir that possesses so wise a mechanism, and I praise the God-Emperor for its existence... However, while the compiler hastens the extraction of intelligible meaning from perplexing imagery, an Astropath must still open their mind to interpretation, which is no less perilous than the rites of receiving or sending an Astropathic message."

475b5746-b48b-4d91-ae6a-8ce2e93ec132.Text: "We receive and send messages. For hours turning into days, we wander the dark depths of the {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}Immaterium{/g} carrying our voice through the warp's eternal night. Bringing it to our comrades in some remote refuge. Accepting the voices, signals, and missives of others into our own abode. Those are most often meant for you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, and at times... they are meant for no one."

aa7cd7a0-adaa-41c3-be54-6546d1135821.Text: "We were all part of the Imperial Tithe once. Psykers delivered to Terra on the {g|Encyclopedia:BlackShipGlossary}Black Ships{/g}. But only a few of the candidates had what it took to study astropathy. Fewer still successfully completed the gruelling training to be eligible for Soul Binding, and almost none survived the initiation."

df78dafe-35cd-44fe-a5c7-8c5176a42298.Text: {n}He throws his head back.{/n} "We were given the privilege to behold the Emperor's light, a light flawless and searing." {n}A pious smile visits his lips.{/n} "That changes you. It wounds you irreparably, it takes your eyesight, but in exchange... you commune with greatness. His presence in our souls fortifies them as we stand against malicious powers."

0066c76d-12cb-4e68-8ba2-a2036a426e39.Text: "After the ritual, an Astropath is assigned their position. At this or that Adeptus, an Astropathic relay, or a ship. More often than not, our first place of service is also our last."

4ac2f8c3-0353-48d5-bb08-70807ba93358.Text: {n}The expression on his wrinkled face grows even more serious.{/n} "It would be more on point to say 'when' something happens. The Emperor's blessing protects us from the warp's various influences. However, there are horrors dwelling in the void for which even this defence would be no obstacle. Especially if one spends as much time in their company as we do."

b6f60878-b89e-4caa-b1d3-3550bf47169e.Text: "There is only one way to procure Astropaths, and that is through the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Adeptus Administratum{/g}. Luck permitting, unattached Astropaths from the sector will be posted to the ship — ones who, for whatever reason, have lost their place of service. Failing that, the request will go to Terra and we will have to wait. A long time."

f263dce4-9ee7-4e85-9ed1-d5a10be6d2ed.Text: "That said, there are other options. Blasphemous, forbidden options." {n}The Choirmaster grimaces.{/n} "Unsanctioned psykers. Unprotected and broken souls who seldom live past their first few seances. But even those would do, should the God-Emperor put our souls through severe trials. And judging by how rabid the warp has been of late, by the number of dead Astropaths, those trials will be upon us sooner than our prayers could reach Terra."

6306aed6-b050-4312-847b-9aff8e7a017a.Text: {n}The Choirmaster replies, slightly perplexed,{/n} "I beg Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s pardon?"

9149c9ba-ae60-4cab-9a19-e43656e9f46a.Text: "It is a sacred compiler that helps us record, store, and, to an extent, unriddle messages. The Astropaths first receive these messages in the form of muddled images, dictating what they see to the machine, which logs their every word. From the reels of the receivers on the ceiling, the machine-recorded words are routed through lines under the floor into transcribers and then the thesaurus core. This core is the most important part of the mechanism, as it contains a vast catalogue of various symbols and the methods of their interpretation."

b8e97271-ee15-40ea-8b0a-af40fced254c.Text: "I suppose you have a better idea of that than I do. It is something I have never thought about before and on which I hardly have an opinion worth sharing, Lord Captain."

ad4824bc-1322-41a0-a7e0-cb61cfafb95a.Text: {n}Weisz's face twists into a bitter grimace.{/n} "My duty is to shield you from the monstrous communications that filter through the warp. The screams of the Emperor's loyal servants, centuries dead by now. The nightmarish, maddening images of the {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}Sea of Souls{/g}. The cursed symbols that cause Astropaths to convulse in violent fits of frenzy. The messages from abominations in search of weak minds to devour... Concealing all of that from you is my duty."

1cbe246d-fdf1-4c0f-af92-e927c731f23e.Text: "We can find a psyker who will help you perform the ritual."

693f050e-59a6-4e53-9078-443040e76edc.Text: "Could it be a message from Voigtvir?"

83a11ba0-7f78-4ae6-bdb3-5793db0301c0.Text: "Reconsider what? I have not asked my question yet."

4f41ec8c-755e-48d8-b678-dcd123be8341.Text: "Get out of my thoughts, Weisz. This is your first and last warning."

d3091fa0-8298-4fb0-a3f6-1f134e52a222.Text: "So you would rather not take part in the search for mutineers?"

30c20fef-0d71-4168-8f27-c48508d90872.Text: "We are about to do something dangerous."

be138b15-7340-4acf-bac6-51b7c5d5d327.Text: "Why are you so worried about the ritual?"

8a427cff-b8ed-483a-9f9b-746f7b209c5f.Text: "I have no time for finding you an assistant, Weisz. Start the ritual at once."

bd5be6a1-6312-4218-90fe-7e85814eb655.Text: "Get in touch with Vistenza Vyatt, Governor of Janus. I am summoning her to me."

8ce75aa9-bc3e-491a-b145-f79dd440b1a7.Text: "Heinrix is a psyker. He could help."

0932bed3-e9f5-4dd0-b876-4418f7d7d9fb.Text: "I could help you with the ritual."

00d4c7f7-f4b9-4e14-8804-1e8ef139dc88.Text: "Trust me, Vistenza possesses knowledge that will prove most useful."

2840c8ad-eaf2-4afc-b085-572c8c4dcd77.Text: "I trust Idira and am appointing her your assistant. This is non-negotiable."

ed5cb0a4-a3c7-4a53-883d-b56e9f6218a9.Text: "I will be helping you. Commence the preparations."

454072cd-f8da-4eff-8b67-db1e704999e8.Text: "You mentioned knowing a powerful psyker employed by the Winterscales. Who is he?"

12f310fa-24cf-4f5d-a59e-ed88d72ea809.Text: "Did your journey to my ship go without any problems?"

1060f868-708d-4880-ae64-32486f058292.Text: "Has Master Weisz briefed you on the task?"

a41f3525-6098-4bca-9f7a-f71044df245a.Text: "I will deal with the report. Right now there is something else I want to discuss with you."

ce229e46-a545-4121-95c2-fa0fc30f4432.Text: "What is the nature of this ritual?"

7877c6d9-a656-42dc-bf44-3bf0a5dfd48d.Text: "The important thing I am interested to know is, was the ritual successful that time? Did you find what you were looking for?"

d76242e0-2ebf-4b59-a7c8-1d4359134043.Text: "You blame Theodora, but it was on your watch that the ritual led to a disaster."

c8a9a39b-cdd7-4c7d-86af-cf3df9d3bcf9.Text: "It is fair to say my predecessor was being herself there."

ea4664c0-0cdf-4c26-b8ab-dd79af90153b.Text: "How is a ritual like that even possible? It is akin to heresy!"

b9972115-d1d9-4481-beda-98846157f473.Text: "My orders are not up for debate."

79f50259-88e7-41fa-8aa8-019ac4f36893.Text: "Fine. Have it your way. Let us discuss other options."

b8bdb710-6c37-4380-8dab-f67d1b6fccb5.Text: "You must tend to your Choir. I shall have good food, recaf, and relaxing balms delivered."

2f56680e-816c-428f-82fa-d11fb86dcffe.Text: "Yes, I do have a few acquaintances with considerable experience in abduction. They charge but a modest fee for their services."

8eea17e3-9dea-4353-8e70-8a5fd5915490.Text: [Raise your weapon] "What is this? Insubordination? You have your orders, Choirmaster, and you will follow them. Not one step back!"

29336668-0ab0-4aa0-871a-1446a29b8e15.Text: "I am reluctant to risk my life for this ritual, and the search for the rebels has become quite tiresome as well."

5a012c83-22dd-461f-ac36-4516a812c8f0.Text: "No, Weisz, wait. If this really is our only chance to find them, then we must not squander it."

c2f40f69-0c03-4441-8b25-6b43327d0e8f.Text: "I am not going to waste any more time or effort trying to find the mutineers. To the void with this investigation — I have enough to deal with as it is."

af4c9a88-ec2a-4ed1-9de4-01a4408e3a26.Text: "I will hire professionals to set up his escape. Send a message to whoever ought to know."

5be6be2b-f70c-4be8-a3bb-84609cfcb145.Text: "So you say you have performed the ritual before for Theodora?"

3c31458f-6290-4cf9-8026-89bc282c7f89.Text: "We will find a more honourable way."

2d285393-0a68-487c-a88a-a2d7a86e7d09.Text: "I need to give it some more thought."

60c457e2-f13c-4555-aef9-6666318fef8e.Text: {n}The strange sensation passes as suddenly as it arises. The Choirmaster shakes his head.{/n} "I know why you are here, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. And with all due respect, I am asking you to reconsider."

e54f0de3-56da-466f-8b3f-b91d5b4d4056.Text: {n}Choirmaster Weisz turns toward you long before you reach him. A chill runs down your spine, as if someone were watching you from inside your own being.{/n}

d085efd4-61e0-4bed-b23f-665d648f307a.Text: "Worse than you can imagine, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It only took a fraction of a second lingering inside another mind for one of the Astropaths to lose control of their own. The affliction spread down the chain like fire. No one was spared. The minds of my charges could not withstand the tension. Their consciousnesses were caught in a vortex of alien thoughts. The fortunate ones died at once. As for the rest..."

b6fcb600-b86e-47b5-a82e-8929fd3a1fa4.Text: "Many years ago. It was a time when Lady Theodora had become... anxious. Perhaps the Lord Inquisitor's interest in her affairs adversely affected her, shall we say, trust in her own subjects. She was expecting a betrayal, and eventually her paranoia brought her to me. I performed the ritual, but the Choir... ceased to exist."

1a19b322-7aea-493b-866f-80f9446cee1d.Text: {n}You feel a strange anxiety as the old man's burnt-out eyes seem to probe your inner self.{/n} "Your intentions are fairly easy for me to infer. You are looking for mutineers, and the only reason you would come to your Choirmaster is to order me to turn to the warp for answers."

eca3ce4e-6a92-4679-af42-df80b285710b.Text: "I cannot say with certainty, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Following the repair work, I went through texts that had defied decoding before. This signal had lost its way in the bowels of the mechanism. It could be a week old, or years."

b060129b-0552-42f8-9647-725923ee45b6.Text: "Your predecessor came to me with the same orders once. Nothing good came of it. Please believe me, Lord Captain, when I say a mountain of corpses was the least of the problems we faced that time."

1fc49e87-ce48-4c68-9f3f-5fe870c1797d.Text: {n}The Choirmaster makes a wry face, as though you have caught him doing something reprehensible.{/n} "Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It was... force of habit. I swear I will never again intrude upon your mind's peace without permission."

d68f23d5-37ad-4064-a7ae-0a61c3c17e76.Text: "And that is glorious, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! A thousand thanks to you for liberating me from my former master! Living at the court of Governor Iskandor is... indescribable. The {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}Immaterium{/g} itself whispers ideas for new perversions into his disturbed mind. Therefore, I am infinitely grateful to be delivered from him. My life belongs to you now."

e22a2d0a-2253-42f0-89e5-b6c148c9ac66.Text: "You saved me from a life of service that would have been a hundred times worse than the cruellest of deaths, and I am indebted to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. If I have to lay down my life to repay that debt, then so be it."

b640e37f-da7e-4b1c-ba24-6cdb4b68ad2e.Text: "It is my wish to be useful to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but what you have come for... will put the ship in peril. A ritual of this kind can — and certainly will — go the worst way possible."

daf1ffdd-14bf-4122-8941-fb64237962ea.Text: "Lord Captain, do you know the proverb about staring too long into the abyss? What you are asking for is tantamount to plunging the entire Choir into that abyss. A ritual like that will require incredible focus from each of its participants. It will take a single careless thought, a single glance in the wrong direction, for the way back to be lost. Human minds fusing into one another, vitrified organs inside still-living bodies, perverse fantasies manifesting in the flesh... Nothing will stop the horrors of the warp from spreading all over the ship in the blink of an eye."

2bad16c8-9b07-46d4-944e-63898bc09d7f.Text: "And even if I agreed... it would be impossible. I would need a second powerful telepath as a defender to shield my mind. The last time, my best apprentice, Adeline, did that, but she is no longer with us. She was exceptionally talented, rivalling... even myself. Now I know of only one psyker in the entire Expanse who is her equal, but he is bound to the service of one of House Winterscale's planetary governors, and thus unavailable to us. Which makes your dangerous enterprise an impossibility."

40c889c8-3bc6-477d-a987-e3744b217d36.Text: {n}The Choirmaster's face is twisted into a mask of horror, which quickly turns into a grimace of wholehearted anger.{/n} "This is a mistake, {name}. You have no idea what you are dooming us to! Dooming this ship! And your dynasty!"

06cd733c-ae19-47a4-9563-26ad0fff7e1b.Text: "Absolutely not!" {n}This is the first time you have ever heard the Choirmaster raise his voice.{/n} "She is a witch... an abomination! She will only make the situation worse! The beasts of the warp will sense her heresy-prone soul and descend upon us in droves."

e516dd33-0e22-4c90-840f-1435309471d4.Text: "You have signed our death sentence." {n}Weisz's anger almost seems to ignite his otherworldly gaze, making it burn right through you. However, his face does not stay contorted with fury for long. There is a distinct coldness to his voice as he says,{/n} "Well, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... Bring your witch here."

95768766-c6ae-4413-ac24-425883ffd6cc.Text: "Why, the abyss will do so much more than stare at us today. We will be throwing stones into it and begging it to devour us." {n}The Choirmaster speaks the last few words with the bitter smirk of a condemned man who has just been told the day of his hanging.{/n}

eb649a8a-8046-4525-9004-9004321626a7.Text: "Will you look at that! The great Choirmaster, scared of my little whispers!" {n}Idira breaks into trills of laughter. Her mirth almost seems excessive.{/n} "Stop shaking, will you, old man. I'm gonna protect you and your bulgy-eyed pals from what's behind the door. You'll thank me yet."

475d6295-b60e-4215-a525-ea1b3f13feee.Text: {n}Weisz frowns, clearly tormented by dark suspicions.{/n} "I am worried by all this reticence and omission, but... I will not presume to argue with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The journey from Janus will take some time. I will report back when Lady Vyatt arrives."

e74cf8e5-6163-4fc9-b077-f4a6fba4e7da.Text: "Master van Calox is a brilliant biomancer, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but, as far as I know, he is not particularly adept at telepathy or psykers' protective rituals, is he?"

3be5f278-d7d1-4237-87c2-13ba0c0740ac.Text: "He is right, {name}. I know some of the fundamentals, but this isn't my primary field."

b8de2ed7-2d91-4bbb-9739-ab05d69932bb.Text: {n}Weisz chews his lips, as though tasting your words.{/n} "I suppose you could, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. However, I would not dare put your safety at risk. What kind of a Choirmaster gets their own Lord Captain killed?"

37823151-31f5-428f-a1eb-258a8f207241.Text: {n}Weisz's smile has a hint of condescension.{/n} "With all due respect to your unquestionable talents, Lord Captain, I need a psyker capable of working with a specific branch of psychic knowledge, that being telepathy."

27c13c4f-2c82-461c-a4be-8c4ef67c9015.Text: "As you please. Master Herimon will welcome the news of his forthcoming release. His present lord is quite... unpleasant. I will report back once Master Herimon has been brought on board."

6ef9acf4-45b0-4f96-a208-63afff034261.Text: "Lord Captain, I do not for a moment doubt your powers, but I insist that you refrain from taking this unnecessary risk."

bd6a926c-3174-4720-93a6-45b099807c92.Text: "My little whispers are crazy excited at the mere possibility that your precious head will be the next one they get to drop by. You might want to think again if it's really what you want."

d958b09a-c626-472b-aa43-f3d0714ec9a3.Text: {n}The Interrogator looks at you with unabashed curiosity.{/n} "Considering the combat experience we've had together, {name}, I'm sure that if anyone is up to a challenge like that, it's you. On the other hand, is it really worth it to tempt the {g|Encyclopedia:ChaosGlossary}Archenemy{/g} when you don't have to?"

e6ddba92-c252-40dc-b94b-1093c7f78a83.Text: "The Emperor would not send a gruelling challenge to one who was not up to it. Sometimes the thorniest path is also the most righteous one."

231c26ec-42ff-4584-b7a0-7d1bd603f654.Text: {n}The Choirmaster's face grows gloomy. For a long time, he stares at the floor, saying nothing. Finally, he raises his head to look at you. His much-wrinkled face is relaxed. A reverent expression has come over it, and there is a hint of a smile on his lips.{/n} "So be it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

e74d2f1d-1b36-47d4-8d14-66bcdb6f3ff0.Text: "Master Herimon is a seasoned telepath, but his lord would never part with such an incredibly valuable specialist. A sizeable amount of money will be necessary to organise Master Herimon's... escape."

be92cf60-e148-45eb-9895-5a4d928bcfe4.Text: {n}The Choirmaster raises his eyebrows.{/n} "Lady Vyatt? The governor? As far as I know, she is not a psyker."

e84f2871-e296-466d-a095-66c83e653d6c.Text: "Lady Vyatt has already begun to prepare for the ritual." {n}Weisz points to the dark red inscriptions in an unfamiliar language.{/n} "I sense a strange and distant power in these glyphs... An otherworldly, unholy might... And I pray to the Emperor that you know what you are doing."

703ea469-dee6-4af9-b964-08b9d0bcc8ae.Text: "Master Herimon, assigned to the chapel upon your orders for the purposes of performing the ritual, has almost finished his preparations, Lord Captain."

fad97512-b8be-4472-86fa-418d8e7cae1c.Text: {n}The Choirmaster lets out a deep sigh.{/n} "Well. You made this choice, Lord Captain."

22dc7bc7-d80f-400c-ab4d-35ccbb9a3a9a.Text: "Lord Captain. Do you still wish to perform the ritual?"

98b3efe2-b09e-4c3f-911f-d7e7a8f28243.Text: "I managed to send out a call for help and did my best to contain the phantoms on my own before Lady Theodora arrived. I was the only survivor out of the entire Choir. Her Ladyship allowed me to spend a month in a secluded cell upon whose floor and walls I drew the most powerful protective hexagrams I knew. I was crushed. I was broken. And, worst of all, I was afraid. Afraid of meeting the same fate as Adeline and my other apprentices... An Astropath must never be afraid, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. One who yields to fear dies and dooms those around them."

711a3533-6640-4b3d-af68-feb52ab55316.Text: "Oh yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the Choirmaster has described the ritual to me in a wealth of detail. I might even say a slight excess of it." {n}Vistenza smiles coyly like a card-sharper at a gambling table.{/n} "I am familiar with certain techniques that could... curb the {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}Immaterium{/g}'s rapacious interest during the ritual."

48ca96e2-8988-4039-8d95-b2e996f6339e.Text: "Thank you for this opportunity to serve for your dynasty's benefit, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Vistenza bows before you with a radiant smile.{/n} "Your invitation was incredibly thrilling. I do not often get a chance to leave Janus."

a3e9ada5-ae7b-4156-a0de-7f119cbc9ca2.Text: "Greetings, {name} von Valancius. I will be honoured to serve my saviour." {n}A middle-aged psyker bows to you passionately. His plump face carries many marks of indulging in all manner of vice.{/n}

d2b2bb76-1403-4bc4-96de-0eb66cc7bceb.Text: "Lady Theodora bombarded the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Adeptus Administratum{/g} for months with requests to provide her with a new Astropathic Choir. In the end, new voices did fill the chapel. They were never told what happened to the previous Choir, but... they have inklings. And I pray to the God-Emperor that they never find out the details of that tragedy."

eee209da-9e34-400f-afe5-eab6623ce5c0.Text: "That is the harsh truth, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It must not be done."

af03cd77-fcd3-4900-bb81-50187629f924.Text: "I remember that day, Lord Captain. When we arrived at the chapel, there was blood and human remains everywhere. But that was the least of the terrifying things we saw there."

f77f6503-ee52-45ac-b269-bf58469b8d7f.Text: {n}Argenta makes the sign of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g}.{/n} "Protect the souls of the stricken and take them under Your wing, that Your faithful servants may find peace..."

42c78678-94be-47a7-9f9a-29f71e94d692.Text: "Most certainly, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! The chartists who took me here were quite forthcoming and... attentive to my exacting tastes. But most importantly, they were fast, as I wouldn't dare keep you waiting for a second longer than necessary."

5c2f9551-2f57-4645-81a2-f0e353e96283.Text: "Only a few words. 'Lillamedh. Odaenathus XI. The winds have ceased. It is done.' Now 'Lillamedh' is Voigtvir's call sign for special reports, but the rest is a code we are unfamiliar with. That said, we know where to look for the truth: the Odaenathus XI System."

d8a6919b-c1f0-4765-85a3-5597ee934f77.Text: "Pity..." {n}The Choirmaster's shoulders go limp and his face resumes its usual sullen expression.{/n} "I was hoping that curious dispatch would distract you from the dangerous idea that brought you here, and I would not have to implore you to reconsider."

49ad97cb-73ee-483d-9248-ebb936836415.Text: "He was more likely the intended recipient."

56b507bd-00fa-48e2-b643-04d2895b4859.Text: {n}Choirmaster Weisz starts the conversation before you have opened your mouth to speak.{/n}

8f525549-7176-49e2-bdd6-89791d4cf86d.Text: "It takes the entire Choir's power to invade such a prodigious number of minds at once. I weave their voices into a chord and steer it into the murky sea of other people's souls. Together, we read tens of thousands of thoughts, emotions, and intents, looking for the thing we are after. The seed of corruption you are interested in."

348fe4b6-105b-4a3b-a256-3b78127e6310.Text: "I—" {n}The Choirmaster cowers, as if cornered.{/n} "I did find it. But the price... The price! Yes, Lady Theodora got the names she wanted, but was it worth it? The tragedy has remained a secret hidden within the chapel — but we were a hair's breadth away from it becoming an epitaph inscribed on the ship's remains."

8b7e015e-995f-4070-8613-3d7474c2707c.Text: {n}Weisz is silent for a few seconds, his face lowered toward the floor, his hands trembling.{/n} "You are right. I do not absolve myself of my own guilt. And may His punishment strike me if I forget about it for even a moment."

a3afc21d-288c-4ae1-a61f-4f81c6086e46.Text: "Please, Lord Captain, learn from her mistakes instead of committing your own."

5a728389-6de4-4d8b-84e8-8ffb2afee1a1.Text: "It is not heresy, but it is indeed a dangerous tool that will only yield to a mighty hand. That time, things were going all too well. The Choir was many-voiced like never before. Adeline and my other talented apprentices sounded louder than the rest of Astropaths in all of the Expanse. We were strong and confident enough to take a bold gamble, and we lost."

670f1445-198d-4f30-9e3e-ecf6eea808cc.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I have something for you." {n}The Choirmaster hands you a sheet of paper with uniform lines of machine type etched into it.{/n} "Thanks to your assistance in repairing the compiler, we have been able to interpret a most curious message. It contains a call sign that agents of the renegade Voigtvir used in their especially important reports."

d24683a2-cf7b-47aa-aa00-61ec4182f8a5.Text: {n}Weisz frowns gloomily as he listens to Vistenza's equivocations punctuated by glowing smiles. Shadows of dark suspicions have fallen on his face, but he keeps a mournful silence.{/n}

d9dffac0-7f6b-4a31-ad27-2c8c9b1b8003.Text: "The Lord Captain helped me {d|Encyclopedia:CompIdira_DamperOn}overcome{/d} my curse, old man," {n}Idira says coldly through her teeth, and drums her fingers on her psy-stifler.{/n} "This thing here protects me from the warp, which means I can protect you as well... if you ask me nicely."

ebefc993-d4e0-4df6-88f5-b0bff6b2fb55.Text: "The Asuryani spend decades tempering their spirits before touching the veil. You lack the gift of time, yet you seek to harness powers that are only too pleased with your ignorance."

a2f28369-8e87-4f4f-b2de-1772cd96e586.Text: "I appreciate your concern. Perhaps these small indulgences will give them strength and save someone's life."

711286ac-e551-43dd-9720-b65e8c24f6ef.Text: "Perhaps you have some {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}useful contacts{/d} at your disposal who could assist the unfortunate Herimon with his situation."

e37c2adc-e46b-471d-ae7c-63ec569b3a37.Text: "And who is it?" {n}The Choirmaster's smile, though courteous, seems ever so slightly sarcastic.{/n}

44897495-bac5-4b92-938f-a2ec78d49b4f.Text: {n}You summon your will and drive out the unpleasant sensation. The Choirmaster smiles sadly.{/n} "You shroud your mind well, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, and yet I can guess why you have come. With all due respect, I am asking you to reconsider."

b9180648-fa3d-4ca1-b12d-69bffb59ed12.Text: {n}The lines on Weisz's brow disappear.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I realise that this ritual may be your only chance of finding the mutineers, but is their plot so threatening as to risk dooming the entire vessel? I do not think so."

5d002cfd-dcd6-48ca-838c-ecc43d45a490.Text: {n}Weisz bows solemnly.{/n} "As you will, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. By your leave, I will return to my duties."

13b6ada0-d985-4513-9f0d-adeea94d29d4.Text: {n}Weisz freezes with his mouth agape, then grimaces in irritation.{/n} "I should not have said anything. I... dare not object to your will. However, I must remind you that performing the ritual is impossible without a psychic protector."

0bfcbdd2-c898-4b5e-a279-1486f185e440.Text: {n}Blood begins to seep out of the corners of Idira's eyes.{/n} "The poison of the undiscovered mystery is eating away at the steel insides and the lifeblood that courses within them. Within kindred flesh lurks a strange mind, waiting for its prey to fall asleep. What is tomorrow worth, O child of Humanity? Rouse the slumbering trouble and find out, or else carry on in ignorance until you lose yourself." {n}As she regains her senses, Idira inhales sharply, then glances sideways at you:{/n} "Do think it over, Lord Captain. We're on the verge of letting the last thread slip from our hands. And if my little voices' whispers are anything to go by, without the ritual, things will get very bad."

94d95de0-9bea-42f5-8731-8ebeec8f90d1.Text: {n}Heinrix casts a tired and almost irritated glance at you.{/n} "There have been millions of people who neglected to remove a hidden threat — and were themselves removed from existence before their due time as a result. Do you value your dynasty? For that may well become the price of indolence and cowardice. Perform the ritual."

d501ec2c-33f7-4a78-9d39-45824daadf1e.Text: {n}Jae's expression becomes unusually serious.{/n} "I'm not keen on toying with the powers of the warp either, shereen. But ignoring the raised dagger in an enemy's hand is an idea I like even less."

8b8b1a77-e767-4c38-a237-18eb9622e7fb.Text: "Internal strife and lurking enemies stole my home from me." {n}Despite her efforts to hide it, you notice a slight tremble in the Lady Navigator's voice.{/n} "If that ritual can uncover the threat, then we must act on it. Better to accept the imminent casualties as a necessary sacrifice than to lose everything altogether."

f5d2ec0a-516a-4eab-97c8-afc65de48dae.Text: "Domin, the Undying One's will has led us to Veni'Zacchary, and He bids us walk a path that is both narrow and bloody. If we stray from this path now, our mark will disappear forever..."

b5e9ee41-915a-4a5b-87ae-1d83f801f585.Text: "That means we will have to cancel the ritual." {n}A faint hopeful smile appears on his lips.{/n}

be38392c-ca0d-4ee7-a7a3-5bb106c411bd.Text: "That would be in order, considering all the dangers of the ritual."

b350d4bb-2b4e-4b01-b967-5dedbd38bd62.Text: "Why are you all crowded next to this thing?"

10ac0311-795f-4bdc-b677-7029bbd5f775.Text: "I should rather say it was my efforts that helped make the machine operational..."

22083913-98a7-404b-ac7c-7ea50c51a86b.Text: "How lucky we are that the venerable Tech-Priest is so pious and wise!"

260d5e3a-e689-428c-9022-479fe1ddac09.Text: "You dare question what I say? Servitorise him!"

610163c3-3b95-487e-a781-ad7a683f35f7.Text: "Why, such a trifle of an error..."

31267a53-67a0-4131-adeb-bf0c61ba695e.Text: "Get everything working fast or all of you will be demoted to the lower decks."

8483d8a5-c0ab-43e8-956f-7bd5b375aa41.Text: "Let us see if there is any way I can help."

a7a833e7-1250-4b59-b6f8-81e8e962d73a.Text: "I will leave you to your work."

f515b0d7-d08f-452a-bacf-83fa8be2680e.Text: "But I have fixed everything, have I not?"

8b4fb62b-6f64-4b2d-8f6d-64c1098f6169.Text: "If prayers have not helped, a sacrifice will. Throw this loafing Astropath into the bowels of the machine."

33ba18b4-7a84-4770-bf0e-2622e645f2c1.Text: "Then your praying has been too feeble. I order you to begin a collective prayer to the machine spirits."

a4ef38f8-954e-4cf5-9db0-a8a9b84a765c.Text: "I have had enough. Deal with your cogwork issues yourselves!"

8c5bf166-86fb-4587-a0e7-58223ba1765b.Text: "Protect us from the machine spirits' unrest, for without His gifts our sacrifices are fruitless..." {n}You can barely hear the voice of the young {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropath{/g} standing very still next to the bulky mechanism, his face frozen in a mask of despair. His anaemic hands are pressed to his chest, clutching crumpled strips of thick paper. He hears you approach and composes himself.{/n}

582d5e50-36ee-42b1-b1bd-ce647306f3cd.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g}, his head lowered, does not so much as glance in your direction. With his hands folded underneath his robe, he makes a barely audible, unpleasant sound: a prayer in {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g}.{/n}

b0483c31-c252-46b1-bfc7-980810857d5f.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} rises proudly to his feet and says in Low Gothic, a language he clearly has not had much practice in,{/n} "With sacred words and virtuous thoughts turned toward the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Machine God{/g}, I have been able to pacify this mechanism's wayward spirits. The Omnissiah blesses!"

944008c0-28ba-4cc1-862d-8ebdb2393726.Text: "The sacred compiler is ailing, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. A gloom has come over the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g}, and they are disrupting the mechanism's operation. The twelfth row of the drum is now adding incorrect symbols..." {n}The man shows you a stack of papers, and you notice at once that the rows of squiggles in each line all end with the same glyph.{/n} "We summoned the servants of the Omnissiah, but the machine spirits are none too eager to heed their prayers..."

6586b67c-774a-41c7-9cea-a99621177797.Text: {n}The Enginseer stares at you sullenly.{/n} "False. I record a three point eighty-four percent decrease in the mechanism's efficiency as a result of the Rogue Trader's manipulations. I also record several blasphemous violations of the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation."

c7d94a9b-ac55-4fb4-a00b-3ce234f928b3.Text: "Unit Sigma-AR87 is currently in a tech-trance of shared comprehension with the spirit of the {g|Encyclopedia:ArcheotechGlossary}archeotech device{/g} catalogued under the name of 'Streamspindle.' Disturbing the unit is not recommended." {n}Pasqal falls silent for a few seconds.{/n} "However, a preliminary diagnostic has revealed several algorithmic faults that are in conflict with the sacred mechanism's processes. A practical intervention into certain cycles will likely aid the release of the accumulated burden."

84783636-cf3b-407d-80d2-5c6658b613fa.Text: "It will be done, Lord Captain. Initiating a ship-wide summons of locally available {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} units."

60995825-8d44-41a7-8c36-7ebf14331aa7.Text: "The esteemed Enginseer is in a state of tech-prayer trance and hasn't moved from the spot for a day now..." {n}He shrinks his head into his shoulders timidly.{/n} "I had the audacity to think the sacred compiler could be better helped by examining its parts... but who am I to question the secret knowledge of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}?"

6cdc62fc-79d5-4dc5-9db7-4e2c59f0d780.Text: {n}The Enginseer eyes you respectfully but with very sincere and poorly concealed confusion.{/n}

9a2cc607-8e5c-413c-a8d1-80f1cbac8305.Text: {n}His head bowed and his shoulders twitching, the {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropath{/g} cuts a sorrowful and anguished figure.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... the sacred mechanism, it..."

43eb7620-41b0-4da1-96ca-51c9dbb40b75.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} rises proudly to his feet and says in Low Gothic, a language he clearly has not had much practice in,{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} have rejected my pleas. The sacred mechanism will continue in its cycle of suffering."

2a7188e2-301e-4a31-a922-f0b4d80cb43e.Text: "Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but I do not know the answer." {n}The Astropath lowers his voice to a whisper, glancing at the praying Enginseer.{/n} "I'm afraid even the Adeptus Mechanicus don't fully comprehend the workings of this mechanism. We're only knowledgeable on the surface-level machines: the receivers commit the messages to paper, the transcribers sort the mental imagery by semantic category and feed it into the thesaurus core, and then the sacred compiler supplements the messages with a list of symbols and their interpretations. However, the mechanism extends far deeper, into the bowels of the ship... Therefore I wouldn't even venture a guess at the possible source of this trouble."

0a8c28f6-c156-4a4f-998e-f175c56f696c.Text: {n}The Astropath is shaking. He bows to you hurriedly.{/n} "Thank you for your invaluable help, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I will make sure to tell Master Weisz that everything is working again!"

5cb4c251-7686-4b5c-b5ba-7c5aee0623de.Text: {n}Horror twists the Astropath's face.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I implore you! I will work harder! I will pray more fervently!"

b1c7d75f-5b90-41b1-a09f-bdac62a570e3.Text: {n}The Enginseer's facial augmentation emits a series of clicks.{/n} "Estimated likelihood of successful machine spirit placation by sacrificial means: greater than zero. It will be done, Lord Captain."

accfe43d-a694-4bbd-ba6c-9501682b7732.Text: {n}The young man exclaims in astonishment,{/n} "Imagine a single extra character creeping its way into the coordinates for a warp jump, and sending the flagship to the centre of a star! Imagine the word 'disloyal' becoming 'is loyal,' resulting in thousands of your faithful servants falling victim to treachery! Nothing is a trifle to an Astropath!"

d30023cf-6215-454c-bba5-5e52802e1c42.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropath{/g} smiles at you — the shy, awkward smile of someone unused to smiling.{/n} "The sacred mechanism is working again with no disruptions!" {n}With a trembling hand, the psyker hands you a strip of paper with smooth rows of etched characters, this time containing no errors.{/n}

02ecfc48-5f3d-4f9c-8358-31b9858d4b9b.Text: "I recommend installing two incense-burning units in this compartment to prevent the spirit's continued anger. The unit Zacchary Weisz will be provided with a list of minor recommendations, one hundred and forty-two in total, for improvements to this compartment's maintenance. Failure to implement will result in sanctions on the part of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} priesthood."

f9d7ef16-cce5-4885-832b-6e4b44179687.Text: {n}The Astropath grows pale.{/n} "Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! It's a... regrettable necessity..."

f70e060a-833d-4f3f-abf8-cd83ba908ae5.Text: "Choirmaster Weisz, I order you to banish the warp spawn!"

016b05a7-854b-4dbf-824a-5b183cfc3d65.Text: "Adeline is dead, and so are the rest of them. Live with your guilt. Do not let it consume you."

acef9e4f-89cc-4caf-9bd3-f60387690195.Text: "What about the other voices? Were they your apprentices as well?"

dbf4ccd6-2ad0-48ab-8d70-1c965c0c167d.Text: "Zacchary Weisz, I find you guilty and condemn you to death."

d675de1f-1bdf-4493-aeb7-7533be9a669e.Text: "You do not deserve absolution. Your service will continue."

4ce0285a-c910-48b3-91c5-18499d6083f4.Text: "I will find your Adeline and bring her out into the light."

c228935b-9ed7-42f5-9ef8-e5954af25c18.Text: "If you got your freedom, why did you stay on the ship?"

ce74c84c-6d72-4a26-8876-23d6de9d2551.Text: "You must help me heal Kibellah, Weisz."

504b668b-75d0-4244-a205-eef49f7645bb.Text: Helped Zacchary Weisz overcome his guilt.

6c897ea1-d728-46f6-80da-c0d88e4cbc2e.Text: [Touch Weisz's hand] "It's not her. You cannot wallow in your own guilt forever. There are people, out there and in here, who depend on you. Living people."

254b14f9-1cee-4943-813d-63a28a220aa0.Text: [Grant Weisz the Emperor's Peace] "It is a Commissar's duty to subdue an out-of-control psyker. The Emperor protects."

9f2b2f90-37a9-45b5-b6bd-2f81db29e8fe.Text: "You have already condemned yourself to years of torment. I cannot give you a new punishment — only forgiveness. And you must forgive yourself."

154bb19e-e6d7-4b66-94a9-1cd27959abab.Text: "You have not allowed the warp to break you, and I believe the Emperor's light is strong in your soul. Continue your service, for Humanity needs you, and in duty you will find redemption."

757f063e-602b-42ef-a5d3-f4bce85a5421.Text: "Your ambition was worth the risk, you were simply unlucky with your students. The weak are destined to be stepping stones for others on the path to knowledge — accept this sacrifice and live without regret."

270bd169-4081-4c51-b26d-c8b2cc581b68.Text: [Address the shadows] "What twisted creature are you?"

96b5bfd6-00ff-4854-beff-a9b2b2b46211.Text: "Astropath, remember the golden radiance of Holy Terra. Remember your own oaths. He wants you to be steadfast."

279f481d-443c-45bc-8d2d-2e008405aafc.Text: [Execute Weisz] "I am sorry, Weisz. You have left me no choice."

9df8b04f-eac6-4f42-ab43-dacc2fdfba56.Text: [Execute Weisz] "You are clearly the problem here, old man. And I cannot put the ship at risk."

4020b9cc-bbf1-409e-9df1-323d892dba4b.Text: {n}An unpleasant heaviness grows in your head, as if a vice were slowly tightening its grip on your mind. The Choirmaster is kneeling, his burnt-out eyes peering into the void. He raises his head, and you see a weary old man, weak and frightened. He whispers,{/n} "She is here. Adeline has returned. She is asking me for help. But you... You scare her. She is hiding from you. You will not harm her, will you?"

751092e8-856c-488d-8fc5-301d98d6ae49.Text: {n}Weisz's breathing is laboured.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The burden was too heavy for me to bear." {n}On the verge of fainting, he musters the last of his strength to sit down on the steps.{/n}

32ad0108-f8ff-48a8-b201-88a53e2a67e6.Text: {n}From every direction, every shadow, comes playful girlish laughter. At times it transforms into an old man's rueful weeping; at other times, into a deep growl of annoyance. The sounds form cold, malicious words:{/n} "The sorrow will be eternal."

93da96e3-62e9-4840-9438-1db795fc0487.Text: {n}The mocking laughter of an old man turns into a moaning whisper:{/n} "I am the victims. I am the murdered innocents. I am his guilt!"

310cd821-7447-432d-aa93-0aca70497771.Text: "The rest were my voices. Antonius was the youngest. He had been in the Choir for only a short while. When the situation turned dire, fear got the best of him, and I... was infuriated by his weakness. I dominated Antonius's mind and impelled him to use up every spark of his life force for the ritual. Annis's doom came even earlier. She was the one person who told me, in front of the Choir, that the ritual was madness. In my anger, I ordered her {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitorised{/g}. I believed I had to protect my authority. She died on the spot where you're standing now. I think she was still aware..." {n}More scarlet drops seep through the Choirmaster's red-stained blindfold.{/n} "All my voices... I remember the name of each one whose life I cut short within these walls."

16a59f83-c205-4a92-9a4a-8a2da9395163.Text: "That is for the best. I can no longer carry this burden alone. With Lady Theodora dead, the thought of my crime being forgotten, erased from history, is unbearable! I want to be judged and condemned!"

d98e47a0-f7af-4364-8efb-6a53479a46a9.Text: "Not all of them. Stavros was the oldest in the Choir — he had been on the ship even longer than I. Mighty, wise man, if acrimonious. He envied me and criticised my ambition, but I was fond of him all the same. Thaddeus was the ship's confessor. Theodora had insisted on his presence. When it was over, he was the only other survivor, and he confronted me with angry accusations. I could not bear to listen to him, so... I silenced him. Killed him."

0b512bc8-2b9a-4cbe-b76b-d975a2603014.Text: {n}Tears of blood are streaming down the Choirmaster's face, dissolving what was left of the inscriptions on his time-worn blindfold. {/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

870c4534-e51f-4e86-add9-69be3d31e81d.Text: {n}The Choirmaster lifts up his blood-smeared face toward you. He says faintly,{/n} "You are cruel. But I bow to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s will."

2dad8cce-471d-4c98-8608-17cfa1739dfd.Text: {n}Weisz's expression is a mixture of pain, horror, and grief. He lowers his arms slowly.{/n} "I... know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I know this is not Adeline, but an echo of the one who devoured her soul. I just wanted to see her again, hear her voice again for a brief moment." {n}With jerky movements, as though shaking off shackles of ice, he picks up his staff.{/n} "Ghost of my failure, now is your time to vanish."

d4e457d1-cd20-4dbe-b41f-62b83b015855.Text: "She is no warp spawn!" {n}Weisz howls in desperation.{/n} "She is my apprentice!"

fb7d269e-8968-4d86-bc40-d676cb3bee50.Text: {n}The shadows croak hoarsely in an old man's voice,{/n} "Why do you seek his redemption? He was always a terrible leader and talentless mentor! He doomed everyone!" {n}The indignant tremble grows into a roar of righteous condemnation:{/n} "He was arrogant! Having no notion of his own wretchedness, he did not put his faith in the Emperor, but instead believed himself to be invincible!" {n}The voice grows weaker. It is now a young man's, soft and full of anguish:{/n} "And he paid for his mistake with our lives... It was cruel and painful."

3c0eefeb-d3e3-4eb8-9c94-651e8bb3e615.Text: "I see her with my own sight, unknown to ordinary people. She is as alive to me as you are, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

0a8fa051-ce5b-48ce-b070-abbd47f1d9b9.Text: "Light? There is no light here, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, not anymore. Only shadows of the past."

b908a878-eb88-4d97-ab50-7ab918ed3eed.Text: {n}The ghost stares at Weisz mournfully. The muffled sob coming from the apparition almost seems to take physical form as it drifts toward the Choirmaster and envelops him.{/n}

c5a598d1-339f-4f4b-8f89-5cab4d25236c.Text: "Sevitia was an ordinary servant. She fought the Immaterium's monsters until the warp began to prevail. She tried to save me, to lead me away, but I did not listen. She stayed at my side until the last moment and died a terrible death... all because of my accursed pride."

bc631714-0a33-4716-b557-57ff4ae3197a.Text: {n}The Choirmaster's mind fades swiftly and eagerly, weary from suffering, and the otherworldly horror lurking in the shadows dissipates. No longer do the daemons who haunted Zacchary Weisz reign supreme in this chapel.{/n}

380cc297-edcf-434a-93d7-6a72e4265746.Text: {n}The voice grows heavy with a metallic clang:{/n} "We begged him to reconsider, but he took our minds away as punishment." {n}The shadows' speech is now gentler and more feminine:{/n} "But we were loyal to him regardless. We tried to save him even though he had not saved us..." {n}The voice becomes cold, resonating with sorrow from beyond this world:{/n} "He is guilty."

bd732f86-0800-4430-ba63-4755cd5d8ca0.Text: "I am guilty. I wronged them. I had been promised a great future at the Scholastica Psykana, for my talents were exceptional. But fate would not have it, and instead of serving on {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Holy Terra{/g}, I ended up here in the Expanse, where barely a gleam of the {g|Encyclopedia:AstronomicanGlossary}Astronomican{/g} reaches. My pride took a heavy blow, but my spirit was not cowed. I set about to assemble a Choir unlike any yet seen here. A mighty, resonant, astounding Choir. Lady Theodora expended tremendous resources bartering with captains and governors to procure Astropaths of my choosing. I brought together talents and budding geniuses under my authority. They were to ensure I would make a triumphant comeback."

fed19013-ed77-4c66-a088-4821262fa1bb.Text: "A reckoning, Lord Captain. A reckoning for my great arrogance. Daemons have been pursuing me for years, following my scent, sending me dire messages, hunting me... And now they have me. The entities that manifested here during the ritual were banished, but a lingering echo of their presence has latched onto the shadows. It has sprouted in the darkness and pounced upon my mind."

190af5b4-edb2-43e4-b844-07d44b6c1923.Text: "At first, Lady Theodora wanted to have me executed for what had happened, but then she regained her composure and graciously agreed to honour our deal. But... where was I to go? My dead were all here."

8ea3ca42-591a-4445-a1ee-f01634b01525.Text: {n}After a long silence, he says in a hollow voice,{/n} "In a bodily sense, yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

e101e5a0-c66b-47ec-8e22-dbffea9ec84b.Text: {n}Weisz merely covers his ears with his hands.{/n} "Please... I am guilty... Adeline!" {n}The Choirmaster is unlikely to be of any help in this state.{/n}

b57e170f-f959-42bc-a72f-ab6c86375b80.Text: {n}After a moment's hesitation, the old man holds out his staff to you.{/n} "Please take it. This mighty instrument is the last reminder of Adeline and the others, of my guilt. It was with this that I performed the last ritual. I have no right to carry it any longer and would like it to be yours. A reminder of the painful lesson my pride has taught me."

d3650f47-6b61-4ea6-a630-09300eaf45bb.Text: {n}The Choirmaster raises his grief-stricken face. The droplets of blood trickling from under the bandage land on the deck with a ringing sound.{/n} "Your words... are medicine for my soul, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

6f0ca6fa-50d1-4444-b87c-d1550781bf6b.Text: {n}The Choirmaster grips the Aquila on his belt so tightly that the gold wings draw blood from his fist.{/n} "You... are right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Wishing to abandon my post is cowardice and an offence against Him."

b5697808-b80b-4030-890b-5f6ee08cac8f.Text: {n}The Choirmaster falls silent for a moment, trying to make sense of your words.{/n} "It is true. They are dead, and to follow them would be to undo all I have achieved. Thank you for believing in me. I will not fail Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} again."

e74f232c-ba03-4c8e-ae86-05cbbc53c715.Text: "Adeline? She is there, in the shadows..." {n}A tortured sigh escapes his feeble body.{/n} "Many shadows lie. The true ghosts are hiding among the false ones. But I hear... I hear! I hear Thaddeus's earnest prayer and old Stavros's words of disappointment — he always doubted my talents as a mentor."

8c552074-2147-4a6c-bdf4-f39c97104cb4.Text: {n}Weisz mutters incoherently, consumed by his frightful reverie.{/n}

337f005d-7c5e-41bc-a257-e746ce35d00d.Text: "I hear poor Antonius's scream... the scream he let out when he unwillingly gave up the last of his vitality. Annis's pleas — I condemned her to an existence as a half-machine. I can even... I almost sense Sevitia's touch. She tried to save me, but she fell instead. So many voices, all condemning me for what I did! Find them... Separate the true voices from the false echoes!"

56476faf-4da8-4fb8-b2a0-ae7ef77a7e96.Text: {n}Argenta's scornful laughter cuts through the sinister whispers.{/n} "Sorrow? To perceive corruption is a triumph, for once you perceive it, you can eradicate it! Cower, blasphemous spawn! I hear your voices, and I follow the trail!"

9f30d184-1d4b-4dce-9df2-5b7d84b4bf93.Text: {n}Marazhai hisses, glancing at the shadows anxiously.{/n} "I can almost feel the claws of She Who Thirsts clamping around our souls! The sooner we leave this place, the better. Have your servants void this compartment once we are gone."

39318a8c-44f7-4a4b-9c7c-cec657d6189d.Text: "The whispers keep saying we should kill old Weisz. They're just so giddy about it... I guess we shouldn't kill him, then? The whispers never get excited about anything good."

d2d78722-eccb-4bc4-bbd0-eed36ede15ba.Text: "His is such a terribly wounded soul... It has all but sunk beneath the grey-blue blisters of guilt, and they are swelling ever so rapidly. The last silvery speck of hope could fade at any moment."

65b89604-aeb3-4f07-bf3a-970adde1440d.Text: "And they could do that for me, that team of brilliant Astropaths whose talents were honed to perfection. Adeline, Annis, Antonius... Every one of them surpassed myself as I used to be. I saw that my time was coming, and... I lied when I told you it was Lady Theodora who had forced us to go through with the ritual. The idea had been mine. When, in her paranoia, Her Ladyship set out to find spies aboard the ship, I made her an offer. A ritual that would give her the names, in exchange for my fledglings' freedom and my own. It was... a good deal. She was willing to trade seven Astropaths for the names of traitors. And I doomed them all. My pride killed them."

43d7925a-2acf-47a4-b9b6-6e9538ff1e29.Text: {n}He chuckles bitterly, and scarlet stains bloom on his blindfold made of sacred manuscripts.{/n} "Adeline was my ritual protector, only to become my greatest vulnerability. When the mad stream of other people's thoughts started to disorient my Astropaths, I became frightened for her. I hesitated, I wanted to spare her... and I lost control. The right thing to do would have been to sacrifice her, but... I couldn't. I had always had a soft spot for her. Her genius had made her my favourite."

63bda794-9763-4c01-9b63-89f887913e96.Text: {n}Weisz blocks your path, extending his arms in a gesture that both calls for restraint and pleads for mercy.{/n} "Do not harm her! Please! The poor girl is frightened to death! Let me talk to her! I cannot fail her again!"

fb93dd52-92be-4d36-8be1-c599d42d000a.Text: {n}Weisz says nothing. His otherworldly gaze is directed through you and past you, to a spot further inside the chapel. His lips silently whisper a name over and over.{/n}

51538e1a-9dc4-4e37-9378-87ede7ec9b15.Text: "What in the Throne's name just happened?"

19a920b8-c0f2-4206-9863-51adcfb1c90c.Text: "You deserve a reward for your excellent performance."

172fe68d-e8bb-4322-9a6e-f7f8fd8ac778.Text: "Inform the Master-at-Arms of everything we saw. Let her search the plasma drive chambers and find the mutants and the old man for me."

1ec0815f-8b28-47fb-8715-34c6ed65a1c9.Text: "I will go to the plasma drive chambers myself, find the old man, and have a conversation with him."

fba8652b-8273-4cd8-a8ce-42b7f97766ca.Text: "You still managed to discover the evil we were seeking."

b1528270-d246-4b36-9094-4ec2425032ae.Text: [Gently support Vistenza's elbow] "Are you unwell? Please allow me to help."

ee9a1163-62d9-4f67-aa49-d3782b80da9f.Text: [Frown] "Vistenza, Vistenza... You may know a few things about how to grow turnips, but rituals are definitely not your forte."

8b461503-64d5-4400-a4e9-ee397d64f0d8.Text: "Let us return to the matters at hand."

e2bb4f90-980a-4262-898a-1983d4807405.Text: "What are we dealing with? Some kind of defensive measure? Sorcery?"

f0af082a-67bc-424b-968d-c2d766570cfe.Text: "Be my guest and rest properly before your return to Janus. I will see that the Factotum attends to your every whim."

b51547cb-7f05-4e39-a0e2-bf7ffd84073a.Text: "I wish to nurture your thirst for knowledge. Take some tomes and scrolls from the chapel for your personal collection."

e408a10e-5c82-4a82-8332-49898999dfaa.Text: "What are your thoughts on the ritual?"

a15c2c65-0c2f-4b92-b71b-9d59052848a1.Text: [Remove a ring from your hand] "This is a token of my favour, Vistenza. Let all who see it know that you have earned my trust and occupy a special position among my noble subjects."

e4ce0dcd-ef25-4e71-af90-1700e223c4e3.Text: Gave Astropaths to Governor Vyatt for her unholy rituals.

0660b282-b03c-4929-9a40-dfd37e18f891.Text: "Choose a couple of Astropaths to serve you. I'm sure they will prove useful to your research."

88c6659c-db90-47b0-9e07-504008412934.Text: "Was that old man a mutant? One of those we were looking for?"

15e313e4-7c50-49c2-96cc-00455de0bafd.Text: "Anything touched by the warp must be disposed of."

6c62a169-ba0e-4cb2-ac2d-9d0d5e4eb0c3.Text: "A symbol of faith shining through the breath of the Immaterium is a good omen. I shall wear it."

3494ca64-4155-4885-aa54-0b312de1f353.Text: "It is a symbol of my victory. Give it to me if you are unable to see this inspiring trophy for what it is."

2df2b2bb-fda0-4042-8131-1d021318b1db.Text: {n}The temperature inside the chapel is dropping. Every breath turns into a cloud of vapour. The Astropaths' resonant voices blend together, following the pattern of the melody playing in the hall. Every now and then, muffled moans are heard coming from the thrones of the junior Astropaths.{/n}

bde4abe0-690b-4375-b6f1-2a0662153517.Text: {n}You hear an interloping voice in your head, like an echo of a distant echo.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I sense... Strangeness... Non-minds... They do not seem human-like... How strange... They are akin to... insects... Parasites! I cannot read them, and that is... wrong! Look!"

cb06fa9d-8340-4f56-86c2-7a78d43985cd.Text: "Even if not, there was nothing more chilling we could have possibly found. An inhuman thing in human form. A true sacrilege against the Emperor. Its mind is strange, like an insect's or a parasite's, but... I saw images in the minds of those around it. Currents of energy. A blue glow. The clanging of metal... Could be the plasma drive chambers? That is where I would start searching for signs of corruption... and a worm tormenting a star." {n}Weisz touches his cheek, which is smeared with blood that is trickling from under his blindfold. He uses the blood to sketch a perfunctory image: a many-beamed star with a fat, fanged creature coiled in front of it resembling either a larva or a serpent.{/n}

ae383221-faa8-4873-961a-1f866a7d99df.Text: {n}Weisz lowers his head further.{/n} "The insidious spawn thrive on confounding one's reason. They donned the faces of those I once held dear. My apprentices. All of whom perished... the previous time I performed this ritual. They have haunted me ever since — in my dreams, in the warp, everywhere. The Immaterium abominations who devoured their souls have been tormenting me with shame and regret, and now they have come for my sanity as well."

0836bd25-890c-44c6-a587-41d1b98b33eb.Text: {n}She lightly leans on your arm.{/n} "Oh, please do not be worried — I have been to social gatherings that were more exhausting than this ritual." {n}Vistenza laughs softly, but the weariness in her eyes contradicts her words.{/n}

1743c5d5-1173-4bcc-b0c9-f9ed3a7f04bd.Text: "Your praise alone is a priceless gift, and as a faithful servant of the dynasty, I must not desire anything more." {n}A coy spark lights up in her half-closed eyes.{/n} "And yet it would be a grave discourtesy on my part to reject your generosity."

abf3f22e-7c33-4a94-9175-841f546eb368.Text: {n}A dark veil clouds your vision, only to be succeeded by a blinding light a moment later.{/n}

2b0d4fc5-eaa4-455e-a2cd-6ec0f1218c9d.Text: {n}A hand is laid on your shoulder. For a second, a golden flash breaks through the ruthless white light, and you hear a fragment of a sentence:{/n} "...brace yourself..."

30713f4d-36a8-4057-9851-7d0060225116.Text: {n}The great whiteness is the ship with its multitude of minds, of which you are one. A shadow of utter Nothingness winds its way across the blinding white.{/n}

5dccce69-fb14-4a15-b55c-bab57a94ec07.Text: {n}The Nothingness turns into a beast's fanged mouth. Its boundaries spread out as though trying to devour you. Your instincts are screaming, "Run! Run and hide!"{/n}

b4f793c6-9b02-4cf7-92e0-f87902b05475.Text: {n}You hear the Choirmaster's voice coming from a distance, but cannot make out a single word. Your gaze slides along an iridescent thread that has crossed the Nothingness. Something shining is towering behind it: a golden giant frozen in place like a statue. A sudden jolt of fear distracts you from that image. Your thoughts turn back toward the Nothingness and its kaleidoscope of absences: no colour, no emotion, no thought. In its furthest depths, there is something crawling...{/n}

6591da2e-8c91-402e-9b16-a45eab146dd1.Text: "It had clearly been warned that we would be performing a dangerous ritual. That we would be vulnerable. So it sought to sabotage us by attacking my mind. And my mind almost got us all killed."

486add07-54af-4d06-b430-62763af2d6e0.Text: "No, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Weisz shakes his head grimly.{/n} "The ritual proved incapable of extracting anything of value. This evil chose to reveal itself and attack. Our enemy is confident and bold, and so it did not hide — it struck first. Suspiciously brazen..."

a811bd82-55a0-4eb4-aa15-2e679de03984.Text: {n}Balanced on the brink, your gaze falters and slides down into the depths. Billions of pitch-dark non-minds stare back at you. A shapeless mass of wrongness. Purple worms of aberration encased in carapaces of otherness.{/n}

52c6dfa3-8641-4e7c-96f7-09afa7fcf9c7.Text: {n}Your resolve is firm, and your mind and soul unflinching. The Nothingness has no power over you. Your eyes follow the thread toward the golden giant. It is not until you get close that you realise that the radiant image is a lie. The gilt flakes away, and the stately body is twisted out of shape as its limbs grow extra joints, mutilating the marvellous figure... A beastly fanged face with a repulsive wormlike tongue turns to you. Its eyes, burning with Nothingness, penetrate your soul. Thoughts, secrets, wishes, goals — nothing is spared as the abomination rummages inside you like a predator gutting its kill.{/n}

333f5e1c-cff2-447d-bf47-d94688fb96ea.Text: {n}The Nothingness cackles and croaks,{/n} "I see you." {n}It assumes a vague shape: a man shrivelled by age and infirmity, his eyes alight with an alien purple flame.{/n} "You have been looking for me..."

4940743a-937e-43a6-ac6c-2137075428ca.Text: "That... thing took the shape of an old man and attacked me. I do not know what it is, but it is neither human nor a psyker. It is something else. Its power is foreign and inimical to me, like a shadow that obscures the shine of the Immaterium's chaotic energies. I was unable to read the abomination's thoughts... and it seemed to find me no less strange than how strange it was to me. Thus, it attacked, for any strangeness is a threat."

457da112-87a9-49bb-a453-fe3700d55c9e.Text: "No. It could be the emblem of some cult on this ship, but I seldom leave the chapel and have never come across it before."

cf440c35-7aba-492e-8b97-bd12a892cd8c.Text: "We sacrificed some of the soundness of our minds to the Immaterium today. I hope it was not in vain and will help Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I..." {n}He winces in pain.{/n} "I still cannot believe we survived this."

6f8ee401-f139-4517-a5f3-09080f3670c2.Text: {n}You sense the attention of something else, something beyond this entity... the Ruinous Powers. The ritual has made your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}soul, marked as it is by the curse of the warp{/d}, more vulnerable than ever before. You can feel the daemons clawing at the thin veil, hungering to reach you.{/n}

09aea3f6-91af-4c41-b846-fa0176732ce2.Text: {n}Weisz slowly unclenches his hand, and a cloud of frost rises from it, revealing his Aquila, now bound in purple psychic ice. He whispers,{/n} "The Immaterium has touched it... the holy symbol of the Protector of Mankind." {n}He pauses, then adds in a gloomy voice,{/n} "I do not know if this is a symbol of our victory over the horrors of the warp, a trophy claimed in battle... or a grim portent left by the wicked spawn of the Sea of Souls."

781c710b-8bde-4908-82c5-3f928b63447f.Text: "Nothing can shake Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s spirit. May this Aquila bring you good fortune. I will have a new one delivered to me immediately." {n}He looks at the Aquila with sorrow.{/n} "If only everything that the Immaterium takes from us was so easy to replace..."

2b0606fa-a3e3-4f1d-baf6-0cf22c6ba17e.Text: "Of course, Lord Captain. The tainted item will be destroyed. I will have a new Aquila delivered to me immediately." {n}He looks at the Aquila with sorrow.{/n} "If only everything that the Immaterium takes from us was so easy to replace..."

dd759333-e545-41fc-b461-6cd51ff533b4.Text: "I feared that inviting Lady Vyatt would prove to be a fatal error on our part. Never before have energies of... another nature been entwined with the Choir's harmony." {n}The Choirmaster is clearly anxious, choosing his words carefully.{/n} "By the Emperor's grace, we survived. But I urge you to remain vigilant: there are perilous currents in the ocean of knowledge."

e27b99f3-b8ce-4cac-bfd0-d82f794bda8a.Text: "Master Herimon's assistance was instrumental, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. He was able to not only protect my mortal body, but also to skilfully blend the timbre of his psionic sound into the harmony of the chorale. I regret that he was not at my side for the last rite."

74cda394-abe9-4702-9a4e-5b4da799de35.Text: "And it is primarily thanks to you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Your telepathic prowess became a pillar of the chorale's shifting consonance. I must confess I have not encountered such powerful psionic weaving in a long time. You have a rare gift."

f9daa94d-dd1b-44cc-ba05-f5f39e346fd9.Text: "Nor can I fail to thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, for the favour you have shown the Choir. {d|Encyclopedia:AstropathCare}Your gifts to the chapel{/d} have bolstered the soul of every Astropath, given them the strength to fight, extending another lifeline in the darkness."

7b4cc0db-1919-4430-8961-3c5247f5f566.Text: "And we were doubly fortunate, given the vulnerability revealed in Mistress Tlass's soul. We nearly became the latest chilling legend of the Koronus Expanse — the ghostly vessel in whose groaning bays roam unquiet souls."

aa4e205f-998b-4635-a4a5-602014578199.Text: {n}A moment of silence, then words of prayer stream from his lips in a monotone, like a quiet lament, a dirge for the departed, a bitter confession. When he continues speaking, his voice is full of strength:{/n} "Yet we escaped disaster. The warp did not take our souls, and there are far fewer casualties this time."

f64870c0-9503-44fa-bf33-c96702aeb84c.Text: {n}The longer you listen to Weisz, the more convinced you become that the warp manifestation was not caused by the conniving of the Ruinous Powers, but by the efforts made to discover an incredibly alien mind. Such an unnatural mind could belong to a dangerous xenos.{/n}

f576c62e-4898-4130-acb1-ed1a5e27efaa.Text: {n}The warp manifestation and Weisz's confusion may indicate that a powerful servant of the Ruinous Powers is lurking on the ship, wielding hitherto unseen sorcery.{/n}

dc4ceaf1-9af9-44f8-b2fe-8346064b8268.Text: {n}The Choirmaster awakens with a sharp breath.{/n} "Lord Captain. We... are still alive. The God-Emperor has protected us this time, but... Curses, did I not warn you?" {n}The old man shakes his head dolefully. His pale fingers are clutching the Aquila adorning his belt.{/n}

73b3db6f-cdff-4b55-b4f9-336af213ddba.Text: {n}When the Choirmaster speaks of his fallen students, there is lingering pain in his voice. His words reflect more than just a terrible memory — they are heavy with the bitterness of personal loss, or of guilt that eats away at the soul.{/n}

34018e49-9778-4532-8e3d-87441834fd05.Text: {n}The Choirmaster seems deeply frightened by how deviously the Ruinous Powers overcame him the last time.{/n}

da871213-d341-4754-b8ac-1997b4436d3e.Text: {n}There is a feverish gleam in Vistenza's eyes and a smile plays on her lips, but her face is strikingly pale.{/n} "I wouldn't dream of complaining, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} — it was an inexpressible bouquet of emotions. I must say, such exhilaration was missing from the languid molasses of my court life. But the greatest of all is our intoxicating victory. It was... incredible! If I close my eyes, I can still see your silhouette standing there, radiating power and confidence." {n}The governor sways slightly, either from weakness or out of sheer emotion.{/n}

cc39f4c2-34ea-424d-8e37-5ff6dcd29069.Text: {n}Vistenza recoils as if you had cuffed her, but instantly regains her composure and responds with impeccable politeness,{/n} "I am exceedingly regretful at having failed to meet Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s expectations. I will welcome any opportunity to redeem myself in your eyes."

2399cc62-ce16-4f84-a78f-524ae1bcb6f5.Text: "Of course, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Vistenza offers you a graceful curtsy.{/n}

ae34c226-93ac-460a-a7e3-de096f58f227.Text: "No, this is not my ritual!" {n}Panic rings in the Choirmaster's voice inside your mind.{/n} "This is his spell! An invasion of our minds! While I was seeking it with my power, it found us with its own! And I... cannot stop it! I cannot force it out of our heads!"

86ed8232-1fff-46d8-92b4-25bf8b945c21.Text: "I'm trying! If it can influence me..."

7cd5e410-9433-4edc-b2ea-5d4af6aaa2ff.Text: {n}The Choirmaster's voice sounds inside your mind.{/n} "I... cannot see them. I cannot read their minds. I cannot see into their lair. I see only images, fragmented and sinister. Forgive me, Lord Captain, but we took this risk in vain."

864e66f5-ad10-4aa7-8f43-18ae976d3b8d.Text: "Not sorcery. Something else. I have never encountered... minds like this before. Something about them is... wrong."

2267448e-63fa-477e-950b-1092720b86bc.Text: "How? I cannot sense it, I cannot..."

4e887277-b49f-403f-9046-f1a6932be122.Text: "Master Weisz has spoken at length about the risks, and I have seen first-hand the level of skill and stamina the rite demands. But I am certain that the benefits we may derive from it are worth all the dangers. And for a discerning mind, such a ritual presents a treasure trove of possibilities."

33485a52-aa98-4a76-b05b-2a160f5d5b8e.Text: {n}Vistenza presses a manicured fingernail to her lips, looking intrigued.{/n} "I have very refined tastes, but I'm sure your ship holds many delights that will revive my weary spirit... I cannot wait to see what the flagship of the Rogue Trader has to offer."
