No one is allowed inside save for the Lord Captain's personal retinue, and they dared... But how? The crypt's defences are impenetrable..."

2f9ae551-d8b7-4a58-ab03-fca31148ccbb.Text: "I wouldn't say that these improvised webbers are that much better than fighting with bare hands, but... until we are done with the clean-up, every enforcer will carry a combat knife fit for cutting through nets."

35cace29-787f-4fcc-bc86-a5444d0cc54d.Text: [Gesture at the bruises on his face] "Einrich, who did this to you?"

0d92e302-a687-4170-9516-0bc0b83f8d49.Text: "Infernus Master, what exactly are you doing here?"

3452aeca-3352-496e-b68c-9c10c563199b.Text: "Nije, have you ever seen a symbol that looks like a serpent in front of a star?"

92627389-31d7-4b73-84af-3b682e21360c.Text: "We shall set an ambush near the caches — sooner or later someone will come to check on them."

3884fb26-7c1e-40a2-833a-2291449d25cb.Text: "There was an old cache hidden under one of the serpent symbols."

27328d99-5deb-44bd-823e-4b2e1254f955.Text: [Show the note] "I found this in one of the caches."

d4557728-b89d-4942-ae00-52bfa6edd3b8.Text: [Show the improvised webber] "I found this in a cache marked with a serpent."

d86d214b-7ecb-4385-9e74-a60ce214a453.Text: "We shall conduct a raid. We'll turn the place upside down, but we'll find them."

f7116d5f-300e-4a58-8106-bfa9a720a7f9.Text: "Nije, shall we have your people lie in wait?"

cd529292-363c-47a1-a256-6c4f094cc9de.Text: "I would like to have another look around first."

b0633fca-dea8-4cb8-b700-385bf3451969.Text: "I am ready. Let's catch that vermin."

4e79224f-015e-4674-998e-ad09ef11e213.Text: "Then we'll use the inferni. They often carry out inspections here, no one will suspect them."

a3a8c312-258e-4972-9e86-3002c60971cb.Text: "Infernus Master, the shift foreman and I shall handle this without you. Return to your duties."

82c6b381-ac96-4fc9-b7ca-201bde0fafc8.Text: "I want to know more about this bay."

3e46b973-ec0d-450c-b115-5654c5040cad.Text: [Nod at Einrich's bruises] "How is your face?"

237a8734-99d7-454e-8a06-3e190f93fb04.Text: "Shift foreman, tell me about yourself. What kind of person are you?"

6de6cea3-d29b-44cd-b39e-2a5c492db7ab.Text: "We need to find and capture whoever set up these caches and hid the weapons."

e76d0360-9c80-45ea-a88d-3c586e8015f0.Text: {n}The light from the Infernus Master's lho-stick reveals his surprised but amiable expression. Einrich's lip is split and a fresh bruise is blossoming on his cheekbone.{/n} "Lord Captain? Didn't expect to see you in this compartment. Are you out on a stroll, taking in the sights of your domain? The blue glow of plasma is especially striking at this time of the watch."

f3b09661-5979-493e-a3ab-0c2a218af3f7.Text: {n}Einrich rubs his grazed knuckles.{/n} "A little gift to remember the enforcers by. We've had a small disagreement. They thought they had the right to beat and starve innocent people while investigating the incident in Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s bathchamber. I thought their noses were too straight and they had too many teeth. So, we politely exchanged opinions."

6829d28a-36c8-480b-aae1-8abf2bb35ca9.Text: "An enforcer's baton is pretty sturdy, but not as thick as the skull of a hard-boiled infernus. I have to give it to Jocasta, her officers earn their rations. They clobber you good."

6f37d617-df81-4205-8638-c035e3b04d8d.Text: "As Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} wishes. I might as well carry out a bay inspection, then, since I'm here. I won't interfere in your business."

07b50ad2-973f-4d29-9bcc-9bf3a00d6928.Text: "Found me out, have you?" {n}Einrich gives you a wink and pulls on his lho-stick.{/n} "I'm not really here about the reactor. I heard a rumour that you'd gone to investigate the plasma drive chambers, so I thought I'd... make sure everything went smoothly. Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} is accustomed to associating with people of your rank, or officers at the very least, but here... This place is home to voidfarers of simpler manners, whose clan customs may be unfamiliar to you."

07f4c90e-0497-4afc-866f-98ac36ca75a3.Text: {n}The "voidfarer of simpler manners" furrows his brows.{/n} "Our customs are decent ones, Master Monteg! I'd rather boil myself in plasma than let anything happen to the Lord Captain!"

216c45f7-90fd-4d8d-b5c9-ca30a44c2104.Text: {n}Einrich rolls his lho-stick back and forth, thinking.{/n} "I've also seen it on some bulkheads, crates, doors. I just assumed it was the mark of some small clan — many voidsmen mark their workplaces with family symbols."

076c7fda-522c-44b1-b8e8-95a9bca0ece0.Text: {n}Nije bows deferentially.{/n} "How goes the search, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"

c89acb8e-7e24-45a9-8472-0c94af168803.Text: {n}Einrich chuckles.{/n} "I think you've found someone's secret stash. What was it? A mouldy nutribar, lho, a few thrones? Workers often hide their belongings or banned items from the enforcers or covetous neighbours. Maybe someone marked their cache with the symbol to make it easier to find later?"

d1769b64-34c1-4a8c-83c7-696cafd21dc4.Text: "No offence, Nije, but if you can find even three people in this bay who can give a report without turning the air blue, I'll gladly admit I was wrong." {n}Einrich grins at the now silent Nije.{/n} "You're a good bunch, I'd hate to see you insult {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} with some foolishness and not even realise it."

ebee5520-36aa-4dde-bf01-393488d412d9.Text: "Mind if I take a look?" {n}Einrich takes the note, careful not to let any ash fall on it.{/n} "'Need more'... More what? Whoever wrote it, they didn't want anyone who wasn't in the know to understand. Using caches to exchange messages is a good way to keep things hidden from the enforcers. It's how some workers procure intoxicants and other items they're not supposed to have. There has to be another cache somewhere nearby. You never use the same one for both the transfer and the correspondence — too risky." {n}He gives you a look and shrugs.{/n} "What? I've never engaged in such business, I swear. I've just... heard how it's done."

cd47cd6c-1dcb-4d3f-b8bf-f9abde89c0fc.Text: {n}Einrich deftly examines the weapon.{/n} "Interesting. Nije is right — this could get a whole bay executed. No wonder these scoundrels are so cautious."

15d16896-1a90-497d-bf7e-1798616e6c17.Text: {n}The shift foreman's thick fingers drum thoughtfully on his tool belt.{/n} "If these guys are smart, they'll spot the enforcers near the cache and stay out of sight. And Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} would be spotted even quicker."

73d1254e-d818-46f0-8be7-c2c7a9423a91.Text: "Hey, Monteg, come over here! We need a couple of your braver boys and girls for a job." {n}Nije smiles and adds more quietly,{/n} "We need people to keep watch over something. And maybe to break a few noses."

a552d717-4212-4633-9a9b-191d017cba7a.Text: {n}Einrich smirks ominously. He throws the lho-stick butt on the floor and puts it out with his boot.{/n} "Consider the dirtbag caught, {name}."

3886c946-279c-4915-b582-76c8a775aa28.Text: "I'll be here waiting for your cue."

ecde592b-7415-468a-addd-a7284c319dda.Text: "Permission to kick off our little operation, {name}?"

2e35b900-0d2c-4d3d-bed1-8ddaba909b49.Text: "I'm just keeping an eye out, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Feel free to ask old Nije any questions you may have — he knows the plasma drive chambers like the back of his hand."

aa510b22-e7b4-40d2-8494-0b5abc2f7fc0.Text: "That's just what we need, more secret stashes. I hope there was nothing forbidden in it? Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but voidsmen are simple folk. I've been trying to wean them off their grubby habits for years. But give them anything worth having and all they want to do is hide it in a hole like a rat!"

d248150a-984b-47cd-8ec9-b0a7ada75bd1.Text: "What is that?" {n}Nije's thick eyebrows knit together angrily, and you almost think you see a power charge jolt across them.{/n} "We've got smugglers on the loose! Who else would be hiding these strange messages? I'll have them all drawn and quartered on the turbine, I will! Now I'd like to find out what they're smuggling..."

f797e240-171f-4701-a8d9-8e23c1660d0d.Text: {n}Nije holds the weapon as if it is going to bite him, sweat beading on his forehead.{/n} "Machine spark shake me! A homemade weapon, and assembled right in this compartment — the markings are the same as those on local machine parts. This is a very serious matter — it seems someone is plotting a riot and secretly building their own arsenal from scavenged materials right under our noses!"

87fb005e-31c5-40aa-9ac4-5de471373744.Text: {n}The shift foreman shrugs sheepishly.{/n} "I... To tell you the truth, I'm no good at hunting rule-breakers. It's not what I do. You give the orders, and we will do it."

3ed7b3c8-f4bc-46bc-aa4f-6222e6fb24e7.Text: {n}Clenching his fists until his knuckles crack, Einrich resolutely says,{/n} "We'll help. I have a couple of people in mind, tough lads. I'll get them here right away."

a6e4186c-7246-4303-87a7-e0cd80a8c00b.Text: {n}The shift foreman's voice grows quieter.{/n} "I just wish I knew who to trust with it... Our villain could be anyone from the bay crew. If we pick the wrong person, we'll blow the whole ambush. We need someone from the outside who won't draw attention to themselves."

5e6ba81a-440c-4152-b634-c709c5dbe347.Text: "That's right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. If something isn't to your liking or if you find anything suspicious, come to me at once!"

60cc15ca-76b1-40f2-9c1d-56709516f80e.Text: "We'll spook them, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. By the time the enforcers finish their search, all the rats will have scattered and covered their tracks."

fdacffcc-b697-447f-9a70-35b12885ba39.Text: "We are proud of our chambers. Power feeds the ship's main engine from here. There are other drives on the ship, but ours is the mightiest. That's to say, we do important work."

63062a4d-9fb5-413a-95b2-d32e5d6812f9.Text: {n}Nije looks at you in confusion.{/n} "I'm... I'm a voidsman, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Grew up on Footfall, joined the crew at fourteen, spent my whole life in this bay. I've raised no family and made no fortune, but I've climbed my way up the ranks. I don't know anything but my trade and this compartment... I am my trade and this compartment, Lord Captain."

394e4596-c6b4-4ea4-9b4b-49f2fcf6d322.Text: "Working with plasma is dangerous, but we have a good crew, and not too many incidents. The esteemed Tech-Priests are satisfied with us, the machine spirits are all working as they should. The inferni don't complain about us either — we fix cracks in the reactor vessel on time, and we fix leaks."

a67dd02a-5b2b-4d49-ae16-2aa9de383628.Text: "Is it just the power surging in the bay, or was there a spark between us just now, Einrich?" {n}Jae bites her lip dramatically.{/n}

ab12e133-f5e6-4120-bea9-ce4d552614e0.Text: {n}Einrich matches her with a theatrical sigh.{/n} "Either could start a dangerous fire, Mistress Heydari. Someone could get hurt, and we can't let that happen, now can we?"

fd5619c0-36f1-44f5-8a1b-45aa7c2e5ecb.Text: "You're the most mawkish infernus I've ever met, Master Monteg." {n}A burly man in coveralls furrows his bushy eyebrows. His sparse hair stands on end.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, welcome. I'm Shift Foreman Nije, in charge of this section. If you need anything, I'm here to help."

d9271ee1-af28-4b00-80ce-b4754aa25fe2.Text: "I'm carrying out a routine drive inspection. The regulations require scheduled checks to make sure the insulation isn't weakened, the sensors haven't been tampered with, and the reactor isn't about to blow anytime soon. Just business as usual."

cd08d44b-4b69-4328-bd32-4d5c18575026.Text: {n}It is strange that the senior officer is conducting the inspection alone. According to the regulations, there should be an entire squad of inferni, and the personal presence of the Infernus Master is necessary only in emergencies.{/n}

1ffc92ee-5cf4-4a4a-8610-dca5675e361e.Text: {n}Plasma drive inspections are a regular requirement — the ship's power-generating heart cannot be allowed to stop beating.{/n}

f8baabd4-d2c7-4854-85c3-db8ba55ebcc7.Text: "Somebody keeps daubing it on the equipment and bulkheads. If I find the scoundrels, I'll tear their hands off and send them for servitorisation." {n}The shift foreman frowns.{/n} "Is it some kind of sedition? I didn't know. If you see one of these, let me know, we'll try to find these artists."

cb83561c-5a29-403e-8969-2b6c82214865.Text: "Esteemed Tech-Priest Deltar, this is unacceptable. For the tenth time, you've sent us the same faulty servitors. It's been over two weeks, and we still can't raise the lift that's stuck between our platform and platform 92-M, all because of your servitors. For the love of the Throne, decommission these things if you can't fix them! Respectfully, Shift Foreman Nije."

fbee5296-d4d6-4fe8-b344-4917c7bb7398.Text: The design of this webber matches the standard pattern, but the weapon was put together from assorted parts.

2be00236-7b3a-4b02-a3fd-81594918a03b.Text: All this scrap reads is, "Received. Need more."

6ba5b5ba-0165-4755-9266-7c92a9d8904a.Text: Examine the room and the body.

d3d8022e-8c40-43ad-ab10-8ad918dc3e99.Text: Overgrown trees and ivy-covered roots conceal an ancient bio-dome nestled in one of the crevices. It would have been impossible to locate this place without the precise coordinates from the armillary sphere.

a63aa207-6e2e-4eee-96dd-5aee41fd0bfa.Text: The structure is in a state of gross disrepair. Creepers cover the walls and ceiling, and pungent flowers and berries hang from beams and equipment alike. The centre of the structure reveals a sealed chamber where vegetation has yet to break through. Inside is a humble bunk — a decayed body sprawled over it — tables with blueprints, parts and tools, and a great number of chests containing treasure.

fa031892-bf29-4b1c-82a6-44776dc0af39.Text: Judging by the dead man's clothes, the diary pages, and the monograms on the blueprints, you realise that you have found the final resting place of the legendary Captain Bartholomeus Ort. During his long and adventurous life, he travelled the entire Expanse, mapping out numerous star systems and, in his later years, realising his life's work: the armillary sphere that he imbued with the sum of his knowledge. The device on your ship is undoubtedly his creation.

2bff37d8-2478-4885-a48e-1a6fb5be5a65.Text: While the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} were still hotly debating whether or not he had committed the crime of invention, Bartholomeus disappeared without a trace, leaving only a single message: "I have gathered treasures from hundreds of worlds, but they will not be handed over to the covetous lords of the Expanse. Instead, I bequeath my riches to one who cherishes the shine of the stars more than any gold or rubies." It seems that you happen to be this very person.

62a09f1e-ba60-48eb-af87-fc22013ddf89.Text: The shuttle's hold is bursting with untold riches. You leave the forgotten dome at the mercy of the invading wilderness and its inhabitants.

d5b072cd-873b-423c-8818-78d181df19b6.Text: Only the rustling of leaves and the chirping of insects respond to the roar of the shuttle taking off. The dome waits motionless in the embrace of roots and vines.

e99ce404-8638-4c22-b2ad-ed20822f0a90.Text: Examine the logbook at the bridge.

e6649599-6167-45e1-975b-4d4760db5015.Text: Relay the contents of the diary to the flagship.

2662569b-af65-42e3-a89e-7ba8ddef7ab3.Text: Use the augurs to examine the ship.

d02e53bf-f86d-4040-9632-7fcfef9934d8.Text: The hulk of a merchant ship drifts through the void like a gutted corpse. The hull is riddled with gouges from macro-cannon fire. The soot-covered letters on the side spell out a sombre name: Finger of Sorrow.

21ef892d-6254-4b54-84d0-c88c245ded36.Text: A squad of enforcers and Tech-Priests put on their void suits and dock with the ship. The vessel is empty except for the frozen and desiccated corpses of the crew. Some retain human features, but others are easily recognisable as genetic aberrations. They have been dead for centuries.

04aeaa7b-54f0-49e4-ad44-5ac9572090d6.Text: The ship is devoid of vital signs. Life support systems have long since failed. Cold, darkness, and silence fill the wreck of the Finger of Sorrow.

46741b2d-027b-4029-b4e8-a903377759e8.Text: An all-out barrage turns the Finger of Sorrow to space dust, forever erasing its sinister secrets from the history of the Koronus Expanse.

ee28f142-d17f-41cc-91e4-f8e3e202980c.Text: The Finger of Sorrow was a common merchant vessel. The log records its travels along many of the trade routes of the Calixis Sector. The last entry states that the ship departed from Port Wander on the border between the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanseGlossary}Koronus Expanse{/g} and the {g|Encyclopedia:CalixisGlossary}Calixis Sector{/g}. The Tech-Priest notes that the protocols for undocking from the station were not followed, indicating either a hasty escape or blatant disregard for the covenants of the Omnissiah.

b27aadfa-039f-47ff-9d64-325ba48f5680.Text: The hold is empty, apart from a few open containers. However, careful examination points to three opened service hatches that bear claw marks. Venturing deeper into the service tunnels, the enforcers find three empty nests with chunks of purple chitin and dried traces of dark slime that has eaten through the metal panels. There can be no doubt that Genestealers once lurked here.

552299b6-b0ff-4d85-a641-47d1cc42ab64.Text: Many of the cabins have become tombs for the bodies of the crew. They asphyxiated when the ship's life support systems failed. One of the enforcers notices a cache marked with the symbol of a fanged serpent with a sharp tail and three clawed limbs. The cache contains an amulet and a miraculously preserved diary.

f3f00ea3-418f-494b-8684-a406072401c2.Text: The diary was kept by one of the missionaries of a Genestealer Cult. According to the entries, this cult secretly spread throughout much of the Calixis Sector, although the author does not mention any specific infected worlds. He recalls with reverence "the promised land, the cradle of faith, salty as the tears of righteous martyrs." The author's branch of the cult had settled on Port Wander Station, the last threshold between the Calixis Sector and the Koronus Expanse.

b0f3acba-caf4-4497-b082-8d3f02ac3dee.Text: The cult grew and gained followers among the workers and the poor, and even managed to infiltrate powerful trade guilds. However, their plans fell apart when the Genestealer's Kiss was granted to an unworthy candidate. This oversight led to the discovery of the cult and a bloody purge. The author of the diary recalls with horror and sorrow how many of the pureblood children of the Star Saviour perished in the massacre.

61bf4799-d628-469d-ba56-7491555c630e.Text: The story ends by chronicling the escape of a small group of heretics who managed to save three purebreds and steal a merchant ship under heavy fire from the station. They narrowly navigated the Maw, but the ship's damage was too severe. "The three phalanges of the Finger of Sorrow," the pureblood Star Children, fell into a long sleep and became dormant. Meanwhile, the cultists humbly watched the ship's life support systems fade away one after another. In the last lines, the author welcomes death in the name of the Many-Armed Emperor with solemnity and elation.

15f7e715-dc9e-41b5-bdf4-92f05f53d892.Text: The enforcers plant melta charges at key points on the vessel, and the explosion rips the Finger of Sorrow to pieces that are obliterated by strikes from the macro-cannons.

0d54e216-2a67-42e8-9fec-1bf1444b2f18.Text: The ship watches you silently with the dead visors of its {g|Encyclopedia:Augur}augur{/g} systems.

2b8185b6-ea53-452e-a1cf-ddcaaea9c15c.Text: This amulet is painfully cold to the touch. It once belonged to an Astropath who stood strong against the horrors of the warp. Though its former owner met a terrible end, his unbending will lives on in this relic.

55c81b16-0eea-4ff7-b6a1-d8f37d8f30e0.Text: Check the vagrant for evidence of treason.

ef8435c1-dd1a-40f3-a2c3-2a648f11d5b5.Text: Terminate the traitor's agent just to be sure.

ffe100e8-fffd-446b-8f1b-044bed002c92.Text: Promote the dynasty's loyal servant and assign him to an important position.

964ab2e4-2bae-4d0c-94af-bd2a044a81cd.Text: Leave the useless vagrant on the planet.

0c38f366-77b1-4d4b-b787-b31ade2c537b.Text: Establish the nature of his mission.

db9b3ad4-8bee-433d-a50b-b3e63211dbd4.Text: Lavish riches upon the faithful servant and bestow some unchallenging yet honourable duty upon him.

6cf75759-0740-4911-af35-56bd2bee7987.Text: The scouting team sent to the colony world returns with a decrepit, shaggy, foul-smelling vagrant in tow. The old man hastened toward the enforcers as soon as he saw the dynasty's colours, and implored them to take him to Master Voigtvir or Lady Theodora.

e2fa6245-06bc-4020-bd1c-1f0afca11b01.Text: During his interrogation, the old man says he is a loyal servant of House von Valancius. Four decades ago, he was sent on an important mission to this system by Master of Whispers Voigtvir. It took him twenty years to complete the mission. He spent the next twenty waiting for his masters to collect him. The vagrant was an ambitious young spy when he left the ship, and coming aboard again has made him very emotional.

48d0199e-0f3b-4bde-818b-9c548e3b97f2.Text: Despite his pitiful wails about his innocence, the old man is thrown out of an airlock. Traitors to the dynasty and their accomplices must die!

dd5e18c0-4735-412b-a493-607f4cb7f3d9.Text: The beaming old man has joined the ship's enforcers in order to teach younger soldiers lessons in fortitude and unshakeable loyalty.

aa37c94a-3e3c-4695-b6c6-92bf77632700.Text: The whimpering old man is escorted out. The dynasty only has use for strong and efficient servants!

bd324854-155a-4419-85d8-1b9b1164f7df.Text: The sobbing old man swears to pray daily for the good health of the new Lord Captain. The story of his amazing adventure and selfless service immediately spreads throughout the ship.

ad63a4e8-e505-4eaf-a1b4-db39d74691c0.Text: The investigation has found no wrongdoing the old man could be held accountable for. His body bears no signs of worshipping the {g|Encyclopedia:ChaosGlossary}Archenemy{/g}. He has confessed to no crime and seems quite shocked at the news of Lady Theodora's death and Voigtvir's treachery. The harsh interrogation techniques have taken an almost fatal toll on his failing health, yet forced no admission of guilt from him.

b9cacfb2-b083-4efd-bda6-a9460329cf3a.Text: The vagrant only agrees to share the details of his assignment with the Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself}. If his claims are to be believed, he was sent to recover documentary evidence of House Winterscale's debt liabilities to House von Valancius. Those priceless papers had been stolen by hired agents of the {g|Encyclopedia:ColdTrade}Cold Trade{/g} on Calligos Winterscale's orders. However, instead of being destroyed as he wanted them to be, they were hidden away for the purposes of blackmail.

adbcf2e6-e606-4048-9d56-926d34634249.Text: The old man describes a long journey full of perilous adventures that eventually brought him into possession of the documents, which he then proudly presents to you. Astonishingly enough, the papers turn out to be genuine.

00f66134-0a12-4a49-8a2c-393359daeff2.Text: Order that the man be put out of his misery.

4af13837-b6be-4644-9a65-cabf504b7201.Text: Send Zacchary Weisz to the station with a squad of bodyguards.

7343afbb-0700-40e3-a04b-dbc3ef679460.Text: Order the station to be explored.

2c2324a4-2ca8-4abc-997b-bd3e19b961b5.Text: Seal the station, dooming its ghostly inhabitants to an eternity of suffering.

0d167c49-298f-4363-883f-cc116c99c6e8.Text: Stay away from the suspicious station.

6036c943-e9d2-43be-ae98-a05e40a0ab94.Text: The station is not responding. Perhaps there is no one left who could respond.

787fcfeb-f3a0-4a37-804d-bd7953bcc55d.Text: The enforcers offered their prayers and proceeded to enter the uncanny station. What they saw inside was monstrous. Astropaths upon their thrones, not quite here, not quite now — smudged, as it were, across time. Servants reliving their horrible deaths again and again, only to be reborn out of ashes and blood into more agony a moment later. The warp manifested itself here, twisting the very nature of existence.

25d03c25-93d5-4dac-84e5-618aa5c4849f.Text: You leave the dead station and all its chilling secrets behind.

21616d6c-019e-45d3-9470-3d30cad0f993.Text: The longer the conversation went on, the worse Master Weisz looked, until he collapsed on the floor and ordered servants to carry him back to the ship. According to him, the mind of the warp-captured Astropath was so lacerated with the Immaterium's horrifying imagery that peering into that nightmarish abyss would have been too dangerous.

b1a927eb-6004-4d01-b898-c46fcca87610.Text: A brief and chilling chronicle of the station's doom was found in the scribes' records. A warp disturbance of monstrous proportions wiped out half of the Choir at once, turning the Astropaths into living portals through which torrents of the Immaterium's energies poured out. Those who lasted longer bellowed and howled about a black rift that had split the universe into Before and After, and a darkness that would devour the {g|Encyclopedia:AstronomicanGlossary}Astronomican{/g}'s light.

cf517171-ae68-4966-9e35-2861cf93aee3.Text: Void torpedoes shatter the fragile station. One can only hope that the unfortunate souls captured by the warp have perished along with their home.

7b89aa16-f9b0-42e5-b8de-96b01dc98973.Text: Choirmaster Weisz boarded the station in person and proceeded to the Choir's hall. He stood silently for hours in front of a man frozen in ice, and held a telepathic conversation with him.

149f3d0c-9136-4cb5-b895-9354bf0cfd89.Text: The Astropathic station is dead ahead of the voidship. It is motionless. There is lifeless silence across its vox-frequencies. Its lights are out. Even those who have no warp sensitivity can feel the presence of death. It is here, lurking in the shadows. All of this makes reading the reports of the ship's Astropaths, who claim to be hearing an incessant ghostly howl emanating from the station, all the more disturbing.

67d9caa9-a87d-4600-b734-d73bd9a14201.Text: The main hall was covered in a crust of psychic ice. A green-robed blind old man sat motionless upon a tall throne. He was quite literally embedded in the ice, yet... he was still alive. And screaming.

c983ba03-c12f-4e1e-add7-4a11810db668.Text: An enforcer who tried to follow his orders aimed his weapon at the blind man, only to collapse on the floor at once, wailing in pain. His mind was ravaged by the man's psychic scream. A second attempt went the same way, then a third one...

8642b61e-211b-40dc-843f-915f29f1ae0e.Text: The psychic shriek carrying across the Immaterium has been silenced, but this has brought the crew no relief. A chilling realisation came to the Astropaths when they discovered that the cry was masking a different sound, one even more terrifying and surreal. It was the melody of a cataclysm born from a warp storm of titanic power, so intense that the entire Expanse must be able to hear it. It muffles Astropathic messages and crawls into psykers' minds, evoking everywhere the same image: a dark, gaping, {g|Encyclopedia:CicatrixMaledictumGlossary}beastly mouth{/g} cleaving the universe in two. Now that the mad Choirmaster has finally stopped screaming, the song of the Immaterium has reached the Rogue Trader's voidship too.

17327f6d-9be2-40d2-9873-bfb3c2f076b5.Text: Then Master Weisz offered a prayer to the God-Emperor, and the unfortunate man passed away. Upon returning to the ship, Weisz reverently presented the Lord Captain with a grim trophy: the late Choirmaster's amulet, taken from his frozen body after his death.

27cbeea8-d8c2-4f20-9749-8184b6dddca4.Text: A pile of papers containing denunciations — in exchange for a ration card, people willingly report the misdeeds of their neighbours, acquaintances, and even relatives to the enforcers.

008f78ec-39be-4430-848d-d15d59a7a24e.Text: The shelves have been cleaned out and all the prohibited goods confiscated.

960c43f6-d481-4622-b99c-e5b8a2b9fe2c.Text: "Lord Captain, here to report: your orders have been carried out — the compartment is already operating according to the new procedure."

7e597dc9-1310-4a98-9393-d855aee7832c.Text: "The soup's heartier now, with meat! It still tastes rank, but I can't stop eating it."

15cabe5d-075e-4ed0-9674-c19132b3d066.Text: "I'm going to be sick... What kind of animal lived here? It's like it ate, slept and defecated in the same place."

e7e6eba0-d78f-40f5-902b-c47afbade22e.Text: "They usually hide contraband in disgusting places, thinking no one's going to wade through the filth. If we don't meet our confiscation quotas, Frensoe will have our hides."

81dc8de7-96d8-4738-ac3a-7203dd1f7576.Text: The scab-covered leper scratches blissfully, staring through you without any sign of awareness.

b3dc0f80-9883-4e05-bf57-1a2d530943c0.Text: "I'm sick with something again. Thought I'd be lying on the floor by now, but instead I feel better somehow. If you're sick, you're alive, and all life is a gift. Yes..."

e2ec1bc4-f02f-41be-90e1-d6d0c9c3ae42.Text: "It doesn't hurt anymore! Ha... Ha... It really doesn't!"

fdb7cf2d-eb2b-481e-82ed-0ed5e9d38af5.Text: The dented plasteel of the armoured barriers, designed to shield the station against the rabble's rage, is dotted with a good many bullet marks.

49935b88-f5e8-4d0c-b764-9b14ea7a1d89.Text: "How many times do I need to tell you ungrateful maggots? Mistakes must be paid for!"

dbe4be19-3856-42b2-986c-f8f931d20766.Text: "Heed the voice of the upper decks: {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} {name} von Valancius has graced Bay LD-A14 with a personal visit!"

9ef17a12-e13a-4013-ae85-ba6ec53d5767.Text: Someone has sketched a hasty portrait of a worker with a red scarf over his face. The artwork still reeks of chemical pigment. Judging by the layer of flaked-off paint, it has been removed several times already.

85d800bb-feb1-4b29-ac3b-ecfb5651d487.Text: "Spare a card... I'm starving to death. Have pity on me."

38e6c1ec-9cfc-4643-8fc0-63985fe58357.Text: "You want a brat? Yours for two ration packs. A bargain."

89500b74-22de-4a2c-8bad-3e4b31ea49a1.Text: "Hey! I live here! And you all just keep waddlin' right through!"

c451c534-9dea-450b-844b-5e5497495462.Text: "Out of my home! Oi! Shoo! Unbelievable..."

3bd8a8c9-99b1-4753-aa04-dbed75bca78d.Text: "Oh, clog the tunnels, so much for a house in the outskirts! They've bred, the void rats, and now they're all over this level too. An old man can't get no peace anymore!"

5bee58ca-1d3f-4b8a-99ae-72da3a72dbab.Text: "Er... sure, you can have it if you need it so badly..."

d563799b-5ab0-44b1-9ed5-0881ca055051.Text: Despite your efforts, the container does not budge an inch. But you heard an unpleasant crunch in your lower back.

8c08899c-1962-47af-92a3-52a61c54b1fc.Text: "Lord Captain, this container weighs as much as a whole train. Perhaps you'd like to use the cargo crane?"

744cf0d6-43c5-4fa4-9801-a0fb98c2d3cb.Text: The bay's bulkhead is marred by traces of gunfire and rust-coloured stains from old blood that was never properly washed off.

12db1cdb-bc3e-43d4-a1e9-fef4917a2b2e.Text: "How do they manage to build their shanties faster than we can burn them down?"

871b488d-74dd-44e5-8f1d-764cea55870a.Text: "Those parasites must be using witchcraft or something! Their shack was blocking the air vent, and the folks in the next bay almost suffocated!"

8bc54c36-a372-4727-9847-b87d0c6abf59.Text: "As soon as it burns down, orders are to cordon off the area, clear it, and let no one past the platform. Anyone who doesn't comply gets their brains bashed in. They're really going to get it this time! At last."

e35c20d4-84dd-4425-be08-4486ccaf6239.Text: During each shift, railway hubs direct thousands of containers carrying the Rogue Trader's cargo to various destination compartments.

8b390c9e-b1a5-48f2-b5d0-405b0286a5f4.Text: The timeworn loader is barely fit for purpose at this point, but the enforcers still see its complex maintenance as the lesser evil compared to hiring ignorant, clumsy scroungers to do the job.

d7a54b4a-93b8-44fb-8a87-16034699c63c.Text: The workers, beaten to within an inch of their lives, are returning stolen power panels, wire, and microlumens to containers marked "Disposal."

ff43c334-033a-4a9d-8181-321097a5785a.Text: "Theta-34 requesting medicae and repair crew. Accident in rear carriage."

ec875bf3-de5a-47b5-92b7-046aa14f9a6e.Text: The door has no control panel — it must be locked from the other side.

f3a8ccdf-ec0c-4a47-8306-5e74d5a02f74.Text: The cogita-dashboard controlling the rail junctions is lit up with indicator lumens for active hubs. Arrival and departure announcements are pouring out of the vox-systems.

a395c0f7-acff-4112-8587-6822e89d5ca2.Text: No one finds the courage to approach the bodies of these outcasts, their rotting flesh and cartilage bearing the marks of void disease.

97ae67a9-5c70-453a-bc42-d29b7f428c01.Text: The stench of decaying bodies creeps into your throat and lungs, forming a sticky film lining your airways.

3ccd2b78-80d4-44c1-bd52-1b633352e165.Text: The attackers' disfigurements look familiar to you. These are mutant abominations, just like the ones whose plot you are investigating.

7341800e-cc3a-415f-bae8-fc1addabcb39.Text: The threadbare rags worn by the attackers are covering signs of aberrant disfigurements.

4c78f194-d6c2-48ec-861e-e29f54965d28.Text: A faint symbol is scratched onto the crate — one of the death cultists must have turned it into a cache.

3ef61f85-ce1a-48cb-a45a-3f5922a3c4c6.Text: The death cultist looks like a desiccated mummy. It appears he has spent many watches in a deep trance, serving the Undying One.

8c41ab6b-786a-4ef2-bbff-91d4c3ea7b1d.Text: "The laypeople are interrupting this spinner's meditation. Then again, even such a disturbance may be turned into training that hardens one's focus."

4a57c617-3584-409f-b1ef-00da0059d4ae.Text: "Looks like a spinner killed him. Anybody know the dead man? He was a heretic, wasn't he?"

e0191c37-e73e-4c5a-9875-abaefef494f5.Text: "I heard those zealots even kill upstanding folk. They say it is the Emperor's will..."

1e5040a0-bdba-474a-9313-77e0658224cc.Text: "So I could be killed tomorrow? And I'd never know why."

507695b3-0438-42e8-8161-27c7f12a3ab9.Text: "May the Undying One shroud your footsteps from the faithless."

670e554a-34ad-4dfd-b60a-7ac3543c56f4.Text: This man is tormented by some malady you cannot identify.

f4815f37-5c6c-47a3-b84e-ad4423e62997.Text: This man is suffering from a severe but curable disease — one vial of medicine administered in the early stages would have saved him.

e0b353fc-6283-4e5a-bdc6-54bcf9f56575.Text: "For Throne's sake, come to your senses!"

0ffbef4d-fa3e-4136-a5da-bbb52b0c6912.Text: "Put your life in the Undying One's hands, Domin'{name}."

b9e67462-13f8-48f5-968c-43db9156e081.Text: "This is getting interesting... Go ahead, jump!"

a0992542-ae19-4cd6-90c6-774c7ab65b49.Text: "Lord Captain, this is where the sick and the broken are herded to die of their various diseases! Don't touch anything!"

6e4996ac-d69b-4ec4-b833-3c64a0767d6c.Text: "Can you sense the putrid miasma hanging over this place? Touching anything in here would be folly!"

c5dd6f37-c50b-4a10-bb5b-f1c65680057f.Text: "My lungs are filled with the decay of lifeless bodies. They are... flashing toxic colours. Please do not touch anything!"

bfebb1f2-8e9e-4a08-82df-d8d123b648ed.Text: "Weird... my little voices have shut up. Now they're just giggling quietly every time you go to touch something. How about we head back and wash our hands with soap ten times or so?"

515590e5-f92f-4685-b8d3-a21483d44913.Text: "This disease-ridden place ought to be burned to please the Exalted One. Do not touch anything."

7ca59cd2-f759-4da8-9960-a9ab3bc2ec99.Text: "Death hangs in the air within the pestilence pit, but it is not yet your time to go. Touch nothing unless absolutely necessary, Domin'{name}."

5825beb5-0b02-40c4-af17-2a5403250ce9.Text: "Anyone who touches anything in here guarantees me long minutes of pleasure as they die an agonising death."

ad02fca4-8f2e-4f72-b37c-3a2f938a4cb5.Text: "I am registering sources of infection. Requesting contact with contaminated areas to be strictly prohibited."

8f8d7db5-15c0-4027-9a46-31286166fced.Text: "I don't need Glaito's analysis to know that every surface here is contaminated. Keep your hands to yourself — this disease could kill you."

355e2ad5-be22-4f32-8cb5-4f84fc68e36f.Text: "This place is foul! Like something a kraken coughed up. Do not touch a thing in here. Reeks of disease, all of it."

c4f8c782-4341-424e-a677-3ee2eb29fb1a.Text: "The marks left by the mon-keigh can be so abominable. Touch nothing here. Death is everywhere, waiting to pounce."

7b12cade-fce1-4614-8109-8dffc8b2a949.Text: Lush yellow-green moss covers the walls of the slums, seeming to especially favour the warm, moist pipes. Judging by the marks, the people here regularly shear off the moss, only for it to grow back again.

b4b4997a-1e47-4b51-90fc-a5d13bbc31ae.Text: "How could they cast me out... One of their own..."

e1e7f21f-b476-41b6-aa06-8654c1e16afb.Text: The bulky doors lead to the enforcers' living quarters and the hub's provision depots.

e622a455-eed6-457a-8cbc-c229fa4f3642.Text: "Those baton-wielding bastards have gone bleeding mad. Another twenty of our folk torched along with their shacks!"

bda7eddc-5cfd-49d5-a247-2ba0d35625af.Text: "I'd rather burn alive once than spend the rest of my life breaking my back, shift after shift, for a few measly ration cards they'll just take from me anyway. And then beat me up for good measure!"

b3dff4ff-3e28-4ddb-9f02-0bf8d8168e0f.Text: "Lord Captain, best to keep away from here for now. Safety concerns, you understand. The huts could collapse at any moment."

0523a7c7-32b8-4330-84c0-18b4ea8f2ae2.Text: "The kids have been waiting for you! How was your shift?"

c1055705-f184-46b5-a645-bdf544566bb8.Text: "We worked hard. I helped out a friend with the loading and he gave me some cards. Take them and exchange them for new shoes, yours are all worn out."

6a1b748f-7299-42b3-bd9a-e506717ad789.Text: "Oh, thank you! I've already made your bed for you, so once we've eaten, you go and rest. The little ones and I will head out to the marketplace and leave you in peace."

74e50515-7f56-4ff1-8efb-8618eb4c1ad8.Text: "Why did the Emperor send me such a wonderful wife?"

8040cde7-3f2e-473a-8803-852c012022a2.Text: "Since the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} has eaten the soup, does that mean mouldslime is a... whatchacallit... delicacy now? Have we been feasting like upper-deckers all this time and not even known it?"

1f15f779-379a-44a6-b24e-f5b128005312.Text: "Don't miss out on a chance to taste the blessed broth enjoyed by the Lord Captain! Boost your strength! Cure your ailments! Be as hale as the Lord Captain! Get a place in the queue for a reasonable price!"

25abef6f-daa9-41d2-909d-7421c3fd73aa.Text: "Gah, as soon as the Lord Captain blessed the vat, all sorts of riffraff started pushing in and eating up all the soup! What about the rest of us?"

5a2406f7-6ae1-47f6-81ba-9ddacdebd3d2.Text: "I hope we get something besides sludge this time."

120c4c21-84dc-4514-8128-bb66c11b7063.Text: "I hope no one notices this is my third time in this queue..."

916b8f60-ec52-4414-bb43-03edc9267f3c.Text: "Cheer up, folks, we'll be eating soon! Unless they close off the vat again, of course."

aad1c35f-a7d7-4aff-bc62-3cf8f6b4a904.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, be careful not to fall! The beam is awful rickety."

e3565c43-9e2e-49a3-a475-3feb64abdda4.Text: Someone has sloppily covered the enforcers' decree with paint. Scratched into the dried paint are imaginative descriptions of enforcer procreation.

142906df-b126-47d1-aab3-5c5479db11b0.Text: "Grandpa, can my toy run around and wag its tail?"

e71f0968-280c-4bd0-bfcb-876e7708d8bc.Text: "No, it can't, dear. It's just a little rat stuffed with a few nuts. Do you want to stick a microlumen on its face so its eyes can glow?"

2365556d-5eb9-4c5f-a87e-51dc56d85e24.Text: "Ugh... The stench on the lower levels is even worse than I imagined."

b8186018-2b88-4438-9031-fb75ba9cde09.Text: "The locals would do anything for a mouldy chunk of a corpse starch bar. Lower deck wastrels."

2191728d-adff-4c71-8104-85cc19435437.Text: The rotting guts of someone unfortunate enough to be flattened by a train lie glistening on the track.

bdf293cf-e196-40d2-a769-03f6d420fdf8.Text: The mould is dotted with glandular tendrils that ooze slime. Sick people who are still alive but can no longer walk are the mould's favourite choice of host to grow on and suck the last of life's juices from.

adb433dc-56a7-4d90-98e8-e69fe619594a.Text: "Burned-out folks' belongings! Hot from the oven! Ha ha! One ration card off the price for regulars, this shift only!"

343a9017-0998-44dd-93f8-3442422fb9d2.Text: "Used power panels and wrenched-off bolt nuts for your homes! Won't find these anywhere else!"

6771ad3b-34a5-4762-8e1c-43922eacf0c1.Text: "This is the last of the hub's vials for this work cycle. Do you have any idea how much it costs?"

b5463534-ad01-4e70-9d7d-d44f46eb6545.Text: "There. Fifty-seven ration cards. It's all I've got, I swear!"

7ed0893d-da89-47de-8ba5-6f3ce0dc6372.Text: "Spent the rest on rotgut again, I'm guessing? I'm not doing you any more favours — give up the drink or get used to life in the pestilence pit."

25601e24-9f5d-4c76-80ee-295bec704d88.Text: "I hope you get hit by a train!"

e1571f40-6968-4ca0-a351-8a05e2301e14.Text: Shreds of rat carcasses and yellow-green moss stew in the cloudy sludge — along with other, unidentifiable ingredients.

f0681b11-1fd6-41e7-93f7-ab04ad6fae1d.Text: The food vat is protected from the vicious hungry crowd by equally vicious thugs wielding makeshift weapons.

8d3cb2ed-8b34-4493-8183-f8f163e467d9.Text: The guards can barely keep the throng of paupers at bay. Having observed their Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} taste the soup, the people are now ecstatically pushing their way to the vat of mouldslime.

e4a20d59-e4f8-4822-8de7-b99e213c63ea.Text: "Those who raise a hand against the Giver of Life will not live to hear the next watch signal."

b40d86e4-639d-47a3-a970-eae3ea7d4f85.Text: "He was granted a good, clean death. As it should be."

234a30f6-9b37-4ded-8975-317d71fe6527.Text: "Look what I got for you, sweetheart. It's a treat from Janus called 'dri-froot.' Eat up, it's good for you!"

be9b96f8-7199-4c69-8399-754f814ac223.Text: "Oh, it's yummy! When I grow up and you're old, I'll bring you treats too."

ff94d088-57f7-4c29-bcd7-06b63db05785.Text: "You're just skin and bones. Don't your parents feed you at all?"

c572c24e-1209-468e-882b-30c05c4e7352.Text: "My pa got hit by a train, and my ma's got three more to raise."

8cb56068-c468-4f9d-a247-a834b550f75a.Text: "You scrawny little snot... Here, eat some rations before anyone sees and get out of here."

3e6d1ccb-c10b-4b28-becf-477d52d8f7b9.Text: "I can have the whole thing? A whole ration pack? I— I mean, thank you so, so much, master enforcer, sir!"

005d274f-2785-4d89-9b75-dad1e9e0cbd9.Text: Scraps of rotting flesh fall from the pleading man's body, exposing maggot-infested wounds.

0c33e5e7-dd6e-4893-8dec-a9eecc36eab6.Text: "Why doesn't the Emperor send His spinners to punish me for my faults? I guess I don't deserve to die by a blade, only by the rot of the pestilence pit..."

86fc48fc-6f04-4ba9-8eb6-ef7d405d42b2.Text: A maimed, enchained person is shivering under a robe soaked with blood and pus. Their teeth and nails have fallen out, and their shrunken skin is covered in abscesses.

49e75e9d-abca-4bdb-8e9a-4f89707c3bc0.Text: "The 'forcers shat their pants like the void dogs they are when they heard upper deck bigwigs might come see all their mess for themselves."

ec4e9de2-3320-4c25-8e83-3933629f0913.Text: "What are you so gleeful for? It's only gotten worse! The beatings come harder and faster now."

0a459441-4080-4492-b6b5-2418ddcb0eba.Text: "Quiet! If you talk too much they'll come for you once your shift's over, too. Do you want to disappear like Endo did?"

66496a85-a655-427c-8af8-2b49e17b8aa3.Text: "The fact you're here means your families have disowned you. You're all refuse, and the stench of the lower decks is all you deserve!"

0adf28cd-2c48-4b50-82fd-0379455cdb85.Text: "Anything more than the baton and the whip is too good for you void dogs!"

8b0b72ba-76d9-451a-87e9-661f34b2fa82.Text: "Although you lot are the most pathetic enforcers on this ship, your purpose is to serve the von Valancius dynasty!"

ed09196b-847a-480b-93a0-24bb56b276a9.Text: "We serve the dynasty! Glory to the Rogue Trader!"

178cad3f-b6c4-4b4c-b761-bca81c489001.Text: "Stop being so bloody difficult! What's that thing the death cultists say? 'Your time has come' or what have you..."

8d264779-8f98-4c5e-8634-f7b73a91c40a.Text: "Talk about being everywhere at once. How about we take his stuff to the marketplace? We'll get to eat soup tonight!"

6a0e89ef-179b-426c-bcc9-01434c7f6eb8.Text: The hapless vendor has rusty junk on his counter and no customers at all. He peers hopefully into the faces of passers-by.

153dae0e-76a2-4342-b684-c380261c464e.Text: Judging by the merchant's round, well-fed face, the rusty junk laid out on the counter is merely a smokescreen for the more valuable — and likely illegal — goods that are for now hidden from idle glances.

c6a18d37-02c7-4433-b167-2cbdebc03809.Text: "Spinner of blood webs! I'm no heretic, and yet, I am begging you for death! Can't you make an exception for a tormented soul?"

d24487f5-0a76-4670-b354-d80a6bf296be.Text: "The Undying Emperor has whispered His will. Your soul is now given unto Him."

12e259e5-c434-41ca-82ff-ddbfc7ca5f6c.Text: Even in a place as dismal as this, people have managed to set up a small altar at which to pray. It is relatively clean and well maintained.

6aa786ac-e6fc-424e-ac2f-0d6b6a2fabc2.Text: "Careful, you poor thing. Don't drink too fast."

0983e010-16b8-4fb7-bfb5-677ce19c78bf.Text: "I'd be dead if it weren't for you. Why are you helping a worthless old woman like me, or any of the other rotten souls around here?"

20a8995d-deed-4f6a-b93d-b17f1eff4cf9.Text: "A good person took care of me and helped me to stand again. They didn't take anything in return either. They just asked me to show that same kindness to somebody else."

688e6c18-f496-408b-9027-6846efae768d.Text: "All quiet on the line, Lord Captain!"

b29fd9b7-febd-4830-8104-6d6faa25225f.Text: "Cargo traffic, stable. Passenger traffic, stable. I serve the dynasty!"

f5165855-0333-48d5-9082-a39ce3dee536.Text: "Why in the towering Throne's name is this lumen blinking? Did the technomats forget to fix it again? Or is there a freight train stuck at junction AR-82?"

bedbfdf0-250d-4303-a4c8-4edc70c5b1c5.Text: "Well, if you hear a loud squeal from Junior Officer Toliman, it's the second one. But if nothing changes in the next few minutes, call for a repair crew."

fb6dbada-493d-47f8-aa47-3c1a4f5f7dac.Text: "Have mercy, in the Throne's name, I beg you!"

fd75a99e-9dbd-46af-94b0-0de3b9275167.Text: "Next door has invited me over again... Maybe I should ask her to marry me. She's a hard worker and not a bad-looking woman."

fe08c0db-1066-4a03-9bc6-68118b77a8b9.Text: "A couple more shifts and I'll finally get a promotion! I used to be a labourer, and now I'll be in charge of a whole work crew."

64292519-036f-42bd-a938-05dbcf589ba9.Text: "Frensoe whipped another bribe-taker yesterday. He's nothing like the last captain who turned a blind eye to everything."

5df69ef7-36ff-4659-bb67-5fdeda70fe8e.Text: "I was lucky to be born in a railway compartment! Where else would you see such a miracle? They even come from the middle decks."

aef7d60b-7557-428f-ab5a-5b06ed8dda44.Text: "Throne, the claw's jammed again! Now we have to attach it to the container manually."

c8794d12-93be-43fe-b752-0273a252991f.Text: "...Let's not mention that in the report..."

8c6ec9c1-1349-4ecf-b575-2b935a97e210.Text: "They promised they'd assign us to a freight train several watches ago! We have families to feed!"

0250c5c2-9e63-4b6d-a1d1-1818d1f9b27f.Text: "The enforcers take bribes to put people on a list! And everybody knows it!"

4f690706-35fe-4bbd-aa02-2e50e8857590.Text: "How long do you think you can keep treating us like this? We want food! We want work!"

86dc9a7b-f570-4613-9451-678a5c663936.Text: "Look at me, boss! Got all my limbs intact! Don't even need to take breaks! Pick me!"

b219ebdf-352a-4ea1-b0fb-a16217e229be.Text: The heavy metal crates look old and battered.

d6dfc963-10b1-4a91-852e-a27172a60c20.Text: These crates are typically used to transport weapons. The worn-away markings make it impossible to determine where the shipment came from, and the scuffed surface indicates that the crates have been moved frequently.

7fce0f8f-9ed4-464c-bd3f-1cf053cfb138.Text: "Have you heard? The Rogue Trader's come down from the upper decks!"

048f618b-89b2-432c-85d9-38115ee9ca23.Text: "Heard and seen, too. Except... that wasn't quite how I imagined Lady Theodora..."

545b6295-7465-4080-869e-98e3452e849f.Text: "That's not the Rogue Trader! It's a plainclothes enforcer! Well, more of a poshclothes one, really. Anyway, they're up to something and trying to play us for fools!"

da366a60-0885-4ef4-94de-2dbaa10e2318.Text: "Glory to House... err... to the Lord Captain!"

c43df3d8-ef6c-44b9-a7a2-fc5ba55c336e.Text: "What's going on? What's all this commotion?"

4a77764e-cd27-453c-95df-8b2162eb758e.Text: The servo-overseer makes a note of everyone who passes by its station. Every time.

445838ed-45f0-47fd-bf41-2ce3134910e2.Text: A statue to Magos Ionius IX, architect of Freight Hub LD-987/A14.

9103179f-7ceb-4446-8b64-0e348a13739a.Text: "Have you heard? The Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} stopped by our bay!"

d7e1f329-6539-4056-a8a0-08bed16c3510.Text: "Yes! And {mf|he|she} looked right at me! When Lady Vigdis learns of this, she'll promote me to the middle decks!"

aa5bc0d0-f107-4adc-a119-7bfb7e6145c6.Text: "Dream on. As if she'd send the ol' half-deaf-and-raspy, pride of the Toliman vox operators, to the middle decks!"

8206c2e0-1829-4952-995a-334bb2e20612.Text: The consequences of a terrible crash on Monorail LD-987 half a century ago are still affecting the efficiency of this stretch of railway.

7933f14e-4961-4ec4-906b-8bd08c5b75d2.Text: The technomats are performing a censing rite on the sacred power transformer, but the machine spirits are running rampant and will not be swayed.

3af7d871-c42d-4093-a438-c2e5d5e09ab2.Text: "On the ground, now! And stay down, lowlife! Hands up! How dare you, you filth!"

15479ec8-bff1-41b7-a9f9-6da058ebaa2d.Text: "Too scrawny. Get lost. A container would just rip your arms off."

553ffa59-cf37-49e5-8d7c-47b642f4fdd7.Text: "Ugh, that's a face not even a mother could love. Get out of here."

6f230ac0-6c1c-4022-9158-24d9437a0c2c.Text: "You... you'll do. Assigned to the next hauling shift. Get moving!"

83d1f3e3-eaab-4a1e-95ea-12a2d367c4d2.Text: "What? What ration cards? Whose pocket? Silence, you scum! How dare you accuse a respectable enforcer of bribery!"

33009715-676e-4ad6-b606-233db82a20a8.Text: "Ah, groxtails! Threw my back out again."

9be35f71-8ed0-400a-aae8-552952918a37.Text: "They won't let us work in peace after that accident the next hub over, it's just frisking and beatings and interrogations..."

0f2e0921-7d48-4f1d-9d12-419783ec8bc1.Text: "Aah! Ah. Who are you? No! Shh! Don't make noise! They... they shot everyone! Please, don't tell them!"

c956dee0-5444-4c21-9120-b67358bbb932.Text: Barbed wire stretches along the homes overhanging the tracks, put up to protect the trains from the brazen, greedy hands of the poor.

e6842b2b-aaec-4b8e-b233-f7a6caf04ae7.Text: A strange rash appeared on your skin after you ventured into the ship's transportation tunnels. Most likely another "trophy" you have claimed from that unpleasant place.

56fb110c-13d2-47bf-b3c1-31f78ad3ad0a.Text: The scene of the worker's beating has brought up memories of your own torture.

c1efb2b5-474d-44cd-b06a-f42e9b5e8e2a.Text: You partook of the typical food on the lower decks. That was a mistake.

5d879086-ce94-488c-ace7-857f359b1bcb.Text: A foray into the world of the lower decks is a great trial for any highborn figure.

4e1e56eb-74d0-4817-a71b-fd4d00db005b.Text:
You can barely make out the crudely scribbled words on the burnt note.
"...then past the marketpl... ...ke sure the enfor... ...t you or you'll rui... ...ntire operation. On the tracks, beh... ...'ll find... ...s a little gift for... Give it to him and you'll see for yourself!"

87f664a9-7c7c-4697-9b33-73b2fd7a56a8.Text: A greasy stack of cards each entitling the holder to one portion of rationed protein and a mug of water.

4bc610d6-2400-4316-8c59-f5010b3088a4.Text: "Give our gift to the one who sees nothing but hears everything. Then the truth will be revealed to you."

fc64a552-011b-4cbf-a541-62c7f5bb9d64.Text: A cogni-stimulation system designed to be connected to the user's body. This sacred mechanism likely belonged to a Tech-Priest or noble who perished during a mission to the ship's holds along with the precious machine.

6f6dbbad-5c08-4dbf-aa80-e0e60f1fb58f.Text: [Kill the beggar] "I am sick of you."

7cb12eee-3157-4ea7-8982-f48956f535a6.Text: [Toss a stack of ration cards] "Let your bellies be full tonight."

0a6db1f6-55c9-4594-83d7-e9cdeb1824ff.Text: {n}A group of beggars are rattling their alms mugs and ostentatiously displaying their hunger-sunken bellies and various disfigurements. A toothless man falls to his knees before you.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! Shpare a throne for thoshe who can't even get the worsht jobsh!"

d0ed0a69-4746-4313-8e71-b39808071cf0.Text: "Forgive ush our impudenshe! We're leaving! We're leaving!" {n}The beggars follow their retreating leader, disappointed and angry.{/n}

d883fb9f-9053-404d-8100-d2b2fec6c589.Text: {n}The sight of a dead body makes the beggars scatter. Other inhabitants of the bay look away lest they accidentally incur your wrath.{/n}

3ea30737-b16f-420e-9710-e220e551a7df.Text: "Praished be the Lord Captain!" {n}The poor descend on the alms like a pack of gutter rats, each one scurrying off to their own corner with what they grabbed.{/n}

9f540143-8659-457e-a8dc-debf03753e61.Text: {n}The beggars circle around you insistently, casting plaintive glances into your eyes.{/n}

e073baaa-b851-406e-9c3f-dbf0fe7e8591.Text: Treated the blind smuggler with compassion.

ce4a5afe-80fa-4d9d-9beb-68c4503bc265.Text: "I did not mean to alarm you. I simply wish to learn more about my people's lives."

79735a97-e425-4a8d-bed7-bb238ce943e8.Text: [Throw a strip of dried ration meat into his mug] "Here. Have something to eat."

8e50ef50-c4c3-4fef-bee6-fa5ff9ec007c.Text: "How does a blind old man manage to survive in a place like this?"

9306ad1b-6d18-48e6-83e1-c7f596eca02c.Text: "What is that junk you are making such an effort to hide?"

acdb1b13-6756-40fc-870e-4ae3cb93c395.Text: [Place a stack of ration cards in his mug] "Perhaps a gift for you will convince you to show me?"

f6598100-23af-439a-aaeb-fc863e13a2af.Text: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius. And you will show me whatever I tell you to show me."

69d9b50b-55d8-4721-9201-107f124ee3bf.Text: [Kill the old man] "I grow tired of you."

76d05d94-a342-430d-a063-be4eaebf62e9.Text: "There, next to you — weapons are usually transported in crates like those. I want to look inside."

484963b8-6bed-47c8-864c-b0d221041932.Text: "I will simply look into that crate of yours. I will not take anything."

bef91b48-eb1f-4989-8179-84d53b375ad4.Text: {n}An old man in pitiful rags listens intently to the sound of your footsteps. A stinking piece of cloth is wrapped around his eyes, with greenish pus oozing out from under it. The old man lays his trembling hands protectively on the heap of junk that serves as his bed as well as his table. An empty beggar's mug makes a clinking sound next to his withered leg.{/n}

89ed40be-bcb7-4e83-8fd1-cfd65b720bb9.Text: "Rogue... Trader?" {n}The old man's face widens in astonishment, and he bows reverently, whispering,{/n} "I've waited... I've waited for so long, hoping to one day serve you, Lord Captain! The crate—"

ec443527-0a72-458f-8c56-49cd43009555.Text: {n}The old man ravenously sinks his remaining teeth into the meat's tough fibres, but soon gives up on chewing and swallows the piece whole.{/n} "Could this be a true miracle of the Emperor? Or... is it just another dream?"

3b192649-3b90-4742-bf7a-a59036f80c6e.Text: "The void rats gnawed them out while I was asleep. And the sewer water my wounds were washed with was infected, turns out. The pain became a stinging feeling that wouldn't go away... And only got worse."

362f0fc1-bd21-4fbd-bf7c-ada8705b9086.Text: "People help me. Good people. Not-so-good ones, too." {n}He sweeps his withered arm vacantly around the slum.{/n}

07ec5468-6fff-4ddb-ad5a-f8cf53897da4.Text: {n}The old man sinks his chipped fingernails into the rotted crate.{/n} "I heard the sound of your footsteps. The creak of your well-made soles against the metal is pleasing to the ear. You walk with confidence. You have everything you need. Don't take everything from this old man who has nothing."

24c274ea-9b61-4a54-82d1-0644a3c8c093.Text: {n}The old man scoops up the greasy cards, grins happily, and moves aside to count them, smacking his lips.{/n} "Benefactor! Nourisher! May the Lord Captain protect you!"

422eabe7-7230-4228-9a87-e061dd4e1c76.Text: {n}The old man carries on listening to the clamour of the slum for a long time, whispering an almost silent prayer to the God-Emperor all the while.{/n}

42f57fcd-4054-478c-98dc-9fcaa7c63b29.Text: {n}The skin shrunken around the man's hunched skeleton is almost translucent. That heap of junk really is likely to be everything he owns in this life.{/n}

6512c858-cc1b-4d7f-b659-13b4b7014257.Text: "Lord Captain, the only thing he has to share with you is a long list of infectious diseases. May I offer you a breathing mask?" {n}Abelard produces an actual gold-encrusted mask from his pouch.{/n}

1e8973d6-db9c-4e80-b2b2-654253c3bf16.Text: {n}The old man shakes his grey head vehemently.{/n} "Take me for a fool, do you? What would the Rogue Trader be doing down here? Liar!"

47097313-ea17-4ed9-987f-e4f720c2450d.Text: {n}A cold voice filled with the promise of death mutters,{/n} "Pathetic fool. That's our secrecy gone right down the shitter. Folks, we're gonna have to make some noise." {n}A common worker, her face so nondescript it looks almost scrubbed off, is aiming a weapon at you that she produced seemingly out of nowhere.{/n} "Leave no witnesses!"

0163510a-1e75-4d0c-bcec-290d23241fa2.Text: {n}Glaito's whole body leans in the direction of the crates sitting next to the man, and Solomorne directs your attention toward them with a nod.{/n} "Some curious things he has stored in there. I suggest you give the old man a good shake and see if he is as harmless as he wants to appear."

81bb0568-e9d0-41d2-a703-d1e2b31845ed.Text: {n}No matter how innocuous or wretched the old man's appearance, it will take more than that to deceive you. Trained always to look for {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}criminal intent{/d} first and foremost, you cast a suspicious eye at the crates — these look too much like reinforced containers used for transporting weapons.{/n}

98315f0c-4272-450d-b97c-ce65cd6754ab.Text: {n}You look into the crate and see a familiar gleam — that of weapons-grade {g|Encyclopedia:Plasteel}plasteel{/g}, polished and ready to kill. The old man was leaning against several brand-new autoguns wrapped in greasy rags.{/n}

16a687f8-73c6-463d-80ee-163bc72ef4d9.Text: "No!" {n}The old man shakes his head furiously.{/n} "Retribution! You won't escape His retribution for this!"

593f9a0d-3d66-4b6f-9dc5-c0384b1d48b7.Text: "Your people? Could it be... Our Lord Captain, our benefactor, is it really you?" {n}The old man looks shocked.{/n} "Our gracious {mf|lord|lady}, we know you well! Your charity gets us through the day, and we pray for you always! But what are you doing down in this... Please, hurry away before they know you're here! They are plotting something terrible. This crate, it's where they hide their—"

65806404-f16b-4e98-a19f-62d3c1e700a3.Text: {n}Or rather, that is what someone with no experience in the art of {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}smuggling{/d} would think if they were in your place. Hiding contraband in caches without leaving a watcher is a short-sighted gamble, as there is always a chance that some lucky scoundrel or patrolman might stumble upon the goods. Someone suitably repulsive and miserable, like this old man, often acts as the perfect deterrent.{/n}

e46d1ef6-f1a3-45df-a363-cb67282c3067.Text: "Weapons?" {n}The old man's voice sounds frightened and pitiful.{/n} "How would something like that wind up in our bottom-of-the-bilge compartment?"

2388432c-f049-41f5-9486-dac47e5f9e45.Text: "What is the situation on the lower decks?"

eba19fe1-8a18-49ec-9cf6-046513251d28.Text: "What do the lower deck officers think of Jocasta Sauerback?"

1ee25720-d72e-4c69-aa29-10a11ad7453d.Text: "Not every voidship can boast of its own railway."

3c8e8381-dd38-41a8-80a3-ebdde9d5296b.Text: "The Cult of the Bloodspun Web has a presence in this compartment, does it not?"

2f04e50b-1090-4d93-8094-d1c8be5a8903.Text: "The rabble cause you no problems, I hope?"

c74dff24-2942-4111-b0e2-e6380a8141aa.Text: "I am only going to ask this once. How did wretches from the lower decks get their hands on a crate of autoguns?"

11aff06e-d687-42ea-883c-abb3325d73f3.Text: "Be steadfast in your duty, Captain Frensoe."

38644df1-5de9-4855-93cb-3518dd3c08d0.Text: "I am satisfied in all regards. Carry on in your duty as before."

4f4b700c-3fae-4ee6-91d6-17734c836a3a.Text: "I came across a drawing of a worker in a red mask. What does it mean?"

929c2802-9615-45db-928f-be8801ce4674.Text: "Don't be shy, Frensoe. Just tell me what you think we could do to make those people's lives at least a little better."

10b102dd-7808-462d-a8d1-8a38ad46d62a.Text: "Medicine is in such short supply that people are killing each other for it. Perhaps there is a way out?"

67ac4b18-30cf-481e-b997-6eb8956207e3.Text: "Those are excellent ideas! I commend you, Captain. Get it done."

7dba41ec-dcbf-4dd4-9c5a-4b231e75a8d4.Text: "I hereby offer you my assistance, Captain. I shall conduct an inspection and then share my thoughts on how to change this place for the better."

d98fffc3-c1f7-4acc-b149-5f345bf2e976.Text: "A secret cell of mutant conspirators was operating in your jurisdiction. They were armed with autoguns and refused to surrender peacefully."

96d9af0d-3023-4b0c-9595-ab879ca94604.Text: "Rejoice, Frensoe, for the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} has deigned to deal with your problems! Rest assured, I will provide you some crucial guidance once I am done inspecting the bay."

bb1b2082-53b0-434b-8c3c-1b1a89cc9b5d.Text: "The situation in the bay does not interest me. I am here on business, and I have no intention of staying any longer than I need to."

037eb438-5d54-4bf1-9465-0cfdb12e1e22.Text: Alleviated the hardships of those who live by the freight line.

87b7a9a2-2703-441e-94ba-98cd469ebdee.Text: "The workers are to be provided with everything they need to service the freight line properly. Food and medicine will be delivered to the bay, and you are to demote any enforcers found to be abusing their authority to the status of workers."

89754911-db51-4069-b04a-d59e461da12a.Text: Imposed strict order and discipline on the daily life of the freight line.

953da432-dc95-4118-ae12-a218958d942f.Text: "Let's consider these two problems: not enough food in the vat and too many starving people around it. What could you do?"

c59c1e35-167b-47cc-a4a5-5ef50abfa6e8.Text: Opened the way for the forces of rot and decay to access the freight hub.

a1cdd0c5-016e-4f5b-bd53-8a851bc911fe.Text: [Smile insinuatingly] "The source of all of this compartment's woes are hunger and poverty, which are driving those people to commit petty crimes. I am sure you would have done something by now, but there are certain rules you have to follow that are simply too... limiting. Isn't that right?"

60663cf4-55d8-46ac-a38f-5cc09e41da35.Text: "Do you know how to reach the temple of the Bloodspun Web?"

4ac84c46-da75-4937-85bd-796c6d43bf7d.Text: "Only harsh measures will bring order to the bay. Establish an execution quota, strip all corrupt enforcers of their rank, and burn away all crime. Any idlers are to be given a job, and if they cannot do anything useful, servitorise them. Organise mandatory sermons and spread the word of faith."

51af2aa0-067f-417e-8e3c-bf49ccd2481c.Text: "I met this 'legend' in the flesh. Nemesite fell after trying to kill me."

ee97ae3c-e1c5-467e-92a3-5c1258c2d35a.Text: "He is more than just a legend. He is real, and he is a dangerous rebel."

fb02df97-085a-44e6-8fe3-6abbaae6297a.Text: [Roll your eyes] "The fantasies of the common folk... 'Protector of the poor'? Please."

670ef050-5710-483f-b80f-075de34ea9ea.Text: "The cultural heritage of this compartment is... interesting."

a664c1a2-6767-4565-87a1-681bd1a03fe8.Text: "I find these sentiments disconcerting. Stay vigilant, Frensoe."

608a86c4-4156-4fd8-8f90-33fa119a40e8.Text: "It seems you were prepared for my visit. How did you and Sauerback know I was coming now?"

7b88c0cf-aa36-4408-8b1c-b5b080b00e9a.Text: "Enforcers have been appropriating ration cards from workers returning from their shifts. Why is that? Are you short on provisions?"

72d2577c-9753-48d9-8463-c5240ecfef5a.Text: "Why are you worried? Is there a problem with this compartment?"

ddfd3ee2-ef94-4d1b-852f-94a6dc85a9b7.Text: "I am here to inspect the entire compartment. I am curious to see how people on the lower decks live."

43e9600e-e440-4e06-9f72-b125d13d0b54.Text: "Do not hold yourself solely responsible. This conspiracy is likely operating on a much larger scale. It is affecting more than just your compartment."

a31caabf-e3e3-4fd7-be1d-56a368b3ecb2.Text: "Learn from this mistake, and ensure that no 'Nemesite' is ever allowed to appear again."

5f2e641d-58b6-426e-9cfc-5322dd4e672c.Text: "I see you are expecting a punishment. Very well. Give yourself as many lashes as your body can live through."

1ce3c9dc-4e6f-4e80-9647-2cdad59e4869.Text: "What do you know about the death cultists?"

7a7b3b45-bbca-4f4f-9609-2d5712ac78e3.Text: "Why I am here is no business of yours."

d6f218e1-ac6d-44b3-a7da-033cbe0d8844.Text: "I encountered mutants in the pestilence pit. They seemed to be under the influence of unholy powers."

a0293c5c-085b-460b-9a27-74fce30dadf9.Text: "There were thieves in one of the technical rooms. I have already dispatched them."

fab34090-c9c4-47fb-96bd-27605f55baa4.Text: "The Foreman believes that the people who stole the autoguns are connected to Nemesite."

19c968da-89ec-4e6e-91a5-3fd087735c5e.Text: "It seems to me that there is a mutiny brewing in your compartment."

00139fcd-ce44-4bfb-9c69-c1fdcf92f1b5.Text: "Now you see the whole picture. Deal with this menace."

0e2cbc95-a784-4a73-8640-d97afc9e0a3b.Text: "Being assigned here seems almost like exile. Did you commit an infraction?"

a9983bff-4fff-4c47-8d96-9476f1234188.Text: "Do you not take issue with death cultists killing people on your territory?"

75f5dd3d-5a35-42ad-8cc4-2e61ea8b9a46.Text: {n}A sturdily built man with an augmented jaw stands at attention. The dark circles under his eyes speak to many sleepless nights, but his voice is loud and spirited:{/n} "Welcome to Freight Hub LD-987/A14, Lord Captain! I am Eddock Frensoe, captain of the enforcers in lower deck bay LD-A14. The Master-at-Arms has assigned me to be your liaison for the duration of your stay here."

d6d03d3b-c70d-43e0-bc7c-c8a92c1659d4.Text: "Most of the locals unload trains and sort provisions. We give maintenance jobs to the more capable ones. The rest... are reserve workforce. Whenever crew are lost on a deck, we find replacements from among those rats. And if extra hands are needed anywhere else, there are always more than enough volunteers eager to work for rations. They even queue for jobs."

6fb931be-fea2-4796-8a17-def9bd57e9c5.Text: "Hub LD-987/A14 connects the lower decks' freight, residential, and artillery bays. Our task is to monitor the flow of the labour force and prevent supply disruption between bays."

09b2caf5-04f7-4e74-ab71-d8c4ad2ffa1f.Text: "Traffic controllers. They're {g|Encyclopedia:Technomat}technomats{/g} trained by priests of the {g|Encyclopedia:CultMechanicus}Machine Cult{/g} to keep the sacred cogitators in working order and prevent train collisions. The consequences of an accident like that... would be easy to imagine. Especially if one of the trains were carrying macro-cannon ordnance."

bc514e73-471f-42fb-8957-737a77a40dda.Text: "Mistress Sauerback possesses all the personal and professional qualities required to lead the enforcers efficiently, Lord Captain!" {n}He enunciates each word with pride, but you note drops of sweat on his brow.{/n}

4145eafd-b6d7-4a1b-8015-019acbefeff2.Text: "That is true. Usually higher-class ships are the ones that get trains, but it's far from the greatest thing a Rogue Trader's {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g} can see done. The credit here goes to Lady Theodora's predecessor, on whose orders the Adeptus Mechanicus assisted in birthing this miracle of sacred engineering from the womb of the dynasty's flagship."

0204ee6c-86d7-431c-9e88-95ab2d69bc4e.Text: "Oh, another thing the bastards do on a regular basis is build their shacks in front of service tunnel entrances. That has delayed the arrival of infernus brigades during several emergencies, and caused air and power supply problems in adjacent bays. We burn those saboteurs along with their shacks, but they just keep pressing on regardless."

57725bc1-2138-4b34-8a63-c6620c307868.Text: "That is correct. The enforcers... do not bar them from carrying out their sacred duties..." {n}He scowls.{/n} "As irregular as it is to have armed crew members set up a secret hideout forbidden to the enforcers, and that they can go around dispensing bloody justice."

094ac3eb-2d79-400c-9a4a-16b541e727e4.Text: "To the best of my knowledge, being paranoid is practically a requirement in our line of work. In any case, the rabble are always plotting. Take my word for it."

8befe14f-7fad-408d-9be1-67f27cda1f1d.Text: "Autoguns?" {n}Purple spots appear on his face.{/n} "Warp take me, they couldn't have bypassed the security of a munitions train and walked away with the cargo without help from someone in the enforcers. I executed one reprobate who was trafficking in weapons not too long ago, but even that moron wasn't so greedy and stupid as to arm the rabble with autoguns. So there is another who dishonours the enforcers' uniform. I will find the maggot and shove their head under a passing train."

26f74ea6-66db-458d-ab1d-5fcc1db102b0.Text: {n}A deep furrow cuts through the captain's forehead. Then his eyes light up with a spark of curiosity, and he says tentatively,{/n} "We could... shorten the queue to the vat. And fill the vat... with the acquired resource. While they are alive and... have nutritional value." {n}He casts an enquiring look at you.{/n}

707dfec5-dc9a-4422-bad3-e15fb3f38533.Text: {n}The captain frowns.{/n} "It's a figure of local legend, known as Nemesite, protector of the poor and oppressed. Ever since I was a child, desperate people have been drawing his portrait on the walls hoping to summon a defender to punish those who wronged them. We've had thirteen or so fools calling themselves 'Nemesite' over the past five years. We... disburdened ourselves of them, just to be sure."

41362c2e-e7aa-4958-8ccf-fcf7f86d2ce8.Text: "We are short on purified air. It currently goes through three sacred cycles of filtration but... that takes a long time. Would a single sacred cycle be... too egregious of a departure from the sanitation code? The circumstances being what they are..."

9ecc6a2d-30f6-402e-ba88-18229316237e.Text: "We have faith healers in this bay practising superstition-based medicine that learned specialists have deemed to be useless at best. At present, enforcers are forbidding these quacks from healing people, but... lifting the ban on their absurd potions would somewhat alleviate the medicine shortage." {n}He stops, apparently surprised by his own boldness.{/n}

9e1ce79a-f979-4e3f-b79c-ac132ba2ec04.Text: {n}Inspired by your approval, Frensoe exclaims enthusiastically,{/n} "At once, Lord Captain!"

e26bd91b-8d4c-4f75-ba9e-71d9c4991592.Text: {n}Inspired by your approval, Frensoe exclaims enthusiastically,{/n} "At once, Lord Captain!"

c8bc12d4-9971-4876-b4f3-d7221f928eb8.Text: {n}Frensoe shakes his head fiercely.{/n} "No, Lord Captain, quite the opposite: I was commended for my service. This compartment has always been a troublesome one, and the Master-at-Arms assigned me here because she thought highly of my merits. I am honoured to have earned Mistress Sauerback's trust."

a590943f-bdbb-4cf6-81de-4e6320332751.Text: "I most certainly do, Lord Captain. I've heard they choose their victims based on omens, and that just screams trouble to me. What if they decide to kill someone they're not supposed to? But the cult's actions are officially permitted, so I have no choice but to tolerate killers walking in our midst."

3ea23659-3f75-4f80-b8a8-50804f38286c.Text: "Surely you are joking, Lord Captain? The rabble are base in nature, and mutiny is always on their minds. They steal whatever they can get their hands on, and lately they've moved from rations and tinned food to weapons. We confiscate these regularly, of course, and keep the serfs meek and terrified. That's the only way we can protect the mindless herd from themselves."

d818e3c5-01bd-49eb-96d7-58932869d726.Text: "Also employed here are an enforcer squad, a team of inferni, the clerks who keep cargo records, and a medicae officer. A fine chap whose medicine of choice is a bullet, may the God-Emperor forgive him."

f76f6cf2-1e4a-4e7b-9a80-2afb9826ef5b.Text: {n}Just thinking about the prospect of walking around the lower decks wounds your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}refined senses{/d}. Your mind conjures vivid images of filth and poverty hanging in the air, seeping out of every crack, gnawing their way through your skin.{/n}

e999baa0-e4c0-4943-bccf-30d9742cd5d4.Text: "But—" {n}Frensoe stops himself mid-protest and assumes a more compliant tone.{/n} "In that case, I urge you to remain vigilant. The freight trains move at great speeds, and the inhabitants of the residential units are... despicable rabble. One must never drop one's guard around them. And Emperor preserve you from stumbling into the pestilence pit — that's where the madmen and the lepers live."

75c20940-85f4-414a-91b0-46e7348b01ac.Text: {n}The captain raises a wary eyebrow.{/n} "Will there be any orders based on the inspection's conclusions?"

7b1f3b93-6601-445d-bfea-8d91341f4061.Text: {n}The captain needs a moment to handle his confusion.{/n} "Orders... understood."

cdc0c29d-f7a2-4984-8785-0e1ad72a5162.Text: {n}The captain nods eagerly.{/n} "Will do! We will increase the pressure on the untrustworthy element, conduct searches and interrogations to uncover criminals. We will herd the rabble to prayer services and remind them that Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s law is a stern one."

083ee7e2-6630-428a-b194-123148ad81ef.Text: "I've been told the next bay has a labour shortage. We are going to deploy our workforce reserve there. In shackles if need be."

86d21102-1bcd-40e9-bda7-ad0bff99bc24.Text: "Lord Captain, would you like to inspect the control room or... to begin your search for the temple of the Bloodspun Web?" {n}He says the last part with obvious concern.{/n}

59425589-ce0d-4489-9e46-759e7849d0d9.Text: {n}The captain throws up his hands.{/n} "We are hard-pressed for resources, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Provisions, medicine, and fuel are all being funnelled to bays that house more... valuable crew members."

504a9dea-5f86-40f4-9a15-c517724814fa.Text: "Initiating the train blessing algorithm: let not corrosive wear separate the wheelsets. Let the traction drive receive the touch of the Motive Force granted by the invisible hand of the Omnissiah. Let His grace strengthen the joints and supports that lift the body above the decay of mortal tracks. Hear me, driver, and praise the Machine God thrice, for it is only by His will that the miracle of sacred locomotion is accomplished. The blessing has been successfully executed."

14a51f19-3c42-48e7-8b7f-bddc79f562be.Text: {n}He frowns slightly.{/n} "I will admit that I have been occasionally tempted to... overstep certain boundaries in the ship's regulations."

3105c722-42df-411c-8a77-b3cae77cca7f.Text: {n}His expression darkens.{/n} "So we have yet another firebrand on our hands... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I am to blame for failing to recognise this new seed of mutiny growing among the rabble. I dismissed these signs as merely the people's attempts to vent their frustrations. I have no excuse."

66e6a693-5ea4-46c9-96aa-2981e7048eda.Text: {n}The captain shrugs.{/n} "Not much can be expected from simple-minded serfs."

415989e5-90b8-4f8d-8d41-c691744f1300.Text: "The Master-at-Arms ordered us to be on standby after the Bloodspun Web openly invited you to visit their temple. We have been awaiting your arrival every day since then, Lord Captain."

aad5ef85-a8d9-4cab-9933-fc5689b7bd99.Text: "Lord Captain, {mf|sir|ma'am}!" {n}Eddock Frensoe stops perusing the reports on his data-slate.{/n} "I hope being in this bay has not caused you any inconvenience."

b989b3e3-8d3c-404f-86d2-223d0c695937.Text: "I'm sorry, Lord Captain, I do not. No one knows — the cultists are too adept at hiding and keeping their secrets. And it worries me that you might have to walk around the entire compartment looking for the temple."

a99e075c-46ca-4b3f-9673-bd78ff6f2ac5.Text: "The lower decks are not suitable for someone of your status. And it's not just the grime or the crowds of brutish labourers — I suspect that the entrance to the temple of death is hidden in some dark corner where you might encounter criminals or contagious outcasts. With the kind of riffraff that dwells there, you might even be attacked."

3df1a885-1d6d-431e-bb8f-ecedc41e7ec0.Text: {n}He frowns.{/n} "To put it bluntly, although the bay performs its functions well, even its more civilised sections are sorely lacking in discipline. I was only assigned recently, so I haven't had time to straighten everything up, since doing so will require making some serious changes. I am not inventing excuses, Lord Captain — as the officer in charge, I accept full responsibility for what takes place in this compartment."

427c4f8a-0ca7-4ac3-a0fd-9eea0c6514f5.Text: {n}Frensoe glances at you warily.{/n} "As you will, Lord Captain. Still, out of concern for your safety, I must warn you that you should avoid the farthest sections of the bay. They are ridden with disease, and the locals can be particularly unpleasant to deal with. With the kind of riffraff that dwells there, you might even be attacked."

be79b6ed-3669-46f7-8445-5155ed022884.Text: {n}Captain Frensoe has acquired a few wounds since your last conversation. Half of his ear is gone, and you notice that he is wearing bloodied bandages under his uniform.
