Seeing you, he quickly injects himself with a stimulant and straightens.{/n} "How may I serve you, Lord Captain?"

5683f923-27c0-4241-ac37-ea0b0efd198d.Text: "Yes, there's been a raid on a local gang. We've finally cleared out the scoundrels who were smuggling goods to neighbouring compartments. No one escaped." {n}Frensoe permits himself a brief smile of grim satisfaction.{/n}

acfecc0e-2d88-47c0-b5f3-1a1b88c30da6.Text: "Yes, Lord Captain. And as soon as my back has healed, I will repeat this punishment once for every so-called Nemesite we've had by my count."

fd9f7723-4ce9-429c-949e-2fe2771bbe40.Text: "You are too lenient on me, Lord Captain." {n}Frensoe sounds completely devastated.{/n}

ccc26974-c114-407d-b865-8166cf0b84c6.Text: "The compartment has just enough food to avoid starvation, Lord Captain. This is why the enforcers are making sure that no serf has more cards than they're supposed to. They used to rip out people's tongues for it, but I reduced the punishment to simply beating the thieves and confiscating all their cards. The orders are to give these cards to workers who are starving due to a lack of work shifts — not that it helps them much, but it's better than nothing." {n}Frensoe scoffs.{/n} "Are there enforcers guilty of misappropriating the confiscated items? Yes. Do those caught stealing receive severe punishment? Absolutely."

b8f05452-643c-4c9f-9ee1-adf624ad3d2d.Text: "Not much, but I'm always trying to learn more, given that they like to pay visits to my compartment." {n}Frensoe scratches his head, thinking.{/n} "The spinners honour the Emperor through death: they kill notorious reprobates and heretics. Sometimes they kill righteous folk, and other times even seemingly at random... Their rituals are morbid and their prayers are strange — anyone not initiated in their rites would struggle to make any sense of them."

bc5232d2-22c2-4d59-83f5-217bced39ffe.Text: "You... went to the pestilence pit. You. Into the pestilence pit." {n}Frensoe stares off into the distance as he speaks.{/n} "Pardon me, Lord Captain. I just can't even begin to find the words I would use if I had to tell the Master-at-Arms that you had perished in there." {n}He rubs his temple wearily.{/n} "The enforcers do regular checks to see if there are any dangerous blight-stricken rejects hiding at the bottom of the bay. I implore you, Lord Captain — leave this job to us."

1ff171a0-68a8-4ce7-ac28-9b43df1ded60.Text: "Thieves... I just had an enforcer hanged for dealing with a local gang. I had hoped that the lesson had been learned." {n}Frensoe winces as if from pain.{/n} "By the Emperor, Lord Captain, why must you be so unconcerned with your own safety? It's our duty to find and shoot lawless scum. Throne, you are going to become the best enforcer in the bay at this rate!"

aa2cc972-5971-44fe-a892-d8b61644b45f.Text: "I can't argue with the fact that these people are truly devout and that they help to uphold order around here in their own way, but the sight of them still chills my blood."

aa0df851-66bb-4f59-9d34-bab9da15e48c.Text: {n}Frensoe avoids looking at Kibellah.{/n} "I do, Lord Captain. But the cult is authorised to exist on the ship, which means their activities down here are not to be interfered with."

fc526990-a8b5-4c09-9bab-708a3f7bc6aa.Text: "The threat of mutiny is always there, Lord Captain. We have uncovered several cells over the past month, although, admittedly, none of the traitors were armed with autoguns. We will redouble our efforts. The bastards will pay dearly for stealing our munitions."

fff894a5-f59c-4100-b9bd-3fb4ee0955bd.Text: "The Foreman... You wouldn't believe the kinds of thugs he welcomes at his vat. I agree that sympathisers of Nemesite's anarchic cause may be involved in this outrage, but I don't trust that Foreman character. He knows everyone in the bay; he sees everything, but he never informs on one of his own. He only complains about problems I am already well aware of."

ed1e222f-73a2-4183-809c-dca05beaafaf.Text: {n}Frensoe lets out a menacing growl as his face fills with blood.{/n} "Who dared?"

d5f818b2-b807-499c-b50f-ebecf89d4035.Text: {n}Frensoe grinds his teeth in fury.{/n} "I will find them. Every single one of them. And I will destroy them all."

7cc4f60d-738f-487d-864a-cef02a7d0d94.Text: {n}The captain grumbles sullenly under his breath.{/n}

9e5cde94-2248-40ea-83b8-d95b385d3128.Text: {n}Cassia shivers.{/n} "Such ghastly places you describe... We are not headed there, are we, Lord Captain?"

a6ebdb33-cd8c-47fa-97f0-3ddc24e039c1.Text: "Cass, knowing the Lord Captain, I wouldn't get my hopes up... Just think of it as an exotic outing."

2e397b2f-0c69-423b-8d3a-bcb5aa38adef.Text: "You treat most members of your own species as either a resource or a parasite. It is unsurprising that the world of humans is so filthy and dark."

3e05c6c6-85dd-43fb-9992-4eced96c4d10.Text: "All I can say is that the cultists frequent these tunnels. In fact, one has just been seen in the slums. The cult's Second Spinner, I believe."

7e46501b-95ca-4f1f-8160-360ead67963e.Text: "Well, they stopped doing that recently, and what a relief it was for me. I couldn't exactly breathe easy with trained killers walking about."

dc6fdfe4-5107-4d52-9260-c7d278a3d878.Text: "Lord Captain!" {n}The enforcer quickly puts the safety on the flamer and points the nozzle away from you.{/n} "How may I serve you?"

db7cd854-6913-4117-93c5-282336ed2db7.Text: "Burning the poor shacks, Lord Captain! The rabble build them, cutting off the air supply to the next bay and making it difficult for the inferni to work. We've told the serfs to get out of here time after time, but they won't listen. Captain Frensoe has ordered everything to be burned down, and afterward, this area to be sealed off."

744b555d-5b07-421c-9497-0e9724e87c08.Text: "I will be speaking to Captain Frensoe about what happened."

b7976539-bc4b-4005-bc5b-731658858d7d.Text: "I seek the Bloodspun Web's temple. Do you know where it is?"

5aa84502-3268-4110-b443-aae4f27c1b95.Text: "I saw you near the marketplace. What were you doing there?"

1300c4aa-b3f4-48c8-8791-e5d8111ad15d.Text: "What happened is of no concern to you. Carry on with your duties."

9c9d8cc9-3820-432b-8e8e-eda127e67d5b.Text: "Tell me what life is like for the workers on the lower decks."

c9c554ca-0ffb-4a95-b25e-a164ef0a5a81.Text: "I see you are indeed loyal to my ship and my house. Get up and continue your service to me by giving guidance to the locals."

d486acf3-93f4-4a8c-8bbe-2def0c334301.Text: "What are you cooking in that vat?"

1eecbeb0-535a-426b-beff-224c7b97d00e.Text: "Give me some of that soup. Let my servants see that any food is a great blessing!"

0883e37e-ca5e-4fb5-a0a8-131ce780d845.Text: "Pour me a bowl! I know what I am doing."

b1c9f5f6-87ee-44bc-85e8-bdb33ca74a36.Text: "I will follow your advice and not take that risk."

abdffb57-a37d-4515-8dac-0e04f13e360e.Text: "Since you are in charge here, you will answer for what happened."

a221d792-15be-414b-8c92-449916cf8000.Text: "This is some good grub. I approve."

f060a6d4-2de0-4ac4-933d-42fcf7807dce.Text: Gave ration cards to the Foreman to feed those in need.

baf5f3f7-c65b-4b2c-8d18-68eb8bdcd123.Text: [Give the Foreman a pile of ration cards] "Hand these out to the people. You'll know who needs them most."

8f24f6a0-bbc0-4269-86ba-22beef593cd7.Text: "How is your life under the new rules I set?"

7c58e6f3-12d9-4fd1-bdc4-ed4d48a49720.Text: "What in the Throne's name was that?"

786cbaf1-704e-4c20-90de-0ada16c9d704.Text: [Address the crowd] "Glory... to the Emperor... who nourishes us..."

4399452a-06ef-4299-91b7-0c2ba794ff06.Text: "Your death will be a lesson to others."

405ae0e5-992e-4bbd-a09e-d4f482cd432e.Text: "Many fine delicacies have a foul smell and an unsightly appearance. Onward, to culinary discoveries!"

408c1cf3-ce38-4f9f-ab92-1b0d812de0c2.Text: "The day the Lord Captain wandered into our slum will be remembered in legends." {n}The broad-shouldered man raises a hand in greeting. His old prosthetic creaks plaintively as it takes the weight of his body.{/n}

e623220b-bcbf-42da-b0c2-3caee50b13a7.Text: "Are you all right, Lord Captain? Those cutthroats didn't hurt you, I hope?" {n}The man's prosthetic leg has been shot, and it carries his weight awkwardly.{/n}

2a3d5858-a056-4fd1-a8b7-f422b6f32dcf.Text: "This is an honour for us, Lord Captain."

45cc6448-50f9-4765-a686-47a769219a0d.Text: "The cultists don't let people like me in on their rites and mysteries. I'm grateful to them for their service to the God-Emperor, but... to be honest, I can't get behind their love of death. I'm much too fond of living."

484e4fe3-364f-4d40-9113-0f50fecff169.Text: "Watching one of my workers take a beating. I feel sorry for the lad, but there was nothing I could do." {n}The Foreman smiles wryly, showing his yellowed teeth. Almost all of the front ones have been knocked out.{/n} "I've stuck my neck out in the past. Not doing it again."

b3e046c2-1da8-446b-93be-fb71c1b1a39a.Text: "They toil day in and day out for the glory of the ship. The rest of the time, they do their best to survive, faced with hunger, the more deranged of the enforcers, void leprosy, fires, floods, noxious fumes..." {n}The Foreman lists these on his fingers, although he has fewer than nature's average to work with.{/n} "In a word, it's a decent enough life. If you work, you survive. If you freeload, you... also survive, if you're clever. Well, and if the God-Emperor wills it."

00d3353b-d377-443c-8a8f-e97070d424f6.Text: "My people keep an eye out for workers trying to eat two bowls in one sitting. One is enough to fill your stomach for an entire watch. Some complain about the taste, of course... Ingrates."

f92cb507-d530-463b-930c-24201cf5999f.Text: "There, now, shereen, don't rush it. Let your body work."

c793bc9f-f6a8-4afb-baa1-825c3838d977.Text: "I don't think that's a good idea. Mouldslime... is something of an acquired taste. Takes two years, maybe three for your stomach to get used to it."

c3364a24-9a4f-4a37-88be-608432d92968.Text: "An outcome most unanticipated, was it not?" {n}Abelard thumps your back caringly as you fight off another wave of nausea.{/n}

9664596a-7109-4ee1-a355-e37bab302c5e.Text: "As you wish." {n}The Foreman hands you a bowl of hot, viscous sludge. The smell... could be worse... probably.{/n}

a95d8b4b-e8b4-4816-988a-ccf2d1d3e976.Text: {n}The Foreman breathes a sigh of relief.{/n} "The last thing we need is to poison the Lord Captain, Emperor forbid."

c7bd49e9-8ae7-4d67-8999-ed69f550b3fe.Text: {n}With the first spoonful comes the immediate urge to regurgitate the disgusting sludge. The heave is followed by dizziness, yet you stoically persist and force a slimy chunk of something indeterminate down your throat. The crowd is gawking at you, wide-eyed.{/n}

0556dec4-050a-4ca1-9afe-b3c0eda85cad.Text: {n}Until now, you would have struggled to imagine the taste of rotten {g|Encyclopedia:Grox}grox{/g} meat seasoned with bad eggs, sour wine, dirt, and engine oil. Now you understand it perfectly. You regurgitate your stomach's contents back into the bowl, cursing your decision in agony.{/n}

7aa2dc4b-6a48-4cd5-8990-eeeaefc75b59.Text: "May the Exalted One help you, shereen. I will hold your cloak... if you need me to."

708398e0-89cb-4256-899b-baa3a3ffb8bb.Text: "While I will certainly be able to rid your body of the consequences of this decision, I cannot say the same for your mind."

94b2f601-1d2f-4613-93ba-8adb6087a499.Text: "Throne blast it... Fair enough, Lord Captain. It's what I'd have done to myself." {n}He sinks heavily to his knees, looking solemn and gloomy. You hear terrified whispers.{/n}

de824b8f-34de-46a0-bd67-1b89c343f95b.Text: "Just a story they tell around here. There's this chap they say wanders the lower decks helping the poor who can't earn a living for themselves, and standing up to the officers and enforcers in defence of the weak. Except he's just a story and nothing more."

79ab7de8-7ebd-40f8-b20d-eaafc34da0f6.Text: "Well, in your case, he'll certainly hear you out and not..." {n}He grins and indicates his broken ribs.{/n} "You know."

c282c310-1331-4f21-bd11-9eb917757615.Text: "The locals and the enforcers call me the Foreman. I have no other name. You might say I'm in charge here, in this hole of a place."

5595c19d-492c-4d00-b659-f4a658ce56c7.Text: {n}Your words echo in absolute silence, which lasts only a moment before the starving poor erupt into prayers to you and to Him, tears glistening in their eyes.{/n}

8037a7a4-68e6-4ba9-84f9-6fbea2e2ac22.Text: {n}The Foreman's dark eyes widen. Shouts of encouragement can be heard from the crowd as he gets up clumsily and gives you a hurried nod.{/n} "I will, to be sure, Lord Captain! I serve the dynasty! Glory to House von Valancius!"

dbf21bc6-e35c-4cf4-9776-1eafa676eda0.Text: {n}Whispers of reverent awe can be heard from every level of the slums. Hundreds of eyes converge on you and the kneeling Foreman, who bows his head, half-closes his eyes, and prays quietly.{/n}

1bc265fb-2f64-4a1b-bbc1-78df7e9a8d58.Text: {n}His stern gaze sweeps the slums.{/n} "Let my repentance be a lesson to each of you faithless dogs! We must serve the Lord Captain with our words and our deeds and our lives — but our nature is corrupt and we have failed in our service! I repent and commit myself into {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}'s hands."

38e02400-d04e-4bb2-aef8-a0bd53c98136.Text: {n}A bubble rises out of the soup and bursts with a malodorous squelch. You can feel your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}noble insides{/d} protest against the crime you are intent on committing. It is still not too late to come to your senses.{/n}

d0800131-8205-4a18-836d-d5bda947ee2b.Text: {n}The first spoonful hits you hard, but you ate worse as a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Militarum}rookie in the Guard{/d}. Once you get accustomed to the salty taste and gloppy texture of the soup, the crowd watches in awe as you finish the whole bowl and lick the spoon at the end. Out there in the trenches, they call food like this "tolerable."{/n}

9b42c738-5069-48af-9762-0cb98af917c1.Text: {n}The Foreman's voice breaks the stunned silence:{/n} "The Emperor has sent us a Lord Captain who walks beside {mf|his|her} people! From here on out, this vat is blessed!" {n}The crowd explodes with cheers, and the spoon that you just used starts trading hands as if it were a holy relic.{/n}

16de3ab8-648a-4dcb-8dc3-7942b87f495e.Text: "Lord Captain, I beg another second of your attention. Please accept this humble gift from us, the common people of the bay, for all the good you do us. The most precious thing we could get for Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

7d3bf122-26dc-49e3-8293-e881293af472.Text: "Substance analysis complete. The outlook is... dim. It is recommended that you dispatch authorised units to locate an appropriate successor."

b604605b-094d-40ce-8b68-9293b64a6453.Text: "Much better, and we appreciate your care! We have half as many hungry and sick these days. May the Emperor bless you for the mercy you've shown us."

9d85672b-5ac6-40e5-a560-038bbd378796.Text: {n}The mention of rules makes the Foreman wince a little.{/n} "We spend every day doing honest work with a prayer on our lips, as the Lord Captain's faithful servants ought to. We don't grumble about the slashed rations. We don't weep for our loved ones who were taken away to work in other bays. We respect our stern enforcers, as... ferocious as they've been. We are obedient and seek to be useful."

d6e3ef18-2178-41f2-81ed-511df2068ff4.Text: "It's a strange life, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Diseases have been on the rise in this bay but fewer people are dying of them. That's... a good thing, right? The hunger's abated. Our esteemed enforcers have been tossing some kind of meat into the vat. It's just that... I sometimes hear something bang against its walls. There can't be anything alive inside, can there? Forgive me. I'm just a fool who hears things."

4d1b4093-83b5-4cde-bddf-decc17f6b7df.Text: {n}He opens and closes his mouth in astonishment.{/n} "Lord Captain, you've just helped some good families survive. I'll divide the cards among them and be sure to tell them that it was Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} who did them this good turn."

e9f3ca32-14e6-47ab-a0e3-fc63b5d9fdbd.Text: {n}You recognise the shaggy red beard and the keen black eyes. This is the man who was watching you during your encounter with the enforcer and the station worker.{/n}

b840459d-49b2-480d-8cf3-d8e0a684ed87.Text: "Believe it or not, this soup made from mouldslime and technical drain water has been simmering here in this vat for at least two hundred years nonstop! See the growth on the walls over there? We harvest it, dry it, and use it to season the soup. If we're lucky, the smell attracts a void rat, and someone gets to have meat in their bowl." {n}The Foreman points a finger proudly toward the vat.{/n} "It's for those who can't even earn a ration card. I feed them in exchange for services or favours. Sometimes it pays off, and sometimes it doesn't."

23551462-f005-4397-9ccc-987ed56621c1.Text: "The Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} has tried our food and found it worthy! Remember to be grateful for any nourishment, as it is a blessing!" {n}The Foreman bellows and roars while discreetly interposing himself between you and the crowd of ecstatic commoners, who look like they might otherwise swarm and accidentally trample their overlord in a frenzy of adoration.{/n}

d883c39d-2906-4ca5-9733-27c923c180b1.Text: {n}The Foreman raises his voice to the crowd.{/n} "What are you lot looking at? Off you go before I close up the vat for a week!"

81dac0aa-dec3-4390-957c-cdcca5965873.Text: "Lord Captain, you must be joking, surely?"

938bbfef-fbec-4aed-8324-4f7ff58eff5f.Text: {n}The grins on the worn-out faces turn to sour grimaces as the crowd disperses and the queue reforms.{/n}

0f67be84-e28f-4099-8b60-17f3a607e7b6.Text: "As if. {mf|He|She}'s serious as a void kraken."

2090f38e-7630-4967-b5b4-94bacc4cb63c.Text: "I'm... not sure. Perhaps those freeloaders believed in the tales of Nemesite. As it happens, I've complained to that bast— to Captain Frensoe about some idiots who've been painting pictures on the walls, inciting people. And what did he say? 'I've got everything under control.' Had I known it would come to this, I'd have nabbed those sods and thrown them into the pestilence pit myself! And now we'll be pestered by enforcers to no end, void damn it all."

8e4f2fd0-224d-49b6-a58e-aad82478a173.Text: "Exciting, is it not?" {n}With an intrepid smile, Einrich places your palms on the controls, covers them with his own, and pulls the levers down in a confident motion.{/n} "Don't be afraid. I won't let him hurt you."

e20c34b9-dcaa-4746-8cd7-a34625371272.Text: "I have decided to get acquainted with my demesne."

76654073-b261-4369-be19-789061990171.Text: [Listen to the rumbling noise coming from the boiler]

f895e2ce-3a43-4dad-b447-d121ff7de8c0.Text: "I seek the Bloodspun Web's temple. Do you know where they are hiding?"

4142440b-66c4-47a2-849a-243d38c6db5b.Text: "I cannot turn down an offer like that."

e946af7a-e310-4a49-8223-99d7165847f6.Text: "A change of plans. Full speed ahead — we are heading down the freight line."

8350d204-9082-4443-aacf-a7158a49124b.Text: [Grasp the lever and gently pull it toward you]

603901d8-b8c8-47eb-92ea-b720baa8beb8.Text: [Reach for the ornately carved levers and awaken the beast]

32268cda-1fb8-442b-9263-3042eb034315.Text: [Wink at Einrich] "Show me how it's done."

33e2be52-6bff-4e38-9755-98b3897bf8a0.Text: [Pull the lever and pump the fuel]

5cf36d85-705d-459a-b534-7724cdff41a3.Text: [Smile at Einrich] "Unruly and defiant, but submits to a strong hand. Much like yourself."

c4f94828-f08c-48be-b57d-ec69679aab73.Text: "I doubt that I will have much use for this lesson."

a43230d6-c665-47c8-bc96-59787212ca1b.Text: "That was most intriguing, Einrich. I am pleased."

7b575e47-16cb-4c84-aae8-f04d56193f4d.Text: {n}The Infernus Master salutes you cheerfully with his lho-stick.{/n} "Lord Captain, what an unexpected encounter! What brings you to this compartment? The famous cuisine and magnificent vistas, no doubt?"

0cdfe7bf-f53e-4b14-acc3-5814b6fddf87.Text: "I don't have the foggiest idea, and that's probably for the best. I have my hands full as it is."

a0b7d7fb-e06a-4fb9-b733-633cee08955b.Text: "I'm here to patch up Savage, locomotive number three, under the Tech-Priests' supervision. That old grump is my personal favourite on the entire freight line. Every couple of years, Savage gets mad: his boiler catches fire and starts spitting steam at the repairmen. Guess who they call to take care of him in these situations. The inferni, of course! And after I've done all the most dangerous work, that's when the iron brains come in. But that's all right. I love Savage."

88684c29-d6be-4d9d-899a-7b20dfbf4ed8.Text: {n}The stubborn machine does indeed seem remarkably similar to a wild beast. The roar of the mechanism resembles hoarse growling, and the scarlet glow of the lumens on the control panel makes you think of the malicious glare of a predator. The spirit of this machine is vicious, but strong and lively.{/n}

9540b4a7-ea17-4b05-bef4-153ba6ff39b8.Text: "You know, that might be for the best. The dynasty needs a Rogue Trader, not a charred piece of ember."

d26e30ef-f8dc-4ae9-9131-636727481d17.Text: {n}A deafening clang resounds from Savage's innards, and the train shudders underfoot, as if preparing to leap forward.{/n} "Whoa! Careful, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Don't let this monster smash us against the nearest wall."

2a536228-5d90-48b5-ad66-a9d5e1633303.Text: "Oh, I refuse to believe Savage would dare scald the Lord Captain. He definitely should not."

4e74aa11-7f8f-461a-a68c-f32789b29171.Text: {n}The panel before you is covered with technical runes, {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumens{/g}, and levers. The platform shakes with the boiler's mighty vibration as the iron beast beneath your feet growls and snorts ferociously.{/n}

c94248b3-b9cb-4300-bab8-abd8f3205b46.Text: "When he's in a good mood, the feeling you get standing at his levers and speeding down the freight line is indescribable... I envy those Tech-Priest drivers who get to operate him every day — the roar of the boiler, the wheels thumping like mad, and all that furious power pulsing in your hands, responding to the slightest movement. How about..." {n}There is a mischievous spark in Einrich's eyes.{/n} "...I introduce you?"

1a344f3f-1117-4231-afcc-c7e86bd1b948.Text: "As you command. I do hope you're leaving with a favourable impression. Enjoy your walk! Meanwhile, I will take a ride on the freight line and see how our little rascal here behaves at full throttle."

1c0fc3a2-ca86-44ba-afbc-37108e54bd5c.Text: "Do you feel it? There is so much energy and defiance in him... This is a rocket, not a locomotive — unruly and enamoured with speed, but... quite willing to submit to a strong hand." {n}There is almost a loving tenderness in Einrich's voice.{/n} "Pull the lever toward you, smoothly but firmly. Then, pump the fuel with this command rune."

7af7d3ba-30ee-47c5-802b-90c4da8a5772.Text: {n}A roguish gleam appears in his eyes.{/n} "You don't say?"

114a3318-6f2a-4e75-b2e9-a65f4abaee3f.Text: {n}A torrent of steam bursts from the slit in front of your face, but Einrich deftly covers you with his shoulder. A moment later, you realise that you cannot hear a thing... Or rather, you hear only one thing: the roar of the engine, triumphant and powerful.{/n} "Looks like Savage has agreed not to kill us both. His Tech-Priest guardians will be pleased."

a4761863-5d7e-4944-8666-3704f309effb.Text: "Not quite, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I said Savage is not dangerous, but 'not dangerous' ends right here. He might just pull a stunt and bake us to death during the ride, and it would be better if the ship did not lose another Lord Captain."

e48e4d9e-bef9-4bd2-bd81-d64518b883bd.Text: "Everything is going to be all right. Savage would never fry me... Right, Savage?"

fca898ee-f1b2-4711-b664-44238022f4ae.Text: "All hail the Lord Captain! You have subdued a mighty beast today. Now, I'm sure you have urgent business to attend to, and it's time for me to drive Savage down the line and see if he is feeling cranky."

e7d5fe79-2f66-487f-80a8-192142a232a0.Text: {n}Yrliet tilts her head to the side in confusion.{/n} "Is this still a conversation about mon-keigh machines, or something else?"

fc45bc88-a0d5-4741-94fb-6eb6fe8a2b51.Text: "In that case, I hope that you at least had some fun. Good luck, Lord Captain."

01b3bb14-878b-4aca-8976-cb5fd858acf6.Text: {n}Einrich squints contentedly and whispers the litany of ignition before turning to you.{/n} "The machine is angry and refuses to obey. Right now, Savage is powered only by the auxiliary manoeuvring engine. We will need to start the main rotor if we want to take a trip down the freight line."

7883c80a-4f93-43a6-9022-f3e896d4f268.Text: "Then you've picked the most unassuming part of it. My mentor used to say that a ship is like the human body. If that's the case, we are definitely standing inside its iron bowels right now."

5290b9a9-9efb-46ea-b714-de4f0e3d9776.Text: "Put your hand on the big lever and gently give it a pull. Very gently!" {n}Einrich's face is focused, but his voice has not lost any of its playful cheer.{/n} "Savage does not like being hassled."

514bf7c2-111b-4894-a941-e4894177d3de.Text: {n}A few erratic jolts shake the platform, and an indignant groan emanates from the depths of the machine. An intense shudder passes through the lever and into the palm of your hand, and there is a strange feeling of emptiness in your stomach. Savage's fiery heart is stirring.{/n}

e85f3b51-5bf0-4b31-a14c-6fb8efcb7660.Text: {n}Einrich lowers his eyes and grins.{/n} "Could I have wished for anything more, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"

799652aa-3333-43ee-923d-b732bc0c791f.Text: {n}Savage lets out an angry rumble, and the boiler mounts rattle pitifully. One nut snaps off its threads and flies past your head toward the platform like a bullet. You hear a scream followed by panicked cries.{/n} "Another accident to your name, eh, Savage?" {n}Einrich quickly adjusts the lever, reducing the fuel supply.{/n}

94c34f29-bfcf-4402-9bef-20bbfb70aa3a.Text: {n}A new explosion inside Savage shakes his iron body, causing your eyes to see double from the vibration.{/n} "Now you are feeling his real power. He can run down the entire freight line in a minute, given the chance... And kill everyone who rides him at that speed. Now, try applying some thrust to the main rotor — grab those paired levers and give them a firm tug."

1a6e73a2-5097-436b-a911-ef363115a886.Text: "I have had experiences with mechanisms that preferred to be turned on quickly and boldly. I guess this engine has a different design." {n}Jae innocently runs a finger along the control panel.{/n}

05690290-3d29-42bf-a94a-f21ccd7ad3c6.Text: "Thank you for your assistance against the mutineers."

94675ee6-c1d6-415d-b815-b6b116e77075.Text: "Perhaps you might help me find the entrance to your temple after all?"

6644015e-662a-4198-9237-210beeae1245.Text: "I have changed my mind. I will permit you to accompany my retinue."

3dcaf8a8-898a-4b5f-a7c5-7d4d3437bb4f.Text: "What is the situation on the lower decks?"

5e5e5e94-dfd7-4b0d-b7f3-10d64ce1713f.Text: "Watching time slip away. People never pause to consider how many breaths they have left to take before they feel the kiss of death. Ignorance... has its own form of beauty."

ed874776-6627-4a24-b95d-2b064ed7f159.Text: "I was simply following the thread of the Web. For their time had come, and the Undying One reached out a hand to receive their souls."

165eae59-9272-4e27-8101-ec4239f76a20.Text: "My duty to the Undying One prevents me from interfering in the Vizsier's design. I cannot become the thread that guides you. But I can be at your side as you walk that path."

59214032-0a03-4830-abf0-f8be3487528c.Text: "The Bloodspun Web has heeded your orders. The spinners are no longer ushering souls to the other side. Not everyone in the cult was ready for the change, and the tunnel-dwellers were less ready still."

20fe4908-8909-47d9-a6c6-010fc3fad97c.Text: "Walk with silent footsteps amid the whispers of the Undying One."

e8d8b48b-a9c8-450e-a391-f26220c78d6c.Text: "The weak and miserable grasp at the chance to live another watch. The strong and cruel threaten them with swift death. Neither realise that the end of the thread is true freedom from fear and pain."

8b6676d9-3995-46cc-a6cf-00bd1e544a3d.Text: "Go forth and I will follow you."

7f3322a4-4d4e-405a-88b5-b85b5390bf0c.Text: "The threads of our destinies have been woven together again. But for how long?"

1dd4defa-3fdb-4f8a-abe3-3c9e7b356f1a.Text: "They believed the Undying One had cursed them and revoked His mercy. They thought murderers and other wrongdoers now had free reign. Fools. There are many ways to serve Him without severing souls from bodies."

b85bc0fc-196e-4419-8bf4-ee1839685a13.Text: "Domin'{name}. You have descended into the darkness after all." {n}You can just barely discern the nebulous gaze behind the eyeholes of the bone mask.{/n}

61091345-4836-4bf5-acb8-a48762a3618f.Text: "Am I to understand that enforcers are appropriating earnings from workers after their shifts?"

3826c368-7d15-4b5d-bd6a-551965373d6b.Text: [Strike the enforcer] "Consider yourself discharged, thief. Tomorrow you are to stand here and queue for a work assignment like the others."

33500858-766a-47be-8784-e68bc134b455.Text: [Stop the enforcer] "I intend to hear this man out."

999cbec4-ca50-431d-91a0-dc0ef9b94195.Text: [Let the enforcer do his job] "Make it quick. I have places to be."

413376d7-fdf6-4af6-ae34-6cf633bfc3a8.Text: [Kick the worker] "Out of my way, blasted filth!"

01e5a79f-d445-4c1b-bb90-4dbe6e991835.Text: [Address the enforcer] "Return the cards and do not dare abuse your position again."

2225de4e-2695-4699-8dee-93554371396c.Text: [Address the worker] "Every crime will be punished accordingly. I offer no protection to thieves."

775b8a89-2e3f-4744-9a33-61daa2356509.Text: [Raise your voice] "The Imperium is surrounded by enemies! They are many, they are cunning, and they are spiteful! Who is to blame for your hungry days? They are! But we, the Emperor's faithful servants, are stronger than their scheming ways! We are steadfast! We will not yield! We will tighten our belts, stand as one, and prevail! Who is with me?"

62465763-d8cf-4995-8723-5e96a3eed582.Text: [Add a note of sagely depth to your voice] "Society, you see, is much like a boot. Its toe proudly directs the foot of the Imperium forward, and yet it needs a sole to stand on. You are the sole, good people. That you are down here choking on dirt without ever seeing a sliver of light is not the result of someone's ill will, but rather, it is the logical order of the world. I hope that understanding this fact will help you make peace with your destiny and free you of all spite."

9d16efde-030c-4bd0-b8d8-cfc4f6d5673f.Text: [Gaze proudly and solemnly at the crowd] "Would I have achieved glory if I had complained about every hardship along my path? No! I pressed ever onward in spite of all the adversity! So must you — and we will remember your names for it!"

feb0087a-6bed-4d7a-a144-209fe3bea3b3.Text: "You both deserve punishment. Strip the arbitrary enforcer of his rank and give lashes to the thief."

4c527cc1-901e-4569-99f9-7460139e363b.Text: {n}The battered worker throws himself at your feet and touches the toe of your boot with his dirty palms.{/n} "Your gracious {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Hand of the God-Emperor! Save your unworthy servant!"

6ff7140b-89d6-4463-9dbb-93c3b06d4196.Text: {n}A murmur of discontent breaks out among the gawkers who have gathered around. None of the other workers dare come closer, but the anger on their faces is plain to see.{/n}

27b3991d-bce6-414b-a602-c928f05131bc.Text: {n}Low, insistent dissent begins to rise in the crowd, only to die back down as soon as the enforcers brandish their batons. The murmurs immediately turn into pleas for mercy.{/n}

c3b9dc09-3b9d-4f9b-aadc-89e54a16536c.Text: "We appropriate nothing. We just monitor and redistribute," {n}the enforcer mutters gloomily.{/n} "The rabble are a lying and thieving lot. We have instructions to stay alert for people holding more than the standard amount of ration cards. To prevent supply embezzlement and famine."

0acdc367-3f55-4b00-8ec0-db184fcee6fa.Text: {n}A sullen, red-bearded man with keen black eyes draws your attention. His oddly piercing gaze seemed to size you up the whole time you were speaking, but now he has hastened to conceal himself behind the gawkers. The next thing you know, you are watching him hurry deeper into the tunnels.{/n}

cb7b7f20-776d-418b-9841-4eda56abaedd.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I work hard, never even take breaks to rest, and all I earn is seven ration cards with fifteen mouths to feed back home! The enforcers shake me down every shift, just like they do every other honest hard worker who—"

da786ac8-45c0-42ed-a4e6-bb0cb02017d2.Text: "Enough whining! You and your pals lifted a box of nutribars a few watches ago, and two canisters of water before that. I didn't beat the life out of you because I took pity on you, and this is the thanks I get?"

4e7520ec-d4a8-4b99-8fe1-1b202a970658.Text: "I didn't do them in, it was an acc—" {n}The worker stops himself, cowers, and whimpers,{/n} "They got their heads bashed in by crates! The dead don't need rations!"

b52eec93-39a8-4379-b3ce-58e1645e1ee5.Text: {n}The clamour rises, becoming too persistent, deafening, suffocating... Then a baton lands a crunching blow somewhere in the crowd, and everyone quiets down.{/n}

97387d9d-8836-4d42-8210-b9cda0731c5a.Text: {n}The onlooking workers bellow triumphantly and point at the enforcers, praising the Lord Captain.{/n}

a6a23a4c-eaf5-4c2d-b609-98cf559f9957.Text: {n}The enforcer hastens to remove one of his gloves, then starts shining your boot.{/n} "Almost d-done, Lord Captain!"

6ec146bf-c620-4059-8e04-37d2fb2949d1.Text: {n}With a crunch, your boot breaks the bridge of the unfortunate man's nose.{/n} "I'b sorry, please, I'b sorry! It hurts so buch..."

7b3bcfd4-7cd9-4a19-bfae-0e036dc47a97.Text: {n}The terrified man glances furtively at the enforcer, who is grinning.{/n}

03a9c0f7-8872-48ce-bc1b-4a22a3eb062c.Text: "May the God-Emperor protect you and all of House von Valancius, Lord Captain!"

b7e9c2b0-0eee-4490-acb1-fe11273b31e4.Text: {n}The enforcer hisses at the worker vindictively,{/n} "Oh yes, Twelve. This time I'm gonna break thirteen of your fingers and ribs, as a lesson to your slimy accomplices."

5a4a0e3c-936f-4454-a815-29e7c06ecd37.Text: {n}Your inspiring visage, just like the one they used for the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}propaganda poster{/d}, sends the serfs into a frenzy of rapturous cries. You hear them channelling all their hopes to overcome the odds just as you did. Even the beaten man stares at you with a wistful smile on his lips.{/n}

86bd5998-ee10-4e89-b033-bd2a6b6b1298.Text: {n}Alas, the ungrateful rabble is incapable of fathoming the sheer grandeur of your views on social structures. Blinking their ignorant eyes dully, the serfs continue to stare at you without proper respect.{/n}

aaf94801-2351-4962-ba47-a42fc4fdda77.Text: {n}The worker snarls at the enforcer, who has suddenly gone pale.{/n} "Didn't expect that, now did you? Once my back stops hurting... we'll see how brave you are without your baton."

ce112fc8-0746-43fa-82d1-83a66c447fbc.Text: {n}The discharged enforcer, surrounded by spiteful leers, glowers at the crowd as the beaten worker laughs uproariously, seemingly far more pleased with the other's misfortune than troubled by his own sentence.{/n}

f73361c1-46f1-4372-abb2-0e282ffc0265.Text: "Shereen, this poor sap is just trying to survive. One small mercy from the Rogue Trader, and this man will go home with at least half of his bones intact."

fd7f1b95-c9d1-4962-81c8-f417894b6381.Text: "Am I surrounded by mon-keigh, or a pack of carrion eaters fighting over a single scrap of rotten flesh?"

8dc95cec-cd04-4c1f-87f1-64bae53b8a73.Text: "Learn to savour their company, cousin. This air of dull, unsophisticated violence is the best their kind can offer." {n}Marazhai leers viciously, looking at the terrified worker.{/n}

e62fb421-7677-4cb1-89dd-e30d6d08306b.Text: "Get lost!" {n}The enforcer's heavy baton pummels the man's back and shoulders several times. His bones crack audibly.{/n}

b2d9af4a-ed60-4742-987e-8d0382e56c96.Text: "My sincerest apologies, Lord Captain! Your boot... I'll clean it right away!"

41db1535-8a0a-40ff-a761-f16ea6865483.Text: {n}The enforcer freezes in place, not daring to raise his hands to his red-hot face, and squeezes out a lifeless{/n} "Yes, Lord Captain."

3ee25321-3131-4f1b-83a9-4052ad247cf6.Text: {n}The sound of breaking bones, the man's cries, and the enforcer's hateful laughter remind you of what {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}you went through{/d} yourself. Too vividly, and too painfully.{/n}

02ad40e5-8f0d-4d97-b7f5-3c90aa5683e2.Text: "They do take our cards, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! And then grow fat using them for themselves!" {n}The worker's eyes squeeze shut tightly as he whispers his accusations. He seems unable to believe his stroke of luck.{/n}

7958dbe2-8232-4321-98b7-92bf0532ee47.Text: "You quarantined the hub for twenty watches and refused to give out rations if we didn't have cards. Cards we had no way to earn!"

52981b6d-519e-4ee1-8dc7-8d86f59b7019.Text: "And today you earned fifteen cards in a single shift because you do the work of three people, right? Or did you take your pals to a dark corner somewhere, do them in, and take their share?"

2abeb5dc-fcc1-48f8-b723-5a2d7ea84457.Text: {n}The crowd roars, inspired by the words of a true {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}disciplinary officer{/d}. The worker wipes his face on his sleeve and makes the sign of the Aquila with trembling hands. He is no longer thinking about ration cards as he stands side by side with the same enforcer who was just beating him.{/n}

4b363527-30da-45ce-b1e9-438d47b2d655.Text: "For what crime did you kill this man?"

5748fe28-e078-4062-a1ca-a4e371a7e893.Text: "I am the Lord Captain of this ship. On your knees, insolent scum!"

9a7bfff7-10eb-41c2-a80a-7b40cf20cff3.Text: [Attack] "The ship will be a little cleaner without you."

16d67bdb-bf1f-4b55-bbc9-e8d05bffd4a3.Text: "You need medicine and food. I shall have them brought to you."

01277120-8919-477f-aefb-16befdeaf592.Text: [Give a coin] "I can see that no one ever shows you any kindness."

3c085cea-b400-4c0a-b42f-1e06946f2514.Text: Propelled the mutants that dwell in the pestilence pit of the freight hub into the service of the forces of rot and decay.

c75d9e8b-8ebc-4c4c-bd46-9837cfb28a22.Text: [Whisper] "I just want you to know: you have been showered with blessings that others can only dream of."

96198db7-6b85-40bc-a5ea-e69245cdad2c.Text: [Attack] "You are sentenced to death for committing murder on my ship."

7a1dc69c-f568-4968-8a01-af01f9796e33.Text: {n}The specimens before you must be the most repellent inhabitants in the compartment — they are covered in sores and bald patches glistening with pus, and the stench of unwashed bodies brings a tear to your eye. One of them glowers at you and grunts,{/n} "Wotcha want?"

75177193-65be-4142-bdaf-92e277527e3f.Text: {n}He grabs the throne and tests it with his teeth.{/n} "Don't expect thanks — you gave it to me freely, got it?"

03634e9d-1b7c-4f95-9bb3-85260fb89c7f.Text: "What the..." {n}The man breaks off, and then his ugly face spreads into a sly grin, and his numerous sores begin to fill with pus.{/n} "It's true, isn't it? Yes... Someone is watching over us, keeping us safe. How did I not realise it before?"

e42b2f71-5a01-483f-ac2f-0298ae9759f8.Text: {n}Grinning, the leader spits out,{/n} "For the crime of wealth. That dead bastard had rations and fuel cells. We'll trade them for porridge."

704f0084-bbe4-4550-a9d0-8ad32d9726eb.Text: {n}The outcasts look at one another and burst into hoarse, gurgling cackles.{/n} "The Lord Captain in our shithole! And I'm Saint Drusus, and here's my rigalia!" {n}The man exposes an armpit riddled with boils.{/n}

810a9e36-bfbe-40d9-89d6-7c7d59ac042e.Text: {n}Cassia lets out a faint sigh, hastily covering her face with her hands.{/n} "Gracious Emperor... Why are we talking to these horrible people?"

c42fd7bf-aafc-44eb-be95-b44d3aa9ccbe.Text: {n}Argenta towers over the freak, looking immaculate and unaffected.{/n} "Even meeting wretched heretics such as this brings me joy. Wiping out even a drop of corruption is still a worthy deed."

f0c81f2a-6634-4d2d-ba5b-b63b11fafca3.Text: {n}Abelard attentively holds out a snow-white handkercher to her.{/n} "I fear, Lady Cassia, that these and many other questions will be left unanswered."

c177b5e5-80c5-4836-9ca8-b6304c5e23cd.Text: {n}The mutant bares the black stumps that are his teeth.{/n} "We'll gut you and trade what you have on you for a pile of scran. Hey, outcasts, come on up if you want a share in the spoils!"

207c6f3f-c527-4902-88eb-06a3e0d6ced8.Text: {n}The longer you stare at the man, the more deviations from the human form you detect. Wretches such as this, disfigured by genetic abnormalities and disease, are the perfect breeding ground for true corruption.{/n}

0ac875c1-96d0-4b98-9119-9289c1fa92ec.Text: {n}The outcast licks his lips and you see a tongue studded with small, underdeveloped teeth. This is no disease, but an obvious mutation.{/n}

50f802e2-4bbe-44d5-9735-2beab227f887.Text: {n}The man bares his teeth malevolently.{/n} "Will you now? We know your kindness — you'll douse us with poison and leave us to die. So we don't sully your ship."

cd777ac7-8006-4e9a-8daf-2344da24ec16.Text: "Oh, you'll leave. But without your boots. And your weapons. And maybe a piece or two of your flesh." {n}He leers mockingly.{/n} "Didn't anyone ever tell you it's dangerous to poke your nose into the pestilence pit?"

83f9fc10-f68f-45c6-84df-f73d2f490cec.Text: "If we're blessed, then we can live in this hole. We can live... and share our blessings." {n}The mutant's gaze lingers on you, his eyes glistening with slime.{/n} "Thank you."

58a8fe41-c749-424b-b392-2956c08f8cdf.Text: {n}You detect a note of hysteria in the vagrants' laughter. The fingers of many are convulsively trembling. And there is something in the fearless way they look at you, an indifference to death... too strange and unnatural.{/n}

8955a1b4-62fc-4bcc-9f3a-072cf34473d0.Text: {n}From the vagrants' mouths comes the most repulsive laughter you have ever heard.{/n}

5f1b8b99-c24b-44f0-b90a-b6ef2829b9a7.Text: "Mould-eaters. Outcasts. Folk who have no place even among the lowest of the low. Some were born that way, some were driven out to keep them from spreading the contagion. The Foreman won't let us near the vat, the enforcers try to shoot us on sight. As if it's our fault that we were born in a terrible place... We are worms in the rotten belly of this ship, fodder for disease."

7e42e963-847f-479e-a51b-179bf5dc070f.Text: "Why are you wearing chains and a mask? You haven't escaped from the enforcers, have you?"

c5d1832b-1edc-4e11-ae0c-59624cc82643.Text: "What is this repulsive place? Do you live here?"

feaff262-49a0-4cac-9295-332eeb4bfbc9.Text: [Peer into the darkness] "I cannot fathom what I am meant to see here..."

fba2bd3d-c9ca-45cd-917b-cae510673a97.Text: "How do I become the flagship's blood?"

044573d4-ae81-47cb-bab6-f80ba32d1f78.Text: "You are insane. Out of my sight!"

df69abbd-819f-4893-8c0b-811a5e82ab41.Text: "There is a blood symbol next to you. I have seen such marks before. Is this another part of the Song of Trailing Blood?"

184be221-9bb7-4ac1-9d54-013a43dd0c10.Text: {n}A figure in decaying tatters is rocking to and fro, muttering indistinctly in several different voices, occasionally breaking into hoarse laughter. As you come closer, she freezes and turns slowly to look at you. An ugly, rusted mask covers her face.{/n} "Are you... here to take Zdena to the other side? No. No no no."

84f28a3b-fd31-437a-bd4a-33ed9af0eb16.Text: "You're just wandering around in the dark. Looking for the light... but it's nowhere to be found. Do you really not see it?"

11b1cb53-9ac2-4360-891e-4dbd18594b7b.Text:
{n}The woman starts chanting hurriedly:{/n}
"She wandered an eternity in dark,
yet was consoled. Web foretold:
Undying One's blood-secrets glowed,
a light to guide her faithful fold.
But threads must end. And so the spider
did that which was owed:
her life and death to ship bestowed..."

796fc83d-f0a7-4517-9886-b4e9dc5d71dd.Text: "Old Zdena. Zdena the Outcast. Zdena the Mad. Zdena the Disaster. Zdena the Curse. Zdena the Spurned." {n}The woman hugs her arms to her chest and starts cackling loudly. Broken chains clink at her emaciated wrists and neck.{/n} "A ghost of the past? A shadow of the present? Only the Undying One knows. He alone..."

ba7a340f-79b5-4ce4-8131-3b3e6aae4f9e.Text: {n}The woman scratches her neck nervously. You note her deformed fingers, ravaged by some unknown disease.{/n} "Here, where the unfortunate meet their undeath. Here, a dumping ground for the bodies of those the Undying One rejects. Here, where pestilence dwells. Zdena welcomes them all. Talks to their ghosts. Here, where Zdena... lives? Yes. That sounds right."

32a4c2ab-07e6-43b2-b732-ce35909735f7.Text: "Ah, these. Gifts, they are. The chains clink to announce Zdena's approach. For others to hear." {n}She slides her disease-darkened palm down the rough, rusted metal of her mask.{/n} "They hide, fearful of becoming like Zdena. Afraid of losing face... ha ha ha!"

fd62b7d9-b25b-4951-a4e5-269d0d5539f5.Text: "You... can't hear them?" {n}Zdena points somewhere off to the side, laughs, then stops herself sharply.{/n} "They don't like it when people come here."

68bbc750-145e-474c-bf50-071d4e20260b.Text: {n}Zdena breaks into hysterical laughter.{/n} "You'll be back! Everyone who's looking for something comes back. Or... do they? Why come back when you've found what you were seeking?"

4a6e8502-8894-4da0-81be-a7312dadfbb8.Text: {n}You peer into the darkness, and are gradually able to make out the outlines of objects hidden in the shadows. Rotting corpses. Rough walls. The twitching death throes of infected people left here to die. You see no light in this place, only more darkness and despair.{/n}

1e1c2f7d-c2eb-4a3b-a05c-619f5be50e7d.Text: "You don't see, do you? You don't see!" {n}Zdena shakes her head frantically and starts tearing off her rags. Strips of her decaying flesh peel off along with them.{/n} "You will not see until you become like Zdena. The flesh and blood of this ship!"

5a03708d-8f19-4899-b134-3b95c22970cc.Text: "Oh, Zdena will show you. And you'll see the true light. Come. Come now!"

ed24f5cf-2c1f-46b1-a7ee-e9f931efb802.Text: {n}The woman turns away and starts talking to someone only her eyes can see.{/n}

5e9a9fc6-559b-43fc-8d85-a2e81c054dd1.Text: {n}Ulfar clutches his protective amulet, his brow furrowing.{/n} "Malevolent, ever-hungry spirits prowl in places such as this. It was they who gnawed the madwoman's mind thin. It is dangerous to speak to people like her — madness is a contagious bane."

29efcbd7-3f65-4c6f-80dd-d674b48ff9d7.Text: "Her colours are all mixed, smudged, poised to reveal a pure shade of madness... And yet, scarlet threads separate these trembling patches, preventing her from losing herself."

b6139151-452f-44f6-9f90-f05cdffb3cb4.Text: {n}Zdena bursts into hysterical laughter.{/n} "Oh yes! Oh yes... The song... Here, listen, listen!"

d7124b4c-3485-4f14-89dc-860e361f35fe.Text: "Lord Captain, this woman is clearly ill in both spirit and body. Best to leave her be."

34cdd0c2-3dc0-42d0-bfa1-6b4931a20652.Text: {n}She laughs again.{/n} "And you'll see, you'll see if you learn to see! Look into the darkness, look, look!"

ef908caa-6b1a-4db7-8d1d-4afdacf8178d.Text: {n}The final test. This time, they want you to make a sacrifice. If one were to {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}interpret{/d} this entire mystical search as a repetition of the saint's journey, then the logical conclusion is that you are supposed to sacrifice yourself — to merge with the blood that has drenched the flagship from bow to stern.{/n}

c788e8a4-4033-40ad-8ae8-0cb0d59c9b8d.Text: "A fairy tale indeed, risking oneself for nothing. If such a man existed, he would surely be profiting from your misfortunes in secret."

93c132e5-88a1-4860-a62d-dd18c0596052.Text: "You there. Why are you idling about and distracting the other workers?"

d2f09db1-5156-4953-9c2e-69873b853a68.Text: "That is a curious-looking flute. How did you come by it?"

a3dcfd13-d2ac-4f10-ac7a-f752b0c8e6fa.Text: "You lost this time, but I know you are cheating. Get out of my sight before I report you to the enforcers!"

40971843-3a5b-4778-8aa6-d4852f01e9db.Text: [Cut a button from your sleeve and throw it to the man] "For the entertainment."

4dc37280-0340-473b-aa40-b7c0b153abc7.Text: "I recently saved a labourer from a beating — where is my song? Or must one be a fictional character to be granted such an honour?"

1a4bda6f-5de3-4843-8dc1-c067425a1e0f.Text: [Leave] "I refuse to take part in any of this."

a67790de-ff63-4c8e-81d1-9f47165ab888.Text: "Jae, you wanted to play, did you not? Be my guest."

f4f76b3f-5ed7-46ba-b09e-a63970adcdbb.Text: [Cut a button from your sleeve and throw it to the man] "I have had my fill of entertainment for one day."

6f66754d-13bc-414b-bc5e-61f1073044eb.Text: [Solve the mystery of the trick by analysing its individual elements]

7ee77b04-1419-4f6a-8c1b-aaba34ae1712.Text: [Play fair] "I will give it a try."

47fa8aa6-ee79-4c22-a89e-3fcb98fd6fb6.Text: [Gesture at the board] "Are you suggesting we play a game?"

cd299095-05e5-4a4d-9a6c-c14d6fdda536.Text: [Cheat] "I have an idea. Let us begin."

249e997c-df8f-4409-83e6-fd6e5a9fa657.Text: "By opposing legitimate authority, your vile Nemesite tramples on the Creed. And everyone who glorifies him is a criminal."

be76e3d2-1768-441a-bea6-496d4c558699.Text: "Play one of the local favourites for me."

ff6df092-ec8c-4cc4-bb25-30e479dbc24d.Text: [Toss a coin into the chest] "A fine show."

04c1608f-5cb3-4a21-9d67-08ade9a53d2a.Text: "I know you are cheating. Get out of my sight before I report you to the enforcers!"

5ddb9824-c210-4549-94ba-1946df95dc93.Text: "May good times come for you one day, and then there will be no need for songs about fighting injustice. In the meantime, strive to lift the people's spirits, flute player."

6059a52a-d40c-4d88-9a3e-608857803630.Text: "Explain the rules of this game to me."

df9a3fab-93e4-4aa9-a2f6-0c47bc0b9d78.Text: "Instead of piping frivolous ditties during your shift, get to work, you idler."

ca9fb172-c002-42cf-8127-2eb16906b9f1.Text: "A flute needs no words to sing, but I am curious to know what story your melody tells."

2c539e1a-15c6-487e-a798-6e1ddf546a21.Text: {n}A group of gawkers are crowding around a makeshift stage, watching a strange duo perform. A man with odd-looking goggles pushed up on his forehead, hands wrapped in worn leather gloves, plays a tune on a handmade flute. Next to him sits a stack of crates supporting some kind of game board. A scruffy rat is rolling small glass balls around the board.{/n}

4d779912-c1dd-43c9-821b-013490667f5b.Text: "I hope you have enjoyed yourself. I certainly won't forget my fateful meeting with the Lord Captain." {n}The flute player clears the board in one deft movement and begins a new tune.{/n}

b3962a4d-0633-4d36-9336-58fc693ac5a4.Text: "Throne's gold! I was this close to figuring out how that ashmag makes his ratling dance to his tune! I must have missed something. Was my rhythm off? Was I singing too quietly? Hmm..." {n}She tosses a coin to the flute player and shrugs awkwardly.{/n} "A thousand apologies, shereen. I guess today is one of those days when luck just decides to show you its ar— backside."

74ecd0ec-d47b-448d-a6ec-a214c4b7366d.Text: {n}The crowd, which has been too absorbed in the performance to notice your presence, turns to you, expressions of frightful awe appearing on the workers' faces. Many start whispering prayers.{/n}

cbd9a847-f5e5-4e32-a603-236141d93898.Text: {n}The man raises his hands.{/n} "The strong need nothing more than words to win! I will remember this important lesson, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

25e371d2-8ae3-4374-ab16-e12b896996cf.Text: {n}Several workers empty their pockets and start throwing ration cards, bolt nuts, and even a few power panels into the small chest next to the board. The flute player winks at the crowd and switches to a different tune.{/n}

0e2c26b0-e355-42d5-afe8-3005fed5179f.Text: {n}The rat squeaks excitedly and starts rolling the colourful balls the players have chosen around the maze of tunnels on the board. But not a single one reaches the goal — a hole marked with a red circle. The rat just rolls all the balls off the board or into dead ends. Once the first group of players get their hopes dashed and leave empty-handed, new workers immediately take their place.{/n}

caf3ce1e-5dba-49e1-b75b-c93bce19fa54.Text: "I am but one of many." {n}The man gestures broadly at the teeming station.{/n} "A voice in the crowd. A cog in the mechanism. His humble servant. 'Flute player' is all they call me, because that's what I am. I make up tunes and give the people respite after a hard day's work."

b5784154-7418-4f8c-8b33-0348899380f2.Text: {n}He pats his instrument gently.{/n} "My mother loved music. She used to hum beautiful melodies to me, and when she passed away, I carved this flute from her hip bone and learned to play. Out of sorrow and respect for her memory."

8cb1b31a-6284-4279-a9c6-b70bfbd02f97.Text: {n}The rat scurries around the board, spurred on by the flute. Its movements appear erratic at first glance, but after a while, you notice how consistently the balls seem to miss the goal at the very last moment. While the rat's clumsy, amusing scampering distracts the spectators, its nimble tail directs the balls away from the hole.{/n}

2a1155a1-1960-4d9e-87e7-3e353140d093.Text: {n}The rat's behaviour is erratic and mindless. When it rolls yet another ball right past the goal, the crowd groans loudly and starts laughing at the loser.{/n}

0e580140-6242-4a1c-9dc2-843a45712c6c.Text: {n}The rat's movements, from the flicks of its tail to when and where it pushes the balls, obey its master's wordless commands with uncanny precision. The notes, the pauses, the rhythm — every part of the melody serves as a signal to the flute player's tiny assistant.{/n}

ec3fad56-81c0-426c-999f-5ddf43ddc07c.Text: {n}The next tune is so catchy that you completely forget about what is happening on the board.{/n}

c9073d14-d34c-45c8-a0f5-69294f096265.Text: {n}Jae leans over the game board and starts humming a slow Efreet melody, snapping her {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augmented fingers{/g} in time with the music. The rat stops dead in its tracks, listening to the new rhythm, and then drives the ball right into the red hole.{/n} "I dedicate this victory to you, shereen!"

9b9f7052-200a-426e-9a9c-3c8a2fbf0067.Text: {n}Jae glares at the board for several minutes, alternating between tapping her {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augmented finger{/g} on the edge and whistling a starkly different tune to that of the flute player. The rat comes close to rolling the ball into the hole not once but three times, and yet ends up missing the mark every time.{/n}

90e68d0e-2928-47e3-bf64-4a39122a77c1.Text: {n}The man readies his flute, and the rat dives under the board. You hear clawed feet scrabbling against the crate, and a few moments later, a green ball pops out of the centre.{/n}

00a6346f-5a52-42c7-b2d0-877cd480b4bf.Text: {n}The man shrugs, earning a few chuckles from the crowd. After you have taken a few steps, you hear his flute starting another tune.{/n}

80dbe071-b31b-486a-b6cd-8c82627c5e8a.Text: {n}Jae whispers conspiratorially into your ear,{/n} "Hey, shereen, what do you say I give it a go? While those poor ashmags were busy losing all their paltry possessions, I think I've figured out that swindler's tricks."

18c22f63-5cc8-40b2-834f-119b7a3ff060.Text: {n}You are not entirely certain how the flute player controls his rat, but you still have your bag of old and reliable tricks at your disposal. Your foot touches the base of the crate stack seemingly by accident, and the board tilts slightly. Meanwhile, the rat, tempted by the piece of hardtack clutched surreptitiously between your fingers, happily rolls the ball right where you want it to go.{/n}

88b0fdbc-3867-45b4-bf0d-f1aa8b4e2a93.Text: {n}You have already seen through the flute player's performance. You listen to him play and watch the rat closely. Then, at a certain point, you start tapping your fingers on the edge of the crate, adding your own rhythm to the tune. The rat scrambles in confusion, mistaking your commands for those of its master, and starts rolling the ball toward the goal.{/n}

ca9326eb-5fe8-44c8-9660-e050ad42591e.Text: {n}The rat almost manages to get the ball into the hole, but sharply changes direction right at the last moment. Then it happens again. And again. At last, the ball hits a dead end, signifying your defeat.{/n}

04909bd4-1880-4dc9-860d-1cd37bdd2f1f.Text: "Another round, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?" {n}The man bows his head with a slight smile.{/n} "You know, I've heard wise visitors from higher up say that this little game offers more than just amusement. They say it's an opportunity to test different strategies. To learn more about others and yourself."

91cea39e-d11d-4e91-a101-c54b9d060912.Text: "I'm sorry, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I don't have anything left to play for." {n}He smiles sheepishly as he turns out his torn pockets.{/n}

4b52ed25-cd8a-4053-8707-26fcdc0d7173.Text: {n}The game goes even better for you this time, but in the end, the insufferable rat gets the ball stuck again.{/n}

893b36fd-02b0-48ac-a8ac-a1930289174c.Text: "That was close, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Would you like to play again, or... was that enough?" {n}Something in the flute player's smile makes you suspect that this game cannot be won. And the game master does not seem to be trying to hide it.{/n}

49c912de-09e0-4700-a7ee-8dad7044c7bc.Text: {n}The man stops playing and shrugs, a guilty smile crossing his face.{/n} "I haven't had work for who knows how many watches now. And even if they did give me work, the enforcers would just rob me of my earnings afterward. So I've found a calling after my own heart: I trade fortune for ration cards. The folks around here peddle away what little they have to spare, anyway, so why can't I?" {n}The crowd echoes his words in cautious agreement.{/n}

e2877400-f17d-4889-80d7-9a86cb813206.Text: {n}The flute player awkwardly adjusts the goggles on his forehead.{/n} "The story of a simple man from the lower decks, honest with himself and others. He risks his life to protect the oppressed from those corrupted by power. He takes from the rich and gives to the needy. He helps without asking anything in return. Nemesite, hero of tales, admired by children and grown folk alike."

e033456e-6b60-4029-94d2-15839e95fa0f.Text: {n}The crowd nods in approval. The excited whispers merge into a single prayer for your health. The flute player smiles.{/n} "For a humble servant, there is no greater reward than his {mf|lord|lady}'s approval. I will try my best to inspire as many of your subjects with music as I can."

f9e23c09-4a7a-426b-a891-ff2dd4003c51.Text: {n}The people look at each other in shock upon hearing this unpalatable fact of life. Their joy evaporates, leaving only the bitterness of disappointment.{/n}

2234f032-b301-4394-bd55-ebbddd2750f9.Text: {n}The flute player smiles meekly.{/n} "All I did was grant your request. I played what the people down here like."

693c49a5-dbd5-4b3a-adef-300d9497b65f.Text: {n}The man gives a grateful nod, honoured by your attention alone.{/n}

eaaea037-a83c-442a-9d15-58366d184f1a.Text: {n}With an obedient bow, he slings the bag with the rat inside over his shoulder, then puts the flute into a simple case.{/n} "I wouldn't dare try your patience further. May we meet again, Lord Captain."

7fa6fbb9-7a67-4a35-a8d7-61a361868572.Text: {n}The flute player glances at the rat, somewhat disheartened.{/n} "It's true what they say. The power of the great lies in the talents of their followers."

de697e8d-59ce-4419-8c61-bd656fa96e23.Text: "By giving in to primitive pastimes, they try to forget the filth and poverty around them. They are deceived by laughter: a brief flash of pleasure, an imaginary moment of relief before the sleeping mind sinks into a meaningless existence once more."

972d0823-28f6-4e45-9a01-93a242f02ed5.Text: {n}Your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}mind{/d} eliminates all irrelevant factors: the ruffling of cards, the clamour of bolt nuts, the excited gestures of naive folk believing in luck where calculation reigns. There is only the game and its structural components: a skilfully crafted melody and a trained pet that is smarter than it looks.{/n}

9aca4e7a-ed3c-496b-af9e-43c305d81422.Text: {n}Where others hear music, you discern a series of coded directives being issued to the flute player's tiny accomplice. The rat distracts the spectators with a show of clumsiness while precisely following its master's commands. This is how the balls just "happen" to roll past the goal, much to the chagrin of the participants.{/n}

613a6500-dfe6-4ab7-84c1-b7db5ce81337.Text: "Thank you for this generous gift! These folks will shower me in ration cards to get their hands on something that belonged to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Fortune gave me the brightest of its smiles today."

f6d62c94-7db4-4d68-b9f6-cddb44a6a20b.Text: {n}The flute player smiles eagerly.{/n} "Please, bless our little lark with your attention."

1ab4cfb6-5ffc-4d67-b805-baeec48ec960.Text: {n}The rat starts chasing the ball around the board. Every now and then, you "accidentally" bump the board to scare the rat, making it run in the direction you want. Nevertheless, right at the end, the ball somehow misses the hole by a hair's breadth. This happens again and again until, finally, the ball hits a dead end, signifying your defeat.{/n}

821613ee-d1e0-4e7b-8754-018daf17be64.Text: {n}When the ball drops into the red hole, a few impressed whistles come from the crowd, and the flute player laughs heartily.{/n} "Cleverly done, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Well, I had no doubt that you would be a worthy opponent. And your strategy... I think I will keep it in mind for my future games."

1dd1715e-6ba0-4e15-a323-bcea65c24f7f.Text: {n}You manage even better this time. You shout at the rat, nearly prompting it to hide in the hole along with the ball — and yet, a moment later, the game ends with the ball stuck in a dead end once again.{/n}

ba9578f7-091b-41c9-8b9c-f8003c5e2b13.Text: {n}The Interrogator's lip curls, but he remains silent, his icy gaze not leaving the man.{/n}

3380f243-cb70-48ed-867c-f8e1536824d3.Text: "This flute player is not as simple as he pretends to be, {name}. I am most curious to know what he's really doing here. I will have him monitored."

51f958b4-56c7-46b5-983e-16a3a460284c.Text: {n}The people cast their eyes down in unison, their intent gazes threatening to burn new holes in their worn-out shoes. Their haggard faces show fear, but not remorse.{/n}

c832a238-3cbe-4dab-b2f9-f00788259a35.Text: {n}The people stare shamefacedly at the floor like guilty children. One of the elders in a tattered robe reaches for the homemade Aquila around his neck, whispering a penitential prayer.{/n}

035312cd-873d-4d7e-9d87-2c495a201909.Text: {n}The flute player smiles mysteriously and brings the flute to his lips. A simple, brisk melody pours out of the instrument, the glum faces of workers and traders soften a little, and the tunnels around you seem less squalid than before. Long after the music has stopped, many continue to whistle the unassuming ditty.{/n}

8a2c854f-4598-42a5-a1db-11b3137b9c68.Text: {n}The people whisper excitedly as they discuss Twelve's miraculous rescue. The crowd looks at you in awe.{/n}

1443c9a4-7ca6-4141-a262-c3f9957d7d62.Text: {n}The people murmur their halting agreement with your words. There is not an ounce of sincerity in this rumbling — the rabble simply does not dare challenge the words of the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself}.{/n}

b780e5a6-39a9-4bc1-9533-d671b7d283f0.Text: {n}The flute player bows his head so low you cannot see his face.{/n} "My humble flute is not worthy of singing the Lord Captain's tune. But since it is your will, I will compose a new melody. I hope it will be so good that it will be heard on every deck."

e977cadb-7f2c-4ff9-9bf5-e818bdb7e3f9.Text: {n}The flute player smiles regretfully.{/n} "I think the song just died. But I won't despair — life always suggests new melodies that people will like."

d21e7664-a8d3-459d-9f22-ae8fe480742b.Text: {n}The flute player's clear eyes widen in surprise. Then, with an open and friendly smile, he says,{/n} "Many a grand story of the Lord Captain's generosity is told, and, I swear on my own flute, today I will add another! To a fortune peddler, the Lord Captain's grace is a gift from fate itself!" {n}He applauds you with gratitude, and the workers timidly join in.{/n}

410e2c9d-d554-4f01-9541-88098752c8dc.Text: "It's simple: on this board, you play with fate. Choose a ball and give it to Bolts, my rat. If she rolls your ball into the pocket marked in red within three minutes, you win. If she doesn't, you lose. Simple."

2c602d0e-3b2b-48b5-bf4d-5126356534b8.Text: "Perhaps you would like to trade us some of that captain's fortune of yours, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?" {n}The flute player bows respectfully and gestures at the game board. The crowd buzzes with anticipation.{/n}

9d8490cf-ac70-4956-bd22-af7c4e90fc8b.Text: "Tell me why I shouldn't execute you on the spot."

c16661c5-5340-44e5-bd66-e38c08306a97.Text: "Abelard, help these wretches realise the full extent of their unenviable position."

634d246a-566f-423c-9f45-e0c05890e073.Text: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, and you will explain what is going on here."

69ee083b-1db7-4ca3-9859-52a73e955ee1.Text: "Who I am does not matter. What are you doing here?"

f2cf275e-aaee-4045-8106-50a9001a92b2.Text: "Today is your lucky day — put down what you hoped to steal and walk away."

8ba7b321-e94b-4144-aff6-4719945dd0bb.Text: "I suppose you may be of some use. I shall permit you to take a few of the more basic weapons and leave. Serve the ship well."

914eded3-dc64-4dc1-afa6-9de883de500f.Text: [Attack] "Criminals on my ship have a single fate — death."

1c02be97-73c5-4660-98c1-0dd68345bf04.Text: [Take a closer look at the suspicious individuals]

272ad2ba-009e-474f-a766-7a30f5b6961f.Text: "Why do you want my weapons? Are you going to rebel?"

8baead69-53da-4656-b4b6-2f9a51929db8.Text: "You all have your little fingers cut off. What does it mean?"

03f5cf76-c5a2-4a0b-ac79-94984e7cee50.Text: [Attack] "I have few words to say to the likes of you."

deb0a551-0e80-4f39-aebe-aeccfcde962b.Text: "You obviously did not expect anyone to be here. Are the enforcers providing cover for you?"

68abb4cf-6948-4e3e-b9d5-81c49675e408.Text: {n}Several people are eagerly rummaging through a rack filled with weapons from the enforcers' arsenal. A big man with a pockmarked face is the first to react to your presence — he attracts the others' attention with a piercing whistle and barks out,{/n} "Who are you? There's not supposed to be anyone h— ah, it doesn't matter. Identify yourself!"

da75b8c5-8689-4647-836f-d23bf9fe97a2.Text: "The Hard Nines, a gang... I mean, a brotherhood from Transport Bay 9. Don't think we're parasites. We do our bit for the prosperity of the ship. We're sort of... er... assistants to the enforcers. Self-appointed. We make sure that order is maintained in compartments where the enforcers are too lazy or greedy for bribes. We put a stop to robbery and freethinking, and well... we accept a small contribution as a show of thanks."

2f5403fe-277d-4165-9844-113ab0f35502.Text: "Have it your way, then!" {n}The pockmarked thug grins crookedly and rushes over to the weapon rack.{/n}

525251e6-1dbd-4ece-a8b8-94d8740a453f.Text: "Before you stands Lord Captain {name} von Valancius, {mf|master|mistress} of this vessel and everything on it, including those goods you are pawing at with your unwashed hands, and your miserable lives as well."

7e4e5ec3-7904-4105-b8b9-ec32c0673d30.Text: {n}The people turn to stare at you in disbelief and exchange heated whispers. The excitement is interrupted by the leader's roar:{/n} "What are you gawping at? Hurry up and bend your backs as is right and proper!"

8c12d7d6-3309-406f-9cd7-814618fabdf0.Text: {n}The leader looks at your gear appraisingly and frowns.{/n} "It matters. You better answer, or this conversation won't last long at all."

37c5d8e2-98be-4f87-bb70-d3aa3f8f1dbd.Text: "If the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}rumours about you{/d} are true, then you yourself know how it goes. There are criminals, and then there are criminals."

b86f9424-6c00-4e2b-87a2-0b00e48bd24d.Text: {n}The leader nods readily.{/n} "I'll mark today as my second birthday — I saved my skin and I saw the Lord Captain, all in one day. Long live Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

221e587f-d907-49bc-aed6-83f7237bf0f5.Text: "Hear that, boys? The Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} is expecting good things from us. We can't let {mf|him|her} down." {n}His cronies make sounds of approval.{/n} "We will fulfil your command to the letter."

1e1a68e1-49e8-4ccd-b081-6bf7c52951a3.Text: {n}The leader spits on the ground in annoyance.{/n} "What in the void have I been standing here making speeches for? I thought we had ourselves an all right Lord Captain, but no, {mf|he|she}'s the strait-laced type! Bring it on, then, Your {mf|Lordliness|Ladyness}."

25453983-ffe2-4e52-95ed-22d34f8991c6.Text: {n}Makeshift armour peeks out from beneath their ragged clothes, and their battered weapons display a patchwork of crude repairs. The group stares longingly at the rack where the good plasteel gleams, restlessly clutching their humble weapons.{/n}

becfc260-30ce-4f99-9180-a5964a40b740.Text: {n}The Seneschal grits his teeth, impotent in the face of your choice.{/n} "One day I will realise the depth and wisdom of your decisions, Lord Captain, but, in the meantime, I will pray that this act does not come back to haunt you."

a04637bf-6c88-44d8-a82a-9d526d8f2209.Text: {n}You notice that the little finger on every person's right hand has been cut off. It is hardly a coincidence.{/n}

4635e91c-86ff-4cd9-acf0-45eff0a2eb56.Text: "Even shooting them feels like a waste of bullets. I doubt these bottom-feeding degenerates have ever heard of the Lex in their lives."

5bef6262-5c5a-4a22-856d-f5f6af8a51ac.Text: "The Lex, eh? What kinda crew is that? They with the Rust Rats from Freight 10 or with the Piperunners from the main sorting hub?"

6f4bbddc-89e6-4192-8729-f6c171c88282.Text: "It's our gang's initiation rite, a fine tradition. By voluntarily removing a finger, the newcomer shows their determination and willingness to join us forever. It's also a badge of honour." {n}He proudly shows off the stump of his little finger.{/n}

a664668d-5529-4c5e-8e6b-f757dd791258.Text: "Erm... You could execute us, but who would take our place? Shameless scum who rob and kill to their hearts' content. Bastards who accept mutants into their gangs and pray to the Archenemy. There have always been outlaws on this ship. You're better off with outlaws like us, who don't go too far and who keep the heretics down."

3019ee1c-2425-4b60-924e-0527bf6e1864.Text: "Why stop there? You might as well call yourselves saints and say the fate of the whole dynasty rests on your shoulders!"

51e968ca-ea1a-4c09-b71a-337de516a5c9.Text: "To do business." {n}The gang leader smiles ingratiatingly.{/n} "We're no rebels. If anyone blasphemes against Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, we call the troublemakers to order. And we shed blood for the flagship without fear. I suppose that makes us... defenders of the ship?" {n}The thug raises his eyebrows questioningly and looks at you expectantly.{/n}

72939c17-9abc-4252-8fbc-aaac6cb70b38.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you must excuse these blockheads. I was taken aback myself — it's not every day you see the Rogue Trader in the flesh. And as for this..." {n}The man casts a grim glance at the rack.{/n} "I won't insult you by denying it — you've caught us red-handed."

f9618d22-4d7e-405f-9b51-b9ee83809046.Text: "I wish... Frensoe, the newly appointed captain, had our informant strung up. He's tightening the screws, damn it, we can barely breathe. Today's the last time we'll come to pick over this compartment."

c5832218-1c05-4ac4-8def-e0eaac7d9185.Text: You think you can make out letters woven into the intricate symbol. And though the meaning of each individual letter eludes you, together they unmistakably form an arrow pointing in a certain direction.

9d7990cc-42ae-4fd3-a0be-6cfbeffb21c2.Text: "It can't be! We scrubbed the deck three times right before the Rogue Trader came! Void take me! The captain will have our heads!"

dd7df929-1915-4be8-adee-03377a394b8f.Text: "I doubt that the death cult would lead us into a trap, but still... I have sent Mistress Toliman our coordinates as a precaution."

a1d1dbd4-a2ae-424b-8d7e-4d2b3c679e42.Text: "If we are indeed following in the footsteps of a saint, the God-Emperor would be pleased if we saw this path through to the end."

8afe4258-c0d7-4c62-8f63-0c5ab942f082.Text: "This symbol... I can still see the colours emanating from it, akin to... blood mixed with milk. It should be a foreboding sight... but then why do I feel so calm?"

6fbf974d-ebb7-4d86-a20b-68e9a643d767.Text: "The blood is still wet. They waited until we arrived."

65a4c7a8-fc7b-4a37-9c7b-2e434afe12d4.Text: "My whispers are getting antsy. They don't like this symbol one bit. And that's a good sign! It means we should keep looking!"

08dc4355-a267-4ead-bd73-42d7c12a0610.Text: "The day will come when we will resist the urge to crawl into the darkest holes looking for the grisliest omens... and I will know then that my soul has gone to meet the Exalted One."

4b2b7aa0-4181-4b87-9f8d-1ac92e1b0757.Text: Kibellah glances at the blood symbol and steps aside, studying your reaction closely.

26db1066-8c0f-44ed-a922-91cfcb17a1c2.Text: "Another mark. Ha! Well, well, Rogue Trader. Someone is keen to play with you."

a79d39af-a11c-4f35-956e-60d111608e72.Text: "Following the symbols will enable the proper categorisation of a yet unregistered crew subdivision and the location of a yet unmapped compartment. Method approved."

4a0f0990-1fb6-4726-9b3b-9267edc9c345.Text: "Glaito has sensed another mark. This blood is fresh... What sort of game are those fanatics playing?"

ba50d881-8637-4b92-8075-0681c7a0a72f.Text: "There is a saying on Fenris: if you seek a meeting with death, it will find you the moment you turn your back to it."

a5b04aa6-a860-4d4c-be6e-ab3563b1bf66.Text: "If these symbols mean a threat to you, elantach, then find the threat and end it. If they are signs of respect, then accept them as they are."

12f238a9-08eb-46d8-bcbb-6afd30504ce8.Text: A boot print has smudged this symbol slightly. The trail leads toward the slums.

57407836-d919-4745-a90f-79978658b9c5.Text: The one who called himself a dead man, having exacted his revenge on the spinners, lies motionless with a poison needle in his neck and a sneer on his lips.

49a43a2e-3044-49ea-81ff-81ed6e6ab0a6.Text: The longer you stare at the mark, the quieter the sounds of the station become. The shadows grow longer and seem to stretch in the direction of the adjacent section.

84606518-a274-45cd-be41-8a67ac2a49d4.Text: A chill runs down your spine. You cannot shake the feeling that some unseen figure is watching you.

31cc9b6c-c2d6-4249-a984-1fe81d019335.Text: "Explain yourself, Frensoe. What is this mess?"

06e5139b-1abd-43b3-9ab4-dd2ef658917d.Text: "So I am invited to follow a trail of blood, it seems. I accept the spinners' invitation."

6aa8426f-af63-4b63-be1e-a29e703e7f22.Text: "Drivel and filth, all of it! Scrub out the symbol at once!"

34f5d62a-d5e8-499f-aeb6-e9b49fc28f46.Text: "Why would they leave this mark here?"

a9471957-adba-4601-9c6c-ad1ff13c1fa8.Text: "Scrub it out this instant, and punish anyone who had a hand in it appearing here! I will not indulge the death cultists by partaking in their mad games!"

3f17a207-d797-459d-b08a-7dae815c3afb.Text: "Do you know what this mark is?"

2a93eb11-19a4-41af-9724-4f01b3741556.Text: "What is the Song of Trailing Blood?"

a3796e8a-0ed8-42e7-a8e1-07a024f90607.Text: {n}The corner of the captain's mouth twitches nervously as he mutters,{/n} "Damn those... How did they even..."

ebc4ba97-0264-4631-bd2e-5af967126074.Text: "Lord Captain, one of the cultists must have sneaked in here and left this mark. Or perhaps they forced someone to do it. It's a disgrace that they can pull such stunts right under my nose, but at least I can assure you that the mark is not dangerous."

00245306-da0e-4520-8f56-b7f931aa821d.Text: {n}You have seen this sort of symbol before. Death cultists carve bleeding marks like this into their own skin.{/n}

6675be32-f857-4a2f-83a5-6bfd116ce998.Text:
{n}Frensoe takes a deep breath.{/n}
"The soundless shadow sank into the dark.
Slashed feet crescendo, a fatal dance:
bladesong in tempo, each edge an echo,
twin odes to death throes.
Now on her sacred blood,
as she once trod the backs of foes,
tread countless souls, but none who know."

d70ebb6b-1100-4540-bd79-4c51605aaadd.Text: "It resembles one of the symbols associated with the Bloodspun Web. What was it called again... 'The Song of Trailing Blood,' I think. It's a prayer familiar to many in this compartment. We've heard spinners say it when they... well... perform their signature acts of service to the Emperor."

5830ab68-f89b-4a19-846e-ecfca51598b5.Text: "Is this the welcome you give the Rogue Trader?" {n}Abelard's nostrils flare in anger.{/n} "Whoever had the audacity to leave behind this... this appalling symbol, I will see to it that the Master-at-Arms calls them to account herself!"

01fa19d1-273c-4586-a5f4-0766c3626273.Text: "I hope you find what you're looking for and return to the upper decks safely, Lord Captain."

cc53c035-48d5-49fb-b835-f1f295379900.Text: "Yes, Lord Captain!" {n}Frensoe signals to his subordinates, and the enforcers hurry to carry out your will.{/n}

4e471607-119f-4179-9480-8b3329bc0f72.Text: "From what I can tell, it's something like a prayer with several verses that tell about the life of one of the cult's saints. Erianne, or the Matriarch Spider, as they call her."

7cde44d2-4ff1-43b8-87ec-d27340f191cb.Text: {n}The blood that was used to paint the symbol is still fresh, but you see no clues as to who left it here or what their intentions were.{/n}

86b722aa-9346-4b6d-a9df-b264c8e34515.Text: {n}In other words, it is an invitation. It is only too {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}obvious{/d} that cultists obsessed with mysticism would never use prose to mark the way to their temple — they are too fond of their obscure chants and cryptic verses.{/n}

fa1beb2e-146a-4db9-bbe1-c517ad07327b.Text: {n}Kibellah carves the same symbol on the back of her hand with a knife and whispers a prayer.{/n}"Domin'{name}, remember this sign. It is the beginning of your quest, the first blood trail."

f693d877-8b85-47ae-945b-96e9180b7035.Text: "When I took up my post here, I made sure to familiarise myself with all the... particular qualities of this compartment.
