I soon heard about the verse and decided to investigate. I questioned a number of people who follow the Bloodspun Web as I was trying to figure out if there was anything pernicious about it, and eventually I learned the whole thing." {n}He frowns.{/n} "The words are certainly strange, but it's nothing worse than that, it seems."

4784d9c5-fd4a-4935-bc54-1e90bd3ab2e8.Text: "Maybe it has something to do with them inviting you to visit their temple. Maybe they're trying to get your attention? Apologies, Lord Captain, I'm no good at deciphering their disturbing riddles."

8a139f9b-0b41-48b9-a11b-e7fc3a6c62c4.Text: [Switch on your vox] "Get some enforcers and medicae personnel in here, now. There is a man in need of revival. Once he has recovered, assign him to be a scribe's apprentice — he is too badly injured to go back to a worker's life."

e83a01e6-e267-43ff-a723-ce7781d65171.Text: "The spinner whispered a verse to you? Can you repeat it for me?"

a9d9a197-fd49-471d-9db9-d9988cdcf0d6.Text: [End the man's life] "I grant you a merciful death."

6d44a65e-370e-4ec5-9c75-6daead84e853.Text: "Do you know anything about the mark next to you?"

4c9b979c-09b6-49b2-b9ec-49e8a90d9dad.Text: Left the burnt man to die an agonising death.

9d446a4b-ba6c-4177-a14d-c96f92fcb912.Text: [Leave] "All of us must face our fated outcome."

37668c1f-9729-4800-b824-efc84194bdd7.Text: "Who are you and what happened to you?"

b11be167-a42e-402b-8ac3-85d8ad5e2a35.Text: "Help is on the way. Just hold on a little longer."

bd8803ee-1703-4daf-839e-ea52448cb647.Text: "Mercy... Please, save me..." {n}The young man gasps for air through burnt lips, slipping in and out of delirium. His skin is dripping from his gaunt body like melted wax from a candle. His eyes, somehow intact, alive, clear, and filled with pain, stare at you from under his caked eyelids.{/n}

3c81fcec-6dbe-4d01-a8bd-2ff11eae036b.Text:
{n}He begins to whisper, his lips twisted in pain:{/n}
"To soot-smirched soul... her mercy she did grant.
Last breath expressed, knife met heart:
removed from chest... passed on to death.
Her duty blessed, a balm for those
who suffer... anguish and distress...
A longing brought to rest:
of mortal bonds the soul divest..."

13fb7eaa-a18f-4787-9e8b-7d8d7cfe2fa1.Text: {n}He might survive, but he will be maimed for life. Too much of his muscle has been charred down to the bone — even if he does retain some ability to move, pain will be his constant companion. His motor skills have been damaged beyond repair. A broken man or a corpse, time will soon tell.{/n}

e6334b17-2812-46ad-ae66-9ef560aba569.Text: "No! Mercy..." {n}Horror flashes in the man's eyes, but once he sees your calm expression, he lets go of the fear and bows his head in resignation.{/n} "So be it... I can't... take this pain anymore... I'd rather... die..."

34ce9fd9-3e7f-49b7-ba6a-5763a3d43980.Text: {n}He tries to turn his head, his blackened skin crunching as it opens into scarlet cracks.{/n} "A spinner came... He painted the symbol... Then he gave me water... and whispered a strange verse... He told me to memorise it and to recite it later... so that help would come. And here you are! Then I should..."

8a4c6a71-db2b-4baa-98d7-69eafcf037cc.Text: "I wonder how long he's been sitting here like this. A watch? Three? The whispers say nobody cared because he didn't matter, but they also say he's somehow supposed to matter to us... Strange."

00ea1aff-4046-46db-be63-9125ea591e1e.Text: "Never forget the mercy that the Lord Captain has granted you."

75476ab7-23e1-4ef9-88be-9eec1acce2f8.Text: "I'm Vayle, a cleaner... I was in my house, asleep... enforcers came... set fire to it... I didn't... make it out in time..."

1b738423-8303-4b5a-b7f2-2e32b04f311e.Text: "When the Undying One is ready to accept a soul, it must be sent forth, and so will it be freed from the torment of the flesh. Yet you have chosen to... prolong this one's suffering. Your intentions perplex me."

1dd90ae6-76de-4620-9043-4bf06558a3ed.Text: {n}The man shakes his head desperately, ripping open the crust that has just begun to form over his burns.{/n} "No... Please... I'm begging you!"

0301ab21-e001-4038-a140-adfcfcdf3951.Text: "There is no curse more terrible than an existence between unlife and undeath. You have liberated a tormented soul, Domin'{name}. The Undying One sees the good you have wrought."

8cc64496-02e6-42e4-b86a-c0485b011e62.Text: "You soulless ashmag..." {n}Jae mutters under her breath.{/n}

15957226-5662-43d5-9ae7-46bcc0bcd9ea.Text: {n}More verses. The crux of this test is {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}clear{/d}: in order to follow in the saint's footsteps, you are supposed to kill the young man and thus release him from his suffering. The cultists want to see if you understand the philosophy of those you seek.{/n}

a52ba31e-4bcc-432f-97dc-c028d359d57f.Text: "I begged him to save me, but he just turned and left... Why?" {n}He coughs and starts feverishly scratching the same symbols you saw into his flesh.{/n} "Please, help me! I want to live..."

97e29b73-6f79-4f0f-b85a-38dfd0c9dff0.Text: {n}A blissful smile twists the man's lips, and a tear forms at the corner of his ruined eye socket.{/n} "The God-Emperor has sent you to save me... You are His light... You are His grace... Thank you... Thank you for not leaving me here..."

d04e03f3-230d-47d7-afbd-ef6c35e180e3.Text: "The death cultists want us to end the poor man? Those sick lunatics! Anyone can be saved as long as they still want to live!" {n}Jae's fingers move toward her neck augment instinctively.{/n} "At the very least, they deserve an attempt to save them before you discard their life."

05651683-bfeb-448a-bb20-64e7dce527ec.Text: "There are times when death is more merciful than a life of perpetual agony."

be534def-90bf-4a65-b6d1-921d9721869e.Text: "The chances of this unit surviving are slim. Functional usefulness in the event of stabilisation of vital processes is minimal. Disposal is recommended."

d12fbd0c-716d-4c37-8def-4b42765dae2d.Text: {n}Brownish-yellow pus has collected under his scorched skin. His wounds have already been touched by the rot of the lower decks, and even if his body survives transport to the medicae facility, the man will still die of either shock or infection.{/n}

30b63dbe-4b8c-443c-bd31-0b1b7bd275e8.Text: {n}Marazhai approaches the mutilated man, closes his eyes, and takes a deep breath. The corners of his lips curve into a satisfied smile.{/n}

fa0c1dc9-85f8-4167-932b-135a56a71090.Text: [Shout into the shaft] "I've had it with this madness and with your riddles! I am not going to risk my life just for the sake of finding some temple!"

e32a5143-7b7b-4856-a3e9-888612b21173.Text: [Call upon the Ruinous Powers] "I am willing to take the risk so that I might learn the secrets of the Bloodspun Web, but I need your aid!"

48ee6ba5-2b46-42cd-99bc-7c096eeaa3ff.Text: [Pray to the Emperor] "I put my life in Thy hands, for I believe truly that Thou wilt protect."

57613faf-063e-467d-a542-c095fc391888.Text: {n}The rotating blades promise nothing but a senseless and brutal death. Slipping past them would require some unreasonably precise calculations... or blind luck. While listening to the air currents, for a moment you think you hear Zdena's whispered prayer rising from the depths of the shaft.{/n}

4ac3f3c3-614b-4751-a122-b87d013000c8.Text: {n}All you hear back is the echo of your own words.{/n}

da72fe39-9e96-4ce9-b104-abc952a6364c.Text: {n}The words come easily, and all of your doubt fades away. Somehow, you know with certainty that your life will not end here.{/n}

e82a1636-2e93-4c77-a276-4cae1dfc79f8.Text: {n}A confident smile that is not your own appears on your lips. The rumbling blades no longer seem dangerous, and the prospect of jumping becomes a mere trifle.{/n}

6b8773d5-91f5-43cf-9989-0c58617adfcb.Text: "Your eyes always return to that blood symbol. What do you know about it?"

8413c615-e1f1-4473-a10a-6b3320119b60.Text: Overturned the Vizsier's verdict on Sebreid, thereby encouraging him to go on a new killing spree.

71098d5a-2cd8-47e8-8029-7e0a775af4d8.Text: "As the Emperor's anointed, I hereby overturn the Vizsier's verdict. The cult ruined your life, and for what? For a few mere killings?"

49754d25-5c19-412f-912e-6ed021c4f2ac.Text: [Leave] "I doubt that you can be of any help to me."

4f7148d0-7521-409d-b761-d03818b56f97.Text: "What do you think you are doing?"

1a228201-c50b-41e6-beec-6d61a6828eb9.Text: "You know the symbols of the Bloodspun Web. You bear similar scars. Are you a spinner?"

ab68f1f8-578c-44f4-b61b-50808341f9f5.Text: "You look like you are about to take your own life. Are you having a rotten day?"

c7c1a218-6698-4653-88bc-e18de8d44c87.Text: "You were ordered to die? For what reason?"

23003374-8617-421f-a037-b308c68b76b6.Text: "So the spinners simply let you go? They made no attempts to find you and kill you?"

201b04e6-b9f4-45b1-a2be-c8885a873169.Text: "You are disgusting. I will not grant you the release you crave so much. May you live on in suffering, fearful of every shadow."

55ff3485-4b1a-4e6d-a033-0af63093128e.Text: "You are a coward and a butcher of the innocent. I will purge my ship of your existence."

4b2a50d5-b83c-45bb-9cc0-05a58823a590.Text: "Have you killed any more innocent souls since you ran?"

d4874307-00f2-465a-a3b5-3926220370b0.Text: "I will not judge you, nor will I decide your fate. Farewell."

497b5a0a-e7bf-4088-ac0c-791f854abbb7.Text: "Do not even think of marring the underside of my train with your entrails!"

8bfb80cd-5e54-45c0-bd98-b725f4b7ba53.Text: {n}A sinewy middle-aged man watches the bustle of the bay with a detached expression. Every so often, whenever his eyes linger on the blood mark inscribed nearby, his face changes strangely and his hands clench into fists.{/n}

f33f8d12-df27-450c-b9b8-54f5069f2a58.Text: "A dead man. I lost my name years ago. I've been just another dead man ever since."

d738a72e-a0f3-49d4-89fe-103863833c79.Text: "You... you're right, Lord Captain! The Vizsier taught me to serve. To kill. I did what I was chosen to do... and they punished me for it. They've kept me living in fear almost my whole life!" {n}The man's colourless eyes fill with malice.{/n} "Thank you for opening my eyes. It's time for Sebreid to return... and for the dead man to disappear, along with his creators."

7b30c0bc-8f9b-4bc1-adf7-212ca58e2aae.Text: "Vicious ashmag! You used people's faith in the Exalted One to justify abusing the power that was given to you!"

8270b646-e1db-43fc-8136-cdc5fb3f7399.Text: "What? I... I didn't..." {n}The man starts and almost falls, but manages to keep his balance. In the dim {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} light, you notice old scars scattered all across his body. The scars seem vaguely familiar.{/n}

cfc54405-4839-4179-8ea3-36499684a545.Text: {n}The scars all vary in length, width, depth, and shape. However, you notice a pattern in the way the scars are aligned, as well as a series of faded symbols on the man's rough skin. Death cultists bear similar marks on their bodies.{/n}

3477c6ff-2a9e-4724-b150-8de66b3e95a7.Text: "You dare insult the Rogue Trader with your impudence? Your body may already be covered in scars, but your tongue seems to be asking for more."

aece4c81-bccc-4acc-9b1e-1913b321ea17.Text: "The Vizsier told me to kill the one who would be at a certain junction of the utility tunnels at a certain hour. I went to the appointed spot. Then I waited. An hour. Two. Five. The junction was still empty. Nobody came. After hours of waiting, I finally realised: the person at the junction had been me the whole time. It was my turn to go to the Undying One. But I was... afraid. I couldn't do my duty. I ran."

d7f75f9d-dfd3-479f-9b2c-5c9e9e357867.Text: "My whole life has been rotten. And I only have myself to blame. I've tried to change things, fix things. But I always ended up here, so eventually, I accepted the truth."

f0d18e8e-4e7f-4f92-a9de-c982fb440755.Text: "If Humankind followed its own Paths as the Children of Asuryan do... this mon-keigh would be one who has lost his Path."

7a151da8-997b-421f-9d08-fbf676e3e3c6.Text: "If this were an interrogation, I would welcome such a response. But in this case we are merely wasting our time."

1d4dad7e-bd7b-4c99-8756-b739758a25cb.Text: {n}Kibellah briefly studies the man's face, then turns away.{/n} "I do not know you. Death's gaze is not upon you."

89c81738-e679-4a4c-a8d9-bc71859a187a.Text: {n}He bows half-heartedly.{/n} "I can't even be of any help to myself."

9c062783-d9df-4e87-a084-54e102a370dc.Text: "I was. But I failed to complete my final assignment, so I was... exiled from the cult."

8596a2d5-8cf1-45fc-979d-0c4b5db7b656.Text: "There was no pursuit. I thought I'd see their black blades the very next day. Instead, years passed without them taking my heart. I tried starting a new life, but the terror never stopped eating away at me. When I got truly desperate, I went to the temple of death myself. But no one there would speak to me. When I gave them my name, they just whispered, 'Sebreid has gone to the Undying One.' They looked through me like I wasn't even there. I've lived like this for twenty years. Like a coward. Like a dead man."

15fd2333-61f2-44fe-9c53-6fc45f841a7c.Text: {n}The man does nothing to stop you. He even leans closer to the rails, accepting his fate with a smile on his face.{/n} "The Undying One is death."

e317f7b8-c679-4504-bf4e-f34ef942e663.Text: "No! What about the symbol? The portent? You... you were supposed to..." {n}The man's tired eyes fill with horror that quickly turns into hysteria. His knees buckle, and he staggers heavily before falling onto the tracks with a pitiful cry.{/n} "No! Help!"

6ee617f4-c684-4a94-9a3b-4d0700a5cbeb.Text: "I've spent years in remorse. I'm tired of it."

2406e8f9-cbbd-465f-aa8a-a70a3b9071c2.Text: "No. I've been afraid to touch my own knife since that day. Thought it might just stab me on its own... But the temptation is always there."

8ef5ff6d-65d4-4d78-8693-02b4a7644835.Text: "Oh, you poor thing, I think I'm gonna cry. You couldn't stop slicing people up! That must have been so hard for you! Even my whispers have nothing to say to a pathetic tale like that. I bet they're thinking, 'What a lousy, self-absorbed sack of scum!'"

da0f33fa-110a-40c0-ab2a-4f06ba1cb711.Text: {n}Kibellah appears behind you and watches the man leave.{/n} "He severed souls from bodies before their fated time. Not because he honoured death, but because he enjoyed killing. He did not have that right. No one does."

6c0a42c6-40a0-411c-b685-71ca1298cbb8.Text:
{n}The man looks at you.{/n}
"But some would choose to leave the righteous path.
These earned penance in due time:
her whip sings vengeance on renegade menace.
Her blades pass sentence.
For cowards seek to hide their hearts,
but death makes no pretendence;
it takes what it is due in essence."
{n}He stops, then adds hoarsely,{/n} "The third verse of the Song of Trailing Blood. The Vizsier recited it to me before sending me on my final assignment. I didn't realise at the time that it was my judgement."

842c866b-5b68-4fc2-81b0-297631b13959.Text: {n}Another verse, another step along the trail of blood. The riddle is {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}trivial{/d}: it is time for death to take what it is due, and the Vizsier is waiting expectantly for you to carry out the sentence he passed years ago.{/n}

caf6890c-cfe2-4e65-8f22-f71216dd9989.Text: {n}Kibellah stares at the remains of he who was once her brother in service.{/n} "Truly, it is better to die for Him than to live for yourself. This, he forgot."

ee837b46-d230-4a85-a4ea-221ee41a9cfb.Text: {n}But spinners are constantly renewing their wounds, while this man's look long since healed.{/n}

f3ed0b86-cca2-4d46-a253-84199cb19e51.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox-synthesiser springs to life with an indignant binharic trill.{/n} "I am registering this unit's intention to use the train tracks for purposes other than those intended by their design. I categorically demand that the unit's self-disposal be carried out using methods that do not violate the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation."

c6c674ef-0a53-406e-8a59-b9d9fffacf56.Text: {n}The man freezes a step away from oblivion, listens, then recoils and goes still once more.{/n}

938aae4d-6ada-4143-8e87-ec9cd3959e84.Text: {n}The man's wandering gaze turns to you as if he is expecting a question of some kind.{/n}

e1accdb3-4f68-4420-a852-35b03d873f0f.Text: {n}Abelard barks out,{/n} "In the name of the dynasty, I command you to step away from the edge and explain the misdeed you were about to commit!"

4d04fc3a-9bf5-4041-8b00-a9bd4c33b184.Text: {n}Just as you begin to hear the rumble of an approaching train, the man's gaze turns toward the tracks. He leans forward...{/n}

0d65cd24-9cfd-4eb8-9599-f183dde88100.Text: {n}The man's faded eyes go wide as he notices Kibellah. His voice quivers:{/n} "You... Have you come to take me to the other side?"

c5464c5d-f480-4660-80e6-56d335360a64.Text: {n}The man lets out a dull groan and turns to look at the symbol again.{/n} "But then why... why is it here?"

bec0c47e-4312-48f7-a7cf-de51f17c2753.Text: "It's a symbol of the Bloodspun Web. I come here every watch, but it hasn't been here before now. I guess today must be a special day." {n}He smiles strangely.{/n}

76ed35cf-d8b7-4bfb-a993-0190da805fa6.Text: "There were plenty of reasons. I sowed death. I offered Him the souls of the most pleasing men and women I could find because it kindled my passions. I killed well-off crewmen who didn't deserve their wealth, and I took their thrones. I killed enforcers who looked into my eyes without fear — because I wanted to be feared! I revelled in bloodshed. I betrayed the Tenets. I realised it, but I couldn't help it... because I enjoyed it."

81c7c550-f716-4ecf-9eb9-7c40348d9fd1.Text: The charred corpses are huddled together in a single lump of charred flesh, with many clearly trying to shield the smaller bodies among them.

8c612763-3f27-4612-805e-26094f4fc3b9.Text: The poor man almost made it out of the blaze in time, but got pinned down by the debris.

c86cb196-d338-4f08-9cfe-fdf42d96d36f.Text: "Our Factotum turned out to be a mean ol' fighter, huh?"

0cdb0eba-fb46-4ec4-9a99-d16a23531fce.Text: "The real Lord Captain — fancy that... At least now I know who I'm gonna be dying for."

35583b91-5da9-4e95-aef2-0a22b3ef85b2.Text: Captain Frensoe lies in an awkward heap, an enormous hole gaping open in the back of his head.

7c12777f-6a5d-4f2e-a7d5-37e4904f5619.Text: "They're still alive! Get me the stimulants — everything you have!"

81fa1053-3f15-4f35-a18f-abae0d275805.Text: "Keep your eyes sharp! Those things could come crawling out of the pipes or drop from the ceiling at any moment!"

2bab45fb-5441-41d3-8b7d-4d2d573c3ac7.Text: "I'd better do a clip count. I feel like I spent a whole hour pulling back the trigger..."

0a6dbc39-d21a-4fc7-b94f-1ca13a787918.Text: Follow the spinner into the temple of the Undying One

a07601cc-05e8-4449-b28e-7978b80783b9.Text: "Forget the void suit! There's no time. Just give me the respirator and a torch — I'm going in."

92bd2cd8-c8d3-4083-8c8a-ba3172fb6e10.Text: "Hey, over here! I can hear voices under the rubble!"

4160430e-f11b-4381-bdd4-b127b41eea9b.Text: "{mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} is alive! We're here, we're holding on! Glory to House von Valancius!"

52b769e5-bb98-4807-a91e-ace40367c815.Text: The shopkeeper tried to rescue his wares. Scraps of brain matter and caked blood on the counter tell of the tragic conclusion to his efforts.

50d5ff44-5cff-4077-a815-3e4ca30dd9d7.Text: The shop smells of burnt meat and scorched hair. The counter mercifully hides the source of the odour.

452c4a5f-1fe5-473b-8c14-c8610a5383dc.Text: Judging from the burns, people were throwing themselves into the poisonous waters of the canal in an attempt to escape the fire.

a3f0131e-1303-4945-b264-3be9c7aca341.Text: The people who tried to escape the fire by diving into the toxic waters were mercilessly gunned down.

36c52378-2653-4380-8962-72581946e143.Text: The bodies of the workers who perished during the riot. They bear no traces of mutation.

c2cca4b9-ebfd-45ba-934d-5e0e2ed82769.Text: The unarmed workers tried unsuccessfully to shield themselves and their loved ones from bullets. There are no traces of mutation on their bodies, just bullet holes and enforcer boot prints.

e8c320e6-eb9c-4caa-8bcd-d074de2314e6.Text: "Get back, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! The wretches have taken—"

2db0358c-d451-4a09-b946-d0bb9245f338.Text: "Over here! Help me, for the God-Emperor's sake! I am injured..."

2103f250-f4b0-455f-8f15-9499d201b53d.Text: Although you successfully defused the bomb, the poor fellow has died of his deep wounds. Bloodied entrails are dribbling out of his clothes. It is a miracle he even lasted this long.

be60b0e3-5369-4123-917f-99d559a22a8d.Text: No matter how many men and women might die to save these riches, one could hire a hundred times more for merely a fraction of this wealth.

af31e264-1c1f-4766-9178-22c79a35b750.Text: "Thank you, Lord Captain! Watch yourself out there."

f4f0d56f-97ec-481e-befb-ee5fad7e2adf.Text: The spinner bows and gestures in invitation.

40865379-dee0-4d57-9aab-a68cd181b93f.Text: "Look — the Lord Captain! {mf|He|She} has not abandoned us!"

a22cda86-850f-400e-a6c8-86c3aac46ce1.Text: "May the God-Emperor protect you, Lord Captain!"

ea3cfa61-08c2-47a8-b90b-940d9e3441ec.Text: The enforcers have been put on full alert and are now better able to fight back against the enemy.

bf23de58-b1d8-423e-9191-9a409f70c4d3.Text: The Rogue Trader has made a vow to the Emperor that {mf|he|she} will not stop to tend to {mf|his|her} wounds until the ship is purged of heresy. May the Protector of Mankind grant His servant the strength to persevere!

4e83bef2-1f4f-40ed-ae91-5196a568c6e2.Text: The traitors have killed the enforcers and seized their equipment.

e687b7e0-9e51-4dbb-b552-6c82b6655f66.Text: The Dark Gods have welcomed your bloody sacrifice and granted you a modicum of their power.

59c7de58-8dbc-4eca-9acc-1b4ce1b392e6.Text: The Rogue Trader has resisted an invasion of {mf|his|her} mind and weakened the enemy with a retaliating psychic strike.

378dd3aa-4814-4092-8634-680c9d915065.Text: After breaching {mf|his|her} will, something monstrous has touched the Rogue Trader's soul.

bc00f265-deb4-4e63-9a39-c6a4c8bdc912.Text: Among the salvaged relics of the dynasty were a number of sacred unguents and ammunition that could assist the Rogue Trader in battle.

9e1c9c38-66d9-40d2-be0d-ee77e9aa0dff.Text: "Hold on. Don't die. I am not done here yet."

e567d2fb-0eca-485a-bacf-fc89ec7a4e9a.Text: "What do you know about what is happening here? Is this a mutiny?"

df069971-ac72-4bd9-b07a-8cda20622e8b.Text: "We must get you to a healer before you die of blood loss."

6b7583ab-6bf1-4097-8caf-53a8cfa3fe21.Text: [Pick up the cultist's blade] "I'm afraid you are no longer a fighter. Leave the enemies to me."

6afca2a9-a702-46db-aced-7d68db4f8738.Text: "I wish to know the name of my rescuer."

f7cb6aff-2b07-4391-b72d-cfb3746b6ce9.Text: [Bandage the cultist's wounds] "I cannot leave you in this state."

1840a58e-4ca2-4a54-8859-9c90a2e36a76.Text: {n}The death cultist is bleeding out, breathing with a barely audible wheeze.{/n} "You are unharmed, Domin... The temple... The Vizsier is waiting... He can help... Let me take you." {n}The blade slips from his weakened fingers and falls to the ground with a clang.{/n}

f3f5f6f7-43ac-41af-be85-a29ac0f0c2a8.Text: {n}Einrich was shooting to kill, and a perfectly aimed shot has torn the young man's lung to shreds. It is a wonder he has not choked on his own blood already.{/n}

9dd27f1d-7b6d-4d26-8da5-70c95a69b523.Text: {n}The bleeding shows no signs of stopping — in field conditions and with the means at your disposal, you can do nothing to stem it. You only hope that the spinner reaches the temple before he perishes.{/n}

987e48b4-0d23-445d-9685-cb1249f74880.Text: "Mutiny... Yes, the aberration of the Ravenous Star... Inhumans... The Vizsier will explain... Trust... no one."

df45b772-b0dc-4074-90f2-3ebaa2d8916c.Text: {n}The cultist shakes his head.{/n} "No need to... waste time. You must... hurry to the temple. And then He will... decide..."

2b4ad9cb-3a5f-448c-bd2a-8aebe5e88c86.Text: {n}The spinner nods.{/n} "I will be glad... if with my weapon, the Domin... cuts the threads of the traitors."

952cc79d-ae96-4628-a3b2-fda9a274b625.Text: "Come, Domin... To the Vizsier... To the temple..."

a869994e-5093-4a01-b3fa-28b0b2ab3e18.Text: "Spinner... Giorek..." {n}He beams with pride — it is not every day that such a distinguished person takes an interest in his name.{/n} "I have not yet... done my duty. Go to the temple... It is safe there..."

11d87848-1c4c-46b2-b9a5-7782463d77b4.Text: {n}The spinner points at Hrotko's corpse with a trembling finger.{/n} "This one was once loyal, if... prideful... But his mind... was... poisoned. It takes only one bite... to put... treachery... in the blood... Trust no one."

46817acd-b754-4897-9280-0df688e2f72a.Text: {n}You render first aid as competently as an experienced chirurgeon. The spinner will survive for a while longer, but he still needs proper treatment to stop him from dying of blood loss.{/n}

8b46816b-e3e4-4e3a-9307-3ae636fe6f56.Text: {n}Its screen flickering, the cogitator dutifully keeps watch at the entrance to the post. There is a slot matching the rod given to you by Captain Klein.{/n}

1ee25a3f-539d-4276-8dda-869c177789c4.Text: {n}The cogitator accepts the rod and draws it in. The vid-screen flashes a torrent of {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Lingua-Technis{/g}, confirming the protocol's activation, and you hear a growing hum from beneath the door. Then, amid the crescendo of noise, the vid-screen suddenly turns black and singes you with a burst of sparks.{/n}

91784db9-536a-4729-ba82-ecaac2235856.Text: "I attribute your inability to defeat the enemy on your own to a lack of commitment. All survivors are subject to disciplinary action."

682509fa-f301-4a17-ae7a-36a1d62b171e.Text: "I am glad I was able to help. What comes next?"

d8758a45-bad4-4238-a8f1-5fb7a21ed6fd.Text: "How did you end up in this compartment, soldier?"

3c4453cc-908f-4a97-b311-16f9d6f5cd3d.Text: "How did the mutineers manage to take over the post?"

320e0c80-0304-48ab-abd8-c70d051a5b26.Text: "I could swear I saw you get killed."

a3ceee41-720a-449c-baba-3b82bf32fcd2.Text: "What kind of propaganda was Frensoe spreading?"

82569f0a-c8ea-48bb-bc07-425b6b6aece6.Text: "As far as I knew Frensoe, those speeches of his were completely out of character."

5c3b48f1-5612-44dd-9b27-c28b8a314367.Text: {n}From the sound of his voice, you recognise him as Captain Klein, the man who performed the autopsy on the mutant during the investigation.{/n}

b1159e1a-7e8a-4be8-8758-b9fae143dfc7.Text: "The enforcer post has been lost and is swarming with mutants. Alas, the only ways to the upper decks lie either through the post or through the transport tunnels, but there are enemies there as well."

71af6c31-4fea-4dd0-805c-64d2c1eb7663.Text: "She sacrificed herself, covering our sally from the upper decks. She wanted to tell me something before it happened, something important — I could see it in her eyes — but she didn't get the chance. Now, I will never know." {n}Klein clenches his teeth and winces in pain.{/n}

7070775e-8045-4fe7-aae3-d89b396cb216.Text: {n}He grimaces.{/n} "A talented enforcer. And a good friend."

2cfe703f-5165-4f4c-b6c6-ad323479a1a6.Text: "Insert the data-key into the cogitator by the entrance, and the post will be hit with a devastating pulse that is lethal to {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g}. It will burn out the detonators and turn mines into harmless chunks of fyceline-stuffed iron."

88cd3ff6-fd49-4604-b288-ee05842264f7.Text: {n}He nods curtly.{/n} "Harsh, but fair, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Permission to report."

4b1728c2-d2fd-47ce-a43e-a57572b0a5ba.Text: "Emperor protect you, Lord Captain. We will cover the rear if the enemy comes out of the tunnels. Be careful: the mutants have mined the guard post. But there is something they didn't know." {n}Klein squints nastily and hand you a small copper rod with a connector.{/n}

2b13e862-4ab2-4064-bfd7-100a4e5f71b0.Text: "This is Frensoe's data-key that activates the Eclipse protocol. The train control node is vulnerable. If something were to anger or confuse the machine spirits, it could easily lead to a catastrophic accident — a trainload of crashing shells, for instance, or worse. That's why there are Tech-Priests' creations embedded in the walls: they are potent enough to rip the power out of any device."

1c5aa97e-84fa-400a-a752-220906f7a773.Text: {n}You see eyes framed by scars and wrinkles above the respirator.{/n} "Captain Klein, enforcer of the officers' deck, at your service, Lord Captain!"

e6c674d3-1ad2-4794-81b6-734c4366056b.Text: "Mistress Sauerback sent my squad and me to the freight line to take charge of the situation. She heard that you had been spotted here and wanted us to lend you support."

d21cff21-b8d3-4d1d-a1cf-9082398941e8.Text: "I agree, Lord Captain. We found a bite mark on his body... one that we've seen before. I suspect he was compromised against his will."

16a93391-761b-4092-b13a-2278f812b02b.Text: "I could swear the same. I suppose the Emperor's protected me." {n}He touches one of his fresh wounds cautiously. Glistening pus remains on his fingers. A fresh wound could not have taken this little to fester. As you look closer, you notice clear signs in the wound's ooze. The foulness you let into this bay has already latched onto Klein and shared its gifts with him.{/n}

de6da139-c005-410d-8db0-7eec8ed6454b.Text: {n}The enforcer whom you clearly saw die a minute ago gets up from the ground. Reeling and noticeably astonished, he feels his body with his hands and sticks his fingers into his fresh wounds. Having ascertained that he is alive, he resets his dislocated shoulder with a cracking sound.{/n}

701a9257-8a8d-43c9-8432-e2ce85aafac5.Text: "I thank Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} for the timely assistance. I thought it was my fate to go down an aberration's gullet, like poor Jinevri, but the Emperor had other plans for me."

febfe2aa-de35-4a87-b6aa-ca477945525a.Text: "Wretched scum! I fought worse than you on Dargonus!" {n}With a look of disgust, the enforcer in the protective mask grinds his boot into a lump of mutant flesh.{/n}

454f8f62-2046-4fe6-b43c-979eb05637b3.Text: "By treason. Captain Frensoe ordered the enforcers to leave the outpost and led them into a tunnel under the pretext of suppressing a mutiny. As soon as they reached it, however, he began spreading propaganda in an effort to stir up irreverence among the soldiers. He urged them to join the mutiny and eliminate the senior officers."

bd0c4592-09b1-4da4-bc37-8be503966579.Text: "He claimed that the enforcers were being pressured into oppressing their fellow crewmen for the benefit of their greedy superiors. He called for a change of order, including reprisals and penance for anyone who had participated in the crimes of the ship's rotten hierarchy." {n}Klein pulls his respirator aside and spits morosely.{/n}

4650dec1-0b5c-403b-88d3-e042488b81ba.Text: "I arrived just in time to execute the traitor Frensoe and reclaim control. I ordered the squad to return to the post and take up a defensive position, but it was already overrun by mutants entering through the elevator shaft. They lured us out and then seized our fortifications."

a7e69827-2b03-47f5-8da9-576273106189.Text: [Look at the Factotum's army] "I see that all of the crew's clans are working together to retake my vessel."

79ace2d5-3094-491a-9f79-48fd5fc4a484.Text: "How bad is the situation on the ship?"

9d75b8d4-5dd4-4fef-8d41-d824a0424d74.Text: "I would never force you to part with something so dear to your heart."

19986c75-3817-4136-8fbd-dba07c39f512.Text: "I do not wear or wield hand-me-downs from my servants. Keep it."

c95edd67-ae20-46c6-a1e1-a571ab9f2c84.Text: "I take it the inspection did not go well?"

99c62283-6f6e-440b-b964-4026db8b430f.Text: "Lieutenant Vent, what fortune led you to fight alongside the denizens of Depot 4?"

bfa88f9f-a7ad-415b-8a1a-bc8e5e322a29.Text: "What do you intend to do next?"

b8580ac8-99fc-499d-8b8f-65f06b2ee801.Text: "I did not expect you to be so skilled with a rifle, Janris."

26439f13-26ce-4bee-9264-604f0d16a0d7.Text: "That is a fine piece of weaponry you are wielding — elegant and antique. I would love to take a closer look."

24c33c87-fc09-4941-9e11-7e42e5cfe3b1.Text: "A worthy addition to my collection. You have my thanks."

6d066a9f-cdbd-4ef9-b1c7-0fcfc1f20052.Text: {n}Janris Danrok puts down the rifle and dabs his forehead with a silky handkercher, before shoving it under the tight band of the ammunition belt across his chest. His gilded frock coat is overlaid with a bullet-riddled and melted flak vest that barely fits around his voluminous waist. Behind him, a motley band of enforcers, armed clerks, and labourers greets you with enthusiastic shouts. A group of captives, silent and dejected, sits a short distance away.{/n}

d331d6e3-a8e0-40ed-8990-e92e8df87ee3.Text: "Thanks to your order to put the enforcers on high alert, the traitors were unable to take them by surprise. I watched them take back the bays in full assault gear, sparing neither themselves nor their enemies. That was a wise decision indeed."

851ce777-7a11-4a6e-a2d9-7d148e4b1c48.Text: "I should warn you that many of the rebels were carrying enforcers' equipment during the battle. Apparently, they took it from the soldiers assisting in the rescue efforts. Those traitors from the Infernus Guild stabbed them in the back. Be careful."

b93754db-bd2f-464b-ab66-3cf346556302.Text: {n}Janris points courteously to a pile of relics, trophies, and chests overlaid with gold.{/n} "Following your instructions, we were able to evacuate some of your riches in time, as well as the sacred unguents and ammunition from the damaged compartments. Use whatever you like as you see fit. I can assure you that the rest will remain with me in perfect safety."

e179dd88-036d-4723-bbee-29468a812c25.Text: "The kindly inhabitants of Depot 4 are unpretentious but loyal people..." {n}The Factotum nods casually toward the ragged labourers.{/n} "They have generously agreed to join my improvised posse to 'beat the mutinous scum bloody raw,' as they put it. A most honourable clan indeed. I shall order that they be assigned additional water and oxygen rations."

1aa209e0-93f5-40a1-83f1-bd0d6c76c161.Text: {n}You see familiar faces among his escort. Lieutenant Avrilla Vent of the enforcers stands shoulder to shoulder with one of the leaders of Depot 4, an elderly woman whom everyone referred to as Old Nan.{/n}

d73e0538-e0bd-4ca4-b41a-5cd5a9d7f11f.Text: {n}The Factotum loosens the straps on his flak vest slightly and gives a satisfied groan.{/n} "It was going splendidly until we were rudely interrupted by the traitorous mutants. I am afraid I have temporarily had to requisition weapons and uniforms for myself and my militia. But do not worry: every spent bullet will be accounted for and added to the 'unplanned extermination of heretics' column in the ledger."

189e25b2-2fe8-4d28-8a46-397bd9e5c357.Text: {n}The old woman raises her shotgun.{/n} "And we're eager to serve. One must keep one's house in order, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, and you {d|Encyclopedia:CompAbelard_Q1_GaveWeapons}gave us weapons{/d} for a reason! So, Stager came to us all quiet, and he brought some lads along with him. They started talking, telling us how oppressed and deprived we all were. They tried to incite rebellion, you see? And so, we blew their heads off."

3e466764-0595-4e2e-b562-6dd94f01c023.Text: "I must emphasise that it is a miracle that these commoners have joined us and not the rebellion. For the Emperor's sake, do not go arming every commoner on the ship after this, Lord Captain."

a0b4434d-6eff-4820-bea7-d9e19add1aff.Text: "Why, I intend to die for you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Every member of the militia, from burly enforcer to puny clerk, nods in sombre agreement with the High Factotum.{/n} "But I must admit, we are quite exhausted from fighting our way here, and we are not really suited to being an assault squad."

88b891eb-9ed3-4c02-8d59-32e16fcc2a88.Text: "I think Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} should head for the enforcers' post. You will be safer there. Meanwhile, we will take a breather and smoke a few more dozen heretics out of their holes. God-Emperor willing, I will not have to die a glorious death with your name on my lips after all and will instead begin auditing the damage the ship has suffered, as well as the losses among the crew. It is a routine procedure — one in which I have become quite proficient."

4830320f-9edd-48ed-beb3-e8cd40db5e9a.Text: "I am flattered, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I can assure you that smiting heretics is no more difficult than shooting up serfs at my aunt's birthday party. In fact, fighting an armed opponent may even add a certain spice."

041f67d2-8b9a-4982-b624-784c0e2ef9eb.Text: "Quite bad, but it could have been far worse if it were not for Mistress Sauerback's paranoia and insufferable temper. As you well know, she has a nasty habit of expecting betrayal from everyone except Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. She had therefore taken care to draw up special protocols for all sorts of mutiny, and had stationed agents on every deck."

b6892888-b264-469a-944e-a65743a0db41.Text: "You have a discerning eye, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Only a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}true aristocrat{/d} versed in the sophisticated art of hunting would appreciate the perfection that is this handsome toy! May I direct your attention to the filigree on the stock? Made by Master Gorenov himself! A superb weapon for—" {n}He stops himself and suddenly goes pale.{/n} "How utterly boorish of me! Such a tactful intimation, and I have made a fool of myself... Please, accept this weapon as a gift!"

4ba32cee-2686-4249-9fb1-5bd241cbd148.Text: {n}Janris lets out a sigh of relief.{/n} "Rest assured, this rifle will serve House von Valancius well in my hands."

07bd3950-e891-4d59-854e-1d3f8303cb1a.Text: "Serve your new owner faithfully, my dear rifle! Please, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, do not forget to apply the finest oils, or she might get right cranky." {n}Janris dabs his eyes with one hand and snaps his fingers with the other, commanding the nearest servant to give him their weapon.{/n}

41672a5f-a147-4283-ade4-dedc69e950f4.Text: {n}The Factotum blows the head off a heretic with a precise shot, then lowers his rifle.{/n} "Much obliged."

891fbf80-9253-4125-ae6a-cf8b7ea476cf.Text: "You have yet to learn the art of subtly hinting at desirable gifts, shereen..."

c49bf361-eda2-42e0-ac48-6a5e32d35bd2.Text: {n}Ulfar makes a patronising gesture.{/n} "Not bad, coffer keeper. I wouldn't have thought there was such a taste for bloodshed in your heart. I approve of your vigour."

daba9dcc-01d5-4f86-b72b-ed2be9a4a682.Text: {n}Janris swells with pride.{/n} "After being praised by the Angel of the Emperor himself, I simply must end no fewer than a dozen mutineers myself!"

d3f73c65-e015-4e10-8dc9-e506a94feaeb.Text: {n}Solomorne gives a nod of respect.{/n} "Meticulous adherence to procedure. It's a shame you don't serve in the Administratum — I imagine your department would be a true example of efficiency and order."

69f2c61d-3139-44a1-b929-101be4da7348.Text: "I am delighted to see you in good health, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I am afraid my report on the inspection of the ship's storehouses will be slightly delayed due to extraordinary circumstances."

d9d18f4a-805d-49a2-9a4c-594dfe7b57cb.Text: "The enforcers reported that you had been sighted in this compartment, and I humbly believed it was my duty to head for the freight line with this very modest army... Would you kindly move a little to the right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"

2df965b4-148c-4ecc-9742-4a799dae131f.Text: "You are indeed correct, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Serfs, enforcers, officers, Tech-Priests, and tunnel rats have all united in their fight against the rebellious scum. The only ones missing are the inferni. It seems they were the backbone of this mutiny... And they strangled all those who were not privy to their dastardly plan."

0a59e866-4cee-4bf5-a7c8-6667fd09d1a4.Text: {n}Danrok glances at the wounded prisoners.{/n} "Yet, as you can see, our enemies also include those who swore an oath to you not so long ago — crew members who fell for the rebel propaganda. It is your choice whether to sentence them yourself, or to leave the execution to me after you have departed on your business."

e28d2aec-f605-4014-8fb5-d8869c583bc7.Text: "When the riot began, these agents took out many of the seditious officers and mounted a defence. In addition, I have been informed of at least three cases in which the officers inciting the enforcers to mutiny were shot by Jocasta's personal aides. It looks like she had already been keeping an eye on her least reliable subordinates. I should give the Emperor a candle in gratitude for making her such a suspicious hag."

6eb701b0-2228-45da-bf63-18e4d3125fe7.Text: "It cost us, though. Our Rivet was made of heroic stuff: he pounced on Stager, screamed, roused the crowd to a fight. He didn't make it, of course, but at least we shot the doubters and our unwanted guests then and there."

4cf668d1-4889-431e-b4d9-d41a56f923e5.Text: "That fortune was Mistress Sauerback, Lord Captain. She assigned me to keep an eye on the captain of Depot 4, with special powers. The captain had become compromised, so I eliminated him. I then opened a special package with instructions to follow in case of mutiny, formed a defence squad, and joined the battle."

a778e71a-3c48-4774-876e-38646460c373.Text: "...ger me silly, Exalted One be praised..." {n}A dishevelled Jae attempts to dust off her ruined outfit. She clears her throat as she glances at you and puts on an innocent expression.{/n} "My heart overflows with delight to see that you too are in one piece, shereen!"

cfeb86ed-47ea-44c1-b0ef-267a910d0809.Text: {n}Marazhai looks as if there had been no crash at all. The Drukhari's impossible agility clearly allowed him to avoid more than just injury: there does not even seem to be any dust on his armour.{/n} "Death was... tantalisingly close there, hmm? I wish your mon-keigh technologies delivered such surprises more often."

6a66f49d-c597-4eed-818a-3184f2a244b5.Text: {n}The bone crunches unpleasantly, and a sharp pain pierces your arm, but you manage to reset the elbow. It has swollen and still looks worrisome, but at least you can move your arm now.{/n}

2e063f5c-efa4-478d-be2e-51f9018f96a8.Text: {n}The bone crunches unpleasantly, and a sharp pain pierces your arm: it seems that your efforts have only made it worse. You can still hold your weapon, but each careless movement fills your veins with molten lead.{/n}

b5b9f491-787c-405a-92f2-f087d969b42c.Text: "How titillating. Now do the same to your other arm, {name}."

bd1a23fc-5f92-4cad-b149-b6de693f81f0.Text: "{name}... allow me..." {n}Heinrix, quite bruised and dirty himself, reaches out with his hand. A chill makes the pain subside, and you feel the bone pop back into place.{/n}

c9d4e5f5-e616-402e-a56e-e4f3029e7209.Text: {n}It is a miracle you have survived. Guide rails lie in a twisted pile over a crown of shattered plasteel.{/n}

bf5dc29d-882f-4a6e-adf0-914ca0a5a8e0.Text: {n}The elevator was equipped with safety devices meant to stop the cabin inside the shaft, but at least half of them have failed. Your fall was no accident.{/n}

dcdd4530-17d9-4532-b05d-405393428d0f.Text: {n}Smoke and darkness limit your vision, but, judging by the stench of rust and unwashed bodies, you are somewhere on the lower decks. You can hear the crackling of flames, groans, screams, and the rumble of falling beams coming from the distance. The disaster has not spared this compartment.{/n}

94d470df-4e90-433a-92bd-29767177bff8.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g} emits only unintelligible hissing. Either it was damaged in the fall or the communication lines in this compartment have failed.{/n}

e4dd1683-b7af-4f85-afbf-17a1e9266838.Text: {n}The elevator shaft has expelled you into the dim of the emergency lights. The smell of {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g} and burnt flesh only adds to the nausea, confirming that you have suffered a concussion. Your elbow is twisted at an odd angle, and your body is wracked with pain. But there is a silver lining to all the agony: it means you are not dead yet.{/n}

7efbe3b8-f4da-4fe6-a32a-78ecd6deb718.Text: {n}This ship is indeed old. Apparently, this cascade of accidents was the last straw for the aged elevator's {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}.{/n}

aaf69c6e-6ca0-4405-ba08-0a823fbfab6f.Text: {n}The elevator shaft has expelled you into the dim of the emergency lights. The smell of promethium and burnt flesh hits your nostrils, but... there is no pain. Not a single broken bone, not even a scratch on your whole body. It is as if your body became as strong as your faith during the fall, and nothing could have harmed you. Even the ringing echo of the crashed lift resembles the glorious tolling of a bell.{/n}

e1c10662-2adf-4d5a-8c40-2f1f185cdaea.Text: [Operate the switch and send the train into the thick of the battle]

9c54ef21-48a6-45d5-a972-60860abf919a.Text: [Leave the console and rush in to save your people]

11652c61-9771-4375-9445-cc3176ee1710.Text: {n}The route control console stares dispassionately at the carnage unfolding on the tracks. The sounds of an approaching train ring in the distance. With a single command, you could divert the train and send it straight into the thick of the battle, ending the lives of both the xenos spawn and your subjects.{/n}

bac54d13-3969-46e0-a5b6-71a86ee8b889.Text: {n}The console silently observes your heroism, its lumens blinking with indifference.{/n}

24c72a10-9d92-484c-818b-8939a39e9911.Text: {n}With a click of a button, you sacrifice the brave souls for the sake of victory.{/n}

ba712576-c4f1-4e9f-a408-d99937f41459.Text: {n}The snarling voice of one of the defenders sounds familiar. It is Captain Klein, one of the enforcers who assisted in the Master-at-Arms's investigation on the officers' deck.{/n}

d645e417-a667-4f5a-aed0-9053d042a651.Text: {n}In the roar of the oncoming train, you hear the rumble of starting engines and the screeching of spinning blades from the distant {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Militarum}past{/d}. For a moment, you are transported to a different time, where you once again watch sullenly as thousands of soldiers cram into Chimeras and Valkyries to go on a desperate offensive. They will not return, because you have commanded them to die.{/n}

fb2d7476-b92d-47ee-80c1-0c54e9cb861f.Text: An ornate needle rifle in perfect condition. Engraved on the stock are the words: "To my dearest nephew Janris on his coming of age."

5ffd19c5-3033-4480-a840-e143ca39c213.Text: This tiny object contains a spark of unadulterated rage, primed at any moment to expel the power from all devices in the enforcers' post, reducing them to a pile of lifeless metal.

2923ce3d-dcf3-4e03-b296-05e4d28e1a87.Text: A data-key that opens a vault containing service equipment.

51719edc-2f2d-4601-a1aa-434990396e70.Text: "I command that someone get me out of this dump immediately!"

21b796b8-6032-4f55-85f1-932722683c81.Text: "To all who remain loyal to the dynasty: this is the Lord Captain speaking. I am still alive and continuing the fight against the mutineers."

0cfcc1d9-ce56-4ded-b343-34505140ce5f.Text: "Describe the situation on board to me."

a6ea7820-bd5f-45d0-9c6f-65bb1f70b88d.Text: "Why has the bridge not been taken back yet?"

33560b82-8f95-4b7b-911e-9bf7f3ebdce1.Text: "No one dares to give commands on my bridge! Lower the emergency elevator: I am coming."

3b3bb1e0-bb1b-47e0-b942-e9bc9b1e2ac9.Text: "Excellent. I shall crush the enemies of Humanity and purge the evil from this ship!"

c4482bac-9d2d-4f27-9ac8-e85ceaf9612c.Text: "Then I shall have to do everything myself yet again. Get your bucket down here. I am waiting."

ef2e51b0-4dac-417e-bc7a-f4469a9054f0.Text: {n}Vigdis's voice cuts through the barrage of white noise.{/n} "Lord Captain! God-Emperor be praised!"

aa3019dd-eae5-42d0-a5e9-80955191f834.Text: {n}After a moment's hesitation, Vigdis enquires cautiously,{/n} "Does Mistress Tlass... still accompany you?"

466001a4-b2a4-4b93-8e5c-e6292a75336a.Text: {n}Idira leans over toward the receiver and says light-heartedly,{/n} "You can't get rid of me that easily, Vigdis. I'm fine."

c19dbd87-a05f-49c8-af18-398cb9bfd6de.Text: {n}You think you hear a sigh of relief amid the static.{/n} "Acknowledged."

4ae254d0-4677-4849-9203-a9f85506424b.Text: "Mistress Sauerback and the enforcers are defending the officers' deck. I am also here, coordinating the loyalist forces. The key compartments are holding, but we have not been able to turn the tide of battle just yet. The bridge has been overrun by the enemy. The Master Helmsman's fate... is unknown."

718cdfdb-fddd-42f9-b67d-b97c2e53859c.Text: "Judging by the density of the defences, it is where the rebel leader is holed up. Mistress Sauerback has launched three assaults, so far without success. We are taking control of the elevator shaft to launch another attack, but the platform has been destroyed and the emergency elevator can only accommodate a small force."

62902ffc-f375-4077-9e66-e58f48baff9f.Text: "Understood. May the God-Emperor protect you, Lord Captain."

3294b6b5-23dc-40ef-9c7e-3a42a9973aa8.Text: {n}The vox-machine belches out a shower of sparks and wheezes in agony. Although crippled by the pulse that kills machine spirits, it continues to extract the ghosts of other people's voices from the ether.{/n}

e8621aac-949c-4e29-bf96-a8a38a66de03.Text: [Hold out your hand] "You could not have come at a better time!"

e431eaa8-e0f7-431e-b95a-8bb654fb9a64.Text: "I appreciate the concern, Einrich, but you are needed elsewhere. I will get out on my own."

316b0b66-911c-46df-a612-25192da064b5.Text: [Turn to the cultist] "What is your accusation against him?"

2e0381d8-d4fa-49ae-914c-c0220b8c1f6d.Text: "Do you have anything to say, Infernus Master?"

cc14f715-908f-4b2d-99a9-29647c64b60e.Text: [Take a close look at the repairmen]

81370b49-fa71-4d41-b68f-09c1530825d6.Text: "I am certain that someone tried to kill me."

9c93acdb-c8e5-46d7-9601-1398d46abf63.Text: "Hrotko, what are you doing on the freight line?"

544e9777-229e-4cd9-963c-9875a0c82a01.Text: "Einrich, you are carrying a lot of weapons there, are you not?"

aa7aade2-7075-42e3-ba6e-581868371dd0.Text: "Einrich, since when is it acceptable for the inferni to carry weapons?"

fe8f94cf-20ac-4ab9-9f3b-e55dc1b6cef8.Text: "Do you have any proof of treason?"

d60585f1-0279-488e-b4a5-bce8c7535ff6.Text: "These accusations are absurd. Einrich, I am leaving with you."

c1950a21-7d89-42b5-bb3e-d6b67406a04d.Text: "You know, Infernus Master, perhaps you should get off the train so we can figure this out."

7b142f2a-1859-4564-af2c-352b55160815.Text: "Have you ever heard of a Rogue Trader flying through their own voidship in a free-falling elevator, Einrich?"

91504bca-df07-4751-8fa7-5af94f954719.Text: {n}Einrich Monteg's face is covered in soot. He smiles broadly, never letting go of his lho-stick.{/n} "Lord Captain, it is good to see you back in good health, however battered! The Vox Master reported that the elevator had collapsed, so I jumped on the first train and headed down here to look for you." {n}He holds out a hand as strong as a lifeline.{/n} "Let me give you a lift to a safe place."

7538adf9-3087-48d0-9623-a35df69d6d29.Text: {n}Idira snaps her head up sharply and clutches your shoulder.{/n} "Don't go in there. You too, emergency man: don't go wherever you are going. That path leads to death."

648fd86e-61f1-47d9-85f2-24039514143f.Text: {n}Several enforcers emerge and immediately fall into line, standing shoulder to shoulder like a solid wall of ceramite. Their leader reports:{/n} "Captain Hrotko, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We are here to provide assistance and escort!" {n}He turns toward the locomotive.{/n} "Hey, Infernus Master, we found {mf|him|her}!"

43516992-ce35-4738-a401-8e378435beb4.Text: {n}Einrich winks cheerfully.{/n} "Being in the right place at the right time is my duty, my calling even! At your or—"

525aa58b-840b-4a93-aead-3ca0a312aac3.Text: {n}Einrich shakes his head stubbornly.{/n} "Lord Captain, I will not risk abandoning you in a burning compa—"

c017fe1d-6842-4837-8945-d7b98bafffe7.Text: "You are being hunted, Domin'{name}, driven like prey toward the hunter. He is the hunter." {n}The skinny young man, who ceased to be a boy only yesterday, carries himself with detachment and surprising dignity.{/n} "The Vizsier said that he must die and that you must live."

d7890b91-fe2a-49b7-92d0-c52e9a1a4f04.Text: {n}A shot from a needle pistol misses Einrich's head by a thread, cutting his lho-stick in two. A frail young cultist of the Bloodspun Web appears beside you.{/n} "Domin'{name}, cast off the evil hand — it holds only betrayal and wrongful death. Einrich Monteg is not human, and he seeks your demise."

083ea54f-c34d-493e-bad9-6dde39dd389f.Text: {n}Einrich spits at his feet in frustration.{/n} "You fanatics are always meddling in the wrong business. First the trick with the blood bath, and now this. We were so close." {n}The gun leaps into his hand and points at you. A shot rings out. The whistling hits your ears, but the bullet was evidently meant for the young spinner now writhing on the ground.{/n}

cab980db-dcda-4155-8cf6-961bf3a8c224.Text: "Do I... What? Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, do I really have to defend myself after being accused by this... I don't even know who he is! It's... It's me. I have risked life and limb for you and this ship more times than that groxchunder has heard the watch siren."

94a6bf1f-a6d0-4a49-9c02-020c43a561e2.Text: "No!" {n}The young spinner shrieks as he raises his needle pistol and fires a fatal shot... which turns out to not be fatal at all. The needle slices into Einrich's cheek before bouncing off harmlessly. Beneath the sagging flap of skin, you see... something purple. It is chitin.{/n}

cc11f97a-4716-4d19-9a5d-2537ee9c4265.Text: {n}Einrich takes out a new lho-stick, lights it from his cutter, and blows out the smoke with a heavy sigh.{/n} "Things would be a lot easier if you had just crashed in the elevator. Or climbed onto the train. I wish you too could hear the Sire's song in your dreams and await the Many-Armed Emperor. But the harvest season has come, and you must be reaped. You must die so that we may live. I am sorry, {name}. Farewell."

6a072f7e-1de5-4edd-9a3b-165454ce16e6.Text: {n}The inferni look baffled, but the astonishment soon gives way to righteous indignation as huge, burn-covered fists clench into instruments of murder.{/n}

a497afdf-2188-4f51-8fba-336ce9030214.Text: {n}But they are not the only instruments. You see hands slip under clothes and curl around weapon grips. Somewhere in the crowd, you glimpse the all-too-familiar glint of {g|Encyclopedia:Plasteel}gun metal{/g}.{/n}

d80a3cda-68e8-49d1-8995-4b47546a17b7.Text: {n}But they are not the only instruments. There are shotguns and pistols too, which you generously allowed them the right to carry. Knives and axes, autoguns, grenades... The inferni went into the rescue mission as if it were a battle.{/n}

430e3767-62c8-410d-b049-3c59eb3bf97e.Text: "Then it is fortunate you are travelling in the company of such big, bad infernus repairmen. How do we feel about people harming the Lord Captain in front of us, lads?" {n}Einrich smiles brightly at the furious, almost bestial growls of his subordinates.{/n}

43c9c8b2-a056-4078-bb74-c965e6d67984.Text: "And even if our forces prove insufficient, Captain Hrotko and his squad will surely find something with which to meet the enemy. That's a lot of deadly toys they're packing." {n}He smiles sardonically.{/n}

615515b7-7073-439a-befa-3f70c0be954e.Text: "Besides, we came prepared." {n}His hand brushes against the pistol on his belt.{/n} "You gave us the privilege of bearing arms, and we won't let it go to waste."

cec1ea6b-a93c-4c4d-ab6c-49f81ee8b36f.Text: {n}Clad in heavy riot armour, the enforcer gives you a dignified nod.{/n} "My men have never faltered in battle, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. All of them are veterans, capable of clearing out a ship from stem to stern."

9dcec84f-767e-4e70-b4af-bfe7d25f7d3d.Text: "When the disaster struck, I took the liberty of selecting a few dependable fighters and going to the lower decks to keep order. You cannot prove your valour by staying back and doing nothing. I would rather march straight into the flames." {n}Hrotko raises his clean-scraped chin.{/n}

cdb79018-f0b8-466e-b04c-139a8f518d64.Text: "After all these years of not being allowed to carry anything heavier than a wrench... I suppose you could say we are overcompensating." {n}Einrich's smile looks somewhat strained.{/n}

df713d21-c991-478e-bf1f-0727dcd09970.Text: "I understand that the situation is critical, but... Damn it, I am a senior officer of this ship, as much as I hate to remind you. And you are a little mutineer who almost put a hole in my head."

09586942-3eef-418a-8724-bfb0544d1e8a.Text: {n}Hrotko clangs the stock of his weapon soundly. In a sneering tone, he asks,{/n} "What do we have here, treason? An attempted assassination of a senior officer? I have long expected trouble from you spinners..."

1bae2b01-afb1-4ac1-8505-4a25f10891b1.Text: {n}A question forms in your mind all on its own: how do you kill a Rogue Trader? Out of {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}habit{/d}, you quickly go over a few plans and come to the unfortunate conclusion: this is how. You create a crisis, lure the Rogue Trader away from the bridge, sabotage the escape routes, and then send in a squad to mop up any survivors. A solid plan — simple, yet effective.{/n}

1622543f-c4dc-4f63-b7f8-c21f8af68060.Text: "The Vizsier has divined the truth." {n}The young man looks at Einrich with haughty reproach.{/n}

fc874a28-aa84-456e-ac63-1af32629ce2b.Text: "Oh. Well, since the Vizsier has overdosed on stimulants and discovered the truth... by all means, Lord Captain, go ahead and arrest me. Take my head."

6f81a4de-c2cc-4dad-8710-451b371e7605.Text: "Maybe you really are the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}bringer of woes{/d} that simple folk paint you as. Are you sure you didn't curse the elevator? That old thing transported Rogue Traders for hundreds of years, but then you stepped inside — and down it went!"

3ecc5036-80ab-4481-97a5-7770f2e88bab.Text: {n}Heinrix grips his weapon, and the chilling psychic aura around him makes your blood run cold.{/n}

b15f3ab4-9167-4c3f-aaa5-0d8232b0cda1.Text: "It looks like I am not alone in having a problem with unreliable allies..." {n}Marazhai's voice is laden with unexpected irony.{/n}

b80d61cf-0548-4709-90e2-5445b47593e6.Text: "I am sure many on this ship would be pleased to be rescued with such daring. But it is only right that the Rogue Trader should get all the nicest things, is it not?"

c178cc36-a80d-493e-9910-7c6f16cd0bc1.Text: "Emperor knows I'm sick of all these cultists, and yet... The boy could have shot you, Rogue Trader, but he didn't. That is worth an investigation, at the very least."

4027e4ea-5434-4c56-9be0-3cd049494710.Text: {n}Einrich gives a sad little chuckle.{/n} "It is my job to take the paths where death may be prowling. But not this time. The train is the safest and fastest way out of here. Worry not, Mistress Tlass. You and the Lord Captain are quite safe with me."

fa599d19-5690-4212-a7e3-d2a294e03e9f.Text: {n}A locomotive enveloped in steam halts at the platform with a low rumble. The hardened emergency workers of the Infernus Guild pour out of the carriages. Upon seeing you, they begin to wave cheerfully and shout.{/n}

de4d3de7-3ad5-47ff-ba33-bdc8529f6f8b.Text: "No, I think that's a first." {n}Einrich raises an eyebrow and says politely,{/n} "Lord Captain, you sure know how to make a dramatic entrance."

6057531e-f2f4-4ab3-aa11-a4c9e0e259fb.Text: "It's repairman's hunch, Lord Captain. I find myself drawn to places where nothing has broken yet, but is about to—"

7245ae5e-ad16-4103-8c08-8af571463765.Text: {n}The Infernus Master pulls the last of the lho-stick from his mouth and asks in a low voice,{/n} "Have you lost your mind, you damned fanatic?"

3332355e-2e40-422b-a941-bae3dc3d8b96.Text: "Get out of my way. I do not have time for you."

d081e8c4-61b3-4dde-8a60-64975401cd7d.Text: "Thank you. This will come in handy."

18f7eda9-1161-4672-b924-0f8e1733b1d6.Text: [Shake his hand] "I will not forget your help."

696c8c2d-364f-42d7-bd23-2fb83abc2d2e.Text: "I am doing fine. You should help someone else."

c74c9292-c38f-4c05-9c67-c61f0518264b.Text: {n}The worker before you is the same man you saved from the enforcer earlier. He is badly burnt, but his face is beaming.{/n} "Blimey, if it isn't you, Lord Captain! I heard the elevator fall, so I came to help in case anyone survived. And, lo and behold, it's Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"

a6c305c3-3d83-4673-b6b0-8675ff125a38.Text: "It's a big ol' accident. Everything's on fire, and the place is packed with corpses. Some burned alive, others choked on smoke, but we'll save our home ship. Just you wait and see!"

363c66cc-eaaa-4c86-a026-1230dc261e37.Text: "I'm following orders: to look for anyone badly wounded and provide them with first aid." {n}He hands you a medicae kit.{/n} "Take this — Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s health comes first."

db3bbbac-2904-4d75-9d0f-80da89686e67.Text: {n}He stares at you, then at his hand, then at you again, his eyes filling with tears of joy.{/n} "Emperor keep you!"

1dafcc76-1e47-417c-9bce-3672dda6c754.Text: "Proud to serve the ship, the dynasty, and Your very {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"

f0ce8f93-5210-4e96-afe3-c276a1973da5.Text: "And you believed them? I am a legend of the Expanse, and oppression of commoners is not in the history of my deeds. Is it not obvious? Our enemies are trying to sully my name!"

8e97b9d5-da14-4f6d-8301-851fb060743a.Text: "Who put you up to this rebellion?"

7ea18256-838e-4b9d-8ea3-6d2876efed2b.Text: "You will atone with your blood or perish this instant. The choice is yours."

317e070a-3338-438f-85dd-9a7f3c02836b.Text: "I shall let you go. It is up to you whether to flee or to seek vengeance."

4049057a-c363-4b05-842f-236a724d5f47.Text: [Execute them] "I sentence you to death for rebelling against the Rogue Trader and for aiding traitors to the Imperium."

3e60ed76-723a-4ab3-a152-c3539cd1337b.Text: "I am not ready to deal with you right now."

00031583-4fe7-4bc2-a69a-36dfa09b2115.Text: "Are you from the Cult of the Ravenous Star?"

375fd00c-5b65-49e7-9cf5-308b855add3b.Text: [Execute them] "If I am a tyrant, then I must live up to expectations. Die."

6cbd5845-84bd-43f1-99e3-cc2d5d59fb44.Text: "The Infernus Guild set up the very disaster that killed your children, your husbands and wives. They are using you."

8c31b1cd-3ffd-418e-b5c0-c7b72cbec1de.Text: "Their Nemesite was a mutant freak, just like these 'liberators' themselves. Purple skin, crest on the forehead — I trust you have seen those before?"

4474db17-1eb6-4bea-89d6-2fd6bc1f66a1.Text: Sacrificed the prisoners to the Ruinous Powers for a surge of power.

87b5fdf3-8559-491c-8882-28375ec7e3b7.Text: [Sacrifice the prisoners to the true gods] "You will pay for your treason. I will spill your blood so that fortune might favour me in battle."

dded71a3-aaba-41d7-8f26-0629e85094b6.Text: Swore to the God-Emperor that you would ignore your wounds and press on until the ship was purged of all corruption.

b645e49c-4489-4fbd-9227-14ef0007d672.Text: "Emperor, hear my vow! I will continue to spill my blood, nor stop to heal my wounds, until the corruption that has befouled my ship is destroyed!"

68dd5370-392a-436e-8bdd-6aae5674e276.Text: [Raise your voice] "You have let your guard down! You have fallen into the enemy's trap! They have used you — turned you into traitors to Humanity! You are all guilty before the Emperor!"

e4989457-fab6-4bd8-8c34-df48c2924c33.Text: "You will pay with your blood. From now on, you lot are a penal assault unit."

cbe34e8c-70cb-4e01-a95b-4c5d98375855.Text: "Arm yourselves and bring death to the enemy. I, your legendary commander, will lead you into battle!"

90bde3b9-790b-40fc-be7e-ad3cc2094d92.Text: {n}A group of shackled commoners are huddled together on their knees. They wear no armour, just filthy rags and tattered coveralls. Some hide their gaze while others sob quietly or mutter prayers. Only one woman, swarthy and heavily built, glares at you. She is trying to appear proud and fearless, but her lip is trembling.{/n}

fd0a49cc-8a92-43bc-b50f-cf51f51113c9.Text: {n}The woman mutters with a shocked look on her face:{/n} "Yes, of course... Word of your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}glory{/d} had reached every deck of this ship even before you arrived on board. So we've been... tricked? What are we supposed to do now?"

71c5e6f3-fc96-4b68-aaf8-5b98dd91cf8b.Text: "The liberators, our true heroes! When the fiery death rained down on our slums, not one of your enforcers lifted a finger to save us. But the inferni went out of their way to pull children out from under the rubble, mend wounds, and comfort widows. They opened our eyes!"

561000ac-1d62-4391-8ff9-32f20ac6aeb3.Text: "What are you waiting for? Just end us and be done with it. Isn't that what tyrants do?"

44c8e3ad-19df-4987-9e1e-4144377ed57d.Text: {n}The woman sneers.{/n} "I get it. So many people to kill. Don't you worry: we'll be right here, waiting for our executioner."

a9606a3b-92b8-4950-8ed0-c012d1cced20.Text: "Cult?" {n}At first, the woman looks confused, but then a bitter smirk appears on her lips.{/n} "Is that what you call our liberators? To you, anyone who fights the oppressors is a heretic."

bd98230f-745b-4125-a985-94c5e2b44100.Text: {n}The woman nods.{/n} "Tyrant. Oppressor. Butcher. Choose whichever one you like."

239700b6-e840-4b57-9c00-c45f4825b1cb.Text: {n}The woman stiffens but meets her last moment with dignity. Not everyone follows her example.{/n}

368fe25e-931f-4e30-95b7-c0bdd2749b31.Text: "They said that we no longer need to endure beatings, fight over crumbs of food, or die after you have worked us to the bone! That people can live as equals, take care of one another, and have dignity. This is what they are fighting for. You profit from keeping us in poverty, and your faith is false! Why would the Emperor want His believers to suffer in vain?"

81f32a4d-fa80-4941-a30f-c5977122c2e0.Text: "I thought they were just mutations. Are you saying... we've been tricked by inhuman fiends? By the Holy Throne, what have we done..."

b702ba8a-e125-4b96-8a74-19048435b5a8.Text: "All sorts of mutations can happen to us bottom-deckers. Who cares what grows on their foreheads? What matters is that their souls are pure. And yours is not."

39dd6924-0d5c-4b1a-b192-d7eafb2d7ca6.Text: {n}The woman fixes her gaze on you, as if searching your face for signs of deception. Then, she turns pale and a single tear rolls down her cheek.{/n} "Set up the disaster... But how..."

8c283cfd-daa4-4044-9b98-4ffa060c3afe.Text: "Of course, make monsters out of them. It suits your purpose. But I know what I saw."

53ad8cfe-cf2f-4e75-933f-a5434aed13b2.Text: "For— Forgive us, Lord Captain." {n}The woman draws a quivering breath.{/n} "We won't forget your mercy. Give us weapons and a round of ammunition and send us forward! The bastards will answer for everything. Even death is kinder than false hope."

837bcbac-2f5b-489c-8167-25d0f502b462.Text: "Even the ship's confessor renounced the false covenants and went on to raise the folk hero, Nemesite! And you killed both of them!"

577af3f0-12a0-4c4c-af20-c4cd74634e29.Text: {n}You turn your thoughts to the Ruinous Powers as you kill the prisoners one after the other. As you silently mouth the words of forbidden prayers, you sense that your sacrifice has pleased the gods. A dark blessing guides your hand, and the agony of the butchered courses through your veins, pulsing with strength and an impetus to act. You see horror in the still eyes of the corpses — in their final moments, they fully understood the extent of your power and their own terrible fate.{/n}

101654eb-a74e-4814-a3ab-0f37fa861e6c.Text: {n}Danrok and your loyal servants freeze in reverent silence. Seldom do they have the opportunity to witness the Rogue Trader swear a sacred vow to the God-Emperor.{/n}

5ed4f953-6f31-46b7-bf67-ffd3e32a2a63.Text: {n}Staggered by the confidence of a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}battle-hardened Commissar{/d}, the woman loses her rebellious spirit and lowers her head, suddenly pale. The sincerity of your anger serves as the best possible proof that you are right.{/n} "We're... traitors? Blessed Throne, is it really true? But we thought... What are we supposed to do now?"

1e7681d4-7458-4fca-bae2-2c0f43e5ef46.Text: {n}Cassia sighs.{/n} "The Imperium's history has shown time and again that the rabble is incapable of building a civilised society without governance. Alas, peasants do not read historical treatises."

3be0123d-91ba-4c8e-84f7-8d9996b07f7f.Text: "Where is your Sire? What is he?"

7856ae9a-235c-45fc-bf69-6e922077fdcc.Text: "I propose a complete surrender. I guarantee you a spacious cage in my trophy room, inhuman scum."

8273dc5c-a657-4895-9387-0628fd116fe6.Text: "I will ask again: who are you?"

c8398dd9-f878-40a7-b12b-7eba6477e2b5.Text: "I killed the previous 'Magus.' Did you two know each other?"

8ac47ff7-0656-4f89-8eb3-304d3cfbe690.Text: "Do you really believe you can take over my ship? How long have you been planning this mutiny?"

faf3e784-ef8a-44ff-9f66-d592ff297626.Text: {n}The woman before you radiates an alien beauty — the bony crest on her forehead, the violet tint of her skin, and the graceful, clawed fingers give away her xenos heritage. Her robes resemble those of the old mutant you put to death in the family crypt, and her posture is regal and powerful. Sapphire light oozes from beneath the half-lowered eyelids, and a haughty smirk stretches her lips.{/n}

b0f415d1-7285-42b4-a263-a5b476be3982.Text: {n}The armour of your mind weakens. Now she knows who you are.{/n}

631f372a-e0f8-4295-a20d-fe132c8c6c3f.Text: {n}You banish the alien thoughts from your head and clamp the Magus's mind in a vice before she can put up a mental barrier. The woman clutches at her eyes with a scream, sapphire light and dark blood pouring from beneath her eyelids. She howls,{/n} "The Reaping!"

83bd902a-b42f-4149-b5d2-d9f8514a7aec.Text: {n}The woman gracefully raises her hand and points a sharp claw at you.{/n} "Children of the Reaping, kill the heretics! Glory to the Sire!"

a0344e05-9342-4ccb-b6c0-ebd2c2e5cd5c.Text: {n}Biting whispers burst through your head, digging into your mind and probing your thoughts — tasting them. The woman does not move her lips, but you hear a voice speak:{/n} "You fight in vain, genetic remnant. We have already won. The Sire's song echoes in the dreams of those who are pure. The rest are destined for oblivion. The Sire's sorrowful phalanx has extended, and soon, the others will follow. Whatever you plan to attempt, it matters no more."

86581793-7394-42ed-a90a-cb7057983541.Text: {n}Mental claws squeeze your brain, flooding it with inconceivable images. You hear the old man's cackling again.{/n}

c9d07dbf-0e48-4a81-bfdd-84153038c935.Text: {n}The woman's voice is indifferent.{/n} "He was wise but old, a child of a different season. While it was his time, the Congregation honoured him, and then his time passed, and he went with it. He sacrificed himself, gave himself up to the heretics to be torn apart. We praise his devotion, but we are of a different generation. We were born for the Reaping. Our ascension is assured."

2dae7c99-ccce-4442-b7ba-58b10a0f39bd.Text: "I am the Harvester, Magus, guardian of the pure, She-Who-Hears-His-Songs. I am the priestess of the immortal angel, our Sire. I am the one who Knows and Understands."

60cc1e63-c4ad-45a7-a62d-5e3ceb7777a3.Text: {n}The gaze of something ancient and vicious burns a hole in your will, filling the void with terror and awe.{/n}

fba51f10-d08a-46cc-bb4f-85f23b1895dc.Text: "The Singing Angel is where you used to dwell, impure one. From his rightful seat, he leads us to the Many-Armed Emperor." {n}The woman's smile grows dreamy.{/n} "The Sire is a child of the Many-Armed Emperor, blood of His blood — a covenant gifted to us. His song binds us in sacred unity. He is goodness, survival, and promise."

a77b742d-6d96-4580-8da1-c7c85d0a353b.Text: {n}You banish the alien thoughts from your head, but the Magus erects a mental barrier and deflects the attack even before you retaliate. A smile blossoms on her lips.{/n} "You are helpless before the might of the Congregation of the Pure."

01573b45-413f-4a17-b901-1af3dee73bc6.Text: "Year after year for centuries, we sowed the seeds of the Sire's genetic perfection on this ark. Those seeds have now sprouted, and the change of generations has produced sufficient purebreds. The sowing season is over. The reaping season has come." {n}A murderous laugh cuts blade-like between your frontal lobes.{/n} "The Sire senses your weakness. Your trials and hardships have exhausted you. You are but prey for our mighty creator. You are already dead."

1a7bfe5e-3103-41df-9342-5e8c44a15654.Text: {n}The whispers sink their fangs into your most painful memory as into an exposed nerve, while the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}canker{/d} in your soul echoes ominously in response. Through the woman standing before you, something is staring at you, something you have seen only in your darkest dreams.{/n} "You are touched by corruption. You know that your doom is nigh, cursed soul!"

28e64ec1-4b89-479e-844f-c7815e5c0dae.Text: {n}If there is one thing you have learned over your years of {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}service{/d}, it is to keep your mouth shut when you should. Your mind has taken on a stamina that has suffered far worse than this witch, scowling with displeasure as she is. Your consciousness is a fortress wrapped in the barbed wire of your will, your eyes the all-seeing searchlights mounted atop its guard post. Nothing. Gets. In.{/n}

65e30b8a-3ba4-44c6-8730-be46021e623c.Text: {n}The whispers sink their fangs into your most painful memory as into an exposed nerve. It knocks the air out of your lungs as you remember the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}pain{/d} that you have tried so desperately to forget.{/n} "Your body is broken and flawed, and your mind is bleeding. You should have given up long ago, fading one. Accept your death, and let go of your torment."

2e7b8012-212a-4837-91c1-a8cb8d6d11bc.Text: {n}The teeth of the mental whispers in your head become sharper. They scratch at your will and nibble on your intellect, eager to expose its secrets. The woman's voice is full of overbearing self-righteousness.{/n} "Speak, impure one. Speak all you want, and I will end this battle before it even begins."

cfe089e6-1d1c-4cc1-a6ec-08e88a4abfde.Text: {n}The whispers sink their fangs into your most painful memory as into an exposed nerve. The ridicule, the looks of contempt, the pitying comments — the long-faded ripples of your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}disgrace{/d} hit you in a burning wave of shame and regret.{/n} "You are pathetic. You do not deserve to lead. An insect like you must perish."

00e752ef-3b3a-4fca-871f-4c6a5d1ae943.Text: {n}Despair slithers into your soul. They have been preparing for this far longer than you have, and they have almost won.{/n}

2494d178-df54-4265-945a-31309e8b9dfd.Text: "We had a saying on my old ship: the only way to escape a void kraken is to ram right through it. Ram the kraken, Captain."

f46d7875-5e43-4888-ada2-476825c9cd7a.Text: "No external signs of mutation, you say? What about internal signs?"

3afa396a-f467-43f1-9e77-b9340a049ca9.Text: [Turn away from Klein] "It would seem that I had an exaggerated opinion of this veteran's courage. He should get some rest. Let Hrotko take over his duties."

9beed596-7ca7-40b1-8361-73bc0d623dc5.Text: "I have heard that medicae officers often perform autopsies in pairs — one cuts up the body, the other records the findings. You should get a partner, Klein."

25dc2ff5-59e4-4095-a06e-798906d9ee18.Text: [Sip amasec] "Specifics are merely an impediment to flexible thinking. Follow your heart."

97602d29-684f-4103-8d79-45fc608af3c4.Text: "No, I do not. You may assign them yourself."

41952304-242e-4b64-9115-c1088c416cb1.Text: "For what purpose was the corpse mutilated?"

a8b44dbb-22ec-4cab-ad28-a5b8cd3305ab.Text: "Remember Saint Quirine. Could this be a sign?"

c62de000-fc3c-4028-8596-238b5fb39eaf.Text: "What tattoo? What do pipewardens have to do with anything?"

cbf18abf-6294-4065-9371-980f55ca4d8f.Text: "Klein, I wish to gift you a glass of amasec for your good work. You look like you need it."

dd7cbe9c-e882-4e04-9df2-250417ae1381.Text: "Well, at least you did something useful on your second attempt."

7686a70c-14f2-4ba8-a853-9e45b3ca7b71.Text: "It is imperative that we find whoever mutilated the body."

551d5fa4-38f6-4c36-8565-30adb0fc59e8.Text: "Look for a lunatic. Only a madman would butcher a corpse in this way."

b5e31c4d-be36-421f-9c46-2513cc34f5a7.Text: "One cannot disfigure a body like that and stay clean. Look for any bloodstained garments, rags, or the like."

6d4c9f25-92b1-4fb5-8eb6-48dd76f2b5c5.Text: "We need to find the weapon or object that was used in mutilating the corpse."

205baefc-11e8-4d15-ad31-bb2615311e86.Text: {n}Captain Klein snaps to attention:{/n} "Identifying the victim has proven impossible. His face has been smashed in and his body is badly maimed. There are too many wounds to determine the exact cause of death, but presumably he died after the killer slit his throat — that's how they drained his blood. No external signs of mutation were found."

8a3cd2ef-9173-407c-aeb9-56df87cd2642.Text: "In other words, we have nothing. Klein, this isn't a report; it's a declaration of our incompetence before the Lord Captain. You will keep digging around inside that corpse until you have produced some results."

9d0d4924-c29c-4010-a9d3-ef97438f8591.Text: {n}You can tell the officer is terrified, even if he is desperately trying to hide it.{/n}

503b4014-5e89-448e-999c-8299eeff3f19.Text: "At once!" {n}Hrotko smirks.{/n} "You're getting old, Klein. Let me give you a refresher on gutting mutants."

6f6b2113-42a7-4e03-b41a-d631afbea222.Text: "Performing an autopsy was... inadvisable, due to the danger of contaminating the area with genetic aberration."

527f78be-bf6d-43fd-ac70-f3d6d23c1971.Text: "According to regulations, one enforcer is required for this duty; however, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s proposal is reasonable. Did you have someone specific in mind?"

44ce3835-6ea0-4123-82b1-36d169302adf.Text: {n}Sauerback twists her lips into a sceptical grin.{/n} "A lunatic, you say... The rabble is vile by its very nature, and would do such a thing in a heartbeat. But we will heed your advice and look only for the most violent among them."

5fecb18d-0e02-401b-82e4-27f70ddc18e1.Text: "The body was disfigured posthumously. They killed the mutant with surgical precision, before opening his throat and draining his blood. It wasn't until after the actual murder that they crushed his head and tried to cover up his wounds."
