3d120b3f-7aab-48c4-b473-6b95eebe6f27.Text: "Do you serve Nemesite or do you command him?"

48562b4a-bd95-465f-91d0-e4a5ddd86c0c.Text: "You are responsible for the deaths of countless people. The time has come for a reckoning."

1335ebc8-5fc8-46e2-bb92-3b6cf791b19c.Text: "I demand an explanation, Confessor. This instant."

2dc90a3a-0f1a-4999-9a98-54c15f96d3e9.Text: "Kibellah, it was you who found him. Therefore, it is up to you to pass judgement."

f5dcd6c7-27a3-4b4c-99c8-0a0e3b4f7a44.Text: "Are you hoping he will save you now?"

8d322aa7-384c-4dbb-ae38-9c2c9325a652.Text: "For betraying the faith, I hereby excommunicate you from the Emperor's light and name you an abomination! And now — die, heretic."

23441c4a-fc66-40c6-8b0d-9a2e6b64e626.Text: "Despite your crimes, I will keep you alive. Sauerback, arrest the traitor."

42b9b5d6-c026-46a6-be42-0d053ac5e1c6.Text: "Any rebellion is a strike against the Imperium, to the advantage of the enemies of Humanity. Repent, for there is no fate worse than to be deprived of His light."

cb5146a3-07de-45b3-93f9-78e0713a4d8b.Text: "I too desire a better life for my subjects. The path to that need not be violent — let us make peace and change life on the ship together."

3bc500d7-6741-4cb0-801b-1639548f0829.Text: "Face the facts — you are no champion of justice. You are a manipulator who raises himself up by standing on the corpses of others. I am not judging you. On the contrary, I could use a man of such talents. Together we could accomplish a great deal..."

69e732a8-c377-4cd8-8eb5-b8145366b9ac.Text: "Your 'liberation' is rooted in betrayal and bloodshed."

64e1e2ac-5df1-4e00-807b-227b01691a91.Text: "Impostor Adalbert, I, Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, sentence you to death for treason!"

0f9793ea-ec48-4113-bc63-b48de2a696f7.Text: "To separate a family would be cruel. You and your son will see each other soon enough."

9b0d1aa3-da2b-4921-a4bd-4fcc541f11dd.Text: "And you were so good at moaning about the servants he killed..."

e7424b67-a021-4fa1-9d13-4fe72c027238.Text: "You are not even trying to lie. This is commendable."

5cbe4b03-eefb-4a15-b96a-fae4d93ca4e1.Text: {n}Adalbert meets Kibellah's words calmly, with almost majestic resignation.{/n} "A defender of the people and a tyrant's minion are two faithful servants of opposing ideas, two souls that have rejected everything else for the sake of duty. I now truly see that your collision with him was inevitable."

dfb21e1d-2cbb-4a41-b9ed-567c0c11d9b7.Text: "And it was by the Emperor's command that I took Adalbert's place through deception, pretending to be him. The dead man had inherited much influence and many thrones from his clan, which hastened my successful rise through the ranks. But it was not for wealth and power that I did this! I accepted the burden of hard work to empower the common people, to pave the way for liberation from oppression and injustice. And my part is almost done."

fb7d9158-c912-4f53-a647-5ccfeee5f670.Text: "This is a war, {name}. The war for our liberation, and we are willing to die and to kill for it, because our enemy is brutal and deaf to our pleas. You have deserved it." {n}He resolutely places his hand over his heart.{/n}

df601f2a-c525-45b8-9b51-77943cbcec68.Text: "Your pet tormentor who extols death is right. I know Nemesite, and I assist him. Just like him, I am your enemy, {name}." {n}Adalbert raises his voice, and in the soft tenor, you hear notes of accusation as deep as rolling thunder.{/n} "And I am also the enemy of your cruel regime, where life is dirt under the enforcers' feet, where a man has nothing to eat, writhes in fear, and knows no hope!"

15d483ce-2fe5-4ea3-9882-0c6b82353ee8.Text: {n}Kibellah extends a finger topped with a metal claw toward Confessor Adalbert.{/n} "The divination has revealed that you stand beside the enemy Nemesite. Speak only the truth before the Domin and the Undying One."

86fa9831-aece-436b-b8fa-ce672dd0f4de.Text: "I follow him as he once followed me. Nemesite is my son, if not by blood then in spirit. I took him in as a wilful child, and I fostered the best in him... a passion for justice, the indomitable flame of a fighter, and unyielding determination. I have been preparing him for years."

3d8522a1-3430-49c1-af9e-ac2a20991abf.Text: "Lord Captain, this is an ambush! They have been waiting for us!" {n}Sauerback's shout hits your ears, drowning out hurried footsteps and the clanking of gun plasteel.{/n}

d3059936-fd71-4378-ab41-c21dbed0539a.Text: {n}Kibellah whispers to you,{/n} "I sense no lie in his voice or bearing, Domin'{name}. He feels and welcomes death with open arms. The moment favours us. We must learn more. He who betrayed his oaths will not deliver Nemesite to us, but from his words we may divine knowledge of our enemy."

fbfb991b-39ce-4408-bfce-44c659337621.Text: "The shackles will fall, and there will be nothing left of your tyranny. Nor of you." {n}Adalbert speaks without hatred. His even voice is that of a martyr on his way to glory.{/n}

9e904180-4000-44ef-bfaf-3bdade4b6856.Text: "One last confession? Why not?" {n}He frowns and pulls back his collar, as if he were short of breath.{/n} "I am not Adalbert. That was the name of an initiate from a clan of confessors who passed away from disease many years ago. I was born in squalor on the lower decks, and at the behest of the M—" {n}He falters, as if he wanted to add something else.{/n}

30d7c393-5a65-460b-aad8-d24a94c4721e.Text: "No, we decided otherwise. I am not worth him risking his life, so do not expect to capture him through me. My son has no attachments, for they would only make him weak. He will gladly sacrifice himself for his dream of liberty and equality, and I must do the same. I only grieve that, thanks to your efforts, I cannot be near my son and ease his burden."

b33cfb51-13b3-4d22-b883-1d2b7b92ca9f.Text: "You seem to have mistaken my humility in the face of death for submission." {n}Adalbert smiles weakly.{/n} "It is not for you to decide my fate. I will make the choice myself — I will surrender my life in the fight for our future. I will die, but I will take you with me." {n}He clicks his fingers, and the initiates who have been standing humbly around turn in your direction, their white robes opening to reveal a variety of weapons.{/n} "For Nemesite, brothers and sisters! For freedom!"

490d5252-5841-432d-ad60-c13ea9353878.Text: "I grieved for them, but... they were unreliable. They could have compromised us. They had to die, but the fault for their deaths lies with you and your enforcer dogs, for fear of whom we are forced to hide."

05566262-e052-4254-b092-79ed90819570.Text: "No. Heresy is what you and your fellow bloodsuckers believe in. The {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Ecclesiarchy{/g} has turned faith into a whip to drive the powerless, the aristocracy has turned it into a shield to cover their transgressions, and the enforcers have turned it into a club with which to beat those who dare to raise their voices. Your faith is an instrument of lies and suppression, and I renounced it long ago. My faith promises salvation, not thraldom."

a791c303-8e0b-4d8f-80b6-3177525a3d70.Text: {n}Adalbert shrugs, his kindly face growing harder.{/n} "Why would I? If the dogs have come looking for blood, they will not leave without a kill. Such is your vicious nature."

47b49ac7-c04c-4a35-bee1-fcb33d057d55.Text: "You were not there for those years of pestilence. Confessors attended every deck and died in multitudes. New ministers were recruited in every port, at every station. Their names and faces blurred together, and we recognised our kin only by their robes. No one who knew Adalbert's true face survived that time. The Emperor saved me from being exposed."

88a532db-1e9f-4bb1-8a0c-f95ac836d895.Text: {n}Sauerback reacts to his gesture with due suspicion, sharply gripping her weapon, prepared to eliminate any threat to you.{/n}

6c86a9a6-56d9-49e1-92b5-72aa2ffc3d6c.Text: {n}Argenta's eyes flash.{/n} "Betrayer of the faith! Your blasphemous words will perish with you!"

1e6139f0-b221-49df-9a9c-db9ca2338a57.Text: "Even when it is fighting injustice, your kind only manages to foster more evil in its midst."

48503c9c-23e3-42cc-aaf2-e46e85ace081.Text: "You holy people are all bloody hypocrites!" {n}Idira spits at the confessor's feet.{/n} "You go on about how rotten we are, but take a knife and scratch your surface a little — and we'll find the worst heretic of all!"

2dff9d4a-fbf5-4024-8bbb-ccf1ef0614f4.Text: "I doubt it. People like you only ever see what they want to see."

e78d71ef-3e6b-47c8-aafb-33612297d1c3.Text: "I am bathed in His light as never before! You worship lies, while the true Emperor desires otherwise for his children!" {n}It takes an effort for him to regain his composure.{/n} "Your light is darkness, {name}. And I am sorry you are unable to see the truth."

8df99026-1a86-40a5-92a7-aa8352de1908.Text: {n}Tortured doubt lingers on the confessor's face for a moment before being superseded by his former conviction.{/n} "Even if your intentions are pure, you are too tainted... Poisoned. No, the matter is clear — you or us. Peace and coexistence are impossible."

a8ea1e6a-3b8f-485c-88a2-1c1ad458fd37.Text: {n}He shakes his head, looking crestfallen.{/n} "I almost pity you — such blind conviction that nothing matters more than power... I will prove that not everyone is as flawed as you."

2fbfcd63-6e2f-45ed-98be-79917f28523d.Text: "You have raised a living instrument that serves a purpose without question." {n}Kibellah speaks cautiously, as if not entirely sure of her judgement.{/n}

99ca7d66-8f69-4fa5-8ba4-831fd7c9a82c.Text: "The words of a tyrant inebriated with power and impunity." {n}He smiles bitterly.{/n} "Nemesite is an idea. And you have the arrogance to believe you can kill an idea made flesh. It is better this way, so keep underestimating him."

f7e31df0-6e55-47e6-9412-be31dfe7f156.Text: "My son, the protector of those whose blood you feed upon, whose hard work has paid for your content life on the upper decks of this ship."

cd448e27-2fb9-4034-89b8-9a960c483d76.Text: {n}Sauerback clenches her fists until her knuckles crunch.{/n} "You treasonous impostor! To think that I listened to your sermons and was anointed by your hand. You will choke on your words along with the teeth I am about to knock out!" {n}Adalbert dignifies her with neither a word nor a glance.{/n}

da9a2c50-f31f-4eaa-a175-f35aac687cc9.Text: "Such is his purpose: to be the hope, to break the shackles, to end the centuries of torment that have passed aboard this ship. A great sacrifice for a great cause." {n}He falls silent, looking at Kibellah expectantly.{/n} "You should be familiar with his ways, except that instead of a sower of freedom, you were raised to be an executioner's sword."

f537e6f6-e0e9-4ba0-b414-69bf38433b31.Text: {n}Kibellah takes a step forward and makes a straight, sharp sweeping gesture, as if crossing Adalbert's figure or severing an invisible thread.{/n} "Death has whispered your name, betrayer of vows. The judgement of the Undying One awaits you."

5693797d-c8a7-4800-bb4c-ce0bc78f4fe9.Text: {n}Adalbert shifts his gaze to you and lets out a mournful sigh.{/n} "I was warned about your visit, {name}. As well as its purpose."

30a1c8ff-b094-4421-bd54-a8290f8581a2.Text: "Attachment makes us weak." {n}Kibellah's whisper is barely audible, and you see her face grow more dismal still.{/n} "You made a weapon out of him, just as he made a weapon out of you."

e7be36a2-3182-4b33-9ae2-c07ac663d800.Text: "You look unwell, Marius. How long since you last slept?"

b8bd5d18-ea8d-4f4b-bced-222731282618.Text: "You deign to speak to me out of turn?"

f5fb4530-519e-45f8-8114-3f3f1fcc734e.Text: "I am unimpressed, Marius. You do not belong among the missionaries. Return to your duties."

197f742e-bd14-4a0f-bc3f-9b6d72600c05.Text: "Prove to me that your epiphany was real. Put your faith to the test."

10bd9136-e13c-426a-be04-89d16cf93990.Text: [Kill the officer] "All I see in you is dangerous madness."

535a9600-1fa4-48e5-910d-d931c10899d8.Text: "I have no time for this and no desire to deal with you. I am leaving."

ace3cbaf-f279-4168-9e0a-58862c337dce.Text: "I see you are going to persist. Fine. I will give you a chance to prove your faith."

1d746044-92f8-4048-94bb-c5597afee6e7.Text: "My decision stands. Now get out of my sight."

dcfdb41f-bde7-4174-a5b4-20a3bddd3945.Text: "You speak of your great-great-grandfather with particular enthusiasm. What makes him so important?"

6450881d-e045-41e5-a998-76df1118016f.Text: "Tell me more about the vision you had."

7aa28f92-3c6f-4b2f-aaf1-40fa93e40fd8.Text: "Sister Argenta, I entrust you with the test."

ec42dc2f-e10c-4490-937c-e788c208707e.Text: Proclaimed Medicae Officer Marius a chosen one and incited him to bloodshed.

6f96d972-7c60-46ad-a24b-70df41b088d4.Text: "Take my blessing, along with any weapon you like from the ship's reliquary. Quench its thirst with the blood of those you deem unworthy."

71a13b76-b9ab-453f-86a0-2e15bafdd193.Text: "Your courage and resolve are beyond reproach. You will make a fine officer. Trust me."

59dbf866-0e69-4ca4-ad1e-6be72d291794.Text: "I am ready to pass my verdict."

7414fe9f-8e03-459a-afa6-a6dff5327138.Text: "Medicae Officer Marius Clemence Sorne Keblau, you have convinced me of your genuine faith. I hereby give you my blessing as Rogue Trader and order you to take up missionary service."

869171a7-7ee2-456c-8f33-291f4d05a29d.Text: Reminded Medicae Officer Marius of his duty to the Imperium.

7484a485-26b0-4dcf-8405-a18984293f58.Text: "You were assigned a position on this ship. That is your place in the Imperium's design. And you seek to upset that order? I ought to have you executed for such impudence."

8cf699a4-4e46-43e2-af4a-9373d8acc06e.Text: Proposed that Medicae Officer Marius serve his faith aboard the ship.

fae6f402-28c5-4a27-9284-d5344c62c588.Text: "Marius, you can do good without having to leave the ship. You have enough work here to fill the rest of your life. Cure people and strengthen their faith: is that not enough?"

67a4b2dc-ae88-462a-85ce-f117d80c4f98.Text: {n}A young man is praying beside the reliquary. His hair is dishevelled and his sweat-stained uniform is crumpled. Dark circles have formed underneath his eyes. As you approach, he jumps up from his knees and makes the sign of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g} with a jerky motion.{/n} "Lord Captain! You are here! I believed— nay, I knew you would come!"

00aa1c79-280c-4726-bf14-16a50e42dea4.Text: "I require neither rest nor sleep! I feel energised and alive like never before. I— I'm overflowing with faith!"

7d50a5fb-1f42-49d3-b6a9-8fe1cc00ced3.Text: {n}Kibellah approaches the officer without making a sound.{/n} "Death is the faithful companion of those who sow the seeds of faith amid the stars. Though it has a thousand faces, I will show you but one... The one you fear most. The one you have seen in your nightmares."

78754e36-9928-4b8b-b3ad-889b9bda2137.Text: {n}His bloodshot eyes, slightly twitching fingers, and nervous agitation point to chronic sleep deprivation or the gruelling strain of too much work.{/n}

67ae7b2c-e8b3-4065-b843-eee14445fbda.Text: {n}Whatever happened to this officer, it has him in quite a state.{/n}

93dc90e0-75ef-42e2-9902-edf0cc5aac72.Text: {n}The officer tries to smooth his hair with one hand and straighten his collar with the other.{/n} "B-but who else if not one of the Emperor's anointed? The vision... I must bring this matter to your attention. You are the only one I can ask."

f5a5cab2-80ad-4cbc-abbc-34701c05fd9d.Text: {n}The medicae officer looks away, struggling to comprehend what he has just heard. A deep furrow appears on his brow — a rare occurrence in someone of his age.{/n} "You are right. There's a lot I could do for my home ship. But I can't just turn my back on the sign I was given and make do with a compromise. The Emperor commands that I dedicate every part of me to His faith, so that's how it must be."

77dcbcca-1307-4841-8b38-3a28f8f28224.Text: {n}Idira smiles back at you.{/n} "Indeed, why not look into this wannabe fanatic's future?" {n}She closes her eyes and rubs her temples theatrically.{/n} "Oh yes! The whispers tell me that you, Marius, will embarrass yourself on the very first planet you go to, and come crawling back to this ship burdened with debt and disburdened of breeches!"

cba726f3-c8c0-4dfb-9e38-6778826d1e21.Text: {n}Marius wrings his hands.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! You have turned my inner eye to things I've never reflected on before. I think... you're right. I am not ready to be a missionary." {n}He smiles a tired smile.{/n} "A vision brought me to you, and you have shown me the truth. Correcting the flaws in my faith is what I must turn my efforts toward."

9209ebf1-923d-4f31-a303-7e7856eaf047.Text: {n}Your words leave the officer awestruck. He freezes in place, waiting.{/n}

64a480a9-212c-41ac-a739-9bdca4992d54.Text: {n}Marius grabs onto the hem of your clothes.{/n} "I implore you! This is my calling!"

d05671d8-719f-4010-965f-332be4c566d2.Text: "He had the honour of helping an ancestor of yours capture this relic." {n}Marius points piously toward the reliquary.{/n} "In that gruelling fight, he not only treated the wounded soldiers but shed blood for the cause himself."

b74af23d-4309-48e5-8677-b894e4fd2c32.Text: {n}The officer raises his eyes to the ceiling and recollects with rapt abandon:{/n} "First I noticed a faint light out of the corner of my eye, but thought it was a surgical {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} someone had turned on. The light grew brighter, and when I turned toward it, it shone right through me! I saw my muscles, organs, and bones under my skin. I was bared, body and soul, as if I was standing by the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Throne{/g} itself."

4dcb604b-0bb5-4477-ba99-05fe373e0a94.Text: {n}An inner fire lights up Argenta's face.{/n} "You believe you have been chosen for missionary work? Do you know what hardships the bringers of His word must endure? Words alone will not make the faithless fall to their knees. Countless righteous men and women have died at the hands of those they were trying to save! Other foes lurk on remote worlds as well. Disease. Hunger. Destitution. The smallest flaw in your faith will be enough for them to break you and turn you away from the Throne. Do you think you have what it takes to overcome these challenges?"

a6fa1567-3b06-4e1f-999d-e2a227f6faba.Text: "Easy, paragon of faith. I was just testing how frayed your nerves are."

47b91e82-8996-4dbc-b077-8f491418c212.Text: {n}Marius's eyes glaze over, and his lips start moving in silent prayer.{/n}

f5ae9b73-4f69-4615-b264-de0db6810e76.Text: {n}The young man makes no effort to shield himself from your strike, accepting death with an expression of genuine surprise on his face.{/n}

2c963c83-3014-47a9-82c1-6171182349a2.Text: {n}Marius makes an effort to stifle the protest within him before it can burst into words.{/n} "Thank you for the honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I will serve you diligently."

f6e4c54e-7d6c-4719-9b04-78a257a6dcbd.Text: {n}Tears glisten in Marius's eyes as he stands to attention and makes the sign of the Aquila again.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! It has been a great honour to serve you. Faith takes time to cultivate on faraway worlds, but one day you or your descendants will hear of my deeds."

f72570b9-fcb2-4623-a022-ae10cae418b3.Text: {n}Marius sputters in astonishment,{/n} "Chosen one? I— you— anything you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I must tell my family at once!"

cf54854a-cc06-4551-aa29-f7229e6d54eb.Text: {n}The young man takes an almost ludicrously deep breath and says solemnly,{/n} "I am Marius Clemence Sorne Keblau, medicae officer. I have had a vision. My great-great-grandfather appeared before me and bid me seek your blessing to become a missionary! Please grant me your gracious leave to embark on my journey." {n}He freezes and stares at you without blinking.{/n}

86809f78-77e3-4238-bc55-2ccd99f61432.Text: {n}Your stern tone frightens Marius.{/n} "I am a loyal son of the Imperium and have, until now, never entertained the idea of abandoning my duties on this ship. But what if mine is a different calling? How could I ignore a message from Him?"

12817dc1-5359-42bc-b1e8-6dfc6eecae46.Text: "An ancestor of mine stepped out of that most pure light." {n}Marius pauses, his voice faltering.{/n} "And he said, 'My child! Your destiny is to bring faith to distant worlds. Seek the Rogue Trader's blessing and set out on your journey.' The words didn't seem to be coming from his mouth but from every direction at once, and other strong and pure voices echoed them, and, and—" {n}For a moment Marius looks like he's about to faint, but he finishes his speech in a tone that is almost serene.{/n} "It was a miracle."

fadc3121-f774-4e5a-b627-7497aeba6be1.Text: {n}Marius is silent for a long time, then smiles timidly.{/n} "If it were someone else, I would try to insist... But if you really believe that I will... Throne, who am I to doubt the words of a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}conqueror of the void{/d} like you? Thank you for your guidance, Lord Captain. I will not fail you."

17654eaf-4c74-4130-8e87-9bde019910a2.Text: "Right you are, Aett-Vater! Everyone on Fenris knows: they who seek a great destiny must first face a great trial! Many of our heroes covered themselves in glory by accepting harsh challenges and proving their valour."

7e4e856d-e8d3-4c09-a2c3-7bf8692c8458.Text: "His colours burn brightly and feverishly, his zealous gold ready to consume all other hues. A beautiful sight, if somewhat frightening."

1a4e0be1-2dd9-466c-a129-d6bba1026c64.Text: "The ray of his soul is so thin and pure, so fragile... A rare glow in the guts of an iron ship."

075c7c56-f882-45d5-9385-ba1e924fc0e4.Text: "Easily remediable." {n}Marazhai continues critically examining his sharp claws.{/n}

177c9583-fa8c-41f9-8800-c712c87d90aa.Text: {n}It is hard to tell if Marius is more intimidated by the Sister of Battle or the hardships she speaks of. However, he juts out his chin and replies in a firm voice,{/n} "I will drink my cup of sorrows, no matter how bitter it may be, and will praise the Emperor for every trial."

70ff4d93-1ab8-407f-804d-b978c54bfef1.Text: {n}Argenta nods in satisfaction.{/n} "Spoken like a righteous man!"

1628038e-9d19-441a-aa1b-f093b0ae2746.Text: {n}One swift movement, and a cold needle flashes by Marius's neck. His eyes roll up and his body convulses. Nothing happens for several long seconds, until he finally forces out,{/n} "O Emperor! What an abomination, what unbearable, Throne-offending blasphemy!" {n}He clenches his teeth and mutters stubbornly on through the froth forming on his lips.{/n} "And I shall fear no corruption, and I shall face my death as His faithful servant!"

6148d866-f654-41fe-9bfa-813985fa4d6f.Text: {n}With another swift movement, Kibellah administers an antidote to the officer.{/n} "This one has gained knowledge of one of death's manifestations. Another of his weaknesses has died off, making room for service."

b6b39d95-da50-48ff-aacf-c52198bdbfc1.Text: {n}Marius clenches his fists, gnashes his teeth, and says,{/n} "That will never be! The cursed spirits are lying to you! They seek to lead me astray, as they do any fervent believer. Drown out their voices with prayer and don't let them make you an instrument of their evil!"

f4e72af8-1215-4586-8796-b7d91fd91ce2.Text: "What fantastic advice you gave me, Solomorne. I should not have listened to you."

2478e586-d252-4edd-a819-e76846657734.Text: [Lean toward Solomorne and whisper] "You shouldn't have taken all the blame like that."

e740a4a0-365a-455f-9f96-519d1407d5ec.Text: "A heretic had seized power on Thassera. I had him executed."

4d49ba35-a211-41e3-b8b6-b061652bbff0.Text: "A heretic had seized power on Thassera. I had him executed and assigned a representative in his place."

0deba675-5b40-4573-88eb-420f77eefd60.Text: "I discovered a warp-active mineral on Thassera and ordered it be studied. If this resource proves sufficiently useful to the Imperium, you must include it in the tithe."

32860745-10dc-4776-9987-b850ccd04015.Text: "I discovered a material on Thassera known as thassertium, a potent psy-focus. I had it destroyed in the interests of the Imperium's security."

eced0b79-94df-41a5-9fed-7fe7d28ea6c9.Text: "I discovered a unique material, a natural psy-focus called thassertium. I ordered it be included in Thassera's planetary tithe."

c6c9aed3-f42a-4282-aa9c-e100042c12c0.Text: "What got into you back then, by the way? You were so aloof."

27d77ff4-c7ee-4984-8892-576c1debb512.Text: "That is unacceptable. Find yourselves another Arbitrator to deal with your problems."

a0f6ce0f-9ded-4668-b299-978a1a7e0c5e.Text: "I see. Good luck on your assignment, Solomorne."

12bab419-5643-47d5-b240-aaed4e7d9971.Text: "One way or the other, we can consider the matter of Thassera closed. Am I correct?"

07a0ff45-c623-449a-82b3-5be0c191272b.Text: "What gives you the right to evaluate Solomorne?"

8b2bf7d7-62b1-432e-b678-1c2189d3e856.Text: "Solomorne did nothing that could be considered a violation of the Lex Imperialis!"

495e1ec4-28b5-457b-a4ad-df201466b8a3.Text: "Someone has finally caught you by the scruff of the neck, eh, lawman? Let's see how this plays out."

6cf72144-4397-43f4-b69c-82d1b8aadf6e.Text: "That is the Administratum's responsibility — handle it yourselves."

9e7ce5af-c217-485b-b50e-494212f331f9.Text: "One of the Rogue Trader's many duties is to mete out justice. I agree."

fddae62b-b36e-4312-8424-a485bc3d11f6.Text: "I hope we can get this over with quickly. As important as these cases may be, my personal business is even more so."

4d1b41d7-1447-448a-90e8-73451b12f238.Text: "You still shouldn't have said anything. I can take care of myself."

e7dd3fcb-7ad8-4b0f-a9a7-17ccae335685.Text: "My Seneschal will give you an account of it. Reporting to anyone in person would be beneath my station."

68134f76-2eb3-42e4-91c1-d00c394a0f07.Text: "Are you not being a little harsh on yourself, Solomorne?"

e2763d0e-e5bb-4a9c-823b-a5e3f90aefdc.Text: "If you think the Thasserian mineral is so important to the Imperium, make it part of the tithe. What is the problem?"

037836ca-40be-468e-acaa-f00103cfaec6.Text: "The tithe deliveries from Thassera will be restored to their former capacity. This is all you need to know."

e568b7e6-5284-4a19-afde-df58514f1606.Text: "The audience is with the Master of Seals, not the prefect. It would appear you... misspoke?"

45cca64d-6865-48e2-89a9-df98eda230da.Text: "How dare you reprimand me for a wicked man's death! It would have been the duty of any servant of the Emperor to cleanse the heretic with fire and plasteel — or are you going to brashly and blasphemously claim otherwise?"

228dffb8-3a4c-43b1-8a1b-02004d9195f1.Text: "Thassera's problems have been dealt with. If you need the particulars, go and see for yourself."

c3cc4802-15f2-4d16-a948-780e135730bc.Text: "How did you obtain such detailed information about the events on Thassera?"

44da33d8-a55b-42d0-bb9b-0f0678b21b65.Text: "An exceedingly hazardous warp-active mineral was discovered on Thassera. For the good of the Imperium, I ordered it be destroyed. I am giving you time to evacuate Administratum property, after which, the planet will be condemned to Exterminatus."

6ff6cba6-37ed-4a7d-a66b-8506da8471d8.Text: "I took care of a problematic world of yours, and you are twisting the facts regarding my efforts!"

b38c85f8-0c32-4c80-a33e-b1ea61d689b9.Text: "Apology accepted. Let's not dwell on it."

8aafb29f-bdf0-49ca-9070-407af715adfb.Text: {n}The shrivelled, insect-like old woman greets you with a keen look.{/n} "Welcome back to the temple of law and order, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I have already been informed that you are here about Thassera." {n}Prefect Vultur nods to herself and snaps her brittle fingers, prompting a servo-skull to flit closer, the creaking of its quill filling the air.{/n} "Begin entry 51/4-Alpha. In the matter of the world Thassera and its obligation to pay the {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}Imperial Tithe{/g}, this audience with the prefect of the Adeptus Administratum is now in session. Now then, what were your findings, {name} von Valancius?"

eac980b2-5027-41f2-aad8-1cc3d8fb3af1.Text: {n}Solomorne turns to the prefect.{/n} "The Rogue Trader's testimony is the truth. It should be noted that I was the one who proposed the complete destruction of the thassertium."

cddb8bae-f90f-4ab3-992f-8e0925d7e466.Text: {n}Solomorne whispers back,{/n} "I told her the truth. I was there, and I let it happen." {n}After a pause, he adds, even more quietly,{/n} "Besides, I owe you for acting like an oaf at the celebration."

96e61203-4d26-4948-a29d-1f33fda10717.Text: "There is one other thing, Rogue Trader: by the order of Marshal Strachs, Proctor Anthar has been assigned a short-term mission. He is to take his leave of your retinue at dawn. As this is a matter of extreme urgency, the Adeptus Arbites would appreciate your understanding."

ed35ae1e-8bb9-40cc-9d56-6cf85abbc80e.Text: "Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius effected the {d|Encyclopedia:FW_DecisionLizzyNotGovernor}execution of the governor of Thassera{/d} appointed by the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Adeptus Administratum{/g}. Preliminary damage assessment and restoration forecast of the world's key structures: Class A, 'severe.' Noted and recorded."

1775b61e-b83d-46d4-bacb-531a6480a632.Text: "Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius effected the execution of the governor of Thassera appointed by the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Adeptus Administratum{/g} and entrusted the governance of the planet to an {d|Encyclopedia:FW_LizzyGovernor}individual who possesses no expertise{/d} necessary for such a monumental responsibility. Preliminary damage assessment and restoration forecast of the world's key structures: Class A, 'severe.' Noted and recorded."

57b9742b-d4b3-4a93-850e-16f59f243c4f.Text: "Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, upon learning about the existence of deposits of a natural psy-focus located on the world Thassera, {d|Encyclopedia:FW_TitheStopDecision}destroyed said material{/d} in its entirety. Consequently, the Imperium was deprived of a highly prized resource. Noted and recorded."

92b2d1f5-0201-4cff-a8b2-42ce5a40f987.Text: "Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius {d|Encyclopedia:FW_TitheSameDecision}authorised{/d} the study of a presumably warp-corrupted material located on the world Thassera. Due to the danger to the planet resulting from this decision, tithe shipments from Thassera can no longer be considered safe and are to be halted until further notice. Noted and recorded."

6ae6aae6-7a6f-42f3-8862-543cc9a162ee.Text: "To which part of the assessment would you impute bias? Everything in it is based solely on facts, and Proctor Anthar himself presented the conclusion. Regardless, the final judgement will be passed by Marshal Strachs."

539aa7bc-6cdb-4c5f-af34-5a4cc548dc63.Text: "Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius {d|Encyclopedia:FW_TitheMaxDecision}sanctioned{/d} the transportation of a presumably warp-corrupted material to the Imperium's storages. By including said material in the volume of the Imperial Tithe, {name} von Valancius changed the planet's {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGradeGlossary}tithe grade{/g} from Solutio Extremis to Decuma Tertius without filling out the necessary documentation, thereby risking potential major upsets in Administratum processes. Noted and recorded."

233a2125-4c7c-4085-a2df-dc96f3a77dad.Text: {n}The prefect chews on her lip in thought.{/n} "I will be frank with you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}: the conclusions that were drawn regarding the Thassera inspection were far from satisfactory. Minor disturbances such as a mass execution of mutants or the rabble's plot disguised as a celebration are not nearly as dangerous as the — if you will permit my choice of words — coup that resulted from your intervention. I understand that consequences are something that those endowed with power are wont to leave to their servants to deal with... and therefore, something they find acceptable to ignore." {n}Inscribia's ocular lenses flash as she looks up from her scrolls.{/n} "However, I hope my words may help you to revise your approach to executing the Imperium's will in the Koronus Expanse in future." {n}With a tap of her nail, she dismisses the servo-skull.{/n}

ea7be15f-1f38-4c70-bf44-3db4d15f26e4.Text: "Closed and recorded, yes." {n}The old woman smacks her lips in satisfaction.{/n} "However, that was just the first item on the agenda. Now, on to the next matter."

d7ffb919-71ab-47b7-b02d-1d37af8f1930.Text: {n}The prefect beckons over another servo-skull, which obediently takes its place at her side.{/n} "Begin entry 52/1-Sigma. Competency assessment of Proctor Solomorne Anthar based on his performance during the mission on the world Thassera."

16cfe430-6dec-4b57-9576-40a32b52dca3.Text: {n}You hear a painful metallic creak as Solomorne's augmented hand clenches into a fist.{/n} "Competency... assessment? Very well, Prefect. I am listening."

10ee181f-779a-49f8-a213-604cc7c1ae12.Text: "So as to avoid misunderstanding, allow me to clarify that I am not making any judgement, but rather gathering information at Marshal Strachs's request." {n}The prefect turns to Solomorne.{/n} "Proctor Anthar, you will be evaluating your own conduct in this instance; for my part, I will merely state a few key points. Let us begin: how would you describe your performance, taking into account the following facts..." {n}Vultur produces a parchment scroll.{/n}

2d2e4cde-7e54-4734-9166-34d1a72fe338.Text: "Noted and recorded." {n}The prefect's immaculately polished ocular lenses bore into you once more.{/n} "Now that the Thassera inspection report has been properly entered into the record, allow me, on behalf of the Adeptus Administratum, to officially extend our gratitude to you for the support you provided to us. May the von Valancius name be forever praised, and may the Emperor protect your dynasty for many generations to come. That said, I must now request your assistance in a different capacity: a number of highly important court cases have accumulated at the Palace of Justice — the kind that require formal resolutions by the Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself}."

3e72ca3d-c335-444b-bf74-17b732688691.Text: "Countless cases do indeed pass through the Administratum, but a very minute number of them are beyond our power to process. As stipulated by our centuries-long covenant with your dynasty, any disputes that are likely to have truly grave consequences regardless of the final decision made are to be reviewed without exception by the Rogue Trader. Only your sacred authority can force the parties to accept the verdict and not rise up in response. We have already delayed the proceedings for as long as we could, but now, we are obligated to pass these cases over to you."

e6ac4147-22a1-44c1-8cf7-410b67c82054.Text: "I have relegated my current tasks in advance, and thus am ready to escort you to the Palace of Justice immediately. Please, follow me."

8c35e541-54e0-497a-b6cc-4c706e4a1499.Text: "The people around us were getting on my nerves. I'm not used to putting my affections on display for all the world to see, especially in front of people I collect tithes from, or might end up bringing to justice. In that moment, being human, and not a living statue, was like going into battle without armour." {n}He takes a deep breath.{/n} "Everything inside me twisted into a knot, screaming that I was doing it all wrong."

f0207dfd-fada-486d-ac6a-80bd0bb6484f.Text: "Of course, {name}." {n}Solomorne smiles with only his eyes.{/n}

1c3a572f-d091-4b22-b32e-c2f7262ffd19.Text: "I know you can." {n}He nods calmly.{/n} "But that doesn't mean I shouldn't worry about you."

fce6bd45-bbd0-4f7d-b140-7fcd3ff80881.Text: "Sadly, that is not an option. The Marshal believes that out of the entire Arbitrator force, only Proctor Anthar possesses the training required to successfully complete this mission. I cannot imagine that the brief absence of one individual — whose services, may I remind you, were temporarily lent to you by the Adeptus Arbites — will be in any way damaging to the dynasty's affairs."

aa411783-b5ba-4db6-9220-ac04df191e5c.Text: "Proctor Anthar is to lead an Arbitrator squad tasked with neutralising some dangerous criminals who are threatening the Administratum's interests. A rather mundane assignment, as you may have gathered."

31725832-fc92-4254-9e7e-17528445c8a0.Text: "I must follow the Marshal's orders, Rogue Trader. I will return to your ship as soon as my duty to the Adeptus Arbites permits."

ab67b080-5c92-4090-9afd-560db5ebd0c9.Text: {n}The prefect's ocular lenses flash as she replies in an offended tone,{/n} "I, His lowly and unworthy servant, have no right to twist any facts. My duty is to assess consequences and do everything I can to make sure the Imperium receives what it is owed. That is the purpose of my existence." {n}Suddenly the old woman's voice becomes less stern and almost didactic.{/n} "Speaking from my wealth of experience, if I do say so myself, taking care of the Imperium's prosperity is a heavy burden, albeit an honourable one. The fact that even a Rogue Trader can run into difficulties while doing it only further confirms my many years of observations."

1a4fa69e-f0e2-409a-9f8e-b68429a79b91.Text: "I am afraid I cannot accept another person's report." {n}Her shrivelled fingers nimbly extract a piece of parchment from her stack of papers. It is covered in minuscule writing.{/n} "According to Koronus Expanse Statute 19/A-11, any decision pertaining to matters of the tithe shall solely be answered for by the person that directly made said decision. A report made by any other person shall be deemed legally null and void." {n}The prefect puts the document back in its place.{/n} "As you can see, there is a sacred stipulation that you submit your report in person and that I accept it from no one else."

342cddb0-47b5-4847-bb39-e9a00e29a680.Text: "I see." {n}The old woman looks at you intently over her ocular lenses.{/n} "This is regrettable news. Even if your action was forced by circumstance, the loss of the governor means the loss of the very stability that any servant of the Administratum is immutably obligated to uphold and protect. Well, let us get to the record then..." {n}The prefect turns to the servo-skull.{/n}

581961f2-32c2-458d-9208-6add65f89ca9.Text: {n}The prefect grimaces.{/n} "I can quite confidently deem that outcome to be adverse to the interests of the Imperium. Alas, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I am duty-bound to deliver an exact and impartial assessment of the events."

94e84b39-ba38-4333-9870-3eeb47070349.Text: "You took part in the execution of an Administratum appointee without its appropriate permission. You also allowed yourself to be captured, thus endangering your mission and imperilling the valuable equipment issued to you by the Adeptus Arbites. What is more, you sanctioned a tithe-related decision that carries adverse consequences for the Imperium." {n}The old woman pauses.{/n} "That is all. Proceed to your self-evaluation."

c3e3c59c-ad90-42de-bfd8-cb88c77886ef.Text: {n}Solomorne's heavy gaze is fixed upon the prefect as he slowly forces the first word out of his jaws, as if they have turned to stone.{/n} "I... took every effort and was acting solely in the name of the Lex Imperialis; however, the outcome of the mission speaks for itself. My verdict is thus that my performance in the Thassera case was inadequate."

86aa6b7f-b489-4267-a5a5-8e72e228604d.Text: "Exactly as harsh as my duty demands that I be. An Arbitrator has no right to mistakes or weaknesses. Our mission is much too important." {n}The Proctor's voice sounds firm but detached, as if his mind is wandering far away.{/n}

fb3c5cc6-227c-40d3-8a3e-90dec0250b80.Text: "Of course you have the power to change your decision at the snap of your fingers, but its implementation will fall to thousands upon thousands of Administratum functionaries. They will have to first record the previous status of the tithe, and then begin an equally lengthy process of re-registering the payment. As servants of law and order, we cannot simply skip the cumbersome parts: procedure must be followed meticulously, lest we become mired in anarchy."

c29db840-1677-44e5-84d7-c1eaab69a5f1.Text: "It is a temple of the law erected by your ancestors. Some cases could only be settled by heads of the dynasty, but since their time was occupied by other important duties, a facility was built for storing especially complex cases. At a certain point, servants of the Administratum were permitted to use the Palace of Justice for hearing disputes; then, in Lady Theodora's time, the Arbites became part of the legal procedure as well."

1aeef20f-77b8-4ad8-bd1b-ca51a375e090.Text: {n}Solomorne's voice is firm, almost to the point of rudeness.{/n} "I request that the following note be added to the record: the Rogue Trader's actions are not to be scrutinised. They were carried out in my presence and thus had the approval of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g}." {n}Solomorne thrusts his chest out imposingly, as if trying to deflect an enemy blow directed at you.{/n}

fa76d31a-70dc-4986-840c-09badd73a90e.Text: "The defendants will speak first, whereupon you can ask me clarifying questions on the case, and then—" {n}The old woman gives you a meaningful look over her ocular lenses.{/n} "—a death sentence must be passed. You are, of course, free to judge otherwise, but an execution is preferable, since in every case that will come before you, an outcome without highly unpleasant consequences is unlikely. Executions reduce the number of malcontents and motivate prospective defendants to solve their problems before they come under the purview of the Rogue Trader's court."

17203e01-83d3-4719-b5eb-e140dc9e56f7.Text: "This order of things was established by previous Rogue Traders, not the Administratum. I assure you that your participation in the court of law is not only an homage to an ancient tradition but also an urgent necessity."

4d91d9fe-c05a-4945-8155-c4e5217a38b8.Text: "Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius {d|Encyclopedia:FW_TitheDestroyedDecision}ordered the destruction of the world Thassera{/d}. Through this decision, the Imperium is deprived of a portion of the tithe total expected from the Koronus Expanse and, more specifically, of a valuable resource in the form of naturally occurring psy-focus deposits. Noted and recorded."

a928e9b8-0a24-46c1-b2c5-6db9cd576f30.Text: {n}The old woman freezes in place, her eyes suddenly bulging behind her ocular lenses. The only sound amid the heavy silence is an annoying fly circling over your head.{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:APA_KnowPrefectDecision}That... is another matter{/d}, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. In my current capacity, I am not directly involved with registry archives. I urge you to answer the aforementioned question."

e013f680-c1fd-4da8-99a6-e8eeb32225c8.Text: {n}The old woman shudders.{/n} "No! Of course not! If, as a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Ministorum}former servant of the Ecclesiarchy{/d}, you saw heresy in the governor... I am only saying that your righteous decision is going to affect the Thassera tithe. That is a fact, and I am merely stating it."

1fcc84c1-c256-4674-bc58-fac13d957862.Text: {n}Glancing at Solomorne with indifference, the prefect says in a creaking voice,{/n} "The Proctor's statement has been added to the record. End entry."

59df6ae0-d233-467e-a322-ddef4762b0dd.Text: "Duty dictates that Adeptus Administratum officials always be adequately informed — otherwise, our service to the Imperium's order would be of rather questionable use. Unfortunately, it is for this same reason that I cannot disclose my sources to you."

7c6ce6c8-1da5-4722-ae75-90b24d38e2c5.Text: {n}The prefect clears her throat in baldly obnoxious fashion.{/n} "Rogue Trader, are you and the Proctor quite done discussing your undoubtedly pressing concerns? If you are, let us return to the matter of court proceedings."

827b0227-dc68-478c-8151-6c3e4360b7f3.Text: "You are going on a mission without Glaito? That sounds risky."

ce365b21-eb0a-4b03-9ee7-8d6a82252671.Text: "I look forward to our next meeting."

8a03eda0-eee2-42e5-8717-bcfdc9ed4ac1.Text: "Your dog will be well taken care of, Solomorne."

bdfb7745-97a0-4963-994f-26d3d643d258.Text: "That does not sound worthy of my attention, but it is noted regardless."

0df02cf0-5203-4562-a6cb-a18d62e09759.Text: {n}Right as you walk out the door, Solomorne moves closer to you and says in a low voice,{/n} "If that concludes our business at the Palace of Justice, I would like to propose something, if I may."

41d370d6-d285-47d1-a37d-25a85ebfa10d.Text: {n}Solomorne moves closer to you and lowers his voice.{/n} "If I am to leave your ship at dawn, that means we still have a whole night ahead of us. Perhaps you would like to spend it in my company?"

a1d39984-7070-4df3-a8aa-752e31b0279a.Text: "It's been a long day, but I know a sure way to relieve tension. One good night together — what do you say?"

6ad8e5a4-f201-41f4-83a6-63903b3f33c9.Text: {n}Solomorne responds without a shred of emotion:{/n} "As you wish."

6ed2395c-71b9-4eb5-a5e1-ba0b091df392.Text: {n}His eyes light up.{/n} "There is another thing that might interest you after all."

b9c7e728-13b4-487f-898b-769e367e402a.Text: "Thank you." {n}His expression of gratitude is curt yet sincere.{/n} "I also have a suggestion to make."

10b33432-359c-48fa-9f85-30b2ebd060f9.Text: "A minute of your time, Rogue Trader. I wanted to inform you that Glaito will be staying aboard your ship while I am away on my mission for the Administratum."

95959d2f-1db7-478f-a689-c9c3ea87be92.Text: "His augmetics have taken quite a hit after everything that happened on Thassera, so I am putting him into the care of your Tech-Priests."

8b074b8b-0fba-4e10-a4e1-f3beb494d824.Text: "It would be riskier still to go with a malfunctioning cyber-mastiff. Since I am pressed for time, I will simply have to adapt to the circumstances."

61f1cd43-73b2-4955-9087-3fc260777381.Text: "Thank you for hearing me out. That is all I meant to say."

6e04e201-21ab-4735-b24b-338aaee33c18.Text: "Before we discuss your affairs, answer one question: did you order Solomorne to lie to me and insinuate himself into my confidence?"

67f8056a-e1d1-4ef3-a632-5d7b156be27c.Text: "Judging by your faces, the matter must be grave indeed."

3d9344b0-b6fc-4885-808a-fdb21375fac9.Text: "It is so amusing to see you two at each other's throats. Would you entertain me by continuing your squabble a little longer?"

f1d78183-b0f5-457d-bdd9-f62e1c5bffd5.Text: "Who are the Fangs of the Expanse?"

675e2604-92d1-4284-8f4a-37515cf2e641.Text: "What danger are you referring to, Marshal?"

aa2a97f6-5955-4124-9cf7-7f18d8f20c6d.Text: [Nod toward the strangers in the room] "Who are these people? They do not look like Administratum clerks."

0ae5ecc5-ed31-4400-b2be-a4e69b94ef70.Text: "Why can't you export the tithe yourselves?"

07f95cb2-745d-45cb-8cf8-88dd80b8ac80.Text: "I must remind you, to my embarrassment, that Dargonus was gutted by xenos not long ago."

57b353ba-6bce-44e9-9426-1b5576ce4e56.Text: "Theodora had a whole secret planet in her possession, and yet no one cared to inform me?"

d896f7ec-74be-404a-b022-033af2dd46d6.Text: "Are you telling me that the tithe from the entire Koronus Expanse is being hoarded on Leethus? Just how much are we talking about, exactly?"

0b102ed8-2bd7-409b-8ab1-d8ca6a65a5b5.Text: "What can you tell me about Leethus? I do not recall seeing it on any star charts."

97a310ef-c719-4cf3-b0a0-b712ca60fd0d.Text: "This must be resolved without delay. I will go there at once."

be4ade5d-039d-4925-8a6f-ba26baec9288.Text: "I might consider making this journey when I have nothing more pressing to do."

0d0fa35d-b07e-4ab9-9869-bea1bf8e241d.Text: "Organising the transportation of so many valuables is a serious undertaking. It requires an entire cargo fleet with its own dedicated navigation."

4635cf4f-91ad-43d1-a9ce-d76b058b934d.Text: "Why me specifically? If this is so important, you should ask the Inquisition."

9a71e8d2-f642-423a-b926-da6cea33dded.Text: "It was the prefect who put you up to this, wasn't it?"

a91acd35-1a59-4a48-92da-7f0a4bd1e034.Text: "‘Increased activity'... In other words, someone is very interested in locating a world brimming with tithe — and is close to succeeding?"

7470bbad-ed71-44c5-9c9b-6a83da94d8b2.Text: {n}Marshal Strachs regards the prefect with an implacable expression.{/n} "...out of the question. I will only speak about resolving this situation with the Rogue Trader directly. No intermediaries."

0bff6d72-ec35-4290-b071-2d323fbdbea6.Text: {n}As she speaks, Prefect Vultur's augmented hands constantly fidget with a tattered piece of paper that may have once been a report:{/n} "But for how much longer might we have to wait for the Rogue Trader? Ten turns? Thirty? Thrice that? Time is an invaluable commodity, and we currently have none, esteemed Marshal. Not to mention that Decree RP/84-289 explicitly states—" {n}She stops abruptly when she sees you.{/n}

ee61daca-4805-4f9a-95a5-70dc22b71515.Text: {n}The Marshal raises his chin.{/n} "Rogue Trader. The Adeptus Arbites request your immediate cooperation. The {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}sacred tithe{/g} collected from the Koronus Expanse is in danger, and you are the only one who can negate this threat."

a7b7ead6-126d-403a-a811-39464c6bd2c6.Text: "Extraordinarily so, and there is no guarantee that we are not already too late." {n}The prefect's glare bores into Strachs's grim figure.{/n}

7f90aaa3-2a9f-4e4f-93ea-f76e04ae5f12.Text: {n}The Marshal's face is impenetrable.{/n} "The disagreement between the prefect and myself was put to rest the moment you arrived. Now, to the issue at hand."

9ddbf21d-5d51-41ef-b56f-a8ab39068699.Text: {n}The raspy voice of the prefect cuts across the Marshal's speech:{/n} "If I may provide certain details: as per regulations, prior to being sent to this temporary depot, all tithe shipments were first brought to Dargonus. These deliveries were made using barges crewed by servitors, with the only people on board with the privilege of autonomous behaviour being key officers and an Arbitrator escort. In other words, the location of both the system and the planet was strictly classified. A special pact was made with the {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobiliteGlossary}Navigator House{/g}... Even I was not entrusted with the coordinates..."

20893101-eb8f-43e7-bd44-9b69c60ac882.Text: {n}The Marshal looks straight at you.{/n} "Given the scarcity of our resources, absolute secrecy is Leethus's main line of defence. However, we are detecting... increased activity near the storage world's location. I do not want to do this, but I am, quite plainly, forced to ask for your help: go to Leethus and organise the extraction of the Imperial Tithe to Dargonus for further safekeeping."

76a00644-3a07-4101-aae8-ed40320802bc.Text: "Enough with your insinuations. I make my own decisions!" {n}With his chin proudly set, the Marshal strives to avoid looking at the prefect.{/n}

741e519f-4c44-4b6e-8de3-b982d8f38b2c.Text: "All of the Expanse is ablaze, Rogue Trader. This state of disorder jeopardises a critical strategic location: the planet Leethus, a clandestine world provided by Theodora von Valancius for the purpose of storing the tithe collected from the worlds of the Koronus Expanse." {n}Strachs's cheek twitches.{/n} "At present, the planet is overflowing with the sacred tribute, amassed over the course of decades. After we lost contact with every single ship sent through the {g|Encyclopedia:Maw}Maw{/g} in recent years, the decision was made to cease all attempts to transport the tithe out of the Expanse until the route is once more secure. It was for just such periods of the Maw's impassability that the storage world of Leethus was devised."

21318c74-46a9-4768-b76c-c842c283d591.Text: {n}The prefect looks at them and snaps her fingers. The fighters immediately make the sign of the Aquila.{/n} "These are my bodyguards, members of the Fangs of the Expanse. They are here to demonstrate my willingness to offer the Adeptus Arbites whatever cooperation I can."

feafb751-67b4-4230-a1d4-82ededf3e190.Text: "That is an acceptable option — one with which we are prepared to proceed. The Adeptus Administratum has requisitioned mercenary troops of the highest calibre. Under extreme circumstances, the Lex Imperialis permits—"

a3368686-7645-446f-aa4a-ba6f3c03c313.Text: "Out of the question." {n}There is steely ringing in Strachs's voice.{/n} "In the Koronus Expanse, there exists a strict separation of authority between the Adeptus Arbites and the Administratum, as certified by the von Valancius dynasty and formalised in the Lex Dargonus. Transporting the tithe to and from Leethus and maintaining its security is the duty of the Adeptus Arbites. Aside from the head of the dynasty, only we have the right to set foot on Leethus or to know its coordinates. Such is the word of the law."

9aab856b-5b9c-46bd-8d1e-5d4c619a9c0a.Text: "And I hope that you have since drawn some conclusions about the importance of guarding your key worlds. The entire Expanse is on fire. Your capital remains the safest place in Koronus." {n}The prefect attempts to speak, but the Marshal presses on, enunciating each word:{/n} "And this is not open to discussion."

5ae2efc4-8e78-49f8-a74e-e93b8366b970.Text: {n}The Marshal sighs in anguish.{/n} "Enough to instantly turn anyone who captured it into a force more intimidating than the {g|Encyclopedia:KasballicaMissionGlossary}Kasballica{/g} Shadow Barons. A tempting prize, as you can see."

6b38ccd7-c828-4e01-a605-e57a4623e99e.Text: "A fringe world of no value to the Imperium. By order of Lady Theodora, it was stricken from all astrogational data." {n}The Marshal grimly works his jaw as he looks away.{/n} "Its security was considered beyond doubt. Until now."

d5d9212d-3e14-4667-aef2-edadaf290310.Text: {n}The Marshal nods.{/n} "I will have the coordinates and passwords transferred to you. They are for your eyes only. Once you have arrived at the location, you are to oversee the tithe's transportation to Dargonus. We will meet the barges here and then redirect them to secure vaults."

f9803363-2c13-4316-b751-2688da3e7f61.Text: "I must ask that you hurry, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... before all is lost." {n}The prefect bows.{/n}

8a203699-ead8-44f9-978d-ac196ac31e33.Text: {n}The Marshal draws a sharp breath.{/n} "Impossible. That would mean that someone commanding vast resources and influence knows of its existence. We have no evidence that could support this conjecture. Considering the current state of the Koronus Expanse, with pirates and xenos roaming where they please, it is far more likely that the storage world will be discovered by accident."

b31e4856-1de0-45ec-afc8-1a96ae8d9e97.Text: "I..." {n}The Marshal freezes with his mouth open, then closes it with a snap and says quietly, with surprising sincerity,{/n} "My duty demanded it. I understand you have the right to be angry with me, but... we must not let the interests of the Imperium suffer as a result of your antipathy. I beg you."

04926a26-0a3b-4eba-b4c2-58d0baaaa8a8.Text: {n}The prefect clasps her hands.{/n} "Lady Theodora was fond of secrets... and good at keeping them. You inherited those secrets when you ascended her throne... but there are so many of them that apprising you of them all would be an impossible task, as is determining the scope of your knowledge."

25124c95-6a09-4101-b56c-20d691aa0637.Text: {n}The Marshal gives a taut nod, a look of wary relief on his face.{/n}

cebc7809-9931-43a2-9f69-eef56d86ce0c.Text: {n}The hastiness of the Marshal's rejection of your theory is the best proof that he himself considers a deliberate search to be a plausible explanation. But it seems he is unwilling to admit it, even to himself.{/n}

385ed4fe-faa5-4fbb-8e10-44109512c106.Text: "If there is a possibility of protecting the tithe until it can be shipped to the Imperium, I would prefer to do just that."

99db7737-302b-4268-be37-4b538ac1c540.Text: "Mercenaries." {n}The Marshal spits the word out in disgust.{/n}

6b1d6df8-3280-437d-bf09-6bcdbaea52fc.Text: {n}Vultur sighs.{/n} "Gregoras, you know we need every fighter we can get these days. You have precious few people at your disposal, and every year, fewer still remain. The Adeptus Administratum regulations do not prohibit the employment of hired force." {n}She meets the Marshal's fierce gaze with calm composure.{/n}

85111a8c-d951-4c06-9f3f-2a83f82facf3.Text: "You clearly {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}have an eye{/d} for practical issues. Lady Theodora assured me that Leethus had some kind of unique system for barge automation. We have no choice but to put her words to the test."

af010d2a-fee9-4cb4-a53a-87d1dc390913.Text: "To be honest, this is the first time I am hearing of this planet as well. Leethus must have been one of those secrets whose details only a select few are privy to — and even fewer among those few ever get to live once their purpose has been fulfilled."

133d253a-acb7-4ba4-8ed3-c6a1ce2f642f.Text: {n}The Marshal turns again to look at you.{/n} "There is another reason. Under the present circumstances, only you can provide the necessary level of security for the Imperium's property stored on your world. The Arbites are too few, and our forces are stretched too thin, as we must see to the stability of tithe deliveries from other worlds — and prevent any attempts to disrupt said stability. Thus, we are humbly asking you to help us."

b4aef8f9-1aa4-4c0e-93ed-da64be82c06e.Text: "In other words, they are here in case the diplomatic approach fails and you need a show of force instead."

2d32ec4e-3ed5-4854-b212-d078b547556c.Text: {n}His eyes glittering, the Marshal says curtly,{/n} "I am unable and unwilling to discuss the subject."

4d864084-044f-4780-9ee1-787563283aca.Text: {n}The Arbitrator maintains an air of haughty imperturbability, but you catch the worried glance he casts in the prefect's direction. The Marshal is clearly discomfited by being the sole focus of your fire.{/n}

c9c634a4-fb7b-480a-a178-8a51e4744c8c.Text: {n}The Arbitrator's entire being exudes haughty self-assurance.{/n}

b03760ff-97fa-4b33-9947-34bf7340eadd.Text: "To save an unimaginable treasure hoard, just as a change of pace? Why not? If you were to offer us a modest share of the cargo, we would be..." {n}Jae catches the Marshal's icy glare.{/n} "...outraged! We require no compensation at all, for we operate solely for the good of the Imperium!"

a6483c02-997a-4340-879a-25364334b488.Text: "The {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}'s resources are not limitless, nor is this within their jurisdiction. The matter is delicate, however, and calls for the utmost secrecy. It is also intimately related to your dynasty and its ancient covenant with the Adeptus Arbites. We indeed require your personal assistance."

d9a52a0c-e726-4cc6-a0e8-7ad6a67901ce.Text: "Ensuring the safety of the tithe is paramount, Rogue Trader. There is no room for error."

e4023e87-f4b8-486a-a673-a5a535e9daff.Text: "The Fangs of the Expanse, dogs of war, salute the Rogue Trader!"

e7a6dd04-1b7e-4192-9e81-741e48aeebdd.Text: "If you will excuse me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, certain administrative matters demand my immediate attention."

9a244235-0924-47a4-8dab-1e9a7935c579.Text: "I can see you have feelings for me. And I can see you're torturing yourself right now. Once we're out of here, you can get your head straight and we'll return to this conversation later."

2823e2dc-36ab-4edd-9b7b-bba2697809b0.Text: "I see. Well, then, enjoy rotting here."

01d47045-8e94-4ffe-b9d6-73dd6a5e8715.Text: "Do not show your face around me ever again. I am releasing you from service."

59028555-b5f6-4cb2-aef8-07766bfef186.Text: "Why did they order you to do something like that?"

127a08d1-35bc-40a0-870e-c76ec1679185.Text: "What about Glaito and your data-slate? Was that a lie too?"

8b454c26-687e-4105-a04a-573800cd3dce.Text: "It seems they gave you the only task you were qualified for: to go around jumping into Rogue Traders' beds."

88a4360d-3112-4240-96c6-e35487c65347.Text: "You have said quite enough. Now what?"

805308e0-d437-493d-9fd2-b79f032c8bb8.Text: "Everything between us was a lie, was it? You're making a fool of yourself. Maybe you were just following orders at the start, but don't try to tell me you never developed real feelings for me."

dac39baa-d05a-426a-b07d-043ad2154d1e.Text: [Slap him] "You utter bastard. I never want to see you again."

76123080-ee41-492d-af29-d5906a5a2628.Text: "That changes nothing. I'm getting you out of here."

21054204-4044-4f0d-b853-f306458066c9.Text: "Goodbye, Rogue Trader. But take one thing with you."

e7c359da-6147-407a-9d22-9bf910fb34f6.Text: {n}With his eyes screwed shut, Solomorne grits out,{/n} "Do I have to stick a shiv in you to get you to leave?"

680f8942-a813-4b40-aad2-408fe2b8e098.Text: {n}A warm light appears in his gaze.{/n} "And what happens if I say yes?"

ace44c0a-b114-412c-a771-d1796aaf6704.Text: {n}Solomorne's voice is quiet and serious.{/n} "Before I answer that... I overheard your officers talking, and I think that you might break someone's heart. Are you sure this won't feel like a mistake to you later?"

53237752-7907-4505-a07a-6c20dda753c5.Text: {n}A warm light appears in his gaze.{/n} "In that case, my answer to your question is yes."

969b39fd-ecc9-4282-bba7-fae4baef1388.Text: {n}You detect a certain strain in Solomorne's hostile tone, and well concealed panic deep in his eyes.{/n}

ae915fcf-5221-4ff5-a2ab-9b864de10066.Text: {n}Solomorne's tone conveys only hostility, as if he blames you for all his woes.{/n}

e4cbe835-8229-4dc7-9ccc-0a4508689eb1.Text: {n}All the intensity and presence seem to evaporate from Solomorne's frame as he quietly says,{/n} "As you command... {name}."

450c4d00-1415-464d-9bcb-79e7baaf0934.Text: "It's always better to have a trusted operative in place next to someone who considers {mf|himself|herself} above the Lex Imperialis."

d3d60880-6859-420d-bcd5-b35eb1be877b.Text: "Yes. It was all arranged — I left the data-slate out in the open and ordered Glaito to guard it. The plan was for you to find it and for my 'clumsy courtship' to take me back to your bed." {n}Solomorne looks at you with a ruthless smirk.{/n}

e151265c-0ac9-4177-8c7b-5a63dca438e3.Text: {n}He growls like a rabid beast:{/n} "I could barely stand even being near you! One night together I could deal with, though it wasn't as amazing as you might like to believe. But to be at your side constantly... It repulsed me to imagine that someone might look at me and think, here is an Arbitrator who was so tempted by status and wealth that he has forgotten his duty. But it IS my duty to keep people like you in line!"

de2a6cc2-3384-4023-9596-d85212c35d90.Text: "That's why I wasn't acting like myself on Thassera. I was ashamed to indulge your advances, ashamed of having people see us."

6a558d0a-7f83-42f8-8e22-a12e3b456cfe.Text: {n}His eyes narrowed, Solomorne responds in a stifled voice,{/n} "Trust me, it is not an assignment I am proud of."

8a481bac-59fb-4c3b-a3c0-8bebe57a18e8.Text: "Feelings? You are so convinced that the universe revolves around you, that I'm supposed to adore you just because you want me to — I expected as much from an upstart spoilt with power! Just like other Rogue Traders, you have done nothing to earn your Warrant other than being born into the right blood. You're a pale shadow of your ancestor who received this sacred authority from the Emperor Himself."

03bce83b-e2e4-400f-9479-1d5d6e284ca0.Text: {n}Suddenly hoarse, Solomorne says in a low, rumbling voice,{/n} "Now nothing. Requesting permission to leave, Rogue Trader." {n}Without waiting for a response, the Arbitrator turns on his heel.{/n}

09ef4b37-300e-4124-934c-7879c14f9826.Text: {n}Solomorne's nostrils flare in anger. Barely regaining control of his emotions, he mutters,{/n} "Even if you insist on my return, that won't change the crucial fact that I am no longer fit to serve the Lex. For an Arbitrator who cannot perform his duties, there is only one verdict."

55ab44af-5b4a-4a7d-abba-6c8a816a6556.Text: {n}The Arbitrator salutes and says tersely,{/n} "Right away."

67a289cd-177e-4441-a747-534d84d0c716.Text: "I do feel rotten, but I've spoken nothing but the truth."

d4b9b901-ca71-49a1-8e3d-ce4fdaed957f.Text: "After we slept together, I sent a report up the chain of command. Then, the order came in: maintain the Rogue Trader's trust." {n}Aggression builds up in Solomorne's voice with every word he says, as though he were deliberately riling himself up.{/n} "My assignment was to stay at your side and become your confidant. Well, I'd say I succeeded in earning your trust, didn't I?"

300ecc1d-1662-455a-9c9f-469db662201b.Text: {n}An aggressive grimace appears on Solomorne's face.{/n} "And besides, you wouldn't want to drag me out of here if you knew the truth. Everything between us was a lie. I was ordered to lie to you, so I did. The truth is I couldn't care less about you."

ca0e92b1-da3d-4a5c-9542-456e78b7f0ec.Text: [Call out to the wounded officers] "Are you all right?"

e13cb4f6-43fb-4954-ae81-7fe8cfcd5173.Text: "Find Solomorne and bring him to my chambers immediately. We need to talk."

a06224a9-2229-43e7-b9d7-b2ae3a5ca116.Text: "I shall speak to Solomorne about this further."

b42329fb-7529-4f53-9838-88d0d10b25b1.Text: [Show Danrok the intriguing notes] "Janris, what does this look like to you?"

aafba8da-173f-4a70-bd86-1fcd7b63e8d7.Text: [Place your weapon against your neck] "Obey, or blood will be spilt. What do your protocols have to say about my safety?"

18475029-1b42-4a3d-9628-8eeec473cba9.Text: [Slowly reach out and take hold of his collar] "You wouldn't dare hurt me."

577a3f60-3ddd-4c26-b93b-b5d98f10f57f.Text: "Danrok, send Glaito to be monitored by the Tech-Priests."

a71e7622-93bc-48e7-8b30-86f9e7136f7c.Text: "Glaito, have you been guarding that data-slate?"

53011f44-0da5-4229-ba41-f4012335347d.Text: {n}Glaito, paws spread wide and growling menacingly, scans the wardroom with his scarlet visors. His blood-smeared kinetic jaw clangs, sending sparks flying. Frozen on the sidelines in animal terror, the bloody officers watch his every move.{/n}

f8c634e3-d2c9-4fda-98ee-7d11398a2105.Text: {n}There are also notes about you, in which the previously dry observations gradually turn into something much more interesting.{/n}

89e70918-ce5d-4cca-9a95-367dd37162df.Text: {n}Glaito seems to be guarding Solomorne's personal items while the Proctor has business elsewhere.{/n}

add261d5-378e-43ab-881e-f61886240395.Text: "We've been better, but as long as we're alive... Keep away from that beast before it eats you, Lord Captain!"

6b79ba37-8d0a-4ff8-a7f6-e31ca38a4856.Text: {n}You have seen enough of Glaito in action to confidently recognise his combat mode. In this state, he is capable of ripping off a person's arm or head in a single motion. He has no visible wounds, and, at first glance, his behaviour shows no signs of malfunction.{/n}

9984db2b-5022-4d66-85d1-37a3cbbe6ea9.Text: {n}Glaito looks straight at you, letting a vox-enhanced growl unfurl from his chest. Twitchily moving his paws, Glaito flattens his ears and tilts his head to the side as if puzzled.{/n}

671d5297-1bed-4b4d-bd61-39109be9a4a0.Text: {n}Your eye is drawn to a line listing character traits. Among the positive ones are: "determined," "confident in {mf|his|her} privileges," "courageous in battle," and "magnetic charisma." The negative traits are somewhat more numerous: "arrogant," "lacking in righteous terror of the Lex Imperialis," "unable to entrust tasks to subordinate crew members," and, out of nowhere, "allegedly — kleptomania."{/n}

79969848-c933-4fce-af1d-b0d0658fe358.Text: {n}The protocols that forced him into combat mode are likely in direct conflict with the protocols that require him to protect you as a high-ranking individual. And now an agonising struggle is raging inside Glaito's mind.{/n}

fce5f96b-956c-4cbf-bbf4-26f47326ea50.Text: {n}He is probably having trouble deciding which of your limbs to rip off first.{/n}

9c1fed74-55a3-47a8-a437-8b84a5bf9dbd.Text: {n}Vague ideas are sketched out in truncated phrases: "delicacies, candles, a spot on the deck with a nice view of the stars — hackneyed? Or good?", "visit the Janus greenhouses — prepare conversation topics," even "jointly track down and end some psychopath." The line "choir of repentant criminals perform a serenade" is written in red.{/n}

aadee833-867d-4873-8657-cb2d136153b8.Text: "I would be immensely grateful if you would also remind him to stop scattering his valuables around the ship, Lord Captain."

62730907-f4b8-4ec0-a019-ec2fea86c3fe.Text: {n}Glaito endures the blow stoically, prepares to make a deadly lunge, and... drops meekly to his belly with a pitiful and frustrated whimper. A trickle of blood oozes from a crack in his armour. He sorrowfully rests his face on the floor, crushed by the weight of the protocols embedded in his mind.{/n}

1ae56eb6-3f65-43e3-9f07-32b8be8ce9c0.Text: {n}Looking Glaito right in the eye, you loom over him intimidatingly, slowly but inexorably reaching toward his neck. The dog lets out a low growl, his jaw opening slightly, but your heavy gaze seems to keep him pinned to the ground. Taking Glaito firmly by the collar, you see his whole body go limp, and he lies down helplessly on his belly.{/n}

3f2e9827-f4ab-4bb1-a309-f920b64a26e6.Text: {n}There is an audible snap, and terrible pain rips through your hand. Surprisingly, all your fingers are still in place — Glaito didn't even honour you with a real bite, just a warning. But if the wound is not bandaged in the next few minutes, you will bleed out.{/n}

2dbb1349-2e97-41b6-90ba-dbc82bf09517.Text: {n}It is only now that you notice a small data-slate on the table behind Glaito.{/n}

a4c006b5-4320-488b-bdd5-d7d217b4472c.Text: {n}Glaito twitches to one side and then the other, his jaw opening and closing at the same time. His harsh growl turns into a piercing whine... and the dog lies on his belly in defeat.{/n}

8c1bdb59-a162-4b03-9af6-5f0cf8bbbe7d.Text: {n}Glaito's growl becomes a little more spirited and confident. The more aggression you show, the readier he is to leave you without a head.{/n}

eb85702c-a541-433b-af6a-86972274cf54.Text: {n}The good boy lowers his head a little, clearly primed to leap onto your chest and rip your face off.{/n}

7af99841-0aa8-4f84-a315-2bd07a1485ee.Text: "It will be done. I've already sent for a chain thick enough to hold him."

392e8f71-423e-4e56-9202-5fdebf4a0be3.Text: {n}You hear a mournful whimper in response.{/n}

bbfa1018-6d9c-45c6-a8f1-c525a4b6f540.Text: {n}The final notes reveal the fruits of Solomorne's obviously taxing mental efforts. Your known and suspected tastes in music, food, clothing, and jewellery have been painstakingly documented. A list of gifts that might please you has been compiled, including "favourite type of weapon," "ornate combat servitor," and "fancy garb like that corrupt bureaucrat wears."{/n}

35ef1d5a-7a5c-4137-93fd-ced577b5d84c.Text: "In my humble opinion, it is very much like the way I, young and dashing in my sixteen years, made plans to seduce my charming third-cousin Byatrice Danrok-Rohen. I recognise the earnest directness peculiar to the callow youth." {n}Janris pokes a chubby finger at something resembling a tactical assault diagram, with "{name}" written in the centre surrounded by arrows symbolising various amorous manoeuvres.{/n}

bbd74861-4c5a-48b4-a0a8-d41162da48ca.Text: {n}Judging by the crests on the case, it belongs to Solomorne. In the first notes, you find entire dossiers of observations of your senior officers and retinue: their habits and petty vices, acquaintances, and psychological profiles.{/n}

32830f42-09b5-4334-804a-80a2f938a9a9.Text: {n}It seems strange that Solomorne would have left a personal item containing data practically out in the open like this.{/n}

92d2f02b-e10a-4f24-9f81-26b90d9b71ce.Text: [Take Solomorne's hand] "Your gesture is well received. Your words are forgotten. Come."

9fc65c1e-25c5-45aa-bd14-53d211210b30.Text: [Place your fingers on Solomorne's hands and play along with him]

2c69d23c-f2ec-4fc9-af09-626997fc73c0.Text: "Is organ playing part of an Arbitrator's training?"

11f040f9-e28c-49e9-b3b1-204f0a0bab79.Text: [Burst out laughing] "I'm sorry, but this is terribly poignant — an Arbitrator playing the organ for me!"

4e581283-85dc-4fbe-a7f3-2400c41a26c0.Text: "You still have much to learn in your profession."

2e450d56-730e-460d-a79e-c052d79f45d0.Text: [Smile] "I wish to know if this creation has a second volume. I am amazed by the author's imagination."

d137a72a-3076-49ab-a1b8-8c0a198bc7d6.Text: "You are not obliged to say anything if you don't want to. I'll just give it to you."

9a174824-6235-48b4-be87-eb3cc5f38328.Text: [Return the data-slate] "I consider this inappropriate. You may go."

e5d2ec6b-bece-4326-9ba6-2307cd519ab7.Text: [Hold out the data-slate to Solomorne, but pull it back at the last minute with a smile] "I have to ask. Which of the ideas was your favourite?"

90d34b2b-dfec-4097-9aff-456fac811aea.Text: "And if I agree, this will be something more than one night of fun?"

378f7650-1414-4187-b54c-4c9d58d3a2bf.Text: [Return the data-slate] "I think we should leave things as they are."

6c1b2ad8-dd6d-4289-b8c4-dde86469ad73.Text: "I can't believe it. Solomorne, you're a musician! How can you hide such talent?"

f0f13f09-9736-4579-a1b0-4a6dca975008.Text: "And what made you muse about how to make overtures toward me?"

6de6b607-0c4b-4846-bc10-2e1ad578273d.Text: [Read out the best parts] "Are you talking about these 'overtures'?"

89fb41f0-6fec-4141-a741-633a9ac876fb.Text: "Your mistake gave me a reading experience I shall never forget."

e73bffe7-568b-44a2-b7ee-d985401d50cb.Text: "Next time, don't admit to knowing only one piece."

20911c2a-bf78-4332-8f13-5b45c69d08b9.Text: "Glaito was injured during the incident in the wardroom. I'm sorry for that."

50885309-09b3-4e4c-8607-0f1c90676eb6.Text: "Something tells me you left the data-slate in a conspicuous place on purpose. You left it there for me."

49c144d3-b13a-4460-942b-5d1267cc9f01.Text: "You are such a romantic, Solomorne. Where did you acquire such experience and self-assurance in matters of the heart?"

5aecf0bc-602c-42a0-8b96-a65be6a526ec.Text: "How did your notes end up in the wardroom?"

70635284-2f18-4170-a155-401d0ac03471.Text: {n}Solomorne's face gives nothing away. His eyes bore into the data-slate in your hands. At last, he speaks, his tone surprisingly gentle:{/n} "I imagine you want an explanation."

33cbba8f-95a0-4cdf-a0ab-1e70df5c5114.Text: "If you do not feel the same, tell me — I will understand. If you do, then I want to apologise for my rash words before and take them back."

a1b257c0-d3cf-4432-8643-ac295eac7807.Text: "If it will bring you pleasure, I will apply myself and try to learn a second." {n}Giving you a look heavy with meaning, he adds,{/n} "For you, I can do anything."

7622359c-f1d2-4ae2-8c50-35d55b953294.Text: "It is far from the only one, trust me." {n}A thin smile, but no less suggestive for that, appears on Solomorne's lips.{/n}

50be2d41-e198-4ba3-8b80-4725b4cd20a4.Text: "No, thank the God-Emperor. But I was once assigned to escort a certain person of particular importance to the capital world of the Calixis Sector. He was to be received by no less than the governor himself. I spent eight Terran months alone with him in sealed quarters while the ship made the voyage to Scintilla. I don't know who he was or what special status earned him the protection of the Adeptus Arbites. I only know he was very fond of playing this tune on the organ. I learned it by heart."

6c95868a-f7f2-4054-a17c-9b278291206b.Text: {n}Without taking his eyes off the keys, Solomorne says,{/n} "At least you're enjoying yourself. Could be worse."

67a7619c-8e45-4e1a-b103-b239b3cc360e.Text: {n}The fighter's strong hands, accustomed to holding a weapon, rest on the organ keys with unexpected delicacy. His fingers flit confidently over the keys, producing a melody at once vigorous and full of restrained tenderness, tremulous expectation, and searing yearning. Solomorne's face is frozen in a mask of contemplation, but his hands dance along the keys, alternating between weightless caresses and precise, bold strikes.{/n}

9c8374ca-092e-4999-af64-846e521670d3.Text: "Everything I do, I aim to do well." {n}Solomorne's eyes crease as he draws out an intricate passage from the instrument with one hand while tucking the other behind his back.{/n} "Perfectly, even."

a196e27e-f9ea-4737-85c6-444c94414d32.Text: {n}Your hands move in sync, weaving a fanciful melody. You cannot predict it, only follow Solomorne's movements — but he leads you assuredly, and you respond deftly. You only notice that your fingers have become intertwined when the rhythm of the music changes.{/n}

b3df8a1d-c3ed-40e4-95ea-5bb847de61e5.Text: "I would not call myself experienced in the subject. I have never met anyone who captivates me the way you do. I simply prefer to speak plainly."

f7f8fffb-e646-428f-8bea-baa5ef94c0c6.Text: {n}Solomorne scowls.{/n} "A foolish mistake. I had been working at my assigned desk in the wardroom and, like an idiot, I left my data-slate in there. Glaito recognised it as an important item belonging to me, so he went into guard mode — and started chasing off anyone who might encroach upon it."

67a3898a-800e-4369-aab2-65e45539c028.Text: {n}The melody turns discordant, the notes leaping to the pounding of your heart. But your hands and his are pressed tightly together, your fingers intertwined, transforming the piece into a triumphant and sensual cacophony. A faint smile dawns on Solomorne's lips, but he makes no move to stop you.{/n}

92fc046e-a2b5-4657-96f0-e84d03ef51fe.Text: {n}He takes his hand away from the keys and draws you to him in a confident and powerful motion. The keys let out a piercing shriek under the weight of your body. Solomorne gifts you with a dazzlingly white smile.{/n} "I'm glad you gave me another chance."

0b01eb02-6f18-4996-b689-7c4b8e63a42c.Text: {n}Slanting a glance at you while continuing to play, Solomorne quietly confesses,{/n} "I have never played for anyone before. This is me making an overture."

ca2dea54-9a12-4b4b-9fd2-68dcb37100a2.Text: {n}The corners of Solomorne's mouth lift slightly.{/n} "If you mean that I made myself look like an incompetent — then I completely agree. And I'm glad I was taught this lesson from an event that didn't end in tragedy."

a60aeaf4-a2b5-4b10-b1b5-8547d35dc398.Text: {n}Solomorne stiffens for a moment, and then a thin yet rakish smile forms on his lips.{/n} "I can show you."

dad16078-8fec-4d5f-9707-e9a007eae4cc.Text: {n}Solomorne nods.{/n} "Much more. And something much more significant to me. I am not brazen enough to aspire to any official status, but I can promise you my friendship, my fidelity, my patience..." {n}He scoffs.{/n} "I'm talking like a fool, aren't I? I just enjoy being with you, {name}. And I'd like to express that feeling openly."

b53fa59e-eadb-4622-acba-40885b9e2d79.Text: {n}Solomorne lets out a quiet sigh of anguish.{/n} "I'm sure that is the first of many jokes you've managed to think up already."

a6dd7c68-dbd6-4e15-8cbf-870046c86644.Text: {n}The silence stretches for a few seconds, and then the hard indifference on Solomorne's face cracks, a shadow of anxiety flickering in his gaze.{/n}
