ca543040-3424-44ae-874a-9ade0bddcb4f.Text: "I think I still have to. To keep things transparent between us."

6050e974-4d72-4413-a988-dfa6dde118ca.Text: {n}Solomorne shakes his head and raises a clenched fist as if swearing to tell the truth.{/n} "No. I don't ferret out other people's secrets or conduct covert surveillance. I only record what I see. It is my duty to remain vigilant."

11d06807-617e-45a1-9924-3f84c4194b6d.Text: "Please forgive me. It won't happen again." {n}Solomorne's tense posture relaxes slightly, a shadow of strange relief on his face.{/n} "If you will excuse me."

91e4ec1f-6686-48a6-906d-8df5b64c82f2.Text: {n}Solomorne's eyes crease with triumph.{/n} "I'll settle for the title of organist in residence if you don't ask me to play anything else. I only know this piece."

84b2a590-cc54-487f-857d-eaf5b7930acf.Text: {n}Solomorne says nothing for a long time, but then begins speaking without reserve:{/n} "I made a fool of myself that night. There was an intimacy between us, and it... perhaps it made me anxious. Or perhaps I wasn't prepared to feel so strongly. But I did feel it — I think about you and about what there could be between us."

095bbde1-13f3-436b-84b9-4c5b20cb6257.Text: "Glaito will be fine. He {d|Encyclopedia:RMC_DogInjuredDecision}wasn't seriously injured{/d}. Thank you for going easy on him."

7aa154db-4d69-4c4f-b168-c2d108a39212.Text: {n}As you read out the idea of attending a service at the reliquary together, Solomorne maintains a stony expression. The idea of a romantic evening by the stained glass windows of the ship's observatorium is greeted with the barely audible grinding of teeth. At the line "maybe a bottle of good amasec and an expensive ring confiscated from some acquisitive bureaucrat?" his eye twitches testily. But when you begin to read out the ornate and likely copied love confession, he snorts loudly, suppressing a smile with monstrous effort, and declares,{/n} "I beg you. I'm willing to part with much of my dignity — it is certainly warranted in this case — but allow me to keep a shred."

669af65c-fb6a-43e6-8812-1e6639ee8754.Text: {n}Solomorne lapses into thought again for a long time, and then says doubtfully,{/n} "There is no simple answer... If I say you are special, it sounds hackneyed, doesn't it? But it's the truth. I've never met anyone like you before."

83734272-96bc-4709-b009-890fd02f5039.Text: "The data-slate contains my observation log on you and the members of your retinue. I use it to record habits, personality traits, and noteworthy facts. And with regard to you in particular... more than that. I think you have already come across notes of a different nature — thoughts about how one might make overtures toward a Rogue Trader." {n}In a less stern man, the look the Proctor gives you from beneath his slightly lowered brows could be considered roguish.{/n}

db44677c-7d11-4e3c-b784-3618aeb9967a.Text: "I will not repeat such foolishness in the future."

9bbf2ef5-c943-4846-930e-f3dce5931882.Text: {n}Solomorne replies wryly,{/n} "Yes, it gave me an... unforgettable experience, too."

ccfa52cb-c200-4adf-8f36-f2745c6d20a0.Text: "You know, {name}, you're lucky Glaito didn't rip your arm off when you took the data-slate from him. I'm sure he had a hard time deciding whose safety was more important, yours or my notes'."

fa36b7ca-126b-490b-a289-e7badd298a9a.Text: "That would be disgracefully devious for an Arbitrator. I'm afraid you are overestimating my ingenuity." {n}Solomorne's bearing makes it hard to gauge the sincerity of his words.{/n}

4629f1f5-2b0d-4c57-86cb-a0608ae9fdcc.Text: "I disagree. Our relationship is worth preserving and strengthening. Think about it."

6854b9ac-4822-47b3-b0fa-3199eb2c887f.Text: "You have entertained me. I am pleased I did not err in granting you this privilege."

c3337c1e-86c4-45b3-a352-731de9fdb671.Text: "Did you enjoy sharing a bed with the Rogue Trader?"

577fd6e0-f6fb-4bda-ac39-63f6c97c6a7a.Text: "I think we should do this again once in a while."

d1c3ac9f-d0a4-4d7b-b2c7-252b89893ada.Text: "Remember this night. It's unlikely to happen again."

37054fa2-3f2c-4459-a9dd-045101705583.Text: "What if I ordered you to continue our affair?"

1c1f148b-1e69-4ede-9b42-e364c5d4cfc0.Text: [Sigh] "Unfortunately, you're right. I can't afford to have an affair with you. It wouldn't be fair."

a16503c1-b62f-463c-9995-ac62da18145e.Text: "You are loyal to your duty, but love will demand that you be loyal to the Rogue Trader. That will tear you apart."

f0741389-a35a-4dff-b0a3-53b66b6d9f8b.Text: "What makes you think an affair would harm our working relationship?"

c06b8bad-398b-4b2d-ba92-296926addb16.Text: "Admit it, you didn't actually enjoy it."

286f7be6-3a60-4fb2-9d25-98f42dd04ee6.Text: {n}Lying back on the sheets, Solomorne stretches out contentedly, rolling his broad shoulders. Drops of sweat cover his dark skin.{/n} "That was exactly what I needed. But far more than I dared hope." {n}He gives you a thin smile, as though he does not know how to express his feelings any more overtly.{/n}

7e200ab9-2481-4d26-a2cd-2794f8e75fbf.Text: {n}Eternally tense and ready for duty, Solomorne almost looks like a normal man without his armour. For once, his knuckles are not menacingly taut on his violent hands, the line of his mouth is soft, and his gaze wanders in drowsy blissfulness.{/n}

60dfa647-13a4-462e-a0c8-6d19cdc4822d.Text: {n}Solomorne nods calmly.{/n} "Of course. We shouldn't let this liaison grow into anything more."

479918a6-3460-4d55-821e-9e2b33d30769.Text: "We had a good time together, and I'm grateful for that. But an affair between us could affect our... working relationship."

851f18f8-817d-4ad1-b9c8-418594b7168d.Text: {n}Solomorne gives a debonair nod in response.{/n} "I strive for perfection in all things."

347b6266-f6a1-4680-9183-2357b8450eb4.Text: "Can lovers be expected to stand in unbiased judgement of each other? Besides..." {n}Solomorne's voice turns soft.{/n} "I don't see myself as someone who is open to having such an intimate relationship with another person."

addc2ff7-afe0-4a35-89e7-dffb572e20ca.Text: "Lying isn't in my nature, {name}. I enjoyed it — more than. But it's a matter of principle."

5d4311cc-2df9-434b-af4b-55c074e6864e.Text: "Then I will, with great regret, refuse to obey that order. For no law of the Imperium compels me to obey it."

d7733e89-fb51-4bb2-8666-5141a89071c5.Text: "Thank you. It's always a pleasure to spend time with someone who understands."

25c89283-b9e2-43c4-9c27-cc1c1a0510d4.Text: {n}Wiping his recent contentment from his face, Solomorne nods briefly.{/n} "I did not wish to offend you. I apologise, I'll be on my way."

36bcc12a-51e3-4018-81dd-b659413131f7.Text: {n}Solomorne stares at you in silence for a long time, and then says quietly,{/n} "If I fell in love with you, I would truly struggle to choose between you and my duty. So let that remain a desire unfulfilled."

ac916081-4e5f-442b-8c9c-52ea40a59df3.Text: {n}Growing serious, Solomorne directs a piercing look at you.{/n} "I don't think so, Rogue Trader."

1876628e-172d-431a-98cd-0cc645bc2275.Text: {n}A mix of emotions flashes across the man's face for a moment.{/n} "You and I are both bound by duty, {name}, and that takes precedence over any matters of the heart."

54af1db4-df6d-451f-b25c-24cb8d66f554.Text: "We have finally discovered your calling. Perhaps I should assign you to cleaning the waste system?"

018aa3ce-a70f-4f1a-94b1-a47da71d4dd7.Text: "Hand in your mop. You have been punished enough."

fff83c7d-bfd3-4fc2-b587-dd2e4a256c09.Text: "Get off my ship. You're no use to me even as a deck swab."

2dcfe2ae-98dc-4f9e-9833-92ecba32e07f.Text: "I commend you. Continue whipping the crew into shape."

1d092270-8fa3-4789-97ef-c21d4551d49b.Text: {n}Solomorne is mopping the deck with diligence verging on zeal. He scrutinises the floor for the slightest speck of dirt, primed and ready to hand down his harsh sentence: intensive scrubbing.{/n}

80aecb60-151e-4b16-bd4e-243cdbe85fc5.Text: {n}Solomorne's voice is full of humility:{/n} "Thank you for your attention, Rogue Trader. The decks of your ship are clean, which means my work is going as it should."

81acffdf-cd7d-4db4-bb39-7fec895386bb.Text: {n}With a grim glance around, Solomorne says dryly,{/n} "I didn't think they would dare disturb the Rogue Trader with their petty gripes. Discipline among the deck cleaners is abominable. They think that because they have been entrusted with mops rather than weapons, they can do their duty with less diligence."

461d4f6c-f756-4796-b386-b17f4e4eb5a4.Text: {n}Jutting out his chin, Solomorne stubbornly clips out,{/n} "If you think I deserve it, so be it. My calling is to serve the Imperium. Whatever work you assign me, it will be done."

8dbbd917-c4f7-4ee5-a27d-88e6dac73bc0.Text: "As the Rogue Trader wishes." {n}Solomorne's expression is indifferent, but you detect relief in the depths of his gaze.{/n}

754a9f29-39d8-4224-b064-b3c951c9b8fd.Text: {n}Clenching his jaw, Solomorne lets go of the mop, which falls to the deck with a clatter.{/n} "Understood. I relinquish my post."

5748ae28-47d4-403e-8ac0-eebc30547ea6.Text: "I will obey the order." {n}Solomorne nods respectfully, but you catch a glimmer of sad disappointment in his eyes.{/n}

86242619-4f6c-4998-a166-dc28bdf639df.Text: "I won't lay a finger on anyone else." {n}Withstanding your unrelenting gaze, Solomorne smiles crookedly, one corner of his mouth quirking.{/n} "I have more subtle training methods."

6c4023bf-f00e-4656-bdd6-104f08c90cba.Text: "I promise to make every effort to instil in them a pious awe concerning the performance of their duties."

0d3b5f31-deaf-4877-a124-61143159ae74.Text: "You're so sincere, Solomorne! It's nice that I can believe every word you say!"

3bfb875a-8328-4e8f-be55-fd74ec74d6dc.Text: "Why do you wish to leave my retinue?"

44166f58-b690-4611-b0a2-a74a8dcde973.Text: "The part about disappointed trust is quite right, you manipulative pig."

50e3e3d4-f2e7-4582-a2f0-8140de19162e.Text: "If you regret what you said, you can simply take it back."

0f5ceaa7-23e2-401e-9a61-eb7d8a4932df.Text: "I saw that you were lying to yourself and me about your feelings. I am important to you, so you're trying to punish yourself. But that is your game, and I'm not playing. Go and attend to your duties."

de6da06b-87d0-4350-90ca-23338232081a.Text: "I care for you, Solomorne. I forgive you. At ease."

1884a19f-ee37-4285-826d-75f78dd87b7e.Text: "Everything is over between us, but that does not excuse you from your duties. Go."

cade6c01-0f2a-4f83-b08f-5c2ae1321705.Text: "Don't show your face on my ship again."

c759d3f6-c0e6-4099-8661-1a296924cf9b.Text: "You coward. You wronged me and you think you can get away with it?"

51112367-3ef8-4ed1-ac92-f7dc2e493657.Text: [Beat Solomorne with the maul] "Let's see if this will satisfy my thirst for vengeance."

dc0b7115-f405-4f76-a942-1368a3b91c93.Text: [Wave the maul away] "I'm not going to torture you."

85a46faa-7f80-4595-9649-fbd7fb890b83.Text: "If you wish to apologise, you will do so on your knees."

69f5d019-4634-4b91-a030-a731004f2548.Text: "You won't get off with simple pain. Since you're so willing to do any job handed down from on high, from now on, you're going to be a deck swab — when you're not on combat duty."

6773f764-8fab-4d77-a21b-ecd53e07c813.Text: [Slap him] "There's your punishment. You may go."

bcc98e71-c5c4-4669-8611-46ab96272661.Text: [Carefully stow the report away in your desk]

5f5889fb-a32f-4b51-b7b0-aaafbdbf61db.Text: {n}A report lies on the desk in front of you. Solomorne, clearing his throat, speaks dryly,{/n} "I, Solomorne Anthar, formally request to be relieved of my position in the Rogue Trader's retinue due to my failure to live up to the high trust placed in me."

87775c01-576e-48f9-b968-e572fe378cca.Text: {n}Solomorne soundlessly flinches as if from a blow.{/n}

737e9ace-0c50-4877-862b-f8d6a6eac215.Text: "Let's not play mind games. I took advantage of your trust, I deceived you, I insulted you. I don't think you want me anywhere near you."

b827c4b4-14ea-4381-a643-021714555c4c.Text: "I was following orders." {n}His lips tighten stubbornly.{/n} "But that doesn't absolve me of my guilt. I failed you."

22ec7d99-3640-43a6-8af9-809d04d95c2f.Text: "That is generous and gracious. But I have no intention of exploiting your trust again."

012ab65e-d3c1-4e4c-b7da-ebdd3d573528.Text: {n}Solomorne devours the solitary page of the report with his eyes, as if he is hesitant to look up at you. A faint blush creeps across his cheeks.{/n}

0622bd8e-578b-462e-b787-3cf6675663d7.Text: "That's not what I... As you will, Rogue Trader!" {n}Solomorne's eyebrows fly upward. His face is stony as he silently salutes you and leaves the study with a painfully straight back.{/n}

cea99a16-a8ea-4f28-8bb0-ebb9ee3e46db.Text: {n}The text of the report is dry and the handwriting pathologically perfect. In a couple of ruthless phrases, Solomorne passes judgement on himself: "failed to demonstrate loyalty in keeping with the favour shown and lowered myself to deliberate lying."{/n}

78442406-c0fa-4c1c-8b36-756bf27a11a1.Text: "I have been extremely honest with myself and you in my report."

67cebe54-dcc3-4c6f-bee4-c192e03e10ac.Text: "As you will!" {n}Solomorne salutes you solemnly and leaves the study.{/n}

88a7b28d-9bd6-4f1a-86e9-4a162f2fa6a2.Text: {n}Frowning severely, Solomorne shakes his head.{/n} "I admit my guilt. I insulted you with lies, and I am ready to be punished." {n}He pulls an impressive spiked maul from his belt and holds it out to you.{/n} "Exact your vengeance in kind. Pain for pain."

92e9fafc-7bec-484d-b387-a0c32ff95308.Text: "An Excruciator maul. A standard tool of suppression for especially dangerous criminals. I ask you not to hold back."

af48ed21-7563-49cc-b206-eeb104185c02.Text: {n}Solomorne's entire body is covered with bruises and wounds from the spikes of the maul, his muscles standing out in stark relief under his reddened skin. But Solomorne, despite the pain, remains upright, gritting his teeth and trying to hold back the roar that bursts from his chest.{/n} "Don't... stop..."

632744a5-7312-4a11-976b-ecc9707fbc7d.Text: {n}A new round of blows forces Solomorne to his knees. Bloody tears well up in his eyes, but he maintains his stoic silence. Each strike seems to bring greater serenity to his gaze.{/n}

b5f0ed13-2e00-42a1-ba78-624536ab043f.Text: "As you wish. But I would consider it only fair."

7a96173b-c711-4035-b6a3-b1621a7a2505.Text: {n}Solomorne, frowning at you, sinks heavily to his knees. With a titanic effort, he bows his stiff neck and murmurs,{/n} "I apologise on my knees, as I should. I behaved unworthily and I deserve it."

f7cb2afe-918f-44e0-b98a-fb9364a04aea.Text: {n}Solomorne's eyes widen, but after swallowing some profane outburst, he bows his head stubbornly.{/n} "As you will. If my shame will atone for a fraction of the pain I have caused, so be it."

8bc897a9-dda6-45f1-bff3-08703405127b.Text: {n}Solomorne takes the blow without flinching. The scarlet imprint of your palm spreads across his cheek. With his head slightly lowered, Solomorne murmurs,{/n} "As you will."

cedc7c91-9568-4640-81f7-233d77c7785d.Text: "I could. But I won't." {n}Solomorne looks fearlessly into your eyes.{/n} "I am truly sorry I lied to you, but... I'm also relieved I don't have to lie anymore."

89ead483-322d-4fee-98dc-0d15ea185590.Text: "Thank you. I hear the offer of friendship in your words, but I must humbly decline. I still feel that I have failed you, however. You may count on my service, but I dare not aspire to your candour and trust."

2798edf5-1cc9-421e-a03c-14d0325f477c.Text: {n}Solomorne's pupils dilate as he watches your fingers tear his letter to shreds. When he opens his mouth, his voice is hoarse:{/n} "You are entitled to do this... to my act of penance."

d172ffa9-d621-48fd-a9e9-ad5225b4110e.Text: {n}Strange trepidation and pained satisfaction gleam in Solomorne's gaze.{/n}

fd2f3dc1-2cff-4cb4-94a1-75b2e9ef8e40.Text: [Say nothing and listen intently to every sound]

da644f9c-ffe6-4aaa-9763-1f374ea3eabb.Text: "I am ordering you to put your weapon away before you kill someone."

4507a642-8391-45a7-baa1-219fe3497c16.Text: "Have you lost your mind, Solomorne? Stop firing a gun in my chambers!"

fe58dc32-241d-4d94-84a9-d5cde771acbb.Text: [Smile] "Nothing to worry about. If I'd dreamt about Vultur, I'd have riddled the whole room with bullets, too."

7c828cae-4f3b-4db9-9049-3bef48ab0e0c.Text: "Do you often have dreams like that?"

c368ca7b-f820-4bd0-be16-dd79b219483f.Text: "I see I'm not the only one who prefers to keep a weapon close to their pillow."

d0498a89-c30f-4ba5-aebe-ddc7b7074ae8.Text: "It was just a dream. You can relax."

4fb59d51-0b31-44fe-9b5c-1859bb84c07a.Text: "What did you dream about exactly? Tell me."

a27fc1fd-893c-40cb-a62d-133e9c663a9e.Text: "All this has taken more of a toll than you've let on, hasn't it?"

990e1635-231d-4b5f-963e-f9269e764148.Text: [Smile] "I'm proud of you. Even in your dreams, you kill the enemies of the Imperium."

b82b412e-18db-4b91-bbc3-2157bb234ae2.Text: [Touch his shoulder] "No law says you have to carry it all inside. Share it with me."

7b4e8ee1-2dc2-4561-98ff-8fa49484bb9e.Text: "I'm not going to make you bare your soul. Let's go to sleep."

6b2313c8-5037-424f-821b-6e70a88d0f90.Text: [Tightly grip his hand] "I permit you to be vulnerable with me. If necessary, I will protect you myself."

1d229177-1b9a-449d-9057-00ed9e6d2c68.Text: [Embrace him] "I look at you and I see no weakness. Only the wounds of a strong man."

82a6947c-2862-4cc0-b44d-5a790bfb13a8.Text: [Smoothly cuff Solomorne's hand to the bed with his handcuffs] "I know how to distract you from dark thoughts."

d90a468f-7bad-4f30-9f31-9ce18167ebb9.Text: [Stroke his head] "It will pass. I promise."

789a6f52-0694-4585-8192-2455969ef0cd.Text: "Since no one is trying to kill us, I suggest we both go back to sleep."

4ab069d1-91e6-41b5-8ce6-34652105ac61.Text: {n}The dream is shattered by someone's sharp movement and the muffled sound of a gunshot. You open your eyes to see Solomorne at your side. He is leaning forward, one hand clutching his weapon behind a smoking pillow. His frenzied eyes are trained on the darkness of your chambers, his teeth bared. He is panting like a hunted animal.{/n}

7c8435dd-f31a-4953-b090-c69985804846.Text: {n}You hear no footsteps, no rustling of clothes, no clinking of blades.{/n}

5f2c796b-c9e6-4ef2-9c84-4ccd9dbdf448.Text: {n}With a disgruntled snarl, Solomorne refuses to lower his weapon. He growls fiercely and stubbornly:{/n} "I saw them."

90dcceb8-d7e1-4469-acbe-949a0a8cbd7c.Text: {n}With each passing second, the absence of any uninvited guests in your chambers becomes more and more evident. Finally, Solomorne puts his weapon down with an exhausted sigh and says brokenly,{/n} "Damn it... I must have imagined them. I'm sorry."

16fad669-9667-4c21-a7b2-045492949f4f.Text: {n}Your fingers find your weapon under your pillow, and you peer in the same direction as Solomorne. There is no movement in the darkness, only the sound of your lover's ragged breathing filling the room.{/n}

ee13fc56-7071-44d0-9086-584487dac7f6.Text: "The face stealers from Thassera. They're here. They've come for us," {n}Solomorne says jerkily, almost barking the words. Tremors rack his whole body.{/n}

d5276316-88b8-48ca-88ca-e7c7f1b3be18.Text: {n}Gritting his teeth obstinately, Solomorne rasps,{/n} "I saw them."

fcb518b1-acbd-4500-8f02-b8e385c254a9.Text: {n}With each passing second, your eyes penetrate deeper into the gloom. The room is empty.{/n}

e6dd8c82-843a-49f2-b8fd-34706cb69420.Text: {n}Solomorne sweeps the empty chamber with his eyes once more and mutters reluctantly,{/n} "Sometimes."

b9740475-d699-4925-859c-b67becd5c034.Text: {n}You see Solomorne's jaw working in his stony face.{/n} "Maybe I am."

150bd5ef-8640-4c87-b6ce-ca244467eca3.Text: "Of course. That's just common sense." {n}Your words seem to surprise Solomorne to the point that his bafflement drowns out his roiling emotions for a moment.{/n}

ca2edbfa-70e0-4337-9fa0-2c49a66227b2.Text: "I don't think I'll be able to."

2de5a389-f4a0-47e3-a571-b526983a0443.Text: "I apologise for disturbing you, Rogue Trader. I think I'd better go." {n}Solomorne's low voice is full of anguish and shame.{/n}

4c599ef2-ee99-4e68-b4f3-c7a4c5692ccc.Text: {n}He does not return your smile. His face is contorted by flashes of furious emotion that he is struggling to control.{/n}

fe12ade5-c607-48dc-9948-986440fc6fb2.Text: {n}Solomorne sighs heavily.{/n} "I dreamt I saw the dead traitors from Thassera. The ones who plotted against us. They entered your chambers wearing others' faces, but I still knew it was them. I realised they had managed to slip back into other people's bodies before they died. It's... It's... Shit!" {n}A groan of pain escapes through his gritted teeth.{/n}

15f2f55b-3447-4198-bd44-11824c9a4a42.Text: "No. It's better if I go." {n}Contrary to his words, Solomorne does not move. You feel every muscle in his arm go taut.{/n}

2d3b07de-2576-4916-a248-8797b9b294c2.Text: "I apologise again." {n}Solomorne gives you a guilt-ridden look.{/n}

bed3d8bb-6cfe-4a04-9132-53ed36c0f612.Text: "An Arbitrator must not appear weak or vulnerable." {n}Stubbornly pressing his lips together, Solomorne glares at the empty air before him.{/n} "I am the gauge by which the Imperium is judged on its strength and its grip on the galaxy."

ce5c9436-095c-4bd9-a674-711a1ceffe9d.Text: "Those bastards were one step away from bringing us down." {n}Solomorne stares intently into your eyes.{/n} "You know, at the time I wondered what would be better: dying alongside you, or surviving with the knowledge that I had failed to keep you safe. I was overjoyed when I realised the end had come for both of us."

240214a5-37ff-4265-ab5e-deec8bd0b824.Text: "Oh, in my dreams I sometimes even manage to save the Imperium a couple of times over," {n}Solomorne replies with a strained smile, not a hint of mirth in his eyes.{/n}

410fbcdd-1b2d-46a6-bdaf-836580e02727.Text: {n}Under your fingers, the Arbitrator's tremoring body relaxes. With his eyebrows drawn together grimly, Solomorne murmurs,{/n} "Not sharing it is better. When you talk to someone about what's weighing on your soul, you become attached to them. And becoming attached is a bad habit for an Arbitrator. In my service, every person you know long enough to develop feelings for is likely to die before their time, and horribly, at that. Losing people hurts. It's like a piece of your soul dies with each of them."

f0f4fbbd-cb24-4855-8c43-8bea7cd0e83a.Text: {n}Giving you a lingering look, Solomorne replies with feeling,{/n} "I'm grateful for that. Go back to sleep. I'll just sit here for a while."

ca49b798-ca3f-40c0-8fa9-9a761e1e34e8.Text: {n}Solomorne raises his eyes to you.{/n} "I have become attached to you, and I regret it. And I regret saying all this too. When you die, it will be very bad for me, and I think of that moment, I wait for it and dread it. And I am ashamed of this weakness."

b493bec4-d2df-46e8-8439-2ded0a83f395.Text: "But sometimes... it's so bloody hard." {n}Grimacing, Solomorne wearily drops his head into his hands.{/n}

8755f384-2f01-424f-8a1c-3aa7fd7dd34e.Text: {n}Solomorne's eyebrows creep upward, the shadow of a smile appearing on his lips.{/n} "This is the first time someone has ever offered to protect me, but... it feels good." {n}Leaning back against the pillow, he speaks softly,{/n} "You know, maybe the only one who can truly protect me from this bloody horror is you."

e00f0b81-f8bc-4867-9dbc-2f59f44aa734.Text: {n}With a chuckle, Solomorne responds to the embrace.{/n} "Thank you. I'll try to be that strong man for you."

5462f194-7fd1-43f4-92f3-bfe1525c6218.Text: {n}Yanking his cuffed hand, Solomorne looks up at you and orders sternly,{/n} "Take it off."

d3968513-63fb-4703-be69-240a27982638.Text: {n}Solomorne's eyes light up for the first time, his lips curving into a cocky grin. With a full-body effort, he begins to break away from the hard wood of the bed. With a deafening crack, he lunges toward you, fierce, passionate, and alive.{/n}

8bf640a4-368c-46ef-bb44-752bc9c7298a.Text: {n}With a caustic smile, Solomorne leans back against the pillow.{/n} "Don't make any promises. We both know this will never pass."

aa7c0b05-9bed-4f3b-810e-d2e2f8e99a39.Text: "Can we say that justice was done today if we blew up the court and overthrew the judge in the process?"

625b7b15-9ddd-4b2f-87c3-98e627ea3054.Text: "You look very much like a normal person right now."

5607789b-f5ff-411b-9b17-2a024a2ced45.Text: [Watch the fire with him in silence]

d1b76fa8-79c4-4f0c-b645-a69519942bc4.Text: "To what do I owe my elevation in your regard?"

ad4cfdda-7245-4309-914c-826383cc32ba.Text: "But, alas, we have already made our choice."

d4926cfd-7f06-4b63-9ab8-af3f8b00eab3.Text: [Return Solomorne's request for removal] "I refuse to accept it."

bb79149d-f488-43a3-88de-2001f17d8c8c.Text: "I don't think I can forgive you."

31de2c7f-61eb-415c-8146-00c82cd63a3c.Text: [Place your hand in his] "Dancing in the midst of smouldering ruins is just my style."

b7f5a681-8271-48bd-9d7d-6331b38bda40.Text: "We don't need to dance. Just sit with me."

5e9c0b44-3e20-481b-8740-ed2c39d21821.Text: "It is not too late. Be my consort, Solomorne."

b674a1ba-a87d-4e40-af65-1dd576c2dddd.Text: {n}Solomorne, his weapon lying beside him, stares silently at the dying flames and at what until recently symbolised the triumph of the Lex Imperialis. His eyes are as dark and fathomless as the ocean.{/n}

74f7e1fa-c0a1-4453-92fc-7598f5952c58.Text: {n}Solomorne takes the letter tentatively, touching it only with his fingertips. His eyes are full of warmth.{/n} "Thank you for keeping it. This... admission of guilt meant a great deal to me. I spent a whole night agonising over these paltry couple of sentences."

452d2c0b-7c07-4a47-8afb-95dc8965be2a.Text: {n}He shifts his gaze to you.{/n} "Thank you for your refusal."

858a54d1-8404-4689-ae82-a7401f4a3475.Text: "Watching justice burn. My justice." {n}Solomorne watches the fire, his expression more contemplative than mournful.{/n}

9513e88d-3eea-433c-971f-350783bdb3c6.Text: {n}Solomorne sighs.{/n} "I understand. Let's sit a little longer, and then we'll go." {n}He takes your hand in his and is still for a long while.{/n}

64ce36a0-dac7-44e5-a1c3-ed6ababeb135.Text: {n}Smiling wryly, he replies,{/n} "Hard as it is to believe, I am very much a normal person."

f951e2c3-e599-4939-a01b-9bc12fa18ada.Text: {n}Solomorne casually shifts so that he is leaning against you. He is big, warm, strong... and so, so sad.{/n}

da40f663-31b8-4c71-9af1-48262f5dcdb5.Text: "I'm tired of being used as a weapon. Not a weapon of the Lex Imperialis, but of specific people. They have used me against you time and time again, and I'm sick of it."

dd69fe75-0dc1-4bfe-b576-7a03904faa7f.Text: {n}He turns to you.{/n} "Look... I'm sorry. I know I've apologised before, but this is different. Before, I felt ashamed and disgusted with myself — for lying to you, for hurting you — I wanted you to punish me. But now I'm just sorry and very sad that I did all that."

b46e4322-480d-4a46-9955-6aaa392d61d0.Text: {n}Solomorne turns to you, the flames from the fire dancing in his pupils.{/n} "If you're not joking... If you're not afraid you'll regret those words... If you really need me... Then I agree." {n}He takes your hand in his.{/n} "I agree to be yours. Forever and in all ways."

9b02d7e5-01e2-4bcf-b04d-1673fb74cd9d.Text: {n}Solomorne unhurriedly draws himself to his feet and extends his hand to you.{/n} "I have a debt from Thassera to repay. I believe I owe you a dance."

ca8bd4c9-1985-4ee8-8781-e17023f47389.Text: "When we were on Thassera, I shouldn't have been so standoffish. I should have asked you to dance. I am trying to make up for it now."

6034fdfe-814d-408b-91cd-bc3bac83694e.Text: "When we were on Thassera, I should have thought less about what the people around me thought and more about how to avoid stamping on your toes. I am trying to make up for it now."

8ae3e293-62d5-4ee9-986d-6e95d822cbcd.Text: "Fire, tragedy, the collapse of convictions and hierarchies, and we're in the middle of it all... It's all very romantic, isn't it?" {n}Solomorne snorts.{/n} "I'll have to add that to my data-slate."

29d3b837-e3fa-466f-a605-c3a6e8361a04.Text: {n}Solomorne pulls you toward him, his hands as hard as stone but his touch full of trepidation and tenderness. As you stare into each other's eyes, the flames blur, turning into glowing streaks, and soon it is just you and him in a whirling vortex of fire.{/n}

8a1f73fd-bad4-42fe-a425-afdf6c7c26d8.Text: "Of course." {n}Smiling softly, Solomorne wraps his arm around your shoulders.{/n}

a20a5e26-b612-449d-835d-4405854c5359.Text: "That... stamp of grandeur on your face. Time after time, you saw right through people — even me. You read their motives. You accomplished incredible feats, won victory after victory. And everything in your words and deeds raised you up above ordinary people, as if the pedestal sprung up spontaneously beneath your feet. To look at many Rogue Traders, you can tell the breed is not what it once was, but you..."

bef3a833-1554-449d-bc35-d4dfdb64d7d8.Text: "And you were bloody right. But I've always been told I have an especially thick skull. As it turns out, that isn't necessarily a good thing."

0656eb9e-42fa-4529-a6f1-44232dfe6b89.Text: "It is because of individuals like you that the Emperor granted the sacred Warrants to the Imperium's dynasties."

4d78b172-4f9d-48a6-8b45-c289d64d443b.Text: {n}With a slight smile, he whispers,{/n} "I've never come close to saying anything as crazy as this in all my life, but... I think I'm head over heels in love with you."

10d8d837-c803-4e39-b8e7-5a07a3f02755.Text: {n}Solomorne does not pull away. His touch is gentle and full of hidden strength.{/n} "Thank you."

e86ec0ca-647e-40bd-84ba-5fe14e9ded56.Text: {n}Staring into the flames, he suddenly lets out a laugh.{/n} "You know, you made a poor first impression on me. Terrible, in fact! I thought you were arrogant, behaving as if you were above every law. An upstart wearing another's regalia, and not a very clever one either..." {n}Solomorne's gaze turns distant.{/n} "How could I have been so blind..."

164086d1-2755-4be8-946d-946fdfd4ee57.Text: "It took a while for me to realise that some people — the rare few — are rightly above all laws. People like you." {n}He pauses thoughtfully.{/n} "Had we met sooner, I think I would have dedicated my life to serving you, and not the Lex Imperialis."

ad877e82-2b0e-4e14-9cb9-8e46643e3401.Text: "Proctor, is it really necessary to keep your cyber-mastiff on the bridge? He... ah... he makes the crew nervous."

c74a6bfa-8fc9-4552-a592-b3dec7419ca0.Text: "Do you ask your officers to surrender their weapons because they scare the rabble? I thought not."

e9556111-3477-4bf6-b5da-566945779fba.Text: "Tell me, Solomorne, have you never once hesitated while passing sentence? Have you never awoken at night, wondering if you have been truly impeccable in your judgement?"

476ce948-3e51-4b76-bf7b-33a83d02e2f4.Text: "My sleep is guarded by the Lex Imperialis, Sister. So long as I serve His Law, I am untroubled by doubt."

229800ed-8f97-429e-9999-daf6a90af33a.Text: "Proctor, several dozen legal codices from various worlds in the Koronus Expanse have been delivered to my chambers... I am not quite sure how to interpret your gesture."

2da0213d-3952-4e2c-993a-557e00075f13.Text: "You once asked me about my reading tastes, and I promised to lend you my books. I would welcome a discussion on legislative amendments in the last two centuries — by far the most interesting period, in my opinion."

f9730576-eea9-4497-a7c8-c00b61abd49d.Text: "You seem tense, Proctor. Did you see something suspicious?"

6dcbb79c-808e-4116-9e60-d3a5e6702063.Text: "No, Master Interrogator. I will deal with any violations that could lead to disorder. As for minor infractions — you and I both have better things to do."

83c21ac5-4800-4ad5-a8b2-6252c5c2e988.Text: "Don't think I didn't see you in the bar on the lower decks, Master Killjoy! Even Arbitrators need to let their hair down once in a while, right?"

2f72899d-4b8f-4ac5-a1e5-c35886099cdc.Text: "Wrong. I was calculating how easy it would be to isolate the place if a drunken witch went berserk."

fa32a1e3-307e-48ad-84ab-5641313ba852.Text: "We both know the law frowns upon the Cold Trade, but you haven't threatened me with punishment like all the rest. Is my charm more powerful than your devotion to protocol?"

4a293892-8bb7-4972-b746-f4afa8c7665a.Text: "Go and charm someone else. An Arbitrator's time is valuable and not to be wasted on petty criminals."

ef35f854-0a1c-463b-a56f-353f6927abf5.Text: "We both kill at the behest of the Undying Emperor. Why are you so desperate to deny our similarities, Amic'Solomorne?"

8f8b04b0-5507-4e06-bf83-5868085a676d.Text: "Because I do not carry out executions in an intoxicant-fuelled haze. Because I do not make a gory spectacle out of my solemn duty. And because I was granted my right to judge by the Imperium, not some below-decks sect."

93dba1b4-fe1c-4af1-bfb3-d4a4aa41f25f.Text: "You keep glaring at me, mon-keigh, but you have nothing to worry about. Your anger is too bland for me. And predictable — I just have to ask which part of your beast I should cut off first..."

12285796-a3d2-4676-b6d9-695d698affc3.Text: "The blessed technologies forged by the servants of the Omnissiah are the greatest gift bestowed upon the Adeptus Arbites and a symbol of the functional alliance between us."

01e4e73c-3eee-412b-be10-58e711292f45.Text: "You are right. The metal of duty in my heart, the metal of weapons in my hands — your gifts complete the face of justice."

d6155851-bc2d-400e-a1b6-efacaed50f14.Text: "You seem a competent officer, Werserian. It is all the more strange that your subordinates lack discipline: yesterday three visitors more than the maximum limit were permitted on the bridge."

4c6e57b4-286c-422c-b1ef-6286f6c1cfd7.Text: "You would be better served keeping a closer watch on your dog rather than the people on the bridge. There are as many of them as the Lord Captain requires, not one more."

cd86f977-0639-4a79-8e96-971c1076ae67.Text: "You could have been an Arbitrator, Sister. Why did the mentors in the Schola Progenium direct you down a different path?"

0e3f56ea-c896-493b-8cf6-0ea1d0bdc45b.Text: "Because my heart burns with faith and hungers for great deeds in His name. Yours is but a list of laws."

2a051759-a977-442e-8c53-4265b8e0d049.Text: "I have seen a few of your paintings, Lady Navigator. Is it some kind of clever code? I would swear there was no meaning behind that mess of brushstrokes."

c84f7066-416f-4354-83c1-bcbf70bb032a.Text: "Your colours turn leaden when you talk about my paintings. Do not trouble yourself, Proctor. Art is simply... not for you."

a95de4e3-67b5-4071-98dc-07204d6b2221.Text: "Master Interrogator, may I ask for what purpose you recently tested my knowledge of the laws of the sector?"

aacd2b9b-2bb3-46bb-8c8e-36ab444d1f83.Text: "Some missions require not only physical strength, but also a solid intellect. I was wondering if you would be suited to more demanding tasks."

b10a5659-4ff6-4604-b91a-e2923791e162.Text: "Every time I see you, my hand reaches for my weapon. It's nothing personal — I will forever be astounded that a witch is allowed to live."

5ef04890-df66-4527-ace2-dacbb236e9a3.Text: "Hang on, since when do you have a personality? Look at that, our resident killjoy doesn't just talk in Lex paragraphs!"

114345b4-b48f-41fa-8a3c-fb45ffb1908d.Text: "You have excellent tactical thinking, and you are effective in combat. You could accomplish much in service to the Imperium, but you are squandering your talents."

9cc0a11b-7258-4ca7-ad28-7051f637d738.Text: "Oh, I see where this is going! You lure me in with the convincing flattery, and before I know it I'm being yelled at like a disobedient hound."

1200f0d7-a702-4959-a9cb-56bea88ed3db.Text: "You do not realise the dangers of living outside the Imperial Law. You are playing with fire, and one day you will pay for every act of mob justice you have committed."

0e794c8d-26c2-40d2-9a97-ec5b66629eb7.Text: "You see a threat in my rituals. But in truth, your greatest enemy is fear. I am not afraid to walk along the knife edge of the law you so revere. Or to act against it, if it means staying true to the Undying One."

6c57dc9d-71f8-41a3-bc89-60f9f7f1f1d0.Text: "I saw a preserved Drukhari head once, back in Calixis. For a long time, I didn't believe something so disgusting could really exist, and I was wrong — you're even worse alive."

4e6e51b7-0e84-49ca-a5de-a5dd533f379d.Text: "Incredible. Strong, stupid, and ugly — you are the perfect raw material for a Wrack. A Haemonculus would scarcely have to lift a finger."

33a2f1f9-2abf-4ef2-b91e-2e9ebdcf447e.Text: "Glaito's visors are in perfect working order — you put the Tech-Priests of the Calixis Sector to shame, Pasqal. I owe you a case of the finest sacred unguents."

7a820a0d-2274-44ea-b878-34ba8584ca07.Text: "Proposal to make an offering accepted. Requesting a verbal exchange of information — topic: the merits of the Glaito tech-unit in relation to less blessed units."

90793beb-146d-48c7-a8be-7340fac5aeb7.Text: "Lord Ulfar, please do not be angry — sometimes in your presence, Glaito goes on high alert. It... is a regrettable error."

4245e743-9529-45bd-a711-9530016d0d43.Text: "Why should I be angry? The beast senses his master's fear, so he bares his fangs. And you fear me, lawkeeper, as a dog fears the Fenrisian wolf."

56d6d9f7-718f-432f-9bcc-67c8caf31dbf.Text: "The Lex Imperialis states: a xenos accepted into the service of a bearer of the Sacred Warrant shall conduct itself with humility and obey the orders of—"

cf12843f-fadc-4872-8703-69b338996a1e.Text: "Once again, you try to pin down with words what the mind cannot comprehend. Instead of questions — hatred. Instead of knowledge — voluntary shackles. Your species lives in terror of freedom..."

8f62ff2f-511e-44cd-ae31-c5a1d84bfafe.Text: "A hound, of course, is a fine companion, but what is a dog next to a wolf? Now that is true fury, true strength and prowess!"

6caaedf8-923f-448e-b9c4-eb55108ee792.Text: "Lord Ulfar, it may well cost me my life, but I'll speak plainly — Glaito is better than any wolf. Not even the words of an Angel of the Emperor can change my mind."

c54ded54-d015-4e55-889c-b997e72a0596.Text: "Your efforts to bring order only lead to greater ruin. If you would accept the world in its imperfect state... it would ease your existence."

477e4be2-e338-4a4f-9078-9c4abed81ae2.Text: "It would ease your existence, xenos, if this servant of the Lex gave way to weakness and heeded your foul talk. But that is not going to happen."

4f340b21-5422-4fac-88e2-d2fd194c0ca1.Text: "I've witnessed ordinary people commit worse deeds. It disgusts me to realise that when it comes to treachery and sacrilege, humans often surpass genetic abominations."

1e9f3c91-eb65-4aae-ab30-fe61aee9583c.Text: "That ship has sailed, Werserian. The cultist already thought herself chosen before, all because of some whisper she alone could hear. And now that she has had a taste of greater power, there is no chance that she will stop."

49d1114c-5ee3-4761-95ca-362ce90c822a.Text: "The den of the cultists who have made a parody of justice... Their sole redeeming quality is that they are really ready to die for the Emperor."

d54fbccf-7455-4a7c-81b8-867dfbf43840.Text: "Uh-huh, but not before they kill for Him, and then kill some more. And not just people who deserve it."

69931164-2414-4fdd-a61f-6c136978d44a.Text: "Where an Asuryani finds gratification in resemblance, you find only bitterness. I will never understand your kind's aversion to connection."

fb4283b4-bdb2-494a-9f37-3eb462fd0a5f.Text: "With the cultist dead and the sect's current leader being old, the flagship has the opportunity to rid itself of the heresy of mob justice."

b3c23e8e-4454-436d-a3e3-6337069b8e24.Text: "I cannot help but feel sorry for the Vizsier's loss. For all his fortitude and reverence for death, to lose a child... is a terrible thing."

aa7d6637-84f4-410b-bc33-79864d26d698.Text: "It is not a just fate for your kindred that concerns you, mon-keigh. No, you only wish that the right to judge and condemn belonged solely to you and those like you. Executioners."

ed5b85a4-eb9a-4d3c-b358-8e31141a76a4.Text: "The Rogue Trader's desire to put {mf|his|her} ship in order does {mf|him|her} credit. Or else, it points to the grave incompetence of your enforcers, Werserian."

73457d22-f4ae-4940-a49b-73637647bf90.Text: "I am certain that the sight of the sacred Warrant leaves a stronger impression than some ludicrous ritual performed under a stream of blood. The Rogue Trader will choose the right path."

2026658e-1d08-4644-b333-4326db4ffcbf.Text: "All prospective Arbitrators must first endure the loss of their parents — it tempers us, and duty becomes our sole pillar. You, however, will likely grow only more unstable after your father's death."

5037335e-a18e-4ae7-9604-db27aff42764.Text: "Glaito, heel. If even the witch is restless, then we must be headed for trouble."

bc29688b-cf0f-45e1-96b9-58ffac0cce9f.Text: "There is frost all over Glaito's coat. Whatever problem we are here to solve, let's do it quickly."

53d33580-7c2b-47a4-97d3-0f09846eab56.Text: "Maybe they are here so that overeager lunatics do not disturb them. With you on board, I would have packed this crypt with traps charged with the machine spark."

080a3cdf-7948-4907-80ea-1f30dcf30f39.Text: "The ones crying should be the souls of the honoured dead who are forced to tolerate the company of xenos carrion."

1ce857ed-5f18-4fae-b647-f3cf93e7a753.Text: "They may not be heretics, but what they do here is a mockery of true justice."

ab25c32d-aa6d-4310-8be5-8c56243847eb.Text: "There is no majesty here — true bringers of His judgement have no need to hide in the darkness."

4cb5773b-a9f2-4555-8781-47d2e0cd18e4.Text: "At moments like this, I sometimes wonder how Glaito perceives such environments, what with all the sensors in his nose — and then I always order myself to think about something else."

4c73ebc7-e938-4bdd-8a63-cd1b83f6640d.Text: "Not one sacred codex of the Lex Imperialis in sight. How can you call this place a chapel if it doesn't have His words?"

4360d8f0-3477-456a-b5af-0dd507a6d25b.Text: "And what kind of prayers would people say here then? 'May we never miss our tithe shipment date, may we forever abide by the grade Solutio Whateveris...' I shouldn't even joke about it — I bet that's exactly how you pray."

628dff5f-d8a7-4c81-988d-2986570f62c3.Text: "I never thought the Adeptus Arbites in the Expanse would cease to exist. I wonder what Lady Theodora would have to say about this..."

1d393b4d-8e80-4c97-99d5-5922deed0d84.Text: "Considering the incident with the watcher of Leethus, I would say she planned for this exact scenario."

622f9eec-bc9b-4741-be5b-3d4bc87cf4c2.Text: "The more interesting question is, who is going to collect and guard the tithe now? It seems the sacred tribute is about to become a much easier target... for pirates and other enemies of the Imperium, of course!"

1ea6c45d-4df1-42b9-9fd0-31f0b596564d.Text: "The Marshal's poor judgement led to the fall of the Adeptus Arbites in the Expanse. As the leader of my House, I must learn from this cautionary tale."

d64e8c2b-9059-4cfa-8dbd-a010647d8583.Text: "He fell the moment he chose to heed the whispers of a shrivelled viper instead of his battle comrades. Such disgrace for a warrior!"

87b4f094-ab70-4b77-aa4d-c963a78f293c.Text: "What cannot be taken by force may be obtained through cunning. That mon-keigh appeared as a monolith on the outside, yet he left cracks in his inner armour."

d8a3ed8d-05b3-4140-b726-724a78b1cfd7.Text: "The very idea of steering a voidship into the warp without the protection of the Geller field! Pure madness! I am appalled that the Arbitrators failed to consider such risks and put the Lord Captain's life in danger."

9a2e230d-1a76-4947-b313-1e9c2af0fb77.Text: "I'd say it was the Lord Captain's kind of escapade. Sure, my head almost burst when my whispers found it hilarious that a whole ship was about to perish in the Immaterium — but who would ask after a witch's health, am I right?"

8c1f4811-faa2-4575-b59d-3526405bc62f.Text: "The Rogue Trader deftly handled all the complications that arose during the mission. {mf|He|She} definitely does not require anyone's protection."

077f6a4b-3daf-4d52-ab90-5ee367b6431e.Text: "The battle aboard the Heartless was a difficult trial, but we prevailed! Is there anything like a triumph against all odds to inspire us to new deeds of glory?"

e0dc0e83-7ffb-4dd2-aac0-3cb5e2380751.Text: "I would readily board a hundred pirate ships just to see you pleased again, Sister!"

477568e4-74d7-4735-b92c-97cfaa47e046.Text: "The Heartless was engulfed in every shade of horror when it almost plunged into the Immaterium... It was a costly triumph, and a valuable lesson."

b8ebcdef-fc68-47c6-a825-0289412bee58.Text: "I identify Captain Sargona's blasphemous attempts to combine creations of the Adeptus Mechanicus with xenotech as effective, and thus, that much more egregious."

21ed26e7-7976-4202-b66f-24af15d86627.Text: "I would bet a crate of amasec that you were biting your mechadendrites because you couldn't poke your head inside those pirate handicrafts."

9ecd94ae-fc90-411e-974f-11c31fb17ba5.Text: "The Rogue Trader should have purged the pirate vessel with fire. Even a fragment of a ship like that could become a carrier of corruption!"

01951bf4-475e-45ea-ad56-4ecffc99c5df.Text: "A fine battle that was, but it was not as satisfying without a feast on board the captured drekkar."

631043d2-5a0c-432b-8551-d30d32b3cd6b.Text: "I fear that your celebration would have substantially increased the repair costs for the Rogue Trader."

aad68ba0-f589-4d9e-a0c8-cdcc6386f5d1.Text: "Of course you would say that. You simply cannot resist spoiling the aftertaste of a good slaughter with sour drinks and half-witted verses."

f1b62886-64ef-4a40-813d-52792a9805e4.Text: "I used to dream of visiting a feudal world, a land straight out of the pages of heroic chronicles. But now... Now, I dream of forgetting that place — the sooner the better."

43edda06-5056-4d21-a1fa-c590549c6e32.Text: "Oh, Cass, I should have warned you we were going to a lustreless hole. And maybe offered you a drink from my flask before the landing..."

f41c53f9-e520-4852-a567-91ef77f8f70e.Text: "It pains me to say this, but I believe visiting Thassera was beneficial for you. Such experiences... greatly expand one's horizons."

d4ead611-393e-451a-8c91-ea3ad41580ba.Text: "Mu-class worlds are of negligible importance due to the level of sacred technology being undeserving of attention. Requesting permission not to disembark upon arrival on other similarly wretched planets."

443b275e-e2b4-42aa-9716-0cc4610218c1.Text: "I thought you'd be excited. The most advanced cog on the whole world — so much attention and adoration!"

eb041106-ee86-48d8-8de9-f7147b198831.Text: "I too find underdeveloped worlds repulsive, but when duty calls, there is no choice but to go."

fac6226f-38d4-43c6-88e5-29288935ac34.Text: "I can hardly believe that the governor of Thassera managed to deceive his subjects so easily. Was no one suspicious of the decoy ruler's manners?"

c4337bb6-0433-47ad-bf4e-b45c2cd04ed1.Text: "Thassera is a feudal world, Lady Cassia. Anyone who blows their nose using a handkercher instead of their hand can pass as a noble."

e1c195e3-62da-43e2-8b0f-386a47ed2497.Text: "The common people do not always know who rules them. I am sure there are some aboard the Rogue Trader's ship who still do not know about Theodora's death."

a9f962bf-e96a-41e2-ac00-379168cb7f2e.Text: "The watcher of Leethus... I still cannot believe Lady Theodora kept such terrible secrets from us. What else do we not know?"

f97f0b6c-16b6-4c20-a76e-105ad43a0150.Text: "This is Lady Theodora we're talking about, old man. She was operating on a scale far beyond our understanding. Wasting a planet wasn't much of a play for her."

19420dfe-bf94-4725-ae0b-05d9a2d8af2f.Text: "Some mysteries can vanish into the void for centuries. We may consider ourselves lucky that this secret of the dynasty was unearthed at all."

b7605e7c-a414-4553-98c6-6cb07a30c6f3.Text: "Along with Leethus, the following venerated mechanisms were destroyed: loading platforms, industrial manipulators, automated guide rails, class C/1-0-5 transporters..."

9adf721d-5a33-4929-a19d-ff5a417f0551.Text: "You know, there was a guy on Leethus who also liked listing things until it fried his implant. Alas, some people are deaf to lessons of wisdom!"

359e3d99-9d76-48af-9c6d-c5843e5f0a63.Text: "I cannot fathom why droning on about lumps of metal fills you with such pain, but do go on... I am all ears."

f794110b-c9aa-4a98-80f1-abb3444da7b8.Text: "Will the mon-keigh repeat their error and carry on locking away their resources, or will they let them flow freely, nourishing their worlds with life?"

88f4ec37-fc99-44dd-8638-922b5482c336.Text: "It seems unlikely that a xenos would be concerned about Humanity's prosperity. I suspect this is nothing but an attempt to impose your views on other species."

42227614-e196-429c-bfe9-169f7c6ff6d3.Text: "A life of satiety clouds the mind and rots the spirit. It is hardship that makes the Domin's subjects stronger."

f240ee07-145a-4709-a232-101f47fff045.Text: "That trial... Those people weren't allowed a chance to atone for their guilt in battle, fighting in His name. A death without repentance in the crucible of combat is wrong."

0b590fbb-a3c1-40dc-90fd-115c3c57758a.Text: "Anyone who severs people's threads as they see fit puts their intent above the will of the Undying Emperor. One day, His whisper will sound as thunder over their heads."

ccd71ff4-e927-4a59-b2d4-b70abfa3f66c.Text: "Not all criminals deserve the privilege of redemption. Far from it."

08a96bf3-10b8-4bf9-8963-6a6f34fe1901.Text: "I am beginning to see why Lady Theodora barely ever sat in the judge's seat. Such proceedings cause more harm than good."

25a15b58-88b7-4fbf-a485-abd80efbe927.Text: "Have you never considered that some things are more important than the dynasty prospering, Werserian? Things such as the triumph of the Emperor's Law and the inevitability of justice, to name two."

fb500a2b-b9e3-4f7a-ba5a-77b1cc784109.Text: "My tutelage prepared me to make decisions in contentious situations. But that trial... would have proved a challenge. To me, and to my late mentor, Theobald, as well."

e1d5daef-d52b-4aae-a1b6-df19a170398b.Text: "A depressing spectacle. The only trial worth holding is one that ends in single combat in a circle of shield-bearers, with a fine verse ringing in the air!"

76f97614-f08b-4c85-a818-73f36370d7f0.Text: "Big man, words can't express what a shame it is that you're not in charge of the rules at the Palace of Justice!"

858bd133-29b2-4ec6-bb47-5350929c1e80.Text: "Yes, even a primitive skirmish would have added a whit of animation to that farce."

9d6dc863-11ed-42d4-a29b-dc3c625e7213.Text: "Mon-keigh trials are so full of delusion... At least my dark cousins are open in their ambitions and do not offer a false impression that the accused might walk free."

157b97f9-f3e5-4578-a2bf-5ca022e8bf69.Text: "Ha! Your existence among the mon-keigh must have truly gotten to you if you have begun to sing praises to our ways."

5ee0c452-72f5-49a0-99e5-3d5e4c90fef0.Text: "I think you're forgetting the fact that one can only leave a Drukhari trial in pieces, after some long, looong torture. But who cares, as long as you get to lambaste the 'mon-keigh,' am I right?"

0fc3c617-3214-4a24-817c-c19050971a79.Text: "That old kaskha! She almost outsmarted us. I hope the Exalted One judges her soul harshly!"

65afd6f5-e05b-4f28-bf60-9bdd65736610.Text: "With age comes experience. The prefect turned out to be better versed than the rest of us combined."

94a90408-805c-47b3-bdc6-b6c56ddde640.Text: "Vultur miscalculated when she thought that controlling the Marshal meant controlling the Lex Imperialis. The Emperor's Law cannot be deceived, bribed, or distorted."

b996d79b-db09-46dc-a076-7ceeefad90d4.Text: "I hope the Administratum learns from these events and ensures that Dargonus sees no more of such dangerous careerists as Vultur."

4cfee753-3b68-4455-bca7-32ad5a0a0470.Text: "They will do that, but for their own reasons: once a new prefect is chosen, it's going to be a bureaucratic nightmare. The Administratum will not want to go through that again."

0fa20782-2ed2-48f5-beb3-5c2cf56f846e.Text: "I always thought that servants of the Administratum had hearts of ink, that they were indifferent to power struggles. Now I see that they are no strangers to intrigue."

674d046b-7628-46bb-8fbe-4793715da2e1.Text: "Who will become the new Marshal of the Expanse? I assume the number of candidates has dwindled after the battle in court..."

72b2a2bb-fdd5-4156-8f01-5a875f4bf7ad.Text: "The Adeptus Arbites has indeed sustained losses, but that does not make it any easier to find a replacement. The choice must be made based on merit, not out of necessity."

a6349abd-e2ed-4e1a-8ee6-efcd56c84d1b.Text: "Can the mon-keigh draw wisdom from tragedy and follow a new path? Sometimes, calamity is not the end, but the impetus for renewal."

bd076e17-57a4-4ca0-842c-6d3ba39566d5.Text: "I just don't get it: why didn't the Lord Captain make Master Killjoy the new Marshal? He's the most hard-headed, immovable boulder of a lawman in the sector — what other qualities are there to look for?"

ab9a1504-f6c7-4dbd-890f-8a7dea481861.Text: "I do not discuss my orders, witch — I do what must be done without hesitation. I am already honoured that the Rogue Trader commanded me to choose the new Marshal."

fa8dd9ec-988c-49e7-abcc-0ff998669939.Text: "You speak of the same paltriness of thought that made the last mon-keigh such a convenient instrument in another's hands. It is obvious that the Rogue Trader does not want to let another fool come to power."

867a42ce-4a44-427f-88c6-9551458f8dfd.Text: "Our killjoy had a real chance of becoming the first Arbitrator in the sector's history who ended his days in prison! A waste of a good legend, if you ask me."

2ccc178d-d32c-41f1-a4e7-fca5465abc0c.Text: "Be silent, witch. You know not how bitterly remorse may haunt someone, or how those who truly believe always choose their own punishment."

42dadf16-0c57-4f24-a0cd-75f02e91b012.Text: "The Lord Captain's mercy is great indeed — the Proctor had better remember it well and remain grateful for the rest of his life."

d869f8f9-3e9b-48b8-90a6-c87adfa55da4.Text: "I congratulate the unit Solomorne on his return from suspension of function. Let the protocols of service be renewed, and let there be no change of authorised ownership for the tech-unit Glaito."

a46b9940-38ab-4bae-8e67-62044b8e88a1.Text: "Thank you, Pasqal. I wish my head were full of cogs so you could always open it and make repairs the same way you do for Glaito."

a7fab33e-e7d5-4c8d-a812-852d530ae9c6.Text: "A Tech-Priest being sentimental about something that isn't made solely of metal? You would have an easier time convincing me that our Proctor is actually a very advanced combat servitor model!"

39e19623-f77c-4a93-b30a-efa428828a14.Text: "The sheer duplicity! After everything the Lord Captain did for the Arbites, Solomorne still betrayed {mf|him|her}."

badbe79f-08a2-4ec4-9dbf-6a18b6f21637.Text: "The lawkeeper was loyal to his scripture — he fought and died for it. Unshaken till the end — a worthy death for a mere mortal."

a824d818-08c1-443c-949d-abc26106a62d.Text: "Amic'Solomorne was wrong. The Domin stands above the law, for {mf|he|she} is the extension of the Undying One's will. That is why He whispered the name of His servant."

6811233f-2a09-4557-848b-73ad45bb1591.Text: "At least that dull mon-keigh did something interesting before he died. The way he bit his master's hand was bland and inelegant, but I suppose that is better than nothing."

5dad1b02-6354-4059-abb2-794a6cb0f72c.Text: "The Proctor's colours never once wavered. He would not be able to live with himself had he allowed them to be mixed with grey."

a6fe0e3e-fa70-4415-a84e-91ddefcc8cb2.Text: "His path was a fallacy from beginning to end. And even though the elantach offered him {mf|his|her} hand in hopes of guiding him onto a different road, unwanted help never bears fruit."

66f72caa-9f42-409b-b1ab-0757314e31fd.Text: "So, you are going to assume the position of Marshal of the Koronus Expanse. What changes should we expect after you enter office?"

db2995c3-c78d-424b-a448-f9da3205fd20.Text: "It is too early to say at this point — due to the internal Arbites procedures, the transition might take quite a while. Much could change by the time I receive my assignment."

5f75fc2d-f337-4219-a96e-8fa3303decae.Text: "Is there even a point in asking? We'll die of old age by the time that assembly of killjoys signs all the right papers. Sure, dismissing a Marshal is a day's work, but choosing a new one? That's a procedure!"

29a68909-ebd4-4d36-87f5-3eef55cbf456.Text: "So then, lawkeeper, has the Aett-Vater endowed you with great power? Will you march onto the battlefield as before, or be content with the warmth of your chambers?"

f749ac9e-cdf8-45f0-8efe-e6ef416787a3.Text: "Considering how few Arbitrators are left in the Expanse, it is highly likely there will be enough combat missions for the Marshal to go on."

234a999f-2eda-4624-8c95-47fd501ee3e2.Text: "That reminds me: I should thank the Lord Captain for not letting me waste away doing paperwork like so many other officers."

57364749-c1a4-47e3-9e7c-9d4d6b74d9b6.Text: "Since you have now officially joined the Rogue Trader's retinue, Proctor, let me remind you that the Lord Captain's word is law to you from here on out."

f98fd505-f0ce-4f55-af8a-45ff236ca51f.Text: "You are mistaken, Werserian. There is only the God-Emperor's Law, which means it is the only law I will ever obey. I am surprised you would think it might be otherwise."

bbcc76db-0aae-4002-ac67-9e28e1ed610c.Text: "You waste your words. He is a shadow of your throned god's will — a blind weapon. And thus, he will never understand why we follow the elantach."

28ace607-d2e0-4095-b6cd-8af53a651725.Text: "I am elated to see new devout servants of the God-Emperor joining the ranks of the Rogue Trader's retinue!"

66ee6bc6-0f41-44c0-bfa7-f56b052409f9.Text: "You meant to say, 'new fanatics who shoot first and ask questions later,' right?"

fd4be31b-e150-42a6-804e-58f2185b62fe.Text: "Oh, Exalted One, why did You have to send me a lawman with a book for a heart and a rock for a face instead of another enchanting sister? Surely that isn't too much to ask?"

1c3dcf3e-38c0-4825-9f12-5cf82c62d9a7.Text: "I cannot shake the feeling that the Proctor was given to us not to act as a bodyguard, but rather to serve as the Arbitrators' inside agent."

642492d0-0a51-4880-b401-0dc840cef289.Text: "You should know, Master Interrogator. Better than anyone."

d373f685-a1ef-4aa4-9000-686e6af1b03d.Text: "What, does the bloodhound not like sharing territory with other dogs? At least this one is not the slippery sort and knows the meaning of honour."

a6078fd6-ad65-4f32-8e30-a38ed1e01c86.Text: "Another crew's deck under my boots, the flare of emergency lights — it has been a spell since I last went on a boarding mission. Why, I feel a decade younger!"

7de48d9b-4c82-4280-ae01-ec33ec9ed80f.Text: "I feel just as invigorated in anticipation of a battle with heretics! Onward!"

e3133cb7-3f37-459b-8567-e35e515f6737.Text: "While perusing the Lord Captain's library, I discovered the memoirs of the greatest quartermaster who has ever served the von Valancius dynasty — Silverto de Iono. His sly tactics will be of great help to us during this boarding operation."

41e19633-d087-4619-a682-1b84ea6a674b.Text: "Forgive my bluntness, Lady Cassia, but there is not a book in existence that can describe the full spectrum of things that typically go wrong on a boarding mission. It is better that you rely on my practical experience instead."

3b562014-7e7a-4412-8ea0-def841e8ed3e.Text: "Is this the drekkar we are to take for the Aett-Vater? Ha! Barely enough for a mighty wolf to sink one fang into!"

6e9bb452-807f-46a6-b0f0-d75cc5078db6.Text: "I'll wager the ship's defenders would be less terrified to see a cruiser appear on their augurs than to watch you charge at them across the deck."

44f5888e-d93b-4166-80d1-83c3f31adb18.Text: "This ship has potential! Once we refit the hull, replace the officers, and make a few other changes here and there, it won't be so bad at all."

5e596320-47f9-4b20-bcef-2522c0bb9fac.Text: "My whispers are laughing up a storm listening to you make renovation plans for a ship you haven't captured yet. Oh, something tells me that whatever's made them so happy, we won't like it one bit."

890410a7-d6b9-4afe-8be4-aada9b97f3c2.Text: "The air is suffused with the fear of prey that has nowhere to run from this mon-keigh bucket — all it can do is wait for the hunters to come..."

715d470f-1c7d-4d82-9c8e-0fe34d1a90e9.Text: "May the Exalted One forgive me, but, for once, I am glad that ashmag is on our side! Why don't we let him go first and wait a little while?"

1fe66ff6-efdd-4e48-8fe9-bf1085bb4cf9.Text: "This vessel must be nourished with the blood of the Domin's enemies, for such is His will. Let the Bloodspun Web stretch across its bowels. Let it sever the apostates' threads."

38ea43fe-d36a-4cde-9349-4eb5317e9879.Text: "A correlation between the functioning of voidship systems and their contact with organic fluids exists only in this laywoman's agitated consciousness."

2e8ba89e-0668-441c-b161-1617e97e115a.Text: "As a child, I was captivated by the chronicles of the feudal world Erbenn II. Knights clad in shining armour riding their fine steeds, battling enemies of Humanity, and holding feasts after their victories... But this world has only grey. And mud."

3b03d0bc-682f-4b32-a0f5-8ea561d69582.Text: "The same is true for many worlds in the Imperium, Lady Cassia. You should accustom yourself to that fact."

b6623376-6ddb-4e43-9278-87ec0a22351e.Text: "The Arbitrators' arrival was certainly a welcome sight. Hopefully they will help to put things back in order around here."

0b4aacbb-27b6-4663-a939-6aca5e15c25e.Text: "Not happening, old man — all they care about is the tithe. Even if the Koronus Expanse turned upside down, they wouldn't bat an eye."

95981eeb-9011-4329-a14b-43f7a64c91fd.Text: "So that is how servants of the law operate! Such coordination, such a wealth of scarlet and gold..."

b56b245f-1688-48a8-bf3c-3937781b738d.Text: "Their dance of blood is more akin to a march. And yet, I sense a kinship in our drive to execute those who offend the Undying Emperor."

aba67fa1-e7f2-4f00-9896-e149a2ebf491.Text: "By the Exalted One, how many treasures lie hidden in this maze? There is only one way to find out..."

469bdca8-e625-475f-86a6-89806460ab4f.Text: "For you, there is only one way indeed — by looking, with both your hands where I can see them, while standing at a respectful distance from the sacred tithe."

3e694c85-a7a2-4ab1-acc5-ac26bfcd13b7.Text: "Requesting permission to rescue valuable technology from this maw of entropy and cesspool of violated storage regulations."

5880fdb1-d5dd-4b94-b5c7-7a8f357c916a.Text: "Pasqal, you are the last person I would want to try for stealing the tithe. Only the Rogue Trader, due to {mf|his|her} unique status, has the authority to remove anything from this planet."

3e49fd18-b743-4904-bb07-7b92decf6fcd.Text: "Judging from our past history of travelling in the Rogue Trader's retinue, I am expecting... profit-related activities to commence any minute now."

e17e1935-1c05-4c07-92a5-40e5adbff668.Text: "Our killjoy's head is going to explode. 'The Rogue Trader is taking things from the tithe! What do I do? How do I judge?'"

edb3067d-40c0-4ee1-af28-f149209f1ce0.Text: "Whatever is the matter, Proctor? Could it be that the Rogue Trader's presence allows for some relaxation of the Lex Imperialis?"

9debf5e7-2ba6-4ff8-b396-610b920ae86c.Text: "That the Rogue Trader has decided to take something for {mf|himself|herself} does not mean I won't report the loss to the Marshal. Do you want to see your name in the report as well — in a separate row?"

6d936545-8dfb-4300-9af1-d9790a091327.Text: "I am registering a violation of the standards of interaction with objects categorised as 'Imperial Tithe, collected.'"

99ac5f2d-4fd1-442b-b2bd-675cd5036d64.Text: "Strictly speaking, as long as I remain in the Rogue Trader's retinue, anything {mf|he|she} acquires from the storage world is still in the custody of the Arbites... Throne, what do you want me to do, set Glaito on you all?"

3d0f1e22-edce-4568-9b05-2caba7d9f466.Text: "Everything here is seeping pale green. This colour... it strangles me like a chain around my throat."

81a5114e-9c14-4712-a336-ae62895b9ef7.Text: "I can relate to your misery, Cass. When the sight of a planet bursting with riches brings only melancholy to a Cold Trader's heart, she must wonder: is it time to retire?"

c7e3332d-453e-4906-9b5f-28fcb53cf075.Text: "Is this where mon-keigh rulers keep the fortunes they take from their people? What I envisioned as a repository for great artefacts has turned out to be... a dumping ground."

f0fe7a70-3610-4d65-8256-314a7ac679f4.Text: "A dumping ground? No, that's practically a compliment. It's a burial hoard — this is where the tithe goes to die."

1fa00930-ffaf-4ac2-8d68-fdd45912e424.Text: "These people were supposed to bring death to enemies of Humanity, but instead, they became trapped in this place. How many of them died here without ever having experienced the bliss of doing battle in the Emperor's name?"

f4a28034-5a2b-423f-9427-3844220a21a2.Text: "It is a terrible fate to wither in captivity, away from the battlefield. I would be ashamed to look into the Allfather's eyes were I to meet such an end."

b2e054c1-d294-487a-b34e-f9e99cdbeee1.Text: "Ambulls. These things navigate by sensing vibrations in the ground. Everyone, get on top of the crates, or we'll be easy prey for them!"

67d1faaf-ad55-40b8-bd66-55b32496c4b8.Text: "Are those the monsters you fear so? They are but xenos gnats! Hide if your spirit trembles — this proud son of Fenris will go hunting."

d0439fbc-7a62-4cb3-8bb2-2bf692bb55ba.Text: "Only a fool sees the scales as a symbol of impartial judgement. A wise person knows that a deft hand will always tip the scales in the right direction."

7bfb18e5-7ee1-4e33-9873-0d184053d48f.Text: "I never thought I would agree with you, Vil'Jae. The position of the scales matters not if the Undying One's whisper contradicts it. You are living proof of that."

092c95d0-a9c7-4e24-af6e-9a3589c5937d.Text: "I am registering unknown modifications made to the melta weapon. I insist on requisitioning this object for the purpose of ascertaining the permissibility of its configuration."

91fcc02e-7ce0-4482-afc7-d2b1044c543e.Text: "They would probably just send you to the archives digging up records on the Tech-Priest who installed the weapon. Do you have a decade of your life to spare, Pasqal?"

7faacae8-018f-4850-8012-5617caf4f4f6.Text: "Is the threat of death the only thing that can make you abide by your own laws? What other sentient creatures realise intuitively, you enforce through violence."

9b94ce67-4844-4553-bfcf-b728c04ae803.Text: "Do not compare the absolute of the Lex to xenos instincts. The perfection of the Emperor's Law is such that it is not meant to be comprehended. But it is meant to be followed — willingly or otherwise."

6fea7a58-4808-4acb-905e-10509c7802db.Text: "Is this the Lex Imperialis? I expected something heftier."

54aee235-fb54-4e6f-a136-a4c99e11b012.Text: "These are merely excerpts from a few chosen paragraphs. The Lex itself is so vast that all of Dargonus's spires could not hold it."

eb4dc591-5a33-48a5-b980-c033bd5ae4cb.Text: "Oh, Exalted One! The damned ashmags won't even let them explain themselves!"

d8cda858-dafa-4060-86b2-4023cd194c7a.Text: "Very few in the Imperium receive the privilege of a trial. Those people aren't part of that circle."

71c65d84-10b5-4e72-998b-aebcf5aa86c9.Text: "What a waste... You could have let them fight for the right to live — and then killed whoever remained, slowly, basking in their despair."

a3b1fd49-33bd-4548-adf2-57ca2411fed3.Text: "Even you, fiend, I would kill quickly — that is the difference between unholy xenos and servants of the Emperor."

0801fde3-badd-435b-b245-9e341a1d8474.Text: "You would be surprised by all the garbage that heretics spout before death. Staring down the muzzle of a shotgun, they will say anything just to spite their executioner."

c889e46d-39e8-4be0-a2aa-508586e17abc.Text: "I am glad to see you in high spirits. Thoughts about unfinished business get in the way of duty."

a11bc397-2f0b-4f3d-a462-f257622eca31.Text: "My duty in the Expanse is not done as long as there is even a single heretic still breathing."

72165d34-cf58-4d32-82c2-a47092495b8a.Text: "The Administratum is the spine of the Imperium. It gives it cohesion and prevents everything from falling to pieces... But, I'll be damned — I'm glad to be out of that queue."

789ab825-1472-4f70-a616-61702667a30a.Text: "Hmm, so, if the Administratum is the Imperium's spine, then what body part is the Arbites? Its grubby little hands?"

de517159-0226-47e8-a63a-d50d2a20a73a.Text: "Pasqal, I don't know what sort of disagreement you've had with your Tech-Priest comrades, but you can be sure of one thing: Glaito and I will deal with anyone who raises a mechadendrite against you."

c91109b8-8fa1-4cdb-88ef-8a8729e17375.Text: "Prognosis for the unit Solomorne's loyalty confirmed. Raising the unit's priority level. Initiating the clasping of hands in order to complete the unit's authorisation in its elevated status."

27c492c1-6d00-4580-ab05-14d54f37d74b.Text: "Mercy is a trap for the meek."

1b5fbd60-e39a-4ce1-bbac-75be9ef765f8.Text: "I do not question your methods, but compassion for the innocent is not a weakness. We must protect His dearly loved subjects."

34f51284-3525-49d4-801f-8f7c6aa963c5.Text: "A well passed sentence — harsh and fair. Death is no escape from liability."

3f8ef8f3-3aa4-4d19-a2e0-e39e5c773208.Text: "I've been recalling all the reports of missing ships I've seen over the years. In light of this new information, I don't like the implications..."

0833afd1-3387-441e-bc14-40848095df87.Text: "I have met hundreds like you, peddler. You obtain any power at all — and your ambitions run wild until you are in violation of the Lex. Don't push your luck — I am watching you."

80814619-324a-4c26-b8fa-3b4925262237.Text: "Your hues have darkened, Proctor. We ought to prolong our next visit to a world like Janus — such a rich flora is bound to please even your... aesthetic sensibilities."

6d99471e-c8de-4312-b046-61fae475d4c4.Text: "My sensibilities are pleased when an agri-world grows valuable crops registered in the tithe. Yet, for some reason, various despicable cults seem to grow more quickly and profusely."

a31c6fdb-8e2d-4e18-add2-5cc2e204069d.Text: "My condolences, Pasqal. The guilty have already been punished — may you find solace in that."

46ac0288-6bdb-4aa1-871d-3d4825427bb7.Text: "As always, the nobleman worries about the nobility. What I am concerned with is a planet's worth of weapons and technology that the Imperium is not going to receive now. That is the heavy blow here."

32912b59-cae1-4ce2-ac5b-b901e07c9243.Text: "The unit Cubis Delphim was found responsible for the defilement of Kiava Gamma. The corruption of blasphemous modification cast many righteous mechanisms into the pit of villainous heretech. I acknowledge these events as a tragedy."

694c76e4-41f6-4ac5-b517-7a45a8337b39.Text: "Mechanisms again... Don't you grieve for your fellow priests too? Or weren't there enough cogs in them for you?"

fb32fd97-c4d2-4465-b312-d74a8af282e4.Text: "Machines are never to blame for a crime — they performed their function correctly. People, however... People will always fail."

4cdfb324-3db8-4489-a1c6-67b8cc5683b9.Text: "You have just insulted every species of serpent known to Humanity, Sister."

8e693f46-0cbe-49c4-8de6-395ddad6f60d.Text: "You are handling yourself pretty well, Proctor. I did not expect that having a xenos in the Rogue Trader's retinue would discomfit you so little."

6d79f078-3e4e-448a-bb28-97b016c3567e.Text: "I cannot express my disgust at having to put up with the presence of a xenos, but the Rogue Trader is well within {mf|his|her} right. I will grit my teeth and not say a word against the letter of the sacred Warrant."

603976cc-2ff5-4405-a4a3-0de55a46422e.Text: "For the first time, we can agree on something, witch. I can't believe it either."

eb6138fb-9356-478f-9f68-5f2f67f7ce17.Text: "The witch was a ticking time bomb — sooner or later, it would have led to disaster. Well then, one less problem for us."

d010715f-4ffe-4910-8305-cdd267660db6.Text: "And one less friend, you soulless ashmag! Then again, I doubt you even know what the word 'friend' means."

f37b2e2a-9cf9-4167-a097-f1d2bef8cf82.Text: "Walking around a wreck like that is not something anyone would call a pleasant experience. You don't need a Navigator's eye to know that that damned place is going to haunt us all for some time yet."

4cdc4739-c5dd-425b-94ff-834a8d164e51.Text: "That charitable gesture has undermined the stability of the entire sector. Footfall is now a contested territory — it will regret choosing not to starve."

738aea12-1188-4439-8d9f-28d52a6ffaf2.Text: "As long as they are not telling you to slit our throats in our sleep, I see no cause for concern."

a1c489db-32a4-40af-8d59-c0c0e0c87322.Text: "Heat, humidity, vicious fauna — I am tempted to ask what passes for ugly and dangerous among you Navigators."

7d48f54a-cba8-4e7b-be43-70c27e413dcd.Text: "You are far too impressionable for someone who has a hole into the warp inside her skull. Or are you simply insane? Trying to make sense of your chatter is giving me a headache."

30d4fdb3-202a-414a-9295-92ce5555f9c6.Text: "Captivity traumatises ordinary people and strengthens the truly devout. As for people like you, cultist — it only makes you more dangerous and deranged."

f3552c63-baa5-415b-b020-20eef5d4fa29.Text: "It is not your place to speak of pain, Amic'Solomorne. You allowed your own anguish to consume you and turn to anger. My pain is, as ever, a whetstone for the spirit."

ce1cbcef-be9e-4e75-911f-f8f7c12dee86.Text: "An Angel of the Emperor... It is as if His punishing hand had joined the fray."

5e9ea42f-b075-429f-8cf9-7e94635520a5.Text: "Do not be frightened, lawkeeper. Fight well, and my righteous anger will not fall upon you."

ca085235-fe1c-476a-89ff-71a9d30c2dbf.Text: "You have no need to fear me, dog of battle. Now, we are one pack."

6a256158-e916-4803-852e-18f78f45053f.Text: "Glaito is incapable of feeling fear, Lord Ulfar. Or... were you speaking to me just now?"

64ee6661-8e9d-4e6e-830f-f018f94efc8a.Text: "You have already been judged for what you wrought on Dargonus, xenos — and for the very fact of your existence. That you are still alive is merely a temporary suspension."

f44614f4-756c-4faf-9dde-3ce90d1603c0.Text: "Mmm, growl on, little beast. We both know you won't bite without your master's permission."

60574207-f60f-4ca6-9674-17fb0738bbff.Text: "You are guilty, Werserian, but less so than I. You are old, and you seek to please the Rogue Trader in every regard, but for me... there is no excuse."

829e4a42-e08d-470b-9afd-07e5af456509.Text: "Let them attack. We'll see whose heads are more securely attached. Right, Glaito?"

75b7661e-a7c2-4b09-a1ef-ce5f0795681d.Text: "That's a dozen fewer miscreants on these streets. Not much, considering the scale of this place's crimes against Humanity. Still feels good, though."

804ab194-4ed1-40bc-9252-16bca749e3b6.Text: "We have cleared a path for new upstarts who will want to take their place. Which means we gave them the motivation to wreak new carnage on the mon-keigh. The irony."

8d052c66-4b85-4e6e-a333-73aa33d2009c.Text: "No, Pasqal, rejoicing at that miscreant's death is the most natural thing that could occur in this Emperor-damned place."

b9997b83-6a83-4805-98b5-8051adc3a44f.Text: "By killing a Rogue Trader, you violated the Lex Imperialis, Sister, and I would have been forced to judge you accordingly, but... thankfully, I didn't have to."

1812847e-cd0e-46bf-8af5-99bc1dfcd205.Text: "A fool governor, a fool xenos... Warp take me, how I hate blithering fools."

74d71d3b-f194-4b0a-bc27-22ab116a2069.Text: "Yours is a cruel gift, Lady Navigator. I wouldn't want to see the rot in people's souls — what I can see on the outside is more than enough."

8b026279-0cc8-4751-b38d-be157a214cea.Text: "Emperor willing, we'll turn every other part of that xenos buffoon inside out as well."

3cf18edc-de1a-4e6e-b096-532700e1eaa6.Text: "Then it's their mistake. I am not going back."

eb8837d8-e785-4fab-aff0-bbb39289e9ee.Text: "When I was searching for Glaito, a man told me the city of the xenos was boundless and incomprehensible. I think I snapped his neck in a rage — at least now I know he wasn't lying."

5727710d-e1a8-4f8e-ad62-6a5b2c841179.Text: "Kunrad Voigtvir... He has earned himself multiple death sentences by now. He won't escape justice this time."

e24127f8-c1b2-49c7-b864-09f4c9a8df13.Text: "To the void with your justice! I'll turn that bastard inside out before you even start chattering about your precious Lex."

3b52b66d-b76f-49b9-87c4-0c8abfb37835.Text: "The traitor's thread coils like a snake. But now, two sacred executioners are on his trail. The Undying One will have the heretic's black soul for His judgement — I swear it."

f854f6b0-d1cc-4665-964f-70e4ee698bc5.Text: "You are alive, Seneschal. I guess that means that the discipline in our squad is saved. That's the first good news we've had in the past hour."

8f8c4772-9269-41b3-b3dd-353688975a78.Text: "This place has certainly not been kind to us. But people like us will endure anything. Because we have no other choice."

7e9b7df3-0860-4f05-a7b6-48c1ae99c128.Text: "I am registering a surgical intrusion into the Glaito tech-unit with the aim of modification. I express maximum levels of indignation and mourn the loss of the tech-unit's machine purity."

62445e88-90d2-43d4-b114-b83fef38ecf2.Text: "We must fix this, Pasqal, when... if we make it out of here. I put my faith in you."

c7e607fd-8508-4a1b-84f1-a003bc9a6cc1.Text: "The xenos butcher could not break you, Lady Navigator. I am amazed by your fortitude."

4065c3f0-536a-423b-be12-a467e21cb6f2.Text: "From our very first meeting, you thought me weak and frail... Well, Proctor. You were mistaken."

26287a3b-5323-4d45-8892-6c6f27de0e4f.Text: "You have suffered brutal torture, Master Interrogator. Allow me to take the front and shield you from attacks — you are too valuable to take such risks."

131fac96-74f9-4b76-9a38-44d7a3e34915.Text: "Despite my apparent state, I am perfectly capable of dealing with attackers — or at least no less so than an injured Arbitrator. I must decline your offer of protection."

e6a54306-79e7-453b-a149-4adbc6452f2c.Text: "You can still rid us of your presence, xenos, by impaling yourself on the blades of your brethren in a dark alley. That is, of course, if your species knows anything about honour and guilt."

9d3c04be-1823-4fab-8d53-79657e4cbf29.Text: "My species knows of something that will forever lie beyond your grasp — redemption. As we know the dead can never make amends."
