41a2be4b-53b7-4541-b8d1-63d7b0db71ae.Text: {n}After affixing the armour back over his shredded arm, Solomorne mutters through gritted teeth,{/n} "If that is all, I must visit the medbay now. After you, of course."

9377e063-2795-48d0-b5b0-634f362d567f.Text: "I am sure a Rogue Trader can afford the best implants."

395c6e91-2c63-44a7-a575-4759909cc8c2.Text: {n}You carefully bring an open hand closer to the cyber-mastiff's face and wait for his reaction. Glaito's dark eyes are watching you, a crimson spark smouldering within. At last, you touch the back of his neck and start stroking his rough fur, your fingers brushing against the cold edges of the dog's augmetics.{/n}

15aae43a-af3c-494f-a7c8-fff1ecd22a98.Text: {n}The sickening crunch is soon followed by searing pain. And yet, the huge teeth threatening to take your whole limb off sink only briefly into your flesh. Despite the copious amounts of blood, your hand remains in place.{/n}

66d56872-2f9a-4ce2-b81e-5f640718ddb6.Text: "No. I didn't want to. There was a time when I wasn't sure what to think of my father's death. Or rather, I tried not to think at all: I didn't look into the case, or for any other reason to go back to Port Wander — Arbitrators are never assigned to their homeworlds anyway. But when I was leaving Calixis, our ship spent several days docked at the station, and so, I permitted myself to go to the spot where my father was killed. I stood there for a while, and..." {n}Solomorne's eyes stop on you.{/n} "Nothing. I knew that another Arbitrator would already have seen the investigation through. I had nothing left to do there."

8a36c0e0-4ee5-4656-90e0-fa1dc977ae7c.Text: "It's possible. He didn't speak much. Sometimes we went days without saying a word to each other. The only time he was talkative was when he was going through his cases at night. He would inform me in terse and simple words who had sold out and why, what depravities the heretics from the lower hive levels had committed, what base motives the workers had had for hanging their foreman... All I did was listen, watch, and think. That was enough."

2e3e6fa5-ce60-4727-ab39-4fb08eb198f9.Text: "It's all true. I am a second-generation Arbitrator, and my father is as dead as it gets. I wonder if being killed in action runs in the family. I guess I should hold off until I have a kid." {n}Not a muscle twitches in Solomorne's face, making it impossible to tell if he is joking.{/n}

087a7cb4-33c4-41ec-9c0d-edc3d6e1df1e.Text: "Born? I don't believe in predetermination, but I know that every man's destiny is to serve the Imperium. In my case, the Imperium deemed me worthy of an Arbites rank, a heavy shotgun, and Glaito. Not sure what else there is to wish for."

21e25f06-7d62-4e9d-bc96-1bc14302b1bd.Text: "Understood. My response was both inappropriate and disrespectful." {n}Solomorne humbly bows his head.{/n}

ca4b60ab-4f67-4c65-86df-e3f005bbd11f.Text: "I have never been a part of a Rogue Trader's escort before. That said..." {n}Solomorne glances around the bridge.{/n} "I adapt to change more quickly than you might think. And as long as Glaito is with me, I can handle any transition."

abcf7063-e34b-4f93-9202-0f38827efdca.Text: "He did send a message — and the phrasing was unusually heartfelt." {n}Solomorne closes his eyes and quotes in an even, respectful tone:{/n} "'Solomorne Anthar, you are hereby restored to your rank of Proctor. Never allow even a shadow of dishonour to fall on your uniform again.'"

45f385e1-3a4b-4d9e-8b6b-d0b3082c3d5d.Text: {n}Solomorne's stony expression becomes slightly more animated.{/n} "You hear that, Glaito? The Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself} is asking about you."

b3485a99-1e0f-4c37-808a-12f7ae1864e6.Text: "Every word? You don't know the Marshal that well, so you can take it from me."

805e7ee1-d685-4344-b68c-53c60452fd08.Text: "You can say that again. I am still baffled myself." {n}Whether or not Solomorne is in any state of bafflement at all, his face remains impenetrable.{/n}

ad4fa390-dc3a-4a82-8d77-7bb1620a9e77.Text: "His serial number is GL-80. 'Glaito' is easier to say in Gothic. Many give their cyber-mastiffs striking names like 'Slayer' or 'Thunder.' I'm fine with 'Glaito.'"

30a9f40e-6475-4cee-b515-fe28b314a93a.Text: "He mostly provides combat support. He is trained in both lethal and non-lethal ways of disabling a target, with the ability to analyse a situation and then decide on a course of action. Glaito is a good tracker too, and he can spot basic evidence. He also knows over a hundred commands. In general..." {n}Solomorne pauses, looking pensively at the cyber-mastiff sitting at attention.{/n} "He is more resourceful and diligent than most people I've met."

af1a8401-cf99-4ed6-ae15-5292058da9a8.Text: "Firmly. It was your words that pulled me out of that darkness, and you have my gratitude."

cae7bee3-62ca-4709-8a4d-c6e40cf97408.Text: "Glaito is not a pet. He is an instrument of justice. As am I."

f2570c0d-ee96-4d5e-8796-59ea3b7293b8.Text: "My faith has overpowered my disappointment and hatred. It is true that people are weak and full of vices, but that's not what's important. All that matters is that the letter of His Law is perfect, and that it guides me — His word, and nothing else."

3af265ba-2224-40ee-bdbe-5682bc48a5a0.Text: "I've been reflecting on the spirit of His Law and what the Emperor Himself wants for us. If anyone had told me before that I would be thinking about things like that, I probably would have caved their face in. But the truth is, I no longer see heresy in such thoughts. No, it's the opposite: I feel like they bring me closer to the Emperor."

6f4f512f-203e-4eba-ac72-e0e628d101a9.Text: "I still have the same hatred boiling inside me, but now, I have means of releasing it — by bringing it down on criminal carrion, and not just on them. Every doubter, every freethinker, anyone who shows any sign of being unreliable, I will judge as I would an outright heretic. Only then will I make people respect the Lex Imperialis."

995ca72e-0f94-408e-b371-c5c8b24ccf6d.Text: "I haven't had to so far. I do not spend time contemplating such things — it is a fruitless pastime at best."

210d5a51-5c2d-4d80-ab15-7da09a8d1c9a.Text: "Him, or any other weapon that lies in the hands of the law. Only my service to the Lex Imperialis determines the 'level' on which I stand."

106ac7eb-12ff-44b2-b0b6-300e1312b8d4.Text: "Correct. Both his training and his augmetics ensure that Glaito only accepts orders from me or from my superior officers. Apart from having the obvious benefits, it also serves to prevent disarray on missions involving multiple cyber-mastiff handlers."

4f92ad71-052d-4d6d-a197-0817eaca69e5.Text: "Generally, cyber-mastiffs have all aspects of their animal nature removed, but Glaito is a special case. His sub-model takes a dog's loyalty and instincts as a hunter and guard and renders them absolute. He is neither a dog nor a servitor — he is something much more: a cyber-mastiff, a living weapon in service of the law."

b2ba4bc2-5f31-4230-ac4a-28e10767b23a.Text: "Glaito, ready." {n}The cyber-mastiff promptly stands up, and Solomorne starts pointing out the different parts of the dog's body:{/n} "The frame is mostly metal, with armoured plates covering the vital segments. The jaw is reinforced — crunching a leg off is like tearing a hair out for him." {n}He turns Glaito's head to give you a better view of the fangs — as if their terrifying size were not apparent to the naked eye.{/n}

fa396b06-dff7-4614-82c7-879853874e30.Text: {n}Solomorne ruffles the dog's hair, staring straight into its eyes.{/n} "I don't even know a tenth of all the things Glaito is fitted with, but it's an impressive list, to be sure. Take the sensors in his nose, for one — a cyber-mastiff is like an odour analysis laboratory." {n}He pats Glaito on the back.{/n} "All right, that's that. Glaito, attention."

0e554297-937c-42cc-ad70-0e5241a5eafe.Text: "They range from 'kill' and 'guard' and the like to more complex guard and patrol protocols. A protocol is a combination of behavioural patterns, which the cyber-mastiff follows according to the present situation. In other words, I don't have to control Glaito all the time — he can adjust and react to the circumstances on his own."

6c4ab9a0-31e1-4171-900a-63cfcd09eb22.Text: {n}Solomorne says nothing, his attention focused on his dog.{/n}

e416b498-adb8-45ba-9cd2-95ec43b0ddb9.Text: "You understand." {n}Solomorne exhales loudly.{/n} "It has been gnawing at me for so long... I guess I just needed to hear another human being voice my own thoughts. Thank you."

cc3aa569-6c6d-48d7-ae97-f4652c9cd872.Text: {n}Solomorne greets you with his chest thrust out like he was preparing to go into battle.{/n} "Thank you for finding the time to discuss my report. I would ask that we hold this conversation in private. Might I suggest your study, Rogue Trader?"

35bd5a8f-f45b-4eee-89f8-0cdb4a8c0d42.Text: "You need not concern yourself with Glaito. I recently finished checking all his protocols — his responses are instantaneous. I... cannot pretend I haven't missed his companionship."

3c4ee89e-ab39-4d00-bc06-bd7cadeebdaf.Text: "Maybe you're right." {n}Solomorne fixes Glaito's already perfectly straight collar.{/n} "Maybe."

e1e3e273-7998-4681-b0b5-c1b6eeb5ed0f.Text: "I wasn't myself for a while, but I gritted my teeth and started reading the catechisms of the Lex Imperialis from the very beginning, as if I were back in the {g|Encyclopedia:ScholaProgeniumGlossary}Schola Progenium{/g}. Whenever I felt like I might break down again, I locked myself in my cabin and recited the Injuncta Cardinal. And it helped."

f2d03a70-c734-40cd-97a3-2b5cadb6a381.Text: "Good. It is about time we changed the subject."

b0bc0d2f-0f7e-4e9b-a777-0a2b912a5188.Text: "Are you talking about the night we spent together? I do not think we should attach any greater meaning to it than it's worth."

f205d245-3e6c-4965-92e1-01da63937ddc.Text: "Of course, {name}." {n}Solomorne maintains his composure, but his eyes are smiling.{/n}

3f0ee87e-721f-436f-8776-4f581a575f31.Text: "Is anything happening at all? I thought we had cleared this up — I lied, and there is nothing between us that isn't dictated by duty."

d21d0519-3457-42cf-957d-23d94aed2c85.Text: "The most significant ones. Beyond the Expanse, the Arbites not only enforce {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}tithe{/g} collection, but also ensure that every planet obeys His Law and that the Imperium's authority remains unchallenged. Corrupt governors, crime syndicates, rebels — not a minute goes by without some parasite trying to take a bite out of the Imperium. We destroy any who dare trespass against the law."

b0201e3e-a48a-48e5-bbf7-a30e084a4dc5.Text: "You disarm me with your words." {n}Solomorne's voice is quieter than usual, as if this admission does not come easily to him.{/n}

1615f157-bf49-4821-a526-69c11e8b6cf0.Text: {n}His jaw clenched, Solomorne says with a frown,{/n} "If such is your wish, then it is done. I dare not demand an explanation."

40c0540d-ea68-4925-ad15-179dc0cb6e50.Text: "...special? Breathtaking? Dangerous?" {n}Solomorne arches an eyebrow and takes a full step forward. He is standing close to you now, too close.{/n} "It takes two to answer that question. I know what I want." {n}His gaze travels down your body.{/n} "But what is it you want?"

7e486ae6-e39d-4095-af8f-ba24c946a8d2.Text: {n}A warm light appears in his gaze.{/n} "And what happens if I say yes?"

cbdb8bd7-5f41-45d8-a059-0f70a5c8d90c.Text: {n}Solomorne gives a respectful nod.{/n} "As you wish."

91b6087b-0238-4b75-bb6e-2ddd35fd278c.Text: {n}Solomorne's voice is quiet and serious.{/n} "Before I answer that... I overheard your officers talking, and I think that you might break someone's heart. Are you sure this won't feel like a mistake to you later?"

8efe837d-5307-4df8-8295-c12e6b9bacdc.Text: "I am... a little out of my depth here. My life has been one of service, and, in my line of duty, I am more frequently faced with the question of a person's guilt than with my feelings toward them. This is the first time I have felt drawn to anyone like this, so, I hope you can forgive my inexperience."

d61d9c40-db78-4b3f-8d76-7e272501aaf5.Text: "That would be an impediment to service — yours and mine."

cb314e3c-36ae-42e1-926b-27dd3241f5c1.Text: "As you saw for yourself on Rykad Minoris, quite far."

ce05621c-7b13-4cfd-80c6-13d75e159161.Text: "There is no need to worry about her or her people — they are waiting for an opportunity to give the Marshal their report. If there is one thing they do well, it's waiting patiently." {n}Solomorne lowers his voice.{/n} "I didn't tell Yeager about the connection between the watcher of Leethus and Theodora — she doesn't need to know."

9daac29c-0fdd-4820-a7a7-49cc8b1428bc.Text: "By Arbitrator standards, I am already knee-deep in heresy, but, frankly, their condemnation does not deter me. I serve the Emperor as I have never served before; I am no longer blind and shackled — but this realisation only makes the burden of duty heavier. So much needs to be done to protect the Expanse from disaster and strife, but such is the mission I have imposed upon myself."

65266d45-335a-47d9-bf84-0c43318023c3.Text: "Narrow interpretations of the Lex Imperialis are a leash designed to prevent weak and short-sighted Arbitrators from stumbling. I have long since outgrown the confines of this system, and I can see its flaws. If I must break something and build it back up again in the name of keeping order in the Imperium, then that is what I will do."

21eb175a-757e-45c1-a9ed-a8f853aefd4d.Text: "Since you have brought it up — does it trouble you that I have found a new path of service for myself?"

6aadb8ca-de22-4f46-9df6-9613ce4c8946.Text: {n}Solomorne lays his iron hand on his heart.{/n} "It means a lot to me, Rogue Trader — to be not just your travelling companion, but also your ally in the fight for the new understanding of the Lex Imperialis."

75552cda-0a7a-458a-80a3-ba9e6220946e.Text: "I change in order to better serve the Lex — is that not part of my duty?" {n}The Proctor shifts his gaze from you to Glaito.{/n} "I did not expect to hear such words from you, considering... Well, it doesn't matter. You said what you thought you needed to say."

3a3367b3-68ba-465c-ba9c-fe3318ca6521.Text: "I can understand your thought process. Leethus seemed like a cesspit of madness and despair, and since the Arbitrators are in charge of storing the tithe, the conclusion is simple. Simple, but wrong. Try to look at it from a different angle: the Lex Imperialis gives us a clear directive, and all we need to do is follow it. The Guardsmen could have waited in humble obedience. The clerk could have expressed remorse for failing to finish his work. Instead, they chose their weaknesses and vices. So, what is the true cause of harm here, I wonder?"

6c5c6071-e62e-438c-87b8-3e75c4b6f0ae.Text: "Your actions speak for themselves, but..." {n}Solomorne looks you dead in the eye.{/n} "I'll be damned if I don't admit that hearing you confirm your loyalty to the Lex Imperialis in your own words is a welcome respite. With everything around us going to the void, I need to know that we are fighting for the same ideals."

2f1f6d5f-b58e-46f6-8b1b-afc797aa6a66.Text: "Quite far, which comes as an unwelcome surprise to many in the Expanse."

a699685d-303f-4a0e-abaa-b5cbf2927c99.Text: "Rest assured, I won't fail you again. And, as proof of my intent, there is something I must do."

712256a5-960e-4fe0-8020-57b59fc0a1f5.Text: "The Arbites pass the sentence and carry it out summarily. Only the highest echelons of {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Terra{/g} and servants of the Inquisition — and Rogue Traders here in the Expanse — can expect the privilege of a trial. Planetary governors, nobility, clergy — to an Arbitrator, they are all equal before the law."

4688fb65-1202-41af-b5f1-703af4dff9b6.Text: "Better. Sometimes, it feels like I'm slipping, but then I remember what you said, and my head clears."

ea657ae5-d990-464b-a2e6-1c014e773b8e.Text: "Terribly." {n}Solomorne brings his slightly trembling iron hand to his face, then clenches it into a fist.{/n} "But I won't let myself fall apart — one shameful weakness was more than enough."

d959a87f-9075-4236-8df5-f5895e0d1510.Text: {n}Solomorne is busy wiping blood from his augmented arm with a rag. He looks up from his task and gives you a tired nod.{/n} "Rogue Trader?"

6d0878ca-2064-465c-8e74-ff9f38e236b2.Text: "First, we should establish how the xenos themselves leave this place and slither their way to the Koronus Expanse to pillage, slaughter, and take prisoners. Once we have that information, we will need to fight our way to the exit — and for that to succeed, we should already be looking for capable fighters."

28bd0660-2af1-431f-8e66-a2cea6c5b514.Text: "Although, that last part stopped being a concern the moment an Angel of the Emperor joined you. What other reinforcements would we even want, a Dreadnought?"

0104a47f-75ab-49a8-a5ff-8ab93363701c.Text: "I cannot. Not because I do not trust you, but because I do not want my assessments to prompt any rash actions on your part — this may be exactly what our opponent wants. We should go to the Marshal and investigate this matter strictly within the bounds of the Lex Imperialis. It is the only way to avoid a mistake."

7aed070a-f642-4f10-a9fe-8f0d219adbc8.Text: {n}The Proctor nods and goes back to examining Glaito with a grim expression.{/n}

be090b93-766c-4639-b2b3-5df61ac358dc.Text: "Testing me, are you? That is fine by me." {n}Solomorne's tone becomes profound, even solemn:{/n} "The Lex Imperialis is both a code of law and the word of the God-Emperor Himself. For millennia, His decrees have been amassed and preserved on {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Holy Terra{/g}, in the Hall of Judgement, alongside the High Lords' orders. It is at once a titanic collection of edicts and a holy text."

b47c822f-f05a-4d75-b272-d6e034d21f34.Text: {n}A warm light appears in his gaze.{/n} "In that case, my answer to your question is yes."

fb389619-48ce-419d-8d3d-b5baf2947c2a.Text: "That is an order I will be pleased to comply with."

a81a215b-dda0-4285-8aa2-2042de6f586d.Text: "Sometimes, I let him play with heretics' corpses." {n}Solomorne pauses.{/n} "That was a joke. If you're asking about entertainment, that concept does not really apply to an Arbites dog. But I like to imagine that Glaito is enthusiastic about training with me, that he enjoys running long distances at my side. And, during target practice, he always seems eager to hear me give the attack order."

00af0b89-a6f4-4c26-8605-7c3ca4787322.Text: "I am rarely mistaken in such matters, Rogue Trader."

347025fe-2fe4-48e6-8107-a64aec406032.Text: "We have no evidence to suggest that they are the same mercenaries. Our enemy is good at covering their tracks, so we should proceed with equal caution."

555bf601-147f-4c83-891d-14851b9ed4f3.Text: "I have arrived at the same conclusion. Sargona never bit off more than he could chew. Rykad's tithe was too big a prize for him — he would have been targeted both by the Arbites and by any criminals looking to scavenge the shipment piece by piece. Sargona was acting on someone's directive, without fear of the consequences."

a2b62474-bacc-4b25-a6f8-ea7298623b02.Text: "Indeed. It is best that we talk about something else."

bcf2aead-9ecd-4e73-bf32-cdba31c73056.Text: "The Marshal may see this as a sign that the alliance between your dynasty and the Adeptus Arbites is broken. What should I tell him?"

e181e118-9762-4b98-80d6-5bbd69579719.Text: "As you command." {n}The Proctor's expression is impossible to read.{/n}

b60787c9-2ced-4ab3-97e9-06f221b78c2b.Text: "Acknowledged. I will disembark at the first opportunity and deliver your words to the Marshal. Farewell, Rogue Trader."

473af26c-5954-4912-be30-d254a4631751.Text: {n}He lets out a small cough.{/n} "Fine, let me satisfy your curiosity. I do have a special exercise that helps to sharpen Glaito's hunting instincts: I take a few ammo casings and hide them in hard-to-reach places. One time, after a raid on a manufactorum, I gave him a whole abandoned workshop to run around in, but I also played a trick on him by throwing one casing onto a ceiling beam. Then, it was Glaito's turn to play tricks: he waited under the beam until I walked up to him, then, he jumped onto my shoulders and climbed to the top. He cut my temple open with his claw and almost broke my clavicle, but he got the casing."

4f8366b5-ddf0-4b12-9f89-68d1152afc89.Text: "No good? I danced!" {n}Solomorne says as if confessing to an act of heresy.{/n} "I shudder to think what counts as leisure to you if our dance on Thassera wasn't enough."

b37dda54-6ac1-4a18-99b1-225cfcbaa4f9.Text: "Understandable. That trial was unprecedented, as was its ending."

31d69f7b-0cb2-4a44-8093-273bc1e5e148.Text: "That depends on how many of us are found wanting. This will be established during the course of a thorough investigation, but even if only a dozen of us are left in the end, we will still continue to serve His Law until our last breath."

5d8523cc-24ef-4f92-a986-329851e077a8.Text: "Other than unerring service? Actually, I've been thinking a lot lately... about how the Creed stands farther from the God-Emperor than the Lex Imperialis. I want His Law to become the sole pillar of faith for the Arbitrators. I wish to guide them not only as a Marshal, but also as a preacher."

2ee3c574-70c9-468f-8277-e0c82bff4a20.Text: "The Marshal's removal is sure to become a test of the Arbites spirit, but I believe in the Arbitrators' perseverance. We were taught to do our duty no matter the circumstances, and even while we are leaderless, the Lex Imperialis will guide us through."

f262a05b-9992-4001-b2f3-e60c8e785483.Text: "Whatever lies ahead, the Arbites will not interfere in von Valancius matters again." {n}Solomorne's gaze darkens.{/n} "Once the other dynasties take notice, they will almost certainly refuse to cooperate with the Adeptus Arbites. These will be trying times."

4c2ee0dd-8758-4992-8051-7a86efe283d5.Text: "Gregoras Strachs used to be an outstanding servant of the Lex Imperialis, and I still cannot understand why he failed to recognise Vultur as an enemy."

19ccb58e-3c9d-401f-9990-55b8985fe4a4.Text: "I'm inclined to believe that Strachs had grown too distant from the Lex Imperialis. The letter of His Law holds all the answers and solutions, but Strachs faltered in his judgement and turned to Vultur for advice. His waning faith made him blind and led him to a predictable and ignominious end."

9a5382e7-b3b7-4079-8482-4a5c959ad081.Text: "I think that in the end, Gregoras's actions were only human. Trapped in the Koronus Expanse, he was faced with the task of guarding the entirety of the sector's tithe — he needed the wisdom of someone who could lighten his load."

5f4f0b4c-d02a-4fec-88f2-1567f858e224.Text: "I see a far more serious problem in his crime. Both his mentors at the {g|Encyclopedia:ScholaProgeniumGlossary}Schola Progenium{/g} who overlooked his weakness and even Lord Marshal Goreman himself, who granted Strachs his high rank — part of the blame may lie with them. I will never bow down to the senior officers of the Arbites again — any one of them could be unworthy of their station."

82c3e3f6-6844-40f0-926a-da420f7e5f39.Text: "It's everything that can hone Glaito's skills and instincts or otherwise prove useful in our duty."

71c122c0-9a2b-4abd-9a6a-c69057ebed07.Text: "I am thankful to you for sparing Gregoras's life. He would have preferred execution — like all Arbitrators, he feels duty-bound to accept his punishment. I intend to visit my former commander on occasion — I don't want to leave him alone with his guilt."

d94ac78e-8ef4-4beb-a961-0d3539b7f5f1.Text: "So do I. Do you wish to talk about something else?"

266f7dd9-b886-40d2-9f5c-143858552864.Text: {n}In a grim and solemn gesture, Solomorne raises his iron hand.{/n} "I swear never again to take up arms against you. Should our views on the Lex Imperialis diverge once more, I will approach you myself, so that you may decide my fate without delay."

b7aa03f3-dda6-4e17-9d9f-0ec8e2847741.Text: "The Adeptus Arbites in the Koronus Expanse are in need of reorganisation. The recent events have shown that we cannot continue to serve the Lex Imperialis the way we did before — I will use the experience I have gained while travelling with you to ensure that less blood is spilt, both that of the judges and of the convicted. Quite the task, considering that Arbitrators do not know the meaning of redemption or mercy."

7a6b59c1-6537-4036-9cde-7d09262162f3.Text: {n}Solomorne folds his arms and looks up at the lumens on the ceiling.{/n} "By the Lex, I don't even know where to start... Strachs has left me only ruins, and now, the Arbites will have to make up for his disgrace and its own paltry numbers with fierce service such as to inspire terror and awe. I will reforge the Arbitrators into a new elite and begin writing the Lex Koronus in the blood of any who dare show defiance in the face of our mission."

189d02c9-1294-4c53-8969-62eed1ab80cf.Text: "I've decided not to subject him to yet another procedure — the protocol that was making him conduct surveillance has been stopped, after all. We might have need of this function someday, but, for now, it has been disabled — and to the void with it."

2fd7c3a1-63ac-491d-88d2-03cdb082d221.Text: "Like {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}any Arbitrator{/d}, I know the Injuncta Cardinal to the letter. Not a day has passed when I didn't recite the sacred laws from beginning to end — they are carved into my memory as distinctly as they are into the walls of our precinct fortresses and the casings of our ammunition. I would sooner forget my own name than a single word of the Injuncta Cardinal."

da605858-9491-4f83-91f2-e7f6fb87e83b.Text: "{d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}You know as well as I do{/d} there is no point in having such a command, as it would put the cyber-mastiff in a position that makes it harder to attack the enemy. Or are you testing his augmetics? Well, regardless, Glaito is behaving as he should by ignoring someone else's order."

6309eafc-f099-4246-acf9-28317099610b.Text: "Did I... hear you correctly? You want everything to end?"

eb253e7b-f841-4eee-8561-7f971ffa8f0c.Text: "The equipment needs to be sturdy — Glaito is unstoppable when he's not holding back." {n}The corners of Solomorne's mouth curl upward.{/n} "Thank you."

0fe70a45-343b-4813-8713-0128d8b301f6.Text: {n}Solomorne gives an uncertain nod as his wary gaze remains fixed on you.{/n}

48002466-78ef-48d6-b75c-3dcbfe2c940c.Text: "Well, you have made yourself perfectly clear. Let us keep our association strictly related to duty from now on."

c0ed543d-8908-4ee1-b826-28c7ed629466.Text: "No," {n}Solomorne snaps harshly.{/n} "Because there was never a relationship to begin with."

f2d36a88-c118-42ea-bfb3-4ed9e102ec4e.Text: "A betrayal in the ranks of the Arbites had to be investigated quickly and relentlessly — just the right job for a unit specialising in capturing criminals. My fellow Arbitrators rescued me from captivity, and then it was my tormentors' turn to scream."

97297f38-10d5-4ba5-b2ed-c39105958cde.Text: "Rogue Trader. I will be straight with you: I know your {d|Encyclopedia:MiniJealousyRomanceBroken}personal affections{/d} have changed." {n}His expression is as impervious as a wall of ceramite.{/n} "Seeing as everything is already decided, let us return to a strictly professional relationship, as it should have been from the start."

756b8e32-ef46-4758-a44f-79b04809d463.Text: {n}For a moment, your breathing falters and your vision goes dark as {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}ghosts of unbearable pain{/d} overwhelm you. Solomorne's eyes glimmer with understanding, and he falls silent, giving you time to catch your breath.{/n}

88bd4e46-6720-4cdc-b710-b0285d365b10.Text: {n}Solomorne stands with both his thumbs in his belt, looking around the bridge with assertive confidence. He gives you a casual nod as you approach.{/n} "Greetings, Rogue Trader. I would like to report that Glaito and I have finished our initial inspection of the upper decks — the list of infractions ended up being five pages shorter than expected. I'm beginning to worry that a servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:LexImperialisGlossary}Lex{/g} might have little to occupy himself with aboard your ship."

f449c74d-796d-4a1b-90e1-2f86eef8bceb.Text: "What you want to see in me is a flaw — a weakness that would make me a simpler man, easier to understand. But trust me: you don't need a man like that in your escort, nor does the Imperium have use for such servants."

81907a2a-e9cc-4874-b29c-1f6afcf270c1.Text: "It does. Your capital world operates under the Lex Dargonus, formed over many generations of the von Valancius line. However, the Lex Imperialis is the final word in every debate. It stands above any legal directives a planet may have, for it comes from the Emperor Himself."

5d82acf2-5f82-487a-a82d-399dc83d88de.Text: "It would take longer than a lifetime to read through even a fraction of His Law. But there are fundamental, integral prescripts that every Arbitrator knows verbatim. These are the Injuncta Cardinal, inscribed on the walls of the Arbites precinct fortresses and etched into our ammo casings. We quote them as the indisputable truth and recite them like psalms as we charge into battle."

70ab0348-ca77-42ab-96f2-f0e1aeb71372.Text: {n}The cyber-mastiff yawns, casually baring a terrifying arsenal of razor-like teeth.{/n}

bef47458-9c66-4f6b-9734-3c62ab2d32cc.Text: "That is a useless command, Rogue Trader. A cyber-mastiff must always be in an advantageous position to attack the enemy. Glaito can crawl or move stealthily if the situation calls for it, but, regardless, he will not respond to someone else's order."

185194f9-6313-449b-9f89-132742ad3eba.Text: "You demand that I violate not the protocol of cyber-mastiff handling, but the principles of the Adeptus Arbites themselves. Those principles state that Glaito is a weapon, and Arbitrators never use their weapons for the amusement of noble persons."

47b5d566-b879-4a08-8db1-e2523174407b.Text: "If I had a throne for every time I turned down a plea, I would have enough to buy your flagship." {n}He rubs the bridge of his nose.{/n} "For your own preservation, drop this idea of yours."

af6f445d-14d8-4e55-8c9e-5bdd13033239.Text: "Did you hear that, Glaito? It's not often you receive praise from a Rogue Trader. Speak!" {n}The cyber-mastiff lets out a thunderous bark.{/n} "Let's say Glaito has expressed his respect and apologised."

f2cab70b-5fd2-4df6-bb37-03443d376bd7.Text: "I would only ask that you no longer try to... interact with Glaito in this way."

dae32408-bba2-4b24-9257-af146ddf6a9a.Text: {n}Solomorne frowns.{/n} "Glaito, couldn't you honour the Rogue Trader with a lighter bite? Well, you shouldn't blame him. That was a standard warning hold, and pretty clean, too — you will only need a dozen stitches."

0128772f-9b4e-4166-b999-15903bfb02ed.Text: "On Dargonus. Lady Theodora gave the top level of one of the spires over to the Arbites. A noble house used to occupy it, before it decided to stick its hand into the dynasty's coffers... By offering us such prominent lodgings, your predecessor both reinforced her ties to the Arbites and made an unambiguous gesture toward the nobility. She was a shrewd woman, and unforgiving."

f12ffbae-2a5d-4eb4-a23a-36417a95adac.Text: "Unless said man's innocence has been previously established, such as during an investigation. In any other scenario, murder is just a common disturbance. My intervention is only required in the case of an attack on an {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Administratum functionary{/g} or some other important figure — then, I must take measures."

1275428a-ae57-4899-96bb-82eb2699acaa.Text: "However, if I have an assignment to carry out, I will ignore any distracting factors. The duties of the Arbites are above everyday crime: we collect the tithe that feeds the military might of the Imperium and sustains its authority over many worlds. To be bogged down in trivialities is to commit a criminal waste of time and resources that have been granted to us to serve the absolute of the law."

ad8fa94f-f0f6-4560-8119-d17818c87052.Text: "Those are indeed the greatest threat to the Imperium, and I never leave a heretic I meet without a bullet lodged inside them. But such matters are primarily handled by other forces, which are influential enough so as not to be mentioned out loud without a reason."

ad3837aa-b49f-4bf5-9274-dfd4b20b7435.Text: {n}You cannot shake the feeling that your question has offended Solomorne somehow — there is a certain vehemence in the way he describes Glaito's outstanding qualities.{/n}

d18fac83-2628-4c8f-8cc0-5407d33eb2ed.Text: {n}Solomorne speaks without emotion, simply stating the facts — this clearly is not the first time he has answered such a question about Glaito.{/n}

637acb8b-09a5-4ce0-9af6-1588c1ea03d5.Text: "Impossible — you've found me out." {n}Solomorne raises an eyebrow.{/n} "Yes, I am one hundredth of a percent less indifferent than I let on."

50658e3c-4155-4487-b136-7a56e39352fc.Text: "There was this one time... I was part of a raid on a gang of mutants. I excelled in battle, received an award, and was promoted to Proctor." {n}Solomorne pauses.{/n} "That is all."

df6149da-da64-44b2-94a2-a5d81ee4b466.Text: "That raid I mentioned was compromised. The enemy had been tipped off to our operation, and we had walked into a trap. Some mutant decided to chew my arm off. That was a mistake: since I couldn't free myself, I pushed my hand down his throat, grabbed something inside, and used him as a shield. While the thing was gnawing on my bones and spraying me with ichor and my own blood, I opened fire on the rest of the scum. That little manoeuvre bought my unit a few critical seconds."

2733e876-000c-4e92-97e5-7acc3e35cde9.Text: "We are servants of the God-Emperor's Law made manifest in the {g|Encyclopedia:LexImperialisGlossary}Lex Imperialis{/g}. The Adeptus Arbites uphold order on the scale of the Imperium and bring merciless punishment to offenders."

40c68dd8-5cf9-41e1-9dbf-33df6c0b0d9b.Text: "I believe you. A Rogue Trader's throne does not tolerate weaklings or idiots."

dd5f0bf4-fc48-477b-96de-7446b1353dae.Text: "I doubt such a word could ever be accurately used to describe an Arbitrator, but there is some truth to your observation. Since we're not in combat, I permit myself to stand at ease — which is to say, I am standing by on full alert."

a381610b-4e84-47bb-a439-7bab59a71f91.Text: "Fortune has little to do with it. You have formed an alliance with the Arbites, just as your predecessor did. My presence here is only the expected result of your decisions."

b6c1d3f8-70e1-4131-a84d-734613e9e16b.Text: "I just hoped it would discourage you. I only know how to give a full and exact account, and this story about lost limbs and odious abominations... I wasn't sure if a Rogue Trader would appreciate having to listen to all that."

f72b5ba8-2dea-48e8-b63d-ab75a1ce7470.Text: "Very well." {n}He raises his metal hand and slowly clenches it into a fist.{/n} "Have you ever been eaten alive? I have."

5f02874b-6b92-4108-bf6b-be9e72327ceb.Text: "You know where to find me, Rogue Trader."

4fe7b046-133a-4f86-b31c-789aa01b6d96.Text: {n}The Proctor looks you straight in the eye with cold impassivity.{/n} "Your suggestion that I could have prevented the disappearance of a star sounds almost flattering. And yet, I never dodge responsibility. Let the Emperor, in the hour of His final judgement, determine the measure of my guilt in what happened."

ba8c89d8-35d4-4db9-b5ae-8d26ca45dd29.Text: {n}Glaito tolerates your touch for exactly one second before jerking his head away, tossing your hand away from him.{/n}

c1790af6-aba7-4550-8848-b236732979a6.Text: "To collect and guard the tithe. That does not mean we ignore other violations of the Lex Imperialis — we simply act within the scope of our limited resources, the first of which being our small numbers. Here in the Expanse, many believe themselves to be too far from the civilised parts of the Imperium to have need of the law. The presence of the Adeptus Arbites helps to remind those people that the Lex Imperialis is in effect wherever there is at least one human being."

72521f77-fe3a-48ad-81a6-ca9c29b25667.Text: "I must admit, I was pleasantly surprised. I had expected something far less civilised, given that the Koronus Expanse is on the outskirts of the Imperium. Instead, Dargonus may even compare to some Calixian worlds in status and stability."

7524f421-cb69-4a42-8a9e-96c6f0e1a65b.Text: {n}Leaning over Glaito, Solomorne carefully feels every stitch on the cyber-mastiff's body.{/n} "A lump here, and here... And what the Throne is this?" {n}His iron fist slams into the floor, leaving a dent.{/n} "Bloody freaks! Gutted my dog! I'll— Ah, Rogue Trader... How long have you been... standing there?"

51e6bce6-6375-4d84-a49b-a8e6d724b09c.Text: "I have told myself that so many times, I don't know what the words mean anymore. Speaking of words..."

49a9129a-02f0-4c7e-84a7-48a7b24ded5b.Text: {n}Solomorne responds with an equally curt gesture, signalling his assent.{/n}

72d335c1-1179-45fb-93da-d1e37d99a515.Text: "You want to repeat your triumph? I cannot guarantee Glaito will be so calm this time."

1fe15b06-cdcc-4e90-9365-6ddc969d79d2.Text: "So do I. I'm more used to having orders and a plan of action — and elimination targets instead of interlocutors. But, every now and then, I have to suffer through these bouts of downtime."

8f3c013a-da4b-4344-9739-e4f84a7ea0ad.Text: {n}Solomorne raises an eyebrow.{/n} "A Rogue Trader and an Arbitrator — you have an interesting notion of normality. Well, I'll try not to disappoint you with my conversation skills."

43304fb4-b2ae-43d8-ad95-6ab354eb3433.Text: "From what my father told me, she was a principled woman of poor health. She died in childbirth. Not having known her might be the sole regret of my life."

26533021-8854-4403-a1f4-16e680c9d81e.Text: {n}A heavy sigh comes from Solomorne's chest, but a moment later, he is back to his calm self. His voice is steady as he speaks:{/n} "How... unfortunate. Well, I am ready to satisfy your curiosity, but I would plead for some privacy."

803334cb-215f-4806-ba62-8f4ac56cb6a7.Text: "As you will. We can have this conversation later." {n}Though Solomorne's expression does not change, you notice that he is trying not to meet your eyes too often.{/n}

9b79571a-bf1b-4c54-95a2-91076691a0bb.Text: "I am not going to call the prefect's judgement into question, but..." {n}Solomorne peers at you.{/n} "You had to make a difficult decision, and you made it. You took responsibility. I appreciate such qualities in people."

0a787bd2-e585-4ab8-a725-b898292d029a.Text: "You stated as much to the prefect, and it went down in my record. If that is insufficient and you expect me to comment, then I will."

3911163a-243d-4e12-84be-cf4d53eb7592.Text: {n}Solomorne raises his chin with dignity.{/n} "You may consider my recommendation flawed; however, I did not force you to act on it. I have nothing more to add."

b8541983-48e1-485f-bbf7-4156da101b5f.Text: "You are the ruler of an entire protectorate — I would not presume to judge you based on a single incident. If it seems like I am censuring you, that's just my face. And voice. And choice of words. It really is hard to readjust to normal conversation after so many years spent in interrogation rooms..."

6f946ce2-bfa4-4c95-9c15-232ae7648f42.Text: "I am beginning to think you enjoy pain."

ec5bca37-36f4-4a77-9d70-92744327dc63.Text: {n}The Proctor pauses before giving a response.{/n} "To assist the Rogue Trader in claiming new worlds in the God-Emperor's name is precisely why I am here."

431e2b56-b01f-41fa-a80f-4314a36915e6.Text: {n}Dead silence falls over the bridge in the wake of the loud noise, but it lasts only a moment. The officers hurry to return to their duties for fear of drawing your attention.{/n}

99ce0fda-e482-485e-95ec-9e47b8af22ec.Text: {n}Solomorne touches his cheek with his metal fingers.{/n} "I would have preferred a shot in the leg instead... Ah, that's right — I am not allowed to object. In that case, thank you for teaching me a lesson — this brazen detractor is sure to benefit from it."

42e3e996-b68c-41d9-b792-b86239bed50a.Text: {n}Solomorne looks slightly puzzled by your response.{/n} "I am not really in a position to edify a Rogue Trader, but... Well, when it comes to honesty and impartiality, you can count on me."

580c457e-6221-4100-a825-b86e87788319.Text: "I do not know. It was one of those tough situations where only time will tell how well you handled them."

ddc09567-3dd1-456d-8bc2-8a8bdd36c89e.Text: {n}He freezes, beads of sweat forming on his brow.{/n} "I need to tell you something about my past... if you care to listen, that is."

089ed759-ca28-4d46-ae7c-633b94fcdc3f.Text: "If I were in your position, I would take the prefect's evaluation in stride and learn from your painful experience on Thassera. Sometimes, life knocks the wind out of you in a way that can't be dodged, so it helps to learn how to take a hit."

4253861a-b1be-4ce4-acf4-d0ee19f5a2eb.Text: "By the way, I ran into that young woman recently, {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_LizzyOnBoardDecision}Maive{/d}. Curtsies to anyone she meets, big smile on her face. I cannot express how much she irritates me, but she is definitely harmless. It is a valuable talent to know when someone poses no threat and can be put to good use."

c0903180-b725-4b5c-ae8c-858523ac0618.Text: "You {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_LizzyServDecision}servitorised{/d} that young woman, Maive — a severe measure, but it was the right call. Now the enemy won't be able to take advantage of her naivety again."

c3f4966f-e858-4274-af2c-18f50f18410f.Text: {n}The cyber-mastiff gnashes his fangs a hair's breadth away from your fingers, preventing you from touching him.{/n}

eba56544-adec-411c-a3a5-9eb8bcfe6265.Text: "I was on a mission, not attending to pointless amusements."

14b29af0-b994-46d4-b3cd-2a412109e575.Text: "You are quite right, and I am almost proud of it — what kind of Arbitrator would stoop to idle revelry, or, Throne forbid, dancing?"

9c51ac39-a186-4c28-8585-f30315e01dcf.Text: "When I think back to Thassera, I can recall only one moment of joy, and that was when we returned to the ship." {n}Solomorne responds curtly, his gaze directed somewhere over your shoulder.{/n}

1c36affd-4d06-4646-942f-84b3676d609a.Text: "Very well, if you insist, let me think about it one more time... The wine smelled like wash, the Impostor Hunt was a plot — I fail to see anything appealing there — and the rest of the festivities had all the characteristics of degradation. I believe that covers everything."

e27b9ce2-568f-4101-a06e-c1b916a56c0a.Text: "No, wait a second." {n}He stops himself, raising a finger.{/n} "I don't know why, but I enjoyed seeing that augmented beast roam free."

e7cd4e6a-6207-41fb-9240-523488972b06.Text: "I am certainly no expert or point of reference on this subject. Perhaps you are simply hard to impress — you are a Rogue Trader, after all."

d50e090a-a440-487d-b091-2276c3bfb7fb.Text: "You should take that into account if you ever need an escort for some high society event. You know, one who actually has your back and keeps watch instead of drinking."

76c72d37-7340-4d9d-ba12-75af65607697.Text: "Yes, I've been looking for a chance to have this conversation." {n}Solomorne's nostrils flare, his eyes darting uneasily around the bridge.{/n} "I must tell you something about my past, so that we might consider the matter closed. If you agree to hear me out, that is."

87014981-0dc5-4fb6-896b-01b7f5363627.Text: "I have a theory, but... I myself give it little credit at this time — it is too unlikely and too dangerous. However, I will gladly listen to your own perspective on these events."

4e3fc2ab-f56d-471b-b175-3c6a965ace29.Text: "I suppose I have what you would call a proven and diverse track record: investigations, rebel suppressions, punitive raids — dozens of completed operations," {n}Solomorne concludes dryly, without any hint of pride.{/n}

61ae7a0d-1308-48da-8571-2fc1b3d818ad.Text: "It's about what really pushed me into the pit of anger." {n}Solomorne closes his eyes, and when he opens them again, he begins to speak with lifeless detachment:{/n} "Back in Calixis, before I was promoted to Proctor, I served in the same squad with another Arbitrator, Emmerson. He wasn't just a comrade — we entered the {g|Encyclopedia:ScholaProgeniumGlossary}Schola Progenium{/g} together, we went through training together, we were assigned to the same hive world. He was like a brother to me, and I killed him."

7843f123-d8e6-4c12-9f0f-9e6229efd965.Text: "Remember that mission I told you about, the one that cost me my arm? It was Emmerson who sold us out to the crime syndicate and compromised the raid."

7420ac96-87b3-48ce-b781-a5098229748f.Text: "We ran into an ambush during a raid, all because Emmerson sold us out to a crime syndicate."

b67c96f5-3c7b-4dea-b75e-6ad933524f03.Text: "I was badly wounded in the fight, lying on the floor, barely alive. The rest of the squad had gone to scout the area, and Emmerson stayed to guard me. He didn't notice that I was awake — he was talking over the vox. He kept demanding bigger payment, and when he started giving our coordinates, I shot him in the back of the head." {n}Solomorne places a hand on Glaito's neck.{/n} "I figured that we weren't making it out of there alive, so I logged my final report, attached my vox to Glaito's collar, and told him to return to the headquarters. Then, I passed out again, and when I came to, I had already been captured. The heretics tortured me for days, but I held on until the exaction squad arrived."

df5856c0-1e7b-4254-8616-9ee3522b6f91.Text: "A special unit. Exaction squads are dispatched to track down and apprehend dangerous criminals. They were investigating Emmerson's betrayal, and it had led them to the heretics' hideout where I was being held prisoner."

e154556e-949d-4fab-b689-0e42e661a1fc.Text: "I was right by their contact's corpse — they had to know how I found them out and what else I knew about them. They tried to beat the answers out of me, tried long and hard. I kept my mouth shut, because I knew that the second I started talking, they would dispose of me."

3a148d14-067c-483b-bb4f-12f9e736acdb.Text: "I could throw pretty words at you about how I went through the Injuncta Cardinal in my mind or prayed to the Emperor, but... I did pray, and I was well trained to tolerate pain, but every Arbitrator has their limit. When I was almost broken, what helped me through was hatred."

14e746d0-b8ee-4b87-a1f6-a7ea0b91fbd7.Text: {n}Solomorne's entire body tenses, and Glaito immediately leans forward, looking for the unseen threat, but his master's iron hand tugs at his collar.{/n} "I kept recalling that bastard's face, and smothered any base thoughts I had about welcoming death again and again. Hours of agony. Hours in the whirlpool of pure rage."

e173a807-4810-4a2b-8d59-d8ef5ee2a3b8.Text: "I was put under investigation, but was cleared of the charges and assigned to Piety, without Glaito. The most corrupt hive world in the Drusus Marches. Two years among the vilest dregs of Humanity... It was a test, and I passed — I got my promotion, got Glaito back. But after Emmerson's betrayal, I was never the same."

274b771b-3756-4d48-9697-d8c393556cbd.Text: "I know." {n}There is no pride, no guilt in his voice — only aloofness bordering on total emotional vacuum.{/n}

430943bc-3ce3-40c3-86f6-3e126226d6d7.Text: "Glaito is not a house pet, Rogue Trader — trying to feed him will get you nowhere. He only eats out of my hands and only at specific times — strict training. It protects the cyber-mastiff against deliberate poisoning and other ill intents. Basically, don't waste your time, or your meat."

9f92e4d0-0181-42f5-a547-cd44e9762144.Text:
The Imperium is founded on unquestioning obedience to the Lex Imperialis, and Proctor Solomorne Anthar is a steadfast servant of the Adeptus Arbites who upholds this sacred order. Together with his faithful cyber-mastiff Glaito, he administers justice without pity or doubt, collecting from many worlds the tithe that feeds the might of the Imperium, and passing sentence on criminals.
Solomorne has been brought into the retinue of the Rogue Trader by an alliance between the Arbitrators of the Expanse and the von Valancius dynasty, and the hour is approaching when the Proctor's principles will be put to the ultimate test.

ecad004b-1079-43f9-99a0-c4406c919582.Text: "You wouldn't believe the kinds of poisons Glaito has detected in your various nobles' possessions. Fortunately, they have made no attempts on your life, so I limited myself to sending them a simple message: they may squabble as much as they like, but the moment it puts the protectorate at risk, they will feel the hand of justice bearing down on them."

dad7d76b-ed83-4e03-a06d-b06c2bd8ad37.Text: "Are you afraid to step into the unknown, where there is no law?"

7c7a748d-e596-4523-a383-c33fa6e6f9ab.Text: [Kiss Solomorne] "Don't you want to wish me luck?"

7df776d8-01b4-4cce-afb4-659a3e186fcc.Text: "What are you going to do if we survive?"

4924b87d-5ee4-4e65-8275-6a971c6f110e.Text: "Hey, Glaito! I'll keep an eye on your Arbitrator if you die. I promise."

a2f7c0ba-0951-4a66-b49a-4e6451eb767b.Text: {n}Solomorne is still, deep in thought, looking more like a statue than a living person. Only when Glaito lets out a low growl, drawing Solomorne's attention, does he break his stillness and raise his eyes.{/n} "Come with some parting words, Rogue Trader? Now is the time — there may not be another opportunity."

35df1822-039f-461a-a9fd-3e645d14b832.Text: {n}Solomorne ruffles the back of the cyber-mastiff's neck, wearing a sad, slightly tremulous smile.{/n} "I have you and my dog with me — the God-Emperor could grant me no better reward for my service than the chance to either die valiantly in good company or overcome unimaginable peril by your side. What more could I want?"

8a56c5a1-64f0-48ac-b357-2ce3dd2b6669.Text: "Honestly? I don't know. The Adeptus Arbites no longer exists in the Expanse, but that doesn't mean I can't serve the God-Emperor's Law. I will consider my future later, if, as you say, we survive."

066d17c1-8c8e-45e6-bcd5-2105029a828c.Text: "I will follow your orders to find a new Marshal, of course. And after that... I will leave you. For how long, only the Emperor knows — every Arbitrator counts now, and I'm needed on Dargonus."

dea80eb4-ac9e-45a8-99b9-bfc307d4538a.Text: {n}Solomorne presses his fist to his chest, looking you straight in the eye. The rote gesture looks unexpectedly heartfelt.{/n} "It has been an honour to serve in your retinue, and it does not matter what lies ahead. Isn't that right, Glaito?" {n}Without a direct command, the cyber-mastiff barks his assent.{/n}

2c166116-e31b-4455-8e78-7d911b4bf469.Text: "You have entrusted me with the leadership of the Adeptus Arbites in the Expanse — whether I become the next Marshal or not, I will have to leave your retinue and devote myself entirely to my new post."

f8eba8a9-d66a-4158-8e38-754d7002eb82.Text: "To purge the Arbitrators' ranks of those who have strayed in their service to the Lex Imperialis. Conducting the required investigations and enquiries will not be compatible with keeping my place in your retinue — if we return to the Expanse, I will leave the flagship and work to restore order in the Adeptus Arbites."

926ba727-7aba-4c65-968a-81ceb7792b0d.Text: {n}Glaito bares his metal fangs, and Solomorne's mouth broadens into a dangerous, death-or-glory grin.{/n} "Let those who hide from us at the edge of the galaxy be afraid — we will bring the Lex Imperialis to them whether they want it or not. So, {name} shall we show them all?"

845e7702-6823-4d76-855a-908b6d727d3a.Text: {n}Solomorne and Glaito exude steely confidence — both akin to living embodiments of duty and order.{/n} "The doctrine of the Adeptus Arbites commands that I cast aside doubt and fear for the sake of service, so you won't see even a hint of such criminal hesitation from me. I am ready to carry the Emperor's justice into the heart of darkness."

8fcea585-791b-4436-b15e-b192907e81fd.Text: {n}Suddenly, Solomorne throws back his head and laughs. His laughter, unusually sincere and gleeful, rolls across the bridge.{/n} "Will you now? As if I'd let Glaito die while I still live!"

14f04561-e271-4cff-b50e-0657c6506bd8.Text: "You know I am." {n}Solomorne places his hand firmly on his weapon, and Glaito stands at attention, echoing his master's determination.{/n}

99197497-a45a-43af-bca3-a83793a72ea5.Text: "However..." {n}Solomorne casts a sidelong look at you.{/n} "That doesn't mean I won't return to the one waiting for me. I promise — no matter how long the road, no matter how dangerous the obstacles, my journey will always end at your door."

8efbc401-429f-433f-9f97-546015f5eb4c.Text: "Or..." {n}Solomorne's gaze is piercing and bores right into yours.{/n} "You will simply order me to stay, and I will. The Emperor did not grant you the privilege of command by chance. If you choose to command my presence, then my place and my duty is at your side."

f0b7da65-f6fe-407f-9a92-12b0dbc9dd37.Text: {n}He folds you into a tight embrace, his voice dropping to a whisper:{/n} "Try to survive. If you don't, I'm going to kill everyone down there, and I won't care if they're guiltless under the Lex or not."

50066a60-7b86-43f8-9206-a9e1350169f7.Text: {n}Solomorne nods in understanding.{/n} "I agree — words are unnecessary. It's time to descend to Epitaph and face the final test."

eff639e2-ef89-4ce8-830e-09bb80b9c623.Text: {n}The raven stops you with deafening croaks. Images from the cyber-beast's head rise before your eyes: the space ahead, riddled with warp breaches; the devastating streams of energy. The raven's support gives you the capability to disarm the traps.{/n}

5321d94c-5586-4d51-81c1-2e6c1ee3f8be.Text: {n}The raven soars. It sweeps past breach after breach like a black whirlwind, and its wings do your bidding as they reflect the terrifying glow of the unknowable back onto itself. Several tense minutes later, nothing remains of the traps.{/n}

69f95f5a-ee0b-4f93-b3d8-4c31244156ff.Text: {n}The raven croaks its agreement and continues to circle over your head.{/n}

e7e659f8-e16f-4d0d-9b69-0665dff35e93.Text: Find out how the survivors managed to last this long with no food.

29c7db79-47dc-4d6b-af06-f2797a492fd9.Text: Threaten to open fire if there is no response.

cbda77a4-6f3b-49ab-8824-f7f7abc484a0.Text: Send a scouting team to the ship.

0e329676-994f-4f22-b7f4-660c5bf5873e.Text: Place the prisoners into your ship's jail cells.

ad5057f1-cbeb-4f48-86d1-2c88c95870e8.Text: Destroy the ship with broadside cannons.

348f824f-4bf3-424e-9acb-013c4862bec3.Text: Bring the toughest ones onto your ship. In the void, there is no such thing as too much manpower.

9e31ca32-fed7-41d4-8f80-e52bf6468f45.Text: Leave the criminals to rot in their jail.

69553be0-4ace-4aa6-b18f-8c14722d5b0d.Text: The Imperium vessel drifting by remains silent. Despite {g|Encyclopedia:Augur}augurs{/g} detecting signs of life on board, the people on the ship are taking their time to respond to a routine hailing call.

5b8b7dac-4943-4ea1-9003-c8ec5e23b047.Text: The enforcers look away. It seems everyone can guess what sustenance those desperate people have been living on, but none are ready to talk about it. Whispers of a monstrous heresy begin spreading through the decks.

237556d0-9e77-4f1f-884e-7c0eeb0c7ed3.Text: A hoarse voice breaks the vox-silence. Through the terrible noise of static, it implores anyone who hears it to "take us from this bloody rustbucket, even if it's into death's embrace."

2555f2af-231c-40b8-ac7e-1f6ed9aacb93.Text: The enforcers return with new information. The ship was transporting convicts to penal worlds, and the man who had contacted the bridge was one of the criminals. The convicts had broken free and massacred the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Arbitrator{/g} squad guarding them; however, in the heat of battle, several crucial bridge officers and a Tech-Priest contingent were killed as well. The ship has been drifting helplessly ever since, and what little food remains has gone bad. The dying rioters would now agree to anything if it helped them get out of their flying crypt.

82a2b18a-e01b-4c4c-85be-13726f524fe3.Text: You grant the survivors their wish, obliterating the ship along with everyone and everything on its decks.

94731605-85a8-4679-97c6-4981a11b012b.Text: According to the report, the number of living people aboard is dozens of times smaller than that required for proper ship maintenance.

69be3889-92c9-4509-9309-896209589064.Text: A handful of shuttles are enough to transport the emaciated prisoners. The inhabitants of the decks steer clear of the newcomers. Rumours speak of a carnivorous curiosity in the looks they give people.

bf07a7f7-e27a-4113-a8d9-ecf28386dbf6.Text: The motionless hulk of the prison ship drifts on. One could hardly imagine a more terrifying punishment.

dc01f405-b537-4282-ae78-0fdafaad5168.Text: The prisoners smile as they are being escorted to their new cages. Any means of escaping the drifting ship is a blessing to them.

7a838731-e398-4e0e-824e-85855c9e5786.Text: A few short macro-cannon salvos send the strange voidship to oblivion.

2c6dc998-0b74-41b7-bc56-4afdd18a51a3.Text: Explore the surface of the colony.

19091056-b2e5-4b80-bdc6-6ce70b8831dc.Text: The tiny colony is buried in an enormous yawning pit, the edges of its civilian structures barely visible even from the shuttle.

dfecc6bd-07ae-4b2c-bd85-9cfc3c41f5b6.Text: Deep beneath the rubble, the scouts uncover the remains of warehouses, depots, and a veritable maze of suspicious tunnels gated with airlocks. Judging by the flattened containers with half-effaced markings, the impressively vast subterranean city belonged to a smuggling syndicate.

29e31ef0-7f8c-410d-b23c-63371e0abcda.Text: Lying next to the shuttle are empty bomb containers and corpses clad in characteristic armour. The voidcraft belonged to the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g}. Surviving records suggest it was the Arbitrators who planted the explosives and collapsed the tunnels on top of their dwellers.

e0abb136-0695-4c5f-bcf7-d97f0e2fa2a0.Text: The settlement was destroyed when the ground swelled up under it. The forlorn bones of dead colonists are strewn amid the rubble. On the edge of the crater, the scouts discover a tunnel entrance: apparently, there was an explosion in the cavities beneath the town, whose unsuspecting people fell instantly into the chasm that opened as a result. Near its gaping maw is a shuttle, overturned and blackened by the blast, forever motionless.

06f987ff-d559-4fdb-97a8-04590d37c43e.Text: Searching through the papers, you find the demolition plans. The Arbitrators knew that detonating the tunnels would bury the colony, but prioritised eliminating the criminals over preserving the lives of ordinary settlers. The documents also include a map of the Koronus Expanse containing encrypted data. It appears the Arbitrators were aware of another smugglers' cache, but in a different system.

5a72bf46-e114-4fd6-946a-e35caebec728.Text: Decline the request and leave the planet's orbit.

00cd475b-a80b-4026-9a16-d050fdf5dad0.Text: Agree and speak with the governor discreetly.

d86269ec-be2f-4bc2-9720-ba63006d5c94.Text: Demand that he have formal talks with you if he has nothing to hide.

47af10df-0e91-4850-8d26-4f8914768be2.Text: Strike at the station with macro-cannons.

2bded9da-102b-4b24-aef2-16ec0f404903.Text: Strike at the governmental palace with macro-cannons.

b7ef7b26-5522-4661-b262-c5cafe2edb49.Text: Ask if the governor knows the ruler of Thassera, Ruoldo, who hails from the planet Idex.

038c1bac-8e87-4ad8-88e5-65e985f36fee.Text: Perhaps the Idex government may recall Ruoldo, the man put in charge of Thassera?

c01bf5f5-2854-4faf-9cb7-fc42841e0fbf.Text: Idex is a planet of no particular note. However, the small station suspended in its orbit sends a distress call to your ship. The man in the hurried vox-transmission introduces himself as the planet's governor and asks for the Rogue Trader's assistance in a delicate matter. He promises to supply the details in a private vox-conversation.

a0e36786-e2b9-46b1-b383-df3f75f4f922.Text: Ruoldo used to be a member of Idex's ruling dynasty, before being sent away by his own family. The government is wary of Ruoldo due to his rumoured involvement in heresies of some sort.

20ddce17-4eb2-45fe-8852-5bb62a2bf238.Text: The ringing silence on the vox-channels indicates that Idex is, as of now, devoid of any planetary authority.

e3f7d184-4cbb-4461-9463-bb031aa75fc9.Text: It appears Idex recently suffered a major coup. One of its noble families seized power and made outcasts of the former dynasty. Such plots are not uncommon — although, notably, Idex has become less prosperous under the new government.

23097b84-a3b4-43d9-b6b2-8b0c47c3276e.Text: The governor's transmission is interrupted by an official request from the planet. Idex's authorities are claiming that the person who just contacted you is a member of a heretical sect of nobles who has escaped from the wardens' custody. The planetary government is asking, in the name of the Imperium, that the traitor be eliminated at once.

f7501978-465b-4225-8bdd-4353ab73db50.Text: The governor transmitting on your personal vox-frequency whispers that Idex's current authorities are not who they claim to be. There has been an uprising on the planet, and a heretical sect has seized control. The governor pleads with you to launch an immediate strike on the governmental palace. With their top tier obliterated, the new authorities will be unable to hold onto power!

390633fb-4474-4ce7-b63d-0ce10b63be30.Text: The station's fiery remains adorn the sky of Idex. Whoever was on there will never be ruler of anything again.

eada71ad-d2b4-43c8-9a97-69bbfef6eaad.Text: Your ship departs into the icy void, leaving the schemers of Idex behind.

05f412e8-5d23-43c9-862e-17253553989b.Text: The governor on the station sends you his tearful thanks along with his generous gifts.

38368241-1a50-4ba0-a532-7fb2cd8a77ba.Text: The Idex parliament that contacted you sends you generous gifts as a token of gratitude for your cooperation.

9fcffd45-d083-4d58-afa9-1ddea178f9c4.Text: The governor is glad to hear that you know Ruoldo, who is his distant relative. Being a friend to Ruoldo makes the Rogue Trader a friend to the governor of Idex!

e47af43a-c165-4460-b35d-2c8461583204.Text: Whoever was the planet's official ruler has been reduced to less than servo-skull material.

de2827d3-3d57-41b5-a290-15399e3af354.Text: Amid the lifeless rocks and lava lakes, the ship's augurs have detected something resembling buildings. There is something off with their outlines, but their presence, in and of itself, suggests there may be some valuables to uncover among the ruins.

bf6f764c-ce72-44fc-b549-194f109fc44b.Text: The scouts are able to discern symbols of the Imperium on the buildings. Deformed and fused together by high temperatures, the ore-mining structures tell a sad story: centuries ago, the planet and all its riches perished beneath the radiance of the system's expanding sun.

723715f9-5819-498d-b499-d21bfda57cf5.Text: The ship's augurs have detected an Explorator base set up in the middle of the jungle. Enforcers sent to scout the area have returned and are reporting that the camp is completely deserted, and the only Tech-Priest they encountered was found dead on the edge of a strange abyss that had split the planet's surface. Judging by the notes left behind at the camp, he had pushed all his companions into the abyss, one after another, and remained forever motionless at the brink, waiting for tidings. As the Tech-Priest fell into a deathly trance, his servo-skulls guarded him until the end, but could not save their master from dehydration.

d5159618-bbf6-4a88-8692-a086ad79ed1b.Text: Send a team of enforcers to explore the ship.

b6d81d9c-6a9d-4da6-b446-48cbdd847aff.Text: Your ship's powerful augurs have detected the wreckage of a small craft hidden amid rock crevices. The shuttles that have approached it are able to make out the name on the hull: "Renegades' Fall."

db486b97-746e-4221-94a3-30a3675a4078.Text: The enforcers report that the craft was downed by a larger ship. Seasoned officers note the amazing precision of the hits on the hull, as if the pursuer was trying to avoid damaging some valuable cargo inside. Whoever they were, the craft's captain was able to steer it into a deep crevasse just before the crash, thus hiding the location of the wreckage from the enemy.

e9b39252-f3c0-4dd3-b71e-6275944c71ff.Text: The blacksmith has somehow managed to forge shells and casings. These do not belong on a feudal world, but there is no doubt as to what they are.

7c11c8dd-6179-4e47-af3d-0faba08164c5.Text: Small, dented metal cylinders are scattered in front of the blacksmith. The objects look familiar, but the poor craftsmanship makes it difficult to tell what they were intended to be.

bdb5e15b-7de0-46e3-88dc-aaa340df0057.Text: Judging by his attire, the man was of high social standing. Someone has carefully and skilfully peeled the skin off his face.

b772daae-20cf-4e88-8b9b-faf045934ba9.Text: Someone disfigured the corpse's face and threw the body off the parapet.

f01f90d0-c463-477c-87d5-635abebe649f.Text: The face of the corpse has been skilfully cut off, but you recognise him by his outfit. This nobleman was murdered by the tailor you allowed to go free.

c93f6743-ba12-4fbe-8f09-7f6295d3d9f9.Text: "Stay safe, dearest. And say a great big thank you to {rt_mf|His|Her} Graciousness for me! I'll never forget {rt_mf|his|her} good heart!"

bd3b988b-f61a-46f8-8594-78f56b40031c.Text: "Every order I get, it's for these thimbles again. What do they even need them for at the governor's court?"

b000cad3-4606-48f1-ba6e-c31b7932b1a3.Text: "This is our chapel where we pray to the Emperor, the holder of the Key to all Destinies. The bell in its tower can ring so loud, it makes your ears pop!"

a1347783-c648-41e3-8ab9-b0c0466adc63.Text: Through the opening above the gate, freedom winks at you mockingly. Your arms barely have the strength to hold onto the edge, let alone pull your whole body up.

60edb4d6-1446-44c4-820b-73c5f3551034.Text: "Requestioning formation on the location of— Pah! Good sirs, is {mf|he|she} gone? Can I come out? Sirs?"

fd5b8601-86ed-4311-8ebd-48d8c53e2879.Text: "I've never seen this much food in my life. Now, how can I stuff as much as I can in me so I don't starve later..."

1ba4ccf6-c74e-4d23-8f81-538ffdfc8d57.Text: "We haven't had a feast like this in a long time!"

45933caa-b216-4642-b12d-c4b52221140e.Text: "I can't remember the last time we had visitors from the stars!"

d9952d5e-be4a-4218-9ebc-1f6167783589.Text: "We have come to honour the greatest among the great!"

ebc22c27-d86b-4949-aa1e-8a1046c22611.Text: "If only I could behold the wonders of the stars… even for a moment!"

fb9900df-411d-44ef-bdca-e5a3be497210.Text: "...'s to your — hic! — health, my Celestial {mf|L-Lord|L-Lady}!"

dacb62a1-b6e6-451d-af2d-a3afa661df9c.Text: "Long live {mf|His|Her} Highness the... {mf|Prince|Queen} of... all the stars?"

5f15002f-6c64-4466-8fb4-8ae45873b158.Text: "I'm... this close to... falling over. Or maybe I already have..."

3cc829c7-2ce1-413c-849a-94f2ec99fd83.Text: "I can't believe what I'm seeing... People from the stars, walking on our planet!"

720e29b1-0c20-4486-8871-e927e0359e55.Text: "Seeing people of such noble blood is the highest blessing!"

fe879c68-3e91-4739-8729-298840b34bda.Text: "What a life! To own entire stars..."

9440f055-e5a8-4319-92ab-26e5a656daee.Text: "This reception is as splendid as any among the stars! Don't you think?"

66b43906-37a0-4d90-8c9d-d06653d683c1.Text: "My noble friends, let us drink a toast — to the arrival of our most distinguished guest!"

39a7b5f6-e011-4829-b658-2def150582db.Text: The cyber-mastiff does not respond to nudges or commands. The lumens on its head are blinking with troubling agitation.

7b2b8755-696e-4d35-9e73-bc60079ae327.Text: The wheel is similar to the ones used to raise the enormous elevator in the central square. This one, however, has completely rusted through with age.

98ab2b35-bea4-4538-9470-445c08eeca7a.Text: "All that food getting wasted on those wretched beasts while we're expected to just tighten our belts..."

c1b76595-1253-44fa-9f81-514be867e369.Text: "So, let's sneak into the stable and pinch some! No one's going to miss a handful of table scraps."

5644c8ae-528f-464c-b524-5d6305191fe7.Text: "If we get caught, no one's going to miss a couple of drudges either. Better to survive on crumbs than become the crumbs."

8e29b04e-6f6f-4e20-896f-dd66e7c11b7e.Text: "Lost something, little bird? Not your ruler of all stars and expanses, by any chance?"

29876ced-7f10-4a6a-8917-c842e618cc78.Text: "Ah, I feel sorry for the common sods... But if I step in to help, I'll get kicked out into the slums with them."

289dc9c4-0b42-489e-a06e-801afedbee08.Text: "You look like crap, Maive. One amasec too many, huh? Well, it's not like you're the only one. Here's my advice: go have a good sleep."

a224b783-2e7f-437d-b6ab-e667d76c97de.Text: The laceraxes' ribs are heaving, thick saliva dripping from their long tongues. The creatures must be terribly thirsty on this hot evening.

0264775d-65b5-424f-b220-490d70936966.Text: Salivating profusely, the laceraxes watch the food disappear into people's throats — judging by their protruding ribs, the beasts have not been properly fed in some time.

36b78bca-c782-482f-b1d3-06cca2626a6b.Text: Judging by the scraps of old scales and the fragments of bones shattered by mighty jaws, this used to be a lair for cyber-laceraxes.

3ec2aa81-e45e-478e-889a-13135d61f031.Text: The lacerax's tongues have fallen out of its open maw, and a thick stream of blood is oozing from its shattered skull. Judging by the pieces of bone and brain matter stuck to the bars, the beast was slamming its head against them until the end.

69f71320-faf2-4ab1-861a-de44c841ecfa.Text: Under the guards' watchful eye, sullen-faced servants are collecting scraps. You can hear their empty stomachs rumble and their watering mouths quietly gulp.

205cc70d-90ef-4a5e-9041-31c3bdd3d497.Text: The lever leaves flakes of rust on your fingers: it has been a long time since it was last used. Your strength is not enough to make it budge.

328e2b1b-0f11-4e11-bf96-5fe24051f4ba.Text: Tiny lice are hopping around the gilded plate. The lady squashes the insects with a small golden hammer, only for more of them to drop from her coiffed hair and into her food.

049aa589-f5dc-4d9c-9f93-da04f58b3f22.Text: "God-Emperor be blessed, you survived! It was so frightful… How could such abominations exist in His world?!"

77427730-95af-491b-af6f-73d343cc58a6.Text: "This gate leads straight to the main square! Let us hurry there!"

01ae14d5-bba4-4f17-a18a-5a50fcccaa1f.Text: "I am so glad you have returned! The celebration in your honour is just hitting its peak!"

0d825223-42f2-4b86-b22b-3539183c4c00.Text: "Thwap your powdered face, you stupid girl! What if it fell on someone's head?"

6caecde8-28fb-4644-9e0c-346e0b3042dc.Text: "We spent the whole day hooking up that thing! Now, we've got to do it all over again... Get out of here before you break anything else!"

0e1f1aa6-48d2-47c5-bac2-b10ed140c026.Text: "Look who's come down to join us... Got tired of never being hungry, did you?"

a3c01931-d23a-46b1-a3b5-186325ad8a80.Text: "Got any food? No? Then keep walking!"

e4c543f5-b70b-49fe-a1ba-baabc830788d.Text: "My hands are going numb... Maybe today, I'll get a quarter-ration at least? Ha! Right..."

e1eb32b9-a9a4-47c6-80b1-2156157be8b2.Text: "This elevator could be the path to the Upper Town — if only it weren't so high up."

6b57e6be-ef73-4a0e-817d-e40d0431ce7f.Text: Half-sunk in malodorous mud, the houses, if one can call them that, are packed together like buboes on a plague-stricken body.

d343e582-33f6-4854-aff4-e8b222b50cb8.Text: "Property of Rogue Trader von Valancius. Do not approach, or it will be deemed an assassination attempt."

2f7d0002-dd97-4890-a3b2-ca3f3ea1b5e2.Text: "What in the void are you doing here, girl? Get outta here!"

76ec0ab8-4ce0-40dd-8125-343605dddcd6.Text: "You're skin and bones, Maive. They're not taking care of you up there."

abfeb574-dfa4-4b3f-bcdc-f625267c9a79.Text: "It's raining again. I hate it. Why do we always have to work in the rain?"

2f9e99ad-df65-49f7-b406-cb5eaaf2b1cd.Text: "Some people are even less lucky. Did you hear the mutants got off their leash? Bad luck for the poor sods who were nearby."

8e8f8c91-d51d-4bd0-b90e-032bd804c163.Text: "All because of the Celestial {rt_mf|Lord|Lady} — when the visitors from the sky appeared, everyone went crazy, even the mutants! So many onlookers died..."

ccc2153d-2ab1-4ce7-b321-818cf100a5fb.Text: "What's that knocking...? Maive, is that you? Hold on, I'll get it."

4b0d954c-c80a-44ee-96aa-49b7f0b0c7db.Text: "That leaves eleven glasses, five bowls, and three boxes... Will they fit?"

89ccc56a-ac75-4d7a-9b46-73f8e3cc6bd1.Text: "Sure they will, I've packed more than that before!"

a854ef9f-3b5f-4301-a387-d6de21a640b7.Text: "Hmm, right... Be careful with your 'packing.' If you crush or break something now, we'll both be going to feed the Phesmophorius."

61a27e3e-90c7-489f-90d0-7315a3b671c4.Text: "Useless swine! They can't even deliver a cartload of belongings without breaking something!"

5f554c03-a4e0-4fda-9649-be375b571771.Text: "I'm sorry, sir. The rain washed away the road, so I had to drag it uphill..."

25dd793a-46a1-4c82-a05a-e84ef1c98e7c.Text: "What are you doing, making excuses for yourself? I'll skin you alive!"

d26e31ee-3628-4b26-99cf-4612541525c5.Text: "Where are they? My eyes. My precious eyes! They've melted... Melted!"

82a6984e-c62c-4956-aea3-7e6b3588d917.Text: "For the record, that was a true work of art!"

a8e1bc16-f27d-416b-be36-82bf1f9aa681.Text: "Do you think this will help you win? My fate is no longer in your hands!"

2a65eebf-4a45-4bbd-84b7-1be31d0cea80.Text: Judging by the deep scratches, there used to be a makeshift bridge here. If you put something in its place, you can try to cross to the next roof.

be5fbb40-d082-4c8e-87cc-fb992cf72363.Text: The rusted sheet of iron could easily reach the other side of the roof, but it is unlikely to hold a person's weight.

bbba9f25-0879-495a-8e29-97d2ea6d1f05.Text: There is no doubt that this piece of iron is sturdy enough, but it is woefully short for a bridge.

eafbfbb9-e3e2-44f8-8a3b-55c1b7e19df6.Text: Despite the gaps, the metal lattice looks both sturdy and long enough.

df46a48b-544f-46ef-8544-cd7ccdef509c.Text: The crystal glows enigmatically, framing the beginning of the sculptor's creation, which bears a striking resemblance to you.

38595e7e-daac-43f9-aaa8-de50d63f92fe.Text: The clear lines of the heretical symbols elicit a vague desire to touch them.

4ca17e12-7fb8-4325-b40f-d8a35bd7637c.Text: Circles have been scrawled over whole stacks of scrolls. Each circle resembles the one daubed on the floor, but none replicates it exactly.

e1b512ab-fee9-4436-bc27-487f02bbc8cd.Text: As you approach, the shards of the monstrous structure make a barely audible ringing sound.

28c43eb0-035f-4019-9278-2a7196070bc7.Text: The shards of the monstrous structure emit a barely perceptible ringing sound... or is it the whispers of otherworldly voices telling of change?

6088670b-9e50-4818-949a-761396990a99.Text: "Maive's coming! Maybe she's pinched a few lordly leftovers for us again?"

39270e95-ee98-47b6-b440-703377ac7974.Text: "Dear me, look at her, covered in dirt from head to foot! Did something happen? She doesn't belong in this bug-ridden place, poor soul..."

0e9bbcaf-682f-4033-9cea-5ea215ac77f1.Text: The enormous gate is locked fast.

cc8e07f2-d3f6-456f-bbb1-59daac15c0ce.Text: The tables are overflowing with rare and peculiar food. There is enough of it to easily feed dozens of hungry mouths, but the servants are unlikely to get even a morsel of this feast.

ce6f2ca2-4bac-46ba-8420-2c167b12fe1a.Text: The horses neigh and glance at you with extreme curiosity. One of them snorts playfully.

9e034204-22ea-4639-a4c5-3de6cc0580c6.Text: The horses glance at you with an odd curiosity. One of them pulls its muzzle closer and clacks its teeth — almost too greedily and hungrily for a harmless herbivore.

1c5f981d-7757-4371-90df-07e686a7034e.Text: It does not escape your notice that a few leftovers from the plates disappear into the servant's filthy apron.

f6ba54fe-4f24-4ec7-bfd5-bce7d37da216.Text: You notice a veritable mountain of leftovers under the table. The guests have been tossing scraps onto the floor without thought.

3d36cebe-c2f2-4856-a79e-08c3c5dc547b.Text: "There's something not right about Number 4. It doesn't know commands, just does whatever it wants. So they locked it up to keep it out of trouble, Your Celestial Highness."

e78de795-0d30-487e-8f39-82db7f40acb0.Text: "You should hurry. I can see your threads are loosening. You might lose your face that way, and even I won't be able to sew it back on."

7abddb54-ac4e-4b73-adf5-dfc2578b1c26.Text: "That tower is even more ancient than the castle! They say the Emperor Himself pulled it out of the ground, along with the entire mountain range."

19d44876-00ca-43d7-8a3f-bd5a55f300dd.Text: "The biggest vegetables on Thassera — at the price of regular vegetables! Sweeter only in the stars!"

d003d028-3ddb-4460-86b5-b74d5b9e01b3.Text: "Buy the freshest! Fish doesn't spoil in the presence of the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}!"

51d967ea-4275-4253-b476-e50c4c3600b2.Text: "Anything blessed by the gaze of the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} will last twice as long! I swear on the Emperor!"

ff97d54e-7803-49c9-b617-140321be792d.Text: "Did you see that? The Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} blessed my shop with {mf|his|her} glance!"

2cbde046-8695-4603-a52b-8defad5f311d.Text: "Don't miss out! Buy it while it's fresh!"

67063bb2-3d1a-403c-92f1-91d239918ae1.Text: "Three for the price of four! Offer lasts only while the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} is visiting!"

5ae6df8a-13dc-4417-a67d-128aa5347ea3.Text: "Pay your respects to the Celestial Lords and Ladies! Honour them by buying more!"

3ec8085b-d19b-490b-bdfc-a6d1992415bb.Text: There is nothing left in the pile of refuse that could be of any use to you. The rusty pitchfork refuses to budge.

e4d74d38-5547-4967-ae20-027fcb7653e4.Text: "Our Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! We've been waiting for you!"

ad1b7849-d1ea-4297-874b-4287352e8458.Text: "I'll be telling my grandchildren of this day!"

2554325b-bfff-408e-ae6b-a8ff4c089934.Text: "It's {mf|him|her}! The ruler of the stars who descended on an iron bird!"

86631f42-4102-4098-84d9-be702bb5a146.Text: The sculptor's masterful skill is evident in every little detail of your countenance.

f264c0cd-51ae-4fe5-af4c-3448b752fba5.Text: The leg of alcedont has gotten the better of you. You are so full that any careless movement will put you at risk of the meal fighting its way back out.

7a302034-550f-44e9-a4b2-0eb00de7f595.Text: Now that you have prevailed over a giant leg of alcedont, is there any obstacle you cannot surmount?

6df71a22-f5e2-44fd-a243-123b6c179b28.Text: Your throat and tongue are smarting from the terrible and relentless heat, making it incredibly difficult to focus on anything else.
