4c2a05e7-1b03-4fe9-8499-b15168a2597d.Text: {n}The girl sniffles and and smiles at the grey-haired gentleman in the doublet. He averts his eyes. The woman in the golden mask scoffs and withdraws into the gaping crowd.{/n}

184c4b25-a4c4-4e4b-b70c-666100787a4e.Text: "This is my former house servant... Timo... dressed as a noble! He is good, but he could never fool the true nobility." {n}The young woman deftly marks the man, who is frozen in horror, and pushes the data-brand back into your hand. Vengeful sparks play in her eyes. The woman in the golden mask graces her with a patronising nod.{/n}

a0f2bbdc-28ea-476e-9bb6-88e3441a9b11.Text: "Here she is, the real impostor, the house girl Renka! She admitted it herself to the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}!" {n}the old man spits and points his finger at Renka, who shrinks away in fear.{/n} "How could you schemers even think of deceiving our supreme benefactor?"

c45bf060-3632-4bc8-af42-7ea7b646f9b7.Text: {n}The young woman's face turns pale as marble behind her half-mask. She casts a seething look at the man in the jacket, then lowers her eyes. The man, meanwhile, sighs with relief and says,{/n} "Thank you. I knew that no intrigue could fool the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."

11913422-2914-4a3d-937a-1d0020e011ed.Text: {n}Their vulturous gazes shift to you in anticipation of your verdict.{/n}

91d6036a-c4a3-454d-b26c-27a224860942.Text: "Kae-morag!" {n}There is burning indignation in the look Yrliet gives the old man, her hand reaching for the blade hanging from her belt... But then, she goes still for a moment, puzzlement etched onto her face, before regaining its usual air of indifference.{/n} "Betrayal comes as naturally to you mon-keigh as breathing. But... it does not concern me. Continue rotting away in your dishonourable existence — I will have no part in it."

6cbefb6b-53c8-4f64-9542-f0d5b5823f4c.Text: {n}A tired sigh escapes Abelard's chest.{/n} "Thassera has more in common with Dargonus than I first thought."

b6172c68-4291-4ee8-bbcd-4fea3f5f02d5.Text: "I..." {n}she whispers quietly.{/n} "I'm just a commoner in a fancy dress, {mf|m'lord|m'lady}. This man is my master. I know I'm supposed to be playing the part of a rich girl, but... I've served many lords, you see, and Sir Timeus is the only one who treats his servants with gentleness. I want to protect him from these cruel people."

af009ea5-a36c-42ca-bcfc-c08c4211bed8.Text: {n}The lady in the golden mask curtsies gracefully.{/n} "Your Celestial Highness, we have exposed one of the impostors. There he is — the one in the jacket — still clinging to his facade. You ought to brand him, quickly!"

74f86125-19b8-4088-9111-182592b6ce13.Text: {n}The old man adjusts his mask in surprise. His eyes scan the crowd again and come to rest on the finely dressed young woman.{/n} "That's Renka, my house servant. What is she— Protecting me, you say? She has no idea what game she's got herself mixed up in. Forgive me, my girl..." {n}His lip quivers as he grips his cane more tightly and breathes in deeply, before suddenly taking a step back.{/n}

971420a5-c45a-40af-acee-06846659e8e1.Text: {n}The nobles around you hold their breath as they try to read the direction of your gaze.{/n}

8810437c-6288-4aa9-afd2-3f92d9c5dcf3.Text: {n}The woman is not lying, but neither is she being completely candid. The way she looks at the accused speaks of an old, inappeasable hatred, the kind one shows to one's true enemy.{/n}

ebe2fae3-e9eb-43ec-985b-ae7f17789eb7.Text: "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} knows how ruthless court intrigues can be. My f-family only recently attained its lofty status, and many here are opposed..." {n}he stutters, his teeth chattering in fear.{/n}

ca3ba748-ee0b-4757-a7d2-20d973bd6df8.Text: {n}Terrified, she drops her gaze and purses her lips.{/n} "I... I just pity him, my {mf|lord|lady}."

2444e378-0f5c-4dad-8e38-4f96e5854e90.Text: {n}The young woman freezes and squeaks out,{/n} "I obey my {mf|lord|lady}'s will! I..." {n}Her voice suddenly calms.{/n} "I know this man well and can dispel all your doubts." {n}You notice the old man breathe a sigh of relief when the data-brand is put into her hands.{/n}

db8dc108-00b4-444c-a9f5-70e0d079737e.Text: Ordered that the thassertium be destroyed and the world subjected to the holy Exterminatus.

c5de4309-7291-48a1-919b-ffb2533b2904.Text: "This world is beyond saving. Heresy exudes from its very depths. I hereby order the immediate destruction of all thassertium, and declare Exterminatus on the planet. The Administratum will be given several years to evacuate its property, after which, Thassera will be cleansed by fire."

a1aef837-b5d7-4bd7-82a8-67a504dfaf6b.Text: "I want to talk about your plan. What was your goal here, Ruoldo?"

cee39074-02f8-4441-a73d-07a4a6eb3c37.Text: "I have learned all I needed to know. You may execute the heretic, Solomorne."

68cd6ab9-b046-4fe1-a4c4-5b8602df57dc.Text: "What was the point of that whole masquerade with the fake governor?"

552fb98f-3f13-47fb-8612-5a2e83f9a700.Text: Supported Solomorne's decision to destroy the thassertium, in accordance with the letter of the Lex Imperialis.

88ceeb0d-97a1-4183-bd79-46f6973df0a0.Text: "Let us do it your way, Solomorne. If that is the solution the Lex Imperialis demands, then I fully concur."

63a19df3-548b-43fa-9d1e-256d10c69fec.Text: Ordered that the thassertium be destroyed and its properties not be reported to the Administratum out of concern for the lives of the world's inhabitants.

1e300e97-9270-48a0-bde2-221411818742.Text: "I agree that we must get rid of the thassertium, but I will not inform the Administratum of its properties. It may result in the planet's destruction, and we cannot have innocents suffer because of Ruoldo's misdeeds."

5a462d88-397a-49ab-b7c1-85627d09ccb9.Text: Ordered that the thassertium be included in the tithe, so that the corruption it hides might spread throughout the Imperium.

8c06494f-263a-4716-a707-bc44430476d6.Text: "Such a valuable material, such incredible possibilities... I hereby order thassertium to be added to the planet's tithe. The Imperium must obtain as much of this marvellous stone as possible."

b836698a-444c-445d-8c28-ac4d436abf29.Text: "I am taking you with me. You will join the ranks of the ship's servitors."

730c4e4a-40c6-48dc-b88e-53f7905a7453.Text: "Thassera needs a new governor. One we can trust."

6f6b4e71-9b32-4d64-b260-cfc99b7634b1.Text: "Are there any other victims of your ritual?"

5448304e-a067-4b2e-96f8-e8163422e027.Text: "You will learn as you go. I am leaving you in charge, Maive."

e423d7f5-070f-4a3a-9ce3-ebad7ec2410c.Text: "Relax. You will serve whatever governor I appoint from among people whose loyalty I can trust. And you will report their every movement to me."

bb561d38-9a72-48ea-a3e2-df8d1ab0e1f0.Text: "I am alive, Vigdis. Prepare to depart."

ef273597-435e-4ae3-bcb9-ab3c85321ab2.Text: "I have had a very difficult day, Vigdis. Get me out of this blasted hole."

14b9353b-248e-4c9d-8cbb-8167fa642115.Text: "What you do next is your business, Maive. I will not interfere with your fate."

f5c982f6-cb36-44f2-a300-b35a94089dbc.Text: "Pull yourself together! You can cry for your traitorous brother later!"

a230180e-6b03-4ab0-9500-95fee9aa02f5.Text: Ordered that the heretical altar be destroyed, regardless of the casualties.

34207769-3247-46ca-82f4-4ff9bd6f1c44.Text: [Destroy the altar] "The sacred fire of my ship's orbital cannons will raze the palace to the ground before this cursed artefact can corrupt another soul."

4559dce5-2954-44b4-af34-7df4a7a6be5d.Text: Left the destroyed altar on the planet but took one cursed shard.

45b92dc5-beb2-499f-b3c3-776e759ef456.Text: [Secretly take a shard of the altar] "This thing no longer poses any threat. Let it stay here."

9f6b2d97-06b8-4eae-854a-75963ee5aa7c.Text: Ordered that the heretical altar be hidden so that it could not harm innocent people.

25070bb4-a1d2-407f-98c6-937f9cc91d9b.Text: [Bury the altar] "We'll fill this abomination with tons of ferrocrete and hide it as best we can. That way it won't hurt anyone else."

f5a30935-5186-48ea-9620-5cbd82981da1.Text: "This is not my problem. We are leaving this planet immediately."

296f161b-8198-41f4-a728-b334f3c57248.Text: "The verdict, Solomorne. I will execute him myself."

c56bbb40-555b-4c88-bc4c-244f168e0cb3.Text: Executed Governor Ruoldo for the glory of the dark gods.

ff807b6d-d059-4bf4-a596-1f9046f8b2a7.Text: [Execute the governor] "Did you think your patrons would protect you? You miscalculated. There is only one person their gaze is turned toward. I dedicate this death to them."

064194d7-3457-453b-83a9-69cab0b75bdb.Text: Ordered that the thassertium be studied, despite its dangerous properties.

3688d5d3-d1ff-4337-8f25-7d713dad399c.Text: "Thassertium has been used for wicked ends, but that does not mean it cannot be useful. We must study the mineral thoroughly before deciding whether to destroy it, or include it in the tithe."

f75a431d-dad9-466e-9e9d-72f8baef3776.Text: "In the end, he realised thassertium was a potent {g|Encyclopedia:PsyfocusGlossary}psy-focus{/g}. After a thousand cursed attempts, and a combination of powers, energies, and sacrificial victims, Tavrisk managed to create his finest sculpture from it — the Altar of Change. A magnificent artefact; a door to eternity! No more limitations imposed by our mortal bodies. No ailments, no injuries! If your flesh is worn... just swap it for new flesh! Don't like your lot in life? Choose from a thousand others! No longer just a dream, but its most perfect realisation. Immortality in stone..."

2f17934c-cb69-4bdd-ae84-a7904a7f3565.Text: "Thank you, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! You are my saviour!" {n}Maive's eyes are shining with joy.{/n} "A servitor is like a servant, but on a ship, right?"

9eda2750-1727-44e8-8325-3c6461a937d3.Text: "The plan was simple and elegant: Thassera starts underpaying its {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}tithe{/g}; the Arbites swallow the bait and send their messengers here. That's when I spring my trap: I change into the body of the Arbitrator or Proctor who lands here, pack up the altar, board the Arbites ship, and wave goodbye to this ball of dirt swinging in the void! A Rogue Trader would have been even better, but greed has a way of spoiling a good game of {g|Encyclopedia:Regicide}regicide{/g}."

e7212060-7747-4f1f-bd63-ae56b46aaa14.Text: "Since you're done..." {n}Solomorne points his weapon.{/n} "Ruoldo, you have committed unthinkable heresy, and I refuse to acknowledge you as a human being or read your verdict as befitting a criminal. You are a stain on Thassera's history, and it is time to wipe you from it." {n}Although he executes the governor quickly, you see a fleeting expression of absolute disgust, perhaps even hatred, pass over the Proctor's face.{/n}

94f3421b-d8b0-464f-8937-1be932f827a3.Text: "Cease your inane mutterings. You may open your mouth when you are asked a question. And your answer had better be honest and to the point, or I swear by the {g|Encyclopedia:LexImperialisGlossary}Lex{/g}, I will make you speak — or rather, whatever remains of you after I finish preparing you for the interrogation."

41747384-b41b-4c8d-9c9f-07951a64d2bc.Text: "That survived, no — and I didn't count the dead. The ritual is a complex one to perform, so it took Tavrisk and me a long time to calibrate it. And you were the one it worked on. To think of all the possibilities that opened up... Using the Altar of Change, I could have worked my way up to a Lord of {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Terra{/g}!"

650cbd84-d2f1-479e-aca8-94055e150f95.Text: "As my father used to say, 'if you've come a long way, keep going!' I'm a dead man as it is, so I might as well dream a little."

79c90d88-cf34-49eb-93a5-707a8052ea90.Text: {n}Maive opens her eyes and immediately jumps to her feet at the sight of the bloodied corpse. She clenches her hands on her chest, and her eyes well up.{/n}

c025d7cb-c07c-49ae-9c88-55cc61ceba70.Text: {n}The young woman nods meekly, and a single tear runs down her cheek. Her voice is hollow when she speaks:{/n} "You're right... He was the one who doomed him."

de7120db-3ef4-4e05-8e66-73c038964911.Text: {n}Maive looks up at you pleadingly.{/n} "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}... what am I... to do now...?"

6910b577-8285-4985-9ecf-1e7956b5400c.Text: "You're going to trust a heretic with brewing your {g|Encyclopedia:Recaf}recaf{/g}? Then, you ought to take a dozen local commoners along as well, to taste anything that criminal has handled."

396d368c-dcdf-465f-9350-d549ed907d0a.Text: {n}You are interrupted by an anxious voice from the vox:{/n} "Lord Captain, do you read? The shuttle pilot reported the rescue operation. Enforcers are on their way. What is your status? Are you alive? Come in!"

41790cc0-02fd-473d-995f-2eabfc8764db.Text: "Thank you, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! You are my saviour!"

1455d5d2-84c9-4bd7-b19c-c0543468cee1.Text: "I can... brew recaf. I can do sweet with a foam of cream, or strong with special spices. I can dance... sing... carry scrolls and data-slates..."

0d9996a5-08cd-42a6-b6fa-e4be5bf30df4.Text: "Please, not me. Anyone but me. Who would listen to a court upstart who used to be a chamberpot maid?" {n}Maive blushes profusely as she realises she has said too much.{/n}

587c1239-7e5b-46d7-bc8c-b8b6fa0c46a4.Text: "If this is a joke, I'm missing the punchline. And if you are being serious... After what happened, the Administratum is going to take serious steps against the hotbed of perverse sorcery that this world has become. You may want to begin envying your older brother his fate, Governor."

36f76a63-4bc5-4e71-9a66-7ad86524fe23.Text: "A drastic decision born out of righteous indignation. Whether or not the prefect shares your views — that we won't know until we return to Dargonus."

ba23c529-aa67-4092-aa35-5c6127ca54ee.Text: "Then, Thassera's fate is decided, and there is no point in staying here any longer."

b22ab3b9-d2f1-4ff6-a7b1-65ab41cef6bc.Text: "She may be an illiterate heretic, but at least there is a modicum of sense in her."

be716d31-e3fd-4e9d-8189-fd6ebd275a9c.Text: "Deciding what to do with the thassertium is far more important. It is a... resource we cannot afford to ignore." {n}Solomorne looks you straight in the eye.{/n} "I propose destroying all the thassertium already mined, as well as its deposits. The probability that the material itself is a source of corruption is too high. It would take years of research by the Adeptus Astra Telepathica to prove it safe for the souls of the sanctioned, years that Koronus does not have even if the local Adept had funds to spare. Allowing an abomination like that to exist is against the Lex. As for assessing the degree of Thassera's corruption and deciding its fate, the law prescribes leaving this to the judgement of the world's owners — that is, the Administratum."

a17026cb-1ff2-4e82-b714-cff5787a8e47.Text: "You are entitled to share any information you deem necessary with the prefect, but I am duty-bound to make a report to the Marshal. I will tell him that the Rogue Trader has taken the Thasserians under {mf|his|her} protection. I can hardly expect your will to be taken as negotiable."

4233a001-f569-4981-a8d0-c7c22e9e30c3.Text: {n}Solomorne grinds his teeth, but obediently declares:{/n} "Your orders are clear, Rogue Trader."

ec2335f8-5dea-41a5-8fde-2d9d7191a649.Text: "Yes, the data-slate with the shipment chronicle that they spent so much time vainly 'searching' for. According to the records, the tithe period is one Terran decade and the quota prescribed is a thousand cargo units. The governor withheld a hundred units from each of the five most recent shipments. That means this world has no actual difficulty regularly supplying its tribute. We can consider that matter settled."

981c12a4-1aff-4e76-81a0-a6a987e02b54.Text: "What are you talking about? The very suggestion—" {n}The Proctor's voice resounds with fury. His steely fingers dig into Glaito's collar.{/n} "You sick degenerate!"

7ada4dd7-8945-4caa-b122-c56afa7b3878.Text: "The irony..." {n}Ruoldo grimaces in pain as he takes a deep, greedy drag.{/n} "The last one is always the sweetest."

c22aeaa8-f240-4cae-a75b-4033c09a794f.Text: "What a monstrously twisted notion of eternity..."

bcb801d3-9d86-43b1-bc7f-fcc33e4af8f9.Text: "What? Ugh, yes, I know it's not an option... I've got my own life to live out, somehow. Why would I want to take on another?"

adcd1f45-9e7f-4f03-9df1-eba978b8f092.Text: "Mon-keigh just love toying with forces beyond their control, all in the name of extending their pitiful little lifespan. I would even say it's... touching, in its own way."

9ccfa9e4-6bdf-4ba8-a534-94586cfc2459.Text: "Master Killjoy, a psy-focus is just a rock without a will of its own. A tool. Like you. So what if some lunatic once used it for their deranged ends? It can just as equally serve a good purpose!"

64e7317a-ab1b-4a90-8862-b41343306c56.Text: "Destroy the goldmine? Has the iron-jawed ashmag lost his mind, shereen? We've got to start harvesting this wonderful mineral! In the name of the Imperium, obviously..."

0c859556-e2f8-4396-bf4f-474e64a0b664.Text: "Dare I remind you, Lord Captain, that no one besides you has any knowledge of this mineral's properties? If it is left here, no one will find out."

33a151df-b654-4b86-acd1-6281bf11f5e2.Text: "What a crafty way to paint me as a mindless henchman. Let me also remind you that I report directly to the Marshal, and my reports are thorough."

aa7bcac4-a6b6-426f-939d-83fecc374a01.Text: "The plan has not changed, Vil'Ruoldo. The Undying One has whispered your name, and the execution of His will is nigh."

213035aa-5b72-4cc7-8276-cca2be2a42c1.Text: "This statement is false, for it is incomplete. The rite of Servitude Imperpituis does not inhibit the unit's communication abilities — it replaces the decay of worldly notions with sacred logo-algorithms. Flesh-speak is flawed and redundant."

efc276a6-f890-4d51-9c58-cc6da98636bd.Text: "Be silent, heretic. Or you will find yourself washing away your blasphemies with tears of blood until the pain makes you beg the Emperor for death."

6fcf683b-1b5f-434d-b205-7422175c9f8c.Text: "This wretched little world held nothing worthy of attention... save for thassertium. When I started having dreams about it, and about changing bodies, I thought I was going insane... And I shared this with my sculptor, the now late Tavrisk. He helped me to understand the essence of the mineral. Experiments and studies followed — mostly carried out by Tavrisk. I don't have his gift, but oh, the things I could do if I were a sorcerer..."

1a48a4c2-1287-4419-95bc-9de77178aa07.Text: "Agreed. Anything even remotely connected to the heresy that was committed here must be destroyed down to the last fragment — and to the last participant."

6bb09512-7209-4a24-a3f2-13207c2966b9.Text: "I understand. Thank you... for your mercy, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}." {n}Maive curtsies, staring straight ahead in confusion.{/n}

52a1fc28-b9a2-4010-97ee-782c279722fd.Text: "The heretic mentioned that destroying the altar would risk deaths among the local population. Whether he was lying or trying to manipulate us is irrelevant: the abomination must be destroyed. As for any casualties... The Emperor will know His own."

e09e55aa-4f2b-4e99-9b4b-6e03896478f7.Text: {n}As you approach the damaged altar, you feel an unpleasant weakness. You hear a faint ringing in your ears, as if the smooth surface of the stone is groaning from the wounds it has suffered.{/n}

ee494b5b-6151-47a8-acb3-0f4745f50f2d.Text: "You were an accomplice to the heretics, and you have been touched by sorcerous blight. In your position, I would beg for a swift execution." {n}There is no hatred in Solomorne's words, only total conviction about their truth.{/n}

e57ca78e-201d-4295-9be5-8797edfaefdd.Text: {n}As you look up at the altar, the ringing in your ears intensifies for a moment. Rupturing your eardrums, the altar roars, threatening, promising to take thousands more with it. But you are deaf to its pitiful threats.{/n}

8eed62c4-d17f-42a9-bae9-94174bfa5c91.Text: {n}As you lean over the shards, the ringing in your ears intensifies for a moment. A quiet voice promises you strength and power, asks you to save it from oblivion, and you graciously fulfil its request. Once the largest of the shards is in your hands, it falls silent, pacified.{/n}

4d480a9d-a992-49b4-9d68-1b544b319c37.Text: "Of course, this game involved one key piece. The embodiment of freedom of choice — my magnificent Altar. So much accumulated potential from years of experimentation. It is damaged, but it still beckons, waiting to be used..." {n}Ruoldo looks you in the eye with a caustic smile.{/n} "I advise you to keep it safe — who knows how many thousands of lives it will claim if something happens to it, unleashing all that power?"

81a43858-0042-4ea5-b279-5c7e9b53c149.Text: {n}The strange ringing stops, leaving behind an unpleasant echo in your ears — your head must still be suffering from the effects of moving between bodies.{/n}

4979490a-a2d5-4d62-9670-87fb2afcc924.Text: {n}Argenta closes her eyes and utters a prayer:{/n} "Emperor, have mercy on the unfortunate souls who found themselves trapped in the grasp of the Archenemy. Have mercy, for they knew nothing and had nowhere to go..."

9a2b61bc-93d8-43c2-9097-f98c7645e850.Text: "To cut the thread of an entire world but prevent the spread of corruption is to please the Undying Emperor. The Domin's will be done, and may Thassera accept its sacred death."

28305efc-6e7e-483c-9d5d-624e199aa68d.Text: "Elantach, your desire to understand rather than destroy out of fear does your credit, but... take heed: the minds of mon-keigh are fragile and ill-equipped to withstand something with such a strong connection to the veil."

1dbe0269-8fc0-4748-ac65-79e6b9f4cbfd.Text: {n}A timid prayer falls from Maive's lips:{/n} "Emperor on the Golden Throne, my whole life I was mistaken in my ways of honouring You, but now I pray to You... not for my own soul, but for his..."

bad04323-03b9-42bd-ae48-31964158254a.Text: "Thank you, Rogue Trader. This is the right choice."

b85a3d09-2665-450f-bfaa-b14040011403.Text: "Y-yes... as you command... But my brother wasn't the traitor — the man who killed him was..." {n}The young woman's shoulders continue to shake a little, but she makes no more sounds.{/n}

ae50b209-b101-4327-a69e-f404005301a6.Text: "Ruoldo, you have committed unthinkable heresy, and I refuse to acknowledge you as a human being or read your verdict as befitting a criminal. You are a stain on Thassera's history, and it is time—" {n}You point your weapon and put the governor to death right as Solomorne finishes speaking:{/n} "—to wipe you from it."

4d444a55-58af-45c6-94aa-8c85e0144c41.Text: {n}Ruoldo's eyes widen with terror. Drops of sweat run down his pathetically shaking chin. You could drink his fear and despair like rich wine. A moment later, blood gushes from the governor's absurdly gaping mouth, gurgling and bubbling as it splashes onto the stone... Far at the back of your mind's velvety darkness, a voice cackles briefly. It is pleased. It is sated.{/n}

58314f22-1dd6-43f2-ad86-3891cb96814c.Text: {n}Solomorne looks at you intently.{/n} "An... interesting verdict, Rogue Trader. Nevertheless, the criminal has been punished, and that is all that matters now."

ff701d33-6d41-43c5-9b70-deeda4a2931b.Text: {n}The Proctor swiftly kills the young woman before she is able to comprehend what you said. She sinks to the floor like a broken doll. Solomorne looks away, not resting his gaze on her even for a moment.{/n}

acdedb02-f1ad-43d7-9d57-40e489ae321b.Text: "A governor attracts too much attention, and I wanted my hands to stay untied. So, I offered my court fool a fair bargain: he would become me — ruling the planet, living the good life, getting whatever he wanted — while I would be out there, flying toward the stars. We traded faces, clothes, and lives. And because I had gotten the local nobles into the habit of sewing other people's mugs on their heads, the switch went unnoticed."

5085096e-85e9-48f1-aca3-7714ea21a276.Text: "But the switch was only the first part of the deal. Naturally, I didn't mention the second part: the removal of witnesses. If someone is going to turn against you the moment there's a knife at his beloved sister's throat, you can't afford to keep him alive." {n}Ruoldo casts a hateful glance in Maive's direction.{/n}

c1e7ad68-3576-4b03-b8cd-4e027932199d.Text: "I am wondering where to start. Should I cut out your blabbering tongue? Or just strike you down now and not beat about the bush?"

477c76d0-a1e7-45e4-b5c5-f2dadca6751a.Text: "How does one find an impostor in the crowd?"

9b1f0cea-7e9b-48df-a09f-31050d39878c.Text: [Glance indifferently at the governor and roll your eyes]

6184c9df-a2ed-4bf8-a450-b741a6a1fefa.Text: "The only dish I want is called 'the warp-damned tithe,' and I want it served to me this instant."

748da05d-e2ba-4013-9a1c-64393eda19bd.Text: "Suppose I found all the impostors. What happens next?"

d63b87c9-22e5-4630-af92-9eaf7f57636e.Text: [Defeat the blaberid shells seasoned with blue glut]

ced084d8-d158-4197-a3be-037026ea2357.Text: "It is well known that laceraxes can only be found on Janus."

83680baa-3e52-47b6-b901-a5439d00dbc0.Text: [Gesture toward Solomorne] "I have grown tired of these savages. Deal with him."

5dfdc99e-1eda-4999-a904-4d70e7ed96f1.Text: "My time is too precious for me to waste it on rabble. Announce the end of the hunt and let us get down to business."

338d3901-170b-4330-928a-e1bbed175b9c.Text: "You cannot pronounce the name of your homeworld? Really?"

32d30f03-c8cb-4b99-9c1c-80da2c93a8cf.Text: "This is not a conversation I am interested in having. Let us discuss other topics."

703514f0-6592-4c62-bb60-247a162d3d62.Text: "Why would servants of the Omnissiah care who had taken the throne of a technologically undeveloped world?"

f18ea7e3-bcc1-4e65-97c1-334dc5ec27cb.Text: "Now that we have had some refreshments, let us talk."

571e761e-d477-49df-a144-ef01a9fcae87.Text: "Solomorne, are you sure this is small talk and not an interrogation?"

abb2d882-c8ba-4cb7-bb78-bb516cefeac2.Text: [Lend cold suspicion to your voice] "A long time ago? Do laceraxes even live all that long?"

ef7c513f-51ff-4890-8877-a1baa059eecd.Text: "They say people go missing after the Impostor Hunt. What do you make of this?"

493df817-5bb3-4dd5-927d-cef6aa46fa35.Text: [Take the lead] "Be bold. Don't think about anything."

687d8880-e64c-43c1-8a08-42e30c1b3652.Text: "Truly, I cannot say. I think I quite enjoyed the local fashion. Maybe I should take a few costumes away with me."

472b11f2-78eb-4aea-8f76-935b22f00f3e.Text: "Best stop there while I still have one working foot."

d4ecbd1a-1869-43b2-b358-1e0bb467b708.Text: "Another local pastime? Very well. I hope it is not as pathetic as the last one."

2773d9c2-1e10-44fd-8df7-c7737da97933.Text: [Smile through your pain] "Thank you for the dance, but... let's stop for now. We can pick this up some other time, when you aren't as distracted."

925092fd-f41f-410a-895b-63de286719ba.Text: "Solomorne, you may ask the governor your questions."

a2da43e1-2624-49cf-bee9-1937139a1242.Text: "I have neither the time nor the inclination to entertain your rabble. The tithe, Governor — I am only interested in the tithe."

a1811e92-6310-4c94-873a-b667b894d0f5.Text: [Wink at Solomorne and take the comm-bead from your ear] "I was presented with this pearl that whispers great secrets and mysteries. What a marvel! I was told it is an artefact from Idex."

ce8be99f-98dc-4a8f-b250-a2351ed2648d.Text: "Your answers are rather reticent and tentative, Ruoldo — almost as if you were merely a chance passer-by and not the governor."

843ea472-0b8d-4491-98ef-28778997732b.Text: "I wish to move on to discussing the tithe as quickly as possible."

98505e46-79f0-45c9-9cf0-232bd55989e1.Text: "What if you too are an impostor, Ruoldo?"

dad0bf39-355e-4cc2-96a1-911a3c80d491.Text: "At the end of the hunt, we hold a great feast. If you guess at least one of the impostors, you will also win a fine prize. If you guess all four, there will be an even more special reward. I remember, at one of the hunts, a servant played the role of a baron so well that all the lords unanimously granted him favour and let him keep the title and privileges of the nobility. Such a thing rarely happens, but... who knows what the evening will bring, for tonight, it is you who will determine the worthy, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."

defd3e03-6b69-4ecd-9467-e9a5b48777c4.Text: "I think I remember... In the treatise 'The Silent Language of Celestial Lords: Reading Their Gestures,' it is said, 'If His or Her Highness first turns their countenance upon you and only then toward the heavens, you have spoken well and are blessed to proceed.' Verily, it is heartening to know that you uphold our traditions and agree to participate in the hunt, Your Celestial Highness! Maive, present the data-brand! Please return when you have found all the impostors!"

e3275f8c-25fb-4e00-ad76-218bbfbf22f1.Text: "Only three people have managed to conquer the shrimperius tonight, and all of them are inferior to you in the sophistication and speed of their forkcraft!" {n}The governor hurriedly toasts you, spilling his drink in the process.{/n}

d3ef3f6a-ed3a-43f5-9055-7e9674625667.Text: "Of course, my lord. The Impostor Hunt takes place every moonlife. Shortly before the event, the servants are thoroughly cleansed of dirt and foulness, combed, dressed in expensive clothing and masks, and invited into the courtyard with the rest of the guests. The nobles hide their faces as well, and then, they try to guess who the impostors are. Telling one from the other is quite a challenge, sometimes."

2d3a7c07-28bb-475d-9e17-85c0a528159d.Text: "My lord! Remember what the physician told you: temperance is the best cure for your ailments! I fear that you have disobeyed his wishes again today."

c6273854-eafc-4bb5-860b-4d65ce9d6803.Text: {n}You sink your teeth into the greasy morsel and deftly nibble it to the bone in front of the entire court, which watches you with morbid fascination.{/n}

8d5e27c4-629c-4130-8048-990858f3b550.Text: {n}As the blue glut stings your tongue, you lose all will to continue eating this dish. You immediately wash it down with chilled amasec, allowing the blend of fire and ice to permeate your entire being.{/n}

dd474be8-845b-4769-8058-e43878c04bdf.Text: {n}Deftly wielding a set of forks and knives, you cut off the shrimperius's escape routes. At last, all five of its tails are pinned to the table with golden prongs, and the sixth fork delivers the final blow, allowing you to send the exquisite meal into your mouth.{/n}

237c590b-fef9-443c-bef7-f5c758481f3a.Text: {n}Your words cause the governor to sober up immediately.{/n} "E-everything is prepared, my {mf|lord|lady}! All records of deliveries and contributions. It truly is a tragedy that you will not get to enjoy our Impostor Hunt, an event that has been so assiduously prepared to delight the eyes and mind of Your Celestial Highness... Unless you... reconsider? My {mf|lord|lady}...?"

82c11600-57b4-4d40-bb0c-3aa6b8f84840.Text: "Magnificent! Not even the rock serpentid that recently ate our cobbler could match you. Unlike Your Celestial Highness, it spent five entire suns chewing through him!" {n}The governor toasts you excitedly.{/n}

f10047ae-4942-44d3-95bd-5c0444f4f2ad.Text: "I am afraid there was a second, less flattering interpretation in that book... which I cannot recall. May you enjoy the hunt, my {mf|lord|lady}!" {n}Maive adds humbly.{/n}

3fec46d2-4fdd-4116-a663-24cc8987f6ae.Text: {n}The governor suddenly perks up again.{/n} "And that is the best part! I highly recommend you try it, Your Celestial Highness. It makes for a very interesting change of pace. And, on this occasion, the privilege of branding, if you will, falls entirely to you, our honoured celestial guest."

9ae4e4fe-d59e-435c-b483-9548fd4bee86.Text: "I hear and immediately obey, Your Celestial Highness!"

853c1971-8db5-4248-80ac-ddba91d5c3e7.Text: "I feel it in my heart that we have failed to please you. And of course, there were those freaks running wild! This entire celebration, this whole endeavour, has been a tremendous waste!" {n}The last words fade into an incoherent mutter as the man's trembling hand reaches for the amasec.{/n}

3ea2809c-fad8-4476-87f0-a2403d444588.Text: "I was interested in the musical servitors. They could only have been brought to you by the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}crimson priests{/g}, correct? Can you tell me why they visited the planet?"

bdb97fb3-4ea9-45f9-9b19-0d27c0926832.Text: "I cannot tell you off the top of my head. Are there not many planets that have laceraxes? I received these beasts a long time ago as a gift."

b16aa124-c73f-4a99-8345-7c829742546a.Text: {n}The governor shrugs helplessly.{/n} "I was too overjoyed at their appearance to ask. A gesture of deference, I suppose? Who can ever understand those mysterious crimson priests?"

6119b415-3e28-4606-8160-80dad1374a39.Text: "Your Celestial Highness, how can you say such a thing! I have never even seen a lowborn village up close. They are cowering down there, thank the God-Emperor." {n}The governor empties another goblet brought to him by the servants.{/n} "Fetch us more {g|Encyclopedia:Amasec}amasec{/g}! Now! What are you looking at? Go, go! Useless layabouts..."

a8690742-ff47-428e-b47e-32b69259085a.Text: "My {mf|lord|lady}, I am afraid one of my subjects has passed off their own creation as the bounty of Idex, perhaps to add more weight to the offering."

90284f6d-28cc-4fee-b365-17b783ae6262.Text: "Verily, Your Celestial Highness!" {n}He reaches his ring-studded hand for the goblet, but stops at the sound of Maive's voice.{/n}

1a405f04-1ae0-43b4-9ddf-1e869c3f208a.Text: {n}You sink your teeth into the greasy ham and slowly chew the brackish, fibrous meat with all your might. At the seventh bite, your jaw begins to ache, and you are forced to give up the fight.{/n}

4f65e53d-278a-4dc6-ad2b-8e3430bd6a7d.Text: "And now, I am paying for it with a compromised sense of balance and a regrettable inability to admire the disguised impostors... And the hunt is already in full swing!"

060a1b4f-2f42-4dc2-af17-688747c2394b.Text: "She almost ripped off my finger along with a slice of alcedont. It's my fault for forgetting they're predators, albeit domesticated ones."

5cc0fc90-c066-493c-80f5-1a94e12f4092.Text: "Moderation is wisdom! And wisdom is the attribute of true sovereigns. To your most Imperial prudence, Your Celestial Highness!" {n}The governor solemnly drains a goblet of amasec.{/n}

8ff26ac1-41c8-4b79-8a4c-e560b3d3d183.Text: {n}You arm yourself with a fork and pierce one of the shrimperius's tails. Much to the disappointment of your sympathetic audience, the creature leaves you with a discarded extremity and scurries off the table with its four remaining ones.{/n}

b04dae99-45f1-4bab-88cd-91f632048196.Text: "You have reduced a beast, born to hunt and kill, to a domesticated pet. Without purpose and discipline, both man and animal alike are destined for degradation." {n}Solomorne nods at Glaito, who is completely unfazed by the multitude of delicacies.{/n} "See? This is the level of obedience and dignity we should strive for."

7dbfd8a1-0536-4720-b27b-31675cf37051.Text: "Do not be upset, Your Celestial Highness. One of those shrimperiuses is still rampaging through my bowels! What naughty critters they are..."

ecd57dc2-9cd8-4c9d-b547-e72929981c31.Text: {n}You pop a fried blaberid shell into your mouth — first one, and then another, and another. The blue glut stings your tongue and throat, but {name} von Valancius is made of sterner stuff than all these milksops. Eventually, you crush the last blaberid between your jaws, before wiping a napkin over your chin and tossing it victoriously onto the table.{/n}

eebd4abd-04b9-4f8a-b431-f873e52478b2.Text: "Incredible! But how? How did you accomplish it? My fellow revellers, let us raise our cups to the unbreakable strength of the God-Emperor's emissary!" {n}The entire Thasserian nobility lift their golden goblets in your honour.{/n}

6d0abc91-2467-44b9-924b-a45a8c7da430.Text: "I can see it in your eyes — you felt it too: the newfound wings at your back, the fresh sea breeze in the mustiness of life, the spark of purpose in the dark alley of consciousness! Isn't it divine?" {n}Inspired by your example, the governor places a blaberid shell on his tongue, shudders, and promptly drains a fresh goblet of amasec.{/n}

daec8a45-49e1-444e-8849-b4371e7a7365.Text: "Delightful! I will immediately summon the court for a final celebration of hypocrisy! And who knows: perhaps, today, one of the impostors will be lucky enough to earn your favour."

cb53c2d5-ac0c-4f0c-a35c-166d170751dd.Text: "I understand, Your Celestial Highness! As our nobles say, measure thy torture ten times; thou canst behead a man but once."

abce1f38-756d-40c6-9927-c52ce2d1e155.Text: "It would be a good adage if not for the local mores. I bet there are at least five course changes between torture and execution on Thassera, and with music."

abf8c878-7060-4d11-8c7f-6c3f986a0cd5.Text: {n}Maive produces a shimmering slate featuring a string of fine inscriptions.{/n} "This is a data-brand — one of our off-world treasures. We handle it with the greatest care. And yet, all of Thassera's jewels and miracles cannot compare to the resplendence of your glory, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. When you find an impostor, you need only mark them with this wondrous brand."

a932abcc-9a39-4829-9997-b65d8d5ee3f7.Text: "He will be useless then. Let him show me the record scrolls first."

1d489769-011a-43e2-949a-fdd98f0aab83.Text: "My darling pet. She is guarding the shrimperiuses. Every once in a while, she gets an allowance in the form of alcedont bones."

f8126cb9-f414-43e3-aa58-74c51d1fbb90.Text: "With pleasure. Cut the festivities, Governor. It is time to discuss the tithe."

2e61e7be-352d-4b1f-b00c-9c0001ef576c.Text: "Then, we are about to have the shortest Impostor Hunt in Thassera's history! Straight to the finale, just as you ordered!"

e80adb5f-c13d-4827-9d88-078d28aac7d0.Text: {n}Ruoldo waves a hand at Maive:{/n} "Be a darling and tell our guest about our amusements. I am a little... exhausted."

0121a27a-e797-4967-a35c-43e925131b02.Text: {n}The governor's hand reaches for the amasec, but flinches under your gaze and abruptly changes trajectory toward the appetisers.{/n} "Today is a very nervous day, Your Celestial Highness. And when I feel nervous, I eat. And drink. And eat again! That is just the way I am. But, Emperor have mercy, the food today is to die for! Would you like to have some?"

ca0ad39e-6480-4612-bc7d-481faaa20e9a.Text: "Did you just admit that there is masquerading rabble among the Thasserian nobles? Illiterate, with no idea how to collect tithes or... By the Throne, that actually explains so much." {n}The Proctor scoffs and glances at the enthusiastic guests.{/n} "Go ahead, Governor. Commence your charade. The sooner we start, the sooner we finish."

695f8b92-e84a-44c6-817a-becd25193218.Text: {n}The governor lets out an audible gulp.{/n} "It shall be done, Master Judicator."

1d4e69bc-c30c-420a-8428-78c9a329639f.Text: "If I can amuse the esteemed judicator with conversation, I will be only too glad to..."

d88ea8c1-8e31-4863-92bc-dccc620589da.Text: "Perhaps you should stay here, my lord?" {n}Maive's gaze is full of genuine concern.{/n}

21722dbc-980c-4e86-9211-c5039629ac6d.Text: "I feel you may be right, Maive. I will be waiting here, surrounded by savoury dishes and plentiful amasec. Have a fruitful hunt, Your Celestial Highness!"

34efacbb-1e45-4476-91f8-2b02e5d766d3.Text: "But of course. I have always wanted to try my hand at casual small talk." {n}Solomorne folds his arms imperiously over his chest, somehow becoming even taller in stature and broader in the shoulders.{/n} "Tell me about the laceraxes, Governor. Such fascinating creatures — where did you get them from?"

971d6b73-10dc-417e-9fc6-ba588cd186b1.Text: "Oh, yes! The famous Idexian pearls of revelation. I often use them myself to keep my mind receptive to new ideas."

4b7e48a1-e132-4b6a-834b-af260ccc116f.Text: "Since laceraxes are used for entertainment, they do not last long on Thassera, and they are brought in batches, hence the 'long ago.' Honestly, beasts from faraway worlds are not that interesting a topic of conversation. Let us talk about something else, shall we?"

8ae483ce-68a1-4e48-901f-a8fab874895c.Text: "Ehm, I think they were the red robes who arrived to celebrate the ascendance of a new governor. That's me." {n}Ruoldo's wistful gaze follows a shrimperius fleeing the table.{/n}

c1ec6321-19e3-4e48-8463-4902a9b8a791.Text: "Indeed. The Tech-Priests are famous for having many vocations outside of pursuing technology and discovering new knowledge. Like music, and visits of courtesy..."

3e266627-b279-4c53-8565-feabb3d379e9.Text: "Down, Garra! Bad beast, very bad! I apologise, Your Celestial Highness. How is your Impostor Hunt going?"

7781469a-c0e7-43b8-980d-6474e26b9479.Text: {n}The governor throws up his hands.{/n} "Can they? And I was sure they were a common beastie! I might have embarrassed myself there, but I would be glad to talk about something else."

77213aea-e6bf-4194-840e-73c2d5cf5d6c.Text: "Do not judge me harshly. I am just trying to get into the festive mood as best I can. We can certainly change the subject. I would like to note that I find your youth-extending face transplant procedure amazing. Does Thassera possess any other unique knowledge or items brought over from your homeworld? What is that world called, by the way?"

bf6c48de-d551-4eab-81e5-0ab3d8d9ef09.Text: "They are not exactly Idexian garments, but who cares? Just say the word, and the hold of your celestial vessel will soon be bursting with Thasserian vestments. After the celebration, of course."

601e8db4-92ac-422a-9239-98b5ad54b5b9.Text: "I... do not know? I would rather tell you about things I am much better acquainted with, like Thasserian amasec, for example."

fe5083d6-8dc7-46ad-bc63-103f8a7782cf.Text: {n}The governor takes a big sip from his cup.{/n} "I am a bit tipsy, so I cannot help it! On a day like today, it would be criminal not to toast such important guests!"

bd58bd85-0e5b-4a15-a77a-090db5080144.Text: {n}Solomorne leans over to you:{/n} "Rogue Trader, once you've had your fill of the governor, let me ask him a few questions."

1df4edab-5dd0-438d-af3e-a8a608a4fbc5.Text: "Ah, my native Idesk... Idex. Unfortunately, I have not introduced much from it beyond the art of changing faces. But perhaps the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} has taken a liking to some of Thassera's original creations?"

279ad275-6128-455c-8107-58d5d60f917b.Text: "Your Celestial Highness must have been listening to a lot of gossip. Who cares where the rabble goes afterward? However, I can assure you that the victors are often sent into my personal service. We call it the Highest Favour, and today, it will be up to you to choose whom it should be bestowed upon!"

9c322230-e1ca-48f6-9e00-a5fcd488e457.Text: "Marvellous! As soon as you are done with your search, I will be..." {n}The governor attempts to rise from the table, but gravity proves to be his superior.{/n}

7d3a33f0-6240-43a5-a0d0-65e9f76095c6.Text: {n}The governor is dragging out his words, as if he is not entirely sure of them himself — or is not telling you something.{/n}

f46752bc-5c9a-4b32-a699-8006a109fc97.Text: "What?" {n}A shrimperius wriggles free of the governor's fork and drops into his goblet.{/n} "Yes, it was foreigners who delivered the mechanical musicians... I'm sure I have not mentioned them yet..."

33bb3256-2317-49a7-bca8-b40f8417cf00.Text: {n}The man's face becomes stretched to the limit on its fastenings, signalling deep offence.{/n} "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! I ask that you do not insult me so! I may not be used to having such lofty conversations, but believe me: I am definitely the governor of Thassera!"

7c0bb4a9-a361-48e4-8163-f4ea0359f7ce.Text: "Thank you for the conversation, Governor. I have learned everything I wanted to know."

30d0fc33-0ef3-4eb3-8dd4-edc7365bea17.Text: "I would never question your title, Governor." {n}Solomorne gives you a long look.{/n} "And the Rogue Trader hardly wishes to offend you either."

6548f68a-4a27-4df7-94b0-392581d72c6f.Text: {n}The governor's voice is unsteady. He seems to be already well in his cups.{/n}

9d49901c-e9be-41b3-9732-a5062b2ba231.Text: {n}With a distracted smile in the direction of his orchestra, the governor adds as if in passing:{/n} "Music... It lifts the spirit, improves digestion, and allows one to refresh oneself between courses by having a nice dance with a gallant partner." {n}He casts an intent look at Solomorne standing beside you.{/n}

2c50acb4-3be3-4e08-ba5c-2f9148f734c3.Text: "It would be my honour." {n}Solomorne's face is an impenetrable glower. He takes your hand, his palm firm and covered with calluses from his weapon grip.{/n}

a57de408-f4cc-437a-8170-c4c84ad4ca2d.Text: {n}Solomorne is clearly trying to move to the beat of the music but meeting with little success — his stiff movements make him look like a broken servitor. His hold on you is delicate, as if you were a fragile vase, but there is no thrill of passion in his touch. He avoids meeting your eye, instead looking off to the side, monitoring the assembled guests. During the next step, he treads heavily and very painfully on your foot.{/n}

72440213-38f0-4813-9fed-239ff640e293.Text: {n}Scowling even more, Solomorne sullenly mutters,{/n} "I apologise."

6c62041b-eab1-4140-834b-2330dc269e97.Text: "By the way they talk, by their lack of restraint — the unfamiliar delicacies overwhelm them so much that they lose control. Impostors are often scared of the responsibility that has fallen on their weak shoulders, and they try to stay close to the real nobles and imitate their rarefied manners. During the hunt, it is most worthwhile to pay attention to separate groups where conversation has already started — a frightened impostor will probably try to hide behind other people's backs... That's all I know, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."

dc766e83-2ff7-4c6a-8f65-fb799e954ed6.Text: "I feel like these people have scopes instead of eyes. And you and I are a paired target."

b8f757ad-296a-4c1d-89d4-4596e6135218.Text: {n}You manage to sweep Solomorne along on your sudden charge, his movements becoming more graceful, your eyes meeting his... until a new jolt of pain stabs through your other foot.{/n}

8cf4135a-ac6f-4eb3-8fd6-0e5775320659.Text: {n}The music fades, and Solomorne lays his hand on his weapon with obvious relief, his movements immediately regaining their predatory fluidity.{/n}

5360be84-dd54-4811-a7cf-fe85fa59aaba.Text: "Analysing... This brand is the property of the Idex-Venteris food factory. It was used to mark the meat of high-protein specimens of the planet's fauna. The inscription in proto-Gothic translates to: 'grox on corpse-feed.'"

2b1c2d5d-8916-45fe-9d95-1c1cfff83878.Text: {n}Jae huffs gloomily.{/n} "A revelation like that puts a whole new perspective on this quaint little game."

123efaec-04e4-4e9d-9c63-248843b774fb.Text: {n}Marazhai cocks his head to one side, looking at Maive in bewilderment.{/n} "You really are a primitive species if your pretenders are so easy to expose."

c90ebe47-6b87-4efa-bf14-6047b6db7652.Text: "Abominations like you will never see the true light of righteous faith. We are the children of the God-Emperor, and you are a festering wound on the body of the galaxy whose fall is only a matter of time."

6379c8ff-844b-44fc-af17-cae595d6f0cd.Text: "You see a beast devoid of free will as an example to follow? All I see is a broken spirit bound in the chains of cruelty."

e021583e-23ec-4ea2-b5c7-c130a80decfd.Text: "If your blade does not obey your hand, it may one day pierce your throat." {n}Kibellah's words cause the governor to shudder.{/n}

b355847a-be47-4854-9e27-56760df4b3ef.Text: "Of course, of course... Stop the music! {mf|His Celestial Highness|Her Celestial Highness} wishes silence!" {n}The half-mechanised orchestra creaks to a halt, staring straight ahead with unseeing eyes.{/n}

f15a2062-8d30-4b3a-aeb7-d74a55110c06.Text: "I recommend you try the fried alcedont, whose horns were still goring my hunters just the other day. And here, we have some five-tailed shrimperiuses in stewed black-eye sauce. These fellows need to be eaten quickly, before they scurry off the plate! As for the side dishes, you simply must have a taste of these crispy blaberid shells seasoned with blue glut. This spice scorches your tongue, but follow it with some amasec, and it will feel like the waters of life itself!"

eab51bc3-61e4-4357-afbc-4908d23fb23d.Text: {n}The governor claps his hands readily.{/n} "Orchestra, music!"

6825350c-57ac-41c8-b259-cd103d5a1aef.Text: {n}The tables are buckling under the spread of steaming hot dishes, oozing with grease and exuding tantalisingly spicy aromas. Quite the challenge for an uninitiated stomach, but {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}you{/d} have taken part in feasts far grander than this.{/n}

e3944425-f8b4-441d-b460-2c7dd335cc1f.Text: {n}The governor shakes his head sadly.{/n} "Oh, what a shame! But perhaps you would at least—"

bebab638-f97b-4179-9d01-d274c1741115.Text: "Would you rather I question you instead of the Rogue Trader? Be advised, I am a man of action, not words."

9f8d4e93-8d26-4e33-b8f7-db0fee2339ae.Text: "May you be each other's pillars of support. We shall achieve all we strive for, and we shall prevail — but only together can we do so, for there is no greater force in existence than our unity."

4a727a78-5fe4-4fe9-bc27-55bdae8ae758.Text: "We stand united in our faith and in our common mission: to bring about Humanity's victorious future. May you all toil for the indestructible fortress of the Imperium and wish for no other life, for the God-Emperor is the one true path through the darkness of the universe. Glory to the Emperor!"

da15234d-bd37-44dc-8d0c-a925f095f686.Text: "Sir Timeus's servant, I grant you my favour."

e51dd11e-dede-4a7c-932a-31b2a0590b91.Text: "Sir Timeus, you are free to go."

cab0cda7-3e1c-425d-b154-47bab569986b.Text: "I choose the lady in the golden mask, who so expertly sets snares for her rivals."

01981197-6996-4ebb-b2a6-456224bc8436.Text: "Solomorne, perhaps you have something to say?"

b06943b4-c2fd-44ef-a9ec-bb3cd8bb68f3.Text: [Point at one of the branded impostors at random] "Since you people love prattling about destiny so much, we will let fate choose!"

05425ad8-6e49-4eb3-affb-e4653678df0a.Text: "Wait. Why are there some people here that I didn't mark with the data-brand?"

30295512-9cd9-467d-b774-bdd3809e6db9.Text: "What is the 'Highest Favour,' Ruoldo? Is it part of the rules of the game?"

06a1e2d9-0241-4565-984e-ef8dd32466e6.Text: "The tailor's victim. You are released and pardoned."

f27ab55a-6aca-4cad-a3a7-fe7a45632913.Text: "When my ship carries me between the stars, cutting through the endless void, I ask myself what the new day might bring. And then, I find myself standing up to my nose in filth, among a gaggle of morons who think that a cogitator is a wind-up gewgaw. You want to hear my wishes? Well, my wish is to be off this planet as soon as possible. The end."

87ef54dd-54d3-4da5-bbe0-d101237e8d2d.Text: "The old priest. The Highest Favour is yours."

19b72eff-f097-4867-944d-db005f572fc1.Text: "However, while most of us were indulging — I would even say wallowing — in the thrill of the Impostor Hunt, {mf|His|Her} Celestial Highness turned {mf|his|her} lofty thoughts away from these motley diversions and toward duty. How can this be anything but a true victory of will over whim? Maive, come and present our gift to our celestial guest!"

a19c5827-1d50-4d5e-8c8d-56be90bcd26b.Text: {n}The cyber-laceraxes' lumens glow blood red. Before the condemned can even scream, the beasts pounce on their prey with hungry snarls.{/n}

98e91dca-05ae-4333-b067-6d9fc2e3175f.Text: "You are so very kind, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}." {n}The woman smiles hesitantly and turns to the castle. With a shuddered breath that betrays her recent tears, she heads toward the stairs.{/n}

04bbbcbe-d9d3-4f11-b0e7-c3e7073a8aeb.Text: "Such is {mf|His|Her} Celestial Highness's brilliant decision, which for some may have been fateful indeed! And finally, the hour you have all been waiting for: the concluding part of our, uh, conclusion! The great feast!" {n}The crowd's patience has worn thin. Filling his lungs, the governor shouts out,{/n} "Laceraxes! DINNER IS SERVED!"

fe5271e9-5861-41a0-b7bd-974417b69ba8.Text: "Had it been me in your shoes, Your Celestial Highness, I would not have guessed any of them — I dare say I would have... anti-guessed! After all, even a scrubwoman would look like a princess if you dressed her in silks and laces. But you are able to see through any deception! Maive, go on and present our special gift to our celestial guest!"

3670845d-878f-48a9-8430-8797ca2771da.Text: "And now, good lords and ladies, the time has come to make the fateful decisions! There is naught but one true reward, the Highest Favour, that any branded impostor desires. Please, Your Celestial Highness, tell us: is there among these people one worthy of the Rogue Trader's favour?"

4fed797e-84eb-4eae-914d-76e3305d5409.Text: {n}You hear the fool's voice from somewhere among the crowd:{/n} "A {d|Encyclopedia:FW_NobleMarkedDecision}noble torso{/d}, branded at the behest of the Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself}... Oh, what bitter irony! My standing ovation to you!"

2630dbb3-4988-4d7b-832d-83902e43d4fa.Text: "Your Celestial Highness, as an honoured guest of Thassera, would you like to say a few words of guidance to our beautiful world?"

ab1bc450-fbfa-420f-a297-33a60703654e.Text: "Glory!" {n}the masked people respond, making the sign of the Aquila over their chests.{/n}

c4d70e81-1869-46ab-9c21-863f28b6266c.Text: "As it pleases Your Graciousness." {n}Clutching her filthy skirt, Edytka crouches in a graceless curtsy, then walks away, dragging her feet dejectedly.{/n}

adc4ed65-30bc-4dcd-8cf4-159339b138ab.Text: "All these impostors have been found out by none other than... our celestial guest, {name} von Valancius! An unsurpassable show, Your Celestial Highness! Bravo, bravo! Maive, present our gift!"

d47357d0-e58c-49ed-8e49-9fc708994451.Text: "Why, thank you, Your Celestial Highness! I knew you had a heart of gold and a sharp mind!" {n}The woman offers you a dignified curtsy and proceeds toward the castle.{/n}

58519216-b418-4825-b6a3-f195a6545d39.Text: "Thank you, my {mf|lord|lady}. I am glad that His Eye has seen the truth and did not let paltry deceptions cloud your powers of insight." {n}With an air of profound sagacity and clad in his rich robes, the priest heads toward the castle.{/n}

6e1a64d7-70e1-4a2d-9a9e-107f915ff8d2.Text: "God-Emperor protect you, my {mf|lord|lady}. The Emperor sees into our souls and keeps us always on the true path." {n}The priest's haggard face is full of humility. He bows, bending like a dry tree, then sets off toward the castle.{/n}

38c151e0-2000-4fc0-8180-dc419c470376.Text: "Thank you, Your Celestial Highness." {n}The man gives you a curt nod, then turns with confidence and heads toward the castle.{/n}

cb45e6f5-efc0-439a-aa5c-0671e1037e2e.Text: "I am quite good at saying the word 'guilty.' Would that satisfy you?"

8c3365d4-1849-48d9-9ac4-7a8a0378aee5.Text: {n}Abelard adjusts his coat.{/n} "{mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, ruler of the greatest protectorate in the Koronus Expanse, wishes rapid growth and many centuries of prosperity upon your homeland. Remember your duty, and may you labour tirelessly for the glory of the mighty Imperium."

b3961889-09ca-435b-82dd-b3b5a9a37537.Text: {n}Straining to add a note of gravity to his voice, the governor proclaims:{/n} "Most radiant ladies and noble lords! I hereby declare the Impostor Hunt officially over!" {n}The crowd responds with uproarious cheers.{/n}

a3473f65-9dec-4917-a6b5-9b77eadcf6e2.Text: "That was... a grand speech! Thank you!" {n}Ruoldo sniffles loudly, dabbing his face with a handkercher.{/n}

029cef59-0ec9-4651-bf3b-5567f9377ab5.Text: "Hear, hear! All hail our celestial sovereign! Glory! Glory!" {n}The masks extol you, roused by your words.{/n}

92cfea80-b4cf-4348-b7ee-475779ef968b.Text: "And now, the fateful moment has arrived. Who among the branded will be granted... the Highest Favour..." {n}Having realised too late that you did not take part in the hunt, the governor trails off and glances at you timidly.{/n}

dcde9893-c5c6-42a6-9716-55ac492109b0.Text: "N-not at all, no! Well, then..." {n}The governor quickly adjusts his dress.{/n} "That is to say, the hour we have all been waiting for has come at last — let the great feast begin!"

2815016c-5a7a-44f9-adf8-783d283f83bd.Text: "The one true path through the darkness of the universe..." {n}Repeating after you, the Sister of Battle whispers the words fervently.{/n}

a9a3df52-e80f-42c3-bf83-eb8d8a182c6c.Text: "Glory to the Allfather!" {n}Ulfar's voice thunders over the crowd. Inspired by the might of his faith, the people praise the Emperor, shouting His name until their voices become hoarse.{/n}

f6725f61-0370-4644-acba-413cac1a3e0c.Text: "That buffoon is as maddening as a wolf louse, and just as slippery. Why do they let him feed off the governor's court? Not for his foul tongue, surely..."

f8db948e-048f-4b05-b5f3-779a047bad1c.Text: {n}Even after the deluge of cries gives way to reverent silence, Argenta's eyes remain bright with zealous fire.{/n} "May the God-Emperor be merciful to this world steeped in mistaken beliefs."

8240021a-a8c5-4479-b464-a3f5afc59bf8.Text: {n}Ruoldo leans toward you slightly, gracing you with the strong smell of amasec.{/n} "And that you see more impostors before you than anticipated — that's just to add to your enjoyment, Your Celestial Highness. A crowd burns brighter, as my mother always used to say. Burns, uh... with righteousness, of course. Fierce righteousness!"

76e5a98b-4434-497e-acac-8eaafbe32d8b.Text: "According to the rules, all disguised commoners must be shown to the audience in the finale, so that we know who managed to pass themselves off as a real noble. That is why there are impostors... whom you chose not to mark." {n}Ruoldo nervously tugs at his gilded collar, which is digging into his neck.{/n} "Now then... Will you bestow a few parting words upon Thassera?"

bd617abe-0bdf-4fc1-82c7-1bab271cf18f.Text: "That is correct, Your Celestial Highness! Whomever you grant your favour will be showered with all manner of honours and go to serve in the governor's palace."

d099497e-fe6b-4d43-a062-de16c897c914.Text: {n}The hunt participants lower their heads, their eyes dimming.{/n}

2e7e8dd0-79d8-4297-ab2f-3cdb5dc5043d.Text: "As you wish." {n}With a chuckle, the man twirls his scissors around his finger and sets off for the castle.{/n}

185e3ed1-33ce-485f-aca4-b749ec5e2f30.Text: {n}You hear venomous laughter from among the crowd and recognise Bluff's voice. As the square drowns in the clamour and applause of gawkers who were spectating the game, you look around for the court fool but cannot spot him anywhere.{/n}

39b52551-d05e-4314-8f89-7fa2096c029e.Text: "The participants of our masquerade already stand before you! Did you guess correctly? Did you expose them all? Please don your oculars and have a good look..." {n}Ruoldo turns to you and whispers conspiratorially,{/n} "Not one noble was permitted to hunt the impostors this time, my {mf|lord|lady}. Still, knowing their penchant for such games, I do suspect they tried to make their guesses anyway — quietly, among themselves."

39be8ed9-8bd5-43d7-8d03-9c47f090cfab.Text: {n}There is an awkward pause. The governor smiles nervously:{/n} "I understand, Your Celestial Highness. All this talking and ceremony and protocol — it's enough to knock anyone off their feet! But believe me when I say that we are nearing the end."

7d507770-90f5-49a0-8d76-a2faf8cc039f.Text: "I am thoroughly perplexed by the logic of your actions, Your Celestial Highness, but at least I will no longer be forced to tolerate these lowlifes. Good evening to you." {n}The man bows, fixes his clothes nervously, and leaves in the direction of the castle.{/n}

d6449201-c543-4669-af2c-ce44d788e910.Text: "How do I know I can trust you, Maive?"

11858137-da3f-4d23-acd7-7cac53d35d88.Text: "So, who is to be considered the governor now?"

354411a0-b744-4520-a1f8-f09141010770.Text: "Ruoldo called your name before he died..."

ded9cd05-7678-4920-ac9c-cca8fba3de6c.Text: "Are you actually shocked? Or is this part of the act as well?"

9b9e1bf2-1827-4a61-b3cf-254d3093c74f.Text: "I need to take a look around."

8fbdeef0-a4b9-495b-9386-87cb36c47fae.Text: "What reason could your brother have to want to get an Arbitrator's blood on his hands?"

dd2fa00f-fbe8-4c9b-be5d-cf432ff4bd13.Text: "Whose soul are you praying for, Maive?"

456306b4-92dc-4828-b435-e2b59a00bbf7.Text: "Ruoldo mentioned being branded before he died... Can you scan him too, Solomorne?"

a67278f6-4d7b-4507-a40f-cbcfba81178e.Text: "I ought to have you executed on the spot, Maive, before you stab me in the back..."

269e99e9-e224-4453-9dd0-026b58028411.Text: "What happened was no accident. And if my suspicions are correct..." {n}The Arbitrator looks at his palm thoughtfully, then holds it out to his cyber-mastiff.{/n} "Glaito, analyse."

764d8f6c-a75d-4ecb-929d-72c5e1852387.Text: {n}The dog's visor shimmers as it scans his skin with a mesh of rays. Finally, there is a metallic click and the descending hum of cooling servo-motors. The Proctor's augmetics respond with a soft buzz.{/n}

50e10d75-27c0-4ffc-9b3d-796dca679282.Text: "I swear by the Emperor Himself, I am unblemished before you in spirit and thought!"

0cd71f78-828c-4f4a-b8fb-3f14051d505c.Text: "But I really had nothing to do with any of it, my lord! All I was told to do was entertain our celestial guests and chaperone them to the castle for talks. And instead, there's just gore and death everywhere!"

f35ef910-a037-4936-a44e-db9be6df0908.Text: "Not now. She needs to accompany us to the castle. Her absence would raise the enemy's suspicions, and the revelation that we know what we know would come too early."

240eb540-0cde-453a-b935-76ca90c479d1.Text: "It's a mystery to me too, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. I think about it and I can't even imagine why. But lately... lately, it's like he's not himself. He keeps muttering these awful rhymes about blood and fate. And it's like he's waiting for something, but I just can't understand what."

f7e1e121-6431-4075-992c-74def1307a3c.Text: "Please—" {n}Maive breaks off as Solomorne walks by, brushing past her with his shoulder before examining the elevator with a fault-finding eye. Not daring to speak again, the young woman makes a gesture of invitation and steps onto the platform herself.{/n}

69b4653a-8ee4-44ea-bc78-f9d4a9438a9b.Text: "A data-brand. The court fool put it on me when he shook my hand. Then the laceraxes attacked everyone who had been marked. However, the beasts were not at all eager to tear you apart, Rogue Trader. It appears you are wanted alive, but without my protection."

f5cd1fe3-174b-427b-b1a5-8ab97088dd98.Text: "So, the court fool is your brother?"

8ab3ebfa-a219-4640-9d2a-bb8ffa12cf12.Text: "My brother's, my {mf|lord|lady}. I had a feeling he wasn't acting himself lately. If I'd known he had fallen in with scoundrels, I would have found them and strangled them with my own hands!"

b4b0ffda-eaff-419c-8f67-b76e697aa723.Text: {n}No sooner have you stepped into the elevator than a short metallic clang comes from somewhere above you...{/n}

5b97e060-c63b-4148-971b-055a47e747dc.Text: {n}Lying nearby is the lifeless body of lacerax "Number 4," which you released from its cage. Its fur is clumped and sticky with blood, its vicious eyes glazed over. Giving its own life to protect another was a stunningly human act for a beast.{/n}

5d4b73e1-b942-4603-8dce-c779707d0d88.Text: "My lord judicator is fond of animals, is he not? I never would've thought you had a... kind side like that." {n}Maive's smile is gentle and sad. For the first time ever, she looks at Solomorne without fear.{/n}

cf620818-4fa2-42c6-b090-9074c4b97e42.Text: "The one with the damaged implants... Perhaps they were the reason the beast defied the order that the rest of its pack followed — to destroy all bearers of data-brands. Or maybe..." {n}Solomorne looks pensive as he straightens Glaito's collar.{/n} "Maybe it was a fine animal that was unlucky enough to have bad masters. This is the first creature I've met on Thassera that has been worthy of respect."

67f7ef76-f575-49db-b7af-0a784e13d216.Text: {n}Solomorne casts a heavy glance at the young woman.{/n} "Or maybe I just cannot stand people."

46a70acb-8dea-4e95-bafe-b7e1162ca4d6.Text: "I thought it was my brother calling my name, not Lord Ruoldo. But Daen wasn't there, meaning I just imagined it in my fright."

866129e8-e582-460e-9e21-f95163255188.Text: {n}You think back to Ruoldo's last moments. It is hard to tell for certain, but it really did seem as though his voice had changed, that it sounded younger and less strained — as if he had cast off a mask.{/n}

85f8916a-c21f-420e-8c13-83349f1834c3.Text: {n}Maive puts a handkercher to her mouth and grows pale, most likely recalling the grotesque sight of the governor's violent demise.{/n}

4cce477d-1f65-4511-bc51-d246ee3340d1.Text: {n}The young woman shuts her eyes tightly and begins to whisper a silent prayer.{/n}

3c013277-6c13-4715-94cc-6a50675fecf5.Text: {n}At his master's command, Glaito directs his scan rays at the dead man's severed hand, which has somehow avoided being reduced to shreds along with the rest of the body. The cyber-mastiff's augmetics emit a warning signal.{/n}

44bf0e7c-cabe-45d5-8b5b-1d618f14e019.Text: "Ruoldo was branded too. He couldn't have known, or else he would not have doomed himself like that. I assume this is likewise the work of that buffoon — the only question is whether he was acting of his own accord or at the behest of someone more important."

8d608897-9a39-4a23-b68b-ca130c6bb689.Text: "I have no idea what's going on! I'm so... confused." {n}Maive stares at Ruoldo's mauled corpse with unblinking eyes.{/n} "Is this just a horrible nightmare? Could it be I'm just dreaming? For a second there, I thought— No, I'm sorry. It's impossible."

05f6a784-74e8-49dd-b020-2cfa23654fd7.Text: "That is what any cornered heretic would swear to try to save their life."

a304499e-ebd8-4b14-9099-605b20ec67d1.Text: "If only I knew, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. If only I knew..." {n}Maive's glistening eyes are full of shock.{/n}

2ab581c0-5c82-457f-91aa-b077b789fdaf.Text: "O God-Emperor!" {n}Maive presses her hands to her chest in the sign of the Aquila. Her lips whisper a prayer:{/n} "Forgive and protect his soul! Forgive and protect..."

58237bc0-12a9-450d-8758-6491aa475f7f.Text: "Yes, my lord." {n}Maive lowers her eyes.{/n} "We are lower nobility, and it is a high honour to be the governor's own court entertainer..."

99134be1-12f3-4ae3-94b0-9fbf459fdffe.Text: "There's a good horse! You weren't trying to eat me, were you?"

512e54fc-71dd-46f2-96ba-59acb58a182f.Text: [Toss the corpse part over the stable door]

9fbafa7d-b0ad-4006-950e-eedce98963f0.Text: "Hey, stable hand! I'm going to slaughter all the horses in here!"

33f24268-cf64-4f26-b8e5-ae898cabeae8.Text: {n}The creature that dragged you out of unconsciousness turns out to be a muddy-brown horse. From the darkness, the beast follows you with its large, black eyes — it looks hungry and frightened.{/n}

0367b2c5-1ea9-436f-a84f-7e052ca5fb2b.Text: {n}You hear a lazy sigh on the other side. It does not sound like your words have convinced whoever is standing there.{/n}

8acd51db-e29a-4181-8071-b8a661348641.Text: {n}The horse snorts and shows you its large teeth. It is unclear what this creature usually feeds on, but right now, it would happily munch on your fingers.{/n}

aa31d25c-5add-4590-8c6c-caac1bb46082.Text: {n}The horse is behaving oddly, lurking in the shadows. You must have spooked it when you came to.{/n}

012e371a-6256-47ad-ab8e-d5926b920016.Text: {n}The horse must have smashed through the stall to reach you. You immediately note the empty trough and the fetid pile of vegetable tops under your feet. For the moment, the approach to the rotting waste is blocked by an iron fence. The horse whinnies restlessly as it casts its eye toward the barrier.{/n}

aedd2a47-9aa0-425b-8717-e465f034dec9.Text: {n}The animal's nostrils flare in agitation. It pauses for a second, watching the arm's trajectory, then trots after the treat with a rumble.{/n}

acc9831f-fe0b-4536-96d0-83b929874d61.Text: {n}Snorting frantically, the horse hurtles toward the stable door and smashes straight through it.{/n}

8d4ad4f7-cc2b-4cc9-8d60-3aca22e4b7b0.Text: {n}The steely note in your voice frightens the animal: the horse lets out a snarl and rushes off.{/n}

23e5891f-5f20-40bd-ba34-7e83af73808f.Text: {n}The horse snorts and bares its teeth. It is too hungry not to see you as a possible addition to its dinner.{/n}

90319fca-b756-40e0-b3d8-e87d62228204.Text: {n}A few seconds pass, and you hear a quiet muttering:{/n} "Damn it. Another wretch has sneaked in for the feed." {n}The stable door rattles open.{/n}

7a3a7069-54f1-491d-b5d2-b3b6413bb5db.Text: {n}The horse watches you cautiously. You can see thick strings of saliva dripping from its lips.{/n}

bd11c10a-4d36-4189-a22d-45e132bc7ae1.Text: "And here comes the fresh meat. Dinner time, little monster!"

20355c08-8c5c-4e26-9f54-dc8a47e307c0.Text: "Step away, Maive. That is an order."

11942c46-4eb1-4c75-98ca-b590394ac6ce.Text: "What are you doing? It's going to kill you!"

2d4de243-ef43-481c-b367-f174edef8f4c.Text: {n}This lacerax's augmetics are just as rusty and in sore need of service, but the creature looks far worse than the rest. Gaunt and weak, almost miserable, the beast looks up at you with glazed eyes as you approach. On the door, you notice a scrawled sign that reads, "Animal Number 4. Downtfeed!" The same number is burned into the skin of the lacerax.{/n}

6f7d9983-d191-4072-8e17-4819fe279ce9.Text: {n}The strange lacerax cowers in the corner of the cage, showing no interest in you.{/n}

b8dffb6b-9a6c-46c8-acf2-943a3060f8da.Text: {n}You find the issue and fix it with ease — one of the circuits was broken, possibly damaged in a fight with the other beasts. When you are done with the repairs, you are hit with a realisation: there is now nothing standing between you and this huge predator...{/n}

63150dc4-0a7c-42aa-8eaf-f19c3fc4e51d.Text: {n}You spend the next several minutes trying to do something about the lacerax's damaged augmetic, but to no avail. The very design of this technology is too incomprehensible, leaving you unable to ease the beast's suffering.{/n}

e6bf622d-0183-4bf6-a2bd-e7ee17eca275.Text: {n}You are unfamiliar with the operation of the mechanical lock, but that does not stop you from disabling it. The cage door opens with a creak; however, the beast inside shows no reaction.{/n}

8f7031f6-0fa3-4ceb-aa18-19eea2da3af5.Text: {n}The carcass slumps heavily to the floor. The creature's torment has ended.{/n}

fcbb275a-d8c6-405a-bef2-3d88d305c8e3.Text: {n}You look over the lacerax, but see nothing that could explain its strange behaviour.{/n}

b278c554-e8c3-41b8-8976-92300bccb000.Text: {n}You try to reach your hand inside to get at the lacerax's augmetic, but the cage's bars force you to withdraw.{/n}

53ca5b66-f2fc-4e2f-8eb9-97da5763c7dd.Text: {n}The antiquated lock proves more of a challenge than you thought. You struggle with its cylindrical mechanism for a long while before abandoning your hopeless endeavour.{/n}

696f1da8-4de7-4d86-9595-7af49b9acca1.Text: "I've seen Glaito convulse like that when his augmetics were malfunctioning," {n}Solomorne says, then adds with sudden anger,{/n} "I doubt the local halfwits have the first clue about maintaining implants. They should have stuck to shovels and left the beast alone."

75a79c6e-d3fe-4026-9356-cd82a1026ecb.Text: {n}Solomorne gives you a nod of respect.{/n} "Not only did you deal with the augment, you also made a deadly beast recognise your authority with a single glance. Though, I cannot help but wonder about the repercussions of this jailbreak..."

a1432263-1bda-4269-a011-f8dade8cf710.Text: "Such a desolate creature... All that finds its way into the chains of the mon-keigh is doomed to ruin."

1896af26-425c-43cb-9f44-55cb34f700ce.Text: {n}Suddenly, you see something moving out of the corner of your eye: a whirl of skirts, a frail figure. With a small shriek, Maive throws herself between you and the snarling beast.{/n} "Off with you! Get away from my {mf|lord|lady}!"

07957ba2-3df0-4ec4-81ee-2cd76ffbf8f9.Text: {n}The young woman is trembling violently, but she does not move an inch.{/n} "Better me than you!"

1c501825-09e5-458c-be9c-97101ae29ebe.Text: {n}The young woman casts a desperate glance at you and is on the verge of saying something... but never musters the courage to protest. She meekly steps aside.{/n}

8d2a2b5e-fcf2-4232-882f-73143b9f7ec3.Text: {n}The silent duel with the lacerax lasts only a moment but feels like an eternity. Finally, with a beleaguered snarl, the beast dashes away without laying even a claw on its liberator.{/n}

fa84b98a-021b-4e7e-8ea1-2c4c23ff5b0d.Text: {n}Maive shuts her eyes tightly and clenches her whitening fingers around her dress. With a sonorous roar, the lacerax swiftly lunges forward... past Maive's frail figure and toward freedom.{/n}

74b8718b-efcb-4d09-8859-82dcb37cce4d.Text: {n}A quick inspection is enough to determine the cause of the problem: some of the lacerax's augmetics are clearly not working correctly. The muscles near the energy conduits are twitching, as if the machine spirits, in their fury, were torturing the beast. It is surprising that only this lacerax shows such signs of torment, considering the poor state of the augmetics of all the cyber-beasts here.{/n}

2bcaff56-fbad-4589-b304-414dd7423bb8.Text: {n}With a flash of its visors, the beast begins to turn slowly toward the exit. For a brief moment, you find yourself only a metre away from a monstrosity whose jaws could snap a person in two. It hisses in your face...{/n}

3912a7cc-2f88-487d-8329-2c73862c49c9.Text: "It's me! {rt_name}, the Lord Captain! I'm here!"

8dfe0847-1cbf-42d6-b854-fec5793afcbb.Text: "Look, I have Solomorne's cyber-mastiff with me! Would he order his dog to guard some Thasserian chit?"

a1c9302f-9618-42ef-b38b-36f08b1f0cff.Text: "I have fallen victim to profane sorcery! I need my body back!"

1f875dec-6185-497a-afe8-784bbdcf2d22.Text: "We need to get upstairs! Just trust me on this: you will find the Rogue Trader at the top! Tell the shuttle pilot to take us there — he won't listen to me!"

73bfbecc-165b-4b98-b5fc-b75085a469b7.Text: "Err... I am {rt_name} von Valancius, heir to Theodora von Valancius, who perished in the course of Kunrad Voigtvir's treachery! What else must I dredge up from my past to make you believe me?"

217d5384-752f-4be4-ac74-9b1d0d8e9e9c.Text: "Rejoice, one and all, for Rogue Trader von Valancius has returned to you!"

be038d0d-5a66-4325-bbe1-6a4e9879dafc.Text: "At last, I've found you! I need your help!"

1c3a7563-acfe-452d-8b8c-1a6316e147b8.Text: [Call the pilot by his name] "The Lord Captain is in danger! Back to the shuttle, quickly! I must get to the top of the tower!"

9cb59fab-046c-4ed2-93f7-8db93f83d17e.Text: [Throw yourself at the pilot's feet] "I implore you, in the Lord Captain's name! We need to get upstairs immediately — the von Valancius dynasty is in peril!"

bd284cf4-cf35-4f64-ab67-65b19b796688.Text: {n}Abelard startles.{/n} "That tone..." {n}The Seneschal looks you over from head to toe in amazement, but you can see that he is still unsure.{/n}

d5f89e9b-d0e6-4ad7-ae83-2a7a8eda4574.Text: {n}Idira stares at you — and her eyebrows start to creep upward.{/n} "I'll be damned... either I'm completely out of my mind, or... No, that's just insane! The Lord Captain, in the body of that court lady? That's rich, whispers!" {n}She starts rubbing her eyes as if trying to clear them.{/n}

eafbc5da-8dec-4992-baf9-04882afd0379.Text: {n}Cassia frowns, covering her mouth with her hand.{/n} "These colours... It is as though they had been copied from those I usually see around the Lord Captain..."

4a064196-b469-477a-9c0c-f3c91161cd9a.Text: {n}The suggestion to stop puzzling over your identity and start acting seems to have had an effect — at least, no one is arguing with you anymore.{/n}

9f991c37-02f7-4940-b3a8-d55cc4078b2b.Text: {n}Your retinue hesitates. It seems your argument sounds convincing enough to plant a seed of doubt in their minds, at least.{/n}

45c83e68-64a5-4c3e-9856-1824bbe988f3.Text: {n}Your retinue exchange a few words among themselves, unable to explain how you know such details.{/n}

a98404d3-a2c2-4d88-8501-05bcca604471.Text: {n}Your retinue hesitates. Some exchange puzzled glances, while others frown and look at you intently, as if hoping to see obvious signs of sorcery.{/n}

0e8d948e-84a2-485a-b903-a94602edb76e.Text: {n}Heinrix grimaces and looks up with a doubtful expression.{/n} "I could be wrong, seeing as this accursed planet has too many sources of warp energies, but I seem to sense an echo of the Immaterium coming from above..."

7de04d2f-4ac3-489c-b073-fdccfe91efca.Text: {n}Abelard furrows his brow — what he just heard does not sit well with the old officer.{/n} "Oh, I feel uneasy, even though the Lord Captain did report that everything is fine. Something about {rt_mf|his|her} voice wasn't quite right... Then again, the Proctor is there too..."

528d4e2d-5caf-4201-b743-7ad94ff43a92.Text: "Shut up, little whispers... Huh, they're really acting up. You know what? I don't care what the Lord Captain said — something's wrong!"

2c9d6d57-cfe2-4f27-b626-0f3d6dca8192.Text: {n}Marazhai looks around with an ominous grin.{/n} "Letting me get bored while I am surrounded by all the frightened prey swarming within this castle is most unwise..."

6204acf6-f5e0-41b2-ae07-a5073e5dc06c.Text: "Kae-morag! Am I the only one who can hear the strange notes in the elantach's voice? We must head to the top!"

a7448425-653f-41ad-b847-128203197cf2.Text: "God-Emperor, grant me the patience to endure this idle wait." {n}Argenta makes the sign of the Aquila and slips into what looks like a quiet prayer.{/n}

b3c18f48-1fb8-454d-af2d-ecd353b82029.Text: {n}Jae jerks her foot impatiently, her heel tapping loudly against the paving stones.{/n} "First that elevator, now the Rogue Trader is stuck in the local archive. Intuition tells me they are making fools of us, and we are playing right into their hands by standing around down here..."

2c84a0a3-8d0b-4b1f-a9c8-6b4cffb56a78.Text: "Every moment spent away from the Domin is another defeat for me..."

45331dbf-80bd-47c8-8ccf-68214072e22b.Text: "Hmph... My dear, were you not the one assigned to watch over the Rogue Trader?"

3404b956-7a1f-4187-bc89-21ad476e49f8.Text: {n}Heinrix's lip curls as he looks at you.{/n} "Warp emanations... strong ones at that. Sorcery at work... before our very eyes." {n}His fingers tighten on his weapon.{/n}

c0538d1f-5751-490f-ae2c-5ebf3227fdd8.Text: "Isn't that the meek little lady-in-waiting that was assigned to my shereen? Looks like she's lost the Lord Captain too... and her sanity to boot."

3cf0d6f6-bb11-4785-945e-aadad3b036a9.Text: {n}Abelard scowls.{/n} "You could have memorised a few facts from the Lord Captain's biography... Are we to play guessing games now?"
