9807793e-27b7-4a9a-bf24-d6749497ffec.Text: "Then our paths diverge. I will find a way to rectify the flagrant violations of the Lex Imperialis, but without you, Rogue Trader."

e4717403-9038-486a-b8e8-49929d910087.Text: {n}Solomorne turns to the Arbitrators. The Proctor's eyes are blazing, his voice thundering with unusual passion:{/n} "Arbitrators of the Adeptus Arbites, by turning against the prefect and the Marshal, you will not be in violation of the Lex Imperialis, on the contrary — we are governed by the Emperor's will alone, and He is pleased by order and stability on His vassal worlds. We must not allow this crude power grab to succeed. Our task is to protect the legitimate ruler of the protectorate and to restore justice."

ddbe4192-bd17-4530-80e4-d334bdeda54c.Text: "Everyone who sided with Vultur and Strachs must die. They have earned neither mercy nor the privilege of a trial. Their execution will be a lesson to anyone who would ever again attempt to assassinate a Rogue Trader or manipulate the Lex Imperialis."

4c7cf60c-d616-4118-b82a-b2a7013355c6.Text: "For Prefect Vultur and Marshal Strachs, the sentence for attempting to pervert the Lex Imperialis is death. The others must face your judgement in accordance with the Emperor's Law."

a0dd92fc-9ed0-4da0-ae5c-e455133efd9a.Text: "Defiling this sacred court with sorcery and especially using it on someone who has already been touched by corruption would be most unwise. Your request is denied."

44ac0c88-d77c-427a-bfbf-a9bb704cf159.Text: {n}Strachs huffs out a laugh.{/n} "You seem offended by the insinuation that you are prone to fainting spells. Well... I admit, there is a difference, and you have just made it plain for all to see."

db5076b2-b3c9-40df-b2bf-188935953cef.Text: "We do not possess sufficient knowledge of the nature of the sorcery wrought upon you. And all the witnesses are dead."

6ecc32c7-cb9c-44c4-acd4-78ce2f34d5ff.Text: "The Adeptus Arbites never hesitate in passing judgement, for the Emperor guides the hand that fulfils its duty. The Rogue Trader has delivered judgement as was {mf|his|her} charge. Therefore, {mf|his|her} decision is blessed by the God-Emperor..."

bad3b7d5-e79f-47ba-a317-93d71cba6d64.Text: "Your decision is law. With such a right, perverting justice and breeding anarchy in the ranks of its servants is all too easy. And probably tempting for a heretic who seeks joy in destruction."

56004001-92dd-4b3f-b799-16b384da5958.Text: "The Rogue Trader is right. If the Arbitrator has dared to stray from the Lex, then he never was an Arbitrator. The fault lies with me for not seeing the weakness in his heart in time."

50897ee5-dfd2-45df-a1c9-b99d18965ee7.Text: "I must refuse. Marshal Gregoras Strachs, I charge you with treason against the Imperium and conspiring with a heretic! Fangs of the Expanse, to battle!"

bff63939-2517-41c7-8cfc-249f57e37a6e.Text: {n}Glaito looks at Solomorne and lets out a grinding whimper. The Proctor sighs heavily, covering his eyes with his hand.{/n} "Fine... To the void with it! Unlike the Marshal, you haven't failed me yet."

7b2f1015-644e-4351-b5c9-122b69af3636.Text: {n}Strachs finally finishes listing your crimes. There is a momentary pause in the hall.{/n}

9899353e-b714-4f55-9a60-a9b24302643a.Text: "Let the record show that the defendant disregarded the opportunity given to {mf|him|her} to repent, which only adds to the gravity of {mf|his|her} guilt. We will proceed to the examination of the individual tithe heresies committed by the defendant."

f3462a74-ed05-41ee-a048-2557250442bb.Text: {n}Barely containing his seething rage, Abelard thunders,{/n} "{name} von Valancius, bearer of the sacred Warrant, the God-Emperor's anointed and sovereign of this protectorate, denies these false accusations. The Administratum and Adeptus Arbites will not get away with this flagrant attempt to sully the Rogue Trader's good name and plunder {mf|his|her} dynasty's coffers, make no mistake!"

f2499641-190e-44e2-ba66-67f88aa3c4a7.Text: "Conspiring with the captain of the Heartless to steal the sacred tithe. Upon arriving on Rykad Minoris, the Rogue Trader aided Captain Sargona in loading the tithe onto his ship under the cover of a planetary riot. {name} von Valancius later eliminated {mf|his|her} accomplice using Adeptus Arbites forces led by Proctor Anthar. The Proctor attempted to appease the Rogue Trader's greed by offering the frigate known as the Heartless in exchange for the safety of the tithe."

03ffe148-1966-4fb6-aa95-fb21250b0d0e.Text: "However, the Rogue Trader instead chose to exert {d|Encyclopedia:APA_WantTitheDecision}pressure{/d} in an attempt to extort more out of the Proctor."

b2153972-adc5-419f-9d0d-99cfe9eb1e4b.Text: "After realising the utter incorruptibility of the Arbites, the Rogue Trader attempted to destroy the {d|Encyclopedia:BS_HeartlessDamaged}tithe ship{/d}. Only the timely intervention of the Proctor saved the sacred tribute."

f787f68e-1ad5-43bc-a972-0faacd9ee629.Text: "Then the Rogue Trader boarded the ship in an attempt to seize the tithe. {mf|His|Her} actions led to the death of a squad of Arbitrators — Proctor Anthar alone survived the Rogue Trader's murderous ploy. {name} von Valancius personally eliminated {mf|his|her} accomplice, Captain Sargona, in order to destroy the evidence of {mf|his|her} schemes." {n}The prefect looks up from the scroll and sweeps her indifferent gaze over you.{/n} "Do you have anything to say in your defence?"

bf408fe7-2471-438e-9657-174876ad0960.Text: {n}Strachs frowns doubtfully.{/n} "It is certainly an unorthodox tactic. Perhaps even suicidal. No, I can recall no such cases."

993e8f9f-b8ed-424c-a261-c6eb166faa53.Text: "Rogue Traders are famed for their love of outlandish exploits and skullduggery. Perhaps you really are insane."

a54ec6e3-8265-4e20-b879-c924ac4e42d0.Text: "Proctor, stand down! That is an order. Your reports were quite comprehensive and are the foundation of this case. You will provide your testimony only when the prefect requests it. Is that clear?"

56e27dab-4701-4851-8227-c5b20c8120a3.Text: {n}A furrow cuts across Strachs's brow.{/n} "Attempting to threaten a Rogue Trader on {mf|his|her} own vessel would indeed have been an imprudent choice..."

f65b8e0d-e916-43f0-9291-29566f55cd8b.Text: "You know perfectly well that the death of the Proctor on board your ship would have immediately drawn the attention of the Adeptus Arbites and placed your dynasty in jeopardy. You would not take that risk."

5ea62300-0a33-44e1-9a02-e512130a13f0.Text: "This information is not in the records. I will make a note of this attempt to distort the truth."

d174ed17-7599-4964-8135-e842effcf9e4.Text: "Let a new charge be added to the record: attempting to manipulate an official. Marshal, I hope I do not need to remind you of your duty?" {n}Giving Strachs a suspicious look, the prefect turns back to the documents.{/n}

cbdc0956-0f8e-42f8-9290-992e423ffdd1.Text: "Let the record reflect: no denials were offered, a priori guilt is admitted."

dc5d236d-b50a-413a-bf84-6ddf4d0d22b6.Text: {n}The prefect nods to the Marshal, who removes a device from his belt. The press of a button — and Glaito responds with a sharp metallic clang. The cyber-mastiff's paws carry him to Strachs.{/n}

8bf52aef-db2d-4302-8208-d83a2d843425.Text: {n}Your own voice rumbles up from Glaito's chest:{/n} "I don't want the ship — I want a cut of the tithe."

658d2a9b-422c-4617-a81a-c50c7f2b46e9.Text: {n}Solomorne pales. A vein throbs at his temple, and you can clearly hear his teeth grinding.{/n} "Touching my dog was a big mistake."

e83913b2-c901-44f9-b956-66d79e483edc.Text: "No. I would have opposed it. I would have found a way to keep Glaito out of it."

02fe53f9-ef6f-473a-b5de-2e7d3af36f55.Text: "That is precisely why the procedure was performed without your knowledge. There is a note in your personnel file about your unhealthy attachment to the cyber-mastiff. I persuaded the Marshal that it was in your best interests, Proctor."

c698e3c9-f300-46ac-a79c-49c78461471a.Text: {n}The prefect sighs.{/n} "I cannot imagine a context in which the words 'I want a cut of the tithe' would cast you in a favourable light."

e4f74aa9-91c9-452e-a7b8-6948c62096a7.Text: "In addition, the defendant led a fleet of {mf|his|her} associates into a classified system, causing irreparable damage to the sacred tribute. As a result of internal squabbling between the ruffians and the defendant, a number of barges were {d|Encyclopedia:TW_LostTitheDecision}destroyed or stolen{/d}, their total estimated tithe volume being the equivalent of two decades' worth of payments from three Alpha-class, Exactis Prima {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGradeGlossary}tithe grade{/g} worlds."

25300539-104e-454f-9620-0a62c8ec75e3.Text: "Trying to adhere to the Lex Imperialis causes more harm than good. Do you still not see it?"

4b16c6f8-518a-45c6-be89-65c3eb2ee6b7.Text: "You no longer follow the letter of the Lex Imperialis... Am I correct?"

a891badf-18aa-4129-87fc-b3f6b2010749.Text: {n}Your own voice pours forth from inside Glaito.{/n}

6b988cfd-42e0-4764-a455-4fd56dcbbbb2.Text: "You think you can judge me? Remember: I am the Rogue Trader, and you have no right to object to a word I say!"

954c98d0-5914-4600-943c-cde1bd6cf338.Text: "I expect members of my retinue to offer useful assistance. You will endeavour to act in my interests from here on out."

78a38932-cf5c-43f8-80fe-762ce65c771f.Text: {n}Something inside Glaito clicks — and Solomorne's voice begins to play.{/n}

21fc1d74-979f-439b-8b84-665050ece25a.Text: "If anyone had told me before that I would be thinking about things like that, I probably would have caved their face in. But the truth is, I no longer see heresy in such thoughts."

115d71bb-6aea-40c7-85c2-cbe0737ef605.Text: "I have been in your retinue long enough to acknowledge that you are the only true power in all of the Expanse..."

2c14915a-e3ea-474d-89db-f13a24705ead.Text: "By Arbitrator standards, I am already knee-deep in heresy, but, frankly, their condemnation does not deter me..."

243f0250-951e-40a3-a2e8-7fb180b15c4c.Text: "Narrow interpretations of the Lex Imperialis are a leash... I have long since outgrown the confines of this system, and I can see its flaws..."

22702472-f082-4475-9b54-e3335f552e1d.Text: "If the Marshal learns the whole truth, it will make things difficult..."

1fc32363-8e7c-4b55-931c-5742a49aab22.Text: {n}Vultur sets the pile of papers down heavily on the lectern and raises her eyes.{/n}

d6e34609-2bd6-4834-96cc-a643c010f150.Text: {n}Solomorne casts you a look of gratitude.{/n} "Don't waste your breath, Rogue Trader. She'll get her due."

1b2495b2-da17-44e7-9342-cb7c918ef1c2.Text: {n}A moment of silence. Suddenly, one by one, the Arbitrators raise their weapons and point them at the Marshal and the prefect.{/n}

2887cb29-9891-4cc6-8cff-19af989c9a76.Text: {n}Your words fall on deaf ears. No Arbitrator moves from where they stand.{/n}

d9e0cf6e-ba3d-49af-a7f7-5cd699af50bc.Text: "I will appeal to the Arbitrators — I'm sure many of them are already convinced that the prefect is manipulating the Lex Imperialis for her own ends."

83b2e799-d187-4da1-b1a9-3177a98e7833.Text: {n}Solomorne nods and raises his weapon.{/n} "Glaito, ready!"

f33c9b15-fc00-4f02-a443-d2f747b12b59.Text: {n}Solomorne's face turns lifeless, his knuckles white.{/n} "I thought my wholehearted loyalty to the Lex was obvious. But you were monitoring me, keeping tabs on me like some kind of outsider. Like a non-Arbitrator. You even dragged Glaito into it too — it would have been better if you'd installed your damned recording devices in me."

31937651-8a56-4cee-8142-d43ecd48f48a.Text: {n}The cyber-mastiff's entire body begins to tremble, his feet clawing up tiny sparks, and then he projects a pict-recording from his eyes onto the floor.{/n}

1bcd6112-48fb-46be-b8fd-bafabb6be95e.Text: {n}Pain flits across Solomorne's granite face as he looks at his dog.{/n} "You have used us as a tool against the Rogue Trader from the beginning. Such tricks and schemes are unworthy of the Arbites."

2a5fa5e2-a3d9-4634-8924-1555165549f9.Text: {n}With practised skill, Strachs's voice reverberates throughout the hall:{/n} "Conspiring to steal the sacred tithe. Undermining the legitimate authorities on an Imperial world, involving sorcery and damage to the tithe. Conceiving and executing plans to disrupt sector-wide tithe shipments."

13a81d89-d823-4c56-a899-e31b3788ba7a.Text: {n}The prefect shifts awkwardly as Strachs recites the seemingly endless list of transgressions — the aftermath of your attack seems to be preventing her from maintaining a suitably dispassionate appearance.{/n}

8977aa58-e80b-495e-91e6-ad1f6c39db6e.Text: {n}All you hear in response is Strachs continuing his list of charges. You look around and are met with a number of bewildered, frightened, and confused looks. The clerks of the Administratum seem to have worked hard to make the obviously feigned proceedings look like a genuine trial.{/n}

07e81a4b-66c2-48f5-9934-8ec925d27986.Text: "Marshal." {n}The old woman stares at the Arbitrator without blinking, as if hypnotising him. Finally, convinced that the Marshal's conversation with you is over before it even began, she returns to her papers.{/n}

0cc2a665-cbf9-49f6-8695-98d22ce167ca.Text: {n}Vultur flinches at your outburst. For a moment, the anger you saw before the trial blossoms once more on her face, but this time you are not the only one to witness it — the Marshal sees it too. He arches an eyebrow.{/n}

c89857a0-4f57-44a5-b9f2-1b451924be99.Text: "Your eagerness to {d|Encyclopedia:VP_KillPrefectDecision}kill the prefect{/d} — even in front of multiple witnesses — speaks of desperation, Rogue Trader. You know that your intentions and abilities are a far cry from what is expected of the Emperor's anointed." {n}Strachs looks at you without a hint of sympathy.{/n}

a6a100d5-f259-4a40-92ff-8174ee5d3f51.Text: {n}The footage depicts a scene from Glaito's viewpoint. The quality is terrible, but you can make out the hall where the sculptor is conducting the sinister ritual. You see Maive interfere with the ritual, and the beam of warp energy connecting the two of you. You hear Solomorne's command. The scene changes and you see Maive, or rather, yourself in Maive's body, wandering through the streets of Thassera. The next clip brings you back to the hall where Solomorne is firing on the altar. The events in the recording are echoed by a dragging pain in your muscles and a fog in your head.{/n}

3f9a51e1-bb15-40c4-9371-233cbe413ff6.Text: "Marshal. Enough." {n}Not a single muscle twitches on the prefect's face, but her eyes blaze with barely suppressed annoyance.{/n}

10fe7a49-08d1-46fb-9af2-895e708ffd2c.Text: {n}Clementia Werserian looks straight at you as if the prefect does not even exist. She makes the sign of the Aquila and speaks in a low voice:{/n} "House Werserian is loyal to the Rogue Trader."

a8e83919-31a0-4a28-a3c3-dc9ab748ce9d.Text: {n}There is a hissing sound as a new recording starts playing. This time, the voice is that of the watcher of Leethus:{/n} "And so, Theodora's plan is accomplished: the tithe of the Koronus Expanse now belongs to the dynasty. Whether her intentions were the same as yours, offspring, I know not, but that matters little."

2abd7b83-bdce-4618-ab3f-bc2472b0a3fb.Text: {n}Solomorne gives you a hard look.{/n} "In the name of the Lex Imperialis, I testify that Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius {d|Encyclopedia:TW_SolomorneNotConvincedDecision}took possession of the tithe{/d}."

f8e2a2be-8e71-41bb-bdb9-7d0c1231dd00.Text: "Your words have been heard, Rogue Trader. However, you are the real criminal now. You stole the Expanse's tithe, of which there is irrefutable evidence including the testimony of Proctor Anthar; therefore you are to be punished to the fullest extent of the Lex Imperialis."

a9958f02-b15c-40cf-88db-1683d553fa0f.Text: "This is where our paths diverge, {name}. There is nothing that can justify your crime anymore."

4d7c891f-4aca-44bb-b323-58fa760612c6.Text: "The replacement Choirmaster appointed in the wake of Master Pras's execution was taken from a Chorda world where he was serving at the time. That left the planet with effectively no Astropathic communication, putting it in a precarious position that soon resulted in significant losses. The Rogue Trader's decision sparked a series of conflicts with the Chorda protectorate."

eeeff681-0e38-460c-a994-b993c9c52739.Text: "On the Rogue Trader's orders, both the Doleful Host and Master Pras were executed. The {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Ecclesiarchy{/g} made an official statement of condemnation, as killing militant devotees of the faith is tantamount to abetting heresy. Meanwhile the new Choirmaster lost several messages of utmost importance on his very first day of service, thus sparking a war between two Koronus Expanse worlds. As of now, one of those worlds has been completely destroyed, and the other deemed uninhabitable."

0c323e0e-af3e-4eed-b804-23bd1384afe0.Text: {n}Inscribia picks up a scroll that carries the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Ecclesiarchy{/g}'s seals.{/n} "Allow me to read out the decision of the honoured representatives of the Saint Drusus mission. 'We brand the one who dared subject Anvylas, a holy votary of the faith, to horrible torture a heretic and an associate to evil of every kind.' At the moment, the cardinal's mental state is cause for concern. Not only has he developed a fondness for bloody rites and repulsive forms of self-flagellation, but he has also, on several occasions, injured members of his congregation who were trying to make donations to him."

33a43e66-c8fb-4ae1-a271-628363e8a553.Text: "The Rogue Trader's ruling in the Lady Molles-Secundas case was to declare both her marriages valid, which forced her to live with both her husbands under one roof. As a result, what had begun as a family feud escalated into a massacre that not only decapitated two noble houses but, worst of all, left manufacturing facilities of great importance to the Imperium without competent managers."

a3e6cacc-2a16-440e-bb13-7b822cd4cd98.Text: "The Rogue Trader ordered the execution of Lady Molles-Secundas, her children, and both her husbands, as well as a functionary of the Administratum, in whose case there had been no formal investigation of any kind. The verdict left the Molles and Secundas family enterprises with no worthy managers, resulting in a catastrophic decline in the efficiency of production facilities of importance to the Imperium. In addition, due to the unexpected execution, the aforementioned functionary had no time to hand over his responsibilities to his successors, which significantly affected the operations of the departments of the Administratum."

5380929f-6b4a-4960-9bd2-1e55184fd0d6.Text: {n}The recording barely fades out before Solomorne loudly proclaims:{/n} "I remind you that the Rogue Trader's decision regarding the tithe was made in my presence. Therefore, any and all accusations should be levied against me first, and I do have much to say on the matter."

0068dc92-9663-41cf-bd86-c86e80270f9d.Text: "The Rogue Trader did not deliver a verdict in the Doleful Host trial, thus leaving events to take their course during an emergency. Host warriors stormed the Astropaths' abode, executed Master Pras, and posthumously discovered his connection to a plot instigated by the traitor Kunrad Voigtvir. As a consequence of the Rogue Trader's criminal connivance, unrest broke out on Dargonus, and the Astropathic Choir took heavy casualties."

64f0fb5e-fa06-4d14-9128-7b926ca81394.Text: "The Rogue Trader exiled Cardinal Anvylas from Dargonus so that he would meet his death away from his parish and flock. The ecclesiarchs of the capital world officially condemn this unfair decision, which they interpret as a heretical attempt to weaken Dargonus's faith through bereaving the planet of a holy preacher."

5bf2537a-73df-44a6-b8a0-35d2b4cd912f.Text: "The Rogue Trader neglected {mf|his|her} direct duties in refusing to pass a verdict in the Lady Molles-Secundas case. As a result, what had begun as a family feud escalated into a massacre that not only decapitated two noble houses but, worst of all, left manufacturing facilities of great importance to the Imperium without competent managers."

e8540a42-45d5-4d23-b72c-ad5566c402c4.Text: "There is weight to your arguments, Rogue Trader. But even if you are right about the prefect, that does not immediately disprove all accusations against you."

793b9f86-5fb9-40c6-99e3-37b314d52480.Text: "Let me present to you a vox-recording of Cardinal Anvylas, who was pardoned by the 'Rogue Trader,' only to be detained at the cathedral next to the bodies of forty members of his congregation slain at his hand." {n}The prefect snaps her fingers, and a servo-skull flies up to her.{/n}

e0c94df6-4584-4412-aa97-d82ddf99873f.Text: "Lord Molles, deemed to be alive, committed a transgression of softheartedness in running his family enterprise. He released all his convicted workers and terminated the contracts with his primary suppliers, citing their moral qualities. His actions resulted in twelve kilotons of undelivered food rations across several recipients."

31569c8a-1085-45e4-8def-9988395152e8.Text: "The potential outcomes of trials that did not take place cannot be presented as evidence of innocence."

9b205e93-98a9-489f-a43c-73d273313153.Text: "Your admission of error is commendable, although it offers little of substance to justify your actions."

731017f4-764a-41ed-bacc-1b3b064e5ade.Text: "Let the record reflect the outrageous irony of the defendant's words."

17200d6f-0574-4e09-aa6a-0c8410c61fa7.Text: "Your words are true. Crimes committed after a verdict are cause for new convictions, not—"

f49b3d6c-ad65-42e0-8322-ad318f7c1440.Text: "Moving on... The defendant was placed in an unprecedented position of trust by the Adeptus Arbites and the Administratum. {mf|He|She} was entrusted with the coordinates of the world where the tithe of the entire Koronus Expanse was held. As agreed, the defendant was to transport the sacred tribute to Dargonus, but what did {mf|he|she} do?"

4155d0f3-6ddc-4062-b48c-8e6bcd8b1a01.Text: {n}The Marshal snaps his fingers over Glaito's head. The cyber-mastiff flinches as if from a bolter shot, but obediently plays another recording. You recognise Solomorne's voice.{/n}

35404f57-c590-47c7-8653-82b952b0f4bc.Text: "Tithe theft. Orchestrated by Theodora von Valancius. Committed by the defendant. Witnessed by Proctor Anthar."

0d0f238e-dbf2-43a4-9685-4de9346b0544.Text: "This court has no authority, as it is part of Prefect Vultur's machinations. Subversion of the Emperor's justice will not be tolerated." {n}Solomorne's gaze sweeps over the Arbitrators and pauses on the Marshal.{/n} "I am forced to explain the obvious, and it only underscores the blindness that has afflicted the servants of His Law."

cd3fb583-afde-49b6-9ea4-98aed48c79bc.Text: {n}Solomorne steps forward, looking into the faces of the accusers.{/n} "You have gathered here to crush with lies and trickery the only person capable of taming the Koronus Expanse. By scorning {mf|his|her} achievements, the power of the sacred Warrant, and the Lex Imperialis, you have signed your names to heresy."

61a99092-b6d9-4d2f-985d-a6a37d9c4a13.Text: "On the matter of the sacred tithe, we rely on facts, not your words. That Theodora planned to steal the tithe is established fact. The destruction of Leethus is also beyond dispute. To allow you to execute your plan would have been highly imprudent."

0f8a712c-1bd9-481c-a62c-714a1bbdca8b.Text: "The sacred tithe is not intended to be used by anyone other than the Adeptus Administratum, the deliverers of His will."

78372f7d-315b-4026-bc0e-b0ac778a3e47.Text: {n}The old woman snatches up the next parchment.{/n} "How good of you to speak up, Gregoras. As an addendum to the proceedings, we will be examining the heresies of Solomorne Anthar resulting from his moral failure to oppose the greed of the heretic von Valancius."

0c795a4e-620b-4421-9d29-bcdd3cc0b36a.Text: "If I might interrupt, Mistress Vultur..." {n}Urbend Drivestem, governor of Dargonus, visibly nervous at the sight of the armed Arbitrators, nevertheless raises his head haughtily.{/n} "We are much obliged to you for arranging this gathering..." {n}The emphasis on the last word leaves no doubt that the nobles' presence at the Palace is involuntary.{/n} "However, all that has now taken place here does not change the facts. House von Valancius holds the Warrant of Trade. House von Valancius is a Rogue Trader dynasty, and no amount of legal contortions will change that! House Drivestem is loyal to the Rogue Trader."

1d7c3ee4-07f9-433b-a612-0d3b79c92686.Text: {n}Toriana Gaprak juts out her chin, her whole body trembling with either terror or anger.{/n} "Von Valancius's power is cruel, but unquestionable. The Warrant of Trade grants the Rogue Trader rights far beyond those that anyone else in this Palace must content themselves with. House Gaprak is loyal to the Rogue Trader."

aae52837-f4f3-443f-a2b9-0ec8ab0c8372.Text: {n}Macharius Sauerback's unpleasant face twists into a smirk.{/n} "I would be the first to condemn the Rogue Traders of the Koronus Expanse for their flagrant disregard for the law, only I do not purport to pass off my opinion as justice. House Sauerback is loyal to the Rogue Trader!"

a4ab6a33-75db-4b07-8794-1a715562c134.Text: {n}Toriana Gaprak makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n} "No shadow shall fall upon the name von Valancius or eclipse the radiance of the beneficent Rogue Trader line. Whatever your mechanical dog may say... House Gaprak is loyal to the Rogue Trader."

48051459-ce3d-4f86-8905-5c769b77a9e1.Text: {n}Macharius Sauerback raises his head, his eyes burning with an almost deranged loyalty.{/n} "Venerating the letter of the law is not fidelity to justice. Straying from the tenets of the Lex is not discerning the essence of truth and the granting of retribution." {n}The man is silent for a few seconds before he almost shouts out,{/n} "House Sauerback is loyal to the Rogue Trader!"

2c786652-b6b3-41a0-b1dd-354bc45ad9c9.Text: "Allow me to address you, even though I am not of the first families of Dargonus. Proctor Yeager, Adeptus Arbites, Leethus outpost. {name} von Valancius made every effort to not only save the tithe, but also the {d|Encyclopedia:TW_ArbitesLiveDecision}Arbites contingent{/d} stationed on Leethus. I propose that such an act would have been entirely nonsensical if the Rogue Trader was intent on simply stealing the tithe. End of report."

06c43225-8c1e-4dd6-994f-87f5ab9759b6.Text: "Well. The proceedings are nearing their conclusion." {n}The prefect looks around at the nobles of Dargonus gathered in the hall.{/n} "The record of sins and heresies presented to the servants of the God-Emperor has revealed the Rogue Trader's true essence, and the verdict is grim. For {mf|his|her} thoughts and deeds were not bent toward the service of Humanity, but to the indulgence of {mf|his|her} own greed and petty ambition. Today, you are here to witness an act of righteous judgement, and the downfall of the von Valancius dynasty. Houses of Dargonus, do you reject the authority of this heretic?"

cb41a902-d743-4018-826d-88fa57be1973.Text: {n}Inscribia heaves in a breath, ready to launch into a vehement tirade, but the Marshal raises his right hand and everyone falls silent.{/n}

9128bc19-3d0d-441d-ba4b-24093bf90161.Text: "That is enough. Vultur, I trusted you, and I failed to notice when your wise counsel turned into instructions and orders. When my every action became subject to your avaricious schemes rather than the Lex. But now I see things with perfect clarity, the way you try to manipulate the truth to achieve your ends." {n}Clenching his fist, Strachs thunders,{/n} "You turned me into a puppet and then trampled on His laws!"

11ee4a08-1af1-41cd-bd9e-62541233ce15.Text: "Prefect Inscribia Vultur. You are charged with fraud, attempted assassination of the Emperor's anointed, and undermining the foundations of the Lex Imperialis. Surrender now and accept a dignified death."

55725d1d-2c16-47b4-bbbe-ead6e36e7889.Text: "Heretic! Traitor! Marshal, execute them! All of them!"

fee1aac1-2459-4b5e-9f2f-bcf930275170.Text: "Anyone who dares to join the heretic is condemned to death! Marshal, carry out the sentence!"

74e5f6c4-5e5b-4b41-bc21-07c51f8d6560.Text: "Arbitrators. The sentence is death. Carry it out."

f7daa744-6ed1-4c55-834b-1f7df70c213f.Text: {n}Strachs stares at you coldly as he reads:{/n} "Resisting the justice of the Imperium. Conspiring to steal the sacred tithe. Undermining the legitimate authorities on an Imperial world, involving sorcery and damage to the tithe. Conceiving and executing plans to disrupt sector-wide tithe shipments, with the subsequent destruction of a strategically important planet..."

ea86733b-31ef-4000-a1c8-05213b04be75.Text: "I certainly do." {n}Solomorne glares at the prefect.{/n} "Prefect Vultur, I charge you with abuse of power and perverting the justice of the Imperium. I have been a repeated witness to your schemes against the Rogue Trader and, even more shamefully, I have been your instrument in them."

fd6fd9a2-6d98-41c4-be48-d82b8f3742a1.Text: {n}Solomorne narrows his eyes and bites out,{/n} "You've made two mistakes — you attacked someone I care about, and you dressed it up in decorations offensive to the Adeptus Arbites. So I promise you — as soon as this is over, I will take you by the throat, put a shotgun to your head, and do His justice."

33b6a2ab-bb62-4ace-8165-7652e52e5e12.Text: "Proctor, be silent! Your behaviour is beyond all imaginable limits! I demand obedience!"

329e8afd-2472-4353-bfe9-c2fdfd4bd547.Text: "No, Marshal. I will not obey you while you obey the prefect, who has put on this farce solely to further her own interests."

9b2a9472-e8b6-4e41-a9cc-ed2cb565abb0.Text: "According to the calculation of the tithe transferred from the Heartless, the Administratum was short three units of volume. It is presumed that the Rogue Trader did not risk seizing more in the presence of the Proctor, but even one ounce unaccounted for makes the tithe incomplete."

f92840b7-78e9-46f1-ba53-36af69f063a4.Text: "When we arrived on Thassera, the Rogue Trader and I were drawn into the machinations of the planetary governor. He used sorcery on the Emperor's anointed, but the Rogue Trader managed to overcome the effects of the ritual and do battle with the heretic. The governor was executed, and we—"

efb07723-5b6b-4d79-8ce0-3c97d4df2997.Text: "A lie uttered in the Palace of Justice is a serious offence, Proctor. Glaito, retrieve recording: Thassera-84/Alpha."

05170efa-2224-4c56-97c2-87dfdafc9fa6.Text: "As we can observe, Proctor Anthar destroyed the heretical altar, and then a fight ensued in which the psyker died. There is not a single shred of evidence that the Rogue Trader actually overcame the sorcery. It is more likely that the person standing before us is a heretic and a creature of corruption."

43ec73e3-b448-4881-8338-03b2ed10fe70.Text: "The request has already been sent. We expect a response within a few cycles. We will add it to the file as additional information. It will be of no help to you right now."

8a82f154-e338-4cfe-b7e4-6ee37a86c4c7.Text: "Any servant of yours would say whatever necessary to curry favour with the person wearing the Rogue Trader's face. Her testimony holds no weight in this case."

5cf45e18-8e06-406d-ad4f-311c77727146.Text: "According to the information we have received, the lady-in-waiting Maive has undergone Servitude Imperpituis. Shrewd, Rogue Trader, very shrewd."

a7f6ed4c-3cbf-4665-b937-458f6ee466e5.Text: {n}Strachs arches an eyebrow.{/n} "You must be confident if you are offering yourself up for examination by a psyker..."

aad65734-939b-4dbe-8eef-89342141fd69.Text: "In the case of sorcery, the court operates on the presumption of guilt."

c53b5667-8407-428f-b550-d1eb0f447d12.Text: {n}The prefect likewise fixes you with a cold, silent glare, her eyes brimming with hatred.{/n}

28c03c02-0a4d-4a78-8726-ee56a72d67c2.Text: {n}The prefect leafs through a few pages in a folder.{/n} "The court also takes note of the pernicious effects of the Rogue Trader's handling of the Emperor's servants entrusted to {mf|his|her} authority. Since arriving from Thassera, the Rogue Trader has done {mf|his|her} duty by passing judgement on several subjects within the walls of this hallowed hall..." {n}The prefect picks up the sheet of notes and wrinkles her nose.{/n}

02554be3-c655-406e-8e55-dc4b146c2973.Text: {n}The cardinal's voice is clearly heard over the whispering statics.{/n} "I begged, I implored... But you did not listen! Oh, how they pleaded, how they cried out to me, how— how they stank of corruption! If I could not purify myself, then I can purify them! All of them! The women, the children, the old! All of them!" {n}He makes a sound between a cough and a cackle.{/n}

174ee2e4-7340-44c7-8dd2-91272d223fd0.Text: "First, the Administratum is unable to do its duty and asks for help, and now, it has the audacity to criticise the verdicts of the Rogue Trader. Prefect, your accusations do not merely cast aspersions on the competence of the Administratum, they challenge the sanctity of the decisions of the Emperor's anointed."

fce38f51-46de-49c5-b954-e652b59c107b.Text: {n}Strachs does not turn to look at Inscribia, but you have no doubt about whom he is addressing.{/n} "The Adeptus Administratum, like the Adeptus Arbites, only oversees the allocation of the tithe. I do not need to remind you of that, do I, Prefect?"

27b87fc0-65aa-4fa3-b1c1-53374b3c5e99.Text: "What is happening on Dargonus? What is the cause of the panic, and why this private conversation?"

98d670e6-b118-4854-bb45-40030db70437.Text: "This was all one carefully orchestrated spectacle, wasn't it?"

8f20c498-c319-459d-ab8c-ecab4992131e.Text: "Your only goal has been to get your hands on the tithe from Leethus!"

98f89ce0-018b-4f7b-989d-395ee341da09.Text: "You wanted to go to Leethus yourself. A foolish mistake, Prefect — your impatience was too obvious."

ae7406dc-6eb1-46cd-aaac-7f363ffb0b8c.Text: "Just admit it: you set me up!"

f4fa488b-9d7c-4d7b-8bec-8127d9a27e07.Text: "Your blatant attempts at manipulation were painful to observe — the crude work of a talentless old crone who thinks herself worthy of judging those who are superior to her in every regard."

aaaa1a7a-66d4-4b1d-994c-59c1b1d5ecce.Text: [Allow yourself to be escorted to the trial] "So be it. Let's see what you have prepared for me."

d3b934e3-8df5-40e7-906f-06bd25ebabe8.Text: "Enough of this nonsense! Answer me plainly!"

7dfcc327-224c-4c0d-b890-afb18b998a92.Text: "You twisted my report on Thassera to paint me as a heretic."

3175cddb-1a0f-414f-a288-2021af059f5b.Text: "You spied on me. You knew of every word I said. How does it feel to sneak glances at one whom you could never hope to become?"

4f860e10-61d1-4af2-b9b4-6786a71008aa.Text: "Is the world under attack? Are there any casualties?"

1187309c-643d-46a8-8c3b-54ab40436d62.Text: "Whatever form it may take, heresy always treads quietly, unbeknownst to its ultimate victim. I believe both of us have given some thought to this in recent days."

d2bfed8f-1382-40b0-b4c3-9e1078bb7acc.Text: "Who in the void do you think you are?"

b06c5e90-d64f-4140-8877-a51915afe1cc.Text: "A trial? This is my protectorate! I am the law here!"

e0699f9f-d0e5-45c3-be6b-3e49a5397053.Text: "Due to recent suspicions of the heresy of concealing the sacred tithe, an emergency inspection has been initiated. Until said inspection is complete, the tithe will remain in the custody of the Administratum for a term amounting to 145 planetary cycles and 17 solar cycles according to Dargonus chronometry."

4a1da765-3692-4937-b4c1-6975784389da.Text: {n}The prefect, who was about to turn away, stops and glances back at you with a fatigued look.{/n} "What?"

17bb2e0b-0d9f-4de1-9f18-62689172a903.Text: "I simply wished to do what you as Theodora's successor were supposed to do — protect the sacred tithe. There is no point in trying to present my reasonable desire in a damning light."

62119bbd-e416-44cf-9655-eb59b1ca1f3f.Text: {n}Vultur takes a few trembling breaths as she finally calms down and seemingly becomes conscious of her own outburst. Without giving you another glance, she gestures to the Arbitrators.{/n} "Escort the accused to {mf|his|her} proper place."

7db70f61-2a7d-4c36-ac8f-a6977fd6cf44.Text: {n}The prefect sighs heavily.{/n} "I shouldn't have even tried to hear you out, Rogue Trader..." {n}She gives a nod to the Arbitrators, signalling them to escort you to the accused's stand.{/n}

d3069a6b-f418-42fb-a936-ce81b5b2cbed.Text: "I do not recommend this course of action, Rogue Trader. You cannot stop the machine of justice, for its millstones have already been set in motion. Such rashness will only worsen your situation further."

2bc788b2-44be-4392-bc34-856e3b620a13.Text: {n}The prefect gives a dispassionate nod to the Arbitrators behind you and turns away.{/n}

35852abb-2791-4bc8-920a-20d54a0b7570.Text: {n}You manage to land a hit before one of the Arbitrators knocks you off your feet with a stunning blow. You hear an elderly groan nearby — despite your efforts, the prefect is still alive.{/n}

2af94430-9280-46f9-af38-72df8f235b99.Text: {n}The prefect gives you a different look from before, and the century-old weariness in her eyes dissipates for just a moment. There is surprise and piqued curiosity in her expression, both of which, however, she quickly conceals behind the usual veil of aloofness.{/n}

fb72953e-bc02-4cf1-9353-a4d74ae5ba60.Text: {n}Prefect Inscribia Vultur raises her eyes to you.{/n} "Rogue Trader von Valancius. Welcome back to the Palace of Justice."

040dd85b-a887-4763-a6a1-b3c03830664d.Text: "That is why you are here, is it not? To learn why the world is distressed, why the air is charged with vox-transmissions... Any administrator worth their station would be concerned — disruptions to established processes always lead to... Well, no matter."

e305d7a5-00b9-4af3-b406-72c6ca2ca086.Text: "No, no physical harm has come to your protectorate during your absence." {n}Vultur shakes her head.{/n} "However, the threat of a different kind of heresy looms over the capital."

342b368c-1eda-4879-befa-8b55ae5ace49.Text: {n}The prefect peers at your face. Her voice sounds strange — deeper, calmer, less cantankerous than usual.{/n} "Have you ever pondered the nature of heresy, von Valancius? Perhaps, to your mind, heresy is merely limited to xenos, warp spawn, and insurgents... But there are other heresies, whose existence is far more easily forgotten: those of negligence, of avarice, of confusion and disorder..."

393b4643-97dd-428c-9dcc-56ee69aefd70.Text: "Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, in accordance with the amendment to Decree 64-98/DF issued by the Adeptus Administratum and the Adeptus Arbites, you stand accused of countless heresies against the sacred tithe and the well-being of the protectorate. All related statements have been formulated and the evidence of your crimes registered — the proceedings will commence as soon as you and your accomplices present yourselves as the accused..." {n}The prefect looks at you with the eyes of a snake.{/n} "A trial awaits you, {name}."

0f149f0c-9e67-4a4c-ab7c-adaf3751b248.Text: "I am His servant and a votary of the Imperium's prosperity. I cannot stand idly by and watch you trample on the glorious legacy of your bloodline."

08a757d4-6a56-46e9-9f56-9ff69afb9a90.Text: "And it is this conviction that has turned you into a monster that, in its charge toward the abyss, aims to drag the whole realm down with it." {n}The prefect's eyes seem to burn right through you.{/n} "The gravity of your crimes is enough to depose your entire dynasty. Do not oppose the law, von Valancius — doing so will only serve to make your situation worse."

89e6e023-b41b-4af8-ac68-1f3245cea0d3.Text: {n}The Arbitrators beat you to the draw — your defiance is punished before you can land a single blow against the prefect.{/n}

e371b0fc-710e-453d-9a12-69c2b898df28.Text: {n}The prefect's lips press together into a thin line, and it seems that the first real emotion she has ever shown is now breaking through her facade — righteous fury.{/n} "I am your protectorate's last hope against the jaws of anarchy, irresponsibility, and complete unravelling! I alone can save this part of the Imperium that had the misfortune of falling into the hands of those whose only motivations are profit, excitement, and feeding their own egos!"

63264f8e-24ce-4750-b8c4-5a57ec126b74.Text: {n}The prefect looks you in the eye without blinking. Her lips slowly stretch into a faint smile visible only to you.{/n} "Resorting to insults in the face of imminent downfall? How base, von Valancius. Not unlike yourself." {n}She makes a gesture toward the Arbitrators and turns away.{/n}

34a1b1b6-f5bd-4ecf-812a-bbebad2a8206.Text: "All I did was provide a summary of the results of your expedition — a summary stripped of dubious attributes such as declarations of good intentions and de-emphasised consequences."

66265790-ff05-4105-8181-a2957f122994.Text: {n}Vultur sighs.{/n} "Not everyone is driven by greed and thrill-seeking, Rogue Trader. I see your position has clouded your mind... Regrettable, but unsurprising — without due discipline in judgement and actions, it is only the most likely terminus."

abec4533-4d5b-4fdb-b7ae-2fda37c9838a.Text: {n}Your taunt hits its mark: an angry grimace passes over the prefect's face. She immediately recomposes herself, but it is too late — you saw how much your words have offended her, and she knows that you caught her reaction.{/n}

6a8c0ece-a2f5-4143-aad2-89d58bb326f9.Text: {n}Yet another, painful crease appears on the prefect's brow. You feel confident that your comment got to her.{/n}

3fd9d967-7762-471f-920e-4f80a6c7996c.Text: "Unsubstantiated conjecture mixed with an inflated sense of self-importance. I am honoured to do my duty wherever His will commands me to be."

a2c052d8-f7cb-46e7-a284-07145ff02127.Text: {n}For a moment, the Arbitrators exchange glances — they may be prepared to take you into custody, but the prefect's furious outburst has not gone unnoticed.{/n}

589192b6-586d-43d4-b23b-f71f5f31a89d.Text: "I want to hear my retinue's opinions."

34eb9cbe-3da7-464d-8680-39d45cfb0948.Text: "Why are they putting things on the scales?"

f06405b4-44b4-402c-b973-95b8fd81095d.Text: "Give me details about the parties to this conflict. I want to see who among them is trustworthy."

a02128c6-a1d6-4281-ba8e-1ea03f0f5660.Text: "Let us see Sister Juth prove her faith: she may execute Pras if she acknowledges that the Host is a minor army of the Ecclesiarchy, for indeed it is one in essence. If the sister agrees, then upon Pras's execution the Doleful Host will be sentenced to exile and expropriation, lest they be tempted to take up arms again."

fb799fe0-546a-4107-be0d-a50f02954b1a.Text: "Am I hearing this correctly? Is the cardinal asking to be tortured to death for his wickedness?"

3e133d9d-e019-4c39-9cb2-1d92472dce6b.Text: "I hereby sentence Lady Molles-Secundas to a duty of exploration and development of the protectorate's fringe worlds. Give her everything she needs to conduct her business. I expect her results to be impressive. As she has been found guilty, Lord Molles is to be deemed alive."

28912d87-ea72-477e-af5b-c9c860f8ab66.Text: "I grant the Drusians the right to decide the cardinal's fate. It is my belief that Reverend Hieronymus is unsurpassed in his comprehension of humility and holiness."

fc0860d0-6317-498c-bc1f-9b1a714438c6.Text: "The situation is complex and requires further investigation."

a8daf876-ead5-4a4d-9442-d2fafe439b2e.Text: "I heard you, and I am ready to pass my judgement."

6a49aa93-5533-4ab4-9d97-b11335300581.Text: "Well, Prefect, let us discuss the crime committed inside the Administratum that has led to this hearing."

0a28a392-dde1-427f-b8b4-baf3dd507929.Text: "I agree with Solomorne: both parties to the case are guilty. Execute them."

e40a6561-f621-4092-abac-da37547977e6.Text: "I declare Pras guilty. Escort him here for his execution."

4f9e7219-ee7d-48e2-a501-d08ddd189d37.Text: "I hereby clear the Choirmaster of all charges, and order Sister Juth to be executed."

e6cf573f-42b1-433a-a34b-dca42fb41ebc.Text: Presided over the trial of Lady Molles-Secundas's case and allowed the criminal's husband to decide the fate of those who had wronged him.

1f26226d-acee-466a-9bae-088508a9f32d.Text: "As you can see, Inscribia, your system is imperfect. But I am merciful: compensate Lord Molles for the damage he has incurred, and let him decide the fate of his wife and the venal clerk."

e40b166f-1905-4078-ae46-7ef2920e7174.Text: Presided over the trial of Lady Molles-Secundas's case and ordered a summary execution of every participant in the dispute.

727b687c-e4ce-4e48-b774-d288c9d21426.Text: "After this session ends, a public execution will be held in front of the Palace of Justice: that of Lady Molles-Secundas, both her husbands, the children, and your clerk. All of you who have wasted my precious time. I forbid taking down the bodies; let them be a warning, should anyone presume to distract me again."

d0cfd35a-548c-46dc-b052-e8b8aa20e165.Text: "We can turn a blind eye to this instance. I wish to pass a different verdict."

3e1a18d1-b9ef-49f3-86de-d5f50314fbf1.Text: "What does my retinue have to say?"

3eee1a4c-59c1-4360-b906-cfd55f3fc97e.Text: "I am ready to pass my judgement."

fc5fa0ba-c81d-478f-9e5c-6cb5a7d44652.Text: "I see the depth of the cardinal's contrition and grant him the right to embrace the death he has chosen. I hope the Emperor has mercy on his soul."

1e744325-25b0-4c16-b00a-0378e13960d1.Text: "I would not dare inflict so horrible a fate on one whom the Ecclesiarchy has deemed a holy man. In dark hours such as these, we need the light of faith more than ever."

3adbaa4e-f6b8-4663-b601-2bcc1fbc7f6a.Text: "I am tired and loath to be part of this. Prefect, rule for the Administratum's side and let us call it a day."

20b40c84-c5b4-4a30-ba2b-ba73006aacdf.Text: "The case is clear to me now. I am ready to pass my verdict."

09a8679d-28aa-474d-8cb2-3d1df6c6e038.Text: "Lord Molles is to be declared alive and fully restored to his rights. All consequences of his death are to be deemed null and void."

2d645a37-3f2d-4e31-98d1-ffec5340a3dc.Text: "I order Lord Molles be declared alive. He is to be fully restored to his life and property. Lady Molles-Secundas is thereby found guilty of document forgery and is sentenced to death. May the Emperor protect her soul."

6d63e064-5c63-432a-b2f4-706b3e9fcf11.Text: "Execute the impostor. No one can be alive when everything points to them being dead."

02adadaf-4825-47b6-8563-1b9ab0a0c017.Text: "Are there no more active disputes in my domain? Come now, bring me a few more misguided souls!"

b30456ec-e49e-4559-ba1c-4e2d2c9f04f4.Text: "This entire court is a farce! They call this the Palace of Justice, but what goes on here is anything but!"

bc803005-54d6-4700-b8fb-c799c368bc3c.Text: "It was amusing at first, but not for long. If we are finally done, I will take my leave."

b3ee2e2b-dcc3-44fa-8bd7-978ee554c284.Text: "Kibellah has made a good suggestion. The cardinal shall undergo sacred torture in the established fashion of the Bloodspun Web. I expect he will reconsider his views on death in the process."

d8954b08-acbd-4e9c-8993-f58eeb00db59.Text: "Cardinal Anvylas, in seeking permission to torture a holy man, you are violating both secular and ecclesiastic law. For that, I sentence you to death!"

bdb2a138-92ec-48c1-9c13-54c39a0a3d92.Text: "Jae's idea is excellent. Let Lady Molles-Secundas have two husbands, and let her growing production output continue to be a blessing to the protectorate."

92773c5a-2496-4313-a887-6b555a79db6f.Text: "Cassia's perspective on marriage in the Imperium is correct. Lady Molles-Secundas may stay with her new husband, but she shall return the family business to Lord Molles. Henceforth, my protectorate will operate under a new concept of legal spousehood."

692262b4-03b6-4f88-85a9-a1e50e6c0678.Text: "I will put my trust in Solomorne's advice. If the cardinal wants to challenge his proposed sainthood, he should go to Terra."

9588f913-476c-40e4-b86f-070da7dbab87.Text: "Prefect, relay Solomorne's words to Lady Molles-Secundas."

470f3014-9a63-4b49-ae20-9ff6d8f84eab.Text: "Allow me to guess the details of Lord Molles's kidnapping: the pirates appeared out of nowhere, knew exactly when to attack, at which point his wife had already prepared all the documents she needed to request the issuance of his death certificate."

495983b3-8243-47cf-bad7-65cbce247fb7.Text: "Have you forgotten that I am a Rogue Trader and I can dispense justice right here and now?"

6039640a-30c0-4798-9e50-c477350fd1b9.Text: Presided over the trial of Lady Molles-Secundas's case and delivered a harsh verdict, sentencing the criminal to death and severely punishing the Administratum.

5239ead2-2d72-457d-bc09-097a7c9acf1f.Text: "Lady Molles-Secundas is hereby sentenced to death. The Administratum shall conduct an internal audit and execute the fraudulent clerk along with all their superiors — excluding you, Prefect. Another case like this and the cannon of the law will be pointing at you."

e706e29c-65a3-4ffa-9af8-01f0c59a4c2c.Text: "I would like to hear out the parties."

0162480c-05a1-4d2c-a3a5-2c15cacad999.Text: "Execute Pras. Abelard, let the Chorda world give their Choirmaster to Dargonus."

32fcde8a-97f6-4d3e-a956-488b13305406.Text: "Solomorne, is it not excessive to execute both parties?"

2bf89121-d87c-45ab-8ee0-65e2ea163a0f.Text: "You heard Pasqal. Cardinal Anvylas shall die an honourable death and continue to serve the faith as part of a sacred machine."

0cf59094-7c37-4d73-aec4-3a6e4eb05522.Text: "Heinrix is right about the importance of paperwork. If Lady Molles-Secundas does not have the certificate in question, her children will inherit her property. The case is hereby closed due to the defendant's demise."

c2cdd7f0-713d-4dd9-b258-4d58117940bf.Text: [Switch on your vox] "Vigdis, quick, ask our ship's Choirmaster whether Master Pras of Dargonus has been known to engage in any compromising behaviour."

7bd90dd4-4829-4b24-97d3-fb811df6e17c.Text: "It is their family affair. Let them handle it."

58d0b766-c7ca-4177-b65a-40dcfd5c6295.Text: {n}Inscribia Vultur's dreary, vox-amplified voice carries across the hall.{/n} "The court will now hear Case DP-1453/2, the Doleful Host against the Astropathic Choir of Dargonus. Representatives for the parties will present their arguments following standard procedure."

8dccee3f-4ff6-48a3-afcc-6b066091ac19.Text: "The arguments are acknowledged and shall be weighed on the Scales of Justice! The representative will retreat to the Chapel of Patience to await the verdict."

b3b5da35-18ca-41df-a99d-4c498b7ce3ac.Text: "The Scales of Justice are a sacred relic installed as a testament to the alliance between the von Valancius dynasty on one side and the Adeptus Arbites and the Administratum on the other. Legends say ancient machine spirits dwell within the relic. The Scales of Justice are only used on extraordinary occasions when an intervention from the Rogue Trader is necessary. Ceremony dictates that items symbolising the parties' arguments be placed on the scales, and once the verdict is announced, the machine spirits weigh the decision made and show either affirmation or rejection through the position of the scales. However, there has never been an occurrence where the Rogue Trader and the spirits of the scales were divided on the verdict."

157a57cc-e03c-47c1-b374-ce587f54fe21.Text: {n}As the prefect leans toward you, you get a whiff of ink and candlewax.{/n} "The Doleful Host is a respected cult of the God-Emperor. The Adeptus Ministorum has deemed them to be paragons of virtue who combat every manner of heresies, and has enlisted their aid in various... conflicts. Naturally, the Ecclesiarchy stops short of counting them among its warriors, but it uses them in very similar ways."

5eeb45a7-b659-4ec7-8ebc-5525e43412ce.Text: "Let us move on to the last case for today. The court will now hear Case DP-1646/7, Lady Molles-Secundas against the late Lord Molles. Lord Molles being deceased, he will be represented by his progeny, Agartha and Sjyllas Molles. Representatives for the parties will present their arguments following standard procedure."

8341210c-17ee-4bf9-8f63-26ff00c354dc.Text: "At once, Lord Captain." {n}The Palace of Justice falls silent for several minutes, until Vigdis's voice returns.{/n}

9be824a8-f4fe-48ac-9360-07691f03a59b.Text: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Who is to face the death penalty?"

a760261b-6adf-46a0-87ba-5b204e00276d.Text: "The Rogue Trader has made {mf|his|her} decision. Arbitrators, carry it out."

f7e199e9-48fb-4942-b0d3-ed76d3466a58.Text: "I am... Molles. When the pirates captured me, I thought I was doomed, but fate proved to be more gracious than that. I hurried home, only to... from my own house by my servants and learn that Lady Molles had already had me declared dead and married Lord Secundas. She'd also taken control of our... everything. Agartha and Sjyllas have recognised me... I'm losing my mind..."

9205b375-7ee7-40f6-9ffa-8d41294450de.Text: {n}A woman with lines of scripture all over her skin folds her arms into an Aquila.{/n} "My name is Sister Juth and I represent the Doleful Host. O God-Emperor's anointed one, we came upon a group of heretics whose minds brimmed with the most shameless thoughts. We captured them and tortured them as befits their transgressions. From what we were able to discern from their wailing and screaming, the head of the Astropathic Choir is plotting to betray House von Valancius. No one is a liar when flame is caressing their flesh! The Doleful Host surrounded the Choir building and demanded that the heretic be handed over. It was solely out of respect for the anointed one that we refrained from burning down the wayward heretic's den on the spot. However, say but the word, and we shall take him, that he may undergo a righteous cleansing."

9a8dd7ed-fd76-418e-b39c-84e4e6250e97.Text: "That does nothing to diminish the stipulations of the Lex Imperialis. Besides, following the letter of the law absolves you of the necessity of tainting your hands with the blood of a potential saint: either the cardinal will cross the Maw, thus proving his sainthood, or he will perish if the Emperor wills it. As you can see, the Lex Imperialis has all the answers."

ccbbec2f-2bde-4601-9afd-4164b74f93e9.Text: {n}The gaunt man dressed in Astropath's robes is standing tall, but his voice trembles with fury.{/n} "I am Master Anjelio. I represent the Dargonus Astropathic Choir. These insidious and ignorant people are passing off their victims' ravings as truth! Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, people will say anything under torture just to make the agony stop. We have served House von Valancius faithfully for decades, Master Pras the longest of all! Please, order them to stand down."

7a78e61d-bad5-4986-85f7-ee7dedead969.Text: "It will doubtless be the cardinal's most passionate adherents who follow him on that perilous journey, wishing to see him sainted. I suppose that would minimise the potential unrest that ecstatically fervent believers are prone to."

d2956e31-ee8f-4c91-a832-35ef5c36f3f4.Text: {n}The prefect's dry fingers press down on the runes on her data-slate.{/n} "As I thought... I deeply regret to inform you that said further investigation is impossible. The Host's fighters are already breaking down the doors of the Choir. Delaying the decision would lead to uncontrollable consequences."

ea74e981-2edb-41c6-911c-c3aa4185933f.Text: {n}You devise an elegant rendering of the sentence, one that will convince everyone that you are in the right, and save you from being branded a saint-killer. All you must do is accuse the cardinal of intending to murder an all-but-canonised individual.{/n}

a63e7f86-0ee1-4e7d-8d04-c01887c31997.Text: {n}You realise that the cardinal himself is somehow to blame for what happened, but your conjectures are stubbornly failing to crystallise into a clear and compelling verdict.{/n}

e256b979-6337-4e26-bb67-43bacefd0150.Text: "Arbitrators will be dispatched to retrieve the condemned criminal at once. All those present are to wait until justice is served."

b56dbd6e-202d-4669-8d1f-98b50ff034f0.Text: {n}Vultur gasps.{/n} "Can you even imagine all the procedural disruption in the wake of executing so many—" {n}She shrinks under your implacable gaze, almost disappearing into her robe.{/n} "The verdict is clear. Each sentence will be carried out under my personal oversight."

7a47326b-62d4-4bc5-a8ab-92c7a98e99b5.Text: "Some lord is going to judge the Administratum?" {n}The prefect lets out a shaky breath.{/n} "The verdict is accepted. A closed session will be held with Lord Molles as the... judge."

453c8017-1a72-49cb-87d9-9e5670d5ece3.Text: {n}Vultur stares at you, her eyes wide with horror.{/n} "Everything will be carried out as Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} wishes." {n}The old woman exhales deeply, shaking off her fear, and proclaims in an unperturbed voice,{/n} "Arbitrators, carry out the sentence!"

8175d1db-29cc-4d96-8185-6fd09e69f27a.Text: "The Rogue Trader has made {mf|his|her} will clear! Cardinal Anvylas will leave the Palace of Justice and accept his fate."

e22349b0-cc3d-4feb-a2ad-a45c6f4b018e.Text: {n}A gaunt man raises his bloodshot eyes at you. For a moment, all sounds cease, even the scratching of the countless servo-skulls' quills. The man's gaze is full of a pain so strong and undiluted that your breath seizes in your throat.{/n} "I am impure, O Emperor's anointed one. I am beset by impure thoughts, but no one believes my confessions. I have been giving away the treasures I possess, only for people to bring me more. Worse still is the knowledge that I am leading people astray. They look at me and believe a state of perfect grace is attainable, while I... I am very tired..."

4d45e324-4554-4dc7-ad3e-6642db67d6c2.Text: {n}The cardinal blinks away a tear and continues:{/n} "But most terrible of all is that my brethren, the preachers of the Koronus Expanse, see me as a holy man. Their delusion has been so persistent that they sent a petition to Holy Terra, asking that I be made a saint. That was when I became firm in my decision to submit to torture in front of my congregation, thus reminding them that no holiness exists unless bestowed as a gift by the God-Emperor. Even clerics of my rank can and must repent, thus becoming more pure every day. Please, allow me to undergo mortal torture in His name in front of my parishioners!"

68097051-1b10-40f0-b704-d513ab5b6989.Text: "According to the Lex Imperialis, a candidate saint may personally challenge their sainting by petitioning the Ecclesiarch on Holy Terra. Sidestepping the head of the Imperial Cult is a violation of the Emperor's Law. Since Astropathic communication with the rest of the Imperium has been disrupted, I propose to put Cardinal Anvylas on a ship that crosses the Maw, so that he can submit his request with every formality observed."

1b54ea19-f3ca-4b83-8de6-853264debed1.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I am Lady Molles-Secundas! Only eight cycles ago, a man broke into my house posing as my husband, the late Lord Molles. Contrary to what I know, he denies that he was killed by pirates. Instead, he purportedly survived, thanks to the God-Emperor's providence. However, I hold here his death certificate, issued by the Administratum, which clearly states that my husband passed away. I demand that this fraud be executed!" {n}The woman belligerently waves around a scroll on which the words "declared dead" are clearly visible.{/n}

e0ea483b-9481-4f04-9ea2-8f7a45e30543.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, our father did survive. He really was captured by pirates, who were going to demand ransom, but the Imperial Navy managed to board the ship and rescue him. After he went missing, our mother, Lady Molles, arranged for a death certificate before we received the good news. Now, we are in the humiliating position of having to prove that our father is alive, while our mother is living with her new husband, Lord Secundas, and has taken over our family business. We implore you to restore Lord Molles to his life and name! He is humbly awaiting your decision in the Chapel of Patience."

afee930d-9681-4914-958c-09a407141c1c.Text: {n}The prefect plays a vox-recording on one of the servo-skulls. The soft voice is interspersed with static, but you are able to make out the words.{/n}

36cc6856-956c-41b2-8013-14dba6e80452.Text: {n}The prefect turns on one of her countless data-slates.{/n} "The Molles family manufactures nutritional rations. They supply the Astra Militarum as well as worlds that have no food production of their own. With the lord at the helm, they covered the needs of three regiments and five worlds. Now, it is five regiments and twelve worlds. One might say Lady Molles-Secundas has done much better than her husband did."

cf363e09-fd83-4b5f-b41b-5e5135e1465d.Text: "As you say, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The man posing as Lord Molles is found guilty of deliberately deceiving the Molles family and stealing a nobleman's identity. His punishment will be death. Carry out the sentence!"

5363a4ea-19e3-4252-9aa2-e082ca3a4431.Text: "All will be silent! What is your decision, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"

a1751bba-19c3-4d8c-8069-8fd34ec3acef.Text: "I assume you realise that, if you declare the lord alive, it will disprove the authenticity of the documents presented by Lady Molles-Secundas. Forging Administratum certificates is a crime punishable by death."

355d1d16-9e0d-4769-9468-e216212dd47c.Text: {n}The prefect looks at you and then the Interrogator with slight alarm.{/n} "No... contradictions found. I imagine the younger Molleses are going to hand the reins of the family business back to the man whom they consider their father. Your decision is also going to affect the work of the Administratum: we can certainly expect to be swamped with requests for 'legally alive' certificates, but that will help uncover false identities and non-existent nobility. This session is now concluded!"

d6a1e4ec-4824-4779-a50e-013be08e4b55.Text: "Lady Molles-Secundas is sentenced to death for forging an Administratum legal document! Arbitrators, carry out the sentence!"

9d6a3340-d068-45ca-b21a-f6bc09251603.Text: {n}As the last attendants leave the courtroom, the prefect turns to you with a delighted expression.{/n} "Lady Theodora held court sessions like this to strengthen her subjects' faith in the Lex Imperialis and their fear of breaching it. A most useful practice, wouldn't you agree?"

8b51f447-010a-43de-8a89-e93b2b0ba4ba.Text: "Of course, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I dare not take up any more of your time."

dbb54405-018c-4ddb-96f6-774448eef002.Text: "Your enthusiasm is laudable, but, as I'm sure you understand, any manner of procedure requires prior registration — which, in turn, involves filling out official forms and signing regulation-approved documents. It is for this reason that I am, alas, unable to honour your request. With your permission, I will now return to my duties. Thank you."

f5dbb031-30a2-4a63-a230-e8d7139fa546.Text: "Delivering justice is incredibly demanding work that requires in-depth knowledge of the Lex Imperialis. Today, you merely touched upon a small fragment of this sacrament. Thank you for your participation. And now, it is time for me to return to my duties. Good day to you."

ba1e3068-7c07-4a38-90ce-7e657d29c911.Text: "That is correct. In addition, he insists on your subjects bearing witness to it — as a lesson to them, so to speak. To refuse a cardinal is impious in itself, but to execute one who is a saint in all but name..."

12f25f04-18ea-44d1-ace4-3c383fabd955.Text: "All arguments have been acknowledged. Let the Rogue Trader's verdict be delivered."

eac860de-8a2b-4582-a9a3-80d78fb1b273.Text: {n}A modicum of respect can be glimpsed in the prefect's gaze in your direction.{/n} "A very balanced decision. It sets a precedent that, through reasoning by analogy, will help in optimising other court cases on Dargonus."

45194a0b-84fc-4890-9277-e8fa91d92fa7.Text: "Lord Captain, without a Choirmaster, the power of Dargonus's Astropaths would be significantly diminished. Unless a worthy replacement is found for Master Pras, he cannot be executed." {n}The Seneschal frowns.{/n} "There is a Chorda world that owes us an old debt which can be repaid with a seasoned Astropath. We can make the request, although it would leave the planet in question with barely any means of communication."

3fd3df34-4367-4d8c-bde8-25b9c54f84e1.Text: "If Lady Molles-Secundas is right, then her children are the impostor's accomplices and are guilty of defaming the authenticity of Administratum documents." {n}Now Solomorne has enough sang-froid in him for a regiment.{/n} "Let the woman know that her heirs must face the same fate as the criminal, for so stipulates the Emperor's Law."

fdbb74ee-c93e-40d7-b9b5-5f34d1bf3b5c.Text: {n}Idira hugs herself, rocking back and forth.{/n} "No more does the blind man listen to the distant light... Concealed behind the false gold, abomination lies at his heart, and it's burning, burning, burning!" {n}The psyker's entire body shudders.{/n} "Oh my, Lord Captain. Looks like our Astropath really is lost to corruption. I swear he's hiding something under that robe of his — either an amulet or some unholy mark! And those rabid zealots are going to find it on him, alive or dead. But the little voices are laughing, saying you may kill the traitor but don't expect any good to come of it..."

ccc68890-7c78-4583-9e8c-15e6512dc79e.Text: "The {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropathic Choir{/g} hardly needs an introduction. They are some of the most valuable servants of the Imperium, without whom any and all communication between your worlds would collapse. The Dargonus Choir took horrific casualties in the recent major warp storm. Master Pras made an enormous effort to at least partially restore communication. While we may not have proof of his innocence, Pras's dedication to his duty is beyond doubt." {n}The old woman locks her shrivelled fingers together.{/n} "As you can see, this is an intricate situation."

03966cc0-5dce-4d17-83e4-e0bfab9b4bcb.Text: "Choirmaster Weisz has known Master Pras for quite a long time. He has made a very measured statement to the effect that for some time now, the mental images conveyed by Pras have taken on a shade of profound anxiety, and have become more aloof and detached overall. Zacchary Weisz attributes this to Pras's horrific experience during the {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}warp storm{/g}, but he is less than completely sure, as there is still something that sets the Dargonus Choirmaster's messages apart from those of his fellow survivors."

a88ad3d4-7d1a-4e4b-a4a0-1cda9166063f.Text: "Unfortunately, Acting Choirmaster Qadd is unable to present any reliable information. He barely knows Master Pras, and the late Zacchary Weisz never provided a detailed assessment of the Astropath you are asking about."

f9c0ce84-6dc0-44f9-a1b2-4a3c2da4b770.Text: {n}You see clearly now that no matter what decision you make, it will backfire on you. However, there is a way to benefit from this: allow the Host to dispense their vigilante justice, then accuse the fanatics of violating an ancient agreement that forbade the Ecclesiarchy from having its own army, and proceed to confiscate the Host's property.{/n}

75936036-16d1-4bdf-bdfa-cf43e311eebe.Text: {n}You have no way of knowing what the correct decision should be. This does look like a complicated case.{/n}

93a73843-4820-425e-b9ee-bb67ad273b18.Text: "Spoken like a true heir to Lady Theodora, who could squeeze gold out of a rock. Sister Juth would never recant her statement. She will have no choice but to accept your conditions."

06c36f85-b01d-4047-b9ff-fbc52ca35118.Text: "Situation analysis complete. Let the paradox cease; let functionality triumph. Suggestion: use the unit Cardinal Anvylas's organic remains to construct a servo-skull herald and place it in an automated chapel. The status of sainthood will be extended to the liturgical mechanism."

e71f9371-6204-425d-a12d-2ab37acd2471.Text: {n}Argenta shakes her head.{/n} "Wise counsel is required here, and it is not to be found within these walls. Reverend Hieronymus would understand the workings of the cardinal's soul. Entrust him to the good shepherd of the Drusians."

ca9da953-e115-4fc1-8b9c-e91d0a7da1be.Text: "The head of the Drusians would hardly deny the cardinal's peculiar request. However, the matter will be outside our jurisdiction at that point, and Reverend Hieronymus will appreciate your high trust in him when it comes to questions of faith."

d57a02e2-b705-435b-ad33-810fed2ae1bf.Text: "How could the woman have possibly known for sure her husband would make it out of a major dustup like that? The business had ground to a halt, so she took things in her own hands. Actually, shereen, on Efreet you're allowed to take several spouses precisely in case this happens. It would be a trifle for you to amend the laws of Lady Molles-Secundas's homeworld. Let her continue to fill your coffers — she's more than able to handle two husbands!"

02dacef7-f8be-40bc-8a50-0aaf378f102b.Text: {n}Heinrix rubs the bridge of his nose, looking tired.{/n} "This absurdity has dragged on for too long... So be it. The Emperor as my witness, I am reluctant to revisit my early training experience in the Administratum, but I am going to have to. Does Lady Molles-Secundas have a paper that certifies she is alive? If not, the defendant is to be deemed dead, with all that entails."

0d14fe95-9479-4556-a2f2-bd199453971d.Text: {n}Lady Molles-Secundas's talents are self-evident — she could easily boost production on any planet. What might be called her promotion under the guise of punishment would bring tangible benefits. You just so happen to think of several backwater worlds that have good potential but lack the capable stewardship to match it.{/n}

b8928143-a3c5-47f2-aaaa-ac3f22177ab5.Text: {n}As much as you would like to turn the situation to your advantage, you cannot think of a solution.{/n}

df437a5b-f114-4bee-9ba8-b783cb2bdf24.Text: "Well, a gesture like that is certain to reverberate throughout the protectorate, but a verdict is a verdict. This session is now concluded!"

b9018d44-abb6-45bd-ae80-fe0c61600f51.Text: {n}The dumbstruck prefect opens and closes her mouth like a fish out of water.{/n} "I... am struggling to comment on that. Will somebody share the incredible news with Lady Molles-Secundas? This session is now concluded!"

b883c732-70a4-432b-bfe1-e136a4e3b269.Text: "Lady Molles-Secundas will depart for her place of exile before today ends. Arbitrators, carry out the sentence!"

29df08bc-51c4-4ff9-8caf-66594d628fff.Text: "As you wish." {n}The prefect's dry fingers tap quickly on her data-slate. Soon afterward, she looks up from the vid-screen and says in a colourless voice,{/n} "Lady Molles-Secundas has confessed to bribing an Administratum official and is pleading for her offspring to be spared."

f9f59c7c-5460-44ea-b361-3c03bc30aceb.Text: {n}The indignant prefect shakes her head energetically.{/n} "She is a mother trying to save her children! That may have been a false confession! And, what is worse, a false accusation against the sacred service of the Administratum!"

298ae51b-6946-40a0-a8e7-125442efda35.Text: {n}The old woman presses her lips into a thin line.{/n} "Perish the thought. Your position as an Emperor-blessed judge is unquestionable."

dbec0aad-39a0-4057-8eff-01253440659c.Text: "No. Such a verdict will remind your subjects that only the Rogue Trader has the right to administer justice. Besides, if you take the Host's side, it will inspire new self-proclaimed executioners, and if you absolve the Astropath and he turns out to have been guilty after all, other heretics will feel safe to act with impunity. That is why I advise you to be stern — the Lex is on your side."

06b71fde-81c5-4104-bd71-505ea9a14c82.Text: "I imagine the verdict will horrify the cardinal, but on the other hand, centuries from now, his followers will still be able to listen to his recorded sermons and worship his remains with the same fanatical zeal as in the notional saint's lifetime. Expect generous donations toward the construction of the automated chapel, since many will want to have a part in such a momentous event."

e065ffee-c8fc-4c70-ae3a-cdb430ddf555.Text: "The Bloodspun Web is knowledgeable in ways to torment one's flesh without going to the Undying One before due time. Domin, allow us to help Cardinal Anvylas attain enlightenment and experience the purity of a near-death state. Undergoing our rite should make him realise it is not in his gift to sever his own thread."

3c51b235-33a0-4c8b-be1b-54c42fa120e2.Text: "This is a complicated situation, but... Lady Molles-Secundas was acting in the Imperium's interests. She had shouldered the duty of care for the family business, and was in no position to wallow in her grief for cycles upon cycles." {n}Cassia throws back her shoulders and says in a dignified voice,{/n} "A marriage between people of noble birth is a union of two servants of the Emperor. Duty toward the Imperium is at the heart of that union. If there comes a long period of time when one of the spouses is unable to fulfil their obligations, the marriage loses its meaning. If you could codify this understanding in law, that would help resolve this situation."

ff23735f-10c7-4805-a53f-44b2dd0d6650.Text: "This sounds like a decision that is favourable in the eyes of the Emperor. Moreover, I imagine it will make kidnappings for ransom substantially rarer. This session is now concluded!"

bf85c08e-d26c-4fa7-90f5-2a2e6f9a1bc1.Text: "Both parties have shown disrespect for the Imperium's authority. The Doleful Host is engaging in mob justice, and the defendant did not even deign to stand trial in person. Sentence them both to death — that would be the optimal outcome."

c99b2934-5e59-4505-b892-6dba3016bdbf.Text: "If that is the Astropath I am thinking of, the Dargonus Choir is going to be headed by a much stronger psyker than Pras. That will definitely improve communication between the protectorate's worlds."

7d65aff0-6907-4164-95a3-a568302c2fce.Text: "A harsh verdict, but from now on your subjects will hardly dare escalate situations to the point of open clashes — in cases similar to this one, of course."

7175fd49-38b5-461e-b58a-395213d55210.Text: "The cardinal was quite desperate to be relieved of his mortal life. But now that both the Ecclesiarchy and the Rogue Trader have refused him, he has no choice but to remain a living paragon of holiness."

84162d0a-a070-4b6c-bc6e-17765a102778.Text: "Today, the people of Dargonus will behold the cardinal's last penance. Master torturers will make sure that this holy man's request is fulfilled to the letter."

038e945e-b91d-4e6c-87cb-b4db0325ea61.Text: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The man claiming to be Lord Molles has been found guilty of deliberately misleading the Molles family and of appropriating the identity of a nobleman. His punishment is death."

770dcf80-bd90-42fb-a906-2a3df8580204.Text: "A loose description of the events, and yet one that is remarkably close to the truth. Surely you do not think that Lady Molles-Secundas herself orchestrated her husband's kidnapping? Although, one might say you are an {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}expert{/d} on such incidents."

e0cdf763-50a6-4491-a010-081b41948a69.Text: {n}In your days {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Ministorum}serving as an archdeacon{/d}, you resolved far more precarious religious disputes than this. The cardinal has admitted to his intention of killing a great and righteous man, and that is enough for you to render a decisive verdict.{/n}

53ec40f1-576a-48ff-9866-1157e89f98b1.Text: {n}You {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Militarum}better than anyone{/d} understand the importance of supplying an army. You immediately hatch an audacious plan: send Lady Molles-Secundas to one of the fringe worlds under the pretext of exile and have her set up the production of rations there.{/n}

d7ff44e9-508e-485a-b12e-7195229232a9.Text: {n}You recall a crucial nuance that has, on numerous occasions, {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}protected the nobility{/d} from zealots looking to dispense arbitrary justice: the Ecclesiarchy is forbidden from outfitting its own army. It should be easy to declare the Host to be in violation of this covenant and, as a pretty bonus, seize all their property afterward — solely as a lesson in humility, of course.{/n}

02014355-187d-40b2-b8cf-815384369b99.Text: "Again? I'm afraid they have already said what they had to say and are humbly awaiting their fate. Whatever questions you have, you may pose to me."

e00651bc-e617-414c-b3e8-e65cf2f3d938.Text: {n}It is highly unlikely that such an artefact actually exists — judging by the design of the device, it is nothing more than a set of regular albeit enormous and masterfully crafted weight scales devoid of machine spirits of any kind. Someone must be secretly manipulating the plates in order to add greater profoundness to the Rogue Trader's verdict.{/n}

1c50a68f-295f-4706-b9f7-3702aa836c33.Text: {n}The dynasty should be proud to have such a great and wise mechanism installed in its domain.{/n}

177fe1fd-9333-4ccf-96c6-f27544593925.Text: {n}The master of the court repeats the same monotonous formula, bidding the other representative to leave the courtroom.{/n}

aa4d81b7-da5a-4ef7-a401-cabc7efb7b3a.Text: {n}The prefect proceeds matter-of-factly to the next scroll.{/n} "The court will now hear Petition CR-1547/33, restated. The petitioner is Cardinal Anvylas. Your arguments, please, Cardinal."

8e9c9c46-0e8d-4d85-92c7-cec872368996.Text: {n}The old woman chews her lips anxiously.{/n} "That grants the request only in part, but..." {n}She glances over quickly at Kibellah.{/n} "You are probably the only one who believes the cardinal will survive the death cult's ordeal. If everything happens as you envision it, the cardinal will back down from his intention, and his flock will not be bereft of their saint."

d700767d-53eb-4f2e-892a-aaae825a709a.Text: "The Rogue Trader has passed {mf|his|her} verdict! Sister Juth is hereby sentenced to death for making an attempt on the life of the head of the Astropathic Choir!"

bdfc79de-8ba3-4ed1-9cb7-9544f32cc38f.Text: "Marshal Gregoras Strachs, taking into account your record of past achievements, I hereby deny you your execution and instead sentence you to punishment by toil. I appoint you high overseer of the world Vheabos VI. That is where you will remain for the rest of your life."

69ab172d-7cf7-489c-b1e8-6502840132ea.Text: "A fiery speech indeed, Inscribia. Shall we expect amendments, additions... or perhaps excuses?"

6f039bd7-6475-46a4-96d7-8349c671490c.Text: "You had trouble dying the last time. Let us correct this bureaucratic error."

de48de8e-d9e1-4ac4-9d98-2f33df9db35c.Text: "The punishment for your betrayal is demotion. You will patrol the lower levels of one of Dargonus's hives. Glaito may remain with you."

a98482d1-a415-408d-bc9e-66853107969d.Text: "Try what? To take my protectorate for yourself?"

db588b72-6bc3-430f-9f13-bce12b5b7b78.Text: "You know, on second thought... Execute her."
