89175dd1-4b73-4a76-a225-df472ec00e03.Text: "There is a suitable world not far from Dargonus. I believe Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} will find it convenient should you ever wish to pay your favourite a visit."

18a2ec92-d08b-4073-bc9b-1a0572275333.Text: "Absolutely, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. There is every possibility that you will come to the conclusion that your esteemed companion has already benefited plenty from your friendship."

571c6b1c-9846-45ca-b64e-d035190db72f.Text: "Your dynastic treasury contains many precious masterpieces. I would never dare to touch something that belonged to the late Lady Theodora, however, I will still find something most special and have it delivered to Mistress Heydari's chambers."

e76a0e55-757d-4cb5-bb8f-beb2c0ebdcf5.Text: "Masters of the Cold Trade, immoral criminals, and notorious crooks to the last man. The Mission is but one branch of this mafia gang that has taken root in the {g|Encyclopedia:Calixis}Calixis Sector{/g}. You can do business with them as long as you take the necessary precautions. They are led by Vladaym Tocara, who recently appointed himself Liege of Footfall. Of course, he is a trusted ally of Rogue Trader Winterscale... but he will not refuse you, another of the Emperor's anointed. If you wish to talk to Vladaym, look for him in the Liege's palace on Footfall."

a10a10fa-fcb6-4489-963b-d9c6bccd2b98.Text: "I think I know of something that might impress her, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. There is a curious little thing in your arsenal that is as beautiful as it is deadly, much like your favourite herself."

f2519c23-c181-4631-99a0-70d30d4159c1.Text: "Already done, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. A couple of years ago I happened to procure something that was made for the despotess of Colgor Alpha. A unique dress for a unique occasion, you might say. I knew I kept it for a reason."

12040975-4a17-4cc9-9d90-07c79c1fe16c.Text: "An acquaintance of mine, a merchant from Footfall, recently had a stroke of bad luck. Now he is forced to auction off his clipper — an excellent ship, albeit on the smaller side. I believe it is well within my ability to purchase it before any other takers."

328e5a58-7319-4ed4-87b6-cd867af27b36.Text: "I laud Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s judiciousness. Under the eye of such a wise steward, the house is sure to prosper."

65889746-ef55-4fce-b106-b81677343c0d.Text: "I will d-deliver the order at once, Lord Captain."

ba980eee-e808-4727-94bc-85f14be55825.Text: "Lord Captain... we have no such reserves at this moment. Living cargo must first be procured and loaded on board — as soon as that is taken care of, we will be ready to utilise such cargo at your command."

6c2dde20-c939-47a6-a7ca-b17e1af51f2a.Text: {n}Janris thinks for a moment, pursing his lips in concentration.{/n} "I am afraid it is not immediately familiar to me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Please, allow me a moment..." {n}He starts rapidly tapping on the screen of his data-slate.{/n}

d6abc155-855a-4f03-8509-5f644cff4e3c.Text: "Hmm... Hmm! I say, House von Valancius did indeed sign a contract with the owners of a vessel with the designation Fiery Reckoning! There are transactions, records of the ship picking up cargo from Kiava Gamma... Well, this is odd. The data log ends there. Apparently, the ship had some interactions with one of the workshops on your industrial world. I beg your pardon, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but that is the extent of the assistance I can provide you in regard to this particular matter."

92df8c12-4302-4c4f-b8a5-72bbd8d5c7d5.Text: {n}Janris emits a laugh-like gurgle.{/n} "A pompous name, is it not? In truth, they are a gang of pirates who are forever squabbling over loot and territory. However, some of their little flotillas need supplies... or can take awkward cargo off our hands without asking questions. Of course, there is always a risk that these scoundrels will change their mind and attempt to board us instead, but so far our macro-cannons have managed to keep them in line. They say Ryzza Calvaria speaks on the Fellowship's behalf. The Adeptus Amasecus on Footfall is rumoured to be her favourite haunt."

81ba5dae-0d21-453a-9dfb-8b1124658241.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you are truly masterful at springing unexpected questions on a man! However, I must admit I don't quite understand this one..."

7cdb69dc-e7fd-4490-b7a1-5daa293f59bc.Text: "A philosophical question! I imagine it is due to a complicated mix of experience, luck, and most of all, the Emperor's favour."

7335e0b1-4cb7-4347-bca8-670a432866e2.Text: {n}The Factotum fidgets nervously with the rings on his fingers until he musters the courage to reply.{/n} "I will not pry into how Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} found out about my confession. I suppose it raised some questions for you?"

51d612e4-8d65-4fc8-ab6b-8e4dfe2dbc69.Text: "Please! No scheming. Everything is duly accounted for. We have higher-priority expenditure items, which is why the orphans only get the bare necessities." {n}Janris sighs heavily.{/n} "They are clothed and aren't starving, but for some reason I find scant comfort in rational arguments. Personal items, gifts on special occasions, or nutribars for their growing bodies would certainly make the little orphans happier."

eb3853e3-3744-4d98-8c0b-9cb518644f5c.Text: "By all means, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Only substantiated expenses for the good of the dynasty. Would you like to discuss something else?"

1d0c5dc9-9e48-420b-8973-4abca40a9c53.Text: {n}The Factotum's eyes glisten sentimentally.{/n} "The children will know that you are their benefactor! As for me, I can assure you that I will find ways to procure enough funds to cover the expenses!"

4c837641-82a1-4b59-977f-c6b4788daaca.Text: {n}Janris huffs pensively.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} is most courteous... But what exactly did you have in mind?"

1c6273b9-d80c-49d7-bd9c-9ba21c74edf8.Text: "I doubt our Navigator and Master Helmsman would be thrilled. The warp does not forgive frivolity, so order and discipline during translation must be absolute... and Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} should not have any distractions, either!"

a859e968-bbe4-4819-a720-a93072465614.Text: "Oh, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... To be perfectly frank, even I struggle to stay awake at those meetings. Poor Mistress Kibellah would surely not last long amid all the droning and tedium!"

38c9bdb5-5af1-4135-b166-381b01f19487.Text: {n}The crease on Janris's forehead disappears.{/n} "Yes... Yes, quite! What a magnificent idea, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"

97a98b26-d7c9-43ab-a413-9fef0e0efa67.Text: "Oh, but of course! You do not have time to puzzle over such... trivial solutions!"

fdc4840a-02d5-4991-a884-f9553344d9de.Text: {n}Janris adjusts his frock coat and nods enigmatically.{/n} "I will see what can be arranged. And do not worry for a single moment — I promise to find the most suitable approach! I will contact you the moment I have something to offer!"

12962c59-f227-4954-8988-225e64e0fe1b.Text: {n}Janris puts a hand on his chest, right where the gruesome wound used to be.{/n} "The chirurgeons spent hours fighting for my life, and I have to say, they are earning their keep! They promised to leave a heroic-looking scar, although, admittedly, I much prefer calluses from an autoquill."

4de98bd1-bed6-4a64-94c3-cea5458e96cd.Text: "Erebis... The clan name is familiar. If I may ask Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship to give me a little time, the flagship's archives being as vast as they are, I will spare no effort in finding Naaki Erebis as soon as possible."

091b73fd-071e-4371-b72e-eb0cbfa3a2d6.Text: "To profit from them, of course. Most of the things you will find during expeditions are complete junk to one such as yourself, but the less fortunate and affluent servants of the Emperor think them treasures... especially when they are bestowed by the great Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself}! Drusian fanatics and pirate cutthroats, Kasballica dealers and Explorators — none will refuse our help in these dark and trying times. And there may come a time when we shall be the ones requiring aid, and it would be beneficial to have allies willing to provide it."

53ee9dac-38b9-456b-a0c8-cd48abf875a7.Text: {n}The High Factotum pokes a triumphant finger at the data-slate.{/n} "I found them, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! The Erebis family are a lesser voidborn clan. They served in the boarding teams for many generations, spilling blood in the name of the dynasty. In the service of Her Ladyship Theodora, Erebises displayed impeccable heroism on several occasions."

216b6278-aae8-46a7-a40f-5dbc8563ccd1.Text: "Gravity is merciless to the voidborn. But that does not mean they are incapable of adapting to it. Living on the capital world is a reward worth putting in the effort for."

69ecaed3-6fab-4ee9-a559-8b752c7c91ff.Text: "Unfortunately, the clan was all but wiped out two decades ago during a confrontation with enemies of Humanity. For their valour and sacrifice, Lady Theodora granted the surviving members of the clan noble-estate privileges and the right to settle on the capital world."

0cecec07-4b5f-4b24-9ea2-70887215f4eb.Text: "I will send the dynasty's representative on the capital world an instruction to summon the Erebis family to the palace."

43217aa8-9d11-4976-a69c-dd2ff32bf2b0.Text: "The name Naaki appears in reports. At least a dozen different women bore it over several centuries, but there is no data on any living person with that name. The head of the Erebis family will likely have more information about the past two decades of their clan's history on Dargonus."

b30cb2a4-c600-4fdc-a7a9-ca43bb2c19b5.Text: "As am I, to tell the truth. Sensitivity is a vice in one responsible for ensuring the dynasty's prosperity. However, I cannot help it, which is why I unburdened my soul in confession."

da73005d-2f50-43d2-90aa-6e8f1fcac23d.Text: {n}The Factotum bows his head in deference.{/n} "A wise decision, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Two serfs with one shot— That is to say, it is good to know that the children will both learn and be rewarded for their diligence!"

72c8cb7c-b63e-422c-9b61-25b48ee7358e.Text: "You are a truly charitable soul, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}Janris looks away, awkwardly trying to pull the handkercher out of his pocket to wipe his eyes.{/n}

7b115cf6-9f13-4261-bb10-0f4e870e9908.Text: "A decree that is both judicious and firm! The children will be thankful for your sensible care that nurtures the best in them and forestalls idle vices." {n}Janris's eyes are brimming with pure jubilation.{/n}

afbecf8e-d56b-47b4-a84d-173c3ea781e8.Text: "I marvel at your generosity! Will there be any specific instructions, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"

690f00cf-5f44-4dd8-99ef-d9c43801f4b6.Text: {n}The corpulent man in lavish clothes bows before you, not without difficulty. A servo-skull whirrs over his shoulder while the fingers of his augmented hand drum against the sheaf of papers he is holding, and he regards you with attentive interest through the lens of his magnifying implant.{/n} "Greetings, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Janris Danrok, at your service."

9a73dea5-c8db-4c59-98de-7dc65dfff572.Text: "You see, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, it is a tad... broken. While the servitors were busy connecting it to the machine spark, terrifying noises were suddenly heard, followed by a... horrible smell. However, my request to have it repaired so infuriated the Enginseers that I dared not pester them with any further questions. Alas, after a while, the stench became unbearable, and then came the maggots..." {n}The Factotum casts a guilty glance at you and sighs heavily.{/n} "To put it briefly, the Cogicor had to be disposed of. I offer my deepest apologies for failing to preserve that specimen of Thasserian culture."

e614cffa-0854-4758-a0ec-97770224b025.Text: "Lord Captain, I swear on the Golden Throne that your treasury is sacred to me! I take pride in keeping records of any and all transactions, and I am sure that even you will find my scrupulous financial chronicles to be to your satisfaction!" {n}The Factotum speaks with passion and dignity, but {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}your stern gaze{/d} still causes his collar to darken with sweat in a matter of moments.{/n}

cb64e201-957f-40eb-9855-9c81742e0fa9.Text: "And, of course, I ensure that the protectorate's worlds prepare their tithe in a timely fashion. Let none ever say in my lifetime that the dynasty has disgraced itself with a late payment of the sacred tribute!"

3db207c1-3f02-4490-ba39-d9c8a3dc2e34.Text: "You see, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the ship's servitors have been malfunctioning of late. They violate protocols, interrupt their tasks, observe crew members for long periods of time, and move erratically with no meaning or purpose." {n}Janris Danrok nervously pulls on his luxurious frock coat as if it were uncomfortably tight.{/n} "Had it been a routine technical fault, I would have decided the fate of these servitors myself, but I deemed it necessary to notify you. I do not wish to hide such irregularities from the Lord Captain."

4ba1b367-b435-4230-8708-feefb89016e8.Text: "Enough questions for now. I shall return later."

5aed9b83-7a56-4c4b-ace1-514e5fc6c14d.Text: "I shall await your instructions, Lord Captain."

bd2668be-5256-44b7-81da-880bae7de8b0.Text: "Rest assured, there are people of the most outstanding talents among the thousands of your crew. I will contact the overseers at once."

8cdbd99b-a62a-4786-9d8f-c8b71303a9cf.Text: "I wish to bolster my retinue with skilled fighters."

69f7afb8-123d-4747-a116-4d8b1a29e1de.Text: "Certainly, Lord Captain! Travelling through the Immaterium without a Navigator is folly. Alas, we will have to wait for some time before our new guide arrives..."

3f9fa3f0-7438-4de4-89ef-1524af5b1a8e.Text: "Both the crew and my retinue are in need of a Navigator."

6b31328f-f82f-4c69-96a6-ed81bdf8f706.Text: "I would like to replace the painting of the late Theodora in my chambers. Hang my portrait instead."

5c7c3471-3e1b-4f0c-b90b-7787ecbfcc89.Text: "I will show you our sparring chambers at once!"

a239d17a-c56a-4a53-8f4d-116073bfdbbc.Text: "My retinue and I are in need of training."

b6e67a26-050f-46dd-b665-debd4acf0fdf.Text: "I would like to order the shipping and transportation of some goods."

ec3cdb5a-202f-4bd8-b671-1509ccc9d0f0.Text: {n}Janris nods.{/n} "Lady Cassia must have brought the flower from Eurac V with her personal belongings and kept it this whole time. Hardly anyone else aboard this vessel would be powerful enough to acquire such an exotic artefact... Aside from you, of course."

86a6fe60-6ff6-44fa-853d-a9f723cff27e.Text: "I know what gift I should give Cassia."

4f8b4144-20f3-4f0f-bb9b-e1372f784e6b.Text: "I received an unusual gift — a living flower sealed in a crystal dome. Does it mean anything to you?"

6d9618b3-5b70-4e3f-8c5d-3fa30d810717.Text: "I have been given an immortalium, and I need help to arrange a reciprocal gift."

cb555863-f34c-44f4-818f-9f05ccad6bde.Text:
"00001111110000101010100100111 N872-04
The final transactions with the Chartist are complete. The Fiery Reckoning is now fully equipp0001111001000
The object has been loaded aboard with its containment intact and placed in the fore bay to ensure maximum contact with the target.
Coordinates sent and received by the bridg1001101010
target's estimat0011001 time of arrival in the system010101010
the Fiery Reckoning is crewed by a servitor hiv000111110000 chances of the ship returning are minimal.
estimated tim01110111000"

b2d8b57d-e434-475a-84a9-9c6ea0f4b3f1.Text: "...his chagrin is irrelevant. Voigtvir's mistake cost me too much. Years of work, tremendous resources, all wasted. He has failed at what he was supposed to be irreproachable at — uncovering spies, and this one was a senior officer. I am not about to discard him — Kunrad has served me for too long for his removal to go painlessly for the protectorate. Besides, he is no fool. He could not have seriously expected to become the next in the von Valancius line when his skills and talents as Master of Whispers are so valuable. Let his disinheritance serve as a humiliating but instructive lesson from which he may yet learn..."

8f8eaaac-d0c9-468d-93f0-bbbe98d1ec76.Text: {n}The pale wisp of a woman, certainly a voidborn, bows to you fearfully.{/n} "May your name shine through the millennia of your dynasty's glorious history, Lord Captain! I am at your disposal — how can the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_FactotumDead}acting High Factotum{/d} be of service to you?"

a9460361-5845-44a0-ba98-95e5af9dbd42.Text: "Chief Record Warden Meryt Sancvida, temporarily holding the position of the ship's High Factotum since the esteemed Master Danrok's... termination." {n}She gulps, and you notice that she is shaking violently.{/n} "I served as his bookkeeper and am well apprised of the Lord Captain's business dealings. I assure you that all your transactions are being completed without fault or delay — the late Master Danrok's subordinates toil day and night to ensure that they are!"

04762048-4e04-407f-8554-694d80515de1.Text: "You are a voidborn, are you not?"

04a72b3c-d20d-4964-ae2f-9a6f264f6fae.Text: "Thank you for your answers. It was definitely not you."

8f035f52-6648-45a5-bc2c-8f4651cffbbd.Text: "I can see you are not a gregarious sort."

f556b4d0-4d03-48c9-98a8-e710b2374645.Text: "What can you tell me about the other officers?"

c14aef4d-bb19-48fe-af14-796dac5785ea.Text: "Did I mishear you, or are you giving the Rogue Trader cheek? Answer me, void rat!"

4633f59e-8437-4408-b1b9-5d73b592b78b.Text: "On the contrary, you are the first person on the bridge who's not tripping over themselves to lick my boots."

15b11964-c055-471f-a302-417b8a10115c.Text: "Who are these idiots you are in charge of?"

b1d49619-96e7-4fbe-adef-2d8aca0fd976.Text: "Do you control the ship in realspace?"

724b7402-0faa-4d45-989e-4c9acb6cf4b4.Text: "You must have dealings with the Navigator as part of your duties..."

a0a688f2-bd80-42c9-9ca8-fe03d8e89a3e.Text: "Tell me, do you like anyone at all?"

6b6c0176-2a0d-4f27-8a19-7ce71fb6726b.Text: "Ravor, it has come to my attention that a fuel lever on the bridge may be defective. Can you not be trusted to carry out your duties without my personal oversight?"

b6b3401b-7f0d-4d46-8c0d-073e60301457.Text: "Does the word 'Epitaph' mean anything to you? Or, perhaps, 'Incident N872-04' or 'tech-blight'? It all has something to do with Theodora's travels. Rather extraordinary travels at that."

f6b9ed90-0e46-4b53-b9b0-b7c5c470785a.Text: "I used to be an officer in the Imperial Navy, and I can say this with certainty: the best helmsmen come from the voidborn. I am glad to have you at the helm of my ship."

8df825fd-6262-4e7c-90af-e3c7024616e0.Text: "Do you know anything about a ship named the Fiery Reckoning?"

d1215a36-eacb-45ec-af94-480a98f6b481.Text: "I am prepared to discuss Proctor Anthar's actions against your voidsmen."

6919cf88-d38b-4826-a36d-02f85212e8db.Text: {n}The tall man before you appears to be woven from tendons and muscle. Blue veins snake under his white, almost dove-coloured skin, and his scalp and chin are covered in cropped white hair. His neck and shoulders are wrapped in wires that hint at the presence of neural connectors under his uniform. The officer's face seems to be twisted in a perpetual grimace of annoyance and anger, but he greets you with a respectful nod.{/n} "Lord Cap'n! Master Helmsman Ravor, at your service."

eb176b50-377d-44c8-ac5a-a6b3e9484e62.Text: {n}Ravor greets you with a nod.{/n} "To what do I owe the honour, Lord Cap'n?"

b53117a0-498e-44c1-abac-78ddba5daf39.Text: "Through my implants, I feel at one with this ship. And I sense that — and I don't know when it happened exactly — it started behaving differently. Became more responsive. Livelier. Yes, 'livelier' is exactly the word... And when you said 'epitaph' and 'incident' it just dawned on me. Pardon my bungled report, Lord Cap'n, but that's all I've got to say on that front."

81ec5210-a9ab-466b-94d6-cc5c2133c0d9.Text: {n}Ravor stays silent for a few seconds.{/n} "Not much to tell. I gutted everyone I could get to, and then I fled upward, to the middle decks. That's where the augur operators took me under their wing — they have apprentice helmsmen of their own up there, you see. Nobody asked me any questions, so I stayed. I grew up, trained, got smarter. Then ended up a junior helmsman. A dozen years later, Danrok spotted me and lured me away, the cheeky blighter."

757a4e68-5d8d-4b48-a5e6-0d0ad803e95c.Text: {n}Ravor winces and rubs his temple.{/n} "Lord Cap'n, I mean no disrespect... But you'd do better to find someone with a knack for conversation, like Toliman, the new Vox Master. I ain't the talkin' type, I just get the ship where she needs to go. Best let folk stick to what they do best."

ce7cf4b6-130a-46e2-bf09-4d5ca2731f5f.Text: "I'm the Master Helmsman, Lord Cap'n. I stand at the wheel of this here tub... I mean, your vessel, and bark commands at the idiots who tend to its related systems. In layman's terms, I'm the one who stops us from running into an asteroid or a disruptive gravitational wave when we're travelling through the void."

38e0b0cc-45b4-4de0-a964-42dc92c2af28.Text: "Lord Cap'n." {n}Ravor acknowledges you with a nod and turns away.{/n}

184af317-572d-4169-b4f6-05462c908860.Text: "That I am. Born into a helmsman clan in the bowels of a Chartist vessel. Studied the family trade until I was fifteen, then my entire clan was butchered in a mutiny by lower hold scum. They spared the young 'uns — of course they did, kids with implanted connectors make great navigational servitors. But I was having none of it — they weren't going to make a servitor out of me — so I escaped into the crawlways. And then I spent months picking them off, one after the other—" {n}Ravor stops abruptly.{/n} "You got me talking up a storm. Anyway, yes, I'm a voidborn."

eaaf6c0e-f678-48a6-8820-adf755105461.Text: {n}Ravor's eye twitches, which makes the grimace on his face even uglier.{/n} "'Ave... 'Ave I done something to displease the Lord Cap'n?"

1b4f2fa7-a4e9-4e9c-b938-9e6547602e41.Text: {n}When you shout, Ravor winces as if the sound physically hurts.{/n} "Beg your pardon, beg your pardon, Lord Cap'n... I do apologise! But the blame for my ugly mug and foul temper can't be laid at my door only."

8c6aa212-dac8-4ff8-a820-25511419dcca.Text: "Good-for-nothing wasters, that's what they are. Each and every one. Take Janris Danrok, that highborn weasel. He fawns over the officers, but some of the deals he makes would get him burned alive. He drags other people into his schemes so they can take the fall for him, too. One of my junior helmsmen was ferrying goods from Footfall for him, got caught by the Seneschal, and ended up in the void hatch. Danrok couldn't care less!"

e45ae7e2-3709-4ccf-a66d-a8531dc8b9f3.Text: "The Vox Master — another Toliman like the last one, void rest him — is no better. She cut off half the vox-channels the day she took up her post. Said the vox-systems were damaged and the enginarium had no contact with other modules... But how am I supposed to steer the ship? Collect the cogs' reports with the power of my mind?"

93245b68-cbc3-4eb9-a1b5-5b940842d23c.Text: "First Officer Werserian... I can't stand him. Like every Navy officer I ever met, he doesn't know a thing about controlling a vessel in the void, but he puffs himself up all the same and throws his weight around. Me and him had to have words a few times before he left me alone. Thank the Emperor Lady Theodora trusted me more than the Seneschal when it came to helming a voidship!"

837699eb-72b4-4860-b3cd-68bd7bee9601.Text: "Then there's that woman, what's her name? Tlass? Lady Theodora brought her along wherever she went, and look what happened to her? I wouldn't be surprised if it turns out it was that witch that delivered her to an early grave, just like countless souls before. I don't see why anyone would want that walking calamity on their ship, but some would disagree... They say she's friends with young Toliman, you know. Or at least, she used to be."

49eebc25-61df-4dd8-94b6-1aa85b55138d.Text: {n}Ravor looks perplexed.{/n} "What kind of a question is that? I like you. And Lady Theodora before you. Where would I be if I was making cracks about the Rogue Trader? Hah, I don't want to die just yet."

8e3c62e2-0eb7-42b9-a390-f2c782a6f362.Text: {n}Ravor gives you a careful look and scoffs.{/n} "Right you are. It's not hard to see that I'm in a foul mood. I'm not the only one to blame for it, you know."

1bfee5e6-ebfb-4b15-9803-1436722a5995.Text: {n}The Helmsman's perpetually twisted mouth twitches as if he's trying to smile. It looks sinister rather than friendly.{/n} "Oh yeah? Well, I'm pleasantly surprised myself that you aren't having me flogged for insubordination. Will wonders never cease?"

78a762e5-9ea3-45ca-9047-e76f30541870.Text: {n}Ravor points at the cables around himself.{/n} "Connecting wires. Once they go into the control panel, I become one with the ship. Except the bloody cogs messed up the wires' stimulus injectors and connectors when they implanted them — they twisted the wires the wrong way or burned something in my noggin. Anyway, I can't sleep. It just doesn't happen anymore. It's been thirty years of non-stop stimulants and a splitting headache. So you'll forgive me if I'm not all smiles, Lord Cap'n."

242ff6ab-5e30-438b-8591-b3962a48e107.Text: "I wish that was my only job. I have to steer her through the warp too, but most of the credit for that goes to the Navigator. The warp's a nightmare, always tossing up something new — all my years at the helm, they count for nothing in there. My part's small enough — I just monitor our systems, follow the charted route, and I don't kick up a fuss when new orders come in from the Navigator's Sanctum."

c7584a75-b360-4c40-90b3-00026dc326a8.Text: "There are too many to list them all. Tech-Priests from the enginarium, voidsmen from the augur decks, the work-shy fools on the bridge. I'd have every last one of them flogged! They all need a wake-up call. They need to be whipped into shape or else this ship'll be going nowhere. Or even worse, it'll go somewhere we don't want it to."

1fe0bd39-4b74-4034-bf74-d3d73fd1f9a8.Text: "{g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}Realspace{/g} — now that's where I keep my eyes peeled. Gravitational anomalies, void currents, hard radiation — that kind of shit shows up everywhere. Thank the Emperor, the augurs on this vessel are holding up, and so far we've been able to spot if something bad's coming our way."

a6b4c6fa-61e1-4d93-9252-c4c009bf111d.Text: {n}Ravor stares at you before blurting out,{/n} "Dammit, Lord Cap'n... To tell the truth, I've been asking myself... where'd the Lord Cap'n fish this Orsellio girl out of? Now, it's not like I've met many Navigators, but this one... I don't feel safe with that little princess pulling our voidship through the warp. She's done a decent job so far, though, so I guess she's managing."

4ffc7ddb-ac55-4330-853c-073991ae53ae.Text: "Ain't got a better one, Lord Cap'n."

6c48a6c6-fddd-4f75-8eb6-0d21022fa0dd.Text: "I'll be blasted if I understand a thing, but I'm here to serve. Something else you'd like to discuss?"

82c6c898-013c-431a-a87d-6a7cf0ef4901.Text: {n}The officer's furrowed eyebrows draw even closer together. He speaks slowly, carefully picking his words:{/n} "I most definitely can, Lord Cap'n. The technomats will inspect the equipment immediately. I will also deal with those in charge without delay."

ebb9c0f7-93f3-4915-a96a-f939c49cca58.Text: "Can't say they do, Lord Cap'n. Doesn't ring any bells. Then again, remembering all the places Lady Theodora went is..." {n}His brow furrows.{/n} "Epitaph, incident... We've always had heaps of incidents happening on board, but..."

b850f40c-97f6-4c6e-a2c2-89883aaed271.Text: {n}Ravor freezes, tensely staring you in the eye and clearly trying to discern if your words are meant as mockery. After a moment's pause, a muscle in his face twitches, then another. His cheeks spasm, his mouth twists... and you realise that Ravor is unsuccessfully trying to remember how to smile.{/n} "Th-thank you, Lord Cap'n. I won't let you down."

162dad1f-2734-4f35-928c-77382e2829b0.Text: {n}Ravor winces as if in pain.{/n} "I've heard the name, that much I'm sure of... but I can't recall the details. Ha... I wonder if it was part of that operation that the late Mort was put in charge of. If it was, then there's nothing I can tell you, Lord Cap'n. The whole thing was kept under wraps. Your best chance would be to ask the High Factotum — maybe some of his treasury records have mentions of this 'Fiery Reckoning.'"

8d70b794-1349-4bdf-add1-8f21cf42fb9a.Text: "No. I'm up to my connectors in work as it is."

fe585391-0ede-4a74-95c2-38f4e4435765.Text: {n}The helmsman scratches the back of his head thoughtfully.{/n} "Damned if I know, Lord Captain. If you ask me, our orphans have it worlds better than they would on other ships."

e2b840c9-5edf-4a32-8523-3e0b285ade4a.Text: "Those some weren't trying hard enough or listening to their higher-ups, is all. Or has someone you know died on you and I'm supposed to offer my sympathies?" {n}Ravor grunts and looks away.{/n} "Odd choice of person to come to with something like that, Lord Captain."

cf05081c-0476-4879-bb30-07627bc5b384.Text: Deployment of the Lord Captain's personal guard on landing shuttles

a72d3816-b7fe-4cef-bece-8f5d64a007c5.Text: Universal surveillance by Master van Calox's network of agents

42ba08d7-3dba-4a89-944a-02f15dfd271d.Text: Adeptus Mechanicus sweep thanks to Magos Haneumann's contacts

2481c899-2aa5-464c-91e1-137c73691fbb.Text: Sanctioned psyker divination led by Mistress Tlass

309bd5d3-213d-4669-8623-a0674aba1cb6.Text: Guerrilla attacks planned by Master Werserian

49c543f0-254b-4a84-bec9-09a02feae166.Text: Planting agents using Mistress Heydari's connections

7f10978e-43d4-46da-8222-2d632f3e0f1f.Text: Large-scale attack by militia troops inspired by Sister Argenta

13fba3bc-10a3-4fea-b613-5fc5a49b40ff.Text: Held planet-wide prayer services during the operation on Janus.

a590ef91-339f-42c5-b717-ab2d8e0e1ddb.Text: The Lord Captain's seizure of the rebels' communication systems gave {mf|his|her} loyal servants a significant advantage.

3cece437-986f-47a3-b2d7-f86c7d62eaa0.Text:
Region: Cinerus Maleficum
Location: Telikos Epsilon
Material: Internal procedural report
Recorded by: Vigdis Surri Otta Toliman, Vox Master Octavus

d22a30d0-a241-4207-9b9c-aed1a6b1fbdb.Text: Report on the operation to ruthlessly eradicate the underground traitors to the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} on the {g|Encyclopedia:AgriWorld}agri-world{/g} Janus

c6845ffb-860f-4433-bbfb-d7846c0ab106.Text: By His grace, the leadership and general command of the operation were taken by {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} {name} of the glorious House of von Valancius.

8a683265-c4b2-49fb-90b3-15f5f8b7e322.Text: The brutal punitive raids, searches, and public punishments carried out by Governor Vyatt's people failed to have a beneficial effect, instead only embittering Janus's population still further.

6e8fbc90-504f-44f8-8870-4fe13a76d920.Text: The Lord Captain's personal enforcer guard was better trained and capable of landing in the jungle on boarding shuttles, although deploying it in combat operations posed the risk of losses to the ship's crew.

286eaded-a036-4bcb-849f-2248bb5d8e2c.Text: Beyond the undoubted competence of the blessed Lord Captain, there was another reason for this decision, namely, evidence of disloyalty within the estimable Governor Vyatt's retinue.

892955aa-2645-443d-b9fb-51852c9c21d4.Text: The esteemed Sister Argenta suggested enlisting the broad masses of the planet's loyal population to aid in the fight. Spurred on by righteous anger, militia could carry out sweeps of the jungles on a scale that would be impossible for the more limited armed forces.

1076f786-5c60-47d9-9040-c7897b7ba4f7.Text: Subversive activity by the enemies of Humanity was detected on the planet Janus. Their insidious propaganda led to dissipation among the Imperium's subjects, as a result of which the peasants sympathised with the rebellious sentiments.

1fcd9d1b-f669-42f9-ba9e-cf557c9952e8.Text: By permitting unrest to take root in her dominion, Governor Vistenza Vyatt discredited herself. In light of this, the crude methods she used to repress the rebellion were called into question, as was her staff.

ea659699-7c5c-4794-b191-1413d6c9860f.Text: The might and authority of the noble Lord Captain, however, were able to facilitate an end to the conflict, though this entailed the use of the Rogue Trader's personal resources.

cf5b5b31-4078-4f50-982d-3855eef4c7ca.Text: The future well-being of Janus was dependent on the success of each stage of the operation. A single misstep could have undermined the security of this valuable colony and, consequently, dealt a blow to the prosperity of the protectorate of House von Valancius.

d3b8d851-f268-4275-9d6b-4f2f977bfbe3.Text: The first step in the struggle against the insurrectionists was to drive their cells out of the capital and major cities. The Emperor-Blessed Lord Captain considered several suppression strategies before choosing the best option.

13d72ef6-13e5-46f8-8f50-0c6f0361016e.Text: Thanks to data gathered by a retainer of the esteemed Governor Vyatt and analysed by the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself}, the rebels' attack plans were exposed, creating the opportunity to devise a counterstrategy.

b7f0bbab-95e5-414b-a13f-c39adac7ebe6.Text: The main rebel forces were in hiding in remote, uncultivated locations, but a substantial rebel network was exposed across major cities as well. Vistenza Vyatt's associates pressed for punitive raids, while the Lord Captain's advisors suggested rolling out a planet-wide propaganda campaign to urge citizens to expose the traitors in their ranks and report them to the authorities. The latter approach, however, would require the use of the Lord Captain's personal funds in a show of {mf|his|her} largesse and patronage.

9278343e-1799-4a1b-912b-d233dbc42147.Text: The esteemed Heinrix van Calox proposed the use of the spy network at his disposal to implement universal surveillance of the planet's population.

9a33a063-8b7d-48b6-b20e-1dfbbd97c2d4.Text: Intelligence revealed that the rebels were collaborating with the planet's criminal underworld. The esteemed Jae Heydari suggested contacting her links in unsavoury smuggler circles with the aim of planting agents in the rebels' underground network.

1100a47f-fa34-4f40-ae2d-9687d42a6d4a.Text: Inspired by the stirring exhortations of preachers, tens of thousands of Janusians armed themselves and descended upon the jungle like a raging storm. With little regard for their heavy losses, the militia wiped out most of the rebels, and the remnants were driven out to the island regions that were no longer economically valuable.

25373bf6-7ac6-459f-a077-f0982c45da98.Text: Inspired by the blistering speeches of preachers, tens of thousands of Janusians armed themselves and descended upon the jungle like a raging storm. Alas, under fire from the rebels and incurring heavy losses, the militia's fervour quickly dwindled. Demoralised, they turned tail and fled, which only increased the death count.

1cd203a6-cba0-4bdc-918e-6944ed4c12c6.Text: The rebels' main forces were scattered throughout the planet's wild jungle areas. The Lord Captain was offered several strategies for dealing with them.

0984926b-8539-4563-88a9-43c51f0c1b6c.Text: Based on the data supplied by the esteemed Governor Vyatt's secretary, the blessed Lord Captain compiled an outline of the rebels' future attacks in cities.

2f25c0ea-f220-4280-af4d-d321bcda1bbb.Text: This outline was the basis for a series of arrests and raids that forced the insurrectionists to abandon the cities and fall back to the planet's hinterland.

bd83d042-5dfc-4d4c-bdbd-eaae5b6d768e.Text: Unfortunately, after the first round of arrests and raids, the rebels quickly adapted and altered their strategy.

aaf008e9-3452-464a-a6e7-20e4565be029.Text: Since the rebels' ranks were swelling by the day, the ruthless decision was made to hold public executions. Many of Janus's inhabitants were immediately put to death, while the rest were caught in the grip of such terror that a righteous hunt for traitors and heretics broke out across the planet. In addition to the many innocents unjustly killed, the core of the urban rebel underground was destroyed, forcing the insurrectionists to abandon the major cities.

74cb0735-5c7e-4af5-b1d1-0a2fbe2fd927.Text: Although the planetary garrison was less well trained than the rebels, thanks to the blessed Lord Captain, who took personal command of the operation, the governor's troops were victorious. The main rebel forces were pushed out of agricultural production areas into island regions of no economic value.

b850e0be-0000-4576-bb24-e631d5452f24.Text: Alas, the planetary garrison was so poorly trained that even the blessed Lord Captain's personal command of the mission was not enough to make it a success. The soldiers perished in droves, unable to orient themselves in the undergrowth or even determine where they were taking fire from.

7fd61b54-9781-426b-8a1f-6e91c8b29d23.Text: The boarding parties from the blessed Lord Captain's crew descended upon the heads of the rebels in their landing shuttles. Thanks to the deft manoeuvring of the pilots, this blistering attack scattered the rebel forces, cutting off their paths of retreat and leaving them in total disarray. Isolated and demoralised groups of rebels were picked off over several days. The surviving insurrectionists retreated to island regions of little significance. Crew losses were regrettable but minor.

f352a05d-a947-4a63-ac1b-e86e8ed92bdc.Text: The boarding parties from the blessed Lord Captain's crew descended upon the heads of the rebels in their landing shuttles. Unfortunately, some pilots were less skilled than others and some of the boarding parties landed in the wrong place, or arrived late on the planet's surface. The exercise, which had been planned as a swift and decisive strike against isolated groups of rebels, turned into a deadly trap for the esteemed Lord Captain's enforcers. Caught in pockets of fire, they assumed a circular defensive formation and sustained heavy losses.

9b075ae4-7c5c-47be-a4d4-7797bc0162a8.Text: The soldiers of the planetary garrison were trained by the esteemed Abelard Werserian and quickly absorbed the knowledge of the ungodly heretics. Borrowing their tactics, the soldiers moved through the jungle in small groups, staying hidden and dealing sudden strikes. Now stripped of their main tactical advantage, those rebels who were not wiped out retreated to island regions of little significance.

72685fd9-4ff9-4546-a261-c093a0ad8db9.Text: Alas, the brief training course arranged by the esteemed Abelard Werserian for the garrison made no difference. Governor Vyatt's feckless soldiers were no match for the rebels. The guerrilla attacks were a failure and the losses mounted with every passing day.

26ab6b1f-da13-490a-9948-ed07691f59c0.Text: Phase 3 of 3: Destroying the training camps

01af7d40-b41e-4589-ad79-d51fa8e7438d.Text: After retreating, the rebels took up the defence of their training camps, which were hidden deep in the forests of the archipelago. The blessed Lord Captain reviewed several approaches for rooting out these nests of sedition and chose the most promising one.

e8cddefc-c2ab-49a5-9607-ec76324e1204.Text: Thanks to evidence gathered earlier, the Lord Captain was in possession of information from {g|Encyclopedia:Lexmechanic}Lexmechanic{/g} Vinzelex which simplified the task.

0b58410d-79a6-4b59-ad56-c88fc8cd8f39.Text: The rebels' training camps were located in the densely forested but insignificant island regions. Moreover, scouting reports indicated that the instigators of the uprising were also hiding there — {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g}, the enemies of Humanity. Governor Vyatt suggested burning the worthless forests to the ground so the rebels could no longer hide, however, there were serious doubts about the competence of the officers she selected for the task. Locating the camps using the blessed Lord Captain's ship's technical equipment was a real challenge possible only for a highly sensitive and powerful augur.

2aa5cb98-2dc3-4c14-9121-1470e820255f.Text: The esteemed Magos Haneumann pointed out that a large number of sacred mechanisms for monitoring seismic activity were present on the islands. He proposed that members of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} who served such machines could contribute to intelligence gathering.

1395c4d9-c72b-40bc-ba55-d6d00960e040.Text: The esteemed Idira Tlass put forth a suggestion of using psyker divination to try to discover the traitors' camp.

c90fa592-3806-4c05-be48-61c416c292f5.Text: The berries found by the Lord Captain among the rebels' belongings only grow in certain regions of the planet where the soil has a unique mineral composition.

734fc502-139e-4dd0-a292-1946c1a79337.Text: After sending scouts to that area, the Lord Captain quickly discovered the rebels' hideout. Sensing that the end was near, the rebels gathered in their camps and prepared to take a final stand.

9c7184bf-0b9e-46f6-8460-d924644511ae.Text: Unfortunately, the scouts sent to that area by the Lord Captain failed to locate the rebels' hideout — they could not penetrate the advanced camouflage provided to the rebels by their ungodly backers, the xenos.

f12b513c-62e0-4e56-9102-4055d2fe05e0.Text: The rebels' camps were nevertheless located and surrounded, but the setback earlier in the operation had given the fighters a chance to prepare and strike their final blow, carrying out a series of terrorist attacks on the planet's vital security sites. It was a desperate act of senseless malice.

26faeda4-a6ba-4313-bc2e-98d31804bf37.Text: Armed with flamers, the soldiers of the planetary garrison began methodically burning the island forests. With no cover left to conceal them, the rebels gathered in their camps and manned the defences, sensing their imminent death.

04b2204f-cb97-4970-a1b6-635334eda3ae.Text: Unfortunately, few of the planetary garrison soldiers were skilled enough to wield these powerful tools of destruction without any adverse consequences. Numerous incidents related to the combustion of {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g} tanks, made torching the forests a slower and more difficult process.

4915d35a-4518-485b-a2fc-7d2426a37093.Text: The ship's all-seeing augurs fixed their unblinking eye on the island forests, quickly flagging points where suspicious activity was detected. The rebels' camps were found, and within them the insurrectionists were taking one last, desperate stand.

f86cc0a6-fe2c-4d0a-a0b5-bcb9aec0ce1f.Text: Unfortunately, even the all-seeing eye of the ship's augurs failed to quickly locate the rebels' camps in the island forests. The scant information supplied by the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} only coalesced into a clear picture when it was too late.

76c7f82d-9002-4b9c-8523-62a222507dcc.Text: The wise ones of the Adeptus Mechanicus appealed to the sacred machines of geological monitoring with prayerful enquiries. After analysing the blessed rhythms of seismic activity, they gave the Lord Captain a report with the supposed coordinates of the rebels' camps. The rebels were locked inside their lairs, preparing to take one last, desperate stand.

c05729f7-b0b7-49fe-a5a6-94432f0eb1c0.Text: The wise ones of the Adeptus Mechanicus appealed to the sacred machines of geological monitoring with prayerful enquiries, but then they fell into a gruelling debate about whether it was permissible to reveal the blessed rhythms of seismic activity to laypersons. The debate was never-ending and delayed the conclusion of the operation.

9df99cfc-68c2-4f18-9022-c60cc5c8a542.Text: The psyker divination revealed the precise location of the traitors to the Imperium. Following the scent of their profane thoughts, the soldiers of the planetary garrison tracked down the rebels' bases and blockaded them.

e47e6331-119b-4c6d-a8e1-6d4feabef01d.Text: The attempt at psyker divination proved unsuccessful — all that came of it were confused and contradictory predictions and strange, tall shadows hiding among the trees of Janus, anointing the planet's core with their tears. The conclusion of the operation was delayed as a result.

9c8bd781-98f9-4ad9-97c8-a5ac62484e03.Text: As a result of the actions of the forces loyal to the Imperium, the rebels were driven into isolated regions, where their camps were then discovered and blockaded.

aa085c6c-c666-4a01-84c6-5b565ff1b5cc.Text: The harsh reprisals carried out by the Lord Captain's servants in the struggle against the rebel underground considerably reduced the population of Janus and diminished its value as a colony.

bc73714d-ded7-4504-b274-32333914801f.Text: When the rebels were being driven out of the jungles, targeted orbital strikes were carried out that damaged the agricultural infrastructure of the agri-world and impaired the planet's production capacity.

cfb5a608-480b-4c71-b514-fb856f3ca471.Text: The planet's defence complexes were damaged in the course of the rebels' terrorist acts, which negatively affected its security.

53914155-7e7b-469e-bdc8-00311d7eb4dd.Text: The operation to combat the xenos-incited traitors to Humanity was a success. The wisdom and will of our illustrious Lord Captain made possible the ultimate eradication of that ungodly movement, and that process was personally overseen by the Rogue Trader — the sovereign of Janus and agent of His will.

8bbeb79f-6244-4cac-b11b-02ac1541ff12.Text: On the Lord Captain's orders, thrice-daily planet-wide prayer services were held, in which the population of Janus prayed for the deliverance of His land from the clutches of the enemies of Humanity. The rituals and litanies had an effect on the agri-world's inhabitants — reports soon began to arrive that the members of the underground had lost the support of the peasantry and had been forced to abandon the world's major settlements.

5e1ea764-ed0d-4f44-8c85-0e79b62249fb.Text: The campaign organised by the esteemed Lord Captain's people took effect. {mf|His|Her} address to {mf|his|her} subjects was broadcast by {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-systems throughout the colony, while workers in towns were granted a shift off work and given provisions, {g|Encyclopedia:Recaf}recaf{/g}, and personal fuel cells. Moved by the Lord Captain's kindness, the colony inhabitants rushed to the recently established confessional centres. The rebel underground was forced to hastily retreat from the major cities.

561ebe9f-5146-4311-8739-158d7afb68dd.Text: The campaign organised by the esteemed Lord Captain's people did not produce the expected result. The dissolute and brutish subjects of Janus did not respond with gratitude to the Lord Captain's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-address, which was broadcast throughout the colony, or to the distribution of provisions and {g|Encyclopedia:Recaf}recaf{/g}. Instead of accepting the Lord Captain's gifts with thanks, the people began to mutter that the authorities were trying to buy them off with surplus rations packs.

1c4fdfe8-2285-4cbc-bb3d-ff33c4317944.Text: With the support of resources from Governor Vyatt, the spy network of the esteemed Heinrix van Calox quickly established surveillance in the planet's major cities. No one escaped the attention of this unblinking eye, and the underground rebels were forced to retreat to more remote locations after the first wave of arrests.

5f541ee7-940d-4f35-bd65-98656aa0f72e.Text: Alas, the spy network of the esteemed Heinrix van Calox failed to capture all of the colony's subjects in its surveillance net. Its success was hampered by sabotage efforts by the rebels and the incompetence of Governor Vyatt's forces, who were assisting the operation. Agents on the ground were killed, surveillance reports went missing, and tracking devices were tampered with.

1ef48575-fc40-49ab-9f0f-95b34460b7a7.Text: The Lord Captain's agents managed to infiltrate the rebel underground via networks of contemptible thieves and smugglers and identify the main leaders. After the wave of arrests, the remaining rebels fled the major cities.

11c710ae-b783-4e4f-ab51-38a90a750e57.Text: Unfortunately, the operation to plant agents in the rebel underground via the planet's criminal circles was a failure. All the spies were executed en masse by the paranoid insurrectionists, and this minor victory only served to raise their morale and harden their resolve.

af2fcd61-7372-4f61-8fe3-7a8e6681cca8.Text: To ensure that the defeat in the jungle did not descend into a military catastrophe, the ever wise Lord Captain gave the timely order for the targeted orbital bombardment of the planet. The merciless strikes vaporised the rebel clusters, forcing them to retreat to island regions of no economic value. Alas, the colony's agricultural infrastructure and facilities also fell victim to the bombing.

ab2a1cfd-3033-44eb-9fde-c3751bd16856.Text: During the operations on the planet, the suspicions of the blessed Lord Captain and {mf|his|her} companions were confirmed: the rebels were being manipulated by even more terrible enemies of Humanity. Creatures identified as filthy {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} — Aeldari, to be precise — were seen fighting alongside the peasants. Vistenza Vyatt's so-called aide, who had claimed to be a mutant, was not the only one of her kind on Janus: scouts confirmed the presence of other members of this race on the agri-world.

ddefb451-7cb4-4356-9ff1-82bf4353bd77.Text: The faithful servants of the esteemed Governor Vyatt assured the Lord Captain of their complete and unquestioning devotion and readiness to serve {mf|him|her} to the best of their ability.

20378d4e-af94-4c24-a892-dd7b44d70f8a.Text: In choosing a strategy, the Lord Captain had to consider the limited trustworthiness of the world's population, which was uncovered by the ship's medics deployed on the planet to support the offensive. Their reports indicated widespread genetic anomalies in the colony's inhabitants for which there was no logical explanation.

2159c685-5af6-44f2-8d39-7839584902c0.Text: Using the rebels' transmitter captured by the Lord Captain, the officers of the planetary garrison engaged in an elaborate {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-game, interfering in the rebels' discussions, spreading disinformation, and sowing paranoia within their ranks.

b4e13dc1-1f3c-4bb7-b944-e242846478c1.Text: This cunning strategy allowed the wardens to quickly push the enemy out of the agricultural production areas into island regions of no economic value.

1de1233d-0821-4c2b-b95d-ffd7e326974e.Text: Unfortunately, the traitors to Humanity quickly realised the deception and changed their vox-frequency, stalling the large-scale jungle offensive.

db9c5a8d-93ce-401e-9255-96502e718354.Text: The voidship's medics who landed on the planet to support the offensive were prepared to render first aid to the wounded.

a7b8a5ef-1789-45c4-8207-25455408b842.Text: Strikes thundered down upon Janus with almighty force, hitting the island forests and turning the ancient wilds to ash. The terrified rebels fled for their camps, where they manned the defences, anticipating their imminent death.

9e6f941b-3809-4a1c-972a-ccd385fbecb1.Text: As expected, the brutal punitive raids, searches, and public punishments struck terror into the population and spurred them to unmask the traitors within their ranks. The rebel underground was quickly driven from the major cities.

7eedbd73-48db-4a5f-b0d5-37ca2042429e.Text: The main rebel forces were hiding in the jungles that blanketed Janus. These sparsely populated regions were home to the colony's key agricultural facilities, which the fighters used as cover for their actions, allowing them to carry out incursions. Governor Vyatt's wardens lacked the training and skills to operate in such conditions.

cebad6d9-fdb0-44d2-9d68-ab4de66bde4e.Text: In addition to this, the ship's medics' reports revealed a broad spectrum of genetic abnormalities among the governor's wardens, and among Janus's peasant population. Active sources of radiation or biological xenothreats were deemed unlikely, but the influence of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Ruinous Powers{/g} on the bodies and souls of the planet's inhabitants could not be discounted. Given this information, it would have been unwise and dangerous to place any trust in the locals.

a9d36e3b-7fdf-4d96-9551-84fa4955a458.Text: The esteemed Abelard Werserian proposed using the rebels' own weapons against them. Their strength lay in the covert guerrilla tactics of their attacks. The esteemed Abelard expressed his conviction that he could teach the basics of these tactics to the soldiers of the planetary garrison, eliminating the rebels' advantage.

6f94a77c-22c4-4380-b8f1-5bf726842bd6.Text: "When was the last time you saw Kav?"

deedd894-9560-4049-9465-200c98a59730.Text: "That night was the last time. Right after he went outside the perimeter, he was gone. Ran into some piece of shit in the dark, I bet."

6dae6d7d-75ef-4353-8c29-6311a9c033db.Text: "They say things used to be quieter around here. Nowadays it's all beast attacks and poisonings from local grub..."

588a5234-89d8-4be7-aa46-67516de3a2cd.Text: "Be glad you're here and not in one of the isolated settlements. My uncle ran away from one... he told me things that made my hair stand on end."

d815ed83-ef3b-4e54-8cd6-2f1af136ae0f.Text: "Y'know, I keep looking at it, but I still have no idea what it's made of."

5b90dfd1-ced4-4086-8f01-bb4e397dc0de.Text: "Looks like some kind of bone. 'Cept I can't even imagine a living thing that size, let alone believe it exists."

7d32f900-18fb-4768-9018-df598bd9948c.Text: "Figure we could try sawing it open? What if there's something real valuable inside..."

7458e199-6fb9-4b35-bd69-de038d0260f2.Text: "Don't. I saw what our 'friends' did to the idiot who thought it'd be a good idea to piss on one of these stone faces. You don't want to be that guy."

340f3716-928b-4cec-845f-62de118b98f8.Text: "Hold on, brothers! I'll call for backup!"

6a118f63-aee4-43bd-9cab-f0b3cf99115d.Text: The plant's outer tissue has stretched and cracked from the swollen pulp underneath. Murky ichor oozes from the long tears.

df6a942c-6192-4de6-832d-746155b6196a.Text: This plant, once a harmless shrub, has now completely changed. Its outer tissue has cracked from the juices swelling in its pulp and now oozing down the leaves in murky rivulets. The mutation looks like the result of some powerful sorcery.

295421a8-470b-4a68-be6b-719dcb0ca3d3.Text: The plant is covered in pulsating purple spots that appear to be indications of some unknown disease.

aa0b2830-3130-433c-9378-e1a16f9b6ce5.Text: The plant is covered in pulsating purple spots. Young shoots are already covered in similar marks — clearly a sign of mutation, not a disease.

79a00003-63a1-46a9-969e-11e21b61539c.Text: The floor of the bunker is littered with sleeping bags, backpacks, and the rebels' meagre belongings — clothes smeared with blood, primitive data-slates, half-eaten nutribars.

b74893e5-0258-40c7-b9e8-83edced652db.Text: In the dimness under the canopy, you notice the outlines of machines — portable generators that provide power to the camp. Some of the machines have fallen into disuse, and it would be impossible to make sense of the cables and wires strewn about the floor without the help of a Tech-Priest.

2e00ff69-eb57-4aa6-839a-dd273886088a.Text: This vox-tower was assembled from parts clearly not intended for such a use. Among the support beams and plasteel sheets, you see arches from containers and fasteners from agri cisterns.

ce06c9da-9741-4a0f-afb7-d631f569a8fb.Text: "The heretics and xenos will get what they deserve... right?"

f86c752c-f5ff-433b-9f4d-4ba7bfb8b3fc.Text: The pad is speckled with black tracks and scratches. Judging by the evidence of landings and takeoffs, flying machines land here on a regular basis — it could be one of the local types of shuttles.

85d8ba3a-f240-48d2-9d54-b317fa947a79.Text: This giant ravenous creature is covered in spikes and bone growths.

08a832b0-8a24-4f85-ac22-c120457ff720.Text: A giant ravenous creature whose hide is pierced with spikes and spines. The skin around the growths is inflamed, as if the protuberances have appeared recently, causing the creature pain.

fe22e5dd-b784-44fe-a123-88370dcd991a.Text: In the back of the corpse's head, there is a strange, narrow hole that does not look like it came from any conventional Imperial weapon. A hole like that could have been left by a thin blade piercing the skull.

bd7cbecd-3cb5-459c-aacc-d7ab65bfd866.Text: The mutilated body is covered in deep lacerations.

397df3c9-ef4c-42ac-8608-244a47ab9f1b.Text: This poor sap was clearly mauled by a large predator, but you don't see any signs that the creature gorged itself on his flesh afterward — it appears the beast did not kill this man out of hunger.

d54d10f6-795d-4de9-96c8-ffb79a1b71d1.Text: The remains of an ancient structure are visible under the green canopy.

91518e81-3922-46b1-a9ee-3baed0d11c54.Text: The xenoruins visible from under the green canopy look remarkably intact. It seems time and the elements have no power over this bright material.

0728e449-1ef1-4f3f-813a-25c921e19c97.Text: The weathered runes are completely illegible.

986faba5-8ad8-467c-84d2-8cee90424616.Text: The runes form the lines of an ancient xenos poem that tells of the creation of a "Lilaethan" — of turning a lifeless dead world into a blooming garden.

5c8281e6-0eed-495b-81eb-674567cbfce6.Text: This massive statue, knocked over by an unknown force sometime in the distant past, has almost disappeared under the green canopy of the jungle.

5be7ac2e-7aed-4600-baad-5adbc34a603c.Text: The massive statue depicts one of the gods of the Aeldari — an ancient xenos race that once inhabited vast regions of the galaxy.

69e041f7-d1e1-4bc5-8e23-1a459a0a2f66.Text: The air around the stone palm dotted with ancient runes is thick with the smell of ozone.

40e42650-ff0e-4350-9106-3e6830f55397.Text: The giant stone hand covered in ancient runes clearly radiates with warp energy — faint, but strong enough to make the skin on your face tingle.

96c0ab4b-e005-4d44-8cc4-063dec3413be.Text: "Laurina Annarus's estate will be liquidated any day now. I've got my eye on that far-flung country manor of theirs..."

d00d323b-00b3-4c18-982f-0321e680d829.Text: "Don't you think Lady Vyatt will keep the choicest morsels for herself? Truly, the Annarus holdings could turn even our governor green with envy..."

70b44961-c113-43ed-ba7d-841489d5fca3.Text: "Hmpf! It seems to me Lady Vyatt is only interested in settlements that are overrun with peasants. One can only guess as to the reason..."

d052860d-20b7-480f-aad6-a312d078d1bf.Text: "Dearest, hold your tongue! You have an audience!"

47fccd48-79f3-4bf0-b973-402f68cf2f0f.Text: "Did you hear? Avexin Goldino caught her husband with the servitors again!"

d8f5fdd9-5c92-4880-8217-314f44241589.Text: "Your surprise sounds terribly feigned. Are you truly surprised to learn that the head of the Goldino family is seeking solace in such predictable places?"

17082def-e0da-4f00-8fd9-3593706b030a.Text: "Quite the opposite — I am appalled the old man hasn't come up with something more original since the incident at their last soiree!"

0c9ea3ac-79ff-4cf7-b2ff-caad0ba286a4.Text: "To guard the Lilaethan is my ancestral duty."

c5ce223d-32ce-491b-b215-30587f17f84c.Text: "If the governor gets it, then... then I could go home..."

f617952c-f8f9-4574-84a6-930a362d9fd9.Text: "So that's what the overlord of Janus looks like. Ha!"

2caea827-f1df-4361-ad18-6ee59d470ce0.Text: "Damn it... We're under attack! Kill the intruders!"

62f9d703-031a-4b72-9f75-702accd97c85.Text: "I await the fulfilment of the vow, mon-keigh."

179dda84-81f7-461a-90e0-92c249bca7de.Text: "Until you end the life of the one who tainted the Lilaethan with corruption, we have nothing to discuss."

fd0aaa4a-1864-4269-bf9d-1be55efc4313.Text: An elegant arch made from some matte material. You see no joins nor traces of fastening — as if the entire structure was cast as one.

3e6afcff-792a-49a2-9855-965f1bfb0f7b.Text: The mystical gate to the Webway — as far as you know, the only method of entering the mysterious dimension created by long-forgotten races of old.

33d07bd3-28d8-4015-95fa-9ec1a3ab4e75.Text: "These creatures were once so timid, so reticent... Could the seed of evil truly have taken root in them as well?"

15b46127-eb7e-437c-8be8-77156b951ce7.Text: "The touch of She Who Thirsts has disfigured the Lilaethan down to the smallest of her children... How deep does the corruption run?"

bdb90d28-ad4c-4641-a8b7-765c97316445.Text: "Look — these are signs of decay caused not by nature, but by the perversion of nature..."

ca86cc05-b455-4ed0-b35a-1f1135e375f3.Text: "Let's go. You will soon see everything for yourself, elantach."

85fca8fc-13e8-42dd-8baf-637f8cb630e2.Text:
"Kert,
I know it's been rough for you since the meeting by the ruins. First contact leaves an impression on everyone. But when I recommended you to the commander, I never thought you wouldn't have the stomach to process the truth.
Think what you want, but I'm still your friend. I don't want anything to happen to you because of your own stupidity. I saw your bag with the packs of nutribars that our lads brought from the settlement. And if you thought no one would notice a couple of clips missing from Torban's backpack, you thought wrong. I want to give you a chance. Return the goods. You know every nutribar counts these days — the stuff that grows in the forest is no longer edible. And we're in need of weapons more than ever.
I can guess why you need all this. You want to split. Abandon our cause, go back home, and pretend nothing happened. But I'm not writing this to appeal to your conscience. I just want to say that you're a marked man now, Kert. After meeting the higher-ups, cutting and running is the worst thing you can try to do. They are watching those who've seen them. They won't let you leave.
Let's talk. Just talk, you and me, in private. Let me know when you're in the camp."

6a92ecd4-a0f8-406e-aa92-37fce250b73a.Text: Joined forces with Yrliet against Muaran to save Janus from the true enemy.

89541271-525b-4595-bfda-93f43e51afac.Text: [Address Yrliet] "I can't convince your kinsman, but I know you are on my side... Will you help me save the Lilaethan from the true enemy?"

ee0b9781-4ff4-4acb-aec9-c5ba3cea966b.Text: [Attack] "I want to cleanse Janus of heresy — of you!"

478e7440-2e4c-45da-8874-d5a1fd6132a5.Text: "I'm sorry to hear that your home was destroyed. But I wasn't there and know nothing of this calamity."

e4f66f99-0006-4431-8165-d2b6fcece323.Text: "And your kin from Janus do not object to sending you Throne knows where to look for the survivors all on your own?"

a449d757-8510-46d3-85de-bfd2746c65a0.Text: "Perhaps Muaran would see a little more if he bothered to pull his head out of his arse."

2e4aec7f-52ef-4a4e-b501-1f0d86a11024.Text: "Let's cool our tempers and try to speak calmly about this."

177bfb5e-6a7d-449e-b353-f7afe2467048.Text: "I am willing to help the Aeldari defeat the Archenemy. But first we must deal with the rebellions you have been orchestrating..."

689ccf20-9b90-4ce1-8982-b1599cf20b59.Text: "If I may, I would like to say something—"

51873eff-32d9-460f-bcf5-d31a835f8eec.Text: [Attack] "Why listen to you talk when I can just kill you?"

160288a6-57df-4902-97f2-4f2c28de382a.Text: "Xenos! Fall on your knees before the Rogue Trader, whose world you have plunged into anarchy, and beg for forgiveness!"

b1de7611-5716-4069-82c2-e60cf199cff7.Text: Decided to exterminate the Aeldari on Janus.

71334990-561d-4773-a0ca-3c90c159b08a.Text: "I've had enough of talking. If you xenos refuse to bow down before the Rogue Trader, you will leave me no choice but to kill you."

65eaecdb-727f-49c0-8217-3e3cb936ec2e.Text: "If this world is in serious danger, there is no sense in fighting each other — let us deal with our common enemy together!"

4e229fc5-fa0c-4abc-abc5-bcfbbeae72b0.Text: "Putting a xenos at the head of an Imperial planet is suicide."

df5d4b42-b679-4a68-a18e-02814e10264d.Text: "And where's my guarantee that the planet and its inhabitants will be safe?"

b5a17706-fe08-46bc-898b-0ecad6e6a48b.Text: [Address the rebel] "Come to your senses, servant of the God-Emperor! Throw off this cursed fog of sorcery and stand with me against the xenos, against these enemies of Humanity!"

07605d54-65aa-4d38-926d-70093b054e54.Text: "I am looking for whoever's behind the uprisings on Janus."

73fdbf7d-3029-45a3-9088-a5e1599b9b45.Text: "I learned there were xenos dwelling on the planet. And I wanted to meet you."

799baf68-7d87-4aa8-9175-507848624e05.Text: "I want to free this world from evil."

aad0a3cf-0521-4827-a95c-429bccef8bf7.Text: "I have learned a lot about Janus in my time here so far, and I see signs of another threat besides that of the 'mon-keigh.'"

324c885c-9526-47db-9762-be6b7487f328.Text: "Why are you fighting against the governor?"

ca6f66dc-6f4a-480b-9bee-1d980e7be2c3.Text: "How did you come to be on Janus?"

08a8c73e-a249-41f5-b6de-7fad1284e32c.Text: "The people on the planet are afflicted with mutations whose origins remain unknown to us. As there are no major sources of radiation on the agri-world, we can discount a technological cause."

ade3f63a-f100-451a-a8c0-2773a72ef1c0.Text: "The forests are teeming with signs of blight — distorted plants, deranged animals. Go into the trees and you will see it for yourself."

194d010a-3df0-4fde-86a3-9ac9ae0c4cc3.Text: "I have heard more than a few rumours that the governor and her circle are engaging in some... reprehensible activities."

138b313b-1bb6-41fa-9b0f-7f82b22ffb84.Text: "I want to stop the violence on the planet — once and for all."

f563ad3f-0202-4f0c-ae7f-afa38fbffca2.Text: Allowed the Aeldari to rule Janus through human intermediaries.

3e19a2c5-db09-4de1-adb1-631636493dfe.Text: "I don't want any more blood — neither yours nor ours. You have my permission to take Janus and its inhabitants into your... charge."

e896fb41-2c56-4b58-9ae4-7efddb375559.Text: "I cannot give Janus to the Aeldari — humans will only be ruled by humans. But I promise that no harm will come to you."

bc22ba2d-2876-4be4-b275-a6450d4d5907.Text: "I'm not obliged to convince you of anything. Think what you like."

699a64d5-5b05-4c0e-83cc-04526cf74dfb.Text: "Even if Crudarach was destroyed by humans as you claim, I imagine you gave them a perfectly good reason to do so."

fa4935d2-8b36-4197-a659-fd509d69ac94.Text: "Watch your tongue, xenos. I'm doing you a favour just by listening to your vile words."

edf11392-213c-4705-99ce-427699de9b62.Text: "My duty is to protect my worlds and my vassals. If Janus is being threatened by the Archenemy, I will fight to the end."

899e265b-c79c-4208-8c55-3bef64c38e6b.Text: [Nod at the rebels] "What have you done to these people? They believe you are their commanders."

06991948-2f17-491e-ab1a-cb4e05a7517e.Text: "An entire herd of xenos. The hunt will be good."

88a37be7-295b-49a1-ab81-e55bf96a17be.Text: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, the sovereign of Janus and {mf|master|mistress} over every living soul on this world! On your knees, foul heretics!"

6556a970-408b-47e6-a9c9-f6fb070f49df.Text: "We? Do you wish to join my entourage?"

4c677550-f7e2-4f32-a5c8-123b7bb34432.Text: "I certainly will not be needing xenos' help in this affair."

e415dff6-81d9-4391-b6ae-0d512d887ca2.Text: "Speak to the Rogue Trader like that again and it will be the last thing you say."

b90bb05f-6d4e-4b31-a9b8-8d5bee3b5489.Text: "Yrliet, are you staying with us? I'll be departing this world soon and heading for the stars — perhaps you want to do that too?"

3594a7d2-f194-4dae-ac63-999f1baa7bac.Text: "Yrliet, don't you want to join me?"

db204874-b33c-497f-bd6c-ef4bd81926c2.Text: Favoured the alliance of humans and Aeldari on Janus.

9589bd37-1dff-46b9-949e-574245402e0c.Text: "We shall do things another way: I shall grant my protection to this form of alliance between xenos and representatives of Humanity. Together we shall destroy Vistenza and her associates, and then humans and Aeldari will flourish on Janus under my patronage!"

b23decb7-250c-42fc-9cc3-b807c932461a.Text: [Attack] "In the name of the Golden Throne, I will purge this Imperial world of the heresy that has tainted it!"

38368048-c7da-46c2-b0bc-5e837d424884.Text: "Yrliet, do I need to convince you? Maybe you can try trusting your own intuition instead of your overseer? You know, that thing that's telling you not to believe everything Muaran says?"

a489e2aa-4d17-456b-b11b-401774999b2e.Text: "I took this skull from the governor's secretary. The secret of your presence on this planet is not as well-kept as you think — at least not among Vistenza's circle."

a9aa8333-26e8-4d80-b756-332374c5102b.Text: "Perhaps we can still come to an agreement? Make mutual concessions?"

94a721fc-4a8c-4b7c-bab2-be50d6452d14.Text: "Stop pretending I am not here. I have come to discuss the situation on Janus."

750d8459-0e34-41cf-bc8d-dabefa569560.Text: Convinced Yrliet that Muaran, the Aeldari Farseer, had succumbed to corruption.

6cd26355-4992-48e5-8314-a1a02816d966.Text: [Address Yrliet] "Do you not see? Every breath your kinsman takes is riddled with corruption. He resorts to lies, obfuscations, and accusations — all to save his rotten little soul. Kill him. You want to save the Lilaethan, don't you?"

321772a4-09c5-4cf8-8a71-c6e8ec97a9f5.Text: "I have already been patient with your kin. And now you are asking for more?"

f87f1890-5c4f-48ee-94c5-550956db4147.Text: "Mon-keigh titles mean nothing to me. If you came here to make boasts in empty words, your journey has been for nothing."

957b3093-0957-492e-9c62-9ec949fc5a38.Text: {n}Yrliet seems to freeze for a moment, and then she turns sharply to Muaran.{/n} "Throughout all the cycles that I wandered amidst the stars, I was sure of one thing: fate can be changed. Cling to your faith, Farseer, but I refuse to follow a blind man who is dooming his kin to a false hunt. I am going off on my own Path — with the elantach."

0b65e2d9-6fed-4d4e-8b20-516692c3e039.Text: {n}Yrliet lets out a plaintive shriek and grabs her weapon, which she immediately turns on you. The other Aeldari quickly follow her example.{/n}

f165cbe7-abd0-49bf-869e-402f41d4c316.Text: {n}The rebel looks at you with undisguised {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusViolent}contempt{/d}. He pointedly spits in your direction and turns away.{/n}

ac7c5a16-3b15-4677-b9af-792eb79b2377.Text: "I am a {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Child of Asuryan{/g}, Muaran, not a plaything in the cold hands of fate, which you claim speaks through your mouth! My choice of Path is no worse than yours or any other Aeldari's — and my Path calls me to fight our true enemies, not eradicate the mon-keigh! If it comes to it, I will stand with them, for this elantach can see what you are blind to, Farseer!" {n}Yrliet's eyes are alight with fury. She pointedly lays her hand on her weapon, looking away from the Farseer.{/n}

d6d98015-9a8f-446a-b805-8689ed92eb78.Text: {n}The rebel lets out a laugh that sounds more like a hoarse caw and wipes the corner of his mouth on his shoulder.{/n} "{mf|Master|Mistress}... Off that voidship the vox-ops are on about, I suppose? You're already working with the governor... There's no point talking to this one, Commander, just say the word and we'll—"

7fc8925e-6914-4824-a9f1-bba853f351d4.Text: "The words of a creature whose will is ruled by momentary whims. There is nothing you can do to make me believe in the strength of your convictions."

a6f57ec5-28be-4da1-bbb4-df49c5f69f38.Text: "Yrliet the Outcast is as beholden to her emotions as you mon-keigh are. Isn't that why she abandoned her true path — and after years of wandering, her {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} blood has run dry and become more like yours. Speak then, if you have something to say."

97d12d43-38f9-400d-b081-4ceb97bc2e1f.Text: "The mon-keigh believe they are serving fellow members of their tribe — their wise and noble chiefs. My gift is potent enough to ensure that the mon-keigh hiding in these forests see us as humans rather than Children of Asuryan, and see your primitive structures rather than the traces of our kind."

04f0c4a0-8e2b-4d71-b509-7148e6419c24.Text: "Are you insane? You're condemning us all to death in Sai'lanthresh's maw!" {n}Yrliet grabs her weapon, her voice breaking into a desperate shout.{/n} "I won't let you kill the elantach, Muaran!"

27dccab4-8fe9-4299-8f40-b2c7878a4a9e.Text: "The name of that danger is mon-keigh, and I will see to it that the Lilaethan is purged of those defiling her face. Then again... there is one way to prove to me that the mon-keigh truly do care about the well-being of their captured world. Eliminate the ruler of the mon-keigh sojourning on the Lilaethan, and relinquish the governing of this world to me and my kin."

9373f5ae-b189-4d85-a8f7-068d56de58b6.Text: "This elantach was the first person to discover the coming of Sai'lanthresh — one of those whom the mon-keigh call {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos Gods{/g}. Without {mf|him|her}, I would still be deceived by your words about destiny and the true future."

0467352e-9a91-4732-a956-1444abc961a2.Text: "Do not forget: the current ruler of the mon-keigh must die — by your hand or ours. And I will consider the conditions of our deal unmet until that happens."

e941d9d5-b9d3-41fd-b982-c0653bfe376b.Text: "Mon-keigh revealing paths... it's ludicrous. Mon-keigh bring pain and strife — in our time, and for all time. How can you trust a mon-keigh after what we taught you? After hearing the sorrowful song of the dying world?" {n}Muaran turns his head toward you.{/n} "It was not chance that brought Crudarach down. Mon-keigh destroyed our ancient home. Stripped us of our defences. Doomed us to wander amidst the cold stars."

08edf3e7-3314-4413-b1c5-9f0810c51c1e.Text: {n}Muaran says nothing for a few moments, then adds mockingly,{/n} "I suppose my demands can be considered a gift for the likes of you. You could not wish for anything better than {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} stewards to rule over mon-keigh without bloodshed..."

3f7dde68-50c4-41c6-9b9c-1629f7e78bcf.Text: "You have the word of a {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Child of Asuryan{/g}, who venerates life far more than any of you. What is more, mon-keigh, I have not the slightest desire to inflict harm upon the Lilaethan, the land of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} ancestors."

0e764548-0553-4508-8006-5910ccb25841.Text: "Silence." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}'s voice is musical, but every word he speaks falls heavily and irrevocably like a stone dropped into a dark pool. The rebel obediently ducks his head.{/n}

c99e50ed-5ace-4026-849e-53bcb44e277f.Text: "Mon-keigh, state the reason for your coming. I hope it is convincing, or else you will be sent to meet your ancestors without delay."

08662e86-4b8c-4ef6-b589-554667f5dcdf.Text: "Your kind is not amenable to talking — only to senseless destruction. The mon-keigh have corrupted and obliterated our home, the Lilaethan — all because of their primitive affinity for violence, no doubt. Your advances in this art surpass those of other more ancient civilisations of the universe."

e07f693a-13c2-46bc-a580-3307556f1765.Text: {n}Yrliet leans forward.{/n} "Of what do you speak, elantach?"

2d4b2574-6dd7-43d8-8f1e-9668dce0e249.Text: "As I have told you, Muaran... even the mon-keigh recognise the threat that has veiled the Lilaethan in shadow! Why are you so insistent on hating the mon-keigh when our most ancient foe has raised its head?"

bdecadd6-0977-4f1a-8eec-3adbd04a292d.Text: "The Lilaethan herself will stand as surety for our agreement. As will your compatriots who live on it. And the profit that you will gain by tilling the Maiden World." {n}Muaran tilts his head to the side.{/n} "Our human helpers will replace the leaders of the mon-keigh. We will be the ones who govern the Lilaethan from the shadows."

4094eeb0-b9cc-4f38-837f-6ca68ba2af1c.Text: {n}Muaran glares at you for a while, then nods.{/n} "So be it."

ff09b7e3-b2cf-492c-9bd8-d0e88776f502.Text: {n}Yrliet pauses, and then looks at the other Aeldari.{/n} "I have seen it before on my wanderings. Taken separately, each of these cases can be deemed an anomaly, or explained by the foolishness or brutality of the mon-keigh... Muaran, how can you not see this? Could your own eyes have been blinded by prophecies? The shadow of She Who Thirsts is rising over the Lilaethan..."

bf6a984a-0ff4-4e1e-8e06-ee82f6fc67bc.Text: "There are even signs of corruption among those who share our refuge. I thought it was the natural way of things for our kind — an early prime, accelerated ageing, and then rotting alive year after year."

108f37bf-1569-479e-a21c-bd299fc45e1b.Text: "I have seen these changes. It is no blight, but the Lilaethan's scream, crying out for help. The World Spirit is defending itself as best it can — with its children, with its own creatures. And these changes increase with every passing hour, as if the threat the world senses grows stronger and stronger..."

1680e578-5f16-46c7-b8f0-617f6eb17bae.Text: {n}Muaran makes a sharp gesture.{/n} "No. We will restore the Lilaethan to her rightful custodians, or our conversation is over."

870d14e4-1c13-45a4-a76f-95235c72a638.Text: {n}Yrliet goes still when she sees the skull — and then whips around to face Muaran.{/n} "How did our kin's remains end up in the hands of the mon-keigh? You claimed we had suffered no losses at all in this confrontation. The mon-keigh should have been completely ignorant of our kind, of me!"

123ef23e-eb09-47b3-b9c3-4469933f4553.Text: {n}Yrliet stares at you intently, and then turns away.{/n}

20eb6fbc-929f-4cd3-8785-58b9db83e563.Text: Refused to let the Aeldari rule Janus and promised them protection.

ee75f464-1c1f-48fd-8374-bf33eae40295.Text: {n}A heavy silence falls between you and the assembled {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}.{/n}

e34ef8a8-f2e4-4b3b-954e-14f9cea52965.Text: "What?" {n}The man shudders, screws up his face, and after a second, stares around in bewilderment as if seeing everything for the first time.{/n} "By the God-Emperor! They're..."

b57d2b7c-d003-4840-a684-27cb040d6493.Text: {n}Muaran utters a florid curse and calls his kin to battle.{/n}

651be724-2a6a-4fe3-a6a0-ea77b65c8340.Text: {n}Muaran's voice rumbles like distant thunder.{/n} "You will not defy your masters and betray the customs of Crudarach again, Outcast..."

545ee4ca-ff34-4078-aad7-46f0389a261e.Text: {n}Muaran leans down over Yrliet, his tone menacing.{/n} "You left Crudarach in our darkest hour to gratify your ego. You came to us on the Lilaethan — and I accepted you as one of our own. I even gave you a real purpose, Yrliet the Outcast... and you dare to insult me, a Farseer? It was a mistake to let you into our circle — you have turned our efforts to survive into dust with your own hands!"

85da7799-0368-4db6-a538-eccb015d06b8.Text: "You speak of the strength of one's convictions, Muaran? You claim it is your destiny to protect your kin... so then what happened to the Aeldari you sent to the mon-keigh ruler before me? The Aeldari whose {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_YrlietShownSkull}skull{/d} is now kept as a mon-keigh trinket? That was the previous envoy you sent, wasn't it? Did you see the same fate for me in your visions?"
