6520cf3d-e94a-463a-9e0e-8295c382d313.Text: {n}One of the figures stops next to Bogul. The female voice is familiar, as is the feeling of being closely watched by unhuman eyes.{/n} "So, outsider. You have achieved your goal and found us — the leaders of the rebellion. Now tell me — what will you do now? But before you answer... Do not make any careless movements. My kin are much faster than yours."

fb926a1a-ad18-4041-80fa-54dd9bd5be3c.Text: {n}The rebel spits on the ground at the sound of your name.{/n} "So it's you... murderer! Torturer of innocents! Commander, just give the order and I'll—"

a8f1b9b6-e911-49a7-9b6f-36436be17195.Text: "His fate was to serve Crudarach — the spirit of our {g|Encyclopedia:Craftworld}craftworld{/g} that keeps the {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} alive. Your destiny is to do the same, Yrliet the Outcast — as long as you aren't planning to transgress our laws again."

e8b7331a-0e10-4dfc-b270-6653edfa8f4d.Text: {n}Muaran turns his head toward you.{/n} "So Yrliet the Outcast has revealed our secret to you. I'm sure you have something to say in that regard, mon-keigh."

89aa7e77-cf5c-4f14-a173-db6e6d48d496.Text: "The Lilaethan is struggling to expel the disease that has settled within her borders. And if the mon-keigh's efforts to destroy this planet are only increasing, isn't it right for the Maiden World to seek retribution?"

0b63dc40-508d-41a4-8552-30d0e618b4ad.Text: "You have revealed your true visage, mon-keigh. My kin, do your duty — get rid of the outsider."

333c501f-5e98-4237-998a-9daeae283275.Text: "I heard the ruler giving out orders... She called them the 'innovations of the finest minds on Janus.' What minds would condemn themselves to such a woeful fate?"

2f1e16d1-4175-47a2-b5e0-84e9aadf79be.Text: {n}Muaran says nothing for several moments.{/n} "The path I set for you had been travelled before, Outcast. Karantar was sent to the ruler of the mon-keigh before you came among us. His fate was hidden from my sight..."

6b9405be-bcf4-491b-9229-a283a4a2569e.Text: "Stop treating my Path as if it were a curse!" {n}Yrliet's voice rings out, and barely suppressed rage dawns in her eyes.{/n} "My Path is not a mark of disgrace! It was what saved me from dying along with Crudarach, a death it was doomed to suffer by your empty predictions!"

74f550d7-2118-4073-be66-e07aaadfc44a.Text: "We will protect the Lilaethan, but we will do so without violence. We will work for the interests of our race and our world through trusted mon-keigh, while we will remain in the shadows of the forests. This will be safer for everyone."

8ca85b50-fff9-435e-8a58-3066e61b3fc5.Text: "You foolish wretch! You have exceeded my patience — your Path ends here and now!"

b8f0f77f-0766-4317-a8cb-55cbc00ef9f2.Text: {n}Muaran tries to say something, but the rebel interrupts him:{/n} "If this... offworlder keeps dictating terms, I won't be able to stop myself, Commander! Have you seen what {mf|he|she}'s capable of, what {mf|he|she}'s {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusTyrannical}done{/d} to Janus? I'd rather die than live in that kind of slavery!"

ce91c793-749f-47df-8aef-14f0d8a26db3.Text: {n}The rebel looks at you with a hint of doubt.{/n} "We'll see. You may have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusHarsh}stuck it{/d} to us... but, to be fair, we did break the law of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} with all our riots. So let's try it this way."

c8f96406-71f7-4d4d-b4a7-220cae727bac.Text: {n}Yrliet shakes her head.{/n} "The governor must die, and she must be replaced by new rulers, ones not corrupted by the touch of She Who Thirsts... We must return to Vistenza Vyatt and put an end to the taint that has afflicted the Lilaethan."

75b442ec-f1cf-4c74-b3c2-1dcce23bccac.Text: {n}Yrliet speaks so quietly, you can barely make out her words:{/n} "We should have remained shadows to the mon-keigh — ghosts wandering amidst the ancient ruins. But you, elantach... whose hand led you to the Lilaethan? Destiny or damnation? Muaran, allow {mf|him|her} to speak."

2fa21e87-4627-40c0-a8c7-d7373f22e3b9.Text: "How can the fate of an Asuryani be hidden from the one who guides them, Muaran? Aren't we supposed to be your greatest concern? Did... did you not even consider that the same thing could happen to me — that I would perish under the shadow of doom?" {n}Yrliet casts a glance at you.{/n} "What... what else do you know, elantach? What else have you uncovered that was — unintentionally or deliberately — hidden from me?"

072384ee-df7b-4827-8084-e4799dbb9c0a.Text: "If the Lilaethan remains in our charge, I am willing to come to an agreement. We will not lose another kinsman and we will be able to tend to this world, which has suffered so many years under Humanity's yoke. As regards the ruling mon-keigh..." {n}Muaran makes a strange gesture, and the Aeldari behind him take off running into the forest.{/n} "We will help you."

42b3ed8a-3278-4f07-82aa-b4bf10c5f293.Text: {n}Cassia looks at the xenos and covers her mouth.{/n} "So... bright... All these blinding colours make it hard to focus... They are consuming the defiant rabble and trying to consume us."

6b9d422e-2b54-4ceb-9ec3-88ee5f40ee76.Text: "I..." {n}Yrliet breaks off.{/n} "I had forgotten my own path. I had forgotten what it means to trust my own judgement. Elantach, you are right. I have seen too many signs to deny it — there is a threat hanging over the Lilaethan, and it is not from the mon-keigh."

e3832dd2-d540-4ec9-8df0-1bde6a6c3dd4.Text: "The colours of these xenos are painful to behold, but there is just as much pain in their hearts. Or could it be... fear? Despair? I cannot tell, the hues are too strange... too... Ah!" {n}Cassia flinches, and a trickle of blood runs down her cheek.{/n}

eda0dddd-0111-4c50-b64f-4be4a6ea96e1.Text: {n}The Aeldar chuckles, his voice turning venomous.{/n} "Or it could be that your uncontrollable hunger to destroy everything in your path reigns over your every thought and deed."

cf84e23c-a13f-4ec7-89fd-f0d6f2c0ad3a.Text: "Rest assured, the very sound of your primitive tongue causes us as much suffering — even a translator cannot alleviate its crudeness."

06028f9a-fd07-473e-b516-bc4f7ccf56bd.Text: {n}Muaran gazes at you intently.{/n} "If these words had come from an {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}, I would have believed them. But you are merely a mon-keigh — a plaything of your own passions. Any emotion that takes hold of your soul can drive out all trace of reason and honour."

c91f29c1-87ee-43e2-a414-702d443d10f7.Text: "It is not my intention to have my brothers and sisters sit on the council, mon-keigh. That role will be played by humans — you may choose whomever you wish for this task. As long as they remember who stands behind them and heed our direction."

416999a8-db74-4e65-b4ae-a99bf0928ae4.Text: {n}Yrliet opens her mouth, but Muaran cuts her off.{/n} "Go on, Outcast. Your place is on the meandering roads of space, not among us."

ca405ae8-55b9-47ee-ad16-76ca8994d069.Text: {n}Yrliet shakes her head.{/n} "You are attempting to cloud my sight, mon-keigh."

7f685ff7-4894-45e4-85fb-af5c44a18b53.Text: "You won't believe what they do to the people! You won't see much at the nobles' estates, but if you go out to the agri settlements... As soon as the governor's dogs come — that's it, that's the settlement gone! First, they make them drink some filth that cripples them after a while, then they take them to these gatherings... I know what I'm talking about — a cousin of mine from one of them settlements sent me letters at first, and then he was gone! If folks start talking too much about mutants and lunatics, they send the wardens and silence anyone who got reported! There are more and more of these dead settlements — what, are we supposed to sit and wait until we're all killed?"

f9c1bac2-9603-46de-bf34-7a2025f985a2.Text: {n}After Yrliet's words, the two tall Aeldari behind Muaran start moving — one looks around at the leader, while the other lets out a cry, muffled under his visor. The rebel beside you cringes, as though the Aeldari speech causes him pain. He strains to say something, but Muaran makes an imperious gesture and the soldier meekly straightens up and salutes, staring at the xenos with slavish devotion.{/n}

82d6037a-05a4-45f0-88ac-8ed01dc18b01.Text: {n}The rebel standing closest to you is looking at you with a mixture of hatred and confusion. His hands, clutching a strange weapon, are trembling ever so slightly. A strange device on a strap hangs from the man's neck.{/n} "You... Throne preserve me, who are you?"

5a1777be-619d-4b80-a42e-fd13042cff6c.Text: {n}Muaran stares at you for several seconds. At last, he says,{/n} "An alliance? That is how you interpreted what I said? Then again, if you prefer that word, let us call it an alliance."

bdf96fe7-c501-4576-8f19-68b099de2680.Text: {n}The rebel nods in satisfaction.{/n} "That's good, that's good... Our commanders should stay in charge, they'll know what to do... they'll know what's best, what pleases the God-Emperor..." {n}He speaks the last words in a barely audible whisper, wincing as if in pain from a splitting headache.{/n}

95b2663b-c32a-4465-bcca-f0180fa1240b.Text: "The statement predicting future success is fallacious. Security dogmas are based on extensive statistical data on confrontations with xenoraces, and there have been zero cases of successful coexistence."

5cac144c-0944-4cab-b114-9ab55891c890.Text: "Ha! Great joke, shereen! Just fancy that, an alliance of humans and xenos... That's a joke, right?"

46797324-9668-43e2-9cf2-55d68afad174.Text: "Uhh, Lord Captain, are you — pardon my frankness — sure that you haven't just bitten off more than you can chew? Who told you this idea would sit well with the locals?"

41773b47-eedd-4f5d-a0a7-9a0d4494e651.Text: {n}Finally, Muaran tilts his head.{/n} "I am not willing to risk my kin's lives, mon-keigh. I will steel my soul and try to believe your promise."

eb412cb1-0ddc-4e11-8052-0329611355d0.Text: "What do you deem evil, mon-keigh? If you wish to eradicate it, why not start with the defilers of the Lilaethan, your kind?"

e3445e43-1070-4c44-ad72-fe58ed5a1bc3.Text: "You've found them. And what do you plan to do with us?"

2ca8a114-7025-428f-b19d-2d06c8de33db.Text: "This is a gross violation of every sacred covenant of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}. I do not know, {name}, what dictates this... this wilfulness... but I promise you: Janus will face the most serious consequences."

d8c4f759-ee52-4134-b3f8-aa470825f31a.Text: "What, now that we've gone against the governor, you lot don't even see us as people anymore? We're all freaks and mutants to you, huh?" {n}The rebel turns to the tall robed creature.{/n} "Commander, just say the word and we'll blow their brains out!"

d39cb400-67a1-4930-b8b6-3b9dfcfc353b.Text: {n}The warriors are the first to raise their weapons and charge into the fray. A moment later, the rebels follow suit.{/n}

8c5666fd-7a2b-4a16-abdf-4e400f6e6042.Text: {n}The tall being in a fine long garment turns to you, their face hidden behind the blank visor of their helmet. When they begin to speak, even from a distance you feel the air around the figure grow cold.{/n} "Mon-keigh. You should not be here."

1c40f929-adaa-4f81-8996-7f0ed081dfc1.Text: {n}You see Yrliet among the beings clustered around the strange, tall structure. She watches you with complete indifference, the way one watches an insect crawling up a wall.{/n}

af248298-bd4c-47f7-9e3e-0b09fedd5932.Text: {n}Yrliet strides forward, her eyes flashing.{/n} "Muaran! I am calling you to account! You said that the great danger threatening the Lilaethan lurked in the hearts of the mon-keigh, in their greed and ignorance. And all the while another enemy was looming over this world, an enemy whose tracks you should have seen in things to come. Sai'lanthresh, She Who Thirsts, is threatening this world — and you hid it from us! Answer me — did you or did you not behold our greatest foe in the Lilaethan's future? Did you lie to me?"

088d4a26-f4a2-4c2c-a526-9777bb4f6868.Text: {n}The robed figure inclines their head. And then they begin to speak.{/n} "Yrliet the Outcast. You left the path that was set out for you. You brought unknown {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} to our refuge. And now you speak to me with unseemly anger. Your long wanderings far from Crudarach have altered your mind and tainted your sight."

14272ef9-167b-4ba2-b43f-42ee974e90c5.Text: "At last!" {n}Argenta raises her weapon.{/n} "May He guide my hand, for I am His vengeful wrath!"

fe3f1c49-16e9-4be6-9b12-75cd3e7cd0f2.Text: "'Commander'?" {n}Abelard's face turns red with fury.{/n} "In what world is it acceptable for the Imperium's subjects to call xenos their leaders? What a disgrace!"

f3379290-7ece-46a0-91f2-e4b60d13042c.Text: "Bring your entourage to heel, Yrliet the Outcast. Their mere presence offends my sensibilities — the least they can do is display the obedience we have impressed upon our mon-keigh servants."

aba1214d-75e4-4a1b-8c4c-95d00b227ea5.Text: "My wanderings are the Path I have chosen for myself. Far from the walls of Crudarach, I have seen and come to know things that no other {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} could hidden away in a craftworld their entire life. Why do you deny my words about Sai'lanthresh? Is it because you were lying to me and my kin when you showed us the true Path?"

fe5cd16d-db2a-40ac-8cfb-93db3df816d6.Text: "These people are not thinking straight, {name}." {n}Heinrix stares at the tall, robed figure without blinking.{/n} "I can sense an influence. A bewitching spell. Sorcery known only to the strongest of the Aeldari — their Farseers."

f1df197c-ab6e-4dc1-b7c0-0d10b33d184d.Text: "You are playing with words and avoiding the question!" {n}Notes of desperation — and rage — are creeping into Yrliet's voice now.{/n} "The Lilaethan is under threat from our eternal foe — and yet you're more concerned about the presence of the elantach than the corruption that is flowing through the veins of this world! Did you never consider that your war might simply be hastening Sai'lanthresh's triumph? Perhaps the ruler's servants, in their efforts to protect her, will resort to more and more instruments of corruption..."

f596369a-e4dd-4a6b-8fc8-e3cb992a5cbc.Text: {n}The rebel looks at you — and you can clearly see the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusBenevolent}relief{/d} on his face.{/n} "That's right, that's exactly right... We won't let any harm come to our own, but we'll figure out what to do ourselves." {n}He grimaces and brings a hand to his temple as if in pain.{/n}

0d115b5b-9950-46f3-9811-668ff30795ef.Text: {n}Yrliet gives you a long, studying look.{/n} "The tale of the Children of Asuryan on the Lilaethan is coming to an end, but somewhere out there, among the cold stars of the cosmos that your kind calls the Expanse, there are others. Deprived of their home. Lost. Suffering..." {n}Yrliet shuts her eyes, and grief twists her finely sculpted features.{/n}

95a78de1-959f-4ae5-bcd1-8bffffb2ce59.Text: "Look around you, mon-keigh. Your kind captured a world that did not belong to you. You broke open her heart, crushed her will, disfigured her face, trying to squeeze every drop of life out of the Lilaethan like a ripe fruit. I have seen the paths that lie before us — on each of them, the presence of the mon-keigh heralds the demise of the World Spirit. I will not allow it."

bfe38527-aea9-4d82-9d3a-00acae372a2b.Text: "We came from the sky, just like you. If you want to know where our ships and our kin are, I will not tell you. The ones who brought us here mapped out the limits of this star long ago — in search of other kin lost in the darkness amidst the stars."

937c47f9-761f-406a-b0d7-1aeb78903cf3.Text: "Accept your release from an unclean existence, and be grateful." {n}Kibellah assumes a stance, ready to begin a dance of blood.{/n}

7f134d7c-1435-49bc-9f8a-5861465d1174.Text: "Is that so? Is that why your servants have been {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusViolent}slaughtering their own kind{/d}? Is that why your weapons sought to disfigure the Lilaethan from orbit? Your words are nothing but lies and hypocrisy, mon-keigh."

f441ccaf-62f3-49cd-ade9-ffd7afbf7b85.Text: "This will affect Janus's tithe assessment. There is less trust in produce from agri-worlds with pest problems."

6f5154bd-19d7-400a-8f36-ae80d0c7b86c.Text: "I ofttimes hear this word spoken — 'xenos'... it appears to be as insulting in your tongue as 'mon-keigh' is in ours." {n}She sighs.{/n} "We call ourselves the {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Children of Asuryan{/g}. The humans — those whom fate has brought to form an alliance with us — call us Aeldari."

fcc8e4f7-363b-4235-9506-e8fd718ae5fc.Text: {n}Yrliet stands frozen like a statue, and then suddenly turns to face Muaran.{/n} "The elantach is right. I mistook the wicked intent in your heart for stubbornness and vanity. But no Farseer would ignore the threat from Sai'lanthresh knowing what it means for this world and its soul... No. There can be only one answer — you have betrayed us, Muaran. You have joined Her side."

a33c9499-5218-4ed9-b149-563a18de586f.Text: "A deal with a mon-keigh is like a dying star — its time will inevitably run out. Then again... there is one way to prove to me that you truly do care about the well-being of your captured world. Eliminate the ruler of the mon-keigh sojourning on the Lilaethan, and relinquish the governing of this world to me and my kin."

f3e2d49a-c947-4130-a1e5-5c84170a4ee3.Text: {n}With a piercing avian cry, the two-headed eagle swoops down to sink its forged talons into the Farseer's face. The cyber-beast's enormous wings and its righteous fury will distract the enemy from the battle for a few critical seconds.{/n}

c4a5849c-cdd3-4a15-add8-7d1800cbcebf.Text: {n}Muaran's voice rumbles like a distant storm.{/n} "You dare to accuse me of such a thing? You have lost your mind, Outcast..."

3f46df14-f1e9-4d66-9a17-f5feb877ad97.Text: "Tread carefully, Outcast. Do not allow another's words to shake your faith in your chosen fate."

9ac3664e-fdde-4a69-8f23-be3bfd65fb77.Text: "Perhaps. Perhaps the mon-keigh sense their impending inevitable end and are ready to surrender. Well... if so, the hour of retribution is closer than I gleaned in the weavings of fate."

13d9648e-737c-40b5-ae6f-7fd708378bf7.Text: You showed Yrliet the strange skull that had been in the possession of the nobles of Janus.

3dde7edd-8dc8-4bcf-bc75-c1596d583405.Text: {n}Yrliet gives you a long, studying look.{/n} "Wait, elantach. Before you leave these forests forever... Take me with you. To the distant suns. The tale of the Children of Asuryan on the Lilaethan is coming to an end, but somewhere out there, among the cold stars of the cosmos that your kind calls the Expanse, there are others. Deprived of home. Lost. Suffering..." {n}Yrliet shuts her eyes, and grief twists her finely sculpted features.{/n}

a6b776c3-bfe6-40eb-941f-2811754492ba.Text: "We can help one another, elantach. You will be my wings, and I your wounding spear. And your voice of reason, should you encounter my kin. If that is still not enough..." {n}Yrliet thinks for a moment and continues carefully.{/n} "I promise you a wondrous reward, elantach. The treasures of my world hidden in the vastness of space in exchange for the rescue of my kin. If you remain true to your word and do not go back on our covenant."

4d971048-0580-48e1-858f-efc5d14f6a10.Text: "Just as the Children of Asuryan settled this world you consider yours, my kin have flooded this region of space. Desperately trying to survive, they will seek shelter in your demesne, perhaps even raiding mon-keigh vessels for supplies and sustenance. I do not wish such a fate for any of my kind, just as I hope you do not wish it for your subjects."

237ef684-ef5b-46f7-9493-7294b73baf38.Text: "It is an honour to welcome an Aeldari wanderer into my ranks."

a4afa5ef-5b3c-40a9-a1ab-2c2ed26fd5c4.Text: "You do not lack for boldness. Even your request is worded not as a plea but a treaty. But I like it, so we have a deal."

8bc2add5-a161-4468-82a8-6bbdd715f055.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} shifts slightly and lowers her head. A ghost of a smile appears on her lips.{/n} "My heart sings at the thought of the Lilaethan's approaching liberation... but we must not rest while Sai'lanthresh's servants still mar the face of the Maiden World."

f605d792-edec-436f-b044-9f682dfe9bb7.Text: "Well, elantach... {name}, yes? I am tired of titles and designations — my own and others'. Since your path lies beyond the limits of the Lilaethan, I will go with you — to search for others of my kind scattered among the stars. Perhaps they will greet me more warmly than this brood."

97aab2b2-5037-4d42-92bf-f10bf19ddf57.Text: "And remember your promise, elantach. When we leave the Lilaethan, it will be to go to the distant stars. Muaran saw them in his visions, and they sang mournful songs about the fate of my people. And I will fight beside you until the song of the stars turns into a funeral lament."

6ec477f8-aa4c-4782-bfaf-e93b8da6b691.Text: "Xenos do not belong in a Rogue Trader's retinue."

630f31fd-997a-4762-b43f-d4363187f50d.Text: "Why should I even be concerned with the affairs of xenos?"

ea331243-e021-46c3-a4c1-026d4a0d2061.Text: "I have always wanted to add a xenos to my retinue! Welcome, welcome."

edcd5855-a22a-47b8-8eae-18e3a9b2649c.Text: {n}Yrliet purses her thin lips.{/n} "So be it."

ac72a1fe-afb1-4d4d-85c5-25404ba50ec3.Text: Sentenced the Janusian rebels to death.

33a5e45d-6ff4-4301-b214-7103b7611c45.Text: [Attack] "There is no excuse for rebelling against the Imperium's rightful authority. That the xenos manipulated you with such ease shows your weakness of faith and cowardice. The sentence for this crime is death."

f57ae3de-6903-4629-8149-d6bafc6480ff.Text: "People of Janus, you have suffered enough! The xenos have been taken care of, now it is time to free yourselves from the Chaos-worshipping governor!"

df9db868-5bca-45b0-a8fa-b7751c22dcab.Text: "By assisting me, you have earned your pardon... Go back to your homes, and I will forget I ever saw you here. Your uprising against the rightful authority on this world is over."

7f9d66a5-92fe-40f1-bc1e-803413bce230.Text: [Attack] "Now it's going to be even easier to kill you all!"

8def90e7-a8fd-4e84-bcd3-8e4b43451f6c.Text: {n}The surviving rebels are panting heavily, catching their breath after the battle. One by one, they look at you expectantly.{/n}

ddc9f5b2-b981-49dc-bab9-96501cddab2e.Text: {n}The tricked rebels exchange a glance — and charge into battle with furious cries!{/n}

47f48d4d-3d7c-4624-bd43-bf9e90bac14a.Text: "Well... what now? What are you going to do with these... these gullible idiots, Lord Captain?"

326c378d-59c5-4f63-9840-0372eb37fe7a.Text: {n}Jubilant cries shake the forest. The survivors shout out your name, praising the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} and gabbling promises of eternal loyalty. It seems that with the removal of the Aeldari, an unseen weight has been lifted from their shoulders.{/n}

5a79c29e-b55d-4cd0-85f5-3e18e27da155.Text: {n}The tricked rebels raise their weapons and launch into a desperate attack.{/n}

17324ca1-8451-4be1-9995-4bca158f8296.Text: {n}The tricked rebels exchange glances, clearly not fully comprehending what exactly just happened. In the end, exhaustion and confusion do their work: slowly, with an odd glance over the shoulder, they all walk away from the battlefield, leaving behind the camp and the ravaged bodies of their erstwhile allies.{/n}

de855764-716e-4532-b196-a21aee8543d9.Text: "They have let themselves be turned into a weapon in the hands of xenos." {n}Kibellah enunciates every word as if announcing a verdict.{/n} "Their lack of spirit has opened the way for His enemies. Thus, they are poisoned — both by their own weakness and by inhuman sorcery."

7e1c1a14-9c69-4abf-9d3a-29f97d503544.Text: "You lot are still studying this gate, I take it..."

ed9ca826-eb24-48ff-9d69-cb830eeedbb2.Text: "What will happen if you succeed in opening it?"

326a78f2-72f1-412c-9051-8639353ae012.Text: "What exactly are you doing to the gate?"

86a90b99-d0df-43f4-9016-2416dcce9e35.Text: "Have you ever been to the Webway? What does it look like?"

beda5f85-4182-43f9-816c-6b0f97de3d09.Text: "If your offer of mutual cooperation still stands, I would like to have you in my entourage."

3f650a85-f342-4ab6-866d-6d714bc8edbe.Text: {n}Yrliet looks down at you from above. Her hands are resting on her weapon, and yet she appears completely relaxed.{/n} "You have returned, elantach."{g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}{/g}

32306eb8-7448-441e-b751-aebd4ececb56.Text: "I greet you, elantach. What brings you to our sanctuary?"

1592db01-0324-402d-80c9-a31a01db2e13.Text: "Upon my return, he found it in himself to believe that I was capable of taking care of myself without him watching over me, so he chose to look after those of us who had not yet earned such a high degree of trust." {n}Yrliet's voice is almost impassive, but a half-smile plays at the corners of her mouth.{/n}

1efb8ee8-d772-470e-8d88-374087219dc6.Text: "The former rebels have returned to their homes. We continue to eradicate Sai'lanthresh's corruption that seeped into the Lilaethan's veins... but now the planet is at peace, and the World Spirit is safe from all harm."

8a2ef716-2b6f-4b37-903f-3447c0f7d801.Text: "Our duty is keeping us on the Lilaethan, but I doubt that all my kin will remain on the Maiden World. Only those who are essential to guarding this planet against the machinations of Sai'lanthresh."

926b2be7-fd1b-49c1-a957-a04675694f96.Text: "My kin labouring over the gate are better versed in the art of wraithbone creations... but even they cannot fathom every detail designed by the Worldsinger — the sacred keeper of the Lilaethan, who shared a rare bond with the World Spirit. Their spirit now rests among their kin — whilst we, blind in our insight, blunder into the intricate tangle of the gate, stumped by the mystery of its silence."

edbe8fe1-7818-4850-83a8-8d72e0959510.Text: "Imagine myriads of trails, intertwined by the will of the finest creators this universe has ever known... The Webway was created in a time of legend, back when the galaxy belonged to beings far more powerful than you or I."

33ba64f3-66f2-4413-ab1a-90d82b4b4d79.Text: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Webway}Webway{/g} Gate is one of the surviving relics of the old world that was forever lost to us. Crudarach had its own gate, but it worked... differently. Not like the creations of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} who brought the Lilaethan into being."

26534f87-f2d0-43c9-beea-d99af9d4da01.Text: "We will leave this world. Was this not your wish when you refused my kin the right to be the guardians of the Lilaethan?"

6999e1e9-81c6-452b-a390-9b19dc28d34d.Text: "The Webway runs throughout the entire cosmos — by stepping through a gate on one planet, one can traverse millions of light years in but a few hours and emerge on the other side of the universe. My people have long used the Webway to travel between surviving worlds — both planets and crafts."

4dc9e8c2-4399-4052-8cee-9bfeeb6226d0.Text: "Sai'lanthresh's corruption is slowly being purged from the face of the Maiden World. The Lilaethan will never regain her former purity... but now the World Spirit has a faithful guardian."

9eb92393-5b50-4a6b-a5f0-b9895615493d.Text: "Enough talking — just lead me to the rebels so I can put an end to all this heresy."

195544a6-6002-44cc-af60-f93297e6846a.Text: "Enough talking — just lead me to wherever you were going."

d0aed5af-683e-4c3e-8f41-299a1a31d5cf.Text: "If Vistenza is to blame, then why haven't you gone to the palace and killed her already?"

5d6365b3-9e90-4aaa-8f3b-797d709698b1.Text: "I don't know who you're talking about, but I promise I'll gladly help you pour the 'cup of suffering' down their throat."

22a03f41-0ed2-4def-a9d0-f9fd69f85258.Text: "Get a grip. I doubt that will be the last battle we see today, and I need allies with all their wits about them."

7af08351-0305-4dab-8e71-ce685e02c8a5.Text: "Well, well, who knew a tempest was raging beneath that unruffled surface!"

8850d7f5-dac4-4d56-91d5-33f26b1fb671.Text: "If we want to meet with the leaders of the uprising, we better keep moving."

3586e727-5c6c-41ed-b4b4-56f5ad5b5321.Text: "Isn't it time you told me what's going on here?"

9d67837f-c5dd-4ff6-be1e-d00e70301f67.Text: "Who is Muaran? What treachery are you talking about?"

d46b90ea-feb9-417a-bbdc-717e28da5a50.Text: "Why did your own kind attack you?"

23b2553e-3b4a-4759-91f6-9f74d0bc737b.Text: "No one forced your kin to go against me and die. Their stones are my trophies now. I earned them."

36647de8-eb33-477b-bd71-693d87c16904.Text: "You may take the stones — I have no use for them."

789b6220-3d5e-4578-8267-19ee30c30321.Text: "It seems these stones are extremely valuable... I think I'll keep them."

74939a1d-d6bb-4bce-b862-7da14dbfe0df.Text: "I trust your judgement, Yrliet. Vistenza will be punished for her betrayal."

864de2cf-c253-4daa-889f-2e1920d567be.Text: "Why would a handful of xenos go to war against a whole planet? You can't kill everyone!"

f72bb9c8-0e21-4d0b-a6ce-32006f53d658.Text: "How did you come to be on this planet?"

a7107bc0-08fa-4fb5-b451-b8d42ed1ec18.Text: "I don't believe that Vistenza is guilty. You may not like mon-keigh, but we do not serve the Archenemy."

bbb17058-8944-411a-b595-6ec2131a6b2c.Text: "You came to Janus along with the rest of the Aeldari?"

d0620c35-c6d2-40df-a268-8bb1f244aaa7.Text: "How are your kin connected to the uprising on the planet?"

093a7711-cb7f-4f8d-b8ea-5254c3cd760c.Text: "Why are you telling me all this? What's brought on this candour?"

4c738b8f-cb82-4231-b90e-4da21add3ac8.Text: "Maybe Vistenza is tainted from consorting with the Archenemy. We will have to find out for ourselves."

8b3aaaa8-6861-4353-8b96-7889696ba88c.Text: "Make another accusation against a servant of the Imperium and I will have you stuffed and put on display in my stateroom."

b2dc6721-cda7-46a2-9f95-eedb125995ff.Text: {n}Yrliet's usually dispassionate face is contorted in a grimace of pain and rage. Your {g|Encyclopedia:Elucidator}Elucidator{/g} activates when she begins speaking in her own language.{/n} "I swear on Khaine's riven heart, Muaran, you will pay for your treachery! May Morai-Heg sunder your fate and cast it away, may the blood of Eldanesh flood your throat—"

1de53f07-383f-46b1-a52a-dc8c735a1628.Text: {n}Yrliet closes her eyes, sucks in a breath through her teeth, and quickly murmurs something. When she opens her eyes, her face is once again a mask of cool serenity. She looks at you and begins to speak, this time in Low Gothic.{/n}

1126e147-cab8-4e0e-9f49-172aaab9546d.Text: "The signs that have been revealed to me — they all indicate the presence of corruption on this world. Tendrils of corruption may be threading through the World Spirit, poisoning it even as we speak. But for corruption to take hold of the planet so quickly requires effort — effort directed by the will of another." {n}Yrliet pauses.{/n} "I believe Vistenza Vyatt is in thrall to the will of Sai'lanthresh."

1c84561d-9d23-4e5c-8e54-089d7025f860.Text: "After the calamity, the Lilaethan offered my kin a sanctuary — a place of respite in the ruins of our ancestors, under the canopy of the forests created by the wisdom of our Worldsingers... living alongside your kind, who reap the fruits of our labour with such vulgarity."

869b1f46-856a-4895-8931-d4617b60fbe7.Text: "Some evil transcends loyalty to one's own kind. What will become of the Lilaethan if you allow the enemy of all creation to live among your subjects? How long with this mutilated world remain loyal to your {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} before she becomes a chasm bringing forth servants of Sai'lanthresh?"

4db142c1-6c44-42f4-829e-fec84ad3b58a.Text: "Please excuse me, elantach — I allowed the turmoil in my soul to win out over my reason. A slip like that could cost me more than you can even imagine — my very soul. I must be more careful... even in the face of treachery."

68eeb97e-8112-4270-99a6-4ec4fce8702b.Text: "Over? Oh no, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}, this path is far from its end!" {n}Yrliet is almost shouting, her voice ringing with fury.{/n} "But when we get to Muaran, I will make him reveal the full extent of his duplicity and tell me where the truth ends and the lies begin!"

f21e94a4-d290-4120-a4ee-d3e181be03b6.Text: "I see no other path. You deserve the truth."

ebb9324d-ed42-4a8d-a115-8be71d35cfd0.Text: "The only punishment for such a crime is death, elantach. The one who steps onto the path of Sai'lanthresh forfeits the light forever."

e323806d-d02f-4c7a-a584-aefc4c3b83af.Text: "There is only one crime graver than serving Sai'lanthresh — it is betraying the Children of Asuryan for her benefit. Muaran saw the paths, he beheld the future... how could he not see the dark stain on its face? How could he fail to do everything in his power to rid the Lilaethan of this canker?" {n}Yrliet's voice grows angrier, more piercing.{/n} "Before I rip this poisoned seed from the Lilaethan's body, I will make Muaran answer me!"

84fc1a98-2f64-4b2e-b5a8-70c6844665c6.Text: "The mon-keigh are weak in spirit — they are susceptible to the propositions of She Who Thirsts, and in their drive to attain her poisoned gifts, they perform perverse rituals in her name... rituals that require sacrifices. Like the mon-keigh who were brought to the palace and never seen again."

aa9d4648-52ad-43d0-8b91-59fbdbfcd53f.Text: "Muaran is the one responsible for the rebellions against the ruler of Janus... but allow me to tell you everything from the beginning."

853b762c-160c-4626-8bc8-f76a0436ba3a.Text: "My kin became military advisors to the mon-keigh who rose up against the ruler of this world. I had a different mission: to become Vistenza's handler, since the rebels would be unable to get to her until both sides were sufficiently weakened. The ruler of the humans had never seen a Child of Asuryan before, and so she accepted the lie about a degenerate branch of mon-keigh dwelling far from their own kind."

88791864-c6d5-4901-aaa6-d8437b3728d8.Text: "No. My path brought me to the Lilaethan later..." {n}Yrliet hesitates.{/n} "...by another route."

114de5e4-0fec-4c04-9e2f-b2a3bd4b5019.Text: "It was Muaran who welcomed me here — he was one of the surviving Farseers of Crudarach. He was with a handful of {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} who had escaped death and found the path here, to the destroyed cradle of our kind. They were outraged when they saw how the mon-keigh had ravaged our flourishing garden!"

d0957071-5597-4a86-9b22-51988fc5d77f.Text: "I know not the answer to that question." {n}Yrliet lowers her head.{/n} "Many cycles have passed since I departed these forests and my kin. They cannot... they cannot have forgotten me, can they?"

220a785f-c464-4380-bca7-89696daca276.Text: "Before we leave this place..." {n}Yrliet's voice trembles.{/n} "Allow me to search the bodies of the fallen, elantach. I wish to collect their spirit stones — the vessels that protect us from Sai'lanthresh's maw after our physical death. Muaran's foresight led these warriors against us — foresight that can be corrupted by ill intentions they were unaware of. Their souls are locked within these stones — don't let them perish here."

2bb89a88-9bd5-4383-bf9f-9e3bb8f36385.Text: "Your soul is full of wasted rage — and hunger for others' suffering. Perhaps Sai'lanthresh has already laid her touch upon you too."

32985580-3918-47a3-8095-578303ab6be8.Text: "Thank you, elantach. I will take care of my kin."

6521c485-df43-4ee5-823d-4b6dbab0f229.Text: "How can a mon-keigh know the value of another's soul? Foul, savage species..."

0719f325-9c79-4415-a7b3-c2eeaaa01720.Text: "You struggle to understand the Children of Asuryan, and I do not blame you for that — we are too different." {n}Yrliet says nothing for a few moments, choosing her words.{/n} "Mon-keigh walk blindly into the future. We choose the path, guided by our Farseers. Crudarach was the birthplace of the powerful watchers of things to come — our leaders were selected from among their ranks, and their word was set in stone, unshakeable like the universe itself."

3c31a434-9154-4880-88f4-bf09f687a9d2.Text: "Muaran, our leader here, is one of that group. The Children of Asuryan are subject to his will, and he is subject to the will of his visions. Muaran saw the Lilaethan in a vision, suffering and crying out to be cleansed, and we did everything we could to rid the Maiden World of the mon-keigh. Our lives, our desires — all that is dust compared to the light of the path Muaran has chosen for us. At least, that is what my kin believe. I used to believe it too... until recently."

e024206b-d8f8-40a4-bc08-71ee7a2891d2.Text: "The Lilaethan's World Spirit senses the threat — and resists as much as it is able. The living things that inhabit this world are becoming its weapons — weapons turned against the mon-keigh. Poisonous plants, rabid beasts — these are all like a blade in the Lilaethan's hand as she fights the coming of Sai'lanthresh."

c8a7af6a-1f93-411e-a8a1-886fe0caa6ad.Text: "Sai'lanthresh is deceitful and cunning... She subtly penetrates the soul, offering false perfection, luring victims into her web with promises of a wicked ideal. The ruler of the mon-keigh perhaps does not even know that her soul has been corrupted."

9119d16c-f3f6-477f-b00b-8c423471cf5d.Text: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} do not enter battles they cannot win. However, it is in our power to direct the currents so that the elements themselves wash obstacles and enemies from our path. And so it was in this case — Muaran, the Farseer from Crudarach, saw a future without the {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}, and we followed his lead. We simply used the mon-keigh's passions against them. Their love of freedom and anarchy. Their love of domination and violence. Stoking enmity between servants and rulers is easier when your targets are governed by emotion rather than reason."

d4ee3e85-f1ff-4957-8ec9-30c842f57d7e.Text: "Perhaps the signs I uncovered have failed to convince you. I pray to the gods that other proof — something more comprehensible to you — will emerge to sway your opinion."

d2659eda-616b-4d13-bf45-89fe3d450765.Text: "Who gave you the authority to vouch for every soul of your kind? There are those among you who are weak or perverted by passion — it is those mon-keigh Sai'lanthresh chooses to serve her."

8a862ea0-82f0-492e-afdd-711877d0d720.Text: {n}His green visor flashing with interest, Pasqal carefully clarifies:{/n} "Which border exactly?"

42f174b5-f7b1-451b-b4d8-f7adbacef5b0.Text: "I have come across references to xeno-artefacts of this type in archives. If Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship allows, I will examine these... trophies." {n}A velvety, curious voice pours from the vox-synth, not interrupted by a single hiss of static.{/n}

19942542-e35d-4c76-9f11-fe462bfe3184.Text: {n}An angry {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} crackle interrupts Jae. However, Pasqal confines himself to this threatening gesture, obviously not wanting to bicker in front of the Aeldari about who has the right to plunder the world of her kin.{/n}

0d77da29-abd0-4ef6-8e5b-6ea1a956b84f.Text: "You don't need to know that, iron mon-keigh. I am aware of your looting practices."

443d3e88-86ca-4470-ab6f-6489938541ba.Text: {n}"Sai'lanthresh" and "She Who Thirsts" are the names the Aeldari give to the Chaos God Slaanesh, their ultimate enemy. Slaanesh is the god of passion, excess, and forbidden pleasures, and is known for his fickle and treacherous nature.{/n}

1099e395-387c-4e83-b07c-46b601f6d432.Text: {n}You have never heard of this entity before. It must be another Aeldari term for one of the beings from the pantheon of the Ruinous Powers known to Humanity.{/n}

cb1fb9be-8bba-4cdf-8751-d014279355ba.Text: "As lamentable as it may be, the Imperium's history knows many cases where even the most steadfast followers of the Creed would turn away from His light. Governor Vyatt had to tap into many founts of knowledge to turn Janus into a prosperous agri-world. Perhaps... one of those founts became her undoing."

9b824543-c959-447d-abba-64c9133d4307.Text: "Ah, xenos... Such wonderful creatures, shereen! Just before we came, Pointy Ears spent her days serving the governor, but the moment the wind changed, she started regaling us with tragic tales about her people's dismal fate and the world's plights... and we humans are to blame for everything, naturally!" {n}Jae clicks her tongue and glances at Yrliet with suspicion.{/n} "Although there is a grain of sense to her words, I will give her that."

d7507549-2863-41f4-a9ec-bd24b61f6426.Text: "Give just about any planetary governor a hard-enough shake, and a whole slew of heresies will come pouring out, so we are not as shocked as you might think, xenos. Regardless, if Vyatt is guilty of anything, she will not be judged based on your word."

12a6bf1f-9ab3-4b1a-b19b-a167b4dcbe2f.Text: "We call ourselves the {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Children of Asuryan{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} is another name of ours. We are the echoes of the great empire that once ruled the galaxy and created new worlds. The planet that you call Janus is one such Maiden World, the Lilaethan. A haven that our ancestors made for their kin. For many millennia, only the shadows of our predecessors lived among the ruins... until you humans came here."

7c923539-2088-403e-ab1d-160387fb10aa.Text: "We are the heirs, and we are entirely within our rights to call the Maiden World our own. However, our arrival is a tragedy, not a homecoming." {n}Sorrow seeps into Yrliet's voice.{/n} "We belong... belonged to {g|Encyclopedia:Craftworld}Craftworld{/g} Crudarach, which fell on the border of this star region. Only the providence of the merciful gods allowed us to escape the fate that befell those whose souls perished amidst the stardust along with our abode."

f54bee87-5c0a-401a-bbfb-3a7d56400013.Text: {n}Yrliet hesitates for a moment, as though preparing to say something, before finally turning away.{/n}

ab79a529-ea9e-4015-843c-0d3f2ceecdae.Text: "Destroying an Aeldari craftworld is a serious achievement. I'd like to shake the hand of whoever did it."

95a644ad-4a65-447b-9f5f-bb8f18a25f07.Text: "A destroyed craftw—" {n}Jae breaks off, and then hurriedly whispers to you,{/n} "Hey, {name}... If we get a chance, we should check this place out. Even if the craftworld was blasted to bits, anyone who finds a piece of it will make a fortune."

d55c947d-0c3b-453c-bbc5-32acfb240cd9.Text: "Disfigurements — it seems you call these 'mutations' — are the surest sign of this threat. By mutilating living forms, this malevolent power subjugates them and bends them to its will. You have seen the deformities in the faces of those who are closer to the Lilaethan's body than others — the rebels who hide under the canopy of these forests."

c35bcb95-7824-4103-b219-9fde99a3b6df.Text: "What? Vistenza Vyatt? The governor who has duly served the dynasty and the Imperium for decades? {name}, I hope you will not stand for such scurrilous slander aimed at one of your finest servants!"

2884bda4-2fe1-4528-abcc-f1775ae3264c.Text: "Elantach, your arrival has thrown my paths into disarray — and lifted the veil on the truth that had been hidden from me. While I was shadowing the humans' ruler, I failed to see the signs — signs that there was another threat looming over the Lilaethan besides the mon-keigh's deeds. The threat should be familiar to you, as it is to other intelligent species in the galaxy. We call it Sai'lanthresh. She Who Thirsts. Goddess of Chaos."

5029429b-84ad-4b7d-87f1-9e6f2fb832dd.Text: "You dispatched the enemies of Humanity admirably. You'll make an excellent sanctioned xenos."

32afcde6-6c55-43b7-8373-a22af14607ea.Text: "You just slaughtered your kin over a minor disagreement. You're in no place to talk about pride."

d9613c97-faa8-4292-b0eb-e0d1b9c54537.Text: Executed Yrliet after eradicating the other Aeldari on Janus.

d618dd33-f271-4598-9cf9-cf87ff302bfd.Text: [Kill Yrliet] "Might as well send you off along with the rest."

500ba8b4-0200-4919-a7e0-9ded34e280f8.Text: "No one forced your kin to go against me and die. Their stones are my trophies now. I earned them."

35efad18-acd0-42a0-863e-fcb0ec9dc175.Text: "It seems these stones are extremely valuable... I think I'll keep them."

e3a9d730-71cd-4188-b695-0b7239441b79.Text: "You may take the stones — I have no use for them."

6ad36ea3-9246-40f9-8886-8b0a28632b7d.Text: "There is nothing more to be done here. Time to return to the shuttle."

e63836b9-73a2-4170-bf19-d6af1def967b.Text: "Get out of my sight. I have no need for the company of a traitor."

18339c83-acef-46a7-896a-97698fa8a4d6.Text: {n}Yrliet surveys the field of battle.{/n} "May the gods guard us against pride and wandering in the vagaries of fate..."

d6cb382d-8fba-432d-ae0e-374142454ad1.Text: {n}Yrliet rewards you with a contemptuous look.{/n} "Muaran was right about one thing: your primitive consciousness prevents you from seeing anything that does not lie on the surface. My actions were not done out of a desire to gratify you."

36a7e6d6-451b-4f05-b93f-05d2564541f9.Text: "My kin have trusted in the visions of Farseers for millennia to show us our path amidst the stars. But throughout my life on Crudarach, I have too often seen knowledge of things to come — as changeable and capricious as deepwater currents — weave chains around the bodies of those who fear to enter murky waters. That is why I became an Outcast, renouncing the traditions of Crudarach and leaving its confines — to seek out my own Path."

0ddaaee9-c7c0-4263-b0eb-88e3e0c0a4e8.Text: "Your consciousness is incapable of grasping the full depth of the abyss into which Muaran lured my kin, and that is why my actions seem monstrous to you. Far from it — at least now their souls will not end up in Sai'lanthresh's maw."

70d89f8d-5bca-4663-b07e-ed530e1a0640.Text: "All right? I am overcome with grief, and anger, and anguish. But if I give free rein to my emotions, I will be drawing the thirst of She who has already entangled the Lilaethan, and, it seems, befuddled the mind of the one who was called to lead my kin."

281d6c3e-1f48-47da-b75c-bee2cff99020.Text: "Perhaps Crudarach's demise filled Muaran with so much sorrow that it poisoned his mind. Or perhaps it was hatred for the mon-keigh who desecrated the face of the Lilaethan that plunged his mind into darkness. Or perhaps... perhaps Sai'lanthresh herself was toying with the Farseer who had found himself amidst her poisoned gardens." {n}Yrliet begins speaking more quietly, though harshness breaks through in her voice at times.{/n} "I will never learn the answer to this question... but perhaps if I uncover the secret of Crudarach's demise, I might be able to lift the veil even a little on this mystery."

f693d433-44d2-4c07-9b12-25267087fa59.Text: {n}Yrliet drops to the ground like a severed vine.{/n}

11df5cf4-a8b4-4b42-ace7-afb9a3beb5cd.Text: "Thank you, elantach. I will take care of my kin."

e011f525-87b5-432a-a53b-4be6e12aa71a.Text: {n}Yrliet looks at you, tilting her head slightly.{/n} "Do not forget that the Lilaethan still needs help. Vistenza Vyatt must be slain so that the Maiden World can live."

ca86bca8-0842-4666-a750-36eaeba7c1b4.Text: {n}Yrliet flinches as though your words have wrenched her back to reality.{/n} "Very well. Then, farewell, elantach. May the stars guide each of us on our Path."

a136336a-8035-4f6d-a7fc-2c2b55296332.Text: "How can a mon-keigh know the value of another's soul? Foul, savage species..."

016a7e79-2158-4076-a1f9-f830ee65da32.Text: "Before we leave this place..." {n}Yrliet's voice trembles.{/n} "Allow me to search the bodies of the fallen, elantach. I wish to collect their spirit stones — the vessels that protect us from Sai'lanthresh's maw after our physical death. Muaran's foresight led these warriors against us — foresight that can be corrupted by ill intentions they were unaware of. Their souls are locked within these stones — don't let them perish here."

f512729c-1865-4f48-bcc9-5d9f64c0c7fb.Text: "I have come across references to xeno-artefacts of this type in archives. If Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship allows, I will examine these... trophies." {n}A velvety, curious voice pours from the vox-synth, not interrupted by a single hiss of static.{/n}

70e02ba8-97f7-4f82-a6d1-7a2b6fb8e11a.Text: "Should you grow tired of this xenos, Domin, I could take her thin bones to the temple of the Bloodspun Web. They will serve as dust beneath the feet of the righteous."

2faa8556-750a-434b-b0c1-389285260785.Text: "Your soul is full of wasted rage — and hunger for others' suffering. Perhaps Sai'lanthresh has already laid her touch upon you too."

3be9506c-27f7-46b4-9026-20842420b2d6.Text: "Sai'lanthresh's voice is dwindling. The Lilaethan is safe."

18701757-2e72-45ec-a1e7-f2faf9a3415f.Text: "This place must be cleansed. Burn it, mon-keigh."

62baefc9-c9ab-4bb1-a9f9-6524434f2710.Text: "We have fulfilled the terms of the agreement. Do not forget what you promised us, mon-keigh."

5fa81dc3-0b89-451d-ada1-0e364eb5ca4e.Text: "Such an important occasion — a visit from a Rogue Trader — marred by such an unpleasant incident..."

edce90e4-f316-4d05-98aa-4a1f480d3e7f.Text: "House Grantis has never inspired respect or trust. I have no doubt that it was they who brought the treacherous servants into the estate!"

d6698d8d-7981-4309-8473-e2c40f7f49a5.Text: An ornate fireplace decorated with a bas-relief depicting past governors from House Vyatt.

21a9a808-70f8-4c0c-955f-99ba54fa51a9.Text: The ornate fireplace depicting past governors from House Vyatt cannot hide from your keen gaze the turning mechanism that opens a secret passage.

e93f7e05-f278-4daa-a19f-519098fef92e.Text: "What was that? I didn't receive any orders..."

1c10b0ff-b56f-4e45-b808-ba286e09980d.Text: "Governor... What happened to the governor? Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"

f16ba546-d89d-4650-a570-962e99fc8b26.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you are safe! What a relief!"

8af68ed1-13e8-40ba-8795-daafc91d23c6.Text: "You need only say the word and I will oblige!"

35cb6978-7a64-462f-a261-bf14361578e7.Text: "I want to speak to the governor alone."

a4030d1a-1139-4d7f-be30-e42de4e63e3e.Text: "My entourage will accompany me in my meeting with the governor."

6a2707a2-60c0-414f-8445-1b0a8d9543a0.Text: "I don't want to waste time on this right now."

a66bd928-a082-46be-a6e1-4596abc60ffc.Text: {n}The door guard bows obsequiously.{/n} "{mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius, we are most delighted to welcome you as our guest! Would Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} prefer to speak to the governor alone or with your entourage?"

341990ed-cace-434c-beb2-36422fc9e530.Text: {n}Upon seeing you, the guard at the door lets out a frightened yelp and doubles over into a low bow.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the Most Honourable {name} von Valancius! The governor is awaiting you in her office, where she is protected by walls and guards. Would you prefer to meet with her alone or with your entourage?"

7e17fabd-3a2a-486a-85c0-28bc67c17c97.Text: {n}The guard at the door bows to you, shaking from head to toe.{/n} "How may I serve, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"

35c141e4-458e-494e-ac8a-dce39a6e83f9.Text: "I will get to the bottom of this. I'm sure the rebels will have something to say to the {mf|master|mistress} of their world."

e8b56c65-34c2-4b13-b8cc-30488fab73b0.Text: "Well, if there are no competent people to be found on Janus, I shall have to handle this myself."

52449e81-a7d6-46be-a970-8eac7ff9f651.Text: [Attack] "Yes, and the first order of business is disposing of inadequate servants!"

716ceb4b-44d0-4343-bb25-f8ed8082ae95.Text: "Your local fuss is of no concern to me. I am in urgent need of provisions from Janus."

432c85e4-3ac0-4de4-b6a0-c6f176d9069f.Text: "Tripled tithes to make up for my lost profits — that will be enough."

d7a09683-a92a-4cb2-b78e-25414bdb4b04.Text: "Where did you go in the middle of the fight? Was that some kind of sorcery?"

3dcebce2-1240-49c8-9985-0f509680da72.Text: "I don't care about your apologies. I could have been killed!"

58cfd27f-a9eb-4e77-92e8-2cb234df8d09.Text: "A couple of crates of the finest Janusian amasec will do for an apology, Madam Governor."

e4ee443e-f04b-47a4-af9b-632567aa9f8d.Text: "Xenos were the ones behind the rebellions. They're dead now."

df370c84-585e-4b8a-bad2-79d98f4840e0.Text: "I expect my subjects to face danger shoulder to shoulder with me. Consider that next time before you press the button."

cf31bc07-f033-40ac-86ba-1aa0d011e992.Text: "Such intriguing technology. I wouldn't say no to something like that."

7cc652f0-6d4b-4f10-8c1f-89429047de0e.Text: "Xenos were responsible for the uprisings. I let them live."

a48c1b28-2705-417a-9c7a-114f076f58c2.Text: "The rebels were being manipulated by xenos. I wiped out those foul aliens, but I let the humans live."

b5a51b1f-af2a-4895-a62b-8d5a725da0d5.Text: "Are you aware of the reasons for the rebellion?"

ff469b5a-6223-454c-9a51-e376308b3d08.Text: "I'm not interested in your excuses. Dealing with the rebels is your direct responsibility."

27deea16-c6eb-4756-9db5-d886eaa1822c.Text: "You stand accused of worshipping the Ruinous Powers, Vistenza."

8e307a41-1bdd-401a-952e-a16638be00c5.Text: "I'd like to get back to talking about foodstuff supplies from Janus."

ff66fa75-dbe8-4eb7-bd8c-b85c8e5d7c61.Text: "Well, I'll track down these elusive fugitives myself. As for you, Vistenza, you will not be permitted to fail again. I am removing you from your post as governor of this planet and I am placing you under arrest. When I have finished with the rebels, I'll decide what to do with you."

7717ff8a-0ee4-4fa6-8387-cb30a90ca820.Text: "I've already heard enough, Vistenza. But if you wish me to repeat myself — we know that your loyalty lies with the Ruinous Powers."

b24ad61f-a1d9-4954-9339-c409ee51b746.Text: "You are not saving Janus or improving it, Vistenza. You are destroying this world with your own hands."

3dd5bebb-d8ca-46cd-81b8-52241ff20ac8.Text: "I won't be able to change your mind, will I? Then I won't try."

4904e9a3-f8e2-4a56-b3a2-1e677563635f.Text: "This world possesses a soul. A soul that your 'patron' is trying to destroy, and without which Janus will become barren."

9e7735e8-69e9-4220-a09b-28a0ff8769ac.Text: "Yrliet's predecessor. Did you know another xenos came to you before Yrliet? Your retinue hid his coming from you so they could capture and sacrifice him."

06c5f3d5-28c7-4532-aecb-a23e30f4a18c.Text: "When was the last time you left the estate, Vistenza? Take one look at the jungles of Janus and you'll see that whatever you may have thought you were doing for the good of the planet, you are actually killing it!"

7d9bac0b-0ebc-450f-b31b-1e6290465b89.Text: "The Tech-Priest mentioned ancient ruins belonging to the xenos."

0d0b0d6d-ab76-4999-baf1-04bb91a02c24.Text: "You neglected to mention the strange changes in the planet's flora and fauna."

100d851a-cf23-4843-83ea-039fec51836d.Text: "How much more proof do you need, Vistenza? That's enough! Renounce that vile sorcery while there is still hope!"

d41c1211-abf7-4a2d-a03c-5d9d6d6f16f7.Text: [Attack] "My reason tells me it is safer to kill you after all. Sorry, it's nothing personal."

f6417606-b88d-495e-bf88-a7fd941ac15b.Text: "I have heard enough. Continue on as you have been, Vistenza — let the powers under your control benefit the von Valancius dynasty."

73b75331-77e4-423a-8ada-166dada1fc02.Text: "It is beneath the dignity of a governor to squirm so pathetically, Vistenza."

4794e68f-aeef-4f02-b72e-842989130cea.Text: "You dare to lie to me, Vistenza?"

aa51b33b-e97a-4768-a131-442c23168fe5.Text: Approved of Vistenza Vyatt's heretical deeds.

690345cb-3d40-4978-b6e9-0c9354197952.Text: "I have nothing to reproach you for. As long as the tithes are flowing into the Imperium's coffers and my own, I see no problem."

59035b96-80cf-40dd-b5d3-b0d04dbabe7b.Text: "What is the situation on the planet?"

77af1aaa-dfbd-4299-a33f-188bfac0aa14.Text: "You want me to go off and catch some rebels for you?"

ef2b3fc8-58c2-417d-800b-97ae8f2360b2.Text: Did not accuse Vistenza Vyatt of heresy.

80706489-daff-4f13-af9b-943dfbd0b6ee.Text: "Everyone has their secrets, I suppose. Everything between us can remain as it was."

8cf2866e-ddc0-4105-b61e-d7d7bd9cc1a0.Text: [Attack] "I'm sick of your games and secrecy. Die!"

6c453a1a-1d3e-45f7-b2d9-ee9a1682e875.Text: Sentenced Vistenza Vyatt to death for her heretical deeds.

7986dfb1-0d3d-4dda-a5ed-6b87d2038101.Text: Attacked Vistenza Vyatt upon exposing her heretical deeds.

762ff6bf-89c9-43fd-a4bd-cab2147b276f.Text: "I will let you live and remain in your post, Vistenza, under one condition: stop trying to destroy the World Spirit of Janus. I will not tolerate a parasite on my world."

7ec97b41-94a8-44ec-afc8-f938920c0574.Text: "Your words carry the ring of truth. Everything can remain as it was before."

ce0fa53d-f149-41b2-8020-aa8170fefcc2.Text: "I promise you, Governor, I will hunt down the seeds of rebellion and heresy on your planet and burn them to ash."

a98306fd-6638-4465-a3f5-be185ce437a8.Text: "You are forcing settlements to pay their tithes in human bodies."

4c283241-c6f7-409e-9101-1c6d63469f5e.Text: "Rumours have reached me about oddities among Janus's population..."

62a411a9-b676-47cb-b6eb-2bb7dce0e07e.Text: "You are forgiven. You may return to your duties."

437b81e2-ba04-4741-9de8-d8f4f9644f40.Text: "One of your wardens helped us in battle. A superb shot. Who was it?"

7f78b6e5-b4fb-477b-b555-1a909fcbabbc.Text: "Death, my dear. Did you really think there could be any other outcome?"

4fe2506e-4fdd-4e01-89f0-5876dea0035a.Text: "Let's not waste time on meaningless chatter, Vistenza. You are a servant of the Archenemy."

e33f0ba5-7246-4974-b0cf-07c9ed0109b8.Text: "A few dozen lashes will suffice. I'll leave you to make the arrangements. Once I receive the pict-report, you may return to your post."

60402842-3de4-46f5-917f-303a3a9f5b10.Text: "Even for an agri-world in the back of beyond, this place is a real dump. What do you all do here for fun — when you have free time, that is?"

fc32d5d7-bb66-4525-ac47-24a300f8a91c.Text: "Everything, Vistenza. I know everything. And now you have one chance to beg for mercy."

845cf68a-586c-485e-b5da-0c40fd2df878.Text: "Then again... let's just leave things as they are."

4a063fbd-a06b-46cb-b3c9-f5f7b122fcf3.Text: "Footfall Station is on the verge of starvation. Can Janus supply the people there with provisions?"

8f9eba69-e49b-448e-b64f-4200fa2443b9.Text: "The strongest. I no longer have need of you, Vistenza."

4a6a6731-f829-4f11-9bdf-2c92e0f9fea9.Text: "Crushing that scum is your responsibility. You will be able to manage that, I trust?"

7ebd96c1-5824-4041-83d3-7db4b1a9fe25.Text: Made Vistenza Vyatt realise that she had been manipulated by the Ruinous Powers.

381b7537-ab79-437a-9466-ad046c739a05.Text: "The will of Humanity, or the will of the Ruinous Powers? Vistenza, you are a strong ruler with exceptional aptitude and a talent for making people see things only as you wish. Have you never considered the possibility that someone could do the same to you?"

3aaf19c8-6440-4783-9f4f-56769513b650.Text: "With your incompetence, you dishonour the very status of governor. In the name of the Emperor, I sentence you to death."

b745f441-cda8-4aa1-b825-1c2b880ac6d1.Text: [Smile condescendingly] "Ah, I can see that you have not been to any half-decent parlours, Vistenza. Your ability to maintain a genteel facade is sorely lacking..."

230bf7d5-f4a7-4186-952c-ba83cf66bd42.Text: "I was recently on Thassera and saw laceraxes there. Those beasts were imported from Janus, weren't they?"

f1ba7ef2-d3b0-42f4-9750-0673c03dba12.Text: [Nod toward her companion] "Who is this person standing next to you?"

42b082b9-f6e4-487d-b637-86bb6cd37726.Text: [Attack] "I'm not going to waste my breath trying to persuade you. It's time to retire the Vyatt line!"

f8770532-1971-4520-94e4-0815818111a2.Text: "Never mind. I'd like to get back to talking about foodstuff supplies from Janus."

3e9c3f24-53a5-419f-b07a-6f7764262677.Text: "You will immediately put to death everyone connected with your sorcery, and you will strike this vile chapter from your mind forever! This is an order from your overlord, Vistenza!"

b932dc05-34aa-49c3-8ee9-eea26b92ddf3.Text: "Reprehensible stunt? I thought firing at moving targets was part of the ceremony!"

8da04fa4-8934-42e9-9143-9f37b77cfe78.Text: "You can stop apologising, Vistenza. I'm not offended."

9fcb4664-77a9-4e54-89c5-e43523e56144.Text: "That is not your concern, Vistenza. You have a far worse problem to deal with."

84cdaffc-3942-42da-87ce-3a5a4ffd830f.Text: "Can Janus fulfil its foodstuff supplies under current conditions?"

fed05b30-160b-49ef-b636-3b3839cc4d16.Text: {n}Vistenza Janus Vyatt ab Aram af Koronus is furiously swiping at a {g|Encyclopedia:Dataslate}data-slate{/g}, issuing commands into a gilded {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}. Upon seeing you, she hurriedly puts away her devices, smooths her skirt, and drops into a deep curtsy.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, accept my abject apologies for the reprehensible stunt that spoiled the reception! Even in my worst nightmares, I could never have imagined—"

62c313b0-15a1-441f-8418-0ee3d3573864.Text: "Have you really, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? And what have you learned?"

6f7b2265-daf5-4241-a581-2e75873e8e53.Text: "Yrliet!" {n}Vistenza exclaims breathlessly.{/n} "How dare you, you filthy vermin! I will have you flayed for that outburst! Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, what is going on?"

b79ba5a6-2c76-4692-a0d7-5e3aa7cf824a.Text: "This world was once a wild planet, full of xenobeasts and utterly unsuitable for growing anything. To this day, despite our best efforts, Janus regularly rebels against us. Earthquakes, tsunamis, the emergence of new pests and weeds that invade the arable land... sometimes I cannot help but think that this world is endowed with consciousness — the consciousness of a capricious and stubborn child who likes to spoil everything that we have achieved!"

572525a1-66e8-4b30-876c-3219d59e276f.Text: "How refreshingly novel — the rich treating the common folk like dirt and coating it all with the best intentions." {n}Jae's usual honeyed voice now grates like rusted metal.{/n}

ffb1a7ff-9a00-4431-b793-19185f75d246.Text: "You forget yourself, Proctor! It is not for you to accuse or condemn me in {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}'s presence!" {n}The governor gives you an entreating look.{/n} "Please, do not let this... this abuse stand!"

67c57b2a-9df3-4688-97e3-3dda85e62d39.Text: {n}Slanting a look at Pasqal, Idira remarks lightly:{/n} "Looks like the sciences aren't only the preserve of the Adeptus Mechanicus. Doesn't that infringe on the authority of the esteemed Magos?"

ef1d6228-7358-4f07-a97e-c7c1b9651f3c.Text: "This statement is true. But who do you suppose were her teachers? The Adeptus Mechanicus. All knowledge flows from us."

824dc859-f442-44c2-b318-a17de640a3a7.Text: {n}Cassia nods in understanding.{/n} "Theobald and Felek tried to limit the effect my powers had on the lowborn servants of Eurac V. The station's laboratorums ran experiments on those who had the misfortune of losing their minds because of my gift. These tests increased our servants' lifespan... and then they joined Felek's side."

4563807a-44dd-4d1c-8257-502ac76ae7df.Text: "Oh, my dear governor, the only truly angelic voice on this world is going to roll like thunder right about..."

2a325d22-76fd-4089-8679-9407b0662c23.Text: "A gang of serfs from the household of one of the nobles invited to the ceremony. All those involved are being interrogated as we speak." {n}Vistenza purses her lips.{/n} "They could not have arranged all this without help from within the estate... that is to say, they are merely carrying out orders. As for the true culprits behind this, I fear they will not be found on the premises."

886b14fe-4246-4be3-af1d-65aff298c4c7.Text: {n}The governor, trembling all over, bows her head even lower{/n}. "I assure you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I would never... I beg you, give me the chance to prove my loyalty and explain myself..."

2fca151d-1efb-4391-9577-a610ccc0088d.Text: "...now. Like honey to one's ears, wouldn't you agree?"

d292b461-1882-49ab-a1eb-9af8223f5942.Text: {n}Vistenza sighs and throws up her hands.{/n} "Oh, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, it would give me great pleasure to immediately demonstrate the productive might of Janus to you... but there are some issues."

758f0b5a-52de-456b-b786-ed6813372622.Text: "Oh, they have their reasons, of course. Insufficient freedoms, restricted movement, disputes with local authorities... and those are only the ones that can be taken even slightly seriously. People do not like restrictions — especially if their ruler has already shown a certain leniency toward the rabble in the hope of encouraging greater productivity. There are those who confuse loyalty with weakness."

35bdd6b0-775d-4bda-a51b-a14c7e704609.Text: "Greetings, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! How may I be of assistance?"

017dbacf-630b-4508-9e3f-0483f2501148.Text: {n}Vistenza inclines her head with dignity.{/n} "In troubled times, we rely not on the Emperor's goodwill alone, but on our own abilities as well."

2ca117eb-ee95-4626-a2b3-3038f622625e.Text: "You must be referring to Yrliet, our chief ally in the struggle against the rebels. I have turned a blind eye to her horrific mutations given the undoubted advantages she brings. You see, Yrliet comes from the local degenerate stock of this world and knows Janus like the back of her hand, so she has provided several leads as to where we can find bases and secret storehouses. Although I admit that at times I am tempted to send her away from the estate — her unnaturalness means that speaking with her always leaves me feeling uneasy. Such a gaunt, unfeminine figure, and so tall..."

7757ad89-41ed-4992-be9e-e105731db314.Text: {n}Heinrix's expression shifts.{/n} "Did I hear you correctly, Governor Vyatt: you have a mysterious mutant on your estate at this very moment? One of prodigious height, slight build, and with a supernatural talent for shooting? Did the arrival of this helper never give you pause for thought?"

b470f9d4-a679-49bc-8e5b-f3e358ad00aa.Text: "Allow me to make myself clear: to refuse Yrliet's help in our circumstances would have been incredibly rash. Yes, mutants are creatures abhorrent to the Emperor and they should be exterminated, but sometimes Humanity makes exceptions for those who can serve the Imperium..."

cdff8c39-fe72-4261-8cb4-fd526d39f3d9.Text: "If you wish to speak to Yrliet, you will find her outside in the orangery, most likely by the gazebo. She prefers to keep her distance from others."

b17a0ba7-ea75-4ac2-af6c-d2f74e28d9d0.Text: "I am not concerned that your aide is a mutant. I am far more concerned that she may be nothing of the sort." {n}Heinrix turns to you.{/n} "{name}? I would like to meet this helper of Governor Vyatt's without delay. Out of professional interest."

53f06f91-8f5b-4777-9044-848ce241d58f.Text: "Of course, you are entitled to insist that the conflict be resolved locally. According to my council's report, perhaps in a couple of years... when the security services have been re-equipped and a surveillance void station has been established on the orbit... we can, attacks notwithstanding, produce enough to satisfy the tithe collectors." {n}Vistenza sighs.{/n} "No doubt this answer displeases you. I do understand. But with our resources, it is the most likely scenario."

844a9f26-f35b-4d51-8b31-57f0ec9d05bf.Text: "Considering what has occurred, your visit is a true blessing. You see, Janus does not have its own fleet. We could organise a planet-wide search, if we had ships at our disposal... ships like yours, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Perhaps you will find a way to support your subjects in their hour of need? I'm sure even approximate coordinates would be sufficient to have the ground forces and ship's crew work together to hunt down the enemy!"

526df193-d1ee-487a-b134-22af2fb3d45e.Text: {n}Vistenza lets out a ragged gasp as though she has been punched in the stomach.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! But... But I have served your dynasty faithfully and honestly, I have worked tirelessly to tame this unruly planet..." {n}She stops herself from speaking any further and nods.{/n} "A-as you wish."

e1afb5ea-9fc9-49d7-8b13-9585f02a15f8.Text: "Enough, mon-keigh!" {n}Yrliet raises her weapon.{/n} "Kaela Mensha, guide my hand as it crushes evil!"

ae3abbf8-f7de-43ae-8029-3a4fed5d5f72.Text: "I, as well as my retinue, are at your service. My secretary is checking the staff as we speak and removing all traces of the attack from the estate. An esteemed Magos, who is responsible for agronomic efforts on the planet, is also here — he happened to be visiting this week to deliver his personal report. And, of course, there is my aide in the war against the rebels, Yrliet. I have no doubt she will be delighted to share her knowledge of Janus with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"

212206d9-926f-4bfa-8f97-c709e1df2c83.Text: "But I do have something to reproach her for," {n}says Argenta, her voice filled with cold fury.{/n} "No mercy to servants of the Archenemy!"

c0f795dc-76fd-4153-b7f5-ff6c926f7668.Text: {n}Vistenza's eyes narrow.{/n} "Forgive me for what I am about to say, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but you're lying! I am not blind — I can see how Janus is changing, how it is becoming tamer, more submissive to the will of Humanity!"

9dc64b1b-d5c1-4ff2-ac6a-6d0b11babbb6.Text: "Mainly, Helican flint corn and red turnip. Apart from that, in the southern hemisphere we have set aside vast tracts of land for the {g|Encyclopedia:Grox}grox{/g} population. And, of course, I cannot fail to mention the several thousand acres of tilled land given over to cultivating fermentable fruit. For personal use and limited export."

61353dae-60a6-4c8b-b752-9715b850ad07.Text: "Where did you hear that? Yes, it's true that from time to time I put on executions for a small circle of friends... Wait, I recall my confidante seeking permission to use the salon for some gathering or other. I thought she meant ideological discussions, not sacrifices!"

4d3cb0fc-426b-4264-8ee0-945c4aa14d38.Text: "What is it you want me to agree with, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? That my transformation of Janus has been for nothing? Never!"

742dfcf1-cb12-4c30-888a-625f3a3d8f00.Text: "I know to what you're referring — strange structures of an unknown material. For the prevention of any unfortunate accidents, I ordered the area to be declared out of bounds for all. Some things are better off left under a thick layer of dirt, beyond the grasp of even the enlightened minds of the Adeptus Mechanicus."

44c9050b-9363-4444-904d-316f7ee11f72.Text: "Magos Vinzelex is a very wise man, but his fixation on evolutionary processes seems a little extreme to me. Janus was heavily cultivated: forests were cleared and mountains razed across half of the planet. It is no surprise that we are still noticing the consequences of those changes."

4ff0babc-0e34-4bdc-8989-1c47821e5efc.Text: "It's possible that the plant mutations are connected to waste run-off from the harvesting equipment. And the changes in wildlife behaviour could be a reaction to the expansion of the cultivated area." {n}Vistenza shakes her head with a laugh.{/n} "Are you surprised by my knowledge of the topic? Our whole dynasty has dedicated itself to taming Janus, this plentiful yet stubborn planet. Every member of the Vyatt bloodline is versed in the fundamentals of planetary engineering — and its consequences."

e36ee909-56d9-4b96-8235-2ffe97cc5406.Text: "That is enough, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I simply don't know what to make of your slavish adherence to this absurd notion! Really now, let us forget all this and return to discussing more serious matters..."

9d5991e1-81e1-405b-bcf6-88ef875fc159.Text: {n}Vistenza bends down in a deep curtsy.{/n} "I knew you were a {mf|man|woman} of reason, one who values loyal subjects. Long live the alliance of Vyatt and von Valancius!"

ec1b7156-ed6e-4f01-a77e-e3b87b16fd0a.Text: {n}Vistenza clenches her teeth so hard you hear a crack.{/n} "I, daughter of House Vyatt, Governor of Janus, and citizen of the Imperium, serve no one other than the Emperor and the von Valancius dynasty! And what... what you are accusing me of... is merely a tool at my disposal! A tool that I have the power and courage to use! Do you think ordinary methods would have been enough to tame this demented planet? No! My family struggled for decades to subdue Janus once and for all, and it was all in vain!"

32d84d7e-2902-4229-a9d1-bd68e2f57566.Text: {n}Vistenza wrinkles her nose.{/n} "I say this with infinite respect, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but your insolence is beginning to try even my patience."

aa7d1748-e6ef-4f13-bdaa-993a14c3f31a.Text: "But loyal servants of those families who have resided on Janus for centuries helped me to unlock a new source of power. Ancient knowledge secretly passed down from generation to generation, accessible to a select few, and which grants power over nature itself. How could I reject it? How could I undo all the work of my predecessors, who were entrusted with Janus, who faithfully served the von Valancius dynasty, and who with a madman's obsessiveness hewed this rock into a stunning diamond? Two days spent among the initiated was enough for me to start hearing the voices of angels in my ears — angels who gifted me the keys to conquering this world!"

d395d4be-ac36-4f32-99c7-5d586579f968.Text: "Not quite, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. My wardens are crushing the lowly saboteurs across the planet relentlessly, {name}, but it will be for naught unless their nests are destroyed. Someone is controlling the riffraff who are perishing in thoughtless escapades such as the one we witnessed today, and that someone could be hiding anywhere! You have resources and capabilities at your disposal the likes of which I could never hope to possess! Your ship alone is an unequalled asset for tracking down criminals beyond the borders of my influence."

22784dd9-f8c8-4c14-b779-91341b400cdf.Text: "If any of those who attacked the estate had survived, then perhaps they could have been a valuable source of information... but you made an example of them for the rest of the foolish rabble." {n}Vistenza glances at the vox.{/n} "Incidentally, I did overhear the wardens talking about some kind of stranger in the area. Besides that, we still do not know who let those reprobates into the estate — the person who did it might also know something."

36d977a4-39a9-4342-89e8-73355549fa67.Text: "Much improved. My people are systematically purging settlements of any surviving rebels, and the nobility are doing everything possible to move beyond this dark page in our world's history and regain their proper good cheer — a crucial component for the prosperity of our precious Janus."

d298474b-eda8-46b5-abbf-ec3150553f5b.Text: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Your wisdom and indulgence toward your inferiors do you credit as a member of the von Valancius dynasty."

8e74d898-08af-48f3-96b0-0dfa44d19b56.Text: {n}Vistenza folds her arms.{/n} "I am pleased to hear that you have seen reason, Rogue Trader. I know this planet like the back of my head. Just a little further, and I will bend it completely to my will."

f3e95298-8a2a-4660-b820-b1e1ea5505ae.Text: "You made a mistake in thinking that anyone would come to your aid on my world! Servants, to me!"

833643b1-8993-4eb3-bcef-71368825c528.Text: "I will issue all the necessary instructions. Supply shipments will begin today, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. And tithes that have been withheld due to the recent difficulties will be paid in the coming days."

0729a2e6-9e54-48a4-8587-cbeab341b2b6.Text: {n}Vistenza's smile is extinguished like a candle in the wind.{/n} "You... you wouldn't dare... it's my life's work..." {n}The governor balls up her fists, before mastering herself. Her smile is almost perfect in its imitation of sincerity.{/n} "Well. Even a wan life is better than a vibrant death. I promise to find a new... pastime for myself."

b355ef09-0c5f-4c4d-b1d1-c5956b22aa53.Text: "Very prudent, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. And as for the slanderers... I presume you will be willing to provide my people with the coordinates of the hole where those repulsive rats are hiding?"

dd8ec992-7c08-4009-a821-8eeadd7ae344.Text: "Several months ago, uprisings broke out on Janus. I was not even notified at first: griping worms are for wardens to worry about. Alas, I only learned of what was happening after the miscreants began targeting noble families." {n}Vistenza shakes her head.{/n} "And then it became apparent that what the Administratum's accounts had referred to as 'unrest,' were in fact organised attacks on infrastructure and society leaders!"

718abf54-5252-4e13-a6b1-5ff8010431f0.Text: "They have already brought 13 agri-complexes to a halt and have now moved on to assassination attempts. My wardens are doggedly tracking down the rebels, but their leaders are slipping from our grasp yet again."

4d32d26c-0a7d-4e1e-aa16-f4aa24cc0828.Text: {n}Concern appears in Vistenza's eyes.{/n} "The r-resolve and valour of the von Valancius dynasty know no bounds. I am immeasurably thankful for your help!"

865bcd23-580f-4da5-84f5-9406eb268562.Text: "What? Really, {name}, you speak as if you actually believe the claims of those wretched peasants... I do not ask anyone to pay the tithes in human bodies. I am reducing the burden on the settlements which have suffered as a result of unsuccessful experiments involving enriched food, and I'm gathering the worst-affected subjects, those who are no longer capable of work, for further study. Some among my circle would call such concern for the underclass a weakness. A weakness which may have incited rebellion among the emboldened rabble."

0bd809b7-2e39-4982-87b1-b93bb4c9001c.Text: "I don't deny it — some of our experiments exact a higher toll on the population than others... You see, recently one of the noble families of Janus has taken on the difficult task of enhancing the attributes of our workers. So far, it has involved introducing experimental supplements to their food and mental conditioning in monitored settlements. Sometimes procedures are disrupted and part of the population suffers from side effects... The specialists of the Gravaz family would be better placed to inform you on this topic, but alas, they are currently engaged in the field."

51492d5d-e4a3-4586-9bd4-dbe769c00526.Text: "Yes and no, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. If the question is: can such an expansive and fertile world as this one feed a few thousand void rats? Of course it can — we lose more provisions to gnawing pests every cycle than those on Footfall could eat in their entire lives. But can we ship said provisions to Footfall? Not a chance."

72cb378c-6510-4385-834d-d20f38aed9d0.Text: "Any cargo shuttle that leaves the surface will be a target for attack — the rebels will not hesitate to bring it down, sending flaming debris over the capital. Our silos could become targets for sabotage — food could be poisoned or mined. The logistics of transporting supplies to Footfall will only be possible once the uprising has been completely crushed."

8cbdf9d2-ae4b-415b-9c46-5f77d9732273.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox emits a pensive hiss:{/n} "Behold, proof of why Knowledge must remain in the hands of the worthy.
