7ae950e7-c91b-499c-9854-e1a8b2ecdd37.Text: "Allow us, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. This rat has had free rein on the estate for long enough. We'll take care of the problem in just a minute — but please step back from the building."

dffdf0fb-f7db-4f8b-bd4f-e28d202841ba.Text: {n}The rebel looks at you in bewilderment, and then bows low before you. When he speaks, his voice trembles:{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... thank you! Thank you for this kindness... I never thought I'd survive this..."

3e835b46-9bd3-46a5-93a1-eb49639771af.Text: {n}The door looks solid and formidable, but you notice dark marks on the hinges — a sure sign that the material is degraded. The lock doesn't look new either — with a suitable tool, it could easily be opened.{/n}

13f0b50f-0e4b-4982-9dce-8697532294f8.Text: "I've never been in their camp — none of us have. Only the chief saw one person from their base: he came a few times, bringing weapons and orders — he said he represented a greater force than we could imagine... and he said that the governor's dogs will pay for their reprisals in the settlements. But that's not where they're hidden — they keep their distance from ordinary folks."

64cb4972-7ed4-4da8-a8c2-758f54e488ef.Text: {n}The young man, practically a boy, falls to his knees and stretches out his bloody hands toward you. His clothes are burned on one side and grimy with baked-in blood.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, have mercy! You are the sovereign of this planet! Only you have the power to save us!"

5997c88f-79f9-4a63-b2a5-37d1a66df979.Text: "She... she's turned the whole world into a slaughterhouse! People are rounded up like {g|Encyclopedia:Grox}grox{/g} from the settlements, supposedly to go to the palace, and they're never seen again! Her servants pour something over the fields and then people lose their minds — they start hearing voices and seeing evil spirits! And while we're dying, she's sitting behind her white walls and feasting on our bones!"

0949609c-1462-4bc7-8165-43f24fe6c020.Text: "You... you can't just stand aside while your vassals are destroying your worlds! The governor is doing whatever she wants! Rounding up families, razing whole settlements!"

85637b13-3139-4189-94b7-66deda63e17e.Text: "Yes! Others are going feral and attacking their loved ones... And then there's..." {n}The boy lowers his voice.{/n} "People say that in some settlements... well... they've stopped upholding the law altogether. Imperial law, and... and... the law of basic, human decency. People are turning into animals."

0ea54150-b894-47e7-bcf3-1f0fc81b7d0b.Text: "We have it all worked out so that if anyone gets caught, the others aren't caught with them. But I swiped the chief's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}... I thought, after I killed the governor, I could use the message coordinates to find the base and hide out there..." {n}The boy retrieves a vox from his pocket and holds it out to you with a shaking hand.{/n} "That's everything I know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

2f3cb4f1-bfc3-4e03-a1eb-265f3359941e.Text: "Youth is a time of recklessness. I heard that said more than once in the Schola Progenium and during my novitiate. But youth is also a time of directness! Let us listen to this young man before we judge him."

a8bb703b-4d42-4cd7-944c-19cb20f8b04e.Text: "I was taught that peasants have a tendency to exaggerate their suffering due to sloth and weakness of spirit. But this young man... Vermilion thorns pierce every centimetre of his body, and grey shackles bind his hands, feet, and neck... There are no lies in his words. Only terror and desperation without end."

5bed5191-f364-4e85-9637-858213751098.Text: {n}Yrliet's face twists.{/n} "Sacrifices, madness, pain, and death... even in so primitive a society as this, such rites seem... senseless, not worthy of such efforts. What is this, a random quirk of nature, or something darker?"

a8b63f25-b786-4b0f-9303-ccbf859570b5.Text: {n}Idira looks at Argenta a little confused, as if she did not expect such gentleness from her.{/n} "I agree with the sister here. People don't become rebels because everything in their lives is rosy. And the kid's green as grass, it'd be a shame to kill him for nothing... Something is wrong on Janus, I can feel it — maybe he can shed some light on what's going on."

246b89d3-80e0-4304-a2a4-24260367afad.Text: "This is not sufficient evidence for a proper accusation, but the Arbites doctrine extols vigilance. I propose we verify whether this is disinformation that the leaders of the rebellion are feeding to their underlings, or genuine testimony."

4d64cc6d-27d4-4bbe-b80d-41ae1e780ca5.Text: "I want to talk to the person inside."

cbec1f4d-b4fc-4daf-89a9-98b4646b461f.Text: "You are obviously busy. I won't disturb you further."

48d7f066-8170-4da1-9a25-d2afbc51e6f6.Text: "All right, fine. I'll take a look around after you've finished up."

accc3d0b-e628-4a05-8067-030e739d4e3d.Text: "You dare to question me? Out of my way."

1fc6aa87-78c8-41fd-bcbb-b7289ee9a803.Text: "I want to solve this problem without too much blood or fuss."

75398481-40bf-48c0-a58a-e3795a057830.Text: Let the young rebel on Janus go.

d890819e-9785-4d6f-8d6f-2fcdd3d9caed.Text: "Escort this man safely to the perimeter of the estate. He is free to go."

d02e66cf-383b-4e75-8211-b315ecaba943.Text: Ordered that the young rebel on Janus be arrested.

5dec22b6-067d-4728-82d0-f38139b1c305.Text: "This man is now under my protection. See to it that he is held safely in custody until his fate is decided by a fair trial."

d38c23dc-4473-468d-a410-c2702207b756.Text: Ordered that the young rebel on Janus be flayed.

0bbdb7c8-e31c-4509-943c-65e0e24e00f2.Text: "Make an example of this scum. Publicly flay him and string up his corpse outside his family home as a warning. If anyone tries to remove it — shoot them."

c3acf6b8-dd31-4856-8a7f-fcfea8bf33da.Text: Ordered that the young rebel on Janus be servitorised.

53e10ed9-1dbe-46bb-9c8f-6a0d40f1fb95.Text: "This man will serve Janus yet. Consult your advisors and see to it that this rebel is made into a useful servitor."

7369c623-e235-4dd4-a384-3aec543af87a.Text: {n}A hulking man dressed in a uniform marking him out as an officer of the gubernatorial wardens is closely monitoring his subordinates as they surround the building. Sensing your approach, he whips around, his face going pale, and he offers a low bow.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Please, do not stray too close to the building. One of the terrorists from today's attack has holed himself up in there. He could be dangerous."

48f1518d-c3f2-41a0-9fd5-84f76c07ba31.Text: {n}The officer tugs nervously at his collar, which appears to have suddenly become too tight for his comfort.{/n} "W-we will fix this. Right away, I swear it on the Throne!"

24b1cbdf-2b43-4909-93b1-a252b98075a9.Text: "I have only one question, officer — why have you not already done it? The Rogue Trader is here, and the longer you delay, the more you put {mf|his|her} life needlessly at risk!"

e33c2135-f084-4d30-98b1-f26db6b64800.Text: {n}The officer flinches slightly at Abelard's snarl.{/n} "It is inexcusable, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! The barrels of poison were only just delivered... But we're... we're ready to begin now!"

af6ba13a-f8b3-4f2e-953e-2a85396e6fd7.Text: "Ready to report, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We conducted a sweep of the area after the attack. All of the assassins were arrested or neutralised except for one..." {n}The officer scowls darkly.{/n} "He's sealed himself inside. He already injured two wardens who tried to reach him. But there's no need to worry — we'll poison him and clear the last dregs of dirt from the estate."

077136b2-5013-4a4c-a602-d33341e9d148.Text: {n}The officer's brow furrows.{/n} "To tell the truth, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I'm more concerned with clearing the area right now than with his identity. We're not expecting to get any valuable intel from him — unless we find something on his corpse after we've done our job."

d807edd4-d929-4c7b-b9b1-794ec1f38da2.Text: "I am the madam governor's security officer. I regret that you had to witness today's incident, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I assure you, nothing of the sort will ever happen again."

8e55a922-649a-4e47-9549-f7ec3eb38bec.Text: "Are you sure? It's not exactly safe, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The officer's eyes involuntarily sweep over you, sizing you up.{/n}

c17ca61c-3f4d-4a0b-9043-0885396c88a2.Text: {n}The officer seems to remember himself and offers another low bow.{/n} "Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Act as you see fit!" {n}At the officer's signal, the other wardens take a deferential step back, clearing your path to the door.{/n}

ed583645-5924-40f6-8514-37be2429833f.Text: "We will be finished in just a few minutes." {n}The officer bows low to you once more, then turns to his soldiers.{/n} "Begin!"

aafcfb30-0e2f-49ee-9911-a2292c57448c.Text: {n}The officer nods.{/n} "We're using insecticide from our stockpiles, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We don't have any military-grade poisons, but we don't need them, not for this parasite."

9f3fadda-4a67-4bc3-aef7-14386d968b11.Text: {n}The officer takes a breath.{/n} "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. {n}At the officer's signal, the other wardens take a deferential step back, clearing your path to the door.{/n}

132fd48f-70fc-4817-a214-e47149af09e6.Text: {n}The officer of the wardens casts a disdainful look over the rebel before turning his gaze on you.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I honour your bravery. Please, allow me to get rid of this rat for you."

6125ef46-5651-48c9-9cec-d51c5accfa3a.Text: "Gladly, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Drag this carrion to a cell, lads."

b9ecc3e2-7a14-4818-9993-e525ea291fae.Text: {n}A dumbfounded expression appears on the officer's face.{/n} "With the deepest respect, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}..." {n}The officer thinks better of his next words and abruptly bows.{/n} "It will be done."

98a7cdfb-bb74-48fb-872d-ade19c512c21.Text: "At once, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}The officer gives his subordinates a signal.{/n}

b5631c5d-c77c-4a10-a7e9-b9d4609c61c9.Text: "It's one of the utility buildings. Fortunately, it was empty at the time of the attack — there were no potential hostages or innocent people inside. If you ask me, I think this was the first place the killer came to when he was beating his retreat. We managed to round up all the others, but this one holed himself up in there."

b8b6427c-f194-485c-9d25-e3725ecd6e56.Text: "One ashmag is up against all the wardens on this estate, yet he is still causing trouble? On Efreet, he would have already been made captain and put in charge of the governor's security — for the Exalted One knows that he has more brains than all of you combined!"

9c404f4a-7163-41b4-a671-3c3e39110335.Text: "This is not an empty utility building, but an inactive backup crypt for storing refrigerant and freezing equipment. This is obvious. Your ignorance is depressing, servant."

e01ea898-4abb-48e2-8537-7735f0200c04.Text: "How many servants of the Adeptus Mechanicus are there on the planet?"

5e57d3df-23bd-4cb2-9fe4-6e869e0d08a4.Text: "What do you do here on Janus?"

23db6248-a924-4760-92f4-17127f2cf65e.Text: "What are you talking about? I can't believe it! We need to deal with this urgently!"

7223822f-687e-4a38-854f-02c16d2512db.Text: "What pathologies in the flora and fauna?"

cd8aa92a-93d5-4afd-9a43-a01126c3d2e0.Text: "How is the governor dealing with 'undesirable pathologies'?"

3ac9657e-b9b0-467a-82dc-11be9a329f9f.Text: [Growling menacingly] "Shut up, you fool. Tell anyone about this, and I will kill you."

bf5e4c69-4e37-4718-b786-77a76c48d383.Text: "I found this on the body of a dead rebel. Can you tell me anything about these specimens?"

96154d67-8712-44f4-9d5b-d5b0f7b31757.Text: "Don't talk nonsense, cog. Do your work instead of trying to catch fictional conspirators!"

19a3d5bd-065b-4d7c-940c-228c9d152e48.Text: "How are things with you and your fellows?"

8df10e0e-6230-4fc8-b182-0fc97554d3f6.Text: {n}Draped in a red cloak, the Magos's body barely looks human. Wires, tubes, and metal manipulators turn him into a whimsical machine, while implants hide his face behind a sinister mask. The Tech-Priest intermittently dictates something in Techna-Lingua to the servo-skull floating next to him, but at your approach, he falls silent and offers a reserved bow.{/n} "Greetings, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Lexmechanic Vinzelex. How may I serve you?"

a5d91392-f2fb-4a70-a74e-bf72762a8698.Text: {n}The Magos notices you and offers a dignified bow.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. How may I help you?"

6d1660f4-2ca5-4234-a99e-30c58e9030ba.Text: "Interesting... It is often what seem to be insignificant anomalies like these that lead to greater troubles."

c2222bac-37f1-4687-b569-a9a63239e348.Text: "The changes may be artificial. Has the possibility been considered that someone is manipulating the ecosystem to reduce our living space?"

09b98b72-715d-413e-a8ad-148430a0633d.Text: "Due to the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarEliminated}eradication{/d} of the anarchic elements and the xenocreatures who manipulated them, there is a positive trend in the field of research into the remote forest regions of the planet. The remains of the xenocivilisation of the Aeldari, whose insignificant settlements existed on the planet in the distant past, have been discovered and subjected to primary cataloguing."

26a1698b-28b2-41c4-a0a8-0fe218c3e9df.Text: "The algorithms of my comrades' work have been subjected to interrogation, all orders of the former governor have been removed from the procedural queue in order to avoid a secret corrupting influence on the sacred works of the servants of the Deus Mechanicus."

1a451267-a9b8-4c72-86aa-d183a0e43166.Text: "Be blessed, tech-brother. Your diligence and the diligence of those like you turns anarchy into order, and bestows classification to Knowledge." {n}One of Pasqal's mechadendrites lightly touches the Lexmechanic's body. The Tech-Priest bows respectfully in return, clearly a little startled.{/n}

305d90a7-ba5a-4d6e-b341-ed06a9d64e62.Text: "Observation of remote forest regions is difficult due to the activity of xenocreatures. The level of threat shown is low. Protocols for avoiding contact have been introduced into the Standard Procedures in order to avoid provocations of aggression."

0db3f231-85fa-4734-97ee-9ca47b560285.Text: "Initialising report. The planet's soil possesses a unique composition suitable for the re-engineering of the planet and the mass production of foodstuffs. Significant cultivation of the eastern hemisphere with the aim of improving production processes and logistics operations. Traces of xeno-activity that do not pose an immediate threat to ongoing operations. Undesirable pathologies of flora and fauna have been noted, which may pose a threat in the short term."

c748341e-b332-43b7-8136-875cde787789.Text: "Your blessing for the examination, Magos?" {n}The Lexmechanic waits respectfully until Pasqal nods.{/n}

009e60db-1ac9-4c32-b586-d75644515401.Text: "Genetic and chemical pathologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Harmless species mutate and become aggressive, while plants change their chemical composition and become poisonous. This is happening more and more often, and if no action is taken, the ecosystem of the world will be irreparably disrupted."

5c5e8f2f-1bf8-440d-ae1b-0feede0ab995.Text: "I have analysed the genome of the affected species and I am currently developing suppressor genes to make the planet's organisms resistant to pathology, but so far I have not been able to solve the problem. Further exploration of the planet would perhaps speed up these processes, but the administrative apparatus has imposed a ban on expeditions that are not directly aimed at improving production."

0c0a6feb-a976-4d54-9f39-009cf2649d29.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest's mechanical voice comes from the speaker on his neck.{/n} "By the order of the Adeptus Mechanicus, I have been entrusted with the management of the Adeptus Administratum, in order to catalogue agronomic data and analyse information about the planet during the process of subjugating it to the will of the Imperium."

a706a331-90d3-41a7-a26d-5c1299c88515.Text: "According to data obtained during the initial survey, ruined structures of non-human origin were noted in different sectors of the planet, but I did not have the administrative capacity to study them in more detail. For now, I must defer the Quest for Knowledge."

084dffa1-3e7c-490d-8fa2-902694925a80.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest studies the dried berries and goes still. You hear the distinct clicks as his cerebral {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitators{/g} process this information.{/n} "Creeping creeweed, a typical plant of the western hemisphere. We have studied the possibility of industrial cultivation, but the process was found to be inefficient due to the specific requirements of the soil, which is found in the right composition only in the archipelagos of the planet."

4a51ca11-75b4-46bd-ba0f-77acedcc99a8.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest hands you a data-slate. The voice becomes even more quarrelsome:{/n} "I am transmitting data of eighteen recorded visits by senior leaders of the colony to the 'L-Than Restricted Forest Area,' carried out in secrecy."

6f9629ac-f81a-463b-a041-8cb80d990100.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest stammers fearfully,{/n} "Acknowledged. Apologies. Downgrading the priority of overseeing colony administration processes, returning to primary functions."

957c5497-0a76-4c21-9933-e461745581b1.Text: "It is the Lilaethan's wrath — wrath that is becoming manifest in nature itself, in the workings of this world... May the gods preserve us, how did we not notice this sooner..." {n}Yrliet glances at you before immediately looking away.{/n}

a812fc7a-0c90-494a-8e64-ba5f23ca956c.Text: "According to the data stored in my {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}, all infrastructure nodes for food harvesting and processing have their own contingent of technomats — the total number amounts to two hundred and fifty-three. Correction: based on the latest data, the figure is two hundred and eleven units."

b0df9ec3-7d66-4bc9-9986-29cc5e0c2420.Text: {n}Pasqal and the Lexmechanic exchange trills of binharic greetings. The series of sounds issued by Vinzelex sounds much longer and more deferential than those of Pasqal.{/n}

d81157c1-1c34-4368-af89-4a178c5413ff.Text: {n}The Lexmechanic speaks the last words with distinct envy, his eyes fixed on Magos Haneumann.{/n}

4ebb851f-7c02-4f01-a864-dc9d48349565.Text: "Not at all, venerable Magos. I... Our tech-comrades from the Magos Biologis are humble workers, not warriors. They could not have come up with a thought of such a militant nature."

945fb4db-6261-423d-a451-20d934054036.Text: "The mind must be open to all forms of Knowledge. I order you to commence a check. In the event that your account of the indolence of their minds is confirmed, I will petition for the appropriate penance."

644b448a-2ea2-4a60-9935-2571bc012bbb.Text: "The current situation on the planet is assessed as — stable. The progress of the prospects is assessed as — encouraging."

d262e66c-6edd-4bf6-a88f-71e079a809b9.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest's voice suddenly becomes grumpy.{/n} "Reporting: the current planetary leadership is also suspected to be {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarGovern}compromised{/d}. The order to form the 'L-Than Restricted Forest Area' limits our ability to comprehend and presumably serves the purpose of protecting region of the xenos population. Circumstantial evidence indicates that senior leaders of the colony are in contact with these xenocreatures and may be under their control. I request an investigation."

f4e2cdb2-ab91-4787-8568-4340ed43d9ee.Text: "Better late than never, I suppose. Show me the way."

c6d77eb7-590d-427e-9475-00e5fde00ce3.Text: "I'd rather show you the way — to your grave. Wardens, seize her!"

6554252d-718d-4ea8-bc43-a092fa98f03e.Text: "If one of the Imperium's worlds is in danger — so be it, I will follow you."

85802291-cc30-471e-b066-0e6c4bd22ecb.Text: "What calamity are you talking about? You're still holding back information!"

8335910d-5064-48c5-9109-80c8bba2033e.Text: "I don't believe you. You're luring me into a trap. Wardens, seize her!"

bcd399de-b4e7-4bfe-bd58-a1cbef7e3a79.Text: "Excellent — I was beginning to get bored without living targets to shoot at."

a935e67b-de96-4a25-b94a-808b41478ebf.Text: "Elantach!" {n}Yrliet gestures for your attention.{/n} "As you once sought my help, now I am seeking yours. The time has come to dispel the final shadows on our path."

3573e49c-b6a7-4175-af12-a056eeea4183.Text: "No other path was open to me, but now our paths are aligned. And my decision was motivated not by caprice, but by reason, which compels me now to be honest with the person who can fix all of this."

5443d13a-26b4-4a01-a854-1522b396e734.Text: "Everything you have discovered, everything you have learned from your kind, they are all traces of the same calamity. A calamity that will eclipse all the strife and wars on the face of this world. All the signs were plain to see, but I was here and the mon-keigh failed to recognise the coming storm... Please, follow me, {name} — you must, if this world truly matters to you!"

b9537a81-add0-4d86-ac11-6eb626326873.Text: "Perhaps my admission does sound like that... but please believe one thing — what propels me now is much more important than my earlier silence."

f466d45b-8844-4beb-8fca-52aeeca4a71a.Text: "Let's go, elantach. I pray to the gods that we are not too late..."

5ede19b1-3794-4306-b281-bf7ccfab0bb2.Text: "You have chosen the wrong path, mon-keigh — the path of pain and despair. Farewell."

736054d5-8f2a-4a61-85d6-caa6c4aa1b2b.Text: "Thank you, elantach. You truly must have been brought here by providence, for— no. It was your will alone that brought you here, which has become a blessing for the Lilaethan."

ac2238de-dd06-4a8b-a3ac-7cf700f1957d.Text: "I will reveal the truth very soon, but not here, not in the place where it seems evil has made its nest... Have patience, elantach — and trust me."

50a604ce-91df-4fb0-b1f8-18ebdb7b20ca.Text: "Please restrain your bloodlust — while I am with you, nothing will threaten us."

790b5be7-bb16-4720-ac2d-de74aa7cb8b8.Text: "I don't think the Rogue Trader needs your revelations right now, xenos... that is even assuming that you are not lying now as well."

abf6c9c2-3c20-409b-a50a-4e342916b5d1.Text: "I have hidden the truth from you. I know a great deal about those who are disturbing the peace of the local ruler, and I also know where they are hiding. Allow me to show you the way — on the condition that you bring me to them."

774b02e6-c1e8-4686-979c-33fae46e0100.Text: {n}Jae lets out a faint chuckle.{/n} "Your kind are usually a bit better at bargaining. Always offer what can't be obtained with torture or thrones."

8616eaee-7d7f-4574-9100-0fd72a2615f7.Text: "The xenos thinks she can dictate terms to us — Vyatt is a poor handler indeed. I keep asking myself why she would want to keep such an unruly creature at her beck and call."

3b74bd7e-8cf8-4f52-9422-63955fac2a06.Text: "I will speak with you, Yrliet Lanaevyss. But keep your hands where I can see them."

8ce501f8-fc90-4375-a801-8c43ea3f5b2d.Text: "Rogue Trader von Valancius will never speak to vermin such as xenos as if they were equals. So, if you want to live, you will address me with the proper respect."

d48beeaf-b658-49f4-be25-43d39481a3e7.Text: Attacked Yrliet upon exposing her true nature.

5a257149-f38a-40a0-835d-698a5299ea12.Text: [Attack] "I don't converse with the enemies of Humanity!"

66a5867c-0b1c-488b-98e1-fc8fe8825094.Text: "You have ten seconds to get out of my sight, xenos. Starting now."

68a74c16-737b-46d4-aecc-1e11253c9318.Text: "To be honest, the only part I understood was that you have no desire to fight. That is one thing we have in common."

8fc80fe6-9e0f-4f4f-b739-fc41c239d566.Text: "What do you know about the rank-and-file rebels?"

39886b01-3200-4f93-b733-81032a504bdb.Text: "If you want, you can join me. None of the locals will dare to look askance at you in the Rogue Trader's presence."

deaf55f1-0689-41cb-8265-303b02a9392f.Text: "How did you come to be on Janus?"

e52261bb-4104-439f-aa9d-bd50a6c86037.Text: "I spoke to the Magos in charge of operations on the planet. He says something's gone wrong with this world — there are spontaneous mutations, animal attacks. Maybe you have something to say about that?"

caccfd5d-9a36-4b1c-b3c5-3fe4afa56b2c.Text: "The rebel that survived talked about strange experiments being conducted on the people of Janus. It is said that people are brought to the estate and never seen again. Do you know anything about that?"

787b23c5-54d7-4c3f-a31f-cf9a1540b6cb.Text: "I examined the bodies of the rebels — they showed traces of mutation. Is that typical for Janus?"

1d005860-b433-4a7d-ae5a-4ba5fafacd56.Text: "Look at this skull. It was given to the governor's secretary by one of the governor's retinue. It looks like you and the deceased share a resemblance..."

d5f6a67b-664d-4849-9447-1e967c7b7116.Text: "Do you know who is behind the uprisings on the planet?"

be8c742a-2c93-4b5a-83a9-488f8f5d2f29.Text: {n}The bizarre creature before you only vaguely resembles a typical human. An elongated body, slender limbs, pointed features — every aspect of its appearance is unnatural and alien. The creature turns its head to you.{/n} "Yrliet Lanaevyss greets you, elantach."

48887377-774a-40ba-895d-837182eac56a.Text: "Would you look at this! Xenos — azhi devour them — mingling with humans!" {n}Jae tilts her head to the side.{/n} "Don't your lot think themselves above that? Anyway, it doesn't change the fact that it's a xenos that's been cosying up to Vyatt, not a mutant."

2c4341a4-0a13-4982-bf7f-e277d32025ee.Text: {n}Heinrix tosses out some words in a strange language — there is a hint of musicality to it, but the Interrogator's rendering is harsh and off-putting. After meeting the gaze of the unknown being, Heinrix turns to you.{/n} "Regrettable news, {name}. This creature is not a mutant as the locals assumed, but a representative of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} — one of the myriad enemies of Humanity. You should not trust this creature. Do not communicate with it any longer than necessary."

158938cf-81ea-473f-b90c-cc7ad8bcc6d7.Text: "There is no need to mutilate my language, mon-keigh — I speak yours well enough to converse with elantach without a translator. And since you have discerned my path, I will be direct in my speech."

e058fab0-93dd-48bc-9f61-d407379949ec.Text: "{name}, with all due respect... are you sure this is the right decision? We know nothing about this xenos or why she has wormed her way into the governor's confidence. As far as I can tell, she isn't especially keen to help us — and yet for some obviously dark reason she has decided to take part in our investigation..."

00f27f3d-a4b9-4e35-a67c-4a394691a906.Text: "Whoa... you've got to be the dumbest xenos in the galaxy, or you're braver than a whole Imperial Guard regiment. Must be a bit of both, if you're talking to {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} the Rogue Trader in that tone!"

975e9c35-6e1c-482f-aa1f-ed797a4f0660.Text: "I am here at the behest of the ruler of these people. Your commands mean nothing to me, elantach."

fcef50af-2d88-497b-983e-8bcdd508146f.Text: "Among my kin, respect is born of greatness, elantach. There are very few among your kind that are worthy of our respect. I will not change my path in favour of yours — but you may yet earn the esteem that your soul seeks."

c2cd4e74-a130-4811-a679-c2fbd72909a6.Text: {n}Yrliet inclines her head by an infinitesimal amount.{/n} "I have banished the shadow of doubt from your thoughts regarding my nature. Now you will answer my question — why have you sought me out?"

89ce3a1a-0862-4a23-9de3-d519cdb32063.Text: "You have not yet spent enough time among humans if you think threats will dispose me more favourably toward you. The decision is yours, Rogue Trader, but let me be clear — I will terminate your pet xenos at the first sign of her noncompliance."

80046cb9-2902-4b26-8b38-c06626c7bb61.Text: "I am, elantach. My hand parried the death promised to the ruler of these people, and I aided you in battle against the lost ones."

39eab94c-66c7-4af9-8f68-772b1e1ac18e.Text: "But you are not asking for help, elantach — you are merely asking questions, the answers to which are either unimportant or wreathed in shadow. Explore this place. Speak to those who know..." {n}Yrliet hesitates and then adds more quietly,{/n} "A simple task for you and an insurmountable challenge for me, since my very appearance provokes fear and suspicion. When you learn anything, tell me. Perhaps then my answers will be helpful to your search."

5dad60b8-1cf2-4f48-ad20-dbc2cf0de0a6.Text: "This world is in distress. I wish to protect it from unnecessary suffering."

5a1217b4-64d9-4235-bad4-182d6cc382cc.Text: "Only that they threaten the established order. There is much risk to this world should the ruler die."

020e663f-dead-43eb-ba18-54b9f2b1a6f4.Text: {n}Yrliet is silent for several seconds, her gaze fixed on something beyond you. Slowly, drawing out her words, she replies,{/n} "So be it. I will go with you."

2d8ccd46-6cd0-4a8a-aa9f-a494bb5dcd08.Text: "The world you call Janus was once created by the will of my kin. I have far more right to be on the Lilaethan than any of you."

c3c5e9bd-eeb3-4cb3-961d-e5e1faf5f057.Text: "I am ready, elantach. Let us go forth."

4e0633a0-6d8b-42cf-856c-b69866a2f124.Text: "The Lilaethan is expressing her wrath..." {n}Yrliet pauses.{/n} "For centuries, this world has resisted the brutality inflicted upon it by soulless machines and unmindful creatures. But what the machine man told you — that is something else, something more frightening. The planet is fighting an evil that has taken root in its very cradle."

8a94e83b-ba5d-40a6-8592-b9c314de1328.Text: "I witnessed prisoners being delivered to the rear doors under cover of darkness, but what became of them I know not. And it is not my concern what you humans do to your fellows..." {n}Yrliet touches a sparkling gem on her chest, as though checking it is there.{/n}

30d96492-ac7b-496f-97fc-1d8cfdc300d2.Text: "This world was pure, until your kind sullied it with its presence. The Lilaethan does not possess such powers — another force must be at play."

7e1c3b50-b523-460d-9069-130ac5f82868.Text: {n}Yrliet looks at the skull in your hands with unconcealed astonishment that quickly turns to anger.{/n} "You are right, elantach. Oh, Muaran, such vileness! And this is the price of your fate? The price of your path?" {n}The enraged Aeldari looks at you and turns her back.{/n} "Take that away... please..."

0967bf7c-6e57-4cb0-8ad9-ae6999edb34b.Text: "Because that is what you are. Elantach means stranger from the darkness amidst the stars. You descended on flame-winged machines in a dark time, when the air of the planet is soaked in blood and pain... Will you be the one to bring peace to the Lilaethan?"

965baad2-e6bb-45fe-9c9f-115896a93851.Text: "Must I remind you, Master van Calox, that the Warrant endows Rogue Traders with the sacred right to have dealings with xenos when necessary? That exceptional memory of yours seems to have let you down."

8037792b-84a9-4966-9af5-aa7e19f69747.Text: "There is a malevolence here that drives your kin down the path of violence."

ed9e5b4e-2f83-4cfd-bc60-7245afba715e.Text: "Elantach... everything you have told me stirs doubt and alarm in my soul. I must take time to contemplate. Do not disturb me further..." {n}Yrliet turns away from you, clearly burdened by her thoughts.{/n}

101afceb-2b1c-4c1e-ac83-d874745e9dee.Text: "Your attempts to intimidate me are as hollow as the lies seeping from your lips. Only the Domin's grace stands between my blade and your throat, xenos."

10d57e3c-8f2a-4215-be3e-dc22b364d9b1.Text: "The proud xenos hears the words but does not see the blade that stands behind them. Good. An enemy who is careless and overconfident is an enemy that poses little threat."

22c2b4a4-fdda-4254-957f-d9835674f69a.Text: "My judgements and choices are for me alone, mon-keigh. If uniting with your {mf|master|mistress} will bring peace to the Lilaethan, then it is the true path. Do not get in my way if you value your next breath."

a41b133d-f276-427b-86f5-384ffa405af4.Text: {n}Yrliet stares at you with her strange eyes, wearing an expression that is remarkably difficult to interpret. At last, she arches one eyebrow so subtly you almost miss it.{/n} "I have met souls like you before. You travel a path that offers you enlightenment — a rare gift among your limited kind."

9ccd8475-1ef4-45d4-9883-e55f111c3ab7.Text: "My soul is nothing kin to yours — your kind call us xenos, as if we are all as one. I came here to protect the Lilaethan by assisting the governor against her enemies. Will you hear me, or be blinded to sense by your precepts?"

d3665166-f62f-4639-8bb3-d740dee6e53f.Text: "There is fear in your words. You know what I am, and so I may no longer follow the shadowed path and must be direct."

43cd30f6-3c13-4aa4-a916-9194dcda6aac.Text: "But, Domin, this is... a xenos. The Tenets of the Bloodspun Web warn us about their deceitful and vicious nature. They compel us to destroy them on sight. She is an enemy of the Undying Emperor, and she is driven by dark designs."

5c7e0b4b-6c6d-4329-ab57-bdd61c8630c6.Text: {n}Yrliet's face is unreadable, but you detect a strange tension in her voice, as though she is choosing her words carefully.{/n}

6a62841b-3eec-4409-a1cb-8fecfbbc1a18.Text: "Do I need any other reason to come to the aid of those in need?"

d29918bf-bcb2-46cd-abce-ecd134cc54d9.Text: "While we're on Dargonus, I will check the secretaries' reports and keep an eye on the logisticians. Master Danrok does his job well, but a little scrutiny goes a long way with him."

b53b294b-5ea3-4e01-ac00-8ffb2d58aaec.Text: "How long are we going to stay here, Rogue Trader? The God-Emperor demands that His servants bring death to enemies, not sit behind walls!"

ea1186c7-2ace-4eb5-9603-4d5b793bf23e.Text: "My compliments to your taste in art: the collection here is extensive and most interesting."

8c5c045b-d4f6-4720-ab12-209c2e4e5805.Text: "The lack of observers on this world has led your nobles to become extremely complacent. Today alone, I overheard three statements that, if I so wanted, could be turned into grounds for a charge of heresy."

b87d1974-7143-4b0a-9e79-50f6cc5252a3.Text: "Ah, good old Dargonus... It's boring here without Lady Theodora — she loved to liven up this sleepy little place with a couple of crazy decrees and public floggings of flabbergasted nobles!"

c5422832-09b1-48ed-8265-9526fe39f48e.Text: "Such illustrious society! Such well-heeled nobles! Indeed, it would be worth visiting Dargonus even without getting to know you, shereen. This world offers huge scope for doing business!"

8a9c7b9c-a341-4a73-8807-d26524d13d4a.Text: "I remember when this place looked different — burning, agonising, drowning in blood... I preferred it that way. Let me know if you would like to see it restored to its former lustre."

d09a4fb2-c4ff-49fc-978f-6e5c22928947.Text: "My appearance has caused a slight disturbance in the ranks of the servants of the Omnissiah assigned to the palace. Analysis of the performance of rituals and maintenance litanies has produced a satisfactory result."

7e208429-fb4a-42f8-af11-53bbba54cbe2.Text: "A good void drekkar, and a respectful crew, but you cannot compare it to a wolf ship."

d7d48cff-b116-4fa8-8774-b88b9be4332b.Text: "The walls of your home suffocate me, elantach. I long to leave this twisted world — at the first opportunity."

755231e2-3937-467a-b616-2ad7946b1c42.Text: This person's body is covered in unpleasant-looking growths, scabs, and ulcers. They look like fresh mutations.

2badb3e2-19b6-459e-be6c-0495f949e459.Text: The sweetish smell coming from the dead body seems odd, and the blood has an unusual hue to it.

b411527c-d23f-476e-9ec9-86adf740fe36.Text: The cogitator's machine spirit stays silent in an attempt to reach the dead systems of the destroyed ship.

bf9ce8d0-a654-43d1-a0e8-1c46a57b5e4f.Text: Books and items of luxury. The legality of some of them is questionable, but the Navis Nobilite often turns a blind eye to such diversions.

8ffef116-e3d0-4423-9e5f-a28e5aaea627.Text: The Navigator's throne. The handles are extremely worn, with visible marks left by nails — evidence of the terrifying hours spent locked in battle with the power of the warp.

6f372bdc-3aee-43e6-9f6c-352c1a3fc8b2.Text: "Close ranks! Do not let them get to the sarcophagus!"

8a908bb5-22fd-4725-b460-f7947041f5fc.Text: Although only charred fragments remain of the pict, you can tell that it is of you, taken on the day of the attack on the ship and Theodora's death.

7f79ee5d-8b7b-4e3b-9c3c-ef764b5597e2.Text: "What happened to the ship and the crew, Hann?"

efc04623-694d-4d23-823d-d9f084bb0fff.Text: Urged Navigator Hann to take his own life instead of falling victim to corruption.

045f9b2d-9b3b-4246-87ee-456e3e33740c.Text: "If you are a true son of the Navis Nobilite, you know what you must do. Don't let the corruption that has touched you devour your soul."

c06237dc-e83d-4525-96f2-ea4f42f9e606.Text: Executed Navigator Hann and the mutated crew.

71d88674-c53e-451b-9244-99499ddfea54.Text: [Attack] "You've all been tainted by Chaos. Death to the mutants!"

b60a40be-3bdf-4e36-9989-68491c5f4e2e.Text: "The affairs of a Rogue Trader do not concern you. Do not trouble yourself with needless questions."

99514c9d-9b93-46f6-9724-d0b041b20e15.Text: "You can come with me, but the remnants of the crew will be terminated. These people are beyond salvation — they're corrupted by Chaos."

c6e09423-38fa-46a6-91f7-49ab547d902e.Text: "So the 'Chaos bomb' package was meant for me? Who's the sender?"

11c6d38c-ab53-4f1c-91c9-c3e5328cf68f.Text: Took Navigator Hann and the mutated crew aboard the voidship.

8c1a7155-1ee5-42d1-a4ed-7b5ad4f8cb5b.Text: "I'm taking you aboard my ship. There, my word is law, and no one will dare to take issue with you, despite the mutations."

00300e81-a2ed-423c-a854-273460980c00.Text: [Attack] "You have dealt me a mortal insult, one that can only be washed away by blood."

85e638bc-d5bd-40ad-81ca-aae7907ee067.Text: "According to the Imperial Navy law, with which I am intimately familiar, I am the supreme authority on this ship, not you, Hann Cassini. Obey the Lord Captain!"

420c9669-a82f-4c53-abbd-39712e717164.Text: "Were you not affected by the mutations and madness?"

c91ef8ce-a43c-48a5-8fde-e4d816efae80.Text: "Do not dare accuse me of colluding with Chaos. Do not even suggest it."

5d6acb8a-21a9-443a-ad2d-5b044a9f4ade.Text: "I am not tainted by Chaos, and I knew nothing of this package. I give you my word as a Rogue Trader."

386de823-cc5f-4800-a352-a47a1bff20c3.Text: "I would still like to take a look at the artefact."

f0361518-057a-4ba7-92c0-ebe0e3120ef9.Text: "Face it, Hann Cassini. You can't leave this ship. The corruption of the Chaos bomb did afflict you, albeit not as strongly as the others. And you know this, I can tell by your reaction."

b6a563ba-4186-4972-bb27-0830a49cfdab.Text: "We could lay mines in what remains of the ship and blast it along with the artefact from a safe distance. I have the resources and the knowledge to do it."

f3a3b422-e51c-4a54-9a40-c5e2b1a2cc50.Text: "Trust me. I will take the sarcophagus that holds the artefact and deliver it to those who can destroy it safely."

1afa8401-55b0-4776-aa05-fb5c456aec61.Text: Punished Navigator Hann for opposing a Rogue Trader.

d58f8e29-b08e-4561-a017-e4c885fdf6f5.Text: [Attack] "You stand between me and that which is mine. You will die for this!"

47b98c79-aed9-4190-b7f5-3270f2a95855.Text: {n}The leader of the ravaged ship's crew wipes the sweat from his brow in a motion characteristic of {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigators{/g} — not with his whole hand, but with two fingers moving from left to right and back so as not to touch his third eye by accident. This movement is the only sign of fatigue he allows himself. His posture is immaculate, shoulders wide, eyes front — as if he did not just emerge from a gruelling battle and is simply greeting you on the bridge on an uneventful day.{/n}

e9c8c9cd-c761-465e-901e-a5bc36e5eb70.Text: {n}As Hann speaks, others glare at you with dour tension. Up close, you can plainly see that every one of them is a mutant. Their faces and bodies bear the mark of incredibly grotesque deformities, the same as the muttering madmen who attacked you. However, Hann's associates seem perfectly clear-eyed, showing no signs of madness.{/n}

d9bf61c9-9345-4423-98a6-1fd97631dee7.Text: "The disaster struck during the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} jump. I will never know all the details, as I was preoccupied with my primary duties, but for some reason, the captain decided to open the package. That, as you may have noticed, had a most destructive impact on the crew."

e96b4728-bd0f-4239-ad2e-c95c300706d6.Text: {n}Hann frowns.{/n} "The package contained a {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} artefact. A Chaos bomb, if you will. The moment it was removed from its protective cocoon, the crew began to lose their mind and mutate. The first to be afflicted was the captain and the senior officers, but the effect spread with incredible speed. Every deck was consumed by it, every last one. The raging mutants, no longer sane, damaged many systems. The ship was in distress and would have almost certainly been destroyed had I not resorted to making an emergency exit from the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g}."

18307899-9869-4865-9dfe-8412eff7aeb2.Text: "The people you see here are the only survivors. Or rather, the only ones who were able to retain both their lives and sanity. I gathered everyone I could, isolated the source of danger, and sent out a distress signal. We were adrift, waiting for help to come and fighting off mad crew members. Then you arrived."

5e395f1f-3a78-48a3-980f-3e3b48672ff0.Text: {n}He gives you a searching look, then bows his head.{/n} "I beg your pardon, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I saw the terrible death of the entire crew with my own eyes, I was forced to bring the ship out of the warp by means of an emergency manoeuvre, and then I had to fight my former comrades, insane and twisted. I am tired."

6f77e497-276e-4642-8b20-7633ff7db28e.Text: "Well, that depends — I was born a mutant, you see." {n}Hann smiles, grimly and wearily.{/n} "Navigators are taught to resist the influence of Chaos, and so I have been, as best I could. But I will be frank with you — I cannot be certain that I have avoided it completely. There have been no visible indications. Yet."

3d02bf3e-6691-40a9-904f-b080d9323b29.Text: "As far as I am aware, the order came from Kunrad Voigtvir, the Master of Whispers in the Rogue Trader's retinue. It is likely that he arranged the delivery, either personally or through intermediaries."

95cf9677-01c0-4f2d-91dc-71ddd704e8d3.Text: "However, the sender wanted all of this," {n}Hann makes a sweeping gesture at the destruction and the corpses of crew members around him,{/n} "to happen to your ship, not ours."

49ac2c3b-8885-4080-acd5-4a13d8ab0f94.Text: {n}The exhaustion and tension in Hann's posture finally get the better of him. His head drops, and he rubs his forehead once more.{/n} "I've been gazing into the eyes of the warp for as long as I can remember, yet I've never been so close to it. It's taken all my strength to keep it at bay. But for how much longer can I hold on? I don't want to go mad and become like the others."

e308bda5-f091-40d4-9f77-dc67494491f1.Text: "I have been gazing into the eyes of the warp for as long as I can remember. I can fight it!" {n}There is pride and aloofness in Hann's voice.{/n}

6dc327dc-ee4c-483c-b390-ca91f206752c.Text: {n}Your words give Hann pause, but he seems convinced. He relaxes a little, but then asks — cautiously, as if testing the waters,{/n} "What about me and the crew? Will you take us with you?"

08dc1d64-c6f9-4c7f-9817-dcc31bb42fa9.Text: {n}The tension in his posture and gaze becomes even more noticeable.{/n} "I have placed it inside a protective sarcophagus, more reliable than the previous repository. Unfortunately, an artefact as powerful as this one could not be destroyed under these circumstances — or rather, I had no assurances that it would not disintegrate every one of us and scatter us across several light-hours of neighbouring space. But once we are off the ship, I will absolutely find a way to destroy the vile thing."

4aec74e1-846f-46b0-abb0-b254011457cd.Text: {n}Suspicion mounts in Hann's eyes.{/n} "You want to see the trinket that nearly wiped out a whole ship? Why? I have seen enough to stop anyone else from coming anywhere near it. I will give my life, if I must, to prevent that thing from hurting any more people."

cc4392ee-29d9-44cd-b9cc-96dd3159d2ce.Text: {n}Hann does not appear to be lying. It is impossible to gauge the extent of the artefact's influence on him.{/n}

6f509ebd-3a37-48b9-baed-85a7ea15a000.Text: {n}Hann jerks his chin up.{/n} "These are my people. We lived through this nightmare together. I am responsible for them. All of us leave this ship, or none of us do."

1e067c10-2805-4f28-abbb-ffed22a97d81.Text: "He's abandoned us — everybody has!" {n}You see fear and despair in the eyes of the mutants, now leaderless. Shuddering, they reach for their weapons.{/n}

02718a0f-69db-40d8-9353-165ef9427f25.Text: "Thank you." {n}Hann salutes you before adding,{/n} "Lord Captain."

9bbc5876-08d3-48ba-8877-f7e75ad89702.Text: "A noble choice..." {n}whispers Argenta. Her eyes are wide and gleaming with sorrow.{/n} "He chose death over letting the corruption consume him entirely."

5e2c1213-e068-4765-8c15-bcd0152da645.Text: "Lady Navigator, what an unexpected and pleasant meeting, considering the circumstances." {n}Hann decorously dips his head to Cassia.{/n} "I have not had the honour of being personally acquainted with you, but of course I know the emblem of House Orsellio. How fares the honourable regent?"

a669fcee-1069-4d6a-90d4-9b6f4da2c512.Text: "Cassia Orsellio." {n}She offers a reserved nod.{/n} "Cordiality will not disguise the ice-blue coldness of your words, Navigator Hann. However, I will tell Regent Aaronto that you enquired after his health. You may pass on my best wishes to {g|Encyclopedia:Novator}Novator{/g} Cassini. And now let's set the pleasantries aside. I'm sure the Rogue Trader would like to ask you a few questions."

f6ca751d-2c2d-4943-a8af-39be10214fc5.Text: "What are you saying?" {n}The usually reserved Cassia glares at you.{/n} "Does the Rogue Trader have so low an opinion of Navis Nobilite blood? If the corruption of the Immaterium could so easily break our will and maim our soul, the Emperor would never have entrusted us with our sacred duty!"

fe7d76d0-1317-48aa-86f8-5f691c595c2b.Text: {n}Hann pauses, then adds bluntly, almost brazenly,{/n} "Your reaction suggests that you were not expecting a package of this sort. That is good to know. I had almost convinced myself that the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} was deliberately collecting Chaos artefacts."

25418133-008e-4b8d-a204-9b20f46a4213.Text: {n}Abelard's face turns a deep puce.{/n} "That blasted traitor beat us to Dargonus and is now free to act with impunity! It would not surprise me to find out that this was the work of sorcery — how else could he have reached the world in such a short time?"

02e7cfe4-5da8-47da-9fb9-bed0d65186e6.Text: "A heretic who is vested with legitimate power and whose latest activities remain a mystery to all... Believe me, {name}, an individual like your former Master of Whispers will not stop at sending a Chaos artefact in his attempts to destabilise your protectorate."

14f9b964-0e92-4775-896f-41076311244b.Text: {n}Hann hesitates for a while, torn between duty and pride. Then he bows his head.{/n} "I am of the Navis Nobilite and thus do not answer to the Imperial Navy... and yet I cannot disobey the bearer of the highest title of the Dargonus fleet. I will disembark the ship with you..."

ffdfee35-96f1-4a67-9296-560350ede03e.Text: "My greetings, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. There is no need for introductions — I know the heirs of the von Valancius line by sight. I am Hann of House Cassini, the Navigator on this vessel, and, as the senior surviving officer, I assumed command after the incident."

203693a5-39cf-49bb-88d0-236658d19c8e.Text: "This ship is assigned to the port of Dargonus. Some time ago, the captain was instructed to deliver a package. Urgently, by hand — to you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We were even shown a {g|Encyclopedia:Pict}pict{/g} of your face." {n}The Navigator's voice seems calm. Yet there is tension in his eyes, which are trained on you.{/n}

0f2c8ca3-57c9-42d9-8a16-ce04918cc63b.Text: "Trust the intended recipient of the damned package? Rogue Trader or no, you are asking too much of me. No, either I will personally see that abomination destroyed, or I will not leave this ship."

bcba3cc9-5e5e-4b88-8e63-a6d278322ea2.Text: {n}Hann grows pale, but raises his head. After a minute's pause, he says hoarsely,{/n} "You're right. I've been struggling against the inevitable for too long."

217c9efa-946b-418e-99e9-2b9e686f1859.Text: "I beg your pardon. I am too tired to speak diplomatically."

69f691e3-d387-4407-874b-2d7988d05738.Text: {n}All signs point to Hann telling the truth. But you also notice clear evidence of just how difficult it is for him to struggle against the corruption. He is extremely tired, practically exhausted.{/n}

5c058713-414c-49a0-ac6f-57a6217c39eb.Text: {n}Something resembling grim desperation momentarily emerges in his eyes. But he nods.{/n} "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

9c67f176-5ac2-491a-810d-77b189cdb7d7.Text: {n}Hann gives you a scrutinising look, then nods.{/n} "I will have to take you at your word, as I have no other choice. But what will become of me? And of the remaining crew?"

0e469671-32e4-480a-a962-eee638979183.Text: Ordered that the ship carrying the heretical artefact be mined.

419c24f6-2123-46bf-b09e-76dccd160541.Text: [Give the order to lay the mines] "This thing must be destroyed along with the ship."

8dfef41e-9677-47d9-9dea-e508db05d50a.Text: [Give the order to lay the mines] "We have sufficient resources and knowledge — we'll destroy this thing along with the ship."

387c3861-ea3b-4352-8b4c-3e66a15e3cfc.Text: Claimed the heretical artefact from the dead ship.

f5d8be38-5e49-484d-ac9b-c8b0a673fbfa.Text: [Take the artefact along with the container]

4c137eeb-955c-41b1-98c3-0766f80eb373.Text: {n}The container is covered in a fine ornament of symbols, among which the seal of the {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobilite}Navis Nobilite{/g} and the personal coat of arms of House Cassini stand out. The container is closed and sealed, but the lock does not seem particularly tricky.{/n}

2e59bd52-897d-4807-a163-74282140f226.Text: {n}Abelard winces as if from toothache.{/n} "Look who's decided to resurface. It will be my honour to rid us of this 'pursuer' if he ever comes within shot."

6fdd1a62-aeb9-4146-8ef3-59ce520a36f3.Text: {n}You realise you have fallen under the effects of the artefact. It appears that your vox was enchanted with your own blood, which Kunrad stole on the day of your confrontation. The artefact was supposed to work like a siphon, draining the soul of whoever opened the container and of everyone around them — but the crew of the ill-fated ship took the brunt of the attack. The residual effects of the artefact are not strong enough to do you any serious harm.{/n}

16c43f1a-5cd9-4f98-b8b0-32ac4ac1c205.Text: {n}You can tell you have fallen under the effects of the artefact, but you are unsure of the details of what just transpired. The remaining silence feels as deep as a well and full of the same dark terror as the blackness inside one.{/n}

5269ba9c-396a-4c39-9d91-816029a3e1b0.Text: {n}You feel slightly nauseous. A cacophony of rasping, muttering voices emerges somewhere at the edge of your consciousness, whispering unintelligible words.{/n}

aaa4d54a-db6f-4b65-af56-003c963a0d30.Text: {n}As you touch the sarcophagus, a slight shiver runs through you. The lock gives in easily, but it feels like the temperature in the room drops several degrees the moment the lid opens. Inside is an ordinary {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}. A series of scratches runs along the casing, forming odd symbols. Tiny red balls are sliding and rolling between them — it is blood, behaving like mercury.{/n}

a4f610f4-e36a-4d3c-b1d7-1fb92bb1a2c5.Text: "You know who this is. You know I'm close and will never leave you be. Enjoy the power you stole from me while you can. But I'm not done with you yet!"

9e9da40d-e5c4-4b5e-9962-d0c1919f88f7.Text: {n}The device seems vaguely familiar. Could this be your {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}, the one the mutineers took from you the day Theodora died? Under your gaze, the balls of blood begin to scurry along the casing frantically, then suddenly go still. The vox springs to life and, through hoarse crackling, lets out a series of short phrases. The voice that speaks them is just as well known to you as the device is — it is the voice of the former Master of Whispers, your rival and a Chaos collaborator.{/n}

7055ffd9-818c-44de-8be9-0af3910ad446.Text: {n}The voice in the vox falls silent, but the silence only lasts a moment. Then a chorus of voices — hundreds, possibly thousands — explodes inside your head, repeating Kunrad's last phrase over and over again. Just like the mutants who attacked you. The chorus is so loud and fierce that you feel your eardrums might burst from the tension. Reaching a crescendo, the voices erupt in an agony of death cries and rattles. Then they fall silent. You feel your blood pounding in your ears.{/n}

4e8af5f5-eab2-4dac-84dd-1cc0fcef2460.Text: "Eh, no. Get in line. My little pal Kunrad's going down just as soon as he shows himself..."

e309e61a-27fa-4b29-b1f8-5c69c129bac0.Text: "So few words, but so many emotions... I hear the echo of deep-seated, long-nurtured enmity. The kind that exists only between lovers or blood relations."

8d0882ca-159e-4a03-a015-90ff505dc7d8.Text: {n}With the pincers on his mechadendrites snapping loudly, Pasqal bites out,{/n} "The spirit of this machine has been wounded by something unknown. I sense it in its electromagnetic respiration. I recommend immediate purification."

3e5a11d5-7a19-4ae3-9e33-9cfc15278697.Text: {n}The voice in the vox falls silent. A moment later, a torrent of voices crashes against your sanity, yet fails to do you any harm. Relying on the lessons you learned in your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}past life{/d}, you instinctively clear your mind of all thought and your heart of all doubt to shield yourself from the dark powers. You have parried the strike aimed at you.{/n}

64198bc4-2a19-4fc4-a3db-27cb3c9c22a8.Text: "The Adeptus Arbites will never recognise that heretic as a rightful ruler. If he shows his face on Dargonus, we will place the traitor in chains immediately and deliver him to you."

a374b665-6bcb-4984-895e-aa8f7f47a798.Text: A pile of mutilated bodies with cut tendons and shattered bones.

20b71aff-f10e-4669-8c34-1d3967ebe632.Text: The bodies are barely visible under the layer of filth, blood, and extracted innards, but they appear to be women and men wearing formal attire and fine jewellery.

ae36fccb-07d0-4199-a290-0ed0bb01d3fa.Text: It looks like this warden died before he could even raise his weapon.

113448fc-812d-40c3-88ae-a16f0c2c1ff0.Text: The face and hands are twisted in a paroxysm of death throes — the victim's last moments were full of torment.

2d9860f0-28ce-4b22-ab55-4ff427ae7d03.Text: The dead warden is pinned to the ground with the blade of their own broken dagger — it was plunged right under their chin to ensure that the victim slowly choked to death.

c5cb1f13-b75c-488f-99a1-fa600a50a264.Text: "Kae-morag! It is not yet time to kill you, mon-keigh. You have not yet played your part..."

daafe0ec-a3e8-4bf3-b5af-1b42006feb3f.Text: The dead noblewoman is staring at the sky with unblinking eyes. Her fingers have been thoroughly broken, and a tangle of intestines lies atop her slashed abdomen.

776afc74-7d1f-41d7-bfb5-f1dcb4352dee.Text: The body is lying face down, its crooked fingers clinging to the ground. This woman had her spine broken, then she was allowed to crawl in the vain hope of escape.

deb62f58-a38f-417c-ae15-bc19f3be1602.Text: The corpse is missing its eyes, nose, and lips. Judging by the maimed mouth, the teeth and tongue were also torn out before death.

bc3e06d5-ac78-4e4d-b550-1749403752d3.Text: Someone split the man's thorax open and turned his ribs inside out.

ef59655a-d74d-4201-9a34-27585d255e6c.Text: The governor's body was masterfully disembowelled — his many implants were removed, after which, judging by the amount of blood, the victim lived for a while longer.

4e8870d4-a95c-4b0d-98cd-bde13ac7a02e.Text: "The xenos got to the runaways before we could. I doubt any of them are still alive."

83c057b6-4e2b-4798-9895-6c7f2e9934f7.Text: "So much pain in the air... So much pointless, hollow suffering around us..."

7700eed4-b06d-4d2f-ae52-7b8d3c324173.Text: "Sorry, {name}, there's nothing we can do to help the people who tried to hide here."

0ac801e4-18e0-48cb-8a8e-f054de10f625.Text: "We met on the mining world. You are one of the xenos who got away."

8e5a3712-e624-4868-b691-4083de3df295.Text: "My, my, this beast can speak our language!"

47c78e81-19bb-4cb7-8e0b-7ef75d428a42.Text: "Yrliet helped me. Now it is my turn to help her."

4b506fd6-542f-4ae8-92c9-0a8b8bc53c5d.Text: "I'm tired of you, xenos. Prepare to die!"

b6e52f09-ca58-4e0e-93b7-bcea07be287e.Text: [Point at Heinrix] "My friend from the Inquisition introduced me to the right people. You can thank him yourself."

3818d867-8806-48e1-9999-6d1bd7636c7a.Text: "Aggravating, is it not — having someone best you at your own game?"

3e2dd513-ca69-4267-8198-38ee9f1959b8.Text: "Not so fast. I answered your question. Now you answer mine."

d969338a-681c-466f-8177-daa622d1b3df.Text: "Why go anywhere? I will kill you right here."

c90a2200-6e1b-4269-bad9-3c059d7e76cb.Text: "I keep hearing about an Archon. Who is that?"

834a0f62-6bf4-4504-903c-ed824af038b4.Text: "What are you doing on my planets? Why are you attacking us?"

38d55661-d8fe-4bac-b459-3e6c67db4be5.Text: "Conversations end when I say they do!"

3d4241b7-e36c-4c38-8fa2-0f45a4ac4415.Text: "Are you and your band the ones responsible for stealing the sun?"

a9cb9764-7cf2-4536-a438-08dd0bc310d3.Text: "I will be there, xenos. You can count on it."

d128712f-061c-4c63-8493-1bbe4be1773d.Text: "We certainly worked over enough of you xenos scum at your little bash — not the type of thing one forgets."

c7cc564a-e89c-497d-bf34-2df742c268a2.Text: "Hmm? Oh, you're finished pontificating? I think I dozed off there for a second — do you mind repeating the whole thing from the start?"

ed3679ab-2edb-4c41-ab48-19ffe2c57ea1.Text: "What wreck stuffed full of mon-keigh? Answer me!"

66dd70c8-3e5c-4b2f-9589-cd3020746151.Text: "What do you know about Yrliet's kin?"

b51494af-1129-418e-b762-2255407cc8dc.Text: "That is none of your business, filth."

88b72c85-fd20-4689-aa9e-dedc98bd2cd8.Text: "I know how heavily this mystery weighs on Yrliet. I wish to lighten her burden."

e21ebc25-a970-432b-91d8-618e0b8121a3.Text: "I have a burning desire to find those xenos and arrange a great hunt."

e5cf7dba-8975-4b71-8bcc-87612d1796e3.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} in ornate black armour turns his head to you. His thin, pale face is covered in tattoos and blood spatters. After a moment, his thin lips stretch into a crooked, unpleasant smile.{/n} "At last. You took your time coming to meet me, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}." {n}A couple of seconds pass before you realise that the {g|Encyclopedia:Elucidator}Elucidator{/g} is silent — the xenos is addressing you in Low Gothic.{/n}

10ae801e-c2d6-46c9-bae5-4dd15da8740a.Text: "How is it that out of all of your kind, you are the only one to discover our feasts in advance? Usually, you are all so slow and sluggish that my kin always have enough time to leave the battlefield before aid arrives. But still, time and time again, your dogs have been there to stand in the Kabal's way." {n}He pauses, waiting for your answer.{/n}

8b727243-800e-43d0-88ec-6cf54e4f5068.Text: "You ruined the reception that our poor little Tazarra had worked so hard to arrange. Now it is the Succubus's dream to drag you to Commorragh and have her way with you. What a terrible disappointment it would be for her if something were to happen to you before then... But we should not get ahead of ourselves, yes? First, mon-keigh, allow me to get a good look at you."

0e8dc6d2-6cc7-40e6-8a97-8786f76eff01.Text: "Yes, mon-keigh. Revel in those memories while you still can, because I will make you regret that stunt of yours yet. But for now — for now, I will take this opportunity to study you."

9291dc63-17ed-418b-88b8-fba6c684d512.Text: "Your joviality is unwise, mon-keigh. If only you knew who it is you have offended, you would slit your own throat this instant to escape retribution. But there will be time for that later."

6c75f4e5-06f9-45c8-b2c6-a07f50e7e74f.Text: "Speaking your language is slightly less trying for my patience than being forced to listen to a mon-keigh machine butchering our tongue. Besides, I want you to understand well what I am about to tell you."

2881d736-7ee8-4eb1-99d5-9cef8259de62.Text: {n}He clicks his tongue.{/n} "So you do serve her. Very well. There is something I can tell you, Yrliet... after I am done with these mon-keigh. Step out of my way."

605c2d39-ac39-4c71-bcbe-46447f2ecf48.Text: "Naive little beast. I won't be soiling my blades with your guts today. My subjects, however... they will gladly amuse themselves with you."

6288121f-a4ea-4c70-aff2-f37a55c9b579.Text: {n}Heinrix lowers his voice.{/n} "{name}, something isn't right here. An Archon wouldn't miss an opportunity to lead a raid and revel in the violence and pain herself. What is she planning? Is this a distraction to mask her true intentions? Or an attempt to get rid of her subordinate?"

c97ae899-f649-461d-84d6-f2906db58a47.Text: "Are you trying to convince me that a mon-keigh, even a well-trained mon-keigh pet, is capable of perceiving the designs of the {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g}? Both you and your 'friend' will pay for this audacity."

57dcfa12-f8ff-4a51-bdd8-46488bf38df2.Text: "I take it thanks will not be forthcoming."

a5e4f5b4-5fcf-4c03-b492-0f210b8031c2.Text: "And? That's it? Just an assertion that your kind are not as brainless as you appear to be? This answer does not satisfy me."

43ad1935-8ef2-4d16-a61c-8b617c7bbaa8.Text: "I suppose you are forthright in that regard. But simple riches do not change the fact of your weak, short-sighted, deficient nature. No, there is another reason why the mon-keigh have so suddenly become so astute."

00c42bfb-ae74-4d87-905f-d6632b14c04c.Text: "You think too highly of your deeds — however insignificant they may be."

581db9fe-e2c6-417a-bec3-9cf887260871.Text: "My name is Marazhai Aezyrraesh. Dracon of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest. First blade to Lady Yremeryss. Eviscerator of Illiridos, Blaze of the Barkhag Kingdom, and Slayer of Carrocius the Pale."

c19db800-d1cf-456c-bb14-0fb67e883a0a.Text: "Mistress of the Kabal whose hunting grounds lie in this region of realspace. It was she who ordered her subjects to gut mon-keigh worlds in order to replenish the supply of meat in the cages of her arenas."

e5b2ad72-edf4-4f69-8ebb-15ca059cb1fa.Text: "Because that is the way of things, mon-keigh. You run. We hunt. You die suffering. We relish every moment of it. When immediate torment loses its lustre and we seek ways to extract something more exquisite from our victims, well... Your kin are frequent guests in my home realm, albeit not of their own volition."

581aec6c-0b5a-4ec2-9b92-5f0a42b50f6f.Text: "An unfortunate necessity. Sometimes I am forced to speak to the likes of you — when the eloquence of the whip does not suffice."

af0d9b60-1931-4d15-963d-ccac0209ac24.Text: "I suppose I should not have expected anything compelling from a mon-keigh. Your questions breed boredom. The conversation is over."

3c461485-3930-472c-ad7e-7e9de945eee2.Text: "Oh, mon-keigh. I do not play by your rules."

cf9b35ad-9c9b-42f8-afcb-dca82c93fa96.Text: {n}The xenos lowers his head pensively, but what catches your attention is something else — a barely noticeable twitch of his fingers in his armoured gauntlet. He is signalling to someone standing behind you.{/n}

3b4242ff-0525-47e6-8f76-76fc0e906973.Text: {n}The xenos lowers his head, clearly considering your words.{/n}

0620a2c0-68b4-485f-aeb7-de2f0eb78da4.Text: "Stealing the sun? The {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g} are capable of that and much more, mon-keigh — Commorragh bathes in the light of three stars stolen by my kin. But if you think I had a hand in this or any other theft of suns — you are mistaken."

1de1d515-1971-43de-bb5f-e70242f41a41.Text: "Splendid, mon-keigh. Well, now that the offer has been extended... I must take my leave. I hope you prove diverting for my subjects, whom I leave in my stead."

409040dd-2686-44b9-ae32-d2b275e20945.Text: "In any case, I have grown quite tired of your attempts to delay the inevitable. Surely you too have run yourself ragged chasing us between the stars. Let us put an end to this. Finish this standoff. My forces against yours. Once and for all."

8e425fc8-40f4-4831-9fde-c6639879acfc.Text: "Do you wish to find it?" {n}His eyes flash with dark delight, and his voice becomes mockingly obliging.{/n} "Well then, mon-keigh, I suggest you send your servants beyond the Cinerus Maleficum. I'm sure they will return with surprising results."

0d80d187-bbd6-4f67-9862-d17cab9d105c.Text: "Hold your foul tongue, abomination! Such filth will not use that tone with the Emperor's chosen!" {n}Abelard is white with fury.{/n}

d4c52fe5-3b90-4d0f-a819-c612ce9fdc91.Text: {n}The xenos tilts his head to one side.{/n} "Why? I sent an invitation — by way of the cattle that dwelt on this world — and the 'chosen' has so obediently appeared. How are my words anything but the truth?"

8d083373-4b7e-4c59-b9cf-b140040f70ff.Text: {n}He turns to Yrliet in a snakelike motion.{/n} "One of my soft-bodied kin. What meagre offering tempted you to lower yourself to attending these animals? Or does their company remind you of being among your lost brothers and sisters?"

0232b1b4-1a2c-4ecf-89dd-a1b47834e197.Text: {n}Yrliet freezes — only her wide eyes betray her dismay and anger.{/n} "What do you know about my brothers and sisters, Dark One?"

0c637958-8134-4558-89ef-41f40d190673.Text: {n}He lets out an unpleasant laugh.{/n} "Only that they wander, blind and helpless, robbed of their home and hope... But why am I telling you this? Isn't it your duty to watch over your kin, Outcast?"

39d6000d-f499-4af7-976f-369514b221e6.Text: {n}Heinrix narrows his eyes.{/n} "How disappointing. This clearly isn't Yremeryss, the Kabal's Archon whom we had the displeasure of meeting on Vheabos VI. Once again we are dealing with a pawn instead of the true root of the problem."

ac181ce3-f553-4507-82ce-b68a4baceee2.Text: {n}The xenos lets out a hiss of irritation.{/n} "The little mon-keigh remembered the Archon's name? Such a clever thing you are... You might just make a good pet — after you have been properly trained and stripped of your misplaced arrogance."

6e42897f-2f7d-4d22-906d-91eaaf588832.Text: "Let's add a couple more titles, shall we? The Runner for the Hills of Vheabos VI and the Insufferable Blatherer of Grantis."

525bb134-5f12-405a-b39c-583f482c324f.Text: "That thing is perceptive." {n}You hear the undercurrent of worry in Heinrix's murmur.{/n}

ec41534a-3b56-45c9-bede-33eb0b692774.Text: "And it is all to prevent your putrescent souls from wasting away in the scorching corruption of Sai'lanthresh." {n}Yrliet practically spits out her words.{/n} "Day after day, century after century, you chase after the torment of others in hopes that the whispers of She Who Thirsts might fade from your ears at last."

d867185c-b1f8-4fec-ba9b-b8b43bf55237.Text: {n}The Drukhari cocks his head and looks at Yrliet with feigned pity.{/n} "Spoken by one who has willingly locked herself in a cage of rules and taboos. Tell me, Asuryani: what part of you is true Aeldari? Have you ever in your life let yourself be consumed by pure euphoria? Have you ever felt real passion? I invite you to join me. I will initiate you into the art of pain and unveil all that your Paths keep hidden."

ca7cf26d-b381-4379-80bc-c77af0ed7393.Text: {n}Jae shrugs half-heartedly.{/n} "Look at that. A xenos family fight. At least in that regard they are reminiscent of blessed Humanity."

41e98f11-708f-44db-b1af-ab2a74eb6e67.Text: "Perhaps I was mistaken, and it is not my craftworld cousin who follows you — perhaps it is you who serves her? Why would a mon-keigh concern {mf|himself|herself} with the fate of those you call xenos? Do you not consider them — us — your mortal enemies?"

754da925-25ba-4fce-a42a-4c7c787f9ed2.Text: {n}Yrliet's keen gaze pierces you. Emotions flash across her face in quick succession, and a spark of light appears in her eyes.{/n}

221c09f4-055d-4773-9fd6-342e681a0fe6.Text: {n}Yrliet curls her fists. After a moment's pause, she whispers,{/n} "No, Dark One. That... will not come to pass."

c0577368-febf-43ba-ba3f-a11d94c56623.Text: "Your hesitation speaks volumes, xenos." {n}Heinrix's voice is icy with contempt.{/n}

1b7536de-44ac-4199-99d5-a57cf41701dc.Text: "Then I have nothing to say to you."

afe4da1b-8c97-470e-92fa-3593e8b60a6f.Text: {n}The xenos hisses in irritation.{/n} "Do not try my patience, mon-keigh."

a4f82697-cd6f-40fd-8f46-349ed8581eb8.Text: {n}The Drukhari tilts his head.{/n} "I am starting to like you, mon-keigh."

12b66585-7e82-49a4-af75-99d87e886dc8.Text: {n}Jae shudders.{/n} "If a Drukhari took a shine to me, shereen, I'd know to expect nothing good out of it. You are too popular, even with your enemies."

d90f9200-36c9-4187-a4c8-054b0c17647b.Text: "You forgot one title, xenos. Your final and true title: the Dead."

9332afd2-6531-41a4-bcbe-966ecab54c02.Text: {n}The xenos pauses, mulling over something. Then he continues in an unmistakable tone of weary boredom,{/n} "I will tell you this, mon-keigh... I know you might be lying to me. Or you might even be unaware of who is guiding your hand. In any case, I have grown quite tired of your attempts to delay the inevitable. Surely you too have run yourself ragged chasing us between the stars. Let us put an end to this. Finish this standoff. My forces against yours. Once and for all."

c53c987d-8039-4392-9d5b-9da5b6f79d6d.Text: {n}The mask of composure vanishes from the xenos's face — spitting out a florid, vehement tirade, he draws his weapon.{/n}

e4ec6532-b687-4e58-ac9d-2e1b415dd678.Text: "You wander among the stars, so you must know of this place. An ancient reach where the echo of stellar agony rings still. A place that serves as a graveyard for old stars, still filled with residual emissions and glittering dust. The place that buried your wreck stuffed full of delicious, frightened mon-keigh and the horrors that devoured them. The threshold of our domain. Your kind call it the Cinerus Maleficum. That is where our disputes will be settled. The Kabal of the Reaving Tempest will be waiting for you, mon-keigh — do not come unarmed."

d860936d-497c-44a2-8d08-cac13036f99d.Text: "Do not play the fool, Rogue Trader. The mon-keigh know when their world or vessel is due for reaping. The mon-keigh hide or attempt to bare their teeth. Somehow, the mon-keigh know what we know — and I suspect that the search for this leak ought to start with you. After all, it was with you that this series of setbacks began."

0d3d3c6d-62f6-45f5-95b2-ab53ef38382d.Text: {n}The xenos pauses and raises his chin slightly, examining you.{/n} "There is deplorably little to distinguish you from the rest of your dull-witted species. And yet, mon-keigh... and yet you are different. After all, you are from the caste of their rulers, are you not? 'Rogue Trader' — that is what they call you? Well, then, Rogue Trader, since you nevertheless deigned to come to this meeting, tell me your little secret."

93fdf58c-0f91-4253-9718-cf8e6e77e180.Text: {n}A bizarre-looking artefact on the xenos's chest flashes with otherworldly fire — and in a deft movement, he dodges the shot. His voice takes on a mocking tone.{/n} "I am not finished, mon-keigh."

703c13a6-430e-437c-80c8-5500a4a9786b.Text: The charge has been safely defused.

35b41095-d9f9-4ddc-b388-332a3bd3dacc.Text: The structure of the xenomechanism is beyond your understanding.

99ef02bb-2d18-421f-90a9-ccdef294313d.Text: This bomb produces short electromagnetic pulses that disable power grids and devices. It is strong enough to take out the power of a whole city district or several voidship sections.

452ea320-001a-49a5-a7e8-a6c8fcb2edcc.Text: Lacerated bodies in tattered coveralls bearing the initials of the voidship dynasty that serves this section.

d5dc5d61-01ba-47c3-9bf9-2fb2df3cdf50.Text: Judging by the bodies of the xenos, the voidship's crew fought the raiders with some amount of success.

c95770fb-0423-4cb1-acb8-4f4e5e8fb93b.Text: "Do not rush me! Or we will perish alongside them!"

74ba9b50-a1fd-4b6c-8d5d-f3a1931c7917.Text: "More mon-keigh? Look, my kin, they can't wait to die!"

f8d15463-211f-4ab2-8975-0bd4b06e69fb.Text: "What's taking so long with the engine? The mon-keigh are already here!"

39b2fadf-99cd-4178-9b1d-0a36f5eac70f.Text: Even from behind the metres-thick wall of the reactor, you can hear the breath of the mighty plasma beast that sets the voidship in motion.

5a0ad7d8-ce60-47b8-94d3-f78246604580.Text: [Point at the patch on the man's sleeve] "Your crew's not stationed in this section. Explain yourself."

08fab4fa-3224-46f1-a703-80bac9bf9c3c.Text: "Put this body out of an airlock along with all the others."

daa92c36-e3ad-4d6e-8480-2695655b3593.Text: "Tell me about these hallucinations. When did they start?"

0ad5cfec-3562-4952-8efa-508ef69c1cff.Text: "You are clearly seriously injured. You must be taken to the infirmary."

a9a73e75-cfda-4c80-ad73-2d7366bcd92e.Text: "There are no Guards here. You are on board the Rogue Trader's vessel... and knee-deep in xenos blood and entrails."

18ad5e71-6c9e-4fc1-b6ce-dc1a41b72b14.Text: "Stand when the Lord Captain is speaking to you, you worm!"

524f4216-7837-4cf6-8116-78a7f9474d0f.Text: "Why are you here and not on your assigned deck?"

a80242e2-e94d-49b3-a953-37fa508ee84d.Text: "It seems you were not in your right mind."

43ce8cd2-3a73-414d-82ea-44d36dd64656.Text: "I don't know what happened to you, but you led xenos to the very heart of this vessel and almost killed us all!"

064f648c-493a-4367-ad26-3a16820913a5.Text: "I'll string up your skinned corpse on the main deck as a warning to other traitors!"

de97f6fa-e4b8-4789-bfd1-d8148a11118d.Text: Watched the mad traitor writhe in agony.

70371873-b478-400c-ad4c-2b442c9edc41.Text: [Leave the officer between the two worlds] "I want to watch the scum suffer."

836e5ae0-04a2-430d-82ab-64bdae6f17de.Text: [Execute the traitor] "In the name of the Emperor, death to all heretics!"

2d474a04-a7f9-4304-ab06-f74145a74897.Text: [Contact the Vox Master] "Take the body to the infirmary and try to identify the cause of his madness."

224edcf1-a331-4e64-88de-4ced5afce3fb.Text: Helped the mad traitor escape into his hallucination.

861de775-1945-499f-ba21-dc7cece75902.Text: [Let the officer slip into the hallucination] "I think I hear your son calling you."

2e7ec1b0-e181-479d-a6e6-bdf24369ce7a.Text: "If your spawn truly is somewhere around here, the only way you will find him is in pieces."

89bd81bd-5cde-41c3-8be3-a2d8bb1c04ac.Text: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}With your experience{/d}, you can tell from a single look at the standard patch on the crewman's clothes that he belongs to the middle decks and therefore has no business being here.{/n}

13173d39-0d68-402e-91b1-9012955869ac.Text: "What? Tacitus?" {n}The man laughs weakly, his eyes now fully clouded with madness.{/n} "Tacitus, my boy... I'm coming..." {n}The officer's body slides to the floor and convulses for a time before going still. Despite his agonising death, the dead man's face shows no signs of suffering — he had found peace before the end.{/n}

de3f9762-4cf4-40a5-af77-d71f7a10933e.Text: "I believe this mon-keigh is not here by chance — he has been in the clutches of the Dark Ones. His current state may be the bitter fruit of time spent alongside those masters of torment and madness."

99da526a-baa2-4981-af6e-e0c19d929a09.Text: {n}Something shifts in the officer's expression and the feverish gleam in his eyes goes out.{/n} "Tacitus, my boy... Swamp devils dragged him off. I'm where I'm supposed to be. I'm looking for my son."

24f84d44-82ff-4e93-9068-ffae47d1d706.Text: {n}Abelard clutches his head.{/n} "Motive Force strike me down, I think I've got it! The xenos that the crew smoked out during the recent warp jump! This poor madman must have taken him for a Guardsman... Remember, Lord Captain? The enraged Drukhari who had bent several crew members to his will?"

c70d9f91-48f9-4c5c-8cf0-ec55c2378f14.Text: {n}Argenta's voice trembles with sorrow and rage.{/n} "Until the last beast among the enemies of Humanity is dead, the innocent will continue to suffer torment... Is this not a sign that we must work doggedly to rid the universe of xenos?"

ddaa692c-8219-4fa2-9f4c-b8f45edae0cf.Text: "The massacre? The massacre... yes, the massacre... the swamp devils jumped right out of the water, and Tacitus, my boy... He must be somewhere around here, in the marshes. Could he have fallen into the water? I hope he's not injured."

f34d3df0-dcca-4117-a707-2f05b9107cd9.Text: {n}The man raises his hand as though requesting permission to speak.{/n} "Don't... I don't deserve to live after what I've done. My mind is probably corrupted for good already — even now, I'm looking at you, and I can see behind you the marsh where Tacitus vanished..."

94b09613-0bb1-44ff-9fa5-be5b159b58ae.Text: {n}Yrliet's mouth twists.{/n} "Our cousins are adept at creating concoctions that turn sentient beings into mere beasts shrieking in agonising pain. Sometimes the effect is quick, sometimes it leaves just enough time for the victims to divulge all that they know."

d4336d24-42a7-44f6-b73a-92a4cb019ea8.Text: {n}Jae looks at you.{/n} "Whatever they did to him, shereen, there is no way back for him now... If it were up to me, I would let him slip back into the illusion, where there is still hope of finding Tacitus. Let him go at peace with himself, and not as a traitor."

9a42cbc0-0a6c-4015-9373-c8fafb132c1b.Text: "The Guards, they weren't... very chatty. One of them called me something strange — 'mon-keigh,' I think? And I heard them talking among themselves. Something about... 'seizing the ship'... 'don't let them through'... through to where, I don't know... oh, it's coming over me again!"

3acd4eb8-68e2-4663-b17e-6b443dcacdea.Text: "Could it be the 'Dracon' who sent us here to this rendezvous? My, my, a xenos who eviscerates human worlds has set a trap for us instead of meeting us in an honest duel! How unexpected!"
