b2d3e99e-fa6b-4955-a9f5-d0200945ff4e.Text: {n}The officer slowly runs his hands over his face, shuddering as he touches his nose.{/n} "Must have been the devils... They're fast — one of them jumped on my neck and sank its claws into my face just now. Yes, that must have been what happened..."

f3b3883c-58d7-4394-bd75-86d365d39f09.Text: {n}The patch on his jacket shows a crest that is vaguely familiar, but you have no idea which particular compartment it is linked to. The only thing you know is that he is wearing a von Valancius voidship officer's uniform.{/n}

d43bac93-ee1f-42c9-816a-ba6096efe923.Text: "I don't understand... Xenos? What... xenos...?" {n}For an instant, awareness returns to the officer's eyes, and he seems to see his surroundings for the first time. His face slowly stills in horror.{/n} "Emperor preserve us..."

c6dfe0c4-dbfc-43ad-8165-6b9b25eb6ba3.Text: "What?" {n}The man tries to stand up, but he slips and falls back to his knees.{/n} "No, no. There's still hope. Tacitus can't have fallen into the devils' hands just like that — the Guards will save him. They have to..." {n}The officer's gaze suddenly clears and he seems to be aware of where he is — his bloodied face slowly stills in horror.{/n} "Emperor preserve us..."

363df3a7-8abb-4ccd-81c6-de6edaa5d333.Text: {n}Jae laughs darkly.{/n} "Blow up the reactor bay, damage the engines... and then disembowel the helpless ship to your xenos heart's content. Oh, yes, that sounds just like my 'partners.'"

2d8b7914-8bd9-4911-ac49-ae3fafdd0da2.Text: "I think you're right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Reason has fled me, I can't hold out — even now, I can see the marsh where Tacitus vanished just behind you..." {n}The man's face twists in a mask of pain and grief, and a powerful spasm wracks his body.{/n}

bfeb1a88-6552-4a90-b405-3ef6b1e60ef6.Text: {n}The officer's death throes last for several minutes — his eyes are still hazy, seeing the false vision, and his screams are interspersed with piteous attempts to call for his dead son and pleas to the Lord Captain for forgiveness. At last, his body collapses to the floor, where it convulses for a few moments longer. The dead man's face is twisted in indescribable agony.{/n}

3f911fff-3e79-462f-8fe5-ac1463d0123f.Text: "I... don't remember? It's so strange... It's like I'm here and I'm there at the same time... But... I remember, many watches ago, a visit from a Guardsman, after the swamp devils attacked, it seemed. He treated my injuries... did something to my face... and said that his comrades would come and do what they had to do. And when the rest of them came, they told me to show them the way to the nest... but we're on the ship... where did I take them?"

71f3a6c7-be44-429c-a8af-8f81e0cb1099.Text: "I'll be damned if this officer has a son... Perhaps he did once, but he embarked without any family in tow." {n}Abelard sighs heavily.{/n} "He's cracked, the poor wretch..."

12fd13fd-a53d-47f8-9344-41123276b8f2.Text: {n}A furrow appears between Heinrix's brows as he considers this.{/n} "It sounds like a mental distortion — the work of xenos... Drukhari are capable of ensnaring their prey without shackles or fetters — they twist and violate their victim's mind using unholy instruments. Your subject has been forced to experience a nightmare from the past in order to wreak a nightmare upon the present."

832220cb-c672-4e76-9d6a-785b824d9bce.Text: "Interesting..." {n}The Interrogator's face takes on a strange expression — stoic sufferance and grim humour.{/n} "How many more like him are roaming the decks waiting for their new masters to give them an order? At least they do not have any means of remote communication. A small comfort, but comfort nonetheless."

bbd97ca6-99bf-43fb-9d64-59d7890fe47c.Text: {n}The man jerks his head up, apparently seeing you for the first time. But just as he opens his mouth, his whole body begins to shudder and his eyes cloud over.{/n} "The Imperial Guard will find my son. They'll find Tacitus, I know they will..." {n}The officer shudders again and presses a hand to his face.{/n}

1a7a0d71-eefb-4323-88d2-802f1d312329.Text: {n}Idira tilts her head to one side.{/n} "Those words, Lord Captain... 'Don't let them through'... have set my little voices singing. I hear them singing about a fine thread that leads to the heart of your territory... I hear them sing of Dargonus... of a black dragon..."

5679ede0-2ae6-41e2-99f9-2095e3cfc18c.Text: {n}The patch on his jacket bears a familiar crest — it is the symbol of one of the middle decks, one that has no connection to this compartment. The officer's presence here on its own is a violation of the ship's regulations.{/n}

2649fd92-1012-4dc3-8b43-8d763b8795c4.Text: {n}A man in an officer's uniform is kneeling and scrabbling around in the mess of blood and dirt on the floor. As soon as you draw nearer, you hear his feverish muttering.{/n} "No, no, no... Where is he? Where is my son?" {n}The lower half of the officer's face is grimy with some strange substance too pale and lumpy to be blood. The officer pays you no attention — his eyes are fixed on the floor.{/n}

8b6f4469-9f13-4e18-8432-cad546fc337c.Text: {n}Your outburst lands like a slap to the officer's face: he jolts and looks at you with a cleared gaze that immediately fills with horror when he notices his surroundings.{/n} "Emperor preserve us..."

3d991e6a-baf1-462e-966a-94958e5e188b.Text: "I'm sorry! It's all a xenos illusion... Even now, I can see the marsh where Tacitus vanished just behind you..." {n}The man's face twists in a mask of pain and grief. He coughs violently and slumps forward as though he is falling asleep.{/n}

d89e6957-7fa2-4179-859d-9e1e244c5687.Text: {n}Tears start to run down the traitor's cringing face.{/n} "I didn't know I was betraying Humanity to the xenos... I didn't know... Even now I look behind you and I see the marsh where Tacitus vanished..."

25e72bfc-be2d-4f55-9126-8d28a0c4ec6c.Text: {n}You take another step toward the man and peer into his face. Blue veins bulge under his scab-mottled skin, and his bloodshot eyes are darting in every direction, sometimes rolling back into his head so that only the whites are visible. The strange stuff covering the officer's face is lumpy pink slime mixed with blood that is streaming from his disfigured nose.{/n}

75fe9d4e-08f8-4190-96db-b7bf6cf1fa84.Text: {n}In one sudden movement, the man falls at your feet, an expression of stoic acceptance frozen on his face.{/n}

9485e3ba-5b24-4235-b13f-53ca817d014c.Text: {n}You bend over the body. Despite the numerous bloodstains on his skin and clothes, the officer had not been seriously wounded. The only noticeable injury is on his face — his nose is disfigured, and a red, slimy substance is streaming from it, staining his mouth and chin.{/n}

36eba7d6-d34a-4f3a-b557-8320153a5557.Text: "Wait... He's an operational officer from Deck 67-3. Not from one of the local clans, which is why I remember him. He helped me bring up the new recruits from the planet. What is he doing here?"

8420cb40-3021-4cb7-ba6d-52ae0854cbac.Text: {n}Kibellah purses her lips.{/n} "Only a heretic would suggest something like this. To die with one's mind dazed by xenos influence? No. Let him die a man who is aware of the betrayal he has committed. Only then will he find his way into the Undying One's hands."

0bdd702c-53a9-4d5f-bb87-29ede0e8a070.Text: "The Emperor's valiant Guards came to save my boy. I showed them where the swamp devils dragged Tacitus. I led them right here like they asked. They'll make short work of the nest of those beasts... and I'll keep looking for my boy in the meantime. {mf|Master|Mistress}, will you help?" {n}The man's face contorts in a monstrous grimace — a mixture of pain, hope, and madness.{/n}

759d4f60-7b7e-4fe7-a79d-32e88424696f.Text: {n}The man jerks his head up, apparently seeing you for the first time. But just as he opens his mouth to reply, his whole body begins to shudder — and his newly cleared gaze passes over the chamber. His blood-filled eyes go wide in horror.{/n} "Emperor preserve us..."

67dc267c-04e9-4516-b76d-eb6307962a59.Text: {n}The man sneezes, and the lower half of his face is coated anew in the slime streaming from his nose. The officer casts you a pleading look.{/n} "What is this nightmarish scene? I was leading the Emperor's Guards to the swamp devils' nest across the marshlands of my homeworld... but instead of that I was showing the way to... them?" {n}He points at the corpses of the xenos with a trembling hand.{/n} "Hallucinations... A heretical mirage..."

b02ab042-1a08-4070-91ce-ca35b37572cd.Text: The crates contain nothing that is not tagged with an inventory number, no personal items — not even a sentimental knickknack, the kind so beloved by soldiers and voidfarers.

36c7b37c-c746-4d7c-ab5d-d4ae117943b6.Text: Judging by the empty weapons racks and the lasgun cleaning table, the inhabitants of this cell turned their lodging into an arsenal.

76d5eaca-85b1-47b3-b422-4f7b05a61069.Text: The flesh of the cocoon has been ripped open and inside you can make out a decaying corpse. Based on the twisted expression and pose, the person died only when his tiny refuge was unsealed.

025b4cc6-7620-425c-8028-f2c3f67d15ce.Text: Through the cocoon's translucent film you can see the vague outlines of a decaying body. The rib cage has been broken open, and a heart still beats inside it.

cbac1d46-2181-49c9-8980-dbeb6878f5f4.Text: From time to time, tiny sparks of psychic energy burst out of the cocoon.

7bff7196-9fc9-4476-b9fb-206cf6cedece.Text: This voidfarer's injuries indicate that he gouged out his own eyes and ears, and then, armed with a knife, hunted and killed his victims by touch.

77c2dc84-5b8e-4418-b527-0914cfc8936c.Text: The heads of these people exploded — the soaring pressure instantly ruptured their eyes, eardrums, and mucous membranes.

574044ea-ed03-4ee2-ab63-e43a1a5c7ae6.Text: The horror-struck grimaces and traces of foam on the mouths of the dead indicate that they were suffocated by poisonous gas. The gas diffuser is installed right on the ceiling.

51bc2d7f-e162-4763-b364-ba6d31eefb08.Text: After being shot, these poor wretches had their skulls caved in around the temple, as if to make doubly sure.

236aecfe-3435-4c2c-8820-72f49fafaacb.Text: These people were not killed by weapons fire — perhaps there was no ammunition left for them. They were brutally butchered with knives and beaten with gun stocks.

ad0f5bfa-60b2-45ae-925e-b334c52ffff6.Text: There is a gaping hole in each corpse's head — they were brought out one at a time and shot from behind at point-blank range.

c8e34c45-d36d-46fb-8bfd-b87c7f54af72.Text: The medical servitor now covered in foul mould was equipped with a hand bristling with long syringes instead of fingers. A foul-smelling substance still sloshes around inside the barrels — an extremely potent sedative.

f4fb4950-8004-41be-b838-a74241bf35ad.Text: The bulkhead, split open by a plant, is composed of not only steel but also layers of mirror-like lamellae designed to suppress psychic energy.

434f4505-b83a-4d80-8c5e-d0742547fa42.Text: "Passengers will keep their mouths shut. There is no screaming."

18555a0e-8b9e-4318-8eb8-a8bf9e3c07db.Text: "No, I hear it too. Oh, Emperor, his screams are so loud!"

f1037909-dad1-4245-acd1-8a60a58e1961.Text: "Me too! It's so loud! Please, stop this torment! Why are you torturing us?"

d971a551-0912-46e4-bb8f-7fe81a3f20db.Text: "Something's not right. Wardens, combat positions! Tell the bridge we have suspicious activity here. Get back, damned mutants!"

d8d85965-20f6-47b8-a9ae-4060e4898201.Text: "This isn't right! You can't treat us like this! What are you going to do to us? We want to live!"

94222061-955b-4a18-8b97-a0c971235a84.Text: "Warden Kappa-322, reporting for patrol duty at the Main Confinement Cell."

34aba8bc-9654-4480-9bcc-1bacaf1e2c45.Text: "Atmospheric sensors indicate the presence of unknown impurities. High risk of contamination."

b0fbc586-e7ef-43bb-b5de-541425a4e773.Text: "What? But... gah... oh, saints of the Emperor, what's happening to me..."

501e64ea-137a-4030-9f15-c8711b66d3cf.Text: "Danger. Detecting extreme contamination levels. Initiating global alert protocol."

e6ea724b-5076-4151-acda-3a4587bd3302.Text: "Sir, we've lost contact with Hold Sections 238 and 239! The riot is spreading!"

1b21e1f7-6401-410a-95cb-9b3df88298d0.Text: "Emperor have mercy on us. I won't let these blasphemous mutants take control of my ship."

ff530135-a683-4f66-b773-838394dc00b4.Text: "Broadcast this over all vox-channels: in the name of Inquisitor Yutan Holl, all crew members are hereby ordered to take up arms and begin a total purge of the holds."

4e87d970-620b-4911-91d3-eccbc94e39d4.Text: "Every psyker on board must be destroyed. Cleanse every inch of this ship with fire!"

26b7b566-6d63-42f2-9242-d607e909f921.Text: You lack the knowledge to decipher the readouts on the monitor.

bca8f2ed-5b86-4d72-93e3-b043c67cb0ca.Text: The readings indicate that the ship's reactor is still running, though perhaps not for long. This explains why the ship's interior is warm.

d4504cac-6d72-465a-8a46-df13094234b0.Text: Tangible psychic radiation is coming from the gurgling sludge. Perhaps it is the source of the vision that seized you.

bfa69ff0-217b-4d74-ba6e-e11f9ff4b3a0.Text: Small fish, eyeless and slimy, dart and wriggle about in the rank water.

d231b177-58fa-4e6e-a958-737bcba9963a.Text: The bed has been made with deranged exactitude.

feac887a-0bf7-48c6-a24e-8cfeee05783a.Text: A piece of the mattress has been cut out to make a hiding place.

bb967aeb-bc7e-45f5-bccc-843344760206.Text: These soldiers died in a brutal exchange of fire, but it is unclear who was shooting at whom.

66d558e0-8175-421a-9207-034f8b016339.Text: These soldiers were killed by shots in the back — it seems they were executed by their own comrade, who then used his last charge to blow his own brains out.

b6e11844-0572-4726-8116-31bfa5de68fc.Text: The eyes crudely daubed on the wall seem to track you as you move.

95d0afaa-192d-43ba-8361-4bd70e234eeb.Text: Crude scribblings in some blasphemous script prove too impenetrable to decipher.

0bf8035a-24cc-4f35-af44-6bbafd3db7b4.Text: "Grant us eternal life, Nurgle, Father of Decay, for we do not want to die!"

27c7917f-d588-4cfb-8ab4-154798130b95.Text: "Where there is death, you will find His Gardens. Where there is decay, you will find His power."

17c6fb0f-b294-4db2-9503-f36b7054fb1b.Text: A squalid berth heavily soiled with blood and vomit. It is also equipped with straps that were used to bind its inhabitant to the bed whenever necessary.

4be9aca7-57ab-41a2-85bc-10e93e2fa846.Text: An asthmatic rasping can still be heard coming from a broken vox — a screeching, cacophonous melody that sets your nerves on edge and scatters your thoughts.

5c0d3070-1c2a-4920-972b-68533550c69a.Text: The bulkhead releases cloudy discharge, resembling a parody of the incense-dripping icons of the Emperor and His saints.

cb575278-60bf-4e48-ad97-91331b03312f.Text: The corpse's flesh has crystallised and turned into a translucent sarcophagus, and sealed within is the slop of their putrefying organs.

ac86918f-76d0-4b7d-9978-338219004334.Text: "I am eternal in His Garden. Begone, unbeliever."

f82f3513-1f32-48d5-9d8e-5f40cae114a3.Text: "Nurgle promised me immortality, and now I am immortal."

66ee72bc-5047-439c-85d2-c10d29a4f6df.Text: "Let me go. I want to move... walk... breathe..."

224448cc-40c4-4cb4-b770-8f735b813773.Text: The walls of the lift shaft are coated in a layer of putrefying goo containing revolting growths — the bodies of the people trapped within it.

268c8e94-1a56-4628-90ba-112e248219e5.Text: The flasks of substances are not labelled. It is impossible to tell what is in them.

bffc5413-6b0d-46ec-af73-d85ec0d95488.Text: The flasks of substances are not labelled, but you recognise a few of them as combat stimulants.

845741ca-8fe0-4b35-bfac-49587b33ee1d.Text: Lumps of flesh float in the reeking sludge, which gurgles quietly and rhythmically, as though there is some impenetrable logic to these sounds.

d1bcc07f-43e3-496e-aada-989fe146823b.Text: A shattered Occluding Sphere, an artefact that dampens any nearby psychic abilities, is lying next to the desiccated body of a daemon. The remains are so revolting that your eyes refuse to look directly at them.

0ffb0512-8b99-4866-b618-f8b89fb36abb.Text: A shattered Occluding Sphere, an artefact that dampens any nearby psychic abilities, is lying next to the desiccated body of a daemon. You feel a strange compulsion to look away, but you fight it and look directly at the corpse. You notice a small metal augmetic in the daemon's flesh.

a6e13020-b26c-4c64-85ce-d28aa9023d15.Text: A rotten brick of corpse starch — a passenger's rations. Judging by the lingering smell, it was dosed with a sedative.

5df42a69-cb62-40bb-96e7-3bf50df4c3d0.Text: The crates contain fragments of plate armour, rusted and covered in fungus.

c9517caa-f53c-41d1-a28a-dc40a5bf0f20.Text: The lasguns, flamers, and shock weapons in the containers are covered in a layer of whitish maggots and partly eaten away by acid corrosion.

ed1ccb80-9d61-494b-903a-cea1db4d3ff4.Text: This tree has sprouted right out of a person — his broken bones have formed the collars of branches, his cracked skull has merged with the trunk, and dried gore now coats the skin-like bark in a thin layer.

7e484f58-0b6f-41c2-9634-330a54c82909.Text: "Maintain vigilance — keep watch over your thoughts."

0ddbbb5d-2a82-473e-9d65-97a4f67bb7a3.Text: The fraying rope ladder is woven from the passengers' overalls — an extremely dangerous way of reaching the top level of bunks.

135eeb61-6d99-414f-83e5-049f49a8c591.Text: "They want to burn us all burn burn burn."

7ee9f55b-fcce-44e1-b077-a62b3fbca232.Text: "I just wanted to live. Why? WHY?"

c0c52bbc-c201-4688-b9a2-633d632ac56a.Text: "No one will hurt us here. And no one will hurt you either now."

13c67c54-57db-4ef1-a17c-d2a24cc49c1b.Text:
"Voidsman, by the grace of the Emperor you have been given the honour of serving on a Black Ship of the Inquisition. You have been entrusted with a unique cargo — psykers collected from the Imperium's worlds as their rightly owed tithe.
Do not be deceived by their appearance — every one of them is a dangerous mutant. Be strict with the passengers, for that is how you safeguard the lives of yourself and your comrades. You must be blind to tears and deaf to pleas.
Listen to the passengers' conversations and report any groupings that form among them to the Ship's Confessor. Any groups will be split into different holds to prevent a coordinated revolt.
Check for certain that the passengers are eating all of their rations — they contain tranquillisers intended to ensure your and your comrades' safety.
Pay attention to any strange occurrences — psyker corruption comes in many forms. Passengers that exhibit extraordinary abilities must be transferred to reinforced cells for solitary confinement.
Do not engage in conversation with the passengers, do not refer to them by name, do not give them your possessions, do not allow them to lose their fear of you. Their fear is the key to your survival.
Appear before the Ship's Confessor every month to have the purity of your thoughts checked. Remember that blasphemous psykers can play with the minds of real people.
Keep the faith and follow these rules. Failure to observe any of them will be grounds for dismissal."

1dc36d80-10be-4d7a-a87f-322361b4ebf6.Text: Key cards like this are issued to soldiers who are posted in compartments with heightened security.

73d7f448-33b2-4a62-b4da-00e7bdd659d6.Text: The carved seal belonging to a senior officer, which serves as a key for the most important weapons stores.

9082ba1e-b9fd-46a9-9130-b8fc38bf52f3.Text:
The ship's log is encrypted, but the last entry was written in Gothic:
"I, Inquisitor Yutan Holl, captain of the Black Ship Monarchia's Bane, write this record for the eyes of any faithful servant of the Emperor who may chance to read it.
My vessel dutifully departed Terra to collect the Imperium's rightful tithes from its loyal worlds and then to return to the Segmentum Solar with thousands of psykers in our holds. Our mission was proceeding smoothly, but shortly after our warp jump, the Incident occurred.
The Main Confinement Cell was the source of the insurrection. It was the holding site for an especially dangerous passenger who possessed high psychic potential and was known to incite disobedience in others. I do not know how he was able to free himself or how he summoned the forces of Chaos to abet him. His psychic outburst spread rapidly across the entire vessel, sending other passengers into a frenzy and causing them to attack my acolytes.
I have given the order for the passenger holds to be purged and activated the automatic intruder elimination systems, but I have no doubt that this measure will be unsuccessful.
Not wishing to surrender the Monarchia's Bane into the hands of these deranged mutants, I have set course to orbit a nearby planet at a slight deviation. Sooner or later, the deviation will result in the ship drifting out of orbit and crashing to the planet's surface.
Keep the faith, and exterminate any mercy in your soul."

bdb4a8fc-101f-4728-a068-675d585576ea.Text: A health augmetic that has clearly undergone blasphemous alteration and is now a vessel for corruption. However, it still performs its earlier function.

10629449-8cde-4ab5-93ce-a949f2591e89.Text:
"After the last shift consolidation, they transferred me to the Pariah barracks. And everything they say about these freaks is true. I don't know if they're raised this way or if they really don't have a soul, but just being near them makes me feel sick to my stomach. Cold, unfeeling, empty creatures pretending to be human. They beat and execute the passengers like it's nothing. A normal person is disgusted at the thought of smashing a person's skull... well, either that, or they like it. But not them — they don't care one bit. If it was up to me, I'd toss them in the hold with the rest of the mutants, but... the psyker tricks don't work on them at all. Very handy when you're travelling on a ship stuffed full of enraged psykers.
I had to move one of the psykers from the communal hold to separate quarters. That traitorous piece of shit was encouraging the others to revolt, and our esteemed Ship's Confessor ordered us to give him a good hiding. We beat him for two hours or so, and by the end my damned cough had got so bad it was unbearable.
I'm worried I'll be called in to see the chirurgeon. If command find out about the crap in my lungs, they'll toss me straight out of the airlock. My only hope is my new augmetic, though the guy who fitted it on Flacia Prima was strange. He gave me the creeps, and so did all his machinery. No doubt it was all illegal under the Imperium's laws. But I didn't have a choice — a wretched bilge rat of a voidsman would never rise high enough to have his aches and pains treated by someone from the Adeptus Mechanicus. I'm just going to hope that this thing clears up on its own."

5a63672c-0b73-4db0-ba08-6a8da9afc7b7.Text: [Request status of the bunker's life support system]

bafb33bb-4885-4d3d-805e-c5141cbc1125.Text: "Energy regulation system: unknown error. WARNING! Backup generator connected."

aa957b35-2ffd-42eb-a4a2-a8f3249f60c8.Text: "System check... Processing input data... Data confirmed. Compressor launch in progress. Pressure levels nominal. WARNING! Error 110011 110000 110011 encountered: insufficient power. Booting emergency energy profiles... Success. Pressurising facility... Success. Booting compressor... Success. Emergency air filters: activated. Automated defence systems: activated."

df8aeda9-cc00-4dde-b075-bdb009ea70e5.Text: "WARNING: request denied. Air duct system malfunction detected."

e2c03ad9-1572-4973-991b-4deaa88509ed.Text: {n}Pasqal offers the cogitator a reverent bow, chanting the binharic aria of launch priming.{/n} "The spirit of this machine embodies resilience and indomitability. In this den of decay and entropy, still does it reign over this place."

ddeb5622-018f-48ec-8423-2572fdeaa070.Text: "Oxygen supply system: failed. WARNING! Air filters damaged."

0bac8d9c-f47a-4355-a5e9-fbc45f30cc78.Text: "Temperature and humidity control system: failed. Reason: unknown."

ee2f3341-3eec-43b7-8362-5dcd49e273a5.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox hisses mournfully,{/n} "With your permission, I would extract the command blocks of this noble machine to hold a vigil for its deceased spirit. The Omnissiah preserves the faithful."

40c07041-ca6f-482d-a1c1-63481aff0899.Text: "Death to offworlders! The Anvers rule Footfall!"

df3439ae-828a-4100-8c7d-b6e0f03f4047.Text: "You are on the right path, Seeker. Remember the place: Small Quay, large windows."

e3c08567-2ec6-4096-af06-c64d3de8ea81.Text: "Hold the line! Don't let them escape!"

0745755f-c7f9-4487-b638-f7f35f52efa5.Text: "I'm telling you, they're stricken with plague! Their whole ship is plagued!"

c8e96d27-dcb4-4990-b596-2ba5d4dbd152.Text: "How can the Liege stand for this? They should've stoned them all! Fine, then... we'll deal with this ourselves!"

5e9e5b39-9477-458f-905a-9e0a0f413292.Text: "You meet all kinds on Footfall. And you can't tell right away who just looks crazy, and who's an enemy of Humanity hiding among His faithful..."

8efad119-37a3-44d3-8729-95b229b052c5.Text: "They say you can find anything your heart desires on Footfall..."

58f4d78b-108a-474e-9067-a41c78dce75a.Text: "The air here is so fetid and stale... How has no one else noticed?"

d20ea980-8ed7-422c-8511-ded9c4b7f753.Text: "When will my shuttle arrive? My patience is almost at an end!"

7157b135-cfe1-4b14-9ff5-0d8f312c89d1.Text: "You look like a worthy servant of the Imperium. A rarity in this place."

13dde5bb-9874-419e-8f08-3cceca210dd3.Text: "Object identified as: Lord. Captain. {name}. Von. Valancius."

4f7e5c90-981f-4c88-b6c6-191c86534c0d.Text: "Unit Opticon-22 extends his official greetings and invites you to a synchronous communication."

ce16ee84-b9b0-49e8-9498-6edbf53977ca.Text: "Convergence point: Dock. Alpha. Rho. Topic of communication: Discharge. Of. Contract. Logisticar. Theta."

b67c0a93-eb2d-4d2d-940c-ccf8f5b3dddc.Text: "Logisticar Theta? I remember that contract. Theodora made that twenty-five, thirty years ago?"

259dae16-61e2-45ca-a063-b800c615ed97.Text: "We filled up six Adeptus Mechanicus promethium tankers on Vheabos VI. And I am certain that we never received payment."

bd612f00-8bac-48b5-83cb-9c82853e4b14.Text: "They say one of the asteroids tore free from its tethers... You have to keep your wits about you round here."

ac82c4ea-be41-4bd2-a41b-74ba209fe4a2.Text: "Furibundus's gravitational waves are playing up again. Mark my words, one day this star is just going to overheat and explode..."

bce5920e-67bd-4612-baf1-40f72fc456cc.Text: "Yes? What can I do you for?"

bb32f303-b51a-43f3-8b71-dfadf47a1e40.Text: "May the Omnissiah rip off the legs of that degenerate who last appeased my vessel's machine spirit..."

4711a25c-bf9b-438b-8d54-657e9b79f69e.Text: "For Lord Vladaym Tocara, Liege of Footfall — a noble visitor!"

9c1ddf68-e474-4269-bab2-3dc79d307224.Text: "For Lord Vladaym Tocara, Liege of Footfall — the most noble Rogue Trader of House von Valancius!"

ef9e7261-c3d2-4cc6-a2b2-33cf656a9d94.Text: "Just had a word with a voidsman from the ship that arrived last... Says he was on the bridge when their Lord Captain gave the order to destroy a whole planet!"

8b2bec67-2f66-43e4-86aa-d25ccd937fc8.Text: "He's got no clue. Maybe the Lord Captain had it in for the governor. Maybe didn't like the climate. Who knows with them high and mighty types..."

35ced39f-1286-42d9-bb8b-4df147189e1f.Text: "How many people died on that world? Oh, Emperor protect us..."

30dc90cb-e9e6-4ceb-a6e9-b0dc2699e871.Text: "They stayed and waited for every shuttle! Every last one! They left no one behind!"

688d0e6d-01d5-4be1-975c-7e5b6953bbc2.Text: "The ground was pretty much burning beneath our feet. I saw people who were losing their minds — just dropping to their knees and tearing their eyes out..."

5a538166-0fb0-47f8-862c-ed9133c31599.Text: "And that's how you made it off the planet?"

dd93fcfe-1c6a-4197-8a28-0eb51918a231.Text: "That's right! My whole family's here. I guess we'll... have a look around, see if we can find a spot for ourselves."

12a72557-3197-44aa-80f4-6c5d744cb8ad.Text: "Hey... you do know what happened to Lowthon, right? After he was taken aboard? Didn't he rip his own eyes—"

62cfbb9b-905a-4709-8313-a315a0aebeac.Text: "Stop. Lowthon was a brainless coward, and he died a coward. Let's not talk about him."

db00062f-67ed-4747-9998-8885dbb13d8e.Text: "Have you managed to contact your kin?"

fbecb3c3-f9e7-44cd-ba8a-a761a6094a0a.Text: "Alas, I have not... The people of Footfall have no respect for my standing, and the local Astropathic Choir is a bungling gaggle of heretics!"

614e0c2e-b424-4ba8-8758-7d12c6407a49.Text: "But my dear sir, you are alive. Surely such temporary inconveniences can be tolerated until you have reached your family demesne?"

03ebfcdf-edd5-41a0-a831-c7a97eb97b8e.Text: "I know, I know. I assure you, I am eternally grateful to the Lord Captain for our miraculous rescue from Rykad Minoris."

b9c6745a-4bba-4d65-8073-d616b0350269.Text: "Yet I must think about the future. We have been left without means of support, and I do not wish for my daughters to stay in this dreadful place a minute longer than they have to."

b3973273-97bd-459e-b66d-5125ed7f2a29.Text: "I offer you my sympathy, my dear sir. Oh, I do hope the bonds will be enough to purchase passage to Calixis..."

e5f4e2ca-00df-427a-af79-8c8824382e1b.Text: "The vox-spirits have brought me good tidings. The Miraculous Fusion Reactor, a sacred artefact, has been delivered to the system with an escort of Electro-Priests."

c744d3a9-c4c1-4b6b-919f-1bb153f87d74.Text: "Wondrous tidings indeed. At what time will we get to behold it so we may kneel before its splendour and offer our prayers to the ancient spirits of the machine?"

32a8d88e-0129-4869-92d5-f321df059fbb.Text: "The relic presently remains in the charge of the house of Rogue Trader von Valancius, who saved it from oblivion. The Rogue Trader's conscience will decide how best to apply the Reactor's potency."

c7c867df-0005-4155-a708-7a98d048a90c.Text: "I will pray for the Rogue Trader to receive a revelation from the Omnissiah that will let {mf|him|her} find a place becoming of the great machine's mighty energies."

71b3849f-5814-45c9-9ae0-d3c04d2ccb3c.Text: "Repent, malefactors. Unburden your souls, and the Emperor will be merciful. Admit what it is you do here! Is it piracy? Thievery? Selling smuggled goods? Talk, now!"

6208ac9e-1eae-4dbe-962c-4aa41cde7051.Text: "Good people, please! What's there to repent of? We're common dock workers. I swear on the Emperor's wounds, we're no lawbreakers!"

9cc488b6-c975-4a48-8f8d-d8a8caa26dd8.Text: "On the Emperor's wounds, you say? So if we happened to know that you're lying to us, that would make you not just a criminal, but a blasphemer too? And do you know of the punishment for blaspheming against Him?"

9aec7e81-b599-438f-b6f4-6339d3d01cf2.Text: "Please spare us! It was just his fear talking! I repent, I freely confess — my husband and I are concealing goods for the Kasballica. We take non-human trinkets from arriving ships and then deliver them to other ships. We repent!"

2486e7c7-3c12-4645-8b65-d3aaff9eaea9.Text: "Confession liberates the soul, does it not, sister? Can you feel the weight of the shame and guilt upon your shoulders becoming just a little easier to bear? You two will come with us to the confessional cells. I will help you relieve yourselves of the burden of your transgressions."

98b93a1b-9b21-4646-8045-9d58720e3a5c.Text: "Repent, unclean soul! Confess your wrongdoings! Do you know of the one who tipped off the pirates about the clipper Saint Cognatius? Were you one of the murderers there? Or were you just playing lookout?"

6868d638-5025-4dbe-9fe1-8f5f5ceea022.Text: "Unburden your soul. Your accomplices have already admitted to everything. If you repent, you will only get the stick and the prod. If you try to deny it, I will take out the knife."

0b0296ff-a0c6-4a70-8cb6-d038f59c0596.Text: "Clipper? What the grox are you on about? I haven't left the station in twenty-two years! I haven't held a single stolen thing in my life! I didn't rob no clippers, all right?"

6a1f9b0c-2e3d-43ae-be04-138f43638427.Text: "Maybe you didn't. But you know who did rob it. Or who sold the goods. Or who talked about knowing who sold them. Oh, you'll repent in our confessional. Everyone repents."

552da446-a1bf-411e-837d-51b83a64e396.Text: "Zander Sonatus's Courier Service! A letter for you!"

c96f75e0-741f-4a99-a249-4ea862adeba8.Text: "Thank you, thank you. It's been a while since I last received a letter. Hopefully it's from some young lady who is smitten with me! Ah. Hm. No, these... These are bills..."

71c89fe5-dc6e-4c3b-86f1-627bbfd47d48.Text: "Your Holiness Reverend Hieronymus! I have been authorised to deliver an anonymous donation to you."

bb032a30-841c-4ccc-b214-5853e7608ded.Text: "Its sender is too humble to give it to you in person. But they hope that it will benefit the servants of the true faith!"

26e7d984-d9aa-4bf2-a4ce-8962d94e645b.Text: "How impotent and vain is one who hopes to save their soul with gratuities!"

7b735a4d-498c-4fdd-a979-fdc24900bb03.Text: "Zander Sonatus's Courier Service! Here's your delivery!"

84af3eac-dd84-4cb3-8e8e-86906fad4265.Text: "Oh, that was quick. I didn't think I'd get it at all, considering the quarantine in the Shadow Quarters and all..."

b03f4781-b55c-453e-ab58-d69afc71e28d.Text: "Here's your coin, lad. Be seein' you."

ddeb61cd-2d2a-49e6-b4e1-b3413ce91fec.Text: "Zander Sonatus's Courier Service! Here's your delivery... a flick on the head!"

5348e6c7-046d-4d76-8e85-353771d0b000.Text: "Oh, lighten up, buddy! How have you been? How's service, how's life?"

c776460e-2240-4ded-96e9-57b60532f828.Text: "Ugh, don't even ask. It's them again... you know... the Anvers. They've gotten so cocky, we're really up against it."

143cc084-3f1d-40fb-9a75-d80261ad8cf5.Text: "And here I thought guarding the rich folks' lounge was a cushy job!"

b629ab4d-6b24-4087-b1ec-8512461e81bf.Text: "Zander Sonatus's Courier Service! Any orders? Today we're offering a discount for regular customers!"

64ba24a9-969e-4197-99d6-9a839e97b0c4.Text: "Listen, Zander. I've known you for five years, and all this time you've been introducing yourself like that. What's the point when the 'service' is just you?"

89701cd2-969c-4934-8515-6ed5c4d8e6b5.Text: "Do you know how nice it is to say, 'Zander Sonatus's Courier Service'? It makes me feel like I'm someone important, not just a piss-poor errand boy!"

efe73c9e-cec6-425e-ae80-254ebcad06df.Text: "Greetings, gorgeous Ryzza! Would you like to send an anonymous donation to His Holiness?"

6e7e3fb6-11e9-43a2-b0ce-ac5c5dbf0738.Text: "I would. Here. Make sure you give it to the reverend or one of the preachers personally!"

6b1b5106-0544-46ba-b163-e2953e5e1764.Text: "Of course. I would never do something as wicked as pocketing priestly donations. The Emperor sees all!"

17e0d768-43b0-45e0-bccf-b5b0d12a96db.Text: "They say He might miss a few things in the Shadow Quarters — He's got his back to us here. Hah! Ack, now I'll have to atone for this blasphemy too. Me and my big mouth..."

c11c29c9-c08c-446a-98e1-a127c04652de.Text: "Doubt is the first step toward heresy! Deliver your weak minds from thought and direct all aspirations of the soul to the service!"

8e2eb196-3089-463b-8abd-c5c5f85cfb7d.Text: One of the many altars. It looks better tended than most places on Footfall.

d5c38faa-0e6f-4331-a5f9-67ceb0bdf782.Text: "They say the cogs kidnap people on Footfall and then sacrifice them on their station near the star. How the Emperor even lets this happen..."

85c1a386-473d-488d-81bf-906c4031212a.Text: "I've spent my whole life on Footfall. I've heard that on the planets it goes between dark and light... what a nonsense!"

41ee57c1-7ee8-4d18-acaf-f31dd9a2db5f.Text: "If you have somewhere to go... you don't linger on Footfall."

fe7d4610-5f5e-4f43-bdf9-d73282d3bdbe.Text: "What's the news? It's been a long time since we had visitors from Calixis..."

8b876c3d-c888-45fb-a2b5-b35072102770.Text: "Long live the protector of Footfall! Glory to Rogue Trader von Valancius!"

ea9376c2-7143-42a4-9e37-944e8cd0fea1.Text: "Everyone, look! Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, we're forever in your debt!"

9d3017c2-d6d5-4e45-b264-3f4e43a30a72.Text: "Glory to House von Valancius! Glory to the Rogue Trader!"

e1016871-42a2-4eb5-9f2a-7acd02377de0.Text: "May the God-Emperor keep you from misfortune as you kept Footfall from dying a hungry death!"

a0a7a987-3f2f-496b-8f62-be4e8ab37f9f.Text: "I'd just made soup out of my last soles... and then, just like that, it was over. They started handing out rations again, and they're even better than before."

84f60d31-e21d-4441-bb95-45ddabb8fb67.Text: "As if, it's the same old corpse starch. That's the hunger talking, making you think the new bars taste sweeter."

1e3db862-1e5f-43dc-a6a7-a9ee20deffe2.Text: "It's not that! Didn't you hear? The Liege's palace received boxes of real vegetables! So they must've made the nutribars out of better stuff too!"

4e0a0f7b-17e8-4e5e-bbc7-23a5d1a06bdb.Text: "Vegetables? What, that stuff they grow on worlds? Haven't seen any in my life..."

3b9b1823-096c-4210-9714-6ac26adc5b04.Text: "They say shipments are now coming in from some agri-world or other... Ooh, I wish I could have a bite of something grown right in the dirt!"

871a3456-9006-414e-8a05-4b3fc4d47088.Text: "Life on Footfall is returning to normal. About time, too — those hunger riots, huh?"

804e23e0-6342-4540-94be-761d4c554266.Text: "The riots were one thing, but the Liege's goons were really grinding me down. Grabbing every other sod, interrogating them, looking for 'instigators'..."

9b90b605-cdc7-481b-abc0-8c8c1bf6cfba.Text: "Well, all that's over now. Honestly, I'm just glad not to be chewing on synth-meat anymore."

a5552449-bcf2-4f63-b198-0ce73e41acd6.Text: "Courtesy of some bigwigs on Footfall, from what I hear. Apparently we now have a powerful patron looking out for us."

373828dd-a2a0-4b6b-ab05-0a35d5ebbc2c.Text: Like pretty flowers overgrown with weeds, the halls of Footfall's former palaces and temples have been overrun by the shabby houses of the present-day inhabitants.

7b4ffdcf-3040-47e0-8c0a-e30037be82e2.Text: "Where are you? Where are you speaking to me from? Come back! Come back!"

b81e5f13-1611-4417-aa6f-a0a337696b9a.Text: "I remember I was supposed to be somewhere... What do I do? Ugh, my head is so heavy..."

101867a7-4d60-487a-a986-8cc2a82e09e4.Text: "Oh! I understand, I understand now! Listen... No, it got away from me again..."

423af694-2280-4828-9559-faa52181682b.Text: "Can you hear the music? It's... the most terrifying thing I've ever heard... Terrifying... yet beautiful..."

b3e49e7b-aba4-4df3-af2f-3e88436a51c8.Text: "Do we have any more of that amasec? Yes, from... that planet?"

4f99928b-c682-44f6-805e-47d5b34c6f39.Text: A stall selling old knickknacks for everyday needs.

6bf6d6d0-3bdb-4040-960c-72985a21a1c2.Text: A small food booth. The portions look meagre.

63025468-5fdd-4045-a4ef-da98afd08787.Text: Footfall's levels are situated between huge supports resembling scaffolding — it seems a new concept for the interior design was started before the previous one could be implemented.

c189c602-3435-401b-931a-65121c90fdaa.Text: The heart of Footfall is a colossal statue of the Emperor carved from a single asteroid.

89b1bb69-9e75-4998-b594-6dd43f5cad92.Text: The wares here are shoddy-looking weapons built out of questionable parts.

1228c166-0897-4b11-8aec-ea6ef92cd1a8.Text: "This rash... I hope my overseer won't notice — he's been a right nightmare lately..."

5aca066c-fb1d-4b01-9e2f-900d8e33dee8.Text: "Something is wrong with the new rations... Maybe we shouldn't eat them? But I'm tired of dying of hunger..."

d27090cd-0510-4c30-8510-fd7ec678b52b.Text: "Emperor... heh heh... what a funny word. Never thought about it... but still, funny..."

6d196d57-60d0-462d-9d9d-b64b763cb20a.Text: "Ah? Who's talking? No, I'm not listening! Heresy again!"

f2e28691-0d2c-4ef5-bed6-bedd906cda8f.Text: "The hunger is over, but it hasn't gotten any better... It's as if some kind of haze spread across the void station. We live in terrible times..."

8dbd3d77-5c6d-4b96-9110-8dc46e5ba238.Text: "The Emperor protects! Glory to the God-Emperor! Glory to Her Ladyship Incendia Chorda!"

e886ccb9-2d53-4dd0-8f87-07f572360710.Text: "No! Don't hit me! Wait, you're not one of those..."

25ec17c0-24c0-472b-a9ea-8c1d1e38fbcf.Text: "Every morning, someone else is gone... A lot of heretics were holed up on Footfall, looks like! Well, now all of them will be smoked out..."

ef7dfe3e-a9d3-4744-b071-9b7e2d92f151.Text: "They say that bonfires were recently seen in the Shadow Quarters... Entire families were burned..."

54958f91-4e48-47e4-82cf-107bac2bc07d.Text: "It seems to be safer here with the patrols around, but if one of them targets you..."

35bb413a-ff3a-4aea-8dd0-1eaf45b9779a.Text: "Now things are looking up! I heard the warehouses are bursting with nutribars — everyone, even the folk from the Shadow Quarters, will have enough!"

c129bc84-7c7d-44b1-813f-22f25d9327ba.Text: "Glory to House von Valancius! If it wasn't for {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, we would have started eating each other by now!"

58d6735b-9c03-45b7-b81d-59404ebdc3c7.Text: "I got rations for myself, and for my brother's family... They've had it tough ever since he got chewed up in that grinder. Well, now maybe things will turn out all right and all the kids will survive!"

40959d3b-14e8-4f10-a7fa-20dbd3589338.Text: "Footfall started buzzing again when the first deliveries arrived. The enforcers even stopped going manic — they didn't even beat anyone to death last week!"

e79d9017-57de-4887-8aeb-7ba52053c223.Text: "One day, I'd love to see the place where these supplies come from... But, ah, what am I saying? My place is here."

54b8b8b0-473b-4bf9-88a2-13c17f6b2d65.Text: "The voyage through the Archenemy's realm was so long... but at last, we have reached our destination!"

9f950074-2ca9-4e50-8488-1fa5aef1ee47.Text: "They say the Emperor sent His angels here, and they used their swords to carve this majestic statue from an asteroid!"

27d1e451-40ba-4728-aa26-0bda297e00c5.Text: "May the Emperor and Drusus the Warrior guide my feet!"

797cc9f2-e284-4fdb-a0cc-ef0eef47b617.Text: "Footfall... at last... Will I really hear one of Reverend Hieronymus's sermons with my own ears?"

6a60ba33-f953-4fd6-86a2-71cdfa9ebe5b.Text: "What a job — keeping order in a place like Footfall..."

e2b60fdc-56ec-4279-8b4a-d30f26580117.Text: "The Anvers are driving us up the wall..."

8cc0cb24-bbbd-473f-b038-743e2d881f98.Text: Life of Saint Drusus, Volume Three

ed0ede70-965b-4e35-b31a-f00dbc9eee7f.Text: "Welcome to Footfall! You can rest here... away from the irksome rabble."

dfe3a092-ba85-47f4-8457-be854c8ff7ea.Text: "Have they cut the rations, the sneaky cheats? I could have sworn there used to be more broth for lunch..."

251105f1-3d6d-438b-96e7-4c9bc1d5dc4c.Text: "Vladaym is not a man to be messed with. A far cry from the old Liege!"

cd65c0b2-57da-417b-b5bb-775f33059eae.Text: "Hey, newcomers. How's this for a warm welcome?"

29d56b12-6ac7-48bb-9d35-1ee8b6e26b70.Text: A small altar depicting the saints of the Imperium.

0f83e4e9-590f-45b1-9fa7-3f12c04d614c.Text: A small altar. The central spot has been given to Drusus — a saint from the neighbouring Calixis Sector who is widely revered in the Koronus Expanse.

e595d000-e89f-4588-8878-7249e3637783.Text: At first glance, these look like standard containers, but their frames have been reinforced and their sealing improved to keep the smell in. These are used to transport contraband.

db09b0ff-72fb-4f95-8fa5-4b8f781c67a2.Text: Standard containers for transporting large cargo.

728afe81-1237-4e11-ae31-fd3973951ab9.Text: The walls of the container have rusted and its contents rotted away. A situation that is not uncommon for shipments trying to pass through Imperial customs.

e7a48253-be00-41de-a9ae-7dd8e57c2d86.Text: The container is marked "foodstuffs," but it is empty and, by the looks of it, has not been moved in a while.

64355ef2-ea06-42a5-aee3-1f8926c37780.Text: The container is labelled "Destination: Janus." It is covered in dust — it must have spent a long time at the docks.

55585200-7c06-4821-83d5-ac343f897e3f.Text: There is nothing remarkable in the old broken container.

c11ec7d1-50f1-4cd8-95a8-209eca5c6c8d.Text: "Are you from the von Valancius ship? You may pass without a check — an order came from the Liege to let you through!"

511529b6-b70a-479e-8809-d3b3d8f32239.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, gracious {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius! Please, go right ahead! No checks are needed for you!"

030dfebd-c1a2-423f-9c97-b3944f413388.Text: The corpse looks horrifying — the victim was thoroughly beaten before being shoved into the crack between the boxes. One of the hands is clutching a bloodstained paper.

8594ec79-d908-4ac5-bf07-e83ac1bfd705.Text: "Voidships are one of the Omnissiah's miracles."

14cdd1a2-7720-4b84-878e-62e2993c09e9.Text: {n}A familiar figure turns to you. Heinrix van Calox, Interrogator of the Ordo Xenos, bows his head respectfully.{/n} "Lord Captain."

a996b650-713f-4ba9-a00e-52370a919268.Text: "Form A/716B is valid for up to eleven hours from the placement of the stamp. You have submitted it after fourteen hours and eight minutes. Your cargo registration request is denied!"

a1d7c7e6-fe38-4d31-9d63-dd2024c8c1e5.Text: "Double tariff? Come on, mate, we've known each other for eight years! Where do you get these numbers from?"

3a77126c-601a-4dac-9c4b-f4f6e534adbe.Text: "I know that bird! The local Adeptus Mechanicus uses it to get around. Their boats are easy to tell apart from all the pirates, smugglers, and other scum."

9a32d569-bba4-4d78-903f-2bae671d770e.Text: "Come and buy goods from the best recolliger crews in the sector!"

e344eea2-529f-45f5-a5b9-c9cdd3311dc3.Text: "What the void is with the ration cuts? What's Vladaym doing with all that broth anyway, having a bath in it?"

e9c1f797-298c-43e0-8f4d-a6866f7047ee.Text: "In the glop we're being fed? Not even sewer slugs would bathe in that."

1a44f11f-0954-4ab8-8e1e-b75c3c9dff69.Text: "Footfall is still the best place in the Expanse. The air here is... different somehow."

39f0e839-4b87-47f1-bbdc-534e2dec4c3a.Text: "My brother's bucket left for Port Wander five years back and still hasn't returned. You'd think it'd be back by now..."

7f2d0e0e-030d-494d-9483-62eeabaa79c8.Text: "Pirate or honest trader — it's hard to tell the difference sometimes... especially on Footfall."

323576b6-651e-44fe-8ef5-1015b9b1b1ec.Text: Note From the Cache by the Dock Windows

93c4c354-ca97-4a9f-b00a-4ec09b85b473.Text: "The answer is close, Seeker. Remember the word: 'realising'. Remember the place: a tunnel in the shadow of a bridge, a bridge in the shadow of the great statue."

6bf88f9b-4cf9-4e20-968e-c5e3c61c203a.Text:
"May the Emperor's faithful forever remain in the light of His favour.
Let me first express my condolences on the tragic death of the most honourable Theodora von Valancius. Nevertheless, I was elated to learn that the Warrant of the Rogue Trader has been passed to a worthy and promising heir. These words are not hollow compliments, but rather the Inquisition's official opinion of your person.
As fate would have it, you have taken the reins of the von Valancius dynasty in an hour most dire, when grim portents of dark events to come are surfacing throughout the Koronus Expanse. I have been duty-bound to become the first sentinel who sees the approaching threat, and I hereby alert you that it is indeed coming. Our loyalty and resolve will be tested. People such as you and I will become the pillars that will unite the Emperor's frightened children and inspire them to fight back.
And so I greet you as my dependable ally and assure you of my favour. From now on, you have a trusted friend within the Holy Orders of the Emperor's Inquisition and a receptive confidant on whom you can rely. Should the dark times ahead require you to make questionable choices, have no doubt that such an incident will be examined in an exceedingly temperate fashion that rules out the most radical forms of judgement.
I have faith in the success of our partnership and thank you for your contribution, both past and future.
Lord Inquisitor Xavier Calcazar"

a12cf8c9-6ead-45e4-a216-009f51e3b3eb.Text: Letter from Lord Inquisitor Xavier Calcazar

7d962758-3d33-4455-a4f7-9f29889b6571.Text: "Take this rubbish back to wherever you found it. I won't accept it — don't even ask."

255804f6-663d-41e9-ab2d-3dbe56fc1a44.Text: Anvers' Note Left From Cinder's Crew

bd0a3030-2aa3-4328-9d3e-0dd0f25eeee0.Text: "He's waiting for you. You know the place, so be there on time. The turn can be seen from the entrance to the Adeptus — make sure some gawker doesn't see where you're going."

b762140a-3619-4e6c-a4d4-e5be5fa07eef.Text: "Who holds a flamer like that, you idiot? We're almost refuelled here, we'll show you how it's done!"

3bce9918-5f42-43ff-87f5-839ee240181d.Text: "I'm just not feeling it anymore, that's all. The guy is pretty much a cinder now — it was a lot more fun when he was alive and thrashing about!"

69f5c30b-c52c-4711-9728-5ba62b6af763.Text: "Look at that. Here comes another training target for us! Fire it up, you lot!"

a1ff4825-0539-4d09-9cb4-d5d6f21d8f11.Text: The crumpled note only has this small fragment of text left: "You are on the right path, Seeker! The other caches..."

20b213a5-2128-4048-8716-760690571a69.Text: The small nook in the stone is empty apart from dust and a few scraps of paper. There is evidence that the cache once had a small door covering it and a locking mechanism.

ec0d3ea4-caf7-4a4d-b17b-4441e976101b.Text: Note From the Cache in the Old Tunnel

daa3c4f5-f3ea-4f34-82b7-98a5e7e6731f.Text: "This is the final stretch, Seeker. Remember the second word: 'design.' Remember the place: cogitator, statue of the Founder, Small Temple."

7a503bc1-8b18-4663-822d-49f9b2a7ebe0.Text: The rusty sign, emblazoned with the words "Adeptus Amasecus" in jagged lettering, is drunkenly askew. Deep scratches and dents are visible under a thick layer of soot, dirt, and ancient paint.

5c95ccdc-8134-489c-ab46-0e9a9328fa5b.Text: Under a layer of rust, scratches, and ancient paint, the silhouettes of long-erased letters are barely visible. Undoubtedly, in the past, this filthy sign was adorned with the proud name of the bureaucratic heart of the entire Imperium — "Adeptus Administratum."

a84a4b1a-4d8e-4af7-8585-8b7c3fdafca0.Text: The victim of a murder — one of the countless crimes that take place on Footfall every day.

85043f6e-0735-454c-b9f0-2d0869d30329.Text: The numerous wounds and injuries indicate that this was a particularly brutal murder. The letters "A N V" are carved into the victim's shoulder blade.

a059c461-59d4-4efb-8f9f-dfee9c4eb361.Text: "That's the one. I think he was from the Kasballica... Well, his troubles are over now."

2a19cc87-6920-4532-aa4c-68a12b4cb0c1.Text: "Oh, by the Throne... that's him, isn't it? The poor sap who got his tongue cut out by the Anvers?"

fc16043d-f112-480e-8f25-f312e3aa4a88.Text: "You saw the chap who blew his brains out? The Anvers cut out his tongue and eyes, and he couldn't pay for implants. So he just..."

b09ff6c2-1485-4eff-8975-1abd2986caf7.Text: "Your cousin's talking rubbish. We don't have toffs like that in the Expanse!"

f1a1a616-4e99-4013-9867-d733957d3694.Text: "Well, a Rogue Trader could gamble away a planet, but I haven't heard of Chorda or, I don't know, von Valancius pulling a stunt like that..."

94e009a2-a8be-4fbb-817a-4359152d1eb4.Text: "My cousin said he saw some aristocrat lose a whole planet in a game of cards!"

6e9c55dd-031a-490c-9caa-3581e5517e41.Text: "The break's about to end... Let me in, just for a minute!"

9b028c2e-3650-4dd0-85d4-60713c66c385.Text: The indistinct hum of discontented voices hangs over the crowd. The street vendors seem to be lacking some essentials, and in their impotence the people do not hold back their angry exclamations and curses.

56923806-06cc-4a2a-bd2d-1304f0524b6e.Text: People in the crowd look greedily at goods for which they have neither coupons nor money.

5c9f4668-56e0-4b74-96d7-e6c0bcb5fa09.Text: This door is not just locked — it is welded shut. Opening it is currently impossible.

feeff70f-ff83-4807-835b-10932eb5805d.Text: The intoxicating smell of a hookah hangs in the air.

c9957980-7011-4833-89c5-cee2f352f107.Text: "You think I won't knock your block off? Think again!"

30b083be-386e-4cd7-8a38-dbb2288183c6.Text: "Worthless scum! Who do you think you are, louse?"

c776c302-4a59-4443-9696-bbf6224da429.Text: "Someday the Liege will get rid of every one of you worthless cattle!"

6b0f2c58-867a-4c1d-98e8-d8b978bdf275.Text: "What are you on about — lying? We haven't even drunk to His Holiness Hieronymus's health yet!"

8a2d9165-8453-476b-a5ab-90d427731d28.Text: "God-Emperor... can you hear me? If you can, take me as quick as you can..."

a207d169-40bc-433a-a5be-294eac9cb5bd.Text: "The gangrene's spreading... Grant me perseverance... that I may toil for Your glory..."

07564c5d-5bf5-45d5-9c11-8fc47b2a5c4d.Text: "Give me the strength to live until the end of my shift... just a little bit of strength..."

d377f44d-fbfe-443b-ab38-b085574f12a0.Text: "I once stood on the pinkie finger of the Emperor's statue!"

8c45d3bf-11d7-4406-bea2-fa472f53ffcf.Text: "If only I could go to another asteroid... The Shadow Quarters are killing me!"

7bb0ca11-5c4b-4548-bd84-bcfb9b611da9.Text: "Help! Help! My brother... he fell off the roof, he's bleeding out!"

8ac102fd-7a0a-44cb-a803-123573d19938.Text: "Please! Take everything I have, just help him! It isn't far!"

a3b3266e-8152-4989-9ebf-2090a109767c.Text: "Everything you have, eh? Fine. Lead the way, just be quick about it."

08aeebba-1d9d-4b94-af04-ce0ea87e8727.Text: "Just give me a reason — I'll cut you in a second!"

c9a8bb4d-c4bf-480d-8b4a-ba498608c654.Text: "Tomorrow I'll climb up to the atrium... maybe I'll stumble across something and stay alive for another day..."

13bf9dbc-2e42-480e-987b-f56a7f2d9ddf.Text: "They're coming to collect in two days... but how am I supposed to get any coins? With my broken fingers, I can't steal nothing!"

de299446-8bef-4ada-935b-7c0d717d1db6.Text: "People are right when they say He's forgotten the people who wind up in this sector..."

203e40f3-ec87-4e29-a87d-c7ed510060c6.Text: "They say that back in Parsimus Dewain's time, they would give everyone on Footfall a crate of rotgut every month!"

1088ea49-e8e3-4a56-936b-0440c3758ea9.Text: "Don't miss out on the best bar on Footfall — the Adeptus Amasecus!"

825c6534-a874-4a98-a363-2e5584e87327.Text: The grimy, scuffed sign offers to install top-quality used implants.

4e1bfe52-2bc7-4711-93df-67e1972fa3d8.Text: A well-worn poster with a call to serve the Imperium.

d591b4c4-6606-4b55-bf94-2c0fab57a68b.Text: A part of an ancient sewer system. The pipes lead somewhere deep within the asteroid.

9ff2f126-4539-49df-9cda-84dd84a461e1.Text: There was once a mine entrance here, but it caved in decades ago.

fc261605-b723-4554-9e1f-9a2f5fcd4954.Text: "Devote your body to work, and your soul to the Emperor!"

54a0a52a-b523-477c-a670-56fb5e203534.Text: The letters "A N V" are scrawled in a few spots on the box.

f7a99a0c-c76e-4dd6-b238-fc7d34f13f47.Text: "Look at that... offworlders... Whatcha doing down here, eh? Footfall is ours! The Anvers are the power here!"

1d335d33-2898-4541-9762-a01b38f30c43.Text: "Hey, you! Don't you know the rule? You lay a hand or an eye on the Anvers' goods — you pay with your hand or your eye!"

f3d5dac7-10d9-4dae-adc7-b43171b7f228.Text: The serial number on the container is FVDA1-16165.

3f22daa5-45f9-48e8-8f5c-ec7ae1b17b51.Text: [The man lets out a strange inarticulate cry]

2acd9fa5-a84c-4015-b2a1-75dbfef11200.Text: Loosely buried under the piles of trash are bodies with obvious gunshot wounds.

89f89921-324b-479e-a748-8f885cecbf4a.Text: "A toast! A toast! To the glory of the Imperium, the accuracy of our weapons, and the strength of our drinks!"

b6636166-9c82-47e3-b3aa-8edb99aa5481.Text: "Footfall sure is a nice place... the best in the Expanse, I'd say..."

bea04914-0a93-42fe-bb7f-a990acec2f44.Text: "I once dreamt of joining the Adeptus Administratum. Didn't work out! But guess what — I'm a full-fledged member of the Adeptus Amasecus!"

b4792421-4288-4c66-8b9c-d87ad129f6c3.Text: "Five rotgut, three amasec... Gotta get it right!"

e15e86a8-1b6c-4a79-aef2-80bdc9024ba4.Text: "My implant's on the blink. Again. Maybe a bit of sacred oil would do the trick... I'll do it myself, no need to involve an Enginseer..."

4d8a9e49-a93d-4824-9461-12e77c0dece4.Text: "I've already had two emergency work orders come through... one after the other! If I'm alive by the end of them, I'll count myself lucky!

1ad36bbb-418d-486a-a553-cc8c4eb746e7.Text: "Twelve more hours... twelve hours, and then I can sleep..."

4cba65e0-c499-4ce7-9822-64493ecbcf87.Text: "We didn't touch anything! We haven't taken a thing!"

04954060-02f7-4311-8360-e7f9ee94cd23.Text: "How am I supposed to work if they broke my ribs?"

010ff5ec-6955-4480-9e4b-d911e18292a5.Text: A pair of eyes lights up in the darkness — too big to be human, too intelligent to be an animal. A moment later, the vision vanishes.

f50e6a0b-d8b7-4516-97f2-3f40aae86a74.Text: "So I'm walking along this bridge, right? I've only had one — just one! — glass of rotgut. And when I reach this very spot, I realise I'm falling!"

f4ceb8fb-1625-4b1a-8288-8f47f6d37353.Text: "Pull the other one. I've known three great lads who fell off this bridge when they were drunk. All three of 'em died."

d32dc7fb-c37f-432a-9103-be81c0dc2382.Text: "I'm not pulling anything! I was falling! I could already see mutants swarming below, ready to eat me alive! But then..."

83a7c876-9782-47d1-ac45-35d737222565.Text: "But then what? Come on, spit it out already!"

065175b8-cc4e-4f07-8284-4d5166c68d28.Text: "But then the Emperor's statue stretched its hand out, grabbed me, and put me back on the bridge!"

57985a39-a473-42eb-b69b-22823d742d00.Text: "Oh, brother. I wouldn't go spreading that story if I was you, pal. Someone might think it's heresy..."

0618e605-2b34-4ad1-ad92-3a55dc6a5d94.Text: "Behave yourselves! Anyone who starts a fight or tries to cut in gets the boot!"

db897c5c-d87f-46ab-af6e-320a51dccf3a.Text: "You jump the queue, you get no rations!"

b6bbb74c-7836-4778-b4fb-aba51f9f6f39.Text: "Right, then, what have we here? Double rations, for you and for your husband... I thought your husband kicked the bucket?"

49ade935-46e0-4885-a8a2-6d3b9e27823f.Text: "You sure this is a stamp? I can't make it out at all. And the letters don't fit in the boxes. These papers aren't fake by any chance, are they?"

740df0c8-8768-4366-ae2d-da47f9170b0d.Text: The supports of an ancient bridge. Many spots bear traces of decorative details that have been ripped off.

478fa166-9329-4196-a671-767aa62cb3a1.Text: "I wonder what's the right way to pray — before going to the bar or after?"

19d79ead-7c83-4966-a9f5-904f31fd03c2.Text: "Finally, home sweet scrapyard! I thought I'd never see you again! The recolligers are still kicking!"

20dfae5d-4aaa-4a8d-8f77-2d920ea34bf0.Text: A moonshine still. The air is thick with the smell of alcohol.

917de979-65b6-4ed2-88b0-7e740317130c.Text: It wasn't time that destroyed these tiles — they were definitely pried out with purpose and diligence.

ac7e7728-4770-4ba8-af51-9898c4c1038f.Text: Waste water, unsafe for drinking even after purification and now being used for laundering.

ed887f6c-41f9-40d4-8437-bc475e55cd1b.Text: From behind the closed doors, you hear the humming of primitive washing machines and the voices of laundry workers singing simple songs.

e7ac60be-0ff2-40a8-b051-9db69d8a752b.Text: "How much longer do I have to wait? My shift is about to start."

017e610b-2308-4f17-b602-6dd94f0185a7.Text: "First they cut the rations in half, and now they're dragging their feet handing them out!"

63e3728b-fda0-43f7-8e36-95df5a61ff83.Text: "Bunch of moaners. What matters is that they're giving you food — queuing up to get it isn't a hardship."

ddc285f5-aeff-4c77-9732-126bd057022b.Text: "I bet they feed those louts better than us!"

488322f2-a8ea-4264-9a35-9cd19b48425a.Text: "I want a hat like that! Where did you get yours?"

342e1a14-5588-4b9e-a100-d3ea6819f540.Text: "How d'you like my new clobber? Got them off a fine-looking fella..."

84a31b5f-94cf-498d-bdf2-1974e1365166.Text: "Can it, you fool! Last thing we need is to be caught bragging about murdering a blue blood in front of everyone! Let's scarper!"

fd8f9de4-dec3-4947-b0ce-966322e2ad8d.Text: "This new wig is too tight. I suppose I could have gone without it, but the old one is just too old!"

e527a997-9636-49b0-93e2-c6606e0cb2af.Text: "Oh, guide? How far away are we? We were promised a thrilling mutant hunt!"

2aede037-c16c-4135-ac30-6ef19c23cf40.Text: "Patience, patience, Your Graces, we're almost there! You'll have your hunt and your thrills!"

a2f34642-6f81-41d2-bc22-92158b8b9c1e.Text: "I saw a rat the other day. Big, fat one. Wish I'd caught it."

e4662b83-e851-47e0-adf8-bc7ed25fc282.Text: "And I was at the Atrium, listening to a sermon. They said things. But mostly just that we're 'doomed, doomed, doomed.'"

bb438389-13ee-4d34-942a-28a5103924c6.Text: "The holy people know best, of course. But I don't think we're that doomed. I mean, a rat's got to be a good omen, surely!"

7d779e99-c0c0-463e-975b-85ca3219413d.Text: "I've been wondering... What's the sky like?"

45640f8c-4d37-4f35-b1a9-718be9706bec.Text: "Well, it's, er... blue, more or less. Most of the time. On most worlds."

bba2fa3d-144b-4acb-b4ea-ad502ef43f1e.Text: "I know it's blue. But what's it like? Can you tell what it'd be like to sit under it?"

6238c653-989a-4f94-a3de-11cdfa9971fc.Text: "Listen here, Master Poet. What are you wasting time thinking about the sky for? Our ceiling don't leak water, it don't shoot lightning — life's good, Smokey, Emperor be praised!"

dec927e9-a4c5-4d7d-9fbc-6af959851829.Text: "No, he... He's not around anymore. Got hit by a loader bucket."

1c1965a8-08ac-427a-a4ba-5a2f5c20b93a.Text: "Wait... Hit and killed? Blimey, that's a bad way to go."

f1814564-7534-4f37-85aa-2d60ebac02a8.Text: "Yeah. The bucket just swung round and — bam! Smokey's head flew right off! He was a good fella. And now he's gone..."

fc1e2cc2-7e41-47b3-abe8-cc8f75bb2879.Text: The expensive-looking wig is smeared with blood... and what looks like brains.

e82801b5-f2fd-49b4-aac6-9b931baf68c4.Text: "No, warden! The papers are as real as they come!"

91d14caa-8d8e-44d0-a7f3-3f0491125361.Text: "Two rations, for me and my husband. Here's the stamp, the signature. It's all in order!"

f1d04311-5079-46b8-8a41-50d9e38be082.Text: "I am coming, Omnissiah! Deliver the Machines from the faithless!"

838763e4-89b7-4949-b8d5-88577cb0c9ee.Text: You can almost feel the evil oozing from the vile Chaos symbol. Your eyes start to water and you distinctly smell the putrid odour of rot.

b68a0047-d16e-4b13-b0d8-6081d0b6cbc7.Text: "Another room has been recaptured... We'll clear the whole voidship in no time!"

7c003faf-1451-4940-8435-c3c1a2d18193.Text: "If it wasn't for the holy sister and you... I don't think we would have survived."

b5ee3f32-535f-4506-94a3-cca8903185fc.Text: "Not a single pest will slip through, rest assured!"

0b32c12b-9050-4e7d-a4f7-11213c79a32b.Text: "We've lost so many... but it's fine, we'll hold out!"

678c6399-399d-474f-876f-c6d368ee49d0.Text: "We will follow you wherever you say!"

888c6233-46ec-4dbf-b8d4-8c2f4cff4121.Text: "I hope the heretics don't send reinforcements for their own."

edb6a74b-4d2b-4c1a-9a6a-5f69cf117e56.Text: "I think I've gone deaf from the noise..."

0bfdcb9c-13e1-4bd0-bc51-b6dc21d9db6f.Text: "If we break through to the gallery, it's only a short distance from there..."

1c94b94d-b3fe-421a-8e3e-08ce5baaa570.Text: "I never thought I'd see this deck in such a state..."

d7c97bd3-da5a-400e-a428-2d45ebf3e027.Text: "We're covering your back, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We won't let anyone get through!"

b41087a5-3266-4a29-b60b-0dd76087b92e.Text: "Damn, this smoke is still making my eyes water..."

830d1cf2-64c6-4647-800f-5d1eb9da1773.Text: "I thought I saw someone in the flames... Ah, never mind."

a51b7de5-00f3-4a85-bc01-2b35cb5d9ff0.Text: The molten rock is radiating tremendous heat. The surface bubbles and hisses softly as if the magma were incinerating the very air you breathe.

8f649726-df62-40f4-8109-35fecf54a848.Text: Massive claw marks are visible on the heavy bars.

36674f5f-0e39-40b8-8ec3-a46de7380481.Text: Judging by the information on the screen, the elevator's functions have been completely restored.

68ef2a0b-5a8b-4222-aee9-05a9a9c5572d.Text: The screen displays the elevator shutdown diagram. There are two devices that prevent the machine from functioning.

089f515a-7897-4271-8fc7-0f5354abf63a.Text: The screen displays a message about the first elevator block being removed.

40a674be-c9b6-434b-9692-5f98929dae53.Text: The screen displays a message about the second elevator block being removed.

5e2b27cd-1cb0-4e30-ad42-2faf3c17aad0.Text: The lockers are full of work overalls, robes, and tools that are covered in seals and emit the strong scent of sacred unguents.

b0ff794d-af83-4ae8-ba23-b4370140cf87.Text: "Free from the shackles of the false god, I was finally able to create the blueprint for a machine that stemmed from my mind's eye. Could I even have thought of such a thing while I was still caught in the Omnissiah's web?"

edb21bea-8b90-48a1-ad82-a60dbd858f05.Text: "But how? All our time and all our thoughts must be devoted to serving the Primordial Truth and the creation of its machine offspring."

384cadc6-7b43-4fc5-b6b8-074d434acf64.Text: "I draw inspiration from our works, tech-brother. The perfect mechanisms we create fill my mind with unparalleled ideas and schema."

23066e17-b2b9-4365-ab63-ad4b0d81b62c.Text: "Before, such words would have seen the True Flesh stripped from you. Blessed be the day when the Fabricator-Censor chose us to accompany him on the new path!"

570d460b-5444-4271-b3f9-e411c49c9287.Text: "Indeed! To let your mind wander free and to bravely plumb the depths of accumulated Knowledge is a pleasure above all others!"

f8336d07-892a-4c5a-a9ed-b7aa764cbd34.Text: "I would like to take a look once your great labour is complete. Perhaps your discoveries will let my mind shake off the ashes of the false faith and reveal new horizons."

562c3ae9-0ebc-44a9-812a-db0bab4f9418.Text: "The first turn of the large threaded rod is complete. Wash the joints with blood."

3e21dade-c157-45af-9972-35a70100064d.Text: "The second turn of the large threaded rod is complete. Offer the gifts wrung from the bodies of apostates."

b3400bcf-72f1-443a-a5e1-cc0e77a6a367.Text: "The machine stays silent. The gifts you offered failed to please the spirits."

02fec7c8-7aac-4bca-a9f4-13ae485c91bb.Text: "We will devitalise the apostates to extract the True Flesh. Prepare the tools, brothers and sisters."

e4b776e1-6e8a-48eb-89e8-33c0560fc009.Text: The carcass of the fallen Helbrute serves as a grim monument to the fearless Wolves who delivered the Allfather's retribution upon the detestable heretic.

1d77e0ff-8a4d-4faa-9297-1a5499f4b76d.Text: "No! We will save you, get you away from here — just hold on!"

77cfc5cc-3eda-41df-a0df-3cf1a311d930.Text: [Kill the woman] "May the Emperor guard your soul."

fb590f6b-a36c-4cc6-9077-32db3a5dbde2.Text: [Attack] "There is only one way to help you."

f7e0132b-6b60-4af9-b0b8-cb1f7c5a54d3.Text: Tried to help the mad psyker on Kiava Gamma.

3121a812-490b-410a-9f6d-a23b6f2c0fcb.Text: "Hey! Hey, can you hear me? I want to help!"

7605677b-01e0-4535-a306-60881db281f1.Text: Attacked the mad psyker on Kiava Gamma.

47998526-be76-4696-89fd-7212aaae61f3.Text: [Attack] "I shall rid you of your agonising existence."

d6dcbb45-12ba-49f6-8eab-a8c35ae740b1.Text: "Don't be afraid. Tell me, who are you?"

26430425-1542-4c10-aa50-fcc317c5ce7f.Text: "Pull yourself together, citizen! Shake off the compulsion and tell me who you are!"

961eddba-08a5-4dde-8cf7-0fab42a20a79.Text: [Try to shoot the psyker from a distance]

9fafc4c3-29ea-4050-897a-c07a8ed0f8c0.Text: {n}The dirty, dishevelled woman pays you no heed, lowering her head and looking at the ground with genuine interest, at something that either does not exist or is invisible to your eyes.{/n}

5086a963-6e0a-4feb-bc9c-e7de25c03f5d.Text: {n}The woman shoots you a crazed, inhuman look — and suddenly backs away with an agonising groan, clutching at her face.{/n}

d43acf16-5e4a-4c83-9ab9-54e375854883.Text: "She is a psyker — I can feel warp emanations roiling around her. One of the cultists' prisoners. How did she manage to get out of the cage and survive? Be vigilant — creatures like her remain dangerous even when they mean to do no harm."

6819f6a6-cdfa-4915-9819-8786b81848e8.Text: {n}Idira looks at Heinrix with scorn but says nothing, just hisses venomously through her teeth.{/n}

a60aaafa-ab01-4d95-98e5-d4a7b79c51d3.Text: {n}A single blow is enough to end the psyker's pitiful existence. You examine the corpse and, with a start, realise the woman's facial features seem to have melted from extreme heat. Whoever or whatever had the poor creature in its thrall has now vanished without a trace.{/n}

58a01c2f-74be-4d20-94d9-48e73dd683f7.Text: {n}Her voice is barely audible, but you manage to make out the words:{/n} "I don't remember how I ended up here... don't remember what happened... there was a bright light, like from arc-welding... and then... the light reached out with its clutches..." {n}She moans and holds her head.{/n}

5f7abc12-5e3b-44c0-9c24-ed1757eae38a.Text: {n}The woman jerks her head and transfixes you with a delirious gaze. Only now do you notice a reddish black mark on her cheek — a many-pointed star, a symbol of Chaos. The prisoner bares her teeth, but you cannot tell whether she does so as a threat or simply out of fear.{/n}

d7087a72-0155-496a-b6aa-a479688f5826.Text: {n}The woman hesitates, looking at you warily. At last she sobs and replies meekly,{/n} "Stay away... In the Emperor's name, stay away from me..."

3b21d5b0-8ee1-471c-a131-34990c0f9e06.Text: {n}The woman snarls, but a moment later, her growl becomes a desperate moan:{/n} "I can't... resist... Emperor, protect..."

7de9ad6a-b072-43b2-9cd8-f99548a4d9b1.Text: {n}With an unnatural roar, the psyker rears up — her features are drooping, melting like candle wax. Her swollen lips part, revealing sharp teeth, and her bright orange pupils expand to fill her eyes completely. The psyker slumps to the ground — and the smell of ozone gives way to a disgusting sulphurous stench.{/n}

04026104-0bda-40ea-b0ff-3a7c809f088e.Text: {n}A shot rings out, and the woman sags to the floor without a sound. The ozone smell immediately starts to dissipate, giving way to the usual scents of an industrial world.{/n}

ae534089-5fb9-404b-a66e-e2d0809fb034.Text: {n}Even at this distance you can detect the distinct smell of ozone — too fresh for this stuffy room reeking of soot and industrial lubricant. The woman raises a maimed hand and absent-mindedly runs its two remaining fingers through her matted hair.{/n}

fe5e2227-e537-4b77-9fcf-2e3563a5dfe8.Text: "The light... is taking me over. It's everywhere already! Everywhere..." {n}The woman turns her head toward you and blurts out in an unexpectedly low and gruff voice,{/n} "Save me! Give me the Emperor's Peace! Please!"

abfa35bf-3c30-43ce-8a1b-86f11a8d896b.Text: {n}Kibellah closes her eyes as if listening to something.{/n} "This tormented soul is beyond help. Grant her the gift of the Undying One while she still can accept it with gratitude."

8f32d823-9c57-48a9-8326-4f022b5818a3.Text: "What an unexpected bit of advice. I can't believe it's coming out of your mouth!"

99c6e355-f171-4d19-9f4e-aa1c51a13152.Text: "No! Too late! The light! The light is devoooOOOOAAARGH!" {n}The woman clutches at her face and recoils from you.{/n}

1d022cfc-c487-4b0d-9de8-43fc222d08c8.Text: [Find a way to deactivate the cogitator's logical network]

a7d864ec-587e-4710-a255-b296287a396d.Text: "Heinrix, have you ever seen anything like this before?"

5ebd5cad-42ef-4b97-b266-bceb0666e3aa.Text: "I need the assistance of a servant of the Omnissiah."

afccbd38-0e9f-4815-ac7f-7cd8b0ce0741.Text: [See what the device is coated with]

82be3d89-2d4d-4713-9177-cf02534e1d25.Text: [Take a close look at the letters on the screen]

31203f77-bb8b-4c65-b6c2-7c9b5c96368e.Text: {n}The cogitator screen flickers as if the system is suffering a power failure. You reach out and touch the control panel but quickly jerk your hand back: the device is coated in some sticky substance.{/n}

b2615e6e-a772-40bc-8bb1-e9d57ab7a4a0.Text: {n}You make a show of removing your hand from the lever — and kick the power transfer relay located on the lower half of the cogitator's casing. The screen immediately shuts down and the snarling inside the machine peters out on its own. Checking the data-crypt port reveals the claws have unclenched, and you easily extract the data-crypt from its socket.{/n}

441c4bb0-292d-4007-bc84-0fa2692db023.Text: {n}Not only do you fail to examine the log, even accessing it is quite an ordeal — any data projected to the blinking screen blurs and fades like images on melting film.{/n}

98ba456e-8fc1-47a4-a2a8-7f64808b4014.Text: {n}When you reach for the power shutdown lever, the growling from the depths of the machine intensifies and the screen starts filling with red. Your hand stops one centimetre away from its goal...{/n}

34b55d1a-7976-4d41-9bdf-6002119b2ee5.Text: {n}You skim the report on the auxiliary screen. It seems the cogitator has been completely purged of data. If there is anything of value left in this machine, it will be on the external drives.{/n}

0a477179-6c64-4d9c-95d3-c5fdbc50cf79.Text: {n}You try pressing keys and spinning a couple of reels. In response, a few lumens light up on the control panel, a low guttural growl reverberates through the machine, and a small auxiliary screen lights up, presenting you with information.{/n}

4039986c-f43f-4083-aac8-68dc6b52f709.Text: {n}The data-crypt slots are occupied: two of them appear to be melted beyond repair, but you might extract the third one without incurring data loss if you successfully deactivate the logical network of the machine itself.{/n}

e484b3ba-154c-4e2c-83a6-7b7ac156daf6.Text: {n}No matter how many reels you spin or how many buttons you push, all of the efforts remain futile: the control panel sways before your eyes, and the swirls on the screen start resembling letters on the cusp of forming coherent words...{/n}

960581f2-8c62-4f11-bb19-4f2716e2ae33.Text: {n}You touch the data-stick and realise you cannot pull it out or pry your fingers away from its surface, it is as if your hand is being held in place by a powerful magnetic force!{/n}

9d000a6e-e395-4641-b04e-aced51fe0e0c.Text: {n}You tear your gaze away from the screen and immediately feel your mind shake off the strange haze caused by the shifting images.{/n}

df8dad27-ad77-43ab-9136-327e43469992.Text: {n}You grab the lever and a powerful electric discharge surges through your body. You jerk your hand away and watch the lever go red-hot from the voltage, melt into a viscous goop, and trickle down into its own socket.{/n}

211b5e2e-6b93-4e46-a6b4-584755d57334.Text: {n}Heinrix gives the screen and the control panel a thorough examination.{/n} "Another manifestation of the same corruption we encountered on Kiava Gamma. Perhaps if we used an auxiliary connection system..."

fc52d8c2-e53b-4f89-913a-8763c4bf1020.Text: {n}Heinrix pries a side panel open with a knife and receives a face full of sparks and caustic reagent. After swearing and wiping his singed face, the Interrogator manages to pull out a bunch of wires and cut the right cables, causing the cogitator to shut down. The claws holding the data-crypt unclench helplessly.{/n}

d36b5afa-9279-4017-88cb-00ed02e06284.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest starts chanting an infrasound litany that makes you feel slightly nauseous and approaches the cogitator. He places his hands on the control panel in one smooth motion and starts performing sacred manipulations. Most of the Magos's actions are a total mystery to you, and you watch as he flips toggle switches and ritually taps several relays while drawing protective symbols over others.{/n}

38f2d4d4-7126-4277-af7b-6303b5cc67fc.Text: {n}At last, when the rituals are complete, your companion withdraws a cord from the folds of his red vestment and plugs it into one of the sockets. A discharge surges along the cable, making the Tech-Priest flinch and filling the air with the smell of burnt wiring, but the cogitator obediently shuts down, erasing the sinister entity from the screen and releasing the data-crypt from its port.{/n}

29f62ec2-e44e-4dfa-90f7-b3b9b47e5dc4.Text: {n}You know enough to determine exactly what happened to the machine. Glitchy projectors, otherworldly sounds from inside the case, an oppressive atmosphere in the room — everything points toward a scrap-code infection, one of the stranger and more frightening creations of the Tech-Priests who devote themselves to the Ruinous Powers.{/n}

c4361db2-7f57-45b3-bf88-e231f0cabdd1.Text: {n}Something is obviously wrong with the machine, but you fail to determine the exact reason for the malfunction.{/n}

07df115c-3b36-4ed7-b445-db05052bc65c.Text: {n}As if satisfied by your retreat, the entity on the screen closes its spark-like eyes, but you can't rid yourself of the feeling that it is still watching you surreptitiously.{/n}

175325e0-1e49-405a-b4aa-b9e21e85687e.Text: {n}You shatter the monitor with a single blow. In its death thralls, the machine envelops you in acrid smoke that leaves behind a thin oily film. The claws holding the data-crypt twitch in agony, breaking the fragile device into metal splinters.{/n}

53657414-a8bc-4583-8a51-fb4c4fef5730.Text: {n}You tense every muscle in your body, plant one leg against the cogitator case, and pull. At last, the unknown force begins to give way and eventually lets go. You come close to falling flat on your back, but the data-stick is clenched in your hand, intact.{/n}

4d95ffe9-a85e-4548-839c-b0a7de0cf5b1.Text: {n}You pull, twist, and tug at the data-stick with no visible result. At last you make peace with the inevitable and break the fragile device, ending the unnatural effect.{/n}

566df31a-1f62-4289-a4db-e7ba65646b25.Text: {n}You smash the control panel with the first blow and the cogitator screens with the second. No one will be able to use this machine, whether for good or ill.{/n}

661a0ca2-3710-442e-9393-1201308a5900.Text: {n}You examine all the slots and sockets on the cogitator case, but to no avail. All that you manage to find is a single data-stick hidden behind a protective panel.{/n}

bc212038-6730-4da6-831b-b3bbc52ad12a.Text: {n}The eye-like sparks are yellowish orange in colour, but you are pretty sure this monitor cannot display such a vivid hue. You lean forward, and you hear a predatory growl coming from inside the device, a sound full of hatred and hunger.{/n}
