bf0f5dee-60dc-47df-a4fa-cb4a1aa0965c.Text: {n}Perhaps if you can extract the data-crypts containing the scrap-code, you will be able to study it later in a controlled environment.{/n}

b192063b-384a-419d-ade1-13b6e293f0da.Text: {n}At the same moment, the cogitator releases a data-stick previously hidden beneath a protective panel, and the device drops to the floor right in front of you. It looks like a logic key used to access additional cogitator reserves. It may fit other systems in this part of the planet.{/n}

ecd8c515-ebd1-4a9a-bd10-423dde644d3f.Text: {n}The machine is obviously trying to tell you something, one letter after another. The gobbledygook on the screen aligns into a few words. You try to read them... and reel back, feeling the cursed phrase ravage your mind like a rabid beast, wiping away all thought and leaving behind a trace of primordial horror.{/n}

81a268a9-357b-49f8-86ca-a5d1f73bb150.Text: {n}You insert the data-stick into one of the available slots. The machine reacts with purrs and clicks. A few moments later, both data-sticks are ejected and land on the control panel.{/n}

75557e50-b93f-411b-ad7d-da76e21a909d.Text: {n}You spend a lot of time trying to establish a connection between the countless switches and reels on the control panel and the twisted symbols floating on the glitchy screen. At last you manage to complete the logical network, tame the rampaging system, and force it to disengage the data-crypt.{/n}

2cd1c23d-656f-457b-8bc7-9d07a99078e8.Text: {n}The Tech-Priests would probably not approve of such rough treatment of their sacred machines, but in the end your efforts bear fruit: you manage to claim the data-crypt by disconnecting several wires and prying open the claws.{/n}

7b2df585-cf1b-4f55-b7c5-f0ec57132b29.Text: {n}You stick your hand in the socket and thousands of invisible sharp teeth sink into your fingers! You pull out the maimed limb, which is quickly growing numb, and clearly hear an evil hiss coming from the bloodstained slot.{/n}

50b7de30-03d6-49ac-94d1-5daedc35ebfb.Text: {n}Something is moving on the cogitator's main screen, but it doesn't look like code. When you draw closer, the image starts to undulate this way and that, like the coils of an awakened snake. Two pinpricks of light appear on the screen — something is watching you from the darkness flickering between the unwinding coils.{/n}

caf13e36-c6dc-4bb7-a73d-d60cbddee423.Text: {n}The cogitator does not react to the buttons being pushed and the handles being turned: the screen continues to display what you saw when you first approached the machine.{/n}

db9fc686-3c03-4612-b04a-ea21e703786f.Text: {n}The cogitator appears to be in standby mode — the screen and sensors emit a dull glow, in no way reacting to your approach.{/n}

15bb79d8-3b17-48fb-a7a2-260119e3f583.Text: {n}The cogitator's case is covered with scratched symbols and signs thickly smeared in a pungent oily mass. You spot tiny bubbles emerging from the gleaming metal: it is almost as if the malodorous slime is seeping from these scratches like sweat oozes from pores on human skin.{/n}

6ba2644e-f812-4bcd-94eb-8c9f11ada3e0.Text: {n}The data-crypt is in place, but its slot is protected by two rows of metal claws growing straight out of the cogitator's casing. They flex under your scrutiny, clutching the device even tighter.{/n}

e35f9d5a-0013-471a-8e14-19d93388f0cf.Text: A storage device containing the remains of the scrap-code from Kiava Gamma.

ecee1436-329e-406d-8ea3-13ad66548b46.Text: A small device that grants access to a cogitator's additional reserves.

0e00d702-92cb-44f5-b57f-742fdbe63b0e.Text: A tome containing revelations of the Omnissiah, recorded in special binharic dialect. Only a member of the Cult Mechanicus with a key to this cipher may partake of the wisdom of the Machine God.

6ec5ebf1-8688-4ecd-9f67-58d369de5aa2.Text: A tome containing warnings of the Omnissiah. This set of unshakeable tenets of the Adeptus Mechanicus is hidden from the eyes of the laymen with a special binharic cipher. Only an anointed Tech-Priest can divine the sacred knowledge from this folio.

b19315ad-f3a4-4a40-b9ca-67bddcb5046d.Text: Commanded Uralon the Cruel to leave your mind.

4d63ed76-1b8a-4c9f-af3c-a78615b3d5e1.Text: "You waste your time trying to tempt me. It is not blood that defines a person's deeds — only their will does. And my will is thus: begone from my mind!"

81d1c0de-d49b-4516-a857-0d86e5a2292a.Text: [Try to get a better look at the figure]

aea647a6-50b1-435e-bb62-53748756f26b.Text: "In the name of the Emperor, begone!"

c3fe106b-4dfd-49ae-bfbe-2079f9e6e644.Text: "I am Rogue Trader {name}, sovereign of Kiava Gamma. The Warrant belongs to me alone."

b074f147-523b-4d82-b83d-584e4403292e.Text: "Where are we? Where have you taken me?"

d37db7c9-6800-4e7f-af25-901d27a0d266.Text: "He... said something about Theodora. About how the blood in my veins will lead me to serve Chaos."

9485e287-43de-43e6-a51b-d6abc8f11a87.Text: "It doesn't matter. The sooner I forget about it, the better."

e431c27d-8421-4995-bbef-99eb9b7be5e6.Text: "You are one of the Word Bearers — the cursed Legion that betrayed the Imperium."

52b93534-fc0c-4e50-9d09-99390dba0bcc.Text: "The only way you are going to acquire my Warrant is by digging it out of the wreckage of my ship."

5349db86-03e5-4be6-8a1b-fe39903a236c.Text: Offered to give Uralon the Cruel the Warrant in exchange for the blessing of the Ruinous Powers.

85bf4c13-9ac4-43c2-9582-cd8bd6ba6417.Text: "I am willing to give the Warrant to you in exchange for the blessing of your masters."

b052b043-5c3b-4e04-8b90-93d204b0a2de.Text: "I am the sovereign of Kiava Gamma. This is my world, not a dominion of Chaos!"

5c8511bb-35c5-4cfa-bcee-c234a7510948.Text: "Hold on. That servant of Chaos claimed that the soul of the psyker who was protecting me had already been marked by his 'lord.'"

f45cf833-dc73-413d-8b28-6e15e17b2b5b.Text: {n}Sharp pain pierces your head, and the light dims in your eyes. You smell smoke and burning, you feel a wave of nausea, your legs buckle, and your knees hit the metal floor. In that same moment, the {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g} surrounding you disappears in a whirlwind of mist, ash, and grey shadows.{/n}

dcb0d7dc-5609-4688-92d7-b9c198c4beee.Text: {n}His expression twists in pain as he stares at you in rage and bafflement.{/n} "Pitiful insect. You dare—"

5b4684d9-c11b-4085-936c-3c7f9aaf302c.Text: "They call you a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}hero{/d}. An empty word, a worthless pedestal among hundreds like it, all built by the lackeys of the false god in their hubris and ignorance. This pedestal will soon become a sacrificial altar, and you will become yet another reminder to the Expanse that no 'hero' can save it from the Truth."

5f74aa64-b261-4886-8d69-b24411bc5b8e.Text: "Especially since..." {n}He bares his teeth and chuckles.{/n} "Especially since the soul of your leashed sorcerer has already been marked by my lord."

0b899291-3957-4d88-9e38-f3cfec3a3a5a.Text: {n}The warrior's inhuman eyes bore into you.{/n} "I am the master of those who have been felled by your hand in the halls of the Primordial Truth. I am Uralon the Cruel. The souls of my followers returned to the fount of power they served, crying out for me to cast my gaze toward this sacrilege. And what do I see? Yet another lackey of the corpse emperor."

d038c3d1-b61d-41f4-9451-e44bb2733e5c.Text: {n}You squint and wipe away the tears — and for the moment, your vision clears. Before you stands a mighty giant clad in dark power armour lavishly adorned with bas-reliefs of snarling daemonic silhouettes and punctured with prayer scrolls. Two braziers are mounted behind his shoulders, burning with unnatural blue flames and emitting thick black smoke that curls and twists upward like a funnel. Behind the giant, you catch a brief glimpse of a crumpled figure bound in chains.{/n}

d8f9f37a-86d5-49dc-9809-e2df619bf53e.Text: {n}Through the howling of the storm, you hear a new, chilling sound — roaring, cruel laughter. The figure advances toward you, and you feel that if it takes just one more step, it will step on you and crush you like a bug.{/n}

f3c2fab8-5b3a-48dc-a27f-62f6cbe54e1e.Text: {n}Writhing in pain, you raise your head and peer into the roiling darkness. You make out the figure's features — it is a huge man clad in dark power armour, from which daemonic silhouettes snarl at you. The wind picks up, and you close your eyes, unable to stare into the face of this raging tempest.{/n}

ef710cec-5c25-43a2-8fc9-eabb5fef9c7e.Text: {n}The giant's voice causes the storm raging around you to die down somewhat, as if the very sound of his voice is enough to make the whirlwind subside. You glance at the huge warrior, and notice on his chest a winding azure symbol — the shades of blue seem to glimmer and mingle together.{/n}

6c31200e-ff05-4a97-b9a0-958932b2278a.Text: "I want to look upon the one who has disrupted my flock's duties and my master's plans. That warrior from my Legion... the Fabricator-Censor... You think of their deaths as a triumph; however, it is but a minor hindrance on our path. There are other worlds that serve our goals. There are other sources of plasteel and adamantine. Revel in your victory — it will change nothing."

3940302e-a501-4423-9cfa-b56bb44f329f.Text: "All things in this world are subservient to change, Rogue Trader. Your predecessor thought herself immortal — and where is she now? What makes you think you won't be joining her shortly?"

59d0ab89-bf28-49b8-949e-43b332b9ba60.Text: "Nevertheless, the blood in your veins whispers to the spirits that you warrant a closer look. Hmm... Yes... You are a descendant of the Rogue Trader whose {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} Kunrad Voigtvir sought to obtain. By defiling the relic and binding it to himself with the tethers of the Empyrean, he was meant to become my servant, a Rogue Trader who would do the work of the Truth... but then you interfered. Could it be that you wish to gain the true gods' favour instead? Do you wish to present the corpse's relic to me and serve the Truth? Hear your very blood calling, begging you to submit to me — what would be the point of futile defiance?"

e783f2a6-d13a-40fb-a935-faef3d2abb1f.Text: {n}Conquering the weakness and pain, straining every muscle in your body, you slowly rise to your feet, straighten, and stare Uralon straight in the eye. He smiles, but there is no mirth in his eyes — only malicious curiosity, the kind with which one looks at an insect with its wings torn off.{/n}

817de1e4-ccd0-44e3-86ab-da21e31aeb6a.Text: {n}You strain every muscle in your body but cannot move an inch — the dark will presses down upon your shoulders, forbidding you even from straightening your back.{/n}

ef720981-8d3a-4d3e-9650-f29214ee633b.Text: "This is the bridge that connects our minds, created by the will of my slave — whose fate you should be envying. The {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} is useful enough to me to be left alive. You... less so."

5bc4c7e7-9197-46cc-abb7-fd4cecfb41af.Text: {n}A gust of wind sweeps Uralon's figure away without a trace. The mist around you begins to dissipate, revealing the dark halls of the manufactorum and leaving behind an oppressive sense of powerlessness.{/n}

f31b8669-313f-4e66-b6fe-cc54fbfb747f.Text: {n}The manufactorum around you looks the same as before the vision — maybe the shadows have grown a little deeper and darker. You dust yourself off and continue on your journey through the darkness.{/n}

90929fe0-0f9c-479b-a692-2225a396bff2.Text: {n}Heinrix is standing beside you, white as a sheet, eyes wide, grimacing. The air around him seems to roil — though the phenomenon passes almost immediately. As he begins to speak, his voice sounds hoarse and cracked:{/n} "That... was not easy."

2e537e40-50e2-4222-b7b6-cdb22fcc7935.Text: "One of the traitors to the Imperium? I don't think it was he who touched your mind — I wouldn't have had the strength to go up against a psyker from the ranks of those monsters. He might have forced some mortal to do his bidding. Perhaps it was through the same hapless medium that he sensed the deaths of his henchmen." {n}Heinrix looks away and frowns.{/n} "Such indescribable power... to have reached out to your mind at such a distance..."

9d3b4c45-cdbb-4110-a062-c75eebff5fb9.Text: {n}Heinrix stares at you — whether in surprise or anger, you do not know. Then he gives a curt nod.{/n} "I see. We can theorise later — although I will say, {name}, that his words do not leave much room for interpretation."

0d2fbffe-b3a2-410a-816e-77d1c26c0f2d.Text: {n}Heinrix eyes you suspiciously, then reluctantly nods.{/n}

d63a5cdf-b595-4d60-bea7-42a37c1c265f.Text: {n}The Chaos Space Marine's laughter is akin to the roll of distant thunder.{/n} "Words of a wretch who wanders through the darkness of ignorance. We were the first among our brothers to discern the great lie and forge the path to divinity. Our Primarch went on a pilgrimage to find the Truth — a path that is still open to the sighted. Your accusations are the words of a blind servant in thrall to an ancient lie."

6cb45ee4-84f9-4d91-8c5a-f56b73e304d5.Text: {n}He chuckles and inclines his head.{/n} "When the time comes, I will remind you of this promise. The sinews of fate have yet to be bound... I will not stop my servants from hunting for that which I require. If you survive, you will have earned the right to serve the Truth."

ff971175-ebd8-41b5-a7be-d7011ad832df.Text: "That outcome is acceptable. Once the servants of the Primordial Truth are done with you, they will see to it that the treasures of the Imperial ship are extracted and brought into the service of the true gods."

1a881492-8cd3-4742-8786-fe2ce116c955.Text: "'Never'... do you know how many mortals uttered this word to me? And how many of them, just minutes later, were willing to give up all that was precious to them to make the torment stop?"

bacefdc9-0531-462e-a0bb-a79e18e1f21a.Text: {n}The blood starts pumping frenetically in your temples as a tell-tale sign of danger. You close your eyes and focus all your efforts on resisting the sorcerous attack. After a few moments, your heart slows down, and your blood vessels are no longer trying to burst from the pressure. The fear that washed over you, spurred on by another's ill will, ebbs away powerlessly.{/n}

67f2507f-22d5-40b1-8e70-410f70c193cb.Text: {n}You feel blood rushing to your face, drumming in your temples, coating your tongue and lips in a viscous membrane. You no longer feel your arms and legs — as if your entire life force is trying to leave your body, pouring out of your mouth along with globs of crimson. The giant Chaos Space Marine is asking you questions, which you are answering obediently and hurriedly, not even comprehending what you are talking about.{/n}

9b56f822-bc5d-46d8-aacc-3f9d0c0470eb.Text: "Oh, clinging to illusions will do you no good. The rituals have already been performed. The mortals are already singing the litanies of the Primordial Truth or decorating the sacrificial altars with their flesh. Kiava Gamma, as you call it, is already saturated in the nectar of the Truth — a fate that awaits all worlds that would stand in our way."

ff317d47-9a65-431c-9e09-7785e5b0226c.Text: "This isn't your first time meddling in the deeds of the Word Bearers. You were there on Rykad Minoris, and so I want to know if you hold in your hands that which is not yours to hold. And you will tell me yourself." {n}He utters a few words in an unknown tongue over his shoulder — and you feel your head being clamped by an unseen vice.{/n}

8b6bcf18-b2dd-4159-9cf7-f511592a5ffc.Text: {n}You feel your blood start pumping alarmingly in your temples at an increasing pace as the wind is knocked out of you... but then the drumming in your ears quiets, and your heart, which was about to leap out of your chest, slows its rhythm.{/n}

1cf6c71b-797d-47aa-90c1-b7a651dbcb2a.Text: {n}Uralon chuckles.{/n} "Hmm... It appears I am not the only one who appreciates the value of a pet psyker. I will make good use of your watchdog when my servants get to you."

cbedd6a5-d260-4a27-8dc1-4f867d2d5de1.Text: "I sensed the presence of another psyker — someone made contact with you mentally, then tried to harm you with sorcery. I did what I could... you at least appear unharmed. Can you remember what you saw?"

063a2f3c-d461-486d-8ebd-357bc3305788.Text: {n}Another's will bears down on you, but as soon as you awaken {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}your own powers{/d}, your soul fills with defiant resolve.{/n}

7d9fb512-7834-43ad-a1e8-dbf8eaafb5ba.Text: {n}Through the thunder and wind, you hear the giant's disdainful laughter:{/n} "You carry merely one part of the whole... Keep it, then, until the hour of our meeting. I will pluck this boon from your dead hands and use it for the glory of the Truth."

e9a3e087-590b-4ffb-9dfd-e8fa209d147a.Text: {n}The giant's voice rises over the howling winds — and it is heavy with fury and tinged with disbelief:{/n} "You... You, a mere insect, have obtained both shards! Do you truly think yourself a new aspirant vying for the favour of the Edge? So be it... Fate shall execute the will of the Weaver. Follow the pattern, then, Rogue Trader... March on."

a9c221f9-a3df-4e6f-a851-b8016740a90b.Text: {n}The sensation is familiar, for this is not the first time the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}shadow of warp sorcery{/d} has fallen heavily upon you. You close your eyes and cast aside all thought — and your inner horrors cry out and rise against the will of another.{/n}

c0e74a38-80e2-4f27-876d-279394748a1d.Text: {n}Struggling against the elements, you can barely raise your head to look. Your eyes sting and burn, but through the tears, you see it — a colossal silhouette rising above you. The roaring tempest is unable to shake the mighty figure.{/n}

852b57db-00fd-4b70-9abc-50e47806bf81.Text: {n}Abelard looks you over worriedly, then sighs in cantankerous relief.{/n} "That was a close call! For the sake of Holy Terra, if I had lost a second Rogue Trader in such a paltry span of time — my only option would have been to shoot myself out of unending shame..."

d29c7eb6-2004-4827-ad67-83a21014615c.Text: "Quit dawdling, Heinrix!" {n}Abelard peers over Heinrix's shoulder, looking agitated.{/n} "I can't lose a second Rogue Trader in such a ridiculous span of time! Oh, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you've come to! Thank the Throne!"

a5d1633c-cd9f-4883-988f-dfc509ef69ac.Text: {n}Sister Argenta, who has been watching all of this intently, grows pale and makes the sign of the Aquila to ward off evil.{/n}

ccb2c95a-3be6-4e4a-b347-60a692f584b1.Text: "Worthless rat... Still, I will rip the answers out of you personally. When the time comes."

c7552760-8789-48be-a1fb-51e64cf12705.Text: {n}After swallowing down your blood and barely catching your breath, you regain the ability to hear. The giant's voice roars over the howling of the whirlwind,{/n} "Enough. Even if you have touched my master's relic, it is not with you now. Very well, servants of the Truth will seek it out and bring it back into the fold. As for you... other servants of the Truth will deal with you."

0709bb1c-89f2-4dff-80be-ac3f17a42fd3.Text: {n}Your soul, {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}tempered by the curse of sorcery{/d}, stands strong against the psychic onslaught, and you direct your gaze forward.{/n}

f1d0ef6f-04b0-43b0-a6a4-5b729388b4dc.Text: {n}A shadow passes over Heinrix's face — astonishment, anger, and, finally, alarm.{/n} "Most likely, our enemy wanted to sow doubt among your allies. If I were a follower of the Archenemy, would I have fought for your soul? Don't trust a word the enemies of the Imperium say, {name}, lest you put your own soul at risk."

ba575a0a-2160-498c-81ca-7dece6b5a0ef.Text: You hear dull thuds from within the thick metal, as if some process, endlessly pounding, is running in the depths of these pipes.

fd7bfcf1-0520-4271-932c-a6840ced221f.Text: The broken panel of the cogitator is sparking, its blind, dark screens showing nothing.

a1303d09-f1f3-4a60-bf31-bf45e2e73a27.Text: "Truth, accept the gifts of the faithful!"

e1335a68-ad61-425f-b106-b526ebe36a31.Text: "Gut the outsiders! Let their blood mix with oil!"

cc362fec-2786-437c-b1b1-778c31911b6d.Text: A massive cogwheel constantly drives the colossal gear system, which is lost in the haze.

9af89cc7-c74c-41e2-8071-ed9cd54424af.Text: "Truth, conceal the path from the impious!"

e36a59cd-3834-4fab-9538-1022d36fc9ba.Text: The massive soot-covered vessels are filled with blood, which produces a horrible stench.

e87d98db-4cf9-48c2-a9d5-f951d79a64a4.Text: The vats, which were previously used to store fuel oil, have been turned into reservoirs for blood — an ingredient for the vile rituals that have replaced the orderly protocols of the manufactorum.

18449c19-452a-426e-ad00-bf5ab042f695.Text: An eerie-looking makeshift structure adorned with revolting totems and symbols. The dim lighting makes it look like the ornate symbols are moving.

7824f160-a82c-4e1c-ba19-d3855daddd7b.Text: This eerie-looking makeshift structure is an altar to Tzeentch. Amidst the revolting totems and twisted symbols dedicated to the Chaos God, you notice a string of nines burned into the metal surface.

72bcdae5-9f68-448d-9974-9456269f1159.Text: The curved parts appear foreign compared to the orderly geometry of the manufactorum. The many holes and fasteners indicate that each component serves as but a single part of some wicked design.

f68158ec-9aa0-4249-be83-e51b69840539.Text: A mishmash of steel, wire, and augmentations, shaped by some madmen into an unknown and frightening monstrosity.

9c651127-8bc8-4946-8723-701a3f39c50e.Text: Looking at the uneven symbols makes your eyes water.

50141222-fe3c-43c2-8009-b2ca6325e4a3.Text: The Marks of Chaos seem to draw your eye and strike terror in you at the same time.

721f5102-119d-469f-a9af-0acf7226f532.Text: A desecrated altar to the Omnissiah. The purity seals have been torn off, the data-slates with sacred code shattered, and some of the teeth on the gear adornments broken off.

77ae885f-bbe2-4851-bb88-7052dbcf0b71.Text: The screen of this cogitator shows a scrolling line of repeating Techna-Lingua. Staring at the obscure symbols gives you a headache.

04bd2b40-0d8a-4230-b520-6d8a44c11528.Text: The crucified body had all of its augmetics removed — judging by the abundance of blood, they were ripped out when the Tech-Priest was still alive.

a1ef15f0-40c7-4ce0-8639-9212701e324f.Text: A strange tool whose blade is covered in notches from frequent contact with metal.

7eec579a-b5f2-436d-b60a-29765e428558.Text: The door's pneumatic actuators have obviously failed — it can now only be opened manually by finding a suitable valve.

b98d822d-3a73-4b3a-ab69-38f447b19646.Text: This huge machine looks forsaken by the spirits — no humming or rattling is coming from within the casing.

d279f77e-484b-4d1d-ae99-2a808d37e00e.Text: This large device is a cargo lift used for transporting parts.

f97ab47d-6fae-484a-bd60-3463331def24.Text: The Lexmechanic stares into space, his mangled hands still mindlessly pounding on the inscriber.

2a18d5d8-0332-43e7-b1e3-23baa6c3a4ef.Text: This bizarre modified device is impossible to identify. Judging by the putrid smell and the pale chunks of flesh stuck to the blades, the machine is used for body dismemberment.

8904444a-90a0-4333-a0e9-414042efe359.Text: The device, now evidently used to chop bodies into pieces, was once an ordinary cooling fan.

189fb565-d356-4b21-b5b8-19f063f42ef5.Text: "Crew 24, second lane of the manufactorum. Commencing standard procedure."

3215afe8-e196-4a9a-bff8-0b06eb93d8bc.Text: The crust of caked blood indicates the direction in which the victim was dragged.

feee9f3a-50a2-4823-924c-31a428bafe5a.Text: Inside the car, you see a dark mess — metal rubbish caked in a wet, fetid mass.

8a53ffcb-ede9-478e-bd12-9e9fd1670dcd.Text: The car is filled with refuse — broken pieces of spare parts, chopped-up lumps of flesh, bits of wire, and other rubbish.

80ad5469-3614-4fc0-b9f4-6e1a4c653257.Text: "Your redemption will be awash with the blood of heathens, and thus will you sate the true gods' eternal thirst."

e348202f-1e82-4848-9786-fbb0ec7834f9.Text: "Find within the Primordial Truth the strength and power to deliver retribution unto those who kept you blind. Sated with its divinity, manifest the will of the true gods and strike down the unbelievers."

1ffbb1ae-ac57-4e99-8a7f-49a1a4af6263.Text: "Peer into the darkness that conceals the true path — avert not your eyes, for the one who looks will witness the essence of things and the power of the Truth."

adf19b0a-49df-419d-abee-4264f59d6f83.Text: "Pasqal, don't you want to see what this creature is made of and learn about any weaknesses that we could use in the fight against heresy?"

68a99100-4485-4d9e-911a-b23b2881f1a5.Text: "Argenta, this is our chance to turn a creation of Chaos against the Archenemy!"

37aac40c-d7e9-4b5b-98a0-4fb0b37f5f6f.Text: Destroyed the subdued Daemon Engine on Kiava Gamma.

3d27f189-206f-4d63-a37c-e4b3cb4eb341.Text: [Destroy the Daemon Engine] "Death to enemies of Humanity!"

c7c4a863-d332-4fae-9522-0670e925cd1f.Text: Took the subdued Daemon Engine from Kiava Gamma aboard the voidship.

c2052c94-0080-482e-a4a6-244687ab69bf.Text: "I am taking it to my ship. I will make it serve me."

344eb8e3-2bfa-4423-85c3-b92f627f8dde.Text: "Heinrix, you were just investigating a corrupted cogitator — and now you would fault me?"

6f902040-d7c0-433a-80a8-70cc6afaf37b.Text: "I intend to use this weapon against Chaos itself."

4313dc4b-06af-4fe1-a05d-14ba6b3a74ad.Text: [Lie] "Just look at this thing. It must be defective if it fights its own!"

95e0a338-5acb-4363-b989-674513af44f3.Text: "Yrliet, you have my word that I will keep this thing under control."

d5a89c03-a093-45f0-b492-0ff644c69f58.Text: "I gave no order to dispose of it!"

a90dbff8-dc86-444e-a585-1220e9c4c132.Text: "Blast it... I was looking forward to enjoying my new toy."

b9fc2ef7-6a34-4687-b709-0458336730b0.Text: "Disobeying the Rogue Trader's will is a crime against the Imperium! I am removing you from my retinue! Away with you!"

61505352-60f0-4b3d-8f7a-ecc31c97e291.Text: "Abelard? Rest assured, my new pet will give us little trouble. I am confident that you will manage perfectly well."

dfe5870c-78b8-4df4-af61-e1eb856b9327.Text: "My decision is final. We are taking the machine on board."

8f62b532-d90a-4cad-b8fc-37f41d92548f.Text: "We are done here. It is time we pressed on."

dc2ada0b-ce0c-4cb1-b4f6-7faba97f0245.Text: {n}The steel behemoth standing before you twitches every so often. Its frame emanates tainted miasmas, as if its metal plates can barely hold the endless anathema contained within this fabricated cage.{/n}

729c4d95-9bd4-42ae-841e-dc46d6d150e9.Text: {n}Idira shakes her head, tilts it to one side as if listening to something, then shoots you a wary glance. As she meets your gaze, her expression hardens and she gives you a slight nod.{/n}

413e8b80-41a9-49ab-b0cb-565fd1842910.Text: "Your words are tainted by the Archenemy's lies, Rogue Trader! Such promises of power are what pave the road to heresy and ruin. You will not lead me astray!"

90279b6d-4296-4161-b099-f82e5a19ab13.Text: {n}Sister Argenta readies her weapon.{/n} "Let fall the Archenemy's weapon that has turned on itself in a fit of madness!"

4bd727e6-8fda-445a-8300-8475b8a1db07.Text: {n}The beast turns its monstrous head from side to side as if trying to catch someone's scent.{/n}

9185f101-719c-4012-986a-59ac354b433e.Text: "What?" {n}The Interrogator stares at you in fury.{/n} "What lunacy has gotten into your head?"

04df2382-9cd3-4e53-8f09-000ac8d58230.Text: "What a hypocritical ashmag you are, cog." {n}Jae meets Pasqal's glare and smirks.{/n} "Go ahead, look me in the eye and tell me again that I'm the one who wants to get my hands on things no one should ever touch."

1cbccae1-336e-4680-a90c-26bfd8507565.Text: {n}Yrliet lowers her head and steps back, her expression darkening.{/n} "Isha, bless the elantach with but a shred of reason, for {mf|his|her} own has abandoned {mf|him|her}..."

a558a0ac-2289-42c6-b5c5-8563677a458e.Text: {n}The Interrogator looks at the Daemon Engine for a few moments.{/n} "You have stepped dangerously close to the line that separates radical thinking from indisputable heresy. Be more prudent in your experiments, {name}."

35c5e85d-a498-4b3a-9039-f5b0edee790e.Text: "Even Rogue Traders should not dabble in what we are dealing with now!" {n}His voice turns into a growl.{/n} "You are putting every soul aboard your ship in grave peril!"

a1b0d240-341f-4bee-ada3-83f9392753ea.Text: {n}Idira bites her lip to conceal a smile. She casts a mocking glance at the unsuspecting Interrogator.{/n}

e997afd6-768a-4b52-9d61-36706156773b.Text: {n}The monstrosity does not fight back when buffeted by a hail of attacks. The steel tears and comes apart, the heat radiating from the construct's bowels instantly becomes unbearable — and then dissipates completely. At last, the empty shell crumbles to the floor with a thundering crash.{/n}

f6349c4e-e405-40be-81e7-9f967b9de5fc.Text: {n}The abomination, seething with heat and malice, digs at the metal floor with its foot and lets out a stifled howl, as if in anticipation of new massacres and victims to come.{/n}

8b2e82ce-368e-4c88-8ae8-18d9c698b1fc.Text: {n}Yrliet shoots you a gloomy look.{/n} "You, who cannot control {mf|his|her} own mad ambitions, frighten me far more than this monster."

0d2c2a9e-6c8a-4239-9847-45cd770e0d93.Text: {n}The monster's hulking frame, a moment ago brimming with ruinous energy, now lies at your feet.{/n}

019a2eaf-ffd0-40f5-a5e7-9a585d04d38a.Text: "Which is why I had to act of my own accord to shield you from unspeakable heresy, Rogue Trader! If I hadn't..." {n}Argenta pointedly adjusts her grip on her weapon, her burning gaze trained on you.{/n}

f982e872-e6d4-4edc-becc-21ebbe7bcfe1.Text: {n}Heinrix's voice drops to a hiss:{/n} "A Rogue Trader's privileges have their limits, {name}. I have the right to punish heresy, and you should be thankful that I disposed of the Engine and only the Engine!"

3580f9b9-c1bb-4db1-a012-bf12cf42bb88.Text: {n}Abelard silently makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n}

73ec453c-2eb6-48c3-a287-d7e3f175dc4b.Text: "Exalted One protect us and Humanity's guardians..."

17954a7e-cde1-4f18-811e-38883ca9bc64.Text: "Your 'toy'? It was built by heretics to become a vessel for an abomination of the warp, an instrument of destruction and corruption! {name}..." {n}Heinrix is briefly choked with fury.{/n}

8ab3fd4b-c30e-4b1d-9265-54d032ba9276.Text: "Should the hour ever come when you indeed employ an abominable weapon of the Archenemy, it will be the hour when my weapon turns against you — and then, trust my word on it, nothing will save you from righteous judgement!"

ad3757b8-1a2c-499f-b648-01ba855073e7.Text: {n}Yrliet throws out her arm as if in an attempt to halt your words.{/n} "Enough! Your obliviousness to the true atrocious nature of this creation is staggering, elantach. Stop, for I wish not to hear another word of this madness!"

22cfecc5-1b1b-4ace-a123-77846f4e75c2.Text: {n}Argenta raises her chin.{/n} "So those are the words you've chosen? Very well. Knowing how mild your convictions are when it comes to dealing with heresy... when next we meet, do not count on me to be merciful and let you leave unscathed. May the God-Emperor's grace guide you onto the one true path!"

a445290a-8782-4eee-bb9d-13ad8ce537b1.Text: {n}Heinrix scoffs coldly.{/n} "It is not for the Rogue Trader to gainsay the will of the Lord Inquisitor. I am in this retinue at his behest, not yours."

b2bf598b-f78c-4963-b210-5b98c46e27f0.Text: {n}As soon as you say the words, Argenta and Heinrix leap up as if on command...{/n}

c3e829c9-46e4-4299-8c03-585de3a74a8e.Text: {n}Kibellah glowers at the metal creature.{/n} "If the unclean beast dares to defy your command, Domin, I will cast it into oblivion. And I will swiftly sever the thread of any of your subjects who may become sullied by its corruption."

a8f06a72-3ee5-4546-b947-bf30d709a3b4.Text: {n}Solomorne gives you a hard look.{/n} "Just because the Warrant allows you many things does not obligate you to exercise every right you have. Not all tools are fit for the service of the God-Emperor. Think on it."

ccf233f5-27d4-4a01-a7d3-1cbfe460b9e7.Text: {n}Heinrix raises a hand, and an unseen shroud of cold instantly falls upon him.{/n}

e46be62a-5b1a-46ae-8a25-565f23ea3e7e.Text: {n}Without saying a word, Argenta aims her weapon.{/n}

f3daf511-6f86-4c12-84a4-ded056384c97.Text: {n}The Seneschal lets out a strange, pained sound.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain. After all, my options are rather limited."

1a56f447-5112-47de-a119-9e6a65c23dee.Text: {n}Heinrix raises a hand, and the temperature around him begins to plummet.{/n}

c5a05c8c-3dfb-4a94-867d-fc1a3e7726b3.Text: {n}Pasqal, even paler than normal, is staring at the creature with a mixture of rage and disgust, his visor flashing blue and green. A few sparks fly out of the burnt circuitry beneath the monster's armour, as if Pasqal's anger is setting its insides on fire.{/n}

ad0be321-afff-43f4-9f4c-24941b0aa34d.Text: {n}Pasqal's voice clangs like military-grade plasteel:{/n} "Unacceptable sacrilege! The abomination must be eradicated!"

6327be82-441a-44b1-a2d6-9ff958dbacd9.Text: {n}Pasqal freezes while his mechadendrites flail back and forth. After a long pause, he utters quietly,{/n} "The anathema must be equipped with a mechanism for cessation of vital functions, which is to be put under my supervision. Then its existence can be prolonged for the duration justifiable by the sacred mission of Comprehension."

efc1a021-5a69-42fc-8320-61ec11691b11.Text: "If the anathema demonstrates the slightest disobedience, this unit will open its armour plating, pulverise its hydraulic pistons, and start cutting its contact wires one after another to see which cogitation groups shut down first." {n}As Pasqal whispers his threats, the monstrosity's plated form shrinks and lets out a vicious but somewhat wary growl.{/n}

5b3a3ccb-f9cf-44f6-a854-ceb779f8a1af.Text: {n}The Sister of Battle raises her weapon.{/n} "Halt in His name! Do you even comprehend what heresy you intend to wreak?"

934e0287-9ade-428d-8b8c-7fdc041b5788.Text: {n}Abelard turns white as a sheet.{/n} "Begging your pardon, Lord Captain... Where would we even... We would have to keep it locked up... It will demolish half the deck!"

c1682b30-e9f3-4db3-a779-6d9ba20038e2.Text: "Shereen, your triumph over the Archenemy's knaves must have obscured your mind, for what other explanation can I find for what I'm hearing? To bring a weapon of Humanity's bane on board the ship of the Exalted One's chosen? I mean..."

4517abc3-defc-4b25-8100-86a493a88898.Text: {n}You force the machine to work around its own prohibitions and restrictions. The strange intrusion and the logic failures might later drive the cogitator's machine spirit mad, but right now, the terminal obeys you completely.{/n}

8a53d63e-e7c4-4066-b008-513f7e781b38.Text: {n}You are almost certain that your hacking has damaged the cogitator's inner structure. The conflicts might lead to the collapse of the entire system, which means that you should hurry.{/n}

50878ca7-81e9-4ddf-8697-f82dd7806cdc.Text: {n}The cogitator is silent, awaiting new commands.{/n}

64dfff7d-bdda-4cf7-b43f-2c1e312b3e39.Text: {n}Your knowledge of {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} is sufficient to trick the system and subdue it to your will. A false query, a crafty manipulation of the controls — and you get what you want.{/n}

7e31b646-92ad-490c-8dc9-ce4b3f7aa8e7.Text: {n}Your understanding of sacred technologies is not enough to get past the cogitator's loyal guardian — its {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}. No matter how hard you try to coerce it, the system remains impervious.{/n}

51d55713-33ae-45a6-9323-5e783be25808.Text: {n}You touch the levers and the reels on the control panel and disturb the slumber of the spirits that reside within this cogitator. The machine dawdles as if still drowsy, but nevertheless performs its assigned function.{/n}

c92170c4-f38e-4b8c-b3fd-8a80581bc876.Text: {n}You discover the local data-crypt with contents collected by either previous operators or the machine spirit itself. Using your access, you study the archives stored on this cogitator.{/n}

d4f83bd6-94e9-4c68-ad8b-ddbc3f663284.Text: {n}You gain access to the cogitator's systems. The device's machine spirit can do nothing to thwart you — subdued by its defeat, it hides in the depths of its lair.{/n}

eaf9c317-0b3b-4edf-9d88-f0d172cfe1d3.Text: {n}Before you is an ancient, but wholly typical console, intended for use by people not trained in the mysteries of ministering to {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g}. The {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} is completely silent, but as you approach, you sense the warmth emanating from its metallic casing — a tell-tale sign that the machine is working.{/n}

540f5aa2-242e-4182-82a6-044c0044b04a.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}'s panel has dozens of breakers, buttons, handles, switches, and other control mechanisms.{/n}

d9036392-729c-4ac5-9f43-dd55271eec6d.Text: {n}As you approach the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}, you notice a number of deep scratches left by huge claws on its metal surfaces. Despite the apparent damage, the machine seems to be in working condition.{/n}

26931ec1-4800-43c7-9dd5-2344bc3a13bc.Text: {n}Something is howling within the metal housing, as if the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} of this {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} are lamenting some irreparable loss.{/n}

03099240-9467-436e-bc27-a0e027954ce5.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} looks dead — only a single lit lumen shows that there is life within the machine.{/n}

efd633dd-01aa-4366-bf43-5c1feae662f2.Text: {n}The cogitator is completely silent, but as you approach, you sense the warmth emanating from its metallic frame — a tell-tale sign that the machine is working.{/n}

23872570-0ce8-46e5-a361-7cea207cccec.Text: {n}The vast data repositories contain millions of strings related to receiving raw materials for processing, shipping processed metals, and schedules for sacred rituals to be performed over the machines coming off the production line... The {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g} once operated like one gargantuan well-oiled mechanism. The last record is from two months ago.{/n}

061a18c0-c5fa-463d-bca1-6cdffae6308a.Text: [View the third log data, which is hidden by the protection of the machine spirit]

2e9a7e1c-fdb2-4174-b834-9c87ce24f0b2.Text: "...praise be to the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}, whose might and power transforms dead metal to make manifest the holy visions of the Machine God. The new protocols received at the synod from the great {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} have been executed, despite those who shuddered at the thought of changing a Standard Procedure. Embolden your hearts, those whose inner weakness breeds errors in personal calculations, for the Fabricator-Censor is the conductor of the higher will and the wisest among us..."

dbaaaf67-7079-44ab-9988-53ca55ee6004.Text: "...today, at the supreme assembly, the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} unsealed the vaults of the sacred designs and committed those deemed redundant or heretical to purifying disposal. Today, dozens of Standard Procedures were lost, to be replaced by new ones, which the Fabricator-Censor will deliver to those who demonstrate the greatest devotion to serving the truth... but the data-banks contain no notion of 'Truth' — could there have been, may the All-Knowing One, the Gracious Keeper, forgive me, an error in the Fabricator-Censor's calculations, and he meant to say, 'serving the Quest for Knowledge'?"

67e3adb3-17a4-4a10-a97c-c03105bca1ff.Text: "...the instrumental terminals have already been replaced, and the material delivery systems are being prepared for divine transformation. The execution of the New Procedure has been delayed, for there are some in our ranks who doubt the words of the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} and his votaries. And there are some who are not susceptible to the Enhancement Protocol that carries our tech-comrades to enlightenment — may the deliverers of fate be merciful to them. Inaction is death, and I must be returning to our great work. Praise be to the Truth that will reveal the path to the Knowledge shrouded in darkness..."

ae64a852-3152-4bf1-ac8e-84aa9eca53f3.Text: {n}The log contains nothing of interest — the maintenance ritual schedule for the sacred machine that moves the bridge, an activation log, and a few notes of a religious nature entered by Tech-Priests.{/n}

b3231615-a272-4479-8666-b11991d726d4.Text: {n}At first glance, the records look like a typical shipping report, but after further reading, it becomes apparent that the focus here is not ore or assembly parts, but {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augments{/g} extracted from living {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}, and "spent mass" — the flesh of the victims killed either during or for the sake of machine rituals.{/n}

7299326b-e6b0-4f25-98b9-d8afd104a07a.Text: {n}The log looks damaged — the lines are uneven, and some of the values seem impossible. After a few minutes of studying the records, you feel your head begin to swim — the stored data can only be comprehended by a twisted mind touched by {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} corruption.{/n}

79e42950-050d-400f-afcd-420411906c5c.Text: {n}This record looks like a sermon of some mad {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} worshipper. The log, clearly written from someone else's words, mentions "the heart that exudes virtue" and "the cradle that rocks the child of Truth."{/n}

880f6bdd-de3a-4bad-ace5-da053602f6b3.Text: {n}Several lumens light up on the panel. You hear distinct clicks — and the cogitator goes quiet, clearly having fulfilled its purpose.{/n}

b64b21f7-eaca-497a-81b7-34bc672217bf.Text: "You are right. Servitor production is inhumane. I wish I could put an end to it — but it is not within my power."

9f5c457a-f55c-4091-a077-e54b4f0b53e3.Text: "What do you find so appalling about this custom?"

3aa7a94a-9f19-40db-88db-b24a2f2e4cff.Text: [Cut away the tumour forming on the spinal cogitator]

96cfc6f5-942a-4839-a4e0-4d2f5a767da7.Text: [Find the malfunctioning augment and disable it]

b38ec9fe-5f46-49f2-8bda-69f2234ae30b.Text: "It is a necessary sacrifice for the survival of our entire civilisation."

10e70a45-5980-4ffb-9fdf-cc1e253d1ac8.Text: "At least servitors have some use. Which is more than can be said for two-thirds of Humanity."

4358ec96-7993-49a9-868d-5a09026b7dd2.Text: [Find the source of the repeating clicks]

cce6a202-9b84-4f48-823d-9d72923d9f77.Text: "Being a servitor is an honour, xenos. You wouldn't understand."

930df17b-f41a-4316-b3e3-fc51d236c6b4.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitors{/g} before you appear as if they are performing some elaborate and confusing dance — striking strange poses, they rock back and forth with their arms bent at peculiar angles. Upon your approach, one of the servitors jerks and tries to turn in your direction. The rest immediately repeat the motion.{/n}

6afd4d6b-f82e-46e0-868f-a54a95a21f9c.Text: {n}It looks like the "dancing" {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitors{/g} have not moved at all — they still stand in the middle of the room like bizarre hinged sculptures.{/n}

f59d2e9e-7cba-41f9-8ea0-77dc20eec60d.Text: {n}The servitor's head turns to you. The {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} built into its throat lets out a strained screeching sound, at which point, in perfect sync, the brainless constructs spring into motion and lunge at you.{/n}

11270212-eaba-4540-8331-4bc4bfe40f00.Text: "You have reduced your kin to the level of mechanisms. You love mechanisms, do you not? You strive to make everything empty, cold... convenient." {n}Yrliet's mouth twists in revulsion.{/n}

ac6671f4-c868-4eea-bf6e-c507c684a5ca.Text: "I do not understand and nor do I want to. At times, understanding can be akin to a burden that weighs upon one's mind and soul."

cb8d5c8d-d1ff-406c-b0e3-9745cbe5fef7.Text: {n}The servitor touches you. Something in the depths of the man-machine crackles — and you are hit by an electrical discharge. The sound causes the other servitors to flinch but they otherwise remain motionless.{/n}

eb41a16e-0841-44af-9409-ca2680c7f869.Text: {n}Gently and swiftly, you step away from the servitor. It stretches out its hand, as if trying blindly to touch you in the space that you have already left, and stills once more — it seems its brain is incapable of quickly processing changes in its surroundings.{/n}

0642a476-b55a-4eb2-ac66-95d3968f6bb9.Text: "It appears, then, that you do not hold your kin in high regard either. Yet you fail to see defects where you should."

6d2ba463-8dd8-4a0c-a66e-3c324a3e1463.Text: "Your kind is adept at surviving, that much is certain. But I do not believe that what I am seeing was done purely for the sake of survival..."

7a704a16-bf5c-48a4-b076-4cb533630565.Text: {n}The strange scene is complemented by a grating sound — dull clicks just at the edge of your hearing, coming from an unknown source.{/n}

d8359729-28c0-4dfd-8d8c-683d21074856.Text: {n}The closest servitor twitches — and the others follow suit. It is clear that the entire group is connected by a single machine spirit, and something caused it to stop working. One of the servitors must have a fault in its cogitator or some other augment — and that fault then ended up affecting the whole group.{/n}

bc92479a-8d19-4b0b-9377-3d7884b9dc21.Text: {n}Based on a cursory inspection, you conclude that the servitors were designed for precision work on an assembly line — possibly circuit production. The number of high-quality, expensive {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augments{/g} in their bodies greatly exceeds basic standards.{/n}

418cc629-2768-44ee-a830-56bf4074a93c.Text: {n}Soon enough, you locate the source of the clicking. On the back of one of the servitors, a tumour, oozing with murky ichor, is growing straight through the augments. The relays, coated in inflamed tissue, are blocked, hence the reason for the persistent clicking.{/n}

fba6b763-dccc-4a55-8f0f-6645482ebc8b.Text: {n}You carefully examine the servitor until you eventually spot the cover on its chest. After unscrewing and removing the plate, you discover the wires for the failed {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmetic{/g} parts and cut them.{/n}

5d210cc3-d3a3-4dd4-9de2-bac380a0efb7.Text: {n}After failing to fully understand the servitor's design, you pick a {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} pretty much at random, one that looks busted, and cut it off from the rest of the system. Immediately, you hear hissing coming from deep inside the servitor's flesh. You catch a whiff of charred meat and burnt wiring.{/n}

49a9d5dc-5238-4bb9-93de-660df804e580.Text: {n}Without much difficulty, you cut the excess flesh from the mechanisms. The liberated relay lets out a rapid burst of clicks, then a spark flashes before your eyes, and something begins to hum deep inside the servitor's flesh.{/n}

7cf18f09-03a8-477d-a3c2-889e9f61f0e1.Text: {n}A clumsy twitch of your hand — and you cut off too much flesh. The stump suddenly swells, and you watch as it consumes the entire relay — clearly a mutation caused by {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} energies.{/n}

9e326104-f78f-4652-8e5d-1f3bb1de74d2.Text: {n}As if on cue, the servitors stop moving, lower their arms, and turn to you.{/n} "Crew 24, second lane of the {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}. Commencing work. State your request." {n}The servitor addressing you is looking past you, and the voice is coming from the {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} built into its throat.{/n}

30422a34-2f7f-445d-a87f-57500eac627b.Text: {n}You back away awkwardly, trip over your own feet, and flap your arms in an attempt to keep your balance. The servitors react to the movement — with deafening shrieks from their joints, they straighten and lunge forward!{/n}

06d2166f-b0d0-4671-9b8c-48064539f5d9.Text: {n}The blow breaks off the servitor's arm cleanly at the joint. The arm falls to the floor, but the servitor does not notice — it pokes the air with its stump, then goes still.{/n}

69d81662-800c-4bfd-8214-c9785389bbac.Text: {n}Yrliet is lost in thought, seemingly not expecting to hear an answer.{/n}

b5af290d-beaf-4b0f-a3e4-fe6d1cc24938.Text: {n}You bat the servitor's hand away — and it lets out a piercing screech. The other servitors straighten and, with the same unbearable screeching, advance on you.{/n}

55a51d5b-8229-4dd1-b7af-b8935eb0c34f.Text: "Crew 24, second lane of the {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}. Commencing standard procedure."

984af335-28b1-4bc8-8e04-768590ebbe94.Text: {n}You step away from the servitors, and they remain in place.{/n}

d4dca28d-72be-4aa4-963d-addf0e3aa090.Text: "A mutation in a servitor? {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} typically reject the use of flawed soft tissue for their constructs. Perhaps something has caused this aggressive growth — and quite recently."

eb2d92ec-6f08-4ca1-a6b0-9d427c67a529.Text: {n}Yrliet glances at the servitors and looks away.{/n} "Many of the customs of the mon-keigh are terrible... but some are more insane and disgusting than the rest."

aa9e47f4-b611-4a8d-ab55-27a77b96811b.Text: {n}The servitor's hand moves — it is slowly reaching toward you...{/n}

2eac250a-84d6-411a-b6ee-28e567ffeeac.Text: {n}Yrliet stares at you in amazement, tilting her head to the side like a bird.{/n} "I did not expect such words from you. You are... interesting, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}."

55095025-cda7-41ef-938a-0410e7851feb.Text: "Is that any way to greet the {mf|master|mistress} of your world?"

cf729c3c-3c93-4ca0-8227-bf264b9c069c.Text: "{name}. Heir of House von Valancius. Rogue Trader."

0d588c4d-482a-492d-b8df-f1937dcaff96.Text: "Where is the Fabricator-Censor? I will only speak with the person in charge of this manufactorum."

53b0c26e-25c3-4162-bc8d-7b556927e968.Text: "I will not be doing anything until I meet with the Fabricator-Censor."

b8f5e3ee-d19c-435e-986d-d7c56128d255.Text: "What's happening on this planet? Why is the governor not responding to the ship's hails? What are heretic ships doing in this system?"

85649d88-1133-4cab-9045-b65a2815920e.Text: "The Fabricator-Censor is a traitor to the Imperium and Humanity. I will not comply with any protocols approved by him."

b6497127-7e70-4425-b8a5-e51c8cb83126.Text: {n}Glaito bares his teeth, and Solomorne quickly tugs at his collar to calm him down.{/n} "Whatever blight has afflicted him, it's dangerous enough that it almost set off Glaito's self-defence protocols. I have only seen this happen once before."

0ce7a5ee-6374-4dd6-8546-d48ec46a2f4c.Text: {n}You carefully study the robe-clad figure. A black border of necrosis spreads out from around the Tech-Priest's implants — for some reason, his body is rejecting the True Flesh. A moment later, you recognise the dominant smell in the bouquet of scents permeating the air around the Tech-Priest — the stench of rotten meat.{/n}

d4de7487-7b88-457c-a411-587db6fbe02b.Text: {n}It is practically impossible to make out the Tech-Priest's face with the hood pulled so low. The air on the {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} is thick with the smell of fumes and molten plasteel, but standing close to the Tech-Priest, you can clearly smell the stench coming off him — a staggering mixture of machine lubricants, old sweat, and something even more revolting.{/n}

8ca8057a-9042-42f8-8c33-251202986adf.Text: "Recommendation rejected. The catechism of protocols could have been distorted. Adherence to the standard procedure of reconnaissance and purification recommended."

3d2422a4-b7e0-4eb4-a7b3-2dfd8629ffa2.Text: "Phew... this guy smells worse than a {g|Encyclopedia:Grox}grox{/g} fermented in spent {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g}. I bet he tastes even worse."

27af07e9-28bf-4f5e-9290-9434984620a6.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest draws his weapon, and as his robe opens, your senses are hit by a fetid wave of rot.{/n}

30f3b06d-29aa-4036-9f38-c5c98bc15edf.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest clicks his relay.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g} Custos of the machine sanctum, tier 2-0. Identification."

8fdf1f23-5996-4e4e-b45a-4cc3be32f199.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest pauses as his external {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitators{/g} whirr, processing the information. Finally, the malfunctioning vox produces a cracked voice.{/n} "Irregularity. Execution of the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g}-approved Protocol 39-42 recommended."

ff32defd-33aa-4e79-92e3-b2f98f2bbcfa.Text: "A sacred decree passed by the Fabricator-Censor that dictates the course of action that tech-comrades of Kiava Gamma in suboptimal working condition are to follow. Immediate execution of Protocol 39-42 recommended."

1bba193c-f92f-4cc2-89f0-49b39aeb144a.Text: "Anticipated process disrupted. Execution of disposal protocol recommended."

c8a13db1-0776-4516-8ce7-9386c5f0f49c.Text: "Denied. The irregularity demands execution of Protocol 39-42 in accordance with the Fabricator-Censor's decree."

e981a59b-d04d-4cb8-962f-22b53156df83.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest nods and gestures for you to come closer.{/n}

3d3cb67d-b979-4f68-9772-b4e00da45949.Text: {n}The lumps protruding under the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g}'s bedraggled red robe hint at the mechanisms implanted in his body. You see his haggard and sickly face under the archaic respirator {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmetic{/g}.{/n} "I... I..." {n}A click, a clank, a barely audible hiss — and only then the Tech-Priest's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} finishes the word,{/n} "Identification."

e96db042-1e67-47cb-b32a-aaf18222fc91.Text: "An answer that is both perfectly accurate and perfectly useless. I do love cog lingo."

7558974a-5f9f-4afc-bf1b-4c9b0c860e65.Text: "Request denied." {n}Pasqal turns to you, his visor gleaming crimson.{/n} "Registering anomalous behaviour within this servant's organics and an invalid Noosphere response. This unit is compromised."

5a6b5f38-2b13-49a5-b2e8-6da850281ec1.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox hisses with a hint of surprise,{/n} "Consumption of the flesh of members of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} is not recommended, irrespective of their smell or compromised state."

9496de5d-5133-425b-98dc-02e615328f5b.Text: [Input the code to disable the gas supply]

52a91bd7-9b67-4511-a058-940edaffbf1a.Text: [Input the code to disable the traps]

a847cd46-de30-46d0-9bd7-47fd6823ae69.Text: {n}The towering furnace wreathed in scarlet light fills you with awe. As you approach, the heavy thrum of ancient servo-motors erupts from the machine's depths along with crackling binharic undertones. The dust-covered keys are illuminated by a faint, pale glow.{/n}

022f1da3-fa65-42e5-ac00-63ff0231cf5d.Text: {n}A long binharic trill from the guts of the furnace triggers a wave of quiet clicks coming from every direction.{/n}

3fa21521-4a8f-42e8-88e1-475ebea7e514.Text: {n}The furnace responds with a short binharic signal that evokes the mechanical rustling of unseen switches.{/n}

c0ad4d3d-45af-42e2-82ea-4f755c7ff858.Text: {n}The machine reacts with a curt binharic signal followed by a low, drawn-out tone.{/n}

a06e5b6f-4d01-47ca-a381-451a6a9cdaa2.Text: {n}Rumbling builds up in the bowels of the furnace, growing stronger apace with the sound of the ancient motors. The rumble is echoed by the screeching of metal gears and the clanging of unknown mechanisms. Slowly, almost hesitantly, the creation of the Adeptus Mechanicus disgorges a data-bank engraved with the coat of arms of House von Valancius.{/n}

c6e4c5d3-2472-46a0-8fd8-b5bc9af3605a.Text: [End the man's suffering] "Go to the Omnissiah."

f2cae0c8-51b1-455d-a87b-00280e4d1836.Text: Ended the tormented Tech-Priest's agony on Kiava Gamma.

b5f18d32-2d18-4bda-8457-408c3ceb00c4.Text: [End the man's suffering] "Go to the Omnissiah."

82c655c6-f2d1-4e61-9baa-6b01189ce5b2.Text: Prolonged the tormented Tech-Priest's agony on Kiava Gamma.

ebe6e8f1-68f8-4c70-98da-0fd0932ec43a.Text: [Delay the man's death by providing medical assistance]

b3c9ddf0-c754-47d6-9caa-59e5c5e66aa5.Text: Left the tormented Tech-Priest to die on Kiava Gamma.

4849ee85-4e5c-421b-99fd-d5e9fc78198f.Text: Appealed to the tormented Tech-Priest's sense of duty on Kiava Gamma.

9d4c4476-ef33-46e1-9b54-64ab8d83e734.Text: "Steel your heart, servant of the Imperium! Your words will help me bring down those who have betrayed Kiava Gamma!"

c1a30c02-2fa3-4afa-a97d-be8bd40ec3b0.Text: {n}This pile of human remains, carelessly tossed together, emits a suffocating stench. The torn, gutted bodies once belonged to {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}, but you cannot spot even a glint of metal anywhere — all their {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} are gone. Suddenly, one of the ravaged bodies makes the tiniest movement. The tortured man's lips move ever so slightly, his half-closed eyelids twitching.{/n}

c8ad4339-56d2-4556-8446-1090705b734b.Text: {n}Yrliet's alien, harsh features are graced with something strikingly similar to grief and compassion.{/n} "Such senseless savagery."

753c5293-2ff3-4e7d-a2b6-23fe9cf02c05.Text: "What a horrible fate... to be betrayed by one's own."

3e56d0c1-051d-48ec-822b-c57c0cfd5212.Text: {n}The man, who is minutes from death, wheezes weakly,{/n} "It's an honour... I am thankful... for the right to serve..."

578b84dd-babc-44f9-8c42-07cd2f09f777.Text: {n}The man can barely breathe without his respirator implant. It is a miracle he survived the horrific vivisection. But it takes you a single look at the gaping wounds where the {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augment{/g} was ripped out to realise — death is only a matter of time. As if having sensed your presence, the half-dead man looks at you and sharply inhales the hot air.{/n} "Machine spirit... deliver me..."

86703f49-65d8-4e34-8319-43cf23f7ebe2.Text: {n}You walk away from the bodies, struggling to wipe the images from your memory — the mangled flesh and death masks forever imprinted on the bloodless faces.{/n}

a976ee99-ebfc-4f68-b889-24fbc061efa3.Text: {n}In a single motion, you bring an end to his long torment. After checking that there are no more survivors in this pile of human remains, you step away from the nightmarish sight.{/n}

a762ca29-37c5-4066-99ee-4b50e7cbbf94.Text: "My... comrades..." {n}His voice is barely audible. It seems each word takes the man a great deal of effort.{/n} "Machine spirit... has the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} truly... abandoned us? Kiava Gamma has fallen... into the maw of the Eternal Enemy..."

4d0a71f9-ec8c-49ff-8821-bcf1924c5c53.Text: "The holy {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magi{/g}... they succumbed to heresy... the rest... were stripped of their True Flesh... to feed the heresy... Preserve us... deliver us... deliver me from erring..."

cee0577a-1627-46e2-8028-e01bec74ebc2.Text: "Sacrifice... living blood... from vessels of the True Flesh... while their heart is... still beating. After that... oblivion." {n}His eyes grow glassy.{/n} "I... knew... you would come... I've waited... so very long. Deliver me from my torment..."

62fcaf44-090e-453d-8127-cabcc581616c.Text: {n}No treatment can preserve the life in this fading body, but for the moment, you are able to stabilise him. He groans weakly.{/n} "Why... why do you prolong... my cycle? Are you waiting... for my repentance? Have I not yet purged... my soul... through my torment..." {n}He breaks into a coughing fit.{/n} "Or must I... repent for the others..."

6178a0ef-db69-4f50-b938-6ad8e5759448.Text: {n}Despite all your efforts, the man breathes his last in your arms. You walk away from the pile of corpses with a feeling that your interference only added to the dying man's suffering.{/n}

f915e666-ad76-425d-9158-0fba5cff504f.Text: {n}Something flashes in the man's eyes, as if your words have allowed him to gather what remains of his strength. Gritting his teeth, he barely raises his head and fastens his mad gaze on you.{/n} "May the Omnissiah strengthen my will... may I renounce the dissonance of variation..."

20a6fdbe-ec48-4212-b7c9-a9ddef77d609.Text: "Without the True Flesh... I am weak, machine spirit... too... weak..." {n}The man dies in your arms. You let go of the deceased, stand up straight, and walk away from the pile of bodies.{/n}

10492b1f-bd10-42ca-9c19-816af7dac01d.Text: "Know, machine spirit, angel of the Deus Mechanicus... that I saw... the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} himself... ripping the Flesh out of our tech-comrades... and chanting a litany over vessels of corruption... sarcophagi forged from corrupted metal... unholy shells designed to house evil!" {n}He lets out a weak howl.{/n}

9177d993-8e13-4775-8d43-ab6c1f373bf8.Text: "The Fabricator-Censor does not serve the Omnissiah... he obeys a different power... the one whose herald... came to Kiava Gamma at the onset of the insurgency... his mouth spewing lies and corruption... Fear him, for he is... he is..." {n}The words escape the man's mouth along with his last breath. Having spent the last bit of strength on his confession, he goes limp in your arms — forever this time.{/n}

758f4020-9329-40d3-8137-018ac548e66c.Text: {n}Behind you, you hear ragged wheezing that vaguely resembles fervent words of prayer.{/n}

077ec6f5-9930-4b73-b6d3-927f3d1d574e.Text: {n}The man gasps violently, as if the very thought terrifies him.{/n} "No! I was robbed... of the grace of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Deus Mechanicus{/g}... waste not your efforts... and hear my confession..."

1577676b-340c-4dce-94fb-3cab0752a22a.Text: {n}The binharic requiem coming from Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} sounds solemn and grim. Upon hearing it, the man's mutilated face twists into a weak semblance of a smile.{/n}

e858ba6c-ef60-4ace-95e4-f02e3658af09.Text: "I attest that the three categorical requirements for assigning the status of martyr of the faith have been met: opposition to the enemy, preservation of adherence to dogma, and a brutal death. Requesting the right to extract the subject's organic matter for it to be used in the creation of an honourable servo-skull."

0e2fddf5-1fc2-4060-8adf-0acb766d1bef.Text: {n}Leaning over the dying man, Pasqal, in a decisive yet surprisingly respectful motion, cuts his throat. Wielding a long scalpel, it takes him mere moments to release the cervical vertebrae from the hold of muscles and sinew and to cut the vertebrae, severing the head from the body.{/n}

8a74b2b9-b232-4ed8-9ead-fba603869c53.Text: "You know why I like deranged tin cans like you? When you're killed, you leave behind plenty of useful spare parts. I think I'll make a portable recaf machine out of you."

0eda18cc-fc82-44ab-889a-cd8757a1adc7.Text: [Check the chronometer] "Your five minutes have passed. I hereby sentence you to death. And I will be the one to carry it out!"

2f919874-ac45-49cc-8717-1bdf6c44ccf9.Text: "I am repulsed to hear Techna-Lingua from the mouth of a traitor."

b9ee6a1a-ced9-42cc-859b-a56f36c1e0f9.Text: "Your minions are dead. Both you and your host will likewise fail to stop me."

83b44bc3-4ee9-4d1a-bdf1-5bcddf108471.Text: "Why don't I just kill you along with your minions and be done with it?"

77e98851-9287-4365-acff-70932378bb68.Text: "I saw the strange constructs on the lines of the manufactorum. What mad machines are you creating here?"

e1cda996-9187-4070-b758-b1e6f74ab728.Text: "Kiava Gamma belongs to House von Valancius, with whose scion you have the honour of speaking."

7e37cef7-8ef5-4218-9761-7670f363935c.Text: "What did you do to the governor of Kiava Gamma? Is he alive?"

61dd3a6d-56d0-4e5c-8f8f-9ca2eda3bbb3.Text: "You deserve a painful death for what you have wrought upon the machines of this world and their priests."

09c557c3-9daf-477d-b5f4-6313f9c8d112.Text: "So you have traded one master for another? I would have expected a Fabricator-Censor to be smarter than that."

6de283dc-b714-4ff7-a93b-1803b6d367be.Text: "This is my world, and it will serve only me."

4bb42976-5c99-4b1a-a547-87960dabe455.Text: "You can still save yourself. Let us stop this nightmare together!"

62ccc1a3-6183-4158-a236-09e313e70513.Text: "In the name of the Golden Throne, I will stop you and those who follow you."

2461b0e7-eda2-4e6c-8c4e-3e5f13dadae1.Text: [Attack] "I shall purge Kiava Gamma of your corruption!"

63bea735-cb3a-4d88-b131-961d851da215.Text: Bent the Daemon Engine on Kiava Gamma to your will.

d7879530-edfc-4dfd-8404-c86754d6f043.Text: [Dominate the metallic beast] "Spirit of the warp! Bow to my will and defend me!"

7e4ee111-d8d2-4da1-a9a1-0529b721a2cb.Text: "Because the schemes of the Ruinous Powers are powerless against the servants of the God-Emperor, who are guided by His light."

a0f36d09-85f5-4b0b-86f4-82e4422c2e9b.Text: "You propose that I, the Rogue Trader of the von Valancius line, kneel before you? I am giving you five minutes. No, not to beg forgiveness. To speak your last words and to offer your final confession."

e8e1f7eb-d977-4214-a1ef-766bbdf4c21a.Text: "I usually prefer negotiating to fighting. Fighting destroys property and wastes resources. But in your case, I'm afraid that extreme measures must be taken."

f71dcbcc-38ae-427d-a2eb-189ad2ae348d.Text: "What's the matter, little tin-comrade? Implants on the blink? Forgotten how to speak properly?"

aeb3cb8b-fb1f-4f95-918b-3101476bb0d9.Text: "We have already cut down that brute of a preacher who brainwashed you and your underlings. Now it is your turn."

7edbf214-f471-478d-9573-dad7e04e8726.Text: "It appears that your masters have turned their backs on you, and now you are on your own."

f43fc9ba-c608-4b98-b71c-9587cb25d798.Text: "I have seen what you have done to this world and its poor people. I will not allow it to continue."

32689844-4cea-4ecd-bc25-115764d7347c.Text: "I shall venture a guess. It is because I am the illustrious Rogue Trader von Valancius, conqueror of the Koronus Expanse, and you are a talking piece of refuse."

c0e101f6-6b0f-46b3-b2e7-858bae0b16c8.Text: {n}The massive {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g} clad in ritual garb lets out a binharic trill and turns to you. From beneath the deep hood of his mantle, two dimly lit eye {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} gaze out at you. You hear another binharic tirade — this time clearly addressed at you.{/n}

11908c46-071e-4490-a26f-2c3073c5e63a.Text: "You dare address me in the vile tongue of savages? Me, the steward of Kiava Gamma, lord of the machine world? Kneel, pathetic spawn, if you seek swift disposal."

62b9464f-265c-4120-b554-6ca190096b43.Text: "To break free from the chains of the Cult Mechanicus is the destiny of those who work on altogether different frequencies and levels of productivity. My mind is capable of conceiving Knowledge in a way that no other biological cogitator can — and yet I am still expected to obey the taboos put in place by intellects far more primitive than mine. But these taboos can and will be undone. You have seen the things we can do once free, thrall of the Omnissiah, and you fear them!"

bfaff66a-cf00-4c62-b5e3-c2931dc751d7.Text: "Even a cursory analysis of the data shows that the probability of this outcome is negligible. You, like your predecessor, are but an artefact of certain calculations, one that requires minimal resources to revise."

5260f789-3234-4793-9489-56159b0f7d55.Text: "Primitive creature, devoid of true Knowledge. Could it be one of the slaves who escaped imprisonment? Kneel, servant, before the master of Kiava Gamma."

47e9110b-4a53-4122-8340-810da709ee68.Text: "The outsider comprehends binharic speech. Perhaps you still have a chance to serve the new lords of Kiava Gamma. Kneel, contemptible one, and I will permit your True Flesh to be used for our great purpose."

9ac5126a-e949-42f4-a1f3-28bcf9bc8e71.Text: "Comrades. Purge the {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g} of any random variables. I must prepare for the culmination of our great work."

e272460d-521d-4074-ab1d-fbe6ff37962b.Text: {n}Hoarse laughter comes from the Fabricator-Censor's vox.{/n} "There are things more frightening than death, troglodyte. To submit one's existence to a false dogma, to condemn sacred machines bound by feeble flesh to pointless calculations... the notion is rejected."

3c792352-9b89-4770-aeca-fd1efb27cd97.Text: "An impossibility. I am not a variable that can be extracted from the process without acutely affecting the probability of its successful realisation." {n}The Fabricator-Censor freezes.{/n} "Possibly a stress test. Unexpected."

a042d48b-4815-44bd-a9dc-757dfaae71ef.Text: "Steel creations destined to serve the designs of Truth. Did you see the elegance of their form? Their flawless ergonomics? And those are mere shells. True perfection fills them when they are instilled with the spark of life and granted purpose — to bring their wrath upon the heads of apostates. Once this army is assembled— but why waste words? You will see for yourself a modicum of the splendour that is in store for the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}."

44f4a83b-e211-4371-be11-0836c3fcc732.Text: "You are one of the troglodytes who once had the gall to oppress my comrades and resist my will? A messenger from the barbarian who drank the sacred unguents bestowed upon her through others' toil? Very well, then, your appearance is the perfect opportunity to teach your ilk a lesson."

2291b3eb-fed7-42fa-8e84-4e81de4b914c.Text: "The removal of unserviceable artefacts was the first step toward retooling this world. Only my tech-comrades heeded the call of truth that reached into their {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitators{/g} and allowed them to pierce the veil of empty dogmas."

ff67f4b9-0c1d-4296-a4c3-18e8128dd857.Text: "My name is Cubis Delphim. I once held the title of {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} of the Kiava Gamma {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}, but I rejected it — along with the other fetters that hindered progress. Once, my faith was flawed and led naive fools from the Cult Mechanicus into the darkness of ignorance. Now I am this world's master, and serve the true gods. You tread upon their territory, and you do not number among their legion servants — therefore, you must be subject to immediate disposal."

a1a29611-58cf-493b-9e74-3178b8d11889.Text: "Imperfect machines merit elimination — as do living elements prone to vulnerabilities such as sentimentality."

6f7440ac-9301-4e52-be92-8726364bb447.Text: {n}Cubis's vox emits a sound distorted by static — a semblance of spiteful laughter.{/n} "The granter of Truth who opened my eyes is far from this world. His son may have fallen, but his work will be completed."

eb51c213-fb3a-418c-8b72-a6bdf96c0245.Text: "Before you are subjected to disposal, you are allowed to confess. What possessed you, a former {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} of the hallowed halls of the Deus Mechanicus, to break the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s tenets and turn your temple into a den of tech-heresy?"

b6ae9530-5cf7-4dac-b089-3146ac5f0267.Text: "Hey, {name}... you sick of listening to the ramblings of this rusty cog yet? It's like he's stalling for— huh."

3dd27312-c2b2-41a8-9223-49f194de2487.Text: {n}The Fabricator-Censor straightens his back and shoulders. You hear a mounting hum as if from some powerful turbines, followed by heavy footsteps and the grinding of metal against metal.{/n}

b86ed33f-ab17-491f-b6c9-42c38b8721b7.Text: "So many open admissions of heresy in so few sentences. Sister, how many death sentences would you say his words warrant?"

f1c0c474-4d62-4ff0-bf59-09b417157f9c.Text: "Your fragile logical construct infers my agreement to once again become a slave to the Deus Mechanicus. An erroneous assertion considering the revelations divulged to me by the Truth."

b3cf1d91-54ab-4271-acb7-7512b574ca53.Text: "You assume too much, thus rendering your conclusion invalid."

141dab01-2876-4c6c-8142-149ca0499b87.Text: "I cannot answer that, Master van Calox. It is not my duty to measure the guilt of heretics. When the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Adepta Sororitas{/g} appear before enemies of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} — it is time to fire, not count."

f027e7f2-e1b0-4b91-b29e-33f6e2efcda4.Text: "And now is one of those times."

b59fe9bf-17c6-48b9-93a4-c2444f4d52b8.Text: "How dare you insult me! Your insolence is an unexpected factor. No matter... the error will soon be rectified. Soon!"

7ec936b6-bbc1-4e4c-91fb-351e8016eccc.Text: "As the senior functioning member of the Priesthood of Mars, I, Magos Explorator Pasqal Haneumann, declare this temple to the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Machine God{/g} compromised and forthwith forbid all service within it. I dethrone the Fabricator-Censor, the ignorant heretic who has betrayed the Omnissiah, and condemn as anathema any and all standard procedures implemented by him. Let the cycle of the blasphemous operations he has put in motion be discontinued."

56820d6d-dc7e-49f7-8cce-75543553ce7b.Text: "Haneumann? Liar, you are not him. Dementz Haneumann obeys me, his mind is open to the voices of the void, and the scrap-code he created protects my world. And I'll not have you, rusted refuse from the misfit caste of Explorators, call me 'ignorant'!"

6dfdcc4f-c996-4101-96e9-8b659cd41140.Text: "This statement is false. Your regalia have been revoked, you have been deemed defective and will be eliminated." {n}Pasqal turns to you and says dryly,{/n} "Initiating {g|Encyclopedia:Heretek}heretek{/g} search, designation: Dementz Haneumann. I wish to execute the retribution procedure."

f82da8b3-4b06-4f3d-9abd-f1d2b1f93e0f.Text: {n}Pasqal switches to binharic, and you hear dissonance burgeoning in the depths of the forge-cathedral — some of the giant mechanisms heed his order and go still while others, obeying the Fabricator-Censor's will, continue their work. Crashes, explosions, and the clanging of crumpling metal signify that some dissent among the machines has interrupted the manufactorum's production cycle.{/n}

85321f93-cfa9-40ce-9643-e92059111570.Text: {n}With practised calm, Pasqal checks if his weapon is ready for battle. His voice is filled with cold contempt:{/n} "A Cybersmith fears the scrap-code that might ruin their work. But I am no Cybersmith. A Forge Lord fears the corruption that might afflict the lathes in their charge and deform the product of their workshop. But I am no Forge Lord."

7eebdd29-96a8-4015-b463-c40c49f09fd4.Text: "I am a Magos Explorator. A reconnoitrer of Knowledge, a beam of lumen in the darkness of the unknown. I know not how to fear you. I only know how to explore and kill."

de5bbd76-4b8e-4921-8040-d0a303e591d1.Text: {n}Heinrix laughs scathingly before immediately cutting himself off with a hard{/n} "No."

008b3afb-7474-4be4-a647-28011fce302e.Text: {n}The words never escape your lips. The moment they touch your tongue, they scald the inside of your mouth and cause you to choke and cough. Nonetheless, the warp spirits heed your intention, and the air around you begins to pulsate with crimson flares. All the sounds in the manufactorum are momentarily silenced as the steel fiend skewers you with an intense and baleful gaze... which then shifts to the Fabricator-Censor.{/n}

f1e247ba-3786-44f7-8049-3bc89c02881a.Text: "For too long was I a prisoner of dogmas, a static unit of obedience. But one who has learned of the freedom that is lawless creation cannot be returned to that cage. I have seen... things you can never comprehend. True Technology! I touched it with my tools, I grasped its mysteries and potential. I beheld depths that cannot be forgotten, and now nothing can drag me back into the darkness of ignorance."

08b4b577-ba81-42f4-b383-0dfac0580134.Text: {n}Upon noticing you, Cubis Delphim straightens — you hear the clanging and groaning of metal as if the pistons and bearings in the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g}'s augmented body have fused together. Repellent scrapes and screeches punctuate his speech.{/n} "You. The probability of navigating your way... of reaching the inner line... was negligible. The Primordial Truth guards me and my work... then why is it that this variable has yet to be eliminated?"

adc3ecbc-0ab7-469d-92cc-b365935cde43.Text: "A gross misconception common among primitive minds. Your existence is but a statistical error that will soon be corrected."

0dfe4296-086b-4c26-bae3-828fbb176a67.Text: "Planetary governors — they always make problems... Either they let a rebellion break out, or they die at a bad time, or something worse. I can't remember the last time I saw a decent planetary ruler."

8e73eeee-328b-4a53-a0f4-cd41f6d8a416.Text: "The Omnissiah's tenets are shackles designed to limit the computing power of those who pose a threat to the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}. The Omnissiah's tenets herald only eternal stagnation in the shadow of imperfect machinery created by worthless revenants of a distant past. The Omnissiah's tenets are but lies encased in a shell of truth."

2428e058-aac9-40f7-b205-f142725bf2a9.Text: "Poor old Gaprak. Ten or so years back, he told me he felt uneasy in the presence of the tin-can comrades — I mean, the esteemed Adeptus Mechanicus. He casually complained about not having been dealt a normal planet. I'll have to honour his memory with a prayer... once we have finished purging this place." {n}Abelard brandishes his weapon.{/n} "Thankfully, the Fabricator-Censor here did not require any coercion to confess to treason."

9c3a7b99-93dd-4d93-b0bc-8ec2be7af611.Text: {n}The Fabricator-Censor lets out a binharic trill.{/n} "Witness the weapon designed to carry the glory of the true gods into the darkness of the Koronus Expanse! My shepherd has sent me one of his iron angels so that its very presence may instil faith and awe in the hearts of his flock. Accept the greatness of the Primordial Truth united with the might of the new Kiava Gamma — and perish!"

405bae81-d242-4100-a641-9665b91d49f3.Text: "I do not know if I have ever seen anything more bizarre than two {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} vying to prove who possesses the greater hubris."

5054ff9c-3432-4a50-a91b-eab5509630c4.Text: {n}The Fabricator-Censor's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} lets out a piercing, barely audible sound that makes your insides shudder.{/n} "I will rip out your spinal column and braid it around my staff, you arrogant creature."

1a8035e0-3ba8-4616-a576-d74f03c4ebd0.Text: "You may be driven by your will to fight, but know this — Kiava Gamma has already been converted. Its lines have been restructured, and its servants have already tasted the fruits of progress. In the crucibles of this manufactorum, torrid liquid metals will be used to forge vessels for sacred spirits. The adepts are already tirelessly delving deeper into new mysteries that were once barred by false tenets. You, servants of fake gods, are too late — the entire might of this world will soon rise up against the Anathema and his slaves."

e7fc8b10-d796-40ee-8732-a076e5b8bb9b.Text: "I would not count on such an outcome. Although... probability recalculation shows that even your unforeseen appearance and disappointing resilience can serve progress — where else would I have found a suitable specimen for practical testing?"

d2021647-3dd3-4990-9e50-e453f5951e7f.Text: Learned the Chaos Space Marine's blasphemous sermon on Kiava Gamma.
