219fa7d4-8a32-479e-bba1-44bbb95d3945.Text: Interrupted the Chaos Space Marine's sermon on Kiava Gamma with a paean to the God-Emperor.

440c4f67-6a03-407d-8d2e-20c10ce2972c.Text: [Interrupt the sermon with a paean to the God-Emperor]

78af631f-5ac8-4685-b014-5d085264e9de.Text: {n}The Chaos Space Marine towers over the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}' bowed heads like a dark cliff. He is reciting a sermon — slowly, almost chanting. From the mere sound of his deep, low voice, you break into a cold sweat and your gorge rises.{/n}

a2c5e95e-51c9-46ad-9658-7b0b8616b105.Text: "...listen, for my words reveal to you a path from the darkness unto the Primordial Truth, which has thrown open its gates for wayward souls seeking deliverance from the shroud of lies and torments of enslavement. Your minds have shed the bonds of the dogma that has guided you into the abyss — accept now the hope granted to you by the greatest of the Word Bearers..."

dfa5123d-3d38-4bf8-8318-800210cdaff2.Text: "Sacrilege! Here, on the soil of an Imperial world!"

2fed4663-fe88-45d2-9ecc-a2f431b61474.Text: {n}The Chaos Space Marine does not seem to notice you — his gaze is focused on his flock, who are hanging on his every word.{/n} "Those living a lie will not see the Truth until they have renounced the false gods. Only through your faith does the reign of those corpse worms hold, worms that devour your very body, wrecking weak souls, gnawing at your eyes and ears so that you do not turn them toward the true masters."

89bcab5d-cb45-481c-aee4-6aa652693e30.Text: "Your world, a foundry in the realm of corpses, was given the honour of serving as the crucible of the oncoming victory, and we, the Word Bearers, shall be at the tip of it, as well as those of you who can overcome the slander of the false idols. The incinerating fires of Kiava Gamma will birth weapons whose advance heralds the coming of a new age — an age wreathed by the glory and resplendence of Chaos Undivided!"

923e9412-e1d7-4362-8a58-d56be7aecda5.Text: {n}It feels as if, with each of the Chaos Space Marine's words, the light around you dims. Something tickles your face — a thin rivulet of blood is streaming down from your nose, dripping onto your lips and chin.{/n}

2f02e943-d9d1-4278-bc57-5744ccfd34da.Text: "...heed the liberating Truth that is word made blessed flesh, which marks every true servant of the Gods. Heed the wisdom of Lord Lorgar, the Word Bearer, most beloved son of Chaos..."

465468e0-7602-4f48-b60b-49d6adf5a172.Text: {n}The longer you listen, the more the words of the sermon blur together into incoherent humming. The itch in your ears turns into drilling pain that crushes your temples and squeezes your neck — and spreads downward, to your very heart, which it pierces with an icy needle.{/n}

6263f88f-3ec8-481f-9fc4-a234de21d69a.Text: {n}Through the haze of pain and the film of tears over your eyes, you sense the scorching gaze of the Chaos Space Marine, who has turned his head in your direction.{/n} "The time for words is at an end, children of {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g}. Praise the Gods with a bloody offering!"

a531f0e0-cc86-4354-a11c-f5837e313eb9.Text: {n}The Chaos Space Marine roars in fury as the Tech-Priests turn and charge you as if on cue.{/n}

eb649461-3ed6-4788-a3d3-f6f809ab3276.Text: "That's it, I've had enough of these profane words. Turn around, beast of the Archenemy! You called down purifying flame upon yourself — and the flame has come!"

5a867bb8-78be-4b62-a82f-253cf487ac31.Text: "Voice... that voice... have I heard it before? Or, no? It's like... it drowns out all other voices... let's leave. Quickly, please!"

e087ab12-977c-42a9-ae31-c156619b4acc.Text: "Registering encroachment upon sacred furnaces through both thought and action. Initiating virtuous eradication procedure." {n}Pasqal's voice is a bloodthirsty growl, its sound reminiscent of the whirring of a chainsword. One of his mechadendrites snaps its pincers as he charges into the fray.{/n}

0c2507ab-9a0a-40c6-95f7-15e0714f8ee7.Text: {n}Pasqal gazes at his former brethren and whispers dryly,{/n} "The Noosphere signature of the defective units has been archived. In accordance with the sacred commandments, I will tolerate no heresy and hereby sentence you to categorical disposal without redemption."

f2de14c9-b7dd-464d-b768-307051f4fccc.Text: {n}Heinrix hisses through gritted teeth.{/n} "I knew our meeting on Rykad Minoris wouldn't be the last, but to run into this anathema here... Kiava Gamma did not merely succumb to heresy, {name}. Your world is in the clutches of the greatest evil known to the Imperium."

9fa2481b-f879-42c6-9fa1-49c7d3fd8158.Text: {n}The words of the righteous hymn cut through the torrent of the heretic's impious proclamations. You feel as if the light of the Emperor Himself touches your heart, warming it with grace and protecting it from the malignant corruption.{/n}

5e5df4aa-3a17-44d3-a8af-d0a31cfa2733.Text: {n}Solomorne stares at the monstrous figure with glassy eyes.{/n} "I thought I knew everything about Lex Imperialis violations, but that thing offends His Law by its very existence..."

0e3b9eda-39a6-4c36-bdaf-b3ca75453da2.Text:
"1000001 1110110 1100101 100000
1001111 1101101 1101110 1101001
1110011 1110011 1101001 1100001
1101000
Identification: Cubis Delphim, appointed Fabricator-Censor of Kiava Gamma
Entry 1.
For a long time, This Unit has served the Great Creator in the Imperium. As a driving gear. As a binding chain. As sacred unguents. By the grace of the Machine God, This Unit possesses extraordinary computational capacity, which is what prompted it to study the most complex logical structures and systems that fill the great gifts left by the ancients.
However, the endless Quest for Knowledge for His glory has provided This Unit with an unexpected reason for variable alteration. Elaboration: Kiava Gamma is This Unit's new destination, located at the edge of worlds.
The conflict in the incoming data indicates that the Machine God prohibits This Unit from making technological progress, which it seeks to bring into this world. Conclusion: The Omnissiah encourages His servants to remain basic, unproductive primitives.
This Unit made a presupposition that on Kiava Gamma, a planet that lies far from the dogmatic thinking of the Order, its subordinates would heed fresh ideas and move the rusted cogs of progress. The results were negative. Those who follow in the Omnissiah's footsteps do not possess the computational capacity required for the Quest for Knowledge, and thus they continue to follow only the most basic commands, not realising their true meaning.
May This Unit be afflicted with the curse of flesh if it lets the simplicity of primitives deter it from its goal: to equal the expertise of the Creator."

840ed874-f68b-47c4-b43a-88bfc01e629f.Text:
"1001110 1101111 1101110 100000 1110000 1110010
1101111 1100111 1110010 1100101 1100100 1101001
100000 1100101 1110011 1110100 100000 1110010
1100101 1100111 1110010 1100101 1100100 1101001
Identification: Cubis Delphim, acting Fabricator-Censor of Kiava Gamma
Entry 2.
I have been systematically adjusting the processes on Kiava Gamma to make even the simplest of primitives see the defectiveness of their own patterns. However, the latest cursory calculations have shown that the effectiveness of my influence on my subordinates is shifting toward negative values.
If I were to make use of the simple language of biological elements, my condition in the present moment could be equated with the terms 'despair' and 'rage.' Despite my computational capacities, I was unable to pursue on my own the research that interests me.
I experienced a logical epiphany upon intercepting a signal of unknown origin. A variable, which I will name Theta, transmitted a continuous flow of information to me, paving in my mind the way to freedom that was once blocked by the Great Creator. At the end of the transmission, Theta made me an offer, refusing which would have been not only difficult but also illogical.
Utilising the newly obtained knowledge, I began making insignificant adjustments to variables in the sacred rituals, weaving the required words and symbols into them so that they remained within an acceptable margin of error, but infallibly altered in their essence. A risk? Affirmative. However, the Omnissiah created us so that we would broaden the boundaries of our own existence. Risk is an inherent, albeit constantly changing variable that must be included in the calculations, all while pursuing the end goal of becoming something greater."

32d4478c-937d-478d-af77-55f5ee08c0a6.Text:
"1001101 1110101 1110100 1100001
1110100 1101001 1110011 100000
1101101 1110101 1110100 1100001
1101110 1100100 1101001 1110011
Identification: Cubis Delphim, Great Steward of Kiava Gamma, Lord of the Machine World
Entry 3.
No longer the sole variable that opposes the outdated and sluggish mechanism of a false order, we have cast off the shackles that hindered our pursuit of progress. The secrets of the warp that were revealed to us by our ally have brought us further in the Quest for Knowledge than our countless years spent in the service of the Omnissiah.
The inevitable process that is transformation consumed Kiava Gamma the moment our genius completed its work on the code designed to repair our subordinates' distorted perception of reality. The chance of our carefully calculated plan being uncovered by simple, predictable, unimaginative primitives was non-existent from the very beginning.
All who were connected to the planetary network when the code was launched finally witnessed the glory and splendour of the Primordial Truth! The most logical of our unconverted brethren bowed down in awe before the might of the knowledge that was promised to them, renouncing the Omnissiah and his archaic dogma. And even those who refused still contributed to our cause by giving their True Flesh for the requirements of production and higher experimentation.
The outdated technologies of our ancestors cannot compare to the machines our world now manufactures. I personally beheld the miracle of the first creation, the first birth. I sculpted its perfect form with my own hands, and the Primordial Truth breathed life into its metallic flesh.
All that the Omnissiah has bequeathed to us is a lie designed to drown Humanity in darkness. We have dispelled that darkness and have ourselves become the light that heralds the coming of a new age of technology for the universe."

11a97282-67be-4fe9-ae58-64264f994f86.Text: The very sight of this damaged shard appals you and leaves no doubt in your mind: this is a piece of abominable xenotech.

57087889-d903-4a0d-9996-05cf9588d429.Text: A storage device discovered in a hidden chamber on Kiava Gamma. The data it contains has been securely encrypted.

e81ef11d-3d0b-4316-bd2a-42384ed203d6.Text: A sacred instrument for manually activating the good machines of the Omnissiah.

4c38c942-923d-4657-a371-7ff866c7bac5.Text: ...continue sending orders from the bridge and request status updates from the other compartments.

009c4ae8-96cc-4b2e-a547-60a4d1617d31.Text: ...decipher the incoming vox-transmissions at all costs.

f458b075-595f-485f-acb9-7eaa6547a988.Text: ...destroy the ship's vox-system to prevent the transmission of the distorted messages.

1cc1147f-27d6-4952-96b7-f6df3a387696.Text: ...assign officers to all control systems to execute manual transmission override and send orders to the other compartments on paper.

c3125d2e-6fdd-46de-9dff-94ac3fa31b53.Text: ...rushes to help the crew, shouting out orders.

1ecf03fe-45e6-49a3-bba0-21da37339b87.Text: ...executes one of the lunatics and roars a series of orders to the rest.

905ea5d6-d8d3-40e2-bed9-fc75134c1f6a.Text: ...begins methodically exterminating any who show signs of madness.

61773d4d-2acf-40c0-a3cf-2c8859e93d22.Text: ...commands the crew to carry on with their duties until the very last.

814200e1-7322-464d-b695-0b308c448be2.Text: ...reiterate the duty that every citizen of the Imperium owes to Humanity.

eb36508f-50e5-4db3-9275-433e13b86546.Text: ...offer a matter-of-fact logical analysis that might help them find the best tactic for this situation.

92fc4134-3140-4740-84f2-5daa06837da3.Text: ...decides to follow Idira's advice and goes back to the bridge.

9d9a5d33-e320-40e5-a8d5-6d523a8fd109.Text: ...stop the transmission process at any cost.

d82afab5-7817-41fa-a9f2-3f25fed5a608.Text: One of the bridge officers turns to the throne. "Lord Captain, the vox-stations are malfunctioning and overloading the system! None of our outgoing transmissions are getting through. The incoming ones that do make it are distorted beyond interpretation!"

1a3c76b3-8e90-455a-9ae4-d415086b87e9.Text:
Sector: Koronus Expanse
Region: Cinerus Maleficum
Location: Cranach
Material: Pict-report on events on the bridge on approach to Kiava Gamma
Recorded by: Servo-Skull Watcher XVI

c8ddd4f0-3b1e-4ab0-9616-65ce051facb8.Text: The voidship's bridge. Sounds of working cogitators and officers' footsteps. The everyday scene is interrupted by an ear-splitting beeping sound, followed by lumens going out. In the dim glow of candles and emergency lights, one of the officers in frame cries out, another falls to her knees, clutching her head. Over the beeping of voxes, shouts can only just be heard: "What's going on?" "The doors are locked!" "We've lost contact with all compartments!"

20cc5130-7d3b-4aea-b155-7cfea65daf81.Text: For a moment, tense silence falls over the bridge. But then the lunatics are stricken with another fit of rage. The officers' orders break through the cacophony — execute them all!

706d541b-8121-44f5-b30d-4cf93a9c5ece.Text: Vigdis enters one command after another. The station groans, shrieks, and sparks under her fingers, and a shock passes through the wires. Blood drips onto the control panel, and Vigdis lets out a grinding cry, but does not relent. A few moments later, she crumples. "The signals... have been... blocked..." Then she falls unconscious.

32063783-8264-45b4-ad38-b00b0e3dbda6.Text: "Proceed!" A team of decryption experts gets to work. Data-tethers are inserted into sockets as they connect to the cogitators. One of the vox-clerics leans over the console, another is writing something on a piece of parchment... but then she bursts into maniacal laughter and stabs herself in the eye with a steel quill. Another scream — a Tech-Priest, who was mid-prayer, tears himself to pieces with his own mechadendrites. More and more lunatics are mutilating themselves and lunging at others.

4190423b-aeb8-4c90-9303-29aa1337579c.Text: One monitors the comm line, another prepares written orders. The Vox Master's unit sets up an internal communications system via comm-beads. The crew's efforts are expedient and well-coordinated, and within moments, servo-skulls carrying instructions from the Lord Captain are diving into the ventilation shaft and vanishing into the gloom.

f6924a67-399f-4105-a1c5-843ba83b9805.Text: One of the cogitators jolts, lets out a piercing screech, swells up — and explodes, peppering the nearby officers with a hail of white-hot shards. The voxes produce an unnerving mechanical sound like mad cackling. The vox picks up a series of metallic clangs as servo-skull messengers carrying prepared orders plummet to the floor. From beyond the pict frame, a shout comes — the distorted orders made it into the internal vox-system and have already been delivered to the compartments!

229b5187-9ffd-4f46-801f-e4ac0f13b3eb.Text: The next few seconds of the servo-skull's pict contain nothing but flashes and gunshots. When the sounds of the massacre die down, the lunatics have been destroyed, as well as some of the sacred cogitators, oculi, and consoles on the bridge.

f87f84fb-1515-4c69-970f-972e34e4e977.Text: The Lord Captain barks out the command. The Vox Master raises her arms in protest, but it is too late — the enforcers open fire on the vox-stations. The transmission of distorted data is stopped... along with the ship's main vox-systems.

2a86092b-0cc3-4038-aa5b-06d1cdcfc279.Text: Currently, the most frightening situation on the ship is in the arsenal. Some of the distorted commands, despite the bridge's best efforts, still made it into the compartment, and the lower-ranking technomats complied — by raising the temperature inside the ordnance depot! The heat is about to hit critical levels, and the shells are going to explode, blowing the arsenal and the neighbouring compartments to smithereens.

bee9a7d0-ef8b-4e8f-8a7e-b098471dbdde.Text: The bridge is littered with evidence of disaster — corpses being hastily removed by healers, broken machinery, and bloodstains all over the bulkheads and deck. Among the dead are many irreplaceable specialists and officers, but the remnants of the command have already gathered around the hololithic map and are in the process of discussing the plan of action.

4d24366d-c08e-4948-b5d7-fe422f425fae.Text: The image on the pict is fuzzy — nothing but glimpses of people, shouting, racket, and the Lord Captain's orders. Within minutes, the crazed crew members are either dead or bound and unconscious. The officers clustered around the Lord Captain are barely breathing but unharmed.

e4a6241d-8d54-4b27-9b2f-fa2376ff66f7.Text: The mad officers are attacking their comrades. The recording shows glimpses of a torn head staining everything with blood and a vox-cleric howling in pain, clutching his broken arm. By the time they have tied up all those not killed in the scuffle, the bridge attendants can barely catch their breath.

8588624d-5c52-4e70-9536-c78aed3e66b9.Text: "Scrap-code..." The voice belongs to the on-deck Enginseer who has turned to the Lord Captain from his station. "We have been attacked with scrap-code, a tech-heresy designed to corrupt machines! The transmission received from the planet was infected with this taint, and it is now running through the ship's veins. Omnissiah preserve us!"

c8c15d17-0043-4ba1-8556-6fe99166aa36.Text: The exhausted crew members, who were still breathing deeply, one by one begin to bend and collapse to their knees. Coughing, wheezing, and the sounds of stomachs being turned inside out come from all directions.

80a6231e-dfa3-40ac-a08e-e6d81f7ed860.Text: Gathering a group of technomats and workers with plasma cutters along the way, the Lord Captain reaches the middle decks. Armoured doors separate thousands of people from the rest of the ship, people who have been robbed of light, communication, and oxygen. A wave of the Rogue Trader's hand — and the cutter gets to work. Ten minutes later, sheets of metal come down with a crash, and a stream of haggard-looking people pours out of the death trap and into the passageways, praising the Throne, the Lord Captain, and all that is holy.

e5bf4ff3-3dd0-49a0-bde5-6bcdc5f70c74.Text: Thanks to the Rogue Trader's efforts and the sacrifice of the senior bridge officers, the rest of the ship's compartments were able to suppress the panic and deal with the raging machine spirits with few casualties. No critical reports.

ef257e71-7076-449b-8469-183cb73e3c25.Text: The Rogue Trader is taken to the medicae deck, where {mf|he|she} is instantly surrounded by doctors — the crowd is so dense that the servo-skull anxiously circles above them, trying to catch a glimpse of the subject of its recording. At last, the Lord Captain opens {mf|his|her} eyes, dragged back to consciousness by a cocktail of medications and biostimulants from several IV bags.

df54494d-dcaa-421d-bc72-519b19c85330.Text: Something twitches at the edge of the frame, and a blow knocks the Rogue Trader into the bulkhead — the vox catches a muffled wheeze and the crunch of breaking bones. Everything else gets lost in the interference that obscures the frame. When the image is restored, the servo-skull shows a group of people finishing off a loader servitor — the one that must have attacked the Lord Captain. The rest lean over a body lying on the floor...

875896e4-b6c0-48e6-be06-9f311b044df2.Text: The atrium is in a state of panic — silhouettes skitter about in the dark hall, illuminated only by the flickering of emergency lumens. Curt orders and someone's feverish words of prayer can be heard. Having lost all communication, the beheaded ship is writhing in agony.

66a3da41-b368-4fcc-b3fc-ed70523d1a5d.Text: The Rogue Trader takes a few steps down the corridor and breaks into a coughing fit — undoubtedly a result of spending too long on the bridge. Splashes of crimson stain {mf|his|her} clothes and the floor, and the Lord Captain shakes {mf|his|her} head...

abe8e65c-6771-4ad2-a0fe-e1da4f6cba0d.Text: With each word, the people around the bed straighten up, and their gazes are filled with awe and faith. The officers salute the Lord Captain and leave the medicae deck in complete confidence, ready to do their duty.

8a49a09a-cfae-47ea-9d23-0e81716230d1.Text: The crew is too tired, barely standing, to heed any orders. The most resilient officers rush to cut open the doors. When the way out opens, most of the crew are dragged out by their exhausted comrades. Last to leave the bridge, the Lord Captain runs out, coughing heavily.

5634a7b0-3324-4826-a948-d72c951ebedf.Text: The Lord Captain gets to the door... and they obediently open, as if they were never locked to begin with. A few more people run out after the Rogue Trader, one of them dragging the Vox Master's body.

3327c961-4656-46ee-9a66-5b1a947f4f13.Text: The Lord Captain tries to get to the doors, but they are surrounded by panicking people who are slamming their fists on them. The doors suddenly open, and the crowd pours out, leaving behind several trampled bodies. It is a miracle that the Lord Captain makes it out uninjured.

a6dbd30a-8bc3-4c25-bafb-f7597c209d8e.Text: Without saying a word to anyone, the Rogue Trader makes for the exit through the smoke, steam, and rubble. The servo-skull is right behind {mf|him|her} — the Lord Captain's back is in the frame, the vox is picking up screams of pain and coughing coming from somewhere off to one side.

bd0969db-767d-455c-afd5-ac0466bd8f61.Text: Leaning on a support beam, the Rogue Trader takes several deep breaths, trying to flush {mf|his|her} lungs with air. Then {mf|he|she} straightens, smooths {mf|his|her} uniform, and heads toward a goal known only to {mf|him|her}. The servo-skull follows.

e5000cc8-a9dd-4f72-92a6-d27db21801e2.Text: It takes a while for the Lord Captain to find the cogitator mentioned by the fallen officer. The panel of the isolated terminal is riddled with cracks and bloodstains, and on the floor by the terminal, a Tech-Priest is lying in a heap with his head smashed and technical liquids mixed with blood oozing out of his ports. The Lord Captain decides to...

82f0b544-e490-4d05-ad04-dc7bb1eab3a6.Text: The Vox Master nods curtly and connects the tangles of cables coming from the back of her head to the main vox-station. "Spirit of the ship, I beseech thee, shield us from this peril and allow not the heretical signals to pass!"

fa49a442-b358-4f08-8ddd-490286bca867.Text: Poisoned and disoriented, the people can barely stand, and they are slow to respond to the order. The servo-skull shows Abelard Werserian, the Lord Captain's loyal Seneschal, stepping in. He firmly gets to work, personally guiding those who are dazed, issuing direct commands to the crew, all the while barking instructions peppered with choice words of naval slang. The screeching of plasma cutters and the loud crash of the falling doors signals that the way out of the trap is clear — the survivors abandon the bridge in haste.

772abf12-de28-4db7-815e-b10fd71dee94.Text: The Rogue Trader gathers the senior officers and assigns each to one of the ship's control systems.

0939146e-97f1-4ec3-ae16-fec41fbdcce6.Text: The madman's body falls at the Rogue Trader's feet as {mf|his|her} commanding voice, magnified by a vox-amplifier, carries over all the noise. {mf|He|She} orders the crew to master themselves immediately, promising to personally execute anyone who fails to do so.

7497f73e-792e-4cbf-861d-8db987bf762e.Text: A loud pop — the pipes over the officers' heads burst, and a blast of hot air flings the voidborn away from the Lord Captain, his body slamming straight through a cogitator panel. The pict frame spins uncontrollably — the servo-skull was jolted by the gust. The pict-recorder fogs over, the vox picking up the crackling of electricity and a death cry. "Gas on the bridge!" a junior attendant shouts and instantly doubles over, inhaling the poisoned air.

f53717af-6463-4f42-be1c-bfa96b7d028d.Text: The walk to the bridge is uneventful. The crisis has passed — although wounded and crippled, the ship nevertheless is returning to its normal operation.

9fafd1ad-c7f8-4a06-87e6-3ecf1a88f09b.Text: The Lord Captain gives the order to...

58802bd8-4231-458c-b474-241f18780d73.Text: Life on the bridge is as bustling as ever — even though the people are surrounded by destruction. The senior officers have the situation under control, and the people have been organised — the emergency crew have already finished repairing the pipes, the technomats are setting up cogitators and consoles, and the healers are bagging up what few corpses there are and examining the wounded.

7ad9eb0b-9036-4630-84fb-cde1b9094eb3.Text: The farther the Rogue Trader walks into the atrium, the more unsteady {mf|his|her} footsteps become. The Lord Captain takes a moment to lean against the bulkhead, but then crumples to the floor, coughing up gouts of blood onto {mf|his|her} chest. Several people immediately dash to the Rogue Trader's side...

26a4173c-19e4-481a-b704-c77ef76327b4.Text: The officers' faces are calm and confident. One by one, they bow their heads, their hands forming the sign of the Aquila on their chests. They soon leave the medbay to deal with the situation on board.

19065bd9-7fe4-49e5-a902-bc9658bb9377.Text: The Rogue Trader enters a sequence of commands into the terminal. The machine goes dark for a few seconds, then whirrs. The screens fill with endless streams, then light up again. The control panel responds to the Lord Captain's requests, warning about the critical situation on the lowermost decks of the ship. The Lord Captain decides to...

30450cc2-1ad3-43a6-98d6-3470f2279002.Text: The maintenance bay is sending out hundreds of desperate distress calls that have gone unanswered up to now — when the machines went out of control and started turning people insane, others, driven by some hateful and paranoid logic, started butchering the servants of the Adeptus Mechanicus. The Tech-Priests have sustained heavy losses, but the remains of the cult are still holding the line. Out of everything that's happening on the ship, the situation in the maintenance bay is the direst.

7219e5f1-56d7-433b-a7d9-2ccd6e34b186.Text: ---Portion of pict-recording damaged after contact with unknown object---

4dad7bf5-1b81-492a-8bc1-6dfa9b4e8504.Text: The most problematic situation is on the middle decks, which have been left without any instructions from the bridge since the disaster began. Due to power supply failures, the bay has been completely cut off from the life support systems. The people, surrounded by darkness, are panicking, and their oxygen supply will last another half hour at most.

88e259df-9fe2-4b88-a34b-00c75055e25c.Text: The Rogue Trader jumps to the side, dodging an attack from a worker servitor. Shrieking binharic trills flood the vox-recording, and the pict-recorder picks up nothing but sparks from the blows. Eventually, the frame rights itself. The Rogue Trader, weapon in hand, is standing over the broken servitor, which claws mindlessly at the floor with its appendages.

d9be9959-50b4-41cc-98d2-abf44127144c.Text: The Rogue Trader arrives not a moment too soon — the crew, frightened out of their wits, have already cornered the priests of the Omnissiah and are about to execute them. The Lord Captain stands between the angry mob and the Tech-Priests, {mf|his|her} sheer presence already giving the crowd pause. Harshly cutting off any objections from the crew, the Rogue Trader orders the officers {mf|he|she} gathered on the way here to escort the mutineers out and set up a guard post outside the bay, where the Tech-Priests begin to offer desperate prayers to the crippled machine spirits.

019a31d8-b2fb-44da-ae16-ca2fe890a171.Text: When the Lord Captain and the officers {mf|he|she} gathered along the way reach the arsenal, the servo-skull's ocular lenses instantly fog over. On the vox-recording, the Rogue Trader issues commands calmly and succinctly — execute those responsible for carrying out the asinine order that came from the bridge and get the compartment sorted. The three technician teams immediately head to the overheated reactors, and the privates to the warhead transporters. An hour later, the situation is back to normal.

9b394482-0324-4ee1-a948-6fb61d5546c0.Text: A number of scared junior officers promptly surround the bed. "The ship is suffering devastating losses!" "The interbay comms are still offline!" "The crew is terrified, Lord Captain!" Eyes full of terror, bloodied uniforms, slumped shoulders — and these officers are the only link the Lord Captain currently has to the world outside the medicae deck! All {mf|he|she} can do to support these people who are willing to risk their lives for the ship is...

c99120d4-9de7-419a-8781-ae6adbafefe2.Text: The Rogue Trader approaches the Vox Master who is rummaging inside the case of a ruined vox-station. "Lord Captain! Praise the Emperor, you're in one piece! The situation on board is unclear. I'm afraid that currently most of the compartments can only receive orders in written form."

bf442be0-121d-464a-b710-163ded429fd2.Text: One of the officers — a burnt woman who has lost her hand — starts weeping, interrupting the Rogue Trader's speech. The officers shudder and quickly avert their eyes, then, after a half-hearted salute, back away toward the exit.

2608f780-40ec-4a58-bcfa-2e628cda4018.Text: The Lord Captain knows where help is needed most. {mf|He|She} decides to...

c5dd24a8-9309-4c6a-a1ac-4ccfecf28f8f.Text: An enforcer shoves a rabid servitor away from the Lord Captain as {mf|he|she}...

0c4db95e-c0cb-4c63-a2ad-6bf7e4f029ee.Text: The officers are too exhausted. It's easy to tell by their fallen faces and hunched shoulders that each word the Lord Captain says crushes their spirit like a rock rather than helping it soar. Ashamed of their own weakness, they leave the medicae deck and shuffle off to their stations in resignation.

3a63ebc1-c9e9-4ee9-b3a0-c735908ac0f6.Text: The bridge resembles a battlefield — the floor is strewn with corpses, the cogitators are damaged, and the people inside are barely standing. Healers in masks are bagging up pale corpses, technomats are hastily patching up the ruptured pipes, and the surviving officers are trying to get the remaining cogitators back up and running.

5075c219-457f-4fa8-9053-33e7f3680d75.Text: By the comm station, the Rogue Trader runs into the Vox Master. "Praise the Emperor, you're in one piece, Lord Captain! The situation on board is satisfactory. I was just in the middle of setting up comm channels — soon all the vox-casters will be fully operational."

b9d4a928-cc5b-479e-becd-ad8fe01d8359.Text: Another man appears in the pict frame — a junior officer, completely out of breath, carrying a heap of scrolls. The Vox Master nods at him. "Ah, here are the reports, Lord Captain. If you find yourself able to return to your station, I can immediately give you a rundown of the state of affairs on the ship..."

a583d88d-98a2-47f9-90da-f7fc71f6a2db.Text: The Lord Captain demands some parchment and a quill. {mf|He|She} briefly questions the officers, outlines the situation on the ship, writes down the data, and calculates possible outcomes. After ten minutes, the officers start to leave the medicae deck, each one carrying a piece of parchment with specific instructions.

6593b0fc-6048-4543-8205-12505aa8d38c.Text: The Rogue Trader analyses the available data, devises formulae, and lists the most optimal patterns of behaviour for the crew to follow in every potential situation. The officers just nod in confusion. They mix up terms and argue with each other as they clear out of the medicae deck, leaving the Rogue Trader alone with the doctors.

e8a4a553-249d-46ff-b1ce-f12d7ae889ca.Text: The Lord Captain falls onto the bed in exhaustion, letting everyone know that {mf|he|she} has used up all {mf|his|her} strength. The medics react instantly by sending the puzzled officers out of the room. Once outside the door, they wander off toward their respective stations and into uncertainty.

f2e0ec90-e833-4c81-ab9d-ebc41378f8c0.Text: The Lord Captain spends some time in bed, in the doctors' meticulous care. Out there somewhere, beyond the bulkheads of the blinded and deafened ship, people who have been left without their leader are fighting against an unknown threat. New victims are constantly being brought to the medicae deck. The servo-skull records medics carrying in a young man, the right side of his body a mess of flesh and bone. Then a young woman with her jaw missing and her ribs bared... as if realising the pointlessness of {mf|his|her} stay here, the Lord Captain demands to be patched up and helped to {mf|his|her} feet.

eea075ed-d067-4c5f-9910-a04ae72af1ab.Text: The officer salutes and hurries over to the bridge vox-system, to the Vox Master, who is leaning over her station. Moments later, a cry of surprise: "Lord Captain, our transmissions are being distorted as we speak! 'Depressurise the lower bays,' 'Execute adepts of the Machine Cult,' 'Disable the life support systems'... If even one command gets out..."

b6c1c21c-a808-47d8-9756-7708e4c3d31f.Text: The Rogue Trader rips the power key off the Tech-Priest's mechadendrite and opens the cover on the terminal. Sparks fly into {mf|his|her} face, but {mf|he|she} is confident in {mf|his|her} manipulation of the tangled wires and clanging levers. After replacing the cover and ensuring that the system is restored, the Lord Captain brings up the required data on the screens.

157bb3bb-c888-4a11-bb25-e53e1fa933bf.Text: Through the wheezes and coughs, the Lord Captain begins to quote numerous codices, whose commandments must be followed by every man, woman, and child in the Imperium. {mf|His|Her} solemn words are filled with a call to fulfil their sacred duty — to the bitter end.

bad66503-77a1-44ff-860b-dd3f21b6630c.Text: The voidborn officer appears before the Lord Captain once more. "Whatever it is that's attacking us, we have a backup procedure that can circumvent the vox-barrier! In the atrium leading to the bridge, there is a terminal for an isolated system that might still be unaffe—"

47faecaa-9a82-4b8c-83a1-c2900d40a59d.Text: The Lord Captain, buried under a mound of catheters, props {mf|himself|herself} up and, taking breaths through a mask now and then, begins to speak of human tenacity, of the trials that the crew have already overcome and those that still lie ahead in their struggle to save the ship.

28206251-4797-490d-a56d-8c6d1332b1c6.Text: One of the officers, scorning the order, steps away from his station... and drops to the deck as a shot rings out. "You have your orders!" Abelard Werserian, the Lord Captain's Seneschal, roars loud enough for the people to come to their senses — the vox-clerics and officers lean over the cogitators. When the doors are broken open and come crashing down, the survivors hobble toward the exit, but the majority of the crew will never leave their posts again. The last to leave, supported by Abelard, is the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself}.

fa97a020-324f-4b81-b255-9cd30b2e250b.Text: Some of the lunatics quiet down, others try to snap out of it — one pins her hand to a panel with a dagger to stop herself from moving, another fervently whispers prayers. Some return to the cogitators, others lean over the wounded. Shots ring out — those still on a rampage are executed by the Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself}, as promised.

e0c79a83-f4d7-477e-8d00-22a72457723f.Text: As soon as the Lord Captain picks up the vox, Idira grabs {mf|his|her} hand. Her eyes are wide, staring off into space.

d86deeca-6454-4ed0-87a3-226a322d3057.Text: As soon as the Lord Captain takes a couple of steps, Idira grabs {mf|his|her} sleeve. Her eyes are wide, staring off into space.

86bfa1f8-2b87-44f1-9ad1-0f39359548a6.Text: "Darkness! Darkness is waiting in the lower bays... the darkness is lying! It beckons, it promises truth, but instead of truth — it's all pain, and suffering, and fear!" Idira continues to speak in a hushed voice, trying to persuade the Lord Captain not to believe the mad cogitator possessed by something foreign and malicious. The Lord Captain...

0c5b8987-36fa-47f6-aade-267e7be359d4.Text: Having entrusted {mf|his|her} loyal officers with handling the remaining problems, the Lord Captain heads to {mf|his|her} rightful station — the bridge.

6d47d77f-6288-4cf6-8321-96810150cd9f.Text: The Lord Captain glances down the dark passageway, seemingly coming to some realisation — and turns back. The long journey to the lower decks has turned out to be a trap set by a system that has gone haywire, and a pointless waste of precious time.

dbf3eff9-39d6-47a3-a1b6-850404c24490.Text: The Rogue Trader personally oversees the evacuation. "Bring the plasma cutters!" "Get the wounded to the exit!" The officers repeat {mf|his|her} orders. When the servo-skull following the Rogue Trader reaches the doors, they fall to the plasma cutters and crumble outward. The Rogue Trader is the last to leave the bridge.

56ca19e9-eee6-4c6a-9bca-42ed1b75bd17.Text: The machine sparks, and the Vox Master throws her head back frenziedly. Blood criss-crosses her face and implants, and her body shudders from the electric impulses. A voidborn officer pulls out a dagger, cuts the cables connected to the station, and sweeps the Vox Master's limp body into his arms.

940a6ee3-8ffe-4fc0-974d-da4abe4ee831.Text: The officers, their lungs full of gas, do not have the strength to stand up even to escape the death trap. Shapes dart back and forth in the dark while clashing voices give commands to tear through the doors with plasma cutters. When the way clears and the survivors leave the trap, they leave dozens of dead bodies behind them.

07ef2132-35b1-4eb2-956f-f4e9a87f4896.Text: Heedless to the gas spreading over the deck, the officers continue their flurry of work at their stations, executing the orders issued by the Lord Captain. Even when the doors to the bridge are opened, the crew carries on for as long as they can. Last to leave the bridge, the Lord Captain runs out, coughing heavily.

cb67274d-8079-41e2-aa34-615363abdd8e.Text: The Rogue Trader contacts several officers via the vox-terminal and orders them to deal with the most critical situation on the ship at once.

25921ab9-8318-4de8-8292-e9160df15063.Text: ...send officers to the compartment where the situation is critical.

91112370-2301-438d-8586-6bc4422450f7.Text: The Rogue Trader rushes to the elevators and goes down to the lower decks, the pict frame juddering from the servo-skull's swift flight. Suddenly, the recording is heavily distorted — noise appears on the screen, and the pict rocks back and forth. The device hits a protruding beam, and the picture shatters into dozens of small pieces:

50574cb5-e8ed-4656-984a-5be34626e313.Text: "Warning! Invalid system pressure parameters! Expected value: 10."

761de32a-a657-4d5f-ba88-5e23b44874ab.Text: "Invalid value. Restoring settings to initial values. Expected value: 10."

929a0a88-01b6-40c0-8038-6100aac42ffe.Text: All signs indicate that the mechanical monster is dead.

ebc3153b-f847-4009-9283-91caba9a88ba.Text: The empty shell of a Daemon Engine. It was this creation — a horrifying mix of realspace technologies and the deranged powers of the warp — that disrupted the ship's systems and twisted the Tech-Priests' minds.

12c41257-47d2-4c97-8a85-ce1c7e82b5b3.Text: "Emperor protect us... this is a house of darkness and corruption!"

747016e7-12a8-4305-bf56-62f204fc2c9f.Text: "This is bad, very bad... The Omnissiah's grace has forsaken this place and these brethren..."

e9c7dd77-9077-4ad8-931e-d96998f2224d.Text: "How dare you disturb the peace of the machines! Desecrator!"

c701d502-67fc-42bf-94a2-08f1dcb8e03e.Text: "Death to the malefactors! Death to the desecrators!"

ecfa17b0-5e31-4293-8a74-b9604c9466bc.Text: "Flawed, weak fleshbags — you have tainted the abode of machine spirits!"

a69342c4-4aba-4b61-8c20-42a2c97e9717.Text: The priest's eyes are completely empty — they are looking through you without seeing you.

95b4e7a5-8cbc-4247-8f15-9aabac14842e.Text: The priest is mumbling an incoherent series of terms and designations.

b8bca5a5-21be-4107-b44c-df5e0da8923f.Text: "I confess my wrongs, I renounce the weaknesses of the flesh, I offer my prayer to the Machine, so that I may stand boldly before your image, O Omnissiah!"

963ecf29-6b51-4673-80fe-6e9e873381d4.Text: "O Machine God! Deliver me from the oppression of the flesh, let me draw closer to the perfection of a mechanism."

2136ada3-23bf-4abd-9e4a-642e1a116bf4.Text: "Who's there? Who's talking to me? O machine spirits, is it you I'm hearing?"

fafd6756-a251-440d-aab9-712aca588f06.Text: Your imagination is playing tricks on you, making you see faces twisted in a scream in the stains on the metal.

b9eb92c6-c7c0-4131-9bd5-e0fcc595b77e.Text: The metal feels a little warm and somewhat moist to the touch, remarkably similar to living skin.

3f34efcb-e4e7-4d5c-bc5c-d86f176cef07.Text: Dark reddish blotches form the words: "O Omnissiah! The hour is upon us!"

9e59251b-0362-4ab4-acf0-a366404afff7.Text: [Disable the gas supply to the compressor hall]

5771cb30-f73f-4d06-b1ca-3d19ab7501d0.Text: One of many modules providing power to the massive ship.

a9ea42a3-2002-43f7-8adf-afe21a86cd42.Text: The odd behaviour of the transformers must have been caused by some malfunction. You are unable to identify its source.

10c86196-4c60-4c4f-9a25-39cd7ac1a3dc.Text: The behaviour of the transformers was caused by no common mechanical malfunction. It is possible that the cause is of supernatural origin.

e2eeb172-474a-459e-b1f9-649283066ffb.Text: The dull sounds produced by the ventilation system create the illusion that the ship is breathing — like a living and terribly sick creature.

7075eff0-2d83-440c-bf49-d598c3de522d.Text: Inspection reveals nothing — perhaps the strange vision was a mere trick of the mind.

73bfe30c-8c64-4bb3-82a4-fc28682219dd.Text: There are noticeable signs of warp activity here. The bloody spectacle you witnessed may have been a simple illusion or a vision of the past or future.

bd78c098-0f40-4c59-bb48-613b4ccb568b.Text: Judging by the nail scratches on the walls, someone tried to claw their way through the cover of the oxygen system.

04c544c1-e5bc-4dce-8a6a-70f5efd6d425.Text: The stomach-turning bloody smears on the wall form a malevolent symbol. The blood seems to have penetrated deep into the metal.

50e9880c-2c9a-456c-8fb0-75e9ae9172d4.Text: Scraps of skin and broken nails and teeth are stuck in the ragged grooves on the bulkhead — someone made a frenzied attempt to scratch the blasphemous symbol into the metal, showing themselves no mercy.

aeec9f41-e92c-402e-9889-90a306c50117.Text: "From the weakness of the mind, Omnissiah save us!"

e195b344-cae8-46ae-a4c7-b17d4700291e.Text: "From the lies of the Antipath, circuit preserve us!"

64c54ea8-0376-41ce-bb56-e666de9761ce.Text: "From the rage of the Beast, iron protect us!"

3123f29a-2f35-4702-9d84-2708ac30ac70.Text: "From the temptations of the Flesh, silica cleanse us!"

4a58cf43-d814-487b-ad01-4d76b2c004f4.Text: "From this rotting cage of biomatter, Machine God set us free!"

fc49199d-7447-48f9-ba33-d44c2ef54669.Text: "Tech-comrade, you are in need of a ritual protocol of repair. We will mend you."

f7c83e06-6cae-4b71-83cc-a5d9f7da0211.Text: The priest is busy attempting to sew together the innards sticking out of his abdominal wound and the flexible wire emerging from the depths of the bulkhead.

da763265-07fd-4e55-8e32-345fd169ae80.Text: Clutching the soldering iron in his left hand, the priest casually solders the contacts on the implant in his right hand to the panel.

1f83c1a1-af73-4adf-9aee-ce8f0a579676.Text: Clutching the soldering iron in his left hand, the priest casually solders the contacts on the implant in his right hand to the panel.

3ce1572a-0158-4865-9723-a9cfaa84261b.Text: The priest is busy attempting to sew together the innards sticking out of his abdominal wound and the flexible wire emerging from the depths of the bulkhead.

aef02cec-7d82-48d8-8d27-3bb0a8447668.Text: This Tech-Priest can barely stand. From the many wounds where pieces of flesh used to be, blood mixed with oil is seeping out.

1a5483b5-785e-4491-bc01-a6ff58bab7a1.Text: Whispering words of prayer, the priest is engaged in self-mutilation, carving sinister symbols.

58f3f7eb-8b5b-43a9-9234-04ed9aefe6f0.Text: The priest, whose body is covered in symbols carved into metal and flesh, is whispering words of prayer.

24a02e53-10b0-4cf7-afbb-7d29a7dd10cb.Text: "Accursed flesh, you betray me, I am drowning in the mire of flesh and sinew, but my spirit longs for the perfection of the Machine!"

07436262-f92d-473e-997e-9a83097922d8.Text: "Accursed flesh, you betray me, I am drowning in the mire of flesh and sinew, but my spirit longs for the perfection of the Machine!"

7764e8e0-07f3-4d08-b2d6-722f93664e59.Text: {n}A formidable-looking door blocks the way into the next module. It is covered in scratches, as if someone clawed at the cold metal for a very, very long time. The door does not respond to your touch and stands fast, refusing to open. The writing above the doorway reads, "Main Computing Cathedral."{/n}

05a3a27a-6794-4936-b6c4-ea13e2622758.Text: {n}The main thing that catches your eye about this place is the state of the wall panels by the door. They bear numerous scratches, five in a row, resembling claw marks. Some of the panels look like they could fall off at any moment; here and there you see the occasional sparks and crackling of the damaged wires behind them.{/n}

da10e3ec-a2d4-44a7-98d7-178a634ef597.Text: "The sacred metal that bars our path is weakened. Let us appeal to the machine spirit of one of the generators so the metal may drink from its blessed energies. There should be one hidden somewhere in this module."

d04fe2b5-49ba-4db2-94f4-d3e7f073468a.Text: "My True Flesh resonates with the machines in this abode. Their pain and madness interfere with the workings of my cranial circuitry and cyber-mantle. Suboptimal, but surmountable."

f3230ecf-2157-46f7-8ba5-13ebc4834f27.Text: {n}The door and the entire adjacent section of the bay have no power. There must be a backup generator somewhere nearby. Once you turn it on, you should be able to proceed.{/n}

9e18f6cd-8e1b-49bb-bf32-b1e81c8ed76f.Text: {n}The intricate mechanism does not reveal its secrets to you — whatever is keeping the door shut, be it perverted sorcery or a simple breakdown, you cannot be certain.{/n}

9ab3822d-095c-4176-8814-1dd1d8f6cab0.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest blesses himself with a protective symbol, his hand visibly shaking.{/n} "Shield us, O Machine God, from the evil that has taken hold of your temple. Save us, preserve us from the corruption, show us the way..."

923e65a1-1946-4794-a91d-3807103344ca.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest says nothing for a while. Then his vox comes to life, but the voice is hoarse, punctuated by static and interference.{/n} "The Omnissiah knows all, comprehends all. I am merely His servant; I cannot discern what has stricken the abode of the Machine God. But I do sense a distortion of the structure, disfigurement of the molecular order. This ship is sick."

6fe43e76-0b29-471f-94fc-6f89a017cd98.Text: {n}This door is definitely powered by the generator you turned on. But the power circuit is broken — it must be restored in order to open the door.{/n}

7fe03d1e-1f0c-489e-945e-92a8844912b1.Text: "Further conversing is unproductive. The will of the Omnissiah has brought us to these doors, thus our task is clear — search for a way to proceed beyond so we can discover a means of cleansing these halls."

13ae8dc2-03c7-4e91-a8fa-87aee168038c.Text: "An offering will appease the machine, but take heed — the metal of this place harbours something sinister."

6454f4a1-4026-45b2-ac8d-83528eed83ef.Text: "I brought peace to Kiava Gamma. Rest in the knowledge that the wicked have been punished, and you and your brethren have been avenged."

d110a602-47b0-4c69-82b0-c73025446778.Text: [Kill the man] "What did you call yourself? A sacred filter? I cannot resist — I'm dying to see what a rupture in the filtration system looks like."

b29b0bbe-24e9-46f5-a599-b89e205dcf70.Text: "You've been consumed by madness. Or worse — Chaos sorcery. If you don't come to your senses, your fate is sealed. Snap out of it and speak clearly — what happened here?"

d8a01b04-62eb-4bd9-9cbe-e7095c973ef1.Text: "I have changed my mind. I will make no deals with something as hideous as you."

f035683b-d03e-411e-b6e2-ae1d8e56bb19.Text: [Kill the man] "I've seen and heard enough."

c7c36c23-5bd8-4d0a-8f2c-169181694e49.Text: "I will not agree to that. I still need my ship. However, I am willing to grant you Deck Theta 5 and the several hundred crew on it."

dc431742-7e0a-41d2-8834-989685cf57e0.Text: "After giving it some thought, I have realised that this was a dreadful idea. I think I shall kill you as a precaution."

5e918885-f01f-4c7f-9d38-d3161b3c1dc8.Text: "Rest in peace. You will be avenged."

ce443ac1-dca9-4468-9e69-0074efddbcd5.Text: "You have succumbed to Chaos and paid for your weakness."

9f9804ab-a6b5-4fb0-96e2-37c1feb141ac.Text: "The symbols your brethren 'protect' themselves with are symbols of Chaos."

4db38129-f305-4768-a447-a9cd05f43c52.Text: "Wake up! All the signs are clear as day. You and your brethren have fallen prey to the forces of Chaos, and you don't even realise it."

e6cb6fd5-e2bc-47ca-a1c4-ae9de394dba8.Text: "Kiava Gamma? Is that where your ship is from?"

34f70719-2bca-4ff3-be2e-7baa84b22fc6.Text: "Either you will rein in your appetites and go where I command, or I will splatter your 'baleful insides' all over the filthy bulkheads of this room."

a63b5ac3-d072-462c-b005-8e84a9e80578.Text: [Force the entity to become your servant on the ship]

682206ce-3deb-4e65-92e0-85408252e88a.Text: "Kiava Gamma was restored to its rightful owner — me."

53a252e6-62b8-4b01-8187-ea741cb0ab84.Text: "Even looking at this creature unnerves me. Magos, speak with your brother, find out what happened here."

2d72fa76-4daa-42a0-95e1-01a4979c8f24.Text: Made the corrupted Tech-Priest see the true nature of the powers that had taken hold of him.

f383a224-8df6-4b79-921c-a5245e3c845a.Text: "There is no fate more honourable than purgation through suffering in the name of faith. But you were deceived, servant of the Omnissiah! Your torment is not holding back the corruption — it is sustaining it. It is not too late to expel this blight!"

af2e8fbf-f001-4871-8924-2d7ad39bb726.Text: Killed the corrupted Tech-Priest to draw out the entity invading the vessel.

4f198123-14a1-4c6c-b021-d50c400f7a16.Text: [Kill him] "I am not interested in you. I wish to see what you have been trying to hold back!"

cd5118cc-36f4-484b-93ff-9d3c5da2e4ff.Text: "Swear loyalty to me, and I shall take you to my ship where you will be able to amuse yourself to your heart's content."

6fc50feb-9bf1-4c14-9119-6d707d40487c.Text: "You may be fearsome, but I have seen worse. I am far more curious about your potential. I believe we may be of use to each other."

7f6056a0-7a2b-48dc-a487-e695c10d5e62.Text: {n}The air in the room is permeated by a wild mixture of miasmas of both mechanical and biological origin. Blood, rust, vomit, machine oil, excrement, kerosene — all these smells blend together into such a thick stench that it almost feels palpable.{/n}

f457f454-3b19-41fa-a435-9996d2968a92.Text: {n}Just as the air here is one mad tangle of odours, the device in front of you is a mishmash of wriggling wires and transplanted fragments. In all the clutter, one could almost miss the main "component" — a heavily augmented man, whose upper body is embedded into the frame of the machine, dozens of wires piercing his flesh.{/n}

1ab3a0fa-7829-42cb-b12e-083691dc87e8.Text: {n}Yrliet's keen eyes are the first to make out the human being amidst the jumble of wires, and she stiffens in shock and disgust.{/n}

a18ee9c0-05da-40ba-b26a-b5e6bea2f5fb.Text: "A servant of the Omnissiah, an acolyte of the Machine, a prisoner of purgatory, and a keeper of corruption," {n}the man whispers via the implanted vox. Every word or motion causes his crippled body to shudder. Bloody foam glints from inside the wire-pierced wounds.{/n}

8ab22404-ed05-49ef-b583-8432a847ea88.Text: "We all know which evil we mean," {n}says Yrliet finally, recovering herself.{/n} "He is blind! He does not see that he has already let the darkness in, that it is here, all around us..."

85a953d2-85f6-4135-b8a2-4c40c9659fb3.Text: {n}The man's eyes clear for a moment. They still lack understanding, but there is a hint of surprise — he slowly looks around the room, at the ecstatic priests, at his own mangled body. His vox hisses, as if he is struggling to say something.{/n}

f6f1c75b-4a70-437c-bb6c-3fc7f6c0233f.Text: "You are not just ignorant. Your words are disdainful and dangerous. Could you be a servant of lies and deception? Could you have come to halt the work of the sacred filter?"

14d41f5b-e9b1-4382-85a8-ad8dff5d4b77.Text: {n}Suddenly, the mingled stench in the room is drowned out by the sharp, piercing smell of ozone and grease. You sense that the nauseating atmosphere that prevailed in the room has condensed into a single point of evil in the depths of the ship... and is now hurtling toward you.{/n}

cd5eb6c5-6d3e-4a5d-8a82-b5509446ce03.Text: {n}The man's mutilated body is wracked by wave after wave of convulsions.{/n} "Evil... that was evil incarnate... evil, the corruption that watches us day and night..."

c7c38df7-897d-459e-83fa-7b6a230951ad.Text: {n}Suddenly, the man raises his head and looks you straight in the eye.{/n} "You have banished the evil... you tried to warn me, but I was deaf... the ship... Kiava Gamma... it followed us from there..."

0dca2fbb-f6f7-4efd-b0af-8661b2bae91b.Text: "I was a part of the great force that drives the universe. I do not fear... the cold of death." {n}A wheezing breath escapes the man's chest, then his eyes close.{/n}

76b553d6-290a-4b2f-b620-dbb057fc5550.Text: {n}A crust of congealed blood and other bodily fluids covers the man's entire body, but his eyes are open and his gaze is keen. This gaze is turned to you, devoid of surprise or deference.{/n} "Who are you, disturbing the peace of holy martyrs in the home of our grief? What do you want?"

85ef1890-0fdb-490b-8f47-122bc5eb5789.Text: "Ship? There is no ship. There is only purgatory, a world of evil, made to harrow and torture those who follow the Omnissiah. It has already killed many of my brethren... but those who remain are strong, so very strong. We will keep the corruption of the Machine at bay. I will! I will hold it back."

03019712-b7ee-47c5-87e7-8ec7dac94f16.Text: "I have accepted a higher calling, the only one among my brethren to do so. As they keep the evil at bay with prayers and sacred symbols engraved on their traitorous flesh, I take this evil inside myself. I imbibe it as one does water! But it can do me no harm, for I am the eye of sanctity. I am the sacred filter, the link that protects other parts of the Machine from this caustic taint. And for as long as I remain here, the corruption will not prevail!"

5e50bbc3-745d-42eb-bdba-7b1130a1b034.Text: {n}Heinrix pierces you with an icy glare.{/n} "{name}, need I explain that you are skirting a very narrow edge right now?"

177a98b3-6df0-4cd0-be52-326914b065f1.Text: {n}Argenta clutches her weapon so hard you hear her knuckles crack.{/n} "{name}. Don't."

afb876c1-a937-41b0-8b35-6c13eedc3989.Text: {n}You can barely make out Pasqal's agitated voice over the angry crackle of interference.{/n} "I am registering that contact with a corrupting entity is tech-heresy beyond categorisation."

d0874412-0ce1-4c45-a749-8a40ada0c137.Text: {n}Idira looks the man over with an expression of disgust and fear.{/n} "I've seen similar symbols. Caught a glimpse of them. In my dreams. Whenever the warp wormed its way into them and whispered about its virulent gifts. I doubt these lunatics were given visions of these runes by their god."

5c0a2e83-f9c0-45c9-82b2-a3dce0eac098.Text: "This statement is false! I am registering corruption in this unit identical to that surrounding us. I am registering a violation of the cleansing protocol, which dictates steering the ship into the heart of the nearest star for the purposes of cleansing annihilation! I am registering betrayal of the sacred machine spirits placed in the charge of those weak in faith."

f3eabb80-ca47-4fca-91eb-9d8d44e7a5e4.Text: "How dare you encroach upon the sacred essence of the Machine! How..."

51f790f0-a2cf-45ba-8409-c3ae949e7a2e.Text: {n}The shaking intensifies, the breathing grows ragged, heralding the beginning of the end.{/n}

30bf8a55-44c6-4c14-99dc-324febd37579.Text: {n}A tear appears at the corner of his eye, he thrashes frantically in the mess of wires piercing his body.{/n} "We fought. We cut off one module after another, as one cuts away rotting flesh. But it followed. Its invisible influence, the corruption it exuded — it claimed us, one by one. The crew were merely humans of flesh and blood, they were so weak, they succumbed so easily... We could not save them from evil, and so we gave the ship to the darkness among the stars."

da92edf8-8eb0-4a9f-adaf-c8c4ba8e049f.Text: "Your knowledge is lacking, invader. Those are secret holy symbols, imparted to us by the Omnissiah. How else would my tech-comrades have survived, if not for their protection? So many of us were devoured by evil..." {n}He falls silent, as if lost in thought.{/n}

dc18265e-ac97-46dc-8f28-811ffcae7e58.Text: "The great evil that pervades the universe, tempting with the unattainable, seducing with false Knowledge. Evil has many names, but its essence remains the same. It was that evil that trapped us in here! But we were stronger."

381c5f14-c895-47d6-909a-edd2a2c78764.Text: "But the darkness came for us too. In this last module, where we intended to make our last stand. Then I... sacrificed myself... I became a filter, a stopper against the corruption emanating from the machine. I succumbed... The corruption came for our souls. The corruption of Kiava Gamma... traitors..." {n}With the last of his efforts, he rasps,{/n} "The Fabricator-Censor! It all started with him! He was the one who let this taint into the sacred code! He was the one who doomed our brethren! He was the one who spawned the steel monstrosities in the furnace of our planet!"

3f7771ef-25af-4bdd-be81-a20aac326c19.Text: "Yes..." {n}the man whispers.{/n} "The ship... and the planet... the traitors among our brethren, tormenting the sacred mechanisms, letting corruption into their systems. They turned that which is holy into the unholy! And they set these new, twisted machines on us, their tech-comrades! We managed to flee, but one of the monsters found its way onto the ship."

59d07ef0-39bb-4940-8a3d-af0f11df3fed.Text: "Weakness... The flesh is weak... The spirit must be stronger... The spirit reaches out to the Machine... to..." {n}The madman's whispers gradually turn into wheezing, then stop.{/n}

fa5e53f1-4054-4857-8bf8-58874051dd97.Text: {n}The beast lets out a vicious roar that turns into the ear-splitting screech of a broken vox — and then it attacks.{/n}

f82d0ced-72c8-443a-8a65-4d7de707fcf0.Text: {n}A scraping sound erupts from the beast — a sickening semblance of a laugh.{/n} "Your word-excrement caresses the furnace of my baleful insides! Give me a new shell where I will play with meat-puppets! Give it to me! I want all of it, all of your shell, all of it!"

44d81e4e-1058-46ac-ab07-e7a6dd6fc2b9.Text: "How outrageously exhilarating! You are the first meat-toy to offer itself to me to play with. Go ahead, spew sounds out of your speech-vent! Amuse me! Amuse me!"

c382c3d1-abbb-4382-8bb7-191dadaf5907.Text: "Fierce, fierce flesh-bag! Billowglut wants no quarrel with you, I want your new toys, I want them, I want them! I will grant you my flaming boon if you keep your part of the bargain! Take me, take me to my new shell!" {n}With a shriek of anticipation, the beast stomps off.{/n}

7c779c94-4785-446e-9f88-f62ba553efdf.Text: "Foul, foul flesh-bag! Then I will take your shell from you and listen to your slimy form squelch and slosh under my feet!"

e79e8cd0-383d-42d8-a738-d02f28e0b3be.Text: {n}You mentally order the entity to leave the vessel, stow away on the shuttle, and, as soon as the shuttle returns to your ship, infiltrate the ship's systems. The daemon responsible for the desecration of the dead or deranged crew will now faithfully serve you.{/n}

8c5415d4-4e12-4e33-825a-2648e7943b75.Text: "Very well, flesh-bag. Billowglut accepts your conditions! I will grant you my flaming boon if you keep your part of the bargain! Take me, take me to my new shell!" {n}With a shriek of anticipation, the beast stomps off.{/n}

f581c50d-329e-4858-bd93-a92c79e8143d.Text: "The mon-keigh has decided to harness the spawn of the Dark Gods? What hopeless stupidity!" {n}Yrliet clutches her spirit stone and takes half a step back.{/n}

5caf8efc-9d53-416d-bb37-bf7265d95769.Text: {n}The man looks at his comrade and replies with a long series of clicks in Techna-Lingua.{/n}

7e97eb4e-254e-4ae6-abcd-01971ee8e6e6.Text: "Permission to use the sacred language has been revoked. Impurity will not be permitted to enter the pure speech of binharic. Your mortal shell will soon exhaust its vital energies. Pray mutely while you still have the time."

9e1346ea-ed6f-453b-8de2-747a94e3c56f.Text: {n}A glimmer of awareness — and joy — shines in the madman's eyes.{/n}

0396ead9-2684-4996-8842-cc32e00a4804.Text: {n}After a brief exchange of binharic greetings, the Tech-Priest's vox barks out:{/n} "You have been identified and recognised, tech-sentinel. I express my sympathy for your malfunctions, may the Omnissiah strengthen your data-vows. Requesting information about the status of the blessed ship."

9616accb-4114-4105-b672-d1562b72af23.Text: {n}As soon as he stills forever, the oppressive atmosphere around you deepens into literal darkness. One by one, flaming slits begin to appear in the gloom — perhaps eyes, perhaps mouths, ready to devour the mortal who has laid claim to it. A foreign, otherworldly will rails against you — and crumbles when confronted by the forces that keep you safe in the service of the Dark Gods.{/n}

eed36141-1835-4039-be4e-6d96067e41be.Text: "Know me as Billowglut! I had been toying with these preposterous leather-puppets until you broke them all. Flesh! Loathsome flesh! I tried, I tried to reshape them in my image, make them scrape that revolting matter off their frames and become one with my new shell. But you ruined them all! Ruined them with your blood-leaking grab-slivers!"

e47edf47-8191-4abf-9612-b970d778d523.Text: "Glory to the deliverer! Glory to the Imperium!"

30fea07e-58ec-4fc6-afef-4ddfc7b9b485.Text: "I made it! Aha ha ha, I made it!"

524f71de-8349-4589-8aac-0fc38c31faa6.Text: "And... this is it? How long will we have to wait?"

429464f9-c5b1-4ea0-9a7b-7fda751beadf.Text: "Wait? All right, we'll wait. Just do it before we're all dead..."

f6ea490d-c94c-4be7-bc87-12ad190320de.Text: "Look at it! Where did they get all this stuff?"

3a2d6189-03df-4bc4-95cd-cc274aa4a48d.Text: "Who are they? Have the Dark Ones found the governor at last?"

5d1708d0-94a1-42f5-985a-0971d6430331.Text: The bodies have been twisted into a pose resembling a servile bow and bound with barbed wire.

3ae3f130-837f-4eb6-b458-fe06c2859e10.Text: The places where the sharp edges have bitten into the skin are covered in blood — these people were bound before they died.

b98ce27b-43c2-4db6-b2c8-8eb92a4854d7.Text: The man's body is frozen in an unnatural pose. The corpse's fingers are crooked and its teeth are bared in a ghastly grimace.

952c711b-9c9a-4481-82b3-aeb4ffdd2ca2.Text: This man clawed at his throat right before he died.

310c3055-6d89-48d1-a9a9-609fb4944675.Text: You can clearly see several thin cuts left by bladed weapons on the body.

7d7e0f55-0824-4025-b747-a6b8ff2c0310.Text: The man nailed to the Aquila is long dead. The body is sagging and looks shapeless, almost like a rag doll.

4d975f6e-8210-48d9-995f-893ce61ce9f3.Text: The man nailed to the Aquila is completely broken, as if somebody shoved him into a stone crusher. Judging by the edges of his wounds and the amount of blood, the nails and hooks were driven into his flesh when he was still alive.

c2346d71-9fff-4bab-bdb4-6e9efb788e76.Text: "I'm bored of this farce, Tazarra. Who rules this arena, you or the mon-keigh?"

4aef1d7f-d4f1-4a2c-88aa-5adcd85381be.Text: "Dracon Marazhai, you know the danger of repeating this... misunderstanding. Draw your own conclusions."

03c93417-4c5d-4d8a-a886-6c665ee2202c.Text: "Your word is our command, Archon Yremeryss."

c6b0ff3e-4ac8-4ad3-a9f9-efd5c52f6485.Text: A jagged symbol daubed in some dark substance.

bdde0c07-b55b-4003-a016-6b5f35849201.Text: The lines cross and twist together to form an elaborate symbol.

2cc52f77-81e7-4941-8b06-b866c5801ca7.Text: An ugly image clearly imbued with some hidden meaning.

93d21118-be3d-4d3f-86b6-33d1f45b4d5d.Text: The ground is marked by grooves, footprints, and several grisly stains.

6877ef42-3d9b-46e1-9759-24d693a1a2ad.Text: There are a few faint grooves in the ground — the trace of weapons grazing the dirt on a miscalculated swing.

210be7b8-4770-40b5-a18a-e2eced62abf2.Text: The body is missing parts of its extremities — it was hacked to pieces with dozens of strikes.

8ce72eac-c7fd-4706-805a-58981910e6e8.Text: The body was partially flayed, and judging by the amount of blood, the victim was still alive when it happened.

05d7f2f6-f6de-42c0-bca4-20951b2710d6.Text: The man died clutching his intestines as they spilt from his lacerated stomach.

e0261174-61ce-47c6-8546-946a04922db4.Text: A massive crusher designed to extract ore from rocks is covered with a thick layer of dust and rubble.

02b8deb5-3ed4-48dc-a7e0-ee36b9410e10.Text: The sacred engine meant to work in the quarry has not been used for a long time.

449034dc-fd44-4d82-9478-54ad7b7276dc.Text: The broken, slashed, and gutted body is still covered with the shreds of a planetary warden uniform.

71e211b1-46df-4fde-ba09-78ba12199e52.Text: The caustic ooze gives off a sickening vapour that eats away at the lining of your nose and mouth, making your eyes water.

8663f129-b6d7-4195-b72c-d0425bc88922.Text: "They're gone! Throne as my witness, we will find these blasphemous wretches and make them pay for everything that happened here!"

d68f2f1e-0980-449b-b94a-e17af251e48e.Text: "Looks like the xenos gave up on this world after you spoiled their fun."

012c454f-6e30-41f2-abff-87b85f968758.Text: "They fled... Judging by the garb of these xenos, they are not like the ones you killed before — must have been their leaders."

607d3d74-4a16-41ab-b01b-300a2b743d94.Text: "There is no doubt the Dark Ones left satisfied — we treated them to an exquisite feast of pain and misery."

16ded739-c9c7-4e06-ad6a-aa811e879f5a.Text: "The sign of Hecataria, a Wych Cult from the depths of Commorragh. Tread carefully, {name} — their footsteps make no sound and their blades strike faster than lightning."

3b10c28b-4cb5-40dd-b7ae-d686ff6d7ae9.Text: "The symbol of torment — this is how the Dark Ones mark the arenas that serve to nourish their withered souls."

94dd1caa-c24d-4b9f-99f6-ef67409defba.Text: "I do not recognise this symbol... It may be the sigil of a Kabal — a constellation of killers marking out their hunting ground."

560999b5-98f9-42e3-99ce-95bf1bfbc0c0.Text: Decided to finish off the surviving convicts on Vheabos VI.

aa548409-fda8-446b-94ed-864e4e35a127.Text: [Attack] "Why have you stopped? We aren't done with you yet!"

ed388cef-de17-4c1c-9964-1090e5773c39.Text: Decided to evacuate all survivors from Vheabos VI.

62bdef78-8582-4d31-bfd7-1010d6837806.Text: "Those who fought with me, get to the shuttle. As soon as we are away from here, I will give orders for the immediate evacuation of the remaining survivors."

e3f751ac-cae9-4177-a991-5a2ed5154ead.Text: "Stay on the planet with everyone else and wait until I decide what to do with you. I do not have time for this now."

58f116ea-994f-4f48-ac97-aad419c8b955.Text: Decided to evacuate some of the survivors from Vheabos VI and servitorise the rest.

26dfd937-5e8c-4f4e-8585-9f246170b144.Text: "By destroying these foul xenos, you have atoned for your transgressions against the Emperor — get to the shuttle. The rest of you will be subject to selective punitive servitorisation so that you may further toil for the good of the Imperium."

fb4a9d9e-8765-4a35-980a-0f871c78f636.Text: {n}The surviving fighters turn their heads toward you one after another. All eyes on the battlefield are glued to you.{/n}

39cef099-36d0-46f0-a4d3-eefe8604b17a.Text: "Tell your Myrmyriss she's not going to like what she's about to see."

c95c572f-a514-4bf5-b99c-b3217b2b9c4b.Text: "It seems it is I who is in for a treat. I cannot even begin to fathom where my subjects found such an exotic beast — and a talking one at that!"

95c681d8-2e27-462d-9e00-c92f57553933.Text: [Raise your weapon] "How about we skip the small talk and get down to business?"

9c5958b7-0ae8-457a-9a45-8ddc529aefb9.Text: "I am a Rogue Trader, the Emperor's anointed, Guardian of Humanity — and your doom, xenos scum!"

5b1d7a16-f0b6-4aa3-ad06-03af61cd0645.Text: "You ravaged the planet. Wiped out millions of people. Made those who survived bend the knee... You will pay for this."

278073de-b9e9-4fde-9392-1a997a9dbda0.Text: "A small group of xenos who neutralised the planetary defences and managed to ruin an entire world... Impressive! How much would it cost to hire you?"

4411fb42-f3ed-4021-8c95-8c661b73c19f.Text: "I presume the toxic atmosphere is your doing?"

c368f8f1-19fb-4a93-9e60-094d62479bba.Text: Joined forces with the fighters on Vheabos VI by appealing to their sense of duty to the Emperor.

98eee0db-3758-4f8d-b366-29796d34b0ea.Text: [Address the fighters in the arena] "Dying to entertain xenos is a path to eternal shame and condemnation of souls touched by the Emperor's undying glory! Let us join our blades — we will destroy those who sought to kill you!"

2ba95edd-fdbb-424e-89dd-c0228c7eacd1.Text: [Address the fighters in the arena] "How could you stoop to this? To killing one another for the amusement of the enemies of Humanity?"

0ef119f2-1c47-41a7-9947-0a649cc6b060.Text: [Turn to the fighters in the arena] "Do you truly wish to die at the xenos' behest? If we join forces now, we can end this senseless carnage once and for all."

f5963295-abd9-42cb-ba77-ff8c7c11302c.Text: "By whose leave are you playing lord on my world?"

ec714c22-cdd4-48fd-82ea-f58845fdd779.Text: "Kneel, xenos, or I shall have you flogged."

856d9d62-3c85-4534-8ad0-42fd06b3ca8f.Text: [Beckon your cyber-eagle] "{petname}, take a look at these traitors. Let the Emperor see their erring souls through your eyes."

02624a2e-913a-4992-8aee-fe25051d6331.Text: {n}The tall, lithe xenos moves with the grace of an otherworldly predator. The creature gives you a dispassionate glance and casually speaks a few words that are immediately picked up by your {g|Encyclopedia:Elucidator}Elucidator{/g}.{/n} "Mecandis, Aelith, what is this? Has one of the sisters found an amusing trinket in the ruins and saved it as a special treat for the Archon?" {n}The xenos takes a quick look over her shoulder toward the platform where a few more silhouettes in tar-black armour can be seen.{/n}

0e50de04-c94e-40f5-9747-0f8574038579.Text: {n}The xenos's eyes light up with interest.{/n} "The mon-keigh understands my speech! Where did you come by a device that can translate our language? Are you trying to impress me by appearing useful? Such words will earn you a bout in the ring at most. Without weapons, and, soon, without your skin."

b929e853-8d8f-4d92-8ef2-2dc635fba142.Text: "I hereby declare you a Category Three blasphemer for tampering with the sacred production cycle of this world's extractiums." {n}The drill on Pasqal's mechadendrite springs to life with a howling screech.{/n}

65a4d496-6890-4339-9c44-07cca8e069ac.Text: {n}Tazarra takes a step back just as the other fighters charge with furious howls.{/n}

08edf781-cc58-462f-a7bb-4e8a1b66c539.Text: {n}Tazarra emits a furious scream and takes a step back, signalling to her companions.{/n}

e7e03d0f-0b1a-41bd-8974-984966050404.Text: {n}The humans scattered around you on the platform stare as if they've seen a ghost. The eyes of some betray their fear, others glare with bestial hatred, and yet more look upon you with hope.{/n}

75a39047-b065-4e30-90a2-1302f1f07d9c.Text: "My name is known to everyone on this planet, mon-keigh. I am Tazarra the Deliverer, Tazarra the Benevolent, the one who grants respite from the choking grasp of this world. I decide who lives, who dies, and who finds new purpose for their existence in Commorragh's many arenas. Surely this is why you have come here? To fight for my ever-changing favour and for the privilege of being the first to be chained?"

f9e2551f-4c9c-4a83-ab47-080bb6595158.Text: "Cousin, what are you doing among this rabble? What an unexpected and tantalising surprise." {n}Tazarra licks her lips hungrily.{/n} "I cannot wait to take you in my arms and clasp you tightly to me!"

87929478-fb38-4583-9fd7-e27fa5107c33.Text: "Do not waste breath on your lies. Only the faint vestiges of blood connect the Asuryani and Dark Ones such as yourself."

4b9ce62e-95d7-4c8c-a383-7aeff8dd3f5e.Text: "To be reduced to a xenos's plaything... A shameful fate for the scions of Humankind." {n}Abelard falls silent, shaking his head in dismay.{/n}

e6be483f-0433-464c-8e34-7347aa50adfa.Text: "It could be. Or perhaps my mere presence is enough to make base creatures like yourselves forget how to breathe?" {n}Tazarra lets out a nasty chuckle.{/n} "Are you really surprised at what happened? You wove the net right under your own feet — we merely knocked out the pin that drew it closed tight around you. A couple of volleys at the seals on the underground well, and the planet, the one you had turned inside out, did the rest."

ccf44ac6-1668-4ab6-a4f9-9a6f5e47671b.Text: "Looks like the spectators grew bored when the performance hit a snag." {n}Heinrix reaches for his weapon.{/n}

11dfbfe7-8949-48f1-89fb-ada849ec13be.Text: "Oh, what passion! What naive arrogance! When all this turns into boundless despair and clinging terror, my guests and I will savour such exquisite pleasure. I would play with you myself, mon-keigh, but then the performance would be brief — and we don't want to upset my guests, now do we?"

eaeaf573-ac21-41d9-83e0-349da7fd29d2.Text: "Am I not paying for our mischief already? Am I not saving the worthiest among your kin, gifting them the right to die for the delight of my brothers and sisters? What kind of abhorrent ingratitude is this?"

20f598a0-3e1d-43d1-b2e0-25b5bdef78d7.Text: "The presumption. The stupidity. You have nothing that could satisfy me, mon-keigh."

fe8cd27b-5e43-4f37-9080-8c44ce69d7db.Text: {n}Tazarra raises her blade and points at you.{/n} "Tell the other mon-keigh that whoever slits your throat will depart for their new home ahead of schedule. And tell them to hold nothing back: tonight they dance for Yremeryss herself, the great Archon of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest!"

d7fb4aa5-e637-4bf4-858a-7b8017295c14.Text: {n}Exhausted and defeated faces trade worried glances. The hulking brute next to you hesitates, then spits and breaks into a grin.{/n} "We're going to die anyway, might as well do it without the heretic's brand! Slay the beasts!"

acc7984c-a223-4e1b-96a8-c0258d45d018.Text: {n}Exhausted and defeated faces trade worried glances — and tighten their grip on their weapons.{/n}

b6403032-2606-40d6-876d-4d29c7a75c22.Text: {n}A hulking brute who can barely stand coughs up blood and wipes his lips.{/n} "What, was I supposed to lie down and die? The ones who survive the arena, the xenos take them away — I saw humans boarding shuttles with my own eyes! They're going to take us away from here, you hear?"

1b198588-f782-4ea5-9e3f-8cf1a168dfdc.Text: "Yeah! Who gives a shit about us convicts? The lanky buggers may keep me on a leash, but at least I'll be alive, not coughing up my lungs!"

bb7bebbb-c69e-4e80-a870-f3706571824c.Text: {n}Yrliet chuckles haughtily.{/n} "Such grandiose names for a soulless wretch who tortures the breathless and torments the powerless. Your words hint at a nobility you have never possessed."

c708997e-689b-461f-a8a7-0e68aff4a659.Text: {n}You do not even notice the moment when you switch to the voice you used in your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}former life{/d} — the firm, uncompromising tone of a Commissar.{/n}

c05454e4-3d3a-44cc-8fa9-1ca290b8f41c.Text: {n}The Proctor's voice booms with denunciation:{/n} "Now you see why Arbitrators prefer to execute criminals immediately — because this is what they will do otherwise with the life they are offered. From the moment they fall into heresy, they hardly have the right to be called human anymore — all they can do from then on is sink deeper."

70523f8d-783c-40af-a5b0-a942d3ce511a.Text: {n}A loud bird call deafens everyone present. Like a living embodiment of the Imperium's Aquila, a two-headed eagle, its wings spread wide, swoops down on the fighters' heads. They recoil as the screeching bird sinks its talons into Tazarra's astounded face. With a furious scream, the xenos shakes the eagle off. Its claws have torn the skin of her face and damaged her eye.{/n}

86515ed4-3daa-42ec-8ee2-c407fb1daffd.Text: "How cruel you are to your unfortunate kin! These mon-keigh have worked hard to entertain their elite audience. Each of them fights with a strength born of desperation, seeking to earn their place in my box of toys. There is always room for more — my toys do break so very easily."

63d799ed-2998-4a9a-9c4b-2453657a4e63.Text: "And your brethren finished what the planet had started. Oh, how they strived to please me and my entourage! How they slaughtered and tortured their own kin for mine and my sisters' delight! How they decorated this little arena with still living mon-keigh! Did you think all that you see before you is the work of our hands? Think again."

43ece919-419c-4b33-ac9c-c738f7c8e49f.Text: "This statement is false. You were supposed to furnish yourself with a means of respiratory protection and inflict maximum damage on the perpetrators before ceasing your vital functions."

e125a478-e201-49b4-984d-38646c0f3eac.Text: {n}From the dusk behind Tazarra comes a cry. The distance between you and the xenos is too great for the Elucidator to interpret the words, but the tone alone speaks of irritation and impatience.{/n}

da85f54e-1a3a-40da-a95f-08cea1ae6609.Text: {n}Heinrix narrows his eyes and gives the xenos an appraising look.{/n} "The Drukhari of this breed are known as Wyches, {name}. They are experts at bloodletting in the arenas and on the battlefield. However, I am more interested in the ones skulking in shadows — judging by their armour, they are high-ranking representatives of a Kabal, a military clique from the Drukhari demesne.
