We hear the ship breathe, know what it is feeling and thinking. We are a part of the ship just like it is a part of us. We perform numerous functions, and there are many officers among our number. Some maintain order and prevent mutiny, others serve as shepherds and support the crew, and some devote themselves to mending the body and spirit of the vessel."

c41255db-e50e-44ce-9e41-d05aee94d31c.Text: "Lord Captain." {n}She offers an unusually deep bow, likely using it to mask her confusion.{/n}

f91984aa-1e8a-4b29-a6aa-5f11ebe5ebaa.Text: "We look, speak, and move differently from the inhabitants of the planetary worlds. Our way of life, traditions, and quirks frighten these people just like the darkness of the cosmos. Many believe us to be the bringers of ill fortune, and alas, it is the voidborn who get the blame for terrible warp phenomena during longer voyages."

de820e86-40af-40ef-9003-2f48df25c974.Text: {n}Interpreting the Vox Master's emotions based on half a face and a vox-modulated voice is no easy task, but you manage to catch the undercurrent in Vigdis's words. The Vox Master is not merely saddened by her rift with Idira, she is devastated by it.{/n}

55501d2f-32c8-4157-bb4b-081d2ca191df.Text: "I hope she will find the sense and clarity of mind to find her way out of the dark place she is in currently."

1bdb9c2c-3d6f-4b4d-928a-a9f5dc6961e6.Text: "Forgive me, Lord Captain. I have no information that would be of interest to you at this moment."

6bb02f49-f19c-49bf-be00-001bb980153e.Text: "Because we are the children born in the void between the stars, be it the womb of a travelling vessel, an orbital satellite, or a forgotten asteroid station. Low gravity, voyages through the warp, and the countless dangers of space travel — everything others hate and dread is second nature to us."

362095d0-87a1-45d7-8a28-1a91dfe976cd.Text: {n}You address the crew with a rousing speech and hear your voice roll through the ship, reaching even the normally quiet corners of the vessel. When the broadcast ends, you hear distant shouts of approval.{/n}

1ed3270e-028b-410a-93cc-ae3ee1a0b3e2.Text: "I offer my apologies, Lord Captain, but such matters lie in the purview of High Factotum Danrok. I am better versed in vox-communications than rare gifts."

cf4b9f8e-ec72-456e-a0c9-c7fee86a1f2a.Text: "Most of the voidborn are members of large voidship dynasties that bear responsibility for a certain aspect of the ship's life. For three hundred years, the main branch of the Toliman dynasty has produced the ship's Vox Masters. And most of our subordinates come from the cadet houses of the dynasty."

5c0bbc53-8393-414c-9902-3112d9813e64.Text: "Is there anything else you wish to know, Lord Captain?"

08227002-c7cf-4379-b4f3-17c1f19623a6.Text: "Right away, Lord Captain." {n}Vigdis connects a few wires from the back of her head to the main bridge's vox-system and closes her eyes.{/n} "An artefact of similar description was retrieved from Eurac V alongside the Lady Navigator's personal effects. However, no one knows its true value or purpose — after all, the refined tastes of the Navis Nobilite are far removed from a commoner's understanding."

5672a42c-f49e-4261-b8a9-ae84d3b9cf6a.Text: "He is feeling better, Lord Captain. The ship's chirurgeon was amazed at his resilience. The esteemed Lord Ulfar is currently convalescing in his chambers."

6182be8f-282b-4d11-adf9-44e393e26649.Text: {n}Vigdis hesitates before continuing.{/n} "Several years ago, an unfortunate warp jump caused all the food on board to spoil. Fifteen days later, a hungry and furious crew nearly massacred everyone on the lower decks, blaming us for the misfortune and hoping to restock the larders with our flesh. I would have been killed during the mutiny had Idira Tlass not shown up in the right place at the right time. She came to my rescue, and the scoundrels' fear of her was even greater than their fear of the voidborn."

c6bd1e52-9564-4633-a123-d608f3b4606a.Text: "Except Idira changed after one... incident, and we started to drift apart. The death of Lord Captain Theodora made her withdraw even more. I do not know if Idira considers me her friend now, but we used to be very, very close. It is good I can still look after her... in my own way."

5ffe23a5-f090-44b1-86f0-023c1e48fe4a.Text: "You may be interested to know that a group of officers was discussing a grim rumour over lunch. Word has it the apparition of Lord Captain Theodora has been sighted on board lately. Yes, you heard right. They say she is haunting the decks, dragging wayward crew members off into oblivion. Disquiet has spread throughout the ship, as the anomaly has been reported in different sections, sometimes entire kilometres apart."

89728b59-c014-4887-8769-c673e8171995.Text: {n}The Vox Master leans closer to you.{/n} "Master Heinrix van Calox expressed interest in our communication stations and vox-nets a short while ago. The Interrogator appears to be very well versed in the matters of sacred technology... And it worries me. A man of his knowledge and in his line of work is capable of discreetly planting his own devices in our systems. We will be vigilant, Lord Captain, but you should try to be more careful as well."

16254a08-daf0-41ab-bd84-a911fbcf2aa5.Text: "All of Lady Theodora's journeys could be considered unusual. Her odysseys were always audacious. As for the words you mentioned... None of them sounds familiar to me as far as I can tell."

22aa8ce6-da3d-49d4-9173-eba57ab392e8.Text: "Except maybe the 'incident'... I recall coming across this word in transmissions several times. I think it was repeated by the former Enginseer, the one who perished during Kunrad Voigtvir's uprising."

0c6757aa-e19a-413a-a0d2-cab0aa57d8c8.Text: "If you ever want to know what worries and concerns your crew are harbouring, what your subjects are whispering about in local networks after their watches, and what their leaders are clamouring about over shortwave vox-transmissions, just come and see me — I will satisfy your curiosity."

b0877e9f-b45e-4441-9bfe-b432ec03ea13.Text: "He was describing it as 'the Incident,' something quite remarkable. Apparently, at some point in the past, the entire ship was hit by a massive system failure. All systems stopped responding for one-fifth of a second. Most of the crew, including myself as I was likely on board at that time, did not notice anything strange. But Tech-Priests are sensitive to such things."

2720bdbf-7fb6-477d-aa58-3d0247be75bd.Text: "That is all I can tell you, Lord Captain. I wish I could help more."

73cf1d63-3e01-4ebe-9411-4d55aa899c45.Text: "Would Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} care to learn the circumstances of your return to the ship? I can assure you that the landing deck was damaged minimally. Mistress Heydari escorted you to your quarters, rather boldly touching the person of the Rogue Trader, and in response to the crew's attempts to help you, you endeavoured to demonstrate your proficiency in several Efreet swear words that, according to you, Mistress Heydari had taught you earlier."

8ea603c3-5977-494e-9682-e652ef3485d5.Text: "Regarding the incidents that took place on Footfall, Liege Tocara has already let us know that the persons affected have no claims against you and thank Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} for the honour of witnessing how the Rogue Trader and {mf|his|her} charming paramour amuse themselves."

2d693faf-96b5-40eb-88a5-8f58baddd697.Text: {n}The Vox Master is looking at you... differently. Even the static coming from the vox-speaker sounds especially loud and nervous today.{/n}

2d217625-9b0a-47c3-a906-fc1b07ce7985.Text: "Yes, {mf|sir|ma'am}, Lord Captain! The last watch passed without incident... At least, none that jeopardised the safety of the vessel and her crew. The situation is under control."

24a184b9-cefc-48f9-8457-a0c477738abf.Text: "Report? Ahem, my report... Lord Captain, if you wish to hear my report, I would..."

4ca10945-c2ad-497d-b6fa-601ac8ee40ff.Text: {n}An inexplicable tension has gripped not only Vigdis, but also seemingly the rest of the officers. They stand frozen, their eyes glued to you.{/n}

90b2620c-1283-43a5-883a-5383571e32ad.Text: "There was a ship-wide broadcast while you and Mistress Heydari were... relaxing. I mean, there was a broadcast of your relaxation activities."

6ea73526-cc43-4eff-bf87-7b51b866b15b.Text: "It was neither, Lord Captain. The vox-broadcast was initiated from inside your chambers. By someone who... was present there. I suppose, if it wasn't you, it must have been Mistress Heydari. I am unauthorised to terminate such broadcasts, except..." {n}A treacherous note creeps into Vigdis's voice, resembling a suppressed chuckle.{/n} "...except in cases where they explicitly jeopardise the safety of the vessel and her crew."

c6128bf5-9edc-4749-9e96-92363602de36.Text: "Life has been quite generous to me, Lord Captain. I am the Vox Master, and only the best in the dynasty can become one. By virtue of my skills and position, no one has ever denied me anything. Our family claims a spacious section for its demesne. I also enjoy long walks through the narrow and dimly lit corridors of the ship, listening to the sounds of her activity, falling asleep and waking up to the chanting of hymns... And admiring the stars beyond, of course."

a659597c-bb37-468f-a738-dd1e07e08781.Text: {n}Vigdis puts a hand to her chest and says compassionately,{/n} "I would not have dared nor even thought of mocking Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} in such a shocking manner. I confess, I, too, was astounded by what was happening."

10a99bde-4daf-495f-a796-3d6fa9388a86.Text: "With the exception of Deck 18-Est. The vox-relay there happened to be out of order at the time." {n}Ravor's nonchalant remark causes someone to choke in a poor attempt to suppress a chuckle.{/n}

018215ca-a096-4e66-89cc-fc20522a4421.Text: "This... feat meets the high expectations placed on the God-Emperor's envoy in every sense of the word!"

d8c5aff0-2eb7-49ff-8bc5-e43ec3fab1ae.Text: "You mon-keigh are remarkably creative when it comes to describing your passions and strikingly grubby and vile in enacting them."

0dafcefb-a7d1-4ebb-a5e1-30ea1d10467e.Text: "As the father of a rather large family, I can assure you that you have upheld the name of the dynasty, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

04d5717b-214f-483c-a44a-ba14874c4004.Text: {n}Danrok's comment bursts the dam. There is an anarchic uproar on the bridge. Your officers, who are not often exposed to such entertainment, are no longer able to contain the tempest of emotions swirling inside them.{/n}

b0d3b964-31b1-484e-94ae-ec3ac4715050.Text: {n}A hysterical giggle comes from the side. Idira is clamping her mouth shut but she cannot stop herself.{/n}

188cd810-0d0c-455d-a36f-dbd04cfad4f0.Text: {n}Jae flashes a smile.{/n} "Where would the fun be in that?"

80ddeebd-fabe-4adc-ab12-e5e2a26a8161.Text: "Emotional reasons are unnecessary when rational reasons are present. Observations show that the efficiency of the command bridge crew dropped by nine point two units during the broadcast."

91e9538c-f4d7-4d41-83a6-ca322ab7c44a.Text: "Lord Captain..." {n}The Vox Master is caught off guard by your question. It takes her a moment to find her words.{/n} "The vox-system is functioning as expected and no communication problems have been reported by any of the crew... Please allow me to check the system's calibration settings in your presence to alleviate any concerns you may have about its performance."

c8054605-72a2-4e32-9e90-9f5095bbe719.Text: "And you agree with these two recognised romantic experts, shereen?"

53b43d3e-34f0-4763-90b9-10bbff921555.Text: {n}Cassia notices your gaze and hastily turns away, shrinking back as if trying to disappear.{/n}

45b73759-cadf-4439-857d-8521b309557b.Text: "The entire ship heard you carrying on with Mistress Heydari, Lord Cap'n. We weren't spared any details — the grunts, the moans, the gasps, and all the other non-regulation activities."

a6fd7f5b-b262-43d2-aae8-661c4ac61798.Text: {n}Jae's eyes widen in astonishment.{/n} "I never meant to offend you, shereen. It was just... a bit of fun. But if it hurt you, I will humbly accept the harshest punishment. Forgive me."

157e6c9e-b9ee-476c-9e9f-3f8f550fe2d4.Text: "Indeed, you will probably come up with something new next time."

36823b0e-fb6f-45c3-a19b-884a99cc9ca4.Text: {n}The crew watches in stunned silence. Finally, Vigdis sighs hoarsely and mutters under her breath,{/n} "I will summon the servitors to clean up the bridge. Apart from this incident, the watch was uneventful."

5ace6e73-10f9-4934-b9ab-7ecb9e193b50.Text: "Perhaps you would be interested in a vox-transmission I intercepted not long ago, Lord Captain. The thoroughly encrypted message contained the coordinates of a landing site on a certain planet, marked as 'rare cargo.' I have not been able to uncover anything else, but I believe the encryption was intended for those who are... involved in unsanctioned trade activities."

ea25befd-ea8d-4604-817a-c52571ce3ccc.Text: {n}Jae becomes serious.{/n} "I want them to know that their {mf|master|mistress} has chosen me, a smuggler and a thief. And I want them to know that we spend our nights together. They won't need to whisper behind our backs once they know the truth. I enjoy being your companion and your lover, but I am not some embarrassing secret to be hidden away from so-called 'decent' people. I hope you take no issue with it, shereen."

ae82f925-aa9a-4545-8eaa-e63997f9da6e.Text: "A multitude of scout ships tirelessly explore the Expanse in search of new resource deposits, but unfortunately not all of them represent the interests of the von Valancius dynasty. I occasionally intercept vox-transmissions from ships prowling in your domain in search of easy loot. An asteroid the size of a small planet has been discovered in the Sotto's Tomb System, and the prospectors believe there may be a wealth of resources hidden under the crust."

6511b10c-c7a2-4453-b896-8c3740455494.Text: "There is unrest on the lower decks, Lord Captain. The enforcers are actively looking for rabble-rousers and heretics, but the population is extremely dissatisfied with the harsh treatment. Many are cursing Abelard, whose signature marks the orders and in whose name the oppression is being committed."

49e20ab8-6060-47fe-b7f2-614955f56557.Text: "And... the last item for today: a few pilgrims from Footfall who were graciously welcomed aboard have been filling the crew's minds with tales of a world of the ascended. They say that prayers on a world near the cold star Cinerus Maleficum have not ceased for several hundred years. They claim that the God-Emperor Himself chose this planet and raised all its people to His halls." {n}Vigdis coughs over the vox system's grinding.{/n} "We have suppressed these rumours to ensure that the crew are not distracted from their vital tasks. But perhaps you might decide to visit this planet, given its unusual reputation."

54d6149b-2172-40ad-9271-01b00e7d0e52.Text: "I assume you heard my confessional message," {n}Vigdis replies, without a hint of awkwardness.{/n} "Do you wish to talk about it?"

775ee399-1fcb-4527-acca-1805eb1f8609.Text: "I was fault-checking the vox-devices in the ship's reliquary. Message recording works but deletion does not. You have helped me establish that. Thank you."

94585734-4199-4de0-b8e4-1f8e81d8f90e.Text: "At that time, I had nothing to repent of, so I dictated an excerpt from an old letter to my mother. As you heard, it contained arguments in favour of keeping lop-eared kleppas on the ship. I can still recite it from memory."

bcea8a17-6e27-4242-a0be-1f624d739a29.Text: "I am going to quote my mother's response: that is impossible. You see, the species went extinct several centuries ago." {n}Vigdis's voice grows ever so slightly warmer.{/n} "I am very sorry, Lord Captain. There aren't any kleppas to be had."

e7e67ace-6ab3-4f79-a7a3-96bafe67e496.Text: {n}The Vox Master's thin fingers dart between hundreds of wires and cables on the control panel. Flipping switches and turning dials, she issues commands and methodically checks the lines of communication with the crew on every deck. At last, accompanied by the sound of static, the crackling of the vox, and the flickering of signalling lights, the dance of her hands concludes.{/n}

84e7f38e-fedf-475f-8e9a-3901e433f765.Text: "Will do, Lord Captain! Would you like to discuss other matters?"

e613b5f1-9f89-49ed-993d-87017fbcc06f.Text: "Wait." {n}Kibellah's gaze, thoughtful until now, suddenly clears.{/n} "So it wasn't a common practice? I assumed it was a traditional ritual of the upper decks. Although I had my doubts."

dec2e1ef-5b7f-49f2-a0a7-c10746a36327.Text: "Perhaps these are matters of long ago, of which only my predecessor or a past Seneschal could have known apart from Lady Theodora herself. But my grandfather never mentioned any such thing, and I never met the old Seneschal."

555bc9c7-7b5d-4bbc-aee3-8441cba783c7.Text: "I am the ears and the voice of this voidship. I supervise several dozen officers and three times that number of support personnel. We receive, send, encrypt, and decode all incoming and outgoing messages through the ship's internal and external channels, and we also ensure clean communications and the optimal efficiency of the crew's vox-casters."

95eb1132-dc07-4e98-9bf2-598e4929c020.Text: "All finished, Lord Captain. No issues detected. The system is working as expected." {n}She studies your face as she awaits your response.{/n}

547f63f9-240a-43d3-9ef8-9f1041b7f636.Text: "And how do you propose we do that?"

01b3f991-4fe9-406a-8ea4-33dbf73735e1.Text: [Aim and shoot the figure that Argenta pointed out]

a4685222-3a31-4953-a586-97eb14cfdce2.Text: "They are beyond saving. Let them go."

4402e41b-6491-4458-8a23-0304890c0bee.Text: "What is it you truly want? To save him? Or to ease your own conscience? He is here because he listened to your sermons, after all."

c90e0c9b-35a2-4ba9-993c-2e4571bacc93.Text: "Your only chance of helping him is to shoot him and end his suffering. It is now or never."

da247f17-3ef6-47ca-83cb-f3b80fcf047c.Text: "Argenta, control yourself! You will avenge his torment another day!"

2ecf19df-f222-49b9-9173-7cbef5d5f46a.Text: [Aim and shoot at the engine] "Be ready. We will need to act quickly."

36a97144-1f06-4f80-82e6-c804daf8444b.Text: [Glance around for any kind of long-range weapon]

67466154-4096-4787-8dd2-2126c8626ebe.Text: {n}You follow Argenta's gaze to the soaring Drukhari craft and the squirming bodies nailed to its side.{/n} "That's... That's Sergeant Vigastes! I recognise him, I know his voice! {name}, help me! We have to save these people from this torture!"

9f82b8ba-2d72-4c0f-ac32-eeab8834e8ad.Text: {n}By some miracle, Sergeant Vigastes is still alive. His sides and forearms are impaled on the crooked spikes that cover the side of the craft but his vital organs are intact: the Drukhari know how to prolong their victims' suffering. The rest of these people are not as fortunate. Some have nearly bled out, while others succumbed to the rough impact.{/n}

7e242d3b-3587-4d66-a6b2-a170dbc548a1.Text: "Those are the words of the powerless! I must... I have to free him from this torment! There has to be a way!"

79074106-70ae-4702-972f-7d2932f0e0e1.Text: {n}Argenta does not hesitate for longer than a second before she raises her weapon and fires. The figure flinches and goes limp.{/n}

8bfbba6c-6127-4028-ab9f-ccb6ac244383.Text: "There has to be a way! We can't... I can't simply stand here and watch!"

4c168201-46ee-4f72-91f0-8df93f0fe80e.Text: {n}A shot rings out — and the figure pinned to the side of the ship flinches and stills.{/n}

83b02893-ef19-4cb6-88c5-ea5958fadd24.Text: {n}A shot rings out but your target is still alive, his cries drowning in the roar of the ship's engines.{/n}

43dae88b-53bc-441d-91d0-1baef9dbc397.Text: {n}Argenta freezes and then turns to face you. Her eyes are brimming with rage, astonishment, and unending sorrow. Her face momentarily twists into a grimace but then she drops her head and begins whispering words of prayer.{/n}

0ca45e9e-8fc7-4f38-a430-30b2979dbd87.Text: "No!" {n}Her voice becomes a piercing cry.{/n} "Not like this!"

63b3311a-f329-44fe-bb8b-4fdeb9e2b695.Text: "Exalted be His name, hallowed be His sacrifice, honoured be His teachings..." {n}Argenta mutters the prayer through gritted teeth, her fists clenched in anger.{/n} "Commorragh will drown in blood... I swear it..."

3b31dfa0-c83a-4d1c-a9f4-59fcca53d643.Text: {n}One of the Drukhari on board sneers upon hearing Argenta's shouts. Eliciting a wave of approving cheers, the Drukhari kicks one of the groaning bodies, blatantly savouring his untouchability.{/n}

01840815-9741-42a8-99b9-f672bdabe01a.Text: "Groxshit!" {n}Jae lets out a choked scream.{/n} "I saw those xenos freaks grabbing people by the scruff of their necks in the streets. They almost got me too. Is that what would have happened to me... if they'd caught me...?"

4422856a-1aa1-48a8-90ca-90bb639e0d82.Text: {n}Argenta hesitates for a split second, as if to confirm that she is not imagining what she is seeing, then rushes over to the sergeant and lifts him out of the wreckage. She applies pressure to his wounds before turning her head to you and whispering,{/n} "Thank you, {name}."

071268f0-1b7e-4f36-a3ee-e6efed6b5328.Text: {n}Among the ravaged remains strewn all over the arena, you notice a severed arm lying not far from you. Its stiff fingers are clutching a pistol. With a crunch, you release the weapon from the death grip and claim it for yourself.{/n}

d96d3855-65e0-4e0e-a26a-fa2e41d47acf.Text: "I do not think they can be saved, elantach. I can see even from where I stand how unnaturally twisted the joints and how badly clipped the tendons are..."

dac0b063-48db-453f-bff8-ee54fd39240f.Text: "Be quiet... Be quiet, you despicable xenos! All this is the work of your kin!" {n}Argenta hisses angrily and grips her weapon.{/n}

f5ebdd89-fa96-49da-8400-cf576c4a8ab4.Text: {n}Yrliet looks almost sympathetically.{/n} "The only salvation you can give to the unfortunate is the grace to end their suffering."

859fae97-6335-4401-bdca-59865162e6d3.Text: "Impossible..." {n}Abelard shakes his head, looking at the prisoners.{/n}

9faca640-86e2-47aa-911d-ebf9d8f83857.Text: "Into the portal, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! We need to get out of here!"

f9e9e819-9ee7-4020-ac57-25bce4447c0a.Text: "A ship is supposed to be... waiting... A ship... waiting..."

0b9600cc-e969-44f8-a9a3-2dcc55aa1302.Text: The world suddenly loses strength and certainty, everything around you looks like a decoration and a sham. Horror constricts your chest.

29955079-5bfe-46b6-9998-afeef7f17ebc.Text: The sounds join in a terrible loop of self-repetition, mixing with a grinding sound, becoming high and sharp like the teeth of a chainsword and tearing at your eardrums.

5cea5229-20f7-4688-bcfa-2ddf3a4b4008.Text: "Enemies! I am curious! I want to see what your insides look like!"

62514622-4e09-40e7-bf2b-dcde91b6ba33.Text: "Damned xenos scum, we will take you with us! For the Emperor!"

c3c36d39-7adb-4b32-8250-17d42f8b1809.Text: "The Emperor will acknowledge your sacrifice, Commissar."

d2c5568d-5c56-4a7f-97b2-4b46a9eb0072.Text: "I said fall back! That's an order!"

6531e3cd-7f8c-4881-8bd3-ef768c633738.Text: {n}The Commissar, towering fearlessly over the carnage, is barking orders to the fighters while simultaneously raining fire with his pistol. He sees you, turns his head, and shouts, still firing,{/n} "Not a good time, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Go, we'll cover you!"

c1518c85-4eb8-46c2-bb98-aa9f293a5b1a.Text: "So... much... gold..." {n}Cassia stares admiringly at the fighters, as if she is not looking at a massacre but at a liturgy.{/n} "It is as if His light had broken through the darkness of this place, dispelling the gloom in the hearts of these men. Oh, how I have missed the steadfastness of these colours."

ca5382d7-b235-45ee-a120-11b091dd7831.Text: "Out of the question. We must hold our ground. It is an order we have given to ourselves. Everyone wants to make those scum pay for all the loss and pain they've suffered. And I'm making myself pay for being the scum that I was. Maybe the Emperor will take pity on me if I at least die a decent man. And you should get out of here, or our heroism will be for nothing! At least one person should truly escape from this pit of despair."

28c05c41-114b-4268-97dd-752a671fd9b1.Text: "Thanks, but you can keep that luck to yourself. After all, we have the Emperor with us!" {n}With a parting wink, the Commissar turns back to his troops and bellows,{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}For the Emperor{/d}!"

7a56a917-e3a5-42b6-bbbf-18e60711b773.Text: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Just doing my duty as a disciplinary officer of the Imperium. Save yourself!" {n}With a parting wink, the Commissar turns back to his troops and bellows,{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}For the Emperor{/d}!"

34c8195c-4a1b-4ea9-a831-110d5927bacc.Text: "It's too bad I'm not a real Commissar who would comply! No. We're staying. The Emperor has no love for cowards. If it makes it easier for you, consider it just another one of my lies, out of force of habit. That's me, a scoundrel to the end."

c5c8e520-5dbf-4812-9b7f-ba1c2cf8e25a.Text: {n}Kibellah stares at the Commissar, her eyes wide with surprise.{/n} "You have returned to the faith, ready to welcome death... For such a thing to happen... in such a damned place..." {n}She grits her teeth and raises her chin.{/n} "Go and bathe in the blood of the Undying One's foes. May He accept your reborn soul into His hands."

8497a805-c6ca-48ea-a525-0db58261c65b.Text: {n}Lingering for a moment, Ulfar winks at the Commissar.{/n} "You are a fearless scoundrel. All right, you can have a line in my saga. Farewell and fight valiantly, so that the Allfather may hear the screams of your enemies."

470572ac-d6d3-4ba1-a7af-db781718ee6e.Text: {n}A furious line cuts across Solomorne's brow, but the wave of anger recedes before it can rise.{/n} "Whatever your past deeds, I admit that you are making an honourable choice now. I recognise your right to choose your own sentence — by the Lex Imperialis, may this act be taken into account when you face your final judgement."

36913ff7-9366-4d51-983f-b252b73d05a7.Text: [Get a sense of where the dust would go]

8eee0ad2-8c7b-43fc-a942-6651ff0f0ed1.Text: {n}The bag of dust begins to glow and pulsate in your hands. Sated with the deaths and torment of your victims, it now yearns to be let loose.{/n}

de1b711e-bbbd-46a4-b2fe-d31fc5229730.Text: {n}You can sense that the contents of the bag are drawn to the psy-stifler above the arena. The will bound within the dust wants to destroy the xenodevice.{/n}

afd1951c-8ea6-4c71-a4ee-2ce880f8937a.Text: {n}A cloud of unholy ashes shoots out of the bag and barrels toward the psy-stifler. The dust forms a tempest of corruption around the device, relentlessly chewing through its frame. A web of cracks spreads along the length of the hovering obelisk and, soon afterward, it shatters. You hear eager, snarling cackles coming from everywhere and nowhere at once — a portent of the oncoming calamity of your making.{/n}

d6b5df75-b66d-4b38-aab6-3ad1607c3253.Text: {n}Before you can put the bag away, it falls apart and seeps through your fingers to the arena floor in a pile of colourless flakes. The power that was hidden within is gone forever, its purpose unfulfilled.{/n}

b04b5084-ada8-4245-a6de-dd815e03a224.Text: "Well, xenos, are you ready to serve me wholeheartedly and discharge your debt?"

c5dfb780-dcf3-4936-a823-69bb675cff6c.Text: "Call me a 'mon-keigh' one more time, and this partnership is over."

1c14c630-eb53-40a7-b675-cfeeedbe000b.Text: "I have no desire to die for the spectators' amusement. I take it neither do you."

7438f6fd-d244-4b82-84ff-c6aefb3bf138.Text: "They will take us to the Chasm now. Let us talk somewhere quiet — the Shriekers' den will do."

d202598e-33c5-4a29-8743-207b26827802.Text: "So, mon-keigh..." {n}Marazhai looks at you with a strange expression as if struggling to comprehend what has just transpired.{/n} "You really are intent on escaping from the Chasm, aren't you? Bold ambitions for arena meat."

9f3c4ab6-2912-4e95-9a7a-b26e25882983.Text: {n}A turn of the head, a quick glance, a subtle nod — you take notice of a wordless conversation happening among some of your companions.{/n}

e1f61218-ef31-45d5-859a-d0b67533d158.Text: {n}He grimaces.{/n} "I will... make an effort not to."

af7d7a20-c069-47a8-8707-deb30cb8da7a.Text: "Never. I will break out of this arena, avoid the Cult's executioners... and make Yremeryss and Nazrakhei pay for every moment of my humiliation."

a427b325-cc83-4373-8a0a-f74a607dc1ae.Text: "Yes, we have much to discuss. I will head there now. Do not make me wait."

9ff447af-5076-4bde-aec4-79a9c90a8051.Text: {n}Marazhai shakes the blood off his blades and turns to you, battle fury still blazing in his eyes. A moment later, his lips twist into a smile.{/n} "Well, now. One can only marvel at the fickle turns of fate, Rogue Trader."

50638721-f344-419f-bce4-5e5277367eae.Text: {n}Yrliet raises her weapon, uncontained rage flashing in her eyes.{/n} "I will do what the elantach did not have the courage to do..."

86e32344-9102-41fd-8281-dbfeed8d248f.Text: "Sometimes we all have to contend with circumstances that make any... any ally count..." {n}Abelard is trying to convince himself, looking at the xenos in indignation and dismay.{/n}

9a368345-c2f9-4f3b-99c8-bb89466a4baf.Text: "Ah, cousin! You have inexplicably managed to earn the forgiveness of the one you betrayed and pushed into Commorragh's embrace, and now you intend to go against {mf|his|her} will by killing me? Your lauded Asuryani restraint is failing you... much as it has before."

7f5aa8ca-e795-4973-9d4c-e67478f70bbe.Text: {n}Yrliet hesitates for a few moments... and shrinks under the mocking gaze of the Drukhari.{/n}

b34a8c50-1294-43eb-8f81-7a652f018e56.Text: "Do not entertain any illusions, little creature." {n}Marazhai's eyes narrow to two dark turquoise slits.{/n} "It is enough that I am treating you almost as an equal by agreeing to an alliance. Look for a pet xenos elsewhere."

a79881fc-a963-4269-9c86-54c6d0f9be61.Text: "It is easy for you to say, Amic'Abelard. The Undying One will call upon you soon, but for how long are the rest of us supposed to tolerate this... ally..." {n}Kibellah sighs sullenly.{/n}

d50333f8-01ca-480b-940b-141faffba40f.Text: "Soon... I beg your pardon? No, no, don't say anything, Mistress Kibellah. I will have none of it."

2739cf3b-5774-42e0-81c2-a82fa4c4604a.Text: [Look Marazhai in the eye] "My offer still stands. Would you consider switching sides?"

0e741a55-ef56-4ab5-856d-bd035ab85787.Text: [Attack] "You will answer for everything you have wrought!"

1d9bddee-a852-4263-8f3d-a616d7d5298b.Text: "I was told I would be facing untested fighters, not the champions of the arena!"

77139b60-36d8-4212-bc85-a9d8cfcc0521.Text: {n}One of the Wyches lets out an acerbic laugh.{/n} "I doubt Yremeryss will change her mind. And Sinisthoria will surely not want to give up her new plaything."

3b31b0e1-3ab9-484a-9332-c9705ad615db.Text: {n}Marazhai grips his blades with such strength that you can hear the scraping of his gauntlets against the handles.{/n}

12f2ad7b-3def-44f5-80df-b3a092a63adb.Text: {n}The tormented expression in Marazhai's eyes vanishes — to be replaced with the malevolent resolve you have come to know.{/n} "Your offer is accepted, mon-keigh."

6e772fa1-5e98-42ae-b477-d0f53c769693.Text: {n}Marazhai glances at the Wyches, his eyes brimming with a sea of powerless rage. A moment later, he looks at you. His expression changes slightly, one eyebrow arching as if he is trying to make some agonising decision.{/n}

f46f7bb1-17d5-4054-9afb-4e835345b9d8.Text: "What did you say, you arrogant wretch?"

c86f8bb0-1c2d-4d0e-a0d7-438ec02da0d5.Text: {n}Kibellah gasps in shock.{/n} "How am I to protect you from xenos if you welcome the vilest of them into your honoured retinue?"

65e6f8a7-1910-44a9-9bde-89de6d649e78.Text: {n}Aebys runs his fingers along the edge of his blade.{/n} "Your former captives. You have a chance to rectify the mistake that made you forfeit your Archon's favour."

176e78f7-b418-46e1-8307-082f62dc73f1.Text: "The plans have changed, mon-keigh." {n}Aebys bares his teeth.{/n} "Keykeross wishes to teach Tervantias a lesson. Refuse like you has no place in the Chasm — you should be hanging from the spikes of the arena."

b03e83a8-f34f-4d49-a202-c9363d85141c.Text: "{name}, did you take too many hits to the head? You're not going to...? Are you?"

fa982650-3022-4d02-83bc-723b88effe30.Text: "Foolish mon-keigh! The former Dracon of the Reaving Tempest is the property of the Cult and only the Succubi have the right—"

c7bd8c05-68f9-4603-93cf-1c38745c6e49.Text: "Ha! A fine jest! {mf|He|She} is joking, yes?" {n}Ulfar catches your eye, and the humour evaporates from his face.{/n} "Troll balls, you're not joking!"

b952a1db-fe69-4596-b0b9-445c6c131e35.Text: {n}Abelard sighs and comments quietly:{/n} "Welcome to our fraternity of the perplexed, my lord Ulfar! Get used to it. The Rogue Trader never fails to astonish."

6fd28a30-1452-4fdf-9d6e-23a98ab81a4d.Text: [Say nothing and turn away from the monster]

1da1532e-93d9-4a4b-94e8-4aab8d31f650.Text: "Will you go to your master now?"

c17b74d1-5348-49be-bd52-1357efa78027.Text: [Attack] "Achilleas Scalander, I grant you the Emperor's final pardon."

d8cffc8c-871b-4f20-97e4-7dc30111c50c.Text: "In spite of your transgressions... I wish you luck."

28e2dcb2-8791-406e-bffa-397033029963.Text: "I would end you here and now were it not for the hope that Commorragh would be more cruel to you than anything I could punish you with."

730c93a4-e023-475f-b1f4-7b9575f165e1.Text: "It feels odd to say this, but... good luck to you."

e6e473c8-c4e7-4b22-8eea-f6cf5bdf398e.Text: "I hope your death will be sufficiently agonising."

30ece596-0ce6-4f59-9aa1-4bababfeccb6.Text: [Attack] "I cannot resist the pleasure of killing you!"

4ff20015-a42a-4632-ab33-85deefb827a5.Text: "Come along. I will get you out of here."

c470651c-8051-403e-b5a2-497ba5e559cc.Text: {n}The monster gives you a long stare and then says in a booming voice that carries an undertone of respect,{/n} "Strong opponents await you. A worthy challenge."

c6a8df7c-578b-461c-a828-a93676737932.Text: {n}An unfamiliar monster, even more terrifying than the previous one of the Haemonculus's servants, bars your way. Its voice is as dry as death itself.{/n} "Master Tervantias sent me."

9814111e-c288-41b7-8004-8028a8ede00d.Text: {n}Achilleas's voice quiets, becoming soft and insinuating, almost like it was in his former life.{/n} "I wish you luck, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I do not believe you will prevail, but you might be able to make a more honourable exit than I did."

d4b276f8-0ec4-496f-894b-cd2434d61d89.Text: "The master wishes for you to send Keykeross on a swift journey to She Who Thirsts. Do not expect a fair fight. This is your execution. However, Keykeross is incapable of adequately assessing whatever she fails to comprehend, and therefore you stand a chance... albeit a negligible one."

c4ef5dd7-bf85-44a2-bb79-ee417c3b0501.Text: {n}Achilleas lets out a growl that must count for laughter now, then falls silent for a while. At last, he says in a quiet rumble,{/n} "A return to the Imperium does not bode well for me. Traitor, monster, spawn of corruption — a bonfire is all I will find there. But perhaps it is the right way."

ff805e61-16d9-46cb-8914-ef2307825bfa.Text: "I doubt that it will smile upon me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. But I thank you nonetheless."

a10e1cae-b577-46c3-b749-c5018f4d8b0f.Text: "I cannot fault you. So be it." {n}Achilleas makes no attempt to dodge your attack, as if eager to end his twisted, wretched existence that has gone on for too long.{/n}

06d70cab-3372-4322-b678-a9ba4b5501d0.Text: "Huh?" {n}The abomination stares at you for a while, then nods.{/n} "Yes."

f56d1d7e-24ba-4c6d-93ce-1a9461816148.Text: {n}The abomination shrugs indifferently.{/n} "Perhaps. That's life in the spires."

b0ab46d3-c1bf-4fa0-99ae-c361082316ff.Text: {n}The monstrosity jerks, bracing itself for your attack, but then something bursts inside its body and its limbs go slack.{/n}

3ced4b12-adb2-45cd-a55e-508dcf56f380.Text: "The help that was promised will be provided. The {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_PatchedMonster}Anguish Prospector{/d} will bring the Wyches the ecstasy of death throes."

4bde7cf7-640f-48c5-9824-fd9bc69b8527.Text: "I believe your hopes are well founded, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Farewell."

9e502177-e3c3-46de-b8b0-c8765c5ec178.Text: "No. His interest in me had run dry, so he let me go. Now... I do not know. Perhaps I'll try to live. Or maybe I'll try to die. I am still debating."

322929df-0eec-49e2-8555-4fb7fd9afb79.Text: "Should you survive, do not return here: the Wyches will seek revenge, which is why the master has already left the Chasm and found new patrons. He suggests you do the same. So says the master." {n}The monotony and accuracy with which the monster repeats Tervantias' words reminds you of the way servitors communicate.{/n}

9c7109cb-bcc0-4e8a-a4dc-5df9ab1055f4.Text: "The master has sent me to tell you that he... equipped his servant with emergency measures... so that no harm might come to you." {n}Even as it dies, the monster is unable to stop parroting the words of its treacherous master.{/n}

9b75265b-3b4a-4780-a6e6-467d71d99e24.Text: "The master doesn't need me anymore. I'll go kill someone. Get their pieces. And make myself stronger."

f1894f53-dda9-4c55-904f-d267f041b30e.Text: "He had almost convinced me that I was a monster. A monster would not follow you back. If I go, I will prove him wrong. Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I accept your offer to enter your service once more... as short as that service may be. Please allow me to enter the fray first."

87c381fe-8c47-486f-98a5-f92118168c3c.Text: "Surely we are not going to leave Master Scalander to suffer in this doomed body, are we? Death must come as atonement for his crimes. And a mercy that will wash away these... horrible, painful, and poisonous hues from his disfigured soul."

7bbceb8d-c1b8-4440-8df7-7150467e15b8.Text: "Whatever for? What awaits me in the Imperium? I am a cursed soul and I should stay among souls as cursed as I am. Regardless, I am grateful for your mercy, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

37406593-a271-4b7e-a541-b470fea72711.Text: "So we have been thrown to the Wyches. Even if we survive this fight, we will not survive the retribution of the Dark City. I hope the Arebennian knows exactly how his play is going to end."

a0041641-d2ce-4c2e-87f8-36ad6924ed97.Text: Convinced the gladiators in the arena to fight together against the accursed xenos.

c7bf1f5e-5070-499c-a846-d4922aaea8a4.Text: [Address the fighters] "This abomination says that our death is certain. But even in death, there is a choice: to be butchered like cattle or to die for the Imperium. Do not let the xenos decide your fate! May you leave this life with the Emperor's name on your lips!"

6ab4bcbb-013e-4cd5-a543-945e2fd7ae7e.Text: "The Commissar has betrayed us, comrades! This is a trap!"

7ffa9a15-c319-4724-968b-8e09ad6daaa1.Text: "What did you do to me, foul spawn?"

ee95d382-e957-48d3-9276-4b0fa707c9ef.Text: [Address the monster] "I would like a deal. We have no desire to participate in fights."

52220508-7f65-43ab-bae3-1541def1eb19.Text: "What will I receive should I emerge victorious?"

032a3852-c0f0-46a7-a81c-a35ca3051a7a.Text: [Fall to your knees] "I am begging you, get me out of this place! I am no gladiator, I am a dignitary!"

6b1a649e-d7a8-41b3-b30a-950956c84444.Text: "The Commissar has turned out to be yet another traitor. I believe I am starting to see how this game is played."

aa2305c3-39cd-444e-9b9f-d176977e73ce.Text: [Draw your weapon] "You think you can force me to do your bidding, do you?"

c96394c1-6c05-40c1-8508-7ab117a6725a.Text: [Give the monster a vicious smile] "Are you offering me a chance to skin a few of your friends? I can hardly wait!"

ea357c19-4316-4760-aada-32fb830230ed.Text: "But should you kill something after all, do it painfully. Unless the masters' craving for death agony is sated, they will release me into the arena. And you will regret that. Got it?"

f40411f7-9927-406e-90ab-a3d0f9ef6d8b.Text: {n}The gladiators around you are exchanging anxious smiles. Whatever awaits you all fills them with a mixture of terror and anticipation.{/n}

fd50dda0-e55c-4ac8-9d26-fbb277d33512.Text: {n}The moment you cross the portal, you realise that something is amiss. The thousands of Drukhari all around you, the towering bulk of abnormally bloated muscle whose face is hidden behind a black mask — none of it fits the Commissar's description of a "quiet dock."{/n}

df201d5d-e008-4128-891d-661cb2ad39c0.Text: "They are about to unleash fighters and beasts that will seek to eviscerate you, so try to survive until the end of the fight, meat. No one is expecting more from you."

c0f44548-ff9d-4170-b2cc-5525cf06f087.Text: {n}Seeing as you are conscious, the monster looms over you and says in a voice that is hoarse with anger,{/n} "Do not play any more games with me, meat, or I will throw you out, forever broken."

9beaca4b-12e8-4235-8616-975e17d864ce.Text: {n}The monster fixes you with a look of contempt and turns away, without deigning to entertain such a ludicrous proposition.{/n}

425225ac-1f46-4d85-a86c-59d23d14d3b1.Text: "No. But they can." {n}The creature is gloating, that much is clear.{/n}

0440724a-51d8-40b7-a977-951b4d2cb0a7.Text: {n}A gloating laugh comes from behind the black mask.{/n} "Then try to keep your dignity from being mangled."

5322f483-2f31-46da-b6da-77b1695fdccd.Text: "Then try not to die the most pathetic death."

62622f0c-23d2-43f2-a5a4-4966b577a531.Text: {n}The creature leans down to get a better look at you, then says acerbically,{/n} "Your life. But do not concern yourself. You will not win."

80abef88-10ac-430d-b342-685f916c7477.Text: "Farewell, comrades. Deceiving, manipulating, and nudging you toward your deaths has been an honour and a pleasure!" {n}The Commissar jumps into the closing portal before anyone gets a chance to stop him.{/n}

f47cf05c-afbf-4d0b-ac30-9af5021dcb51.Text: {n}The Commissar laughs in your face.{/n} "How perceptive! You should join the Inquisition!"

1341d497-f756-465f-b141-37d4d97b9157.Text: "Impossible... He—" {n}Argenta's eyes flash with fury.{/n} "You will pay, treacherous serpent! You will pay for all our brothers and sisters! How many have you led to their deaths? Confess!"

8085e36e-bda3-4c2e-b117-ae546bfb82b4.Text: {n}With a roar, some of the fighters make the sign of the Aquila and ready their grenades. Their pale fingers clutch the pins as they steel themselves for a fight to the inevitable death, intent on taking as many enemies of Humanity with them as they can.{/n}

0316d5fd-d5fc-4121-a76f-53591830b431.Text: {n}The monster scoffs.{/n} "Pretty words. I hope your death will be pretty enough to match them."

f210cdcd-f78a-457b-bee1-14f699714ba8.Text: "It's all right, you won't be so gullible next time. Oh wait — there won't be a next time!" {n}The Commissar makes no effort to conceal the sarcastic mockery in his voice.{/n}

8acd44d2-f5da-4854-95f4-019ec8f0c60f.Text: "Kae-morag, this is another trap!" {n}Yrliet backs away, clenching the weapon in her hands, then turns abruptly to the Commissar.{/n} "You knew you were leading us to the slaughter, mon-keigh! Yes... you knew."

8b18638f-8a99-42fc-83ee-b7152b90ce22.Text: "Saints' blood, I will rip out your throat with my own hands!"

f9401576-d16b-42e3-ada0-d370ee84ef5f.Text: "You're amusing. Overconfident fools like you always die first."

f3aab3b6-4fe5-4526-a1b2-5175fa21da7e.Text: {n}A stifled roar escapes Solomorne's throat, and Glaito bares his teeth, his lumens flickering wildly.{/n} "How many more of you bastards must I..."

782f248e-e6de-460b-8d0a-a887e3b7a43d.Text: {n}The Arbitrator clutches his forehead with his metal hand.{/n} "No! Not now, not again!"

feaddddf-333a-4efd-9ba5-aaddf917ef10.Text: {n}The Proctor exhales fiercely.{/n} "No, I won't lose my grip again. Not over scum like you. I will sentence you with dignity, as befits an Arbitrator."

a8404a74-ea9e-4abc-a2ec-d912df8b38c8.Text: {n}Satisfied cackling booms from behind the monster's black mask.{/n} "Foolish meat! Falls for the same trick every time. Here is what happens to you now."

5d5549f9-cea0-4495-8645-8ac618bfefa1.Text: {n}Consciousness returns to you in a flash of light. This has happened to you too often lately.{/n}

6c8cc616-1c56-42ef-b63b-e63ae2b5d969.Text: "Oh, so many, Sister! Even more than usual lately, ever since volunteers started flocking to the sounds of your sweet sermons!"

69373958-6ab3-4556-9331-e4317aeeadfd.Text: "The gladiatorial arena of the Cult of the Fatal Thirst. This is where masters come for a new youth and where pathetic meat from the Chasm is brought to die."

c51d12fe-9c58-46f8-8aa6-0ade0572e7c0.Text: "...eviscerate you, so try to survive until the end of the fight, meat. No one expects more from you." {n}The hollow voice belongs to the giant that so guilefully neutralised you with gas.{/n}

917afa6e-2b9e-4267-8f61-9166cd2bd6b2.Text: {n}The monster's voice becomes strangely calm, almost human-like.{/n} "I won't. But they will leave you no choice."

1ea39091-1bc7-45d5-bade-638dccc6b983.Text: "You have brought good meat. You have done well, Commissar." {n}The creature's guttural voice emanates menace.{/n}

5bea7f41-db3f-4ab4-9b37-a5c24c6f9cd2.Text: "It can't be! Fight valiantly, my comrades-in-arms! The Imperium will not forget you!" {n}The Commissar makes no effort to conceal the sarcastic mockery in his voice.{/n}

bc619fcf-5752-471d-a22e-bbcf1d9e06f0.Text: Cut away a lump of flesh

f14a6ba8-579c-4d74-88e1-8210bcf826c0.Text: "But why? What is in it for you?"

d0ec1251-3ed4-42c2-98af-94faf62882e3.Text: "Xenos scum! You set me up! I am not one of your gladiators!"

6e8f7353-31a8-4ed8-8c0c-d7b987a36c95.Text: "What are the Shriekers? A gang of criminals?"

271b2cd8-7a68-4191-8717-342ea398f4be.Text: "He is of no use in this state. Let us draw what benefit we can from him — he can recruit new Shriekers for us."

753a648d-b7e8-43e0-9f13-d310cbfbf3ab.Text: "Reprobate though he was, the thought of you, a xenos, keeping him in such a wretched state is repulsive to me. No more."

003e9cb8-22a6-46d3-b3d5-a15d4c4f67aa.Text: "There is actually something dignified about this grim readiness to die."

cb4f15b6-29e0-4e67-b2ad-013a8e72bd62.Text: "So, you have simply resigned yourself? A rather... craven choice."

0d84eaa0-074a-4900-af42-c13d80e8f0df.Text: "Wrap it up in lofty drivel if you like, but, in the end, you are animals kept for blood sport."

e758fec1-d7a8-401b-8355-b3d7354078db.Text: "A good lie. Do they all truly believe it? You sell it well!"

8022390c-b212-484f-9782-2413a4297ae1.Text: [Present the Commissar's head] "Is this the one who was giving you trouble? He was the only Commissar I could find."

76938dd4-59f2-4085-af54-69432c064022.Text: "Did you lie only about your ability to extract the parasite, or about its existence altogether?"

9b704ca1-577f-44e0-a742-ae353a971bf8.Text: "If I am to kill the Commissar, I will require decent equipment."

c847fff4-884e-4b1b-905d-7ea348352b8b.Text: "Why stop at his head? You could stitch something else onto him."

f80476fe-04d6-4c73-8cf7-35497525ddde.Text: "I want to know more about the arena."

726974ff-22da-4c6b-9b97-d2a0a9ea06e8.Text: [Show him Yrliet's spirit stone] "Are you willing to give me something useful for this?"

65c98ce4-10f5-4965-9574-3760915bc621.Text: "I can make do without your half-dead cast-offs."

c6c486a8-556c-4822-9246-c47a0e85c099.Text: [Attack] "Your reign is at an end. I shall be assuming control."

bd6da128-28a9-425f-978f-f033e01a4f24.Text: "Commissar, I know of your betrayal. Why would you commit something so vile?"

70c41032-1c9b-4af6-ba09-53b22f4c812a.Text: [Gesture at the Commissar] "Did I not bring you his head last time?"

e08bbba0-51fc-40b8-9d15-b6bc2c2693c0.Text: "Why do you think I wound up here?"

b5829178-462a-4a6d-8b9d-5f76c6ff454e.Text: "You lied to me. You owe me."

7af81d00-f870-4648-834d-45801aacfd55.Text: [Attack] "You'll be quicker to understand when I rip out your lying forked tongue."

e8337d58-4a49-4daf-abe8-893bf7e78619.Text: "Fine. I'm alive, and that is all that matters."

01b005b3-049f-414c-9a7a-dad9276269b2.Text: "He deserves such a fate. A traitor, a liar, and a killer."

eba654d9-f709-4390-845d-f00c0d78f72d.Text: {n}Malice's translucent eyelid membranes are closed. His voice is drowsy and languid.{/n} "You alive, humanling? You really must be someone after all, if the arena spared you. Well, you should celebrate — from this day on, you're a Shrieker. My protection, shelter, and equipment are now yours to claim."

7f9aa63c-c475-493f-9723-8172eef791a5.Text: "Humanling. Relax with us. Take a stimulant and enjoy yourself."

03ea14f5-7b1b-401f-aef5-25145afebf70.Text: "Hmm. I couldn't care less why you're here. My guess is you were dumped. The Chasm is a cesspit. Everything gets thrown in here — rubbish, bodies, prisoners... It all simmers together until the Drukhari masters fish out whatever they need from the pot. Fighters. Entertainment. Living flesh."

c35a0769-d3f6-4d3e-9a8b-dc1b9df3de7c.Text: "This is the Chasm. The place where those destined for the arena of the Wych Cult of the Fatal Thirst eke out their existence. It's also where the Haemonculus's cast-offs end up. Tervantias from the Coven of the Baleful Thorn — he has his own little nook where he conducts his experiments. The Chasm is an endless source of... raw material for his work, and the best results are destined for the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest — the patron of the Wych Cult and of Tervantias in particular."

3368fb97-e5ab-4658-ad21-d0100aa3dfc0.Text: "We are gladiators — we go into the arena to rip helpless meat to shreds, then we become the helpless meat ourselves. When the end is predetermined — and in the spires, it's always predetermined — you start to see death in more simple terms. You stop being afraid of it and you learn to enjoy life. We are a gang of people who enjoy life."

cc114d31-496d-4879-b29d-7e55b563332e.Text: "Have it your way. It will be funny if your own greed and arrogance get you killed."

2ddb1355-6f95-4bc5-907d-5ba72187d7c6.Text: "You're a touchy one, humanling. Fine, fine, I owe you." {n}Malice carelessly rifles through his own gear, unclips something from his belt without looking, and tosses it to you.{/n} "There's your compensation."

711271ec-40f4-41d0-bf43-a6fdc8a15ec5.Text: "You shouldn't have done that. You don't know when to stop, humanling. Now my Shriekers will have to finish what the arena started. And I'll watch you draw your last breath."

d284fd25-5081-4812-ac96-dd04381df859.Text: "The name is an accurate reflection of my nature, more or less. It was given to me by Gipaeral, Archon of the Kabal of the Sheared Tongue. He was a competent master and he knew his servants well, which is why he didn't trust any of them and gave me the honour of guarding him."

15bafc7a-971d-40bb-9282-e518988ee75c.Text: "Hmm... So you do know how to enjoy yourself. Maybe I'll look into your suggestion. Hear that, Commissar? What should we sew on you?"

6e2277f3-6cc2-4e07-91f3-cd9747605752.Text: "Ask away, humanling. But try not to bore me with your chatter."

abf51994-b0eb-4f4b-92b1-1420d1b43286.Text: "Criminal... In Commorragh, the word sounds like a joke. The Shriekers are a gang of the doomed. They live in expectation of their inevitable death in the arena. And that death makes a lot more sense than all the other deaths on offer in the Dark City."

cb7455b6-b05d-454c-970d-855de65e2501.Text: {n}Malice's voice turns wistful.{/n} "Commorragh is hidden on the underside of existence and is stitched together from scraps of various dimensions and spaces. Long ago, the Aeldari created this place as a port, but now it is their refuge from She Who Thirsts. Commorragh has more bleeding spires than you can count, powered by the energy of stolen suns. An eternal war for power rages here, ambitions and passions are the fuel in the fire of an endless conflict of open clashes and covert treachery."

23c9d229-294f-4c34-932d-3aee44b7a964.Text: "And what are you going to do? Force me to kill him? Let him go? And if I refuse, are you going to fight me? For the sake of this — what did you call him? Reprobate? I'd like to see that."

f42158f2-f0a5-4787-a550-f885949c9cbe.Text: "The Sslyth? My kind were a greedy people. We always wanted more, and that's why we were rapacious and indomitable. Nothing could sate our growing appetite. We could have conquered half the universe... if we'd needed to. The bonds that held us together fell away, replaced by more beneficial and attractive alliances. And my kind scattered... Some called it the fall of our civilisation. But they did not understand the realisation we had come to — that no one needs other people. All you need is yourself."

8e181b83-d680-4d3c-a328-ebbb9c24c24b.Text: "Good. In Commorragh, unnecessary questions can kill you quicker than a blade."

8b7a95fb-da8f-41db-88c0-44cfb4224dd1.Text: "I only just saved you and now you're trying to kill me. You've learned how to live in the spires, I see. Shriekers, kill the humanling slowly. I want to enjoy {mf|his|her} torment."

4dc2d842-5786-4411-8cfc-a099af3f291e.Text: {n}The snake laughs and leans toward you.{/n} "Oh yeah, we're really dignified. Death is a rare and exquisite event that only happens once in your life. Only an idiot would fear it and avoid thinking about it."

ed92093a-1d3d-4b88-97bc-93df1b0aafaf.Text: {n}The snake laughs and leans toward you.{/n} "That's what you think. Yes, they're just livestock, but I'm the shepherd who gathers them into a herd so the Haemonculus's servants don't have to trouble themselves running all over the Chasm catching meat for the arena."

3989872e-64b7-4083-8178-f0a5fabbfb2a.Text: {n}The snake laughs and leans toward you.{/n} "But you're not going to resign yourself, is that it? You're not asking for my help, you're not going to work for me, not going to kill in exchange for security and comfort? Right?"

52c09df4-ef25-4488-8c12-c0d3d76c2499.Text: "I don't think you do. Not yet, at any rate. But witness a few more deaths, and then you really will see."

47e5161d-1d77-43e9-83fa-acd904a44bb0.Text: {n}The snake laughs and leans toward you.{/n} "They believe every word of it. And as long as there are enough believers, the Haemonculus's servants won't drag me off to the arena. Why would they go to the effort of catching meat for the arena when it's all here waiting for them?"

5978c574-63bb-4eab-8a30-ee185e5419d8.Text: {n}Malice's mouth opens disturbingly wide, revealing long, dagger-like teeth. He stares at the head with naked hunger in his eyes.{/n} "A fine offering. His mangy brain would make the perfect snack, but... I have a better idea. Well done, humanling."

4e629613-8d6a-4730-826a-bdc5d84d04ca.Text: {n}Your conversation is rudely interrupted by a crash and thundering footsteps.{/n}

ab014016-1212-4bfc-9860-995a3a6987e4.Text: "Now is when I should hold up my end of the deal and remove the mind maggot from your body... But even if I tried to, I doubt you'd survive. I'm a fighter, not a hacker of flesh. I lied to get you to act fast. That's just life in the spires, you see."

551a53a3-3b36-427a-8996-98cecf197ff9.Text: "Why are you shouting, humanling? I'm not denying anything."

f4c8bd90-bd4e-4fc6-be67-bd2cf0355e5c.Text: "It's in you. And you'll die soon. The only thing I lied about was being able to save you. The rest of it is true."

ea90710d-fff4-4eb8-a708-17a9892e017b.Text: "Good to see how fast you're getting the hang of things in Commorragh. It's really a nice way to live."

bdb7177a-b251-4866-964f-d901822b2bfe.Text: {n}Malice shrugs.{/n} "How would I know? None of the living refuse you'll find lying around here in the Chasm, that's for sure. Maybe a Haemonculus could cut that shit out of your body without... changing you too much in the process."

7f64ad0e-4b08-4be6-87ea-f74d0f89b1f5.Text: "Let's see what Malice has to lavish upon one of his Shriekers."

645b836c-a164-4206-b0cd-b9c229c867b5.Text: "If I gave you that, it would all be too easy for you. When you leave, I'll enjoy wondering if next time I see you, it'll be in one piece or several. Don't spoil my fun."

23e98e17-ca65-4d62-8834-68caaf248095.Text: "You're starting to understand how we do things here in the Chasm, humanling. Think about the future, not the past, and trust no one."

dc4d5b6a-9dec-45ff-9c4d-abb2d21fc3c3.Text: "Like everyone else here. No, his crime was something else — he got in my way. As for the treachery and killing, I have no complaints."

1faeda72-a057-479f-9288-ed1fa80e7563.Text: "The two humanlings have plotted against me — how predictable! Shriekers, kill the humanling slowly, I want to enjoy {mf|his|her} torment."

d32de4a4-db67-442c-80c3-ce6e3a598ce3.Text: "Learn from me while you're still alive. You humanlings don't have any sense of humour, but you're lucky to have met me."

c233543a-d026-403e-884a-08e525bedd20.Text: "What do you mean 'us'? Watch how you use that word — it makes me antsy. There is me, my gang, and my recruits. As for the Commissar, it suits me best to have him in this useless state. It's a huge improvement on how he was before — unusually damaging."

24b935d0-08f6-4576-8cf4-4e608b4caa95.Text: "I have no idea. But a maestro needs an orchestra, and in the spires, there's only one kind of music — screams of agony. I'd go looking for your maestro in the Anatomical Opera."

77588262-118f-4fd7-91ff-4fb579a69dd2.Text: "Interesting. There's a soul inside, right? I wonder if it's possible to make it suffer... I'll give you my most skilled and savvy Shrieker for it. You could do with a decent fighter, right?"

49dc06de-ed0c-4401-98ea-48ec10316f2c.Text: {n}Malice summons one of the gladiators — a lean, twitchy human with animal brutality in his eyes.{/n} "This is... I don't know this humanling's name. Let's call him Meat. Meat is a good fighter, and he's my gift to you. Meat, this is your new {mf|master|mistress}. Fight well and die for {mf|him|her}."

7a454edc-b84d-4a9a-832a-a0b96ea39b47.Text: {n}The gladiator nods impassively. Perhaps intoxicants and stimulants have boiled his brain, or he does not care at whose behest he kills.{/n}

ad2479f0-bff8-45cb-920f-20ab546c5942.Text: "The Chasm is controlled by the Fatal Thirst — not the biggest Wych Cult, but an old and respected one. Three Succubi stand at its head — Tazarra, Keykeross, and Sinisthoria, the most influential of all. But Tazarra disappeared not long ago, and Sinisthoria's been lying low ever since she forged an alliance between her Cult and the Reaving Tempest. So the deadly Keykeross is in charge of the arena."

70de2620-d577-4523-916b-fad816105622.Text: {n}The Commissar merely looks you in the eye with a brazen smirk. It seems he is able to find amusement even in a situation like this.{/n}

9ed323f2-f469-49af-bfed-a2378dc84b50.Text: "I like looking at him. Suffering, helpless, so... comforting. And when he starts threatening me in that little rasping voice—"

5073e585-ac96-40e2-8b66-e6427d25fb89.Text: {n}The Commissar lets out a burbling rasp. It is surprising how much murderous rage can be infused into such a brief sound.{/n}

20fdb730-485d-471b-8087-3e933846408b.Text: {n}Malice laughs nastily.{/n} "You wanted my help, didn't you? Well, I help Shriekers. And when a Drukhari messenger comes to my den, they go off to the arena nice and quietly, and they try to survive. That's life in the spires."

4d80fc10-f0c0-4468-be3e-009fade3d0e7.Text: "But now I'll look out for you. I'll give you shelter, and good weapons, armour, and combat stimulants that will make your mind light and easy. What's not to like, humanling?" {n}Malice appears relaxed, but the lazy drawl in his voice seems forced.{/n}

f1b2e547-0f85-4007-a7ab-c56eb92863e5.Text: "There's nothing in it for me. In the spires, plenty of things are done for no good reason, just because, or for pleasure. This is Commorragh — a moment's pleasure here is often the only sliver between your life and death. I was having a delectable time while you were still in the dark. That's what I got out of it."

24e20d50-2b7f-4cc2-8550-bb89fd4f5dcc.Text: "The Archon liked to watch me savage the assassins sent to kill him, and he named me Malice. I fended off a hundred attempts on Gipaeral's life, and only once was I too slow — but that was enough to lose my employer. And now I'm here."

aa9716b0-1deb-49de-a2d7-30cd7870c6fe.Text: "The tops of the spires are the domain of the Kabal Archons, and reigning over all is Asdrubael Vect, the Supreme Overlord of the Kabal of the Black Heart. You will see them, the ruling elite, when you die in the arena, and they will feed on your suffering and gain new youth through it. They seem eternal, they live so long... but they will die one day. Commorragh itself will die — it has been dying for thousands of years already, disintegrating at its foundation. Nothing in this world is eternal."

2185ce09-9fa8-49be-ad4f-391f22b9b178.Text: "The arena is the giver of life in Commorragh. Without the psychic sustenance created by pain and suffering, the masters of the Dark City would die off — it's just how they are made. The hungry come to the arena to gorge themselves. And the Wych Cults that rule the arenas ply their guests with bloody spectacles and heinous torture."

e9cd2a53-2b5e-405f-b076-0fe7f5aee44d.Text: {n}The snake's eyes glitter malevolently.{/n} "You did. I realised I wasn't finished with this lump of meat, so I stitched it back on. The result was... imperfect. Then again, your race are defective to begin with, so a few more flaws like madness and regular attempts to drink your own blood aren't very noticeable."

3f468d70-5f5c-4065-853a-4748a098d2a7.Text: "Don't get ahead of yourself. You killed him once, and that's it. He's my plaything now, and I'll be the only one to kill him. As many times as I want."

8a2ad00c-4733-41ea-a42b-a517687ba691.Text: [Grab the injector from his hands and use it on yourself] "I need this more than you do, serpent."

e24f14dd-83e0-421f-93e2-affce092a1f7.Text: "I beseech you, O mighty Malice, grant me salvation!"

5c22023c-340f-4f72-8c59-f8d6bfccf656.Text: "Perhaps I will seek another way to win your favour."

2b1c0723-1085-4762-b64c-ba2f9a28f0c0.Text: "The convector has been repaired. Help me."

9a6dd394-0d0b-43e5-a3ab-e7944dfaf1d6.Text: [Get on your knees] "Please! I need help."

935a37c7-75ab-4ebc-8fca-9777c731b135.Text: "Does the offer to grovel at your feet in exchange for help still stand?"

4d1f792a-e97f-4c2b-b305-09ab500e1afd.Text: "I think I shall decline after all."

a20dd616-c98d-4225-a470-d7edcbd76d41.Text: [Address the scaled xenos] "You are Malice, I take it?"

7ed847d5-6d41-4784-b7b9-62b282b2005f.Text: "I can pay you handsomely for your assistance."

f6261249-1279-43fb-8a84-d9dcc47944e9.Text: "I have power. I can make you rich."

c53e5607-f51c-4780-91ba-a8f8fd73d0b1.Text: [Shoot the Drukhari in the head] "Is there a problem with your hearing? I come to you with a business proposition."

5d50fe75-54ea-4c65-90b8-87b47315a204.Text: "I wish to return to my domain in the Koronus Expanse."

e622d9ad-b195-4f87-a2f5-bad12c79fc02.Text: [Shoot him] "I shall take all that I need myself."

4d602426-79f4-4b79-9948-f6ab99001c9d.Text: "What do you mean? I am perfectly well!"

b43b5d06-0be7-49d6-9e2f-54a2bb0d664e.Text: "You are right. I could use the services of a healer."

eb88912d-73c4-4a69-a9f9-e13a9e30b7a8.Text: [Smile] "Pain? I relish pain! It is my betrothed in this accursed world!"

b3467ec7-34c1-4e4f-bf01-fad14dc3aaaa.Text: "A great deal, I must say. I could do with some bandages."

ac92ad25-ca89-485d-919a-191455d4c0ac.Text: Tore open the throat of Malice's companion and drank her blood.

b1234a3c-31ca-4372-810d-1dedb82e87fe.Text: [Tear out the Drukhari's throat and start drinking her blood]

87dd6310-8612-48ab-b9d9-8ee3bb421b4f.Text: "I believe kneeling before you should suffice."

8081fe21-acff-4d65-8cf7-8ac3cf7beb43.Text: "I will render valuable services in exchange for assistance."

007789f8-6b8d-454a-b7ff-e2e226315d24.Text: "I shall take care of the problem."

040c1c47-d49e-4f18-9fa8-eed4ed28b726.Text: "Enough. I will crawl before you no longer."

dba58abb-8426-4b26-9d25-28daa2f81c9b.Text: "I am up to the task, but... you are just mocking me, aren't you, by giving me this grubby little job?"

a0f2909e-d883-4a9d-8681-078dea009678.Text: "My race is cold-blooded. We like our nests warm. None of my gang have a knack for hardware, so if you can fix the convector, I'll take pity on you." {n}Smug and mocking, Malice stares at you unblinkingly.{/n}

67f3b881-e9e8-4bd7-ac43-47be3bd29d0d.Text: {n}The den you have found yourself in is filled with heady smoke, and the walls are lined with living shadows. The centre of attention is a snake-like xenos. He is engaged in conversation with a pale, harried-looking Drukhari and pays you no mind, much like everyone else in here.{/n}

8d458044-5265-4e3e-b351-89c9c8fffea8.Text: {n}You give this self-destructive performance your best effort, but the xenos's face sours as he watches you.{/n} "Stop. Your laughter is insincere. You don't know pain and you don't enjoy it. You're just pretending."

893b9fe1-1b93-4cd5-a37c-a3fe31ea0588.Text: {n}The xenos is clearly more comfortable now — the sleepy torpor induced by the low temperature has been replaced with the languid ease of an undisputed leader in his element.{/n}

ce236b1b-48de-4cdd-a1e5-3bb15c2d7941.Text: {n}Everyone gathered here is armed. They all bear scars, and some even have fresh wounds. You notice a few humans among the xenos. They clamour in a mishmash of tongues, and their laughter rings with lunacy and bloodlust. The air is thick with an all-pervading sense of doom.{/n}

839e2e80-7735-415e-bfd2-a7e5abb4e3c6.Text: {n}Through the drumbeat of your heart, you hear Malice's voice from somewhere far away:{/n} "Patch up the humanling. {mf|His|Her} pleas have amused me."

c79e795a-5254-4382-821b-08cb8d411f51.Text: {n}Your trained eye does not fail to notice that virtually everyone in this place is under the influence of some substance or other, and powerful ones at that. It seems you have wound up in a narcotics den.{/n}

acd278fa-0092-40fe-9757-4ea8d691bc48.Text: {n}There is a bloodthirsty flash in Malice's eyes as he says,{/n} "You shouldn't have stopped. I have acquired a taste for your pleading. If I wish to hear you plead, you will plead."

be73f56e-7ce7-45bd-931b-683cd22424d8.Text: {n}The leader of this gang is powerfully built — his scaled hide is reinforced with engraved metal in several spots. His long tail coils around and around as his snake-like head sways gently from side to side — the xenos is enjoying a state of blissful relaxation. His companion, the gaunt Drukhari, is looking at him obsequiously. Her entire body is adorned with hundreds of embedded steel beads and thousands of red injector marks.{/n}

7977beb8-7872-4990-ae25-0b3b9e5c6f0c.Text: {n}The scaled xenos continues his leisurely conversation with the haggard-looking Drukhari.{/n}

0036b5f2-17a0-405f-a106-4c700701c501.Text: {n}His tail coils into a tight spring in irritation.{/n} "I grow tired of your dithering, humanling."

832322fd-a612-4c5c-b42e-ca8689cb4474.Text: {n}The snake-like xenos either fails to notice your presence or is simply ignoring you. Iridescent eyelid membranes slide over his eyes, momentarily shuttering them — no doubt a telling look among his kind.{/n}

10b6681b-20da-4800-a775-b984eb8d564e.Text: "What makes you think I care? No — don't answer. I don't care what makes you think that."

d46f5410-fc59-4bc0-9373-82a0457f5843.Text: {n}Narrowing his eyes in satisfaction, Malice growls,{/n} "A little more."

027a0ef2-ff08-4b34-8b59-8ce3bbda9bad.Text: {n}His serpentine head turns to you with inhuman fluidity, his forked tongue tasting the air.{/n} "I am Malice. You are an inconvenience. Get lost, or you'll find out how Malice deals with inconveniences, humanling."

cf9f001b-5b0d-4a1c-a48d-e0c6b474d3e0.Text: "You have nothing. Don't waste my time." {n}The xenos keeps his attention focused on the Drukhari, but his scaled fingers holding an elegant-looking injector clench in displeasure. He speaks slowly and indolently like a snake about to enter brumation.{/n}

b779a4cc-b41c-4d4e-aa79-920d9045fbb9.Text: {n}The xenos's casual tone is full of contempt.{/n} "This place does not believe in promises, humanling. Commorragh believes only in strength and spilt blood. You have spilt plenty of your own blood on my floor, and I see no strength in you."

9f3a185f-9f6d-4b77-848b-36f8948ac577.Text: {n}Wasting no time, you approach the scaled ringleader of this rabble.{/n}

e28dfcf5-1ce3-45e5-accc-1419f537cdcc.Text: {n}He gestures with his fingers imperiously, as if dismissing you. The motion is slow and full of sweet sluggishness.{/n}

48420d00-7eeb-4c29-a518-159c3f1c23b8.Text: {n}The Drukhari's head shatters, and some of the scraps stick to the snake-like xenos's face. You now have his undivided attention — and that of everyone else in the room.{/n}

e227f647-ebfd-4542-afcc-4264a04a099b.Text: {n}The xenos's idle apathy drops in an instant, his tail coils as he readies himself to strike, but... he freezes. His eyes are transfixed on the barrel of the pistol aimed at his face. With a satisfied hiss, he says,{/n} "I respect the fearless. What do you want?"

d87ae71b-cef4-4af8-ae63-b1c4e5c60f2a.Text: {n}The xenos's idle apathy drops in an instant, and his tail coils as he readies himself to strike. You try to anticipate his attack with a pistol shot, but he is too quick.{/n}

18651beb-1925-4216-9175-f1f3c81c685d.Text: {n}With a menacing hiss, the xenos says grimly,{/n} "You thought that would be enough to kill me?"

dfc16347-898d-478d-bf66-fd244359a736.Text: "Ha! Many dream of that... And how do you imagine that would work? You think I'm going to take you there in my voidship? I don't have one."

34cb1216-dc4f-45c4-90da-c604aeef95a0.Text: "And what will you give me in return?"

3f437149-5209-4531-b586-17f7a846d0eb.Text: {n}The little strength you had left in your body has run out. You collapse to the floor, and the darkness that nearly extinguished your mind permanently envelops your vision once more.{/n}

1ed65293-6deb-4319-a42e-077ae06ef202.Text: {n}Through the drumbeat of your heart, you hear Malice's voice from somewhere far away:{/n} "Patch up the humanling. {mf|He|She} has character. I like those ones."

5fc6090f-1e6b-46a0-aae9-00e275a691a7.Text: {n}He casts a sidelong glance at you and says sceptically,{/n} "Not for you, by the looks of it."

05e45f9d-30d0-4707-8ef8-c35e10bc4d58.Text: "So go and look for them elsewhere."

badfeff8-0046-43a7-a0e9-769ae25689e2.Text: {n}The xenos's eyes start flickering hypnotically. You sense a subtle, unhealthy curiosity in his tone as he points at your wounds:{/n} "You are bleeding like a butchered carcass. Are you in pain?"

0d0b8a08-86a2-40b0-973f-3d4471d3e3fb.Text: {n}He does not hide his disappointment.{/n} "Talk, talk, talk. That's all you pathetic humanlings are good for."

f937f2a2-52ed-4c5a-a338-c8da0776d71f.Text: {n}The xenos stares at you with a hungry look in his eyes.{/n} "Prove it."

1a9bd62c-49ce-40c7-b714-e267d239f7c7.Text: {n}Malice's eyes flash with menace and he says mockingly,{/n} "Here, I'll help you."

4e9e0348-6706-4a7e-8d8b-ab4c1c0e35c4.Text: {n}Judging by his pleased expression, the xenos is enjoying himself.{/n} "Hurt yourself. Now."

536b0370-402d-446a-88ff-1175b6a8fcb2.Text: {n}His expression changes to that of lazy annoyance and he brushes you off half-heartedly.{/n} "Then go and die on your own. Killing you would be too boring."

7e72f3d5-bf16-4ff9-a13c-3c7e44bfc5b1.Text: {n}This particular breed of abominable xenos is unfamiliar to you, but its appearance alone speaks of a vicious nature and inborn wickedness.{/n}

abef0862-91a8-4068-ab6a-87e52f2358b6.Text: "That was an agent that we Sslyth inject to protect ourselves from the cold. I can only guess what it's doing to your bloodstream right now... But I am impressed by your fortitude — and your limitless nerve. What do you want from me?"

f6c90f76-f0c8-4dfb-86c8-525b2417a502.Text: {n}Without deigning to look at you, the cadaverous Drukhari mutters,{/n} "Malice wants you to disappear, pathetic whelp."

285aeeae-0500-48f1-bf58-9736fe0d9190.Text: {n}You watch in detached surprise as drops of something red spray slowly through the air. Is that your blood? The clawed hand that has sliced open your throat leaves behind a crimson trail. Surprise is the last emotion you feel before your consciousness goes dark for good.{/n}

675e9b45-5711-4e23-a61e-032047983977.Text: {n}The xenos is now staring at you intently, his gaze depraved.{/n} "More."

8f390558-9271-4b82-b89e-3fe69968629f.Text: {n}Your knees buckle, and you fall. A shrieking cry of agony erupts from your throat.{/n}

a7f50102-3818-4031-ad91-d5c46aa4d530.Text: "What use could you be to me...?" {n}The xenos yawns sleepily, his mouth opening disproportionately wide.{/n} "But if you want to serve, I have a task for you. The den's temperature is controlled by an atmospheric convector. The scavenger who sold it to me forgot to mention that it was faulty. Unfortunately for him, he was unable to repair it. Now the scavenger is dead, and I have to suffer the discomfort."

d6960328-0d3f-41e6-b709-f3b43a46f053.Text: "Why should I?" {n}Malice looks at you with contempt.{/n} "The convector's fixed already. What's the point in me helping you?"

7f4ad70a-82bc-4886-8695-4828c301753d.Text: {n}Malice hisses in disappointment.{/n} "You have been interesting for a pitifully short time, humanling. Do not displease me again. I detest fickleness."

d356c376-9a0f-46a1-acf5-f4f58f272de8.Text: "Will you, now? Going to pin your hopes on my good and gentle nature, famed throughout the Chasm?"

b2921ac0-033b-44bc-832a-0352b73c980e.Text: "Why shouldn't I? I'm allowed to enjoy myself. Or perhaps it's just that I don't believe you're capable of anything more."

65d42051-c385-4c62-aa42-9ea944f87d73.Text: "Then you can use your pride to bandage your wounds, and plug up the holes in your hide with honour."

a6049240-9924-44d1-b75f-ca7c3f5b6b96.Text: "Hurry. Looking at your wounds, you don't have long to get the job done."

4d412a68-b895-4203-8882-020589a54b4a.Text: {n}Through the drumbeat of your heart, you hear Malice's voice from somewhere far away:{/n} "Fine, patch up the humanling. {mf|He|She}'s proven to be more useful than the rest of you put together."

482b9c06-fe1f-4d0c-89db-91f8dcaff508.Text: {n}Before anyone can react, you seize the scaled xenos's companion and sink your teeth into her neck. A pop — and a fountain of scarlet blood gushes over your face, while the Drukhari gurgles in astonishment. You greedily gulp down the hot red liquid, staring into Malice's eyes, and you sense warmth spreading euphorically through your body.{/n}

3dd32819-889f-4509-9775-454e2c68bf63.Text: {n}Malice watches spellbound, frozen like a small animal that has sighted a predator. Try as he may to hide it, you can sense the fear rolling off him in waves. When you have slaked your thirst, he slowly says,{/n} "You are one {mf|sick bastard|twisted bitch}. What do you want?"

987b0cc3-4d9d-4857-b600-5ffe29ce01a9.Text: {n}You clench your teeth and endure the torment without making a sound. You have had worse. You have {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}known{/d} pain that was far more harrowing and dismaying.{/n}

727a9b67-0766-4a9a-a0f2-5d51d4dfd6e2.Text: {n}But you will yourself to maintain your composure instead of dropping to the floor to roll around howling in pain.{/n}

99cc4bd7-6a77-44e1-8e3b-205a0dff7d5f.Text: {n}The xenos hisses his approval as you squeeze and mangle your own flesh. While the pain is unbearable at first, you grow more and more accustomed to it, and you begin to find it... sweet? You feel your blood pounding in your ears, you hear the xenos's cackling... and your own.{/n}

5acf96c7-53a0-4dea-a887-0cc98861845f.Text: {n}Whatever you just injected into your body, it has not done it any good — you feel as if you are engulfed in flames, and every muscle is cramping as if struck by lightning.{/n}

e19fd05c-83fe-405e-8caa-c12b93909a94.Text: {n}You have heard of this breed of xenos — the Sslyth. These creatures can often be found in the entourages of powerful Drukhari lords, where they serve as bodyguards and champions. They are just as depraved and vicious as their masters, but theirs is a more primitive intellect and they are driven by baser needs.{/n}

b3ee6cf4-573b-4b30-b9a3-e0b3bb3d6344.Text: {n}He responds in a mocking yet satisfied tone,{/n} "You beg? Go ahead, show me. I like it when they grovel before me."

60243a3a-f226-4438-a41b-25ca1328baf3.Text: {n}The xenos's voice becomes demanding.{/n} "I. Said. Grovel."

9d87b0cd-073f-4757-b896-93713a14497b.Text: "That was an agent that we Sslyth inject to protect ourselves from the cold. But I can only guess what it's doing to your body right now. I suppose whatever happens now can be considered an act of mercy."

3712a301-069a-440d-ae4f-86ca4d167cb0.Text: "I'm going to need a more serious weapon."

8da01788-1d00-4a97-9dc1-3a57747fcca6.Text: "I owe you. What is your price?"

2779203d-c5e3-48fd-946e-4f4ad333f184.Text: [Wait silently for the xenos to continue]

5328d631-e159-449f-ad97-3bc377e1a930.Text: "Why did you decide to help me in the end?"

0efb5ec9-e2d7-4dd1-a424-448aa2e71ce0.Text: "The Mangled Sector? What an off-putting name."

bae64ea2-5095-40e0-8651-465fb5cc021a.Text: "Why do you want me to do it?"

0964eaa2-672c-40f3-adc1-b2cfadb66a8e.Text: "I have no interest in killing anyone for you."

5a609515-87f2-4b3b-8564-25be092a1477.Text: {n}Sensation slowly returns to you. Your body is still in pain, but you are no longer on the brink of death. Your wounds have been crudely closed with metal clamps, and your throat is pocked with injector tracks, as though you have been wearing a neck pillow of needles. The one who rendered this first aid to you was certainly not a qualified chirurgeon, someone who would typically be permitted to minister to the person of the illustrious Rogue Trader.{/n}

962a66ad-c6f7-4697-a0cc-882477fed146.Text: "It looks like you're back with us. I don't know whether to offer my congratulations or commiserations." {n}The scaled xenos looks at you without the slightest deference.{/n}

3a06d5c5-aab5-4a14-a3ea-245ba974c8c7.Text: {n}The snake-like xenos hisses in satisfaction.{/n} "Commorragh. The Dark City — the underside of existence, the realm of the Drukhari. You heard of it, humanling?"

959645b3-9f69-46ac-8609-acbb87666189.Text: "I am Malice, and the rabble you see are my Shriekers. We are gladiators, the bleeding meat of the Fatal Thirst's combat arena. We are the beasts who go out there to kill and to die inglorious deaths for the entertainment of the Dark City. And this den is our pleasure ground."

eb47bc66-7d09-4fc2-b02a-47221a7e6f7e.Text: "I do not want your thanks, humanling. You will earn back every stimulant I spent on you."

52b46efe-9c34-49ea-83be-cf172bc13f35.Text: {n}The xenos does not move.{/n} "Make no mistake, humanling — just because I saved you, that will not stop me from killing you this very moment. Get yourself up."

002c285a-72af-4bfc-9b21-a632b5dd4aed.Text: "Straight to business — I like it. You truly do owe me, but we will discuss that when you are no longer lying on the floor like a scrap of dead meat."
