That would have been an interesting question indeed. I think I may be an artist at heart." {n}A beaming smile lights up the Commissar's face.{/n}

23f99b1b-a1b6-4459-ae11-bc6f3ebb0599.Text: "That's when the planet's governor conscripted the entire population of seventeen hive levels, everyone who was of age. I lived on one of those levels. That's how I became a soldier, or to be specific, how I joined a penal legion. Our regiment was branded from the start for some heinous act committed by one of our dead predecessors."

92c4d5e8-44b3-47fc-af96-dda846e98aec.Text: "Except Tazarra seems to have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_TazarraDead}forgotten all about me{/d}. Would Malice have dared to make a move if she hadn't? She must have grown bored — sooner or later, they become bored of everything. But I'm trying my best to win back her favour — I already have a few ideas for new little stage plays."

d1a88f07-8f76-4872-9d58-aeda0c86d9fc.Text: "When they left us to die at the hands of the {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g}, I decided I'd eaten enough crap out of the Imperium's hand. I beat our Commissar to death and convinced my unit to surrender. And that's how I ended up here."

ab0e78f8-0779-4501-a46f-1af885a36cd0.Text: "The only difference is, nobody here demands that you jump for joy about the way things are. So yeah, I like this place more than my former world."

a5ff4d4e-09d7-4cbc-889a-de2f2339159c.Text: "But I did beat a Commissar to death with a spade and take his uniform. Does that make me something of a Commissar in your eyes?" {n}He chuckles in amusement.{/n}

c430c306-0fa2-4e00-b74a-1c871b67a366.Text: "What exactly awaits us on the other side?"

2cabad1d-b2bf-4973-a3f3-21549128a3d0.Text: {n}The Commissar's resolve is palpable.{/n} "Victory, comrades! Duty beckons! Our allies are waiting on the other side of this strange rift, so let us not waste time!" {n}He is holding a strange xenodevice. The Commissar points it at the rift, presses a few buttons, and the roiling entropic energies die down, forming a stable portal.{/n}

ac789063-2423-4f24-a388-e19633800bb8.Text: "I'm sorry, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I didn't know that you were so zealous in the fight against the enemies of Humanity! I underestimated you! I will spill twice as much xenos blood to atone for my mistake!"

cb118806-0aba-4c4c-bcc1-c62356fb8989.Text: "I will bring up the rear and make sure no one falls behind. You will lead the charge. Act as a shining example of duty and valour!"

7928171b-8415-4817-87da-0dcede7d6535.Text: "Loyal comrades and a stolen escort ship with its pilot taken hostage. It will take us back to realspace, where, Emperor willing, we will send out a distress call and be saved."

dc98b063-ea01-4ec2-88fa-b719fd7fb5c0.Text: {n}The Commissar raises his voice and shouts triumphantly,{/n} "The Emperor is watching! Let us not falter under His gaze!"

790eb15e-da27-473b-ae5a-e7a05544509e.Text: "The path we tread is shrouded in shadows. Careful, elantach. Tragic foreboding grips my spirit."

dd6e15ba-658a-40ad-b243-faa569f3601a.Text: "It sounds too good to be true, but if we can do it... Oh, Exalted One, we can do it, can't we?"

860c80a6-1f48-4da9-a156-f39634d1b150.Text: "By His grace, may this turn out to be true." {n}Abelard's voice is dull and lifeless.{/n}

331fb114-3613-4dd9-991c-b4dd3644330e.Text: {n}The beast peers at you with a gaze filled with hatred and thirst. The voices in your head form a chorus that is far more resonant and distinct than the one you heard at the corpse dump.{/n} "You have taken the first step. Continue on your path, chosen one. Find the place that those like this one call the Anatomical Opera. Find the creations of the faithful and create a new breach."

2b85b49c-1889-4045-9228-36044e421757.Text: "Once you have completed this task, summon the faithful and offer them as sacrifice. The third strike will reveal the way to the finale. The Dark City will be rendered defenceless and you... you will have your road to realspace."

d3472675-20f8-4274-9d4e-8ef45ede5d49.Text: {n}The warp beast revels and shrieks in unholy ecstasy. The voices in your mind have reached a crescendo.{/n} "The third strike! The third breach! Soon will the Truth flow into the Dark City and become a great flood! Take the last step, deliver the last blow, and you will be upon your path to ascend out of this abyss!"

bb4dc04a-3ab5-450e-ab3f-5b670a0beec5.Text: {n}The beast snaps its jaws and something falls to your feet.{/n} "Your weapon of ruin. Use it against the stifler that still supports the veil in the arena and then witness a new spectacle, the likes of which the wayward children have never seen!" {n}The creature reaches out a limb and touches your chest.{/n} "Your blessing of revival. Go forth and let none stand in your way."

50c7c8c8-104d-4e0a-a585-58e3f4909a13.Text: [Smile obsequiously] "Until this day, I could only dream of meeting such a wise and enlightened being!"

f730792a-9af0-46b9-a83b-fc204b6175b4.Text: "I will kill... whomever you want... Just stop!"

6e9f4d3a-9299-488d-b240-818ced4d8dcb.Text: [Smirk] "Now I understand the reason for all this arrogance. You are simply making up for the humiliation of living as the Wyches' lackey."

29c1f968-0b57-49e4-aa5a-a329ca832f7b.Text: "Am I to understand that the most fearsome Drukhari warriors are created by artisans such as you?"

076793ba-0482-4d6e-a8a1-e7c9f5632d6f.Text: "Jae, we do not have time. We will discuss this later."

b31107a8-4b2f-46d4-af86-019c64c7aa1d.Text: "Master Tervantias, I require a moment of your precious time, and I am willing to pay for it."

5513223c-3828-41d7-9274-2844853f3bdb.Text: "I am looking for Heinrix, my companion."

ad2b5dc1-c3be-4bdd-80b3-1de9ae2fc39b.Text: "We made a deal. You promised you would provide help. Do not think of reneging on what we agreed upon!"

1a7469d1-14f7-47af-b85c-75e6f1dfa05f.Text: "I am looking for my Tech-Priest, Pasqal."

eeaf001d-6a8c-4b6b-bf1e-cf2ed95be782.Text: "In doing so, I would betray the rest. I will either save all of them or none at all."

5273db4b-f37f-402c-aff2-13299297c155.Text: "What is your connection to the arena of the Fatal Thirst?"

21b075dd-4745-4ccb-a838-5c9627be80ac.Text: "You must be the most powerful Drukhari in the Chasm!"

5f0849bd-c86c-4b67-ae2b-0b66fdd61eaf.Text: "I shall need equipment if I am to kill your enemies."

b91db73e-3148-41c0-b5d4-c8b6a8241d2f.Text: "You took my companion's respiratory augment and now she is dying. Return it immediately."

b572bac7-4f37-4379-9645-ae5ea56a1fca.Text: "I wish to know more about you and your craft."

c6157610-4abb-41be-963a-7171f1786481.Text: "Why did I survive the interrogation to which Marazhai brought me?"

350ad7df-1e7b-476e-baa3-ef56ddea0627.Text: "The last time I was in the arena, I saw Marazhai. What was he doing there?"

9c7e4a93-95e2-4063-a4e7-593384171398.Text: "I would like to speak with you about a member of my retinue who was delivered to you."

c5a6ac95-8c7c-4878-85ba-38fffd70a36e.Text: "I would like to take the Space Marine you keep in a cage."

08bf7d48-0d76-4e37-9f52-222a856fda04.Text: "The traitor who lured me in here became your servant. What did you do to him?"

2246a3ad-d2b3-4aa9-8b67-a6ffc205d51b.Text: "I shall find you some interesting samples."

39ee9931-4539-41cc-a9e4-00e319e2a4d9.Text: "A fascinating experiment. I am also curious to see how it turns out."

fe0a2fea-8838-42ac-83a4-85b27852103e.Text: "To the Nine Devils with you, inhuman. You surely do not expect me to help you!"

cc96ce5b-eb69-4d2d-9348-374f13c66fdd.Text: "Does no one here wish to hail the victor who defeated the arena's best?"

240f9f32-e34f-4620-972b-6ea986d204d8.Text: "Look at me, inhuman! Or I shall deal with you as I dealt with the Bloodstained Proselytes!"

a8ab053b-4f44-4808-881a-cf9a7dff023e.Text: "With him, I would definitely succeed. It would further both our interests."

69adbb6e-d654-4f52-85a6-41e9a287abc2.Text: "Surely it is dangerous to keep such a prisoner in your abode. What if he escapes and comes for your head?"

d0015cc0-5cc1-4d3f-a3fb-0041beaf32f6.Text: "That poor soul. Surely nothing good awaits him in captivity."

11f873c6-66e1-41a3-8123-6c16c5489cff.Text: "Why do the Wyches desire my death?"

a7411574-6386-4872-b7e8-782a7729aa8b.Text: "I don't care about Keykeross. You promised to help me get out of here."

84e7dc4c-940b-4c09-98c2-b6a3667a7260.Text: "This is all your fault! It was your idea!"

e97e17ae-10a4-4054-8431-e2345f4ac52a.Text: "Take me with you! We are allies!"

8ded3016-fe56-4da1-b64b-3585346ebdc3.Text: "Don't be such a coward. Let us face them here and kill them. All of them!"

d1c29576-7ab1-4497-b1cc-c3a0fff43d3b.Text: [Grab your weapon] "Away with you, vile spawn!"

eec608bd-8c3f-434a-9c65-483ef4007134.Text: "You must have misunderstood. I take back what I said."

b2b5c74f-b62b-472e-a46b-1fa1fcaa0c15.Text: "Ha! So, you're merely the Wyches' errand boy?"

02bb9816-3a01-490c-b493-387c995713bf.Text: "You dispatched me to kill the Wyches. Are you telling me you did not anticipate such consequences?"

65ec544b-7a0d-4e36-b1d0-a42ce5833a33.Text: "The loss of some mon-keigh could never impede the work of a mind as great as yours."

e78a3047-01b9-4b85-8c2b-28231a0107fc.Text: "No. We will speak no more of this."

0ab9cf8b-e6fb-4a84-8408-4a21b0f4ab92.Text: "Tervantias, I offer my apologies for seeking your aid without showing proper respect. What payment can I offer you for your invaluable time and attention?"

7499384b-3584-484a-9e3b-d3c42290f83a.Text: "I am afraid I cannot resist the temptation of leaving a few more scars on your overblown sense of self-importance."

9a067c82-0edd-4442-91b4-622b094a8c50.Text: "Those from my retinue deserve better than to be confined by you. Relinquish them."

ed34e749-fa1d-420d-afe4-7cb3de435cb4.Text: "I demand recompense for all the outrageous experiments you have subjected me to."

d3fade5a-fbf3-46c4-bf9a-e289a1cf0b6f.Text: "I am looking for my Seneschal. His name is Abelard."

624da414-4680-4953-89d7-4bd5625d131e.Text: "Yrliet. The xenos who lured me into that trap. Do you have her?"

4dc94a72-94a2-4d12-8187-d8a409f224bc.Text: "My Navigator, Cassia, was with me when we were captured. Where is she now?"

300b0fab-efff-4171-a6ae-7a2f9d234460.Text: "I want Idira back in my retinue."

a8c16787-bcc5-4f36-bc0b-142c7dad0aaf.Text: "There were hired bodyguards in my retinue. I would like to have them back."

db55e7dc-3612-441f-9c56-b178c92fe09d.Text: "I found some materials. Are they suitable for your new monster?"

ed6a5b0f-064a-4e43-b3b7-b76e538b0f12.Text: "If you do not release the Emperor's Angel, His retribution shall fall upon you, xenos."

c03979bf-72f9-4ad7-90b0-24b87f2471f1.Text: "I give you my word that we will fix everything once we return home. I put more stock in human technology than in his services."

09302d54-aa58-4475-9c5c-eda19a5542ea.Text: [Raise your voice] "Do not dare go against my will, Heydari!"

7b654c87-12d6-4c5d-bd9d-c28f4758fad8.Text: "Is there anything I can offer to repay a being of such brilliance for the attention he may graciously grant me?"

6377c19e-e71f-42ff-b44e-c9f798beb616.Text: "One of my comrades had years of his life stolen from him. If you wish for my success in the arena, return the stolen time."

0eee5485-428c-4d39-8306-f5436a0fa64f.Text: [Draw your weapon] "I will not let you keep my companions captive!"

7cdc0417-3d8d-4f58-bcac-32d4a6c249c1.Text: "That thing in my head is your pet?"

83335448-4758-4130-9904-f8b0854783f5.Text: "I offer you my gratitude for saving my life."

2fdd1611-426e-49fc-b73f-92fa55cd6786.Text: "Your vile arts are nothing compared to the will of a servant of the Emperor!"

6108b082-1145-416a-b7d8-96069e18aca6.Text: "This good specimen desires a reward for {mf|his|her} impressive performance."

ebc33888-f8e4-4b61-b409-e5af745a8b2b.Text: "By the Emperor, I will make you pay for your profane experiments."

6ebc7b8c-6300-40d4-b303-4f29e9cbad9a.Text: "What exactly did this Arebennian tell you about me?"

49f113c5-d744-4276-bde0-38a3a6e5cdce.Text: "What is your quarrel with the Wyches?"

f5b139f8-18e8-429d-ae9c-fdc6c91fcc86.Text: "You, a Drukhari, would do business with a human? How remarkably open-minded."

a97bbb38-7b26-45af-936e-c883e7c0cc4b.Text: "Let us discuss what you expect of me."

d005808c-40e3-4b09-b77f-2924307a697c.Text: "What will I get out of this? Or will you coerce me as you do everyone else?"

2ee222c6-a885-466a-b4ba-b3e670fe3591.Text: "I shall serve you if you help me make my escape."

50e03074-4ca7-4e28-b420-a4828503aaf4.Text: "Choke on your own ichor, inhuman! I will not be complicit in your foul schemes!"

8404b3e3-2673-4051-8723-6a1fbfa0ba21.Text: "I will not stand for you keeping my companion captive! Do not try my patience, xenos!"

50004ea1-9859-47f8-a7d7-276ca3c55c13.Text: "I am Rogue Trader von Valancius, and I have not granted you permission to extract a single cell from my body."

336f6aeb-ffa6-4f32-8463-9158b057e914.Text: [Sigh] "So what do I owe you now?"

c32709b3-b462-47d7-9b33-fbe1893afe4c.Text: "I am afraid you do not realise with whom you are dealing. I am not a contract killer. I employ contract killers."

972acef1-61ad-42bd-adb4-7788e557c41e.Text: "I do not serve enemies of Humanity. But I never turn down the opportunity to kill a few xenos."

5208b7e2-2208-4cd0-93bb-119ff4b3e69f.Text: "You did a poor job training your pet if I was able to shake off its influence."

68fbb07a-476c-4bb9-8edb-aa9cd5fe0cdf.Text: [Glance at the dissected maggot] "Do you eviscerate everything you lay your hands on?"

7320a987-2950-47e3-8b73-1d4875929908.Text: "So, I managed to bring about your downfall after all, unholy spawn."

fcd68d5a-a620-43e7-87e8-76707c89131d.Text: Gave the Haemonculus Tervantias a sample of warp-corrupted flesh.

3e5908c7-497e-4f7f-a9b1-d6a21333f7b1.Text: [Sabotage the monster using corrupted flesh] "I found some unusual material for your monster. Truly unique. One of a kind."

715cd82e-c6b8-4e75-a6ce-e377d4349df1.Text: "Since you are intent on fleeing, you might as well release my companions."

9e379194-fc31-4440-a8cb-a0e55f3b2d46.Text: "With a full escort, I would have better chances of succeeding and contributing to your plans."

e0d90094-db31-4d97-947d-e56519d31ea1.Text: "My condition has been rather grave since my arrival in Commorragh. Can you mend my body?"

855614bb-c431-4727-93dc-3c2b04f4a60e.Text: "I see. It appears that you are of no use to me whatsoever."

57ab8cb9-ff80-4dfb-bd8c-d4d020261d42.Text: [Kneel] "I recognise your power over me and beg you for leniency."

a350710a-45f7-44a5-9e00-9b41e538341b.Text: "I will find a way to free them, no matter what you do or say."

1373e884-da17-4e98-adb2-752c5f43470a.Text: [Press your weapon to the base of your own jaw] "Unless you want to lose a valuable specimen, you will release my companion immediately."

0e6be38f-f327-43a8-92c5-c8fd6a7c169e.Text: "Seeing as you are abandoning your lair, would you be willing to share some of your creations with me?"

74685d2a-9254-44cb-8137-c14e78e69fa0.Text: "Do not touch me, you foul abomination!"

8d2a7d1d-81e3-4b6d-864e-338ae42a40ac.Text: "If you dare touch me again, my retinue will see you dead."

6d8cf8f9-b794-4bb0-99f3-83290746a652.Text: "My success benefits you. It is reasonable for you to help me."

a54ceb4e-fd01-4097-95eb-ef19bc62b425.Text: "Twice now you have taken advantage of my weakness. There shall not be a third time. Give me all that I demand of you, or live to regret it."

731ddb95-eefc-418f-a71b-efdf302af075.Text: "Master, allow me to take the Space Marine you keep in a cage."

6166e029-15c0-49f2-bcae-4a17dd0e19ca.Text: "I met a monster in the Mangled Sector, a creature that can steal years of its victims' lives and mutilate their bodies. Are you able to heal that?"

eb98c251-16f3-44ec-960d-92a92411ee92.Text: [Hold out the bag of samples] "Of course, Master."

865dda85-7e31-4008-8d65-ca4f815dcd45.Text: "I have nothing to pay you with but my own flesh. Please accept it as a gift."

b0ee0356-46db-4cdf-ad08-1c54cc2341ba.Text: "My bodyguard, Kibellah. Do you have her?"

23829ddd-65ed-47c4-9f94-1f41e36d6920.Text: "My comrade's cyber-mastiff has been subjected to modification. Can you make him the way he was before?"

53d42543-bf8c-4c69-a106-a92834d24254.Text: "I would rather die... than serve... an abomination... such as you!"

0a755643-d39f-420e-9cc6-8e79b085243a.Text: {n}The touch of the Haemonculus's claw makes your flesh burn in agony.{/n} "You are no more than one of my experimental materials. You have few options. The first option, and by far the most reasonable, is to obey and thereby demonstrate your value."

1058f000-ae8b-40c3-b322-8e98b3fda341.Text: "You've brought me nothing of interest, only the trivial and dull. Disappointing. Search harder, specimen."

c2095679-245c-4d9d-b560-6af8c08e72c1.Text: {n}With an irritated hiss, Tervantias waves a hand and nearly slashes your face with his bladed fingers.{/n}

73e769a2-d18f-4ae1-9067-36751ddaecea.Text: "If your silence means you have run out of questions, I will gladly return to my research."

7a6f84fb-a7cd-4ab5-9a03-50843f2259e7.Text: "If it is a sacrifice you want, artisan of flesh, then I am ready to offer myself as one." {n}Yrliet's voice vibrates, but she keeps her eyes locked on Tervantias.{/n} "Will you take my flesh?"

2380256b-b6e5-4436-b9c7-6fd79f244758.Text: "I will take more than flesh. I can extract something far more valuable from a single shred of your organics." {n}The Haemonculus smiles unnervingly.{/n} "This does interest me. I will not remove much of her. Her functionality will not suffer."

9b3f7ab8-7bab-4b81-a77c-cb2ee999952c.Text: {n}Tervantias places an appendage on his chest in an almost comically human gesture of wounded pride.{/n} "What striking proof of the innate shallowness of your kind. After ridding her of that crude device you refer to as an augment, I restored an intriguing feature of her genetic code! So be it. I will not squander my best materials on her. I will return her mechanism without delay."

ae2f718e-6efb-49ad-a641-bef0bb683011.Text: {n}Yrliet shakes her head.{/n} "The master of flesh is twisting the truth, elantach. Had the Arebennian not interfered in the Archons' trial... it is unlikely that anyone could have survived that questioning."

e4ffc57c-988b-408a-a14c-f136321c537b.Text: "Same as you, little moth." {n}The xenos points a mangled limb toward Yrliet.{/n} "Unless, of course, the darkness of Commorragh burns you as fast as the others."

afe619cc-906f-4f75-b796-37c3c5b2df85.Text: {n}The Haemonculus lunges forward, looming menacingly over you, his face twisted with fury.{/n} "Mine is the hand that shapes the greatest creations of sowing death. Mine are the essences that sustain their spectacle of carnage. And mine are the delvings unfettered by any weakness of the mind, for I am the only one capable of pondering the blood-curdling secrets the Drukhari blindly fear and that even other Haemonculi are too cowardly to behold!"

74840491-55f6-4fa2-861f-6013589677ef.Text: "The concept of 'gratitude' is unclear to me. But you will work off your debt."

165fb981-8b5e-4b7e-9465-8441f8124241.Text: "Curious. Decreased cognitive function, including the loss of basic survival instincts. An expected effect of brain intoxication in a lesser organism."

147d784c-c0b2-458b-b372-606b5ad1e634.Text: "The specimen prone to technomaniacal compulsions? He did reveal that name during his interrogation." {n}The Haemonculus twitches his spindly blade-fingers in the way an insect moves its legs.{/n} "Working on him was a curious process. He resisted my enhancements with such intensity... But then the specimen fell into depression, so I lost interest and cast him into the Chasm. A flawed specimen. He must surely be dead by now."

c6b94a9b-0de3-4c6d-a1c4-cd76822ad367.Text: "A deal?" {n}Tervantias hisses.{/n} "You wretch! I do not make deals with the likes of you! I command you! And if you insult me by even insinuating that you and I are equals ever again, I will deprive you of the privilege of cohesive organic existence."

20d4b158-44a5-4b69-aed4-6bfe6126e905.Text: "I was curious to see what kind of symbiosis might emerge between rudimentary mon-keigh augments and my own unflawed creations. Much like cartilage infused with steroids will swell a subject's feeble body, new computational circuits sprouted throughout his algorithms. I found the process enlightening."

ef9f9405-8056-43bd-9535-63a42a15dec5.Text: "You will return to the arena of the Fatal Thirst. You will kill a few of the Wyches' fosterlings for me. You might even spill the blood of one of the Bloodstained Proselytes." {n}The Haemonculus looks past you as he delivers his imperious speech.{/n} "They are long overdue a small lesson in humility. They have forgotten their place, they lack respect, they do not appreciate my work, they fail to recognise my authority..." {n}Still staring into the distance, he continues to list his grievances with maniacal thoroughness.{/n}

11ba513c-dd26-4387-9934-86920724ef30.Text: {n}Tervantias makes an indifferent gesture.{/n} "Specimens awaiting disassembly are kept in the pen. Take whichever ones you wish."

478aeb7b-ee2f-4ecf-a451-b6fb0b2ec7c2.Text: "Secretary Achilleas... Back on Dargonus, I noted the dirty grey chains that bound him around the arms and legs. At that moment, it seemed to me that he was blaming himself for the attack on the capital world. If only I'd had the courage to speak to him about it just once... perhaps we all would have been spared the fate of becoming prisoners in this place."

88822778-fa07-48b3-a491-a00feb3c5561.Text: {n}A sadistic smile is playing on the Haemonculus's lips.{/n} "Yes... I wonder what effect this will have on the rest of the specimens once they learn of your decision."

c28d0725-18b1-4410-95a0-71500805b791.Text: "Believe me, Cass, you are not the only one feeling like a fool around here. My whispers were treacherously silent too."

b8066291-cb22-4537-af48-9f6cf1519ddf.Text: {n}The Haemonculus smirks.{/n} "Not just the Chasm. The entire Kabal of the Reaving Tempest depends on my augments and essences, which is how I secured the Chasm as my domain. Here, I never lack for subjects... or spare parts."

cf457994-f937-4706-b7af-cb195ed801ac.Text: {n}The appendages protruding from the xenos's back move restlessly, emitting an unnerving screech. Tervantias is completely engrossed in his apparatus and spares you no attention.{/n}

e7247c0d-3702-4d59-a959-ccb3a604f4b5.Text: {n}There is something fundamentally wrong with the xenos's silhouette and its twitchy, abrupt movements, and it sets your mind reeling in disgust. Each of its mechanical tool appendages seems designed to be as sickening and horrifying as possible.{/n}

7397afc6-3c86-482b-88a4-dc7addb29028.Text: "I am not in the habit of conversing with specimens. But if it increases your motivation to serve..."

5b370c92-0355-4400-98bd-17877d2be91a.Text: {n}The Haemonculus looks at you with an impatient and unsettling grimace.{/n}

18aad016-4838-462b-8aac-7ed382fc23a6.Text: "Your body was given to me for disposal. It was thrown into the cesspit." {n}The Haemonculus's voice grows thoughtful.{/n} "It is an anomaly that the specimen did not die. I must consider fitting the disposal chute with a shredding mechanism."

333e97b5-4960-44e0-9782-e978194de5de.Text: "Obedience will be rewarded. Take your crude gear with you. I abhor such technological banality, but a creature as undeveloped as you may find it of use." {n}You hear one of the joints in Tervantias's arm click.{/n} "Once you are finished with this, go and look at the ones who will be your executioners when the time comes for you to die."

ebc805ee-6e46-461f-953a-68b66e9c005b.Text: "That brazen, ambitious, and woefully imprudent whelp. He was cast down from the Dracons of the Kabal but earned the good graces of the Wyches of the Fatal Thirst in his very first fight in the arena. He was invited to join their finest, the Bloodstained Proselytes. Some say he was involved in the death of their Succubus, Tazarra — if so, then Marazhai may be disappointed by his reception in the ranks of the Cult."

f0ed8ac3-37fd-48d1-a815-20bfdd6b6bf7.Text: "Perhaps the genetic subtype of all three specimens was defective, and this is the cause of my limited success... In that case, the loss of this specimen would not be significant."

058ca95a-2a1c-434a-ba67-585eb623a726.Text: {n}The Haemonculus smiles in satisfaction, but then fixes you with a stern look.{/n} "I perceive that you hope to convince me to lower my guard, specimen. Do not test the limits of my favour."

ff81eb96-2a02-4d74-97f0-135e7056bda1.Text: "The specimen driven by a self-destructive desire for punishment? An interesting project. He was so committed to his petty sense of shame that he welcomed the changes I wrought. I used his materials to create a Wrack. He performs adequately as a servant."

b5419288-0986-432c-a994-09036af6423c.Text: "Without a doubt. Even the most skilled Wyches and mighty Kabalites are outstripped by the pure destructiveness of our genius. Yet I long ago rose above the building of commonplace battle beasts. The monstrosities I create are unique! My last specimen, the Chtonos, surpassed every trifle ever made by my rivals! I fed it elite warriors until it escaped and hid in the Mangled Sector... I would have caught it, but then a new idea drew my attention!"

3bbb4a1c-5a29-49d4-ba26-4c037a86e098.Text: "Good specimen. Your cooperation will be rewarded."

7fb93ae4-603f-444f-b97e-58166e88d6db.Text: {n}Tervantias gives you a look of patronising curiosity.{/n} "Your lesser kind is not completely devoid of the inquisitiveness characteristic of full-fledged beings."

b9681b6c-e847-45a6-ad12-c683f7f28c22.Text: "A defective specimen. Only my interests, of which you are the instrument of execution, protect you from an immediate separation into more obedient parts."

f7556a62-47f0-4b4e-b482-0506c3bfe73f.Text: "The second option, which is less rational but just as acceptable, is to be obstinate. I will find a use for you in any case. For instance, you could be processed into a sentient soup that retains the sensations and awareness of its original form and is therefore aware of everything that happens until it dissolves completely at the end of the digestive process. I see from your expression that you have already chosen."

2aacd00f-0fa6-42a9-853e-4550679d5be7.Text: {n}With a weary sigh, the Haemonculus turns away from you, his knife-like fingers making an unnerving scraping sound.{/n}

6f9083ba-210c-4d23-bb0d-f0c509674a59.Text: {n}Tervantias rushes about the laboratory, snatching up certain tools, vials, and notes. He conceals some of these items inside his own body cavities and destroys the rest.{/n}

94d0b672-1c42-4167-99f0-a2e07e9bc657.Text: {n}Tervantias remains silent for a long moment. The limbs behind him click ominously.{/n} "The mon-keigh male with an altered genetic structure... Ah, such phenomenal parameters... I previously studied two other specimens of the same breed but have yet to untangle their genetic secrets. He also performs well enough in the arena. Losing this final specimen would be an undesirable outcome. Denied."

f143aa6e-31f4-4c45-93a5-dda0ad682a18.Text: {n}The Haemonculus scoffs.{/n} "Do you truly think some mon-keigh can frighten me? His body may be strong, but his mind is simple, and therefore he is no more difficult to keep under control than any other member of your species."

13f3feb5-f063-4ca5-b82b-e75ba16ed510.Text: "Sooner or later, I will turn his flesh into a fount of sweet knowledge. Until then, he will contribute by killing another dozen gladiators in the arena. Perhaps even two dozen."

73df1703-9e64-4f7b-a8e4-d7ca3c91dd58.Text: {n}The Haemonculus glares at you and roars furiously,{/n} "This isn't what I desired! Not to this extent!"

74eb10a3-545f-462b-acf2-1d6e3695f44d.Text: "The Cult of the Fatal Thirst craves blood, specimen. Your blood. My blood. One must be astoundingly insensitive to the vibrations of the Dark City not to realise this."

6a01aff8-d524-49ae-a9be-7894fca40d6f.Text: "I would rather hail the walking corpse who invited {g|Encyclopedia:Sailanthresh}She Who Thirsts{/g} into my Anatomical Opera."

47e73bd2-3558-4371-8369-ff23c1dbb880.Text: "You will first need to dispose of the throng who desire the same as you but who declared it first."

d8941684-3208-4ec0-8272-f4a9fdd914d8.Text: "You humiliated them, mon-keigh. Keykeross and I agreed that she would send fresh meat against you, but she decided to undermine my authority by sending out her best. You slaughtered them, and so it was the Cult's authority that suffered. But who cares about a pathetic mon-keigh? You are my lackey and thus it is I who is responsible for undermining the Cult's authority."

b6935646-fed2-4ca4-a2a8-bf429217305f.Text: "I will leave the Anatomical Opera and withdraw to the Spire of the Reaving Tempest. The Wyches won't dare to settle their scores under the eye of my patrons, so the Kabal's valuable servant is safe from their ire. As for you... Go out into the streets of the Chasm and die. Or go to the arena and try to kill Keykeross. Even if you succeed, you will still die."

f581ea84-c438-4261-a577-ec12dc5c6977.Text: {n}You hear mockery in the Haemonculus's voice:{/n} "Forget the old promises, mon-keigh. This is war. My loyal servants are being slaughtered across the Chasm. I cannot take any more specimens away with me, and the ones I have already packed are far more valuable than you."

4c8d62c5-3d45-4297-a8bd-2a5e290d79ae.Text: {n}The Haemonculus thinks for a moment, snapping his mandibles.{/n} "No. It must be your fault. My scheme was brilliant, but you ruined it. A defective specimen!"

9f8c84e2-5ac5-470f-b546-6b80ad8d9734.Text: {n}Tervantias examines you then dryly states,{/n} "No. You, defective specimen, are not as valuable as you think. And the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest certainly won't extend its protection to you."

c77e3db4-2f90-4f16-a7e6-2f764636c794.Text: {n}Tervantias becomes so absorbed in his thoughts that he starts shearing off pieces of his own flesh with his scissor-like claws.{/n} "Enter the arena. The Succubi will not pass up this chance to gut you in front of an audience. If you could simply wound Keykeross, it would give us both enough time to escape. For that, I would be willing to sacrifice the deadliest and most valuable specimens in my collection."

60d7f7b7-1951-40c5-baea-d07bf0269031.Text: {n}Tervantias is silent for a few moments.{/n} "To repay Keykeross for her treachery, I will send the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_PatchedMonster}Anguish Prospector{/d} to the arena. While the Wyches are preoccupied with ending your life, the Prospector will kill several of them. Regardless, it is too conspicuous for me to hide from the Cult's huntresses. Let my creation perform the symphony of pain for which it was designed!"

387c835c-e348-4774-82dc-3fb1664f5f0a.Text: "If you manage to kill her, run. Sinisthoria will not let such impertinence go unpunished, and her wrath is a hundredfold more dangerous than Keykeross's fury. Do not return to the Chasm — you will find no shelter there. Seek salvation in other spires, and you may prolong your agony for a short time."

6c072d00-c0ec-4e90-8528-5b80d64f0175.Text: {n}The Haemonculus's anxious movements slow to a halt, but the mandibles on his face twitch nervously.{/n} "An unnecessary risk. This is not a hasty retreat, merely... a temporary change of workspace."

30467074-0c2f-4e9f-9d7d-2a29db73e8e2.Text: {n}You feel as if the bones of your skull have begun to contract, crushing your spasm-ridden brain from all sides like an ever-shrinking cage. The world becomes a swimming blur obscured by a veil of tears, and you hear a strange ringing from somewhere far away — most likely your drawn-out scream.{/n}

7ec2ad42-7ab4-4b62-bd00-507b00259ae3.Text: {n}Tervantias's expression does not change, but his white skin becomes speckled with bleeding wounds as his bones grow through it like horrifying barbed spikes. He asks, his voice silken,{/n} "What did you say?"

6a24bb41-952d-4004-b82d-23ab20fb4f15.Text: "Choose your words wisely when addressing your master, mon-keigh."

0f29d80f-fac6-4460-8791-1faf36010228.Text: {n}Tervantias narrows his eyes.{/n} "If you are so helpless, then what use was there in letting you live?"

4a3b3859-9c62-4f0e-9abc-3e4661834296.Text: "The sheer primitiveness of your technologies... Go, specimen. Deliver Tervantias's message of blood to the arena Wyches." {n}The Haemonculus gestures imperiously at the exit.{/n}

9ea2436e-c980-4cd2-b908-a150ff58897d.Text: "And it wasn't enough for you to just kill them! You {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_MarazhaiRecruited}enticed one of the Bloodstained Proselytes{/d} to join the mon-keigh side! As the entire Chasm watched! A slap in the face of the Cult wasn't enough for you, so you decided to spit in its face as well?"

2406fe0e-92f7-406e-91e2-57ed9dfd10ac.Text: {n}Tervantias produces a device fitted with an unusually long needle.{/n} "Try not to squirm, little insect. The needle needs to go through your spirit stone, heart, and spine so that I can collect all three samples at once. And it is so very fragile..."

25cce966-9d5c-478a-a29f-dd3c8f7171bb.Text: {n}Tervantias shrugs, and the spark of curiosity in his eyes fades.{/n}

06dd7317-b07d-48d7-9283-39c9ca10329b.Text: "Was that a threat? I struggle to follow your kind's pitiful metaphors, especially those that are supposed to sound threatening — you are simply incapable of inspiring fear. If that was an attempt at intimidation, I remain unshaken."

a0d688fa-95b5-4a93-9a6a-39d861090ffc.Text: "This will be a step upon the path of atoning for the errors of my past, elantach. If my sacrifice will bring us... bring you closer to salvation, I will commit myself into the hands of this tormentor."

b6cce451-e8a9-43e1-bea9-158f3b593153.Text: {n}Yrliet presses her lips together and nods.{/n} "Do your work, flesh-stealer. I do not fear you, nor do I fear pain." {n}She goes on to mouth these words over and over like a mantra when the Haemonculus drives the needle into her chest. A click comes from inside her body. Yrliet pales, her face twisted in torment... but she remains as still as a statue.{/n}

481fb11c-37ec-4ab3-aca5-9c8005c5ff12.Text: "A single specimen is all you get. Make your choice."

a12d9f49-2c8e-4848-9a61-bd5774fd6efe.Text: "Coercion will be more than enough. If you disobey, I will turn you into material for my creations and ensure that you feel and are aware of every manipulation performed on your flesh. But if you do what I tell you to do, I will let you live for a while longer."

8d64969c-fbd2-482c-bb96-f02e1568ee35.Text: "Once they have exhausted their utility, I will let you take the scraps."

f6bde9d5-7035-4ad2-adda-be24722babbe.Text: {n}Tervantias responds with a derisive smile,{/n} "You are so naive, mon-keigh. Have you been convinced by your impotent mind that I could be appeased by such a trite demonstration of obedience? You should be on your knees whenever you are in my presence. Now get out of my sight."

897bb7d7-9591-486c-aa30-4134a763c9d3.Text: {n}The Haemonculus lets out a laugh of contempt.{/n} "Recompense, you brazen scrap of flawed flesh? I did you an honour by lowering myself to interacting with your trivial organics branded by inferiority."

dd1a6b89-2e10-4227-af99-3c88db0f63af.Text: {n}Tervantias arches an eyebrow.{/n} "You forget yourself, specimen. Go and serve my will, and should I ever decide to show you favour, I will do so at a time of my choosing."

1525a988-8192-40a7-bc79-1ec0b46b1659.Text: {n}The Haemonculus does not react to your impudent remark. Or, more accurately, he does not seem to be listening at all.{/n}

d7ee7a14-169f-4194-818b-d06a3c02e21e.Text: {n}Tervantias's smile is a strange combination of contempt and pleasure.{/n} "Your paltry possessions do not interest me. If you had something that could intrigue a master sculptor such as I... perhaps a remarkable piece of organics... then I might grant you a few short moments of my time."

08b67673-c255-4a43-bf1d-3b2ff284fbd6.Text: {n}After rummaging through what you have, Tervantias pulls out a fragment of flesh that has caught his eye. He splits off a piece of it, places it in his mouth, thinks for a while, and finally concludes,{/n} "Curious. You have earned my attention, specimen. Speak quickly."

6409238f-97d2-47ac-abe7-60c564197488.Text: {n}After rummaging through what you have, the Haemonculus snaps out with vexed disappointment,{/n} "Specimen, you have brought me nothing worthy of attention. Get out!"

0d476b8b-a20d-4953-bf13-432a8a235f7f.Text: {n}Very slowly, Tervantias pulls the needle out of her, examines it critically, then finally nods.{/n} "The sampling was successful." {n}He gives Yrliet a dismissive glance.{/n} "I have no further need of you."

8f3cb9f3-ed50-45ad-a055-35a8617faf90.Text: {n}The Haemonculus meticulously inspects the piece of flesh you offered.{/n} "Unusual properties. The tissue mutates spontaneously, constantly changing its own structure. Extremely unstable, hazardous, and unpredictable. Good work, specimen. I am intrigued."

1631c1e6-e9e1-46ed-8625-dd6d957ea4dd.Text: {n}Tervantias cringes squeamishly and mutters,{/n} "The mere thought of you tarnishing them with your filthy hands is revolting... but if it serves to ensure my safety, I will tolerate this obscenity."

929c21c2-342b-4d2b-bf7d-7100847de755.Text: {n}The Haemonculus's rib cage opens wide, the skin around it tearing with a wet squelch. You catch a glimpse of his internal organs coated with a strange film and riddled with shapeless growths and mushroom-like tumours. Where one would expect to see a heart, you see instead a glistening, translucent mollusc that has attached itself to the xenos's veins. The revolting thing lets out a groan, and a stream of caustic liquid burns your face. Blinded, you start thrashing as a horrible spasm seizes your throat and prevents you from breathing and your body convulses in pain. The light around you instantly fades.{/n}

f2ad3dcb-944e-43dd-aec7-d55ccbdcbcca.Text: {n}Tervantias makes an irritated gesture with his fingers, and you feel a sting in your neck. Your hand finds a tiny dart that has lodged itself in your skin. It could have come from anywhere — the Haemonculus's lair could be hiding dozens of killers or automated weapons. Your heartbeat becomes erratic, and you feel a dull pain spreading in your left arm. Tervantias observes your agony with an air of disdain.{/n}

e06c3e95-e0da-4a1e-b29c-0e13b9a6a5ef.Text: {n}The Haemonculus waves you off in irritation.{/n} "If you are unable to make yourself useful, I would rather wait for you to die and find myself a better tool. You should be worthy of my attention, not a drain on it."

1a090db5-5f87-48bb-aad0-634b3e6fe8e1.Text: "First, let us remove the... redundant parts." {n}Several instruments of death with blades of varying length, thickness, and curvature appear in Tervantias's hands. He bares his teeth and addresses Jae in an insinuating voice,{/n} "Which one do you choose?"

6a766d6d-be7b-4c93-9e01-fb291a029b8b.Text: "My path must not end here. I have already {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_Yrliet_BrokenPromise}sacrificed much{/d}, and this new price... is one I can pay. The children of Crudarach deserve to have the mournful song about the fate of our home flow through the ages. If it means escaping this place so I can learn the truth... I will do it."

c96167a6-1bb2-4e92-94b2-c6dec1dc1d17.Text: {n}Yrliet frowns, and you catch a strange look in her eyes — a mixture of sadness, relief, and... shame.{/n}

8ed53385-7b7c-43f6-b587-c9aa3906b523.Text: {n}You hear a shout and the sound of someone moving behind you, but the Haemonculus points his claws directly at your eyes, and all goes quiet. The monster turns his gaze on your companions.{/n} "Intervening would be inadvisable, servants. This specimen and I are having a conversation."

46582c2d-5c80-454b-a9e6-abe0b50f85b7.Text: {n}The creature in front of you is a patchwork of skins stuffed with darkness, corruption, and sharp objects. Staring at you with its scalpel eyes, it grumpily remarks,{/n} "Such a disobedient specimen, you're still not dead. An anomaly?" {n}Its foul, corrupt thoughts reach out to you, groping at your face.{/n}

6e2b7058-122b-4bdc-9988-e761f637eb34.Text: {n}Tervantias flicks a needle finger at some kind of apparatus made of bone.{/n} "The sarcophagus for containing dangerous specimens has been unlocked. You may take what is left of your servant."

116f3c37-9802-4a5e-89d1-4b2aa9e71902.Text: "But I see you will soon become a very obedient specimen. Convulsive spasms, hysterical reactions... Come here." {n}The creature pokes you in the chest, its triangular fingernail easily penetrating your skin. A strange sound throbs at the edge of your awareness. A sound similar to your own scream.{/n}

0902fa34-00b2-4037-a014-a4db5254382c.Text: "No," {n}the Haemonculus snaps curtly, and he returns to his work. Noticing that you are still waiting for something, he hisses irritably, still not taking his eyes off the experiment:{/n} "If you wish to continue wasting my time with your pathetic pleading and whining, specimen, then you know the price: pay up or get out."

8ae68e56-e331-4cee-9d87-03c903d08c9b.Text: "Oh, I doubt that. While you were floundering between life and death, your servants became very agitated. Several ridiculous threats were uttered before your lackeys realised that the life of their {mf|master|mistress} was completely in my hands. So they are going to behave themselves, aren't they?" {n}The Haemonculus smiles mockingly at your companions.{/n}

750860c5-8bfc-47de-9fca-9045166cb43e.Text: "Then get out of my sight and do not disturb me again, specimen."

55fe7ebf-7827-4e32-84b5-27fa88c56c0f.Text: {n}Tervantias extracts a piece of flesh, examines it fastidiously, palpating and tearing off fragments, then places it in some sort of container.{/n} "It will do."

bacf63c8-5fad-48e9-b0d1-eac1feef1614.Text: {n}Tervantias thinks for a moment.{/n} "Your tissues are of little interest to me — you are a rather unremarkable piece of meat, mon-keigh. However, luckily for you, I happen to be in need of a fresh spinal cord sample."

ec3f1f2a-18a0-4608-98f2-744fe970c27c.Text: "Obedient specimen. So be it, you have earned a few minutes of my attention. The answer is still no. This particular mon-keigh specimen has phenomenal parameters. I previously studied two other specimens of the same breed but have yet to untangle their genetic secrets. He also performs well enough in the arena. I will not part with the last specimen."

f6186b1e-656f-4e17-b222-3a53f9208a01.Text: {n}Without warning, the Haemonculus's limbs seize you in a death grip and a shrieking drill bites into your spine. You want to scream, but you cannot — your throat convulsively constricts in agony, preventing you from drawing a single breath. Your jaw twitches, clenching and unclenching with such force that you nearly bite off your tongue. Just when you think you cannot take any more, Tervantias extracts the drill bit with a squelching crunch and closes the wound with some kind of staples and needles.{/n}

71e4874f-2863-4c33-8edf-d20dbf7824d2.Text: {n}The Haemonculus makes a snapping sound.{/n} "Here comes Aebys and his fosterlings... The leader of the Bloodstained Proselytes has paid a visit to the Anatomical Opera. Take this opportunity to study them properly — they won't dare touch you here."

d71f12a4-a315-4251-be0a-c9ae97447ef3.Text: "It was supposed to go differently. Your performance was supposed to be a lesson in respect, not a declaration of war! You would have killed someone unimportant and made the Wyches' vanity bleed. The Wyches would have received your head as a salve for their wounded pride. They would have been reminded for a time that I was still someone who could greatly complicate their existence. Instead, you have failed me, all of you! Keykeross did not keep her word, and you did not die in her trap! It is all your fault that things have spiralled out of control."

1535e84f-616b-49a4-88f6-a2bbe32fbf7c.Text: "Remember: if you try to deceive me, you will suffer a fate worse than death. I even know which fate specifically — the pale mon-keigh, the one who could not stop prattling about your pitiful faith, was quite susceptible to my method."

b6957a88-e774-4672-b7fb-ac482db4fb30.Text: "Female specimen, negligible veil influence, primitive notions of death. I disproved her views on cessation of existence by way of reanimation and uncomplicated manipulation of the mind. You may take your mon-keigh servant... or however many of her are left in there — I intended to dispose of them all the same."

d0d1a143-2205-4fdb-909d-8eeda2ae6e24.Text: "No!" {n}Solomorne cries out desperately before you can even finish formulating your request.{/n}

0be4dffe-3f52-483a-be03-12cb8b5b1482.Text: {n}Tervantias hisses in displeasure.{/n} "Sift through that beast's inferior implants again? I would not have done so even once if I didn't have certain... plans. It seems they have come to fruition, and so, the animal is no longer worth my attention."

47f46760-dfb7-4957-984f-ef037a713fbb.Text: {n}Despite the Haemonculus's response, the Proctor steps forward to shield Glaito from the xenos.{/n}

d57fb3f6-7ec3-40cd-95ca-860aad99ca68.Text: {n}Tervantias gives you a look of confusion.{/n} "Why would I, specimen?"

267911ec-d650-445e-8256-83de0a9d1c79.Text: "An absurd question befitting your small-minded kind. The Haemonculi are artists of anguish and the masters of flesh. The delvers into unexplored sources of pain. The greatest among their people. My head holds a brilliant intellect, my hands command power over life and death, my body is the pinnacle of surgical discipline. Our minds hold the knowledge of hundreds of generations."

5ed6591f-5c74-4a8b-8e66-f946c7c4d200.Text: "When Sinisthoria reigned over the Cult of the Fatal Thirst, the Proselytes behaved with more respect, but the senior Succubus has since withdrawn into the shadows. Now Keykeross reigns in the arena, and Tazarra leads the raids. An insolent hag and a presumptuous nonentity, a perfect match... As soon as Tazarra drew her final breath, Keykeross's ambitions doubled. She became utterly insufferable."

fc2c7fb3-6b5d-43c4-a616-3c575d7246a4.Text: {n}With an irritated hiss, Tervantias waves a hand and nearly slashes your face with his bladed fingers. His voice clangs as sharply as a guillotine:{/n} "No, specimen."

6a700c82-caa7-4501-ae76-886b8ee5a182.Text: {n}Tervantias' mechanical limbs start to wave with excitement.{/n} "I recognise the mark of the Chtonos's exquisite feeding. What an honour it is for you to be the vessel with which my marvellous creation satisfies its thirst and to give your modest life force so it may be transformed by an energy converter... Fear not, specimen, it is within my power to reverse the effects of its touch."

95de2983-7902-4779-9dab-2edc483b27c1.Text: {n}Jae turns to you with a grim smile on her face.{/n} "Well, shereen... I don't know if we should be celebrating our victory or our final moments. One way or another, we'd better get sloshed. No time like the present — let's head straight to our hideout at the Shriekers' den."

b80df87c-1b5d-4868-a0b0-48c4513398fd.Text: "Still, the specimen's endurance leaves much to be desired. I estimate the irreversible collapse of the cardiovascular system will occur in four to seven cycles of consciousness — a curious yet altogether predictable effect of implanting the psy-stifler. I will perform a more detailed analysis of the organic damage after the specimen's dissection."

d8c9e861-3e2a-4ddb-8a64-dbcf0a65d8b8.Text: "I estimate the irreversible collapse of the cardiovascular system will occur in seven or more cycles of consciousness — a curious yet altogether predictable reaction to implanting the psy-stifler. I will perform a more detailed analysis of the organic damage after the specimen's dissection."

15a887fe-d616-4037-9c18-92711412a18e.Text: {n}The Haemonculus digs through the chunks of flesh with the enthusiasm of a hungry vulture. Finally, he snaps,{/n} "Good materials. Good specimen. Bring me more!"

30fc6b6f-f9c7-4c72-b2ad-6bdab81447fd.Text: {n}Tervantias examines the bloodied body parts with lascivious interest, then he rips an organ out of his own chest, adds it to the trophies, and hisses in satisfaction,{/n} "An interesting composition. An unusual set of starting parameters that can be strengthened by an original mixture of essences. This will be a mighty beast... I will call it the Anguish Prospector! You have done well, specimen, and for that you will be rewarded."

eb3bcc47-9b5d-4f07-a8c2-bd0eeb174c2f.Text: "Praise be to the Exalted One! Shereen, I thought you'd up and pegged it and left me in this shithole."

61e5512d-1c6f-4345-a3b4-cfae0445878d.Text: "Silence, specimen! Or I will take your speech organs and your head."

a84fdcb8-321c-49ef-8286-aa5640d5f857.Text: "And after all this, you decided to grovel before the master of flesh? How very... primitive, elantach."

7d8b1f94-126e-4f8a-8f7d-c821fba131f5.Text: "Who knows, Asuryani, who knows..." {n}The xenos makes a chuckling sound.{/n}

2fe2855f-7a0a-4c84-9e53-7f9fede7dc54.Text: {n}The Haemonculus thinks for a moment.{/n} "The mon-keigh male who exhausted his body beyond recovery? I kept him in the pen, but his attempts to escape to search for you grew so irritating that I cast him out. I overheard the servants whispering that they told him to check the Mangled Sector. Quite the devious trick. I approve."

76268cf3-62be-4657-a370-218a818da2aa.Text: "The Chtonos was an interesting experiment, one that could convert the life forces of its victims into fuel. But it was a flawed, disobedient specimen that escaped." {n}He glances at you mockingly.{/n} "I do not recommend escaping, specimen. The pain from the transformation only stops after I inject the blocker. And I only do it at the end of the procedure. Do you wish to spend the rest of your existence with the sensation of your skin melting and your bones snapping?"

ec4f3a24-db5b-48b0-9eb0-e0134d7e701d.Text: "I recommend pain as a means of pacification. And you can take his armour — I found it entirely unintriguing." {n}Tervantias hands you a bone key.{/n}

93aaf8db-19e4-43c1-8566-59f52ce947d4.Text: "The flesh master is mad enough to help us escape in favour of his own unholy designs. But the price, elantach, will be unfair and terrible."

ba35f71a-b9d7-4696-8d22-ffad6531a559.Text: {n}Tervantias smiles acidly.{/n} "Very well. I will release... one specimen. As for which one it will be, the choice is yours."

bcac2f66-0051-47b7-ad3c-96649ef55238.Text: {n}Jae coughs violently.{/n} "H-help from you? You think anyone will believe that after your foul experiments?" {n}Jae touches the scar on her neck and coughs again.{/n}

859ccf1d-2159-40b6-8725-d385bcb6b3a6.Text: "Are you aware of the beautiful variety of essences that can be extracted from the psychic energy of a dying sentient creature? Of the ways shades of torment and methods of termination alter an essence's properties? This is the great alchemy of death and transformation!"

db293bcf-4400-4a9c-bcf0-5f73e7e227ce.Text: "You should be careful what you wish for, xenos."

37f84dd0-d0e1-4e6f-a01c-b69df89c2884.Text: "And so unravel the rotten threads in the tapestry of fate. Elantach, here is the true nature of the Dark Ones, a lie hidden behind sweet promises. Having learned from a cruel mistake, I foresaw this outcome."

17597809-13c0-4cca-9e34-baba604237c8.Text: "We have heard the xenos call us inferior, primitive creatures so many times. But they behave like petty nobles from a backwater planet, ingratiating themselves with the powerful, humiliating the weak, disposing of rivals through dirty means."

c3c17506-c8f1-484c-a396-739aae264e57.Text: {n}Jae's mouth twists, and she looks ready to unleash a torrent of profanity in the Haemonculus's face, but she stops herself and swallows her ire. With her head bowed, the smuggler lies down again under the xenos's knife.{/n}

287c789b-e983-4276-93a6-85f938ca3a58.Text: "So your original plan would have still had us all dead. You self-dissected creep."

091ef54b-0a78-4428-b22d-84b8065e9701.Text: "I grew this specimen specifically for you, mon-keigh. During your interrogation, it intoxicated your feeble senses to limit unnecessary resistance. What a curious experiment it was. I usually extract control worms from specimens posthumously. You possess some degree of bodily fortitude."

c6873955-d191-4daf-8656-82d3713d3dde.Text: {n}Yrliet gives you a concerned look.{/n} "Your memory must have been weakened by the deleterious influence of the controlling worm. The Archons' court condemned him."

b297bbfb-95a1-4bbd-9c2e-caa525a27eb4.Text: {n}Yrliet gives you a concerned look.{/n} "Your memory must have been weakened by the deleterious influence of the controlling worm. You personally {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_RTSentMarazhaiToArena}condemned him{/d}."

5c25470c-b106-4741-988a-505d0662216d.Text: "Shereen, are you really still trying to find logic in this ashmag's actions?"

4c7303e6-7e88-43a8-b9dd-6e2739641808.Text: {n}Cassia nods briefly and whispers,{/n} "Know your enemy, and then crush him... This is a tactic I will remember."

742eb962-e445-4680-8e5c-45c0ed480099.Text: "Kae-morag, elantach! Do you not get enough monsters in this accursed city?"

934c9cc0-6362-460b-9fe4-84eec121689a.Text: "She was claimed by my patrons from the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest. I hear they sent her to the streets of the Chasm to teach her what it means to be a Drukhari. She has many harsh lessons in suffering ahead of her."

c67c0dee-a49a-409d-b026-2fdad93d3081.Text: {n}The Haemonculus's limbs react with an excited clatter of blades.{/n} "I have few equals in Commorragh. My knowledge is vast, and it goes beyond the mysteries of flesh and essences. I have observed many dysjunctions where the destructive energies of the unreal erupted here in the {g|Encyclopedia:Webway}Webway{/g}... I have studied that devastating force and learned to harness it."

b4aa8304-e7e9-4ed9-88ab-434ada38d47d.Text: "Hold a moment! Off on your merry way, are you? Well, good for you, but what about me and my azhi-damned problem?" {n}Jae points to the scar on her throat.{/n}

3903f380-1c4d-48fb-9274-1f62b648461d.Text: "The mon-keigh male with a consistent connection to the veil. Beautiful endurance for pain. His stubbornness produces high-grade essences of torment positively frothing with agony. Wait until he is expended, and you may have whatever is left."

614cbdb1-2b0e-41ef-9398-9ae30a4ddd39.Text: "The female with an exceptionally strong connection to the veil as well as a number of rare mon-keigh mutations, most notably a third eye? I am studying the influence of complete isolation from the veil and the outside world on the specimen's abilities, sanity, and physical condition. She no longer screams inside her reservoir, but she is certainly still alive, and I am not yet ready to conclude the experiment."

857cf32a-0fd8-4827-b517-b15f3eb7f3c6.Text: {n}The xenos lets out another nasty chuckle.{/n} "Very well, specimen. When you are no longer useful, I will perform another test on you and prove it is not so."

976d7ce2-c3a8-4bdf-9b49-923cafa6799f.Text: "Ah, the volunteer specimen. I equipped her with an experimental device to isolate her mind from the veil. The specimen performs menial tasks around the laboratory and serves as a willing source of essences. She is allowed to choose her own torment, be it fracturing her bones with vibro waves, placing herself inside a capsule of extreme heat, implanting an electro-scarab under her skin, or shutting off the psy-stifler. Not once has the specimen chosen this last option."

2431ae1c-85a4-4417-b299-5590605ca9b9.Text: {n}The Haemonculus notices Marazhai.{/n} "Dracon Aezyrraesh. After you went against the Archon of the Reaving Tempest, you decided to violate the wishes of the Archon of the Black Heart as well? You were thrown into the arena to die. You show wretched incompetence by defying your masters."

d06d4848-d8fb-49a8-8951-6365623a2b40.Text: "In mere moments, your heart valve will be ripped apart by the spasms. I could replace it, but... it would simply be too tedious to drag you back from beyond the brink for the third time. Farewell, specimen."

99e605d4-2dc8-4894-8e61-926a2412cf23.Text: {n}With a look of disgust at Tervantias, Jae reluctantly says,{/n} "Perhaps you're right, shereen. This butcher doesn't seem the type to wash his hands between procedures."

1f94c830-ebf3-4fc9-beff-58647380c863.Text: "No! I'm dying! DYING, don't you understand? I want this ashmag to put everything back the way it was! Now!"

7afaa669-7b48-48cc-a700-a880e2c199bc.Text: "Is that so? To the void with you, Your Precious {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. If you don't want to help me, why in the grox's crotch should I help you? I'll take care of my own problems, and you can deal with your own from now on!"

c98acafd-c155-47d6-a3d2-49fbdbaaa7ad.Text: {n}An inaudible yet deafening sound invades your mind. Your eardrums are ready to burst. The only sound you can hear is the xenos's limbs chittering and his ice-cold voice.{/n} "Abandon any illusion of choice. You will do my will. And, if you stop resisting and start behaving like a good specimen, you may eventually receive my help in escaping Commorragh."

f3b5b92d-77a2-4865-89fc-6363ef7ba5bc.Text: "My presence offends you, I see? Good." {n}Marazhai sneers and looks around.{/n} "You have made yourself quite comfortable here in the Chasm. Is this where you have kept the things that you dared not bring to the Spire of the Reaving Tempest? It must be vexing, having to abandon it all as you flee the Cult's wrath..."

d859d096-037e-4246-a84a-99c2f9ccb81a.Text: {n}One of Tervantias's limbs twitches and strikes blindly. Only Marazhai's reflexes save him from a fatal neck wound, but the Haemonculus makes no further attempts to attack — he seems to care more about his substances and instruments than the insufferable Kabalite.{/n}

d63e271f-22da-439f-91aa-bcaa4d7daeba.Text: {n}Tervantias hisses and jerks his fan of limbs fitted with sharp implements.{/n} "Do not make demands of me, specimen. Or I might decide that you are also in need of a collar."

77dd9467-560a-4424-a7d0-2925bdbfe997.Text: {n}A grotesque, spider-like figure looms over you. Its limbs wave frantically, chittering and clicking as they rip something apart then stitch it back together... and you realise its canvas is your flesh. The {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g}'s gaze is indifferent, and his low voice echoes through the room:{/n} "The sample has been extracted. The specimen is alive. Body and mind expected to function within normal parameters, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}."

fecb9c06-1094-4f8c-a9e0-f59246202b00.Text: "The control worm in your nervous system detected my proximity. It signalled it was dying by injecting a lethal dose of hallucinogenic euphoriants into your bloodstream. A resourceful individual."

7c8cd4fa-f882-407a-9b53-89d749a3cda9.Text: {n}The Drukhari holds up the pale maggot, the same one you saw in Marazhai's hands. As you watch, the tool appendages perform a swift dissection: the maggot's flesh bursts under the scalpel-like claw and blossoms into a disgusting, slimy flower. The xenos's slow manner of speaking creates an unnerving dissonance with the frantic movements of his limbs.{/n}

3577a332-03ee-424c-94bd-33c0be2b90fe.Text: {n}Marazhai's face suddenly changes. His mocking grin gone, he fixes his gaze on the Haemonculus.{/n} "Into the Spire of the Reaving Tempest? To hide under the wing of Yremeryss, an Archon fallen into disgrace? What an imprudent choice. You should run away from her and her troubles, unless you are somehow connected to her crime."

3f205499-8d09-4279-8de7-da6dea682029.Text: "I rarely use positive reinforcement. But your behaviour has been obedient, so why not?" {n}The xenos reaches one of his smaller appendages inside one of his own body cavities, pulls out a bundle wrapped in skin, and tosses it at you without looking.{/n} "This no longer interests me. Take it."

616f36b4-94a0-46e1-b091-69d784d83cbf.Text: "You are absolutely correct, specimen. I am Tervantias the Archmachinator, Haemonculus and the conductor of this place that staggers the imagination and soul. My Anatomical Opera."

6b10596c-c283-4079-91cc-5d02554d65b0.Text: "The Arebennian urged me to pay attention to your allegedly extremely gifted self, specimen. Let us see if you make a good tool."

36f265da-7628-482a-a101-d72d6ef8e640.Text: {n}The xenos lets out a strange sound that almost resembles a scoff.{/n} "This information should not burden your undeveloped mind. The Arebennian told me enough to give you the chance to enter my Anatomical Opera. That is all you need to know."

3af21c61-684d-40ec-b671-59fca2c301dd.Text: "Lately, they have shown arrogance and disrespect toward me. They want to rise in the eyes of the Archon and belittle me. They rank their tasteless flesh dances above my art! They come to my abode to gawk at my treasured secrets! It is time the Chasm was reminded that Wyches, too, can bleed."

9d6d4c7e-59be-466a-a8ad-08de625bfd91.Text: "'Do business'?" {n}The Haemonculus looks puzzled.{/n} "I will do no business with you. I will use you. You survived a battle in the arena, which means you have uncommon parameters for your kind. You are a lesser organism, true, but the towering heights of my wisdom make it difficult to distinguish between your inferiority and the inferiority of most of my kin."

5c0df6bf-08d7-476e-80ff-d66525d4d567.Text: "At present, I am working on a Grotesque of previously unknown power built from the most exquisite and exotic body parts from strong fighters. Specimen, should you ever see the corpse of a fine warrior or a mighty creature lying at your feet, cut out the best part and bring it to me."

db8b4232-6454-4af0-8972-40fadb6ab59a.Text: "Cooperation will increase your odds of survival. As long as you continue to be of use, I will maintain your organic parts and perhaps even let you play with some of my less significant samples."

bc5a772a-fc03-4d03-b216-d6eba092e62f.Text: "The response is acceptable. If you behave like a good specimen, mon-keigh, you may eventually receive my help in escaping Commorragh."

b9782a9d-2596-4af1-8020-06cdc67feafa.Text: {n}A sharp claw touches your chin, pierces your skin, finds an imperceptibly thin nerve — and your body convulses in pain.{/n} "This response is unacceptable. Focus, mon-keigh, or I will make you into either a Wrack or a divan on which I host orgies. You will be far more useful in either of those forms."

0b091d38-0bff-4441-94b8-190208a4f281.Text: "You will serve me. Such is life in the spires."

3132ee64-6c2a-40d1-96b3-7c995947ac0b.Text: {n}Tervantias pauses before responding, as if dissecting your question inside his head.{/n} "Ask."

dfbb8387-e6b6-45cf-9287-86c59c013e26.Text: "Wyches rule the arenas — this is the way of the spires. They are lethal, brides of our dead gods. When they enter the arena, the crowd writhes with ecstasy, but this is a rare sight. Typically, their fosterlings, the Bloodstained Proselytes, oversee the butchery. These are the best killers and athletes who serve the Cult... Such arrogant upstarts. They have been undefeated for far too long."

f22c1c90-808f-4341-b5db-2b6a1ae61907.Text: "My servant harvests meat in the Chasm and delivers it to their bloody performances. I improve it with augments and stimulants to make it interesting enough so the Wyches will enjoy killing it. Sometimes, I indulge them with little treats — biomachines or beasts moulded by my surgical genius."

aae71c0c-60f8-4ff2-8181-d02edc377f0b.Text: {n}You can hear impatience creaking in Tervantias's voice as he says,{/n} "Have you enough information now, specimen?"

0a9ce759-c9ed-4af5-86d7-9b2431943ad2.Text: {n}With a gurgling sound, the xenos slowly yet steadily moves his sharp finger to your eye, closer and closer, almost touching... then stops with a sigh.{/n} "Not now. Perhaps later."

8a348053-cc1f-43d5-a74b-6eb86316a351.Text: {n}The xenos thoughtfully clicks his appendage studded with dozens of needle-thin stingers.{/n}

26794ffd-aa7c-4f07-9258-e2c0fa65e084.Text: "I have created psy-stiflers to keep the space around this spire intact! I have touched knowledge so ancient..." {n}Tervantias abruptly ends his speech, casts a suspicious look at you, and then snaps,{/n} "It is not necessary for you to know this, specimen."

384548e4-dc56-4647-83ab-a90612af8333.Text: "Evisceration is one aspect of my most respected art." {n}His scalpel-fingers scrape together with a hushed metallic shriek.{/n}

0c4117ea-6459-4f4a-9ed8-57b5626f51fe.Text: {n}Tervantias's voice is filled with loathing.{/n} "Your insight is astounding, specimen. But have you noticed that you have also doomed yourself?"

32246f88-b603-428b-b6ed-1f1d55e8658a.Text: "I cannot transport them to my new sanctuary. You may take them. I have unlocked the containment sarcophagi for dangerous specimens. Go and inspect them. Some of your servants may still be alive. But do not allow them to use their abilities until I have left the Anatomical Opera!"

a362f131-66f0-4185-8a75-521e3bc39334.Text: {n}Tervantias dismissively throws you a tiny object.{/n} "This is the key to the device worn by the volunteer specimen. The one that suppresses her connection to the veil. I wonder if it has already caused permanent physiological damage. No matter. You will only require the key if the specimen resists. She has always been free to remove the device herself."

ef7c9324-94ae-4ac2-881f-154ddd51c10a.Text: "My pens are filled with captives taken in raids. You may pick any specimen you wish, even one whose organs I have not yet extracted."

5c47e58e-8dcc-45be-adcc-9459205d8508.Text: "What a confident specimen." {n}A thin smile spreads across his lips.{/n} "Do it. Kill yourself. I can always reanimate your body. But will I?"

7d3bab4a-7708-4a5d-bd39-e50c952fcb05.Text: {n}With a loud click of his scissor-like fingers, Tervantias voice turns ghoulish,{/n} "Let's see what kind of interesting damage your body has taken and which parts of your miserable organics can be improved without inflicting any substantial harm on your sanity. Try not to scream — some specimens end up tearing their vocal cords during this procedure. Then again... you will scream whether you want to or not."

adaaf19b-ed32-48a1-931f-06a7621241c0.Text: "Oh, but there is more... I hope Keykeross and Sinisthoria are now writhing in horror at the mere thought that their headless subordinates have lost the Kabalite who was sentenced to death by Nazrakhei himself. First they decided to play at charity by making me a Proselyte, and now... they let me slip through their fingers. Oh, I wish I could see the Succubus's face when she was given the news."

6a1fe6d3-49bc-4f1b-80a2-56d045514383.Text: {n}Tervantias glares at Marazhai.{/n} "You were not in a position to know about the Archon's plans before, much less now."

cfbfee1e-5e58-46da-91b1-e3f07c4f555c.Text: "Then find yourself other fighters. The Chasm has enough prisoners, mercenaries, and gladiators. My specimens are not yours to waste."

723f742e-22b3-4cee-bf57-221b810ff507.Text: {n}The Haemonculus mutters furiously and haughtily,{/n} "I should have stopped wasting time on this idiocy long ago. All those pathetic simpletons did was weaken my focus and distract me from my masterpiece. At last, I can devote all of myself to it!"

4154ba2c-07ba-4920-ad10-753a7d4bb68f.Text: "Good specimen." {n}He pulls his claw out of your flesh, and you notice a heavy drop of blood hanging from it.{/n} "Very responsive to pain stimuli."

6e26174e-1aed-4bae-a932-7705a080d148.Text: "How can you be certain of that? You have not yet tried... but you are about to."

e16e3289-6a86-45e9-8b1f-728386fe1d7a.Text: "Are you trying to be resilient?" {n}The xenos's smile grows wider.{/n} "Do you wish to put my talents to the test? You have not the slightest understanding of who stands before you. I am the choirmaster of agony." {n}A second claw, this one tipped with a thin and impossibly sharp needle, pierces your forehead slightly above the bridge of your nose, reaching through bone as easily as through air. For a few moments, the needle wanders inside your brain, causing strange sensations throughout your body, and then...{/n}

b467045b-f6c0-4cd4-bdfd-9451a2c6c2f9.Text: {n}The darkness is dispelled by a sliver of light — the glinting scalpel in Tervantias's hand. The Haemonculus offers you a crooked smile.{/n} "I can keep tossing you from one side of death to the other for as long as I so desire. But I doubt that reanimating you again will be quite as amusing. I would suggest not incurring my displeasure."

d89a5038-e376-4f92-b4bd-cb00cec900a6.Text: "I made your body perish... for a short time. And then I bade it function again. Such manipulations are trifles for one such as I. Even if you were to get hacked into pieces, I could bring them back to life. Although I would not waste my time on you — you are not worth the effort."

207f8bab-6b76-4b5a-bb38-0ed7436d9c0e.Text: "I see that you are incorrigible, specimen. My expectations of you were higher than this. If you are incapable of following the simplest of commands, there is no reason to try to use you for something more important. I will find you a more practical application." {n}One of his mechanical appendages bristles with a crown of barbed hooks that reach for your face, then inside it.{/n}

23e28460-c7d2-44b2-bf1f-015257fb0c7d.Text: {n}You cannot move your arms. The xenos smiles faintly and cocks his head, watching as convulsions rack your every limb.{/n} "Mon-keigh pain signals are so impractical. They drown out every other impulse in your brain — cognitive processes, motor patterns. This is indeed the only advantage you have over most other races — you are better at feeling pain."

0e788884-7dc8-467c-95e6-198841232390.Text: {n}The xenos suddenly lets out a spiteful cackle, a surprisingly lively reaction for such a cold creature.{/n} "Which made for an unpleasant surprise for Dracon Marazhai. Former Dracon, that is. That foolish whelp expected less of you, and you {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_TrialFailed}humiliated him{/d}. It gave me something to think about. A good specimen."

de61ea93-3c54-4ba8-a2f9-a002647767fb.Text: "The servants are always dragging worthless trifles in here. I have no use for them. Find yourself a club or a sharp stick suited to your abilities. You could try something more advanced... assuming you are not afraid of accidentally killing yourself with it."

53b9bd80-eb93-4070-87d7-d6292d67549e.Text: An awkward and unimaginably hideous pistol with an uncomfortable grip of unknown brand and origin. This deadly abomination of a weapon could have been made by a human or just as likely by any of the numerous xenos races.

92bf5f7d-201e-4f1f-84a1-b8c2b33e7f5f.Text: A heavy weapon capable of raining fragmentation projectiles, grafted onto the biomechanical body of the Chtonos by the cruel Haemonculus. Its magnetic radiator feeds on the liquid essence gathered from the bodies of the monster's victims.

d5a3f5ef-682f-45d3-b104-27620e0d0766.Text: The disembodied head of Commissar: the daring leader of captives from the Imperium.

010bb729-bf18-45ce-9aba-a2c4580f5813.Text: A bag of strange dust that shimmers with impossible shades of colours that should not exist.

5e395146-0615-4a23-afde-fa9d5b2e3945.Text:
A hastily scribbled note saying:
"You've pissed off the Wyches big time, you won't escape their fury. We need a plan. Meet me at the Pit. The Emperor protects.
Commissar."

6854403c-abd7-4004-890b-c344af6296bb.Text: This prism-shaped xeno-artefact is made from a black metal that is oddly cold to the touch. The strange device has no visible seams, buttons, or holes.

c2593a19-484f-40bd-a088-d3b44618c5c2.Text: Drukhari carapace armour remoulded for the mon-keigh frame. A built-in agoniser sends carefully calibrated pain impulses to the wearer's nervous system, stimulating the spinal cord and enhancing reflexes.

547a686b-760f-4452-b69b-62d483acc804.Text: An exquisite shardcarbine. It is light enough to be wielded by the great raptor of Commorragh's skies: the Scourge. Now it belongs to a more worthy wielder.

fd32ceee-8836-4e91-bff4-afd03f26b19d.Text: A cape infused with magnetic threads controlled by a crystal matrix in the clasp. A servant was skinned to make it, as a punishment for failure. The servant's eyes are forever watching the wearer's back, as the Haemonculus did not grant him the release of death or the right to be mercifully unaware of his miserable condition.

9cc27d9c-7bc6-4f62-98e8-86349e0df60e.Text: A key made of osseous substance covered in a myriad of tiny spikes. It can only be used if fed with the right type of blood.

a0448270-38b5-4e04-8cfa-384dd56ea477.Text: An unremarkable and weak pistol. The engraving covering its surface is far more valuable than any meagre stopping power it might possess.

5c9fade3-81f0-4bf3-9772-26e1a4b70abc.Text: "Mend this creature, we are taking it with us."

66b23099-083a-4698-a2e2-90a13794fd28.Text: "Pasqal, would you like to study this device?"

620ad0eb-24e8-474b-89ec-bd8b1c46b2d3.Text: "If you think this thing is alive, you may end its suffering."

3b7043ea-1f7a-4f10-9234-59b97639d4f8.Text: "Is this thing more than a perversion and an outrage to you?"

63ca1c35-a964-4cb7-aa7e-8853c259d8f1.Text: "You are an Explorator. Study it before it gives up the ghost."

6e597d49-a49f-4a76-a21e-6127ed6ba269.Text: "I will not hurt you any more."

748c37b6-717c-4d3c-aff9-07eda8f52cf7.Text: {n}The biomechanical creature is flailing its limbs faintly. Its body is broken and bears the signs of combat, but it seems no one is planning to repair it. You can see the glistening flesh under the cracked carapace and the bunches of wires that permeate it. The armour plates rise heavily and the creature emits a wistful, creaking sigh full of regret.{/n}

f2f494b7-d70c-47d4-af60-9ab5856c7530.Text: {n}The claw on Pasqal's mechadendrite clangs loudly. The visor emits a series of clicks, switching the observation spectrum. Pasqal's hands automatically reach for the combi-tool on his belt even as his eyes closely watch the dying creature.{/n}

c5848347-1980-4a89-b47c-517a05283ea6.Text: {n}Pasqal suddenly freezes and takes a little step back.{/n} "Process interrupted. An operational collision has been detected."

72f1ad33-b264-4b24-b8df-1a40cb1fabff.Text: {n}Cassia's entire body is shivering.{/n} "The colours of this creature... it is oozing with stained crimson shades and the tenebrous blackness of suffering. It is as if this construct was purposefully made to absorb the most dreadful colours that living things can exude. But how is that possible?"

431a037e-e68a-4ef0-9aed-3890b4208e08.Text: {n}Every limb of the creature, the hard ones on skeletal paws and the flexible ones on metallic cords, is equipped with a variety of implements similar to surgical tools. The jagged circular saws, twisted drills, and vibrating monoscalpels promise unbearable pain.{/n}

431c2140-1630-4f33-8f60-37d9c854f82b.Text: {n}If there are any functions in the design of this creature beyond maiming and brutally killing opponents, they elude you.{/n}

8430e030-dbe0-4b33-906e-a711311ede94.Text: {n}The impact lands on a cracked armour segment, and a wet, rumbling howl erupts from the guts of the mechanism, a sound that could easily be confused with a painful groan. The monster's limbs twitch in fear and retract under its belly.{/n}

d4ad4da4-d167-4541-ac6e-407a0265a51e.Text: {n}Pasqal does not say a word, but you think you see his face wrinkling in disgust and disapproval under his respirator.{/n}

a92a8e90-0289-42a0-9d03-bf297aa3bbf1.Text: "Void take you, Heydari!" {n}The women glare at each other but then relax and chuckle quietly.{/n}

1baed1d8-962d-4594-bc07-a5cdc6334057.Text: "Request approved." {n}Pasqal eagerly unfolds his mechadendrites and they all rush toward the monster. A shrieking drill cuts deep into the armour, while a claw hungrily snaps off chunks of the flesh pierced with strands of metal wire. The creature thrashes and wheezes but cannot escape the merciless vivisection. The collected samples are sent to a portable analyser and the Tech-Priest's visor clicks, recording the procedure in pict-images.{/n}

77d6b76c-1a13-4622-8f67-8d9d71c6f9c3.Text: "This unit is under the influence of conflicting impulses. The operational vector of cognition dictates the necessity of studying this subject. The operational vector of obeying the Omnissiah and His Universal Laws dictates the necessity of recoiling from the subject and purifying it."

7b6124dc-bc7b-4aad-be0d-c4b63cc3e394.Text: "The categorisation is correct. The object is a perversion and an outrage, one dangerously close to the creation of the anathematised Abominable Intelligence."

bc8f45d6-9869-48b3-9d1f-ba6fa8c3bf4f.Text: "Request approved as doctrinally correct." {n}Pasqal leans over the creature and the drill whirrs, its sound even, soothing, and right. The Tech-Priest's voice vibrates with shrill otherworldly frequencies:{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued, let your suffering be discontinued!"

658677b9-2d9c-43f9-8a37-aa5c62f64201.Text: "Request approved as doctrinally correct." {n}Pasqal leans over the creature and the drill whirrs, sounding shrill and relentless. The Tech-Priest's voice hums with the ice-cold determination of a divine vivisector:{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued, let ignorance be discontinued!"

fb9cd209-9e82-4495-9812-91d36cbfb1ef.Text: "Request approved as doctrinally correct." {n}Pasqal leans over the creature and the drill whirrs with wrath and fury. The Tech-Priest's voice boils like lava, ringing with the promise of divine punishment:{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued, let corruption be purged!"

36d2eaa7-1b7c-45a2-b908-37740b610cf7.Text: {n}The creature responds with a series of choking and snarling sounds. After a moment, as if realising that its language is not clear to you, it extends a fighting limb in your direction in a menacing gesture. The message is clear: "I am a warrior. I am a killer."{/n}

6b424831-cd54-4457-ac05-100b7b2952b7.Text: {n}The creature emits a series of wheezing sounds. Was it an answer, moans of agony, or just the normal rumbling of its mechanism? There is no way to tell.{/n}

2e9d9438-a6f8-4f10-9e28-6b763488cb5f.Text: {n}The creature's servo-motors howl as they send the last remaining energy into its body. One of the limbs lunges at you, but the charge is not enough for the strike to reach its target.{/n}

f3f374f8-6771-4fbf-98f6-1c11ae337225.Text: {n}Something bursts in the creature's gut with a quiet squelch and a puddle of oily ichor spreads from under its belly.{/n}

44aacd9a-ef10-49d4-a5fb-476236b79793.Text: "Presenting a hypothesis. Existing under the oppression of the Haemonculus was unbearable and painful even for such an unholy construct."

9e14fd2e-ced2-4c4e-b393-fe965ebd224d.Text: "The nature of the damage indicates that the unit has been in combat. I hypothesise that its constructor sent it into the arena. Based on its current condition, the result of the combat tests was unsatisfactory. Otherwise, the unit would have been repaired."

f65c3857-fe19-4e11-ad58-8f8bf4ccb941.Text: "The creatures in this place only understand the language of pain, shereen. Let's smash its head in before something happens that we can't undo."

253ea8d1-8902-4ded-a158-6c5364b97762.Text: "The Dark Ones are caught in a cycle of torment, desperately seeking pleasure in the suffering of others. This machine is but an instrument of their endless desire, a symbol of what they are willing to do to slake the thirst and fear that consume them."
