6a357b7f-f6ec-4bd2-8a2e-c19b9751d316.Text: "What an amusing plaything! You can sing me your silly tale when I am pulling the nerves out of your flesh. You will have plenty of time — I intend to savour every moment."

4a638362-bca4-4b5e-a7a1-cfc30e386342.Text: "I expected something like this. At least we are no longer in the arena — there are far fewer xenos here capable of opposing us."

de7a1833-f786-426e-934a-ba1a631b039d.Text: "A Farseer... Yremeryss had the temerity to bring a Farseer to Commorragh, only to feed it to some scum from the Dark City's gutters?"

61653fda-6f28-42cf-8378-3faa53fbb40a.Text: "A mon-keigh serving as a messenger of the Reaving Tempest? Preposterous!"

cca980b3-5f34-4510-8a07-099e1f7a8010.Text: "I see you have not wasted your time in the Dark City, and you have properly studied our... way of thinking." {n}Smirking contentedly, Marazhai places his hands on his blade grips.{/n}

750f6f90-377d-42f7-9b7b-4f874bbdf013.Text: "It would be an outrageous stunt... An extravagant one... But not impossible. Whether or not the mon-keigh lies, the Wounded Skies desire to ally themselves with the Reaving Tempest. And achieving it will be easier if the Poisonous Whisper dies here!" {n}The two xenos simultaneously go for their weapons.{/n}

2a208d78-fc44-4117-a1be-b1f3baf0dd71.Text: "You are most entertaining, mon-keigh. How can bloodshed ruin a celebration?"

65e5c5fa-eecb-4a1e-b39a-232914443260.Text: "Step aside, Poisonous Whisper! I will have the first meal!"

2ed16863-a6e0-4787-a52f-d7defa58753c.Text: "The outer halls of the Spire of the Reaving Tempest. The esteemed Kabal invited us to indulge in a small celebration. The Poisonous Whisper came as their desired allies. As for the Wounded Skies... I have no clue why one would invite them."

1cb8ec39-8fcd-4b40-9407-6b236ed9cfc7.Text: {n}The xenos casually points at the writhing figure.{/n} "This knowledge is far beyond you, but I see no harm in humouring a soon-to-be corpse. This one is an exquisite delight: a Farseer. Nothing can compare to their heightened psychic emanations. Most delectable."

f7f8d959-cf20-4a57-b5b6-d8a47d88e478.Text: {n}The giant looks down at you.{/n} "My name is Ulfar, and I am a proud Space Wolf of the Allfather."

a243f500-c4ec-4c93-9f8c-f9c1db1d9725.Text: {n}A bestial growl comes from behind you.{/n} "Did the jester bring me here to listen to these dung-ridden beasts practise their meagre wits? These blathering xenos are making me angrrry... I'll kill them."

6ff0c33c-5e26-4e00-91ed-4b173bda0edd.Text: "It fascinates me how pathetic and transparent the intrigue of their lesser kind can be. However, I have grown weary of this one's tales. I wish to taste {mf|his|her} anguish."

789191e2-2e16-48ea-ad5a-cbbdb4b60944.Text: {n}Ulfar lets out a ferocious roar and his eyes become bloodshot. Spraying spittle like a raging beast, he bellows mournfully,{/n} "I don't want your eternity! How can I claim the glory of a warrior's death if I am forever to trudge through honourless battles, to know of no taste but that of the putrid blood of inhumans spilt at their own behest?"

8ed97f83-be82-47c4-837d-4eb36dae41a7.Text: "No... no no no... we were supposed to escape! What is this place? Are we the main course at this shindig?"

574144c9-7c1e-4b86-bea7-5a95827e3e9b.Text: "You insolent mon-keigh! I will cut pieces out of your liver one by one and feed them to you as I relish your screams. Believe me, I intend to savour every moment!"

f79af47b-dcb0-4b65-8e7c-c7ad5cc975b1.Text: {n}The red-haired Drukhari smiles faintly.{/n} "Let's see if you can make the savouring last longer than a handful of moments this time..."

9e4eda99-116a-44d6-8de2-dbad096c63e3.Text: "That's enough out of you. This habit of talking to pets is ridiculous. It is time we toyed with {mf|him|her} instead: the old plaything is nearly spent and its pain has grown stale."

ad9dcc89-98e3-4c52-b15a-1a7fca204e68.Text: {n}You can sense the despair and the blind rage boiling inside Ulfar's chest. They are trying to gnaw their way out and you know the exact words that will drive them down the shortest path. This knowledge delights you.{/n}

c5bc5f0f-6932-4851-a3ba-fa74e8178c5d.Text: {n}It is hard to tell whether these two xenos are trading insults out of genuine enmity or merely as a result of their foul temperament so typical of inhumans.{/n}

61272f37-2cbe-4137-8c37-db1092ed42d9.Text: "Let the nonentities run away. Marazhai, take us where we need to go."

abe3898c-0afb-4003-9a45-771b97387dd0.Text: "Everyone inside is dead. I need this boat. You live or you die — your choice."

5e142acd-3949-4dc6-b4d6-602854eaac7b.Text: "I need to get to the top of the Spire of the Reaving Tempest."

4449afc1-e117-48c0-a211-d16ef91bd3a9.Text: "You are in the presence of Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius. You will be granted the privilege of ferrying me to the apex of the Spire of the Reaving Tempest."

5b573255-675b-4752-8628-bcc91a6fd576.Text: [Shoot one pilot and address the other] "Is your answer the same?"

7d29b5ef-9bc6-4a2c-8fd1-cc7bad4639e1.Text: "I killed all of your little friends inside. Would you like to join them?"

85342a0f-cf8b-4bfa-88e1-8d61e5956282.Text: "Everyone inside is dead. If you take me where I need to go quickly, you will make it back in time to loot the bodies."

2349fc82-45aa-4c75-9d96-1883e1a84157.Text: "Leave while you can. Yrliet, take the helm."

ffe14723-cedc-4724-b2ef-aaab23f9b59d.Text: [Kill them both] "You are surplus to requirements."

433ca807-3e15-402d-bf03-f83840226abb.Text: "It's getting too loud in there. I could go and check on them."

650bc3fc-e802-44d0-9ed8-6e7b793516c2.Text: "You want to join the revelry and leave me here? Stay where you are, they are just enjoying themselves. They could have taken us with them, but no, they had to make us play guards instead. Greedy filthspawn... Look at this! I think a few playthings have slipped away from the festivities!"

2155a0f4-4ad2-4994-9780-3a3101c986dc.Text: "In the event these xenos units refuse to cooperate, there are ways to ensure their obedience. A lobotomy to excise certain parts of the temporal lobes, cauterise the prefrontal cortex, and extend a direct electrode bridge to their somatosensory cortex... A surgery of this kind, if performed without the necessary equipment, will be excruciating, but useful and informative."

0c5207bc-993e-4757-917a-63eb98f88798.Text: {n}A mix of wary disgust and... greedy interest dawns on the faces of both pilots.{/n}

21560070-6030-45df-b521-7777b7dca39d.Text: "I can steer a gondola, elantach. We do not need these pilots."

6ba98578-9e8a-4efb-9d06-dc66f41f0322.Text: {n}You take a glance at the xenos boat. Sure, its design and certain parts appear bizarre but you can still guess their purpose. You could probably steer it.{/n}

9650473b-b78e-4e0a-ba27-e02d622ae073.Text: {n}You take a glance at the xenos boat. The design looks utterly foreign to you. You have a vague idea what some of its parts might do but you do not even want to attempt to guess at the intended purpose of the rest. You need a pilot.{/n}

f46f9cb8-dc6a-42db-b787-d8bda561b436.Text: "Serve as a mon-keigh's chauffeur? I will decline such a questionable diversion. Why don't you come closer and offer me your neck instead, plaything?"

14a4fef3-183d-44e3-938e-bd0fcaa7899f.Text: {n}The Drukhari swallows nervously and gestures invitingly at the gondola.{/n} "Welcome aboard."

ba57b703-8ffe-4650-b9f4-6639f5364e41.Text: {n}The Drukhari triumphantly jabs his finger at his partner.{/n} "I told you something wasn't right in there! Easy, mon-keigh, I have no plans to die today."

94b6f37d-46ca-47e9-a1f3-695e38b914df.Text: "Hmph. Be careful what you wish for, mon-keigh. Very well. I accept your payment. Just give me a moment to dispose of my competitor here."

3a43e79f-6a0b-499a-bea3-0e7d1a3704f5.Text: {n}The pilots catch Yrliet's cold gaze, exchange glances, and take off running without saying a word. The gondola is yours.{/n}

6f5f4fc1-323a-4a8f-a385-ad4583aa9552.Text: "I have piloted these vessels a million times before. We can head for the central spire right now."

13e25ba2-552e-4bb3-aaed-7af39724c6af.Text: {n}Marazhai gives the fleeing pilots a scornful look, one tinged with regret for the missed kill.{/n}

c46ef3e9-d248-44aa-ac9c-c7c4dcf4a82f.Text: {n}Before the less cooperative Drukhari can finish, his more accommodating copilot pushes him into the abyss.{/n} "Now there is room for everyone. Welcome aboard."

f205c21c-9a4a-4ba9-8ec0-1bb85af4c32c.Text: {n}The pilots look at the fresh blood all over your face and clothes, exchange glances, and take off running without saying a word. The gondola is yours.{/n}

723933eb-2d4a-433d-87b8-3e270000b401.Text: {n}Two pilots are already disarmed and under guard by your companions. They give you a haunted look as you approach but do not dare say anything.{/n}

a837831a-2623-4190-84af-8f0c13c9d743.Text: {n}The pilots exchange glances, and one of them says with a nasty smile,{/n} "Are you trying to escape, mon-keigh? Don't you think you are the one in our hands, not the other way around?"

f89744ea-8c49-43d8-8801-152ecf2394af.Text: "The Harlequin brought me here. Do you have any idea why he did that?"

f9453b03-6223-4e06-92f4-792657201f27.Text: "Stop. All your foes are dead. I am your comrade."

f80396ce-5d7d-4171-ba23-ec070931ea87.Text: "Warrior, you honourably dispatched the Emperor's enemies!"

8aedc4cc-75dc-452c-8a90-b2e57d29b674.Text: "What kind of grief must it be, to have nearly cost you your sanity?"

8149d36d-5605-4ebe-a6e3-546ea48c7269.Text: "You have people to fight for. People who need you as you are: a warrior, not a beast."

c27b4d35-4313-4bf5-92d8-58376bf81fb9.Text: "You have a duty to kill the Emperor's enemies, not whomever you please."

5a08df83-cad4-495e-8d2b-32f8c43e4ab9.Text: "If that is your nature, you should embrace it. Even blind destruction can serve a purpose, can't it?"

554568bf-9505-470e-b277-c01572bf0c1b.Text: "We are no longer on the same path. I do not trust you."

0fd5c370-7149-436f-810a-3c46df791889.Text: "I suggest we go and see why Nocturne of Oblivion has dragged us to this place."

b38b3d45-5f7f-42fc-8352-ada9046f76fa.Text: "Surely you won't say no to an opportunity to kill a few xenos together, will you?"

be2ea609-5c68-4670-906b-0f4e2338134d.Text: "I intend to get out of this place. And I can take you with me."

19dc755a-a39b-4774-8240-1a4d13d6e03a.Text: "From what I understand, you have been surviving on your own for a terribly long time. Aren't you tired of being alone?"

b681bbdb-6426-4b3c-8dd5-e3b858e5cd85.Text: "Forget what I said. It was a pleasure to make your acquaintance."

3e517065-81fa-47ba-9941-76a9f74806dc.Text: "You mad beast! You have killed everyone who could have told us anything!"

90e5109b-bd13-44eb-9e41-329b718b0e41.Text: [Aim your weapon] "Stand down! Or you will fall right next to this scum."

e92a4657-3233-4500-9748-a193eebe7dd2.Text: {n}You are staring into the eyes of an animal that enjoys killing. No, it does not enjoy it. It just kills, finding no joy or delight in doing so. It kills because that is its nature.{/n}

29d95419-c08d-4e20-91bb-8211c442e974.Text: {n}Ulfar shakes his head morosely.{/n} "It was not devotion to the Allfather that guided my hand. Only the black malice of Wulfen."

b28c67a5-24ee-430e-83b9-31feb751d93c.Text: {n}Ulfar rumbles grimly,{/n} "Mortal, if you were to know of the bitter taste of Wulfen's malice, you would learn that grief takes no prisoners. Grief claims lives."

e1f7c7f8-b134-4e29-953a-4bee6e448270.Text: "Comrade..." {n}This word has a miraculous effect on the bloodthirsty warrior.{/n}

99c98f00-bf18-4724-85c1-826878d020d4.Text: {n}Like a bolter shot, your commanding cry pierces the shield of bloodthirsty indifference on the giant's face.{/n} "I hear... and... obey..."

2901a12d-d95e-4cbb-b007-cf3f575736bf.Text: "It is the breath of the frost that chills the bones. It is lightless malice born of despair. The curse that preys upon them who have seen too many things and hate with too much heart."

146403ed-f4cd-4d5d-95cb-cfd0483e8061.Text: "Too long have I been here. Too long have I served as a tool of unrighteous wretches — a shameful fate for the Allfather's warrior, and shame is what scorches my soul. When I saw that I had once again become their plaything, that yet another xenos had set me upon his foes... I thought it would go on forever. My mind could not accept the indignity of it, so my mind hid like a coward would. Only thirst remained."

234c0620-1283-4d28-b348-4c5452a2a76c.Text: "The Allfather. Russ. My brothers. I belong to them. I am their blade. And this blade will never break."

54df5229-f5dc-4139-8d1b-c1972a932270.Text: "And so I will. No one will say that Ulfar was a craven who could not walk the bloody path laid out for him. That a single foe meant to fall at Ulfar's hand escaped their doom because Ulfar wavered."

ed0258e1-26c8-4aa0-b441-92c8e73a9927.Text: "The hour will come, and the Curse of the Wulfen will have me. And that hour approaches. I can hear the crunch of snow beneath claws. But it has not arrived yet."

b21de2a7-4a88-45e8-b73d-8933d92e3a82.Text: {n}Ulfar gives you a doubtful look but says nothing.{/n}

66f41983-6710-4b8d-99c7-2fbc6058e6f7.Text: "I... understand. Farewell, {name}. May you find your escape from this poisonous nest. But my soul has been trapped here for so long it has put down roots. I will go and kill someone who deserves it."

d461d885-d4da-4607-88fd-dbea8134f606.Text: {n}With a growl instead of a farewell, Ulfar turns around and walks off in search of new prey.{/n}

f2f5ee4f-62df-49bf-adfa-0e28a515fa61.Text: "Yes. Where is that slippery wretch? Let me have a word with him."

e7df5549-2430-4317-9d06-b8479c9e58ff.Text: {n}A faint but mirthful smile appears on his gloomy face.{/n} "Kill a few xenos? I would never say no to that."

1758faeb-9c2c-49ee-b250-05fbd5501b6b.Text: "Maybe you will succeed. Or maybe you will meet a glorious end. Whatever happens, I want to be at your side at that moment. I'm in."

b8a6dbde-dfa3-46c2-9e8b-e5a1dacaa9ff.Text: {n}He gives you a long, pensive look before he says,{/n} "You do not even know what it is you speak of, mortal. I will tell you about being alone sometime. Once we are out of here."

5a742d8a-70ad-431e-873b-7e7774e838fe.Text: {n}From beneath the veneer of bloodthirsty indifference, something resembling a living emotion surfaces on the giant's face. You hear words breaking through the wall of bared teeth:{/n} "For... the... Allfather..."

cb5813d2-ac4b-4390-81a6-10465e0cd70c.Text: "The malice of Wulfen beset my heart. And nearly consumed it forevermore."

8208bc08-6b75-4349-9c2f-91db9fcde2fc.Text: "I know nothing of his reasons. Here is my advice to you: do not try to peer into a xenos's thoughts. They are too perverse for a sound mind to comprehend. You would only risk catching that blight of degeneracy yourself."

daa9fbc3-04c2-4f29-9a53-f14995ec8763.Text: {n}Ulfar's bristling fiery hair lies flat once more and the imprint of death vanishes from his gaze. The face of a wild beast gives way to a grimace of weariness, grief, and... shame.{/n}

7566232a-335b-4bee-927a-c54814ab8b36.Text: {n}Marazhai stares at him in disgust.{/n} "Blight of degeneracy, you say? Those words aptly encompass both the tragedy and the comedy of your kind's existence."

b3fc4f60-829e-4749-8855-ec729959cf49.Text: "Blind destruction. No thoughts. No regrets. No purpose. To be a beast, not a human. A sweet temptation for a lone wolf."

5fe7c192-8de7-47b9-9e1b-5bd0899b1033.Text: {n}The giant shows no fear as his body shifts forward with the promise of death... and stops. His lips barely move as he musters the words:{/n} "I won't kill... my own..."

253a2363-2b15-42b9-8cd7-68157879892c.Text: "Bring my servants, the Shriekers, from the Chasm."

4e613e13-b2a7-4ffc-8dde-0b5ef18bae9b.Text: "Thank you for helping me. The time has come to end this performance."

49b17361-0670-4031-8fa9-ccf0393a7660.Text: "Why will you not even entertain the possibility that Yrliet is not lying?"

0bbaf5e0-26c2-4d9b-a8ab-3a73bb9aff85.Text: "You dragged me here to save this Farseer, is that it?"

dcd5305d-404a-4ef2-9bf8-0a4cc3b063e5.Text: "If what the Harlequin says is true, we will save whomever we can."

c42ba6c9-aff9-4d51-896c-ea31c2c97905.Text: "I have not yet decided if I can trust this strange xenos."

8a03261e-26ab-432b-a5a1-1a800d455418.Text: "They are like me — simply actors. The show is not yet ended, which means their place is on stage with me."

f4e6b981-cd84-4b52-801c-efb30bb25ce3.Text: Called your allies from the Chasm your instrument when asking Nocturne of Oblivion to rescue them.

4091739f-c35f-4f13-857d-62849c3daa19.Text: "They are my instrument. Let them continue to serve me."

a2e4eb43-dd3b-4147-9b7c-295d0675a477.Text: Called your allies from the Chasm victims when asking Nocturne of Oblivion to rescue them.

35b341be-5ce8-44da-9397-237edaa52da8.Text: "They are victims of the brutality that reigns over this place. I wish to save them from torment."

c04e9792-4fcb-47f2-8585-faa54994cff3.Text: "You led me into a trap! Is this your idea of a path to salvation?"

87f392ee-8a14-4456-8e47-6e130b328e84.Text: "So. I am off to find the promised vessel. You can stay here or you can come with me... Quietly."

9413111b-f930-47fa-b1ab-cc243cb929d4.Text: "Why are you even interested in the fate of this dead Farseer and his fellows?"

9272eeb4-56dc-4ff9-8d19-01b074253735.Text: [Point at the dead Aeldari] "What was he doing here? I presume he was a valuable prisoner."

8be2997a-d55e-461c-a3ab-d3347c69eb5c.Text: Asked Nocturne of Oblivion to rescue Achilleas from Commorragh.

6005600c-265f-42ef-9507-9eb2467689e0.Text: "Take Achilleas to realspace — he is losing his mind and I fear I will not be able to save him on my own. He does not deserve to be abandoned in the Dark City."

bb1315ae-d0b3-461c-8c9e-3e42917ff928.Text: "I am tired of your deceit and manipulation. I will no longer be your tool."

31c98c17-ddf0-4b8f-a739-c050985cc151.Text: "Now I know the path to freedom. I have no reason to help you. Get out of here."

477e2500-781f-4c93-b316-b224ab929c1b.Text: [Attack] "I have my own ideas about how this show should end!"

4d6a48eb-7521-4296-9948-e6ed6bfac521.Text: "I don't care about you, but I won't leave anyone in the clutches of these abominations. Not even xenos."

80ccb591-29b2-4871-b956-60f1cafb98b8.Text: "You will do it. I have faith in you!"

ee2091aa-46f1-4c5a-8daf-1ce10515005a.Text: "Go and meet the death that a worthless traitor deserves."

14dbb074-9513-426c-ad5a-95266f75d654.Text: [Stand between Heinrix and Marazhai] "Enough, both of you!"

498423fd-8917-4c02-a2e6-9aca4e2aeaa4.Text: [Strike Heinrix] "I have no need for an unhinged psyker!"

815ca2ac-23f0-45d2-97c3-6715ea19699d.Text: "How is all this connected to my escape?"

ae835240-be0b-4bac-a763-f651e4d279cf.Text: [Strike Marazhai] "You will die for everything you have done, here and now!"

f047c619-9293-4321-be13-e933aab9e813.Text: "Here is the proof you wanted, Heinrix."

a90eead2-45f3-4dfa-bb18-180639aae299.Text: "What do you want from me? Why have you involved me in your plans?"

57ad3295-904c-4e2d-94fe-bf4afe95c6c7.Text: "What is so bad about Yremeryss imprisoning the Farseers in the spire?"

f4789893-7ab9-42b5-9907-3be17250f59d.Text: "Wait... You brought the sorcerers to Commorragh yourself!"

1485b034-19d2-4932-839a-d75cee4ac584.Text: "Very well. Just one more reason to finish off Yremeryss."

744a6a33-807f-4ff7-ae4a-02155d602be8.Text: [Silently turn from Marazhai to the Harlequin]

c028b00b-ed00-43e5-b6f6-a0ea7792e5db.Text: "After all the trouble xenos have caused me, you are still asking for my help?"

87850a72-b632-4495-9d84-3790b2bb5246.Text: "Bring my comrades who previously served the Commissar from the Chasm."

4e2924e1-101c-494c-98be-be408bedb870.Text: "Take Achilleas to realspace. He is losing his mind, and I will struggle to break out of here with such a burden."

2dc3de5e-e46a-4435-b603-ebef1cefc8e8.Text: "Save the Commissar and his people from the arena."

905fc65c-4859-4240-bd1f-be4d67dbef92.Text: "My visit here was part of your plan? Everything has gone as you wanted it to?"

3eb94458-e2e0-4018-9d06-6fe6273729f3.Text: "Bring the Commissar and his people from the Chasm."

97b46283-208c-4f17-8fef-0aae8e4a7bb9.Text: "Are these Aeldari truly that important to you?"

ef7bc33d-0e6a-4372-83ce-213fe28134ff.Text: "Enough. We have to get out of Commorragh first and that will require the strength of each and every one of us."

17f22d81-7965-4d06-8b91-c53adc60abb3.Text:
{n}The slender figure of the Harlequin emerges from the shimmering haze. With the grace of one performing a sorrowful dance, he approaches the dying Aeldari nearby.{/n}
"Your dance is now tableau, and I lament,
The darkness in the eyes that saw the Path,
I peer into those tunnels black and bleak,
A gleam I seek, the one that points the way
To your imprisoned kin in tempest's cage."

befa0eb0-63df-45ae-a80e-8717403b51a7.Text:
"Disdain you not will I with a refusal,
Your soul's refrain will I keep safe as well,
But leave to me reality, Farseer,
And dreams I'll give into your worthy hands."
{n}With a solemn strike, the Harlequin ends his kinsman's torment and carefully takes the spirit stone from his body. When the xenos turns to you, his hands are already empty — the stone is gone.{/n}

e06f134f-86dc-4d9d-930a-7ceef30853c6.Text:
"The Merchant wishes them another fate?
A sudden turnabout, and curious.
What path ought they to take? All ears am I."

dbc3d94a-1130-4584-a334-6077ce56cedc.Text:
"A role miscast, alas, I do concede,
But all the same, your steps you will complete:
A solo, no one to mislead, and to
the tune of silence. Nocturne will retreat."
{n}The Harlequin vanishes in a blue shimmer. The horned mask disappears last, its empty eye holes seeming to stare at you in silent reproach.{/n}

23291300-9045-4586-a9c2-233aa3923512.Text: "Lord Captain, beware, the colours of this xenos are constantly changing. Where there was clarity one moment, there is mystery and darkness the next. Foulness sprouts where there was goodness and then everything is stirred up and turned upside down. I cannot bear to look at it. It is making me feel dizzy..."

c1cd526f-dd9a-4791-b257-ad68961ff830.Text: {n}It seems the xenos is trying to save the Farseers and their spirit stones at the behest of another, whose reasons are known only to them. All you have to guess now is if the "laugh of jest unending" that gave the Harlequin this mission is a living creature, a philosophical principle, or the figment of his deranged mind.{/n}

1acc6e33-6317-48e5-88ae-a3716159e5a2.Text:
{n}The Harlequin makes an exaggerated show of drawing back an imaginary curtain. The shadows beneath the black eye holes in his horned mask once again form a mocking smile.{/n}
"The grand finale of this gory piece,
Where perfidy and cunning reign supreme,
Shall now unfold, my Merchant Vagabond."

024ae480-efae-4086-9455-00d58038e927.Text:
"You listen well, oh pathless wanderer,
Night music's leitmotif you have discerned,
And title virtuoso you have earned."

d7715e12-509e-4f8b-a701-a5a77a9793a4.Text: {n}After a blurred flash of movement, Yrliet appears between the feuding Heinrix and Marazhai, pale with fear and anger.{/n} "Enough! Hate has blinded you when Commorragh is about to let us out of its clutches. Marazhai, still your intractable tongue and stand down. And you..." {n}She looks at Heinrix in apparent bewilderment.{/n} "Do you really want to deny the one who makes your heart beat faster a chance at survival by dying or killing her allies as she escapes? Is that what you want?"

6de5b88b-2c77-4b47-9d15-cebc650f5cd0.Text: {n}Marazhai gives you a mocking look and turns back to Heinrix expectantly.{/n}

8b738fbd-714a-428f-90d5-d23c31aa2440.Text: {n}The horned mask tilts, as the Harlequin observes the mon-keigh and the Outcast's conversation with interest, but he does not make a sound.{/n}

14f3da45-48fd-4c34-8c0b-5c81ae82ff45.Text:
"A drum or harp, or any instrument,
Of maestro's eye it is the apple prized.
I will ensure that yours sounds once again,
From death I'll save your precious property."

37acb382-4fbc-43c8-a47c-a2a7cf64cec8.Text: {n}Yrliet laughs bitterly.{/n} "You can kill me. Torture me. Grind to dust the very memory of my existence... But you cannot change what has transpired. The burnt mon-keigh made a misstep. I killed the traitor."

8ff1efa2-0ffc-4eea-be16-0a0135af9deb.Text:
"You blame the music for your graceless dance,
But who here is the means, and who the goal?
Of both together are sensations made.
You'll have the outcome, I the path thereto."

ba55528a-40b7-41f3-9a0e-c6d5ee3c768f.Text: {n}After delivering his speech, Heinrix seems to snap out of his haze of undiluted hatred. He takes a breath and glances at you, now looking weary beyond words.{/n} "Come on. Every minute in this cursed place brings us all closer to madness."

539ebe32-e5b5-49b8-937f-6c1095ac8103.Text: {n}Heinrix freezes.{/n} "What..." {n}He slowly turns around and raises his gaze to the Drukhari.{/n} "...did you say?"

b48269bf-03b2-4d79-bb16-1e93c17e1d9a.Text: "No, he was squealing, like all cattle do at a slaughterhouse. Back on the ravaged world where I spent hours twisting his mind and spirit." {n}Marazhai draws out the words, slowly advancing toward the Interrogator.{/n} "Your servant traded away the most terrible secrets for a reprieve from pain. Yours, Heinrix van Calox, and those of your little mon-keigh Inquisition. Did I need them? No. What I wanted to know was beyond your servant's knowledge but he still would not settle down, desperate to purchase my mercy. He kept mumbling incessantly, both about you, whom he feared so much, and his beloved mistress... Lichtenhart, wasn't it?"

1bca364a-3296-46b2-af8e-9f3c7805e048.Text:
"Commorragh's ancient law was boldly spurned,
And too despoiled were Crudarach's remains,
The Tempest's mistress, spurred by avarice,
Forbidden plunder brought to her dark nest.
And though the City shrinks from those whose souls
In darkness gleam with coruscating flame,
The interdict is scorned, the pact ignored,
Commorragh waits, Commorragh tastes its doom.
To make of drama farce beyond belief,
A pair uncredited assume the stage:
A cutthroat mon-keigh, captive of a thief;
A dancer, makestrife poet, guileful knave."

07a364bd-c749-4599-93cc-735cf366359e.Text:
{n}With a weary sigh, the Harlequin concludes,{/n}
"When coda's note falls silent ever more,
The last a duty will perform, and then,
The first will move, {mf|his|her} exodus enact."

197ee901-f705-4b1a-b1e9-b1d9417fbca6.Text: {n}The xenos scoffs.{/n} "With pleasure. Especially now that we have both got what we wanted."

16cd28d2-1129-42d6-b9a4-9b40629b55a3.Text: {n}Heinrix looks at you with dead eyes, struggling to say something.{/n}

291452cf-6654-4412-b634-54488a9fa0cb.Text: {n}Marazhai does not hide the contempt in his look aimed at the Interrogator.{/n} "You should have killed the burnt mon-keigh immediately and not deluded yourself by putting faith in his strength and resilience. You mon-keigh are clueless when it comes to the art of espionage and treason. I could teach you a thing or two... If you ask nicely enough." {n}He turns his gaze toward you.{/n} "I am finished here. We may go."

f7bca644-1736-45de-8521-d35a84a36a25.Text:
"The starved ones' fate to shelter from the storm,
Enlisted me the laugh of jest unending,
The soul is not at home amidst dark walls,
It yearns to sing, and I to hearken long
Its elegy, by name oblivion.
A cradle I'll bestow, where may this song
Forevermore resound in endless echo."

e6cc8ab3-7911-4d8d-8595-4fe0588c7a28.Text:
"The Executioner lost interest,
And blithely tossed the toy despised aside.
Proclaiming it a gift to empty bellies,
He let the rabble tear it into scraps,
And tooth and claw they fought to claim a share,
With every one extolling his largesse."

140f0f54-591b-463e-899a-3e8f89bcb23c.Text: "A fitting end." {n}Marazhai snorts contemptuously and looks at you.{/n} "I am finished here. I trust we can move on to important matters: finding that ship the Arebennian kept babbling about and dealing with Yremeryss."

b783636e-09c3-4c9c-84d8-2b0c27b03f1d.Text: {n}Heinrix and Marazhai give each other one last look — a hateful human glare and a disdainful Drukhari sneer — and silently follow.{/n}

af583830-bc72-4c84-9606-3be1486a6a14.Text: {n}Yremeryss acted recklessly when she decided to bring captive psykers back to Commorragh. The Webway is extremely sensitive to psychic powers and the psykers' presence could force the Dark City apart at the seams, opening gaping chasms to the warp. If the other Kabals knew about this audacious stunt...{/n}

c9961868-2fa7-4714-a3b5-6f923203389e.Text: {n}It is clear that Yremeryss acted recklessly by taking such valuable prisoners and she risked starting a war with her xenos cousins.{/n}

145829fa-5c04-4f66-950e-098708623d92.Text:
"As surety this feral brute has served,
That to my plan there would be blood released,
Without remorse fate's course I've whipped and spurred,
A cruel hand on old, unruly beast."

d014596f-8115-46ed-8bd3-33aa68f77a3f.Text: "Agh, you rotten-gutted swine! Used me as a war beast, did you? Set me on your enemies?" {n}Ulfar's face darkens in fury, but with gargantuan effort he forces it down and manages to prevent a fit of blood rage from taking hold.{/n}

579cb62c-30f2-4cf3-b137-56574d3ea2fa.Text:
"A fragment's all that's left of what was whole,
The rest now worn away by treachery.
But if you prize this repercussion so,
This gesture I'll perform, and in return,
The laugh with no beginning you will serve."

4f371f84-0332-43df-8a28-6f82aa4bd4a2.Text: "Be careful, elantach. Arebennian weigh each word with meticulous pedantry. If you do not take care, you will receive what you want, only turned inside out, like the fabric of the void without any stars."

be509fd9-d2a4-4c15-9af2-def7f4fccd45.Text: "Watch your words. Arebennian love nothing more than interpreting words superficially, and not how they were intended."

b4a37992-6683-415a-b2ef-6cdefc96ea39.Text:
"What is a stage when actors do not tread?
Naught but a pile of pointless wood, that's what!
Before the culmination thunders past,
Your friends will find a part to play, fear not,
Your words I've heard, my Merchant Vagabond."

1967a55c-985c-470c-8612-a9a4d165e71d.Text:
"The picture of compassion, so you are,
Remembering the weak and bare this way,
Why not? I'll show my care for them as well,
And guard them from Commorragh's horrors all."

78eaf987-4206-48c8-8f10-a7f7eb4b647e.Text:
"No sooner said than done, offstage they go,
Their fates do matter little to our show."

0b26edff-dd31-4a69-95c8-2f2e74b959fe.Text: {n}Saying nothing, the Harlequin vanishes in a blue shimmer of air. The horned mask disappears last, with vicious laughter drifting out from beneath it.{/n}

1c6a0319-054d-4631-9118-21cd4cebe526.Text: {n}Through his overwhelming rage, Achilleas chokes out a farewell:{/n} "I leave you... here... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I am a danger to you."

753b1a6b-cf12-4c1a-8bfa-8e7cfe459662.Text: "I was made for... fighting. My body is excited by the smell of blood... It wants more. If I lose control... during the voyage... the best case is that I destroy the gondola... and we all die..."

dea10f13-ecdf-4027-8b6a-77cfc961ccc4.Text: "I betrayed you... once. And I swore... never again."

c8697378-763e-4d1a-a99e-d2a6c6a7496d.Text: "As many... as I can... I promise."

fd25673c-575c-4692-a980-7d8078f5f7da.Text: {n}His weakening human voice collapses into roars of rage and bloodthirst cloaked in flesh.{/n}

1822967b-82a4-43d6-b605-741f833549d4.Text: {n}The Farseer's voice is weak and tremulous from pain. It is strange that he is still capable of speech — his body has been horrifically maimed. The colours of his garb are familiar — the group of xenos you met on Janus wore the same.{/n} "At the top of the spire. They are all there. Help them, Arebennian. And help... me. Take me away from here, when it is all over... Soon."

804d3d2f-dbe5-4a6d-8b52-cfb69c4c21cd.Text: "I'm surprised that anyone can understand a thing he says. I stopped listening after the first sentence — now I'm just waiting for the Lord Captain to decide on whatever it is."

19ca879e-5809-47cc-83ca-0cb808baf819.Text: {n}The Harlequin's mournful mask gives no sign of his intentions. Who knows what goes on in his head?{/n}

7807e84c-3db0-4d98-8398-e25638537c55.Text:
{n}The xenos tilts his head, staring at Yrliet.{/n}
"The cradle's fragments smoulder dimly there,
Where tight has drawn the Tempest all together.
Dare you plunge your hand into the flame,
And drag truth's embers out into the light?"

f47e021c-0fa8-4772-adfd-a72fa366eb0b.Text: "Oh Arebennian, you ask if I am too afraid to try to save the little that remains of my home? Now that the wind of hope fans the flame of the coming truth?" {n}The stone on Yrliet's chest flares crimson — a timid glow that goes out as soon as the Aeldari touches her chestplate.{/n} "Even if the fire of truth burns me from within, I will follow this Path to the end."

dda6202d-33cf-417e-be3d-361e4fbfe309.Text: "Do you... truly not understand, elantach? It pains me to recall how I was willing to exchange your life for the pathetic scraps of information Marazhai scattered at my feet. But the Farseers... with those scraps, they have the ability to grow an entire forest of truth."

89fc255d-7f83-4368-9934-6e6a15e0e72a.Text: {n}Yrliet tenses her lithe frame in an attempt to hold back the shudder of despair that rocks through her.{/n} "I understand your doubts, elantach. I but ask you to consider my request... and to do it not for my kin, for the Arebennian, or for anyone else. But for me."

e0d53ee2-79a0-45d6-9c0b-04c174692113.Text: "Elantach, the Arebennian love jests, but this is not one. Please, before it is too late, I... we must save the Farseers! Allow me to go with you to the spire — to that nest of depravity, to that haven of pain, anger, and betrayal of my kind." {n}Yrliet's voice wavers like a taught string, and her eyes are veiled with darkness.{/n}

73fc2e7a-0617-4999-91d9-5cf82bf94b74.Text: {n}The Harlequin said the words "laugh of jest unending" with reverence, as if it were a title or rank. You recall that Harlequins serve the Laughing God Cegorach. It seems the xenos is saying that it is at Cegorach's behest that he is attempting to save the Farseers.{/n}

599b9aae-6a04-4073-967c-c66002591e1f.Text: {n}Yrliet half closes her eyes, her lids fluttering from suppressed emotion.{/n} "A very long time ago, an old friend once told me, 'A bird does not know its feathers' worth until it loses the gift of harnessing the wind.' I think I understand now."

67b9c706-9a02-420a-a2f1-eecc4cf5157c.Text: {n}Yrliet shudders as if she cannot believe your words, and her expression shifts subtly.{/n} "I... am grateful."

7c70b468-1ab7-4f3f-b34f-9379a5f3dc2b.Text:
"My Merchant Vagabond, their {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}part is played{/d},
It's not for you or me to denigrate
The artful script directing this charade
That writes them out — cast off to stormy fate."

185b6af1-94cb-41e6-a509-90da3ba27885.Text: {n}Several encounters with the Harlequin have been enough to teach you that everything that is happening is merely one grand show or dance for him. It is pointless to converse with him like a typical xenos — he is a director, playwright, and actor all in one. All that interests him is that the performance comes off successfully.{/n}

d6896c43-e5dd-4a3e-9163-736588c0e680.Text: "Cantraetal, who chose the Path of the Seer... Muaran told me he disappeared as soon as the cataclysm befell Crudarach. Does this mean my kin are being held captive at the top of the Reaving Tempest's spire? The truth is ready to reveal itself to me if I but stretch out my hand..." {n}Sparks of impatience flicker in Yrliet's gaze. She wants to talk to you, but she will not interrupt your exchange with the Harlequin.{/n}

2badfc66-3d81-4f7c-83a1-63db2385fec8.Text: "The accursed jester, back again. If you start weaving your webs of rotten claptrap again, I'll rip out your useless tongue!"

50004d75-a5e1-4acb-a57a-fab1e25a93f1.Text:
"And yet the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_DaemonicBreach}feast of waking nightmares{/d} draws
Another pen into this narrative.
The playwright's face remains a mystery,
But message mine I hope will reach those ears:
That nightmares suffer nightmares of their own,
Where Nocturne of Oblivion resounds."
{n}The black gaze of the horned mask's eye hollows lingers on your face before the Harlequin continues his speech.{/n}

ae4026c9-b3e8-413a-9d18-2dd0d3b2897a.Text: "Here we go again! Trusting the pointy-eared ones and saving xenos! We don't learn from our mistakes, do we? Nah, of course not!" {n}Jae's plaintive groan is directed more at herself than you.{/n}

b18844c9-853e-42ed-a397-39995fed2fff.Text: "Ah, a ship! We will finally leave this horrible place flooded with scarlet hues of agony and washed-out tinges of despair."

342f3b3d-fbe5-42d6-8e9b-6cd338b051ec.Text:
"Strive up to where the thieving storm has built
Its squalid nest among the darkened sky,
The tempest's plunder hoards are buried there,
And captives, riches, trophies all within.
Amidst this cache a gate to realspace find,
Pass through to freedom tempting and so craved,
Companions have I brought, and steps revealed,
My lines run out, I have no more to give.
The stage is yours, my Merchant Vagabond,
Go fetch a vessel swift — and get you gone!"

d3e670bf-d973-4256-9125-ae182ecbc186.Text: {n}Achilleas's growling becomes louder and louder. Through the rasping and gurgling, a tortured voice breaks through:{/n} "Combat... stimulants... Too many... I need... slaughter... Slaughter. Slaughter!" {n}Your former servant is teetering on a knife edge, threatening to tumble into bloodthirsty madness at any moment.{/n}

34f12224-713b-4da4-ae8f-ca493c970540.Text: {n}Achilleas's rasping snarl drowns out the Harlequin's last words. The beast looks around bloodthirstily, but there are no enemies left, and its interest in the xenos becomes more and more pronounced.{/n}

eb7d0bbf-627c-452d-a1c0-51630e7d4028.Text: {n}Through his overwhelming rage, Achilleas chokes out a farewell:{/n} "Good luck... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... Until we meet... on the other side."

4daf636a-3857-4d5e-ae8e-ce6f15f392af.Text: {n}Heinrix stares for a few more moments at the spot where Nocturne just stood.{/n} "How much longer will we be playthings in the hands of damned xenos? The torture... the arena... even this effortless 'escape'... And the source of all these degrading ordeals is still alive." {n}His eyes, burning with hate, shift to Yrliet.{/n}

d3698e7a-5ead-44f2-ad67-0da356d8606c.Text: {n}Yrliet looks at Heinrix with empty eyes and shivers slightly.{/n} "The deluge of misfortune did not start with me, mon-keigh. It was your charge, Achilleas..."

43d9f4c4-4ff9-4061-9557-a8a4b3d3b57c.Text: "Do not speak his name! You sully the name of a servant of the Throne by uttering it." {n}Heinrix's voice has dropped to a rasping hiss.{/n} "And stop trying my patience with your lies."

232a3c58-5b16-48d0-9a8c-58d8c089ddc2.Text: "I don't know what's doing my head in more — my whispers or his damned metaphors. Why can't he just say, 'I saved your asses, now do this for me — whack these upstarts and get out while you can'?"

4fe456c1-e669-4dce-b83b-9c92069d8443.Text: {n}Marazhai, who had been engrossed in his own thoughts, springs to life at the Interrogator's frenzied words. He turns his head with snake-like grace and stares unblinkingly at Heinrix.{/n}

b301dded-e44b-48cb-b565-ba80e70f6f6c.Text: {n}Heinrix's gaze turns on you — and you are suddenly trembling, enveloped in an icy fog.{/n} "Because it is a hastily concocted tale that would fool only a naive simpleton. If you wish to trust the word of an enemy of Humanity, that is your unfortunate choice to make. But until I have better proof of Achilleas Scalander's treason than this pathetic prattle, I will not change my mind. Not now, not ever."

1374f436-9eca-4db6-bf07-1fa84a76905d.Text: {n}Marazhai's scathing laugh seems to cut through the air.{/n} "He was weeping when he begged me for death."

5bbb2271-8e76-4a84-9c6b-d3c967185a7a.Text: "Enough, xenos! Repeating the same thing over and over will not convince me of your ridiculous lies. The Rogue Trader takes you at your word — that is {mf|his|her} vice and heresy, not mine. And until I have more solid proof of Achilleas Scalander's treason than your prattle, I will not change my mind. Not now, not ever."

c4f2fe97-c2c5-4441-9171-1f1847b16eaa.Text: {n}Heinrix's face, twisted with hatred, turns whiter than snow.{/n} "No..."

5002e2a5-75e6-452d-8c8b-528e2c77b18b.Text: {n}Marazhai's eyes flash with pleasure at the look of horror on Heinrix's face.{/n} "Yes, mon-keigh. You wanted proof of how weak your kind is and how insignificant your servants are, didn't you? The name of Emelina Lichtenhart. The poor singed beast... He tried so hard, he was so eager to please his new master that he sold out every one of you..." {n}Marazhai cocks his head as if straining to hear a distant sound, then grins carnivorously.{/n} "Oh, Heinrix van Calox. The shards of your naive illusions are slicing your soul so sweetly..."

12e1a5d4-21ef-43eb-bb2a-ebbf9f3d501e.Text: {n}The Interrogator remains still for another second, then his eyes glaze over, his face twists, and the air around him turns icy cold. Marazhai twitches and coughs strangely, his pale face turning purple. He staggers and reaches for his blade...{/n}

bd7100ca-4e15-46c9-9a06-14e1f31ed6db.Text: {n}Heinrix takes a step back and looks at you in shock. After a moment, his face regains its usual stoic expression.{/n} "That is enough. You are right, xenos. About this..." {n}Heinrix hesitates, struggling to say the next words.{/n} "...and about other things too." {n}As if drained of the last of his strength, Heinrix turns away from you.{/n}

80394bbe-edf8-4575-95db-40c3b4d64f15.Text: {n}Marazhai rubs his face, bruised from the ruptured blood vessels under the skin. His voice oozes contempt.{/n} "Keep your broodmale on a shorter leash, {name}. I might break your little plaything next time."

4486b247-e86a-4cc0-af58-ef9058eedd31.Text: "An Arebennian would not lie about this! Or did you not hear the words of the dying Farseer?" {n}Impatience burns in Yrliet's emerald eyes.{/n} "I hope your soul's doubts will be dispelled before we reach the spire. I am not asking you to rise to Nocturne's words, but to my request."

a00b5b77-01d1-4971-9aa6-87d381fbcc9d.Text: {n}Marazhai nimbly evades your blow and, having lost precious time, drops to his knees with a wheeze. The next moment his eyes burst, a fountain of blood gushes from his mouth, and the xenos's dead body slumps to the ground.{/n}

dde81931-988f-496b-b86d-12745476f418.Text: {n}Heinrix sighs heavily and stares down at the corpse at his feet. He looks suddenly forlorn.{/n} "Foolish... So foolish... I could have interrogated him... extracted every bit of information he managed to get from Achilleas..." {n}He looks up at you, his gaze filled with pain.{/n} "I'm sorry. I... lost my head for a moment. I will not let it happen again. No, I won't." {n}Casting one last hateful glance at the dead Marazhai, Heinrix turns away.{/n}

9fe75ed9-e063-4eb6-aba0-22a797ecc82d.Text: {n}The blow catches Heinrix off guard, and he gives you a stunned look before a razor-sharp blade slices through his face, cleaving his skull in two and severing the rest of his head. His decapitated body falls heavily at Marazhai's feet.{/n}

44aedb69-6786-477b-9940-d5eb1173f882.Text: {n}Heinrix flinches when you appear before him. He hesitates for another moment, and then, clenching his fists impotently, he looks away.{/n} "I am sorry, {name}. I... lost my head for a moment."

d43e4b42-0ce1-4a7d-99b6-0d11c7d52a3e.Text: "{name}..." {n}Heinrix's voice is barely audible.{/n} "I have detained us. I beg you to forgive my outburst. Please lead on."

72951f0a-57fd-4622-ac13-ca32aab984d3.Text: {n}At the Farseer's words, Marazhai's face stiffens and he opens his mouth, but to no avail. The Drukhari appears to have lost the power of speech.{/n}

97a52a1e-73d4-4aff-b6d6-74ceaea19cc0.Text: {n}When Harlequin's voice fades, the silence is broken by a torrent of untranslatable but highly expressive xenos profanities — Marazhai has regained the power of speech and is using it to curse someone's kin and progeny.{/n} "Farseers! Yremeryss brought Asuryani Farseers to the Dark City! You stupid, desperate shrew! If this news reaches the— oh, but of course it has reached him already! You, Arebennian! You came to Commorragh to inform Vect of my sister's crimes and rescue her prisoners!"

fad76087-5900-400e-904c-e2ad5b686d4f.Text:
{n}The Harlequin makes a jester's bow.{/n}
"I am revealed and intrigue's curtain torn!
The Puppet Master deigned to briefly let
Me be the crosspiece of his artistry,
That tweaks and tugs the strings for dance and death.
To tempest's mistress, 'Vanish!' I do say,
I've fashioned from your shackles a garrotte.
Your burning wrath, my thief, direct her way,
And forth you'll see the fruits of vengeance brought."

c224760a-8cf5-4443-9257-b8f09b49ce60.Text: "The accusations of consorting with mon-keigh are such a trifle compared to an attempt to bring about a dysjunction... If only I had known it! Had Yremeryss not managed to keep it secret from me..." {n}Marazhai shields his eyes, contemplating something.{/n} "I wonder how many times Nazrakhei cursed himself for not overthrowing Yremeryss at the Obsidian Court when he had the chance? He had unknowingly spared the one his ruler had condemned. Hardly an excuse that will help him at his next meeting with Vect."

ab83401f-94f3-43ff-9eac-dbe6298b196c.Text:
"A fragment's all that's left of what was whole,
The rest now worn away by treachery.
Reality for him is out of bounds,
But nightmares in Commorragh find a home,
Depart. Forget. And leave the past alone."

3cfa0b9f-db52-41f2-94cd-f45c1738764d.Text: "The Webway in which Commorragh resides is fragile. A ripple of the veil can breach its boundaries and cause a dysjunction, an incursion of Sai'lanthresh into the streets. Each such occasion is an ordeal that weakens the Dark City, and so those capable of piercing the veil are banned from the spires. Of course, there are madmen who try to exploit any dysjunction and the ensuing chaos to take down competitors and move up the food chain... It appears that Yremeryss decided not to wait for an opportunity, but to make it happen herself!"

960e9294-c25e-4216-9c11-80aa2b103d0c.Text: "I did, because such was the deal with Tervantias. In exchange for his help, I was not to kill the veil-linked mon-keigh, but to sedate and hand them over to him, a degenerate obsessed with studying the forbidden. I expected them to vanish without a trace into the shadows of the Anatomical Opera... and believe me, the damned of your kind are far less dangerous to the Webway than the Farseers of the Asuryani!"

491fb8d6-faf3-4531-8f33-d867cca0b63b.Text: "I had enough reasons even without this revelation! Kae-morag, I am half a step away from starting to see my expulsion from the Kabal as a blessing and not a punishment!"

77ed0347-2b52-4787-acf8-bb6587a7f0c8.Text: {n}Nocturne of Oblivion watches the raging Drukhari with obvious amusement, but his interest barely lasts a moment.{/n}

130fe0d1-1830-452b-946e-27f1534c5391.Text:
"You may applaud my disappearing act
The reaper's fatal steps I did conceal
From eyes that dreams of blood so wildly craved.
For unbeknownst to them, death merely moved
Into another hall, in harmony
With inmate's steps and night's own melody."

d841a527-b903-4e89-9966-5dca929a8dfa.Text: {n}Although the Harlequin's mournful mask is absolutely still, you cannot shake the feeling that a nasty grin lurks behind it. This is a game, a test. You must choose your words carefully.{/n}

77cd80e9-5642-489e-9642-94886e54be54.Text: "Even flesh-speak is more efficient than the speech patterns of this xenos. Hypothesis: the elucidator machine spirit has been affected by the pernicious influence of this place and is producing distorted output. I seek permission to conduct a technical survey."

a124bb9c-2c03-411f-9e4f-00aeec97955e.Text: "The Hundred Dreams Crossroads, was it? Send the word: we are heading out at once."

709f202c-8fb3-4f54-8d56-cc4661aaa0b3.Text: "So Voigtvir had a hand in this as well?"

af0ee152-9d46-442a-87e0-ebe77badc30d.Text: "It has only been three cycles since the attack. How are your wounds?"

130a698e-103c-4911-aad9-7c9d93590f93.Text: "Ah, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Achilleas appears uncharacteristically pensive.{/n} "Might I ask for a few precious moments of your time? Critical information has come to my attention, however... Please let us first proceed to your study lest we be overheard."

1c0e507f-2048-426c-a13d-9d48d35238e6.Text: "I implore you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It brooks no delay. We have the element of surprise on our side and an opportunity to lay a trap for Kunrad Voigtvir. If that opportunity slips away... we cannot be certain if we have caught every one of his spies on Dargonus and your voidship."

03a7bead-814c-4d59-bad7-b201f4f9613c.Text: "Your former Master of Whispers, Kunrad Voigtvir. Now we know how he's been able to dodge our spies time and time and again: he has the technology of enemies of Humanity on his side. Vile traitor! My agents ascertained the location of the base where Voigtvir has been meeting with xenos in secret, a station in the system of the Hundred Dreams Crossroads. The station is allegedly out of commission, abandoned some time ago. That plays into our hands: it is an excellent place to set up an ambush and strike where they least expect it."

9208fbe1-937c-4547-9db2-7b81c6903c62.Text: "Consider it done. I will go with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, for my investigation into this matter has only just commenced."

12f805ff-331d-4472-895e-e0033901545d.Text: {n}Achilleas presses his lips into a line.{/n} "Since the xenos attack, I have been working relentlessly to follow their cold trail. I have had no time for rest but... My body is functional. Its condition is beneath Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s notice."

e6e70dd8-4c18-43b8-9842-0fc3e0f5e617.Text: "That is hardly surprising. His connection to cultists has already been established. He is to blame for the death of Her Ladyship Theodora von Valancius and he came close to taking your life as well. Another betrayal of the Imperium, this time fraternising with xenos — although such crimes must come as easy to him as getting up in the morning."

52c37631-c7a5-4c0a-b114-dbe45a275c6d.Text: "If I may, I will get right to the point. After the attack on Dargonus, I focused my efforts on trying to discover how the xenos were able to launch that devastating raid. According to my findings, the enemies of Humanity received assistance from a hidden cell of conspirators. My agents spent a great deal of time tracking and interrogating infiltrators on Dargonus and other von Valancius colonies. The results... surprised me, to say the least." {n}Achilleas pauses to press his respirator against his burnt lips.{/n}

cb0bc9e1-1554-4a82-a73f-9f8747c32a0a.Text: "Secretary Scalander has articulated his desire to meet you in private. For security reasons, he has resolved not to inform me of the exact reasons behind this request." {n}Clementia grimaces faintly.{/n} "The secretary is waiting at the doors to your room. He asks that you speak with him at your earliest convenience. Apparently this matter concerns the security of the entire protectorate."

aac62e20-87d1-4bdb-a040-6639593abe1e.Text: [Say nothing while maintaining a bored expression]

215942af-c8d5-4058-a94e-2e998f282260.Text: "Truly, the God-Emperor has blessed me with diligent subjects! Speak."

c3048cce-34b7-445b-b7e2-bce207ba63a8.Text: "Did I hear you quite right? Macharius Sauerback is sending me gifts, correct?"

6c101b4f-f0d5-4222-90c4-0152c4ce19ec.Text: "I have lost track of how long I have been trapped on Dargonus for the good of the protectorate. Hurry up. I better hear some good news today."

72b3cbff-828f-48b4-baf2-7e48da3b0384.Text: {n}Clementia barely contains a yawn. Once Janris Danrok has finished, she pulls out her data-slate.{/n} "Thank you for your report, High Factotum. Your work is highly appreciated, both by everyone here and the Adeptus Administratum. Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, we are almost done here. We just need to go over the final items on today's agenda that I would like to report to you personally."

f314ebd7-a5f7-4903-9122-61170a120643.Text: "Your pet xenos... Yrliet, I believe, is seeking a meeting with you. She had the audacity to defile the Rogue Trader's palace with her profane presence and refuses to leave until she has spoken with you. I would never presume to be able to read the emotions of xenos, but the Aeldari appeared perturbed. I believe she mentioned a voidship of some sort. It may be best if she told you everything directly."

b5865d71-a6c3-4ea4-bfea-2927e736fcff.Text: "Especially since His Lordship Winterscale's luck seems to be running out. Riots have broken out on several of his worlds, and yet, he has shown no intention of quelling them. Instead, the Rogue Trader inflicted brutal punishment upon one of his oldest colonies, Vesuvia Secundus, based on allegations of seditious sentiment. Oddly enough, our agents were unable to find any proof of sedition among the populace there. As soon as we have any updates, you will be the first to know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Clementia glances down at her data-slate.{/n} "Lastly..."

aef3eb36-7a45-4ab9-b1cb-9e1857d4d5ae.Text: "Allow me to pass on gifts from your loyal subjects, the high nobility of Dargonus. It goes without saying that every living soul in your protectorate is blessed to serve Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} faithfully and wholeheartedly. However, this humble gesture is meant as a token of deepest appreciation of your magnanimity toward their esteemed families."

e304ed8c-b8bc-45d6-98ed-5333eea47970.Text: "House Werserian made arrangements for the delivery of several tonnes of supplies for your future journeys. The house is also transferring a regiment of its finest into your personal charge. Each of these brave troopers has undergone rigorous voidfarer training and will be humbled to lay down their life for you, Lord Captain." {n}Clementia is trying to maintain a neutral expression but you can see her face is beaming with pride.{/n} "Please command them as you see fit."

a4081735-f4dd-4f85-a13b-a6ef06767179.Text: "In the past cycle, House Drivestem tripled the tithes collected from the house's subjects. Your coffers are overflowing, and the governor has expressed hope that this modest gift will become a symbol of your present and future successes in your new status."

d4b79442-8c6d-4122-ba1c-e89558d8f22d.Text: "House Gaprak has sent shuttles carrying sacred technology and manufactured parts that can be used to replace old joints and connections within mechanisms. The machine spirits of these devices have been pacified. They are slumbering peacefully as they await your decision on how to employ their capabilities."

363db6f4-5ae4-49fc-95e9-f38d7e942ba8.Text: "House Sauerback has arranged for several regiments of expertly trained servants of the Emperor to be transferred to your personal command. Each of them will also serve as an honour guard for the holy relics that are to find their rightful place in the hold of your personal voidship..." {n}She stops, staring at her data-slate in surprise.{/n}

5d944b63-8cb9-4d41-90f7-be46228fa0d5.Text: "No, not at all, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! The people and the cargo have indeed reached the port services, so there is no reason to doubt the sincerity of the house's intentions. It's just... such substantial and valuable gifts coming from Lord Sauerback..." {n}Clementia trails off.{/n}

23a56f35-3562-4045-beb5-8a8d34711122.Text: "That is exactly correct, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The port services have already received the aforementioned resources and are now in the process of accommodating them aboard your ship. It's just... Lord Sauerback..."

72d85225-794d-4be2-a446-ed0b0db46745.Text: {n}The chancellor coughs in an attempt to break up the awkward pause.{/n} "Right, so..."

18fc22a8-44d7-43a4-b7ee-209806340702.Text: "And with that, please allow me and Master Danrok to take our leave." {n}The chancellor and the High Factotum offer you their bows.{/n} "Perhaps that last request will serve as a welcome distraction? Indeed, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s stay on Dargonus has been rather long. However, your protectorate is now enjoying a period of relative stability that, for the time being, no longer demands Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s personal involvement in its affairs. Glory to the Rogue Trader!"

a1310cba-f790-41c3-b2ff-8e8d426bad55.Text: {n}Danrok lets out an amused chuckle.{/n} "If I am to venture a guess, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I believe the esteemed chancellor was staggered by such an irregular display of generosity from a man who is rather known for voicing his... doubts in Rogue Traders as a class. It would seem you have made quite an impression on Macharius, the old miser."

9559d328-1dad-49e2-9a8d-d410ad2699ae.Text: "Lord Captain, news of particular import has come from the house's intelligence network. Lord Inquisitor Calcazar is rumoured to be planning a visit to Footfall. A number of Imperial Navy ships were commandeered by Lord Calcazar and they are also being scrambled to Footfall. Furthermore, we have received reports claiming that secret messages were delivered to the capital worlds of Houses Chorda and Winterscale. It is possible that the Lord Inquisitor's call to arms may smother the conflict that is brewing between the two dynasties. We are seeing an increasing number of skirmishes between their ships in neutral systems. I do not doubt that Her Ladyship Chorda will attempt to sway the Lord Inquisitor to her side."

a1f33cb7-8ff7-4fc7-9872-60e6a560cedb.Text: {n}You have spent the first few hours of your morning listening to the High Factotum's lengthy report on the latest trade exchanges, arrangements, disputes, and countless bureaucratic procedures. From outside the illuminated, tightly closed windows, you can hear the muffled sounds of Dargonus and its everyday life — the life that has been passing you by lately, as you have been preoccupied with the affairs of your protectorate from dawn till dusk.{/n}

9fb33ea6-a9ce-44b1-8d98-6abc3cca7258.Text: {n}The chancellor and the High Factotum exchange nervous glances.{/n} "I will strive my best to live up to your expectations, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

4922ede6-5113-4248-b764-a14120ba6e98.Text: "You are quite right. No more delays. To the Master of Seals!"

42727b32-f0a1-4991-921c-e7c7fba5091e.Text: "Have patience. You will get your certificate when I find the time."

aaac43e2-80a1-42c7-94b1-16ea8a35c6a9.Text: "Enough! I have no intention of going anywhere and I do not wish to hear another word about your papers."

2e0cf68d-9fa9-4290-a6e6-9fe8d3970751.Text: "Shereen! Dargonus is absolutely fabulous this season, wouldn't you agree?" {n}Jae greets you with a familiar pearly smile.{/n} "Incidentally... We've been dealing with the aftermath of the xeno-invasion for three cycles now... And far be it from me to hint at anything... but the ceremony of your succession has long since passed."

7840b78d-048d-43d5-a934-092a673c9527.Text: "May the Exalted One bless your whole dynasty!" {n}Jae claps her hands and something in her prosthesis clicks in protest.{/n} "Shall we proceed to the shuttles, shereen? I will be right behind you."

c9058aa4-8f39-4e23-9bfc-1390c4c37d7d.Text: "Of course, shereen! There is no rush. All the time in the world is at our disposal..." {n}Jae rubs her chin with a look of slight worry.{/n}

8d415cb3-65e5-4ae9-a1b7-b78b67982fd8.Text: {n}Jae says nothing for a while before offering you a saccharine smile.{/n} "But of course! I beg you to pardon my indiscretion, shereen. It does not befit people of your stature to concern themselves with the pleas of lowly... subjects. I dare not trouble you further."

6ea4d9e1-6034-4301-8382-231ec779b630.Text: "Will my shereen, perhaps, find the time to visit the Administratum Palace with me? I am worried that, should we sail away on another voyage to the stars, I will never obtain my certificate, the Mercatum Tabula Officiale. And neither will my shereen savour all the benefits that said certificate could offer the von Valancius protectorate."

afebdc1c-697e-46a2-a9f9-96e59457b36f.Text: "Give me the coordinates, and I shall take you wherever you wish to go."

fa4c59e1-c0bd-4e21-99b5-ccf5baa1297a.Text: "Let us discuss this another time, perhaps."

f7f4b4f0-92d0-421e-88a7-60bed3661a59.Text: "Crudarach's fate is no concern of mine."

fa116887-1dbe-4b44-9143-0c35a3f4000a.Text: "How were you able to contact those Aeldari?"

3cb1bb48-57e4-4293-a3ef-97133e81e065.Text: "Elantach, at last you have left your ornate cage." {n}Yrliet casts a look over the stone palace walls.{/n} "For many a turn have I sought to meet you, and yet, your servant, the one who is like the silver-haired Abelard but twice as young, has no favour for the requests of a Child of Asuryan. Take me to a place where the hearing of others will not steal the words intended for you."

359289c2-2975-4fff-ba44-914fba55d68a.Text: "While you were mending the wounds of this world left by the twisted ones' attack, I was able to discover... no, not Crudarach's fate. Merely traces of it. As Muaran found sanctuary under the boughs of the Lilaethan's forests, so did my other kin find refuge in a system known as the Atlas Reach. We must make a journey there with haste... before new dangers destroy the witnesses who can show me a way to the lost Crudarach, whose fate remains shrouded by the stars!"

5ab47029-539e-4fb6-96c1-9a7323be99fe.Text: "I will wait for your decision with great anticipation, elantach."

1bab6d00-2e6c-40f3-bb2e-25053edd33bd.Text: {n}Yrliet focuses her piercing gaze on you.{/n} "Their knowledge is the sole thread that may lead me to the truth, elantach. I ask that your metal-winged ship take me along that thread before it tears under the strain of time and circumstance."

8535f59a-6fcb-4328-895f-f4cf056609b6.Text: "No, I... I did not contact the Asuryani. I have no means to do so. But I had enough time to explore the stone jungle of your world while you were preoccupied with your urgent matters. The Path of the Outcast has taught me to observe and listen to the world around me — in this case, the throngs of mon-keigh at the port. Errant conversations, rumours, chance words — like parts of a speckled mosaic, they came together to form a hazy image. My kin were seen in the Atlas Reach, and now all we have to do is pull at the web of connections and possibilities to uncover whatever is concealed from the unseeing eye."

5dbb30b4-40c4-4ec5-b4c0-7e1876b745ed.Text: "You... will?" {n}The ice in Yrliet's eyes melts away for a moment.{/n} "Thank you, elantach. If this path indeed takes me to the truth... I will be indebted to you. A rare happening between our kinds."

c9c80183-995d-461a-9314-7ed955252aa8.Text: {n}Yrliet's gaze burns through you.{/n} "I only joined you to seek out my craftworld, mon-keigh! I helped you overcome adversity and foes, at times turning my weapon against my own kin! The time has come for you to honour our pact! I will leave your palace and wait for you to give the order to embark!"

e9cccbfa-df1d-416c-a091-bbb0ca503118.Text: Moans and wheezing fill the space, like a viscous substance in which it is impossible to breathe.

9d11eaf4-0ce6-4e03-9edc-d1f9c445937d.Text: A sinister device clearly designed to bring pain to an inattentive stranger.

35caa99b-2ab3-4585-80b0-452292c23a3d.Text: It seems the sinister device can be disabled, if one can get past it.

8d431f3e-3e09-4433-8c6b-1eb99b4ddefa.Text: It is difficult to make out anything in the cloudy liquid — only a silhouette can be seen.

3205169b-1b1e-4dfb-bef1-efe122b3cca4.Text: Whoever is imprisoned inside the capsule, they are moving ever so slightly.

d9e0fa22-72f6-469e-96ed-d53c297f9b56.Text: Muffled cries of pain come from the impenetrable darkness.

8b1d86fc-dd40-4c17-9169-c11e9e243646.Text: The corpse was dismembered and then reassembled — apparently, while still alive. Numerous stitches and burns indicate that the surgeon was not concerned with humane treatment.

2dbfde76-1fcf-4955-8680-d0b5e6085a47.Text: Somewhere, an unseen mechanism whirrs to life.

8caf7396-f017-4a51-9ac2-7ca3fb83e877.Text: The spires of Commorragh pierce the darkness like needles through living flesh.

74fbe665-5895-4b00-b412-e33233d85338.Text: A gloomy landscape appears before your eyes.

1b750077-1c1a-4709-ae9b-ce8f1c265111.Text: The laboratory is crammed with mechanisms and devices unknown to you, the sight of which makes you sick.

539b6f23-6432-4ba9-9753-5eed3e12c9f0.Text: "My interest is exhausted, specimen. Get out of my sight."

56e0e375-d3dc-4483-bc04-8c63510c0cca.Text: A strange capsule suspended in the air above the laboratory.

c0d68430-a847-4aed-a882-23cfdd0563a8.Text: The strange capsule emits a barely perceptible buzz. Its thick walls barely contain the sounds coming from within — the sounds of a living and tormented creature.

56f3b0f5-e0e5-4cca-a5e7-bfb0f6b9fbca.Text: A bizarre sculpture made with superhuman attention to detail.

e53d6d5c-3ca1-4ba6-8af3-321679482091.Text: The bizarre sculpture emits a barely audible sound... vaguely resembling a pained moan.

6243f1ce-77d7-4abc-9f7c-339cefbfe078.Text: The statue looks strange: you struggle to understand what culture it represents.

64fe3ee3-c422-4089-b9f9-164920e5c36c.Text: The alien-looking statue is clearly a trophy brought to Commorragh from somewhere in realspace.

5876fde9-08ef-4f12-8ada-7d1796d9036d.Text: There are faintly visible field lines on the smooth surface — probably some sort of power system.

494da36b-c9fc-48b6-987a-1dedbf327cba.Text: The bizarre stele emits a subtle humming sound. As you listen, you feel your head is about to tear apart in unbearable agony, as if the sound is resonating with something in your mind.

f7203e8e-006f-4664-8477-eb882f16771f.Text: The elevator is controlled by unknown mechanisms that the human mind seems unable to comprehend.

4320b00d-a232-45a6-bb2b-e3a47f37001f.Text: A strange panel whose purpose you do not comprehend.

171949fb-8037-48e9-8fc7-f44889eb1352.Text: In front of you is part of a xenodevice that controls the traps in this deadly place.

9f91efc8-153d-4c86-8561-e033fe9f49b3.Text: The sinister labyrinth looks like a death trap: it was probably created for just such a purpose.

17fc11f1-00c9-48b2-9e23-0d99b30b6c22.Text: The view of the intertwining and intricate passages of the labyrinth fascinates and draws the eye.

9a16789e-c423-4357-9f22-b64977b324e8.Text: The set of symbols looks unfinished, as if you only have half of the mysterious message in front of you.

f8362781-7dc9-4061-8854-373c428b54d6.Text: The dim light sources of Commorragh glow like swamp lights, making you dizzy and nauseous.

514c380c-9792-4268-95b8-fa7a186c6d13.Text: The vast towers of Commorragh spring up out of the darkness surrounding the spire at insane angles, violating all the laws of physics and perspective.

bfe1d27b-65dc-4180-87eb-dce091cb150c.Text: "I will tear your throat out personally, mon-keigh!"

dd539415-e934-43c5-add5-4d3157f44312.Text: "Why are you hiding behind a force field, Tervantias? Are you afraid of me?"

08f49d25-be60-4b8e-9d34-5cf52ede8fcd.Text: "Is that the Anguish Prospector next to you?"

44de02ca-dfee-41c5-8d43-dd54b06fe7ef.Text: "Hmm. What happens if I destroy this construct, I wonder?"

03e750a3-9eed-4b39-83e0-2367baa86937.Text: [Break the construct] "I think I shall try anyway!"

69763f93-edad-42dc-8883-ba0f092435dd.Text: Let the gods of the warp into Commorragh.

5462d7b9-750a-4102-8984-c9de94ffe10b.Text: [Pray to the gods of the warp] "Edge! See through my eyes a doorway into the Dark City and pray accept it as my offering!"

5e660b2e-b2cc-47b9-9c38-57c8be060295.Text: "You do not seem to share your kind's fear of the warp in the slightest. Does that make you mad or simply arrogant?"

06742de9-cf95-449a-b3ce-cfde0e1f7917.Text: "You said you were using the power of suns? Does that mean you are the one behind the disappearing stars?"

6e09161d-50af-4462-8146-4b8e6b798635.Text: [Break the construct] "I shall take the risk. The prospect of seeing you shriek in terror is just too tempting."

f198e15b-5368-4bcc-b96d-d44728355f47.Text: [Destroy the stifler] "I shall break your toy, but not because I care about ridding the galaxy of the Drukhari. I shall do it because I want you and your kind to know: no one uses me. Ever."

3698c8d0-a2b5-4fed-b6a7-b1be6e9aa5a8.Text: Destroyed Tervantias's stifler in the Spire of the Reaving Tempest.

79980141-a4a0-4d2c-a02a-6716e6e981bb.Text: [Destroy the stifler] "I cannot leave knowing that I did not make use of my chance to destroy this putrescent city. It is high time I put an end to this place!"

407780ec-afcc-422f-98b4-fe1048dbf20a.Text: Decided not to destroy Tervantias's stifler in the Spire of the Reaving Tempest.

c26e05e1-d159-4360-a479-084a3d0f014f.Text: [Leave the stifler intact] "Until our next meeting, Tervantias. It will be your last."

f8446cf2-8587-4e71-aa71-23ae52876e8f.Text: "While I'm here... do you happen to have any special equipment reserves left?"

57b61011-8818-437b-998c-1757f3113114.Text: [Attack] "At last, a chance to get rid of you, inhuman miscreant!"

890feb3c-e0fb-402f-964a-6e0f88a2c47e.Text: "Hello, Tervantias. I have not missed you either."

01317a65-8305-4a0b-9f3b-6e4fd335896e.Text: [Leave the construct intact] "I see. I have other questions to ask."

13fbe58e-447d-4924-b749-2b5ef8db8f84.Text: {n}The Haemonculus looks up from the control panel and gazes at you with disdain from the other side of the impenetrable force screen.{/n} "You survived, specimen. What a woeful lack of ability to follow orders! You were supposed to die, be it in the arena or in the Chasm. However, the servants of Aezyrraesh will soon remedy your blunder."

5634b54d-369b-4e59-be3b-37a6c59dea36.Text: "Specimen, as you might have noticed..." {n}The Haemonculus's limbs simultaneously gesture at the massive construct supporting the force field around him.{/n} "...this version of the stifler blocks both the energy that bleeds in from beyond the veil and any physical attempts to intrude inside its range. Your attempt at conversing is pointless — simply continue on the way to your demise and do not disturb me."

d38f658f-e9ba-48b5-8688-39c20df5d1bf.Text: "Go, disciple of the Truth. Return to your realspace and serve us as you did before. The path is open."

0dbdae45-e9dd-4fff-a425-4335659402a9.Text: "You think highly of yourself, specimen, but make no mistake: that will not make me deem you a worthy opponent."

c41e86d1-b7a8-433e-9826-ab75b85a7561.Text: "Elantach, though your heart may abound with anger..." {n}Yrliet looks around.{/n} "The immeasurable torment of powerful Farseers pervades this spire. If you were to risk destroying this construct... it could cause an irreparable tear in the veil in Commorragh."

a7d08548-93b6-4577-9a02-73f92c20fe10.Text: {n}Your shot finds its mark. Lightning charges run down the construct and the force field flickers a few times before dissipating. The heavy metallic hum is followed by a series of dull pops coming from every direction and you see warp portals bursting into bloom around you one after another and horrific, malformed claws reaching toward you from the other side.{/n} "What have you done? A curse upon you, mon-keigh!"

4c40a9ab-5d93-460b-8f61-f1a227c85d3c.Text: {n}A faint smile crosses the xenos's face.{/n} "Farewell, mon-keigh."

7628934e-fcba-4ca7-b771-4f6450612f69.Text: {n}Tervantias does not respond. You notice his upper lip twitching in a display of utter disgust.{/n}

d80afc09-51af-4706-b75f-4589b731bc1a.Text: "How strange... Next to this construct, my soul is both naked and swaddled at the same time. The colours around me melt away... and so do my powers!"

5d504108-df2a-44bc-890b-2d7c3c406845.Text: {n}The stifler is enormous and resembles the devices you have seen before. There is no doubt that its purpose is to suppress warp manifestations. However, you notice a few details that are out of step with the construct's otherwise typical Drukhari design: several of its parts were made from a material foreign to Commorragh and fused into its frame by an unknown force.{/n}

65b72423-d7d7-430d-8676-0be528701b74.Text: {n}The construct does not look too different from other creations of the Drukhari you have seen: an angular amalgam of unknown metal, sharp edges, and hints of wriggling living flesh.{/n}

ea0decb3-28f6-4948-86ad-3b092f17c265.Text: "What—" {n}Tervantias does not get to complete his question.{/n}

87205871-660f-47d3-aba9-27ba181d4085.Text: {n}The Haemonculus stares at you with eyes filled with unnatural light, like a shimmering ocean of silvery-blue with glimpses of nightmarish shadows lurking within. His body jerks and his many appendages contract convulsively.{/n} "Disciple of the Truth, you have outdone yourself. The Truth marches ever closer with quiet inevitability and once its blessing runs through the veins of this one's machinery... the Dark City will become its domain. Commorragh will fall."

91405cc0-21fb-42e3-83dc-4b492c64f541.Text: "Then you will give thousands of souls to Sai'lanthresh, elantach! You will wound one enemy to empower another. Once She Who Thirsts is done feasting in Commorragh, she will surely sink her claws into your worlds as well. Because nothing can sate her hunger."

30d242f9-c97a-4bcd-921e-2b2838010df9.Text: {n}After carefully examining the device, Pasqal says acerbically,{/n} "You did not make this, did you? I see more sophisticated structural elements in this mechanism than your mind is ever capable of fathoming. You observed someone do it and copied their work."

59d52b6c-2092-4f6d-8443-dacc13e06313.Text: "Nonsense!" {n}Tervantias leaps up, his voice ringing with genuine rage.{/n} "This is the work of my genius! The initial data was just a resource transformed into a masterpiece by the brilliance of my mind! How dare you even comment on my creation, you mon-keigh degenerate?"

7950b47c-5312-4beb-90de-2212a9b8a953.Text: "And the dispute between the Tech-Priest and the Haemonculus as to who is more skilful in the art of inflicting pain is won by Pasqal Haneumann. Well done, Magos."

10fc29b7-e09e-444f-9229-b7d0a466e7b4.Text: {n}Ulfar's voice turns quiet and insinuating, and a smile plays on his lips.{/n} "Yes, you are safe... for now. But as soon as you step out from behind this field, who knows in what shadowy corner we'll catch you? Any step outside could mean your death. Then again, perhaps you will not come out. You might sit here for a day or two, a month, a year... forever. Sitting and trembling. A small, frail inhuman, trapped in a prison of his own toys and fear. Which of us is in a cage now?"

acbba07b-9cc8-4a8c-a703-540c75a6698e.Text: {n}Tervantias's face stiffens into a mask of contempt but his working limbs begin to twitch nervously and his chest heaves with a mechanical creak as if he is suddenly running out of air.{/n}

1e09fe39-2531-48cc-8681-f32d87686d7b.Text: {n}The xenos responds with a self-satisfied chuckle.{/n} "Fear is the reaction of a weak mind presented with the inconceivable. Even our masters are liable to it... Oh, the pains it took me to convince the Archon to bring the spirit warriors into the Dark City. And to then conceal the evidence of the dimensional collapse that had destabilised the spire."

968ba6b0-37f2-4a25-94d2-29dc67d4599a.Text: "I alone acted without fear. I delved deeper, as a scalpel delves into flesh. I have designed devices that stifle the breath of the unreal, I am creating a weapon that will make the warp itself tremble, and I am using the raging power of suns as sustenance for my weapon! I know no fear, for in my mind, there is no inconceivable — only the unconceived."

67476d03-ea79-4b61-99e6-54772feacc38.Text: "Of course. My masterpiece needed an unthinkable amount of energy, but how could I let something as trifling as 'the unthinkable' stand in my way? The star you call Rykad was stolen at my behest, as were many before it."

7d701898-3db2-44ac-a7e5-5458afb26a8f.Text: {n}Tervantias's gloating tone becomes insufferable:{/n} "Have you been to the world you mon-keigh know as Santiel's Pride? I only recently took its sun while you were busy spilling Wych guts on the arena floor. It was most amusing to watch your pathetic planet freeze to its very core... How fascinating it is that such a paltry sacrifice as the lives of several million mon-keigh can serve something as great as my masterpiece."

090e3865-7a25-41e3-9f6f-9d82232baa8c.Text: {n}You hear a whisper behind you — Kibellah's ardent, ecstatic whisper. She is praying to the Undying One, her eyes closed, a blissful smile on her lips, clutching her weapons in a white-knuckled grip. Then she opens her eyes wide and says quietly,{/n} "I cannot tell you how glad I am to meet you again, Vil'Tervantias."

a51e984c-f6e3-4ec6-ae03-e5639f78425c.Text: {n}Heinrix laughs, but his laughter sounds morbid and disturbing.{/n} "What's this? A chance to open a warp breach in the heart of our enemies' bastion? I did not expect anything in this damned place to put a smile on my face. I was wrong."

943f8448-bc2a-47f5-9199-f4b56644b559.Text: {n}The Haemonculus cocks his head to one side and stares at you.{/n} "No, mon-keigh. No more handouts."

397e2f87-aaf9-4651-ac51-6c03a691869c.Text: {n}The {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_CorruptedPatchmonster}warp-infected flesh{/d} that Tervantias implanted inside the Anguish Prospector at your suggestion responds to the call of Chaos energy coming from the portals. The monster's body develops lumps and begins to burst, revealing abhorrent purplish light emanating from within. Its chest erupts with a revolting squelching sound, forming a maw with claws in place of a tongue that bites its master's head off, then its serrated tentacles tear the rest of his body to bloody scraps and fall to the floor, still squirming.{/n}

2e09e0e9-9bd7-4975-92cb-a91f115def7d.Text: {n}Jae swallows nervously.{/n} "Look, shereen, I'd love to slap the damned ashmag myself for all the foul things he's done to us, but I just... I don't want to be torn apart by daemons, you know?"

275e19a8-8464-4275-9dd1-f538b5587bc7.Text: {n}The xenos narrows his eyes at you and hisses,{/n} "You must be thinking that the moment you do it, Commorragh will descend into daemonic mayhem and the valorous Rogue Trader will have rid the universe of the abominable Drukhari and finally flee these dark halls? Before all that happens, specimen, the daemons that will arrive will rip your flesh to shreds and devour everyone in sight. And while you are busy writhing in agony, I will have enough time to put everything back in order."

bd4b5177-134b-47ba-9d57-a5b0533ebb36.Text: "Yes, it is. You had the opportunity to admire its potential in action, didn't you, mon-keigh? Are you senseless enough to follow Keykeross's example and experience my {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_PatchedMonster}new Grotesque{/d}'s abilities first-hand?"

34a335b5-526b-4b3f-a459-d859d0df803d.Text: {n}Your attack misses its target: the force field that separates you is too strong. The Haemonculus lets out a few clicks.{/n} "You waste your strength. This version of the stifler can both hold back the veil and protect me from distractions such as you. Now go and do not disturb me."
