7c0ee664-159a-440e-a05e-ef781df5999e.Text: {n}Your gaze momentarily loses focus and the only thing you can still see clearly is the massive stifler construct to which Tervantias is referring. You suspect... no, you know for a certainty that the device contains a flaw invisible to ordinary eyes. A flaw made by Tervantias himself, one that is enough to channel warp corruption into the heart of the stifler.{/n}

e464308a-92e5-4cdc-94bd-d9573abfb643.Text: A mysterious tool required to open a Webway Gate.

eaff6368-6aff-4a2e-9964-b98f739df420.Text: [Give Marazhai to the Mandrakes] "Take the xenos. I have no need of him."

c584ef86-1a44-4121-98be-dbfe30c50f02.Text: "Marazhai stays with me. Away with you, beasts!"

c640afb4-3db3-4f26-8e3e-135f13b93e45.Text: "I certainly hope that our partnership is worth it, Marazhai. Keeping you around is costly."

9fed8973-5ec3-4f2f-93f3-c4db4aaa61b5.Text: [Kill Marazhai] "Grant you the pleasure of torturing this vicious freak to death? I think not!"

b6b24c81-05c7-478c-8d75-0844b6b56379.Text: {n}The Mandrake's words are barely comprehensible: the creature is clearly not accustomed to the tongue of its dark kin.{/n} "The Dracn din't offer a scrifice for our dids. The Dracn must become the scrifice."

9703788a-82f7-43c6-a289-7a391046f54c.Text: {n}Marazhai places a hand on his weapon. His voice sounds calm but his gaze is tense as he peers at the dark creature before him.{/n} "You should not have crawled out of the abyss that your wretched kind call home. Consider our pact broken. Nazrakhei did not hold up his end of the bargain, so I had to finish the job myself."

cc028b9f-23b6-4fa0-8736-372f9970b7f2.Text: "The rsult... matters not. The scrifice will be made." {n}The Mandrake's head turns to you.{/n} "Make the sacrifice, mon-keigh. The tribe never relents. The tribe will find you."

d2c40a0d-87e4-4196-afae-dab03c817ab4.Text: "Throne's mercy... Lord Captain, it was extravagant enough of you to get yourself a pet xenos and now we discover that he comes with a whole gaggle of his kinfolk!"

b4f61230-59b7-432e-b231-e1a057a049ad.Text: "Mind your tongue before I cut it down for you. The Mandrakes care not about mon-keigh. The Mandrakes want me. Even if they were to grow bold enough to come for me... oh, it would be quite an amusement to behold."

c9368d36-e39a-4e0d-8252-1bb37776c3f5.Text: {n}The xenos's body crumples to the floor, staining it with dark blood. The Mandrake scrapes its claws against the floor and lets out a wrathful hiss.{/n} "You will pay, mon-keigh! The tribe will take you and your whole pack for this one Dracn!"

380d7afc-fcb3-425d-88bd-ecc22a718bed.Text: "Hshhh... Senseless crture. The tribe will fnd you. The tribe will have its scrifice."

8fd4e1a5-2e42-4287-a433-9b36be1fda76.Text: {n}The Drukhari glowers at you.{/n} "So is keeping you, {name}."

3a76add3-6d44-4e74-9a82-528373e728cc.Text: {n}The Drukhari draws his weapon.{/n} "And if your filth needs a lesson in the language of pain..."

34916282-6f83-41bd-afca-60f986ef658c.Text: {n}Marazhai gives you a look of bafflement and fury but does not get the chance to say anything in response.{/n}

0ce5b203-3a06-4c42-a5fa-1b2b94b7771c.Text: "Oh, you can have him! I'm sure no one will miss him."

81c5ae49-6bd2-4725-b1f1-7a88788499a9.Text: "Lord Captain, these creatures... It is as if they absorb the colours around them and spew out darkness. I do not think they are lying or trying to intimidate us. They will come from the shadows, just as they came once before."

4ecf0339-94c3-47bb-8567-1a3d906b11f7.Text: "It appears that the consequences of a certain someone's actions have caught up to them."

4a303258-3236-4183-a9c0-516721437a88.Text: "With a pure heart, I will raise my horn in praise to the Allfather on the day that this sharp-tongued scum dies. The foul xenos may be a meagre trophy, but he is still our trophy. Giving him up without a fight to this talking mop is shameful."

c17a03e6-5f05-41ce-86f7-6a0c11745e12.Text: "This xenos's actions have done great harm to Humanity, and justice demands that—" {n}Solomorne falters.{/n} "No, I can't lie to myself — I don't want any human being to sully their weapon with killing that scumbag. Let him be devoured by his own kind."

9393ceb4-af0f-42f5-9fbc-eb2543a2b586.Text: "Fine. Just point out where this property of yours is."

1de5a9bf-6ae0-429a-b854-bec1607b83fd.Text: "I will not waste my time on that."

b8be5925-2e9f-47b2-93d9-06e40d5afe7e.Text: "Yrliet, what is the plan to find your kin?"

3a8b7a93-68fa-4bec-b715-b06d1557a712.Text: "Marazhai, what should we expect to find inside the spire?"

e1722209-1b7c-4b59-bc7f-217b006d479c.Text: [Venture into the depths of the spire]

54120a05-44d3-4d9d-ac14-e60c2629556a.Text: "It's settled then. Let's get out of this hole."

2046ba5a-c804-4ae2-b15f-30f2a555e86e.Text: "How do you know how to unseal the Gate? I find such deep trust between two Drukhari too good to be true."

7728a532-8c3e-4dba-9118-2094429c8e47.Text: "I do not trust you. It must be a trap intended to secure a pardon for yourself."

982c13c2-916d-494b-a2d3-9a14810b0bfe.Text: "Come along. When we find the Farseers, you will have all your answers."

42f1e8f8-2135-465d-87c1-8b33cb26923b.Text: "Don't even think about it! If you leave now, there will be no way back for you."

d6e75ff0-6d63-425b-9e8b-a118a4d0b8f7.Text: {n}The gargantuan spire is too large to see in its entirety. Its true proportions are shrouded in shadows, and you feel as if those shadows try to envelop and swallow you whenever you look away.{/n}

b04b6781-221d-491e-9bba-d3aacdd16659.Text: "Ai'elethra has long since guided me down the roads of thorns. And you, elantach, are just another fleeting companion along one of them. Ask me a hundred times if I would choose to save my kin or walk at a mon-keigh's side, and my answer will not change once. Farewell, stranger from the darkness amid the stars. Here our Paths diverge."

638b741a-96c4-4466-bf14-2b12561632f2.Text: "So that's our way out, eh? Can't wait... I can't wait to get far away from here... I can't believe I'm saying this but I really want to see a real sun, not those pale feeble things among the spires!"

38437e42-0ccb-4e87-af29-f3960056fd6d.Text: {n}Grinning savagely, Ulfar says with undisguised joy,{/n} "I smell blood in the air — blood that is about to be spilt. I hear the echo of clashing swords and the terrified screams of xenos writhing under our heel. Allfather, what a marvellous feast you have prepared for me!"

e6fe8bfe-22f6-4cc5-9a30-0d27edc67f0a.Text: "Of course. First, we need to find my raider. Most likely, at the end of the dock outside the spire. Let's go to the end of this terrace before we enter the spire."

b16d98a6-fa79-4cf2-84d4-f2058d3f3825.Text: "If you wish for me to use my knowledge and open a path out of Commorragh for us, find this item. Without it, I am powerless to make the Webway allow us entry into its labyrinths."

847f5a46-bd2e-4603-8c4a-edf0217fd7d2.Text: "The Spire of the Reaving Tempest. The seat of my Kabal. Both a place to find respite from the scheming of our enemies and a deadly trap for those too weak and soft for our ranks." {n}Marazhai tilts his head and glances at you.{/n} "The heart of the spire contains a secret: an ancient Webway Gate that has remained sealed for many, many aeons. Yremeryss kept it in case Vect's noose happened to tighten around the Kabal's neck. No one save for her and a certain other Kabalite knows where exactly in realspace the Gate leads. A perfect escape route. And I can open it for you."

605f60bf-a994-4819-aed6-a44d3d8886e6.Text: "Elantach..." {n}Yrliet touches the glowing stone in her chest and turns her aching gaze to the spire. Her face is burdened with a strange expression, as if a roaring torrent of sadness, fear, and rage is about to erupt.{/n} "My kin from Crudarach are still there, I can sense it. As I can sense the flames of their souls inexorably going out."

7cc51106-6813-4b62-b8e9-1fa03362dbc1.Text: {n}Marazhai grips his weapon.{/n} "You cannot wait to leave Commorragh... and I cannot wait to pay my sister a visit. Rest assured, she is somewhere nearby."

0470daaa-75e5-4f58-9f43-2773664d2039.Text: "Trust? How unreliable. No, I simply abducted and tortured the Kabalite who was privy to this secret. There is even a chance that Yremeryss believed the story about the pathetic weakling running off."

cad50131-650d-4a5a-8743-a0385945d1b3.Text: "Bah!" {n}The Kabalite lets out a grim laugh.{/n} "It will take more than your hide for Yremeryss to accept me back... Still, have it your way. It will provide me with a great deal of amusement to watch you scurry about in search of a different escape out of Commorragh."

c48cf473-bf37-4f98-93d1-b724aab05d12.Text: "Please, while there is still time, I... we must save them! Let me accompany you into that nest of depravity, that domain of pain, anger, and betrayal of my kind." {n}Yrliet's voice is trembling like a taut string and her eyes are clouded with darkness.{/n} "Fury and fear are devouring me from the inside out and I do not know what frightens me more: the grim answers that hide behind the spire's walls or the scars that my heart will bear once I discover them. Yet, I must learn the truth about my world. Perhaps... this is the day the Outcast finds her Path again."

3865877e-2715-4756-b16b-bcbd5df9fbaa.Text: "Farseers are not easy captives to keep. Whatever the Dark Ones are using to repress my kin's powers, those... tools will be noticeable. I will find a way to them."

f0bf6cff-ad05-4fa0-a49d-da930370514d.Text: "Kabalites. Wyches. Incubi — at Yremeryss's side." {n}He pauses for a moment, an expression of concern flashing across his pale features.{/n} "That is all."

ee363996-10ed-4e59-a833-6ab6d3d1ea24.Text: "Then I will go alone." {n}Her voice is calm and quiet, without any hint of a plea or reproach. All you can hear is unshakeable resolve.{/n} "Only after I have found the germ of truth within the spire's dark halls will we reunite."

7c788f1e-8474-43b6-a6ea-75726ae804f2.Text: "So that is your answer?" {n}Yrliet covers her eyes with her hand and laughs for the first time, sadly and bitterly.{/n} "How could I ever have thought that a mon-keigh would... It does not matter. One day, your fear and hatred will consume you from within, elantach. Praise Isha, I will no longer be at your side when they do. Farewell, stranger from the darkness amid the stars. Our shared Path ends here."

50c74d2a-c356-42f1-9235-bf613edc99e8.Text: "Fury and fear are devouring me from the inside out, and I do not know what frightens me more — the grim answers that hide behind the spire's walls or the scars that my heart will bear once I discover them. Yet, I must learn the truth about my world. Perhaps... this is the day the Outcast finds her Path again."

3a5a4cfb-3641-4efa-9258-8619f10a43d5.Text: {n}Yrliet sends you one last look of suppressed sorrow, turns away, and disappears into the darkness a moment later.{/n}

4b684ac2-cb7d-4e38-a46b-a36ab1f42b54.Text: {n}Tossing her fiery-red hair as she turns, Yrliet rushes off.{/n}

bb41ced7-6611-4ba9-942c-2769670fbe5f.Text: "You speak the truth, elantach. Let us be on our way. We will tear their lives from the clutches of my insatiable cousins." {n}She turns her face to you and, despite her tense expression, you see the corners of her mouth twitch.{/n} "I find myself wondering if a single Farseer, gazing at the hazy visions of things yet to come, ever glimpsed a future where the key to their salvation stemmed from the duo of a mon-keigh and an Outcast."

04e9e8dd-44e5-4f36-a649-f11bcb3a3a11.Text: {n}The Spire of the Reaving Tempest welcomes you with muffled noises seeping from its dark walls: distant voices, footsteps, and screams of pain.{/n}

6f66c448-9b4c-41b7-800b-177ded654a4a.Text: "As for the Webway Gate that the Arebennian mentioned... For it to open before you and let you enter the Webway, you would require help from one of our kind." {n}Yrliet's brow furrows.{/n} "I could... try to open the Gate. But to do that, I would need a certain construct: a resonance device. The masters of this place must keep it close at hand."

5b8fbfe1-a73a-4da3-ad8c-ba7d61c15130.Text: "Try to avoid dying before our next meeting, elantach."

bc8e2708-11d2-498e-ab51-73d6bd67aa9c.Text: "I have a..." {n}Marazhai stops, searching for the right word.{/n} "A desire. Before we leave the spire, there is something I want to pick up. Something... memorable. I left it in the Kabal's abode. I do not want it to fall into the hands of others when carrion eaters and looters flood the spire after we are gone. There could be something in it for you..." {n}He lets the last words hang in the air.{/n}

0378f420-25ab-482b-b951-90110cf928e5.Text: "By the Golden Throne, we made it! And all in one piece. Not bad... But we can't relax just yet — we've still got a long way to go."

81e68fae-e9f8-4630-bff8-f069749b9a6a.Text: {n}Marazhai scoffs with contempt and turns away.{/n}

988803a8-4255-4aeb-84dd-51215fd80ba5.Text: "The colours here... are especially dark and dangerous. It is as if I am drowning in a bottomless ocean of billowing haze. But... what is it? I feel a faint tremor coming from deep inside the spire. Like the call of the Immaterium, except much purer."

d9386c21-6701-4d9d-8e59-e2ee01d6534d.Text: "You are right, peddler: hope blinds. You sounded like a true commander just now. The xenos city must have given you a shock — have you considered repenting and breaking away from your shameful past once we are back in the Expanse?"

23f05a81-b1b5-4a26-9c95-d815eb4e8fc6.Text: "There's only one past I wanted to break from, and I have already done so, thank you! And also — warp damn it, lawman, you've said it yourself: hope blinds. So drop it with the daydreaming and making plans about my future!"

7d7ce810-4aff-4abe-bbe1-7d7d70fd4479.Text: "We will save your kin, Yrliet. You have my word as a Rogue Trader."

4dd9b2ac-13e6-4de1-aff5-6abf1058ac7d.Text: "We might look for them or we might not. I will not promise you anything."

a5b01130-806b-4cd6-a023-66b0976cae03.Text: "I find myself wondering if a single Farseer, gazing at the hazy visions of things yet to come, ever glimpsed a future where the key to their salvation stemmed from the duo of a mon-keigh and an Outcast." {n}She turns her face to you and nods with gratitude.{/n} "Come along. Let us tear the Farseers' lives from the clutches of my insatiable cousins."

5c2a2d0e-e79e-4cef-b0ff-c1a0ed1e3218.Text: "The xenos have caused my house enough grief. As have you. Begone! I am no longer interested in your talents."

f1bff5b2-47ad-4522-b4b5-675978656343.Text: "I doubt we will have time for xenos rescue missions."

69272bbd-2db0-4814-a87a-44c2f2cb7848.Text: "I see you have taken Tervantias under your wing. Again."

8c050375-552d-4377-ad8e-f8b7f73ce743.Text: "All those craftworld fragments, all those prisoners... Was it all worth it, xenos?"

0de61c40-a5d2-40e4-a325-f37da5ea196c.Text: "The toys of your pet Haemonculus did little to help him."

a72cb848-385f-456d-b108-7f8566e039e5.Text: "If you wish to live, then get out of my way. I have come for the Gate, not your life."

03e0b389-4ec6-4e79-a0ab-c922857b1d4c.Text: "I have grown tired of the games and machinations you have ushered into my realm. Prepare to die, Archon Yremeryss."

75a746d7-8e12-4386-8225-f0ac09b8360b.Text: "What did you need the Farseers for? Why take such a risk?"

59f39a88-efcb-48f0-aa60-5234b8400b97.Text: "Marazhai, do you have any last words for your sister?"

a782ab6d-077d-4ba0-a393-c52bb9969a39.Text: "In the name of the God-Emperor, I will destroy you, xenos!"

84725bd6-0a6c-45a6-b2fa-56891beae8f5.Text: "Have you any final words to speak before your demise, Yremeryss?"

31c988b7-632b-408a-aacd-61982825a50d.Text: {n}Yremeryss gazes at you. The two of you lock eyes for the first time, an icy darkness churning in her stare.{/n} "Worm. Insect. You have... the nerve... to stand before me again? You should have gasped your last breath long ago. Very well. I will rid this arrogant mon-keigh of {mf|his|her} final breath myself."

44b89f8d-dbce-435e-83c0-32f48330ed2c.Text: "Miserable vermin!" {n}Yremeryss hisses through her teeth upon seeing you. Despite her blazing eyes and her bared teeth, you plainly discern what is in the Drukhari's heart: {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_DaemonicBreach}fear{/d}.{/n} "I will see to it that death comes for you slowly!"

3c76c13d-28e8-4550-b70c-cf23ad666d63.Text: {n}Marazhai draws his weapon in a single fluid motion.{/n} "Before your soul perishes in the maw of She Who Thirsts, I will teach it pain — the kind of pain you have never known in the whole of your existence, sister."

cd01d844-c81e-4fef-9f07-63cce7dba5c4.Text: {n}The Archon's gaze shifts away from you — to Marazhai. A venomous smile spreads across her face.{/n} "My former Dracon... My inept executioner. Have you found yourself a new {mf|master|mistress}?"

80863cab-fc3f-4f49-bb9f-5c8bdeaa8fdc.Text: {n}Yrliet's spirit stone flashes on her chest and the Ranger's hands tremble on the grip of her rifle.{/n} "Your death will give me no joy, Archon Yremeryss. But it may give peace to the spirits of my kin."

32a97142-9cdd-471e-a9e8-aead3260ba1b.Text: "What about you, child of Crudarach? How does it feel to know that you could not save yourself, your family, or your precious craftworld?"

7f2560de-d1d7-4942-93a9-a0667b0e33cb.Text: {n}Yremeryss tilts her head.{/n} "I intend to live, mon-keigh. I will live. And I will continue my work and lead my Kabal to greatness."

91013677-06b4-4f46-9dc9-fb6a2ec1fef8.Text: "Spare yourself the struggle of comprehending the meaning behind my deeds, wretched creature. Crudarach was to be my key to power the likes of which the Reaving Tempest could only dream of. Majesty is mine alone to claim, and I will claim it!"

812e0bbf-1d3d-455a-b1be-fb1c1579db65.Text: {n}Yremeryss smirks.{/n} "Oh, I am certain the Haemonculus still has plenty of unbroken toys left. You haven't seen even a tenth of what Tervantias commands."

241d7675-77f2-4f9d-bae8-e3f9b15124b0.Text: {n}Yremeryss laughs. The sound is reminiscent of a snake hissing.{/n} "Oh, mon-keigh. You are a brazen one, aren't you? Will you still be so brash when I flay you open and string you up by your sinews?"

6b2defb6-d3c0-4794-8cc3-08a3e6a8dc7d.Text: "My servants are heading out on a new hunt as we speak. Who will become their prey? Which lights will wink out in the void? How many mon-keigh will perish in the darkness?" {n}Yremeryss lets out a mocking laugh.{/n} "You will never know."

4d33db7d-fb23-45a7-8366-7175249fd388.Text: {n}Marazhai narrows his eyes.{/n} "You purged the ranks of the Kabal and cleared all obstacles from your path? Even in that you failed, you talentless wretch. I am still here. I will be the one to purge the Reaving Tempest of you."

283906b9-8ceb-43e4-83e6-7d0279c1f3bd.Text: {n}Yremeryss stiffens, and a moment later bares her teeth in a furious hiss. The Archon of the Reaving Tempest raises a hand to signal to her underlings.{/n}

d42cc4c6-000e-41ec-9951-67db11e5e2fb.Text: {n}Marazhai laughs mockingly.{/n} "Dragging Farseers into our spire in an attempt to trigger a dysjunction — that was your grand vision? It is a pity you have not bothered to lead a single raid in recent years — it would have been entertaining to watch you order a fleet to fly headlong into mon-keigh structures and detonate their engines, all to secure a bright future for the Kabal!"

1b9a677d-f130-4126-b759-6963e753c58f.Text: "You lie, xenos! This is the foul slander of an enemy of Humanity!"

43138142-055d-4e0a-8202-1d795110f677.Text: "Blessed Throne..." {n}Abelard closes his eyes and shakes his head in sorrow. It seems the xenos's admission has aged him five years.{/n}

22a2a4f0-af37-46e9-bdf6-ff02dccc7522.Text: "Die? Ha!" {n}Yremeryss draws her weapon.{/n} "You are the only one who dies today. And after I am done with you, I will pay a visit to realspace — to observe the terror and ruin wrought by my Kabal."

5d105f63-24fa-4824-9249-144214b47333.Text: {n}Marazhai's lips stretch into a saccharine smile.{/n} "My poor older sister, you still cannot stand the fact that I was born... but how can I be surprised? It is hard to think of more glaring proof that our mother considered her first attempt to continue the line a failure."

2d11bff7-13ef-47c4-8fc5-c847f89a908a.Text: "Do you know, mon-keigh, that so many of your kind have had their lives cut short at the hands of their own kin? I used you to purge the ranks of the Kabal, to clear all obstacles from my path. I used you to accomplish my goals. I colluded with your kind — despite your much-vaunted hatred of xenos, which ought to have prevented any of you from even considering such a thing!"

06252b62-1998-4392-abcd-93dd974146db.Text: "You destroyed your future with your own hands. When the truth became known, all the weapons of Commorragh would have turned against you — and against my Kabal!"

43659072-d962-4db4-8b89-d73b600fdb0b.Text: "And this coward was my Dracon? You are too quick to call the Reaving Tempest your Kabal — you have neither the ambition nor the vision to lead all these warriors full of lust for power and blood!"

af00239a-d5c8-44d0-bf1d-a2c0bd81f1b8.Text: "It sickens me to say this, but I believe the xenos. I know what kinds of things people will do in the name of personal gain, and now that the foul spawn has confessed, the situation in the Expanse suddenly makes a lot more sense."

3f09a6e9-d2b5-47ca-b015-d073828fe2c9.Text: "No, Archon, you are destined for retribution. Blood for blood. I cannot destroy your entire Kabal as you destroyed Crudarach but I have the strength to cut off the snake's head."

bbbdb71c-0dbe-4ad4-9990-2223a8bc6b00.Text: "Oh, no. That could not be further from the truth. Archon Aezyrraesh dies today. Here. Now."

83e6d1fb-3e5a-48aa-a287-14c845b37f43.Text: "The Haemonculus may play as many of his little games in the arena as he pleases. I am satisfied with what he provides for the ranks of the Kabal. That makes him valuable enough to spare his life."

621f8b2c-7de4-4453-86f5-a6fd291400a8.Text: "Poor little Outcast..." {n}Yremeryss leers at Yrliet, staring into her eyes like a predator.{/n} "The suffering of your brothers and sisters nourished us for a long time... Now you too will give me your pain!"

32be10b6-9007-4eb9-b54a-4ff46889d768.Text: "So be it, I will humour you before death... If only to step out of another's shadow once and for all. I wished to orchestrate a little dysjunction — and with my helpless brethren in my clutches, who are capable of tearing apart the veil with their mere presence, it could not have been simpler. When the time came, the Farseers would be my weapon against the Reaving Tempest's rivals — under cover of the cataclysm, my blades would behead all those who stood in the way of my ascent!"

8696bf52-40f1-4963-8252-edd1ec9c9ff8.Text: "Now you speak only with the permission of your pet mon-keigh?" {n}Yremeryss laughs mockingly.{/n} "My insignificant little brother, you never should have crawled out of our mother's womb, your existence is a disgrace to our blood..."

579dd309-9107-47ca-9d9e-e55ae798ef37.Text: "Such amusing loftiness coming from an insect... Your toy god cannot help you. And nor can he help your fellow kin, that delectable prey still confined to the boundless darkness of realspace."

738337d9-8f3b-48ae-b030-486259899e65.Text: "Where can we find the main cogitator?"

2e7946b7-79f0-48ad-abc7-3eb767abaeea.Text: "Where should we set up the ambush?"

6d2cc62e-6e52-4ba0-bb0b-5fe7335e0751.Text: "How did your agents discover this place?"

341856a6-0992-444d-8bd8-7f53f78f8978.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, my agents report that Kunrad Voigtvir and his pet xenos will soon arrive. We have roughly an hour to inspect the station and set up the ambush. Unless, of course, you prefer to face the conspirators head-on." {n}Achilleas brings a trembling hand with his gilded respirator to his lips.{/n}

8cb3802a-55d0-4426-8ab0-6b514cc03b1b.Text: {n}Heinrix looks at Achilleas intently.{/n} "A shrewd and well-considered suggestion. I can see that you have taken the time to learn as much about this station as you could. Good work."

5a6d39e6-c33f-4cda-a81d-2c3ca3ad91b0.Text: {n}Achilleas coughs.{/n} "Far from it, Master van Calox. Alas, my options were rather limited: we never properly scouted this place." {n}He lowers his head, too ashamed to bring himself to look Heinrix in the eye.{/n}

7231604a-a06e-431b-b2db-0b34cb315af8.Text: {n}Achilleas sweeps into a bow.{/n} "I'm sorry to have made you needlessly worry about me. Discerning the traitor's plans and preparing a place to capture him... cost me a great deal."

7e21fda7-da69-43de-adb4-4ee7d4f2b59b.Text: "Regrettably, my agents did not have time to draw up a map of the main compartment. The cogitator must be somewhere nearby, perhaps in one of the adjacent chambers."

05ac1aeb-e650-468d-a807-f07d3dc94286.Text: "We have two enforcer squads and your personal retinue. We should look for well concealed or safely protected places that could fit enough of our people. The station may offer other opportunities that might help us capture the enemy."

37f48e98-cd87-496e-949f-658d95e8fd3b.Text: {n}Achilleas smiles enigmatically and shrugs.{/n} "Rogue Traders have their secrets to success. The Inquisition has its own."

cd9828fb-b87f-431e-9057-fc31df0dfc15.Text: "I will remain by the entrance and stand guard in case Kunrad and the xenos arrive earlier than anticipated. Once you have completed the inspection, please make sure to depressurise the other compartments, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. And may the God-Emperor help you!" {n}He coughs.{/n}

6247fa4c-cb35-4b9d-be2b-522b9aac7932.Text: "Whatever course of action you choose, we should depressurise all compartments except for the main one. That way the conspirators will have no choice but to try and restore the station's systems using the main cogitator. And that is where we will engage them."

6a048aeb-c5d0-403f-b737-64314f550c22.Text: "Am I the only one who thinks there's something off about this place? It's too... easy. Everything's coming together too nicely. When have we ever been so lucky, shereen?"

70870766-d8f2-4863-9c28-ba53d31203b7.Text: "Heydari, what exactly is it you are doubting — the credibility of the subjects of the Golden Throne or the Lord Captain's decisions? Take some time to carefully consider your answer."

d0c25f41-0162-4608-a3f2-3ef1c4eed0a0.Text: {n}Cassia draws her pale brows together as if agonising over something.{/n} "Your colours are so mottled, tattered, and feverish, Master Scalander... I have not noticed such turmoil in your soul before."

9773e2ec-1010-4719-9a5b-c80c1046c99b.Text: {n}Idira sniffs and brushes her fingers against your sleeve.{/n} "My voices are harping on about treachery — about what Voigtvir did, obviously... This is a chance to pin down the Master of Whispers, isn't it? Oh, I'd wait here months for that!"

815fd7c1-292d-4b32-ba22-5f70528374b1.Text: "Plenty of room for manoeuvre and solid cover from the front... This spot will do for an ambush."

5a88b443-facc-4c79-a3c2-ea8fd8b9107b.Text: "Hmm. There is enough space behind this grate to fit a small unit."

6a9b9c8c-2ef5-4578-b9a7-5acba23a84af.Text: "Would you look at that: these containers are packed full of explosives! Your people do know how to set up tripwires, don't they?"

c9c8689b-35b7-4b69-a552-d98bfc196242.Text: "The chant of the sacred mechanisms contains an error. Detecting evidence of tampering—"

c95db39e-7c25-4630-a6b2-1dc44da9b2a1.Text: "These sacred machines are in need of a maintenance ritual. They could serve as our allies in the fight against the traitors."

f78e64b3-350d-4136-aa52-084b3eeec869.Text: "This unit is perplexed. The protocol is flawed. Immediate withdrawal recomme—"

1eda595e-6909-4289-891a-edc2f999dc98.Text: "What did you do to him, xenos?"

b3dd9d39-253c-4b81-b283-af1555c6efd0.Text: "May the God-Emperor guide my hand when I bring punishment upon the traitorous heretic and the unholy xenos!"

1211c3a5-bff2-4443-96ac-aca2ef10408f.Text: "Damn... you..." {n}Heinrix growls hoarsely as he tries to get up, driven more by rage than by physical strength.{/n} "I... will strangle... you both... myself..."

91f8143d-fa06-4ac8-84af-2fb6fc6be25f.Text: {n}Marazhai nonchalantly kicks the arm Heinrix is using to prop himself up and he tumbles to the ground.{/n} "That seems unlikely, mon-keigh. Both of your fates are now mine to decide."

530ce142-535f-4e8b-9148-5bdb6420f9b9.Text: "Forgive... Forgive me, Master van Calox..." {n}Achilleas's voice is trembling with sorrow and regret.{/n}

b838799d-eb44-4c30-9356-4341d4cb0aa7.Text: {n}The xenos turns his attention to someone else.{/n} "You have proven quite useful, mon-keigh. An uncanny quality for your kind." {n}He is speaking to Achilleas, who is lying nearby, his pale face contorted in terror and pain, and his eyes wide open and tearful.{/n} "I may find other uses for you in the future."

28e4a5a8-d72c-4c01-8a70-d57b881716b2.Text: "Nothing untoward. We merely had a conversation. It happened long ago when I was visiting your pitiful planet. You thought the burnt mon-keigh escaped with his life because of his talents? No. He escaped because I let him go. But not before ordering him to arrive at my command with you in tow. Which he did as soon as I sent him the signal."

cc4268cd-c91e-4636-b38f-0d4e92f73d73.Text: {n}His last words fill your head like the deafening echo of a ship's siren. The gas creeps deeper into your lungs, eating away at them hungrily, as the agony spreads down your every limb. You are suffocating.{/n}

47163698-681b-4064-a8c2-b47181924db6.Text: "Do not judge him so harshly, Rogue Trader. I have yet to meet a mon-keigh who can resist my powers of persuasion." {n}You hear a predatory laugh from inside the helmet.{/n}

701116da-fd1a-4858-971a-40fb6b5c47b6.Text: "Y-Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I..." {n}Achilleas shakes his head, grimacing from the pain wrought by the poison gas.{/n}

0925b54e-d2a3-438d-a1ba-f2220b22b3f8.Text: {n}Servo-drives whine under the Tech-Priest's scarlet robe in a dogged but fruitless attempt to lift his body.{/n} "The inferior flesh... has betrayed me..."

fcc5c77e-1d09-4692-a350-e03d49fb1136.Text: "You must have punished it poorly, iron mon-keigh. No matter. As a captive, you will learn how to apply the art of torture to make it fear the very thought of betrayal."

782aa063-b7ce-4cf6-a35d-c96f7f39fca4.Text: {n}Kibellah reaches for her weapon with one hand while trying to support herself with the other.{/n} "How could... intoxicants... overpower me..."

21dca961-1e83-4795-9d38-371295f23e98.Text: "I was warned that one of the mon-keigh was fond of experimenting with incapacitating substances. This gas contains something prepared just for you." {n}With a gloating sneer, the xenos steps on her head, pushing it into the floor with a crunch.{/n}

2d711356-d7ad-493e-aead-0c384d6bc4aa.Text: "Glaito..." {n}Solomorne is either trying to reach out to the cyber-mastiff or gesture a command to him, but the dog is lying still, completely unresponsive.{/n}

6a27aa10-7cdf-4360-b926-6a576336a504.Text: "A futile effort. I was informed that the mon-keigh might bring some of their primitive toys here with them, so I made sure that the toxin accounted for their particular quirks."

6a428210-d379-4747-bd00-634719093284.Text: {n}Marazhai clicks his tongue and shakes his head.{/n} "You disappoint me, mon-keigh. I have heard the pleas of millions and the curses of billions. You can do better."

a6540d5a-0941-4c70-92e1-07ba767ce69c.Text: "As for you..." {n}There is a disturbing gleam in the Dracon's eyes.{/n} "You will have your share of paralysing dreams too. But I am going to keep you. You are far too precious to be surrendered to a madman playing with fire."

640b0a6f-b370-4586-98b9-50196d9974dd.Text: {n}Marazhai takes a close look at your companions squirming in agony, then gestures nonchalantly to someone you cannot see.{/n} "Bring in the injectors. The mon-keigh I promised to Tervantias are among them. I do not want these wretches to move an inch until they are in the hands of the Archmachinator."

b2e91295-0886-49d8-bdae-173fd3268e8a.Text: "You mon-keigh never learn. I am beginning to think that your kind is eager to step into our snares."

0a4810f4-c148-4295-a8ca-301893da082e.Text: "Easy, Yrliet. We are about to find out."

2b88311d-40ec-4de7-ba26-fcfe760d2876.Text: "How do you know that I am a Rogue Trader?"

37d96c59-8592-4979-b469-b272d4ad6b4e.Text: {n}The lanky, haggard-looking officer with sunken cheeks stares at you in fright. His body is shivering as if from a feverish chill and his eyes are darting back and forth anxiously.{/n} "Y-Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} Rogue T-Trader, what b-brings you to our humble ship?"

2225d03a-666d-4f6d-9fb0-94befabf837a.Text: {n}Idira lets out a piercing shriek.{/n} "There's no path, Red! There's only marsh, marsh, and underneath it... rings! Black dragon rings, they have already encircled and broken you, they're encircling u—"

2685dc52-2a02-4ec0-ada0-28d45d7ddad0.Text: {n}Idira flinches as if from a blow. She turns her head, and with unblinking eyes stares at Yrliet.{/n} "Red, where are you going? Where are you going? There is no path, you only think there is, you only think..."

7a8e81a5-4ad1-4a0b-8c6c-06d5682cb077.Text: "Stop shivering like a leaf in the wind, mon-keigh. Answer me: have you seen others like me in this system? If you have, tell me where, when, and under what circumstances your paths crossed and diverged afterward."

109a6d2c-4365-4cbc-9648-16a4468df43b.Text: {n}The officer's eyes widen at the sight of Yrliet. His face grows even paler than before and his lips move in a wordless prayer, unable to utter a word in response.{/n}

1cd41728-f3ab-43bf-a496-d7701ab3cef3.Text: "A whirlwind of orange and blue torments their souls. Can you not feel its gusts in the air all around us? Its hues are... terrifying indeed."

ba7c74e9-2451-4688-bf14-365acb5073f8.Text: {n}The officer glances at Yrliet in fear. He forces out the word:{/n} "Pain."

f690b473-2452-4d54-96a0-1a0cf1ab40ac.Text: "P-please, don't! We saw it, yes, we saw it all!"

ef1f7768-58b5-4cdc-8676-3089209c0547.Text: {n}The officer swallows, gives you a strange look, and then closes his eyes.{/n} "Emperor forgive me..."

e9fcf36b-3acf-42a6-9159-69c192ddef37.Text: "What did you just say? 'Rogue Trader'? How would a mere officer know who's standing in front of him?" {n}Jae's face changes and she immediately grips the handle of her weapon.{/n}

22dda1fa-4959-4eea-8217-3f2e7da3fcb7.Text: {n}Heinrix sets his hand on his weapon and nods at the trembling officer.{/n} "I have seen people like this before. Afraid of their own shadow. More than that — I have turned my 'underlings' into this. He has been tortured."

025ff0ba-762e-46a3-a7f7-f6e52ede7bf9.Text: "Devious xenos! I will see you both dead!"

5624f585-4824-4dae-8094-2f77cd16ed9d.Text: {n}Yrliet, who is writhing in pain next to you, is barely able to breathe out,{/n} "No... What have you... done..."

4a7abe38-0ce2-431f-81d3-70945a6ada8f.Text: "Hmm? Are you dissatisfied, my kin? I promised that you would have your precious craftworld survivors. And so you will. I will take you to them. I might even be there to witness your jubilant reunion."

e85c7613-c9e0-4f97-a036-7b8648f98110.Text: {n}Yrliet tries to respond but the best she can muster is a tormented groan.{/n}

a1d582d7-cb9b-49cb-976a-d02415f60722.Text: "What a display! Did you truly put your trust in my cousin? Did you think that, between a mon-keigh and her blood brother, she would choose you?" {n}Marazhai's laughter drips with poison.{/n} "Remember this and never forget it: you are an animal. When we have need of mon-keigh, we use you. When we require something more, we turn to our equals. Just as Yrliet turned to me."

22f2e766-a1ea-4066-82da-71d6ea81aa92.Text: {n}You gasp, sucking in the poisoned air, each breath scorching your insides with liquid fire from throat to lungs. Every cell in your body is engulfed in maddening pain, as if you are being doused in molten metal, skinned alive, and subjected to yet another form of torture. You hear sounds coming from somewhere far away: the moans of your people, the shuffling of bare feet... and light footsteps slowly getting closer.{/n}

848bb92a-4c82-4be5-a1e0-923f7f75e873.Text: "Rogue Trader. A long-awaited meeting indeed." {n}You can barely see anything through the haze of agony but you still remember the voice well: the voice of the xenos who devastated your capital world. Marazhai's face is hidden behind a helmet, but his tone leaves no room for doubt: he is smirking.{/n}

20b296f5-ff7c-4e0c-a445-426829751b07.Text: "Are you enjoying the sensation? I had this poison made for you! Who could have thought that a mon-keigh would one day earn such an honour: a special gift from a Dracon? But your suffering..." {n}The xenos leans closer to you.{/n} "I knew the taste would be exquisite were I to add a touch of the Drukhari's talent for extracting anguish..."

d257c341-7fc1-497a-aff8-486e7e251984.Text: "I am the one... you need... Leave... my people... out of this..."

ee502b47-a4d9-45ef-a3bd-3da8e65b7b83.Text: "Negotiate with me! We can still... come to an agreement..."

cab44e9a-63e1-43f5-a5c6-de2c8cb2c57a.Text: "However, there will be time for that later. No matter how I wish to play with you all one after another, I need you for a purpose, Rogue Trader. Commorragh awaits you, all of you. Mandrakes, take them. Leave none behind."

29d678a2-1bd7-47f3-b9d5-3405ea5b417d.Text: "Would you negotiate with a worm? Or, say, a pet?" {n}The Drukhari chuckles malevolently.{/n} "After I am done with your training, you will never even think of such insolence again."

410ea3bc-cfe7-4149-87a4-0431c685b2d6.Text: "You are more amusing than I thought you would be!" {n}Something heavy strikes you in the face and you hear the crunch of your own bones.{/n} "There is no need to be hasty: we have plenty of time ahead of us to enjoy each other's company."

8a0f65a9-b34a-4401-955e-c760dfdc1463.Text: "Where are the others? What have you done to them?"

2e3c66f1-2749-4b1a-b1ff-38c4bed1c046.Text: "Burn in the Emperor's scorching light, you filthy xenos!"

838709ab-1a48-4eeb-8259-6e13ae802add.Text: "I shall do what you want. I have had enough suffering."

284e42cb-3aec-4e0f-b396-6c1ea6d09f09.Text: "How about we make do without roles and posturing? There is still a chance to strike a deal."

52608f2a-2d2e-47c3-ac32-b82565c776ee.Text: "I might be able to play my role better if I actually knew what it was."

da74150d-09d5-4cb3-a3af-65d533a830ef.Text: "I have a secret for you. Something your spies and agents failed to uncover."

b41326a6-1960-4d03-93e7-d0e4ea8f0374.Text: "Your entire conjecture is a pile of grox dung. Never have I cooperated with the scum that is your kind."

0d93a866-eff3-47b3-9c57-b09e9ee95b85.Text: [Muster your strength and flash a dazzling smile] "Poor fool, you were so easy to deceive."

72147e4d-1bc5-4515-9dcf-eb7de597b5dc.Text: {n}Your consciousness emerges from an ocean of darkness and nightmares, as if someone's powerful hand reached into its depths and brought you into the light. In the dark room, long and angular shadows move around and exchange remarks. One of the shadows approaches you, ripping apart the veil of pain and revealing features that look familiar to you.{/n}

7c163ca5-7dea-4de1-b8f7-c404b0678832.Text: "As for your little friend from the craftworld... Oh, you are going to meet her soon. I bet you cannot wait to look into the eyes of the one who brought you to me, can you?"

d483a3d9-9259-4aa5-aab9-c58caaf95224.Text: {n}For a brief moment, the mask of self-confidence on Marazhai's face slips. The twitch of his eyebrows and his altered expression almost betray his... doubt? The xenos, however, quickly turns away with an affected sigh.{/n} "Enough talk."

08e1243e-a3d1-4fc5-b5ce-56cc940646cd.Text: {n}The slender fingers in the Kabalite's glove clutch at your face, the claws leaving deep scratches on your cheeks and forehead. The edge of a razor-sharp blade presses at your throat. Marazhai furiously hisses something incomprehensible... But then he releases his grip, suppressing his desire to kill you on the spot with an enormous effort of willpower.{/n}

951c4ba7-6493-4cbd-8031-5d5d70f60086.Text: "A good question, Rogue Trader. You are my tool, you see. A sharp and narrow scalpel that I will use to cut away the festering boil on the body of my Kabal. I spared no effort to set up this performance: the witnesses, the spies, the agents... and a small bargain to guarantee the result."

7f6fcee5-b479-4be0-b6bb-3344e139d68f.Text: "All that is required of you is that you quietly play your part. I will even go so far as to put you in your native surroundings... in a manner of speaking. But if I see you stepping out of your role, I will make sure that you bitterly regret it."

c6d6e94f-171c-473e-90e0-922f7c1b7def.Text: "Only the truth, mon-keigh. So very simple, is it not? A little honesty before the powers that be. I have the tools to extract the most coveted mysteries from the deepest recesses of your mind, but I am not interested in your personal secrets. I only want that which will protect my Kabal."

e61fd593-240e-4331-91f1-d18d40cb79db.Text: "I do not know, Rogue Trader. Perhaps they are exuding suffering in one of the choirs of pain and torment. Perhaps they are rotting in one of the vats on the tiers below. I care little for their fate."

0806744b-6ec4-44ba-bc77-c611cc811d68.Text: {n}Marazhai clicks his tongue and gently caresses the object in his hands with the claws of his glove, making it emit a little squeal.{/n} "It looks like you have acquired a taste for pain, mon-keigh. Have it your way, then: resist the inevitable and know a new facet of suffering."

eb2a10cc-6fe8-4c0d-b5ac-484e91b71046.Text: {n}Marazhai is silent for a few moments, playing with the mysterious object in his hand.{/n} "You, mon-keigh, hate creatures alien to your kind — and this hatred is fuelled by primal fear and awareness of your insignificance. To us, you are cattle that exist to be butchered and to entertain us. Sometimes we use you in our little games, but to involve you filthy brutes in the politics of Commorragh... let alone in feuds between the Kabals... there are few worse ways to bring dishonour to oneself and one's Kabal."

ae079788-96cb-49ee-b690-eb2b949a0058.Text: "From the first day I saw you, I knew you were being controlled by another hand, far too experienced and flexible to belong to another mon-keigh. You stayed ahead of me and Tazarra, anticipated our moves, fought back with surprising skill... and I can guess — no, I know exactly — how you were able to know so much. Only one creature was sufficiently aware of our tactics and raid plans. You will help me expose her — and restore the Reaving Tempest to its former favour."

5b90ea58-d76d-48af-9131-58a75745bf57.Text: "It looks like you are starting to respond to the training, Rogue Trader... Who knows, I might keep you after everything is over. The new Archon's court will be in need of illustrious entertainment."

460c677c-e38b-455b-84cc-69c53adbc2f2.Text: {n}Marazhai laughs caustically.{/n} "You are trying to hold your own even in the face of overwhelming force... How touching! But enough talk."

62932d50-df67-44ae-a11a-d203c247f303.Text: {n}The Drukhari gestures to one of the shadows near you and your head is forced backward. Marazhai brings the hand holding the strange object closer: you manage to make out translucent, glossy skin, bluish, pulsating organs beneath, and a little head with serrated jaws, before the Drukhari pushes the larva into your face.{/n}

c0f3ec96-df5c-466a-a119-dc71ce7a099f.Text: {n}Something about the tone of your voice makes Marazhai freeze — and then come closer and lean almost into your face. His black eyes greedily devour your slightest movement and his voice drops to a mocking whisper:{/n} "Very well... I am listening, mon-keigh."

7d10568e-880a-4423-a4dc-3033f2271f0e.Text: {n}Marazhai mockingly cocks his head.{/n} "No, mon-keigh. You have nothing that I could not extract from you myself... using my favourite tools."

b4332f2c-fbfb-4e9c-ad6e-deeacd80bc89.Text: {n}Lightning reflexes fail to save the stunned Kabalite: you smash your forehead into the pale face in front of you, the crunch of broken cartilage drowned out by the frenzied hissing of the Drukhari. Unbearable pain washes over you but, even in its crimson haze, you can still make out Marazhai's twisted face and the patch of blood spreading beneath his nose.{/n}

6162954d-ad73-4d90-bfc1-9d3bb8daee31.Text: {n}Marazhai's pale lips stretch into a smile.{/n} "I would love to see you do that... But no, mon-keigh. I will be denied such entertainment."

fbe30f35-1810-4b1d-9361-cd77b57cc188.Text: "You are awake, mon-keigh." {n}Marazhai's voice is sickeningly sweet. He is looking at you with idle interest, rolling a soft and milky-coloured object from one hand to the other.{/n} "Our toxin masters spared no efforts to drag you out of the induced dream. I must commend the nightmare weavers. The emanations of fear you exuded in your delirium are worthy of the highest praise. However, it is time to finish what you were brought here for. It is time to work for the good of the Kabal, Rogue Trader."

eefb286f-d27e-414f-a039-545d16d0dd37.Text: {n}Darkness clouds your vision but the sensation of an alien presence does not relent. Something both primitive and stupid in its stubborn effort is rummaging through your mind, churning through thoughts and changing them. You gather whatever remains of your willpower and desperately hold on to the part of your consciousness that has not yet caved to the invading power. A prick of surprise, a burst of disappointment... The spell takes hold of your weakened self, but part of it still belongs to you and is ready to fight back. A stray light dawns at the edge of your perception...{/n}

378d84ec-d295-4481-b4e2-9532e80051b1.Text: {n}Darkness clouds your eyes, but the sensation of an alien presence does not relent. This is not a conscious mind but something primitive yet unbelievably strong in its unknowable pursuit. It is crawling around in your thoughts, scratching them with its sides, and changing their shape. Perhaps all this is just a bad dream... A quirk of the intellect exhausted by endless troubles... A calumny of a mind too weak for the burden it was made to carry. A stray light dawns at the edge of your perception...{/n}

bc3c1330-a121-4ea3-9154-1da0bc10b620.Text: {n}Sensing warmth, the creature springs into motion a moment later. As it blindly pokes at your skin, it discovers your nostril... and rushes forward, stretching the skin and tearing through the mucous membrane. Unbearable pain overwhelms you as the larva begins to force its way through the soft tissue and cartilage, each of its movements causing a crunching noise to reverberate through your skull. The creature greedily bites into flesh and moves ever upward, past the bridge of your nose, past your eyes... and then something alien invades your consciousness.{/n}

957e7b53-ff2e-44b5-a082-11a6b6563131.Text: Remembered that Theodora is dead at the trial.

69859cb6-297d-42be-9e69-0bbc8a975f03.Text: "The xenos is gone... Why is the Lord Inquisitor here? And Theodora's reanimated corpse too... Didn't she die? Everything is wrong here!"

fbec7395-8435-4c7b-8108-22db91f7b8ab.Text: "The only xenos plan I am aware of is the one where they play foul games with my head."

567665e5-f9db-44ea-986e-d76422531cb4.Text: "Now I see that I have been blind. The xenos have been fighting one another all this time and I was their unwitting cat's paw."

34591ccb-5de0-43e6-ab6b-1eed5696f35d.Text: [Submit to the illusion] "I swear by the Emperor, every word is the absolute truth!"

9968dc55-bd16-4852-a83b-7b10b219aaec.Text: "You forgot to add I was also using the xenotechnologies that are banned in the Imperium and sold them to my associates all over the Expanse."

daa2e744-06d1-4e25-8034-2f15a7e39d5b.Text: [Say nothing: no one asked for your opinion]

890892e8-c679-49e3-bfbf-0a3ed749c2d0.Text: "No, this is wrong... No court in the Imperium would ever admit the testimony of a xenos."

2beef4e6-d0d3-4a38-b8b1-69bc52fbb607.Text: "Yrliet, you should have spoken to me about this! I thought we had a special bond."

a0bc7bad-37b3-4a29-99b5-ee48b02733de.Text: [Submit to the illusion] "Before the court and the God-Emperor Himself, I plead guilty to all charges."

31fd17a0-f0d3-4383-bb20-aa4e0bb36df7.Text: [Submit to the illusion] "Yes, I did cooperate with xenos. This I will not deny."

374c086d-1a6a-46fb-98cd-f522208a27f9.Text: "Something... is wrong. According to the statutes of the Imperium, not even a Lord Inquisitor can unilaterally pass judgement on a Rogue Trader. I refuse to take part in this!"

aec340cb-b504-49ce-9506-59ea9062272b.Text: "I have nothing to add, Heinrix. You have said more than I ever could."

092b2e81-0333-4113-8dad-73a68f60fe21.Text: [Submit to the illusion] "You have uncovered mine and Theodora's plan. That is exactly what happened."

1697e73b-7d7e-44e9-ab74-62323e608532.Text: "Lady Theodora, please, let us confess! I... I do not want to tell any more lies!"

d7433b9b-d7f9-449d-9d62-8db5119be196.Text: "Enough of this circus, Heinrix. I did not set up any attacks!"

901ec3b8-42aa-4f6b-9dca-560ef42cb9cd.Text: [Submit to the illusion] "It was Lady Theodora! She made me sign a blood pact with the Drukhari!"

2bb55109-f939-4864-a35a-4e90d8acce4c.Text: "A plot? What are you talking about? Ask Achilleas what happened. He is your agent, after all!"

b621a358-2bd5-4dc8-9ef0-366c142baca7.Text: "Wait! The Inquisitor himself gave me his blessing to use xenos as I saw fit. Why, then, am I standing trial?"

8ba9bb42-8fe4-4d2b-ad65-ffe9bc490ae1.Text: [Say nothing: no one asked for your opinion]

a4c32d67-a906-49aa-a5d3-b9d41ab292f3.Text: "Achilleas, come to your senses! You are slandering both the Rogue Trader and yourself!"

aafb7eef-b13d-455f-b7c3-0f02325a3351.Text: "I will personally execute you for betraying the Imperium, Achilleas!"

e1a8246a-8e6f-4ecd-8ec2-37e097b29bcd.Text: "I... am nothing but a puppet in this charade. Everything that has taken place at this trial is a vicious lie!"

55be646a-bc1a-477a-ba07-cc0565b58915.Text: Refused to play a part in the fake trial.

77fabb39-bc84-4a00-8222-870751feabce.Text: [Look directly at "Heinrix"] "This is all just a dreadful illusion. I will have no part in it!"

1a8b3a54-3056-48bf-b6bc-33c678ea54e6.Text: Tried to reach out to Achilleas at the trial.

56c1f756-c780-40d2-a2fd-d6554321a36c.Text: "Achilleas, what have they done to you? Are you all right?"

0fb25c09-f585-4237-8a15-2275ec36dfb6.Text: Tried to reach out to Yrliet at the trial.

52046e11-28f7-40fb-9f0e-1b2df9b2edec.Text: "Yrliet, can you not see they are manipulating us? This is just a mendacious farce!"

a9f8b567-3249-4fdf-a6c7-442c080f171c.Text: [Silently nod because everything Yrliet said is true]

7cf74a01-663f-4078-b111-6a80e67a9205.Text: "Wait, something is wrong... Why are you all here? Where is Marazhai? What... what happened?"

5990722c-f826-41a9-a940-0579ff50b23d.Text: "Lady Theodora... You died. Why are you here?"

842eaea9-c010-452b-8fed-5ec754dea01c.Text: "I am still struggling to make sense of what is going on here..."

0f4dd446-982d-4ac0-aff5-964ee3df8382.Text: "Is that all you've got? Xenos, I expected a better performance."

0d85f91d-4ae9-4f3a-8335-539e3777a53e.Text: "I hope I succeeded in spoiling your little show, Marazhai."

9fa3b940-b4b6-45f3-be7a-cbcda019706c.Text: "...And here comes our principal witness, the Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself}." {n}Heinrix gives you a cold look.{/n} "If the presented evidence was not enough to convince you, {mf|his|her} testimony will conclude this confusing case, full of oath-breaking, lies, and heresy."

eab34666-048f-45ea-9a00-478a032b5366.Text: "Died, you say? {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_TheodoraAlive}But who are you talking to if I did?{/d} Get one simple truth into your empty head: your role in these events is negligible. You shall think me the Emperor on the Golden Throne if I so choose and think me dead if it strikes my fancy, but this is not what matters right now. Just looking in your direction makes me sick. Why must I speak to the filth?" {n}The last words are obviously meant for the court, not you.{/n}

e1df81e3-a995-4ad2-814c-e302ebd55826.Text: "Then let us continue. Shielded by the powers of the Warrant of Trade granted by the Imperium, Theodora von Valancius more than once allowed herself to openly collaborate with xenos." {n}You have never seen such a contemptuous grimace on the Interrogator's face.{/n} "She plunged her entire protectorate into apostasy and heresy, including the current Rogue Trader, and went out of her way to prevent the Inquisition and me personally from maintaining order inside the Expanse."

79164fac-1007-4eb7-b4ab-118cb087e5b7.Text: "However... the thread that bound our paths broke the moment I realised the mon-keigh's involvement in the disappearance of my home. To flee the Rogue Trader, I tracked down and eliminated {mf|his|her} chief tracker who has pursued our kin in this part of the galaxy for many years. And thus earned clemency before this court."

392e4114-cd42-46f7-87f9-c45472caff86.Text: {n}The Inquisitor leans forward slightly at the sight of your anguish. For a brief moment, the boredom in his eyes is gone.{/n}

01f95884-ad3d-4a48-ad22-3c6f204e3abb.Text: "We surrendered Vheabos VI to the depredations of the xenos {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_IsItTrue}on the Rogue Trader's orders{/d} so the Drukhari would not have any unnecessary suspicions about our continuing success. We let them attack the capital world for the same reason, hoping to cut off the Dracon's head... But we failed. The Dracon was too swift and too cunning."

26c137c4-9962-4122-a727-2bbab0577ff3.Text: "You need not worry, dear Lord Captain. It was not my intention to bring up unsupported claims." {n}Heinrix produces a data-slate and skilfully manipulates the device until he locates the necessary information.{/n}

5fa7244a-eb18-45cc-8c75-b34fe685239e.Text: {n}Heinrix bends over you with a crooked smile.{/n} "Rogue Trader, are you all right? Or was your {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_YouServed}heretical association with xenos{/d} so disruptive that you lost your mind?" {n}The mocking words do little to hide his irritation. The Interrogator is obviously displeased with the turn the conversation is taking.{/n}

ecfb0d65-a6d7-4a74-8c21-f8dc83822f13.Text: {n}The Interrogator gives the data-slate a sour look and puts it away.{/n} "There was not much evidence to collect, but the mere fact the Rogue Trader inevitably ended up in the right place when the Drukhari attacked {mf|his|her} worlds and merchant vessels, even sometimes late, is the best proof that {mf|he|she} was {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_ServedDrukhari}collaborating with other xenos{/d}. Who else could provide detailed information about the Kabal's future movements and raiding targets?"

db45ff75-57f4-4460-806d-929cdc0226ae.Text: {n}There are only a couple of steps between you, but the path to Yrliet is blocked by an invisible wall, cold as if built of impenetrable ice.{/n} "Do not be ridiculous, Rogue Trader. What special bond could arise between heaven and earth? Between an ocean and a puddle? A star will never see the light of a puny firefly, no matter how hard it tries to reach the sky."

6deeb86f-d8d7-4454-a34a-0e6a3b3508d5.Text: "This much is true. I certainly did." {n}Xavier Calcazar looks at Heinrix with amusement.{/n}

aa6ccd35-8dc6-48aa-9386-0b258554032b.Text: "The Rogue Trader uncovered the crimes of the Aeldari on the most important agri-world of the von Valancius protectorate, which feeds many Imperium colonies in the Expanse."

878ce12b-b99a-4ad6-8190-06de5fd6cac9.Text: "Except {mf|he|she} did not stop at purging heresy from the planet: {mf|he|she} {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_ItsTrue}let the xenos take charge of the entire colony{/d}! Millions of human lives have been tainted by xenocorruption. Not even the Warrant of Trade can justify such a crime against Humanity."

d0dd7bae-7079-4f95-a441-4de0315336fa.Text: "The Rogue Trader has often been accompanied by a {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_YrlietComp}xenos companion{/d}. And though the Warrant of Trade does allow one to grant sanction to individual specimens, what is this if not a confirmation of the von Valancius family's loyalty to the enemies of Humanity?"

48b61541-4c82-4af8-bf6b-649f2c29eb6f.Text: "The Rogue Trader's {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_ServedDrukhari}ties to the Drukhari{/d}, a different subspecies of Aeldari, are just as obvious. Who else could help {mf|him|her} divine the carefully prepared plans of the Drukhari if not other Drukhari? {name} von Valancius always ended up in the location of the next Drukhari raid, knowing for certain where they were going to strike."

c016cfb5-67f8-48ac-8810-ea648e7c4e0b.Text: "Are you really saying your war with the Drukhari was not a hoax? Then how did you and your foolish subjects know the coordinates of the enemy ships every time? How did you know their targets? Do you think your expert on all things xenos was shrewd enough to divine the carefully devised plan of the Kabal's finest? No, only other Drukhari could do that... and even then, only a few. This means {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_ServedDrukhari}you were in collusion with them{/d}."

4a2591a2-72f1-49ba-8449-9371c1f0b5ae.Text: "The previous... arrangements... no longer apply to you, Rogue Trader." {n}Heinrix clenches his fists so hard the knuckles turn white.{/n} "I advise you to cooperate with the court unless you want to end up on the scaffold at the earliest opportunity."

0e354e7e-1acc-4c19-9a98-0e237ffc4b9c.Text: "{name} von Valancius, speak truthfully before the court, before the Lord Inquisitor, and before the God-Emperor Himself. Do you admit to {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_IsItTrue}conspiring with Lady Theodora and one of the Drukhari Kabals{/d}?"

4eee78bd-7806-4288-8e67-2ffc97c196de.Text: "Allow me to explain what actually happened. {name} von Valancius personally invited the Drukhari to {mf|his|her} worlds and then used their strength and resources to sow chaos in the Expanse to gain leverage over {mf|his|her} rivals. It is very convenient to play the victim while working with those who rob your neighbours blind and terrify the worlds that pay you tribute. How much did you profit from this, Rogue Trader? Did you think I would not uncover your {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_ServedDrukhari}pathetic conspiracy{/d}?"

123b941f-0747-4ada-8022-796dfb0a5c7c.Text: {n}Dangerous sparks flare in Heinrix's eyes.{/n} "Achilleas has not contacted me for a long time. He vanished on your world, Rogue Trader. Have you killed my agent on yet another one of your whims? But it is your other transgressions that we are addressing at present."

8091d887-83ab-461d-869e-eac6ab2f5678.Text: "Rest assured, we will move on to the testimony of Achilleas Scalander as soon as we are done with you."

0828f86f-bba8-40d7-818f-0c5beca2ace7.Text: "You are only allowed to speak when questioned. But since the Rogue Trader is so eager to make {mf|his|her} voice heard, by all means do. The court is curious to know what you gleaned from this interrogation."

66b799bb-edae-4d3b-9a3a-d1b95875b47a.Text: "How interesting!" {n}Xavier Calcazar pensively rests his chin on his hand.{/n} "What will you say to this?"

7944153e-68e5-4d05-b524-704c0d7711f2.Text: "You have no choice in the matter! You would do well to submit meekly under His steadfast gaze and not obstruct the proceedings!" {n}The Interrogator grits his teeth viciously.{/n}

1e18d5a7-7f32-4e98-adbb-e23ae99d7c05.Text: "Cooperation is a double-edged sword. Sometimes you use your partner and sometimes your partner uses you. Which is what happened to the Rogue Trader. Lady Theodora {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_TheodoraAlive}used {mf|him|her}{/d} to undermine the standing of the Imperium in the Expanse."

5fcab7b3-77e5-46f4-8b09-f34435c8541a.Text: "Rogue Trader." {n}Heinrix addresses you through clenched teeth.{/n} "You are destroying your only chance to make yourself useful to the Inquisition and to me personally. Do not tempt fate and do not resist... the examination."

be4128e1-72e8-4549-a0e0-d2e4e5a51c89.Text: "No pleas, no denials, no desperate lies? I think we may consider this a heartfelt confession."

b8dbd723-8f78-4a8f-9334-392dfaa8b571.Text: "As you can see, this is a confession straight from the horse's mouth. What other evidence can the court possibly seek?"

83acdf44-4c03-4a4f-ae04-41f5550fc247.Text: "That's it? I expected more from you, mon-keigh."

53611f13-6623-4c4c-9668-48ab7d80d374.Text: "You do not need to understand, mon-keigh. You have done what was required of you. Now muster your strength, we still have a fun—"

9109e19f-d44d-4d53-95bf-4f6cc0e91502.Text: {n}Yrliet's thin lips purse for a moment after she hears your words. She stares into the distance, even more pensive and sorrowful than usual.{/n}

0defbe4e-4270-4f3f-94ff-41ef8bdc2fd0.Text: "You... useless, arrogant, soon-to-be dead mon-keigh! The trial is almost complete, and when the judgement is pronounced, I will gut you, fill your bowels with flesh-eating worms, and drag you through the streets..."

96eba8bb-8091-4fcb-a6aa-7603579733a7.Text: "All you had to do was submit, useless mon-keigh! Trust me, you will pay for your antics a hundred times over. You like jokes, do you? I will cut your filthy mouth wide open, from ear to—"

6bf85944-2d2b-435e-be78-0ac67e22cc9b.Text: {n}Heinrix raises his head triumphantly and looks around the bridge and at everyone present.{/n} "A servant of the Inquisition would not lie at a sacred tribunal hearing, would he?"

6a0765f7-0d81-4575-9959-c0dae181e022.Text: {n}You try to recall anything at all but your thoughts keep swirling like a turbulent maelstrom in your head and searing pain grips your temples.{/n}

80cedc88-caa9-4b08-943b-e5693decb758.Text: {n}The same feelings return: impotence, submission, and weakness. You no longer belong to yourself, even though your mind has not yet fully left your body. You keep fighting {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_YouServed}whatever is stuck in your head{/d}, but it is a losing battle. As if from afar, you hear your voice:{/n} "I... I confess to collaborating with xenos..."

0b65bb8c-839f-4cd9-be8f-5c5a8b67c25b.Text: {n}Heinrix nods with satisfaction, noticing your reaction — or rather, the lack of it.{/n}

9cd81be5-ea6b-4348-9e13-f9fd0e1f4ae9.Text: {n}The words erupt from your throat and your head fills with fog again. A sharp pain, like a needle prick, pierces your left temple.{/n}

7d8e7ca1-568c-4ce1-85f5-afa4e758fb53.Text: "But instead of purging the planet of the xenos menace, {mf|he|she} {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_ItsTrue}allowed the inhumans to take refuge{/d} in the shadow of {mf|his|her} power. They are corrupting Janusian society even as we speak, and who knows, perhaps another rebellion will not be long in coming."

26430c0d-2e0b-4321-9d88-18733aa39f32.Text: {n}Yrliet is standing at a distance, with her slender arms crossed over her chest. Her gaze is resolute and aimed straight at Inquisitor Calcazar. Even if your words have reached her ears, she does not show it.{/n}

973181d2-8cd3-4fe2-a950-fd5a6e9c13dc.Text: "No, I... Where am I? Rogue... Trader?.. The palace! We received the news about the Drukhari attack, everything... happened so quickly..."

3336fabd-59d5-415b-b39c-f7dc6570ab08.Text: "At this point, the tribunal probably wants to know what the true intentions of the von Valancius dynasty are. The Rogue Trader claims {mf|he|she} has been waging war against the Drukhari this entire time. Except... was there really a war? Or was it another carefully staged performance?" {n}Heinrix is looking at you closely, almost without blinking.{/n}

c4d227f5-7122-4cda-a2ca-dd1806831fa3.Text: {n}The words fly from your lips but {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_YouServed}their meaning{/d} belongs to someone else. And you are aware of this, except there is nothing you can do about it.{/n} "I..." {n} Your voice is dreadfully hoarse from all the screaming and torture.{/n} "I confess to collaborating with xenos..."

9842860e-1db5-4559-8e5f-b9a41e58b551.Text: {n}Heinrix makes a disgruntled face, looking at you strangely.{/n} "Oh, you do not know, do you? Allow me to remind you, then, and the entire court as well." {n}A data-slate appears in the Interrogator's hands, adorned with purity seals on both sides.{/n}

e7a8bd8e-2d61-4005-818f-0d407de008d9.Text: {n}The words fly from your lips but their meaning belongs to someone else.{/n} "I..." {n} Your hoarse voice is barely heard.{/n} "I plead guilty..."

823812c4-5cb1-4625-8081-5ba77a70fe8d.Text: {n}The tribunal remains silent, although those present cast anxious glances at your predecessor.{/n}

7b46a5bc-18ab-4998-9041-c55faf136b66.Text: {n}...Or at least, that is what you wanted to say. However, the alien will makes you say something else entirely:{/n} "It was originally Lady Theodora's plan. She... her servants... always let me know where the next Drukhari attack would take place."

5a349a2a-1c5d-4c03-b587-3e158ff1b595.Text: {n}The Lord Inquisitor makes a vaguely dismissive gesture.{/n} "Enough. Let {mf|him|her} speak. The sooner this business is concluded, the better."

0e2c42b7-ba07-4840-95fe-c14791491deb.Text: "Your pathetic attempts to paint me as a heretic are like a blunted rapier: tedious and useless." {n}Theodora's gaze is not directed at you — she is addressing Heinrix.{/n}

9cdabd3e-d678-48a0-adbe-9d3642b05ac3.Text: {n}Heinrix's face contorts monstrously, his skin stretched to the limit across the bones of his skull, his voice ringing with fury.{/n} "Kae-morag... do not try to squeeze between the strands of the web, mon-keigh! Do what you were brought here for!"

c9cfd0a5-cc42-4561-962e-0f210e95603c.Text: {n}Yrliet's lithe body tenses when she hears her name come out of your mouth. A shadow of doubt flits across the otherworldly face, but Yrliet does not grace you with a look. She stubbornly stares into the hollow eyes of the Inquisitor languishing on your throne in apparent boredom.{/n}

0ddd5b60-3aff-4b1d-a50e-c86e10d17e76.Text: {n}A wave of anxious whispering sweeps through the bridge.{/n}

3e9decae-d0de-4c38-b645-982ab25e38f8.Text: "I do not think so. Another witness to your atrocities arrived alongside the Rogue Trader."

76bc344d-fd27-42d3-b7d4-ea732a5b9de6.Text: {n}Pale as death, Achilleas emerges from the shadows. His eyes are fixed on the Interrogator and are overflowing with almost manic submission.{/n} "Ahem... I want the court and everyone in attendance to know that everything Interrogator van Calox said is true. We did collaborate with the Drukhari. We were apprised of the upcoming raids and knew which colony had the sword hanging over it in critical moments."

722fc07c-5a81-4dad-9223-050bfe371262.Text: "Bull-headed stubbornness does not befit a {mf|man|woman} of your pedigree, Rogue Trader. But since you have decided to deny everything, I will summon another witness. I am sure everyone will find it interesting to explore this sordid story from another angle."

3fe2613c-6003-448f-bc9c-9a7b041a0ec2.Text: "So Achilleas did not simply vanish... You helped him disappear." {n}Heinrix nods curtly.{/n} "I say he had only himself to blame. An agent who cannot recognise an impending threat is useless."

ba297237-7a7a-4fd6-924b-23f444bdedce.Text: {n}Noticing your reaction, Heinrix nods in satisfaction.{/n}

b166ff07-8007-4010-8d72-2294433961ce.Text: "A special bond? With this... person? I would personally cut open your scrawny Aeldari throat for that."

c1cd816f-e6e1-4de9-aff1-a16020c34398.Text: "Do not be deceived by {mf|his|her} breed. There is a cunning predator lurking behind the fluttering of fragile butterfly wings. The mon-keigh before you is a bizarre amalgamation of qualities not usually inherent in {mf|his|her} feeble species. {mf|He|She} has mastered the mysteries of many of this world's cultures. The secrets of the universe and ancient artefacts, the fine art of war, the intricacies of deceit... All are embodied in a single mon-keigh, however hard it may be to believe."

7e95c43a-7f23-4e3a-8ef9-934cb30f68d1.Text: "What are you talking about, Rogue Trader? I distinctly remember each of your orders. I remember the Drukhari too. I spent enough time with these xenos to never forget..." {n}Achilleas's voice rises to a feverish pitch and breaks off.{/n}

5db571ea-16c6-4a2f-a818-076cc5ef1c1a.Text: "Achilleas, you are looking a bit tired. And confused. If the Rogue Trader has threatened you in any way..."

fa78cdf3-29d2-47ae-bf01-806033ba8a0b.Text: "The court has been presented with enough evidence, and I hope no one is harbouring any doubts as to the guilt of the von Valancius dynasty. But let us allow the Rogue Trader to say {mf|his|her} final word. We are all curious to know what you have gleaned from this enquiry."

dbb78064-98a3-495b-bc2a-5f858cbdbfa8.Text: "I hope no one is harbouring any doubts as to the guilt of the von Valancius dynasty? But let us allow the Rogue Trader to say {mf|his|her} final word. We are all curious to know what you have gleaned from this enquiry."

5f6273ce-9bd7-45b0-8ec8-84c60478bd61.Text: "What are you talking about, Rogue Trader? I was carrying out your orders in full accordance with your instructions. And I served the Imperium just the way you wanted to. Was an alliance with the Drukhari not part of your plans?" {n}Achilleas's voice rises to a feverish pitch and breaks off.{/n}

89435a18-89dc-4c52-8d57-f61ba1306219.Text: {n}The Interrogator glares at you angrily.{/n} "All you had to do was remain obedient, worthless mon-keigh! The trial is almost complete, and once the sentence is announced, I will deal with you properly!"

792e089f-131c-4cb7-8bfe-5b8d2a60b30f.Text: {n}You try to push the words out of your throat but they become stuck in a suffocating lump, choking you. Heinrix notices your struggle and quickly changes the subject:{/n} "The Rogue Trader is obviously stunned by the realisation Theodora has been using {mf|him|her} this entire time to impede me..."

074695e3-cb8e-4803-aa36-7f3b601140e7.Text: {n}The Inquisitor's harsh and cruel laughter echoes across the corpse-filled bridge.{/n} "It looks like your plaything is refusing to dance to your tune. It is pathetic, Heinrix. Should I have expected anything better from you?"

395d2c06-fa4a-4c66-aba8-d7dfc788a3ea.Text: "Indeed?" {n}Xavier Calcazar shoots the Interrogator an amused look.{/n} "What do you think {mf|he|she} is talking about?"

b8094179-7995-422a-b327-e424b1f4ef49.Text: {n}Yrliet silently takes a graceful step forward.{/n} "If the court so desires, my speech will run like a river and wash away your doubts. I found a shard of my home in the Rogue Trader's chambers. An entire craftworld vanished among the stars, the only clue to its fate resting in the hands of this mon-keigh. That was when I began to suspect that {mf|he|she} had something to do with the misfortune that had befallen my Crudarach."

692a3a68-a981-4e7b-ba82-2933f9a26a1f.Text: "{mf|He|She} is obviously trying to disrupt the trial. {name}, I suggest you watch your tongue and behave yourself. And perhaps, only perhaps, it will be enough to preserve your miserable life." {n}The Interrogator shoots you a withering glare.{/n}

aa8b2845-3eb9-4a8f-9f95-26821ef13ff3.Text: "You dragged this {mf|boy|girl} into this trial and now expect someone will lend an ear to a lowly heretic's testimony? I thought better of you, Interrogator van Calox. I was so very wrong." {n}Lady Theodora's voice sounds even harsher and angrier than you remember.{/n}

7865fdfb-4224-48ce-83b1-bb2a5110c7a0.Text: "Does the Rogue Trader admit to {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_YouServed}fraternising with the xenos{/d}, serving them as a puppet, and rejecting the God-Emperor's blessed light for the sake of {mf|his|her} heretical desires and base profit?"

f30d3000-7eea-4311-aed2-d246727a6216.Text: "It was amusing but the joke has outstayed its welcome." {n}Theodora shoots the Interrogator a nasty look.{/n} "It is painfully obvious this heretic is dancing to your tune. {mf|His|Her} word against mine? You had lost before you even unsheathed your blade, Heinrix."

9d757259-637e-4201-a475-6cd62d77c7ca.Text: "Some reports note instances of {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_Trial_ItsTrue}close cooperation{/d} between the von Valancius protectorate and a crime syndicate involved in the Cold Trade, the Kasballica Mission. Sullying oneself by rubbing shoulders with such individuals... is unworthy of such an elevated servant of the Imperium."

ec313efe-2b19-417d-9048-0b57aafa0b4c.Text: "Damned xenos, I will burn all of you in this den of heresy, in the God-Emperor's name!"

7e9ce4cc-a08d-4f34-aabb-1d8d95210bc8.Text: [Look at the Drukhari upon the throne]

0e7c8ae7-0890-4dd2-ac67-7dc66fdfc127.Text: [Look at the Aeldari who interrupted the trial]

feb4792a-42e4-46c2-8095-c2de541d3bf3.Text: "Beat him half to death and throw him out like rubbish!"

6d5cd3d3-6e8d-4de1-9a0c-8a927ff02276.Text: "Listen and remember, in the Emperor's name, I will end you all!"

ee0464b3-5a25-46fc-a792-916945673b19.Text: "To the void with you, xenoscum. I will not be a part of your games."

261f58d6-7295-4b66-b348-8c42e5a1626a.Text: "Marazhai was a worthy opponent. Let him go to the arena himself."

b5404a25-e829-4f4c-a514-567b3bc0b17d.Text: "Hey, Archon or whatever your name is. I shall soon be adding your mask to my collection of xeno-artefacts."

f28ec5e4-5537-4f78-941d-01962bafc768.Text: "Stop acting like I am not here!"

d9793f5d-2cff-4f84-938c-7e85e104d683.Text: {n}After the spell is lifted, staggering pain pierces your body. Darkness clouds your vision and nausea creeps up your throat, but the wounds you managed to forget soon remind you that you are still alive.{/n}

dba52e95-7746-48b8-b9ad-b13583ba6ead.Text: "The weakness of your subjects is an insult to the Council of Archons and the supreme overlord of Commorragh himself, Yremeryss." {n}The commanding, inhuman voice tears you from the vice of agony, and you see an unknown Drukhari in the centre of the chamber whose presence alone causes your insides to clench.{/n} "Instead of fighting and ripping what they are owed from destiny's hands by force, they dare to crawl into the Dark Palace, begging for favours!"

01c57325-2505-47bc-a87b-5f45174fa125.Text: {n}Muffled clapping tears you from the vice of agony. The Drukhari in the centre of the chamber observes you coldly from under the golden mask, causing your insides to clench.{/n} "A Dracon of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest has been cast down by his own ineptitude in an attempt to take part in thyllian ai-kelethril. Never did I think that my eyes were destined to behold the greatest disgrace for a Dark One, a trueborn humbled by a lowly creature before the Council of Archons."

1565e402-c326-4a88-9063-4fff758c64b4.Text: "It has been a long time since the Obsidian Court last saw such an... entertaining spectacle as this. The accusations flung at Archon Yremeryss may be serious... but I see no reason to attempt to delve into their substance." {n}The Drukhari on the throne looks at Marazhai with a hungry leer, clearly waiting for his reaction.{/n}

75471578-a3fa-4969-8329-e2fa67b7e228.Text: "I humbly bow before the Council of Archons and apologise for this... outburst on behalf of the Kabal. Allow me to prove my respect to you with a humble gift." {n}Yremeryss points at you with a clawed finger and flashes a satisfied grin.{/n} "The Dracon of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest himself and his amusing mon-keigh plaything with their entourage of hapless freaks will enter your arenas and fight the best warriors for the crowd's amusement."

0360a911-c018-4d70-bc44-db89910dd093.Text: "I will rip out your heart for Khaine to devour!"

6797e8e4-5420-4afa-8c8e-2ad84307f1df.Text: {n}The words almost fly from your lips when a sharp pain seizes your head in a vice-like grip. Blood and nausea roil inside your throat, and the world starts swaying before your eyes. It looks like the creature Marazhai shoved into your head is still suppressing your will with all its might, but you can already feel its approaching demise.{/n}

cec09977-6d4c-40aa-b7d2-a021d60328d1.Text: {n}Achilleas remains indifferent to what is going on. It is as though he does not notice the terrifying decor of the hall, or the wounds on his tortured body, or the enemies surrounding you. His clouded gaze seeks out Marazhai over and over, and, failing to find any response there, it roves from one face to another.{/n}

b1c7ad7d-954c-405b-b8a6-d71250829fab.Text: {n}Yrliet absorbs every word, occasionally wincing in pain and covering her weeping wounds. Her posture and gestures are full of tension — like prey cornered by a pack of predators, Yrliet shrinks under the hungry stares of those around her.{/n}

213c9259-1747-441e-8c34-f0deb14caea2.Text: {n}You have heard many gruesome tales about the atrocities of the Drukhari, but the cruellest and vilest always involved Asdrubael Vect, the Archon of the Kabal of the Black Heart, the supreme overlord of Commorragh, and the most dangerous of all his dark kind.{/n}

f844de69-ea96-4cad-8535-c1960f87f43c.Text: {n}Judging by the Archon's reaction, this is a prominent figure in the Drukhari hierarchy, but memory fails you — you are not familiar with a xenos by that name.{/n}

6bc49cbf-d357-46cb-a6c6-615d236250c9.Text: {n}The xenos is wearing armour encrusted with jewels and stands calmly next to the speaker. Such behaviour is typical of the xenos occupying the higher tiers of the Drukhari hierarchy, which means you are facing one of the Archons.{/n}

d0f81d23-58fa-40c6-94ad-5cd9e3cb3d7f.Text: {n}The xenos looks menacing. Perhaps she is the personal guard of the Drukhari sitting on the throne.{/n}

1a87a02c-47cd-46b1-977f-6d92bbe07c1f.Text: {n}The bright motley, the holo-suit, the mask hiding its owner's face, and the graceful, subtle movements... Before you stands a Harlequin, another representative of the multifaceted Aeldari race. The xenos catches your eye and nods. For a moment, the play of shadows on the mask appears to twist its expression into a mischievous grin.{/n}

872ebb43-0da3-4426-8d8d-14afa1866196.Text: {n}The smooth, subtle movements of this xenos are unlike the rough lunges of the Drukhari or the cautious gestures of the Children of Asuryan, but your aching head and the lingering fugue prevent you from focusing your eyes on the daring soul who interrupted the Archon. The xenos catches your eye and nods. For a moment, the play of shadows on the mask appears to twist its expression into a mischievous grin.{/n}

a48fd284-c372-4944-8793-f969668e784c.Text: {n}The smug grin has fled Marazhai's face. He clutches the hilt of his blade and casts a vicious look at the female Drukhari in sumptuous armour.{/n}

f3945d8a-f3bf-4c13-9a15-d96744df801a.Text: {n}There is genuine terror in Marazhai's gaze, but his face remains impassive and calm. At one point he catches your eye, and you can clearly see he is lusting for blood. Your blood.{/n}

71f64c40-5d82-43e8-ac16-8c0126121ace.Text: {n}With a hiss of rage, Marazhai draws his blades, preparing to fight back.{/n}

449ae01b-4630-4bdb-8427-82f85fb970b2.Text: "To contradict my decision is to contradict the decision of Vect himself, fool." {n}Something in the xenos's tone makes your heart skip a beat.{/n} "Allow me to discipline you for your weakness. Today, the Dracon will lose his wings and plunge to the very bottom of the chasm — you will go to the arena to atone for your mistakes and impertinence alongside the rabble you have dragged to Commorragh.
