If you are a true Dracon, you will rise again. If you do not... your suffering will satiate the worthy."

2e3b8a27-41e4-412d-9a6d-e9a0c29a5016.Text: {n}The Archon nods in satisfaction and makes an unfamiliar gesture. The guards draw closer to you.{/n} "Let us return to you, Yremeryss."

d8cfbc50-879a-424f-b334-25f08585f96d.Text: "Lay down your weapons and follow the guards. I will let you keep what little dignity you have left. This is my final gift to you, Marazhai."

90fd834b-93d5-42fe-bd33-6a503e942c7a.Text: {n}A muffled chuckle can be heard from under Nazrakhei's mask.{/n} "Commorragh accepts your gift, Yremeryss. But what should I do, for Marazhai is the first among your blades? Should I cast him out of the palace and condemn to disgrace? Or should I be merciful and allow him to leave the chamber on his own?" {n}The Archon's chilling gaze falls upon you.{/n} "I think I know who will make this difficult decision. A creature whose mewling the Council of Archons was meant to heed. Is this not right, Marazhai? You will receive what you have been longing for — it will be the mon-keigh who decides your fate."

fbd61dc9-4275-433f-aca7-5139fc87a7e1.Text: {n}Marazhai's face contorts in despair. His gaze shifts from the Archon to you, then to Yremeryss and back, but he does not dare to utter an objection.{/n}

b9a4a3b3-909d-4e38-9ec1-f9ecd2b0fc75.Text: "The mon-keigh has decided your fate, Marazhai. Let this be a lesson to you."

e71f8d32-8799-4d25-a37c-f52d2237e7aa.Text: "Silence, mon-keigh! You can choke on your pity, I have no need of it!"

37876814-dc8a-49dc-9712-34b0af84238b.Text: "The lesser races are disgustingly primitive." {n}The Archon of the Kabal of the Black Heart addresses Marazhai, ignoring your words.{/n} "The mon-keigh cannot even decide the fate of its enemy, and you were hoping that someone here would lend an ear to its words? Amusing. The arenas of Commorragh will devour you and your playthings."

2b9c0213-7329-43ab-b595-e68bd1459322.Text:
{n}The laughter of the masked xenos interrupts the Archon and echoes under the vaults of the chamber in a resounding baritone:{/n}
"And all the masks upon their marks now stand:
The slave of vanity the spire ascends,
The thief and traitor cast downward by her hand.
Unbeknownst to all, their fate depends
Upon a lead unseen, a player green."
{n}The xenos leans forward and eyes you with genuine interest. The mask hides his narrow face, and his motley garb shimmers in the dim light.{/n}

238044a5-4c47-48a5-a2b7-95d1ae428e1d.Text: "The mon-keigh has chosen your fate, Marazhai. Let this be a lesson to you. Lay down your weapon, follow the guards, and may the pity of a lesser being serve as a mark of disgrace far worse than the wrath of the Archons. Go!"

9ace785d-66c5-4e0c-b676-a00663eb5800.Text:
{n}The Harlequin's laughter interrupts the Archon and echoes under the vaults of the chamber in a resounding baritone:{/n}
"And all the masks upon their marks now stand:
The slave of vanity the spire ascends,
The thief and traitor cast downward by her hand.
Unbeknownst to all, their fate depends
Upon a lead unseen, a player green."
{n}The Harlequin leans forward and eyes you with genuine interest.{/n}

317d5449-5116-4b51-b085-c4a33e5f36c5.Text: "Is this how you treat the hospitality of Commorragh, Arebennian?" {n}The Archon angrily balls his fist, the shadow of his wrath hanging over the Aeldari interloper like a thunder cloud.{/n} "I thought your words were worth more. You insult me by interrupting the trial again."

03f28075-1221-4d55-bcea-54111e498fda.Text:
{n}The xenos sweeps into a theatrical bow without taking his eyes off Nazrakhei's face.{/n}
"You, Archon, speak a just rebuke, in truth,
Fate's melodies in snarls fantastic have
Entrapped me here, and when I heard them play
I could not keep my lips from grinning wide.
Here comes the hour for shadows to retreat:
To where the curtain waits to rise, the laugh
With no beginning now sends forth the call."

5adfdba4-1942-45e6-8929-750128c73e0e.Text:
"Of vitriol verbose the cut and thrust
Keep time with fate's own machinations grave,
But whose deft footwork leads to naught but dust?
While from its brutal finish none can save
This play, the Puppet Master granted me
Through murky stalls a path obligingly."

3ab7edd2-59ad-4075-8604-f7b4c6d22b1a.Text: {n}Nazrakhei dismisses Marazhai like a bothersome fly.{/n} "The Council of Archons has heard enough platitudes, Dracon Marazhai, and no longer wishes to—"

9021836d-0484-4e25-985b-38a4b998dfce.Text: "The Puppet Master? Has... has Vect himself invited you to this chamber?" {n}The Archon chokes on his own words but quickly regains his composure.{/n} "No matter. You may be our guest, Arebennian, but you are merely a spectator in this performance. And spectators do not belong on the stage, as you undoubtedly know. Do not interfere."

c9a105b5-7c81-4943-a68b-5b87fdf99e53.Text:
{n}The stranger presses a delicate finger to the lips of his sorrowful mask and says with a twinkle in his eye,{/n}
"A shadow in the shadows will I be."

c6907e17-97e9-4ef8-be63-c75cf9ddaba3.Text: "The arena will make you answer for this insult to the court. The arena will strip you of your titles and your skin, and the contenders' blows will break your bones and your pride. Nothing but blood and suffering will wash away the shame the Dracon has brought upon himself this day!"

4f3ba786-6979-40aa-961b-d9a36d537205.Text: "Marazhai Aezyrraesh. Dracon of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest. First Blade to Lady Yremeryss. Eviscerator of Illiridos, Blaze of the Barkhag Kingdom, and Slayer of Carrocius the Pale..." {n}The commanding inhuman voice tears you from the vice of agony, and you see the silhouette of a Drukhari whose very presence makes your innards clench.{/n} "...how dare you come before the council of Archons of the Dark City with this... lesser creature?"

f76e13ba-afad-473d-8428-80abacabb02e.Text: "Marazhai Aezyrraesh, considering the circumstances..." {n}The Archon looks around the room and rests his troubled gaze on the xenos in bright armour who interrupted him.{/n} "The council finds Archon Yremeryss guilty. The blade of your truth cut through the shadowy veil concealing her transgressions. However..." {n}A glint of cruel mockery appears in his eyes.{/n} "How dare you insult the council with such a pathetic complaint? You should have ripped Yremeryss's heart out with your own hands and granted her soul to Vect if you wanted to atone for the mistakes of the Reaving Tempest."

77dcfb53-61d1-4603-b7a8-c50a0400f0ef.Text: {n}A triumphant grin erupts on Marazhai's face, but the xenos remains surprisingly composed and does not dare to interrupt the unknown speaker.{/n}

c562c81a-bbe2-44a9-8845-af409912245f.Text: {n}The Archon addresses the female Drukhari standing beside him, his eyes alight with mockery — not directed at her, however, for he is still looking at Marazhai.{/n} "How does the Archon intend to pay for her Kabal's blatant disrespect? I am waiting for your reply, Yremeryss, and my patience is growing thinner with each breath you take."

30f5461f-57d4-4919-b8d9-5d16522c3315.Text: "With the greatest respect, mighty Nazrakhei, Archon of the Kabal of the Black Heart, First Among the Chosen, Voice of the Overlord of the Dark City, Bringer of Demise, Conqueror of a Hundred Worlds—"

7842e926-b73a-418d-bc1a-818837f74ee1.Text: {n}One half of his face is hidden behind a golden mask with an intimidating visage, the other half is showing a malicious, sharp-toothed leer. The xenos's elaborate armour is decorated with skulls and patches of human skin impaled on countless blades and hooks. He carries himself with authority and ease, as though he is a ruler who holds the threads of fate of all those present tightly in his grasp.{/n}

e67b9c5c-b91d-4e38-aa45-f247d6c6abf5.Text: "I..." {n}Marazhai's eyes widen, filled with astonishment and disbelief. He seems to have been certain of the outcome and did not expect what he is hearing now. His lips twist in an enraged snarl — hatred directed at the xenos on the throne — and yet it finds no outlet under the gazes of the dozens of Drukhari in the chamber.{/n}

c997d207-3ca6-453a-9680-acc39962db0f.Text: "Heinrix, who am I about to kill?"

66971439-66ab-4ec4-873a-2e2b4fc9602f.Text: "Barging onto my bridge was a big mistake."

8b9cdf31-b8bc-4974-95ff-194e790b18e6.Text: "If you lay down your arms right now, you will be spared and taken captive."

40cec4fc-1b44-485a-b494-c7b3d9e191b4.Text: {n}The heavily armoured woman eyes you and sneers.{/n} "A Rogue Trader... That's a new notch on my gun's stock. Never killed one of you before!"

f91dea2d-fd8b-4c3b-bad0-db3443b61678.Text: "Aishara. What made you think you had the right to invade the ship of one of the God-Emperor's anointed?"

19356ffa-70d1-4309-b46c-0c4ba4b86e6c.Text: "Van Calox. Wrong place, wrong time again? This time will be your last. And don't you dare lecture me on how my actions deviate from the Creed, you who've already proven yourself unfit for our cause."

8132407b-b103-492b-a86a-7f02d10a7b17.Text: "One of the Lord Inquisitor's acolytes. This is Aishara, the cleaner. She cleans up what has outlived its usefulness to Calcazar."

afd0b74d-9777-47be-b0c3-d2f1cd8cc4a1.Text: {n}The woman laughs a cawing laugh.{/n} "I can't promise the same to you, Rogue Trader."

a4b6939b-3fe7-4757-8d2d-e34836953076.Text: {n}The woman lets out a bloodthirsty chuckle.{/n} "Yes, it was... I was hoping to blow up your ship's reactor and just send bits of you flying into the void, but I'm going to enjoy this even more if I do it all myself."

eb12ee57-289a-4449-a0c1-97112e016d41.Text: "Wrong. I have reliable information that He is in fact with us."

5ce9346b-ee66-49f5-a7c9-a0546292ab56.Text: "Ah! Fearless, mighty, with a heart as cold as stone! A worthy opponent, a far cry from wretched xenos and stinking heretics! It will be glorious to slay you!" {n}Ulfar greets Calcazar's assassin with the softest smile you have ever seen on his face.{/n}

3be787a6-82c7-4459-a11d-641735796364.Text: "Stand aside, redbeard, while I cut off the Rogue Trader's head. Wouldn't want to kill my first Emperor's Angel in a hurry." {n}The woman reciprocates with an equally friendly gaze and you see confusion on the faces of those around you.{/n}

5d642306-8f10-41bf-8723-3114a1245b55.Text: {n}The woman's lips curve into a bloodthirsty grin.{/n} "I find cocky opponents so amusing — they're always shocked to discover they're mortal!"

60c310c1-fb65-489e-a2f9-99587d3f4e4d.Text: "Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius! In the name of the Inquisition, you are under arrest!"

79b9149d-edfd-48fc-a66d-b5867882bcc3.Text: "Bridge officers, to battle! Protect the Lord Captain!"

6edd4fda-cf8b-4b3a-a873-d45f77dc07d6.Text: "You old heretic! You'll answer for this in the interrogation chambers!"

3a01b193-db54-4df7-8528-03a7f4714a28.Text: "I have not received an invitation to your Magnae Accessio."

c82214c3-294a-4886-b590-53f6ccc0cbf9.Text: "Why did you decide to strike at the Lord Inquisitor's people?"

df59efc7-22c1-4026-918f-cada6b9db02d.Text: "Calligos, I see your wounds could not stop you from paying me a call."

2b512d9b-064c-4932-a6f7-c7af8dd53e78.Text: "Have you really renounced serving the cause of justice?"

40bab5db-9365-4415-9137-4bc30ed8d4ae.Text: "It seems you will be in charge of the Expanse after I'm gone."

320b2166-4499-487b-b49b-097115569394.Text: "Uralon the Cruel, I am pleased to be sharing this bloody harvest with you."

9deb3c00-efb2-46c0-b856-488dcd511017.Text: "What does my path hold for me, prophet?"

9e37f86c-8fd7-42d2-bc18-13698c575b74.Text: "Do not repeat the mistakes of your predecessor."

1527ce55-7098-484d-b547-add51d8e08e8.Text: "Nocturne of Oblivion, your visit is certainly unexpected."

f7d2452a-7aab-43c6-b989-63989b91c9de.Text: "Factotum, report on the state of the ship and the crew."

ca6b770b-ad1c-401c-a1c1-b2d0a8c9d2c0.Text: "It would be an honour for me."

cff9205a-9914-4d60-9cac-e2e53b6063fc.Text: "There is no need. A Rogue Trader of House Chorda ought not to swear allegiance to another dynasty."

0bce818d-2d90-44b2-a920-21d813a2e596.Text: "No. Calcazar is mine and mine only."

126ae314-f552-4a8b-a3a0-2fd218fd1de3.Text: "My greetings to you, Incendia. Now that you are no longer preoccupied with hunting heretics, you have much more time on your hands, I see."

9488b288-e28b-40c7-9d7f-e5a99d5964a1.Text: "What do you intend to do next?"

64ecda2a-36b3-4c4f-90ef-a143384ab42c.Text: "Will you return to your domain now?"

a006aea9-fbb7-48f5-93ce-e8d024062b3d.Text: "No. You will stay here and deal with the remaining misbelievers."

e0534dfd-c5db-4906-ac1c-4ca521b0db7c.Text: "Glory to the true gods of the warp!"

4e7cba05-13a6-446d-8e89-cdefb9f11e0d.Text: "Shall I break something else of yours to make sure you don't turn back to your old vices?"

63ba59de-0aa8-4dce-a3c5-df0efb9bacdd.Text: "How did you know you were needed here?"

a53b122a-96d4-414a-9c70-895322522ea3.Text: "Your brothers' might could benefit me on my crusade."

9e6a72cb-0870-4502-aa8d-b6adc4a2e51d.Text: "May the blessing of the True Gods be with us."

188535d4-0d00-4e28-b5d1-c89e5e283979.Text: "I shall give you a chance to justify even some small portion of your deeds."

8a51265d-f63b-4a50-bcef-70c3caafe6b4.Text: "What do you mean to do next?"

db624e96-324d-4f8b-8ff9-0e3e884daa34.Text: "What manner of business is keeping you here?"

bf339df2-cd4d-4d76-ab88-1dbc8a174e8d.Text: "What is the purpose of you coming aboard my ship?"

051d6434-55b1-415d-b018-445f3ff77781.Text: "It is astonishing that you chose to challenge Calcazar's people."

86345ec6-33b2-4d1c-a52e-e43bbfee7904.Text: "Why have you come? Surely not to bless me for my expedition."

77be8d33-290b-43bd-8f9c-33150c674521.Text: {n}Sporting a holstered autogun you have not seen before, Janris Danrok clears his throat before he begins.{/n} "Reporting, Lord Captain: the attack on the ship has been repelled. All decks have been cleared of trespassers. Hull breaches have been or are being mended. You have eminent visitors who wish to congratulate you on your victory."

5b0fdd0e-0d87-43c7-b5dd-758ccb583f9b.Text: "Friends and allies of your dynasty have arrived from ships currently in this system. They would like to pay their respects to the Rogue Trader in person."

0dd98129-78c8-449b-8975-9a7b169eabd9.Text: {n}Incendia Chorda folds her arms on her chest, making the sign of the Aquila. Her eyes are aflame with {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_ChordaExileNot}fanatical conviction{/d}.{/n} "{name} von Valancius, I bear good tidings. The Emperor looks favourably on your campaign. Head into the darkness and be undaunted."

cb08795c-0064-417d-a557-406a67ca9d6a.Text: {n}Something has changed about Calligos Winterscale in a way that is hard to pin down. A new harshness about his features gives him a predatory quality. His yellowed eyes are filled with rage.{/n} "What a slow talker that servant of yours is. Ha, I bet cutting off his legs would make his muttering a lot livelier!"

35750e6e-2653-4bca-b736-7d1ae9be5d0f.Text: {n}Young Evayne Winterscale looks at you with a solemn expression.{/n} "My friend, you have been by my side whenever I... no, whenever my dynasty has needed support from a wise ally. Please know {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EvayneIsAlly}this will never be forgotten{/d}."

ebc3c50a-2ede-4103-9686-c9989f244b5e.Text:
{n}The Harlequin, paying no attention to the anxious glances of the crew, {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}takes a bow{/d}.{/n}
"Behold in silence, Merchant Vagabond,
The crossroads laid before you at this time.
The laugh of jest unending has declared
Your dance adroit and worthy of applause.
And I, his words' mute echo, now arise
To send you on your merry way at last."

38352f99-8c90-4d68-a3f3-2a21b6a42e80.Text: "I shall strive to find important lessons in them, so that I may become better and thus redeem his legacy in the Emperor's eyes." {n}Evayne bows his head in sadness.{/n} "Speaking of legacy, this used to belong to Calligos. It was made for war, but I have no desire to wield it or anything like it. Perhaps it will be of use to you in your campaign."

1e995363-3646-404b-b0db-86d8fba547b5.Text: "What could be better and more dangerous than spilling the blood of that haughty degenerate Calcazar's minions? Punishing him for his insolence was long overdue. If you ever face him in battle, end the miserable bastard with this. And give him Calligos Winterscale's regards."

376cb3b2-9679-485b-a50d-f794c64baae5.Text: {n}Calligos strokes the weapon, looking pleased.{/n} "What I was born to do. Make war and sweep away any who stand in my path. I have a healthy list of those whose heads will make great decorations for my ship's bridge."

aad144ad-9cc5-41dd-801f-8583a59f2683.Text: "I accept this duty with humility. The seeds of the Final Dawn's corruption will be destroyed, and the xenos banished from our systems. House Chorda will protect the Koronus Expanse, undeterred by the boundaries of other domains or the powers that be."

37f52808-ca37-4a74-91ba-98b3211e5865.Text: "Sharp-tongued as ever, eh?" {n}Winterscale nods his approval but remains serious.{/n} "There is no need. When the Tech-Priests patched up my body with their steel, I ordered them not to be overzealous. I want my every step and my every movement to bring pain. I want it to be an eternal reminder of what I have done."

8074a24a-78d6-4e28-9921-311524b1292c.Text: "Now that a single step brings excruciating pain, I am being very cautious about the paths I choose." {n}Brazenness still colours the contours of Winterscale's smile, but the spite has vanished.{/n}

87d894fd-5ee7-4a12-a5c0-2bc9bba8739d.Text: {n}The Factotum coughs.{/n} "Minor damage to the outer plating in the midship hull and negligible personnel losses as a result of offensive action by enemy boarding parties. The key systems are in order. The enginarium reports impeccable compliance on the part of the machine spirits. In other words, we are fully combat-ready, Lord Captain."

76d5f35d-c863-4190-b997-7869d41f54c8.Text: "May the path of those who enact His will be as a radiant ray, an all-consuming inferno of light. May that ray pierce whatever darkness hinders their progress."

888d2b93-2a82-44eb-8e51-d85bc576ee31.Text: {n}Incendia Chorda calls for attention with an imperious gesture.{/n} "{name} von Valancius. When the hour is dark, only a coward and a heretic will not dare to look death in the face. I would like to join your crusade beyond the boundaries of the known universe. Will you allow me to do battle under your banner?"

64911a8f-2af6-4c96-afa1-7e5e84a7ded3.Text: "Hold on." {n}Calligos's voice thrums like the growl of a hungry beast.{/n} "You mean to say you're off to snap Calcazar's neck while I'm stuck here? Forget it. I'm coming with you to gut that bastard myself!"

4dd00a44-2d2f-4943-be22-25617f201ff9.Text: {n}Calligos Winterscale has grown hollow-cheeked and pale. Instead of the graceful movements of a fierce predator, he now {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_WinterscaleRedeemed}lurches like a lame bird{/d}. The augmetics in his broken back are unable to make him as light-footed as he once was. He lets out a tired sigh and says joylessly,{/n} "We meet again, {name}."

55b0dc92-f9a9-4884-97f8-1a24fb025290.Text: {n}Incendia avoids locking eyes with you. Her cheek twitches nervously as she says,{/n} "I have briefly suspended my {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_ChordaExile}exile{/d} in order to wish you luck on your travels."

6797daa9-1284-4d45-b5a9-0f9e80d68e4e.Text: "May a river of blood flood forth toward the Master's throne! May a pyramid rise from the skulls of His enemies!"

5ace4471-0e8c-4a89-97e6-8e7b985add11.Text: "So be it. I lend you my blade and my pistol as loyal companions on this quest."

95681289-3acb-43e0-8463-648ab47bd0b6.Text: {n}Incendia breathes a faltering sigh of disappointment.{/n} "There is truth in your words, von Valancius. Well, then I shall continue to stand watch over the Expanse until your victorious return — or that of your funeral ashes."

70ee6036-139a-48d4-91a2-31aa59d46517.Text: {n}With an animalistic howl, Calligos raises his weapon over his head.{/n} "Whoever stands in our way, they shall bleed!"

b06dfc73-8e13-400f-9b67-15b07b8cc35a.Text: {n}Winterscale growls furiously, glaring at you, but soon lets up and spits out resentfully,{/n} "Fine, {name}. You have the greater claim to that trophy. Good hunting."

a378126f-1004-41ca-aac3-951b90a310a6.Text: {n}Dozens of pairs of eyes hang on your every gesture, your every sigh. Every crew member waits with bated breath lest they miss your decisive words.{/n}

6794ac36-0095-4557-a1e3-4c2f940ec206.Text: {n}Janris sighs.{/n} "The xenos simply materialised on the bridge. Whereupon the enforcers simply refused to approach it. After all, the enemy of Humanity has not acted aggressively in any way. As of yet."

8bc80957-f364-4bd0-aed5-4593279dacc6.Text: "To give you a trophy that may serve you well in the battles to come. This used to belong to Calligos. It was made for war but I have no desire to wield it or anything like it, for that matter. Perhaps it will be of use to you in your campaign."

6dc0033b-9de6-4611-be75-98550c928c3d.Text: "To give you something. I used it to enact the Emperor's justice, but I proved to be a poor instrument of His will. Therefore I am handing this weapon of His wrath to you. May it protect you from evil in the darkness into which you are heading."

13b1f6b6-bb15-46ee-b12f-f4fda8a2b583.Text: "And since I shall never see combat again... take this. You could use a sturdy weapon, and this one deserves better than gathering dust in my trophy room."

c8494a1c-c81b-4f5a-85ee-f7f4877038d3.Text: {n}Winterscale grins bitterly.{/n} "It takes more than a broken back to fix my bad temper."

957f46cf-2306-41ea-a298-18306f0dec61.Text: "Much has changed since my time ruling over Footfall."

c3462132-fc93-475f-9901-29cb991b4a0b.Text: {n}Evayne smiles.{/n} "That is merely because the ceremony has yet to be held. You had done quite a bit as well before you officially announced yourself as heir. I have taken the dynastic reins of power — though, unfortunately, my ascent was not a bloodless one. But now is no time to celebrate. My protectorate stands to perish. I will invite you to my ceremony once you have returned, and my people are no longer suffering terrifying deaths."

303ba460-231d-412e-804e-581afd44ea1d.Text: "My dynasty needs healing. It falls to me to discover new paths to the colonies isolated by the warp storm. To weed out the villainy that has infected Calligos's court. To help the worlds he has bled dry. To stand up to the xenos who terrorise the protectorate. To wipe out the Final Dawn infiltrators. To make peace with House Chorda and reclaim the planets taken from us... I don't know if I have the strength to do all of that. But I will not back down."

e524afe8-d072-422c-a7f4-d078c1d70bb3.Text: "My dynasty is indebted to you. And Winterscales do not abandon their allies when in need. I may be inexperienced, but naive I am not. I can see that something is happening — something of great and alarming significance for the entire Expanse. If your aim is to unravel this matter and forestall further cataclysms, I will provide whatever assistance you require."

fb2021a3-f3c3-4fb2-8659-5703411f8fae.Text: "Quit playing coy, {name}. You know very well why. I am here because I owe you. Alas, Winterscales never find themselves in debt for long. Besides, I have never liked Calcazar. Your acknowledgement of me as a threat speaks to the trustworthiness of your intuition. And now that you have decided to take on the Lord Inquisitor, I would much rather align myself with a tried-and-true ally than someone of dubious repute."

dfbf122e-b904-4255-8e70-59c969dfb297.Text: "Correct my mistakes. Save what is left of my protectorate: find the worlds lost to the warp storm; drive the xenos out; weed out the Final Dawn infiltrators. And... negotiate peace with House Chorda." {n}The spite with which Calligos spits out the word "peace" makes him look like his old self for just a brief moment.{/n}

e865be6b-006e-40dd-9610-0efdcbcb9327.Text: "I wanted to make sure Calcazar's thugs, the ones guarding the gate, don't... give you any trouble. All sorts of things happen in the Expanse these days. I won't be boarding any ships myself anymore, of course, but I have enough soldiers to convince them that harassing Rogue Trader von Valancius is a bad idea."

23247849-eee5-4265-b217-c768c86f2ffc.Text: "I may not see as clearly now as I once did... but the visions have not altogether forsaken my mind. And I sense some vile enterprise being plotted where you are going. You are able to stop it, which means your path must be clear."

14c1ed2e-ff37-4c30-870d-86ef04dfcbdd.Text: "Never. My heart is forever with the Emperor, but I am a poor instrument of His will. I will serve the cause of justice, but I have no right to enact it. And so, I entrust this tool of judgement to you."

b3453085-6c35-4515-8538-acf9c340b667.Text: "Yes. Being here awakens... such terrible desires within my heart. To be the bringer of justice. The passer of verdicts! I must keep the Expanse safe from myself. I must return to my solitude."

045b2644-e987-4a09-9e72-5b193c4a2c24.Text: "May it be my destined lot to attain comprehension of His ways, His wishes, and His will."

8e7a8a70-8659-4cf6-b32e-88984dc88bb5.Text: {n}There is nothing in Incendia's clear eyes but a righteous conviction that almost seems inhuman.{/n} "That was the path revealed to me. You are going to a place where evil is being wrought against the Emperor. If you step into this darkness, you can pluck the poisoned root from which the vile deed stems. As such, your path must be charted and cleared by those pure of faith. Therefore, accept this gift of righteous annihilation so that, come the hour of judgement, it helps direct you to the right course of action."

3ed8d871-87d8-4e1d-bdbc-f1336359b192.Text: {n}The Harlequin begins taking off his mask, as if he is about to reveal what is beneath it, but before you can make out his features, he laughs and vanishes in a blue haze. Where the mysterious xenos just stood, his parting gift remains.{/n}

3f37c9dd-3ee8-400a-aef4-84955e62b47e.Text: "May the faith in the hearts of the devout never waver."

d73feda4-584b-4da1-9670-2b3088e51793.Text: "I will join you, {name}. My blood divination did not reveal to me all that lies ahead, but it did show that it is far more momentous and dangerous than a stray band of heathens. My brothers can complete their mission without me, but you may require the aid of the True Word."

d2d5598f-74f0-4fcb-a5b6-c1f5234e6218.Text: "As you wish, {name}. You chose this path yourself."

3ccd3f50-eaec-4896-a736-7eede589c9b1.Text: "I thank you for the honour of being part of it. My brothers and I were impressed by the determination with which you descended upon the corpse emperor's lackeys. Brother Skarikitus, who fell in that battle, wished that his flesh be used to create this gift to you, for such vehemence must always be rewarded." {n}Uralon regally presents you with a bleeding package. Brother Skarikitus's remains are wrapped in a torn and stained banner of the Inquisition.{/n}

2ec17b93-6975-44bd-b207-f53f1c01a24c.Text: "I was granted a vision, and we could not let this chance to deliver a crushing blow to the misbelievers pass us by. Euphonious are the vox-frequencies that carry the dying screams of the godless."

7a6e88f4-55a7-4041-99ce-79370de78684.Text: "Ha! We shall see, {name}, we shall see. When my blood's up, boundaries cease to matter."

347a5dd8-eba5-426f-8abc-c59db4119667.Text: {n}Janris mutters under his breath,{/n} "A new era has dawned in the Expanse. The era of the Rogue Trader whelps."

c10698b2-2340-4b0a-8d51-b32b9014e4b3.Text: "A different path is ordained for them. Calcazar, the watchdog of the Expanse, ran, thereby condemning the worlds he was tasked to protect. The Word Bearers will see to it that the entire sector hears these tidings of despair, for it is in terror and woe that the soul opens to the will of the True Gods."

116b3c71-d350-4819-9c03-545e8903c651.Text: {n}Abelard chuckles quietly and whispers,{/n} "His Lordship Winterscale does remind me of someone..."

91e6ce0c-ebb9-4bf7-8175-459d931aa3f7.Text: "A becoming. The prophecy led me to the Expanse, for I saw the blaze of the Final Dawn usher in a new and true fate for this dark sector. The rays of the Final Dawn wreathed you and guided you to ascension. Now it is time for you to become the new fate of the Koronus Expanse."

e9923c3e-f65c-4738-bd24-ba28bcc14373.Text: "And when I finally find a worthy heir, I shall entrust my power to them, outfit a small ship, and set off for the Heathen Stars or some other such place. There are so many worlds I have not yet seen."

933f10e1-a487-41db-9c47-6f38f5cf4a47.Text: "May our lips perpetuate the Truth, now and for all time."

8fcacb3d-884c-4d06-b432-1254a1bd9bb4.Text: "Tell me..." {n}Chorda looks up at you with obvious effort.{/n} "Is there any leniency in your soul for one who has strayed? Your crusade is a worthy endeavour, and I long to be a part of it. Let you stand in judgement over others — I shall be but your instrument."

41747c6c-b46f-4476-9f39-9a67d874db56.Text: "So be it! From now on, I am your follower and your smiting hand!"

346f11e2-39b2-4278-b98e-00600e67bc7b.Text: {n}Wasting no time on meaningless good luck wishes, your distinguished guests leave the bridge in solemn and respectful silence.{/n}

4edb2906-61d9-4079-b8de-afe1c94a1979.Text: {n}Chorda's gaze fades, and she averts her eyes.{/n} "Very well. Then may the God-Emperor favour you on your path, and me on mine."

1bde13e1-bcda-419b-b026-697fe12abcd5.Text: {n}The voidborn looks up at you with his habitual grim stare.{/n} "Lord Captain, we may commence the spatial translation."

b39061b6-0ca5-4cbb-8681-71cac782d004.Text: "I would have liked to follow you into the fire, but I am afraid I have much in the way of business keeping me here. The Emperor protects, {name}."

9b30f127-fa4a-4b4a-a833-3613b1c86864.Text: {n}The Rogue Trader bares his teeth in a cruel smile. For just a moment, it seems that instead of teeth, you glimpse the sharp fangs of some beast.{/n} "I had long been waiting for an opportunity to get into the fray with those mongrels."

152bdd83-5bd3-4c0f-9b21-7168928f2bd7.Text: "Verily, the righteous shall inherit His realm." {n}The Rogue Trader readily finishes the line from the litany, as though waiting for it.{/n}

2b599097-5a7d-4ac7-b963-61437ee5b827.Text:
"The briefest moment I will here abide,
The lull between two heartbeats, nothing more.
Your deeds have left their mark in memory's halls,
Where few among your kin have earned a place.
The Merchant Vagabond's grand tales I'll keep,
And be the steadfast guard of every page.
Oblivion's Nocturne will be heard no more,
For with these words I play my final chord:
Farewell is not an ending but a thread
That leads you into a new drama's web."

43c66b65-63c8-49c0-a19c-760117644d7d.Text: {n}The armour of Uralon the Cruel is adorned with fresh blood — likely that of the prisoners captured in the last battle.{/n} "I hope that you relished every moment of {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Eufrates_ChampionOfChaos}eradicating the godless worms{/d}, {name}."

b7ee7a15-ee6f-44fc-ad55-e38cc1175e55.Text: "Who is it that wants to come aboard?"

f1127fdd-13ae-4a3d-8ecc-ca8ef069800f.Text: "Welcome our visitors and usher them to the bridge."

24d63bd0-e19f-44b8-a723-f7a28940c4f7.Text: "Isn't anyone going to try and talk me out of this venture?"

d72d6f9c-0b1e-4d60-9330-78641f845b11.Text: "The enemy has been routed, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We are receiving a vox-signal requesting that we admit a convoy of shuttles on board for an audience. The augurs have confirmed that the shuttles are unarmed and belong to the forces that aided us in battle. Do you wish us to welcome these visitors?"

a7d2f592-204c-4b84-b7f1-aea8d26b6b1c.Text: "Rogue Trader Winterscale is on his way aboard a shuttle."

50700a0f-badd-4cbc-be42-27c499fa69d3.Text: "We have detected the signature of Her Ladyship Incendia Chorda's personal transport."

67a4726c-610e-4105-a88d-b23abdcbb839.Text: "Uralon the Cruel wishes to have a word with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} in person and has requested an audience."

f937fe63-2df3-4eae-9abe-a916271d772f.Text: "One of the vessels could not be identified. The augur operator believes it is equipped with cloaking field generators of xenos origin."

9a666901-72c9-4db1-b39e-18e627a1f0fa.Text: "Will do, Lord Cap'n. Glory to House von Valancius!"

c6b17fc1-81ad-4e57-a9b6-e02cf7dc0bb4.Text: The broken body has been smashed into the ground with such force that there are cracks radiating out from under it.

276e0f46-e923-4c0b-851f-dc41d9859294.Text: You can still recognise the von Valancius coat of arms in the half-abraded emblem on the side of the shuttle. Parts of the hull and equipment look as if something vaporised the ship's components one layer after another.

8839078c-bf7e-4960-8ea2-2a12264632e9.Text: The monoliths loom over the small plain — black, ominous, as inscrutable as the race that created them.

0ca30ccd-05d7-442b-b2e1-d8c56f82d950.Text: Drawing upon your patchy knowledge of the xenos, you guess that these monoliths were once part of a mighty transport ship capable of transforming into ground-based structures.

65f6e150-699a-45fa-a3b8-70ad0b729422.Text:
The vox does not produce sound immediately. The officer who made the recording speaks clearly and confidently but also softly, with a barely perceptible vibration in his low, orator-like voice. It seems that the tape is partially damaged.{br}
"Entry 1. We landed successfully, but were unable to report to Her Ladyship: the communication channel was filled with interference. The navigation system has been affected as well, so we will not be able to take off anytime soon, let alone return to the ship. Sergeant Damani is looking for the source of the interference. The only thing left to do is to keep a log."
***
"Entry 5. Thanks to the information we received earlier, we managed to partially decipher some of the inscriptions on the obelisks. Only the general meaning is clear, the creatures buried here are extremely hostile. We have not been able to identify the source of the interference affecting our communications and navigation. Lady Theodora made it clear that this expedition is extremely important, so we will continue the exploration regardless of obstacles. Whoever finds this vox-log must give it to Her Ladyship personally and no one else."
***
"Entry 18. One of the structures being inspected incinerated Corporal Monroe. We buried him with as much dignity as was possible in these barren rocks. His sacrifice need not be in vain, we will be more careful next time, and we will not embarrass Her Ladyship."
***
"Entry 19. The explosion of the xeno-artefact damaged the engine, the fuel compartment, and the cargo hold where we were keeping supplies. It is unlikely that we will return to Lady Theodora's flagship, but we have almost completed our task and are about to enter the buildings. What matters is the preservation of the data we have obtained."
***
"There were no dead people behind the monoliths. The creatures attacked us as soon as we managed to activate the gate mechanism in one of the buildings. Their weapons destroy flesh and plasteel with equal ease, and their bodies recover from any wounds." The words are interrupted by a bang and a yell. "I will keep recording until my final breath, and I hope it benefits the house of von Valancius. The weapons of the xenos burn with green fire and hurl bolts of lightning, and energy charges burst from their blades. Damani has fallen to the ground and cannot get up, her body is breaking, the rocks beneath it are about to crack. Tell Dahlia that her father gave his life for the good of the von Valancius dynasty, may she be proud of..."

5f23a255-51b9-4964-9fc7-07a96da3a79c.Text: "Mercy! I won't dare stand in the way of von Valancius's smiting strike!"

b558ad0d-00e2-4ea2-b240-922b482bfe85.Text: All the augmetics were brutally ripped out of the Tech-Priests' bodies while they were still alive.

c6a289ed-4e5f-49c2-a09e-d1f9dc4c3b70.Text: "For the Deus Calculus, the Changer of Ways!"

662c00e6-9957-46c5-a532-5b99be09e911.Text: "Registering a Category One blasphemy against the Deus Calculus!"

c3324336-9088-4aaa-95e0-bfe521b60bdf.Text: The body of the Space Wolf Halbrandt has been torn almost in half by the pincer of the vicious Helbrute, yet a triumphant, hungering smile graces the Wolf's lips.

a7de70ab-fbc3-4a72-8f57-e5b3c250782d.Text: A multitude of blows dented the armour of the horrific Helbrute known as Doomscream until the final axe blow split open his glyph-covered skull.

29eec601-e990-44ca-ac0a-f60c7db2f7af.Text: The shell of the possessed machine radiates sickly heat — a warp spawn is slowly taking over its mechanisms.

61e18bb4-9485-4870-9e66-84b4768ecc52.Text: Parts destined to become a holy weapon of the Imperium's reckoning have instead been assembled into a frightening and sacrilegious construct.

87dde469-b7e1-4ffc-803b-d716220330d3.Text: "The Omni— the Deus Calculus changes ways, comprehends ways..."

994efd10-e228-42e6-89e8-bf19a4a947cf.Text: Data-nails, corrupted with blood runes, sink deep into the brain of the false Skitarius.

af73d8c4-9909-4b91-9719-6197d5e5e05e.Text: The wretched prisoner's eyes have been burned from within and sorcerous glyphs carved into his body.

e6dde7c3-89e5-4eb6-a43e-ae1f7cb2764b.Text: Judging by the prisoner's eyes, which have been burned from within, and the sorcerous glyphs carved into his body, this poor soul was a psyker, and someone used his life to corrupt a sacred machine.

b0798813-a7ae-4fda-9d77-e95903fd780c.Text: Ordered an assault column formed from workers to capture the void cruiser on Eufrates II.

354d764a-5f45-4408-8f50-b96f2755fb2e.Text: ...ordered an assault column to be formed from the repentant manufactorum workers, granting those captives the right to atone for their crime with their blood.

432c2cf4-96d4-483c-9ff3-e0757b5ed327.Text: ...deliver a tactical report to the officers.

40534ac5-846c-4e29-8687-d661ea4ce5a7.Text: Summoned the officer for a "special assignment" on Eufrates II.

e1741576-e38a-4328-95ae-147696d4ca92.Text: ...the commanding officer who had led the first assault to present himself to {mf|him|her} for a "special assignment."

a1efd9fb-1554-4bcf-b610-347cbef86bd0.Text: ...questioned the survivors who had witnessed the ruin that Doomscream had wrought.

eaa96322-aef6-4653-a2f5-a292d48e697d.Text: ...sent scouts to assess the fearsome weapon.

d43bc9d8-2e6d-4814-ba7e-573d0b029c9a.Text: ...commence a rapid tank assault in accordance with the military doctrine Armoured Wave devised by Lord Militant Justas Quinn.

7040d1fe-86ab-4ba8-a8f3-54f26074ce58.Text: ...proceed with caution with the support of comprehensive area reconnaissance.

91903f42-4547-4b91-a08d-a24afd6a7816.Text: ...advance while utilising the surviving planetary populace as human shields.

0ab4e5c4-9b55-46ac-8acc-bb65fb59df28.Text: ...the assault force to proceed with the tech-sabotage.

4e98a8c1-2b79-4fed-9b8e-aba82e22152b.Text: ...the deployment of infiltrators and the execution of enemy commanders.

03e4f7ee-f70d-4304-9226-788850945fbc.Text: ...the shelling of the enemy with gas munitions procured on the surface.

5a583191-91f0-40a7-8a8b-169b63b321ac.Text: ...ordered that the cruiser be destroyed using blessed megaton charges.

e6df9a17-622a-4ecc-816b-69fc825f6615.Text: ...commanded that the sacred vessel be reclaimed from the enemy's clutches.

ff13785e-af5d-4b7c-bc04-2a4593ded99a.Text: ...had an entire voidship dropped upon the cruiser from orbit.

6d5cb235-55a5-496e-bb93-8ee54e2fd68b.Text: ...commanded us to close ranks and direct all available forces against the Word Bearers.

a7934191-9023-4b75-8dc0-6cee0d14ecf4.Text: ...devised a plan that placed the Space Wolves at the forefront of our strike.

cb3cd0ef-4b05-49da-85f9-f1afb51a9c1c.Text: ...brought the might of the captured Explorator cruiser to bear.

f412e32d-f260-449c-bbb7-0f2fb7cd53a4.Text: ...gave {mf|his|her} blessing to Opticon-22 and his suicide mission.

6acf3c65-1994-4fc7-90f3-c735205c72f4.Text: ...led {mf|his|her} retinue to hunt down this ancient killing machine {mf|himself|herself}.

b7c3b3a1-1243-4f4e-9b11-1301d7a39f3b.Text: ...the use of combat-class servo-skulls coordinated by {mf|his|her} personal swarm, call sign {petname}, to assist with the tech-sabotage mission.

f54ad881-9d6b-4479-85ca-5c03e6e324fa.Text: ...the vanguard regiments to detail the reasons why the first assault failed.

44e9b28a-83e6-4c32-ae11-948ea76bdd9b.Text: ...send a scouting party supported by {mf|his|her} personal cyber-mastiff, call sign {petname}, ahead of the main force.

0cbef0cf-43bd-4ddc-b1b0-8bf1cd6aa0e0.Text: ...ordered the troops to capture the cruiser at any cost and bolstered the strike force with a resplendent symbol of the faith: {petname}, {mf|his|her} own two-headed eagle.

e2564a73-c528-4e24-bafc-6f3e4f60ec62.Text: Upon descending from orbit, Sister Argenta inspired the troops with the very first notes of her prayers — her singing was the Emperor's voice commanding us to fight without any regard for our own lives. After rousing the soldiers to launch a daring raid, she quickly captured one of the heretics' commanders. That was when we heard a starkly different voice come from the Sister of Battle. Trembling with fury, she personally interrogated the miscreant, pulling one poisoned confession after another out of him. Once she was done, the world was purged of his impure breath. And she was the one wielding the flamer. The sight of that heretic writhing in flames was imprinted upon our memories, shining a light on the cruel darkness of our immediate future like a brilliant beacon.

f3f99473-38be-402c-a472-25ce38411ac6.Text:
Sector: Koronus Expanse
Region: Mundus Valancius System
Location: Dargonus, palace of the Lord General Militant
Material: Extract from the memoirs "When the Expanse Burned"
Author: Corvan Lazarus, Lord General Militant of the Dargonus Planetary Defence Garrison

20314d0c-295c-410f-b28d-519bb4200f9f.Text: A general once said that all wars are fundamentally the same — if you've seen one, you've seen them all. Groxshit. That general didn't witness the events on Eufrates II.

77a0d1c0-7fec-4691-a06c-1cb18d5195c8.Text: It came as a surprise to all when the Space Wolf Thorbald supported the Magos Dominus. After the Lord Captain had reconciled him with the Explorator leader, Thorbald had tamed his pride and spoke in favour of the Tech-Priests' cause of liberating the noble machine.

433452ac-c610-4543-be3b-ff2750a59f92.Text: And that's when it came. Doomscream. An ancient and bloodthirsty Helbrute, a merciless executioner forged from adamantine and ceramite. That single foe was repelling our assaults one after the other, turning hundreds of soldiers into a bloody pulp. For as long as that abomination lived, we had no hope of reaching the heart of the enemy citadel.

5c65898c-76c2-47b2-8dea-fcc9620e33e5.Text: The shuttles would have blocked out the sun, if you could have seen it through the smoke of the manufactorum city of Sigma-S-13. At its heart stood the Machine Cathedral, our primary objective.

297f676d-9802-49a5-b8f6-13faa18b1ccb.Text: The Lord Captain showed us mercy by having the landing zone bombarded from orbit. All the shuttles carrying troops — and, more importantly, precious vehicles — reached their destination. Daunted by our numbers, the enemy withdrew. That was the perfect moment for a decisive attack — with an armoured vehicle force of this size, we had the upper hand.

8f55df3d-3ccc-43a7-a97f-e63afc127731.Text: The Lord Captain's orders were to commence a lightning-fast assault. We were flying straight into a hail of artillery fire. For many of us, that was the end. The rest were being thrown around in mid-air, praying that the next shell would miss their shuttle. But the losses were justified — with that surprise attack, we seized the initiative at the start of the battle.

5705573d-1f69-4aba-9e7f-d23742816d20.Text: Ignoring the protests of the venerated Tech-Priests, the Lord Captain gave the order not to spare the world's infrastructure. We struck at the sacred chapel of the Magos Alchemys, triggering an emission of toxic gas. The noxious cloud blanketed the enemy's positions, but even that did not make the heretics retreat. By the time we had fought our way to their positions, they were so weakened by the gas that hung in the air that they showed us no resistance and surrendered by the hundreds.

c1fcd014-b5ad-4c63-b75e-900035dfcc21.Text: Opticon-22 and his cohort, their armour painted with black chrome, marched into the darkness of the manufactorum in silence. Hours later, we heard chilling sounds of combat, and then a flash erupted from the depths of the sacred workshops. The Emperor's Angels charged forth and found Doomscream there, crippled but still alive, and routed the fiend. His bloodied pincer, ripped off by the devastating explosion, was presented to the Lord Captain as a trophy. The body of Opticon-22 was never found — it was disintegrated by the atomic charge he carried into battle. Such was the high price for the grave and humiliating wound that he and his tech-comrades inflicted upon the unholy champion of the heretics. We chanted the name of the brave warrior of the Code in our prayers.

3bc15dc7-7fb1-44b6-a7c2-edb2ba786921.Text: What happened next would become legend. The Lord Captain at the head of {mf|his|her} retinue challenged the bloodlusting heresiarch that had crawled out of the darkness of time. {mf|He|She} dealt the wicked executioner a heavy and mortifying blow, and thus Doomscream was routed.

6621266e-a2df-45b3-a5a3-0e13273c56cc.Text: The Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} was wounded in battle. It was at that moment that Opticon-22 walked onto the battlefield with his cohort of elite Skitarii.

82c8eede-7022-44fb-8a3e-105de45c181a.Text: We began our advance. I will never forget the roar of the tank, its treads tearing the heretics' infantry to pieces, accompanied by the shrieks of lasguns and the rumble of heavy artillery. The deafening symphony of war.

a4fd9c02-faed-4ba6-91fd-439ec49041ad.Text: Nothing could stop us. We marched in the wake of a column of armoured beasts, not turning to look at the mushroom clouds, climbing over piles of enemy bodies and those of our own. We had our orders.

74bc8da6-5294-400b-bb3b-1a9545371f43.Text: The swiftness of our assault turned out to be a double-edged sword. By bravely charging into enemy fire, we lost many vehicles and soldiers to the traps set by the betrayers of Humanity. The tanks were getting stuck in the mounds of bodies, trying to chew through them with their treads. We breached the enemy's defences at the cost of countless lives.

cdfd50eb-7aa9-4cb5-b290-fd4d154009a9.Text: We were commanded to prepare our auspexes and commence the assault. We consigned our lives to small green vid-screens and their machine spirits.

16c21ea8-31f9-4df8-909e-42afc6a980e7.Text: Whenever we avoided another one of the enemy's traps and ambushes, we would then vox-cast their coordinates to the artillery gunners. While our comrades rained thunder and lightning upon the heads of those skulking whoresons, we gave the Emperor's Peace to the rest, making slow but steady progress toward the city walls.

208dc600-9977-46dc-b0b8-22be2260ef14.Text: A fatal mistake. Apostate Tech-Priests sabotaged our devices with scrap-code that made them lead us straight into the enemy's traps and ambushes. Surrounded by the death cries of my deceived comrades, I had only one solace: my lasgun never failed me.

b3467e62-f188-4ac1-8ad9-11f92c03c851.Text: When the Imperium orders you to do your duty and give your life for the cause, you don't ask questions. You comply and pray to the Emperor that you have a lasgun and a flak vest on you. Those civilians had neither.

84329a79-bed5-487d-9bd4-61bd26751248.Text: Rows of crying, terrified civilians marched ahead of us, spluttering prayers to the Omnissiah. Too many times I heard their sobs cut off by enemy fire. All I could do was grit my teeth and walk, trying not to look at their mangled bodies, praying to the Emperor for their souls. "Better them than me," was all I could think.

6d9b95f2-1afe-4dff-8d00-b52b397f7f3e.Text: I've seen old soldiers give in to fear on the battlefield. It's little wonder, then, that a throng of desperate labourers would panic the moment they saw the bloodbath they'd been thrown into. On top of fighting the heretics, we now had to deal with droves of civilians scared out of their minds, trying to break through our ranks.

c861eb45-28cb-4db3-ad1d-a54a3e408738.Text: At last, we reached the gates of Dock Mu-514, the threshold of the metal nightmare that was Manufactorum Sigma-S-13. However, the initial attempts to storm the dock shattered against the enemy's defences.

3eb92ca3-ae1b-471e-b319-6eca06a862be.Text: There were several enemy commanders among the heretics we captured upon landing. They were eager to show us the exact locations of enemy cogitators and provided us with decryption litanies to access the defence systems. That was the hour when we all thanked the Lord Captain for having made the wise choice of intimidating the enemy at the first stage of the planetary assault.

a705f351-cbbc-4cb6-9709-729324ac79f6.Text: Thorbald, the fierce leader of the Space Wolves, proposed to send infiltrators beyond the walls to kill enemy officers and weaken the dock's defences.

57b8d130-0ff5-4586-8834-e61dc4f0783f.Text: I was part of the escort for one of the Tech-Priest crews that broke into the dock to carry out the sabotage mission. It's one thing to watch a technomat wave a censer over a cogitator on a cargo deck, but another to observe sacred tech-rituals being performed under a hail of bullets and carpet bombings.

7a14f061-0449-4ce2-bdc9-1b7621f0e52d.Text: Their binharic prayers, decryption litanies, and blessed cryptopurification viruses did their work. Every turret in the vicinity instantly turned on the traitors, and the dock filled with gunfire and screams. When silence fell, the gates opened before us.

8ddaeac5-bc99-4e66-b47d-e10596ccca16.Text: A battle ensued between the cryptopurification viruses and the Chaos-stricken cogitators. Many Tech-Priests lost their lives in the fight against the devious scrap-code. It's not easy to forget the sight of a rabid mechadendrite ripping its master's head off. Once the rituals were complete, the turrets ceased their fire. However, as soon as our front ranks approached the gates, the last remnants of the heretical taint that had somehow survived the purge awakened the weapons once more, claiming the lives of many brave souls.

fca76091-a82f-4435-8d1f-1a8a3656d8e7.Text: The Space Wolves entered the city undetected and reaped a bloody harvest there. None could hide from those fierce and cunning warriors.

6361613c-6fdf-4443-be44-bee7ba5fc641.Text: The infiltrators killed one officer after another, sowing panic and disarray among the enemy. The bodies were impaled on spikes so that the heretics could see their commanders from afar. Once the mayhem had reached its peak, the Space Wolves demolished the turrets, opened the gates, and gave the signal to attack. The dock was ours.

1dab5318-ab83-49fb-8b69-3c033b0823d2.Text: The Space Wolves' skill was second to none, but alas, there were simply too few of them. The dead officers were replaced, and the fearsome Adeptus Astartes were forced into a direct confrontation. They destroyed the defence turrets and opened the gates, holding the line until we arrived to assist. The dock was taken in a decisive assault, albeit at great cost.

9813991a-294b-4625-a618-d5c837316179.Text: As per regulations, we waited until the gas cloud allowed minimal visibility, checked our filter masks, blasted the gates with our tanks' meltas, and charged in.

39547350-4cc1-4e91-8121-db8693ae375d.Text: Many heretics had already perished at the hands of their comrades who were fighting nightmares only they could see. We had no trouble cleaning up the rest of the disjointed lunatics.

4436e259-4fbf-4f9f-8484-0880fef61b66.Text: But the gas concentration was still too high — even the filters in our respirators couldn't block it entirely. As soon as we entered, disaster ensued. Our soldiers opened fire on our own, trying to destroy the nightmares in their mind's eye. I saw... things I won't describe here. When the gas cleared, the dock was ours, but the losses we had suffered were great.

b2399871-0bbf-4621-8d27-10c663e5fe64.Text: It took us many days to break through to the metal heart of the manufactorum. In the third week of the assault, the vanguard was halted and swept away by a salvo of plasma macro-cannons. Scorning every canon of sacred engineering, the heretics had placed the hull of an unfinished void cruiser on treads several kilometres long. This leviathan of adamantine and plasteel barred our way.

4f2a1854-f5eb-4bad-a9ef-3c262a2b74e2.Text: Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius was the supreme commander in that battle. A {mf|man|woman} of iron will. Unfaltering, unshakeable. I served in {mf|his|her} personal enforcer guard back then, just another cocky kid who thought he was an expert soldier. The Emperor was gracious to me, He gave me a chance to realise just how wrong I was. Most of my comrades didn't get a chance like that.

1934c42d-915c-492c-97b8-6988efb19130.Text: In the command centre, the Lord Captain ordered {mf|his|her} generals to...

31e0be95-d516-42e7-af1f-843192d6c5f9.Text: The Explorator Tech-Priests took this grim duty upon themselves, refusing to let the laypeople anywhere near their voidship. The mournful processions of Skitarii, Enginseers, and servitors set out toward their target, dragging the tank-sized megaton charges behind them.

1cdce982-90b8-4b8b-a568-e498daa49c7f.Text: The Omnissiah watched over them that day — every charge reached its target. The Tech-Priests offered prayers to the Machine God as they activated the charges in their final act of sacrifice. I imagine one could see the death of the mighty cruiser from orbit with the naked eye.

51d1913e-2d0a-410a-962e-49f6827a883b.Text: Not all of the charges made it to the cruiser. Some were destroyed en route and wiped out many of our offensive formations. But those that did reach the captured ship were enough to blast it asunder.

95dc0652-a040-436a-8414-1b0c1f653d1d.Text: Having the sacred machine on our side could have given our offensive a sizeable edge. Our orders were to get a landing force to the cruiser's bridge and escort the Enginseers to the main cogitator.

9b6ae4b8-332d-4011-942f-415317adc68e.Text: Our shuttles used the turrets' blind spot to deploy elite troops on board the cruiser. While they were engaged with the shrieking heretics, the Enginseers reasoned with the machine spirits of the main cogitator and initiated the blessed purgation protocol on the inner decks. It took us three days to drag every last cultist corpse out of the compartments.

86792b53-1824-4f76-aa66-cdb5e674b033.Text: Only one shuttle made it to the target. After losing many of its own to the superior enemy forces, the surviving unit had lost all hope of regaining control of the ship's systems.

b0bf2646-8a5b-43b6-bb7f-7a34ac8a1735.Text: The escort frigate Righteous Redemption was taken out of orbit with a simple order: to die for the glory of the Imperium. After the crew had evacuated save for the thousand souls who had been condemned to operate the ship's primary systems, the Righteous Redemption commenced her final attack.

86033c2e-cfa8-4748-b746-5cbed891da55.Text: The calculations were flawless, and the strike followed the trajectory straight to its mark. I will never forget the sight of her hull, set ablaze by the macro-cannon fire, crashing into the manufactorum halls and piercing the body of the heretics' cruiser. This fiery embrace obliterated both of the ships, leaving behind a colossal crater.

674eec39-3c5d-4e64-bb06-f9ff5425cafe.Text: I will never forget the sight of her hull, set ablaze by the macro-cannon fire, crashing into the manufactorum halls. Alas, the flight trajectory of the Righteous Redemption was flawed. She began to lose altitude too early and crashed into the ground, ploughing straight through our ranks. But her plasma drive stayed strong, and the frigate, after destroying everything in her path, pierced the enemy cruiser. Both perished in a blinding flash.

935fcf85-0fde-4dfd-84b4-76759d38d6d7.Text: Slipping on pools of blood mixed with sacred unguents, we made it to the Machine Cathedral. A gargantuan hall breathing with the flames of a thousand furnaces. The last bastion of the enemy army. That was where I first faced the Word Bearers, betrayers of Humanity and unworthy sons of the Emperor. What could we, mere humans, possibly do to match their unholy, bestial rage?

bafededb-1e64-42be-83ae-d6beb36b21d9.Text: Because the Lord Captain ordered the entirety of our main forces to begin the operation with a swift assault, the enemy troops were still in disarray, and not all Word Bearers squads had had the time to regroup at the Machine Cathedral. They were scattered around the battlefield and could not retaliate with a unified strike. This gave us a chance to surround and crush their squads one by one.

e08e1ff6-28d4-4f65-a058-c0f33010df09.Text: With booming battle cries, we stormed the traitors' positions in a tight formation, raining fire upon the enemy. It was a daunting attack, but the disciplinary officers drove us forward, cracking their electro-whips and shooting those who showed a lack of conviction in the back of their skulls.

2f937994-bf47-4030-8f83-4bbdf295002a.Text: For every thousand shots the ceramite of their armour deflected, a single one hit a vulnerable optical sensor or joint. One by one, the unhallowed giants fell under our onslaught. Our tenacity prevailed over their nigh-impervious protection.

a8d0aacf-595b-4b9d-88ad-1d60bb71f2fa.Text: Our weapons could not even dent their accursed armour. Upon seeing the futility of their struggles, our soldiers fled, tearing through the barrier units and leaving their backs open to enemy fire. Unable to resist the temptation, our adversary gave chase. Thousands of my comrades-in-arms were butchered before the armoured vehicles arrived to destroy the damnable heretics one by one.

01ce1f69-23b2-42b9-a51e-aa23867b7824.Text: The Emperor's Angels themselves led the charge that day. Magnificent in their rage, they forged a path for us to follow, and even the appalling champions of the Archenemy could not stop them.

c33c6707-db10-4889-b61c-0a2ab4f84e44.Text: While we distracted the enemy with suppressive fire and a hail of grenades, our unyielding leaders charged the Word Bearers and tore them to pieces. We were the anvil of His wrath, and they were the hammer!

0421aff4-7e9d-4083-b6a8-a8baef2641ac.Text: Alas, in their exalted fury, our unyielding leaders forgot about the wretched mortals that marched in their wake. They forgot all about the Lord Captain's instructions and revelled in duels and solitary hunts, abandoning us to our fates. Once the enemy was crushed, we gazed with horror upon the bloody mess that was left of our front ranks. In their futile hopes for the Space Wolves' aid, they could not fend for themselves.

f38159a2-33eb-44ba-b6bb-2aa3ec9655be.Text: There is no greater pleasure in war than turning the enemy's own weapon against them. Chaos Marines are stronger than an army of ordinary troops, but even they cannot survive a direct hit from a macro-cannon.

22a1c199-17cf-44a3-8f74-3d5b3335dfc3.Text: The cruiser's weapons tracked their targets well, and no armour could protect them from shots like that. The leviathan's treads rolled over the enemy defences, decimating the contemptible Word Bearers and bringing us great triumph.

00fcb369-6fe6-4eb3-93ba-89eb980e9d58.Text: The Word Bearers launched a suicidal counter-attack. They boarded the cruiser and cut a bloody swath to the plasma reactor. In their unbridled malice, the heretics triggered an explosion that made ashes of themselves, our fearsome landship, and a great many of the Emperor's good warriors who took part in that attack.

0bdf6fbb-1842-4b2c-8c6d-67b6777df3a1.Text: Despite the great cost we had paid, the planetary assault ended in success. However, many, too many heretics had withdrawn into the Machine Cathedral and entrenched themselves at the very heart of the enemy territory. The battles ahead were sure to be vicious and gruesome. Nevertheless, we had established our supremacy over the world's surface.

cb51be03-6c44-4990-86b9-adf9709cdf46.Text: The sight was both terrifying and mesmerising. A majestic cathedral that was designed to cut through the void was instead resting on treads of a size that staggered the imagination. Those treads were grinding buildings into dust, and the ship's heavy cannons were incinerating entire tank formations. How could mere mortals hope to defeat a behemoth like that?

3f971fd3-98a0-46a8-89b4-e263b95c5209.Text: The intelligence we received from the captured cultists proved valuable. We knew exactly where to look for the heretics' cogitators and how to gain access to them.

fc691f78-f2c1-478a-a656-fef17bd7859e.Text: Magos Dominus Opticon-22 insisted that we retake the sacred machine, for the vessel had been in the making for many decades, and its destruction would have meant a great tragedy for the Imperium.

f35775d3-60f0-4ff6-bfe9-cead7fc55eba.Text: Even divided and few in number, the Word Bearers posed a mortal threat. But we had the advantage, and we had no intention of losing it.

2fe2e9c8-9f57-4d00-a855-e985f52db538.Text: The Enginseers made the grievous decision to overload the plasma reactor in order to destroy the cruiser. The metal monstrosity was felled at the cost of great losses.

2013d788-6e65-4202-be08-e371cd6e5fb5.Text: But the stern Tech-Priests drove us forth with electrical prods, never letting us stop and explore the hallowed machine halls.

58ac8035-841d-4c50-81e8-dcb23a325346.Text: Pushing through the ruins of sacred workshops, we looked with awe upon machines that, up until that point, had remained forbidden to the eyes of the laity. Those were palaces of incredible and frightening technology: voidship assembly halls, alchemical atriums, sacred arsenals, generators producing invisible fields unsettling to the mind, and scriptoriums containing knowledge of horrors best left undiscovered.

35a5bba7-e37d-4f26-8621-22e328e8e0cc.Text: The dire-eyed Thorbald volunteered to track down and destroy the vile spawn, but fate had other things in store for him and his brothers — the Space Wolves pack was to be the first to storm the Machine Cathedral. And thus Magos Dominus Opticon-22 assembled a cohort of elite Skitarii and said that he would locate and eliminate Doomscream. The soldiers were whispering that he was willing to activate the so-called guaranteed annihilation protocol — a terrible and ominous rite that is as lethal to the enemies of the Omnissiah as it is to His faithful servants.

f9b5a275-e6d8-4333-ac5c-b4f554dbc544.Text: Those lucky enough to have escaped with their lives had little to tell us. They remembered a terrible howl hanging in the air and a death machine, impossibly quick for its size, dismembering people and crumpling tanks with its horrific manipulators. This enemy was ancient, devious, and utterly mad — the heretic's mind was clouded by rage and hatred, and his body was bound within a prison of metal and mutated flesh.

12f15fb6-7f0f-4a7e-a3b7-8265dfe5d0b0.Text: Upon arriving at the front lines, the Lord Captain...

c7d5be75-5c54-4abb-9685-af3f40a40804.Text: The Lord Captain's retinue and the Space Wolves band delved into the shaft, heading toward the heart of the Machine Cathedral. We watched them leave with reverence in our eyes as we were setting up a perimeter around the entrance. We knew that the true outcome of the battle of Eufrates II depended on them and that our fates were theirs to decide.

814e8d35-9ad4-431c-9194-759f45ab462c.Text: It was the Rogue Trader's wise guidance that allowed their strikes to pierce Doomscream's armour. Brutally wounded and humiliated, the profane executioner had no choice but to flee from the fight.

77cdcfb4-5278-4e4b-9cb8-f3dca59dbc9f.Text: Alas, there was no understanding of each other's customs of combat. The Skitarii hindered the Emperor's Angels, and the latter destroyed the Omnissiah's warriors with careless attacks. Victory was slipping from their grasp, thus Opticon-22 issued his final order.

7a64a585-f077-46c3-861a-b86c398af23e.Text: It seemed then that the Lord Captain's abundant luck was about to run out, but then Opticon-22's Skitarii and Thorbald's Space Wolves joined the fray. Their strife forgotten, the two commanders assailed the unholy weapon of destruction.

98f1135c-6ce4-4835-85b7-dc519cb90fcc.Text: The abomination's torn pincer, fitted with an ancient and powerful bolter, became the Rogue Trader's rightful trophy.

f9cb90bc-9972-4f9d-8764-2c2a3a5e3a54.Text: The fight was gruelling and bloody. Even the Lord Captain's retinue could not pierce Doomscream's indestructible armour.

2ddc843c-7667-4e39-bf60-89387d27f499.Text: The Omnissiah's warriors clung to Doomscream's abominable frame like ants. When the hour was right, the venerable Magos Dominus activated the sacred atomic charge that was affixed to his body. The force of the explosion tore off and mangled one of Doomscream's pincers, and the ancient heretical machine fled in shame. That was Opticon-22's feat.

eb18d4e3-6c10-484d-9838-d79d18340e5b.Text: The glorious warrior Ulfar, who had marched into battle with the Stormbiters pack and earned his fellow fighters' greatest respect in the very first hours of the assault, entered the enemy fortress by himself and returned with the heads of three high-ranking heretics, proving that this plan was well within the ability of the Emperor's Angels.

b8ec06a7-0bcf-4d1c-a90d-301811609afd.Text: Magos Dominus Opticon-22 proposed a tech-sabotage: he could send small Skitarii units behind the enemy lines and have them subdue the spirits of the area's defence systems.

d3cba8e9-b8e1-460e-be9f-3409e45c95c4.Text: That was the last time I saw Captain Sawyer. With a figurative bloodied nose from the first assault, as well as actual blood still fresh on his bandages, the hastily patched-up captain limped eagerly toward the command HQ upon receiving the order. There are no eyewitness accounts of what happened to Captain Sawyer — only rumours and speculation. War was raging all around and someone going missing is never a surprise in wartime. But for the sake of historical accuracy, I am going to cite them here, to give you an idea of the far-fetched tales that can be bred by the minds of worn-out soldiers faced with the unspeakable horrors of the Archenemy.

81cdfdab-55e1-42a6-91f1-d64f2b951d81.Text: There was talk of the valiant captain coming to the command HQ and stating his willingness to repeat the assault, only for the Lord Captain to smile and invite him in. There was talk of someone's strangled screams coming from the command HQ, sounding barely human and so loud they could be heard as far away as the rear guard. There was talk of the captain vanishing without trace and of human viscera found in the command HQ, laid out in strange patterns as though for an unholy divination. There was talk of many other things which I would rather not recount in writing.

e0d4f5e2-162c-496f-9007-c99cc3b948e8.Text: The fact, at any rate, is that immediately after the captain's disappearance, we received an order that contained detailed instructions concerning holes in the docks' defences, the blind spots of turrets, and the positions of enemy patrols and sentries. The information was chillingly accurate and no one knew where it had come from. However, it was instrumental in the success of the second assault on Dock Mu-514, which was achieved with minimal casualties.

db50d9f9-9e0d-4032-9543-98e470b6f53b.Text: The Lord Captain was merciful. Each captive was issued a single-shot las fusil and bayonet, whereupon an order was given to take the cruiser at any cost. The deal was that those who survived the attack would be granted the Emperor's pardon and could enlist in the liberation army. Traitors in wartime can seldom hope to be given a second chance, let alone an offer of such generosity.

3f974415-cf7d-44af-94e6-a08945ef996d.Text: No more than a hundred of them were left alive that day. The Emperor was harsh on those who had turned against Him. But many a seasoned soldier could have learned from their fervour. Covered in oil, blood, and soot, their eyes full of desperate zeal, the penal unit's fighters somehow managed, despite their losses, to break through to the mighty cruiser. They climbed shafts, used their bayonets, and applied what scant knowledge they had of sacred technology. Eventually, they destroyed the heretics operating the macro-cannons. Enforcer strike groups were then able to land on the cruiser and clean up the remaining cultists. The cruiser was conquered.

107c0e96-a81f-4ef0-8e31-819244c9ff71.Text: Because of their size, the servo-skulls proved instrumental in the tech-rituals. They easily slipped past the patrols and placed cogni-shackles on the enemy defences, buying precious minutes for the Tech-Priests to perform their rites.

38a72427-ead5-43af-b2f9-085c1119ba72.Text: It was for the first time in my life that I saw the blessed cyber-beast technology in action. The cyber-mastiff's advanced auspexes allowed us to identify patterns in the placement of the traps and avoid them with maximum efficiency.

6a30e71f-8212-448a-aa89-71ef3fd9cd6f.Text: Flying through the hailstorm of plasma unleashed upon all living things by the heretical vessel, our shuttles successfully reached the target. The pilots later described a "living Aquila" guiding the ships through the enemy's blind spot.

35029e05-6019-4d6a-9c05-4c6c3e283407.Text: The best breakthrough point into Manufactorum Sigma-S-13 was Receiving Dock Mu-514, one of the oldest parts of the city whose fortifications and defence systems were starting to show their age. Every approach to it was covered in traps — atomic mines, mechanical mayhemcallers, skin-rending arch-viruses. But we were ready to advance, taking sector after sector... even if it meant throwing our bodies at whatever the enemy had in store for us.

f5561e03-a27c-4ea9-a638-543068981c6b.Text: But then, not a moment too soon, a squad of Space Wolves arrived to their rescue. The Emperor's indomitable warriors drove back the trembling heretics and gave the Tech-Priests the precious time they needed to bring the machine spirits of the main cogitator to their senses. The cruiser was conquered.

d5e87b33-16f9-4221-b0f2-9f24c21ccf6c.Text: Our negligible losses during the landing stage gave us enough armoured vehicles for a decisive push against the enemy's positions.

235dba06-951d-4d06-abe0-fb129f63c1e6.Text: In one of the chemical chapels, we came upon a shipment of cisterns containing hallucinogenic gas. The Tech-Priests protested that the substance was not designed for warfare, that it was created for higher rituals, but the officers wasted no time pumping our artillery shells full of that gas.

1216d8eb-4d77-4fa1-bad6-d80673615f82.Text: The influence of the Ruinous Powers had corrupted and twisted Dock Mu-514 beyond recognition. Many potential approaches were blocked by walls of flesh fused with metal and anomalies that bent reality around them. Hundreds of possessed machines assembled on Eufrates II rose against us. The enemy was expecting us to strike, and we needed to disrupt their defences before attacking.

45dd03cd-0f2c-4a36-b594-65f8d3aa3f28.Text: At last, we reached the Machine Cathedral. We saw a yawning lift shaft left behind by a colossal land-gnawing drill that had burrowed for kilometres into the depths of the planet. There, deep below, lay the last hiding place of the heretics' leaders. Hundreds of grenades, accompanied by promises of swift judgement, were hurled into the pit — such was our righteous anger.

d5e1a5de-2918-451e-9aa3-9f60a890c7e0.Text: The planetary assault was a resounding success. The enemy forces were shattered and broken. A small fraction remained in the Machine Cathedral, but the rest either had been destroyed or were destined to meet the same inevitable fate soon.

be0ed374-e16b-4807-a6e1-d6d5377e1611.Text: The Rogue Trader's offensive struck terror into the heretics' hearts and shook their confidence in their own strength.

d9a9322c-e025-4836-8fe2-b7570183300c.Text: This creature's critical hit chance is increased by +50%. The heretic forces retreated deeper into the manufactorum and rallied together to take the last stand against the Rogue Trader.

0a1fd27f-6940-4ea3-b0f4-ca56c7b5c520.Text: The Lord Captain and {mf|his|her} retinue suffered heavy injuries over the course of the planetary assault and in the fight with the Helbrute Doomscream. Yet the battle rages on, and these warriors have no time for healing or rest.

424f4583-23e4-41e3-9316-a71ed489bfe4.Text: A gift from the Edge of Daybreak, these forbidden words fill you with great power. Yet, they are unknowable to you. Their secret will only be revealed with your very last heartbeat.

41a014df-9345-4b8a-af07-648d4e4949cc.Text: [Execute the heretics] "Showing mercy to enemies of Humanity would be heresy. I sentence them to death."

e5cd754e-0caf-4964-a10a-8aaad927497f.Text: "Lay down your weapons and await your judgement. We will hold the tribunal once I am done here."

c67f88c2-3be1-4f2e-961e-2c200df70137.Text: "Why the silence? Go on, keep praising me! If I like it, I shall spare you."

53c0106d-d39a-4b37-8211-325a40977c0c.Text: [Execute the heretics] "'Inevitability' is indeed the word. This is your reward."

c0c91a35-8341-4708-81da-a8d116e6bff2.Text: "Not bad, but there is room for improvement. Everyone lay down your weapons, and you, come up with some more impressive words of praise by the time I return!"

12964268-3e13-41a8-be66-6385d83d034e.Text: {n}The crowd of heretics fall to their knees and hold out their hands to you, pleading for mercy. Their leader, a heretek with worm-like tentacles stirring about in one of his eye sockets, howls plaintively out of his vox,{/n} "{name} von Valancius, conqueror of steel and smiter of True Flesh, we initiate the capitulation protocol! Nowhere under this chrome firmament and leaden haze is there a cogitational array capable of designing a productive method of opposing you."

e6d01470-8a26-4001-b25e-8b5895c17c37.Text: {n}One after another, the heretics hand over their weapons, like a congregation bringing gifts to a terrifying god whose stare alone could pulverise them. Perhaps for them, now that they have witnessed your tactical genius and unbridled might, that image is not far from the truth.{/n}

4282079e-b93f-4c8a-acc1-82bc861e0650.Text: {n}The heretek's tentacles recoil and his vox howls again as he pleads.{/n} "Even a mighty Titan could not withstand your wrath, and would turn into a lake of boiling metal!"

c17a5b2d-7df8-4545-9511-7f91d408dd65.Text: "Your wisdom is inscrutable as the warp's depths and boundless as the arcane technologies of ages past!"

b5d7b101-c905-4445-8516-c2ade2baaaf6.Text: {n}You think you can hear cogs creak inside the heretek's skull as he tries to squeeze out some more words of praise.{/n} "You are inevitability. You are doom. You are the scourge of unbelievers..."

81375c67-00a5-4eb2-a7e6-a98bc766cf19.Text: {n}The heretek falls abruptly silent. The soundless tension is only punctuated by the strained breathing noises coming from his vox.{/n}

05130a65-f753-4ecb-bb98-6abef2a1cee0.Text: "Your indestructible legions have annihilated all who dared to stand in their way. No matter what we threw at you, it all turned to dust, which your servants then trampled into oil and soot. Our survivors are few. Mercy! We beg for mercy!"

c49f1ba1-152d-41b4-b4b1-15f10f0ad0c7.Text: "Why are you revealing Calcazar's secrets to me?"

de30e3ad-d67c-4fa1-8f59-d3f13b92aa84.Text: "So what is the treasure you were looking for here?"

f2bb12ce-1f97-4c88-b772-b7c9c47e2af8.Text: "Thorbald, did you understand what is happening here?"

72a5dec1-2197-4f7d-a641-043c7cf11e48.Text: "Tell me: was Kunrad destined to be sacrificed all along?"

1ea31811-3981-4758-adeb-f8e9e2edab79.Text: [Honour the fallen Tech-Priests] "May the Deus Mechanicus accept their souls."

aaaccb63-4ee2-4ac5-9565-a9f4da31469a.Text: "If Opticon-22 were here, he would say that this victory has brought him pleasure, along with three scores of synonyms for it."

a6221960-00be-4c20-b878-e9d80520d4e5.Text: "It is not my place to judge you. You were following orders."

ee0b206f-cc75-417b-8190-aa7027f09f70.Text: "You were wrong to obey Calcazar. He used you to commit a dark deed."

8fe6e139-f907-44d5-8d26-3ce44775e6e7.Text: "How is your pack, Thorbald? What are your losses?"

a66323f9-0cd4-47d2-ae2f-026c743c76dc.Text: "I am returning to Footfall. I have questions for the Lord Inquisitor."

af0948f8-8c1f-4624-9117-9cfa06d130ef.Text: "I did not expect this from you, Ulfar. You have betrayed my trust."

c91f79e5-68c1-4a70-9f5d-b3c61f849974.Text: "What else do you know about this weapon? How did Calcazar learn of it? Against whom does he intend to use it?"

6e16290d-5a0e-442d-b220-9a356a939bb1.Text: "What was hidden down there? What was the treasure that Uralon was after?"

de01fd23-3803-473e-acb5-6f518b6e453c.Text: "What else do you Wolves know about Amarnat?"

983c0896-4517-41f4-956b-59089f36d2b2.Text: "Why did Calcazar need you to do it?"

a8d4ab96-e0b9-41ae-8923-6580287139f1.Text: "You are not the first servant of the Omnissiah I have met who goes by that name."

d2085e21-505f-476e-a132-09075be2ed77.Text: "What are you planning to do next?"

3b9ef865-6277-482d-b18e-86fd15a7ce3b.Text: "How did you come back to life? It cannot be that corruption is in control of your body now, can it?"

72d84f75-4ccc-439d-9083-3e0f4d69e5dd.Text: "Uralon, I demand an explanation. What is really going on here?"

e27f7dc2-d309-464f-8c80-0ae1e383a2ae.Text: "She is still alive! Call the medicae!"

573dd83f-a61a-4936-bd87-d3a9c2a9c327.Text: "I respect your oaths and do not think less of you."

3096d947-c4fb-4a6c-bb4b-8af6fb70b9f4.Text: "Do it, Thorbald! The heretics' corruption must have tainted her body!"

d18a727e-6034-44d1-8d82-1562a5234f39.Text: "The Lord Inquisitor will answer for daring to manipulate me. I will chase him down on Footfall."

3b5bea00-b4bc-4fb9-afdc-93e1789b5cab.Text: "Pasqal, permission to commence the interrogation procedure granted."

77185978-1657-4524-8bc4-5a445ec63e3a.Text: "I need more details. How does it work? What is this Yoke?"

636db75d-825f-4fdf-99ec-e2daa0da634b.Text: "How exactly did the object affect you?"

4cdcc594-d4d1-4dd5-8e3d-05368e996d7c.Text: [Point at the dead Tech-Priest] "Was she your sister?"

580309da-58d9-4c5e-924a-541ca8bc5a61.Text: "I doubt I can learn more from you."

4c43c32f-cad0-4ab7-b266-459073d774de.Text: "You spoke of a shelter and a Maimed Hunter. What did you mean by it?"

1e538e51-23ab-47d6-ba02-f3ca05564420.Text: "Pasqal, what have you learned from your... conversation?"

197a5010-47c5-4380-9ec8-7986c7c15365.Text: "And what do you know about this secret weapon?"

5d0de386-b5ec-4d56-8605-7d11b38bd9d1.Text: "I see you and Ulfar have worked through your quarrels."

b760841c-4c0a-40e1-80d8-3e19e0ec02a9.Text: [Send a vox-cast to the ship] "Stop the loading. I will inspect the trophies personally."

1fbbcedb-24f3-4384-ba6d-6365c5cbb9be.Text: "Ulfar, why did you keep quiet about this?"
