c51d538c-d786-4cc3-b0d1-4cf491f7a494.Text: "Because her actions fly in the face of all that you believe in. That you truly believe in. Incendia's world has no place for redemption, or mercy, or penitence. Would the sight of such a world please your eyes?"

c927d904-c363-48bf-972e-92b1829b7b9e.Text: "If you are so sure of your own righteousness, why have you not faced Chorda's justice yet?"

e3495e79-33b4-42cf-a8c3-2c98411a0330.Text: "Now look me in the eye, Reverend, and tell me you are ready to meet your death right here and now, without a shadow of fear or regret."

9bb3302c-34b1-42fc-a636-4ced78cb4a72.Text: "Stop denying it, Hieronymus. Admit, once and for all, that your faith is not as strong as you thought it was, and that the Emperor will not protect you from the murderous zealot's fire."

c23900fa-8831-4543-aee1-1a8e3a3cc714.Text: "I will not bother you with unwanted advice."

7b692bd9-4439-4ef4-925f-bf59cdf7f196.Text: "You are going to die, and there is nothing you can do about it. Not a moment goes by without the horror of it consuming you from the inside. Admit it."

d06c0ce1-a6a0-4867-949b-61340bed6f8c.Text: "You have raised a worthy daughter of the Emperor. I see no wrong in that."

5d416510-098d-440d-8670-4e00a0043d7a.Text: "If this place is so full of vice, why do you not cleanse it yourself?"

791bcae5-1c13-423a-92db-1fb62c7e823e.Text: "You have breached the laws of the Imperium. I will see to it that justice is done."

0aa457a4-80df-4c9f-aea6-3f2560a6c809.Text: "You give penitents a chance for redemption. That is commendable."

39714f50-bbf3-4e14-ace5-4e5ac9335493.Text: "Your cult is dangerous, welcoming criminals with open arms."

3e3c5026-c27b-4a43-967e-3ca92717d383.Text: "Spare me the tedious list of your crimes."

e3b85fa2-3053-482b-89c4-2775209b4ef8.Text: "You aid and abet a vicious criminal. You will pay a harsh price for that, do not doubt it."

9850d457-b4af-4907-ae90-fa1ca9e4dbb2.Text: {n}The priest staggers back, stunned. He opens his mouth... and a tiny, barely visible fly passes between his gapped teeth and disappears in his throat. The preacher does not even notice.{/n} "What is all this heretical talk? I— I do believe! Why would I be afraid of death?"

e2ad4558-581e-483e-9bff-60e510d4797a.Text: "The Emperor protects, young von Valancius. What has brought you here? Perhaps you would like to confess? Repentance is the first step on the path to redemption!"

c179ad1d-88eb-4a38-bab0-e2ffb8d38918.Text: {n}Hieronymus sighs heavily and is silent for a while, then he replies, in a hollow voice,{/n} "It was done on my orders. All my life, I have been a confessor to lost souls. Now let me make my own confession to you. I seek no forgiveness or understanding; I only want to tell the truth. Aspyce Bastaal-Chorda had imprisoned her heirs in those cryo-vaults, to stop them from challenging her authority. Incendia was among them."

40df13d1-b6e8-4b66-a661-0ebedd16be56.Text: "I sabotaged Incendia's cryo-vault, and she spent three years conscious, blind and helpless. My brothers and sisters recited prayers over her prison, to plant the seed of faith in the soil I had weeded. I hid the truth from Incendia and became her mentor, setting her on a path of service to His will. And that was how Incendia, the offspring of a felonious heretic, became His vengeful hand striking down enemies of the Imperium. At the cost of the evil I had done."

86141bef-480e-4d99-842d-529a5e4a59cd.Text: {n}Looking into your eyes, the preacher opens his mouth several times to say something, but never musters the courage. He frowns, and his lips twitch.{/n} "I— I cannot utter that, for it would be untrue."

67cbc9a1-25ec-4630-af25-a0f543bd59a3.Text: "And it will be done. Without mercy!"

d3b5786c-012e-44b3-88ba-ce0b20be1064.Text: "Although I will not lie, I am finding it hard to look upon this cleansing fire, for its blaze is terrifying. I was Incendia's shepherd for many years, but now she leads and I follow. I would not have had the strength to lead Footfall down so terrible a path toward justice, for my heart is weak, and I am sometimes given to unrighteous doubt."

f901e799-ddd7-4d0e-98d8-7c54524741a2.Text: "You have both banished some of my doubts and given me food for others. I will do what must be done. My faithful will assist you in battle. And afterward... I will find a new path."

f8f78484-ebcb-4970-b09c-635c9dc4a624.Text: "I am glad that I can lean on your words. I will fortify my soul and cast away my fear. Thank you for not letting me stumble and banishing my doubts, noble {name}."

8909fb3e-b747-4013-bc42-aaa1893d1677.Text: "The Expanse is aflame, besieged by the Archenemy's hosts and the cursed xenos. Anyone with a worm burrowed in their soul is a traitor in the making. At a different time, one could deem Incendia's justice to be too harsh, but not now."

138a2264-7abb-464b-9c4f-8c044213226f.Text: "I do indeed! A great cleansing is underway, and all those unfortunates have brought their suffering upon themselves! All of the vices that lurked like serpents in Footfall's belly have slithered out into the light, only to be met with the righteous fire of retribution. Or, do you believe that you or I could be better judges of who deserves to be punished for their deeds and who does not?"

69ea3388-9e97-49b2-bdd1-d51cee8e7ffc.Text: {n}Hieronymus grimaces bitterly.{/n} "You are right. No one escapes retribution for their past deeds, as much as we might believe we were doing them for a good cause. I thought I was raising a paragon of righteousness, forgetting that my soul was more tarnished than many. And I have raised a monster, not a champion of faith. Now those who truly needed me are paying the price for my simple-minded pride."

2d6e2ba7-10bd-4e05-9a98-9c0659002294.Text: {n}Hieronymus laughs a dry croaking laugh.{/n} "Are you suggesting that I commit a new crime to undo an old one? That I stand shoulder to shoulder with the godless, the heretics, and the xenos, thus betraying a true-believing servant of the Emperor? I would rather let the righteous fire take me into its cleansing embrace!"

4d772782-ba9f-4d9f-9e6c-2d4cc9b9f88b.Text: "Chaplain is a deeply devout servant of the Emperor. Few are as intimately familiar with human vice as him, and that is what fills his words with sincerity. His flock heeds and respects him. And as for all the hardened rascals and cutthroats who are part of that flock — why not? Our doctrine shuns no one, so long as they are willing to receive its word with an open heart."

24bda12e-36ea-45b6-a9b6-01e1f9a0d0fb.Text: {n}After a long silence, Hieronymus says,{/n} "I have thought about it. I have seen Incendia convict people for trivial past infractions. There are many outcasts among Saint Drusus's faithful whose old misdeeds she may deem unforgivable. I... cannot allow this."

6f6acaa7-fc87-4132-adc1-08e1a461a73f.Text: "I hope that the suffering we inflicted upon ourselves as penitents has cleansed our souls enough for us to face righteous justice. But if the blessed Incendia gleans corruption inside my soul and judges that only fire can eradicate it — then so be it!"

3e139b95-b521-499f-badf-9dadfdc64132.Text: "What else would you like to know?"

724ab241-b8c0-4561-ab1e-540c02c4bbfa.Text: "We would never refuse our help to one who makes generous donations to our mission."

5fadfcac-264f-4c4f-ac84-840773aea55f.Text: "It is not rebels that I see. I see fools and malefactors whose weakness made them reject the law of the Imperium. Who are in need of repentance and instruction. Had I come here earlier, perhaps I would have been able to prevent this heretical insurrection. And what do you see, Rogue Trader?"

0da44947-4a7b-434c-a765-13b35f8982c2.Text: "On the contrary. Better to repent a moment away from death than to have lived a life of iniquity, and die corrupt, without once seeing your deeds for what they are."

002d3dfe-7b72-4f4c-9f84-6fd982078724.Text: "I have tainted my hands with the blood of scores of helpless men and women; then, for years, I tortured an heir to a sacred Warrant and lied to her, albeit with what I believed were good intentions. Yes, the blessed Incendia became a model servant of the Imperium, but the path toward that was paved with many crimes. My crimes."

aac254b0-9f9c-4efd-9e43-7701d60ae87d.Text: "And I will be eager to receive my punishment. Saint Drusus taught us to partake of punishment with humility, and gratitude."

d5585237-dd43-4f57-b34f-7dee3b6de3a3.Text: "Are you openly declaring your intent to move against an enactor of the Emperor's justice? And why should I, her mentor in the faith, help you commit that act of treachery?"

e1a7caa3-9398-483c-848f-d44f6db6e4b9.Text: {n}Hieronymus bares his yellowed teeth in an acerbic grin.{/n} "Indeed! I would rather call the worst of all scoundrels my brother if he repents of his crimes, than someone convinced of their own soul's purity."

253944bf-af0d-4455-a64e-b107421dba8f.Text: "And a liar and murderer as well. If you are accusing me, do not omit any of my crimes, for I will not deny them."

d8656670-fbbf-49d8-ae61-0466e2cedb1d.Text: {n}The priest snarls angrily.{/n} "I am not your executioner, Rogue Trader. I serve the God-Emperor, not your whims."

bd03f344-20b4-46aa-ab8f-e93be76f70d6.Text: "I take no credit for that. They choose that path for themselves. I merely point out that the path is open to all, and instruct those who have started their journey to redemption. For thus Saint Drusus taught us."

e61cbfa5-e3ca-4cef-ae4b-75ee58cdf12a.Text: "Saint Drusus taught that everyone deserves a chance at redemption if they sincerely wish to return to the fold of true faith. It is a thorny and painful path, which is why it is beneficial to the soul. All my brothers and sisters follow it, and thus serve the Emperor faithfully. Who are you to judge them?"

1f98f242-8a03-42a5-bb35-f71b00e88529.Text: {n}Hieronymus hesitates. The colour has drained from his face, and he no longer has the look of a firebrand. The man in front of you is old, shrivelled, and frightened.{/n} "I want to argue with you, to denounce your lies, but... it is true. Incendia does scare me. As does death. But how do I not fear it?" {n}The reverend seems transfixed as he looks at you, ready to hang on your every word.{/n}

dac55ebf-630c-4593-869b-a9217b3fe311.Text: "Now you have banished my doubt. I will do what must be done. Saint Drusus's faithful will aid you in battle."

3f368048-1834-4e6b-b7d5-1156647115a7.Text: "I am glad you have realised this! Justice will be done. All you can do is to accept it."

e73bc5a3-8f26-492a-91ec-0459ebbe0799.Text: "You... are right. All our lives belong to the Emperor, and no one has the right to needlessly take them away from Him. People who, in this dark hour, could have atoned in battle against the enemies of Humanity, are instead perishing senselessly, robbed of their privilege to serve the Emperor. Incendia thinks herself above Him, and that is an egregious crime."

3ac79721-11bc-4902-a5a7-5c42d532608d.Text: "That says more about you than it does about me, Rogue Trader. My greatest crime is in the past now — yours, it appears, is yet to be committed."

766dfbc7-fe4a-43c2-9840-f9f315c7457f.Text: "Indeed, her fervour frightens me. Sometimes I feel she takes pleasure in doling out punishment and revels in her own power. She has forgotten that punishments exist to purify His servants and return them to His light, so that they may continue this service. Senseless slaughter is at odds with that goal. I regret never managing to drive that point home to her..."

86aeeba5-ac2f-4e4f-bb67-8a2bd2515d51.Text: "My confession is over. I have bared my innermost self before you, and the truth concealed therein. You are free to do with it as you please."

b0e65ea8-ef8e-4651-b524-84d3303cdae7.Text: "Redemption is but one aspect of our teaching. You forget about Drusus the warrior, who teaches us to be ruthless toward the enemies of Humanity — those who can only be redeemed in death. Incendia was always inspired by his relentlessness in confronting corruption, and nurtured the same quality in herself."

54b93fab-dfa5-41b3-86c4-f4572bce27ce.Text: "Enough! The pains you are taking to tempt me into betrayal are merely strengthening my faith. Incendia's justice is righteous, and retribution awaits the heretics who reject it. Now you have banished my doubt. Is that not wonderful?"

a023b164-434c-4e7d-8311-ffd23b0e9f81.Text: "Thank you for your tact, young von Valancius."

7ae9f625-82c3-43a1-8f95-ea615e7e7618.Text: "I am afraid, young von Valancius. I am afraid that I am wrong. And my words will lead a champion of faith astray."

7b56e7d8-8c81-434c-b085-777a8b8ba52a.Text: "Sooner or later, we all will. We can only pray to Him that we will be able to pay the price when our time comes."

1e23d776-fa4b-446b-9e9b-c5ff421a9d97.Text: "You are entirely right! But it is not their lives that they should be saving: it is their souls that are truly in peril."

5ea2a4b7-38d8-4548-81f2-1aed3ec04b3f.Text: {n}The priest shudders and mumbles, more to himself than to you,{/n} "Blasphemy. Heresy. And yet... do I have a choice? Is an unrighteous life the only thing that can save me from an unrighteous death? I am a vessel of depravity. And if so, what is even the point of redemption?"

b4e635c9-59cf-441a-9f27-e729c36d810c.Text: {n}Hieronymus's eyes are filled with bitter sadness.{/n} "No. It would not. My way of serving Him has always been different from the paths trodden by the Ecclesiarchy. Saint Drusus's doctrine taught me virtues that are unknown to many among the righteous, and I, in turn, taught them to my brothers and sisters. I tried to teach them to Incendia, too, but... she chose a different path. It is time for me to remind her of those lessons."

06531ab8-9280-4c9c-9b54-e268ee16b194.Text: "What could a lost soul like you know about her justice? Incendia truly has an eye that no vice can escape, nor can anyone hide from her avenging hand! I will face her justice and accept my lot if she so wills."

640c4683-d8f8-455e-8e20-7009596df8ff.Text: "Because your invective caught me off guard. Did you really ask me to join a rebellion, then at once turn around and accuse me of heresy and treason? You say I am afraid of death — why, you positively crave it!"

86001a72-43f1-4b91-a571-384c20e85793.Text: "Never once have I called myself a righteous man. My soul is burdened with many past deeds that prevent me from doing that." {n}The preacher thinks long and hard. He frowns, and his lips twitch.{/n} "Perhaps that is the reason I am biding my time before facing Incendia? Perhaps you... are right?"

54158f50-1687-4cec-8c51-b478c9dc3f8e.Text: "They must. And so must you, and I! Or do you imagine your soul is pure? It is not. You, me, all of them, we are all reprobates, and only repentance can save our souls from heresy."

c7d7967d-5b3d-40c3-b5f3-7a98ac8942a3.Text: "My body is indeed worn and pathetic. But do you really think I am devoid of compassion? I grieve for each fallen soul and am more invested than anyone in their repentance! Bitter sorrow, not triumph, grips my heart in this place."

6378c0bd-815f-4e1a-b91a-0a7f8ea717ac.Text: "Or would it have been better for Footfall to still be ruled by Vladaym? The Liege tainted his name long ago by mingling with enemies of Humanity and dabbling in their creations. Now he has but deepened the corruption in his soul. Wilfully bringing xenos into the Emperor's domain to assist an insurgency against His servants? Heresy!"

6554da2e-0f18-4cea-a25d-31caf163c27d.Text: "My fellow faithful chanced upon those ice crypts. Aspyce's wicked design horrified them. And I thought, if Saint Drusus had died a martyr's death to be resurrected in faith, perhaps another could follow in his footsteps. I chose Incendia; as full of worms as her innermost soul was, it had not rotted completely. As for the others... I put them to death, for thousands of years of suffering would not have been enough to cleanse the stench and rot from their cursed souls."

d7a42d95-01be-42c6-b334-96deb63d9b14.Text: "Because I believe that at least some of these lost souls can still be saved and returned to His light! I would separate the wheat from the chaff, not put the whole sheaf to the fire. But I will not lie — even I am given to doubt when I look at the heresy that reigns supreme in this place."

df87296e-b820-466c-a136-004810eff751.Text: {n}As you look into Hieronymus's eyes, it is clear to you that he, not you, is the one who ought to confess and repent. Hidden behind layers of piety and fervour is some secret the reverend has been carrying within him for years. A secret that is now gnawing away at him more strongly than ever before.{/n}

0ab3db0b-a6c1-4256-8735-3e79b44d24cd.Text: {n}The preacher does not argue. He knows your words to be true. Hieronymus sighs heavily and is silent for a while. Then he replies, in a hollow voice,{/n} "All my life, I have been a confessor to lost souls. Now let me make my own confession to you. I seek no forgiveness or understanding; I only want to tell the truth. The blood of House Chorda is on my hands. I chanced upon a secret world where Aspyce Bastaal-Chorda had imprisoned her heirs in cryo-vaults, to stop them from challenging her authority. Incendia was among them."

7001d826-76c7-42a7-85e8-6f9b8161d8de.Text: "What forces do we have in place and what is this rift that occurred between the commanders?"

c7359bbb-e36e-4e0f-8a69-4f254c4acf86.Text: [Look at Calcazar's solitary cup] "Hospitality is not the Inquisition's forte, I see."

e3e72ecc-3077-4de4-86e9-f8a66913f6f3.Text: "What was the dispute between you and Calligos Winterscale about?"

2945c1a3-d978-4d3f-bc04-d5653da2422a.Text: "First, I am barred from entering, and now I am summoned here like a servant. An appalling way to treat a Rogue Trader!"

d489f0a2-ba6e-49d0-ba4b-22d44cff9a0a.Text: "I am told you have business with me."

4c7b3984-be53-4cd1-88b8-7438040a94e9.Text: "May the Emperor grant you strength and some time to rest, Lord Inquisitor."

75490077-b83e-4c4d-a4b9-6deb5d744082.Text: "Last time, you congratulated me on my rise to power, and now I am here to return the favour."

a4e6c46d-fec1-4616-a2b2-ca45744dcf18.Text: "Is there any way you can help find them?"

05e5e9fd-a2ad-4a8c-9813-4cec065fa579.Text: "Calligos was under the influence of the Ruinous Powers, but I put an end to it."

b2b5f345-c8ea-4a5a-91f8-c4c28ae4f7cf.Text: "I convinced Chorda of the error of her beliefs. She has left the station."

5b92f40d-1e80-463a-a4a7-048f488796b3.Text: "I helped him deal with the xenos."

7b18dafc-8452-4b03-87e0-68c8dd0f815a.Text: "Why do you think they diverted their attention?"

7f3df0f5-f28e-42f3-ab6d-c74a3154791f.Text: "I escaped from Commorragh, where I was held captive by xenos."

f7d23476-2d80-4944-ada5-a7a8a070edae.Text: "What is the current situation in the Expanse?"

f5eb044f-a9a5-490b-b152-e5fe47c7de62.Text: "What help do you want from me?"

4f4f70fa-08d1-422d-9046-06d0590ccfa7.Text: "You are a mighty warrior. Shame that your prejudice has got the better of you."

c62b888f-e44e-4144-8d08-8106d7a56ffe.Text: "What has prompted the Drukhari to act so brazenly?"

f75f149b-c4f0-4f4d-b367-c14f073f72b2.Text: "Why has the Cult of the Final Dawn become more active?"

bb8455d1-7eb2-4ff9-b8c3-0b98217b3041.Text: "You have mobilised all forces... but not House von Valancius."

92b114a5-352d-428d-9d5e-f20e43d39718.Text: "But you must have an ingenious plan to save the Expanse?"

b5e641d9-f95a-4efb-81b8-ceb77f370cc3.Text: "To what do I owe such an honour?"

be6c6fe5-d89c-4675-b6aa-bba3f365774e.Text: "Can you tell me more about Eufrates II?"

96a45502-4be5-4f32-bbdf-c4738ef4bf72.Text: "Are you aware of the changes Incendia has wrought on Footfall?"

b74ec2f3-9f59-420f-b431-419951bf6cdc.Text: "The Word Bearers went there themselves? They didn't just send in their puppets?"

520b9b01-a955-4086-8ea8-322e881a9c25.Text: "If you think she is unnecessarily brutal, why have you not intervened?"

e7558238-f061-4fb0-acd4-78a5c586f8d2.Text: "What do they want with Eufrates II?"

c00043bd-ec4b-46b0-aae2-85980216f3f3.Text: "I put an end to her dictatorship."

571b91b9-96cb-4761-bcba-5118deb02ab5.Text: "I helped Incendia to force the station into submission."

0c66a259-b006-4428-b7b2-9e6373f04d56.Text: "Did you even try to discuss it with him? Or did you immediately set Incendia on him?"

5d174256-8b6a-4956-a168-5fb477cd2214.Text: "I'm afraid I must decline. Deal with your problems yourself."

446afe09-0ba4-4380-9ab7-116b8fd53fc2.Text: [Point at the servant] "Is he your valet? Or another Inquisition assassin?"

3b805b8b-8892-428b-bb7e-36ff9abe3948.Text: "People disappearing in the vicinity of an Inquisitor is always cause for suspicion."

bd237216-a05b-4bce-ba53-1fdf5dd2c122.Text: "In my torment, I seek salvation from the corruption that has gripped my essence, eclipsing Your light from me."

326722f6-492a-4686-bc71-d75a11ff7d1d.Text: "Master of Mankind, my life belongs to You, for I am a blazing weapon of faith that will crush the heretic, the xenos, and the mutant who have raised a hand against Your kingdom."

e9360cdf-3204-49ac-8c37-15b364b79403.Text: "Are you going to leave me just like that, Ulfar? I saved you!"

4d5f7203-8f95-4db9-b312-1b86fd23907a.Text: "What makes you think you are capable of commanding the whole sector?"

1025b1f2-7f42-4954-8f9d-16e0ae0e0f1d.Text: "As if you are without transgression, Argenta."

aabca912-070a-413c-a30f-1ec23d00defa.Text: "Yrliet, I thought you and I had reached an understanding."

7b83ba3d-ef32-46c8-89aa-01ce5819213a.Text: "I have had enough of these absurd accusations. I am leaving."

875a2490-d379-4e96-9d86-2ff05a047815.Text: "Shame about that. We could have reached an agreement. I must take my leave."

ac5fde9f-a053-442b-b0de-33b321b24a0c.Text: [Bend your knee and drink from the flask]

499c26c7-23e0-4e28-9cae-4a33a6476256.Text: "Wait, I have changed my mind. I am not ready to part with my transgressions. They make me who I am."

89e8fe40-0cb4-486b-867e-b5c72ad95de1.Text: "You are displeased with ME? On what grounds? By what right?"

90e3d2e2-25f2-4639-84ac-c01fe7313bfa.Text: "What have you done to me? I— I'm dying!"

7159c824-c136-491b-ab97-be7d2fbb1834.Text: "Stop the rite! I prefer to own my guilt."

769dd04f-420b-4b74-a90f-f94c039699f9.Text: "What was it you said once? 'Threats are the recourse of the weak'? Thank you for illustrating the point."

2f17b6e1-2f4a-4d12-aefd-431e802d1c20.Text: [Repent sincerely] "You are right. The shadow of corruption has fallen on my soul. I want to banish that shadow with your help before it is too late."

34760258-e878-4c02-a9cd-7c3dc3077aa2.Text: "Touching. Write a poem about it, Wolf. Perhaps it will make you feel better."

c431e994-ecf2-419f-8975-42642f43aa46.Text: "Would you really find it in you to burn me after all we have been through together?"

e782c086-9d74-4e81-bab5-69119d27c6d2.Text: "You know, I have always found your sermons nauseating. My ears will be glad to be free of them."

a87c6c5b-d66d-4791-ad9e-9e344b31c2ec.Text: "What matter first brought you to Eufrates II, out of interest?"

acdc715a-f88b-476a-875d-518fb05ea21b.Text: "We may have our differences, but I shall miss your fervour."

c7f541dd-78fd-4ef6-af49-3512095d8f03.Text: "Complaining to daddy about the big, bad Rogue Trader? How predictable."

a9da2322-5579-4061-aafe-1545a1ea49f4.Text: "Watch all you like, Heinrix. For as long as the Inquisition still needs me, there is nothing you can do."

089237c5-ad89-4e58-ac83-10bc04ddeaad.Text: "I did not expect such an excess of scruples from an Interrogator of the Inquisition. You are elbow-deep in blood yourself."

131e2434-e275-4afd-afef-44f99db07a60.Text: "It is a shame that your kind did not die off entirely and spare the rest of us their arrogance."

a0c2bb8b-aa9a-445e-a4c3-73ac62cdcae7.Text: "You wished to speak to the Lord Inquisitor, Ulfar?"

0b28f995-a2fc-4923-85eb-09c203f10126.Text: "This is not who I thought you were. I am sorry for it."

9e656895-b823-4744-ba92-dcfcd4cca643.Text: "Fine, I will take the chance you have given me."

8d5de1cd-4fb8-4959-9a8d-4577d9c2eea2.Text: "One of your acolytes, Emelina, accused you of cooperating with xenos."

5ce746ed-0b71-4999-95d7-8554caa8a2e0.Text: "Wait, Heinrix, did the Lord Inquisitor not order you to accompany me?"

ae0c4707-9d6c-4961-9a55-2695d65e3e1c.Text: "How did you manage to enlist the aid of Angels of the Emperor?"

fee4432c-0d44-4d01-bfb3-6dc94b49de97.Text: "God-Emperor, our shepherd and warden, hear my sorrowful cry of remorse and humility."

00e363a2-2e4c-47c1-b4de-c6bca87b43f8.Text: "Why do you think he acted that way?"

b46fb027-8bc3-4640-9015-6ed102bcf9a9.Text: {n}The Lord Inquisitor is engrossed in studying star system charts and reports, which are amassed on the desk like the ridges of a formidable mountain range. There are shadows beneath his eyes, which are ruthlessly dissecting the latest report, and his skin seems stretched taut over the bones of his skull. Without turning his head to you, Calcazar says wearily,{/n} "Greetings, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Your timing is impeccable."

b6a229a8-a7db-4425-a36a-db24fa6e5ec4.Text: {n}Despite the lightning speed at which Froscher served your drink, he managed not to spill a drop. The taste of the recaf strikes you as a perfect match for the palace's new master — brutally strong and burning with a sharp hit of precious aromatic spices.{/n}

051e5117-eac2-434f-ba68-f7b2bb981521.Text: {n}An aged servant with the bearing of a veteran approaches the two of you. In a precise movement, he replaces the untouched cup of cold recaf in front of the Lord Inquisitor with a new one, slightly steaming.{/n}

62dc684f-c071-4210-82c1-9906994fd50c.Text: "I am afraid not. According to the information in my possession, they withdrew from the battle raging in the Expanse." {n}The Lord Inquisitor's deferential tone now carries a dry edge.{/n}

83bf616b-d012-4738-8824-9199b146d2a8.Text: "His Lordship deemed it more important to show off his stubbornness than to safeguard the interests of the Expanse. Stupidity of the most burdensome kind. But my sources inform me that he nevertheless has joined my efforts against the xenos, and so I have decided to stay any sanctions... for a time."

3767e224-397d-4ba1-b57f-d7c825979792.Text: "In my torment, I seek salvation from the corruption that has gripped my essence, eclipsing Your light from me."

61e3f9ef-8d9e-4f4b-b78a-41460e881dea.Text: "You will be given the details when you arrive in orbit around Eufrates II."

63c09eac-8045-4a60-a7f1-ea2f5592cf6a.Text: "His Lordship has long displayed a susceptibility to... corrupting ideas. His loss of interest in managing his protectorate and his appetite for violence drew my notice some time ago." {n}After a moment's hesitation, Calcazar adds,{/n} "The only question that remains unanswered is how many agents of the Archenemy have infiltrated his entourage."

46c69be3-7723-416f-ad89-7810a3427ac4.Text: "Sounds suspicious. This is not how we Wolves conduct ourselves..."

93fb38e0-6617-4a99-b0ef-318683644fd1.Text: {n}The corners of Calcazar's mouth creep upward. In a befittingly grave tone, he replies,{/n} "I would be loath to trouble our Master with a prayer for such an indulgence, especially one so utterly inappropriate at this fraught time."

88c86acd-e020-4554-8b38-6281c075cb8e.Text: "I value your directness — it will save us much time. Yes, there is something you must do — it is time for you to play your part to save the Koronus Expanse. I would not disturb your esteemed personage for anything less."

daa19429-f750-46d2-935b-39b09d0c59aa.Text: "I offer my apologies. I have been slightly preoccupied, attempting as I am to deal with a dozen uprisings and two dozen xeno-incursions, while also trying to convince the powers that be in the Expanse to unlock their jaws from around each other's throats long enough to listen to reason. Being familiar with your extravagant mode of communication, I thought it best to delay our meeting until a time when keeping my hands off a weapon would not be so great a trial."

347ac3af-de4e-4669-a133-ab8a50000cac.Text: {n}Calcazar's voice turns as dry as the reports on the table, and as sharp as the symbol of the Inquisition stamped upon them.{/n} "I would not wish you to make any assumptions, for you would be quite mistaken. I am but a servant of the Emperor — governing is beyond my purview."

64ed636a-87e6-42ff-a6e8-94a24898b0d6.Text: "I appreciate your willingness to dispense with ceremony and get right to the point."

657dd76c-84b9-42e4-ae02-d52e64349259.Text: {n}The Inquisitor raises an eyebrow, impressed.{/n} "You escaped from the Dark City? A feat that few have accomplished. Truly, I congratulate you on an exceptional performance, and I won't even mar your triumph by telling you that the Inquisition will, of course, be watching you very closely henceforth. I sincerely hope that your grand escape was not part of the xenos' devious machinations."

c603080a-f97c-41ae-87d0-740fb4c5b56d.Text: "Earlier than I planned, but that is all to the good. On behalf of the Inquisition, I hereby inform you that your action will not be considered an attack on the privileges of a Rogue Trader."

e409e591-a395-45b9-9189-13aeaa01516d.Text: "How curious. When all this is over, I will certainly call you as a witness at Calligos's trial. Together we will decide how best to handle him while ensuring the safety of the Expanse."

b12df619-8053-4f2a-9a3a-4d90cccb9b32.Text: "I am delighted to hear it. Since the two of you are now bound by allegiance, when all this is over, I will call upon you to carry out House Winterscale's punishment for its disobedience. I hope Calligos will be gratified to see a familiar face in his executioner."

a7f55fd6-983f-4111-b297-ccb60b9806b2.Text: "The Cult of the Final Dawn and Drukhari raiders are vying with each other to see who can cause us the greatest turmoil. I have mobilised all the forces I can to repel the attacks, which is why we are still alive. Combined militia brigades are hunting for xenos and guarding convoys, and expeditionary platoons under my command are crushing heretic rebellions. The situation is unstable, but... I will not pretend that I was prepared for this crisis. However, we have not lost our footing yet."

ea5c9cfe-cb2b-46e9-9fe9-eb8d1f4a10ac.Text: "Froscher, if you please." {n}The Inquisitor nods imperiously at the servant, who draws some kind of remote control from his pocket. All sounds whose sources are more than three metres away fade to nothing.{/n}

28ede6cc-5f98-4ba0-b88d-c0bdbb501d16.Text: "You have misconstrued me. It is I who intend to help you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I am displeased with you. You inherited a certain reputation from Theodora, and you have thoroughly tarnished that reputation. Under these difficult circumstances, a person in my position might decide that you ought to be killed before your actions become truly {d|Encyclopedia:Conviction_Heretical3OrMore}deleterious{/d}."

9b9f19b2-deae-47cc-a4d7-34d9f27a8c76.Text: "To my chagrin, the ability to be in two places at once does not number among my talents. That is why I wish for you to serve in my stead. I place such trust in very few people, you understand. You will feel what it is to walk in my shoes and attempt to compel a gaggle of quarrelsome blockheads to work together."

455357c5-65c9-4a6b-9a01-63f5ff683248.Text: {n}The Inquisitor sighs heavily.{/n} "What can I say? Few among the Emperor's servants are without guilt. Forcing heartfelt repentance out of any of them is more than even I can do. As for you, I have already told you the price of my lenience. Eufrates II."

bbc1f1fe-0ec8-4216-a80d-b66b3858b7fe.Text: "You will reconquer Eufrates II for me." {n}The Inquisitor gestures to the servant and the silencing field disperses.{/n} "Froscher, another recaf — this one has gone cold."

5c4bfb75-2423-407f-a38e-3e2f26e65bc6.Text: "Prisoner interrogations indicate that an incident occurred in the Dark City, what the xenos call a {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_DaemonicBreach}dysjunction{/d}. A dimensional calamity that forced them to step up their raids in realspace. Their audacity speaks to their desperation, which in turn will translate into new trials for His servants."

8ac593a0-4393-4946-9e37-7022e238437f.Text: "The warp is raging. This baleful sign always portends change, and crises beget desperation — the most fertile ground for heresy. I believe the Archenemy's servants think their time has come. Or perhaps this day was marked in their profane scripture as the date of the end of existence. I will not trouble myself with further attempts to make sense of their blasphemous doctrine. They are bent on destroying us all, and so they must be destroyed."

91c604fe-1c1e-4431-a429-677e28409904.Text: "Prisoner interrogations indicate that a relatively major political upheaval has taken place in Commorragh. The Kabal of the Reaving Tempest has lost its grip on authority and become a target for enemies and rivals. Many vassals and members of the Kabal decided that fleeing to realspace was preferable to waiting in Commorragh to be killed."

e6fe3820-101d-417e-9a94-21d077a4b467.Text: "Are you not standing before me now? While your... status remained unclear, I preferred not to requisition the resources of the von Valancius protectorate. Your people dealt with Uralon the Cruel's agents and with xenos raids, and that was enough for me. But now is the time to add your might and talents to the scales."

bd90d1f6-f73a-4fa9-ac9e-ab6643a1e7b1.Text: {n}The glance tossed at you is like a shot from an autopistol at point-blank range.{/n} "If such a plan were to exist, information about it would be of the utmost secrecy. I suggest you focus on the current strategy of putting out each fire as you encounter it."

3ad52500-8f4e-4604-8f38-60b504ad2111.Text: "I see no need to get bogged down in the details. To apprise you of all the information I currently possess would require... more time than we have."

9a8aa751-4a81-4c34-85ff-db99f5159f8e.Text: "Naturally. Her Ladyship has done me an invaluable service by taking on the task of instilling order on the station. Though her style of leadership seems unnecessarily brutal to me, on the whole her actions have not exceeded the bounds I set."

1997fb9c-474c-46b6-9e44-4bddbbef5a01.Text: "Clearly, the stakes for them are high enough. Uralon the Cruel has stirred his profane self to make a personal appearance on Eufrates II. Kunrad Voigtvir, incidentally, is also there — I hear you two have unfinished business. Him I will generously leave to you. When you are finished with him, you may simply dispose of his mortal remains — no need to surrender them to the Inquisition for an inquest. Consider it my gift."

13441bcf-4fb1-4fb6-80b4-0066cdc5dd56.Text: "Firstly, I entrusted the task to Her Ladyship, and she is executing it competently. And secondly... {name}, are you unaware of what I am striving to do here? At present, I am trying to prevent the deaths of billions, yet you ask me why I am choosing not to save hundreds."

f656c322-7aa7-46b0-96f7-866fbfca680e.Text: "Yet I am surprised that this xenos is still alive. What is it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? Sentimentality? Revenge? Cold calculation?" {n}Calcazar gives Yrliet a long, significant look.{/n} "If you do not finish her off yourself, send word when you have tired of her. My acolytes will be only too eager to learn her secrets."

bf79cec7-57b0-4e7a-8011-63b5318ba4c9.Text: {n}Clenching her jaw to the point of pain, Yrliet hisses Aeldari curses under her breath, but retreats half a step.{/n} "I have looked into the eyes of death... and of creatures far more dangerous than you, mon-keigh. Do not try to frighten me."

aaee2c7e-c55e-452e-863f-c95b735fd40e.Text: "A death cultist and the Rogue Trader's personal bodyguard." {n}The Lord Inquisitor gazes at Kibellah intently.{/n} "I am curious: do you still adhere firmly to your cult's dogma, or has your loyalty to your {mf|master|mistress} outgrown your faith?"

5e09c45d-bd11-4a42-a051-a5289921d158.Text: "My loyalty to the Domin stems from the Undying One's will. Such is the thread of this blade, until His whisper bids it to spin a different one," {n}Kibellah responds with calm assurance.{/n}

ab2f7f4f-778b-4eea-90be-2e09d1aa9ba9.Text: {n}Solomorne's face, already difficult to read, now becomes an impenetrable mask.{/n} "Only the Marshal can speak for all the Arbites in the Expanse. But for myself as a Proctor, I swear that I wholly serve the Lex Imperialis."

59a12a8a-c9ea-49d9-9c50-a64da97ffb26.Text: "I heard the Adeptus Arbites had renewed their alliance with the von Valancius dynasty. One would not get far without it in a sector ruled by Rogue Traders, I imagine. However, under such circumstances, and considering all the rights granted by the sacred Warrant, you may struggle to distinguish whether you are indeed serving the Lex or, in fact, a particular person."

a7f96e7b-1d32-48e3-b7a2-db6320ce2a47.Text: {n}Calcazar bows respectfully.{/n} "Glory to the Emperor's Angels of Fenris. Your words will be heeded, my lord."

e8ad0e5e-4d5c-4eb7-929f-08e3ea91ebca.Text: {n}The Inquisitor's jaw hardens.{/n} "Despite the impression I may have created, I am not a schoolmaster obliged to rein in misbehaving Rogue Traders. Calligos rejected the call to fulfil his duty to the Emperor. What discussion was there to be had?"

0015c79b-cff6-46c4-87a7-fc64d5bb30cd.Text: "I never doubted you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The Emperor protects."

7178f291-7ea3-4e70-86e7-2c3c46dad4be.Text: {n}The Lord Inquisitor replies in a soft, arid voice,{/n} "But it is not a request. It is a command. And I am far past the point of humouring your pride and vanity."

5a8d91de-3106-473a-becb-705e561d0081.Text: "Why can't both be true? Froscher has been a member of my retinue for fifty Terran years and the person in my entourage who comes closest to being my confidant." {n}Something akin to a warm smile touches the Inquisitor's lips.{/n} "We have had cause to be involved in many incidents whose reports have since been marked with a seal of silence."

3b3044e8-a7d5-4561-9d0f-07aaff5336f1.Text: "I am surprised you managed such a feat. However, it is probably for the best — I assumed the two of you would clash, but I expected a more tragic outcome. I admire your zeal for peacekeeping."

968266ca-5243-4147-a750-ea51a4f7b326.Text: {n}The grey-haired servant's eyes burn with vicious indignation, like an executioner's pyre lit by a fanatic.{/n}

d350c35e-a001-47cc-be1b-4730142b3d2a.Text: "Indeed. You petitioned our aid in fighting xenos. We spilt much alien blood. But the wind of battle carried me far, and I lost contact with my pack. Do you know where I can seek out my brothers, the Baleful Howl?"

ac8469e3-8c50-42ff-80ca-d5c12d3aa146.Text: {n}Calcazar nods at the paper that his servant has deferentially delivered to the table.{/n} "This document attests to the extraordinary powers you now have at your disposal. I am counting on your success, {name}."

47f735dd-23cb-4009-bced-a2a0597cc3b2.Text: "Do you see a better candidate for the job?" {n}The Lord Inquisitor closes his eyes wearily for a moment.{/n} "I may no longer be in the first flush of youth, but believe me when I say that there are many things I would much rather be doing than playing constable to the Koronus Expanse. But, alas, every ruler in our sector chooses to confine their concern to the well-being of their own holdings, whereas I alone must take care of all."

86cff3ff-b768-4f6f-a2d1-469897f3be30.Text: "We will both tire before I finish reciting the list of all your transgressions. You are not here to test my knowledge, so let us just agree that you have already more than earned your sentence. Have I expressed myself in terms basic enough for you to understand?"

7c30d3a8-a498-48fd-a1b0-7b9c72fe9b21.Text: "I sent my troops to aid the Explorator forces laying siege to the world, but a... rift occurred among the commanders. They need an authoritative general, and you are perfect for the role. My confidence is not misplaced, I trust?"

09db26a5-88d8-4a7c-801b-1e21d016a9ee.Text: "Unfortunately, the leaders have failed to find a common language. The esteemed Thorbald is at odds with the conclave of the Mechanicus's battle congregation, and the Omnissiah's servants find Thorbald's strident nature off-putting. And neither group is fond of Militant Sibilek, who commands my forces... Were not fond, to be precise. The esteemed Militant perished along with his ship a week ago when his noble allies failed to support his offensive."

2c63f434-9bbe-46f6-bd38-d7ae2dec43f8.Text: "But instead, I am giving you a chance to redeem yourself. To serve me and therefore the Imperium, to demonstrate your extraordinary talents, and to dispel the doubts surrounding you... at least partly. This is a most generous and rare opportunity. Do not squander it."

010abfb0-b228-46a3-b879-f6aee84d8ba0.Text: "You lie. The Baleful Howl never run from battle." {n}Ulfar's reply to the outrageous claim is surprisingly calm. Only the frosty chill of death born of his voice and carried across the room makes everyone's hair stand on end.{/n}

e9a875ff-dbcb-4073-b029-298232d4c938.Text: "Contrary to my request to continue hunting the xenos, they embarked on an expedition whose objective is unknown to me. There has been no word of them since."

35f1ce0a-e096-4ccf-81cc-d9e29df82dfe.Text: "No, but I believe I know someone who is better informed. And I will name that person as soon as we finally start discussing the matter that prompted me to summon Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship."

f8df41d3-e09d-44f3-bc7d-7992ecb7b0a6.Text: "By the right, it seems, of the sole person in this sector who still remembers his duty to the Emperor! And on the grounds of your numerous grubby little deeds, of which I have full knowledge!" {n}The Lord Inquisitor's voice snaps out like a weapon bolt. Pressing his lips into a hard line, in a harried and vexed tone, he says,{/n} "I have no time for games, von Valancius."

377e8a32-3149-4c08-9c8d-27421e4a3e42.Text: "If this is some scheme of yours—"

f25987ba-2c25-41ea-afcd-0fe78f2e20b7.Text: "To whom else could I entrust this mission? No need to feign ignorance, von Valancius — we both know the... shortcomings of the other candidates for this position. At present in the Expanse, there are two people with the perspective and steady hand required to control this situation — and they are both standing in this room. So, if you will, dispense with the humble Rogue Trader act and win this war for me."

b8c4757d-07cf-4a70-b092-282ff7b20de7.Text: {n}The warrior of Fenris folds his arms on his ceramite-plated chest regally, and says in a dour voice,{/n} "Greetings, Inquisitor. You and I need to talk."

e04439e1-a801-4c7f-b88d-1b28699262b1.Text: {n}The Inquisitor dryly interrupts the Allfather's warrior:{/n} "Dare I remind you that your presence in the Expanse is not a favour to me, but the promised repayment of a debt? I was not so haughty when I returned your... lost brother... to Fenris. I did not demand recompense for my faithful servants who died saving him. I kept secret those details that could have damaged your honour. Why, then, does your gratitude taste so poisonous?"

1a1aaed6-279b-4e60-870e-9b98b3b6fad3.Text: "A sacred world of the Adeptus Mechanicus, off limits to laypeople. I am one of the few who do not worship the Omnissiah to have set foot on its surface... Or rather, I was. Now it is crawling with unbelievers — the despicable Word Bearers attacked and captured Eufrates II, and the Cult of the Final Dawn brought an entire horde of heretics to the planet."

0554adfe-bd01-49ff-a9f3-8683bead9610.Text: {n}The mention of Ulfar's lost brother makes him grind his teeth in anger before he falls sullenly silent.{/n}

e26d2493-c408-41cc-a087-2f2a80dc9123.Text: "I presumed it was to search for Brother Ulfar. It is common knowledge how deeply Space Wolves value the ties of brotherhood... Far more deeply than the ties that bind them to other subjects of the Emperor."

1d22113c-f1f7-4e6d-9d15-ebc826c88a26.Text: "An utterly transparent attempt to learn secret intelligence. I offer to make you my general, and you try to pump me for information? Poorly done."

fd8efb46-0e0d-4b6c-818f-61ef7a13d366.Text: {n}The Inquisitor bows to Ulfar curtly.{/n} "I recommend that you, too, go to Eufrates II, my lord. Perhaps your pack was less reticent with the esteemed Thorbald than with me, and told him where they decided to direct their efforts."

6004e0eb-78f9-4b50-ba4c-7b54814cb27d.Text: "It is a fine suggestion, which I accept gratefully, Inquisitor." {n}The expression of respect on Ulfar's face does a poor job of hiding his antipathy.{/n}

5a1e7e5d-f8d4-45f9-8ae4-b38e0c165e04.Text: "I can tell you no more. As you well know, your pack preferred not to report their plans and intentions to me." {n}Albeit no match for Ulfar's tongue of ice, the coldness in Calcazar's voice, too, could freeze an entire world.{/n}

7488c06d-27ad-4c8f-95a4-c86ff66cf64b.Text: "Are you confessing your transgressions before the Lord Inquisitor and seeking to repent? That is brave. As I said, all you have to do to redeem yourself is to take Eufrates II. But if you truly do repent of your deeds and seek to wash away the stain they have left upon your soul, I can perform a rite of purification. Bend your knee and drink this." {n}The Lord Inquisitor holds out a flask to you.{/n} "All of it."

b57e9175-c79a-46c3-a036-675c069587f3.Text: {n}There is nothing special about the taste. It is water, cool and pure. Whatever effect it was supposed to have on you, you do not feel it.{/n}

18996551-319c-4462-baa9-fa3d19d96cd2.Text: {n}The Lord Inquisitor does not appear aggrieved at the news.{/n} "As I understand, this was a private confrontation between two Rogue Traders, yes? As such, I hope your house will reach a reconciliation with Her Ladyship's heir. You have not hindered my plans — Lady Incendia purged Footfall sufficiently that I was not distracted by the need to pacify it."

ea3309cf-8e8f-43a9-9e6e-42517f469d74.Text: {n}The Inquisitor nods.{/n} "Now get ready and repeat after me. The rite must be completed to take effect." {n}As he says this, he grips your shoulder firmly with one hand and reaches for his sheathed dagger with the other. He touches your forehead with the tip of its blade.{/n} "God-Emperor, our shepherd and warden, hear my sorrowful cry of remorse and humility."

54e89bf7-c2d5-4f69-beb6-26b7d5cb86e3.Text: {n}As soon as you finish the sentence, the Inquisitor presses down on the blade and carves some symbols into your forehead. You instantly feel agony spread through your body — as though the water you drank has turned into a holy fire that is burning out the roots of corruption in your soul, one by one.{/n}

8d052a0c-6e47-4c59-93f6-c0c0b8374661.Text: {n}The dagger draws more symbols on your forehead with strokes of incandescent pain. Your blood is boiling lead. Your nerves are poisoned wires. Your every breath shreds your throat like a hundred razor blades.{/n}

984833a1-fd47-4e6e-a101-e1e3c906e9fb.Text: {n}The Inquisitor's flat voice seems to be coming from a different reality:{/n} "Master of Mankind, my life belongs to You, for I am a blazing weapon of faith that will crush the heretic, the xenos, and the mutant who have raised a hand against Your kingdom."

611c31dd-6633-4f6c-b083-88096a7287c7.Text: {n}The final symbols bite into your flesh, and just as you feel your body has reached the limit of what it can take, the pain subsides. A warm wave of grace rolls over you, washing away the last of your transgressions. You run your fingers over your forehead and realise there is not a scratch on it.{/n}

7498425c-e85f-48bc-a848-a1de3f54a53b.Text: "Rise. The rite of purification is complete. Now go forth and carry His light within you, and let your actions prove your loyalty to the Emperor. Eufrates II awaits you, {name}."

f4bb5054-538e-4b48-9302-506ffbd98bbb.Text: "I warned you, Rogue Trader. You reek of corruption from head to toe. Even an honourable death will not wash away the stench. The Inquisitor is free to absolve you of whatever he likes, but for me, being part of your warband is a disgrace. Farewell." {n}Ulfar spits and stares past you contemptuously.{/n}

305f2065-2e50-4b9c-a692-3fa03d71cb8d.Text: "You have carried Theodora's unholy legacy, {name}, and you have surpassed her a hundredfold in unholiness. How regrettable. Farewell, and pray to the Emperor that you will find redemption before I have to grant you His Peace. For heretics—" {n}Argenta pauses. The fire in her eyes could incinerate you.{/n} "—deserve no quarter."

76fd3538-038f-4ceb-933c-b772d5122313.Text: "This is where we part ways, {name}. I have seen enough, and I no longer wish to be an accomplice to your crimes. Although the Lord Inquisitor was generous enough to look past your transgressions, I have no doubt that we will meet again in circumstances you will find less auspicious than these."

569dfae4-eee9-4117-b0dd-024fc1b4c09c.Text: "Enough words, elantach. You have brushed my warning aside, and now there is no saving your soul from corruption any longer. If I remained at your side, I would risk forever falling into the embrace of She Who Thirsts. Our ways part here. Farewell, and you would be wise not to seek another meeting with me."

0c6940ea-765d-4cd7-999f-9749d1a609de.Text: "I am pleased to see that Rogue Traders can indeed work together. This serves as proof that you are a worthy candidate for the mission that I am about to give you."

b557501d-9133-45e0-ab75-3595b665edc2.Text: {n}The Inquisitor's fingers tighten their steely grip on your shoulder.{/n} "On the contrary. You are being reborn. Repeat the prayer, {name}."

d9bcd4a2-7279-4f11-ab6f-c61d4abce60e.Text: {n}He lets go of your shoulder and removes the dagger from your forehead. The pain is gone at once. Several deep cuts on your brow are the only reminder of the rite.{/n}

dad9ac52-ff6e-475b-a507-41bc262193f9.Text: {n}Heinrix clears his throat.{/n} "I submitted a comprehensive report on my time in your retinue to Lord Calcazar. It contained a wealth of... interesting details. I supplemented it with a formal request to return to the Lord Inquisitor's side, which he immediately approved. But don't worry. The unsleeping eye of the Inquisition will continue to watch your every step."

739b9c92-ba31-4bbf-8bec-5e86d5e5360a.Text: "Back then, I did not know who I was throwing in my lot with. If I had, I would have denied you the honour of fighting shoulder-to-shoulder with me. It does not befit a warrior of the Allfather to follow the orders of one whose name is tainted. Speak no more, for a craving to exact justice is brewing in my heart."

436b443e-fabd-43a8-893d-7b3f97c32541.Text: "There is a difference between 'not without transgression' and 'steeped in heresy,' {name}. The former can be atoned for by righteous deeds and service. The latter can only be burned away by cleansing fire."

02d631fa-9645-4b2f-9e44-b61191b911e3.Text: "Without a moment's hesitation. I gave you a chance to return to the path of righteousness, but you rejected it. I have sworn to eradicate corruption. If you have succumbed to it, then I will do my duty no matter what it takes."

a5f9cbe0-264b-4586-be1d-914993c3fdc1.Text: "What are you talking about, mon-keigh? You are as far from understanding my soul as the light of the faded cold stars is far from your wretched worlds. You are enthusiastically opening yourself to the evil that destroyed my people at the dawn of time. Understanding? No. All I have for you is pity."

fddd1ee7-957a-4bfc-bb54-277e4179bf37.Text: {n}Argenta grinds her teeth and tightens her grip on the weapon in her hands.{/n} "Burn in the abyss, {name}."

2a8dab40-9652-4186-9d67-e57eb148cf43.Text: {n}Argenta merely looks away, her eyes grim.{/n}

57767485-c3ba-4396-97ff-3db196ad1055.Text: {n}Ulfar scowls ominously.{/n} "Pray that my next verse is not about an arrogant Rogue Trader who got {mf|his|her} comeuppance. You wouldn't like it."

5e15a0d3-ea3d-4928-90a1-1a2cbe8ccb5a.Text: "The reasons behind their machinations would be pure speculation at this point. Bring me prisoners to interrogate and perhaps we will gain some much needed insight."

30b612a2-2ef7-4093-9574-401b3413e298.Text: "Prejudice? A fine thing to call my faith in the Allfather. I warned you, {name}. You have made your choice."

7df3ac57-e5ca-4d7f-bdb1-30cb107749fa.Text: {n}The Space Marine lets out a guttural growl as his face contorts in a beastlike expression.{/n} "I will forgive you this one brazen insult, Rogue Trader. Do not utter another."

cf4c226e-d602-4408-ba68-11a5060700e3.Text: "If you want to rile me, try harder. I've heard worse taunts. They were usually the last words of a heretic."

7a63431f-f722-49fa-8fd4-c4b761e78f45.Text: "'Still' being the operative word, {name}. Don't overestimate your usefulness."

0636b8ef-06ab-4588-8b4e-212af723443d.Text: "Mostly the blood of heretics, xenos, and traitors, {name}. The Inquisition's methods aren't always decorous and often require great sacrifices. But I am loyal to the Imperium. Keeping it safe at any cost is my highest priority. And that includes keeping it safe from the likes of you."

1277c5f4-f788-4ab1-9f71-2c1fc901d98b.Text: "Save your regret for the fate that awaits you, mon-keigh."

7671431b-99d7-4321-a615-ea09ad853ee4.Text: {n}There is no spite in the look Yrliet gives you in response — only coldness and detachment. She no longer deigns to answer you, for talking to a mon-keigh is a pointless waste of an Asuryani's time.{/n}

e366ca99-43aa-49d3-9cd2-2de8dac1de34.Text: "My Path of the Outcast has taught me to trust no one, mon-keigh. And you have reinforced my belief that trying to find common ground with your species was an exercise in futility."

200a275c-f024-4a75-8319-8e9571190e3c.Text: {n}Calcazar, who has been observing the unfolding scene in silence, takes a slow sip from his cup.{/n} "Well then. I hope a diminished retinue will be no obstacle to doing your duty, {name}. Dismissed."

50ebc969-0929-42e5-94c7-af388fce6cf9.Text: "Explorator Fleet Divine Cognisance 78-21 recalled its most combat-ready units to retake the world. They were supported by my most powerful strike fleet and a group of... deadlier allies. I dispatched a pack of Space Wolves to hunt down the transgressors."

a155aad3-2c39-479e-bc98-67cf0f7443dc.Text: {n}Heinrix nods silently at Calcazar, who responds by ever so slightly bowing his head.{/n}

50e67836-7a74-4e87-a0a9-51e4689f730f.Text: {n}Calcazar gives your retinue a cursory glance until his gaze rests on Marazhai.{/n} "Incendia has allowed a xenos of the most dangerous variety to roam freely on Footfall. The esteemed Lady Chorda has a frankly surprising amount of respect for the privileges bestowed by your Warrant."

99974f1f-f7d0-43dc-a22e-6adbdee2eddc.Text: "I rather think the mon-keigh fears what may befall her should she try to get rid of me." {n}The Drukhari stares baldly at Calcazar with no deference whatsoever. Perhaps he has no inkling of who he is talking to.{/n}

2bb248af-d607-4a36-8b3d-e3771548bd26.Text: "Rest assured that His Lordship will face the consequences of his actions."

9c1a620e-22a4-44fa-888d-9b44b9e53a00.Text: {n}In response to Calcazar's question, Heinrix's eyes narrow, smouldering with anger.{/n} "Emelina is dead. By my hand."

69cf96e4-07fc-4b84-ac6f-0c5c0fda2ef3.Text: "Indeed? Well, I hope I can continue to trust you to know when a useful resource is finally exhausted and must be disposed of."

a9a4110b-d45e-41b0-b0f1-179e542cfd96.Text: {n}Marazhai tilts his head slightly to the side, eyeing Calcazar appraisingly. However, the Drukhari is in no hurry to speak his thoughts aloud.{/n}

7bd7d462-70d5-40c0-8e06-f50437ba8f0a.Text: {n}Marazhai's mocking gaze rests on you.{/n} "An entirely unpredictable turn of events... Isn't that right, {name}?"

a711235b-7511-47c6-b2d0-c9b34ca71e7d.Text: {n}Yrliet sighs raggedly. Her voice is scarcely above a whisper:{/n} "And so your quest for revenge has brought forth a new era of suffering for mon-keigh, elantach. Are you satisfied?"

99718c71-628d-46d8-bf4b-0a052ade1144.Text: "I would remind you that the particularities of the Inquisition's work lie far beyond a Rogue Trader's purview, but, given the circumstances... Yes, Acolyte Lichtenhart's words are true. It has been several years since I established contact with the Drukhari. They informed me of upcoming raids, and I thwarted them. I kept the Expanse safe while the xenos were absorbed in their internal squabbles, which are of little interest to me."

70b29748-b75f-491f-82d2-d23133d879fb.Text: "I must remind you that I am still Lord Inquisitor of the Koronus Expanse, not merely some — what do you always say, Froscher? — some 'grox-bothering prick.' If certain Rogue Traders at times allow themselves to speak to me in an overly... wilful manner, that should not give you cause to doubt my authority."

18d2c34e-1be9-44b8-a21f-271aa12a290c.Text: "Intriguing news about the fate of my Kabal. More so than expected."

6dba230c-21bd-4818-afdd-4683f754702f.Text: {n}Idira shrinks under Calcazar's gaze and seems to try to sidle behind you, but the Lord Inquisitor does not even deign to address the psyker with a remark.{/n}

870d3b86-007c-4718-afac-9cfc142d9563.Text: {n}Calcazar notices Argenta and inclines his head with a dignified air.{/n} "Sister."

1b27de6c-b792-42d1-b235-577ea933c8a8.Text: "Heinrix, I have to say I am disappointed by how easily information pertaining to the Expanse's security reaches the ears of those who should not be privy to it. This will be noted in your record. Would you care to put my concerns to rest and tell me that Emelina is not out there running amok around my sector and continuing to sow unrest?"

ebea58ca-60d9-4709-a9b9-030f0ce10ca3.Text: "I regret incurring your disapproval, Lord Inquisitor. I will learn from this mistake. Emelina... no longer poses a threat. I have seen to it."

04769cd6-d826-43cc-bcb1-842abf27d594.Text: "Strictly speaking, one might regard my actions in this situation as unorthodox at the very least. In reality, however, they are undoubtedly beneficial. Acolyte Lichtenhart has demonstrated her inability to surmount the bounds of convention, and had she been in my position, the Expanse would have likely already fallen under the blows of the present crisis. Fortunately for you, she is not, and the Drukhari, drained by their power struggles and bereft of their best raiders, can do nothing more than run from my fleets."

cdafc9d6-cfad-4c7c-80c3-9f3a4ae80223.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I hope it goes without saying that I would appreciate you not spreading dangerous and misleading rumours going forward — and keeping the content of this conversation private. Given the current state of affairs, I would have to treat such actions as subversive, so I thank you in advance for your considerate silence."

0cef724a-0848-45fc-9703-18757df04a3a.Text: "Much obliged, Interrogator. In the future, try to refrain from involving third parties in our conclave's internal matters."

b41027a0-316a-4436-b143-e88d8c46418a.Text: {n}The Battle Sister's eyes gleam as the Lord Inquisitor addresses her.{/n} "May your path be blessed! It is gratifying to see that the trials endured by the Expanse have failed to extinguish the flame of your fortitude!"

9e035a0a-2a62-44e4-b96c-0fa66c7957f2.Text: {n}Pasqal jerks his head up, clearly recognising the name Calcazar just uttered.{/n}

09e7d297-5fa0-4d62-b8c2-7b7b84e8362d.Text: "May the Emperor's mercy ensure that you never have cause to experience the hospitality of the Inquisition. Froscher, see to our guest." {n}Calcazar's voice seems to endow the servant with a phenomenal ability to move instantly through space — a cup of recaf appears in front of you before the sound of the Lord Inquisitor's voice dies away.{/n}

73c48aab-6e3f-490d-a539-aba4afbdd539.Text: {n}Abelard stifles a grunt of displeasure, his mutter pitched for your ears only:{/n} "'You will reconquer Eufrates II for me'... The esteemed Lord Inquisitor has done away with all pretence and politeness now. His orders no longer come with even the veneer of a request..."

b47aab47-a469-483c-b822-606e4a6c7ca1.Text: {n}Abelard belatedly raises his hand as if trying to stop you.{/n}

df36015b-07f3-447d-a79b-d7c4c3d22e57.Text: {n}A venomous chuckle escapes Marazhai's lips. He is looking between you and Calcazar with great interest.{/n}

83f63a39-7f01-4635-ade6-9b672c41621a.Text: "Registering a Sanctity Alpha priority mission. The scourge of corrupted misbelievers reigning over blessed workshops fills the Omnissiah's faithful with anguish. Activating autoasceticism protocol: I offer a prayer for the liberation of the sacred world." {n}From beneath Pasqal's crimson robe comes the sound of mechanisms whirring to life, and dark bloodstains streak across the fabric.{/n}

eb909685-ec10-434c-a7d1-c4b949026fca.Text: "Lady Navigator Cassia Tisiphia Evriaella." {n}The Lord Inquisitor's lips curve into a thin smile as he catches a glimpse of scarlet eyes.{/n} "I hear that House Orsellio is going through a difficult time: change is coming. I sincerely hope it is for the better."

1a65743c-9202-48d1-b4e9-dc3918a55205.Text: "Your colours, Lord Inquisitor, are as rich as they are multifaceted. I have never encountered anything like it before — unclouded hues flowing from one to the next... Amazing harmony. Amazing and... frightening." {n}Cassia raises her chin and nods demurely.{/n} "That a man of such status and talents has taken an interest in the well-being of a Navis Nobilite House is a great honour."

24ddf872-ba84-4712-aacd-2b2c61ace636.Text: {n}Jae touches the Aquila on her chest and drops her head in an unnecessarily deep bow.{/n} "O Lord Inquisitor, smiting spear of the Imperium, with the gold of faith cutting through the nebulae of the Koronus Exp—"

da1d1bec-29d2-48fc-9b60-a0cd70a3d37d.Text: {n}Calcazar raises a hand in warning.{/n} "If I were you, Mistress Heydari, I would endeavour not to draw the Inquisition's attention to my person."

3cdbf2b5-f6d4-4215-bc9c-2cc914669e82.Text: "A Mercatum Tabula Officiale can do many things. Reattaching a head to a body is not one of them."

65682229-dc16-4459-8ec1-21a9ebf72dc6.Text: {n}Froscher nods deferentially, and on his aged, jowled face appears an expression caught between eternal loyalty, motherly affection, and religious devotion.{/n}

bc2b5e3d-b13e-48ee-bf28-63c5e1928466.Text: "What makes Calcazar think he can summon me like some lackey?"

d819649b-4073-432f-af55-f279d50094d5.Text: "I shall visit the Lord Inquisitor as soon as I can."

4bef5de0-b437-43af-84dd-2bfe4e07f83d.Text: "Calcazar will have to wait. I have urgent matters to attend to."

d226c459-e95f-4aba-b6d8-7880d3a76bc9.Text: {n}The elderly man in front of you is moving with the noiselessness of an experienced servant. He bows primly and says, in a raspy voice,{/n} "The Lord Inquisitor bade me inform you that it will be his pleasure to see Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship at his palace. There are matters of the utmost urgency that he wishes to discuss, and he hopes you will find the time to meet with him in the near future."

4c44e939-1e66-4dbc-8d4e-df1fe932121f.Text: "My name is Froscher, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. I have the honour of being the Lord Inquisitor's retainer." {n}The man is unarmed and wearing no Inquisition insignia, but the military sharpness of his upright posture suggests he is a servant who doubles as a bodyguard.{/n}

420b8b64-3bdc-4a5c-b3a3-3f155ebebf3a.Text: "I will pass on the good news to the Lord Inquisitor." {n}The man bows respectfully again.{/n}

6ccb99ca-e1e2-4b14-97b1-52d8cb83f44c.Text: {n}The servant's face twists a little, but his voice remains perfectly flat and polite.{/n} "I will pass on your reply to the Lord Inquisitor. I dare not intrude upon Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship's time any longer."

5950498d-d28b-45a7-b5bb-6d0e48f6e966.Text: "Your handling of Footfall has been overly harsh, Incendia. You share the blame for their rebellion."

da6ddb48-9f9d-4794-98d3-3fe47dddb43c.Text: "He betrayed you, so you should be his judge."

717bd616-047d-4b9a-909f-48ed70fb48e4.Text: "Vladaym, do you have anything to say in your defence?"

73cecabc-324d-4411-a435-79d6b53864b6.Text: "I would suggest a show of mercy. We have demonstrated our power. They will not dare rebel again."

465c4167-b673-41f9-8bca-872a1671bddb.Text: "Most interesting. I hope you are creative in your punishments, Incendia!"

a7e67d68-a57c-4b0d-812a-bbb6e3e57e4c.Text: Defended Reverend Hieronymus at Incendia's trial.

50ff7116-aeb1-4280-8c53-9bbb79f43df3.Text: "He was trying to prevent a new Aspyce from coming into this world."

1f3b99bb-a5c6-42f5-881c-d60881c3f8c6.Text: "I have an excellent unholy man for your consideration. His name is Hieronymus Doloroso."

284d36b4-a8a4-44ad-a9ce-e19d2a7adfd3.Text: [Point to Ryzza] "She must face the tribunal."

3fde4ffd-24dc-49b1-ad01-bdcb8c451272.Text: [Kill Vladaym] "Don't bother thanking me. I'll just take what is mine."

4b12de10-4464-463d-91ec-0a4ef131e022.Text: "Hieronymus lied to you. It was he who condemned you to years of torture in a cryo-vault. He turned you into his loyal personal executioner."

b44b30e7-f646-442c-976e-dbced7875d49.Text: "We are at war. We have no right to squander fighters."

e89de7d5-7fcf-4ee7-9666-b3b6745ac654.Text: "There is not a single reason. He deserves to die."

773dc2a0-ee15-4c28-bbf1-7b3876a728c8.Text: "He sabotaged your cryo-vault, condemning you to suffer, and killed off your relatives."

c4f8eb8c-6de8-4a2c-af1d-ee48675afb8b.Text: "Never mind. It was just a joke... And not a good one."

d3e59a0b-63e5-49d5-aa49-158edfa38ddb.Text: [Smile acerbically] "Let us dispose of him as he disposed of people — let us throw him for a loop."

12716160-ab06-45ba-a859-3a0ecb5d88f1.Text: "Hieronymus, tell us why you betrayed her."

f1c9d027-1b93-49b6-8e75-a0a97d93fab2.Text: "Do you see now that you were manipulated? Filled with hatred and unleashed on people?"

4aa23ad6-657d-43f4-8599-fde79dbfe3ab.Text: "What do you have to say in your defence?"

d2924741-27a9-4766-8b76-3562287fb8cd.Text: "The verdict will be lenient. Incendia Chorda, I banish you from Footfall. Depart."

c5ccfa7e-2975-4eb8-bc34-54f71b999c23.Text: "Hieronymus may have betrayed you, but he was driven by faith."

05588894-4635-4e58-9e4b-46e242fefd5e.Text: "Well, are you going to string him up as a traitor, Incendia?"

4351869a-681c-4d29-a492-fd0abd0333fc.Text: Executed Reverend Hieronymus at Incendia's trial.

fb7b80cb-e129-4236-a7dd-a4f4b675c82b.Text: [Kill Hieronymus] "As a favour to you, sister Incendia, I shall deal with this myself."

c391294a-d483-41e9-b560-a205ed4c8180.Text: Demanded that Reverend Hieronymus be assigned penance at Incendia's trial.

e6284960-c633-45f7-894b-f165e4196c0e.Text: "Hieronymus deserves a harsh penance, but not an execution. Give him a different punishment."

12c781c0-cf3f-47fc-acc4-68ca0cb36167.Text: "I do not want Chorda's enforcers to face any reprisals. Let them leave."

3a97d625-b634-41d7-a1f7-3e44b39401c7.Text: "Do you realise that the way Footfall is governed must change?"

6c8a522c-f971-4b56-bb85-c5703c627813.Text: "You probably won't believe it, Incendia, but none of this is what you think it is. I—"

cda82d3a-4776-46a7-b7b1-0acf47a71699.Text: "On that, we can conclude the trial."

65f761fd-b54e-4175-9a91-330705b12d7e.Text: Accused Incendia of hypocrisy and demanded that Reverend Hieronymus be brought to justice.

25985680-8ffd-44c4-8a38-4e1bbe07c916.Text: "You dish out death sentences, but you pardon your own murderous confessor? Such double standards are very much in keeping with your predecessor's modus operandi."

bf371c0a-baad-4812-91bf-51a0fc0be072.Text: Urged Incendia to repent of her crimes.

070e5ce6-c679-43eb-a1bd-b7850162785c.Text: "Repent, Incendia. You have strayed from the path of righteousness and turned into a monster!"

bd1b3533-3e6f-4d46-a7c1-457784eac123.Text: "I have seen your thirst for blood. You revel in the sentencing and the executing. Are you going to dispute that? Am I lying?"

6f58517b-3edb-4af3-b036-1226c4fb68dd.Text: "Your verdicts bear no relation to the codified justice of the Imperium. Your justice is arbitrary and you are creating your own law — in essence... your own Imperium! That is heresy!"

b8fb26bd-f8b1-4d01-839d-7d0be4d66007.Text: "I give up. This is an exercise in futility."

37c4326b-a395-40da-a5b2-6516c9b96bc3.Text: "Did you know she was a heretic all along?"

8661ca4d-8354-41d9-bf17-6ba61f4ed2ce.Text: "Perhaps it was your cruelty that propelled her into the Archenemy's arms."

90f7599f-930f-4319-93a9-a34a4d2c2a93.Text: [Feign righteous anger] "The venom of corruption, for which Hieronymus was the conduit, entered the hearts of his followers as well! They are all complicit in his crime, and therefore must share his punishment."

06cd45c6-18ce-40ba-b8cd-a81a238ea222.Text: Demanded that all Drusians on Footfall be punished for Reverend Hieronymus's crimes.

13988ed5-3a07-4986-bda4-7c8f5b01b9af.Text: Suggested that Incendia turn Vladaym Tocara into a deck sweep.

1f71b7c8-77c4-43e4-9164-a529ad7bb194.Text: "He can still atone for his crimes. Give him to me. Let him purify his soul by sweeping the decks of my ship."

4dc9fdf1-2001-458d-acbc-b07df8d0cbeb.Text: Proposed that Vladaym Tocara be servitorised at Incendia's trial.

95ebde10-b795-4866-8e40-f3cf4b63adb4.Text: "Death is the Emperor's Peace, and it must be earned. Let me turn him into a servitor on my ship. That will teach him obedience."

cd7e5ba4-fcc5-4803-baf5-a797af114689.Text: "A lesson in humility. His power is in shambles, and his rebellion never took off. Vladaym is no more: all that is left is a servant of the Emperor who has lost his way. Servitude will bring him back to the true path."

4499ba95-12bb-44fd-8009-03e3721e13f0.Text: "You are right. He deserves a harsher punishment."

25cbac02-6294-47dc-a3ae-e1e22574f5b4.Text: Charged the pirate Ryzza with heresy at Incendia's trial.

ebd07fb9-d8ab-4ab9-bfe5-f4b516df5e89.Text: [Point at Ryzza] "She is guilty. Her soul is full of corruption. Allow me to carry out her sentence personally."

dc0cb096-025c-4efc-b734-c76040f80e44.Text: "You are right. I shall never see you again."

1278b5b7-d516-4757-a064-45452bfdcc6d.Text: "Ryzza, by siding with the Archenemy, you have betrayed the Emperor Himself. For this, you are hereby sentenced to death. Perish, heretic!"

8ebb8d18-ab62-4325-be72-298eaecc03f4.Text: Proposed that Vladaym Tocara be tortured to death and his screams be broadcast over Footfall's vox-system.

cc437b29-ba58-4cff-8987-bbac2f2d23d5.Text: "The people must know what happens to traitors. Torture him to death and broadcast his screams live on Footfall's vox-station. I shall provide you with my best executioners for the occasion."

b8b595dd-1018-4a51-840d-795c27f8b3cd.Text: Declared Footfall an abode of faith and piety.

5de7a3d3-c6af-420c-84dd-afb2a86edaa1.Text: "Chorda's methods were cruel, but her goal was righteous. From now on, Footfall will be a bastion of faith and piety. Observance of the Imperium's laws will be monitored more closely."

4249498a-a9ce-4074-a774-7d11b134bac3.Text: Ordered that shelters be organised for the needy on Footfall.

afe49fad-efa9-4fec-a524-a8ec5778a807.Text: "Footfall is exhausted and wounded by Chorda's cruelty. I will have shelters set up where those in need and in pain can find a roof over their heads, sustenance, and medical aid."

7bd4d800-3121-49a9-9632-36e2406be953.Text: Announced the beginning of an era of lawlessness and impunity on Footfall.

fe94edb3-1967-4676-8c48-4bf910c364cb.Text: "To the abyss with the Imperial Creed. It does not belong on Footfall. From now on, absolute freedom will be the only law of this place. Whoever disagrees can head for the nearest airlock and take a walk into the void."

33621d05-3350-49da-bbdd-6c894d051b38.Text: "Let things gradually return to the way they were. I will not interfere in the station's affairs."

36580587-6eb9-48b2-bc29-8f76cae52ebb.Text: Secretly collected the pirate Ryzza's blood at Incendia's trial.

5eb026ce-af3f-4d25-a872-12d151680c22.Text: [Discreetly wipe Ryzza's blood with a handkercher to use it in a dark ritual]

1c202a42-7dc8-4d1a-98ea-fcce01766a35.Text: "What a pathetic attempt. She deserved what happened to her."

70cfe458-80e2-46a8-945e-172fd523016f.Text: "Wait, does her repentance not earn her a lighter sentence?"

04405fd3-7bab-4504-8dec-98af544d6b1e.Text: [Execute] "Incendia Chorda, having weighed your crimes, I, {name} von Valancius, hereby sentence you to death."

63301f51-50ac-4ede-85ce-0cdbc02869c3.Text: "Hieronymus, perhaps you can talk her down?"

3cb9fbd2-9535-4ec7-a77b-8e104b5c1aab.Text: "Lady Incendia's body is to be transported to the domain of House Chorda. Untouched."

0c5a259c-58ed-4844-a874-4afac256e3ed.Text: "I do not care. Do with them as you will."

93a3800a-a867-4e1a-b4a4-63a349c9d13a.Text: Proposed that Vladaym Tocara be hanged at Incendia's trial.

6639fb14-d731-48f4-adf7-5fcf65233675.Text: "The law states that these are hanging offences."

00ac86ca-cb20-4c09-acfb-9049f2b43004.Text: Granted Vladaym Tocara an easy death at Incendia's trial.

8bf50c91-caa9-4265-9cd5-235d65d20d71.Text: "What are you meaning to do next?"

d3649983-7c4d-4bc1-a164-18bb4fb772c1.Text: Proposed that Vladaym Tocara be assigned to a penal unit at Incendia's trial.

44a6f219-98d6-4e20-8cee-e17b87c08054.Text: "Let him and his people atone by shedding blood in the Emperor's name."

38a986ca-5371-44e8-9cc2-9b59bea753da.Text: "Now is the time to lay down your arms and come to the negotiating table."

4c5e8b71-bb06-43d8-a915-ad19adf7572c.Text: {n}Incendia casts a damning glance at Vladaym, who is shifting about in a puddle of his own blood. She says sternly,{/n} "Footfall will be relieved to know that law has been restored in every sector of the station at last."

6522319b-bf81-4a3a-8a9e-74e6f7506b83.Text: "Footfall... will be delighted to know... that you're dead... you redheaded bitch..."

0ac30a22-5289-4b70-bf08-4f71af5b5431.Text: "I disagree. I see one more dangerous plotter here." {n}Incendia's finger points at Ryzza.{/n}

37de1bc0-66b6-4f69-bb56-02a8f1b8c4d8.Text: "I'll regain my grip on the station. I'll free the prisoners and give the merchants back their impounded cargo. I'll replace the lowlifes Her Ladyship put in charge with my own lowlifes. I'll take care of those of the station's sectors that are slowly dying in isolation. And, of course, I'll send an envoy to the Lord Inquisitor to bring him the news and inform him of my willingness to cooperate."

738ad77f-b761-4f04-92e7-21cd45774da7.Text: {n}Incendia whispers softly and passionately,{/n} "You are not lying. You made me what I am. And I was corrupt and wicked before."

6e37473a-f4ce-4eba-af7e-10465cfe7830.Text: "Footfall has always been dirty, like the threshold of a temple is dirty from all the shoes wiped on it. But it's always been, and will remain, the threshold of the Expanse. Here is where our conquest of these systems began. If you don't like it the way it is... why, then, you're too squeamish and have no concept of what a frontier of any era looks like. Not that I care to justify myself to a madwoman. Everybody knows she's fixated on judging people."

4d9dc689-bb92-4133-a315-8d31e6e374bc.Text: "And if that is so, they will all face the same trial as the others. I will not indiscriminately massacre servants of the faith for the deeds of their preacher who strayed from the righteous path."

5ea26d6b-b733-41ea-9ec2-18ce89b69366.Text: "Vladaym Tocara, you will be hanged for your crimes. Let the sight of your cold corpse serve as proof that the Cold Trade has no place on Footfall any longer."

e5962867-3658-4a8e-9604-a260148184b0.Text: "That is out of the question. I will not let them slip from the law's grasp again."

5c456ebe-0c69-496c-a2f9-3cfc598143be.Text: "You have contributed to the restoration of order on Footfall, {name}. Therefore, we shall preside over the trial together."

889c7445-714c-4e41-af5a-fd17c05c00db.Text: {n}Chorda surveys the bar and asks in a ruthless voice,{/n} "Who will face trial next?"

9bc24d85-a39b-4176-9a06-7108a1e9a3c5.Text: {n}Overcoming the desire to spit on Incendia's corpse, clearly manifested on his face, Vladaym turns from a thug into a cold bureaucrat again before your eyes. He says curtly to one of his associates,{/n} "Place Her Ladyship's body in a cryo-vault and take it to her ship. Make sure no damage is done to it — no further damage, that is. We were enemies, of course, but that's no reason not to act in a civilised manner."

43d907ab-04c1-4e86-8d81-1ef1e029e937.Text: "And because of that, we are supposed to pardon you for your past offences? Commoner Ryzza, you are charged with piracy, with aiding and abetting rebels, and with blasphemous heresy and worship of the Ruinous Powers. Burn for eternity, ungodly wretch."

8255542a-d497-47ac-aae8-20739de18f5c.Text: "Vladaym Tocara, I charge you before the Emperor's stern gaze with contempt for the Creed He gave us, with harbouring lawless heretics, with crimes against His loyal servants, and with armed rebellion against His will!"

5a2f00c0-53e2-42ab-9ed0-cc28f0dfacfb.Text: "Yes, that's what they say about me. And what they say about you is that you're an obscura-huffing maniac who kills people for sport."

bf4d93aa-43a3-40eb-895e-6770f245f896.Text: "Me?" {n}Ryzza bares her teeth, grabs her weapon, and stares at the enforcers like a hunted beast.{/n} "But I never fought against you! I never backed Vladaym!"

79d9b0a3-f87f-4b17-90ca-e75cfebf96d3.Text: "What?" {n}Hieronymus and Incendia's cries of astonishment blend together.{/n}

d7a81b32-45e2-4ff9-a755-c2418b7e34a5.Text: "You are right. Vladaym Tocara, you are hereby found guilty. The court sentences you to a lifetime of penance. You and your associates shall be enlisted in a penal boarding squad operating from my flagship. As part of that squad, you shall fight enemies of Humanity for the rest of your life."

8a80cd82-b582-4a8a-9a69-ee748b8b99b9.Text: {n}Silence reigns. Incendia and Hieronymus stare at you, dumbfounded. Her expression is one of confusion, while his is one of secret fear. Incendia's eyelid twitches nervously.{/n}

b3162fca-85e5-4f6c-8adf-cfb6a4847e62.Text: "An excellent idea. Vladaym Tocara, for your crimes, you shall be expelled out through a void chamber. Take this filth away and dispose of it as rubbish should be."

0bd57397-d29d-4f07-a110-e47182f9590b.Text: "You are not lying. I... do enjoy it."

4371f035-b6c2-469f-8b3f-8b457ffc8492.Text: "For a Rogue Trader, the ultimate crime is... to reject the Emperor's protection and make their reign absolute, becoming a brazen rival of God and a blasphemous tyrannical heresiarch."

7c65f5d1-9ffa-4da5-8ae8-894e51536e07.Text: "Treasonous nonsense! Never has the Emperor condemned a servant of His for assiduity and rigour! I do not make my own law — I make His law absolute!"

0d501ffb-931e-4b61-81bd-1ddca5c31484.Text: "I will not offend you by telling a lie, Incendia. It was on my orders that your cryo-vault was tampered with and Aspyce's other aspiring heirs killed. I admit to my crime."

9003f729-ec1e-49d0-ae81-46ddcd4a772c.Text: {n}Incendia lowers her head, and the shadows in the room seem to darken. The radiance fades from her eyes.{/n} "Enough. I... repent. I yearned to serve the Emperor, but exacting vengeance upon His foes was so delicious that I abandoned my duty for the sake of my own gratification. I made Footfall my house of pleasures. I was a harsh judge not because it was what He wanted, but because it was what I wanted. I executed those His law forbade to execute.
