0bfca705-a5eb-4f96-90c5-cd4a50c37d3b.Text: "A small band of my most daring cutthro— staff members who were by my side when I came to power. Business partners who still remember that any venture is only as reliable as the grip of the venturer's hand on their pistol. Add to that the group of xenos mercenaries which my... colleagues from the Kasballica Mission have provided me with. A radical solution, I know, but they don't care who they kill as long as I pay them, and I have the means to pay them."

acf13e31-5968-455f-ba4d-18dde8652d8a.Text: "We would have greater numbers if Ryzza wasn't so damnably cautious, and Hieronymus did us a favour and shut his preaching trap..." {n}Vladaym grits his teeth and adds quietly,{/n} "I would've thrown the good reverend for a loop long ago if it weren't for the fanatical mob that would show up here to avenge him."

d80db847-be1c-465b-9644-0c28f1df42f0.Text: {n}The former Liege looks {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallNotAlly}exhausted{/d}. His glasses cannot hide the circles under his eyes. His coat collar is greasy and unbuttoned, showing the meshwork of the ceramite-reinforced armour hidden underneath. There is a conspicuous dent right beside his throat, left by a bullet. However, as tired as he is, the man is showing no sign of having given up: his lips are pressed together in a hard line; his movements are sharp; and the bandit tattoos under his rolled-up sleeves are a reminder of who Vladaym Tocara was before taking the Liege's throne.{/n}

edd393fb-75cb-46b7-93ee-5c3957322173.Text: {n}The former Liege looks {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallAlly}angry and focused{/d}. His coat collar is unbuttoned, showing the meshwork of ceramite-reinforced armour hidden underneath. He is wearing a gun holster on his side. Now that Vladaym has thrown off the mask of a disgruntled bureaucrat, his sleeves are rolled up, showing his old bandit tattoos. He exudes an aura of imperious cruelty.{/n}

cad54133-fb01-4206-a027-fc69502e8983.Text: {n}You note the contraption replacing Ryzza's right leg — a tangle of thick cables around industrial cylinder pistons. A makeshift augmetic, rigged up from whatever was available at the docks. The pirate {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallNotAlly}has not been wearing it for long{/d}, judging by the still fresh stitches on her stump. Every so often, the leg emits sparks.{/n}

6f935760-c130-4f13-b1b0-8b65d62bda5a.Text: "It's turned into a kingdom of death. Executing protesters, cracking down on corrupt traders, and suppressing dissent are all good, useful policies within reasonable limits. I've used them myself, in fact. However, with Lady Chorda, reasonable limits are a distant memory at this point."

2c323721-270d-42f8-9f65-35f248ddd578.Text: "And I warned you, didn't I, that this would happen unless you helped us with provisions? When Chorda showed up here, we stood up to her dictatorship, but the ranks of my loyal partners thinned by the day. In the end, a single good punch in the teeth was all it took for the station to roll over and beg for mercy. Few found it in them to resist."

31e6a88f-a556-4108-a1a6-fde8bcddfe6b.Text: "Fortunately, I'd been preparing for that turn of events ever since that hag tried to take Footfall the first time. You helped us then, giving me time to organise. I set up weapons caches, enlisted more fighters, and deleted my agents' data from the cogitator network. When Chorda seized power, she thought she'd won, but the station was still mine... to an extent."

21deec7b-97ea-4df0-803e-ab8ccbe4c322.Text: "My little army is waging war on the enforcers. We slaughter patrols, wrestle back detainees, and punish those who collaborate with the enemy... or are close to someone who does." {n}Vladaym's ruthless smile is like a jagged steel trap.{/n} "Incendia is conducting her reprisals and I am conducting mine. Everyone must remember that there are consequences for collaborating with the occupying force."

c282c48e-6976-4050-9397-63a9ef44252f.Text: {n}Vladaym chuckles darkly.{/n} "Surrender? Go crawling on my belly, begging for leniency? If you had any idea how many corpses I've littered across this station's decks on my rise to power, you'd know I would rather die in a void chamber than watch that possessed bitch destroy my station."

b670a6a0-e94e-4d25-ae08-a575641e02fb.Text: {n}Vladaym smiles tersely.{/n} "Old habits die hard. I'll admit, I wasn't exactly yearning for the days of my youth, but to find myself in the line of fire again is... invigorating."

ea45c3ca-fe2f-4040-b162-0a4160f90b38.Text: {n}Vladaym's presses his lips into a thin line.{/n} "I got into all manner of situations when I was a young man... including desperate ones. This rat has been cornered more than once before. But it always got out of that corner with its belly full of its hunter's flesh. I assure you I have no intention of reneging on my old principles."

46e2a0f8-3d79-4c1e-a223-90b99dbb3415.Text: {n}The former Liege grimaces as if from toothache.{/n} "No arguing with that. Here I thought that order should be imposed by killing the people who are harmful to Footfall and protecting the useful ones, hanging rabble-rousers and encouraging traders and explorers. More fool me. Turns out I should've just hanged whoever I could grab, and put all the sector's commerce in front of the firing squad."

8e59f79e-ced1-442c-817a-dc89d2b8be80.Text: {n}Vladaym nods attentively, then looks down at a data-slate showing a map of the station's systems. He scrutinises it with a pensive expression.{/n}

91a4922e-508b-457e-8b65-ef8c663c0a56.Text: {n}Vladaym is lightning-fast as he whips his pistol out of its holster and... smiles.{/n} "I've missed this. Everyone — if I pay you thrones, that means you — to battle!"

f121b0e2-1f86-4c62-a581-2b92e075c78a.Text: "I'm glad you're with us, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. This is a fight we must be well prepared for. As a... colleague of mine used to say, if your brain doesn't hurt from all that thinking of where to hide, it'll discover even your skull isn't thick enough once the fight is on. Which sounds especially ironic considering how he died. I'd like to ask your opinion on how prepared we are to entertain Lady Incendia."

92e666f3-ceb9-40a6-ab89-0dcd37895068.Text: {n}An unblinking gaze fixes upon you.{/n} "I hope you think it promising."

422ef459-63b3-4592-b805-9dee631e4bc9.Text: "Because a critically important station in the Expanse is about to become a graveyard. Once commerce dies, merchants will turn to piracy. What else could they do? Connections between worlds will be weakened, since Chorda will make short work of Astropaths as soon as she gets to them. And Chorda — do you think Footfall will be enough for her? No, she'll march on... perhaps to your worlds as well."

b90a81f4-1e48-4308-9415-2c5c85ceffc1.Text: {n}The Liege — newly restored — looks tired but... {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Footfall_VladaymLiege}pleased with what is going on around him{/d}. His fingers rap away at his data-slate as he sends out instruction after instruction.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship? Is there anything Footfall can do to thank you for its liberation?"

90e0c030-b3f7-4e6e-8e32-e488862469ae.Text: "She has misgivings about... the prospect of our cooperation. The old rogue prefers not to pick fights unless her victory is a foregone conclusion. And right now she seems to be planning on fleeing rather than fighting. She needs the right kind of motivation... It's a shame there's no one the cold bitch values enough for me to take hostage."

69caf2cc-7cf7-4757-bfa8-8c27cb2dc130.Text: "He preaches repentance." {n}Vladaym remains stone-faced for a few seconds before giving in and letting a sarcastic smile form on his lips.{/n} "Chorda sent him here to make us lay down our arms and renounce our rebellious ways."

e11e1ea7-7fe4-4256-9c02-db883494ef62.Text: {n}Vladaym is lightning-fast as he whips his pistol out of its holster and... smiles.{/n} "I knew this was exactly how our little war was going to end. All right, then, let's do this the Footfall way. Everyone — if I pay you thrones, that means you — to battle!"

76ddbbce-04ee-4ab4-9527-a022f8b0363d.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, you may have little love to spare for me, and you certainly {d|Encyclopedia:KasballicaRep_Min}have not built a strong alliance{/d} with the organisation I represent. But if seeing the new order of things on Footfall gives you even the tiniest suspicion that it's all damned madness, step in and help me stop it."

b565c5c5-5752-498f-902a-be0cfaa77773.Text: "Incendia Chorda has nothing to offer you, while my organisation's gratitude is guaranteed. Between losing an influential partner and strengthening your ties with them, I'm sure you'll opt for the latter."

6077b3ad-05a4-4f91-ad86-d07099177f11.Text: "Considering Calcazar has never once interfered in the station's affairs, he clearly couldn't care less about Footfall. This means he also doesn't care who runs the station, so long as things are quiet here. I'm going to make sure things are quiet. Granted, he did give Chorda a security detail, but if she's already..." {n}Tocara emphasises the last word.{/n} "...dead, and her death doesn't reek of deadly heresy, he likely won't bother to investigate. The Lord Inquisitor will simply entrust governance to someone who won't cause him problems. Someone like me."

7fb81230-9576-4633-990a-fcc76bb7d204.Text: "Besides, the Kasballica Mission — and I'm authorised to say this — sees Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship as a proven and valuable ally."

b3a474c0-76c3-4144-8792-11aac7d721fd.Text: "I will send my least important associates to the entrance to take the brunt of the initial assault. That should thin our guests' numbers." {n}Without thinking, Vladaym reaches for his pistol to check how easily it slides out of its holster. Then... he smiles. It's an easy-going, young, and bloodthirsty smile.{/n} "I'd almost forgotten how much I love all this."

6e695981-e52b-489b-acaf-42f332ceafdc.Text: "By the Throne's radiance, Vladaym, if you don't tell me this very moment where you and Falco are keeping my guys—"

2e91adf3-171f-4ec7-8730-cb548843d9d1.Text: {n}The former Liege interrupts Jae with a dry gesture:{/n} "I don't do business with rats, Heydari. And, surprisingly enough, for once I don't mean you."

e906e869-4a17-4f14-b052-b12116242d93.Text: "I'm only carrying out the duties imposed upon me by my position as Liege. After the House Chorda forces retreated in a hurry, it turned out that, surprisingly enough, there were unaccounted-for scumbags on the station who wasted no time in seizing the opportunity. I took the smartest and most useful among them under my wing, and told them I didn't want any shenanigans. As for the rest... a hundred or so names were added to the grievous toll Lady Chorda had left behind."

e1ddf3f1-aa0d-4ba7-841f-fc7e3cec840d.Text: "In that case, pray to the Exalted One that Falco backs up your story before he dies." {n}Disappointed, Jae takes her hand off her weapon and bows her head before you penitently.{/n} "Forgive me my brazenness, shereen. He's all yours."

0ef62907-e687-4dde-a703-19bc2ebb5ad1.Text: {n}Vladaym grins wickedly.{/n} "Dangerous words. Very dangerous. But powerful. I have no doubt you'll match them with your actions."

decf5c34-689b-4a3b-ac7d-aa58c1ee9abb.Text: "Regretfully, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, I have nothing to offer you at the moment. My access to the assets you're interested in has been temporarily restricted. It's going to take putting a bullet through a couple of heads for me to once again be able to offer an adequate range of merchandise."

08c24b21-4bda-4db1-8c5d-27657e69e652.Text: {n}Vladaym hesitates. Even this thoroughly unprincipled hustler knows there is no going back after crossing certain lines. He stares at you intently. Despite the dark glasses hiding his eyes and the mask-like expression on his face, you can easily see — no, sense — the exact moment he brutally crushes the last remnants of faith inside him and decides to step into the abyss. Vladaym casts away his doubts and gets down on his knees.{/n}

84cbb8a2-9dba-41a7-b0ce-4c001d4681d6.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, I'm asking you for help. Not just on behalf of the portion of the station population that isn't already scared shitless, but on behalf of the Kasballica Mission as well. My people and my organisation's assets are in a vulnerable position. Help us protect our interests, and {d|Encyclopedia:KasballicaRep_Mid}we'll help you{/d} protect yours."

6d03880a-15cc-4256-86d8-183b03486eb0.Text: "I renounce all other patrons and pledge my eternal fealty to the Great Beacon, the true {mf|god|goddess} and {mf|master|mistress} of fates. I most humbly beseech you to help me drown Footfall in the blood of Incendia Chorda and her minions." {n}Vladaym looks at you expectantly.{/n}

5feaaa67-d8fa-4904-881f-9c081bd272e7.Text: "Old nicknames die as hard as old habits. I used to be known by that name on the station. The Vackemo is a myth. A malicious spirit stalking its prey in Footfall's empty sectors." {n}Tocara chuckles.{/n} "I had a terrible reputation when I was young."

bed43bfb-73da-4648-b22e-5de9cf7531ef.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship is too late. The Lord Inquisitor and his people have already left Footfall. They were in a great hurry. That said, you can see I'm in no rush to return to my old abode. I wouldn't like to be thrown out of it, should the esteemed Lord Inquisitor suddenly decide to come back."

9a95adab-3c1f-44d7-8b51-157c144c5839.Text: "She knows we use the Amasecus as our meeting place. If you let the enforcers know I can be found and grabbed in here, she will come — and she will hardly drag her throne with her. We'll lure her into a trap, kill her, and take back Footfall."

99ccaa33-e039-4026-bbf5-44d8465ec02d.Text: {n}Vladaym grins darkly.{/n} "Then Octaviana's bitten off more than she can chew. It's too early to write me off yet. But I appreciate Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship's decision to inform me. I'll keep an eye on that overly feisty bartender."

f1592e19-650c-4aa5-b484-a167a6beabaa.Text: "Perhaps some of those gathered in here will support us. Ryzza's people, Hieronymus's zealots... even Octaviana's regulars. We can use whomever we can get. If you think that it may be worth fortifying our positions or preparing a few surprises for our guests, my people and arsenal are at your disposal — all you have to do is say the word. As soon as we're ready, send Chorda a message saying I'm here. Let her come. We'll settle our differences the Footfall way. With a gunfight."

7a0b9fa0-278c-4d0d-a85a-48e5064c5be9.Text: {n}Vladaym nods and stands up.{/n} "Then let's get down to business."

9b664e47-d7bd-4af3-a15c-2b2d731c395f.Text: {n}With a feral snarl, Ulfar says sharply,{/n} "You speak tainted words, Aett-Vater. Yes, the priests here are murderous dogs, but do not dare blaspheme the Allfather." {n}Looming over you, Ulfar brandishes his finger at you in warning.{/n}

e597bb72-c13d-4a15-888b-110c19a7a41c.Text: "But he seems taken aback by the scale of Lady Incendia's purges, which opens up possibilities. If we put pressure on him, he'll bring over zealots who'll tear apart whoever he points his finger at. A useful man. I regret not getting him onside sooner."

8193ff98-c017-4de6-b7d9-c6cdbb168846.Text: {n}You feel Ulfar's burning gaze directed at you. His face is devoid of emotion, but there is a hostile glint in his eyes.{/n}

d3f5f29f-34f3-4585-b180-edddd697874a.Text: {n}The word "mercenary" causes Marazhai's eyes to flare in fury.{/n} "Careful with your choice of terms, mon-keigh. Or I will demonstrate my expertise in flaying victims alive, here and now."

effd12f8-f22c-4616-a321-e3dcd817a265.Text: {n}Vladaym looks over at Marazhai.{/n} "You really aren't picky at all in your choice of mercenaries. Then again, the unholy xenos are too adept in the art of carnage for one to refuse their services out of trivial squeamishness."

ca0b9d0c-95f0-43cc-a629-4b9e8007fa39.Text: "Your vanity has crossed the line that divides stupidity from blasphemy." {n}Heinrix clenches his fists. For a moment, you feel as if the air is going cold... but the illusion is dispelled a mere second later.{/n}

1bd5f489-a2b5-415f-9f3f-c485e1bbf548.Text: {n}Argenta stares at you grimly from under her locks of white hair. Her hands on her weapon are trembling with impatience... but the warrior stops herself and looks away.{/n}

065c2507-3919-44ff-b3aa-ff90ba340156.Text: "Thank you, Lord Captain." {n}Idira's words are barely audible, breathed out rather than spoken. Her expression is clearly one of relief.{/n} "As filthy of a place as Footfall is... blood and tears won't wash away that filth — they'll only make the stench worse."

4b4545fd-c001-44d5-80c3-07aa7ad7b37f.Text: {n}The Seneschal furrows his thick eyebrows.{/n} "Hmm. I cannot say I approve of antagonising Chorda... but her methods being what they are, I definitely disapprove of assisting her."

f207a0c0-bfe5-4683-bacb-427970b5ddde.Text: {n}Turning away from Ryzza, Vladaym's expression does not change, but an indistinct curse falls from his lips.{/n}

80362a9c-c26e-4d3a-8c0d-774abe838970.Text: {n}The Proctor clenches his teeth with an audible screech.{/n} "Do not equate Chorda's preposterous court with the Lex Imperialis. The God-Emperor's Law remains perfect, even if the judge has erred beyond all hope."

d57b1437-9459-4e6d-ac8e-9c9a847a0ef1.Text: "A general uprising will be doomed to fail. The enforcers have isolated the asteroids. We can't strike out against Incendia: she has the greater numbers, and her throne's refractor field will protect her from any attack." {n}An insidious smile appears on the Liege's lips.{/n} "So we'll ask Her Ladyship to come to us. Exploiting her overconfidence. If she wants my blood, let her come and spill it."

ed468109-ccb2-44c0-b879-f102830fb34d.Text: "However much Chorda would like to believe she's kicked the Kasballica out of Footfall, she hasn't. We're scattered all over the station, lying low, and there's still enough of us to cause trouble."

203ba5ca-2ee3-4f82-925f-eeb84b3b4db7.Text: "Besides, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship has not yet considered the possibilities that working with the Kasballica Mission opens up. Now is the perfect moment for you to gain a new ally. In a time of crisis, every friendship is valuable."

49276aac-5c50-4b22-b361-49567445e428.Text: "I realise it's a bold hypothesis, and the Lord Inquisitor may have me hanged for Chorda's death. But my life is at stake as it is, so I may as well take the risk."

7d2ff89a-d39c-4507-8749-63856f9e2b56.Text: "Enough, Vladaym! I was hoping I could temper your pride, but you are too rooted in your arrogant and heretical ways! All you faithful to the Emperor, let us take a stand for His liege, Rogue Trader von Valancius!"

52d31b6d-e395-41d5-a064-0744cb614b3a.Text: "Alas, most of my people on the station have perished. Incendia had what I couldn't offer — provisions. It's amazing how many people will break their oaths of loyalty for a nutribar... forgetting about the inevitable consequences." {n}Vladaym grins harshly.{/n} "Well then, let's give my modest fighting force a head count."

012feee2-77f8-4366-ac3c-2b533f8328dd.Text: "To battle, Wolves! Do not allow the malefic any respite! Von Valancius, find cover before you lose your head!"

0bbd3cbb-86cd-46d8-8897-1ee937b94a91.Text: "May the energies of the Immaterium flow into the core of this mechanism."

3489650b-d32c-4170-a9ac-8f31fcad9ae5.Text: "May the gears resume turning, may the batteries be infused with the blessed poison of the unreal, may the vector be set."

a0900926-44bf-4a4a-80b5-39caf7d4912c.Text: "Courage and steel alone will not be enough to change the Ways drawn by my master!"

4a2ca3d6-e69d-400a-b13e-f5d145f65fc9.Text: "The battle was hard, but that makes victory all the more glorious."

c5750d2f-a6ec-4e82-aebf-7dd048b7b99c.Text: "Cut off the fallen heretics' heads... Just to be sure..."

ecb6d4e6-7df5-4660-a95a-716036c57e0c.Text: The furnishings are clearly fitted for human comfort, but everything is covered in a thick layer of dust.

3be5bc2d-42fc-4ef7-b71b-48e7e6c41d46.Text: Scarlet forbidding signs blaze on the vid-screen — someone has placed a seal of silence on the cogitator.

bacb6ffa-3637-4ab1-b721-f8318f587a24.Text: There is a seal of silence on the cogitator, but it is not difficult to break it. The machine spirit has been tormented — someone ripped every bit of useful knowledge from its memory.

408a8c94-9c5f-404c-afb2-246da8cd6dff.Text: The cogitators are deep in dreamless slumber and the sacred unguents on their connection ports have long since dried.

80b01066-cd19-48ff-a5a3-145e5d9c18fc.Text: From a distance, the creature resembles a Haemonculus, but upon closer inspection, it is more like a bad caricature of one.

1ad68447-fe41-4a95-87b9-c7458c57c9dc.Text: "I can feel... bones cracking... tendons snapping... blood..."

256bb1d5-c1d5-4a26-85a5-f14300ca33f7.Text: "Who is screaming in my head? Is that... my voice?"

8323f607-aee2-44c0-806a-833ee2fc33b3.Text: "Something is stirring in there, tearing at my flesh! Inside... right beside my heart!"

0bb00a2d-3508-49f9-9f10-22d54d5f2c00.Text: A thick layer of ancient dust covers the walls, floor, and equipment.

7305457f-12bc-4df8-8b2e-4e754bb41256.Text: The cage bars and floor are covered in caked-on blood.

c2f30ea8-5fea-44ea-a6cf-037e4059a50c.Text: The broken stairs end at an empty spot where all that remains is the shattered floor and a small hollow.

c2918d8e-440f-4d81-8a62-a42180ef3830.Text: A bio-fount designed to grow flesh.

555a8141-a7b6-48fa-b4af-b010ed2e2acc.Text: The xenos torture device has been placed out in the open. It clearly sees regular use.

6cfcf864-d6c7-4b56-a1b6-29510bfd4154.Text: Pieces of flesh, skin, and bone are stuck in the dark, sticky sludge that covers the tables.

b1a95d35-321a-4a1d-9e11-85bc2bf1aa60.Text: The lift call panel is unresponsive.

23b57aaf-6861-424f-b79b-59f796d9fa39.Text: Several bodies and a multitude of strange clanging mechanisms have fused together in a single creature.

2d1b9deb-9cd6-4f6b-8b34-ae46a977c38d.Text: Several bodies and mechanisms have fused together in a way only warp-affected matter is capable of doing.

692c8551-4889-4e69-a764-725ee450cea8.Text: Viscous greenish sludge is still sliding down the walls of the large, heavy glass capsules.

8f014a55-a64f-486f-81f6-e000ba1f8497.Text: Thick green sludge — a condensed solution that xenos use for growing clones — is still running down the walls of the large, heavy glass capsules.

d1bc0e23-93dc-45a8-a50c-1189a19a58a3.Text: The pitiful, deformed creature looks like a cruel parody of a living being.

f3a6fa99-6ed6-45c3-b5bb-a60aeb10f1fc.Text: The deformed, feeble, and crazed creature is a pitiful and clearly unviable copy of the Haemonculus Tervantias.

468deb87-d469-458e-a47c-c9fc754d91b7.Text: What used to be the captive's body is now a mess of bones, flesh, surgical tools, and instruments of torture.

bc086701-7ddc-482b-a1fc-34a4e36b3d43.Text: What used to be the captive's body now resembles a living operating theatre, complete with a full inventory of surgical tools.

d0ae8619-49c0-4e92-bbef-7991b4f4cd00.Text: "Neu...rosurgical... stim...ulation of the rear part of the hy...ptham...pothalamus... Required... for what?"

ec095a8e-f9c3-4ef8-8935-7748c124ee8a.Text: "Experiment number four thousand three hun...dred eleven? No... seventeen? What kind of experiment is this?"

2dbb0e88-b6bd-473a-8d2a-39bfdcd301e0.Text: "Source of pain... visible, tangible. Sensations are... absent entirely."

722ca1ff-c191-4a8f-94d1-f1273e89c17c.Text: A strange construct is blocking the entrance.

c0e652c3-b0ec-4877-a3c2-304f396ce7f3.Text: The corpse in Tech-Priest garb was shot in the head: more likely a cold-blooded execution than a death in combat.

0a48b07a-cc0a-446e-8d3e-3c47773bbcc6.Text: The shallow hole is filled with stone fragments and other debris.

60dcb861-f8bd-4697-9b2c-9d90ae04cb8f.Text: "I killed you with my own hands!"

1371961f-6d6d-40e3-b52b-c89aa7d32353.Text: [Draw your weapon] "Trust me, this time I will fell you much quicker than the last!"

57e145a4-2c9b-434f-ac5a-3ba286612d2c.Text: "I see you have found new company, Tervantias."

da71494a-ccf4-4d5b-a3f3-e3ba1dcdfc54.Text: "Why are you here and not in Commorragh?"

9cdfa89a-1652-4e26-bead-7020c22c98cd.Text: "What is this place? It does not exactly look like a Drukhari laboratory."

b1d45bf6-c1ae-48df-bb89-0d29881c73e7.Text: "Am I talking to one Tervantias or several? Is each of you a separate individual?"

b54e10e9-dc48-44c1-85ff-3232a565c212.Text: "I saw the body of a dead Tech-Priest in this lab. Where did he come from? Explain."

e769ecc1-fd93-4611-8558-67aeee1d4616.Text: "That hole in the ceiling is a peculiar design choice. What happened here?"

f197b889-85f7-4bbd-a4e5-2f5080a2a4db.Text: [Draw your weapon] "This meeting shall be our last, Tervantias."

6a5f7795-8bb5-477b-8030-a15cb2f2b9e0.Text: {n}You are looking at several completely identical Haemonculi at work. A disturbing sight. The indistinguishable, and familiar, faces turn their attention toward you, morosely and almost indifferently.{/n}

d815ccc2-41b2-412b-aff8-322f1965c6ff.Text: "Because of you, specimen! Because of your feeble wits and your deplorably stubborn reluctance to die!" {n}In the thick silence, several clicks are heard as the copies move their limbs in an insect-like fashion.{/n} "But I had to finish what I had started... finish the masterpiece that had been taken away from me! Because of you! All because of you!"

96effa4b-0e54-4225-8fb8-d8d5bba60fa7.Text: {n}A broad, repulsive grin appears on one of the disfigured faces.{/n} "How would I know? I can't tell one mon-keigh from another."

5b1d66bd-4681-496e-a701-140fd4d90204.Text: {n}The identical faces look annoyed and spiteful. For a moment, it seems the Haemonculi are about to reply in unison, but a barely perceptible electrical impulse stops them. One of them scoffs and mutters through his teeth,{/n} "Just more proof of how unreliable partnerships with lower life forms are."

e2813c28-4c6f-4805-8b8e-f2356683aed4.Text: "You're different from others of your species, specimen. This time around, I want to study you much, and I mean much, more thoroughly, which necessitates your death... I hope dying once isn't enough for you either."

ce5a8b77-3a46-4389-9438-2c102a0f3296.Text: {n}Marazhai clicks his tongue.{/n} "All Haemonculi are endowed with an intellect that is as keen as it is deranged. But this is probably the first coven member I have seen who has well and truly lost his marbles. Dying has not done him any good."

924569c1-55a1-441f-97a3-b57bbc106cef.Text: {n}An indulgent chuckle rolls like a wave from one Haemonculus to another. They answer all at once, an ominous choir filling up the room:{/n} "Have you forgotten that I am a great master of flesh who has transcended death itself? Do you think it would befit me to let a mon-keigh cut my path short?"

251d3c42-bcbe-4505-a3e7-5b71d38cd4f7.Text: {n}One of the Haemonculi starts to talk — with all the usual arrogance:{/n} "Specimen. We {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_HaemonkulusAlive}meet again{/d}. Your escape from Commorragh was both a statistical anomaly and an act of abject cowardice. You should have died in the Dark City, instead of overstepping the limits of your own usefulness. You caused too much commotion."

f82c8f80-4318-4e53-a159-316c6997ea54.Text: {n}The monster falls silent. Barely perceptible electrical charges run through the Haemonculi's bodies. Then the one who spoke continues,{/n} "So you're here. Now what? Are you going to bore me with your questions, mon-keigh?"

e2337a2a-f2ac-4d1e-a1a6-a2b4c10d2fda.Text: {n}The clones look around them in a movement that is almost synchronised. A disembodied voice answers you:{/n} "This dreary vault is lacking in practicality and function but it has served as a passable refuge for me and my research."

286e789f-e558-4efc-a7ee-976bba309384.Text: {n}You notice one of the Haemonculi glance at the hole in the ceiling. Fury contorts the xenos's face. Tervantias is unable to hide his anger at what happened. Whoever did it and whatever it was they did, it enraged him.{/n}

4130e731-7a96-4be3-b49d-b8f29c17ec99.Text: {n}Tervantias's voice sounds dry. The grim gazes of his hideous copies are fixed upon you, watching.{/n}

691d5894-e199-4c7f-aed1-5e604b3b6486.Text: {n}The Haemonculi are quiet, and then... they start to giggle. The revolting sound makes your skin crawl.{/n} "Scary, isn't it? The thought that you're not the only mon-keigh who serves me. Try and guess, specimen. Try and guess."

730623a9-c4ea-4904-834e-6ad5f85e7129.Text: {n}You hear the Drukhari's voice again but cannot see who is talking to you.{/n} "'Found'? Don't you mean 'made'? I've had a backup shell stored away for centuries, but the events at the Spire of the Reaving Tempest convinced me one active body was not enough."

e73d37bc-74fb-41d1-be1c-f34de8530974.Text: "I am obviously here because this is my laboratory containing my research that requires my attention." {n}The familiar voice of one of the xenos sounds as though he is lecturing a child.{/n}

bbfe0ddb-276a-4c4c-92d5-906ab96f6f2c.Text: "Their... their colours! Horrible, frightening, tattered shades! Only a madman could do something like that to himself..." {n}Cassia looks away, horrified.{/n}

45b14387-c7c3-44a5-8432-81723cd3f505.Text: {n}The Haemonculi you can see are silent, and yet, you still hear Tervantias's reply: his voice seems to be coming from every direction at once.{/n} "My new multiple form is intriguing, isn't it? I'll leave your question unanswered, specimen, to give you something to ponder."

abd733ca-dc4e-4363-b832-d2ce38f31f3a.Text: "I haven't finished yet!" {n}The Haemonculi break into psychotic laughter.{/n} "One corporeal shell is too few! Deplorably, unacceptably few! Once my work is complete, not one mon-keigh in the world will be able to destroy me completely!"

a512d118-fbe2-4e93-8a7d-07f84400dbd2.Text: "Good. That means I can add a new note of agony to your every death. And I won't repeat myself even once."

75ebd261-e821-4cc6-960c-daf473b662b4.Text: "One... many... what difference does it make? I'm on my way toward infinity, specimen. Toward genuine, limitless immortality!"

5b2e70ac-dc4b-43c3-b190-3443c69bb3fd.Text: {n}The Haemonculi are twitching slightly, as though from invisible electric impulses. They look virtually identical, yet each seems to be missing something: a limb, an implant, even a facial feature or two. The single gaze of the many faces no longer seems full of haughty superiority only. Some kind of a shared defect also shows in it.{/n}

16321eff-a028-4722-b216-c047991f0ab4.Text: {n}The Haemonculi appear identical. Their repulsively indistinguishable faces are looking at you with a single condescending gaze, full of haughty superiority.{/n}

52ae5979-b141-4f43-b4f1-671da76ec77e.Text: "I'll turn this place inside out to find out who has conspired with the xenos. I've had it with traitors among the ranks of Humanity." {n}Heinrix's voice overflows with anger and bitterness.{/n}

af09931d-55b6-40be-8ea9-e656f25386da.Text: {n}The Haemonculi start talking over one another.{/n} "You!" {n}one of them hisses through his teeth.{/n} "How dare you..." {n}echoes another.{/n} "...show up here alive!" {n}a third one finishes.{/n} "This is even better, though..." {n}—{/n} "...now I'll cleanse the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_HaemonkulusKilled}shame of my death{/d} with your blood..." {n}—{/n} "...and then transform you, and the scum you've brought along, into something useful!"

b70c1cc0-8b7e-4fc8-8956-2d4a6b676a1d.Text: {n}Jae unconsciously reaches for the augment on her neck to check that it is {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_JaeWasInCommoragh}still there{/d}.{/n} "Bore you, ashmag? Oh, no, no. We'll just stuff your skinny arse full of metal. You love pain, after all, don't you?"

d38b0973-6452-485a-9756-b64f473e115a.Text: {n}Kibellah's eyes flash.{/n} "You! I have been praying for my thread to cross your loathsome path. Today, you will die as many times as you made me die."

40f3b33b-207a-4295-9d70-803023999b53.Text: "But you are not immortal, and we both know it." {n}Yrliet clenches her fists and gives the Haemonculus a look that could incinerate him.{/n} "I am going to kill you as many times as it takes. In the name of my fallen kin. And in the name of Crudarach."

f7339a45-cf12-4a1c-b772-c3242cbc7197.Text: "Look at that despicable ashmag, shereen. He still has hope of surviving our meeting."

c337abf5-3417-4cdf-b806-9da674a842be.Text: "Haemonculi can create copies of themselves by leaving samples of their body tissues in secret labs. As soon as a Haemonculus breathes their last..." {n}Marazhai clicks his fingers.{/n} "I don't suppose Tervantias shared his secret with Yremeryss."

44b36124-c139-491c-83fb-9b82f1c45664.Text: "You are just a coward hiding behind a panoply of masks. I will pluck off every last one."

11743931-9360-4b32-84a1-f94221a2be73.Text: "A stupid question, the answer to which is of no importance to one who is about to be taken apart."

9979a111-7706-44b1-a11e-9478b31ff47f.Text:
The data-slate is dented, its screen displaying flickering coloured stripes. The readable parts are twitchy and contain repetitions.
"...merous prior studies pursued the goal of breaking new ground in recreating and reviving the specimen in the event of its death. The above-mentioned experiment laid the groundwork for modernising and accelerating the recreation of a living organism from a minuscule sample of bone or muscle tissue.
Every variety of living organism has been observed to release a number of chemicals at the moment of death that enable the creation of an entirely identical clone with intact memories of its prior life up to and including the moment of death, most vividly detailed as to both physical sensations and emotional distress. As mentioned before, even a tiny modicum of bone or muscle tissue is sufficient for 'reviving' or creating an organism in an adequate lab setup. Bear in mind that work on creating the new body must begin before the third stage of decomposition has set in."

1ae9001f-6380-4f28-a7bc-53cc55886bdf.Text:
The notebook contains detailed observations, formulae, and diagrams, and is thickly covered in a viscous greenish liquid. Almost all the pages are firmly glued together, their contents turned into blurry stains.
"...riment No. 78. Outcome: failu...bject capable of maintaining minimal vital... falls short of every...quireme... Degree of ...sical abnormalities and deformities unacceptable.
...ilure. Upon being removed from the ...psule, the subject's vital pro... ceased in an excruciating manner following a brain ...rhage and multiple interna...eeding.
...riment No. 13... Outcome: partial succ...cimen capable of maintaining basic vital proc...es but only if continually neurally ...mulated by means of drilling through the elbow, knee, and hip joints.
Experiment No. 21. Outcome: ...u... The last ...x subjects conform to the minimum requirements, but their capabilities are limited. They are incapable of lear... no capacity for... of the original organism..."

6df970fe-79bb-4ddc-8d8f-bff54d56b72f.Text: [Try to surmise what destroyed the lab ceiling]

d835af5e-7dc8-4247-b2bc-410c8a3e3eff.Text: [Address your companions] "What do you make of all this?"

2e6c6fff-96f5-4161-a54f-73e2da1aa4db.Text: {n}The space around the hollow is littered with lumps of broken rockcrete. A feeble breeze blows through the ugly hole in the ceiling, stirring up whirlwinds of stone dust at your feet.{/n}

5f556bd8-68eb-47b0-b0d9-418be2ff5e43.Text: {n}Through the piled-up rocks, dirt, and thick dust, you are able to make out parts of fixtures that were ripped out of their sockets and thrown to the floor. Parts like these are used for fastening industrial girders in place at large manufactorums around the Imperium.{/n}

5f4f2181-2ec4-4476-811a-aba0c3a6341c.Text: {n}The pile of rocks, dirt, and thick dust densely covers the entire bottom of the hollow and the entire space around it. There is nothing of note here, just debris that the Haemonculus never bothered to clean up after returning to his lair.{/n}

2a211acc-43af-4efd-a690-51a1ee565bb4.Text: {n}The multiple marks on the broken pieces suggest that the ceiling and the layer of rock above it were shattered in an explosion. The details elude you.{/n}

ed204b7a-364a-46eb-a674-b43358a1629e.Text: {n}You study the edges of the breach carefully, reflect for a few minutes, and conclude that the hole in the lab ceiling was created by several powerful targeted explosions. After some more time, you note the characteristic marks on the debris and the walls. The ceiling was breached using melta charges.{/n}

8e60ea3d-389a-4642-be60-8eb2e6d7a356.Text: "They would if they were going to do business with representatives of Humanity." {n}Heinrix's voice is dull and quiet, as if the Interrogator has suddenly been drained of all his strength.{/n}

34f83e89-5d43-4a58-92c8-9e208a7539e5.Text: "Tervantias was... robbed? I really wish I could have seen his face the moment he looked upon his lair!" {n}Marazhai laughs mockingly, then looks around the room.{/n} "Although this place... is not a Haemonculus's lair. Too safe. Too shabby. More of a last refuge."

52074aae-42f4-4116-bab5-aac1f14280fb.Text: {n}The hole in the lab's vaulted ceiling and the hollow underneath it point you to the obvious conclusion: something broke into this room, ripped out a piece of the lab, and dragged it outside. You are, for now, mystified as to what that something was.{/n}

c57471d6-afe6-4087-932e-59102aaa0088.Text: {n}The Seneschal looks around, frowning.{/n} "I don't understand... Drukhari machinery and their toys seem out of place within these walls. They seem positively alien, in fact. These walls... why, this is the standard architecture of an Imperium bunker. Why would a xenos conduct their business in a place like this?"

d0a38728-e07b-4ff7-8e8d-9d3d6f954d0a.Text: "Cold Traders. Privateers. Rogue Traders..." {n}Heinrix breaks off, as if stopping himself at the last moment.{/n} "Mutually profitable commerce with xenos is not that uncommon, Abelard. And that is what went on in this place, a place built by humans and furnished by the Drukhari."

45be32dc-582e-4593-a552-f6d55f71b9b8.Text: "My kin were unable to find this place. The Dark Ones... would hardly have been content with a single trophy, even one as great as this. No. This was done crudely and quickly — behaviour more typical of mon-keigh."

3af93b4e-0c88-4adf-88bc-3bd8baed619e.Text: "The work is precise, though not the neatest. Whoever did this clearly knew what they were looking for and where to strike. Just look at the edges of the breach, shereen — they were definitely ripped apart by a targeted blast."

bab3f4c0-1e7f-414f-92d1-d59aa1a605c3.Text: "This world belongs to House Winterscale. But I don't believe... I refuse to believe His Lordship Calligos would ever collaborate with xenos. Dark red and brownish-green would envelop his figure every time the subject of hunting the enemies of Humanity was brought up. He... despised them. Hated them."

c1d6ddaf-029b-458a-a089-17d53c331d05.Text: {n}Whatever contraption this chamber used to house, judging by the size of the fixtures, it could have gone through the hole in the ceiling. The only question is: what was it? Although, given Tervantias's obsession with his "masterpiece," one could venture a guess.{/n}

2fbe3147-7079-4b65-804f-a4836d5f4bdd.Text: The rejuvenation procedure may have restored the body's health, but only to a degree. The time-stealer's tentacles have left their scars.

a888a8ae-3aa4-4ed4-a057-0255a02706bc.Text: "Break this altar! It's our only hope!"

9839cbf8-dc50-4eac-9d73-922997732824.Text: "Come to me, little mortals! We are going to have so much fun together..."

7510b088-9142-4932-8de8-e1d4fdb88ac0.Text: "Somebody open the door! Open the door before he gets me!"

b790bb79-a63b-4494-b252-babf1a025b49.Text: "It seems you have spent too long in the company of mon-keigh, Outcast. Why should their lives matter when retribution for the executioner of our world is at stake? Justice for our innocent brothers and sisters?"

42451ebd-1770-4f1b-bd36-7174bb5e115a.Text: "This is what we are here for, Outcast. Stretch out your hand, grasp the spear of vengeance together with us — and plunge it into the dark heart of the architect of torment."

07986f0a-4cb5-4517-9c18-8f4337aa6a43.Text: "You invaded this world, and I want to know why."

d3e1e1a5-9ab6-433c-bc0f-e09a05fd50a7.Text: "I need to know more about the Haemonculus."

d318500e-70ce-43ee-b150-d65470988113.Text: "I am here to resolve this conflict peacefully."

4cb773c3-61e3-457a-856a-20ce0a208e36.Text: "I do not support the methods of the xenos, but I understand their motives. Perhaps they could pay you compensation?"

6599b440-b0b3-4a4f-a3de-6e2ddf473c71.Text: "You lost your world and are now depriving others of theirs out of vengeance. Why do you think you are different?"

0c26d3bf-6227-4872-b1ff-e9f072325152.Text: "It looks like I can kill two grox with one bullet today."

80ebefd3-5bfa-4203-a8bb-5f6cf23e5c39.Text: "What are you talking about? I killed the Haemonculus in Commorragh with my own hands."

86500a00-1194-4643-b8a4-06fd6aa4463c.Text: "I will give you a chance, Yrliet. Stand by my side — or perish."

4d876ca6-bd6f-4583-b7d8-0f453ca24a57.Text: Spoke against Calligos killing the Aeldari on Quetza Temer.

bba41147-e86f-4a6d-8711-0b7acd9cade7.Text: "Your ships are destroyed, Crudarach is lost, and so are the Farseers. You sacrificed everything to attack this world. Why?"

f4246b40-55c9-4dff-8327-18c90adf83d5.Text: "By the vastness of space, can we not come to some agreement?"

61b8b428-3c1c-4dfc-b2ba-97779c941b9c.Text: "Your brothers and sisters are exhausted, you are trapped, and I am the only person who can change that."

7d3d1a02-7312-4fdc-93ef-548a9c5f6728.Text: "It is simple, xenos. Tell nothing but the truth if you want to live."

bbbd4625-f4dc-471c-b264-426467bef5fd.Text: [Attack] "Let us get down to business, Calligos."

128fb9fe-6067-4cf9-a035-1a82295484d3.Text: [Attack both sides] "I shall just get rid of you all."

f3f748f2-85cd-456a-b70c-3603d8164a0b.Text: "You call purging an entire world a decisive action?"

2b04428c-e889-4b5a-80d4-563f2232fc2b.Text: "What if I were to say it was my predecessor who was to blame for Crudarach's demise?"

bdec5b67-9160-46c9-9f93-eb97fd99e7e2.Text: "Yrliet, your kin butchered hundreds of thousands of people on this world in the name of vengeance. Is this the path you see for your people?"

ba433601-3535-4b85-bc1d-23590499db49.Text: "Look at yourself, Calligos. You are becoming a monster whose only desire is to kill."

b269aa8c-bb36-4af0-ae0c-77f4e95bb9ca.Text: "You no longer see profit beyond the thrill of the hunt. You and the xenos can help one another."

f843196a-83c0-4702-80be-d58a9ef3c739.Text: "I presume there is no avoiding the confrontation?"

3e667c1c-b80c-449c-95e8-c2c3253a656f.Text: "I do not want to kill you and you know it. You sacrificed everything in the name of your kin, and it is now the time to think about yourself."

29e534b8-1891-43a6-98c8-21efd77e8893.Text: "Enough talk. You will perish on this planet like the rest of the xenos."

3d43ff9c-bade-4601-81d7-e7ce780cc510.Text: "Says the one who has already betrayed me once without a second thought."

c0998e56-c003-49e9-8c2a-8d63e74cf488.Text: Proposed that Calligos and you both savour the slaughter of the Aeldari on Quetza Temer.

010f773f-8c32-440b-aca4-e9b21938f7bb.Text: [Attack the Aeldari] "Calligos, let us butcher these curs until the very ground is a gory mess of their bones and innards! More skulls for the lords of the Expanse!"

b583fae3-a71b-4083-ba2f-22c07a542c9e.Text: "The xenos had a valid reason to attack this world. I see no issue with sacrificing the lowborn if it helps a good cause."

f6c88eb4-1d88-48df-9f9f-3c1502215673.Text: Decided to fight against both the Aeldari and Calligos on Quetza Temer.

1ffcbef0-8e75-48ff-a57b-650b00c69fd8.Text: [Attack both sides] "I would rather get rid of you all."

d2a5fc6c-1029-4676-907f-14d2bec35f7a.Text: "Yrliet, I will permit your kin to explain themselves."

553ba489-3925-486b-b34a-e1dde0c949b5.Text: "Nocturne of Oblivion, it has certainly been a while. What are you doing here?"

5b1fa7cb-8e39-44b3-907f-b9c5eb2384f5.Text: [Attack] "We have tracked down the prey, Calligos. It is time to have some fun."

4a992243-75de-4ae5-b278-76bb74e26f8e.Text: Attacked the Aeldari on Quetza Temer.

2566fb78-3521-4f04-ae26-d6b3d221ee79.Text: [Attack] "You are guilty before this world and the Imperium. The time of retribution is at hand."

79c0df55-fb89-4f6c-b8ce-c4f4e5238bdc.Text: [Whisper] [Lie] "I will kill them myself after I find out what I need to know."

397a54fa-71fc-4b86-b152-c8a1647db968.Text: "Lay down your weapons, and I promise to judge you fairly."

8fd1e458-ac85-40ea-8d06-e98de95ac165.Text: "Do you still think your kin are worth saving?"

f4adf29a-1ebb-45b4-a9f1-9e83fa5a98f5.Text: [Attack the Aeldari] "We have nothing else to discuss."

57976787-60e7-450f-b207-5d3d1b192a08.Text: [Attack Calligos] "I think I can strike a deal with the xenos. With you, not so much."

deded2f5-ad15-4617-8f88-1a07e7b8b193.Text: {n}A stately Aeldari warrior steps forward, calmly looking at the intruders. His armour and its adornments gleam in the sun despite the traces of dried mud and caked-on blood.{/n} "Not a step further, mon-keigh." {n}The smooth voice of the xenos sounds out of place in the rough wilderness of Quetza Temer.{/n} "I grant you the mercy of leaving the emerald halls of the Children of Asuryan — begone and never return."

08243049-d6a0-4854-98cd-58ec7659f50d.Text: "Elantach." {n}Yrliet's face is covered with a patchwork of tiny scars. There are dark stains of clotted blood on her, and she holds her leg slightly bent, as if leaning on it would hurt. The {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Quetza_YrlietRunAway}time she has spent in the woods of Quetza Temer{/d} has not been without consequences.{/n}

7ed155d1-d1be-44ff-aedf-da46a6cefdea.Text: "And I do not! A glorious chase must end in a glorious battle, and I like these xenos! I will put the horned one's head above the holo-fireplace, and as for the shiny one... I will just chop his ugly mug into bits!"

b0be78dd-b9b0-4ab3-bf56-4ce41dc6898c.Text: "I knew you were rotten to the core, new blood. I am not surprised." {n}Calligos snarls like a wild beast.{/n} "The more trophies, the better. Blood for the Rogue Trader's throne!"

cc9655ec-0c84-44c5-804c-9ea35a06b99a.Text: {n}Despite their affected ease, most of the xenos are pushing themselves to their limit. They are exhausted, nervous, and frightened, even if they hide it well. This may have eluded your companions, but not you.{/n}

2269a2d5-cbe0-44ad-9cdc-86457c094428.Text: "However, should you turn back and leave the camp, and then do not impede our departure... I swear not a single mon-keigh will come to harm on this planet. Or on any of your worlds."

0c46a67a-b2e7-47e6-a880-2a1dfaddaed0.Text: "I sacrificed everything for the Children of Asuryan. It was, it is, and it will be true. And you stood by me and accepted that." {n}The spirit stone in Yrliet's chestplate is pulsing a bit brighter than usual.{/n} "So I will accept your choice in return. This is where you and I... go our separate ways."

fd9d49c5-dd39-4c6f-8fb7-06766fbd6f9a.Text: "The Haemonculus is a threat to both our species, elantach. You know well what his dark heart and perverted mind are capable of. Tervantias must be destroyed, and my kin have taken on the role of vengeful blade."

bf8bb8d8-d1e9-404b-aa94-362f6447fd95.Text: {n}Yrliet ponders your words for a moment and nods curtly.{/n} "You are not wrong, elantach. I have had enough of the blind arrogance of my kin. Of meekly following the blind who are supposed to see the future but who drive my people toward death and suffering instead. I am an Outcast. And I have done my duty to the children of Crudarach. They will have to pay for their own mistakes themselves."

1aaeebab-3914-4de3-8903-3212118b8ea6.Text: "That's how I like it! Fewer words, more blood for the Rogue Trader's throne!"

c5540b2e-c035-44d3-a865-42e27e6fea04.Text:
{n}A {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ZanniNotEnemy}sorrowful sigh{/d} comes from beneath Nocturne of Oblivion's mask.{/n}
"About my neck a loathsome coiling snake
Has latched itself and swallowed down my lines.
So trite an end tastes bitter on the tongue,
For death awaits, my Merchant Vagabond,
The curtain now will serve you as a shroud.
Enough of words — our dance will speak the rest."

436ada73-e2c8-4344-9221-5c3c72e78141.Text:
"Your sense of timing, Merchant, lacks finesse,
You sing midst lightning flash and thunderous boom,
A choice deranged and deadly — I confess,
I glimpse myself in your strange dance with doom."

e5e2b311-1950-4f22-afb4-2ce96d2ad6be.Text: "I exact my compensation in blood, {name}." {n}Calligos sneers.{/n} "You would be wise to remember that, too."

e015c039-e090-42cb-9b2e-a3f3bc46e79c.Text: "What is the meaning of this, new blood?" {n}Winterscale narrows his eyes in suspicion, clutching the handle of his power axe.{/n}

7242cf38-41d0-4d09-b411-2d32549f2311.Text: {n}The Aeldari warrior does not appear to comprehend his words.{/n}

d3bf772b-0327-4d64-8a60-e989160f6b37.Text: {n}The Aeldari warrior considers your words.{/n} "We lost the treasures of Crudarach, but the memory of the Farseers holds knowledge, the value of which is difficult to describe in the mon-keigh's primitive tongue. If this helps to avoid bloodshed here as well as later... I am {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}willing to come to an agreement{/d}."

1e20b432-b820-4410-8a82-6004db677058.Text: "What are you talking about, elantach?" {n}Yrliet fingers brush your shoulder before she draws her hand back.{/n} "Could it be that your designs are murkier than the foul waters of the Dark City?"

72bc76d2-e6fc-4c42-a42c-ef377af21f4c.Text: "And you believed you could dispose of him so easily? The minds of mon-keigh are dull and undiscerning indeed." {n}The Aeldari throws up his hands in irritation.{/n} "That was only one of Tervantias's many bodies — bodies which he is capable of growing from a scrap of his own flesh."

ab32d53d-4add-4f95-a037-09b642badef7.Text: "Were you not the one who welcomed me back, elantach? Why?" {n}Yrliet's face is flushed with anger and shame, almost making her hiss.{/n} "Ah... I see it now. The resentment wrapped around your heart like a venomous snake, and you were powerless to tame it. Or simply chose not to. In that case... we have nothing more to discuss."

4f2bb7da-2d84-4598-ac40-89e95c13db7b.Text: "You fancy yourself strong enough, pup?" {n}An inhuman roar erupts from Winterscale's throat, and his Arch-Militant smiles serenely.{/n}

b989ae96-053a-4e72-891f-f5b97ddc11b4.Text: {n}The warrior looks at you tiredly.{/n} "We did not attack this world, elantach. The last of Crudarach's children assembled once more to scour the master of flesh Tervantias from the memory of the universe — the Haemonculus who abducted and tortured the Farseers from our craftworld. We learned that he is hiding on this world, but something prevents our Farseers from discovering his lair. And so we were forced to act... decisively."

8d5cde2c-9eac-4180-8b14-86ee14b419ec.Text: {n}The warrior sighs tiredly.{/n} "We did not attack this world, mon-keigh. The last of Crudarach's children assembled once more to scour the master of flesh Tervantias from the memory of the universe — the Haemonculus who abducted and tortured the Farseers from our craftworld. We learned that he is hiding on this world, but something prevents our Farseers from discovering his lair. And so we were forced to act... decisively."

a7b46671-1d14-45e3-91dc-90e98b854675.Text: {n}The warriors behind the leader freeze in uncomfortable silence, but he does not appear to be taken aback by your words.{/n} "You may be discerning, mon-keigh, but only half of what you say is true."

09359731-1aa3-4c24-8903-d3e101f3fd7e.Text: "The more prey, the merrier, I say. And besides, I do not yet have a Rogue Trader's head among my trophies. Blood for the Winterscale throne!"

0c1d50a1-c8e9-44fc-87e8-8342722cecaa.Text: "Our Farseers... the ones we managed to save... could not name the exact location of the master of flesh. Even after our ships circled the world for a third time, something prevented them from seeing the truth. Something... powerful. We knew your patrols would soon discover our presence. And so we decided to do something else — to exterminate the Haemonculus along with the world he had chosen as his refuge."

d1811419-af13-4732-b0ed-7ea4485de47a.Text: {n}A smile twists the Aeldari's features for the first time.{/n} "We survived the demise of our craftworld, wandered the darkness of space without a home or protection, without a family or hope for the future. We were tormented, butchered, driven insane, and sold off for the amusement of our dark kin. Do you really think a handful of mon-keigh can intimidate us? There are worse things in the galaxy, and you do not fear oblivion once you have survived them."

bb0699ab-044d-4729-9a28-22637ef0067a.Text: "So this is how the gods decided to end it." {n}The Aeldari makes an unfamiliar gesture, and the warriors reach for their weapons.{/n} "Children of Asuryan, fight with the fury of Kaela Mensha Khaine!"

1c37a731-cb46-4e3a-bbba-f271caf4230e.Text: "What? Why?" {n}Taken aback by your statement, Winterscale lowers his power axe for a moment.{/n}

85c5278e-5e62-410f-a2de-139168e8c828.Text: {n}The gazes of the assembled xenos turn to you, their eyes piercing you like the points of many swords.{/n}

ccf0a198-ebac-47d2-abb0-c67bf2adf153.Text: "Stop tugging at my conscience, {name}. You sound vile, like the Incendia from my nightmares come to life to ruin the mood!" {n}Calligos grimaces in frustration. Your words seem to not have angered him, but upset him.{/n}

8b205f13-2822-4b5e-a708-4dc432abee8c.Text: "At least I am killing enemies of the Imperium. What about you, {name}? Whose side are you on?"

4557d537-6eca-4922-82c3-f90fe10e1d76.Text: "What do the xenos and the fanatical zealots of the Imperium have in common? The answer is simple — both are willing to sacrifice billions of their subjects." {n}The sullen grin that follows does not become Jae's face at all.{/n}

ea91998a-6c35-4b08-9b99-42283e45ac02.Text: "How about we wring the necks of the puny vermin, Aett-Vater?"

f5e47bd3-122a-43c3-bcf1-02cf45f4dacd.Text: "You may hide your anger behind a facade of benevolence all you want, cousin, except I can see straight through you — a dejected, lost, and frightened soul. Are you not worried about your precious Path, hmm? Or have you decided to study our arts at last?"

b1a5920b-2c72-41c5-aac6-1248f1d4ba62.Text: {n}The Aeldari warrior purses his lips and glares at Marazhai furiously but does not grace him with a reply.{/n}

2c278fdc-12c5-4a4e-95db-dc172b7e7ffc.Text: {n}Your words startle Yrliet, who looks at the assembled Aeldari with uncertainty.{/n} "The elantach... is right, Shairenkhei. Does the Path of the Warrior teach you to sacrifice countless lives to achieve your goals? The Children of Asuryan are not the executioners of worlds, nor slayers of the innocent."

956e80ca-0585-4c84-86e8-bdaf11f28466.Text: "The master of flesh is here, elantach!" {n}Yrliet inhales hungrily, doing her best to remain calm.{/n} "We. Must. Destroy. Him."

6e6779dd-1f21-4fad-b365-ebb79bfa57de.Text: "What is that I hear? {name} von Valancius {mf|himself|herself}, a Rogue Trader of the Imperium and a loyal servant of the God-Emperor, goading me into betraying Humanity?" {n}Calligos arches an eyebrow mockingly.{/n} "It did not take long for the power granted by the Warrant to go to your head."

a5301132-2b1e-4b6f-a241-678c784aa9b4.Text: "Oh, I say!" {n}Winterscale's booming voice sounds like the roar of a wild animal.{/n} "Only if you hand over all the trophies and personally bring me the heads of these two on a plate at the victory feast."

42283771-bdaa-4264-8823-76bda3a1232a.Text: "Learn to lie first, new blood." {n}Calligos dismisses you with contempt.{/n}

6076e663-d729-428e-8949-f271e4e8d0f5.Text: "Do you see?" {n}The warrior addresses the Solitaire standing next to him.{/n} "All mon-keigh are the same — wild, foolish, avaricious. Empty shells. There is nothing interesting about them."

6658eaa0-f588-4f89-bf53-f7969666cd82.Text: "I almost had no hope of hearing something like that! Blood for the Rogue Trader's throne! Drive them toward me!"

3a1fa9f9-d83c-4fe7-8cc5-235da17acc71.Text: {n}The Aeldari watches Calligos closely.{/n} "After everything the elantach has done for my people, I am willing to answer {mf|his|her} questions. But you had better not make any sudden moves, mon-keigh."

add04cad-d41e-449c-836b-527da5b49156.Text: "I do not think we have anything to discuss either, mon-keigh. The deeds of your kin have spoken louder than words." {n}There is grief on the xenos's face.{/n} "My home, my family, my people, my Crudarach... Everything is gone because of you."

27185b8f-a836-4d86-9ca2-3e921543dd38.Text: {n}Winterscale meaningfully raises an eyebrow.{/n} "And you still deem him worthy of conversation?"

ee5ddbd3-33b2-4151-a01f-2ac95e4f81c9.Text: "The master of flesh from Commorragh... He is here?" {n}Yrliet ignores the veiled confession and inhales hungrily, doing her best to remain calm.{/n} "We. Must. Destroy. Him."

a0a5a975-a84d-48ba-bd18-3a7a75a1e337.Text: {n}Yrliet's eyes grow wide with anger and dismay.{/n} "Does the Path of the Warrior teach you to sacrifice countless lives to achieve your goals? The Children of Asuryan are not the executioners of worlds, nor slayers of the innocent."

8177c156-e33e-4424-a275-09ce5a2366b0.Text: "I never doubted it, elantach. To you, the deeds of my kin may appear cruel or even criminal, but spending enough time among the mon-keigh granted me clarity of vision. Sometimes you treat your own kind even worse in pursuit of baser goals or personal gain." {n}Yrliet proudly squares her shoulders.{/n}

6880f61d-80f9-4ea3-8499-5e43dcf4c5a5.Text: "I... am growing increasingly doubtful. Although I understand why my kin have acted this way. Why they took on the role of vengeful blade... You know well what the dark heart and perverted mind of the Haemonculus are capable of. He must be stopped!" {n}Yrliet's sharply angled features are softened by sadness and uncertainty.{/n}

8e945de7-81b1-4d18-b357-a81a46fe322a.Text: {n}The Harlequin's metaphor implies he has been accompanying the surviving Aeldari for a while now. It is not clear to you what "hearth" he is talking about, but perhaps he has managed to find them a new home.{/n}

d186185f-b5be-4983-9908-0dbd0629200a.Text: "I never doubted it, elantach. The Haemonculus is a threat to both our species. You know well what his dark heart and perverted mind are capable of. Tervantias must be destroyed, and my kin have taken on the role of vengeful blade."

92740526-c69a-4d94-bcb4-c1fda730445f.Text:
"A tapestry complex is peace, and one
That many threads demands for warp and weft.
For this design, three wills together spun
Its greed will sate in hands of weaver deft.
The gruesome scars of past distrust bewailed
With compact's subtle gauze shall now be veiled."

09f0392c-499d-48b2-a8e0-ab1cfadd6590.Text: "You may donate all of your worlds to the Imperium, the xenos, Chorda and the Inquisitor — see if I care. But when the enemies come to MY world, when it is MY world that falls into turmoil, the heads of those responsible go up on pikes."

23c51983-4064-47c0-af75-dde83f2eb7a5.Text: "I do not wish to fight you, elantach, but nor do I wish my kin to come to harm." {n}Yrliet's tired gaze shifts away from you toward Calligos Winterscale.{/n} "Stand down. Let the Children of Asuryan leave this world. Its land has already been soaked with the blood of our species."

bccea7ae-4db2-4c23-a3a0-ef853fd7100e.Text: "Even if I wanted to pay you off, we lost the wealth of Crudarach along with the craftworld itself. Bargain for my life with a mon-keigh? I would rather go into the eternal night."

17637543-d052-49cb-9210-5ec089fde0c8.Text: "How dare you compare a dragon to a lizard? Starlight to the dim glow of a guttering candle?" {n}There is fury in the Aeldari's eyes... as well as doubt.{/n} "Make no mistake about your inferior species — a single Child of Asuryan is worth thousands of your kind."

3805eb92-3161-4727-bc83-9f039fd1db6c.Text: "We shall be heading back now. What kind of hunting is it when the prey does not even struggle in your grasp? I'm disappointed!" {n}Calligos flashes a provoking grin.{/n} "And don't you think I am going to forget about your words and promises, {name}. We shall revisit that later."

776a50b0-00dd-4b29-89e8-f6f3d05759d4.Text: "I do not know about you, {name}, but these xenos bastards are giving me the creeps!" {n}Calligos shifts his excited gaze from the Aeldari warrior to the Solitaire and back.{/n} "This one, in the motley. I want to kill him. Now."

b6fa335d-7428-4de4-8f85-59ec8c78ca44.Text: {n}Worten the Grey bares his teeth in anticipation and clutches the hilt of his sword.{/n}

bd4bb4ce-983f-477a-9ba0-f1f109ac9f16.Text: {n}A stately Aeldari warrior steps forward, calmly looking at the intruders. His armour and its adornments gleam in the sun despite the traces of dried mud and caked-on blood.{/n} "The Farseers instructed me to send you away, mon-keigh." {n}The smooth voice of the xenos sounds out of place in the rough wilderness of Quetza Temer.{/n} "However, I recently stopped meekly heeding their counsel, and besides, my sister is among you... I am curious to hear the Outcast's tidings."

91c098b0-93bf-496c-9594-21c3110af65b.Text: "And I will become your scourge!" {n}Calligos howls. His eyes are brimming with inhuman fury.{/n} "Purge Quetza Temer of filth! Blood for the Rogue Trader's throne!"

9e3ae65b-fa05-4c36-bed6-581e13fe5e0a.Text: {n}The warrior stands motionless, only occasionally casting a worried glance at the Solitaire.{/n}

e8da6f0a-c29a-4b94-8ec1-65aa9a9aa9ac.Text: "You overstep, {name}. Quetza Temer is my world and my demesne! And I have already passed sentence on the xenos bastards."

22106bf8-c675-43ed-bfc5-f9af6b767544.Text:
"True enmity unerring blinds two kinds:
Youths fierce and ravenous with seething blood,
And old who refuge find in arrogance.
But past revulsion's hood they cannot see
The single path that both of them unites.
Will two fall into step and dance as one?
The laugh of jest unending knows alone."

4b9cd05b-e13e-4496-ab86-52f2d1fbd4eb.Text: "Act decisively, you ashmags? You call mowing down two-thirds of the world's population 'acting decisively'?" {n}Jae sticks out her augmented hand, and the mechanical joints squeal piteously under the weight of her indecent gestures.{/n}

82a01373-9f88-44b8-8f98-eb3b92db6067.Text: {n}Shairenkhei rests his hand on Yrliet's shoulder encouragingly, but he is looking at you.{/n} "Our Farseers... the ones we managed to save... could not name the exact location of the master of flesh. Even after our ships circled the world for a third time, something prevented them from seeing the truth. Something... powerful. We knew your patrols would soon discover our presence. And so we decided to do something else — to exterminate the Haemonculus along with the world he had chosen as his refuge."

3ec2a7e6-a64c-4c57-8dec-753e527ebbc2.Text:
"So many names we hang on villainy:
Deceit and cunning, guile and treachery.
Though mon-keigh know them well in any guise —
The trap slams shut before your very eyes."

fc4d62d6-b947-4dbd-b63f-5c11db26fd26.Text: {n}The Aeldari shrugs vaguely.{/n} "The mon-keigh are flooding the galaxy at the speed of a meteor shower, and this world will repopulate... eventually. Is a single world not worth eliminating a powerful enemy who threatens hundreds of such worlds, both yours and those of my kin?"

ed27d427-41d7-463c-8a91-9c8ee739812d.Text:
"With thirst for blood, that wine of dark delight,
Appeared a Beast in human hide, and with
Him one who scorned all barricades and blight —
A Merchant who the door now opens wide.
But what awaits beyond this gaping portal?
The lead alone who snubs the stage will say:
Will boards be spared the brunt of combat mortal?
Or will the dance of blood conclude this play?"
{n}Nocturne of Oblivion {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ZanniEnemy}abstractedly adjusts his mournful mask{/d}.{/n}

da8e8cc7-d9bb-47a0-a075-58e65044f6ef.Text: {n}A stately Aeldari warrior steps forward, calmly looking at the intruders. His armour and its adornments gleam in the sun despite the traces of dried mud and caked-on blood.{/n} "The Farseers instructed me to send you away, mon-keigh." {n}The smooth voice of the xenos sounds out of place in the rough wilderness of Quetza Temer.{/n} "However, I recently stopped meekly heeding their counsel. My sister, Yrliet the Outcast, wishes to speak to you. And I will grant her this chance."

7452ce1e-1beb-4226-9aee-a369867d731c.Text: {n}A tense silence pervades the ruins. The stillness is disturbed only by the wind rustling through the centuries-old canopy.{/n}

fc8dd0b7-694c-45f5-b550-73afda547df7.Text: {n}Yrliet's gaze wanders from Calligos to the Solitaire, from the Solitaire to the Aeldari warrior, and back again. An outcast among her kin and strangers alike, a sorrowful burden that not all can bear.{/n}

6d0048a1-bca7-4bd0-9002-ecd847a6b936.Text: {n}The Aeldari cast confused glances at their champion.{/n} "A {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}temporary alliance{/d}? So be it. Children of Asuryan, fight with the fury of Kaela Mensha Khaine!"

6c1439bc-868f-426a-99f6-43874457561f.Text: {n}There is no trace of the bored Calligos from a few moments ago. The Rogue Trader is now closely studying the potential battlefield, his enemies... and the heads he intends to claim as trophies.{/n}

8aaca292-4d76-44bf-b028-0a177ae5fdb9.Text: "Who would believe you after what you have said, mon-keigh? No. We are not going to rely on someone so weak in spirit."

d3190466-7306-4ab1-ae70-b083cdfd14dd.Text: {n}Winterscale sneers viciously.{/n} "Let us say I believe you, this once. But there will not be a second time."

48b79672-71a5-4c22-8492-9c8886216ea3.Text: "I did warn you not to test my patience, new blood." {n}Calligos grabs his axe and charges at you, followed by his entire retinue.{/n}

de5e8e16-32bc-45ac-8c1a-9ee0930f62b3.Text: {n}The warrior brushes Calligos away like a bothersome fly.{/n} "We are not seeking your justice, mon-keigh. We are yearning for retribution."

fbfb3b24-b425-46da-b0a6-c8e563216472.Text: {n}The Aeldari warrior glares at the Solitaire.{/n} "So you knew, Arebennian! We will talk about this later. As for right now... The mon-keigh has left me no choice."

a3aea3d9-91b9-4f02-afc3-62cc33ba6104.Text:
"Vain rhetoric — a masterful display!
Your temper, brother mine, you ought to quell.
Bravado has no place within this play —
Indeed, the Merchant's proved this all too well.
This actor excellent, who did alight
Upon the stage, now will this piece complete
By choosing a finale apposite:
Who shall survive, and who their doom shall meet?"
{n}Nocturne of Oblivion's mournful horned mask {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ZanniNotEnemy}avidly tracks your face{/d}.{/n}

6a99afdc-8873-4e89-a39c-ea7b0faee6b0.Text: "We were reluctant to shed blood on this land, to begin with. But your companion decided otherwise — he shot down our vessels, chased us into the woods, harried and hounded the survivors..." {n}The Aeldari's eyes gleam in the sunlight.{/n}

d1224fbe-8847-4ece-8894-8b50288839f2.Text: "I do not need any prophecy to tell you this, Lord Captain... You are in for a fight. A nasty fight."

23b83d97-3aab-421b-8677-a38b0f3f9416.Text: "And I will finish what I started!" {n}Winterscale glares impatiently.{/n}

cb46510c-3527-4b15-ad1f-8ed827755551.Text: "I do not believe a single word, xenos."

140cc773-7522-49d0-91e1-a3825d80b28a.Text: "But spending enough time among the mon-keigh granted me clarity of vision. Once you stop valuing the lives of others, be they your kin, strangers, or enemies, you gradually become a monster yourself. And one day someone will come to stop you."

d47c0cb3-f392-4e13-867f-53edef885e00.Text: "Throne take you, and all the misfortunes in the galaxy along with you!" {n}Winterscale gives you a clap on the shoulder. The expression on his face is mysterious and almost sad.{/n} "I must confess that all this dismal talk has given me a migraine and made my old wounds ache. So you want to save these xenos? Suit yourself! By my grace, I entrust you with the lives of the enemies of Humanity. Have fun!"

e77681d6-4116-4a7b-ad27-5a2bd93b80ec.Text: "That can be arranged, xenos." {n}Calligos chuckles nastily.{/n} "The only compensation I accept is blood!"

ee7c8a1f-be2d-467f-a483-46f9f3173724.Text: {n}Winterscale looks over the ruins and salutes his entourage with a gesture only he can understand.{/n} "My patience has run out, {name}. Enough words. Drive the prey toward me, and my hounds will assist."

5baefceb-7c68-4f44-bd6c-a600500a2cc0.Text: "Time to crush skulls!" {n}Worten slams his iron fist against his armour, and Winterscale's vassals draw their weapons.{/n}

cd45b1bf-b799-4212-a728-8ea8a108fc5c.Text: {n}The Harlequin is being his usual self. His answer only leaves you with more questions that are just as pointless to ask as the previous one.{/n}

69f55fc5-3df8-444f-86fd-2f1188bbe78b.Text: "Playing with your prey like a cat? Fine, new blood, you are still young. Just remember that patience is not my strong suit."

cec0b26f-5ff6-42dd-b441-de8c17abbd0e.Text: "I do not know about you, {name}, but these xenos bastards are giving me the creeps!" {n}Calligos shifts his excited gaze from the Aeldari warrior to Yrliet, and from her to the Solitaire.{/n} "That one, in the motley. I want his head. Now."

c85bebfe-e07a-46de-8aa6-5436567a5154.Text: "Do you understand now, elantach? The one responsible for the demise of my home. The one to blame for the suffering you had to endure in the streets of the Dark City... He is somewhere on this world. And very close, too. We must find him..." {n}Yrliet pauses, carefully choosing her words.{/n} "And write the closing chapter of this sorrowful tale."

30c48e99-c696-46d1-b5c8-f613014683f7.Text: "I always knew how your path would end, elantach. I knew... but I still hoped for a different outcome." {n}Yrliet nods curtly, but her bitter gaze betrays her true feelings.{/n} "Ready your weapon, mon-keigh. Our fate will be decided here and now."

c9ed2d23-ebe0-4c98-a9d3-3005d6c11901.Text: {n}Calligos' mouth foams with rage and anticipation, and his eyes become bloodshot. He emits a guttural scream:{/n} "Blood for the Rogue Trader's throne! Skulls for the lords of the Expanse!"

0dfc5012-bd44-44f1-a074-73afb1bdee28.Text: {n}The Arch-Militant smiles so widely you fear his mouth may split and reveal several extra rows of teeth. His deafening inhuman bellow fills you with power and thirst, a desire to rip, tear, and exterminate.{/n}

23353a0e-7ab8-474c-a61d-8873c8bc75c3.Text: {n}Yrliet raises her weapon.{/n} "Enough, {name}. Your soul has already been drained by the Enemy — there is no turning back. I will end your bloody path with my own hand."

6dd23e63-58af-466d-abe3-fbb962625be1.Text: "There has been less good hunting to be had in the Expanse since your arrival, new blood. If the xenos hold useful information about the distant stars... that is a reason to consider your offer."

8c9840f8-3352-4bc2-ba07-7850ca9efb74.Text: "But his immortality has a limit: resurrection requires reagents, equipment, energy — the fleshmaster had those in abundance in Commorragh, but now he is on the run and vulnerable. And while the Haemonculus has not yet returned to full strength, there is a chance to destroy him forever."

1956fccb-0b96-4ec3-85f8-953023877f6d.Text: {n}The Solitaire mockingly presses a finger to the mask's lips, indicating that he is {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ZanniEnemy}not going to grace you with an answer{/d}.{/n}

cf31063f-dd49-436e-99ce-65514d6b84f6.Text: {n}A stately Aeldari warrior steps forward, calmly looking at the intruders. His armour and its adornments gleam in the sun despite the traces of dried mud and caked-on blood.{/n} "My people have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}heard about you{/d}, elantach." {n}The smooth voice of the xenos sounds out of place in the rough wilderness of Quetza Temer.{/n} "Are you here to help us deliver justice? Or will behave as most mon-keigh would and betray those you once helped?"

d1e9b57d-9643-4cf7-87f1-e3e31975832e.Text: {n}The xenos have made their camp among the ruins of an ancient city of the Imperium. Only the alien growths of the xenotech and the wreckage of the Aeldari ship disturb the picture of centuries-old devastation and rebirth.{/n}

86f0c29c-d556-418e-86bf-4df5c130ddf2.Text: {n}Despite their meagre weaponry and flimsy shelters, the xenos are ready to attack at any moment. Their bodies are relaxed, but their minds remain cold and focused.{/n}

382a03e3-b0c5-45d3-b222-0eabcd6e313a.Text: "Your kin had a valid reason to attack this world. I see no issue with sacrificing the lowborn if it helps a good cause."

9657f4c1-6dc8-4f1d-9860-4f90627d3f4a.Text: "It does not work that way, new blood. You either pick one enemy or have to deal with both!" {n}Winterscale's grin is growing wider with every word.{/n}

0102501e-5881-430d-a5f5-a3075389d52b.Text: "I am sick and tired of xenos and Rogue Traders alike. Sort it out among yourselves!"

69e39ac8-bddf-423e-a0fd-976791002716.Text: "I will not say a word until you let my kin depart from this world." {n}The warrior squares his shoulders, but whether out of fatigue or to make his words more impactful, it is hard to say.{/n}

0c29709e-3add-4800-8e84-a8347682b009.Text: "I could not care less about your interests, {name}. You know what I have been scouring these cursed woods for these last thirty days and nights. Don't you dare ruin my fun!" {n}Calligos speaks calmly and almost quietly, which makes his words sound even more ominous.{/n}

f715db2c-eb20-42c8-b20f-1b82a61d3bfa.Text: "Tell me about the Haemonculus. Where is he?"

acac3f11-fd5f-4a90-aaea-010d47f92c99.Text: "I thought I had already figured out the mon-keigh. But you, elantach, chose to walk side by side with me all this way, to earn new scars of the soul, to endure the horrors of Commorragh... only to spurn me at the very end?" {n}Yrliet pulls away and slowly reaches for her weapon.{/n}

1035f005-288e-43d6-9ad3-5acb4f422504.Text: "What are you doing, elantach? My people are not as lenient as I am, they will not understand or forgive!" {n}Yrliet backs away from you as if from a deranged psyker.{/n} "You have just drawn a line between us, {name}. Forgive me, but I will stay on the other side."

94535639-fc6e-42d0-87cc-dc306cfbfd2f.Text: "O Blood God, accept this sacrifice! Skulls for the skull throne!"

8fa30964-492f-4349-936b-cb0ad075d7e4.Text: "The master gave orders to be prepared. We're moving out soon. Worten is prepared. Killing xenos is what Worten loves to do."

098ac195-49c5-4c35-9979-24ae098368f9.Text: Artefacts from a war that ravaged Quetza Temer in ancient times. Now only moss and creepers reign over these forgotten trophies.

2db85d63-6813-4adc-819c-f95cfdd20c6f.Text: The Winterscale search shuttle crashed during landing. Neither the pilot nor the scouting team survived.

6121e26d-6d53-43c1-9de6-29ff39acb885.Text: "That's Calligos Winterscale's Seneschal, Aerdrig van Tornsten! By the God-Emperor, he was sliced in two with a single blow!"

c7078b74-35ed-4993-8bfe-99f9543817e7.Text: "There's no point in thinking about the weaklings who couldn't survive in this place. The master doesn't need weaklings in his retinue. The master needs the best."

a1c4877c-96b7-4da6-ab89-f4c6f411799f.Text: The putrid stench of decaying flesh comes from the enforcer bodies that have not yet been torn apart by local wildlife.

76de57c7-6ad7-4bf3-8c31-6920a4c162e0.Text: Judging by the traces of blood, the xenos attacked the camp from high ground, reluctant to get too close.

a9163d2b-7902-4d40-b3c1-9d66c2443443.Text: "Am I the only one feeling that something... wrong happened here? Something we're not seeing and cannot understand?"

f83630f7-f593-4b7e-8921-8d77172a0783.Text: "I can still smell blood. This place is drenched with it. How many mon-keigh died here at the hands of my enraged cousins? A dozen? Three dozen?"

ec7c3a9c-0264-40c0-ae6a-29bfedb83cf8.Text: "You know nothing, Asssuryani. Your kinssspeople are weak. We may have retreated but they lossst that battle."

7acd361c-0fed-4e00-bc3a-1eff729b74d8.Text: "The accursed xenos fell upon us late at night and slaughtered three enforcer squads! We had to retreat into the woods. As for Aerdrig... I knew he didn't make it when the damned forest closed behind us again."

3627b0bd-6ab9-482d-a25b-0195fef2cacc.Text: "The camp was routed. Was it... the fury of my kin? They fought monsters from among the mon-keigh, only to become no different than monsters themselves."

24782680-7b92-43df-b909-83fadc2dc5e0.Text: Calligos Winterscale set up camp amid the remains of an ancient military encampment.

d7524cec-f780-4a34-9dee-1a75220ce64c.Text: The markings on the containers date back about 500 Terran years. Inside are decayed remains and unusable equipment.

1b4511e0-1fa8-4d23-84d3-bc51555fc7bd.Text: "This forest... Does it move of its own accord? Amazing! I have read about vegetation behaving in this way on some Imperium worlds, but I never hoped to see such unique plants for myself!"

f1787126-c429-481c-a6f8-0dfbc5756c46.Text: Lush overgrowth has sprung up in seconds, blocking the way back. The trail is gone.

4215bf82-e0ff-4454-bc10-fbe521cccac5.Text: "Throne take us! This is the trap Winterscale walked into, and now we're in it too. Rampant forest growth. The plants spring up and wither at an incredible pace that makes keeping track of movement through them all but impossible."

46df89d0-ad54-46f7-999d-2c50468f366b.Text: "Ha! Did you see it? Those bushes popped up right behind me! And the craziest part is, I'm not sensing any warp influence here! Is it... doing it by itself? Is it alive?"

dbcfda5c-17d7-4301-895d-abc3285735c7.Text: The sweetish smell of decomposition comes from the woven baskets. For whatever reason, the fruit was left to rot under the scorching sun.

e6c272aa-5e89-4db1-b700-f4db7387af92.Text: The fruit gatherers' bodies have been savaged and gnawed on by local wildlife. They likely were prevented from leaving the area by the moving forest.

47ffd411-d22a-4669-b188-189625758f87.Text: Fruit and sweet tree sap used to be harvested in this clearing, but now the branches are weighed down by overripe fruit.

f91be1f9-5bcd-4a50-924e-fe9b1b63260a.Text: "O Aendriel, Calainaen, and Ytrisha... The mon-keigh will pay for your suffering!"

4b9a99fd-7f63-476f-b960-e6bef367c7af.Text: "Suffering? Their spirit stones are shattered, Ssirtan, and She Who Thirsts has long finished her feast! We will destroy them. Every mon-keigh who— did you hear that?"

2d473900-6eef-4bdf-80aa-0f49943aaaec.Text: "The soul destroyers are back! Khaine, fill our hearts with fury!"

ae670e18-3a51-48a3-b66d-0c3ec219d65b.Text: "Relent, for Isha's mercy! We are here to help you!"

632c783f-48c6-47e7-8c38-b138025a3a5d.Text: To the scene of the slaughter

4e406f81-afb0-4fdf-9009-a99a171b48f1.Text: The body of House Winterscale's Seneschal has been dismembered and his bones picked clean by wild beasts.

c69bf8a0-1f3a-4e90-9b85-329b44af56ad.Text: The body of House Winterscale's Seneschal has been picked clean by wild beasts, but the marks on his spine and his split skull suggest that the man was sliced in two with a power weapon.
