1256f6ba-a205-4109-8677-d1d8ac012ef5.Text: "ATTENTION: vox-broadcast impossible. Error: ?%&#-/0%. ATTENTION: botanical threat. Level: Alpha II."

a636cebd-68e1-443c-811a-9ed17d05e6af.Text: Mould, birds, and rodents have ruined these fruits of the local vegetation.

d425aed5-3e71-4e0f-b534-b8c459468116.Text: Rusted containers for transporting supplies. Their markings indicate that they are several centuries old.

5f7d9c69-39a1-47da-941e-03b3e01baf0b.Text: "This? Just a random skirmish, unworthy of attention. The real hunt is still ahead for the master and his guests."

2fdfbcbb-391c-42b5-9d82-bee3d061837f.Text: "The aftermath of Calligos Winterscale's hunt, I presume."

c7ddf648-2c39-4ce6-95a6-f0628278e987.Text: "Pain, agony, fear, madness... What a wonderful cocktail of suffering — and we missed it!"

658742c8-7115-4e96-8be1-15d357d2732e.Text: "Hsss... You don't have the ssslightest idea..."

d725879a-2e0d-40fa-9214-0ea101930429.Text: "Ah, a fine battle was fought here! I'd gladly lop the heads off a couple of filthy xenos right now, too!"

fee0d878-e252-46a0-8b7b-acb1bbc56722.Text: "The cowardly bastards jumped out of an ambush and wounded my Navigator. And paid for it. I hacked each of them to pieces myself!"

c7829af3-e9b4-4fc9-8be5-4e9a905fa846.Text: "Gracious Isha... Only a true monster is capable of such an atrocity."

d88ab978-276c-497b-97e7-72e652cce2f0.Text: The bodies of the Aeldari have been hacked to pieces with extreme brutality. Their wounds indicate it was done by a power weapon of some kind. The soil under the bodies has turned a rusty brown from the gore.

3aa2b8b6-9751-4810-86e4-ff817b604e06.Text: "God-Emperor, preserve the souls of Your children who vanished without trace in this world's impassable forests."

b7853793-1147-4ae7-b0f3-1e80d45d01a4.Text: "I... hear... the voices of the dead! They ran into the forests — from the shadow that loomed over this world. They fought. They fought and... lost."

c990dff0-a182-48a4-a6c7-be23b0121269.Text: "Throne blast it, this place is practically a mass grave! Rank-and-file Guardsmen heaped up outside while the big bug kicked the bucket inside. Ha! The Imperium never changes."

45a4b39c-1b41-49aa-9a59-0fc24a93a158.Text: "I am registering a non-standard use of a field structure. The ritual burial of these remains does not conform to Astra Militarum protocols. Hypothesis: the rite was performed by the local inhabitants."

1e63fa73-4ec0-4a8a-809c-82a44b090fa4.Text: "Hallowed ground. Sacred place. Holy ancestors. This servant of the gods and his kin bring gifts and offer prayers to rulers of old so that the tribe may prosper under the Eagle-God's wings of fire."

dd202ae4-4ff2-411b-b36a-19c5bdfbda8c.Text: The tattooed mummy lies in a ceremonial pose, dressed in bizarre fur attire and with an Aquila burned into its forehead.

258b7eb4-04fe-41f5-8917-9d174e41f944.Text: Someone repurposed old containers to build a ceremonial tomb. The remains of Imperium soldiers were placed inside a long time after their death.

a8738665-2555-4180-8faa-ed47d978d0d8.Text: The unknown captain's body has been preserved thanks to the properties of the local troposphere. Traces of inky secretions are visible on his skin: evidence of poisoning by a rare Drukhari toxin.

f67667ac-a498-41c9-b048-5f1690cd9585.Text: Time-worn Imperium breastplates and chainswords gleam amid the mummified remains.

30ed6cb9-402e-420b-be43-2b554255689e.Text: "It's just a piece of a column adorned with trinkets. Nothing divine or mystical about it."

2bb45c25-53fa-4f55-ad35-a6137c01ec9d.Text: "The people of Quetza Temer believe wholeheartedly in the God-Emperor, albeit after their own fashion. However, the Adeptus Ministorum would likely deem such worship to be heretical."

1a0b9f11-c0bf-4253-8b00-fd7ab86daa02.Text: "This 'altar' radiates a strange energy. As if rituals involving psychic powers have been performed here many times."

830ae478-6f73-4186-b572-54ed0d170d2d.Text: "This thing here has a weird energy to it. Like it's singing a lullaby. Can you hear it? You can't? Even my voices have fallen asleep."

6aa31184-c24b-472c-bbc1-441193215fca.Text: "I doubt Adeptus Ministorum servants would show up on a Rogue Trader's world and start punishing the locals. House Winterscale has a complicated history with His followers."

81fd8b9c-6ec0-44f8-abef-deec6cf76ba7.Text: "I am registering the presence of dormant mechanisms. Anomaly: unknown rites have put the machine spirits to sleep in contravention of the established protocols."

ee2292a4-be42-4cdd-a902-9d4bcd122fa2.Text: "This servant's ancient forebears erected this wonder so that tribes can worship the Eagle-God, bring Him gifts, and commune with Him. Here is where this servant listens and hears. And relays His will to his tribe."

a7d4f221-eb3d-401a-9614-7ce095bbb50e.Text: The vicinity of the carefully erected place of worship is quiet and peaceful.

276aa68c-8815-4284-affd-8d68e8395314.Text: Decayed Drukhari remains rest amid the forests of Quetza Temer along with this world's sorrowful past.

1656d543-762b-40a5-9e8c-2f2c2d58ae35.Text: "The Starborn descended on the Eagle-God's wings of fire to help us!"

8c51f8fc-a72a-479a-a16b-64634db19514.Text: "The forest is our home. But the forest is angry. Speaks-With-Gods will appease the forest and we will live as we did before."

043bde89-c831-40a4-8db8-882a1df8114a.Text: Wires braided with vines run throughout the inside of the cogitator. Its wooden components somehow support its rusted gears and prevent the mechanism from shutting down completely.

ba5da723-d387-4793-8e7f-5cc523a280ca.Text: "A fine battle, {name} von Valancius. I might invite you to hunt with me again some day. For now, go about your own business. I'm off to my ship. I shall see you among the stars!"

222e686a-ece1-4350-b213-92528a85264d.Text: "Traitor! I'm going to bash your rotted brains out and bathe in von Valancius blood! Skulls for the Rogue Trader's throne!"

1702ba8b-16db-4fd9-909f-dcdc419010e5.Text: "Come on, new blood! Let's see who can lop off more heads!"

069d3279-a500-4226-8ec3-d7c0bc18ba86.Text: Winterscale's shuttle awaited its owner's return in vain.

1bf1b6cb-8720-48fb-bf00-e5ddc0d26fae.Text: "Elantach, this forest... I sense its will, driven by the essence of the universe. It is not my kin's powers that are making the paths tangle. No, the forest simply has a life of its own."

57eb3089-cdd2-41b5-a80d-cb50f8e97558.Text:
"You seek reprisal where there could be peace,
And raise the blade of vengeance overhead,
Which hardship will rain down upon your house.
That blade is I. Until we meet again..."

d84a3c37-d363-430e-a829-3d727c2d59aa.Text: "We will search the part of the world where the local star sets. You should go where the star awakens. Good hunting to you."

5e1b5e8f-4f79-48c0-9d1f-dd68eb34da7c.Text: "I hoped to find understanding among those who share my Path." {n}Yrliet's voice trembles with weariness and anger.{/n} "But even the ancestors from Alaitoc, despite all their wisdom and supple intellect, could not reject their hatred of the mon-keigh who doomed thousands of innocent souls of the Children of Asuryan. I tried to appeal to the light in their souls, but all my arguments broke on the rocks of their intransigence like waves of sea-foam."

6596070f-3cb7-4a6b-b8df-e09e570f5556.Text: {n}Yrliet glares accusingly at Shairenkhei and the Farseers.{/n} "You chose this path. Not only did you invite doom upon Crudarach, you have also condemned our kin on Alaitoc. You have repeated the same mistakes over and over, guided by fear, stupidity, or pride. And even after losing everything, after losing... our home, you keep following the same thorny path, unwilling to change. No. I have had enough. My duty as an Outcast is fulfilled. From now on, your fate lies in your hands."

ecd05ad4-b4bf-49ff-a0ea-d7e01053ae57.Text: "I am tired of the Farseers' blindness and my kin's hatred, Shairenkhei. All of the choices of our people led only to suffering and the loss of our loved ones. I no longer wish to be an accomplice to another's hatred and pay for the mistakes of those who were supposed to guide us toward the light but who led us into oblivion." {n}Yrliet glares at the nearby Farseers.{/n}

8161c9a3-67f4-45dd-9022-78fdfd875756.Text: "I convinced my kin to divert the river of their anger. The ranks of Outcasts will arrive in the Expanse, unseen and unheard. But not for the sake of war — they will find and take away those who remain. The last sons and daughters of Crudarach. And then they will depart the mon-keigh stars without a trace. Forever."

a62389b4-3a1b-43f7-a0d3-2e709b79cd23.Text: {n}The angry Farseers try to object, but Shairenkhei gently interrupts them:{/n} "Your brothers and sisters would not dare ask you for more, Yrliet. I understand your choice... even if my spirit cannot fully accept it."

dc253b26-6128-4835-a43c-c0f97d583a51.Text: "I simply used you to get rid of a rival."

2a4a0892-336d-4370-a8ca-040af4389ada.Text: "Yrliet, are you going to leave me and escape with the rest of the Outcasts?"

84e80d64-db84-4d84-b0fc-d0d8923a6864.Text: "Trust me, you would not want to face Calligos in battle."

0deb1cec-2c01-48da-b478-fa940e1f6530.Text: "I trust you understand I did not help you out of the goodness of my heart?"

f69b82ef-aaaf-4b08-a32b-093414d18ff4.Text: "Humans are better than you give them credit for."

6cde5868-379d-44b1-981f-55eae9837c88.Text: "Are you saying there is another Aeldari craftworld heading for the Expanse?"

540fc4be-d325-45fb-8e1e-803b7e9533e9.Text: "What are you planning to do now?"

319762bf-c7c8-44da-a56b-2d0b19c2b308.Text: "It is time we talk about the Haemonculus."

08c0f8b3-54ef-4a5d-8c21-4f3f5e104714.Text: "Do you think I require your protection?"

48dc992b-d75c-4eff-9427-1a108fdeac6a.Text: "Do not attack Humanity's worlds ever again."

ccec7ee4-9a24-4d54-9d5e-8b9ec9b7723b.Text: "Winterscale was a great man, once. I regret his inglorious end."

a0c16747-63c1-4f20-b094-bc43ce3dc968.Text: [Draw your weapon] "It was naive of me to hope that your intentions were free of trickery."

2738c057-f770-4dad-affa-e6e550bb1f36.Text: "Yrliet, your kin's plan is insane! Convince them to relent before it is too late."

e3595958-c5b5-453b-a4a1-a28656773489.Text: "I will destroy the Haemonculus and avenge us both."

c241910c-23b5-4641-b09d-49b79d0bcb03.Text: "The Expanse has been through hard times of late. We do not need trouble with the Aeldari, now or in the future."

a884579c-0f16-46b9-b059-e8572139ffaf.Text: "Yrliet, I object to this ritual if it means your life will be at stake."

8425108a-937b-4d9a-a1a9-7f5e7a9423af.Text: [Leave] "I hope your coordinates are correct. The time has come to corner the Haemonculus."

a6fb8bbd-f079-4946-909f-9b9cfe825ef4.Text: "This is your life and your people, Yrliet. I will stay by your side no matter what path you choose."

09744cb9-a4a4-4f34-80c7-6d77dd75cbaa.Text: "I would be glad if you stayed."

db6a7213-f5e9-4fd2-8e07-2a8fb220c8a7.Text: "I think it is time for us to part ways."

e9b7daea-a41e-4975-a6d1-fa7352061d87.Text: "I will not stand in your way if you genuinely wish to stay with your kin."

1884179a-b311-43f3-9959-af692bdd16d8.Text: "Indeed, you do owe me. And you have not worked off your debt just yet."

da0003f8-b671-4b8a-9150-784486bfaa83.Text: "Yrliet, let your kin decide their own fate. You do not owe them anything."

937e34ce-7395-472d-bdea-4af75d764f0f.Text: "Yrliet, are you all right? That Aeldari sorcery looked dangerous."

09586fb2-b867-4192-8a93-2a927d36885a.Text: "I stood up for your kin, and guess what happened next?"

e0a7beb8-da2d-40ba-8609-6662f7950685.Text: "I did not sign up for yet another war against the xenos in the Expanse. Call off your kin."

9b85f39d-533f-4440-944e-52c2e001cd1e.Text: "Very well. The more xenos in the Expanse, the merrier!"

8b20b93f-f214-4e8d-943f-7480fd835e85.Text: "Why are you so certain the Aeldari are going to attack our worlds?"

b8b4c912-3338-45c5-834f-3ad62ddc1918.Text: "Yrliet, will you not stay with your kin?"

4f3bb5a2-7782-472e-affe-1ec039703e68.Text: "I do not like the sound of this, Aeldari."

11c315ce-2a21-4ccb-921f-55b3736c05c2.Text: "Do you still hope to find the Haemonculus?"

82a1679f-db7e-4b36-a14e-5f3c37fbc26d.Text: [Leave] "It is time to track down the Haemonculus."

f86cc825-850f-4a97-af9f-ae81df0a264d.Text: "I rid you of Calligos and brought back Yrliet. Do such acts not merit a reward?"

366f9db5-fdd4-480b-b7dd-1de2a3f07fbb.Text: "No matter how fair the starlight, the star is destined to fade some day. Your fellow mon-keigh was not of the light, for there was darkness clouding his heart. You need not grieve his loss."

2ddc20a0-a229-44fa-b4e1-8414c5f921d7.Text: "You... survived? Asuryan showed you mercy, Outcast, and so did our ancestors from the Alaitoc Infinity Circuit. Tell me, sister, what was their answer?"

ec6eeb8f-d951-4636-960b-8e5ae342643a.Text: "Oh, yeah. That's much better, thank you!"

a272f5fa-99e9-436e-8004-7527ea4b1b21.Text: "Before you chide me for my decisions, consider how many of our kin you managed to save in the void between the local stars. And {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_Yrliet_BrokenPromise}how many more you could have saved{/d}."

ffd1d0a3-d2c6-4c15-969f-8638ad8514ce.Text: {n}The Aeldari pays no heed to your words... though he may be just pretending.{/n}

ef39dce5-c386-469f-8f68-5b6295d889a8.Text: "I would expect nothing else from a mon-keigh. But one good turn deserves another." {n}Shairenkhei produces an unknown xenodevice and scrutinises it.{/n} "The Farseers could not divine where the master of flesh makes his lair, for an unknown force is hiding him from the penetrating gaze of the wise ones. The Children of Asuryan... have never encountered anything like this before. Having circled the world several times and failed in our search, we ventured to unleash our pent-up fury on the planet in the hope that we would be graced with a fortunate accident."

9c680971-d41a-4a9a-85c7-a2f1ab99d26c.Text: "I usually do not think about your kind at all." {n}The Aeldari shrugs softly.{/n} "But I am prepared to admit that there are... certain worthy specimens among the millions of your kind."

93aaa9a8-f186-45fc-a925-14afc8e53331.Text:
"The beast in human guise is tamed, and yet
There does exist no throttling chain to quell
That thirst for blood that slumbers in his veins.
Comes now the hour when rattling links protest,
And, with a grisly roar, he turns once more."

78269c43-6af3-434f-8016-ddb26208d169.Text: {n}For some reason, your words bring a faint smile to Yrliet's lips.{/n} "Worry not, elantach. It is my turn to rescue you and your people."

5b576fb3-112e-47b9-bcca-b47fc9996388.Text: "After the master of flesh has been dealt with?" {n}Shairenkhei sighs tiredly, a faint shadow of a smile gracing his face.{/n} "We will go home... Not to Crudarach, no, but to our kin from the other craftworlds. The Farseers have already contacted our allies, and they are already on the way to the system."

a37d92f0-cf7d-4f27-98a7-16fa5e2c4769.Text: "The Farseers' mistakes doomed Crudarach, Shairenkhei! And their excessive cruelty and thirst for vengeance almost doomed those of us who managed to survive against all odds in the void between foreign stars. You know it just as well as I do, but you continue to do their bidding. Oh, Shairenkhei, you could take the Webway Gate — and go away from the dangers and tribulations of the Expanse. But you have chosen to stay here instead. You are dying. You are feuding with the mon-keigh. Have not the Children of Asuryan spilt enough blood? Is it not enough that we have lost our home? Why do you wish to expose even more of your kin to mortal peril?"

01d0019d-1ddd-4737-983b-5809e44c4c62.Text: {n}Shairenkhei's iron will falters under Yrliet's relentless pressure.{/n} "It is... it is too late to change anything. The deed is done. Their will carried out. The Outcasts from Alaitoc will come to the local stars, and we will leave with them, sister."

e457f5e7-8cc8-4c75-908b-9ca364de7768.Text: "Once the master of flesh is defeated, we will be relieved to depart this exhausted world... and the Expanse. Is this not what you call this region of space?"

686f5c7c-2be5-41b8-99d4-0244d187bc55.Text: "Did the darkness of space drive you mad during your exile, sister?" {n}Shairenkhei recoils from Yrliet as if from a scorching flame.{/n} "Even those who walk the Path of the Seer baulk at joining souls with the ancestors inside the Circuit. They are wise and know that the ritual is perilous to the spirit. Your chances of success are... simply non-existent. You would die without achieving anything! And even if you did not die immediately, ask yourself honestly: why should the ancestors listen to a simple Outcast?"

8f87dc6c-6345-4696-8d97-7c30bd4b509c.Text: "As you said, Alaitoc is a world of my fellow Outcasts. They would not wish harm upon me, which gives wings to my hope. Look me in the eye, Shairenkhei. Do you wish to end the suffering of our kin? I can see the answer in your heart. You must accept it and help me." {n}Though Yrliet's words are addressed to her kinsman, she is watching your reaction closely.{/n}

9f165e86-3443-4ae9-b076-f29473776d8a.Text: "It would be humiliating to end up as a game piece in the hands of a mon-keigh... had we been interested in the internecine strife among the lesser species."

923348a2-085e-4462-83ef-0d15798eb238.Text: "Your eagerness is commendable, but we will not abandon our search until the flesh sculptor is destroyed... or until we are presented with proof of his demise. Let us pursue him separately. If you reach the Haemonculus first and cut his life short, our Farseers will feel it and we will vacate this world."

a5ba00d0-634b-4e12-9458-efcbef54b7db.Text: "Our Farseers paid an insurmountable price to contact a craftworld located billions of stars away from here. Many of them perished to give the rest of us the chance to be rescued. And I will not jeopardise the lives of those who yet remain."

19bf9453-f51a-4a90-bbba-9599d9bf4b9d.Text: "Because they are driven by grief. Sometimes pain and loss blinds even the best of us."

2b5ad580-3414-4bd8-ae43-ba14c211d2bb.Text: "More pain? Did you manage to prevent the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarEliminated}death of our kin and Muaran{/d} on the Lilaethan? The Arebennian told me everything that happened."

4c072341-d3de-4b6d-88cb-65af6186d049.Text: "I am sorry, elantach, but it is not up to you to shape my destiny. Not this time."

826330ba-5f82-4a44-ae05-542313f8ac48.Text: "And I do appreciate it, elantach." {n}Yrliet nods and underscores her words with the familiar gesture of gratitude.{/n}

5c6583ee-bcab-463f-9772-1e098c4c08da.Text: "I have done all I can, Shairenkhei. You know what you must do."

94454059-835a-4a7f-81ad-0006d7e282a7.Text:
"With words alone fate cannot be constrained,
But deeds add weight behind words' cutting edge.
Behold, the cup of strife and vengeance drained,
Its bitter wine of grief drunk to the dregs.
The Outcast's cry is set to fly beyond
The frozen light of clusters long forgot,
And to her will in tribute might respond
The Seers of the Path with bridge outwrought."

a006d17e-2248-4238-8f8e-de0beddb7988.Text: "I did not think you would let me go so easily, elantach." {n}Yrliet looks at you in surprise, as if expecting a catch.{/n} "But if it really is the pure desire of your soul... so be it."

82e543b0-87fd-4f6a-8b78-444d8642beb0.Text: {n}Yrliet cocks her head pensively.{/n} "I think I will return to them some day. But our paths are too tightly interwoven to end them here."

62ee127c-ac50-4704-adcd-117a83e49859.Text: "I know my kin are to blame for their own troubles!" {n}Yrliet's spirit stone glows brightly.{/n} "But what I have been fighting for my entire life is teetering on the brink of the abyss right now. Do you see, elantach? I must speak to the ancestors from the Infinity Circuit. That is my Path as an Outcast."

bc2360da-3ed9-4564-9e14-d4756b88c776.Text: "Wait, elantach!" {n}Yrliet breaks away from her kin and hands you a small amulet.{/n} "Human memories are as fleeting as the span of your lives. But I would like you to have something to remind you of our journey together. Think of it as a symbol of gratitude for all you have done for me." {n}Yrliet bids you farewell with a warm smile and disappears into the woods with the other Aeldari.{/n}

23c892ad-c406-4119-ac6d-d7d4b1c67f01.Text: "May Asuryan forgive his children." {n}Shairenkhei sighs and gestures to a few of his warriors.{/n} "Fetch the Farseers. Tell them... the Outcast wishes to perform the ritual. We will wait for them here."

422940b6-3ca4-450a-adf0-3dabfa07683a.Text: "Is that what an adherent of the Path of the Warrior wishes to tell me? Were these words meant to comfort my heart?" {n}Yrliet's words ring with contempt and desperation.{/n} "O Asuryan, your children once again seek to appease their pride by sending their kin to mon-keigh worlds — there to find nothing but blood and death!"

1639d452-a163-49f1-9de3-0e4413803289.Text: "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}Not you too, Arebennian{/d}." {n}Shairenkhei frowns and sighs loudly.{/n} "So be it. We will give the Outcast a chance, but I doubt she will survive even the beginning of the ritual."

c2be89a6-1a2a-48bb-9c1a-d75dcd8a49a3.Text: {n}The Solitaire does not intervene, but shifts his gaze to Shairenkhei as if expecting to hear the last line of a play before the curtain falls.{/n}

8b51984e-bdc0-4a4c-8ded-c1cc23f17f41.Text: "Is that what worries you now, elantach?" {n}Yrliet gives you a disapproving look.{/n} "I may leave the Expanse one day, but the only thing you should be concerned about now is how to quell the wrath of my people."

641ec181-6441-4dc9-978b-a7a951ce19fb.Text: "May Asuryan save us from this woe!" {n}Shairenkhei folds his arms on his chest in a graceful gesture, but the horror is obvious on his face.{/n} "No. I will not allow another world to perish at the hands of the mon-keigh, even if this means forsaking my soul!"

25d1761f-d770-4304-af5e-41e7987256c1.Text: "A bold statement from one who has not yet forsaken his soul even once."

88c66bae-b4ac-4cca-9a6f-72ab253d1ee2.Text: "And I am not going to reveal all the secrets of my kind to you, mon— elantach. You may have helped us in our hour of need, but I trusted you at the Outcast's behest. But I will say this — the warriors of Alaitoc are coming here, to your stars. This is an unalterable truth."

bd648fbe-0830-447a-9ac9-67c27bd384e3.Text: {n}Like a forgotten shadow, the Solitaire steps into the light and leans forward with interest, a spectator watching the culmination of an exciting performance.{/n}

583f9ccd-c72f-4f6c-a599-c323fe2e53a2.Text: "Elantach, your anger is like the raging winds of desert worlds — restrain it, and listen."

b75a7954-cd84-4f7d-a89d-f056f1c0da68.Text: "During my exile, I met many companions who temporarily joined me on my endless travels." {n}Yrliet closes her eyes.{/n} "One such companion was a fellow Outcast who had already completed many Paths. It was he who told me about the ritual of unity — a great opportunity for one's spirit to reach out and touch the Infinity Circuit of the craftworld known to the Farseers who perform it. Shairenkhei said that the Crudarach Farseers have already contacted Alaitoc. This means... This means I can, too."

8a69fee0-5d86-456c-bcca-54538da253ed.Text: "Have you already forgotten who is responsible for Crudarach's demise, elantach?" {n}Yrliet's spirit stone glows brightly, but the disapproval in her eyes is even brighter.{/n} "The only thing my kin are guilty of is getting too close to the stars of the mon-keigh. They... We... lost our home. We were hounded by your people. We were tormented by dark ones. No... None of Crudarach's children deserve such a fate. And I will not let those who yet remain perish in darkness."

5e68e33c-e486-433e-aa96-642d4e73c47c.Text: "What do you mean to do, sister?"

c3e75fa2-3a1a-449b-97c7-0fc57735e840.Text: "No! Do this, elantach, and your entire demesne will be drowned in blood. Not only the blood of my kind, but your subjects will also meet a terrible end. And I... I can prevent it. It is my turn to rescue you and your people."

0777a3e7-e35e-4c6c-af9b-c70880537011.Text: "How can you describe the inevitable demise of your and my own kind so nonchalantly? If you let this happen and leave things as they stand, rivers of blood will flood your demesne. Not only will the Children of Asuryan die, your subjects will also meet a terrible end. So will your worlds and your entire protectorate. And I... cannot allow this. It is my turn to rescue you and your people."

b0d84a6c-284a-44b0-ba53-e95e7d6298dc.Text: "Unless the warriors of Alaitoc arrive in this part of the galaxy, the sons and daughters of Crudarach will perish among the worlds of the mon-keigh. Is that the fate you wish for us?"

63c0dfad-926e-40ac-b454-1fbd632ce3d4.Text: "It will take the Warriors of Alaitoc many years to discover the Webway Gate capable of bringing their strike force to the Expanse. Perhaps you will be too old by then, and only on your deathbed will you hear the news — the Children of Asuryan have come to exact their vengeance."

15e5ba6f-c16b-4ac8-95ed-6955ba99153d.Text: {n}The strange energy that permeated the clearing where the paths of humans and Aeldari happened to cross is gradually dissipating. All eyes turn to Yrliet, the Aeldari who managed to survive the deadly ritual, but who awoke looking angry and dejected.{/n}

027e54a4-2217-4aa3-b2ad-e2fcb9bcdf8a.Text: {n}The strange energy that permeated the clearing where the paths of humans and Aeldari happened to cross is gradually dissipating. All eyes turn to Yrliet, the Aeldari who managed to survive the deadly ritual, and who awoke looking pensive and enlightened.{/n}

ebc86e19-43a0-49b7-b435-12da429670c1.Text: "We will have to find another way. I understand that it is not easy for those who have lived all their lives sheltered within a craftworld to accept that sometimes life leads us down different paths. But the path that you and the Farseers have chosen only leads to more pain."

0bd52342-bc52-4a24-8c0e-943b2aa6dc67.Text: "I am fine, elantach." {n}A gracious look and a slight smile underscore Yrliet's words.{/n} "Thanks to you, I have finally reached the end of my Path. This Path. And I am grateful I had you to walk alongside me."

34e1a039-8d93-4a2e-9d15-476c1d02c420.Text: {n}Yrliet brushes a strand of fiery hair from her forehead and nods appreciatively:{/n} "I know how difficult it is to go against the will of your kin. And yet I cannot hide my joy that we both lived through this moment... and emerged with a tale to tell."

a68214e0-c874-45cf-8c2a-5feefd16ae62.Text: "I am an Outcast, elantach. My place is among the stars."

d0d50a0a-0632-48f9-8963-507d5e0ca68f.Text: "I would be lying if I said I had not thought about it. But you have helped me and my kin all this time to the best of your ability. Should I not repay you in kind, elantach?"

783980a6-1e4a-4fc2-8430-d47ae4f05581.Text: "Then so be it." {n}Yrliet folds her fingers in a familiar gesture of trust and accord.{/n}

7e6125da-e4f0-4c1b-bbb5-451981e1093a.Text: {n}Yrliet's lips twist and she nods silently.{/n}

feea0db2-e3a8-432e-8de9-59e4df32fd63.Text: "An Outcast returning home? Truly a joyous occasion, considering how many of our kin have been lost. We are glad to welcome you back, Yrliet."

6320de7a-3b20-4655-b391-f09c04c99e49.Text: "Did you prevent the death of Eklendyl, follower of the Path of the Seer, one of the Crudarach Farseers tormented by the master of flesh in the Dark City along with the rest of our kin? Yes, I am aware of {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_EklendylDiedInSpire}his fate{/d}."

9801e1f6-1447-4694-bcb2-05d3e95d47a6.Text: "However, I dare not complain — for my kin, the hour of triumph has arrived at last. Once the master of flesh is no more, we can go to the edge of this stellar expanse, away from the gaze of mon-keigh. And peacefully await the arrival of our kin from distant stars."

e2595b7c-d1d1-4bba-9d7b-df913b118d1b.Text: "What are you talking about, Shairenkhei?" {n}Yrliet stares intently into the eyes of the Aeldari warrior, but his gaze remains steady and calm.{/n}

c3f7af55-1b56-4685-8073-131dc6ab9cad.Text: {n}The xenos hesitates and adds with slight embarrassment:{/n} "Lesser... {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}allied{/d} species."

be58909a-5eab-4c91-9609-609a7d6a8f3a.Text: "Outcast Yrliet, I have some good news for you. Our Farseers managed to contact the children of Craftworld Alaitoc, and soon your fellow Outcasts will visit the part of the galaxy that the mon-keigh call the Expanse. They will take us away, give us a new home, and..." {n}Shairenkhei pauses, his gaze on you, wondering if he should continue.{/n}

47fe9af9-f73c-4142-ad45-846eb7b5d414.Text: {n}The Aeldari produces an unknown xenodevice.{/n} "The Farseers could not divine where the master of flesh makes his lair, for an unknown force is hiding him from the penetrating gaze of the wise ones. The Children of Asuryan... have never encountered anything like this before. Having circled the world several times and failed in our search, we ventured to unleash our pent-up fury on the planet in the hope that we would be graced with a fortunate accident."

dd763ae1-b512-4b84-a1cc-1e85c789b9bb.Text: "Alas, the fate of the master of flesh remained unchanged — the Farseers could feel the beating of his black heart but were powerless to do anything. That was when our rangers began to deduce the coordinates of his lair based on the readings of the wise ones and the lands untouched by the fired weapons. And they would have succeeded had the mon-keigh not attacked our fleet."

405dcd02-b941-449b-b681-c4ba118e8220.Text: {n}The Aeldari device thrums and a holographic projection of the world with several marked coordinates appears in his palm.{/n} "I will share the information I have gathered, for I hope that even a master of flesh will not be able to elude two pursuers at once."

09d1e571-edae-473c-b5b8-0823eea9c520.Text: [Let Yrliet handle it on her own]

8bab7a05-868c-4f5b-bf32-d5f1ea2cdc20.Text: "If our paths cross again one day, we will {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}begin our conversation by greeting one another{/d} and not unsheathing our blades." {n}Shairenkhei ponders something.{/n} "Your time in this world is too short to hope for it, but I will remember our promise, elantach."

b5753cbd-2437-4f2e-95de-f614c8bb1e18.Text: "I do not think this is possible, mon-keigh. Our temporary alliance will run its course as soon as the ships of my kin leave the Expanse, for I hope never to return here."

31a1520f-e8da-4f6d-a356-6bf4b0ca5531.Text: "I would not be opposed to cooperating in the future."

388847a4-7b19-46e0-8316-b30077d37a51.Text: "After all the suffering that the mon-keigh have inflicted upon the children of Crudarach. After all the punishment we have inflicted upon this world... My heart remains troubled, knowing that we have only tempered our grudges for a time and have parted without bloodshed today."

25da6ec9-7599-4cf3-bf6f-cd018300bf4d.Text: "I do not know how a mon-keigh would benefit from betraying one of {mf|his|her} own, but our temporary alliance has fostered a fragile peace... Let it remain for now."

5f61bfc3-c9b0-479f-bdb3-f0e7631d976b.Text: "You always come to the rescue of my people, elantach. I wish I could grasp your true motives — perhaps it is the impulsiveness of your species? Or is it a personal anomaly that has affected your agile mind?"

64a422f8-1013-4a29-aa17-da1405d57e71.Text: "The gratitude of the Children of Asuryan to your kind is already a precious reward, elantach. Accept it as a rare gift."

e7a86eb3-f034-498e-bb6b-8bdb6a6698c0.Text: {n}He makes an elaborate gesture, and one of the Aeldari hands you a parcel.{/n} "This is my first and probably last gift to one of you, elantach. May it serve you faithfully as it has served the Children of Asuryan."

ee0787a0-fa71-4aeb-b854-37d5f548374f.Text: {n}Shairenkhei gives you a long and penetrating look.{/n} "The gratitude of the Children of Asuryan to your kind is a precious reward in itself, elantach. But I have been observing your kind for a while now. As a gesture of goodwill, I suppose I should reward your labours in a fashion more... customary among the mon-keigh."

953f158b-3449-41f8-a7aa-fd5266cc6705.Text: "After the master of flesh has been dealt with?" {n}Shairenkhei sighs tiredly, a faint shadow of a smile gracing his face.{/n} "We will go home... as soon as possible."

ebc9ee2a-dc52-40f9-8778-6bc24c65c8ab.Text: {n}The shuttle disappears in the wild vegetation of the island. Several hours pass before the Rogue Trader finally admits that {mf|he|she} has been aimlessly wandering around in circles. Any attempts to get back on track by retracing {mf|his|her} steps have failed. Vox-communication cannot reach the ship. Now it becomes clear how Calligos Winterscale could get lost on his own world.{/n}

2529fd2f-940c-44bd-af6b-4df86091010d.Text: {n}The forest is alive with the constant rustling of thick leaves and the creaking of wood. It is as if the trees themselves are walking around like lumbering, looming people. But surely it is just a trick of the eye — plants cannot walk, can they?{/n}

763c2c01-1cbd-440d-89c7-947c7804eaee.Text: {n}Quite a few hours pass before something worth noticing finally shows up amid the dense forest: a pile of charred human bones lying in a shallow pit, and in front of it, like a standing stone, a broken fire cultivator with melted nozzles is stuck in the ground. Other corpses can be seen in the grass nearby, just as old and charred, but distinctly non-human. Scattered alongside those are xenos weapons, covered in dirt. Some of the weaponry appears to be in working order, so it is still possible to get some use out of it.{/n}

d887bf43-65fb-46bb-800b-bee573da899f.Text: {n}The irresistibly sweet aroma of fruit teases the Rogue Trader's olfactory senses, especially after so many hours spent in the stuffy humidity of the forest. But after locating the source of the aroma, {mf|he|she} decides against tasting the appetising fruits: several mummified corpses lie under the fruit trees, their withered faces a testament to their agony, their bodies covered in dark wounds resembling the bites of giant leeches.{/n}

13e96b45-b838-4fc8-a58c-751d33b24749.Text: {n}The trek among the monotonous forest landscapes is becoming dull. The Rogue Trader's weary eyes are ready to close of their own accord when the usual sounds of the forest are interrupted by a blood-curling scream. The cries are drawing closer and closer, then their source finally appears — a small creature with slick black fur and a long tail. As if mocking the Rogue Trader, it lets out another piercing cry and scurries away, its yellow hind paws winking between the tree branches.{/n}

ab12370e-575a-4fda-88a1-fddccc0e65d2.Text: {n}The rich flora of the forest at times staggers the imagination. Among the trees covered in ivy and moss, the Rogue Trader notices a spiralling pattern of small white lumps on one of the tree trunks. Someone has cut the bark, causing the milky sap to flow down the damaged parts of the tree, harden from the heat, and turn into uneven rubbery cocoons.{/n}

7e198105-7bae-494f-bda8-a85c7f70164c.Text: {n}The sound of rushing water comes from somewhere close by. After a few more steps, the forest parts, revealing a stepped waterfall. The clear currents flow gracefully from one step to the next, carrying peculiar colourful ribbons, which turn out to be living creatures that latch onto the porous surface of rocks with their flexible bodies, snapping at small fish with their eyeless, toothy heads.{/n}

e0ba8777-4a96-470d-8629-f03ac9afef40.Text: {n}The forest hike lasts an entire day. In the golden rays of dusk, the Rogue Trader sees a small hill crowned with an Aquila — a double-headed eagle totem made from the plasteel and rockcrete components of an ancient ship. The foot of the hill provides a much less scenic view, however: the soil is stained brown from all the flesh smeared upon it, contrasted only by the white specks of bone shards mixed into the dried-up bloody mass.{/n}

2c508147-61f7-49d0-964b-546ddc356731.Text: {n}After a day's journey, the smoke of the smouldering fires has been left far behind. The wind has changed, and with it the forests of Quetza Temer, if only subtly. The path the Rogue Trader just followed has become an impassable wall of tangled vines. The rare anomaly of the local florosphere has once again played its insidious trick — the forest has changed, reference points have swapped positions, and paths have become intertwined.{/n}

d6a0ab7b-4175-43be-a95c-2c8065cea8ea.Text: {n}The now familiar rustle of the centuries-old canopy and barely perceptible movement at the edge of the Rogue Trader's vision announce that the forests are once again in motion — are they fleeing the distant raging fires or simply migrating? It is difficult to say. However, spacious meadows have now been replaced with dense forest, and the trails have changed direction once more.{/n}

595b8554-f113-4c1d-a452-e73a650a57ab.Text: {n}Part of the forest is obstructed by a thin grey veil emitting barely audible clicks. The translucent curtain ripples and starts moving in the direction of the Rogue Trader. Upon closer inspection, the veil turns out to be woven from many threads carried by fast-flying bugs. The hive attacks the intruder, then retreats into the foliage, leaving behind burning, itching bites and wisps of shredded web.{/n}

45a869f8-0ff8-4966-af3c-ad8fabe22f3d.Text: {n}Hours of wandering bring the Rogue Trader to a tall, sprawling tree. Something shiny is stuck in the foliage. Coming closer, the Lord Captain recognises an obsolete heavy void suit model that has been subsumed among the growing branches. A heavily damaged skull bares its teeth from behind the murky glass — at least their death was quick.{/n}

e6d6ab8b-3f05-48f8-81aa-91d4024996a3.Text: {n}After several hours of traversing the forest, a small mountain blocks the way. Something about the pattern on the stone seems wrong. A few moments later, it becomes clear that there are cogitator parts glinting at the base of the mountain. The machines appear to have grown into the stone itself along with the dirt and grass, with the only proof of their artificial origin being the occasional flashes of lumens powered by some random unknown impulses. A carcass is lying on a flat stone nearby, cut open in sacrifice to an unknown god.{/n}

806e29bc-6e5b-43c5-972d-cccdffaa9adb.Text: {n}The Rogue Trader has never seen an anthill of such size before. But the most disturbing thing about it is a xenos skeleton tied to the anthill with bonds made from some unknown material. The Drukhari weapon stuck in the corpse is the only detail that can point to the perpetrator. Being eaten by ants is a horrific torture that makes the blade in the back seem like an act of mercy — a most uncharacteristic gesture for this race.{/n}

816a102d-300d-47b3-9c55-2609ad288622.Text: {n}The skies break open, the heavy rain penetrating even the dense canopy of the forest. Luckily, the elements relent before long. As the sun emerges once more, the forest comes alive with the singing of birds accompanied by the quiet sound of falling droplets.{/n}

77a7732f-449f-4bd4-827e-cc7f9b7a60b7.Text: {n}The Rogue Trader requires rest, and {mf|he|she} soon finds a suitable spot for a camp — a meadow with a few fruit trees. A creature with an elongated body and large blunt claws leisurely descends from one of the trees. Its muzzle is red as if stained with blood, but it turns out to be merely the juices of the fruit from the nearby trees. The fruit has a peculiar taste reminiscent of grox meat baked in sweet and sour sauce.{/n}

b548367e-21eb-4d57-adcd-6076b7ab585a.Text: {n}Halfway through the day, the Rogue Trader discovers a new wonder of Quetza Temer's forests — a spacious stretch of land overgrown with reddish-brown grass covered in sickening yellow blisters. No other plant can be seen among the red blades of grass. The answer to this mystery may have something to do with pale spider-like insects crawling on the underside of the blades.{/n}

e0ddbf2a-65b5-4a78-aa58-64fb1d5b1070.Text: {n}In the shade of the tallest trees in this area of the forest, the Rogue Trader spots mushrooms that come up as high as {mf|his|her} waist. Strands of sponge-like tissue hang from under their pale lilac caps, almost reaching the ground. As soon as the Rogue Trader approaches one of the mushrooms, the strands draw in, the cap rolls up, and the mushroom spews out a cloud of reddish spores. Perhaps it would be wiser to give this place a wide berth.{/n}

2261ae3a-8651-449c-8d8f-de209739180f.Text: An imposing blade covered in blood that never clots. The wielder is consumed by unspeakable rage while holding this sword.

2291275a-48cd-4817-9917-6465330a4059.Text: A Monograph by Karl Emmanuel Cerubion Dho on the Culture of the Imperium's Far Worlds

eb2140ef-7379-4c2a-95c2-7205e1317ccb.Text:
"You know, Stanzo, I miss the times when fire cultivators were only used for working in the fields. Back then, I thought: by the Throne, damn that forest! Can't take your eyes off it for a tick, or else it'd mess with production. But nowadays... The damned forest is the only thing that can defend people. Who'd have guessed? And we, the Silvarius, are the only ones who can pass through it — if we have our fire cultivator intact, that is. I did hear, though, that one of the Astropaths managed to lead a group of fifty people through the brush, but nobody has heard from them since. The enemies of Humanity got them, didn't they...{br}
Come meet us halfway. I'm leading a new group, and the promethium in my cultivator is running out."

0a9e95fe-9251-4187-82d7-c615d35449d2.Text: "How do you even survive in these forests?"

f3b35001-42a3-4714-90af-d7a9e2f3ea33.Text: "You think that several gods have set foot on Quetza Temer?"

6ac3ec0f-3348-4689-9185-59e72aea5ebe.Text: "And how exactly do we conduct the soothing ritual?"

f14fa389-9c4a-4668-8596-0ac5795fea98.Text: "Speaks-With-Gods also calls Calligos and me 'Starborn.' Why?"

5210f330-d410-4ec1-a253-c9dd2f015155.Text: "How does your tribe manage to survive in these forests?"

93608ca9-6b89-4ba9-b95e-cd56550fe44c.Text: "Do you know where your brother and the other Starborn are now?"

0a68205a-eab9-4bfa-8abd-3548af7d759d.Text: "No time for rest. I shall set out immediately."

63864fdd-e3d6-4c9e-a6bd-c26f7a80f53d.Text: {n}A group of lean young people surrounds you, shooting anxious glances between you and the grey-headed elder who has stepped forward. Unlike the rest, her skin is completely free of decoration, save for the two-headed eagle branded on her wrinkled forehead.{/n}

2191230d-fb97-4f6f-afe5-5a28bf5f365c.Text: {n}A group of lean young people surrounds you, shooting anxious glances between you, Calligos, the priest, and the grey-headed elder who has stepped forward. Unlike the rest, her skin is completely free of decoration, save for the two-headed eagle branded on her wrinkled forehead.{/n}

b9d20bbf-41c5-45ee-9740-46668ba2d578.Text: "Something's calling, it's calling, and calling..." {n}Idira covers her ears with her palms and forces her eyes shut.{/n} "There, in the place of no return, sits the shadow of one who is both alive and dead at once... The voices are calling me there, calling so desperately, but why? WHY?"

4dcd52dc-7208-4a95-8f92-357f029538d6.Text: {n}In a stern, brusque manner, Ulfar asks with interest,{/n} "Offerings of game? Protective amulets on the trails?" {n}After receiving an affirmative answer, he gives a firm and satisfied nod.{/n}

e90f1f6b-f2b7-4073-b41a-d69acb8146d1.Text: "Nevertheless... This ruler knows that you will bring Speaks-With-Gods home and soothe the forest of Quetza Temer. The prophecies of the priests have never betrayed our tribe before, and thus this ruler asks you to forget about your worries and rest here, in the heart of the forest."

43a324f7-8b2a-4589-a179-12ace1b1f002.Text: "Because you are the Sky-Herald of the Eagle-God, created by Him from the stars' glow and the night sky's darkness. The one who carries His seal in your image, clad in the armour of our ancestors' most ancient prophecies."

fda3d7dd-4f80-4bf5-be06-d39e5bb7c18e.Text: "It is an honour for this ruler's tribe to serve you, O Starborn. Follow the path of lights, and you will find your shelter, food, and water. When you decide that it is time to follow the priest and your Starborn kin, this tribe will pray to the Eagle-God Himself for your success."

9b9f631c-37e1-48bc-adf1-89837e141db5.Text: "The Starborn had lost his priest in battle, so he ordered this ruler's brother to help him trace the spirits' footsteps and cleanse Quetza Temer of their filth. But when Speaks-With-Gods left his home, something enraged the forest. Thus both the Starborn and this ruler's brother were trapped by the ever-changing paths and lurking evil spirits."

bb2f3a6d-3d5e-4c26-9154-65c53b03c1fe.Text: "Food and shelter?" {n}Jae's eyes light up.{/n} "So long to our worn-out boots and sodden cape, shereen! My homeworld has a wise rule — never dismiss the hospitality of those who consider you their overlord!"

d9947c57-bee3-47c3-bc84-3e27cfdebf4f.Text: "The collected data partially matches and completes the data received from the Emperor's Vow. Calligos Winterscale descended upon this world, lost a psyker in battles with xenos, and found a replacement in the village at the current coordinates."

fc9e893f-22c5-4f66-9025-4b6df7bfac25.Text: "Like you've never heard that one before, Lord Captain."

5e186da0-63d4-4637-8151-b0822617e118.Text: "The powers of my kin may have disturbed the wild flora of this world, which then concealed the remnants of the children of Crudarach from the wrath of your rival. That means that they are somewhere in the forest. Surviving. Hiding. Preying on one another."

5085892e-93a9-4309-91c0-40e9563d0a5d.Text: "Oh yes, Speaks-With-Gods is the priest of this tribe and this ruler's half-brother. He listens to the forest and calls to the earth, wards off the punishing lashes of the skies, and speaks to the Eagle-God on behalf of our tribe. Before disappearing in the wandering forest, he told this ruler to prepare for your arrival."

4bb2f844-2bcb-4a78-8201-09db89127d85.Text: {n}It seems that the priest went into the woods with the Starborn's retinue and vanished along with them.{/n}

94c0006b-4b0f-424b-b516-bd1e13db9024.Text: "I presume this 'priest' is another unsanctioned psyker with the gift of divination." {n}Heinrix tiredly pinches the bridge of his nose.{/n}

41a437ac-f2c5-46f8-b7cb-e9659276fdd2.Text: "Everything happened just as Speaks-With-Gods foresaw. The Starborn are back, and with them our—"

5857c387-1d0b-4800-83b8-68821f84931a.Text: "It is done. This good-for-nothing psyker has finally proved himself useful." {n}Winterscale looks around the settlement with a bored expression.{/n} "I intend to have a good night's sleep and enjoy the local delicacies. One good thing about Quetza Temer is that the fruit here is sweeter than Calixian honey and more tender than the meat of a young grox."

c113ce9f-2a04-40de-aacc-b4068ea0a3db.Text: "You should get some rest as well, {name}. And remember, it is better to go hunting when you are full of vigour, but slightly hungry. The hunger... adds acuity. Makes the kill more intoxicating, you know?"

aeafcdb7-495c-4e01-b6d9-79c7514e460a.Text: "Our meeting occurred just as Speaks-With-Gods foresaw." {n}The woman's accent grates on your ears — her words sound like a fusion of High Gothic and the most vulgar tongue of the rabble.{/n} "Welcome to the heart of the forest, Starborn. This ruler—"

a3f54a1c-6c52-41e3-881b-9c055cacdcdf.Text:
{n}You hear the elder whisper some sort of prayer as you approach:{/n} "...shelter your herd under your wing from the spirits-from-the-darkness.
O Eagle-God, dispel the darkness, and show us the way on our arduous path, and bless your Starborn scions..."

99db64a2-a7ac-4f4d-916b-67d3a0ad09e3.Text: "The name of this ruler is Leads-Ahead, O Starborn. And all of us..." {n}The elder looks at the settlement.{/n} "...are the children of the fiery mother and the pale father who look after us by day and guard us by night. The faithful servants of the Two-Headed Eagle-God who shields our lands from misfortune with His wings. We are the ungone forest-dwelling children of the earth and the guardians of the Temple of Quetza Temer — the first Starborn to have ever set foot on the virgin soil of this land."

cf3e9ad3-7085-4f37-b119-b40309ff5623.Text: "Because you are the Sky-Heralds of the Eagle-God, created by Him from the stars' glow and the night sky's darkness. The ones who carry His seal in your image, clad in the armour of our ancestors' most ancient prophecies."

da3aed9d-870c-4ee4-82ee-09f56f47e5e0.Text: "This ruler has lived many of Quetza Temer's seasons for this moment. Please, ask away, Starborn."

757fa00f-76d2-4acc-866a-127972dd6312.Text: "This ruler wishes not to lose her tongue for wearying the Starborn."

802b92ea-8ae9-4810-9f1e-9dd7d9b5a006.Text: "May the Eagle-God shelter you under His wing, Starborn."

ac19f4dc-b971-48c3-93d2-8163b0fc8fcf.Text: "Speaks-With-Gods is the priest of this tribe and this ruler's half-brother. He listens to the forest and calls to the earth, wards off the punishing lashes of the skies and speaks to the Eagle-God on behalf of our tribe. Before disappearing in the wandering forest, he told this ruler to prepare for your arrival."

a9f4691b-050f-4650-a1b2-ad1770d828f5.Text: "Speaks-With-Gods hears the whispers of the leaves and can commune with the tree spirits. Speaks-With-Gods performs soothing rituals when Quetza Temer needs them, just like today, and that allows this ruler and her people to tread on safe paths."

24817ce1-b83c-4e9c-9657-f6ec76f32aa4.Text: "Don't look at me, Lord Captain, I don't know the first thing about this priestly groxwash. It doesn't take a diviner to realise that I'd fry my brains if I tried to mess with some weird ritual... and that's if we were lucky. If we weren't so lucky, I'd end up frying everybody else's brains. Doesn't sound too promising, does it?"

55b071c3-982a-4327-add1-a4ad5580d7ca.Text: "Over hundreds of years, the limited minds of the rabble have invented their own twisted history, one that the colonists' descendants still believe to this day."

a44951cb-85ba-479d-b85c-2bfb37d72341.Text: {n}Calligos waves the woman away and turns his flinty gaze on Speaks-With-Gods.{/n} "I am sick and tired of aimlessly trudging through the woods, old man. I am a hunter. And without a quarry, I turn into quite the beast."

47352ea7-7940-4980-a9d4-22bb6cc2c121.Text: {n}Ulfar grunts in approval.{/n} "Hospitality is the banner of a worthy tribe. Respect for the spirits is the banner of a wise one. A fine planet."

1f4ebf16-468d-4f8d-9538-2e2e8cef87ff.Text: "Enough of your bleating, old hag! I already told you your speech offends me so — it makes me want to cut out your tongue."

7a513dfc-e47b-4090-82d4-9d2179c9e1cf.Text: {n}After making sense of the elder's speech, you realise several important things: Calligos Winterscale did, in fact, make planetfall on Quetza Temer. It would seem that he lost a psyker in battles with xenos and replaced him with a priest possessing psychic powers. Then they ventured into the forest, which drove the local flora into a frenzy, and the priest could not calm it in the middle of the forest labyrinth because the ritual can only be conducted in the village.{/n}

b80511e8-e7dd-4a51-9a63-466f790bca3c.Text: "Then this ruler and her tribe will pray for your success to the Eagle-God Himself, O Starborn."

7a61d57a-5a0b-4018-84c6-85690de55d7a.Text: "Enough of your bleating, old hag! I already told you your speech offends me so — it makes me want to cut out your tongue. Not even a Chorda preacher would have the patience to listen to you blather on about your stars, gods, spirits, and other nonsense."

6e097762-7967-4abb-870d-656ad2eac4cc.Text: {n}Humbly covering his eyes, the priest nods slightly.{/n} "Speaks-With-Gods is ready to conduct the ritual, O Starborn. The heart of the forest is calling out to me. So let this priest serve his gods not in word, but in deed."

5fa64e1d-260b-4d00-b155-6f9e4155127f.Text: "Speaks-With-Gods foresaw our meeting, Starborn." {n}The woman's accent grates on the ears — her words sound like a fusion of High Gothic and the most vulgar tongue of the rabble.{/n} "Welcome to the heart of the forest, where Leads-Ahead and her tribe have dwelt ever since the rule of Quetza Temer himself. This ruler has ordered her tribe to prepare a feast and warm shelter for our Starborn guests. Please, make yourselves at home."

c0cc921a-d36b-4f00-8cab-a943b3b216ed.Text: "Let me know when you are ready to depart. Or if you decide to share a few stories, then come to the bonfire. It's not often that two Rogue Traders can indulge in confidences away from prying ears." {n}Winterscale sardonically clicks his tongue and nonchalantly salutes you in farewell.{/n}

987fe4a8-1519-42e1-8f85-f02693de805f.Text: "Speaks-With-Gods hears the whispers of the leaves and can commune with the tree spirits. The entire tribe participates in his soothing rituals, and that allows this ruler and her people to tread on safe paths."

386ed2d7-396f-429a-affe-df4e56fec010.Text: "The ritual requires a site imbued with the powers of Quetza Temer — the heart of our village — and a priest to perform it. Alas, the fire-rain claimed many of this ruler's priests. And thus this ruler's tribe can only pray for the mercy of the Eagle-God and His Starborn Sky-Heralds."

7c4f6af6-783c-442e-9408-1851ed5903a4.Text: {n}The elder shifts her gaze to Ulfar.{/n} "Great spirit of the Eagle-God, we are glad to see you. This ruler will have the joints of your iron skin anointed with the oil of dire oak acorns so that they never corrode. And she will have sacred symbols drawn on your precious skin so that the spirits of this place may have no fear of you."

705db2eb-2e71-4eda-8692-251da9d4f8d7.Text: {n}The woman shakes her head.{/n} "The Eagle-God's Sky-Herald wanted to find the den of the spirits-from-the-darkness and destroy it. But the forest of Quetza Temer is as endless as the skies above. Where the sky touches the forest's edge, the Deadlands begin — the realm of the dead whence there is no return."

84824176-22e9-4c46-9290-c3214448a0d4.Text: {n}The elder looks at Idira with genuine reverence, nodding slightly after every word, her mouth half-open.{/n} "This ruler's brother did warn that a priestess-from-the-stars would descend upon this ruler's land in her search for answers. Just as he said, she would wish to head down the path of death to find reincarnation."

c5880471-b98d-4441-aa74-75f2be9a2fad.Text: "This ruler has already had the honour to greet a Starborn: as strong as a sabre-tooth boar, as nimble as a forest jha-guar, and as wise as the three-tongued guardian snake. Like a whirlwind, he charged into Quetza Temer's forest, chasing the spirits-from-the-darkness that had descended upon the world three ten-day moons before."

1d922152-fa1e-44ad-894f-990deab67b08.Text: "These lost souls have forgotten the true image of the God-Emperor! The only reminder they have is the sacred Aquila." {n}Argenta shakes her head sadly.{/n} "Calligos Winterscale should concern himself with educating his worlds instead of indulging his craving for the hunt."

00f062e9-2bbe-4129-b8d8-42f4c55151af.Text: "The Eagle-God, you say? Is it his brand that is burned on your forehead?"

405e7368-5e87-4376-a8b9-a894a40f92c8.Text: "Oh, yes." {n}The elder nods respectfully.{/n} "Many seasons have changed since this ruler received the Eagle-God's blessing and became the leader of this tribe. Only those close to the gods are allowed to bear their brands, and this ruler is one of them."

145f754b-11ee-4fcc-a63c-ba0b274c7f63.Text: "I thought that Quetza Temer was the name of this place, but you speak of it as if it were a figure from the past."

3dc01798-c4c2-4dbd-a128-86e151cf85ba.Text: "The legends of this place claim that a long time ago, the first among the Starborn descended upon this world together with this ruler's ancestors, created the ancient cities and temples, and brought the blessing of the Eagle-God unto these forests and lands. The fast-flowing time has erased the Starborn's name from the minds of the people. Only his title remains — Quetza Temer, the First of the Chosen, the Sky-Herald of the Eagle-God, and the Father of Tribes."

c47fd468-689e-4852-b12c-98ff17b38f2c.Text: "The flow of time is truly merciless to the meagre memory of peasants." {n}Cassia lets out a weary sigh and slightly rolls her eyes.{/n} "According to the works of the archivist Zacchary Fein III, Sebastian Winterscale was the first to discover this world for the Imperium's subjects. And half a century after, an ark descended to the planet's surface — the Quetza Temer."

406ee4b2-1d53-4113-9c6a-f5ec51810e6f.Text: {n}The elder's gaze darkens.{/n} "Quetza Temer is enraged by the invasion of the spirits-from-the-darkness that have called a rain of fire and metal upon this world. He demands blood — and blood shall sate the soil! No matter the path chosen by the gods who have come to right the wrong."

1a17d3c4-b089-47bf-942a-d5a03058d762.Text: {n}The elder recoils in fear after making out Yrliet's true face with her half-blind eyes.{/n} "Th-the Starborn will be accompanied by a spirit to put an end to the misfortunes of this world — thus spoke the priest. Seeing a spirit among the living is... wrong. Spirits should stay in the spirit realm, and humans in the realm of the living."

cee464a2-faf3-4c2e-ad19-96f8f43aec16.Text: "If only you knew, my honourable damaar, how I agree with your every word." {n}Jae casts a knowing glance at Yrliet, but says nothing more.{/n}

594797a5-b232-415f-bdd1-77bc21f6391f.Text: "The spirits from the darkness... So that is how the mon-keigh of this world see my kin. As invaders. A calamity." {n}Yrliet lets out a strained sigh.{/n} "But these mon-keigh have neither teeth nor claws. They are not even aware of the most basic technologies that your kind uses. So then why do my kin burn their world so fiercely?"

b68a0fbc-685d-4b89-8521-36a5c42a3e3d.Text: "We are the children of the fiery mother and the pale father who look after us by day and guard us by night. The faithful servants of the Two-Headed Eagle-God who shields our lands from misfortune with His wings. We are the ungone forest-dwelling children of the earth and the guardians of the Temple of Quetza Temer — the first Starborn to have ever set foot on the virgin soil of this land."

5af2023a-9763-4067-b9e3-08ad2b2b7ec8.Text: {n}The vox-caster under your armour suddenly spits out a cacophony of sounds: the growl of chainswords, human screams, the screech of metal, and the rattling interference of an active vox-cast. Working the buttons, switches, and tumblers only makes it worse.{/n}

cb500dc4-092d-4798-ac21-16e32e66f782.Text: {n}And the illusion fades away, leaving only a splitting headache in its wake.{/n}

5acf170c-6c3c-40b5-90f4-1bc30116f72c.Text: "O Star~orn, Sky-He~ld of th~ E~g~le-G~d, he~r t~e pra~ers of y~ur ~erv~nt, s~nt to ~ou thr~ugh ~he myr~ad for~ests of Quetza T~emer!" {n}Through the interference, you hear the familiar voice of Speaks-With-Gods, hoarse and feeble.{/n} "Th~ nigh~mare has be~come re~l, the dark~ess lef~ ~he ~fo~est~ But t~e lig~t of th~ ~dyin~ st~r c~n sti~l be sav~d! Th~ ~eart of ~he f~rest cal~s out f~r you..."

c3b6b79a-db33-4d45-b0b2-3b95bf31553d.Text: {n}The vox-caster hits the ground with a crunch, and a web of cracks scatters along the magno-glass. After a few more stomps, the device lets out one last screech... and falls silent.{/n}

fe3600fc-07fd-4c01-bbc8-db32328e6923.Text: {n}With the help of a portable vox-caster toolkit, you carefully remove the overheated battery from the vox, and the wave of sounds dies down.{/n}

c8af88b0-238e-4e96-ad43-993fc94b3e3c.Text: {n}The primitive design of the caster is crystal clear to you, but none of the manipulations you can think of prove effective — the vox-caster keeps groaning and hissing with static.{/n}

882265e1-e89f-4b5c-9d06-a13b0702fb10.Text: {n}But the calm does not persist for long — right before your eyes, the device's remains burst into purple sparks, and the squashed speaker emits the familiar voice of Speaks-With-Gods, hoarse and feeble.{/n}

fed50c53-3fe5-4c55-8376-93e96fd1c282.Text: {n}Skilfully wielding your tools, you open the device's case and check each part's condition. The vox-caster does not enjoy your manipulations and hisses at you, then the lumens on its screen glow red, and... the broadcast stops.{/n}

f64839af-d294-4752-bfeb-e2b11b2c8f92.Text: "O Star~orn, Sky-He~ld of th~ E~g~le-G~d, he~r t~e pra~ers of y~ur ~erv~nt, s~nt to ~ou thr~ugh ~he myr~ad for~ests of Quetza T~emer!" "Th~ nigh~mare has be~come re~l, the dark~ess lef~ ~he ~fo~est~ But t~e lig~t of th~ ~dyin~ st~r c~n sti~l be sav~d! Th~ ~eart of ~he f~rest cal~s out f~r you..."

77b36ed2-f783-4e14-8ee0-4944aa6ca2b5.Text: {n}But the calm does not persist for long — right before your eyes, the device's remains burst into purple sparks and the dead speaker emits the familiar voice of Speaks-With-Gods, hoarse and feeble.{/n}

82a3b78d-4d82-421f-a6dc-e9a44f3c810b.Text: "Aah!" {n}Idira digs her nails into her face, purple sparks gleaming at the ends of her hair.{/n} "The dusk sun has reached the treetops... And the crimson heart has struck its last beat... The dying stars have no hope left — run, fools! BACK!"

cf16d128-d3e9-4398-9623-7e42db03cacb.Text: "Grox's chunks, even a fresh recruit with his teeth knocked out would've given a clearer report! What happened there?"

4d22b9c8-97e6-4c80-afed-23fdc3f08e89.Text: "Quickly! We must return to the settlement! It may be a psyker's sorcery that leads us, but in the end, we will either help those who await us or purge this world of more corrupted delusions!"

2ba4c4c0-cc80-4e78-8831-db4d3a7c3d50.Text: "I could barely understand the speech of this mon-keigh, but one thing is clear — their settlement needs help. I care little about the woes of those primitive creatures... I am simply paying reparations for the pain that my kin have brought upon this world."

e9124c64-cec8-4b52-a27d-844e6d76dbba.Text: "By the Throne's radiance, those psykers certainly love speaking in riddles! And now we are supposed to go haring off and make guesses about what has happened!" {n}Abelard nervously fiddles with his moustache.{/n} "Still, his tone made it clear that it is nothing good, and I fear that it is already too late. A rotten feeling, I daresay."

6fd63a48-00f8-4917-aeea-c804e12eed2f.Text: "Processing acquired data. Restoring... Restoration complete." {n}The slightly altered voice of the priest comes from Pasqal's vox-system:{/n} "O Starborn, Sky-Herald of the Eagle-God, hear the prayers of your servant, sent to you through the myriad forests of Quetza Temer! The nightmare has become real, the darkness has left the forest. But the light of the dying star can still be saved! The heart of the forest calls out for you..."

4c0760d3-9341-450f-9b3a-b4c865f7ad6a.Text: {n}As soon as the priest's voice stops, your entire body arches with a crack as if electrocuted. You are standing on the tips of your toes, staring at a crimson sky at dusk that has turned into an ocean of spilt blood. Its still surface is broken by a hand with fingers covered in rings, and Calligos Winterscale emerges from the depths — only to take a single breath and disappear once more into the blood. It happens again, and again, and again... until he finally notices you. He throws out his hand and reaches for you... He reaches out... {/n}

9bc9f847-0a6c-45f5-af5e-f7783ca12d12.Text: {n}Closing his eyes in satisfaction, the Wolf says with deep feeling,{/n} "Do not try to drown out this voice, Aett-Vater. The Allfather sends us the music of this battle, calling us to the raven's feast. We must make haste!"

764ec9d4-5214-4ea2-88be-ecc0f1886318.Text: "He is gone. An unclean and painful end. I can hear it." {n}Kibellah speaks with perfect composure.{/n} "On the other side of that vox, only evil and unrighteous death remain."

c5957f5b-1bb5-4a6f-8990-83997af23d75.Text: "Are you suggesting that I go looking for the Haemonculus Throne-knows-where in the Deadlands?"

150f3816-443d-4ce4-8870-698c30900714.Text: "If you are here just to irritate me, then I will kill you as well."

182108cb-3732-443b-8708-28332986628d.Text: "I am tired of having to decipher the locals' speech. Abelard, find out what she wants."

41017fdc-68eb-47e7-9bbf-9c8327ec7bd4.Text: "This has been a riveting hunt, Calligos."

4cdced1c-a1dd-45af-a777-5299a836c806.Text: "Blood for the Rogue Trader's Throne? Did I hear that right?"

d1e2db4a-1b39-4973-b507-24bcc26e62e8.Text: "What will your tribe do now that you have lost your priest?"

5635bc13-0463-4574-8ce5-c4ff3de4ca5a.Text: "Am I free to traverse the forest without having to worry about its movements?"

148c9a89-1579-42e6-8537-725f63e1487d.Text: [Kill her] "You are of no more use to me."

327f2e04-7d92-447b-9dc0-f22bfac984b9.Text: "Tell the other tribes and their rulers that this world now belongs to the von Valancius dynasty."

8d0852e2-c0d1-47f1-974b-de5fca7d0d0a.Text: "I bet I killed more Aeldari than you did."

d8ac3a2a-ba25-461e-b817-c8a31ce5de0c.Text: "Wiping out all the xenos was unnecessary. They could have told us something about the Haemonculus."

730e42fa-8479-4dba-b241-b836c06e8a07.Text: {n}Leads-Ahead cautiously steps into the ancient ruins of her ancestors' city. She waves her hand at someone behind her, and several figures disappear into the forest's shadows.{/n} "O Starborn, the Two-Headed Eagle-God is merciful today, granting you the strength to crush the evil spirits! The descendants of this ruler will praise your bravery for ages to come!"

40a7ed30-f6da-467a-9c7a-35ebb653a62a.Text: {n}Kibellah flashes her an ominous smile.{/n} "Who do you think the Domin is? Even in a den of hollow bodily pleasures, {mf|he|she} would find a worthy enemy just as easily as on the field of battle."

c9a5e9b1-d227-448a-ab23-d73cac4e61a5.Text: "Well, the coordinates are vague, to put it mildly. But if we pinpoint the scans, our augurs may be able to spot the xenos scum. Or whatever is left of him, I should say."

7dde24e7-2da4-4429-b925-b61d95d69dfc.Text: "Before leaving, the brother of this ruler shared another nightmare with her: in the Deadlands, there is a monster whose body is made up of bodies sewn together with rusty threads. It waits for a fallen star, trembles, hides... and guards a secret that is darker than a starless sky. A secret about the past and thoughts about the future."

1fdf34a5-753f-480c-a043-abc9cdb7126c.Text: "I-I humbly beg your forgiveness for the foolishness of this ruler's words, for the Deadlands do indeed spread as far as the eye can see... However, this ruler's brother was not precise in his predictions..."

e5ccf09a-1c73-4637-90bf-805d97f627e8.Text: "Finally, I can go to the Emperor's Vow, to my cosy cabin with a bottle of Calixian amasec and a hot bath. I will see you among the stars, new blood! Stay on your toes around the self-righteous and try not to perish in the warp before our next meeting."

fdd9f186-1155-4e2d-b9d5-c90d4ad0c727.Text: {n}The woman notices the body of Winterscale and nods her head sadly.{/n} "Before departing, the brother of this ruler warned her that their paths would never cross again, for one star from the sky shall eclipse the other. When the gods are in discord, all that is left to do for us mortal folk is to pray for their mercy."

7bb439e6-39b4-4a98-92cb-5960220f5e18.Text: "In the Deadlands... there is a monster whose body is made up of bodies sewn together with rusty threads. It waits for a fallen star, trembles, hides... And guards a secret that is darker than a starless sky... A secret about the past and the thoughts about the future." {n}The priest's violet eyes glow gold, then return to their original colour a moment later. His gaze dims, and he comes back to his senses, blinking apologetically.{/n}

5735f709-e71b-49b2-89ba-6a81120079f4.Text: "Ha... ha ha ha ha ha!" {n}Calligos Winterscale is standing in the heart of an abated battle, covered head to toe in the blood of his enemies. His excited smile gradually twists into a grin, and his glazed eyes emanate an alarming coldness.{/n} "The xenoscum struggled to the very end — now that's what I call a hunt! It's a shame I missed the garishly dressed one. I wish I could have cracked his horned mask along with his skull."

7ab0628f-f9c7-4619-8004-d8eedea2d724.Text: "As for me, I will finally go to the Emperor's Vow, to my cosy cabin with a bottle of Calixian amasec and a hot bath. I will see you among the stars, new blood! Stay on your toes around the self-righteous and try not to perish in the warp before our next meeting."

bb0ba59f-31b2-4f5e-b22b-a6366472eb73.Text: "As if I am not... Ahem. As you command, Lord Captain."

58bcd5a7-9a17-4e44-9a8b-b456b370f10a.Text: "Allow me to report, Lord Captain: according to the acquired data, the lair of a certain 'monster' — the Haemonculus, presumably — is located on a neighbouring continent, the so-called Deadlands. The coordinates are vague, to put it mildly. But if we pinpoint the scans, our augurs may be able to spot the xenos scum. Or whatever is left of him, I should say."

b86c5258-9839-4d64-9dc5-ffa0a333b1f8.Text: "You and I now share the bond of battle, {name}! Let me know if you ever feel like shooting some xenos, and I might just bless you with my company." {n}Calligos winks at you.{/n} "And I, in turn, will have no choice but to invite you on my future hunts."

5e408a6a-afea-4393-81d7-8127bf152712.Text: "Better than yours, that's for sure." {n}Calligos's tone is provoking.{/n} "There is nothing better than raw power and direct blows. Standing face to face with your foe with an axe in hand, breathing in their fear and rage, crushing them with your own body... Only in such moments do I feel truly mortal... and exhilaratingly alive!"

5b4208b0-d036-4e1b-9c0f-85596cba457a.Text: "Hear... what?" {n}Winterscale shrugs his shoulders incredulously.{/n} "I don't remember saying that. But anything can trip off the tongue in the heat of battle."

83d74cef-6091-45a6-ab01-64af3b2ca9a8.Text: "This ruler will think of something. The neighbouring tribes are indebted to her tribe. They would be honoured to offer this ruler their priest or one of their apprentices as a gift."

9e9ffb9e-237b-48fd-9ddf-eb8985e331f3.Text: "Oh yes, Starborn! You have banished the darkness from the forests of Quetza Temer with your own hands, and the ritual of Speaks-With-Gods soothed the tree spirits for many moons ahead. The paths are open."

c014211d-7081-4d32-bcd7-a994e83dc1b4.Text: {n}Her eyes widen in fear — but only for a moment.{/n} "If the Sky-Herald demands a sacrifice, this ruler is honoured to serve as one."

4adfaf79-5a61-42d9-badc-7dd49f1e8444.Text: "May the Eagle-God save you, O Starborn."

a352595b-3e2a-4ea2-92f9-36961883c88c.Text: "Throne's gold, I forgot how much excitement you can have with an unsanctioned psyker!" {n}Winterscale smiles, as pleased as if a rare treasure had jumped into his hands all by itself.{/n} "Let's call this my parting gift to you, {name}. You wanted horror stories about the Haemonculus? Then it's off to the Deadlands for you!"

6175de50-ad0c-4702-a25c-e5b49b0efec7.Text: {n}The violet eyes of Speaks-With-Gods glaze over at these words.{/n}

26b27ef7-71b8-49e9-8931-72e9a0f0eb1e.Text: "When the Starborn are silent, the Eagle-God speaks with their souls unseen."

2427e79d-6f1f-43ae-87fd-bab11aa10d75.Text: "Let not the Starborn be angry with this ruler!" {n}With trembling hands, the old woman blesses herself with an intricate sign vaguely resembling the Aquila.{/n}

7e4909d1-5548-4a8c-9594-c105b67cdfd9.Text: {n}Leads-Ahead blinks in confusion and shrugs.{/n} "As long as the gods favour the inhabitants of Quetza Temer, we will continue to pray for the goodness of their eternal lives. If a god{mf||dess} claims that the world now belongs only to {mf|him|her}, then, with the blessing of the God-Father, the Two-Headed Eagle-God, we entrust our lives to {mf|his|her} will!"

ab685d4f-9226-455d-8b1e-e66524f3c531.Text: {n}Worten the Grey nods at every word of his master, licking the fresh blood off a thin blade.{/n}

1fa51704-33d3-46aa-9d04-e2466000d796.Text: "Do my ears deceive me? A challenge — for me?" {n}Winterscale roars with laughter.{/n} "I usually don't count my foes in the middle of a battle, but we'll make a wager next time!"

4350134b-4283-4906-89db-dc126bf1794d.Text: "Or you were lied to, and there is no Haemonculus on this world at all. In any case, you can ask the locals — their psykers talk to the trees or some such nonsense. Maybe one of their 'dire oaks' will tell you something." {n}He offers you a sarcastic smirk, enjoying his little joke.{/n}

2509f8a9-2e3d-4451-ad7b-cbf78cce5af3.Text: {n}Silver sparks flash at the ends of Speaks-With-Gods's hair, distracting Calligos from the conversation. The priest shudders as if from cold, moans, claws at his face with his nails... and throws his head back to face the sky.{/n}

c332e9ec-db1d-4df8-aff0-2b10d2f3993b.Text: "Oh, I don't know about... No, you're right. Throne damn it, you're right. You're both psychopaths looking for your own death, that's all I have to say!"

221cbd86-41bf-477e-86a6-12f81f6dbb1e.Text: {n}Jae sighs in defeat.{/n} "Can we go not to 'the Deadlands,' but to, say, a local bar? No? Just for a change of scenery."

6aff5dd5-5dc2-4b1b-bd5d-d925962952c4.Text: "Did you not foresee this in your visions?"

3a10833b-0aad-489c-a44e-c829bbadeef6.Text: "Your way of speaking is strange, just like your sister's."

d1d157b6-9b50-4469-8155-8f7cb860d220.Text: "Do you know that sorcery such as yours is punishable by death in the Imperium?"

8b45fabd-131d-4958-9e20-df4317ad2756.Text: "You are a good man. Even if you are an unsanctioned psyker."

baeed8a0-94d9-4f73-ba4c-51c733024c6c.Text: "Tell me, how did you and Winterscale survive all this time?"

370e222f-78f7-4a8a-b230-2add06bbf751.Text: "Do you mean to say that Winterscale killed his Seneschal?"

01540afc-a4ac-47de-81fe-da080cc4a34c.Text: "What consequences of my coming to this world did you see in your visions?"

7ec96064-f65f-475f-bf8b-6b6aa7160983.Text: "Pray that your forest does not cause any more trouble."

b1f70603-75ba-4f93-8380-1bd5dcb0f96d.Text: "Did the ritual truly make the forest safe?"

566cd182-d3a8-43aa-b346-160252acb082.Text: {n}The sinewy old man bows his head in reverence.{/n} "With your arrival, the blessing of the Two-Headed Eagle-God has descended upon Quetza Temer, O Starborn! This servant of the skies, earth, and those in between foresaw this conversation in his dreams a long time ago. This servant hopes that Leads-Ahead and her tribe welcomed the Sky-Herald of the faraway stars with utmost reverence."

c516888a-8d6e-4232-8092-0433c14376c4.Text: "Speaks-With-Gods is the name of this humble servant of the forests, rivers, and mountains. For when the Two-Headed Eagle-God speaks — this servant listens, and recounts the words to his tribe, and the tribe carries out His will."

65058634-f447-491b-90ce-1923c0202462.Text: {n}Idira almost snorts with delight.{/n} "If only the holy folk of the Ecclesiarchy could hear that! Equating our 'unclean powers' with the God-Emperor's blessing... That's brilliant, just brilliant!"

8910f51a-b371-42bd-ba51-0ea00be9d378.Text: {n}The priest nods affirmatively.{/n} "The spirits-from-the-darkness brought the fire-rain down on Quetza Temer, killing many of the tribes who had cared for the forests young and ancient. This blasphemy enraged the guardian spirits, but as soon as this servant of the wind, rain, and sand soothed them with the ritual sacrifices and divine sorcery, their wrath gave way to mercy."

deda2240-8d2c-4ecb-a88e-3a08bab039bc.Text: "May the Two-Headed Eagle-God shelter you under His wing, O Sky-Herald!"

86d0848f-5f8a-4903-af85-a2e79ecda768.Text: {n}The old man closes his eyes, and his body sways to the rustling of the leaves and the babbling of the stream.{/n} "This servant of dreams, nightmares, and reveries can see things that others cannot see. What has transpired and what is yet to be. Your appearance in the heart of the forest and..." {n}The priest falters for a moment.{/n} "...the consequences it bears for Quetza Temer."

6b3bfe47-3172-42ea-8c13-eec874d1958c.Text: {n}The old man looks down, embarrassed.{/n} "Forgive the servants of Quetza Temer for their speech, O Starborn! No matter how much the ancestors tried to pass the language of the gods on to their descendants, the tribes seldom use it, for the gods only descend from their heavenly palace not more often than once in three life-dwells."

bd54ffac-7d51-4a24-afba-7eacee9ddecf.Text: "The dreams come and go, Sky-Herald of the faraway stars. Sometimes this servant of the gods can understand the mystical visions of the days of old or the future... But even Speaks-With-Gods cannot fully comprehend the divine design of the Two-Headed Eagle-God. Sometimes I am blind even when I can see."

0763fd15-f452-42ab-8c7a-5f85689d0404.Text: {n}The old man is deep in thought.{/n} "Imperium... This servant of the stars, clouds, and eclipses does not know this word. The priest's sorcery is a gift from the Two-Headed Eagle-God. How can His gift be condemned by mortals?"

74b7c196-46df-41d8-bf74-3475ed1c831c.Text: {n}The old man smacks his lips, pleased with the praise.{/n} "Blessed is a life that serves the Two-Headed Eagle-God and His Sky-Heralds!"

f48ea41a-0a69-4471-9a2f-f482fc6d0146.Text: {n}The priest shudders, his eyes staring into space over your shoulder. His pupils dilate, and his head leans to the side... Then, after dispelling the vision seen by him alone, he gives you a friendly smile.{/n} "Silent questions hang in the air... This servant knows much, and even more is unknown. But if the Starborn seeks answers, this servant will not hesitate to help."

b1b41bbb-13a7-45ef-8b04-282617ae8177.Text: "The Starborn who carries the seal of Quetza Temer's descendant is strong in both body and will — as befits a god. This servant, like the rest of his entourage, had grown weak on just the seventh night of our journey. But the Starborn continued to lead us fearlessly, pressing forward to seek out the spirits-from-the-darkness even among the twisted paths, delivering the sky's judgement!"

6fb8fd89-f0df-43bb-be7e-3f3a59f6115e.Text: "This servant of the grass, flowers, and trees regrets only the imminent death of the Starborn's companion, the one you call the Seneschal. He quarrelled with the iron-clad guardian, and his words enraged the Starborn... And thus he slashed the unfortunate man's body up with his axe, and threw the remains to the wild animals of Quetza Temer for them to feast on."

3baf5c88-63ee-4971-8f5f-e98524cfa69b.Text: "This servant saw everything with his own two eyes." {n}The old man pauses in hesitation, then continues,{/n} "It is not proper, perhaps, for a mere speck of dirt under the heels of a Sky-Herald of the Two-Headed Eagle-God, to muse upon the deed... However, this servant did sense, with his entire being, the rage that possessed the Starborn at that moment. And the iron-clad guardian revelled in his god's wrath."

dd3b8043-3c50-477d-adcc-ee6229005fe4.Text: "This servant knew that you would say that."
