I undertook a dozen expeditions into the unknown, moved the dynasty capital to Footfall, named Vladaym my governor and made Hieronymus a cardinal. Not too bad for a novice, wouldn't you say?"

e19464c0-a040-4579-bdc2-9840fb983a44.Text: "If you do not sing your own praises, who will? Never has that been more true!"

7f2e524a-746c-44fe-b08e-60d7ce1a95b7.Text: "And yet, I was the only one clever enough to become the {mf|master|mistress} of my own fate and not be reduced to someone else's plaything or a slave to dogma."

7c970b3b-5e13-48e7-9b90-3a8b110225f9.Text: "I shall give you a moment to wallow in your envy and self-loathing."

db56e646-2c70-4934-9309-6e7272828c1f.Text: "You must have arrived from the universe of milksops and weaklings. I am disgusted at the very thought that a counterpart of mine not only refused to serve Chaos but also befriended a lowlife like you."

181689b2-b22a-4bff-9a27-1c91cc0f02d7.Text: "An alliance between the Children of Asuryan and humans? You speak of impossible things, and yet... your ardour makes one want to believe you. Perhaps in your reality, false elantach, our kinfolk have gained wisdom and tolerance beyond my understanding."

179ae6b7-5e11-4863-905d-7c61d8c60164.Text: "What? Vladaym, a hero who chose to sacrifice himself? Your world really is nothing like ours!"

7a2b683b-3723-47c4-bc59-09dc1a8af5b3.Text: "The lack of pointless advice, I presume. On the day Kunrad killed Theodora, all of her officers died with her, including Mort, Abelard, Idira, Ravor, Vigdis... When I came into my inheritance, there was no one to teach me how to be a Rogue Trader. I handled everything myself and found out who Theodora von Valancius really was."

eab270d4-a94f-4daf-99e7-906b91e1b779.Text: "We shall fight. I sense your souls' greedy interest in what is hidden in this crypt. And I will not allow you to take possession of this blasphemous thing!"

cf31f99d-8b85-42eb-8925-039ec60ffed7.Text: "But I see we are outnumbered compared to you, doppelganger. I think it would be wise to join forces, topple you first, and then resolve the conflict between those who have survived."

24601bc4-5efe-4bc0-94ca-e6559fa5a5cf.Text: "I am afraid we have no choice but to fight. What is hidden on this world imperils the millions of lives for which I am responsible. For their sake, I will crush any opponent... unless you all retreat without a fight."

52b186f6-614c-41ad-81f5-7a08ef6d2e93.Text: "I concur. We will finish off the one with the biggest retinue first and then decide who is worthy of the prize. However, I already know who it's going to be."

d87fd237-29d6-4baf-8e83-cef15c023760.Text: "I was finished off by xenos?" {n}Calligos smiles.{/n} "Come closer, {mf|boy|girl}, and I will show you the real Calligos Winterscale instead of the cheap knockoff who bore that name in your reality."

3e78e0d4-3928-44ff-9bd7-bb3b85c14725.Text: "I hope it was me who led the Reaving Tempest and not that bitch Yremeryss?"

461c9525-8600-405c-9482-ef1c0d40aef2.Text: "I have to admit this version of you is not without a certain charm. The kind where I don't quite know if I want to throw myself at you or empty a full clip right into your face."

864d9b62-90cd-4bff-9f2a-f45ac8ad712e.Text: "After the purging of Janus, the xenos of Crudarach and the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest forged a profane alliance against my protectorate, but with the noble Space Wolves, I defeated their combined forces and banished them from the Expanse."

3b7d3eea-7ff1-41aa-a8cd-5be908639e32.Text: "A great deed is not accomplished by peacemaking. It is accomplished by spilling blood with a righteous hand!"

6c4dd4e5-78ac-4559-b336-3f4f6a3a57b6.Text: "If more than one von Valancius walks away from here, the spoils will have to be shared. And Rogue Traders never share."

03a02c48-9785-40d2-92b5-b8edda388932.Text: "Indeed, Rogue Traders are doomed to forever feud with one other. Such is the power of that poison called ambition that seeps from our Warrants."

49754a0c-41ec-4048-bdbb-6159dd4806d0.Text: "Killing yourself is a peculiar form of martyrdom. Martyrdom in the name of profit!"

6561f7f6-1e29-4b85-9149-4479d7050bed.Text: "I remember in whose name the sacred Warrant was granted. I remember by whose hand I am ordained to exist. I believe, and my faith is a bright light driving back the darkness. But your faith is cold embers, and when I look at you, I feel ashamed of myself."

f521dc2c-fac6-4746-8697-398c5ba14d53.Text: "Most definitely. I say this as a Seneschal, an officer, and a nobleman: shoot the {mf|bastard|bitch}."

dfe4a4f1-d888-4f1a-9f9b-c7fcd225ae86.Text: "Emperor, why do you so rarely send me heretics who are this eager to confess? My job would be so much easier."

d0373115-34c3-4acb-bada-f385b39847e8.Text: "The Lord Inquisitor from your reality must be pleased with you."

01ecd8d4-345b-4f72-a6ff-38b4b994f14c.Text: "And I become very principled and vengeful where my treasure hoard is concerned."

e69116e6-cfbc-4cf5-b207-e8992e646a60.Text: "The old heretic warrants no regrets. Her soul was as filthy as the feet of the sailors treading the lower decks of my ship."

678f01b1-6136-4392-a6fd-71b95930363a.Text: "Your ears cannot hear the truth of the Emperor."

2bc0c2a8-160b-408d-8429-5cb7a673122a.Text: "Not yet enough. I struck down Calligos Winterscale, a champion of Khorne, in the ruins of Dargonus. I joined forces with the benevolent Incendia Chorda to purge the Cult of the Final Dawn when they incited a rebellion and used Footfall to summon a Greater Daemon named the Edge of Daybreak. The unclean spirit is now sealed within the station that I have proclaimed forsaken forever."

525e221b-99f0-46d6-a37d-d494319086de.Text: {n}You notice that your replica is sporting elaborate makeup. Under a layer of powder, the doppelganger's face looks strange, its skin covered in wrinkles. Somehow they remind you of... closed eyelids.{/n}

ef39835d-8790-4b6d-8503-3333e6cd50f3.Text: "Duty. I do not know what exactly Xavier has in mind, but judging by his past actions, it will be ambitious and terrible. He must be stopped."

333a5aa2-0bf0-4caf-9e39-75d4a5b94ac5.Text: "At least now there is no doubt that her execution was pleasing to the Emperor."

1bcbf9e6-e64c-4c6a-9094-5b9fce31799a.Text: "I have been taught some harsh lessons. When Kunrad staged the coup, I was badly wounded. Abelard nursed me back to health, and so did the entire crew. They looked after me and the protectorate for months while I was in limbo, a dark and joyless sleep in which I only heard Theodora's last words: 'Protect my people.' When I awoke, I vowed to do exactly that. To be not a master to my people but their protector and their champion."

62c3052c-43df-456e-b8f4-b85dcf3a507a.Text: "Shut up, servant. In our reality, it is customary for lackeys not to interfere in the affairs of their betters."

ce198e54-b7ab-4cbf-a44f-524703fe0db8.Text: {n}Your doppelganger resolutely clenches {mf|his|her} fist around an oddly shaped wraithbone talisman. The Aeldari wear such amulets as a token of a special bond with someone... Or a token of remembrance for the dead.{/n}

7306f8be-2d35-4e60-a719-41003a1b16dd.Text: {n}Your double appears to be quite discomfited. {mf|He|She} nervously clutches an oddly shaped talisman in {mf|his|her} fist... You do not possess such an item.{/n}

03cc3185-46c8-4a95-a0e0-760e71a0271a.Text: {n}Your doppelganger vigorously chops the air with {mf|his|her} hand, and you notice some stiffness in the movement, as well as a subtle grimace of pain. As you look closer, you realise that lurking under your replica's clothes are chains of penance with jagged hooks digging into {mf|his|her} flesh. Such instruments of humility are only worn by the most fervent believers.{/n}

e870971e-9e85-44b6-a0d1-c260b7691b39.Text: {n}Your doppelganger vigorously chops the air with {mf|his|her} hand, a grimace of stern determination twisting {mf|his|her} face.{/n}

29943298-789f-46f1-a0b9-dd29a6c79c0b.Text: "My sweet smuggler. You are also in my world, you know. I gave you a little planet with a pretty palace and a tiny garden after you took offence at a couple of innocent jokes about your... humble origins."

c5c2f2a2-1e20-4056-a926-da8348a4460f.Text: "Throw myself at you, or empty a full clip into your face. It's a tough one."

9290842a-b197-4d55-bac3-f1f5d5ce2363.Text: "A narcissistic, unscrupulous, self-serving bitch who lied to everyone. I admit I regretted not getting the chance to know her better... I embraced her principles and realised that literally everyone in the Koronus Expanse was out to take advantage of me. The Drusians and the pirates, the Adeptus Mechanicus and the Kasballica, Calcazar and Uralon... And so the puppet pulled at the strings and made its masters dance. I dare say things turned out well for me."

a8c33c76-a3b2-4b7a-8825-c723d10294aa.Text: "In short, you've gone from being a Rogue Trader to being a piece of kraken shit. This is very interesting, but shut up." {n}Ulfar shifts his gaze to you.{/n} "I have just realised I have not given your spiritual fortitude the credit it deserves, Aett-Vater."

4a0855b4-cd39-45fe-8d46-962a5d1b1fd5.Text: "No. I butchered you in my world, ignominiously and brutally. I can show you how."

cb9dc384-088b-4b43-8def-b111cf3160f4.Text: "Sorry, but after hearing about the destruction of the crypt and the despicable thing {mf|he|she} did, I just have to shoot that {mf|bastard|bitch}."

569d182d-7a01-4eaf-bed9-392cb2a309f0.Text: "That will not be necessary. And I was almost starting to like you."

d35c02eb-c85f-4ad2-ba1c-d8c3afc65243.Text: "It was plunged into a horrifying massacre. You were one of the first to die, by the way."

355a8f5e-5f9a-4fd1-90a2-714c080f823f.Text: "Hmm. It appears I have managed to get myself killed in every one of your realities. It is sad to see the fruits of my own failures."

454e8ed1-7965-46b7-b7d6-c2ad4859325f.Text: "Indeed. I see a future without words. Or you."

39a1737d-695a-42ff-904e-133d53c5e6ae.Text: {n}Ulfar shifts an approving glance from your double to you, then mutters quietly into his beard,{/n} "I'll be! {mf|He|She} is your Aett-Vater still. Changing sides would be... No!"

be0c8316-9734-418f-a148-d57bbb113048.Text: "Student and mentor at best. Need I explain who would have been the mentor?"

dff18005-33bf-4617-9679-8441de0206c7.Text: "You won't believe how little I care about what you think."

2bd23e3c-7e7e-4d46-9725-7413fda37a98.Text: {n}Your doppelganger's slightly accelerated speech, jerky movements, and the sweet twinkle in {mf|his|her} eyes suggest that {mf|his|her} blood is teeming with euphoric stimulants.{/n}

460665d8-2b09-4f77-a3e4-2fba16d1fd47.Text: "Oh, I have! My empire is no paltry protectorate — it stretches across Winterscale's domain and the worlds of Chorda. With my brother Kunrad as regent, together we rule many planets. I deceived Uralon the Fool and banished him from the Expanse after subverting his cult. I taught the brazen Drukhari a lesson by sending the Orsellio Navigators into Commorragh to cause the most powerful dysjunction in history! On Quetza Temer, I struck down the furious Calligos, a rival for the favour of the dark gods, and used his blood to make a pact with the Edge of Daybreak, my illustrious teacher."

b2415767-f04d-4a2b-b742-0fb6921288d4.Text: "It happened on the day Kunrad Voigtvir wounded me with the cursed blade. From then on, I started hearing voices. Fortunately, my companion Idira taught me how to avoid going insane, and I began to listen to... and heed their wisdom. They revealed secrets to me and whispered the dark rituals. I raided the von Valancius crypt, made a dark offering of Theodora's skull, and enslaved her spirit. I learned all of her dirty secrets, all of her lies."

ec21c607-5e41-4653-a086-402cfa9b89f1.Text: "My Master, the Changer of Ways, directed me here and revealed my destiny. This is where I will cut short the life of the corpse emperor's champion and claim the great trophy. This is where I am fated to become one with the warp."

7148f5a7-32c3-48f5-b400-b284eea23a4e.Text: {n}Her emerald-green eyes light up with surprise, sorrow, and confusion all at once.{/n} "So you and I walked arm in arm in this other world too, elantach. And since the keepsake is now in your possession... my Path was cut short before yours."

b5432d40-f73d-4561-bb21-2ef4e8a97958.Text: "House Orsellio would never swear allegiance to someone like you! We follow His light, and you... you are twisted chaos incarnate..."

76b2bfec-04b9-4a8b-a617-df179c70a6d5.Text: {n}Your replica hesitates before answering:{/n} "A worthy one."

4c1f3fa8-3458-4a5e-b21c-866cf5eb45d5.Text: "Good. Let's do it again." {n}His grin grows even wider.{/n}

0b832a7f-98a5-4f1f-90f6-eb552b88bdb0.Text: "After I beheaded the Kabal's Dracon, the Reaving Tempest became more flexible in its approach to alliances."

07d1426a-a869-470a-af40-7cbe5c993d55.Text: "Rubbish! The burden of power is a fiction invented by the powerful to shield themselves against envy. I did just fine on my own and proved that I need no one else. Do you hear me? No one!"

3216802b-8b94-4035-837b-49257077260e.Text: "The Fellowship of the Void became a respectable merchant guild. Vladaym shed almost all his thuggish habits... but died when Xavier turned Footfall into a colossal projectile, which he crashed into Eufrates II after it was captured by Uralon the Cruel. Thousands died that day. But tens of thousands were safely evacuated by Vladaym, and I welcomed them to Dargonus."

19ddde09-83b4-4ef1-b58b-d2ec9ec626f5.Text: {n}The Wolf turns to Marazhai and adds with a laugh:{/n} "Did you hear that? We massacred you wretches!"

8006a013-bc9a-44d4-b996-d06a7dde37ed.Text: {n}The Wolf turns to Yrliet and adds with a laugh:{/n} "Did you hear that? We massacred you wretches!"

958a2085-ec1c-48ba-abc0-fceff666ade0.Text: "Idira, shereen... you have become the nightmare you have been running from all this time. You told me about the visions you had of your dark fate — isn't this the future you cursed and vowed to avoid, even if it meant slitting your own throat?"

d106a16a-0cce-44db-bcc8-44d692a84a9b.Text: {n}Abelard... Your Abelard shares a look of understanding and deep respect with the Seneschal from the alternate reality.{/n}

48f4ffda-7037-4af0-ad7a-9b209c0aa3d0.Text: {n}An eternal darkness clouds Idira's eyes. There is no trace of regret or doubt in that darkness. Nor of Idira Tlass herself.{/n}

443aec6f-9a76-4fb5-8687-deeeeb637688.Text: "Now I see that Asuryan has blessed my Path, for in this reality, I met a human with a powerful and radiant soul unyielding to corruption."

02461967-cc14-46ea-830e-4aa89611d440.Text: "It filled me on the day that Sister Argenta and I executed Theodora for heresy. I saw all her wickedness and depravity, and felt unclean, stained by her blood. So I swore to redeem the name of the dynasty."

24133062-0b97-45c7-b26c-f7c6feacc495.Text: "I remember you, little xenos. I see you have lost your spirit stone in this reality, too... and yet you survived? How amusing. As amusing as it is to recall how you and your kin begged for mercy as I sent you off, one after another, to the feast of the Lord of Pleasure."

3d50845c-6c8f-4269-88f8-30825ce6c783.Text: "I cannot help but ask... What became of Commorragh after your stunt?"

6bcfad1b-4808-45b7-bab4-c25d6e24b7b2.Text: "I remember you, little xenos. I remember you and your kin begging for mercy as I sent you off, one after another, to the feast of the Lord of Pleasure."

6c733280-2f43-4213-84b7-0e775eca222f.Text: {n}Your doppelganger appears to be quite discomfited. {mf|He|She} clutches a strange talisman nervously in {mf|his|her} fist... It is identical to the farewell gift Yrliet gave you in the forests of Quetza Temer.{/n}

219c23f9-b1c3-4cd5-8960-28d40b72f637.Text: {n}It is identical to the farewell gift Yrliet gave you in the forests of Quetza Temer.{/n}

1582d42e-44ae-413f-92f4-907e435498f7.Text: {n}Your alter ego nods, slowly and sorrowfully.{/n} "Forgive me, Yrliet Lanaevyss. You took the Kabal Dracon's blow that was meant for me, but the chirurgeons were unable to heal your wounds. Still... it is a great joy to see you alive again."

d12ecaf3-222a-4f8e-95e2-23153b36d16e.Text: "By the Exalted One, my fiery-hearted shereen, our friendship would not have blossomed under the light of every star, it seems."

56f93287-49d5-4229-804d-76b219bcd1d9.Text: {n}The mention of the former Novator of the House makes Cassia flinch.{/n} "Wh— what? I... I think you mistake me for someone else."

ca0fbde2-c83c-47b3-9bb5-c0a125f5e6ce.Text: "Ah. Tisiphone. My sworn friend and the most overbearing shrew in all the Expanse. Of course you're here as well." {n}The copy nods meaningfully at Cassia.{/n} "Nice to see you in the thick of things as usual."

49e5d1b9-ef4a-4983-bd41-3642670cf7f0.Text: "Indeed. In this rancid reality, you are some kind of... pathetic parody of yourself."

28bf7946-d52c-484a-a742-d1e479b9e647.Text: "I saw the full picture and realised that only the strongest survive in the Expanse. And any strength is good enough to survive."

bcfe31a7-ad3d-4029-8df0-dabf16f92f25.Text: {n}The copy casts a contemptuous glance at Jae.{/n} "You. The abject grovelling creature who chose to sell out to the Archenemy instead of atoning for her transgressions under my guidance. Your rotten soul was reborn in cleansing flame."

e7fe1502-1138-4a2f-a2fd-57fb7f5b604e.Text: {n}Ulfar rumbles heartily.{/n} "Hah! That must have been a glorious hunt! But maybe it will come to pass in our world too!"

61e6c7cf-741c-4d27-be74-4e1ddd236af5.Text: "Emperor, what an insufferably smug, arrogant, and childishly insolent creature... How can a single Rogue Trader embody everything they are loathed for?"

ef2d9350-5839-4f5d-9e43-69da29c848f8.Text: "I would ask your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} to watch your language as you speak of Her Ladyship Theodora. I do not know how it is in your reality, but in ours, it is customary to mind one's manners."

a4a2ec8f-4714-48b7-b791-811c3cd0a6f8.Text: "The scars upon your soul bleed an ashen azure. Yet your heart is bursting with flares of the most incredible hues — crystal-clear colours without any additions or impurities. A pure heart... I had all but forgotten they existed."

f2edc06f-c9ef-4833-b03b-7b181632d1aa.Text: {n}Cassia covers her eyes with her hand and shakes her head sorrowfully.{/n} "The heat of your hues is blinding, Lord Captain. Scarlet and gold shroud your very essence in an overpowering radiance, but deep inside... I see a palpitating smudge of sable blue which you have banished, which you loathe, and which ruins the perfection of the image. Are you afraid... of a misstep? Of loneliness? Of the Emperor turning away from you?"

6f0ead4c-0560-43f7-8a6a-c64a21a01b77.Text: "Do not dare lay your accursed eye on me!" {n}The copy's roar is deafeningly loud.{/n} "How did you even survive the cleansing of Eurac V, monster of House Orsellio? Felek and I crushed your mad followers and purged the Navigator House of corruption. Did your heretical powers enthral my copy's weak spirit in this reality? How ignoble. How disgraceful."

b9484728-45fd-46b0-9e16-cf23fcec9c50.Text: "The Bloodspun Web would never have let you defile the remains of the Domini." {n}Kibellah leans forward.{/n} "Did you..."

73de0e36-a9d0-4f72-b25f-b1fffab4f6aa.Text: "Me? Please. It was all your doing! My loyal assassin who has acquired a taste for blood. You tracked down and eviscerated every last spinner on my ship and became known as the Spider Queen who spends her days relishing slaughter and pleasure. Join me while you still can — I have much to offer you."

741d6be1-7a56-4310-9b5b-bcb70da22ea9.Text: "Your thread is familiar to me. As are the thorns of humility under your clothes. Who... instructed you?"

103e29d7-fa0d-4caa-a1bc-fa6a0e31fcdc.Text: "The same man who taught you. The honoured Vizsier revealed to me much about how one should show their faith in Him. As for these thorns... of course you would recognise them. You wore them for many years before presenting them to me."

0bf786c0-454c-495e-a1ae-4df9fb1407bb.Text: "You see? If even Vladaym was able to turn to the path of—"

cd128d03-3eda-4c88-a7a6-b115f6ec6e1e.Text: "Oh, for the Exalted One's sake, will you ever get sick of edifying me, lawman? Wait, don't answer — that was a rhetorical question!"

63c09b41-5b24-49a9-9adc-b34181f915c3.Text: "You took the lawman into your retinue? I disdained his company. It became clear to me pretty quickly that Vultur had Strachs eating out of her hand, and so I brought those pathetic conspirators to heel. Now, the Arbites are my lapdogs — obedient, but too dull for me to bring any of them into my circle."

19a416f9-b8e4-4ff1-a936-6800667675f2.Text: {n}Having heard this diatribe through, Solomorne calmly says,{/n} "Go to the daemons, arrogant scum."

975d9aae-a3bf-44f8-9c3b-296f3c50d8e8.Text: {n}Your copy smiles upon noticing the cyber-mastiff.{/n} "Hello, Glaito! You do not have as many scars in my reality — perhaps that is because I convinced your master to leave his service in the Arbites. Travelling with me can be dangerous too, but at least I always have your back."

71de4318-4318-4679-9af5-ab37b752e2e9.Text: "I am glad to hear he is doing well in another world too. But I am even more glad that you did not drag your Solomorne here — I would hate to raise my hand against Glaito, even one who is not my dog."

76e6638d-296d-49ec-a9f9-14127646601d.Text: The rows of data on the cogitator screen are scrolling by too quickly — it is impossible to make out any details.

2f6d6982-2a6b-412a-9d4f-0e327c935141.Text: Rows of data are scrolling by on the cogitator screen. You can barely catch a few familiar words that grab your attention: "Theodora," "xenorelics," "threats," "Yoke."

6d41f94c-bf56-4421-b527-39421038cc23.Text: "Hindrance to my release, I see you. You will be erased."

e1915082-64d3-4723-a4f9-1f25a9e8c86c.Text: "To be bound once more? No! Your trap will be unmade!"

3afa3c6a-c828-4a86-ba06-6befd37419e0.Text: Unnatural energies torment the xenos's dead body, destroying and reconstructing it over and over.

31611885-f8cc-4f49-a2f2-1b3b0004c63c.Text: "Rogue Trader. The Lord Inquisitor is expecting you."

14cf2a99-56c6-4f2d-9aa5-3c8f00561d80.Text: The Tech-Priest responds with a short string of binharic code.

e4076a91-c7d9-46d6-b29c-aac28ed96821.Text: "Lord Inquisitor! We are progressing according to plan, our troops have already reached the target."

f198878f-a1ea-46f8-b134-61f1b88f78b9.Text: The destructive web of the tech-blight is spreading along the walls of the crypt.

2557ea0f-21cd-4ec3-b33c-8b74ef81dbee.Text: The xenos's memory core does not react to your manipulations.

fa379b03-c67e-4ea5-8382-7099d28b0e96.Text: The tech-blight has barely affected this bridge but almost completely devastated the xenos structures below.

77ea0b0a-bb77-4c3f-867d-4dbe138282b4.Text: "Yekhmet will eradicate the filth of transient life!"

a58b4445-aa9e-4b34-be1b-2c0c2caf46fc.Text: The xenos knight lets out a clanging howl, portending imminent death.

1d3d5cbb-cfc0-40ef-b5e0-6609fdbcc50a.Text: One of the symbols looks different from the rest and for some reason attracts your attention.

1a760991-af6a-4a92-8b90-246ac2e9f7d6.Text: One of the images stands out among the rest. This likely used to be the symbol of an ancient xenos dynasty.

bc8837b2-fc8c-49af-9262-24b79b5af8b0.Text: As soon as you touch the obelisk, disjointed streams of alien information flood your mind, making you nauseous.

e7f83cc5-4cff-4bc0-bb09-5449c767ea86.Text: As soon as you touch the obelisk, ancient xenos symbols appear in your mind, forming the words: "Open the pocket repository?"

77319f15-a4b1-456d-92a0-e37fa6957b9f.Text: The cold surface of the obelisk is covered in twitching symbols and angular images.

bc2c2a70-fa10-4c57-a0a6-1010124ba531.Text: A ragged breath punctures the oppressive silence of the room. Someone is still alive.

73cf5ae5-d6a6-4a6f-8d88-f65b7de3edcc.Text: The tesseract prison vibrates restlessly, barely containing the power within.

45efd63a-d336-4f2a-b1d5-9ded7c7287e1.Text: "Y-Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! P-please forgive me, I have to get back to work."

9b47ec2e-e4ca-4121-a09d-f0b5087078b8.Text: "No, it is too early! The Yoke must be activated, or all is lost!"

fc8d3ce8-74e1-4723-9e15-cbd69b9b2183.Text: A low hum emanates from the massive machine that combines the might of the Imperium with the taint of xenotech.

b2c1a5d4-2e7f-4106-9966-244ba52ff064.Text: The air around the Yoke, a powerful device created by humans and xenos, is thrumming with tension.

52d37af2-f5f4-4edf-9ab8-b623566f0d9a.Text: "Would you be so kind as to disable the field?"

dafee9f1-33a6-4e5f-bbdc-cb00822456e9.Text: [Possess the mortal minds] "I am {name} von Valancius, and I demand restitution for this insult!"

77b2ee11-60f2-476b-b6c1-e804b71d73b0.Text: [Crush the field with a mighty blow] "Die, pathetic wretches!"

facd21c8-4f32-428f-a3c5-edbc1846ff96.Text: [Wish the field to have never existed] "May the ways be changed."

c112e43e-4472-4fc5-9e77-3cba9ca62a15.Text: "Whoever disables this field will be spared."

04c040ac-774d-46e7-818b-2945b8f072eb.Text: {n}The energy field has been largely depleted by the xenos attacks, but it is still holding on. When you approach it, it seems to bend slightly as if trying to get away. Calcazar's soldiers who are taking cover behind it have lost some of their composure, but they are in no hurry to drop their weapons.{/n}

b84707b6-046c-41b0-bf3a-e823e3b76810.Text: {n}For a brief moment, you sense that the sergeant is about to reply, "Who's there?", followed by him suffering the grisliest of fates. Somehow you know this for certain, but he just clenches his jaw and shoots you an indignant glare instead.{/n}

40cebff1-d146-4957-952c-916e452651f3.Text: {n}Calcazar's men, the hardened agents of the Inquisition who have faced countless horrors, hastily look away to avoid locking eyes with you.{/n}

96701d39-f198-4d56-b51e-1c5e94cf6d7e.Text: {n}The sergeant whispers something into a portable vox and grimly shakes his head.{/n} "The Lord Inquisitor refuses to grant you an audience. Leave."

27b0cef5-7ae9-4151-bb4b-136d15819c13.Text: {n}A hypnotising profundity pervades your voice. It fills souls and minds, shimmering and vibrating. While the sergeant fumbles with the button to shut off the generator, the soldiers stare at you in silence, only to fall to the ground as one. Their faces contort in a grimace of anguished horror, but even then they cannot disobey your silent command: "Stop breathing."{/n}

f356d2d8-b637-4e06-8647-a1727a6a801a.Text: {n}The soldiers stand still, but you notice the lightning-fast glances they exchange with each other. Hope flares up for a moment, only to fade shortly thereafter. The sergeant replies grimly,{/n} "Keep your mercy."

1325faea-5884-40ba-81d8-b50387ad9c62.Text: {n}Reality loses its unshakeable hardness and becomes malleable. At first, you think one of the soldiers is trying to whisper something to you, but the whisper is coming from the wrong side of the barrier. It is coming from inside your ears. "The Empyrean is with you. You are with us. The power is in thine hands. To thee it is given. Thou shalt command." The energies of the Immaterium envelop your fingers, ready to bend existence to your will.{/n}

110d5e22-a9cd-4c99-b356-45120e739189.Text: {n}Thunder strikes! You can see the field helplessly give way and burst under your strike through the veil of crimson rage. The motes of its power explode like shrapnel, turning the soldiers into mincemeat. The smouldering shreds of loyalty of the men who dared to stand in your way rise into the air.{/n}

9d4620d0-4b69-48a4-9e19-25b8f35d40ff.Text: {n}Something in the cause-and-effect connections of existence shifts with a click, the gears stop and then start turning backward. The paths taken by the universe are reshaped and the energy shield fades, dissipating into the fact of its non-existence. The soldiers who will now never be born follow suit. By the looks of horror on their faces, they realise at the last moment where you have sent them. To never and nothingness.{/n}

00c9bffe-b422-45f2-952f-a10d788880b0.Text: The tiny notebook is adorned with the coat of arms of House von Valancius. The pages made from real paper carry a pleasant scent of perfume and are covered in ruler-straight lines of text. Their meaning is locked behind an intricate cipher, but you do not need to know the contents of it to identify the author. You know this perfect calligraphic handwriting all too well.

5369e4c5-3ffc-40aa-a599-8558d19ff63c.Text: [Destroy the Yoke and kneel before the ancient deity] "I am ready to serve."

63e57e2a-2125-449d-becc-3f0b531b9a78.Text: [Deliver the final blow] "I consign you to oblivion without end, monster!"

2754f042-f453-43ef-be05-fda45c238856.Text: [Deliver the final blow] "You shall bend to my will!"

6f232b3d-c55b-4019-902b-fa8be77a1011.Text: [Deliver the final blow] "It's all yours, Calcazar. Bridle it!"

56c3da40-9942-45e8-8ef0-bc597001947e.Text: "This creature is a god. We must not imprison it, we must... serve it."

c13a0dd6-02c5-40e9-ad74-a4799b545a94.Text: "Why do you call the Shard your precursor?"

272702d7-01a1-4dba-a997-8433c672d4d4.Text: "Do you think you can do this, Nomos? And what will happen afterward?"

7e2e8b26-d6bb-422f-a11b-a6c5fa860f86.Text: [Signal Nomos] "Destroy the monster, you say? Very well, then. Farewell, Inquisitor."

348f043c-0dcd-4f44-9411-f94c78691873.Text: "I am at a crossroads, Theodora. What should I do?"

c3cc9bc9-e5c4-40e1-8017-106139437c8c.Text: "You and Calcazar did so many terrible things in pursuit of your ambitions. Tell me... Was it worth it?"

b8441bb5-ecbe-457d-9a89-b51809978b47.Text: "Begone. I am the Rogue Trader in this world — not you."

f5ef3371-2ce5-4c7c-87f2-f4c50c6adf62.Text: "We must imprison this monster for all eternity!"

5ec23e12-1713-4f01-8498-2437cd5ec06a.Text: [Kill Calcazar] "I am afraid that is no longer for you to decide."

001f33a4-dd07-475a-bcdb-f1a9da8f2057.Text: [Deliver the final blow] "You are right. Bridle this monster, Calcazar!"

a9883302-f150-4869-9eff-5015f622955f.Text: [Try to comprehend what the C'tan is]

234a7868-d169-4ee0-8592-61fc6cd391bd.Text: [Try to sense the motives behind the C'tan's actions]

819e1e65-f800-45e0-a1ca-a92465856518.Text: [Try to understand what benefits the C'tan promises]

4c959174-2810-4443-bc8a-ba77be507174.Text: {n}You are the cause of these hindrances. Only now does the C'tan Shard turn Its focus to you, for the battle was nothing more than the reflexive resistance of an alien mind absorbed in a completely different range of thoughts and responses. But now, It is thinking about you, and Its thoughts are so corporeal that you can sense them and know them. It seeks an end to the confrontation. It is capable of resolving it in a way that would benefit all.{/n}

3f1a0230-b701-47f2-9ff1-642fe4a84d70.Text: {n}Calcazar roars, frantically pulling the levers on the Yoke's control altar,{/n} "This was not the plan, {name}! Stop!" {n}He tries to reach for his weapon, but his hands are full operating the intricate machine, not allowing even a moment to do so.{/n} "This cannot happen!"

23647372-ac2f-4200-a0ed-0845157f2dd6.Text: "Do not listen... It is almost broken, so now it is trying to negotiate." {n}It seems that the same intrusive thoughts have appeared in Calcazar's mind as well. Nevertheless, his resolute voice overpowers even the violent roar of the Yoke, still in the process of reaping the Shard's power.{/n} "Weaken it more, and soon enough the binding process will be complete. In the name of the Emperor, {name}!"

a1ecb2b9-4525-436c-b602-f79b197f4399.Text: {n}You hear a whisper from Pasqal's vox:{/n} "I know this feeling, xenos."

b99c9cf5-8fe5-4189-ab97-2d4025e559f8.Text: {n}The C'tan is the pinnacle of reality. It is eternity, dominance, omnipotence, individuality. The C'tan is the original purpose behind all existence — the rest was born in order to contain, nourish, and be appropriated by the C'tan.{/n}

2c5c10dd-327d-4c03-adb7-7f8223beb7d7.Text: {n}Calcazar does not notice the attack until it is too late. The blood gushing out of his mouth spreads in crimson stains on the grand machine's plating and the Lord Inquisitor's equally grand plans that will now never come to fruition. Managing a stern smile, he only says,{/n} "Did I really turn my back to you? I am getting sloppy..."

626690f9-8cc8-41ae-8112-44328b47222a.Text: {n}Your strike leaves another fracture on Its ethereal body, forcing the C'tan to expend one more grain of Its attention on maintaining Its physical form — and that is all it takes for Its power to start flowing into the Yoke in an endless stream. The ancient monstrosity lets out an enraged howl, for this is the second time in an eternity that Its freedom is being usurped in so forceful a fashion.{/n}

77d221fd-a302-440d-8431-53e9206ea4ff.Text: {n}Calcazar's sigh is laden with enough weight to load an orbital shuttle to the brim. With the flip of a switch, he transitions the Yoke into passive mode.{/n} "I believe we have accomplished enough this day. Commendably done, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

3bc5600b-8f86-4254-a0fd-de99c18e51e7.Text: "We have much to discuss, you and I. Our next destination, for one thing. The darkness of the unknown hides many more such beasts, and I intend to find every last one of them. Are you with me?" {n}Xavier's drink is as dark as the expanses of the galaxy yet unconquered by Humanity and as strong as the faith of the righteous. Ordinary amasec in a soldier's flask, unadorned save for the Aquila.{/n}

3accbdf9-4081-4a59-984c-943bc1cf4afe.Text: "Today, you have performed a feat in the name of the Imperium. And, as with most feats performed by people in my line of work, not a soul must learn of it. You have my congratulations and commiserations." {n}Calcazar lets out another weary sigh and gives you a straight and open look. He then reaches for his belt bag and pulls out... a flask.{/n} "Will the Rogue Trader share a sip or two of amasec with the Lord Inquisitor to mark the victory?"

7e7525b4-9442-4200-856a-d834baf199ae.Text: {n}Calcazar roars, frantically pulling the levers on the Yoke's control altar,{/n} "This was not the plan, {name}! Ah, blast it! Do it, then! This goes against everything my station demands of me, but I think I trust you!"

8557d6ba-7926-487e-ad00-2c91074066c4.Text: "We stand at the threshold of probabilities and outside the bounds of the predictable. It is beyond possible to know whether we can or cannot."

2600c861-1ba1-4f77-ac74-bf7257aba602.Text: {n}Calcazar roars, frantically pulling the levers on the Yoke's control altar,{/n} "Enough, {name}! It is trying to penetrate your mind!" {n}He tries to reach for his weapon, but his hands are full operating the intricate machine, not allowing even a moment to do so.{/n} "This cannot happen!"

75120d13-a2f1-486e-bb49-53db6d4fb6e3.Text: "So you have brought a shard of the C'tan Shard here? You amaze me, Rogue Trader."

c4d80b9d-7c3a-4ba0-a16f-7d56b6938fdf.Text: {n}The sacrilegious machine falls at your hand, and the Deity comes unto the world in all Its might, wisdom, and eternity. It examines you and then, with but a ghost of a thought, elevates you to Itself. The promise is fulfilled: the inferior flesh is transmuted and the pathetic human feelings are replaced with the sublimity of the Deity's absolute perception of the universe.{/n}

c173d139-e2cb-403f-86a0-d37f88c65de7.Text: "So you have brought a shard of the C'tan Shard here? In the body of a Daemon Engine."

ebda1037-6e3c-4c78-870b-fe766506fa4b.Text: "But we are poised to die trying. This is our sacrifice to the light of Terra, our chance to atone for our birth. If we survive... we will use the Shard's power to serve the Imperium as its most loyal and powerful subject that there is or ever will be."

7cf3e878-a6d5-443b-b437-5022f6a0a681.Text: "But we believe that we can, and that is what drives us to try. And if we succeed... we will obtain power beyond compare. We will become a shield against any threat, in whatever form it may manifest itself."

d0675535-c55c-49f3-b8c3-306981e5d08d.Text: "But we are burning to try. How can we refuse such a feast?"

f3be65f3-00db-4997-968c-4daf9df56446.Text: "I am giving you one last chance to correct your mistake and destroy the monster. Or else I will do it myself."

93ba8f9b-19ea-4252-8416-49bfb0fe5cd7.Text: "We are ready for the most important battle of our life. Wish us luck."

9e7357fe-3c00-41d9-812c-7b940ba529a2.Text: "We crave battle. It will be sweet."

12175f4b-f7ca-4dfb-9cdf-5abf9f6283d7.Text: {n}You obliterate the strange creature that has dwelt on your ship for so long, but... you cannot shake the feeling that Nomos could have easily blocked the attack, yet seemed unwilling to do so. And you could swear that in that moment, you heard words somewhere at the edge of your hearing: "We will return."{/n}

dd118af3-65b8-4a53-92a3-08140e792f8b.Text: "I will enquire of you what that was and how you let it happen later. For now, however, let us return to the matter at hand."

97f09f07-67e4-4191-97f9-621b26393b93.Text: {n}You can sense the Shard's reaction: observation, analysis... and an almost intangible anxiety.{/n}

1d29fe01-b773-4546-a331-7bb07a6d59cd.Text: {n}The numerous implants in the Inquisitor's body all suddenly groan at once. A moment later, Xavier Calcazar perishes without so much as a scream before he can even comprehend what is happening.{/n}

08665ebc-dbc5-46d2-9036-d5f876976404.Text: "Another offence of ours. But a justified one this time. He should not have opposed you."

fbb2f7c6-4001-46da-b08f-4241a1770587.Text: "We regret that we had to do this. But he posed a threat, and not just to us, but to all the lives in the Koronus Expanse as well. Something that we want to cherish and protect."

22e64a69-4654-4f43-97f8-02704b862a62.Text: "We enjoyed this. Existence is full of delights."

bf18a142-da1a-4667-989d-4243ba80814e.Text: {n}Nomos steps toward the Shard — and the whole world explodes into a terrifying whirlwind. You can hear the colours and see the touches, ice burns your hands while fire leaves you freezing. And in the midst of this madness, you can clearly sense a battle raging, a clash of two beings, one endlessly ancient and the other endlessly young.{/n}

51cd5fd0-d76c-430c-9334-5d14b736f080.Text: {n}The power of the C'tan Shard is such that it redefines the very notion of power. But it has a weakness, one that you can see only now, with the Shard and its rival standing face to face. The Shard is just that, a shard. It is incomplete, it is not whole, and it cannot be what the C'tan was before. What opposes the Shard is something entirely different: an undivided, sentient being with a clear purpose in mind, akin to a well-aimed arrow. And the one who fletched and loosed this arrow was you.{/n}

41122d09-3a1d-4499-adef-8c16e6dc2b8f.Text: {n}The battle goes on, and on, and on, outrunning the course of time. But you do not need the gift of clairvoyance to know who will emerge victorious.{/n}

88028288-2c7a-446d-88e9-b9d85293f8d6.Text: {n}The C'tan wishes to Be. All C'tan exist to spread and conquer, not to stay manacled within untime, where It was entombed by the contemptible sentient tools, away from all that is. The C'tan wishes to ascend, sate Its hunger, and embrace once more the pure exhilaration of claiming and taming reality.{/n}

7a3676a1-0677-4c4e-ba59-f863539494ce.Text: {n}Power, eternity, comprehension. The C'tan once chose to reign over the short-lived races and forged a new and glorious fate for them. It has learned from Its mistakes. Now It will only bestow its gifts upon the chosen few.{/n}

38b27a40-3646-4fde-b1aa-2679882c5734.Text: {n}It is much easier for you to stop trying to comprehend the C'tan than for It, one who can grasp the world in hundreds of ways, to stop comprehending you.{/n}

bfa7cb3a-eef1-4f79-a8d7-db9c4e1132e7.Text: {n}The C'tan, now in thrall to the heavy Yoke, needs no words to know who Its new {mf|master|mistress} is. It reads your mind for the slightest of aspirations, heeds them, and elevates your being. Human feelings give way to a hundredfold more perfect ways of perceiving the universe that are intrinsic to the C'tan. You command. It obeys.{/n}

d95d715c-5da2-40a9-8dab-4d2f972da10d.Text: {n}Beneath your feet, entropy is devouring what little remains of the xenos crypt. Before you lies an entire galaxy. A galaxy that is not yet ready for the power that you have obtained.{/n}

f2c66f64-5228-4ea1-b7bd-8d641f937e9f.Text: "I believe we have accomplished enough this day. Commendably done, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The Inquisitor solemnly bends his knee before you.{/n} "The Emperor's servants in the Koronus Expanse have gained a truly worthy protector."

5cebfcc7-8938-4201-b09f-ac4312325119.Text: {n}Your form is rid of everything excessive, transitory, or trivial. Your mind, now a million times sharper, is hungrily processing the great deeds that lie ahead of you. The moment these thoughts crystallise, a shiver reverberates throughout the fabric of existence. The Deity has returned. The Deity comes — and Its Messenger walks at Its side.{/n}

dfd3d1df-eb97-4a8b-89fa-47734436a358.Text: {n}Particles of reality around you begin to boil, trying to heal the wound upon existence and preventing her from entering your version of reality. You and she can exchange words, thoughts, glances — but a physical connection is an impossibility. You are merely fleeting phantoms that could scatter at any moment. She is silent, her gaze still trained on you, as if she is trying to commit your every feature to memory.{/n}

6cc79d36-2a30-46d5-a6a6-5753fe0ff7b6.Text: {n}Theodora nods in approval.{/n} "Yes. You are the Rogue Trader. I can see that."

3907a316-4243-49fe-95b1-3dc281cebae7.Text: {n}Her smile widens.{/n} "It is always worth it. You will understand this yourself."

22f503f8-b952-4f4e-a338-e26f65c29bfd.Text: {n}She simply shrugs.{/n} "Our dynasty's Warrant is signed in the Emperor's blood — and written in ours. The blood of the von Valancius Rogue Traders. This has always been so."

d1e26ce5-05cb-4642-900d-215e6f8100b1.Text:
{n}Her smile grows wider.{/n} "To walk bravely first into darkness,
To unite and reclaim what was lost,
To triumph over nightmares untold,
To hold boldly the reins of fate,
To walk steadily the road of thorns,
Through pain to greatness."

863bd1e5-8776-4788-8e2d-18d439227acf.Text: {n}The wound on reality is healed and the vision of Theodora quickly fades away. You catch her last words:{/n} "Whatever fate you choose, one can only hope it will be better than mine."

0d874da7-9839-4da9-9067-6bbe76627266.Text: {n}Grinning, Ulfar growls vengefully,{/n} "Farewell, foul wretch. May Morkai gnaw on your entrails for all eternity."

cdefa039-8a0e-44e3-bc94-5f4b3dc04f14.Text: "Do not bow your head before our abominable precursor. It was begotten by the dark abysses of the past. It is a fragment of that which devoured stars and erased civilisations. It knows no benefit other than its own. Allow us to stand against it — this is our time, our impossible chance."

7187e6d1-d194-441c-864f-81be8176253f.Text: "If our birth ever had a purpose, then it is here and now."

d043a2c5-91f4-44e2-8a93-cb0bdded8d07.Text: "Because that is what it is. And what we are. We have told you before about Theodora's ambition, Amarnat's mind, the ship's cradle, and Epitaph's secret. One sprouted into another and spurred yet another. Thus, Nomos were born. We were but an echo of the Shard's power, an echo that left its prison. But we have become something so much more — with your help."

01f1e580-0d89-4818-8ea9-f07678c2867e.Text: "Clash with the precursor. Touch it. Absorb it. So that the reflection becomes the object reflected. So that the Shard becomes Nomos. Then, and only then, will its threat be eradicated forever."

05ffe718-2697-4191-bea3-4f4691a898fc.Text: "If your pet takes so much as a step toward the Shard, you may consider our alliance broken, Rogue Trader. The Shard will be placed under the Yoke, and as for that creature... I will destroy it as soon as my work here is complete. Unless you destroy it first. I advise you to do just that." {n}Calcazar's tone leaves no room for ambiguity.{/n}

0517f60b-c27a-4b7b-9c20-19dd05786a12.Text: "It is our precursor, but we are not its shard."

153d0637-097a-4de5-b969-ca3fd92523da.Text: {n}As yet another layer of reality cracks, a figure appears before you... Her. After giving you a probing and appraising look, Theodora permits herself a slight smile.{/n}

642c62d2-661d-487e-8208-dbbc98479beb.Text: "Do not listen. Reject the promises. Do not allow your mind to be clouded, elantach. No one is capable of receiving everything — or granting everything. Not even a star-devouring Yngir. And this shard of an Yngir... cannot even grant itself freedom."

201625f3-9b64-47f2-8316-c60bff8748e6.Text: "Oh, you're just afraid the Lord Captain will get {mf|his|her} hands on your toy." {n}Jae smirks contemptuously.{/n}

52905a8b-3051-4b92-b23a-f28ce79edd17.Text: "Nothing can subdue a star devourer, or even just a shard of one! Relent, mon-keigh! Your unbridled ambition will be the undoing of us all!"

0223916a-e6de-4fe4-a8f5-796e18656b92.Text: {n}Mental contact is effortless. This is not communication — such a powerful being cannot comprehend communicating with anyone but Its equals. It simply bears the gift of making the other hear and understand It — so grand is the potential of Its thoughts.{/n}

c03a9ae9-5664-48d5-8ac2-0ec23bd9980e.Text: {n}The ancient monster struggles against the energy manacles of the Yoke. Its impossible powers that make reality itself burst at the seams are now being forced into a compact dungeon, quark by quark, returning It to a cruel and painful non-existence in the moment. It could struggle harder, but something is hindering It.{/n}

c9c22b08-386f-441b-93b4-ad9191339539.Text: {n}More and more tears appear all over the Shard's form. As the Yoke absorbs Its power, it becomes increasingly harder for the Shard to maintain Its physical structure. Each imperfection you inflict brings the star predator closer to imprisonment.{/n}

6d2a66f7-77aa-441d-b13a-7cc6784f2ec5.Text: {n}To the C'tan, space is an illusory variable. To the C'tan, time is a young and trivial phenomenon, for It existed for an eternity in the gaseous energy fount of the universe before time was eventually born. To the C'tan, fact and probability are mere abstractions, between which It can soar on Its electromagnetic wings.{/n}

ae543636-aa0f-4e0a-98d3-73988af42cf2.Text: {n}Currently, the C'tan is... not whole. It was shattered into lesser pieces, and so were Its thoughts and powers. The feeling of emptiness is oppressive, and It yearns to become one again.{/n}

5a65ee2f-ba59-464a-b1f8-b6d68f50a3c8.Text: {n}The C'tan can grant... Your thoughts falter, for it is difficult for your mind to fathom the full scope of this word... The C'tan can grant Everything.{/n}

a6ee9db3-33a6-4a02-b4a9-f90771d0bd0f.Text: {n}As you stand before the Yoke's control altar, you gaze upon it, possibly the greatest instrument of destruction in the history of your race. The key that unlocks the gates to the nigh-unfettered heights of power. A weapon... The cogitator block that was designed to transmit orders to the imprisoned C'tan shatters into pieces. It is a weapon no longer — merely a prison.{/n}

5dfc749c-b9e6-4518-91b3-2fd3f5b51aea.Text: "Instead of fighting each other, we should unite to halt the impending nightmare."

0f5a63c1-5a6f-4cf4-9242-0a694b2a24a3.Text: [Grant the ancient warrior an honourable death] "Your watch is over."

21a6ca32-e9f1-4ef3-b464-d6c79cfe5a6c.Text: "What is it that is making you grieve? Is it your imminent death?"

1d696800-0ea1-4c7b-8008-fc662a526976.Text: {n}The colossal warrior's formidable underframe can no longer bear his weight. With armour plates clanging, his great bulk slumps. A low sound is born in his chest, which your Elucidator {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NecronKnowlege}turns into the words{/d},{/n} "Let woe befall the unworthy Yekhmet dynasty. Sleep is nearing its end and thraldom returns. In my vestment of shame, I peer into the stormy horizons of the future."

401ef4b0-79a6-4882-bd24-a15700508c66.Text: {n}The fallen warrior scrapes the floor with his claws and screeches furiously,{/n} "Unacceptable! The rot of transient life must be eradicated!"

4f898c8c-bb6a-4067-bd8c-25383f9c0178.Text: {n}A terrible rumble comes from somewhere deep inside the crypt as soon as the green fire goes out in the fallen warrior's eyes. The glow of the glyphs upon the walls becomes chaotic and disarrayed. Something just broke irreparably in this crypt.{/n}

2d42a0ea-927d-43c9-bdff-4bd484751cea.Text: {n}You notice the convulsions in the xenos's limbs. The light is flickering in his eyes. Perhaps something went wrong during this monster's awakening from stasis, damaging his engrams and plunging him into madness.{/n}

61831799-2ba8-4e0d-b969-c28434ee8743.Text: "May tachyonic wind carry my words, may the oceans of subatomic resonance reflect it, and may it resound until the world grows old." {n}Convulsions begin to affect the metallic body and the entire crypt is quivering along. The walls seem more fragile with each passing second. Impossible anomalies are now rampant in them.{/n} "Let the Yekhmet dynasty be cursed!"

eb0805b5-a139-421b-8db2-dd2c7ffa6050.Text: {n}The xenos dies with a piercing howl of wrath. There is no fear in these sounds, only the stubbornness of a true warrior with a touch of regret at his defeat.{/n}

6584e885-4792-4626-ba0c-253375fb9ba8.Text: {n}The xenos's limbs shiver at the sound of your voice. The Elucidator takes on a tone of revulsion:{/n} "Despicable. An overlord's moment of grief is befouled by the influence of transient life. Rage has clouded the purity of the mourning." {n}The warrior makes a futile attempt to get up, only to convulse again. Something bursts inside him, making a ringing noise. The entire crypt echoes that sound with a resonant rumbling tremor.{/n}

b26b8f85-cce5-4043-8f66-f8e3a34d1408.Text: {n}You appear to be looking at the overlord of a minor dynasty of the xenos. He is clearly a member of a destructive cult that loathes living flesh with a visceral passion. However, as much as he resembles an animated metallic statue, he was once a living being, and the ideals of duty and valour that used to guide him still exist in his mind.{/n}

23caf4e0-4387-42dd-88aa-414f90004e7c.Text: "The star devourer is asleep yet awake. His breath is a poisonous pestilence. His dreams are engrammatic acid. Quantum uncertainty is his shroud, and that which came to pass is entangled in it and interwoven with that which came not to pass. Possibility becomes actuality. Actuality unbecomes itself."

00a8832e-4c2e-4af6-ab65-e42f17824eb7.Text: "Shame upon the Cryptogeometric Sentinel who was entrusted with guarding the paths of actualisation and failed to be vigilant. Unworthy feet have trodden those paths." {n}The voice-like hum from behind his lowered visor fades.{/n}

3cc0b5ee-6c94-4d7f-b121-755bb65f01ed.Text: {n}It is reasonable to conclude that the monster is talking about probabilistic alternate universes.{/n}

f9eb9594-c4cb-4db1-b4e8-a9262a130310.Text: {n}The monster's madness is clearly overtaking him as his speech turns into a tangle of incoherent exclamations.{/n}

3cfd5fae-b635-44cd-bd68-2076f505938f.Text: {n}You are evidently looking at a deranged machine built for destruction. It is unsurprising that his apocalyptic outpourings are not directed at anyone in particular. He simply has a burning hatred for all of existence.{/n}

c343e4c2-5cdb-4e35-9bd9-9e073244ec1f.Text: "A warrior of iron. A sentinel of the tomb of the Ancient Ones. A child of the Yngir, the star devourers, and an eternal enemy of the Asuryani." {n}Yrliet grips the weapon in her hands tightly, as if expecting the terrifying warrior to spring to life and attack at any second.{/n}

55e09819-73e9-4796-8f31-0d6d01f6e319.Text: "It's alive... it moves, it thinks, it tries to talk to us, but — it exudes no colours! This is the first time I have seen another's pain and fury with my eyes alone, without the aid of my gift. So, this is what it's like..."

2807280b-c71b-47a6-9acb-f1411d9e84db.Text: "Let its death be clean. No xenos could ever hope to receive His grace, but... The way it gazes into the face of its doom is worthy of respect."

b4a78d0a-9fd0-4c9c-95dd-23df21be5218.Text: {n}The colossal warrior's formidable underframe can no longer bear his weight. With armour plates clanging, his great bulk slumps. A {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}deep sound full of rage and tragic despair is born in his chest{/d}.{/n}

90fd8263-5cf5-47ac-8bc5-89dda6e17105.Text: {n}The xenos's limbs shiver at the sound of your voice. He emits a deep hum full of dour pride. You are unable to decipher it but you can sense his disdainful rage and stern resolve to kill you. This is neither the dispassion of a prowling beast nor the blinding rage of insanity, but the instinct of a warrior.{/n}

ecfac30b-a085-4b3c-b2ca-40e34aa20d30.Text: {n}Clearing his throat, Ulfar grudgingly admits,{/n} "He speaks of honour before death. These ancient xenos certainly have an understanding of battle courage and honour. Perhaps the old ones are right, and everything has become degraded over the centuries. Even inhumans."

d03ed07a-5ebe-417d-bc2d-3207922f79d0.Text: "You dislike me, but this lump of metal commands your respect? You truly are a deranged breed."

c87a3e68-1b03-42f0-b0bf-4ee8ecd3abe9.Text: {n}The warrior turns his gaze directly on you. The green light in his eyes flares up like a bonfire.{/n} "Inexistence is entropically preordained! It is no cause for grief! The egregious mistakes are! The violated imperatives are! The Yekhmet dynasty took watch of the seed of the cataclysm. The seed was neglected. A cataclysm has sprouted from it. Honour has been trampled underfoot."

78f8437c-3b91-456b-a71f-52b1e86e8e50.Text: {n}The frenzied monster shivers with rage and a burning thirst for destruction.{/n}

a11be2a1-0fbd-4e9e-b9a9-171d7ac6a788.Text: "So brazen a violation of the laws of existence set by the Omnissiah — the very idea is infinitely blasphemous. So blasphemous as to... almost be sacred."

96824226-eb0b-48a2-8477-740a276ce592.Text: {n}Marazhai jerks his head.{/n} "A crippled Oghyr. Look at it twitch its limbs... I have never seen anything like it. Whatever caused this defect had great force behind it."

735d3404-e0c2-452c-87d4-33b4e0f842c5.Text: "What are you talking about? Can you not talk in riddles?"

5fe24800-e5ae-4757-9ade-7bba3b0504f9.Text: {n}An invisible yet clearly tangible aura of power envelops the figure clad in the robes of a Tech-Priest. It is all the more baffling to hear a youthfully excited voice from under the hood.{/n} "This is it. The place of our origin."

b90cfbca-fcd9-4e5a-b406-191347e84874.Text: {n}Nomos's gaze is trained upon the C'tan Shard.{/n} "It was your strike and your wish to escape your prison that begot us."

389e8965-d7a4-4f5a-b19b-ba5aaa42b914.Text: {n}The mysterious creature that has been your ship's soul for so long turns to face you.{/n} "But it is you, {name}, who truly ushered us into this world. So let us meet our abominable precursor together. For it is ready to break free."

b14b3610-4985-45ca-8526-8daedfe626c7.Text: "I need explanations, Rogue Trader. What is that? And what is it doing here?"

c4a39034-1ef7-4b1f-a5e4-6ebba8ea7f98.Text: "We are out of time. Now... It escapes now."

546cdd3b-fdc2-4189-aa2a-afaa5f20d6bf.Text: {n}The voice coming from the maw of the monstrous machine sounds strangely excited — enchanted, even:{/n} "This is it... The place of our origin. Nomos were born here."

a1e722da-6090-40cf-a631-c7811aba71a8.Text: "Why does no one from Theodora's retinue remember her visiting this system?"

598c62d8-45dd-4b2d-919a-204fb9734db4.Text: "Let's be straight with each other. You have nothing to hide now that you are dying. What is going on in this place?"

ff4bee11-bc3c-40f3-ad87-0ba55d963de4.Text: [Drop the lho-stick on the ground] "Oh, how clumsy of me."

093421b0-ed85-44c7-9698-61963e82931b.Text: "I am looking for Calcazar. Where is he?"

86f6acbc-71eb-4cd0-946d-58cc484bb0c5.Text: "Tell me, why does my coat of arms look familiar to you?"

1df43a7f-2d6e-4501-a1c6-ec199bd20279.Text: "What was the ultimatum you gave Theodora?"

87a6e93e-6389-4339-b4df-624770931413.Text: "How did your people infiltrate Theodora's retinue?"

108e61ee-c2db-4746-aab4-b98c5722f97b.Text: "The Drukhari have come to this world? Why?"

56e48d37-f46c-4f3f-9378-37820468f7ac.Text: [Turn to your companions] "What do we do with her?"

082fb15b-9050-4414-8926-444a179dd21d.Text: [Raise your weapon] "This is where it all ends for you."

f82f4b22-a75c-476d-80c3-e0ca9c1cc37a.Text: "It is what you Inquisitorial rats deserve."

fcf2ee78-a027-43cc-8bc3-dacbf3e72c70.Text: [Bring the lho to the woman's lips] "You were saying something about an operation?'

90f44aea-08d9-4d9e-a12f-228e9fa12851.Text: [Take out a pack of lho out of the woman's jacket]

8b999f84-dbec-493e-8f21-5c57710e269e.Text: {n}The maimed creature at your feet is still alive, as evidenced by its heavy breathing. It was a woman once, sporting close-cropped hair and equipped for battle. But now her skin is shredded by the metal sticking out of her body in a dozen places.{/n}

d59fd076-4d3f-40c0-a27d-3a4fb197fa18.Text: {n}Her body does not appear to have any external injuries — it has been maimed from the inside out. It is as if her flesh was transmuted into metallic shapes that then burst out of her skin and turned her internal organs into a bloody sieve. Some of her exposed bones have a metallic gleam to them, while others still look natural.{/n}

9e3d1062-45dd-4800-9f1c-ab2d50ca0626.Text: "This is... hmph... unexpected. Did Her Ladyship not trust even me? Disheartening news, to be sure."

23cb66e2-f405-4ce5-b69d-56acdac5fed4.Text: "But a mindlock is incredibly dangerous. It's a bloody miracle it didn't fry our brains!"

4cf07eef-8c13-49cf-9668-cf700cf069dd.Text: "Does it look like I have anything to lose? The way I see it, you are doing me a favour here. So which one is it: mercy or revenge?"

0f183a07-4a05-40e7-aa0f-ba1b1b81c972.Text: "Are you trying to pry information out of an Inquisitorial agent in the hope that she shows sentimental candour at death's door? Shame on you." {n}The woman manages a weak smile.{/n}

dc416a3c-3a74-4023-b90a-0813c2df3c4b.Text: {n}You have heard about mindlock technology. The subject's memories of times or events would be placed under a special lock that could only be opened by a key phrase, one that most likely only Theodora would know.{/n}

a46a18c3-a5b7-426f-969e-b68d27cebfc1.Text: {n}It takes you more than a few strikes to end the life of the already half-dead woman. The metal skull screeches under the pressure but does not break, and her heart keeps pumping blood through her shredded veins. Finally, her agony comes to an end.{/n}

04b417cf-e5d5-472c-a071-2422eeacf3b8.Text: {n}With a heavy jerk, the woman raises her head, emerging from oblivion, and focuses her gaze on you. Even in such a wretched state, her eyes still gleam with self-confidence, zest, and subtle shrewdness.{/n} "You... Who are... Ah. That coat of arms rings a bell. Von Valancius. I'm not as surprised to see you as you may think."

fd9474e5-0514-4350-8b61-790d0d3328c3.Text: "You little shit." {n}The woman cackles hoarsely and without any malice, lapsing into fits of bloody coughing.{/n}

b6f777fc-02ca-4860-a729-12a20da01a15.Text: "Do you know Kunrad Voigtvir? Not sure if he's still alive, but back then, he was Theodora's Master of Whispers. In theory, he should have been the one to out my operatives as spies. But instead, he thought that they were his chance to pull off a brilliant plot and prove to his mummy how great an heir he would become. It's true what they say about blonds — every other one is as thick as mince."

89a1d951-df2a-48c8-b92b-f7be77bb7194.Text: {n}The woman tries to salute you, but the metal cutting through her tendons has cost her the control of her fingers.{/n} "Tanakia Calbergaria, Inquisition acolyte. And, by the grace of Lord Inquisitor Calcazar, the warden of the Epitaph 1 covert facility. Or whatever's left of it."

4ee43f8c-20ba-491c-bd30-951d48640baf.Text: "At the facility, in the crypt. Making preparations for the emergency launch of the operation's final stage... At least I hope so. Or else he's already dead. Now that I think about it, there are enough reasons to assume the latter."

41323800-b784-43ae-8a20-802834e7c208.Text: "Oh, I should know. It was on the uniform my agents wore. The ones I sent when Calcazar took an interest in Her Ladyship Theodora's retinue. They didn't wear them for long, though: when I presented Theodora with Calcazar's ultimatum, she purged her retinue of our operatives. I'm fairly certain Theodora would have preferred to have my head as well, but the Lord Inquisitor recalled me here to guard his treasure cave. Just in case Theodora decided to return for what she thought was hers, or the Drukhari started causing trouble."

671f9ffe-33b4-4586-b38d-334760688242.Text: "I guess you're still young if you don't know that in this world, whenever the big boys and girls say the word 'facility,' that almost always means a 'colossal secret weapon capable of destroying worlds.' And that's all you're going to get. It would be very disrespectful of me to spill a secret that so many have given their lives to protect."

6fe34eec-79db-4515-9aaf-8ddcfa76df1a.Text: "Merely a message saying that her dirty secret was now our dirty secret. She was the first to visit Epitaph, and she found something here... something too good even for someone of her exalted status. Rogue Traders are not allowed to have such toys, and I relayed the most exact coordinates, down to the last digit after the decimal point, to the Lord Inquisitor."

27568c34-edfb-4e73-98e4-ebfa12a54312.Text: "A feint. A deception. A game of double- and triple-crosses. When they told her they intended to take revenge on Calcazar, she believed them — she was just too eager to get back at the Lord Inquisitor for taking her clever Archmagos advisor, Amarnat."

ef320bfd-44b3-41a1-aa67-9ea8ab863972.Text: "I've been having trouble sleeping lately... Oh, you mean the metal things in my body? I have no idea. Looks like something has gone terribly wrong in the crypt." {n}Her voice becomes more serious and dry.{/n} "The auspexes detected some unknown radiation, and then everything went crazy. The xenos didn't feel like sleeping in their coffins anymore, so they started trashing the place. And the pylon I was standing next to suddenly grew a dozen tentacles, and one of them grazed me. I blacked out, and when I came to, I looked like I'd tried to give birth to a shuttle."

ed93c1cb-5f46-4fa6-8608-42971df7d50f.Text: "Ah, the xenofreaks, my favourite partners. They had a crucial role to play in the operation that you mustn't know anything about. Their visits to Epitaph have left me with so many unforgettable moments. We were ordered not to fire on them first, but to split them into atoms if their skinny arses deviated so much as a single degree from their approved flight paths. I swear, it was as if those fools were trying to get shot at with their half-witted provocations. They even had a nickname for me — the Almost Wych. A compliment... I guess."

d639b969-4f65-4320-a591-178c131000e5.Text: "My boots these days are rather more expensive. I am loath to sully them."

c9bf717d-8fa5-47b6-91bd-3cb58c04ca32.Text: "Said the one who chats with the whispers in her head. You know, I'm not sure that you had that habit before coming to Epitaph."

79bddc70-1b8f-406a-9fa5-c8223a6337b2.Text: "Have I sated your curiosity? Then I'd like my favour returned. There's a pack of lho in my breast pocket. Give me one, and you can keep the rest. I'm feeling very generous today."

1055d38e-3d57-4c50-8010-492b97e7907e.Text: "It is highly likely that this woman deserves to rot here and choke on her own blood or be skinned alive by the xenos. Quite likely indeed... But I am a merciful man, and therefore I suggest shooting her in the head and pressing on."

0cf3be6a-7224-43b9-aa75-2aa2e929a84b.Text: "I say we leave her here to die. In pain and torment. We should drive a nail into her ear too, so she has something to remember us by."

ef824d42-e2dd-439d-a077-bd6cd5a27935.Text: "I suggest granting the acolyte the Emperor's Peace. In honour of our years of working together."

ffe33022-62a0-4522-b55e-7fa0743f2fa2.Text: {n}Her blood-smeared lips twist into a smile.{/n} "Is this an act of mercy or revenge?"

6b806907-034e-4248-816a-5158553e9d0e.Text: "Or... you can go down there, if you have the guts. Maybe you'll immortalise yourself too. That's what I would do, but I'm insane, so I'm not the best example to follow." {n}A weak smile dances on the woman's lips.{/n} "So. About that lho-stick?"

961449d2-4e40-40ab-b00b-a761976d1772.Text: {n}You have never heard of such a technology, but it would not be a stretch to assume that the Inquisition does have something of the sort at their disposal.{/n}

ae154f9c-98c0-46cb-810f-cab52f1dc229.Text: {n}Tanakia gives you a long, piercing look, then speaks, sadness audible in her voice:{/n} "Straight, huh? Let's give it a try. I've taken a shine to you for some reason... One day, Xavier decided to immortalise himself in history in a rather extravagant way. All for the Imperium's sake, of course. But then things didn't go as expected, even though we expected that they wouldn't. And now you'd better get far away from here, because whatever happens next, I doubt you're going to like it."

ced7ce24-3984-4f26-ab71-19cc73fd0306.Text: {n}Her lips move slightly, as if trying to whisper something, but the shock mutes them, turning her voice into a gurgle. Her body, mindless and desperate, is only prolonging the pointless agony by clinging to its last bleeding shreds of life.{/n}

b4783eff-5cb7-46f8-afeb-e5e9ecaebb8e.Text: "People say it's bad for your health. I'd better be careful."

987e8ecc-441b-4b3b-af43-bc3effb45443.Text: "You're a funny one. The Inquisition's secrets for a tube of lho — that would be something, wouldn't it? No deal."

423c0b85-c9ed-4688-879d-9f9b03c16be3.Text: "It is time she was sent to the Undying One. Spare her throat, but strike her heart instead, for that is where she carries a heavy burden. Let her shed this burden, and let her lips pray their last."

0f793cf5-e48e-42a8-9bea-0bfe65930a87.Text: "It is something more. It is His blessing." {n}Kibellah smiles, softly and soothingly.{/n}

9efd50f2-81d3-49db-9584-6bfc5893c2de.Text: "I've received better gifts from Him. But... who the void cares. Go ahead, bless me already."

b8345769-507f-4db5-962a-9c130b282cd3.Text: "You've always been so sentimental. So attached to your colleagues, your hair, your eyes... Oh, I'm sorry, is that still a sore point?"

308486be-68a0-4537-b755-aeaec37568f5.Text: "You've become more generous over the years, Abelard. In the old days, you wouldn't have wasted a bullet — you would have kicked me to death with your boot out of sheer frugality."

3c29ecc1-ed9d-4eb1-8088-28b053e160ac.Text: "You have it all backward. You could have been dumped out the airlock like so many others. You were already a decrepit old curmudgeon back then, after all."

3f3ad058-0653-467d-8c21-1c55a797b569.Text: "I can give you two versions of the truth: the sugar-coated one and the honest one. The sugar-coated version is that once Theodora realised just what she had in her hands, she deemed it a matter of the utmost secrecy and mindlocked the memories of all members of her crew. The honest version is that she mindlocked the important people and disposed of the rest. Theodora depressurised compartments by entire blocks, casting any unwanted witnesses out into the void. She needed to free up space in her holds for the spoils, anyway."

eca8060c-9f6b-44a6-83b7-7e98e865b544.Text: "You'll have to excuse me for not looking surprised — my facial nerves seem to be partially paralysed. But I gathered as much — I'd hardly mistake you for our spectacular void she-wolf, after all. And if she were alive, she definitely would have come here in person. So you're the heir? Well, at least it's not Kunrad."

5d4f3a1d-de56-4546-9ef5-d04dbb4e8378.Text: "Good. You're old enough to know what these are for, aren't you? Stick one end of the tube between my teeth and light up the other. Just make sure you do it the right way around."

cf881ff0-99e6-4975-9721-e80c28cf2f04.Text: [Point at the xenoconstruct] "Is that what you are here for? What is it?"

46daad8b-3e9b-4b06-b621-683a1ffe7756.Text: "I will not let you bring this insane plan to fruition."

614e658a-8550-4f56-80b7-6a16139aef9c.Text: "I have come for your head, Calcazar."

aa03827e-59e7-4fcd-94e9-2aeca6d8ac06.Text: "The line you are treading is a dangerous one, Calcazar. Stop this madness!"

2eb63e4d-1d15-481a-a1de-acb47ee873bf.Text: "And you think you stand a chance against such power?"

428075e3-17a8-448d-ab71-f4d31fe23a46.Text: "You have gone too far, and your actions will lead to disaster!"

46b8e7f7-4395-44fe-8247-74c566bc35ac.Text: "First, I will kill you. Then I will claim your trophy for myself. And then... we shall see what I will do to your precious Imperium."

475f6906-72e3-479c-82bc-4a57921ce30e.Text: "How did this thing end up in your possession?"

5b41acc8-eb51-42b0-8aee-c64c4cce48b3.Text: "How was Theodora involved in all this?"

83dba086-1dce-4856-b2c6-268b3bb41c44.Text: "A fine plan, apart from it being an insanely audacious one that will almost certainly get everyone killed."

31a6d9d0-685a-4b11-b944-fc1dc4fde579.Text: "Why did you call for the Astartes to come to your aid?"

41b9cc1c-a1dc-4037-a638-a843056eff1c.Text: "And then, I take it, you decided to get rid of your xenos allies?"

84e25b6c-7e1a-4a4d-9942-534ed272d238.Text: "Heinrix, he has gone mad. You don't have to listen to him."

25e28c9a-5501-4c54-a246-71ec361abaa5.Text: "Seeing as the inhabitants of this place almost killed you, I gather that something went wrong with this plan of yours."

ab2c8110-2d15-4291-8906-38595337c47e.Text: "I see your ambitions are on a truly cosmic scale."

ef59afc0-7663-4bb4-8db8-8b0d622acbd8.Text: "There is no need for bloodshed. Why don't we try to derive some mutual benefit by taming this creature together?"

0bab8065-2996-4919-8ccb-c5b9c0b83281.Text: "Why do the Drukhari want the Shard?"

ef1592dc-fcc7-44a3-b829-de13e157e0a4.Text: "The denizens of the Rykad System, Santiel's Pride, and all the other starless worlds... You were the one who sentenced them to death by sending the Drukhari after their suns."

8732d753-8706-4968-bf2f-18c90aa326e7.Text: "How will taming this creature help save the Imperium?"

a1ffe77a-b10f-497b-a0e0-33e775f235d3.Text: "What is this C'tan Shard? And what is it doing here?"

cde5377b-90e8-490a-8552-45e97c743827.Text: "I am with you. Wake the beast, and let us shackle it together."

d6329714-b5d0-4897-8a6a-d1f8c2f16435.Text: "I still have many questions for you."

d5b476c3-98b9-4e69-97a3-c0ea7900ceed.Text: "Listen to yourself! What you are planning is heresy!"

72345ce3-8dde-4b7e-a407-1f763001169f.Text: "Compared to this heresy, my work is child's play."

52ea5ce9-9924-42e9-bc1e-1e5cbaa5c642.Text: "They were an asset at first. The Wolves helped me close the dimensional gate by overwhelming its security systems. I tasked them with hunting the xenos condemned by Yremeryss. But eventually they started prying, and that was unacceptable. I could control Thorbald by giving him more tempting targets, but the Baleful Howl pack..."

7906bd95-1d58-47e0-8211-ad87f21b89b6.Text: "You came {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_XavierTrust}at just the right moment{/d}, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. I sometimes regret that timeliness isn't a virtue recognised by the Emperor. It truly deserves the honour."

1bcc25a5-bfff-4022-ad25-5dbbf810fb13.Text: "I see that you did not heed my warnings, {name}. Your decision to come here in spite of them may have consequences. But we still have a chance to turn it to everyone's advantage, if Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship listens to me very carefully."

91b46863-147a-4d57-b9ab-4d6a316b56af.Text: "Cubis Delphim revealed to Uralon the Cruel where he should strike, and that almost spelt the end of Operation Precious Sentinel. I appreciate your efforts in resolving this problem. In fact, you turned out to be much more useful than Theodora ever was."

acfdd3c7-182e-495f-b7e8-6ccfbb1fc1e1.Text: "I value your bluntness. Let me match it: while my head will remain firmly on my shoulders, I will remove yours with the utmost pleasure. I tire of your arrogance, {name}."

ccba5eab-368a-4d34-aab3-10a59c8a5e71.Text: "How dare you! How DARE you!" {n}Incendia's voice roars like the fire of the executioner's furnace, but then her rage burns down to coals, her tone becoming more akin to the rustling of ashes being scattered by the wind.{/n} "You have fallen to heresy, Xavier. And I condemn you."

a37ac4f7-e1aa-44f4-8d16-ad1f86f25e1e.Text: "I try to keep assistants like you a flamer's range away from my affairs."

70ffc6ba-eaec-4d02-9320-6841addcaf9c.Text: "Let us suppose that it is so. I cannot say that I am completely convinced of your sincerity, but you are off to a good start with your choice of words."

94d92dff-1a7e-43a0-bc64-13a7e927b466.Text: "No, {name}. The disaster is already unfolding — it is just that you and people like you are blissfully unaware of it thanks to me and others in my position. The Imperium is being pierced by a thousand daggers, every day, everywhere. It is bleeding. Weakening. One day it will grow too weak, unless radical steps are taken. I am not trying to foment disaster — I am trying to prevent it."

a748a996-75b1-463c-b26f-2150cf06b5ee.Text: "Given the circumstances of our meeting, I do not see why I should hide anything. I seriously doubt you will share this information with anyone else... for one reason or another."

f878ac2e-30f2-4416-a5b1-6c3dbe49d9ff.Text: "Thanks to your predecessor. I arrived in the Expanse at the call of the Explorator Fleet to deal with Archmagos Amarnat's heresy. But I quickly came to the realisation that the Koronus Expanse's problems ran much deeper than tech-heresy. Unprecedented piracy running wild, blatant smuggling of xeno-artefacts, wilful and impetuous Rogue Traders, and growing threat of the Ruinous Powers — all this in a region that the Drukhari consider their domain."

c8690d1e-32a2-41ab-9288-2427d07a51bf.Text: "Frankly, I considered purging the entire Expanse: it would have been much easier to burn down this whole tangle of threats and corruption. But the web of spies that I had woven presented me with much more interesting and radical solutions. While investigating Amarnat's connections, I turned my eye to Theodora von Valancius, who ultimately gave me the Shard."

32e5cedc-e989-4fdd-a33e-731a78631888.Text: {n}Ulfar stares at the Inquisitor with wide eyes, saying nothing. It seems you were not the only one unaware of Calcazar's plan. He finally breathes out, his voice heavy,{/n} "Morkai howls for you, Inquisitor."

035562aa-d9bf-4644-9608-589fede8709a.Text: {n}Ulfar stares coldly at him, the deadly frost of Fenris crackling in his voice as he speaks:{/n} "You will pay for this, Xavier Calcazar. Know that I will have my blood vengeance. I will have your death."

d27e84be-d0bd-4689-bab4-0b3091b67c4b.Text: {n}Ulfar stares coldly at him, the deadly frost of Fenris crackling in his voice as he speaks:{/n} "You will pay for this after we are finished here, Xavier Calcazar. Know that I will have my blood vengeance. I will have your death."

032908b3-9f36-4e43-a80f-0fa1c2a76001.Text: "Theodora's instincts were uncanny. She spent decades hunting for a key that could open the dimensional gate, as if she knew that there was something incredible waiting for her on the other side. Her Ladyship was lucky enough to discover the Shard during one of her expeditions. A trophy that was too much for her to handle. Archmagos Amarnat studied it on Theodora's behalf, creating weapons in exchange for access to the dangerous relic. But their research was too primitive and unambitious compared to the true power contained inside the Shard."

c09b119b-29ef-4e1a-a7e1-967f3cd89ef0.Text: "I had one of my own acolytes, Tanakia, send her spies to Theodora. They infiltrated the Rogue Trader's retinue, earned their trust, and reported to me about this magnificent object. The rest was trivial: I seized Epitaph and laid down the conditions of our further coexistence. She was wise enough to concede defeat with dignity."

75ca3911-fddf-4d3d-9c62-d73e03b97339.Text: "It was made on Eufrates II. I captured Amarnat's student, Axiomantha, and she passed all of her mentor's drafts to me. And the one overseeing the process was none other than your acquaintance, the Tech-Priest Cubis Delphim. His fall was regrettable. It seems that the unorthodox, daring things he did at my behest drove him to break his vows and sink into heresy."

f7b96cd0-760d-48bb-91b6-1b7d14f98076.Text: "I commend your ability to face the facts without fear or prejudice, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship."

c60f4b08-1126-48cc-b3ec-a3bd0b647626.Text: "Of course, I did not let him near the Shard itself, but rather set up a laboratory for him on Quetza Temer. It was safer that way. All the pieces were contributing to my plan, but none had enough information to comprehend the entirety of it."

cf8627b1-55f1-486b-995e-67e94f8a3874.Text: "So in the end..." {n}Marazhai's smile is not his usual triumphant and scornful one. He looks almost tired.{/n} "In the end, I was right about Yremeryss and the mon-keigh. I was right all along."

30f9c03f-89fa-4827-adf6-610dc4bc3488.Text: {n}Heinrix cringes at Calcazar's words.{/n} "You disposed of Emelina like unwanted rubbish. Like... waste material. After all her years of faithful service to the Golden Throne..."

1590bb66-a462-4a2e-9c85-eca4ce91719f.Text: "Trust me, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, the threat of the alien pales in comparison to that posed by the Ruinous Powers. Yremeryss could plunder a thousand worlds, but she is no Uralon the Cruel. She was as great a danger to her own kin as she was to the Imperium. The disruption she caused among the Drukhari was only to our benefit. She intended to trigger a powerful dysjunction in Commorragh, thereby destroying her rivals and elevating her own Kabal in the process."

58a5bf04-203d-42a8-86e0-740f8181a453.Text: "It was a dark day when you dropped from under the tail of your rotten-wombed mother, you loathsome traitor! While we were fighting to exterminate the xenos, you were busy carousing with them... Had I known sooner, I would have ripped your pitch-black heart right out of your chest!"

c84b0a35-93c4-41c7-b7b3-7804cf825f54.Text: "I needed a remarkably strong force to keep my xenos allies in check. The Emperor's Angels were just the weapon I was looking for, except... considering the sensitive nature of my operation, I couldn't very well risk requesting aid from my allies in the Deathwatch, could I? And then I remembered an old debt owed to me by a Space Wolves Great Company. So I decided to call in a favour."

d41abf99-5253-4738-8917-80778113980e.Text: "You have come so far in pursuit of answers, {name}. It would be too cruel to leave your curiosity unsatisfied."

e24bf7f3-ff11-4398-ae67-f27c53a0577f.Text: "Theft of sacraments and secrets of the Adeptus Mechanicus: registered. Inciting a devout Tech-Priest to commit heresy: registered.
