The inscriptions freeze and fade away. The symbol you touched is erased from the slab's surface.{/n}

6286674d-e654-4fbe-9420-70e0969ed483.Text: {n}It seems that the enigmatic text speaks of some distortions of causality, resulting in multiple alternate versions of existence. It also suggests that these versions are hostile to one another.{/n}

04976091-cf6e-4d5b-8c07-3ccb37f7d5ab.Text: {n}Even while being flooded with xenos visions, your mind remains sound enough to analyse the incoming information. Now you grasp the nature of the pernicious "Malefice." Someone powerful on the outside is broadcasting insidious interferences that disrupt the xenos' awakening from their stasis sleep. Madness is the nearest human equivalent of the effect this has on them.{/n}

bddeab2f-056c-49fa-a202-26864d8cd87c.Text: "Lord Captain! Are you uninjured? Sound of mind? Why am I even asking... the answer has been obvious for a while now." {n}The Seneschal mutters the last sentence under his breath.{/n}

fcb0df7b-c74f-4f28-8837-187a7b1e4231.Text: {n}The symbols begin to change at a frenzied pace. Their light burns your eyes, and their rapid flickering makes you nauseous. You are struck by a splitting headache, like an alien entity squeezing your mind out of shape as if it were soft clay, refashioning it after its own image.{/n}

a1f3dd97-3877-45fb-89ca-feef08f5372f.Text: {n}You see an image of a voidship: a black crescent shape, its plating veined with green lights. Right before your eyes, its various parts start crumbling and flaking away as though gnawed at by invisible termites. It is being consumed by tech-blight. When only a lifeless carcass is left, you feel a searing pain in your hand, as if the Pestilence has spread to your flesh and is now consuming it.{/n}

15042584-0a89-4157-8982-6eeb1aa77ac7.Text: {n}A cyclopean pyramid comes crashing down on the rocky ground. It seems intent on preserving its shape, but tech-blight twists it and eats away at it. An enormous hand cuts short the fortress's death throes as it crumples the pyramid into a shapeless lump and tosses it away. The shining metal giant lifts its little finger and points it at a cohort of mechanical warriors. They are turned into puddles of black metal. The giant clenches its fist, and the soldiers' remains merge into an enormous tentacle that lashes and sweeps at everything around it. Rays of wrath radiate from the giant's face.{/n}

b52a984b-fe34-442a-827e-64963660e8f9.Text: {n}The vision of the vengeful deity ends. The pain subsides at once, and the metal releases your hand unscathed. The flickering symbols freeze instantly and slowly begin to fade. The symbol for Pestilence is the last to disappear from the slab's surface forever.{/n}

a79ad1ff-d966-43ff-881a-d089ab8c6f23.Text: "This I ask myself, my Lord: if my existence were to be reflected in myriad eternities, would they be the same?" {n}Your mind is now drowning in a flood of thoughts and memories, ancient, alien, and indomitable. With a titanic effort of will, you hold on to one of the images and vest it in the sound of borrowed words, and utter it in a strained voice that is not yours...{/n}

ddec05d0-3f2b-4298-8800-bec89f676802.Text: {n}The obsidian smoothness of the enormous slab begins to ripple and roil. A set of {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}mysterious symbols{/d} appears on it, as if impressed on its black surface by an invisible finger. They shimmer forebodingly, like a martyr gasping for air as life drains from them.{/n}

ef655483-a5ca-4237-910a-11411b250547.Text: {n}The symbols come together again underneath your palm and then vanish from the slab's animated metal.{/n}

f3918156-ef37-4a49-aef3-935da1dd4d60.Text: {n}Forever frozen in a silent scream, you feel the haze of approaching madness cloud your mind as it is overrun by rows of distorted emerald-green symbols. As soon as their glow becomes unbearable, they go out at once, and you find yourself standing beside the black slab again. Right under your hand, the symbol for Malefice vanishes from the smooth black surface.{/n}

c6cfd7cf-5e4f-43f4-8f6c-da340ab22bf4.Text: The Last Confession of Magos Theseus-Delta-Praximus

83695769-97c4-4e37-9068-db0a7cd9742b.Text: [Touch the surface of the slab carefully]

2257e5e9-a5c4-4a0f-bfee-7a6fc1c2a321.Text: [Place your palm on the Star symbol]

4de1e035-7354-43e2-ac44-82a2c597e68f.Text: [Place your palm on the Transfiguration symbol]

b8f9b170-20e7-4915-a030-f2253a09af0e.Text: [Place your palm on the Imprisonment symbol]

41bd3444-c990-491c-9550-42b2a0926a9a.Text: [Try to carve your initials into the slab]

e1217e47-f408-4c48-9e6b-29db77e736bd.Text: [Slowly sink a knife into the slab]

e4ff5592-8dd0-4818-b3d1-14d5f25da3af.Text: {n}As you approach, the black metal of the ancient slab begins to move. Geometric shapes appear on its surface. The three brightest ones are {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NecronKnowlege}symbols for "Star," "Transfiguration," and "Imprisonment."{/d}{/n}

124d2b94-4e77-4449-9dd0-67c2ade7927b.Text: {n}Above them is another inscription, its flickering as feeble as a dead man's breath.{/n} "My Lord, I have spoken this testament to edify my spirit, so that after my reverie's vision comes to pass eternally, I may shed my oblivion of that, which I lost when I gained all, and that, which I gained when I lost all. I absorb the lifeless images, unheedful of the fleeting moments, for eternity is my worship. I lay my hand and hearken, until my memory is an imperishable tomb wherein the ashes of times past are laid to rest."

87d2bc20-5174-4b87-b30b-43bfad6bfad6.Text: {n}The blasphemous and convoluted tales of these xenos are scarcely different from the equally whimsical narratives dreamt up by any other inferior inhumans. They are not likely to contain even a modicum of truth.{/n}

cfccc0fd-6386-4069-9552-8af528002953.Text: "Our artisans harnessed their craft to erect biofurnaces, the gates of indestructible permanence. And we entered the crucibles of immutability, and the tyranny of the withering flesh was cast off, and an eternal existence in bodies of living metal commenced. While They gorged their maws with our souls like carrion-eating beasts, for that was Their fee. Only select Overlords preserved their selfhood tenaciously and fended off the oblivion of their minds and wills."

cba47d5d-caac-4aa4-bd20-0632ecce49bc.Text: "Thus delivered from transient life's decay, we came forth as mighty unity. Guided by Them, who had now sated Themselves, we turned our foes to nought. But Their tyranny had not made us oblivious to deception. Preparations were made and armaments were fashioned. And They were shattered, and Their fragments were engaoled in timeless tesseract prisons. There was war."

a079f76d-8594-41e4-9fd4-ac6e08d2f69b.Text: {n}The black metal rests silently before you, the rows of mysterious symbols glowing in the dark.{/n}

1cd2feaa-f032-4200-959f-fc218f85d688.Text: {n}The slab's surface wavers and ripples like a bottomless lake. The symbols are washed away and replaced with new ones, their green glow as bright as it is lifeless.{/n} "My Lord, I behold the truth of Them, the rapacious reapers who drank stars dark. Blind was Their eyes' gaze set upon us; futile was Their engorgement, for They would never be sated."

c26f33df-1dee-495f-99ca-401b0ecf20d0.Text: {n}A wave of animated metal sweeps away the symbols, and the slab shows you a new set. Their glow cuts through the crypt's darkness, making your eyes sting.{/n} "My Lord, I behold the truth of the rite of Biotransference: the renouncement of our decay-bound bodies, the soul-splitting agony that doomed us to an eternity of triumph. Their messenger manifested among the Overlords of Overlords, bearing the gift of triumphant indestructibility. No fee had been promised, yet a fee was to be paid. There came no refusal, and the gifting was done."

119a3bdf-6220-4bb6-9e3a-5f8b75b886b7.Text: {n}Your touch sends the symbols scurrying away like crypt beetles, only for new ones to take their place.{/n} "My Lord, I behold the truth of the fate that befell Them, fashioned by our touches. Their imprisonment is our liberty: this is the enthroned truth that reigns supreme."

9d537ed5-91ce-4d0b-82c4-60d14f50b1bc.Text: {n}The metal yields and takes in your blade as clay would. You try to pull it out, but to no avail. Forever stuck inside the xenos monument, the blade itself now is a glorious monument to your stubbornness.{/n}

22cc9e9f-3ae5-4267-a8cb-7e2918e5ea3b.Text: "The Nephilimechs' books of wisdom. Knowledge received from the Omnissiah Himself by His most beloved children. Knowledge that led to the most terrible betrayal of all." {n}Two of his mechadendrites extend toward the stele with covetous trepidation. Two others coil tensely, as though about to attack it.{/n}

9ea73ce0-e68f-4789-93aa-3df03e497ac5.Text: "Bathed in the ferocious rays of a deadly star, prisoners of our own brittle bodies, our race was withering, doomed to hurtle toward imminent and inglorious obliteration. War devoured existence within and without, and unity was a spectre of dreams unattainable. Such was the way of things, and we knew nought else till we heard the call of the reapers of deathly stars."

4f80c135-05dd-4db8-a8fe-7be865c7c4f6.Text: "They made the summons, and we heeded Their call; and we crafted at Their behest indestructible bodies of living metal, for in Their voice we heard a hope of escape from the putrescible nature of existence."

e00d0b02-0fc9-4b69-b5eb-bcc22e81f7e2.Text: "Born before death itself, They were strangers to inexistence. Therefore, my Lord, I place one of these prisons in your immortal custody. For as long as the Yekhmet endures, so too will its impregnable walls."

fbed32f2-588c-4124-8522-40ea22aa22cb.Text: {n}The obsidian smoothness of the enormous slab begins to ripple and roil. A set of mysterious symbols appears on it, as if impressed on its black surface by an invisible finger. You do not know what they mean, but the mere sight of them gives you a splitting headache.{/n}

60bec975-8fcc-45f5-97b9-8dcd44aaf020.Text: {n}As you approach, the black metal of the ancient plate begins to move. Strange geometric shapes, symbols of some kind, appear on its surface. A host of smaller symbols glitter above them. They are no less {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}mysterious and inscrutable{/d}.{/n}

e8aae7d9-a41d-40c5-8f9c-79c6d7888f55.Text: {n}At first, the metal feels not much different from plasteel to the touch. But as soon as you apply a little pressure, it becomes pliant and viscous like cold resin. Emerald-green marks linger for a moment where you touch it before being swallowed by the black metal.{/n}

29469d4a-35bb-4da8-9af0-0e80a9bc1008.Text: {n}You spend several minutes trying to carve your initials into the ancient xenos artefact with your knife, but the metal instantly heals any damage done to it. The idea seems more pointless with each passing moment.{/n}

96ae8142-5163-4f7a-8854-8ee5d6c91f5e.Text: {n}You have come across theories that speak of an ancient xenos race that gained a metallic form, of mighty beings that showed said race the ways of unlife, and of a cruel and bitter conflict that subsequently ended their coexistence. Now you have an eyewitness account of those events.{/n}

56e86044-05bb-4e59-a5d5-33fbf98c06b2.Text: {n}You might as well have stabbed a tank — the blade recoils from the monolith with an unpleasant grating sound, slips out of your hand, and flies off.{/n}

41b933fa-deea-43e3-bc2c-41f04b51110d.Text: "Do you think I have made a worthy Rogue Trader?"

2a8381aa-eda7-4dce-8a80-be7928e96b1b.Text: "For fortitude, so that my soul may resist the temptations that beset it."

d556407a-f2b3-4586-acb3-ceaee526ce6c.Text: "For strength, so that I may crush His enemies."

604609f0-e930-4743-be0a-5740c7be6186.Text: "For mercy upon those who have joined us on this perilous expedition."

d2a63625-f974-449e-8b99-a067bf5a73e3.Text: "There is every chance that our meeting with Calcazar will end in battle. Are you prepared for such an outcome?"

228b8bd6-b96c-4773-8b6a-33d0756fab13.Text: "What do you make of the systems we have found ourselves in?"

f5579c29-3bc0-4e22-bf1c-6ea3b7046408.Text: "What do you suppose was Calcazar's purpose for coming to these accursed systems?"

56937617-c487-4033-8894-6871893afe2f.Text: {n}Incendia's eyes blaze with fanaticism against her deathly white features. She rasps in greeting,{/n} "The Emperor protects, {name}. Even in a place as dark and abominable as these stars."

9faec42a-24f3-411e-98f6-7ae738d4cac5.Text: "May your faith serve as your shield, {name}."

716b0b15-2e18-4e71-92f3-00dada68396f.Text: "You bear this privilege with greater dignity than Theodora did. In this dark hour, the Emperor has sent a worthy leader to guide the Expanse."

8e58f0d9-2244-46f6-a0ca-5153bf3a236a.Text: "Let us open our hearts to Him, for even in this fetid darkness of xenos impurity, He hears our voices. What wish you to pray to our Protector for?"

5a73a4a0-1025-4d18-a1d7-314bcd395803.Text: "You can sense flaws within you and admit to them freely, and that is good. Indeed doubts and temptations are the most terrible of our foes, for they are the bane that turns a righteous warrior into a heretic."

39a7a2cb-ad64-48cf-8705-ded4fa15d078.Text: "This plea is virtuous, for our lives are insignificant, and all that matters is our service and the condemnation of His enemies."

ccdc4473-7683-45a3-9f1e-9ffd148e6567.Text: "Very well. Pray that He saves your soldiers, and I shall pray that He graces them with enough conviction and courage to die a righteous death when the hour comes."

5d894b59-223c-4e67-912f-09cbd45348f1.Text: "Then join me in asking Him to illuminate our path and show us the wickedness that we have come to exterminate. And to let none hide from our hand, and to see retribution served."

f7099b13-260f-45f1-a1af-d1288c1973ac.Text: "A battle is imminent, for I am guided by the scent of a crime in the making, and where there is a crime, there is a criminal. If the Lord Inquisitor came here to oppose this malefactor, then we shall help him. If the Warden of the Expanse has erred and abandoned the path of service to the Emperor, then we shall punish him. None are without fault before the Protector, not even Calcazar."

8787fe69-956a-4921-9ec7-083b045b4b33.Text: "A hotbed of xenos filth." {n}Her pale lips twist.{/n} "These dark reaches are meant to test us, our faith, and our resolve. From the moment we arrived, I have been tempering my spirit through ascesis and self-denial. I would counsel that you do the same." {n}Incendia's appearance really does look even less healthy than usual. There are deep shadows under her sunken eyes as if she has not eaten for a number of days.{/n}

0e4fb550-37da-43f8-b31d-29ca44ca4df3.Text: "While I cannot approve of your detestable habit of keeping ungodly xenos in your retinue, I will admit that their presence does not dim the fury with which your devotion burns."

65509937-c4ca-4ad9-82ef-4cbd30248ec5.Text: "I have seen Foulstone burgeon under your hand, and with that, a new beacon for righteous souls was lit in the sector. Such an endeavour takes diligence and patience, and these qualities I, regrettably, lack — mine is the path of a castigator, not a builder."

6309d129-96a9-446c-a06e-5fa763fd1262.Text: "To serve the Emperor, I would hope. I detect the scent of a crime in the making, and pray that the Lord Inquisitor came here to punish and prevent blasphemy against Him."

93875f89-ec52-4188-98b7-764207e74727.Text: "Humanity's foes tried time after time to rob us of what we had conquered, but you were always there to stand in their path. Vheabos VI was doomed to fall and become a heathen wasteland, but instead it rose as a bastion of solitude and contemplation for those seeking repentance. This implacability is your great virtue."

ba614b09-8dd7-4103-b06a-6c7c48415736.Text: "One day, you will be gone, your flesh will turn to dust, and even your very name will disappear from the memory of the living. But your legacy will live on. At the Schola Progenium on Dargonus, new warriors in His service will be trained to uphold the same ideals that you upheld before them."

80ae835b-35cd-4776-9445-b444ac112732.Text: "You seem broken. Do I need such a fighter at my side?"

56679b9b-47a3-4784-8ccf-e1ff9dd68734.Text: "What do you make of these systems?"

894dc597-f90d-4e20-89bb-5332dc5cd2a3.Text: "You do realise that our meeting with Calcazar may end in battle, do you not? Are you ready?"

f6b83a6e-d02b-4268-9b2d-c0f63a231ac9.Text: "Has your faith truly wavered so greatly in such a short time?"

680563f8-757b-4166-a54f-83537cfa026e.Text: "Tell me, why did you choose to come with me, truly?"

20728033-e67e-41be-b437-70651f273c89.Text: {n}With a neurotic twitch of her pale cheek, Incendia offers you a resolute nod.{/n} "We find ourselves in a grim place, {name}. It frightens me to think of the horrors that dwell here. I only hope that we have the strength to fulfil our duty to the people of the Expanse."

79200f04-ccc4-4d3e-8f96-9e292c089175.Text: "The Emperor protects, {name}." {n}You hear none of the former zeal in Incendia's dry words. She sounds tired.{/n}

1fe2db53-bf87-4329-80c1-2fd3440618b2.Text: "I wish not to speak ill of Theodora, but you treat people with far more grace and nobility than she ever did. Guided by your hand, your protectorate flourishes and your people extol you. And if it is so, then what does my opinion matter?"

4daf141a-125f-4d40-a3a7-89f0cd78be51.Text: "I was impressed by your decision to grant rights to the people of your capital world. Most rulers are afraid of their subjects, but you are not one of them."

28c83f2d-594b-4bde-9ff9-dff64086b6bc.Text: "Many in your position would have stopped at watching over their own colonies, especially in an hour as bleak and difficult as ours. And thus I found the mercy that you showed to the refugees from Winterscale's Realm all the more admirable. By allowing them on Janus, you saved millions of lives that Calligos had forsaken."

a70264cf-7fed-49bf-bed1-6f0c24ebd5b6.Text: "In a time of trials, the Emperor sent a true leader to the Koronus Expanse. Just as your servants from Foulstone selflessly lit void beacons to save lost souls from death, so have you, through your tireless toils, become a beacon of hope to us all."

85829d8b-1e3c-47fa-8736-32ebf1187965.Text: "Keep steadfast, {name}. And be watchful of the temptations infesting our path."

e1c0dd30-c46a-4de6-90d9-492d1c7ee883.Text: "The Lord Inquisitor... I once thought of him as an impeccably pious and devout servant of the Emperor. But he used me as a tool, and when I started doubting myself, I started doubting him. I was a monster, and he... I have a feeling that he may be a monster just as terrible. And monsters must be destroyed."

20b487e7-1ffe-4316-8f1b-22bc152f74c1.Text: "No human should have to journey to a place as dire as this. We are wandering in a graveyard of ancient terrors whose existence strains the mind to acknowledge. Touching their relics, reading their words... Who can say how it will change us? Who can say if we even ought to return to inhabited worlds after this, befouled as we will be by the poison that this xenos darkness is feeding us?"

584776e1-4ce7-42fd-be6e-e9548f1c59e9.Text: "My hands no longer sow murder, but my fingers are forever stained with blood. I had too high an opinion of myself, but shame pierced the shell of my hubris. I do not wish this feeling upon you — to realise that your ideals and deeds were shaped by another's manipulation."

aee0c7c7-ccdb-42fc-8204-3df3712758bd.Text: "Subdue my wrathful spirit. My servants can see to the needs of my protectorate, while I must ensure that my hands hold prayer beads rather than the reins of power. And that, whatever weapon I wield, I use it to protect the people of the Expanse instead of smiting them."

94c2accf-9716-48cd-aa9d-2c84c4c7ee3b.Text: "No, I remain truly devoted to Him, but... the fire that once fuelled my faith is gone. I can see the future that I rendered with His name on my lips, and it was akin to a graveyard. A field of towering statues proclaiming His glory, and not a single flaw among them, for all who had been found flawed would be lying dead. And I do not believe that Humanity heading toward such a future is the Emperor's will."

a182381e-000b-4c41-8061-577f392f1c98.Text: {n}After a long pause, Incendia says reluctantly,{/n} "I seek forgiveness. I did far too many things that cannot be expiated or corrected. I hope... blast it, {name}, I hope that out there, in the darkness, I shall get a chance to die with dignity and thus absolve myself of even some small portion of my wrongdoing."

b17257cb-47db-4fdf-bf1c-a3b01c0649e6.Text: "Thank you for making its existence possible."

c22b2489-f300-4c9c-b5e2-2f81111add7f.Text: {n}You see the corner of Incendia's mouth twitch, and a familiar crooked smile appears on her face as a hint of venom creeps into her voice:{/n} "That my pride lies in ruins does not give certain fledgling Rogue Traders the right to look down their nose at me. I have embarked on hundreds of expeditions and fought hundreds of battles, and my heart yet remembers the heat that calls for the Emperor's justice to be served. When the hour comes, that heat will turn into a blaze, which I shall unleash upon His enemies."

8f1520d4-9791-4c12-adb7-454c887da5f8.Text: "What will you do after my becoming?"

30955e56-4f59-4d6c-bde8-1a15234b7b70.Text: "Why are you known as Uralon the Cruel?"

ebd67a3c-0a18-4951-bbac-a393d440bb99.Text: "What is that book in your hands?"

b85c0b03-fdfa-4783-9b8d-cdecb74bd8a6.Text: "You betrayed Kunrad. How do I know that you will not betray me next?"

86532ad3-a05d-4982-bbb8-e1050ab7cc72.Text: "You call yourself a Dark Apostle. What does it mean?"

6e51b731-c4c4-44cd-9d5b-b22835d5901b.Text: "My path is clear. I shall wear the wreath of the Dawn upon my brow and take what is mine by right."

8a202c9e-67fd-4f7c-8ea2-0ef925f53bdb.Text: "Not bad, but too plain for my taste. You lack a certain charm of madness. I should ask Idira to show you how it's done."

c96d1ae5-d224-4a7d-be6c-4bd5b43860ba.Text: "Is that it? Your prophecies are worthless!"

48bafd65-1e8a-41d8-ad78-bb1165d3a186.Text: "You are hiding something from me, sorcerer. Answer me: what else did you see?"

6ab3a889-73e4-4745-8b4c-171dd9625491.Text: "You are a prophet, are you not? Reveal the Ways to me."

e1c3afcc-1ebf-4068-822d-fd6e37bd7843.Text: Recited a passage from the Book of Lorgar to Uralon the Cruel.

5e126a9d-1cf2-427b-8472-13561b6e8e03.Text: [Recite the dark prayer you heard on Kiava Gamma] "Are those the words of your lord?"

c111c378-2b48-4af4-ae30-65ccd8652f4b.Text: "I have disgraced you more than once, I have killed your brothers and ruined many of your plans. Are you telling me that you harbour no malice toward me at all?"

d67deb4c-e784-4ad7-b541-c1f3a59fbd8a.Text: "The Emperor is strong, but that did not stop you from betraying him."

9b5288fb-b301-4835-974b-67c1012a06c5.Text: "First you betrayed the Emperor, then Kunrad... Old habits die hard."

b6ad388d-e445-478d-8cf3-1d889136bfa3.Text: "I see. Let us discuss other matters."

f40dde7b-bd2c-44d6-9f25-49f02aefba11.Text: {n}The sorcerer's fingers, clad in heavy gauntlets, are leafing through the pages of a grand tome bound in rough, dark leather. Upon hearing your footsteps, Uralon the Cruel looks away from the tome and bares his sharp, uneven teeth.{/n} "I greet you, champion. Is it time to spill the blood of misbelievers? Or has the path of the Truth brought you to me for another purpose?"

d19f04b6-f854-49c8-bb2c-71ebdecc739a.Text: {n}Uralon the Cruel looks away from his tome once more.{/n} "Champion. What is the Truth's reason for this arrival?"

e35c9464-2d24-4fe7-bab6-d220932967f2.Text: "We have many toils ahead of us, {name}. You are destined to make the Koronus Expanse witness the blaze of the Final Dawn. I will help you in this through word and deed, until the call of the Primordial Truth shows me a different path. For now, leave thoughts of the future to me — you must focus on your deeds in the present."

090d92c6-ea74-4805-902a-f4231a2471ac.Text: "It is a collection of sermons from the Book of Lorgar. The Truth spoken by our Primarch and carved into human skin, which was then removed and turned into pages. The wisdom and verity of the Primarch's words fill my being with awe whenever I open this scripture. In it, Lord Lorgar casts down the false faith in the Emperor and grants us the tenets of the true faith in the great gods of the Immaterium."

5dcb1f67-13a4-4f55-baa7-9949f670fb78.Text: "It means that I am the guide of the true faithful. I am their teacher, prophet, and master, who leads the Legion's disciples in their service to the Truth. I share this burden with my brothers on the Dark Council. None but Lord Lorgar and the Great Four can command us."

b433f2ff-ff57-4ae4-b4d1-3a159fa4760f.Text: "My sermons have converted entire worlds to the true faith. My hands have brought populations to ruin. Stand proud, {name}, for only those I deem my equal have been allowed to fight at my side."

7f41c3f0-7607-4cf5-a3a5-95138cf476d5.Text: {n}Uralon closes his eyes, and the symbols carved into his face flare like embers.{/n} "I cannot perceive what the watchdog of the Expanse is planning. All I know is that he holds a key, and that key must be yours. Only one path will see you alight with the crimson wreath of the Final Dawn. The rest hold only oblivion and death."

03503fc0-8ed9-4252-ba55-e4b4a0318d2d.Text: "Over thousands of years, I have learned how inconstant fate can be and how often its turns that I perceive as defeats reveal themselves as my resounding victories. I have learned to put my fate in the will of the Changer of Ways and follow the call of the Truth. There is no malice, {name}. Your ascension is one of my greatest triumphs."

7b4e7afe-76b1-4aef-8877-909f65545dbe.Text: "His strength is feigned and built on lies amplified by the servility of his lackeys. Our actions were not a betrayal, {name}. We were overthrowing a tyrant."

367b891d-d8a1-4b08-a07a-55c6176eea37.Text: "Do you know what they had in common? Both could only see as far as themselves. Although, even I am loath to compare the corpse emperor to carrion like Kunrad — at least the Imperium's former master had a backbone and a vision, albeit one that was inexcusably deceitful and short-sighted."

e1ce24c6-8e24-4fdd-8dd9-36193657d76d.Text: "It makes no difference to the Truth whether you find its portents agreeable or not. You asked me to show you the twisted Ways, and I have revealed what you are meant to know here and now, no more and no less than that."

0c13c9cb-c509-48a3-90f5-92d4fe9f1013.Text: "Your paltry witch is beneath me. She is a broken vox that spews images and noise, unable to discern the Truth among them. An amusing sight, but that is all."

d2012611-cadb-42e8-9e26-42619a1bc3b3.Text: "May the blessing of the True Gods be with you."

0e9f3914-092c-437c-a57f-2ef29f6e330f.Text: {n}For but a moment, you see lines of unease and doubt cross his brow. There is something he is not telling you.{/n}

cbf9207b-3426-49e9-960b-ef1553888816.Text: {n}He opens his eyes.{/n} "That is all I can tell you, champion."

b8a595ee-3986-4129-8386-70da97248635.Text: "And I will stand at your side when you do, champion. May the faith in the hearts of the devout never waver."

49b01370-4ade-4fff-8a1b-41fee8b6d121.Text: {n}Uralon's long, heavy look presses down on you.{/n} "There is one more path. No, it is not a path — an ancient abyss beyond the edges of fate, a place where no Ways lead. You wear another wreath there. With this wreath, you have everything. With this wreath, you have nothing. Upon accepting it, not only will you renounce your destiny, but life itself will become your enemy. That is my final prophecy to you."

a83018a4-41e9-487f-bb8a-11c95b49f3d8.Text: "The general's will was strong, but it was not his will that I had been trying to break — among the children I had brought to the slaughter were the sons and daughters of his closest officers. I was true to my word: I took the general, let the defenders take the children inside the walls, and left. But the Truth had already touched the souls of the youth. The same night, they cut their parents' throats, gutted the sentries, and opened the gates for me and my brothers. The bastion had fallen. The name of that world has long since faded from my memory, but the epithet Cruel I bear to this day."

1dec5a99-3263-4837-83ed-5a97c8dc2ee2.Text: "Once, we were fighting for a planet that was on the verge of embracing the true faith. All that stood in our way was a single bastion whose troops had hidden behind impenetrable walls, refusing to kneel before us. Their commander was a valiant and talented general, an unshakeable protector without a doubt in his heart. My brothers were ready to reduce the city to dust with an orbital bombardment — what did a single stronghold matter when we had already brought the whole planet to heel? But I decided otherwise."

a7c1be43-eb19-4a21-84cc-2518e29ba55c.Text: {n}He lets out a hoarse laugh.{/n} "Kunrad was weak, pathetic, and vain, and he was nothing compared to you. You spoke the name of the dawns, you spilt the blood of misbelievers, you released the master from his ancient prison. Kunrad could not accomplish even a shred of what you proved capable of. Why would I betray someone as strong as you, champion?"

6ef1a9ca-9121-40d9-a9e3-3b1679d77080.Text: "One morning, I walked to the bastion's gates with a hundred children whom we had captured on our triumphant march, and offered the general a trade — his life in exchange for theirs. The general, whose will was stronger than adamantine, refused. I then put the children to death before the defenders' eyes and left. The next day, I came again with another hundred and made my offer once more. Again the general refused, and another hundred screaming, crying children died by my hand. On the third day, when I approached the gates with a hundred more, the general, beaten and wounded, landed at my feet, cast down from the walls by the bastion's defenders."

4148b4a8-a9c8-42a9-a8ee-a388ad5107ec.Text: {n}Uralon's torn lips stretch into a satisfied smile.{/n} "You impress me, champion. Yes, that is one of his many sermons. I will gladly share more of Lord Lorgar's wisdom with you, should you so desire. Later, once your ascension is complete."

079e69f6-6bc4-4339-bc83-eef85644a5c5.Text: "What do you wish to know, champion?"

dfd27da0-5fe0-4b9a-9a42-b8f817b85027.Text: "That the Imperium is a rotting corpse, as is its worthless master. Worms writhe inside its guts, praying to the putrescent husk, believing that it will protect them from the storm. They swallow the damp flesh, smack their lips, and vomit it into each other's throats, gorging, choking. And all the while, the crumbling corpse only continues to rot away. Storms and carrion eaters pick the reeking flesh off its brittle bones, piece by piece, as the frightened worms struggle to mend the gaping wounds with their own flesh."

dc2e2465-6e0d-4d5f-9cd4-d2303b7c61c9.Text: "The Truth is that the corpse is bound to turn into nothing but pus and bonemeal. And the worms, if they wish to survive, must behold the storm of Chaos that rages outside and offer themselves to it. And we, in our endless grace, will accept them into our fold. For the Truth is in the service to the storm."

d57760ae-09f4-4c47-89b7-0689d586d1b5.Text: "I do not blame you for taking great caution, {name}. The paths devised by the Weaver of Destinies are twisted and obscured — it is easy to stumble and lose sight of the Truth. Do not misstep, champion, and we will remain allies."

89c62d31-283c-4d83-a8cb-5ba72a9455c8.Text: "What do you think of the way the 'new blood' has handled {mf|his|her} protectorate?"

ad9d6a17-b271-4a88-b8fb-38dea7cf9226.Text: "What are you going to do after Calcazar has been dealt with?"

32de666d-b449-44d9-9628-2251310ec879.Text: "You often talk about your hunt. Will you tell me how it started?"

da24a646-4cab-4646-84f9-6fccd5d3b3d0.Text: "We are traversing a new part of the Expanse. Do you know anything about it?"

0b6540f7-a27c-4a75-b850-86ba6b7ae539.Text: "So, you are going to abandon your trade protectorate?"

f380889e-016f-4ffe-b8b2-439a4f11f9fc.Text: "How are you finding life aboard my ship?"

e2dd53bd-31e8-4d77-973b-74af09ead581.Text: "I shall see you at the hunt, Calligos."

f833fcc7-a442-4fd0-ae87-4d2cd4334524.Text: {n}Calligos's broad-shouldered figure exudes strength and authority, but his tense jaw muscles belie his impatience.{/n} "Waiting on this rust bucket for the hunt to resume is trying my patience, {name}."

2c0684e2-4cd8-4a3f-b869-135599f5893a.Text: {n}Winterscale scorches you with an imperious gaze.{/n} "{name}. How soon will our hunt continue?"

d1b55698-d885-4e32-b125-248903bfb42a.Text: "And yet your flagship is cramped and unbearably dull." {n}Winterscale looks you in the eye and flashes an almost good-natured smile.{/n} "If you keep delaying your hunt with me, I will have to hold it on one of the decks. To relieve my boredom, so to speak."

1eccad71-149e-45e8-8bfe-7176167d42d7.Text: "Those poor bastards from Vheabos VI whom you sold to the pirates? Ha! You are an enterprising sort, I'll give you that — you always find a way to turn a profit!"

cfeb637c-8cb1-47d6-bb26-d04471eb3838.Text: {n}He leans closer and gives you an ominous smile.{/n} "Did you think I wouldn't learn about your little ploy with the Kasballica? Did you think I would assume that one of your clever subjects just happened to figure out how to set up gas factoriums? Well, you were mistaken, {name}. But I am not offended. I must admit, I'm actually a little... awestruck."

6207fcdb-55cd-4710-8fd7-e15830836c3a.Text: "Gladiatorial fights on a pillaged penal world — a bold move, new blood, a very bold move. I am tempted to pay a visit to Vheabos VI myself to place a few bets and enjoy myself... Perhaps later."

b69deb22-8de9-468a-8d93-4e1563385463.Text: "It takes a lot of confidence — or nerve — to poach another's subjects and put them to work in the quarries of your own penal world. I can picture the governors' outraged faces when they learned their workforce was now breaking their backs on Vheabos VI!"

6c65273f-96d3-4185-85ce-f785e8f97137.Text: {n}Bloodthirst dances in Winterscale's eyes.{/n} "My purpose is to flirt with death in the heat of battle and to tear my enemies to shreds. The list is long, and the degenerate Calcazar will be just another name that I will wash away with blood."

52c2a103-d457-44c9-aca1-0ddfa8b6ad3f.Text: "Why, are you already planning to take it for yourself?" {n}Calligos's upper lip twitches in a menacing half-smile.{/n} "The Winterscale dynasty is greater than me alone. The affairs of the protectorate will be handled by the heirs and servants who indulge themselves in that miserable game of politics. That dreary fate no longer appeals to me."

b0e40fa9-c983-4fa5-be47-61565ecd30e3.Text: "Oh, {name}, my hunt began when the blood rivers spilt in the Rifts of Hecaton! When the song of a chorus of the damned echoed among the stars, pleading for death!" {n}Calligos's joyful voice booms like thunder.{/n} "It was in the midst of a great battle when I first experienced what it means to be truly alive."

bd0e99f7-d6fd-4870-a8fe-37f0a20c59e9.Text: {n}The Rogue Trader pauses before replying.{/n} "While I've never seen anything to like in that bastard, it would be a mistake not to recognise his power. Calcazar is dangerous and far from stupid, which means the hunt for him will be a thrilling one."

e9516d2d-3dfc-4951-b7b1-350a23ba21df.Text: "The Lord Inquisitor is a worthy adversary whose skin I'll have made into a fine pair of boots. It pleases me to know I will be trampling him further into the dirt with every step I take."

180dcbe4-aa5f-4f8d-a068-322fcf135926.Text: "{name}." {n}Winterscale's face twists in a predatory grin.{/n}

6f3b2333-6881-435c-a73e-e110ca42d0a8.Text: {n}Calligos laughs gleefully.{/n} "Are you calling this rust bucket a ship, {name}? This washtub would pale next to the Emperor's Vow, but I admit that it does bring back memories. I used to command a similar vessel back in the day."

8eee291a-96ce-4f75-a2c7-cd62c5cc4220.Text: "Then again, I do not think your subjects would be very surprised. You yourself enjoy splashing in their blood alongside your pet xenos, do you not?"

179ad528-643c-4692-8092-a77cdce99705.Text: "This area has been obscured by warp storms for so long that no data about its exploration remains. The diaries of my predecessors briefly mention that something unimaginably dangerous lurks here..."

1f0e8564-bbbf-48f7-b71b-3ac88324a8c0.Text: "But that is what you and I want, is it not? There is nothing quite like a new and deadly enemy." {n}Calligos greedily licks his dry lips in anticipation.{/n}

93034390-d45f-43ca-b34d-1b0afb3342e7.Text: "After we are done hunting him, I will set out to find a new quarry just as glorious as this one. I will look for a worthy opponent all over the Expanse, enjoying every new skirmish."

11b112ee-b24f-46b7-8365-2d612a1af8b5.Text: "My prayer was heard. The mighty foes fell before me, dissolving into a crimson mist. When my hands squeezed out the eyes of the last xenos and crushed his skull until it cracked..." {n}Winterscale's fingers clench threateningly in front of his face.{/n} "It was then that I got my first taste of the hunt and felt the urge to plunge myself into the bloody caldera."

00687563-4953-4d04-8731-6de375470820.Text: "The xenos legions were relentless and lethal. Wounded and broken, I felt the icy ring of death tighten over my heart, stifling its beat... In a moment of weakness, I pleaded for help, never before wanting so much to survive, so I could destroy and tear my enemies limb from limb!"

87ab2762-6753-44b8-a8e8-5f1dc0dbca42.Text: {n}Calligos scoffs.{/n} "I care little about matters that I have long since delegated to my planetary rats. Had you done something worthy of my attention, I would have remembered. As you can see, that has not happened."

73214de7-b2a8-4719-90e1-de9bfa698c2d.Text: {n}A slow grin cuts across Calligos's face.{/n} "I have heard things, new blood. Things that have impressed me."

da032392-ffb1-4df8-a5c4-2ed3a431f0a7.Text: Someone disrupted this experiment in the most brutal fashion. It is impossible to determine what was inside.

1872d527-fe66-46c5-a5b1-35ef9b1eedcc.Text: Synthetic amniotic fluid pools across the floor. Barely discernible traces stretch to the side opposite the entrance.

44277d98-ccf2-42bc-8cec-12925fa7b3d8.Text: "I am not authorised to engage in discussions. If you need information, talk to Proctor Anthar."

69007518-9248-4883-8474-e2a594e1aa28.Text: "The Arbites are operating in this area. Find cover and do not obstruct the Emperor's justice in any way."

12e52fea-350a-4311-a686-c596f1aa2fa4.Text: "I am continuing to monitor all available frequencies. Over the past hour, there have only been distress calls from civilians. Nothing of importance to the mission at hand."

34833e80-af9e-4f3c-ad1d-97445abb336f.Text: "Acknowledged. Our key objectives have most likely fallen. We are following Protocol M-N-23."

3369f524-ad50-43bc-b14f-66f09058dd09.Text: "See? And here you were moaning that we were done for! Now look who's come to our rescue! The Adeptus Arbites! Have you seen their shields? And that iron dog?"

f3c0ec20-d7d6-4f8f-bdad-a292134fa976.Text: "I've seen them, all right... I've seen one of ours get his jaw dislocated by one of those shields. Didn't get out of the way quick enough for their liking."

80282285-8522-4115-bfb5-568276151010.Text: "Really? Well, I suppose we've got to keep a respectful distance from them... Just in case."

58c998b6-aa65-4b31-832d-1bed88b83bc9.Text: "An honest person has no reason to fear the Arbites, right? Right?"

97694463-f1d5-4223-b0cb-2a535db6062c.Text: "Those Arbitrators might as well be made of ceramite! Maybe we're going to pull through now."

70229f84-b20e-47ee-9475-d744d2962c50.Text: The technical litany is full of unfamiliar words. The only step in the ritual that you understand is the prohibition against touching the lever.

eb963569-0e6c-4890-95a8-0f1c0facdb7d.Text: You manage to decipher the technical litany. According to it, in order to perform the ritual of the Motive Force you must supply power, make sure the relay is closed, check that the damper is latched and the supplementary external relay is shut. The supply must be correctly distributed, and in no case must the flow be reset before the circuit is closed.

a7225620-a891-41e9-acd4-0484ad807524.Text: "Your secular attempts affront the machine spirits. May the blind be forgiven for their ignorance..."

5111f5c6-d209-4045-b35a-47e0f527d588.Text: "The sacraments have been laid bare and put on public display. Outsiders should avert their eyes, for it is not for their minds that holy scripture was created."

2b807dbf-c4f0-4711-9af9-39def73236a2.Text: The Motive Force will not be able to pass through an open circuit. The cables should be examined and all sacred nodes should be checked.

0865a511-b7ea-492a-b038-e9326fcdff10.Text: "Sometimes action without meaningful intention produces results. The Omnissiah must be protecting you from punishment by the Motive Force."

3222fc8b-e4d3-473d-9d95-af49e230edcb.Text: The circuit is broken. It looks like you will have to start everything from scratch.

46b3c8df-1a0c-4727-934a-ec3a129df695.Text: This vault can be opened via the cogitator. All that remains is to figure out how to awaken the machine spirit by supplying it with the Motive Force.

1b88469a-da88-4a8f-a4a5-e9d3bb631851.Text: The safe unlocks with a grumbling rattle.

c5083b98-0c65-49a0-84ad-fad464163398.Text: Distribute supply of the Motive Force

d28b72fb-fce6-410c-8d86-e71eef9a00ed.Text: Reset supply of the Motive Force

d9d17e3b-3515-4373-bf8c-2505d2924465.Text: The new omniscopes appear to have caused quite the stir: the commoners, who have never left the station's bounds, stare with mouths agape at faraway suns and majestic ships cutting through the void.

99b70fed-f585-48f4-9fdb-58cef142cd5a.Text: Someone has turned the omniscope away from the breathtaking sights of the void to watch the windows of nearby buildings.

55219453-b813-4b9e-8ea1-c76b76f0267d.Text: The grand astrogational mechanism inspires awe with its very appearance. It is unlikely that the station's denizens understand its actual purpose — to them, it stands as a symbol of prosperity brought to Footfall by the von Valancius dynasty.

4ec5627a-81e5-424e-9401-089fb1bd5881.Text: A nearby preacher is squeamishly wiping blood off his weapon and hands. The bandits must have taken followers of Saint Drusus for easy prey and paid with their lives.

99875fd2-fe4d-4fd9-aa98-4b5583c95ff1.Text: The deck before the altar is strewn with bodies of parishioners and preachers. Judging by their condition, the attackers were not above ripping implants from their still living victims.

94681c85-404f-4d45-8d2a-31d70c812e81.Text: The towering statue of the Emperor that used to stand majestically in front of the Liege's palace was toppled and shattered by a rampaging crowd. The charred husk of the throne that formerly served as the seat of Incendia's court is lodged between its remains.

0a0d60a0-835e-4435-ba3a-ade8d8882760.Text: "So many people crammed in there... I hope it doesn't all kick off..."

2951fdb7-d40f-4ba7-8701-b01977b91506.Text: The contorted bodies, the faces twisted in agony, the foul-smelling ulcers and boils — there can be no doubt about the cause of death.

d9730a72-6654-4c73-a3c5-2effca7bb45c.Text: The dead are covered in ulcers and several show traces of repulsive mutations.

d6d81b49-7af9-46a7-9271-1ae440c45945.Text: These people did not die from the disease. It seems they simply fought to the death over the remaining provisions.

ca696b83-e050-40d7-a4e5-2c4e0a8a755d.Text: Judging by the traces of destruction and the corpses all around, many people tried to break through this door.

ea99450d-980a-4378-891f-27595a628416.Text: Open areas of skin have turned into one massive burst ulcer. The buzzing of flies and the heinous stench complete the picture.

8e6232b8-e927-41c8-a4cc-151e74c2d43c.Text: "I beg your pardon, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Everything is in place for your special evening."

405ea391-7421-48d0-b74e-f7556e7f38fc.Text: The liquid burns your mouth and leaves a taste of decay on your tongue after you spit it out.

bdd79d55-a68a-460f-9c8f-4df948a8a2c4.Text: The drink scalds your throat and blossoms into a molten flower once it reaches your stomach. Your vision blurs slightly, and your legs feel unsteady.

b950e0c6-6cb6-45ff-bf08-0dc16f3473eb.Text: The bodies are mutilated and covered with countless marks left by blades and whips.

7017439a-cff3-4449-b5f2-6a239d823384.Text: You see a number of containers of some sort beyond the enclosure.

e665ce79-bce7-4006-9b34-1528069e783f.Text: "What is this sudden hurry? 'The Shriekers' den' — where is that?"

e0157c72-2845-4534-80c6-06a2055c4381.Text: "Shades of crimson and scarlet... Such a barefaced desire to kill! Where will this trail lead, I wonder?"

35ad27e1-561c-4fb3-8824-9600648790bf.Text: "Oh, {name}, the voices are whimpering that we're in for a lot of blood..."

e5915e27-fcba-419f-b354-9025e85a7a04.Text: "Hmm... My gut tells me that a scuffle is about to go down... and I wouldn't be surprised if it was at the Shriekers' den."

d83ea1fc-ea29-421e-a199-4e4f93e09cb2.Text: "I must return to the Shriekers' den. My duty calls me."

c6f28496-0ec9-4dc4-be1c-977e0bbfe213.Text: "I will leave you for a time, Aett-Vater. I want to stretch my limbs."

10f0699c-ca27-4044-b907-8f5518ae1d62.Text: "I must... step away. On an urgent matter."

4b648009-10ff-4bb0-a695-a1359eaf811a.Text: The xenos's ornate clothes and solid-looking armour are caked in his boiled insides.

2e573cc4-bbe8-466e-9527-0ae5075b86c1.Text: From what you can tell, the Drukhari's insides were somehow brought to a boil. His flesh has liquefied, yet for some reason, his skin has remained intact.

9dff41c1-4c0d-427f-8ee4-73b15542ef1b.Text: A gruesome blow has caved in the gladiator's skull, but, surprisingly, he is still alive.

ba134c1d-4c87-45a8-b8b5-c23c53d3d399.Text: A powerful blow has caved in the gladiator's skull. If not for his large and clearly expensive cranial augment, his head would have surely exploded.

d22b814c-cad2-4b75-bd8f-8388dd584c8b.Text: The barrels exude the smell of cheap fuel, which the owners must be using to power the bar's generators — and, quite possibly, to dilute their rotgut.

cbab9c78-ff06-44d5-bb0a-79c6cca57208.Text: This shoddy cover will offer little protection against a well-aimed shot, but at least it will conceal the target from the shooter.

6c74b493-91f3-4a2f-97f6-63e7a7a03087.Text: An assortment of rubbish — belongings of questionable value likely stolen from compartments purged by Chorda's enforcers.

cf3843c2-8daa-441a-953b-72a4bde8de0d.Text: The recently functioning airlock is now refusing to obey any commands. Someone has deliberately compromised the mechanism's machine spirits.

8597a819-cc5f-4d1c-a82c-9cf7e193e311.Text: Order that the fuel barrels be placed throughout the room

bbb8e8c6-d603-4a96-bb99-5decd548eafc.Text: Order for barricades to be assembled out of the rubbish

b6bf427c-b1a5-4329-84e6-0e972a5e2273.Text: Order a mine to be set here

6f1a3554-e146-42b3-9ed6-cfbccf923ff5.Text: Enraged after having their slumber disturbed, the machine spirits strike you with a lash of electricity... And then the cogitator comes to life.

d6972f22-0e74-464b-8255-17deb255cdb9.Text: You hear the displeased grumble of drowsy gears from deep inside the cogitator, but the machine spirits obey and awaken the cogitator's screen.

071d2bad-84c6-42ab-9a9d-b2d4a708665d.Text: "Intruders! Over here! Just like Falco warned!"

6a9e7404-7dc9-4119-a5ce-2b9d6a737b90.Text: "Where are you going, shereen? The hunt for the void rats has only just begun."

cd8809ae-e65a-4859-95bc-1f2023dd5265.Text: "I beseech you in the Exalted One's name, try to keep a low profile, shereen! Or else Falco will make short work of my crew!"

c643c99c-f30c-4561-9b25-84d7632597ca.Text: "Shh! I think the Exalted One saved us from trouble again. But I beg of you, shereen, by all the stars in the galaxy — we can't make another mistake. Falco's nerves must be at their limit by now."

c71e9961-2c17-4c9d-b869-0bfeb52b26a2.Text: "Throne damn it, now Falco definitely knows we're here! We must save my crew! Hurry!"

1fb809eb-0119-48be-ae0f-4bfd6eb39b7e.Text: "Here's the cogitator I told you about, shereen. I just hope we can turn it on."

70346e94-121f-4f8b-be28-54a45fa36827.Text: "This is where the gas cylinder goes. Hidden in plain sight, if you will."

a420c5c9-ca5c-4c15-a376-e46f0afa2b4b.Text: "By the Exalted One, shereen, please try not to attract this much attention when you're turning the valves!"

84d22357-2451-4feb-9308-a1b4148e0b7d.Text: "Let's not be too hasty, shereen — Falco's patrols are up ahead! We should blend into the shadows and move quietly..."

0e3a9ef4-33d9-46e1-b751-bbf677d60358.Text: "You're just what we need, you rusty piece of metal."

6c6b1947-fbd7-4370-a6d7-8d45a20be3ee.Text: "I see one of the valves we need, shereen."

63bc78de-4e01-4920-9cf2-bd543041c0d5.Text: A loud whistle echoes through the sewers... and dies away. You must have damaged something while attaching the tank to the intake.

7c2814f7-9d95-4eb5-8cb2-77bb53d5aafe.Text: "I'll rip out your liver and give it to the wind spirits to eat!"

aa842750-0a61-4036-936b-663690b84f9e.Text: Build a bridge out of planks

a895ce55-e258-4e20-afce-9a60609ddc9c.Text: The withered victim's face is forever twisted in a silent scream.

4dbde49a-df02-4d8f-b05c-9d9fc400d39d.Text: The tank filled with repulsive green liquid contains a mutilated figure. It is difficult to say whether you are looking at a xenos, a mutant, or a machine.

362924c6-07ac-4800-b0ff-31e2e08766e1.Text: The tank was shattered from the inside by an unthinkable force.

68e242cf-78b2-4e3e-9182-3c935b7c50cb.Text: Revolting biomass, some elements of which can be interpreted as human features, floats in the green liquid.

70eeaeda-1522-407d-83c3-1c5af5a9b7df.Text: Bodies of runaway test subjects. They failed to find a way out and died from hunger and disease.

f1104152-cbf7-40b2-8c32-dc1d949c9dd9.Text: A group of runaway test subjects barricaded the door in a desperate attempt to escape from a terrible fate, but help never came.

9dc5e89a-2b88-4ff7-a641-76350a81129a.Text: Disfigured bodies hang all over this old maintenance bay like worthless slabs of meat for which the owner could find no better use.

49b20555-3861-4280-be3d-7dfffb63521b.Text: "With any luck, the xenos will stumble upon some of the traps the late technomat left behind..."

fd6345c2-5708-45a8-8c62-1700440590bb.Text: "Lord Captain, this enemy of Humanity will not get in here, we guarantee it... as long as he doesn't go down the technical shafts deep inside the ship — then there's no way we'll find him."

e3da94fd-0922-4420-8c6e-23564b8b5098.Text: Judging by the blood dripping from every crack in the broken armour, the xenos inside practically exploded. The cause of this gruesome death is unclear.

a77835b1-69d3-4e31-9389-d3f70d684063.Text: There is a glistening, gaping wound under the Kabalite's cracked armour. This xenos was not just killed — his insides were turned into paste as he was slowly eviscerated.

88149a0e-43d0-420c-8305-0ff8eaa559a0.Text: The destroyed xenotech gives off a repulsive chemical stench.

a3bdd764-7fd2-4c29-b2f0-938010e0b87e.Text: "The litanies of service have been recited — the necessary obeisances have been made to the machine spirits. Requesting permission to perform the sacrament of vesting."

eb5ea659-0b35-4b01-912a-63140aa1107d.Text: "Request denied. The sacrament of vesting is suspended for the duration of the privileged unit's visit."

1e880c53-e802-494c-9008-9f0b69347f92.Text: The resplendent armour of the Emperor's Angel, which has seen more than one battle and taken more than one ferocious blow in its centuries of service.

b3e9317b-b878-4456-b7a9-d648d7c14f82.Text: The skin of the wild beast conjures up images of a bloody battle between the one who now wears it and the creature from which it was taken.

aad886a3-a22c-47b4-a796-3277e73faadc.Text: The backpack is the repository of the mighty machine spirit that supplies the Space Marine's armour with the Motive Force. Its efforts ensure that the heavy armour does not burden the wearer but rather multiplies his strength and endurance a hundredfold.

3a7d6c58-baed-4aea-94de-3c01d6f8cd44.Text: Ulfar, standing on a dais beneath the gilded vaults, resembles a cast-metal statue of a Space Marine as seen adorning many temples. All that is missing is the armour. Sensing a task not yet complete, mechadendrite tentacles descend from the ceiling toward the Wolf, preparing to begin the sacrament of vesting.

4bd4c86e-8ff1-4446-8236-dddd4636f827.Text: The bodies of uniformed Imperial scouts have been scattered around by a detonated mine.

6c226c6f-6b8c-4d8d-833f-b90999eb9769.Text: "Wandering among the stars without family or friends... Don't you get lonely?"

8f3868d3-f936-4dad-9623-12de923dcb44.Text: "You're not the Inquisitor's only acolyte, correct?"

f0509b3e-e961-4e04-af57-07d76ae5a788.Text: "I don't know what I'm more surprised by — the absurdity of this story or the fact you're capable of such a show of emotion."

e0fb098f-d07a-455e-a03d-b45fac8e7659.Text: "I know nothing about you, Heinrix. Could you tell me a little about yourself?"

ddd850d4-13f5-4c5a-9747-f5db6aaaa024.Text: "Are there other acolytes in the Koronus Expanse?"

c579bf63-9121-4793-98e5-7fbbf05a2838.Text: "I think that will be all for now."

2be72792-3311-483b-af15-c26d95bc8cd4.Text: "You killed your colleague in cold blood."

1deafe9e-b55b-48f1-88f3-aa41b3da66ba.Text: "I find myself with some free time, and I would like to spend it in private conversation with you."

e820bbc4-3c62-4ef0-b0c2-ef882b91755b.Text: "Everything Emelina said about Calcazar — should we be concerned about it?"

3660893c-35db-495a-ba0c-b3552d541555.Text: "How long have you served in the Inquisition?"

60ca23dc-487b-4e35-994d-57f3ba46eaf2.Text: "Yes, that is all I have to say on this subject."

7c22132c-90ae-47a1-87a9-294943cd6174.Text: "You've visited many worlds during your service, I'll wager..."

2dd9459a-352e-4049-8c20-0ae7a6aafc81.Text: "What duties have you been carrying out for the Inquisitor?"

493d618e-1084-4c65-bde7-7e5cd98ca336.Text: Handed Yrliet over to the Inquisition.

c83c7a65-4a53-46e6-afed-0ac2e2beff26.Text: "Just so. See to it that I never set eyes on that xenos again."

45961bc3-affa-46f3-a690-1e0704316198.Text: "No, wait. I must consider this matter further."

33747221-b3af-447a-bf16-0097def01a21.Text: "I want to discuss the Cult of the Final Dawn. What can you tell me about it?"

4414c206-0914-41e8-aea4-593482900f2c.Text: [Kiss Heinrix] "I promise you will not regret your decision."

6d226f80-4b43-405e-915b-268c4fb5e7fa.Text: "What are you going to do next?"

88728fde-a3bf-41df-b3c5-ff55c293f1fd.Text: "You seem to have been investigating this cult for some time..."

664853f6-6e2b-46a8-8b5c-ed35b4c23144.Text: "What can you do as a psyker?"

e8966924-66b1-47f0-a5f4-3224870150e6.Text: "For someone who's been in service for decades, you certainly look young."

c7302535-30cc-495a-9696-07da8aa72352.Text: "Remind me, what is your mission regarding the cult?"

e7c0d970-3507-46c3-96ad-74a28ecfccb8.Text: "I have something to tell you. Yrliet confessed to killing Achilleas Scalander."

6bb57cd2-f230-464d-a1b9-fb576b19daac.Text: "If you're an Interrogator, does that mean you hold a special position in the retinue?"

b27c078c-bc7f-4a8c-a9f7-d4fa24225e01.Text: "I want you to leave my retinue and my ship."

0cb8cd51-2a21-46b8-83c3-03e0bf29be4a.Text: "What do you know about this place?"

b4f481b3-cb33-4df8-8d0b-47696b3f7704.Text: "Am I mistaken, or is the present company making you uncomfortable?"

9f6482e9-c5e7-4add-abfb-8be04f2e3106.Text: "I misspoke. Stop looking at me like that."

12645f7d-7491-4979-a711-976a71d2e3a2.Text: "She said that Scalander had betrayed the Imperium and was himself conspiring with Marazhai."

2487b050-dac8-4695-bd63-b552e55ca7b0.Text: "Nevertheless, I intend to keep her in my retinue."

591d9f7f-5600-463b-943e-24998ec2fe92.Text: "We shall have to wait and see."

3574a31e-f03e-4ebc-9406-18db8035a1d9.Text: "We need every ally we can get in this place. If only to enable us to escape and continue to serve the Imperium."

5cf5c01d-463b-4392-98f9-f8ea62b97a65.Text: "As soon as we escape this place, I will be handing the xenos over to you. Do with her what you will."

30481812-f86f-494a-b4a8-1dacb16e5848.Text: "I am bored of Yrliet. I would like to hand the xenos over to the Inquisition."

aa70626c-d0e0-4d72-9682-40ac5d181fa7.Text: "I'm not a bad conversation partner, should you ever want company."

c1a26318-c27a-4107-b9e6-1b277df26209.Text: "You wanted to discuss the nature of your mission."

75d9d430-bf7b-455d-9cc9-242ee1749ddd.Text: [Give Heinrix a lascivious look] "Such criminal neglect of your needs."

8956a509-3b5f-4eb0-b2d6-6bb1d9b94446.Text: "It would be a pleasure. Why don't we go to my study?"

a58ba76b-ad05-4a7d-8a17-21ce245e38c3.Text: "I am rather busy just now... but we shall certainly revisit this."

c364310d-ac7f-44fb-8042-b71c1f23cb04.Text: "I want the Inquisition to take care of Idira. Rid me of her."

87146707-695e-418c-b45c-36a7ad2d6dd2.Text: Handed Idira over to the Inquisition.

d067484b-51bf-4ee3-b1ec-1d0af87fc367.Text: "I would like to spend some time with you. Alone."

9f651d79-c66f-476a-9082-989684621bc1.Text: [Lay a hand on Heinrix] "You did what you had to do. Do not punish yourself."

1f72fadd-a508-4be2-b72d-1966a2500cb7.Text: "You were sent to the Inquisition straight after training?"

0b0c2cca-83b8-42e0-a2ae-752fb6bd7dc3.Text: "What are you going to do now that this is done?"

2521a4ea-733c-4ce7-8a76-ffcbb3743e21.Text: "I have had enough of Marazhai's stunts. It is time to hand him over to the Inquisition."

13fa5f60-dc36-4d2c-8715-394dd6419665.Text: Handed Marazhai over to the Inquisition.

3a3c3fbb-5e48-4a73-a6ff-9742cdfa03b9.Text: "I wish to speak with you about a personal matter."

7a1c4440-b1bc-4451-ba8d-475a89b10a01.Text: "I wouldn't mind playing a round of regicide."

d45ff934-1cbf-437e-a8a4-c6724bba5d94.Text: "I think I am ready for my regicide lesson."

c03d35f6-eb43-4e90-a1f8-f5d5794cb5d2.Text: "We have crossed a line. I think we should return to how things were between us before."

9ede9117-7362-4455-847b-7a1a14ba2ea3.Text: "It is, Heinrix. I've had enough of games."

96a0fc0e-be1f-4ee9-ac88-a45ed0f88c4c.Text: "Heinrix, what kind of gift do you think I could give Jae?"

5991a259-c418-45f5-8b97-cb7205d00355.Text: "Are you satisfied with the results of your mission on Kiava Gamma?"

53dfd2fc-d457-4501-ae15-ce424e6400d0.Text: "You wished to discuss an Astropathic message and an urgent matter."

60a9ab0c-4ef6-4e49-938a-f30d318f9115.Text: "I am still waiting for an explanation."

ca34e3c8-a910-4e6a-9656-d7ea5becfa23.Text: "I see no need to. I fully understand what happened and the circumstances surrounding it."

ce6758dc-a853-4b12-b5e3-5261d2f762e9.Text: "I am warning you: if such a thing ever happens again, you and Calcazar will both regret it."

9475f12e-8872-4290-bfe1-aa82a9c81878.Text: "You warned me. I was prepared for the unexpected."

ab6fb3f3-f60f-4dd6-8943-7d1315285be6.Text: [Move closer] "Must I throw myself at you every time, or are you going to take the initiative?"

b99719a8-081e-4992-bb0c-62b3bb3f4078.Text: "Warning me about Calcazar's visit, taking that risk — you must have had a reason for it."

e81d290f-8565-4b58-bdf8-1bb6ac592f7c.Text: "Heinrix, speak plainly: what is going on between us?"

a4ee94b8-1537-4a2d-9e0f-598a184c63c0.Text: "You have decided to leave the Inquisition. What will happen to you now?"

be64a2b4-7af0-467d-9c27-f7c74141c513.Text: "Is your control over your psyker powers going to weaken still further?"

0accf804-d762-40a1-b0c9-e8fc58a4dcda.Text: "You have that little control over yourself? You're simply dangerous!"

3de56fd0-bc0d-4ee5-879e-4308d194eebf.Text: "Sorcerous powers are truly dangerous. I hope you have mastered your abilities since then."

f901dea0-96cb-4f5c-b79f-7255f4d774db.Text: "Touching the cogitator did... something... to you. I want to know what."

20b40a2a-9041-4ab9-91c4-18d44676821c.Text: "So now I can be rid of you?"

7a215431-e35b-421b-a91c-2ea297a75993.Text: {n}Heinrix looks at you intently, his head tilted.{/n}

37f6685c-4552-4095-a96d-d880d77dd80d.Text: "To what do I owe this visit, {name}?"

8752613f-24f9-48a1-9c07-34d6aacdfcb3.Text: "Of course not. The Lord Inquisitor's entourage comprises dozens of people — the best of the best, experts in various fields and disciplines. Some of them I know personally. Others I have never met."

62ae7bdc-0f43-4d6e-af35-32ad2ef5bd80.Text: {n}Heinrix's expression becomes pensive, and he seems to look through you to something beyond.{/n} "To be honest, I'm not even certain that the people I know are still alive. I used to work with other acolytes of the Lord Inquisitor, but in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}, I have been working alone."

652f7a79-2240-43ba-b591-ddef54291849.Text: {n}Heinrix's face is momentarily split by a sarcastic grin.{/n} "I'm usually the one interested in the pasts of those around me, not the reverse. I come from a {g|Encyclopedia:KnightWorld}Knight world{/g} — Guisorn III. I belonged to a branch of one of the noble houses... until my exceptional abilities were discovered. After that I was sent on a {g|Encyclopedia:BlackShip}Black Ship{/g} to Holy Terra, where I was trained and I began my service for the glory of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}."

f1c95dd5-c284-4253-a08d-2a9672955160.Text: "When I arrived on {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerra}Holy Terra{/g} and was tested, I was found to be suitable material for becoming a sanctioned psyker, able to bend his curse to his own will. I can assure you that the adepts of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAstraTelepathica}Astra Telepathica{/g} were right in their assessment."

d9b3b010-5de5-4e39-9481-588f85136667.Text: {n}Heinrix gives you a sidelong glance, his lips stretched into a caustic smile.{/n} "I don't consider raw emotions to be a necessity in everyday communication. But let me assure you that I am more than capable of anger. Fortunately for others, I learned to focus it. Properly measured rage reveals the full potential of combat psykana in much the same way as aged cheese reveals the notes of a mature amasec."

bd6dccf2-fb5a-453b-a91d-a515597b1c44.Text: {n}Heinrix is silent for a long time, his eyes distant. Then he meets your gaze.{/n} "No servant of the God-Emperor has closer dealings with corruption than the agents of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}. In its quest to guard the Imperium against its foes' most devious and secret schemes, the Inquisition seeks to understand the essence of evil. It is not enough for us to burn or cut down a rotten seedling — we must study it. Understand it. Touch it. Every time any of us do our duty, we are risking our very souls. But when it comes to psykers... the soul of a psyker is especially enticing to the Archenemy."

c9301a07-2700-4212-bbc8-edd3cc9e3be4.Text: {n}The Interrogator narrows his eyes at you and releases a disappointed sigh. After several seconds of silence, you realise that you will not be getting an answer.{/n}

1a132b01-36ea-4a82-9dbc-64e59fa87333.Text: "Like many {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psykers{/g} unaware of their curse, I found out when a strong emotional reaction triggered an involuntary response." {n}Heinrix falls silent. Then he sighs and reluctantly continues,{/n} "My great-aunt had a pet grink. One day, it bit me, and I boiled it from inside out." {n}The Interrogator looks away and adds more quietly,{/n} "And when my great-aunt slapped me for what I'd done, I boiled her too."

4ae8a33d-feef-42ce-97e6-6fb6fbe39c90.Text: "I would tell you more, but I can't — not because of the prohibitions of the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Inquisition{/g}, but because the information is fragmentary and unverified. Based on what we have learned here, we are in the prison of one of the arenas where the Drukhari kill their prisoners as public entertainment. These {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} feed off pain... which means that entertainments like this are not a whim, but a necessity for these abominations. They need pain more than they need air to breathe, and so these performances must be held unceasingly... and raids to acquire new victims must continue without interruption."

58ad6de0-4587-4e87-b636-a0e8e68773d8.Text: {n}Heinrix is silent for so long, you begin to think that an answer will not be forthcoming.{/n} "Picture a vast prison ship filled with frightened, angry {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psykers{/g} who can't control their abilities and who have just lost their homes and their families. Some of them were children and adolescents like I was. Some were monstrous creatures who no longer had the right to be called human, or psychopaths who revelled in their impure powers."

a9a8640f-dfca-4504-bceb-003811611d91.Text: "So long as Lord Inquisitor Calcazar's decree remains in force, I am obliged to escort the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} of House von Valancius and provide all possible assistance and support. I am afraid I cannot comply with your request."

649fa5b1-dd31-4b6d-af07-bd3ea5e38ec5.Text: "I do, but I have no ties to my homeworld now, none except my first name." {n}Heinrix's mouth turns down.{/n} "I left Guisorn III when I was still a child. My family disowned me, stripping me of my family name — I was given a new one by those who trained me. Even for a noble, being branded a {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} is a mark of eternal shame. I experienced that first-hand, before I was put on the Black Ship."

f268d30f-be2f-4595-b8c1-18a7816ea9ac.Text: {n}Heinrix crosses his arms and drums his fingers on his forearm.{/n} "It is dangerous information, but you are already too deeply involved... In the Inquisition, there are two main philosophies — puritanism and radicalism. The adherents of the former are conservatives who strive to follow the letter of Inquisitorial doctrine in all matters. The radicals are more... pragmatic. They believe that the end often justifies the means, and they use tools that a puritan would condemn as heretical."

ab413f0b-d045-4ef5-aa35-043c1c500af3.Text: "Since the day of my initiation as an acolyte — so, decades." {n}Heinrix shrugs.{/n} "How many real years it's been, it's hard to say. When I return from a journey through the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g}, I often discover that much more or much less time has passed in {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}realspace{/g}."

3b742d95-4e50-4459-b37d-197d9159fa3c.Text: {n}The stiff bow Heinrix dispenses is calculated with millimetre precision.{/n} "If the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}'s hospitality has run out, I am loath to inflict my society upon {mf|him|her} any longer. I will leave the ship at the first opportunity and inform the Lord Inquisitor of the change in circumstances."

f6f98bb9-81da-4fb6-8f3e-8fa24b1625ca.Text: {n}Heinrix inclines his head slightly and begins to speak more quietly:{/n} "Being near you is a trial for me. A trial I was not prepared for, and so even speaking of it is... difficult for me. As it always is when it concerns my own desires, rather than my responsibilities and obligations. My duty comes first, even before myself. Please, {name}..." {n}He hesitates for a second. Then he takes your hand, brings it to his lips, and tenderly kisses your fingers.{/n} "In our position, I can allow myself... very little. And for you it is no different, really. Just... let me be here for you and help you. That is more than enough for me."

264238e8-9222-4040-ae1f-50f7ae018467.Text: {n}Heinrix is silent for a few seconds. Then he looks into your eyes.{/n} "Let me be frank, {name}... you are remarkable. Unique. Not only by virtue of your special position, but by virtue of..." {n}He hesitates.{/n} "I am grateful to the God-Emperor that my duty to Him has brought me into your retinue. And that I have had the chance... to be near you. Believe me, despite the... particular role I must play here, I do sincerely want to spare you... any unnecessary distress."

6eb864c9-e713-49b5-817b-092e9ee43a62.Text: "Indeed. I have visited many of the places brought to the Emperor's light... and those sullied by the filth of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}. In truth, even after all these years spent visiting the various corners of the Imperium and looking beyond its borders, I still consider the Segmentum Solar to be the greatest of all Humanity's bastions. Nothing compares to the majesty of {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerra}Holy Terra{/g}, the might of {g|Encyclopedia:Mars}Mars{/g}, the grandeur of the segment's other worlds."

ff8b93a9-a77c-4620-ad50-fe95c0c31d61.Text: {n}The Interrogator returns your look and smiles — but thanks to the expression in his ice-cold eyes, the effect is rather unnerving.{/n} "You can't really be expecting me to answer that question, can you?"

f838435c-5a24-4cdf-95e0-29afa22ae923.Text: "I am a heretic, {name}." {n}Heinrix gives a slight shrug, smiling softly.{/n} "It is strange to say and even stranger to hear... but that is my decision. No more sacrifices in the name of the Imperium. I have paid my debt to the Golden Throne — now I serve you."

324389a5-aa38-4886-ba18-3b3f4bb85144.Text: {n}The Interrogator bows to you.{/n} "Thank you for facilitating this, Lord Captain. I will arrange and personally oversee the extraction of the xenos from your crew without any casualties or damage to your vessel."

d0ddfbf1-0e1f-4073-b5b9-18c0de72bd51.Text: "The cult's ordinary members are humans who have been corrupted by the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}, traitors to the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}, and accomplices of Chaos. Participation in the cult's rituals always entails brainwashing, literally and figuratively. The longer cult members spend among other cultists, the less critically they think and the more closely they resemble obedient livestock, stripped of their fear and instinct for self-preservation. The worst of them go to their deaths without an inkling of doubt, ready to take hundreds and thousands of souls with them."

315bd700-279d-45a2-9d5d-94cc49145a24.Text: "As for those at the top of the cult's hierarchy... we have not yet managed to get a lead on all of the cult's leaders. I imagine that some of them are hiding in the depths of the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}, but those who are orchestrating the fanatics on nearby worlds are hiding very well indeed... or receiving protection from above."

dc1e2f11-4805-48e2-b760-3fcde853e827.Text: {n}Heinrix responds passionately to your kiss, then laughs huskily.{/n} "I know."

be2e6b8c-d291-4f48-a14a-c7066df2519c.Text: "I understand your concern. You may no longer trust my judgement in this matter, but... since that breach, I have no longer felt the same tension or the same danger. My control over my sorcery seems to have recovered... at least partially."

a8126bef-36f4-471e-8c6b-43e5b617ca01.Text: "But if you think my excommunication from the Inquisition will automatically strip me of all my psyker techniques and my will, leaving me utterly unable to resist the warp... then, no." {n}He allows himself a chuckle.{/n} "That's not how it works. My self-control is solely mine."

73c3a260-b401-47b9-a0d2-b20f26ee0d2f.Text: "Governors. Commanders. {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Traders{/g}. History is full of those who neglect their duty to the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g} and seek allies in the wrong places."

35bc2950-8348-4067-b94d-60991375808f.Text: "I need to confirm the reports from my agents. According to them, one of the cult's leaders is in the Kiava Gamma segment — an {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} within the dominion of the von Valancius dynasty. I hope you won't impede my investigation."

5bb81830-d0ff-46cf-96ea-4e5499c5026d.Text: "We discovered the first traces of it as soon as we arrived in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}. Since then, the more we learn, the better we see just how far the roots of this blight extend. Destroying individual cells is pointless — we must cut this beast off at its head."

6c7dcb63-0dac-4c9b-b604-613836af05d6.Text: "My visit to Kiava Gamma did not produce answers to all my questions, but we did succeed in dealing a blow to the cult by destroying the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g}'s machine. I have directed my spies to track the sect's surviving leaders — I am certain that they will have useful information for us soon. Though small, this is a victory for the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}, and I have you to thank for it, {name}!"

c1ec9374-974b-4e27-b72a-ea1635b9b4a3.Text: "The Lord Inquisitor was most insistent that I master the discipline of Sanctic Daemonology. I use my faith and my power to crush the enemies of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} — servants of {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} tremble at the sound of the Emperor's name, uttered by my lips. I am also a skilled biomancer — I can manipulate bodily processes. Sometimes... sometimes I resort to those skills in the course of my work. When it is necessary to make the subject of an interrogation more cooperative."

501f7464-b055-48e4-91f6-cd8fae161110.Text: {n}Heinrix politely inclines his head in response.{/n}

fbbccdb9-9bb1-4ea9-896e-eef36cc66518.Text: "The first step for biomancers such as myself is to take control of the processes of their own body — including ageing." {n}Heinrix smiles crookedly.{/n} "I have endured innumerable hazards in my work — if I allowed every trace of them to remain, I would look completely different today."

74f8b900-fcb4-40a5-ae96-375641bc6b7b.Text: {n}Heinrix blinks and looks at you almost as if in surprise.{/n} "I... had never even considered such a thing before you asked. Hmm. Perhaps I do. Sometimes."

0d1d4d55-439c-4bb6-89de-62df1d4cb956.Text: "The vast majority of newly discovered psykers are extremely uncontrollable and unstable. I was no exception... However, I lived to see the arrival of the {g|Encyclopedia:BlackShip}Black Ship{/g} to our world, which means I did not cause my jailers too much trouble, all things considered."

02d2d166-d9e3-4b18-818b-a89726000357.Text: {n}Heinrix shrugs vaguely.{/n} "I rarely have the time or the opportunity to think about it."

969f703a-7023-40f1-adfa-1293fad9a2e3.Text: "Thank you for finding the time for our conversation."

bb4b1e27-fa72-4abb-8f1a-8c8a0c210499.Text: "We are not a retinue, {name} — we are acolytes. As for your question, I am closer than anyone else to the one I call my personal teacher. The Lord Inquisitor deemed me worthy of undertaking the most important and sensitive tasks requiring the attention of agents of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}."

262df89f-2174-4562-b857-2e5ae018e7a9.Text: "I touched the corruption of the Archenemy, {name}. Did you honestly think the experience could somehow be a pleasant one? {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}Psykers{/g}, even sanctioned ones, even those who have performed all the rituals, passed all the initiations — we are all gateways to forces hostile to Humanity. I survived a difficult battle on Kiava Gamma, one that was invisible to others and potentially fatal for myself."

ce7eba3c-5d02-44ca-8af8-b0b5d80aebad.Text: "When I touched the cult's cogitator, I drew the thousand-eye gaze of evil upon myself — as any agent does when they interfere in the schemes of those who serve the Ruinous Powers. And that evil undoubtedly left an invisible mark upon me — as it does on any acolyte who fights against the Archenemy. And this will be the case every time I do my duty. I know a good deal about the fates of those who have served the Throne before me. Enough to know that my path leads to one place and one place only."

a524a9d6-d5f3-4fac-b8e1-c752dbc7efd6.Text: "As soon as we dock on Footfall. That's assuming, of course, that the von Valancius dynasty is committed to serving the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}... as it should be."

b1dbb5fd-1a14-454a-8cce-b27b8a290f29.Text: {n}Heinrix turns his scrutinising stare on you.{/n} "Is this the wish of the head of the von Valancius dynasty?"

3b52e0d1-00f3-4142-8b6e-cb740125281c.Text: {n}The smile fades from the Interrogator's face.{/n} "However, there is something I must tell you. Back there, at the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}... my decision to let it complete its operation allowed me to... I can't even find words... to perceive something of what is to come. You deserve to know this. The cult is threatening the worlds within your protectorate, after all, {name}."

ca88624f-b924-4f1a-bda9-d8807898ea21.Text: "Then, for Throne's sake, stop making these pronouncements. It's quite unnerving," {n}Heinrix says in a tone that could be exasperated or sardonic.{/n}

6fd4d7b1-49fa-4549-92a6-5554458c85e2.Text: "I could choose to think of it as an echo of the past or a spectre of the future, but that's not it. {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}Warp{/g} sorcery joins stretches of time together, violating the accepted sequence and flow of events. I heard a resonance of the person behind the cult. I've faced daemons more than once before, {name}, but this? I couldn't have imagined such a concentration of evil and corruption. {name}... I am convinced that one of the Greater Daemons is behind the Cult of the Final Dawn. Beware the day when that daemon finds a way to appear in this world."

1d499f99-289e-47f9-a9a6-66c5352a37ba.Text: {n}Heinrix's stare seems to pass straight through you, but his face is tense almost to the point of twitching. He nods wordlessly to you.{/n}

e382c9ab-f2dc-42a1-8c3f-664276e32a86.Text: "I was operating the machine created by the servants of the Archenemy, and in doing so, I attracted the attention of the cult's master. Thank the Throne that it was only a glancing touch — if it hadn't been... we would not be speaking here today."

4ffbc317-503f-43a1-871b-8dc2f6e39057.Text: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} was stopped, yes..." {n}Heinrix closes his eyes briefly, and a note of bitterness enters his voice.{/n} "I touched an infernal machine that was created to serve Chaos. I used it. I delved into the principles of its operation... That was enough. Corruption needs only the briefest brush of contact."

c372ce36-74cc-4612-9748-cab70db25599.Text: "It will take some time, {name}. I can heal grievous wounds and correct disfigurement... but remake my nerve endings from scratch? Such delicate and painstaking work is beyond my capabilities. Every day with you brings new challenges." {n}Heinrix delivers the last part with a grim smile.{/n}

6a00de4f-9900-450b-80e6-60f8f00675d4.Text: "I hope you do not need me to tell you that taking any {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g} into your retinue is a stunt that falls somewhere between blasphemous heresy and incredible foolishness — let alone a Drukhari who has already succeeded in bringing myriad calamities down on our heads. I cannot imagine even one good reason why you should have taken this step... but I can think of plenty of bad ones, and that is what alarms and troubles me."

623005d4-3fce-46fd-894e-2120c7c0860b.Text: "Yrliet is directly responsible for us being lured into her kin's trap. They plotted against us together.
