fc5a58f0-3b02-474c-9783-68254059949d.Text: The place reserved for a centrepiece is empty, awaiting a worthy relic.

85de9a94-7728-4a16-ad12-97d90db89868.Text: The sarcophagus containing holy remains is polished to a shine and smells of precious incense.

1b6ee01d-4d6a-4c26-aaf2-0543576b2e64.Text: "The Aquila Anima: a fragment of the Cathedral of Eternal Redemption, brought from the shrine world of Solis VI, now lost."

0c6b4dec-b048-4425-a7fd-c4f253c7062a.Text: A power maul rests inside the glass. The inscription on the reliquary reads, "I am wrath. I am the cleansing. Whosoever wields me walks in the footsteps of FURIA."

926968c6-d603-4d56-865e-b36681e25abc.Text: The mechanism rotates steadily, adding dry clicking notes to the chapel's melody every time a manipulator catches against one of the dents on the drum.

5a2574be-16a2-446d-ab2e-858027df5cf6.Text: The voices blend in an unnatural unison. The longer you listen to the choral chant, the stronger your headache grows.

2dd63bf6-0693-44ba-99de-1f8aac7f8712.Text: The wax-stained interpreter is silent. Having had a new thick candle set on top and a prayer offered to the Omnissiah for the cleansing of the running gears, you feel confident that the machine will start working again in no time.

285a3135-5a60-4f14-9a20-13e28663428b.Text: Once clean of the candlewax that had seeped inside, the inner workings of the interpreter move much more easily.

35a3ecd4-14da-4683-9e31-1618e210f2fc.Text: The text-correcting calibrator is not responding to the moving tape. A confident smack makes the machine start doing... something.

cbfe5acc-d88c-46db-8198-d3eaa460344f.Text: The sensors of the text-correcting calibrator are dead. A prayer to the Omnissiah makes the new sensors spring to life.

cd2fd08a-fff9-44e7-bc49-7f177c7095e4.Text: Strange sounds are coming from under the receiver's grid. After a couple of kicks, the sounds grow quieter. The mechanism has been pacified.

b565dac2-7c74-4d81-8f63-2d0bf8e14482.Text: Scraps of paper are stuck deep inside the mechanism, causing it to rattle terribly. Cleaning the machine's parts and anointing them with sacred unguent restores the machine to its clear, clanging voice.

3a477325-4909-4c75-a9d8-9ccd41838032.Text: The transcriber's quills are leaving blots on the paper. After a couple of jerks, you are left holding the broken manipulator and quill in your hands. It will no longer be a disruption.

128b652f-e880-4a62-9407-cbe8ad286b1c.Text: The transcriber's quills are leaving blots on the paper. You remove the device's casing and discover a leaking ink supply hose.

1d8a8694-58c9-421a-b328-846c10e4badc.Text: The miniature screens are displaying red error messages. You cut power to the screens, banishing the worrying sign.

23b32752-73f5-4e91-9229-06c0c36a1d3a.Text: The miniature screens are displaying red error messages. You command the machine to run a diagnostic, and the messages disappear.

1f6ec298-9926-4190-95a2-1112d5fed808.Text: A deceased Navigator's organ repurposed for the Choirmaster's needs. Here is where processed messages converge from all over the chapel.

47e4d5b0-7bec-434b-b012-131e83810bb4.Text: Underneath the grille, you can see enormous outlines of formidable machines in a greenish haze.

98db708c-742f-4649-9aaa-dca860586d23.Text: The back of the throne is smeared with something dark red and old.

fe3639d2-9e77-4776-9e41-6d49285ed77c.Text: The throne is furnished with a conductive charge supply and can be turned into an instrument of execution at any moment.

cb327969-f8c7-4fb0-90c9-34f2bc88fb7f.Text: An endless stream of symbols fills the paper tapes.

2f689d70-df8c-400a-8643-2a6e78bf1d90.Text: "Accept the service of Your loyal servants, give rest to them who toil for Your benefit..."

9ca42e50-1df9-4b0a-910d-051afe1f2852.Text: "The Astropathic Choir is ready to serve you, Lord Captain."

46b7adce-66e8-4f6c-9eaa-977ba1506ead.Text: "The last beacon cannot be saved from the thirteenth storm! The lapsed father's beloved son will open his yawning maw!"

d3aacaf3-8685-41db-9162-fe5fcdcd2aff.Text: "Oblivion is inevitable. After the boundless sunset comes the horrific sunrise! Brought forth into a wailing world from the womb of—"

ec760051-fa21-42b3-aac4-2a4a5cc53b98.Text: "Hyremiah from the first shift died the other day. The safety switch on his throne didn't engage, so he went mad and gouged his eyes out with a tool."

50e14c5c-a68a-4c06-bad8-2c38726a7ef2.Text: "His screams drove the three beside him mad. One of them's still drooling on his pillow."

3dccddc4-ed0d-44c5-a7c5-008b96e4dda0.Text: "Better make sure those vacancies go to our relatives. Double rations for working at the chapel, am I right?"

8dc77e50-caa0-48d7-b948-a46620cf0097.Text: "I saw the Choirmaster praying again on my shift. Like the previous times. I don't think he sleeps at all. All he does is pray."

e0dcea62-25d4-44a0-92f3-69f73c0d665f.Text: "Master Weisz is a pious man. You ought to follow his example."

1e174176-2cf3-4e04-aa9e-a1802ec84ce5.Text: "Yeah, except I once heard what he was saying... It was enough for me. I'll never listen in on his whispers again."

a23f57de-5a47-4cbe-b7bc-abc45dbbebdb.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! The Emperor has blessed this day with your visit."

6700a244-9522-4b6a-a8be-e79f7fe112cd.Text: "Am I caught in the song's reverie or... is this really you, Lord Captain?"

2f0063e8-31fa-4e7d-9112-0bebc4a09988.Text: "Candles gone out again on thirty-four... I hope at least this time I don't have to scrape psychic ice off of them."

b6da40cc-cffa-4472-88f0-c81ab9d3f87c.Text: "Detecting extinguished candles on thrones... Seven... Twelve... Thirty... Maintenance staff, perform reignition."

daa012a6-68cf-492e-87c2-0d5b8e567b49.Text: "Remain vigilant. Check the throne's pacifying safety switch before activation."

c2d49130-41cd-4126-b234-5f251bcc945a.Text: "Safety switch malfunction on throne thirty... Enginseer action required."

2147fe96-8c9c-4bdc-9354-a56a5af02dc9.Text: "Servant SK-291, upon completion of your shift, you will receive... five... lashes for... violating protocol item five three nine point six two..."

f5775061-0ac6-4acb-869e-aac85cdf1973.Text: "I will begin preparing for the ritual at once, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

273f564c-6a5c-4748-a39e-91c1076f298e.Text: The corpse's blueish skin is coated with frost — no one has bothered to remove the body. Death has become too mundane an occurrence at the chapel.

4f9ef137-067e-4d36-a5ee-f11b67a654dd.Text: "Alas, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... the sacred machine is still deaf to the Enginseer's ministrations..."

137a2530-4aee-4132-8a5b-919705661c98.Text: Ink blotches appear haphazardly on the paper tape, likely the result of the machine spirit's mischievous nature.

1ab34c6e-4152-404b-8577-18a24ef6e92d.Text: Once the text is ready for final interpretation, the compiler sends it to the Choirmaster along with a list of meanings for the known images.

35a75892-f55b-4184-a9a3-3d7473d90c59.Text: The enormous reels are perpetually dragging the paper tapes along without any apparent practical reason, leaving one to think about how they could make for perfectly good rollers for tank treads.

92ca8a9d-419e-494c-bf67-33e9d962af79.Text: The receiver's enormous reels direct paper tapes containing unprocessed text into the chapel's depths after blessing the paper with an imprint of sacred cogs.

6ec97d85-6818-409a-8d84-af79a2a0c80f.Text: The machine uses its many quills to waste precious paper, ruining it with incomprehensible scribbles.

1f68e0ac-3b52-4e1e-ab02-dc3674984689.Text: The machine uses its many quills to commit the Astropaths' whispers to paper, then sorts the resulting raw mental images based on their meaning.

dea713fa-a804-4b65-ad26-a7959b22cd41.Text: "The ship needs you, Lord Captain. We humbly await your ascension to the command throne."

c8895384-116a-45fe-919e-53b284b2bacc.Text: "Have you lost something, friend? Let us give you a hand. Get him, boys!"

e16612f5-de9e-4b06-b8b9-f4335f1461d8.Text: "Hrost, buddy, what kind of insulation is that supposed to be? If you kill us, Mathias will drag me back from beyond the grave just to give me an earful. Scrap this and start again. I will double-check it."

326d88ba-c609-4447-9373-8a17e1a4a1e0.Text: "We won't let that scum rear their ugly heads. My people are already on their way to the crypt. We'll be waiting for you there."

a83b5689-a69a-4348-9188-7a2bc22d428c.Text: "My inferni will sweep the bay for any remaining caches. We might nab a couple of the bastards too, while we're at it."

ca7fe936-5bec-4900-9073-f51b1861975d.Text: The skeleton in decayed Tech-Priest robes is missing its right leg. Judging by what remains of the bones, the leg was hacked off. It seems the person was still alive when it happened, and they reached this spot by crawling rather than walking.

650036e8-2955-4f94-91fc-d4d371c7505d.Text: The motionless servo-skull shows no sign of damage — looks like it hovered next to its dead master until its battery ran down.

13ea5f0f-f008-4961-963a-12e991df64cd.Text: "We should sniff around here some more, Lord Captain. There should be a bunker, a control room, or something else that was used by whoever set the trap."

8603929e-2ca3-4995-982b-6980e4e623e1.Text: There is something hidden beneath the fake snowdrift, but you cannot make out what it is or get close to it.

899ce130-b023-4787-b7d9-f7f842063d41.Text: There is some kind of mechanism hidden beneath the fake snowdrift. You were not able to reach it, but it seems you managed to put it out of action.

827664bb-a0ee-45cd-b99a-c7415d24f08f.Text: It is impossible to determine to whom these bones belonged just by looking.

969c55e2-a3de-4469-9708-7929e82755ff.Text: The bone structure indicates that these belonged to an Aeldari, not a human.

dc8fda48-d298-4e12-becb-0ce1d60adde9.Text: This horrific unknown creature does not look like a typical inhabitant of this planet.

9a117747-b028-42b5-b7a1-5ba4fa7e8399.Text: You recognise the horrific dead creature as a medusae — a monster from the depths of the Webway, the favourite pet of the Drukhari.

13926ec7-24a4-4dab-9478-adbb3dcf7d5b.Text: The explosion exposes the channel of a cable leading away from the transmitter. This is probably not the only element of the trap.

d33d15cd-ae92-4b54-8e4b-c0de78ba3835.Text: It seems the transmitter did not survive the blast. It is unlikely it will lure anyone else into this trap.

72c816f9-05e5-401a-af90-4dd2c03ad6ac.Text: The transmitter has been destroyed and will never lure another person into this trap.

86b83355-1a21-4f01-8ec6-f1ab910e0836.Text: The turret is seriously damaged. Nothing of value can be gained from it now.

31ebb711-a27d-4f15-892b-3242fa34e855.Text: Intact components are scattered amidst the turret wreckage, perhaps they could be useful.

d59f1a51-5828-43b5-89c9-0503e6f9afed.Text: [Carefully inspect the skeletons and their gear]

e1ee28ea-9691-4a43-b542-f7b7be7f367e.Text: [Try to extract the data from the cogitator]

51d82614-ddaf-4707-bca7-eddae0a30677.Text: {n}Two skeletons are lying in strange positions — as if one was either carrying or hugging the other and did not let go even in death. Their gear is badly damaged and decayed.{/n}

dc37b853-e545-4da9-9d46-11a49891e1fd.Text: {n}The trinkets are clearly of xenos origin. They are miscellaneous, time-worn items that have no particular value. One can assume that they are petty trophies looted from several corpses.{/n}

fc0da6e1-fd00-4065-85da-4a6abed4a807.Text: {n}There are three things worthy of note: fragments of some sort of devices that both skeletons carried on their belts, some shiny trinkets in the remains of the carried skeleton's bag, and an old portable {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} in the other's bag.{/n}

ea119ff2-8c1f-4425-a49a-0fa64bd5bc45.Text: {n}The skeleton's decayed gear contains hardly anything of interest. The only find worthy of note is an old portable {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}.{/n}

a53664bb-9018-4f07-8c1b-0d1e763052a4.Text:
{n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} has been exposed to the elements for decades or even centuries. It is a small miracle that you are able to extract a fragment of a {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-recording — apparently the last communications.{/n}
"Scout 1: WE'RE RICH! Chaos take me! RICH!
Lookout: Fly, for crying out loud, spit it out. What have you found?
Scout 1: RICH! Screw {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g}! The Expanse can go to the Orks! WE'RE OUTTA HERE! CALIXIS, HERE WE COME!
Lookout: Yeah, because with our record, Calixis is definitely the place to go. What makes you think life's better there anyway?"

97f17807-daa1-4dbb-a6a4-bbfa021f77fd.Text: {n}The old tech has been exposed to the elements for a long time and is practically crumbling to dust in your hands. But at least now you know that the skeletons have been here for decades or centuries.{/n}

5cf18651-8139-4da0-9685-a56b98611def.Text:
"Scout 1: I want a house on some planet... a mansion! With a lion statue at the entrance! It'll have a servitor with one job — dusting my lion statue!
Lookout: Fly, you idiot, you're still on a dangerous planet. Quit sending me your hollering. Get back here or just tell me what you've found already.
Lookout: Fly.
Lookout: Fly. You coming?
Lookout: I'm coming for you, dumbass. If you're not responding just to mess with me — you're dead meat."

6806152a-5e37-45d0-89c9-20faca5b273f.Text: {n}The pieces of broken tech suggest that this was a rudimentary radar jammer — an item commonly utilised by pirates in the Koronus Expanse.{/n}

9ec67fca-ae2c-4342-b96c-5efa2387cd5a.Text: "{petname}, grant me access to this cogitator."

ad095915-5b7d-43c4-8e07-3be99142de06.Text: "A very fitting prank to entertain noble lords! I like it!"

3a77a6b3-15ab-4f5f-a847-bfe1475adfc7.Text: Destroyed the sinister transmitter designed to lure travellers into a trap.

36edad74-eed3-4f7e-aa4f-400e5eb371a8.Text: "Let's see what other things you have discovered."

dcec2902-47ea-4d24-a3e2-8dd92998d840.Text: "I don't want to believe that this is the work of loyal subjects of the Imperium, whether of noble birth or not. Using cunning traps to exterminate xenos is a good thing. But not killing our own."

0bdde464-7e17-457f-ab99-be7ce4c2c18b.Text: "I would bet my money on ordinary thieves. Set a trap and plunder the bodies of those who get caught in it — not a bad scheme."

eda05661-da1f-46cf-bc35-4e1efc49fef5.Text: "Right now we don't have enough information to determine who did this."

03edd441-cbbe-4532-b665-1b811c07952a.Text: {n}This unsettling structure adorned in strange masks vaguely resembles the antenna of a powerful transmitter. At its base you see a {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} and a few other devices. It seems that some part of the structure is buried underground.{/n}

5c2e8344-4062-45d3-9de5-87ecbfdfa5bc.Text: {n}The servo-skull swarm lets out a string of binharic signals, and the largest of the skulls instantly digs its mechanical drill into the side of the structure. A painful screech heralds the breaking of the machine spirit's will.{/n}

d9254576-03db-4775-972d-9a97a728c8dc.Text: {n}Yrliet inspects the construction closely and draws your attention with a graceful gesture.{/n} "Look — there among all the mon-keigh gear — an Aeldari-made device. A beacon, as you would call it. I recognise other components as well. Items from other races, but they are all serving a single purpose — to call for help..."

abca4b8d-24b7-4f1b-b1ab-358c2ff98f5b.Text: "So, someone loaded this miserable place with transmitters from various races... in the hope that someone would land here and run into their welcoming committee? Clever. I saw similar tactics used in my years in the Navy. True, in a war zone, you are usually on high alert — you don't just hare off after a lone distress signal. But in an isolated place like this — you expect the most likely scenario, just a ship that had to make an emergency landing. It looks like plenty fell for it."

1262556d-1fed-4eec-b864-eef0f6a48952.Text: "But who would set such an indiscriminate trap? One intended to lure in Aeldari and humans and anyone else? Who is an enemy to everyone and everything?"

09ae40b0-ff81-45dd-bd7a-29d93e19f657.Text: "We have a common enemy, an eternal enemy, one that devours all living things. Have we not already seen its servants on the Lilaethan and elsewhere?"

538146da-b10c-4cb1-a8ab-074953994621.Text: "I've seen it all in my life, and I can tell you one thing — this trap could be a malevolent plan by servants of Chaos. Or it could be a prank by some bored offspring of a wealthy lord, one whose parents failed to instil in him the barest speck of self-awareness."

455da6c4-be0a-4082-a19c-9f8e436c7297.Text: "Don't pretend your kind wouldn't be saying the same thing about us humans."

76a2131f-0c0d-4cef-ac30-9fa94592890e.Text: "It's possible, very possible... But I'm not convinced. There's something strange about this — it's highly suspicious."

8cb6c0c0-115e-4fa0-80f8-e351c6c148a6.Text: {n}You identify a number of elements of the structure — the long-range antenna of a design standard for Imperial colonies, the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}, the Aeldari beacon, and half a dozen other devices of varied origin. They all have one thing in common — this tech is designed to transmit basic signals to neighbouring space, the most common being requests for assistance and ship distress codes.{/n}

2a5bd1b7-bd78-4f55-8ffc-5cecd0858acc.Text: {n}This mishmash of wires, devices, and decorative details appears to be a mixture of technologies from different eras and even of different races — some of the items show signs of xenos origin.{/n}

ab936c57-0051-45f4-a017-0a9b09cd538d.Text: {n}You manage to penetrate the cogitator's defences. Its function is rather simple — the program is designed to activate the transmitter once every five years and send out a ship distress signal into space.{/n}

40975134-7bec-4ae8-b796-1245c67bfcb1.Text: {n}The cogitator is well protected against unauthorised access. What is more, your attempt to penetrate these defences causes it to turn off and no longer show signs of life.{/n}

85062a53-1c13-4051-b94a-93ddc5da0c68.Text: {n}You destroy the program and disable the transmitter. No one will respond to this sinister signal ever again.{/n}

8655618f-327e-4154-bd5d-2135065642ae.Text: {n}You set the charges carefully. Without a doubt, the structure will be destroyed with expert precision along with the underground part.{/n}

5daffe3d-b440-4f3a-87fd-c66b99d64b85.Text: {n}You set the charges and hope that it will be enough to destroy the entire structure along with the underground part... without hurting you.{/n}

f17a77a3-a9d5-43ad-a530-b4bab1fdd282.Text: {n}Noticing the interest with which Pasqal is surveying the construct, Heinrix asks,{/n} "Are you studying the device? Isn't its very existence a violation of the protocols of assembly?"

655a5b5d-227e-4fd0-b603-dc7e67e7fca3.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest's tone is pensive, and his visor flashes:{/n} "This statement is true. This construct has been assembled in contravention of canon law and must certainly be disassembled. But not quite yet."

4261e493-35ad-4707-93db-74b297b9a1ea.Text: {n}The swarm's anxiously flickering lumens signify that it has managed to extract additional information from the device and is eager to share it with you. As soon as you look over at the servo-skulls, they begin to move.{/n}

15b641f3-4044-4999-a3c0-019959571015.Text: {n}The swarm hovers near a wall of ice and emits a binharic trill. There must be something hidden behind it.{/n}

9eb87f87-c5d8-4e5f-b168-8cf9110a0306.Text: {n}Abelard shakes his head in annoyance.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, would you like me to set up a shooting gallery on the ship? With live predators as targets? Set in a miniature forest? You can go hunting, satisfy your daring that way. That would be a suitable entertainment for a noble {mf|lord|lady}. But 'pranks' like this one are a disgrace to Humanity, plain and simple."

84d34163-64d3-4faa-a45c-6be55e747bb0.Text: "Ah, I see. Killing xenos who respond to this distress call is acceptable to you."

cf2b107f-54cf-4083-af1c-4f00bc2254bf.Text: The surface bears the marks of determined and protracted effort: someone made dozens of scratches, which chaotically intersect at different angles without any order or logic.

eaca79af-90f9-4c9f-b038-2c58a7e9de6e.Text: The surface is covered in countless scratches, and you can discern some logic in them. Someone began by scratching strange symbols, but then defaced them, adding extra marks and lines.

009ee723-1079-4078-a4ea-141872be61ff.Text: Black, impenetrable darkness carries on with its silent existence.

165867e0-e905-45a0-a7fc-75df40f42a47.Text: The machine spirits have long since left the rusted shells of these ancient cogitators.

d2262e62-1905-46f2-b1bc-b54690fb1c3d.Text: These ancient cogitators are long dead. Despite this, the covers of the machines are still intact — it seems unlikely that the inner parts were ruined by the elements, so they could still prove useful.

600311ae-ea54-4177-9521-cee197e8aa8f.Text: Inside the containers are the remnants of stones and frescoes depicting a black spot surrounded by structures of some sort.

c4bbde66-07b1-4aa8-bc6a-1519a82f0c12.Text: Time and weather have almost wholly erased the writing left by an unknown author.

89caacc4-d5af-4af9-95ad-3b793c82c6bb.Text: "...speak to the fear that dogs you..."

c336a713-60ca-4e25-959c-258b74d7ecca.Text: Rudimentary tools and devices are now covered in a layer of dirt and local flora.

85e05d63-07d1-48f2-ac9f-ffc6403607a1.Text: Numerous ropes and cables end abruptly at the very edge of the pit, vanishing into the gathering darkness.

0d95715f-f677-4ce4-bd80-070d2aadfab6.Text: The barely noticeable words in shaky handwriting read: "TOUCH THE DARKNESS, AND THE DARKNESS WILL ACCEPT YOU."

6d01b162-3255-415b-b760-104ed639b66f.Text: [Get up and run as fast as you can]

35f69c5f-7c7b-4fdd-ac90-7ecd6885b4f1.Text: [The strange animal-like creature with barely noticeable shadows swirling around it]

588adddd-1178-4061-8a34-88d13b149b69.Text: [The sinewy young man wearing a blindfold]

2299a172-6d70-4fa6-8675-f0cfabce38b6.Text: [The ancient woman who only recently joined your caravan]

bf735a1c-3ecd-4d48-b480-6a7c14206f46.Text: [Kill your brothers and sisters and be the sole ruler of the civilisation]

5847d02a-8e46-43fc-8cdf-381f6b32b6af.Text: [Pervert the ritual to stop the insane civilisation for all time]

f0b708ae-6018-4675-bfc1-eaa1a3a7d611.Text: [The feeble-minded one who is gnawing on another's bones]

50007106-46f6-4a57-9fb3-6d67ebe6a8e8.Text: [The infant who is crying piteously, calling for its mother]

c293aaba-22e8-48d9-8253-96241e90ab5b.Text: [Proceed with the ceremony for the sake of future generations]

9a7f72d4-9ddf-4390-b942-715bfea01688.Text: [The bloodied guard with two animal heads]

36259a4f-acdd-4931-88b6-2948b275835d.Text: [Lean over and stretch your hand into the darkness]

44c03422-6cfd-465a-bdc1-06de7da09783.Text: [The decrepit old man in the tattered remains of a military uniform]

fffd3118-1c18-45c3-8783-6ed878d7bce4.Text: [The broken youth with empty eyes and a madman's laugh]

993c23ad-ce8f-42e7-9b59-a8a9cbebba23.Text: {n}The bright daylight cannot pierce the darkness lying over the slopes. The longer you look into its depth, the stronger the feeling grows that this darkness isn't just an absence of light. It is something immeasurably vast, endless, capable of reaching the farthest stars or swallowing a galaxy... Through sheer force of will, you avert your gaze.{/n}

3f7fc9d5-cb89-40f4-b2c8-141033c03c70.Text: {n}You lunge forward, but fall, as if someone has grabbed hold of your legs. Your bloodcurdling scream rings in your ears as darkness envelops you in a suffocating wave, pouring into your mouth, nose, eyes, into your very soul...{/n}

efbe2dbf-b388-47c6-816a-2f230dbc4c22.Text: {n}You gather your willpower and try to push the thing out of your head. But you and the darkness are still sharing your thoughts, and instead of retreating, it sinks its psychic tentacles even deeper into your brain.{/n}

cb661aa9-94d5-45b6-b84f-12a2d884abd3.Text: {n}...you find yourself on the floor of an abandoned estate. You feel someone's disgusting presence behind you, and raspy, foul breath tickles your nostrils. A drop of water trickles down from the stone ceiling and shatters the silence with a deafening splash. The heavy door before you is open, you could try to escape — it is now or never.{/n}

4e1b15aa-652f-4b31-b2a5-e81406133d24.Text: {n}At the edge of your consciousness, you sense something slimy and intangible answering your invitation for contact. It seeps into your thoughts, tasting your emotions. Surprise and curiosity envelop you, but these feelings are not your own.{/n}

9dcea9ea-1163-4e41-8019-9b921c84a325.Text: {n}You turn around, intent on killing the Thing with your bare hands, but then exclaim in hesitation — you recognise the disfigured monster that is staring at you balefully from the darkness. You let out a heavy sigh, and a cloud of hot, fetid vapour settles on the smooth surface of the mirror.{/n}

ab1cbccc-35b3-46bb-b2e1-0b2ea914c288.Text: {n}You gather your thoughts and strike up a conversation with the unseen creature. You tell it about yourself and your crew, about how you do not remember how you got here but would like to avoid conflict. You feel the fear retreat and take the first step toward the creature...{/n}

c1fa81d3-b277-4e36-8661-fff387b3eeeb.Text: {n}You clutch the knife in your hand and strike. To the darkness's glee, you close your eyes and gorge yourself on the hot blood, sating your hunger... until a heavy smack across your face brings you back to your senses. You are lying on the ground, some distance away from the hole, surrounded by your worried comrades. Looking around, you realise that someone is missing.{/n}

6628e779-fb7f-45f5-8144-01a1a2a90b8e.Text: {n}As your brothers and sisters surround you, you release your powers and consume every last one of them. For ten thousand days and as many nights, you battle their souls until you subdue them completely. Immortal, you remain on the throne for thousands of years, watching your civilisation blossom, die, and fade into darkness.{/n}

d376a2d9-1ed7-4834-b325-92a9dcd83bc5.Text: {n}Solemnly, you are placed on a cold black slab covered in glowing script. You close your eyes and pray as your brothers and sisters rip your seven hearts out of your chest. By the end of the ceremony, they are gnawing on every last bone of your body, shedding tears of sorrow. You join your ancestors within the black monolith, and for many centuries thereafter, you watch from above as your civilisation blossoms.{/n}

2e32f327-e53c-4877-b1ea-a4dea201688c.Text: {n}You approach the altar covered in glowing script and change it to the symbols you saw in the abandoned camp — in some other life of yours. When your brothers and sisters tear your seven hearts from your chest and the royal white blood trickles down onto the altered symbols, the skies above the pyramid split in half. In your last moments, you revel in the cries and groans of your thousands of victims, then an unknown force changes you as well, but you are already no more.{/n}

dcac2fcf-18b8-421a-ac1c-695fa1ab1046.Text: {n}...you are lying on burning sand, struggling to open your eyes, but your eyelids feel too heavy. You can barely move your arms and legs, your stomach hurts, your throat is bone-dry. Several of your kin, all emaciated, are scattered around you. The hunger is so strong that it is driving you mad, and you let out a bestial howl. Something metallic clinks next to your right hand... A knife! This is it! You can survive, you MUST survive. All you need to do is decide whom to sacrifice.{/n}

61ac1619-097e-4b38-a6ed-8d3836201227.Text: {n}You are hit by a sudden wave of all-consuming silence. A moment later, the world around you disappears, leaving only black, viscous, boundless darkness. The absoluteness of it is overwhelming, and you slowly sink into the void that is sucking you in.{/n}

daac154c-3010-412a-82bb-05e9ac07b230.Text: {n}The moment you approach the darkness amassing beneath your feet, something immediately takes root in your thoughts and emotions, much more forcefully this time. Your mind fogs over, and silent insistence spreads throughout your body.{/n}

f5724795-84f3-4764-8e9c-506f3ae33fd8.Text: {n}You turn around and walk away from the ominous pit and its secrets. Back on your ship, you give out a few orders, play a game of {g|Encyclopedia:Regicide}regicide{/g}, and turn in for the night. As you open your eyes, you find yourself back by the abyss. You run for dear life, get back to your ship, go to a different system... And when you wake up the next morning — the darkness is once again staring at you from beyond the edge of the pit.{/n}

3adfb4fc-59e8-4c1f-abb4-31b3fd9041a2.Text: {n}...you are looking at a tiny person peeking over the edge of the bottomless darkness. You are looking at yourself. Then you blink and see the same place, except the camp around you is full of life. Scholars are zipping back and forth between field structures, switching on unfamiliar machines in an attempt to know the unknown. A moment later, they are all nude, singing and dancing around the pit. The smell of heated bodies, blood, and sweat assaults your nostrils, drowning out your thoughts... one by one, the lunatics fall into the embrace of nothingness.{/n}

9a4e1eaf-c864-48f7-a930-61aae6bc0622.Text: {n}Heinrix peers into the darkness in the depths of the pit. You feel the touch of an otherworldly chill. The Interrogator arches an eyebrow.{/n} "Whatever this — hmm — phenomenon may be, there is no warp sorcery within it."

72058ae8-d947-4606-9e44-89b6c1c26577.Text: "Creepy..." {n}Idira tilts her head to the side, listening to something. Then she scowls and spits on the ground.{/n} "Grox knows what it is. It's beyond my remit."

11f81281-2e28-49c5-8e9d-bb6194c1793c.Text: {n}Again you run, again you change one system after another, you go without sleep for several days... Yet it happens all over again. You spend months, or it could be years, in desperate flight. At some point, you simply give up. With resignation, you sit down at the edge of the pit, no longer moving. Alien satisfaction fills your mind.{/n}

e568801f-4f6b-4813-b246-096e545a6b3d.Text: {n}The streams of fate were changed when you defeated fear and docility. With all your strength, you cling to the vision and do not let go until the darkness yields. The entity shows you the process of an incredible transformation and you cannot hold back tears at the sight of it. And yet, the human brain cannot fully comprehend something like this. As soon as the vision fades, you realise that you remember absolutely nothing. And still, some inscrutable warmth spreads throughout your body.{/n}

6e064906-1d43-404d-bc45-9435a00da9d9.Text: {n}You try to cut the beast's flesh again and again, but the blade cannot pierce its thick fur. You raise your knife for a desperate strike... but then a powerful shove brings you back to your senses. You find yourself standing at the edge of the bottomless pit, surrounded by your worried companions, one of whom, Ulfar, is shaking his head sombrely.{/n}

3cbcde44-1d4e-4734-b10d-7892cf6a1187.Text: {n}You raise the knife up high... when the youth suddenly bares his teeth and strikes you first, too quickly for you to react in time. The pain causes your consciousness to come rushing back. You find yourself standing at the edge of the bottomless pit, with a bleeding stab wound on your body, surrounded by your worried companions, one of whom, Marazhai, is staring at you ferociously, clutching a bloodied Drukhari dagger.{/n}

bea1aa77-94c9-4a11-927c-04a1a65e4b1f.Text: {n}You swing to strike, but one of the heads lunges out at an impossible angle and bites you... You regain consciousness at the edge of the precipice, surrounded by your concerned companions, your hand clamped in Glaito's jaws. Solomorne quickly commands the cyber-mastiff to loosen his grip, keeping his anxious eyes on you.{/n}

c42545c9-85bc-4cfb-bd31-ec50b3b02329.Text: {n}...you sit at the apex of a massive onyx pyramid. Your abilities are limitless — with a single thought, you can raise mountains, drain an ocean, or disperse the clouds. But nobody cares anymore. Soon your brothers and sisters will sacrifice you so that they can share your power among themselves and guide the civilisation to prosperity...{/n}

3bf07c7e-7676-41f3-aa0c-9a5eb59e629d.Text: {n}You can sense the darkness's triumph. It has been following your thoughts with great interest, rummaging in your memories, studying your emotions, savouring your resolve and rage — its bottomless gut rumbles with satisfaction. At last, grateful, it lets you go and presents a parting reward.{/n}

b688896b-ac58-45c1-83b1-49321497077c.Text: {n}You sense the darkness rampaging inside your mind, unable to fathom humanity. At some point, its desperation gives way to resolve — it needs new specimens for its studies. The darkness retreats, having lost all interest in you as an individual.{/n}

76cd4ec4-476a-44df-8ec4-065d26ba2198.Text: {n}Solemnly, you are placed on a cold black slab covered in glowing script, but at the last moment, your love for your people fails you. You thrash in the hands of your brethren as one of them, with an expression of incredible pain, rips your hearts out — one after another after another...{/n}

01411520-b5fb-4e99-b1ba-02efd8b6cff3.Text: {n}As your brothers and sisters surround you, you release your powers, but your attack is met with desperate resistance. When the last of your kind is finished, you feel completely drained and can only watch helplessly as the dark figures of your enemies draw closer and closer...{/n}

d3bf7498-1ff9-40b4-acf5-1ff52757ac20.Text: {n}...you make out toadlike xenos building a temple around the pit. They are praying, conducting rites, making sacrifices to the darkness in hopes of unimaginable gifts. Then darkness shrouds everything once more. Or rather, you are the darkness. Something immeasurably vast, endless, capable of reaching the farthest stars or swallowing a galaxy. But some will pulls you out of the cosy embrace of the void, toward the light... And you snap out of the vision as sorrow fills you from within.{/n}

600b6095-eb68-41fd-8d22-7b8847a066dd.Text: {n}The darkness swirls beneath your feet, a void of impenetrable gloom. You do not hear a single sound from the depths of the pit — no wailing wind, no rustle of dust.{/n}

e94e26bb-4dad-4867-baf1-892a7ed57d5f.Text: {n}You feel your way to the barely tangible edges of the entity's consciousness, separate it from yourself, and squeeze it until it is reduced to the size of a bead. The entity trembles, trying to break free of your mental grasp. Surprise, rage, elation, and fear replace one another. After a while, the entity stabilises, but the moment you loosen your grip, it escapes, leaving behind a piece of itself inside your mind.{/n}

5e54673b-3e31-471d-85d1-2c6ce765a885.Text: {n}You bite down on your belt and cut off a piece of your own flesh. The pain is so terrible that your vision darkens. Unable to bear it, you let out a frenzied groan, but you still shove the slimy scrap into your mouth and swallow it.{/n}

62da426c-282c-4b21-aa07-a20476c09c7b.Text: {n}You turn around to fight the monster — and you feel terror taking hold of your thoughts, turning you from a sentient being into a shaking, brainless creature that can do nothing but vanish inside the maw of the beast...{/n}

1af12f55-0d36-46f3-b967-8d813a650bbf.Text: {n}You raise the knife over your leg and sit like that for several minutes, unable to bring yourself to carve off a piece of your own flesh.{/n}

e7c79018-eade-45e9-baa6-623a65c9b3ff.Text: {n}You summon your courage and dash through the open door. Your will to live guides you through the deserted halls of the estate, and the Thing is right at your heels. At some point, you smash open a window and see your crew — unmoving fossils among withered plants...{/n}

9eacfe20-d270-46e1-a5cd-7ec3ee92869a.Text: {n}The darkness is greatly displeased with what it has witnessed — as if it has found your decisions disagreeable. You feel anger and vexation, and after that — unsatisfied hunger. Then the darkness crudely spits you out, severing your consciousnesses and leaving your mind with a thought about a harsh lesson...{/n}

b4f48533-4c27-43eb-b998-987882be28f5.Text: {n}Each step takes a tremendous effort, it feels as if you are being smothered from the inside, grinding your very being to dust to the point where your heart just might jump out of your chest. But you stubbornly continue walking until the alien thoughts release you, and the illusion immediately falls away.{/n}

995d64e9-cbed-4bcd-987e-54f2e25c6d79.Text:
"It has been several months since we arrived here, and yet we are no closer to understanding the local phenomenon. All that we were able to learn quite literally lies on the surface: the object does not reflect sound or light, on the contrary — it very much absorbs them. After extensive excavation, we did ascertain, at least, that the object is vast and goes deep below the planet's surface. However, any attempts to measure it resulted in loss of machinery or staff.
Archaeological studies have turned out to be more productive. Their findings have revealed an amalgamation of architectural styles of various cultures, including those of xenos origin. According to the boldest theories, the earliest of these structures date from the beginning of the thirtieth millennium, and all of them are, without a doubt, of a religious nature.
Analysis of bas-reliefs and remaining epigraphic texts shows that a cult was formed around the object. For many centuries, xenos and subsequently humans worshipped the object in exchange for certain 'boons' — undoubtedly imagined by primitive or corrupted minds..."

8d8a6c63-4c1b-441c-a96d-e0f3079c079f.Text: It is impossible to glimpse the meaning behind the twisted symbols, but a sense of unease still creeps deep into your soul.

bd60f67b-001e-4a57-b4ef-5bec897ea8e8.Text: The skulls are carefully stacked in the likeness of a mass grave. An Aquila on a thin chain glints faintly at the heart of the mound.

559436ba-f798-475a-83a6-3ae1615729e5.Text: The young man's withered face is frozen in a grimace of horror. The eyes and tongue were carved out with exceptional skill, along with the fleshiest bits of his body.

822137bb-1a40-452c-8f2c-76b72f6db60d.Text: "Wh-ere are you go-ing? I have not yet tast-ed your fle-sh... kh'arg maar!"

ac964b0b-c9bb-4d24-a520-f418c39f8fd8.Text: "My gut tells me something very bad happened here. This sinking feeling, I feel like I am staring death in the face."

ad0c8a0e-de7e-48bf-91ad-94e8b3cec17b.Text: "Blood, rot, and bones... This place deserves only purification by the sacred flame."

e9f68de1-2dae-43ac-9852-868bc6dbb871.Text: "Can... Can you feel it, too? There is a rotten brown flux coursing through the hall and these corridors. I can barely breathe. What a horrible place!"

542da4e0-68dd-42c4-973b-39b2aa88888d.Text: "It is so strange, Lord Captain. I feel like I am inside a bubble, seeing nothing, feeling nothing..."

5140c4d5-dbbf-4c34-b7ee-b74d59a72b87.Text: "How very peculiar, shereen. The palace is ruined, and still all of the valuables are sitting exactly where they should be. Either we are the first to discover this place, or... nobody wanted anything to do with it."

ae904726-3141-4e17-a852-190b8f789e8e.Text: "I smell blood... And the immortalised suffering of mon-keigh! Perhaps this is the reason."

f6f18845-451c-43a4-9724-45d2807e1294.Text: The desiccated manuscripts date back a dozen centuries. This palace is probably one of the oldest outposts of the Imperium.

21b7df08-2b0c-41d8-8e58-b6742e7e6a74.Text: There is a gruesome pattern to the mess of desiccated bodies and rotten limbs — all of the unfortunate victims died very young.

d91cfa40-13df-4705-b3f0-3aa0982d1bad.Text: The servitor mechanisms are old and obsolete, and the organic parts have been replaced with improperly sized counterparts.

bb3ca8f7-3ed1-4b74-8aa9-4c5a0c93e532.Text: The servitor's organic limbs were embalmed with an unfamiliar solution that has preserved the joints and kept them flexible.

3a05d9bc-e3e7-4b83-ab54-dfa500ece7ac.Text: The open areas on the body are riddled with deep, even cuts, as if someone had been savouring each piece of severed flesh.

9e70d65e-ce50-4b9c-8bc3-a8eedf7bdf3b.Text: "Did I hear that right? Did you just say immortality?"

26d3e337-9b7e-499b-8284-2efc545f1f7a.Text: {n}The ingenious creation of an unknown craftsman shimmers, hypnotising you with its faintly glowing patterns. The trinket is so captivating, you cannot take your eyes off it. When you try to shift it into your other hand, you notice that it can barely separate from your skin — there are thousands of fine flagella stretching between the surface and your palm. You tear the device off with effort and see countless tiny droplets of scarlet left behind.{/n}

7eed3040-b898-4d1a-867a-3bdf3f7e8065.Text: "A Halo device." {n}Heinrix reaches out sharply and pries the mysterious object from your hand.{/n} "A cursed xenos creation that twists the mind, and soon the body, of its master. An item subject to the Inquisition's general decree of total annihilation. In this matter, my authority exceeds your privilege, Lord Captain."

6dd4ca08-0a84-473b-be45-e1a4c61fcb68.Text: {n}Yrliet looks at the object in your hands and shakes her head with concern.{/n} "Get rid of it, elantach. This creation is the fruit of ancient and twisted minds that tempt the weak with the promise of eternal youth and life unending. You have seen the price it exacts with your own eyes."

b2ec26f5-783a-4a00-859e-7639dec9865d.Text: {n}Marazhai slightly narrows his eyes.{/n} "I have seen similar devices among the trophies of the Kabal. I do not know who created them, but it is hard to deny their devious ingenuity. In exchange for immortality, they turn their prey into something similar to what inhabited these chambers until recently."

d170aa8d-4448-43eb-a96d-93acbd0ecce8.Text: {n}Everything inside you screams in terror, and your body shakes in pain as you try to rip off the device. The area of skin touched by the brooch burns as if it has been grazed by a miniature melta charge, yet you manage to tear the xenos creation from your flesh.{/n}

5ed3a24a-c3de-4d75-86eb-8aa9e1df04cd.Text: {n}You swing wildly and hurl the mysterious device as hard as you can through one of the broken windows of the hall. Now only the God-Emperor knows where to look for it, and perhaps that is for the best.{/n}

cda2c268-0e72-43f8-a42e-23d3cb4abf84.Text: "That is enough, elantach!" {n}Yrliet swiftly knocks the device out of your hand. It tumbles away into the darkness until a distant thud announces that it has fallen into the wreckage.{/n} "I will not allow you to destroy yourself!"

f880f4c8-5a60-4dfe-b1c9-06cdcd9b1546.Text: {n}The Drukhari's movement is almost too swift to be registered by the eye. Marazhai slaps the device out of your hand with a perfunctory swing. The mysterious artefact flies off into the darkness and, judging by the clatter, falls through some crevice. The xenos turns his gaze to you.{/n} "No, {name}. No trinket will ever compete with me for your attention."

02e87427-e2c6-45eb-9e39-c54edfc40a65.Text: "If one could call it that. Would you like to become a bloated husk like the one we encountered? I doubt it."

d3d7e4aa-525c-4ea6-a7f5-38f880beb223.Text: {n}A shot, a torch, a sharp rock, you go through several ways to break the xeno-artefact, but your efforts are futile. Not a single scratch appears on the smooth surface. All the while you sense something strange — you hear ringing in your ears and the metallic taste of raw meat in your mouth.{/n}

5bde114f-84c1-4474-91fa-024e9808c9ec.Text: {n}The patterns on the device glow brighter the closer you bring it to yourself. The lack of fasteners and the vague visions in your head tell you that the brooch should be placed against your bare skin, not worn on your clothes. As soon as the artefact touches your body, the skin underneath it burns, your heart races, and your head feels like it is being squeezed by an adamantine garrotte.{/n}

a5b0366d-38f9-4fca-9534-891696363def.Text: {n}The artefact quickly embeds itself in your skin and bliss spreads through your veins. Small scratches heal, and your battle-weary limbs grow strong. You are full of energy, and the only thing bothering you is mild pangs of hunger spurred on by the smell of blood.{/n}

20012020-493a-44ab-b2f0-4ca8ea400cd2.Text: {n}Yrliet gives you a hard look{/n} "Immortality at a price far worse than death. Cast out the thoughts I am now reading on your face."

59ab158a-e462-49cb-8b23-172a2672991a.Text: {n}Everything inside you screams in terror, and your body shakes in pain as you try to rip off the device. Your mind yields, and you let the object do its work.{/n}

611522b7-ead3-42a0-8330-45af0d22e21f.Text: "A fascinating accessory. I am taking it."

5966e568-455f-45e3-8cef-fdd22f0d3b51.Text: "The Halo Device should not have gone to such a weakling. I will take it."

2da62ce4-cc6f-4158-a584-c8ad1f309352.Text: "I will put an end to your eternal life and destroy the artefact."

9fae074b-da9e-4e3b-b83f-21f8432e4d58.Text: {n}A lushly dressed, vaguely human-like carcass sits reclined in a massive Calixian oak armchair. Calloused brownish-blue patches cover the dead flesh, overlapping one another like snake scales. One of the hands, claws of exposed bone, supports a grotesquely bloated face.{/n}

fe7e5c32-143c-4d27-b981-def4f52f21e9.Text: {n}Heinrix raises a hand, commanding you to stop, and then presses an index finger to his lips. His face is more tense than usual, and there is a semblance of doubt in his eyes. The Interrogator gestures toward the exit.{/n}

8efebedd-5cfc-4f11-8759-a10199acd99e.Text: {n}The creature's chest remains motionless and its eyes stay tightly closed. And yet the muscles on the distorted face twitch ever so briskly when you approach.{/n}

726982b0-4ad7-40c7-9c72-ff8b0fd39f3b.Text: {n}The creature's chest remains motionless and its eyes stay tightly closed. It is hard to say whether it is dead, asleep, or merely lying in wait.{/n}

d18eb831-b808-4143-afb4-59e1c4bae3e3.Text: "Wel-come to my fe-ast..." {n}The creature idly jiggles its chins in an effort to remember human speech, its jowls melding into its shoulders and faintly glowing ribcage. A peculiar accessory shaped like a scarab and covered in luminous patterns has painfully lodged itself into the flesh of the creature, something that undoubtedly used to be a man.{/n}

c6fcfea7-28d1-4dd9-bb0e-9c9026c24378.Text: "W-what?.." {n}Cassia covers her mouth with both hands, trying to speak quietly even as her body is shaking. The Lady Navigator's wide open eyes are brimming with terror.{/n} "I... I want to leave this place... Right now!"

c4057aea-413a-4702-a4b4-a0b7013ab44f.Text: {n}Argenta draws her weapon, looks at you, and cocks a questioning eyebrow.{/n}

2bdaf08b-17bb-49ba-a59c-30b5c48c5539.Text: {n}As you take a step forward, the creature's eyelids flutter open, searing you with the unnatural glow of its yellow pupils. The disfigured lips twist, stretching the smile wider and wider... Until the thin skin bursts with a sharp snap, revealing row after row of pointed teeth.{/n} "K'ho mr'dash'ng ro fnagl hept!" {n}A twisted, guttural voice bursts from the creature's throat, and it roars with laughter.{/n}

c95b2093-6f62-4173-b9f5-d84c72a0c6b7.Text: {n}The creature's eyelids flutter open, searing you with the unnatural glow of its yellow pupils. The disfigured lips twist, stretching the smile wider and wider... Until the thin skin bursts with a sharp snap, revealing row after row of pointed teeth.{/n} "K'ho mr'dash'ng ro fnagl hept!" {n}A twisted, guttural voice bursts from the creature's throat, and it roars with laughter.{/n}

65ece103-8d72-45b4-a8e0-1e338477ba41.Text: {n}Meaty chunks fly across the hall, staining the antique furnishings with pungent blood, black and viscous like tar. A rotten stench mingled with the fetor of scorched flesh assaults your senses. An eyeball has rolled under a dining table and twitches slightly, glowing maliciously with an unnatural yellow light.{/n}

a4f9cf4f-954d-4dbc-9a11-6f5aa8154bea.Text: "K'ho mr'dash'ng ro fnagl hept! Ha-a..." {n}A twisted, guttural voice bursts from the throat of the creature behind you. It roars with laughter. The yellow pupils lure you in with an unnatural glow, the disfigured lips twisting, stretching the smile wider and wider... Until the thin skin bursts with a sharp snap, revealing row after row of pointed teeth.{/n}

ca60bf4e-99be-4aea-9585-131596044459.Text: {n}Sharp scales break away from the dense skin with every shot, and the creature's flesh is torn apart by countless projectiles that reduce its ugly carcass to a bloody pulp. The mutilated face, completely stripped of skin, and even bones, grins at you with the demented smile of a severed jaw. The sole remaining eye hangs from a bare nerve and glares angrily, shimmering with an unnatural yellow light.{/n}

7d006b9d-c743-44c0-9984-946be27edf9c.Text: "God-Emperor, hear your daughter's pleas! May you guide my hand such that this heresy no longer defiles the ground upon which your servants tread!"

38cc0253-1357-4df6-8464-e07c50a5718c.Text: {n}Sharp scales break away from the dense skin with every shot as the creature's flesh explodes, reducing its ugly carcass to a bloody pulp. The mutilated face, completely stripped of skin, and even bones, grins at you with the demented smile of a severed jaw.{/n}

0f7d58ed-6a89-48ef-b646-2300522d7e35.Text: "Kae-morag, elantach, do not get in the way!"

abd2b567-e09d-44ca-bdf2-d6d869636543.Text: {n}The creature's flesh starts swiftly regenerating before your very eyes. Within seconds the bones are once again fused together. The vessels, internal organs, and nervous system grow back. The spatter of blood flows back toward the carcass, being absorbed through the exposed tissue and rapidly recovering scale-marked skin. The same creature is standing before you a moment later, but this time its fiery yellow eyes are burning with anger.{/n} "Thma o'drft pa'ktch vngld meh'k!"

7db7b046-6f5f-49b6-b410-030f76bbb3f3.Text: {n}The projectile strikes right between the creature's glowing eyes, barely piercing the scale-covered forehead. The blood, black and viscous like tar, slowly runs down the malformed face.{/n}

dade525f-8f30-44e6-a3e3-c58691300823.Text: "Light of the Throne..." {n}Jae clutches the Aquila, looking at the creature's corpse with disgust.{/n} "I had to deal with mutants both in the sewers of Footfall and in the depths of the underhives. But this one... Did you see his eyes? They burn like embers in the empty eye sockets."

ac9d1944-a178-443f-a5c1-86f1cead63f8.Text: "Hungry." {n}Idira rubs her temples, shaking off sparks from her fingertips.{/n} "You have no idea how starved I am! And thirsty. A thirst that cannot be slaked... They want to eat. It wants to drink. We are hungry. EAT! DEVOUR! Eat! Eat! EAT!"

314adcf0-cd2e-4cd5-b46e-2673789a55f7.Text: "Do not think me a coward, Lord Captain, but I would prefer to leave this place as soon as we can. Who knows how many such creatures lurk in the palace depths."

1c42a986-687a-4f62-82f7-c8f0762b701f.Text: {n}You have heard of the powerful xeno-artefacts from the distant Halo stars, discovered by Humanity millennia ago. Artefacts that belonged to a race more ancient than the most venerable among the Aeldari. Artefacts most impure, fatally dangerous, forbidden in the Imperium on threat of the cruellest of tortures... And yet capable of granting the darkest of human desires — a means to cheat death and to embrace life eternal.{/n}

c0c6a19c-95fb-40c6-a1ae-1577b713f438.Text: {n}The accessory must have been a brooch at some point, but burrowed into the owner's flesh for some inscrutable reason.{/n}

41752896-21b0-4923-a0ac-4ccb007df49c.Text: "Khe mpra'ks vndrt'kd." {n}A long, snake-like tongue emerges from the creature's mouth and licks its own blood, savouring it like wine. The wound from the shot heals before your very eyes, as if it was never there.{/n}

2a442516-05f2-480d-a9be-9e6a1b5cdc18.Text: "I do no-t li-ke play-ing with my fo-od..." {n}The creature angrily shakes its chins in an effort to remember human speech, its jowls melding into its shoulders and faintly glowing ribcage. A peculiar accessory shaped like a scarab and covered in luminous vermilion glyphs has painfully lodged itself into the flesh of the creature, something that undoubtedly used to be a man.{/n}

b85644f7-5e70-4c29-b810-7dc0b88d16e1.Text: "Rogue Trader, stay back!" {n}Heinrix grabs his weapon, and the air around you shimmers with otherworldly frost.{/n} "The bearers of the Halo Devices pose a grave threat even to the finest agents of the Inquisition. They are fast, strong, immune to poisons, and..." {n}Heinrix stammers.{/n} "...immortal."

ad3cf1bd-80ac-4a39-a8d3-8a463568cd28.Text: "Halo Oculus... There are many legends among the Cold Traders about the ancient xeno-artefacts lost among the stars of the Koronus Expanse and the Calixis Sector. A little something that would make you more influential than the honourable Navis Nobilite and just as wealthy as the esteemed Rogue Traders. The price of immortality..." {n}Jae presses the Aquila to her lips.{/n} "Not even in my own heart does the flame of greed burn hotly enough to betray Humanity and stain my soul forever."

b5d7f3af-3f91-4748-8d57-79d80f89a70d.Text: "Bethink yourself, {name}! Every educated nobleman knows of the bloody consequences that befell the Rogue Traders Balastia Irem, Rath Longinus, and Edward Maissus in the fifth century of this millennium. Do not follow in their blood-stained footsteps!"

366a82f7-e168-4f86-90a3-9d1b88c453d2.Text: "It is not dead. It is dead, but in the wrong way. It's not—" {n}Kibellah bows her head as if ashamed of her muddled explanation, then places a hand on her weapon.{/n} "I ask your permission to fix... that."

7ee662ec-0e43-4c9f-8943-8f0bbb128caf.Text: "Need I remind you that Halo Devices are highly illegal? And that anyone, from a lowly smuggler to a mighty Rogue Trader, will be burned alive for their possession and use? Such is the fate of all who succumb to the vile temptation of xenoheresy."

b5a46313-0b56-4ec4-a3bd-c1feef0fed74.Text: "Brah'ts onk vfsteh'kh omss pk'nglf. E rh'st kho. Am je!" {n}The Elucidator fails to interpret the twisted speech taking root in your mind like a pestilent weed. The creature contentedly smacks its lips.{/n} "I will fi-nal-ly... tas-te the sa-vou-ry fle-sh... a-gain!"

16003a10-049a-422a-aeb5-69843dbded59.Text: "The penalty for blasphemy against the Machine God is inevitable annihilation. Initiate the abjuration protocols and commence sanctification through destruction."

b7458ad8-02be-4700-b4e4-0a93826eea38.Text: "If you ask my opinion, I would make sure to point out that bringing such rubbish onto a voidship is irresponsible. Leave it to rot on this Emperor-forsaken world."

3b49f359-beb3-4cd1-91c5-befb3ac9fad3.Text: "But you did consider it. You appraised the benefit and calculated the price." {n}Kibellah's lips twist into a cold smile.{/n} "And you found the limit of your lust for profit no sooner than hitting the lowest depths of heresy."

67fe606a-e0e0-4dd8-8bb9-dc42a4b773d9.Text:
An artefact of an ancient xenocivilisation that even the acolytes of the Ordo Xenos know little about.
Properties: recovery from irreversible injuries/ inhuman strength / immortality — ?? / unknown
Threat level: fatalis maxima
Recommendations: immediately consign the artefact to oblivion on a desolate world and report the coordinates to the Holy Inquisition

9ef75d97-71e4-4ec7-a903-bbece81f0578.Text: "I... cannot go on like this, Helona... I cannot! I served my master loyally, as did my father and his father before that. But this cannot continue! No. No... I am tired. To bury the corpses of murderers and traitors to the Imperium is the noble thing to do, but now I must conceal the deaths of these innocent young men and women. They are almost children! Cursed be the day when the governor became the ruler of this world. I... I will break this vicious circle. This I promise! Tonight, I will flee the estate and together we will journey to the Starspeakers. They will warn the servants of the God-Emperor about the heresy lurking in these walls. They will return for us. They will save us! Just wait for me, Helona. Just wait until I return..."

e70f7ca4-7760-4527-b75e-ab16c8376cbc.Text:
<align="center">"DECREE OF GUBERNATORIAL WILL</align>
By the Grace of the God-Emperor of Mankind
We, Jamon-Nigel von Powen,
for the Good of our World and the Deliverance of our People from the Wrath of the Heavens and the Fury of Distant Stars,
<align="center">HEREBY COMMAND</align>
to Provide for the Needs of the Governor's Office
<align="center">NO MORE AND NO FEWER THAN TWENTY</align>
Faithful Young Men and Maidens picked in Accordance with Our Instructions
each Seventh Rotation around the Heavenly Body:
- Robust and Firm in Body and Spirit
- Voluptuous in Shape, of similar Height and Stature
- Dainty and Beautiful
- Fair of Hair and with Eyes the Colour of Midday Sky
<align="center">SO SHALL IT BE"</align>

726585b5-6870-4924-878a-dd4fdec0cb34.Text: This human skeleton is curled up in an unnatural position. It is inside a void suit with a hole burned right through it.

fbac0b06-ed7a-46c5-90e4-76f81bd05cf6.Text: Unlike the other pedestals, this one is missing its crystal.

28d5120d-8f03-49e2-b5f7-e43415bca52c.Text: "Veherd didn't obey the masters, and the masters ate Veherd... I will obey!"

8199d2f2-e082-425d-b99e-664772f54753.Text: "These are not living people, but echoes of the past, brought to life by sorcerous powers. You should be more careful."

bdcc9bbb-c02f-45a0-b4c7-24d69f05886e.Text: "What... Was it me who carved this out? Why can't I remember anything..."

8a148fd2-fc0a-49c7-b410-ec4c0e60637a.Text: "I can hear so many voices... I feel like I could just reach out and touch whoever is talking!"

a15b8831-8031-4231-9ddd-a342406d4a49.Text: "I do not like any of this."

8885fa68-7b37-4e84-9d9a-3de69328682e.Text: "One thousand and one, one thousand and two... One thousand... One thousand... One, two, three, four..."

f25d30ea-fcc9-4d0c-a060-e1552b86e9fb.Text: "This poor man... Even through the centuries, I can still feel the despair that consumed him..."

90785939-5ad7-4ab1-b612-ba01742aeccb.Text: "My name is Beonna, and I am not food. My name is Beonna, and I am not food. My name is Beonna, and I... I am food for the true masters of space!"

f2d81e4b-f01e-405e-9e66-a9eacb30e800.Text: "Someone's had a thorough brainwashing. How about we make ourselves scarce before we start singing praises of these new masters?"

ebec722b-0f17-44a9-af14-d667f73d8f1b.Text: Some unknown force is making these crystals hover over the exquisite pedestals.

af6bf9d5-6f4d-4cd5-87ab-db8e55a670b7.Text: It appears that these crystals are tuned to warp emissions similar to psychic abilities.

b49f8757-699f-4c0c-b332-297f7d4cf2da.Text: Someone has carved a strange pattern on the floor. As you look at the lines, a fog descends over your mind.

8131ee9a-3cd5-4b38-b50f-979c456d2061.Text: A single look at this strange pattern is enough to send your mind reeling.

7f45eb16-39d2-4bf1-8b6f-dd735160a52c.Text: The remains of unknown structures are haphazardly strewn about the plateau.

1dbbc1b6-bbc2-4df2-af13-05d111dd94f4.Text: "Curse it! Back up, it's a warp breach!"

bd6dd327-1479-4e1b-b60c-096d8fef5417.Text: "This... awful feeling... The warp is twisting reality!"

14e67a4b-85a1-449d-a1d7-fbded6c8130a.Text: "The voices are whispering, hinting... WATCH OUT!"

10425002-22b8-4b48-9969-d1e56ab5a4ba.Text: "A daemon? Of course. As if we could get lucky twice."

f585d388-2d45-4685-9c07-1340151a496c.Text: "Warp spawn! We will destroy this abomination!"

23bf6178-4dc5-4c25-87d1-662e7d5e069b.Text: "The cracked chest has altered the expected result. Outcome: a daemon. Threat level: maximum."

a8f72822-2114-4158-8a27-3c0fae30b72d.Text: "Are you certain you know what you are doing?"

420050d6-8bac-40a6-af51-8ac942f73246.Text: "Ow! Perhaps we should stop turning these things?"

f85687ad-b185-468a-b958-b8a025529e33.Text: "I can feel reality getting thinner with each failed attempt..."

8bcdf0c4-45ae-47d5-8302-8e59ca66e8b6.Text: "Continuing to play around with this xenoheresy without thinking is unwise, Lord Captain!"

8467a373-b7f5-42da-b837-c20ff5d7f23d.Text: "Looks like something went wrong there, eh, {name}?"

6f3fe9ba-c941-431a-90ec-af4ab27a63c1.Text: It seems the pattern no longer works.

fd984940-198b-4ec2-b8cc-90779a2d3a48.Text: You do not find anything of interest among the rubble.

c5ae3db4-469e-4c24-bdb4-a0b65959a16d.Text: There is a cracked, dimly glowing xenochest under this heavy stone plate.

d77c7265-9939-403e-8f7a-2b371e2023d0.Text: The evidence of some unknown race among the man-made structures feels unnatural and frightening.

b196adf7-fe64-4724-9e0a-cdca1e4b9c29.Text: The beacon's psy-tech belongs to the ancient xenos called Khraves — monstrosities who enhanced their mental control over entire planets with the use of such devices.

d2425c9a-aabb-4b7d-8484-f90bc279f74b.Text: The ruins vaguely resemble the architecture of the Imperium, and yet there is some subtle difference to these structures.

8139dbdc-ab8a-4b24-b12f-b4aad3ab881c.Text: The small chest made from a strange material has no keyhole or any other openings. The murky crystal on the lid is cracked but continues to glow inscrutably.

30ab7468-9037-43ce-86ac-742bb40363c6.Text: A furious male voice is coming from the old vox: "This is Captain Trevor Durhath, calling the Bullion. Get your arses back to the surface and get me out of here, you shits! My guts may be fused to my suit, but I'm not dead yet, no matter how much you wish it were otherwise!" A moment later, the raging tone gives way to strangled rasping, "Hey! Can any of you hear me? Respond! I'll pay double, just don't leave me here... DAMN IT! It was going so well! We even figured out how to open the first sphere thanks to the pattern on the floor! Yeah... Yeah... Who knew there'd be so much trouble with the second one? I didn't. They didn't either... Cowards! The moment that beam was directed back — I was already lying with my guts turned inside out, and they were running off with my goods! Ohhh... Emperor, you whoreson, why'd You leave me like that! I'm scared... Oh yes, yes... No, I don't want to die. Not alone! Aren't You supposed to watch over all Your children? Quiet... Quiet, you lot, shut it already! I can't even hear myself!" The recording is silent for a few moments. All you can hear is the sound of someone pounding the shell of a void suit with the recording device. "I'm cold. I wonder if I'll die from lack of oxygen, or will my organs give out earlier? THE DAMNED GOD! THE DAMNED IMPERIUM! IN THE END, YOU WILL ALL SERVE THE TRUE MASTERS!" The human speech gradually deteriorates into an indecipherable mixture of howling and clicking sounds.

3712cd17-9e70-45f4-a4cf-b2bb35712bcf.Text: "Hey, where are the others? Ah, there's no time!"

b87a0a60-b469-4d40-bf82-ea609f7776e5.Text: "How far we have fallen — the Rogue Trader digging through rubbish. I can scarcely speak for grief!"

9d018883-9f44-4da1-8f63-aecb314445d6.Text: You can barely make out the writing on the plate: "Laethano's Pride". This is likely the name of the ship, but it does not ring any bells.

74c4e5b9-01a6-4f5c-a96c-1d8a091f1427.Text: The plate reads, "Laethano's Pride". The name Laethano surfaces in your mind, the history of a family from the Koronus Expanse who invested all they had in a family ship. The ship perished in the warp on its maiden voyage. The Laethano line never recovered from this crushing blow.

1df2141a-fcec-47b2-87d5-ac6d7cffc86c.Text: In this work of crude craftsmanship, you can just make out one of the depictions of the Emperor commonly seen in the Koronus Expanse.

fbc82884-ea54-4eb2-8c5c-81e02d620b9d.Text: The apparatus gurgles and emits a strong smell of alcohol. Probably not of the industrial variety.

a345ed0f-14e6-409c-96dd-2919fd8b9ce9.Text: "Welcome, Your {mf|Lordiness|Ladyness}! Please, please, come right in! Our chief, she'll greet ya!"

64adc9cc-18d1-48b5-8d0e-aa959fc1b580.Text: "And you, nitwits — quit yer gawking and get to work!"

60ba41fa-e812-4d9c-a753-1b7b7c2f091c.Text: "You should... talk to the woman in charge. It's not proper for the likes of us to talk to the likes of you..."

7fc0ee52-c894-4bb9-9886-192755186492.Text: "Wow... someone's actually come to visit... Seeing new faces is a right luxury in our situation..."

5b5b6526-dbef-4f1a-a525-39751cecfba5.Text: "Whoa, check out the visitors over 'ere, must be someone big!"

624d3799-49a7-4637-a28c-76a45fb6a0dd.Text: "Well, I'll be! They opened it! Must be nice to be learned, we never would've cracked it."

4c027474-71b7-4af9-84b3-dac1ec443677.Text: "{mf|Lordiness|Ladyness}, it's just rubbish! Now why wouldja wanna go through it, eh?"

cf4556ea-e072-44df-8fca-bb00071a2c0e.Text: A working area where fragments of the ship are dismantled in search of scraps of valuable metals or parts.

e67aaeca-9065-407c-a94a-7e0fad742506.Text: The simple machinery and tools look a little worn but well-maintained.

3f4efbf4-2308-4f59-a13c-946030f69e91.Text: A dump site of cut pieces of metal and other materials — probably from clearing out a path deeper into the ship.

d99eee5a-57cc-498a-80a1-d6890acfefcf.Text: Something is propped against the door from the inside. You can hear the piercing sounds of a saw and other tools coming from behind it.

2d445ca1-cc9b-4712-b43f-225951b75b71.Text: A small selection of valuable finds, carefully sorted and packed.

3d124193-5c64-446c-9d46-829a6e1f9443.Text: "This component doesn't belong to you. I will simply confiscate it."

d3b86bd3-54bb-4cdb-82c0-1ab340fe49b7.Text: "Think carefully now — are you sure you want to defy a Rogue Trader and all the power {mf|he|she} has at {mf|his|her} disposal? I need but give the order — and there won't be a single cinder left of your entire colony."

c7885e2a-cc3b-4898-9d22-d8dfcc01ed91.Text: [Attack] "You have the gall to oppose my will. I will not stand for it."

b9a7e258-22af-42d5-a189-386d8293fdc5.Text: "You take pride in your trade, I see."

8edf9b82-8380-451a-9152-9a7d5b452220.Text: "Nonsense. There are those who are great and those who are nothing — that is the nature of things."

163f42e1-535a-4cf7-8501-e93a79a25e1f.Text: "You speak as if the world is set in stone and none of us can change anything for the better."

e6eb6399-13c7-4ea2-a8c1-d56d21fa28ed.Text: "Can you tell me anything about this wreck?"

17a1b69b-70d3-42e6-adea-cd5aed6adbe7.Text: "Do not dare talk back to me. Another word about me thinking too highly of myself, and I'll leave you in no doubt about your place."

182cbd2c-beb0-4fbe-b83d-8802f0c91098.Text: "I can take you from this place. It's not safe here, and sooner or later, it will drift somewhere so remote that nobody will ever find you again."

4cfc331c-e9bc-4c53-8a9e-ab9f073406a9.Text: "Would you believe it — well-spoken rabble! It is rather sweet in its own way. Go on, then, amuse me. Tell me about yourself and this place."

5333705d-5d29-417a-ba12-c7119597e981.Text: "It's unlikely, but I want to ask — you haven't come across any Imperial stamps in your 'searching,' have you?"

75aefa12-dab0-48c5-a6c8-0b28fb6b42d8.Text: {n}A tired-looking woman of indeterminate age, clad in work clothes, breaks off from her task to greet you. She freezes momentarily, clearly unsure how to address you, then says simply,{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, please excuse me, I don't really know your name. Welcome to our little colony. May the light of the Emperor be with you — and with us. My name's Reta Machsimova, I'm in charge here."

b606d7fd-920f-4cc1-b9df-f580bf763387.Text: "Hope you don't judge me too harshly and don't take it as insolence, but some people — even big people like you — think too highly of themselves. Let's say your ship hops into the warp someday and doesn't hop out of it in time. And around a thousand years later, another gal like myself, who needs to feed her three ankle-biters somehow, will be rifling through its remains, looking for anything good. That's just the nature of things — each of us comes and goes, but the way the world works stays the same. We all have our lot in life, and mine is just as good as any other."

0cd5ef28-d916-4ac5-ad40-c37a25ccdc48.Text: "And about fifteen years ago, back before I had my first little one, a ship took three crews to locations and ran into pirates on the way back. The ships go out on expeditions for years at a time, so it was ages before anyone realised they were missing, and it was even longer before they remembered the scavengers, plus it took some time to find a ship that could check on them and pick them up. Long story short... all three crews had bought it. Yep."

d783a2de-395a-49fb-8105-c46139ced9b3.Text: "Well, isn't this something! The Emperor Himself must've smiled upon us!" {n}Reta makes a triumphant gesture.{/n} "I mean, uh, thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. You'll be pleased with the results."

43895f1e-1f35-4821-87db-501d442ece2f.Text: {n}Reta pales a little but lifts her chin with determination.{/n} "We risked our lives to find this thing and pull it out. This is our trade, it's what feeds our families. We can't just give it away, that wouldn't be right — or fair."

a7d4adbf-9aa4-408f-96ed-efccabdf0d66.Text: "We just call ourselves Reta's Crew and this place is Reta's Camp, that's it. We're recolligers. Scavengers, in common terms." {n}She does not speak the word "scavengers" with any kind of disdain — on the contrary, there is dignity in her voice, the kind with which one would announce their affiliation with a respected guild or family.{/n}

ba4d4359-9841-4c5c-b29b-7deb80e73ed0.Text: "If that'll be all, Y'{mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... you mind leaving us alone?"

a3ad7b73-0574-48c4-aadd-1cb52de085a3.Text: "This little bird's got all kinds of bells and whistles. Most of the tech is dead, but we do find working pieces now and again. We spent two whole months clearing out this shaft we found — finished just three days ago, actually — and we found this thing, a bit weird-looking but still functional." {n}Reta's expression brightens a little.{/n} "Perhaps Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} would like to buy this component from us? I'll bet that big ship you've got could get plenty of use out of it..."

e7ce0fca-6321-4f67-b16e-4783407bd676.Text: "Sure do. It takes skill, and luck, and a good head on your shoulders. We risk our lives every day, crawling on top of these old buckets. If something goes wrong — we die, by the scores sometimes. One moment we're there, the next we're gone, kind of like worker ants. But you know what, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? Our job also has something... how should I put it... poetic about it."

013e0fc2-96dd-4162-b475-ccba341db5c1.Text: "It's been a pleasure to serve Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

26cfbce8-dd92-4d5b-b11d-9de3910bea6b.Text: "Those are some big things you're talking about, way outta my depth. Change for the better? Heck, that'd be nice..." {n}Reta pauses to think.{/n} "If I was younger and didn't have three youngsters back home — maybe I would dream about stuff like that too. But as it is, I've got no time for dreaming — I've gotta work!"

df47d8a9-53eb-4720-9d53-10ece6bbea72.Text: "It's what my gramps taught me, he was a recolliger and a foreman too. He had some fancy-schmancy thoughts in that head of his, but he lived to a ripe old age with them — in our line of work — which means those thoughts weren't all bad."

0397234a-1e15-491f-88c1-17d924642256.Text: "If you say so, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I'm a simple woman, living a simple life, having simple thoughts, and if I happen to blurt out some bunkum — that's just because I'm not that bright." {n}Reta shrugs.{/n}

760a6259-57c1-4dc2-ad75-3fb983095311.Text: "Not much, we're no eggheads, you know — we're manual labour. It's an ancient thing, pretty dangerous, and we don't really know much beyond that. Before we came here, some Tech-Priests had done their own bit of gutting... I mean ritualling, bowing to the spirits, all that. That lot don't tend to leave a whole lot of valuables behind, it's true, but it's way too scary to go in before them. And hey, we dragged a dozen of their broken servitors out of the mines after. The carcasses smell awful, but you can pluck a decent number of parts out of a servitor and sell them."

bb34aa9e-d126-459d-82e2-35a53979ac9c.Text: "Doesn't seem like there's anything nasty living inside the wreck now, but the wreck itself is barely holding together. You go a couple of modules from here — and that's it, you won't take another step without fearing that a broken reactor might cook you alive, or a whole module might depressurise. Well, it's nothing we haven't handled before, so we're having a poke at it. But we don't have a clue what this ship is or who it belonged to."

f1b9100e-4638-4c65-b51d-366183643805.Text: {n}Reta frowns, but nods cautiously.{/n} "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

da4d98d4-3569-4d14-b71f-42ad353eb263.Text: "But this... this is our whole livelihood, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! You take us from here, and what are we gonna do — sit in some hold, slaving away? Here, we've got our own colony, our own operation. No, this is our path, and we won't stray from it."

dc3ea123-2bf4-4280-a0ae-eb5aefa70e3e.Text: "You are amusing, little mon-keigh. Your life is shorter than a moth's, and you spend it digging around in the carcass of dead, malevolent metal. But you speak of eternity and the stars. I like that. It is like seeing starlight reflected in a puddle."

9f358ccd-0260-48fc-b6e8-40c404f54b97.Text: "Disobeying those in power is apostasy. But depriving a poor person of the little they have is no good deed either. Forgive their insolence, {name}! Let them keep what they have managed to scrape together."

b94dc380-a03b-4010-b68d-990fc374ea13.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox crackles to life. Imperiously, he tells her,{/n} "Present the object, laywoman," {n}but curiosity creeps into his voice nonetheless.{/n}

943dc7a3-d51b-4a70-a043-fa30a09bfd66.Text: {n}Pasqal stares dispassionately at Reta with a hint of disgust. Evidently, he has not even considered the possibility that replying to this creature's words could be anything other than heresy.{/n}

72314135-2408-4e7e-849b-cad619167479.Text: {n}Tossing a glance at Pasqal, she grimly adds,{/n} "And our work is all legal, even though your brethren have no liking for us."

5e051bee-681c-4629-9e19-3ab0a422a24a.Text: {n}Reta shrugs.{/n} "We definitely haven't found any stamps here, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I keep a record of all the bits and bobs. Then again... Hang on, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I just remembered something..."

c9ba53bc-e30e-447e-b820-4d0aa89c89f8.Text: "Here you go, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Reta holds out a weighty seal. There are scratches on the handle where a coat of arms should be.{/n} "I don't know if this is what you're looking for, but we got this thing in a trade with some shady bloke years back. My father thought it was something important, so it's just been gathering dust until today. Take it as a gift — we have no use for it anyway."

5722b192-72a1-4190-b5c0-742b79b566ca.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}..." {n}Reta falters, as if flustered by her own nerve.{/n} "Please don't take it as insolence, but it's not like I have much choice... It's not often that we get well-stocked ships around here, and we could certainly use more provisions and some warm clothes. If it's something you would be willing to provide, we would gladly barter for it with whatever we can dig up inside this here ship. It's just a respectful offer of fair trade." {n}She bows slightly before stepping aside.{/n}

585e166c-da33-419c-8eb2-88e73ffd9899.Text: "Right now we're gutting this old heap of junk, slowly but surely. That's a recolliger's life for you — they drop us off at some decrepit station or an ancient battlefield, and we just sit there for years on end. We look for working tech, or valuable materials, or whatever else might be useful. If we find anything, we sell it to passing ships. Not the easiest job out there — these wrecks are chock-full of all kinds of dangers. But, and I swear it on my plasma torch, it's an exciting one for sure."

8685147e-1430-4a5c-9ee9-7a7f12d10946.Text: "No, not even close. A luxury like that? You could count the recolligers who got their own ship on one hand — an old worker's hand that got sucked into machinery three times and slashed by a plasma cutter twice."

28eb282e-fbc3-4755-9450-14dcc7d042bc.Text: "We fly with whoever, mostly just taking our chances. Sometimes we hitch a ride on the promise that we'll pay with what we find later, other times we find some other means... Risky business, obviously. Five or so years back, a crew got dropped off at an abandoned station, but something wasn't right with the life support systems. The ship came back to pick them up two years later, and found nothing but bodies."

c4a67646-6c6f-49b0-b7ec-7514516d1488.Text: {n}Reta clenches her fists, her eyes narrowing slightly. Her gaze darts over your gear and weapons, as if assessing the threat. When she finally speaks, you can tell she is forcing the words out.{/n} "In that case... take it."

d1b5fb23-5e88-4b5c-be20-a7557bcd5727.Text: {n}It is easy to tell by the gritted teeth and narrowed eyes what kind of battle is raging inside Reta — a battle between fear and pride. Pride wins.{/n} "No need to throw your weight around. We may be rabble, rummaging through old, rusted scrap from birth to death, but we value our labour."

08b31621-e664-42c1-8847-8d10890bcc06.Text: {n}Her mood visibly improves.{/n} "You know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, it's kind of embarrassing to offer you this, but over in that corner there, we keep things we don't rightly understand or can't really use. You could send some of your people to check it out if you'd like... clearly you know more about this stuff than us. You might find something useful."

64afb229-d23d-492b-83e9-d06ddbf250e8.Text: "A shame, that. But it's your call, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

a0f0cb3d-6a80-478e-8bdf-21946a71653e.Text: [Order somebody else to touch a leaf]

f128dce6-2904-406d-ab1b-53196af98355.Text: "Abelard, kindly pluck a leaf for me."

0bbb068f-e3c8-47eb-9243-ebc76a395421.Text: "Idira, the fate of this plant is literally in your hands."

4714cb85-3a40-42a2-a8b1-795c1193b622.Text: "Don't you love nature, Yrliet? Save the poor flower."

2aeb7e29-ae07-4d36-8e7f-b5baa537e920.Text: "Lady Cassia, since you have taken an interest in this plant..."

68f36df7-28f3-426a-b961-9247c16e6c08.Text: "Pasqal, can you help? Purely for research purposes."

f1beed38-fa35-435c-b4dd-278a345ce67a.Text: "Marazhai, you will be the one to carry it if you want it so badly."

6f3d607a-844f-4199-a5e3-60d8cdee8a1d.Text: [Step away and leave the plant alone]

98c9f797-85dd-4252-935c-e4de0c89dba1.Text: {n}A grey, unsightly vine winds through the surviving remnants of the cage, almost merging with the cold stone of the depot. Each tendril of the ragged plant is topped with a single leaf, shrivelled but still alive.{/n}
