b558311d-d2f1-4d6e-adf5-f0802f53044e.Text: {n}Her voice quivers slightly, but even her fear cannot stop her from using typical voidsman jargon,{/n} "That was some f-flight, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. If we'd been a little less lucky, we'd be checking in at the port in the sky right now."

a823cf6f-ff53-412e-affa-186364b53f2b.Text: The Lord Captain peered into the darkness enveloping the room.

3125ef5f-22e2-4abd-a67a-e4ef8e8be6bd.Text: The Rogue Trader surveyed the peculiar structure with great attention.

50e1941b-4f36-41be-8e94-3e26c3e50661.Text: The Rogue Trader took a closer look at the gathering.

a0ad877e-c8d1-473e-a4cc-1395c04d8e40.Text: The Lord Captain ran a cursory glance over the room, assessing the situation.

fe6dc99c-e0e5-4a36-a0ae-4a72ed59486c.Text: The Lord Captain patiently observed what happened next...

d76464e5-3972-42ca-8959-70bc692cd5ec.Text: ...shot the warp lens, destroying its charms.

71c527be-bb89-43c5-87b6-7de1606e15a6.Text: ...blew up the fuel barrels, thinning the heretics' ranks.

e4699b62-24d5-4110-a83d-1839d67ef93b.Text: ...charged bravely into battle to crush the enemy!

c120122a-0852-4e34-bae6-446ac8312e10.Text: ...could only rush blindly into the fray as if trying to escape unseen pursuers.

abb44ab7-1c15-485b-8a7d-f32c4f8af82e.Text: The Lord Captain recognised the structure: the Archenemy-corrupted warden on Rykadi Philia used similar ones to cast sorcery.

41050105-e7a4-4152-a22e-27d00be4ea9e.Text: Bulky power transformers, cogitators, crates, and vox-casters took up most of the space. Against their background, the structure in the centre stood out oddly: an enormous lens mounted on a stand. It caught the thin sunbeams that made their way through slits in the ceiling and crossed the half-lit room.

33941353-312e-4693-801d-75a777d9299b.Text:
Sector: {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}
Region: Rykad System
Location: Streets in the vicinity of the Rykad Minoris starport
Material: Report based on oral accounts and pict-recordings. Added to the archives of House von Valancius by the order of Seneschal Werserian.

fc4b1a98-d180-409f-9f9b-fb2816198baf.Text: On h{mf|is|er} journey across a world caught in the throes of a heretical insurgency, the Lord Captain accidentally witnessed an unholy rite that transpired in one of the maintenance rooms of an aqueduct. This abandoned nook turned out to be a heretics' gathering place for performing their grim and profane acts. The large group of rebels stood frozen in patient anticipation, all staring into the centre of the room. No one moved. Only the murmur of hushed voices echoed against the metal walls.

8344ad83-c417-4c56-b699-59ee2819d85c.Text: Although barely visible behind the closed ranks of the insurgents, the rusted barrels with evidently flammable contents, had not escaped the Lord Captain's keen eye. One good shot at those barrels would decimate the number of heretics on Rykad Minoris.

6b422e49-8997-4a9d-8ab2-800e7f771131.Text: A sound of bare feet broke the sinister silence as a man emerged from the deep shadows. Reeling, he entered the circle and collapsed on his knees in front of the enormous lens. Not a second had passed before many rebel hands gripped the fallen man's shoulders and hair.

2b0a4c6d-0d62-4cb7-b503-861eccc22def.Text: "Remember, comrade! The last sunray you behold will be yours only, shared with no one else — your holy Final Dawn!" bellowed a lone heretic's voice amid the silent crowd. By the doing of someone's hands, the lens had turned, and its focused ray feasted on the prisoner's eyes!

19ae9722-f46e-4ae3-82dc-0427ee493b78.Text: The blinded man's harrowing scream shook the very walls of the place. Consumed by the rite, the rebels had not yet noticed the stranger in their midst. The Lord Captain braced h{mf|im|er}self and...

55d2efa3-d43d-4418-aaaf-283f2a3a903c.Text: The rebels were unremarkable in appearance: they were dressed in the shabby clothes of abject rabble, spoke in coarse voices, and had repulsive faces. But what caught the Lord Captain's attention was the look of strange, almost sinister anticipation in their eyes. This was no gathering of loud blasphemers or bored idlers. Only occasionally would they exchange brief, unintelligible remarks. As they stood in a frozen circle, their gazes turned toward the hulking structure in the centre of the room.

dc91342d-9ed4-47a7-97df-d3b63ebf2a37.Text: The enormous mounted lens was doubtlessly imbued with the power of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}, inimical to all that is noble and virtuous in the universe. Anyone caught in the corrupted light it emits will face horrifying consequences.

c83845cf-469b-4e23-977f-89abd7d49318.Text: The abominable outline of a device so antithetical to the light of the God-Emperor dispelled all doubt that the intended use of the lens would be thoroughly repugnant and offensive to the soul of a true servant of His.

f439d09a-35c1-4567-88fd-e7fa0ca5c289.Text: ...suddenly faltered, as if something had stopped {mf|him|her}. Dark shadows danced in the Lord Captain's glazed eyes — {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}ghosts of the past{/d} that had risen at the sight of the warp atrocity and shackled the Rogue Trader's will. Breathing heavily, the Lord Captain...

7ed0a575-78a9-4101-87cc-a07bdac76d9f.Text: Alas, it was all but impossible to glean anything of note, let alone of use, through the huddled shapes of the heretics.

d0f9f108-0e29-4425-a61c-d07100fc5531.Text: As if commanded by a grim unseen force, the insurgents fell silent at once and, in a single movement, parted. A thick, sticky silence filled the room. The heretics' gazes were turned toward a metal structure with a lens on top of it, standing tall in the middle of a circle of melting candles, piles of books, and unholy symbols drawn on the floor. The structure flashed as a single sunray illuminated it.

29d7351e-6acf-4d93-b4c7-2c0ea8c81607.Text: [Flash a derisive smile] "Oh, you miserable, pathetic, lower order scum... Rebelling against your masters, are you? Care to show me your rebellious spirit now instead of taking sneaky shots from a safe distance? Do you have the guts to do it? Well? Do you?"

03d7f1a4-0b09-4bda-bd4d-b3cebcc0172d.Text: "An insurgency against your lawful governor amounts to heresy. I command you to lay down your arms at once!"

cc432fc5-d9f7-460f-801c-cef8de230249.Text: "The Chief sent me to take over from you."

a3f74730-d0bd-46cc-8797-5715b1553fa9.Text: "Speak. What caused the insurgency? Who is the Chief? And what were you doing with that anti-aircraft battery?"

1fb43e3a-bcd2-45d9-99bd-128ef7a35e50.Text: [Let the insurgents go] "I give you the gift of life. You are free to go."

53dd62c8-83ba-482d-91d3-a338ab5e7048.Text: [Execute the insurgents] "Your crime is punishable by death."

3364af72-85c8-4395-857a-2b4f09a79134.Text: [Remember the basics of handling sacred mechanisms of war] "I believe I know of a way to rid us of this menace..."

d7b67558-c62e-49ef-8f51-7a968f528e41.Text: [Look intently at both women] "With your own hands, you are branding yourselves with the mark of disgrace. Do you know what that is? If you do not, I can tell you. I know."

2c1071d5-738d-4c70-9a6f-f84b5daf58ab.Text: "I am new. I was sent here to take over from you."

46a3b021-8c8a-4856-9cea-255388d58f8f.Text: "I, Rogue Trader von Valancius, am ordering you to surrender at once!"

23aeaffa-4943-42ae-898f-b7f8ff1a6be1.Text: {n}The two women are arguing furiously, oblivious to everything around them. An impressively huge anti-aircraft battery towers over them.{/n}

3cd8849a-1e83-443e-89fa-0f6fcc5eb65c.Text: "I can't do this anymore! I pushed the exact same lever I did yesterday, I swear! But instead of turning the barrel, it splashed us with hot oil! What genius thought that experience operating a paper press would translate into handling ancient weaponry? This thing is going to kill us {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Raycad_Early}before long{/d}, I just know it!" {n}The exhausted red-headed woman is on the verge of tears as she rubs the fresh burn on her cheek.{/n}

67dda732-f7cb-472c-9660-e20475b55b84.Text:
{n}Her portly workmate waves her hand dismissively.{/n} "What's with the cold feet? Afraid the Chief's gonna punish us? I dunno, I like the gun way better than the paper press! We've turned the tables on the nobles at last — now they're afraid of us!"
{n}She turns toward you sharply and whips out her weapon.{/n} "Now who are you?"

cba582f2-fe51-4d78-8de4-a48bacfb3f59.Text: {n}A powerful explosion destroys the ancient anti-aircraft battery, showering you with shards. This gun will not harm anyone ever again.{/n}

3dc450a9-49d9-4dba-9323-916e4c58c057.Text: "Curse you, noble bloodsuckers! The Final Dawn will get you!"

0ca27e6a-4326-4910-ae93-a2d0c8c9f8ed.Text: "Hmmm... The Chief, you say? Take over from us, you say?" {n}The portly woman hesitates.{/n}

dc29dd1c-25d4-47e9-b558-03d4c1338591.Text: {n}The red-haired woman grabs her partner's arm.{/n} "Of course the Chief sent them! Of course they'll take over from us! They're our lot, no question about it!"

92d1a1ee-c5e2-4776-b527-3d8e13abcca4.Text: {n}Her mouth stretches in a strained smile.{/n} "We'll get going then. We had three people in our crew get scalded with boiling oil when we first calibrated this thing. Anyway, good luck. Try not to die!"

fe20c8e1-518d-4ea2-bc30-e7b7ae70dd7b.Text: {n}The anti-aircraft battery certainly was constructed a long time ago — long before the colonisation of this world began. It comes as no surprise that the insurgents were barely able to operate it. Modern arms protocols are incomprehensible to the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} of such an ancient construction.{/n}

320e005d-cd83-4ebd-b45e-d0ebdf24b9ad.Text: {n}The women exchange nervous glances. Finally, the red-haired woman gives up, throws down her weapon, and puts her hands up.{/n} "We surrender! We surrender! Just don't kill us!"

d99c2c97-e105-47d4-a9c5-e01fcd3df022.Text: "Take over? Ha, we don't work shifts here. It's just us and we're in charge! Get 'em, lads! For Aurora and the Final Dawn!"

2817ab6d-1d90-4db0-be74-4e64ae01a3e9.Text: "Well, sorry to disappoint! Get 'em, lads! For Aurora and the Final Dawn!"

30358efb-9d63-47fa-8dff-dd79df98e05c.Text: {n}The anti-aircraft battery's control panel has a panoply of mysterious levers and buttons. Deactivating it quickly is not an option. All you can do is blow it up, destroying it completely.{/n}

8f75cbc5-bab2-4de3-8df0-c4958a7b9e16.Text: {n}The blast consumes the ancient weapon. The sky above the city is safe for flying again.{/n}

3bce1e13-00ab-49f6-ab17-fa57c719f0ae.Text: {n}It is a formidable and lethal weapon, the likes of which you have never seen before.{/n}

00fac459-6869-4f08-a065-85f72c41f6c9.Text: {n}Abelard casts a reproachful look at you but says nothing, merely shaking his head.{/n}

0395d2b6-185d-4191-ad18-68cdc5594565.Text: {n}It does not take knowledge of the ins and outs of ancient technology to do what you intend to do — your experience from your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Militarum}time in the Astra Militarum{/d} is sure to suffice. A simple manipulation of the breech block is enough to jam the shell inside the tube and cause a fire in the chamber...{/n}

6986480f-0260-4b55-9123-7769717f207b.Text: {n}The kilotons of venom and {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}hubris{/d} in your voice have a miraculous effect on the rabble: the two trembling women instantly fall to their knees.{/n} "F-forgive us, my {mf|lord|lady}! Have mercy!"

0d539174-7c56-4848-886d-78196ba233c0.Text: {n}Something in your voice — genuine {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}sincerity{/d}, or notes of shame — causes both women to lower their gazes. One after another, they drop to their knees.{/n} "M-m-mercy! They bamboozled us... frightened us..."

7d4fdb35-c9dd-44b9-ba76-5db2caf09b28.Text: {n}The woman merely sneers in response and gets a more comfortable grip on her weapon.{/n} "Boy, did you just mess with the wrong crowd. We've got intruders! Come at them!"

f9a48f6a-4885-45c8-a294-6fb76f22af67.Text: {n}The red-haired woman breathes a sigh of intense relief.{/n} "Thank you! Thank you so, so, so much!"

5a4a63ed-9081-4624-9faa-8ae3f07c896f.Text: "That's enough whining, lads. We won't be getting any more visitors. We've {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Raycad_Late}lopped the heads{/d} off all of them! And as for that coward, I gave her a taste of my true sight — where's she gonna go?" {n}The portly woman gestures toward the redhead. Her eclectic gear has clearly been scavenged from her less lucky friends as well as foes.{/n}

953f797c-16ff-428c-a55b-8e6551c390ef.Text: "Well, we... er... our entire crew joined the rebels and we tagged along. The Chief, well — he's the Chief. He's in charge because he used to work under the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Red Robes{/g} and man their heavy machinery. He's not here. He only comes over to check up on us every now and then! He wrote us a manual for operating this big boy, but it only does what it's supposed to do half the time! The previous shift got all maimed. We haven't been here long and we're already head to toe in burns. Let us go, will you? We won't be insurging again!"

7fbb92a1-3ab3-427a-92f8-8a0d7fd40ab8.Text: {n}An ancient anti-aircraft battery of impressive proportions casts a dark shadow on the ground. Kneeling in the shadow is a red-haired woman with gaping black holes where her eyes once were. She is feverishly scrambling for something on the ground around her, dully repeating, "Light... light... light..."{/n}

52d0c1d1-4809-4aa1-8d72-ec641e375217.Text: "Die, scum! For Aurora and the Final Dawn!"

35d6286d-4b58-464f-80b3-02ffabe154d8.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} cannot hide his amazement as he listens to the confessions of this paper press operator, who has been unceremoniously thrust into the ranks of the gunners and is now in charge of aiming this formidable anti-aircraft battery. His visor's lens gradually turns scarlet.{/n}

1fc31d98-f356-4430-8be4-e238d349b7b7.Text: "We may be rebels, but you — you're all blind! But don't worry... you'll be made to see! For Aurora and the Final Dawn!"

edf00d43-4ca0-4e70-ba1f-13cc64dba517.Text: "You believed the heretic lies. You sold your soul to the Archenemy. But if you renounce this path, you will still have a chance to be truly saved."

e211db7a-293a-4ad9-ba15-b4b641817b98.Text: "Think about it. What good has the Final Dawn done for anyone at all? Some have died. Some have had their eyes burnt out. Some have gone insane."

eddf2530-dbbf-489b-aa6e-72746509504c.Text: Executed the rebel Aryld who blinded people with a heretical lens.

068f6fe8-087c-4782-924d-6476700fcf9d.Text: [Kill the old man] "Your family will be taken care of. As for you, I condemn you to death."

7f635d23-bcc6-4cb3-a060-390cceba027c.Text: "What are you trying to 'save' them from, and who is behind all of this?"

540a903b-64e0-44d2-a68b-61c6b5bb8ad1.Text: "No, you tell me: who are you and what are you doing to these unfortunates?"

07f65c9b-fde5-4b63-9afc-67aa5c876538.Text: "You have been torturing your own family in order to 'save' them? You have been blinding them so that they could see the truth?"

ab086db8-3b97-49bd-a209-a574c2c35e7e.Text: "I, Rogue Trader von Valancius, order you to release the hostages at once!"

53970928-5fa3-47c5-a5c8-c0eb4cccd985.Text: Convinced the rebels led by Aryld to lay down their arms and stop blinding people.

cb1c4702-7ec6-4060-a7f2-76e7a2e23f09.Text: "What you are doing is no salvation. Stop taking your fear out on the innocent. It will neither ease your suffering nor rid you of fear."

cf84be91-e7a1-43f5-923f-2510f09f30de.Text: "Aurora, whoever that is, has exploited your naivety. Can't you see you are causing nothing but suffering?"

8f936986-49e1-43e8-a8f9-a30823b2c070.Text: "Arguing with you is pointless. Prepare to die!"

f552f2d0-9e5c-4ed8-acc0-db4e24e8dc06.Text: "Look what fear has done to you! I see my past self in you — broken, humiliated, cloaked in disgrace! Is that how you wish to be remembered by the Emperor's servants?"

4f4fc4c8-009b-48f6-8af3-b267e8c0c7a7.Text: Spared the rebel Aryld who blinded people with a heretical lens.

0c33cde8-b819-40f9-88eb-a6b6d3997b10.Text: "Your family may go. And so may you — but make sure I do not ever see you again."

67617b6e-222b-4e6b-9711-d5d1c71068c1.Text: {n}Some ten people, children among them, are huddling together in fear. The elder family members are doing what they can to calm the young. Several armed insurgents are watching the frightened yet {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Raycad_Early}unharmed{/d} hostages, but the watchers themselves are looking around nervously.{/n}

55b100d6-9321-449b-bf04-212c58657597.Text: {n}Some ten people, children among them, are huddling together in fear. You see that half of them have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Raycad_Late}black holes where their eyes used to be{/d}. Some maintain a gloomy silence. Others are wailing. Several armed insurgents are carefully watching over the terrified hostages, snapping every now and then at someone for shaking too much or crying too loudly.{/n}

388fc8b9-1a1e-4292-948c-c39ad143d9ac.Text: "Come to your senses, Aryld! Look what you're doing to your own family!" {n}A woman of about sixty, grey-haired but still strong, is kneeling before a stocky man with a thick pure-white beard, stretching her arms toward him.{/n} "Take pity on us! Let us go!"

b790fd6b-6825-457a-b12b-8a62a57b656a.Text: "Can't you see I'm trying to save you?" {n}The man clutches his weapon tightly.{/n} "Only Aurora can help us! Why can't you understand that?" {n}Upon seeing you, the man points his weapon at you. The other insurgents do the same.{/n} "Who are you and what do you want?"

2e00c5d9-b38b-4638-83ec-48e60b53dedb.Text: "Stop talking and embrace redemption! Our children have gained true sight, while you still believe the lie!" {n}Upon seeing you, the man points his weapon at you. The other insurgents do the same.{/n} "Who are you and why are you here?"

1a5e99ac-f0f0-481c-a8d7-284c1f7f9194.Text: {n}The old man gestures to the other insurgents, who lower their weapons. Then he shifts his gaze to you, trying to hold back tears.{/n} "What happens to us now?"

ab722dd7-7008-4e25-957f-6f5b55a9676e.Text: {n}The old man's body falls to the ground. As soon as the hostages see it, they start moving faster and soon disappear around the bend.{/n}

b0d25f77-9a67-4f0e-b08d-2f4ec10e4872.Text: "I'm the Chief. My former name, Aryld, is meaningless now. I am a father leading his family to deliverance from woes — to salvation! Aurora has opened my eyes to the truth — and my children will see it!"

9561b19f-fb97-4646-a30f-4206292c2de5.Text: {n}The old man sighs heavily.{/n} "I don't need your mercy. Protect my family — and as for my own fate, I place it in your hands!"

cf28a6ad-66a0-4eaf-bb46-17e2bf9b4543.Text: "Aurora is no enemy of mine! No one will take the light of truth away from me!"

10700b8e-af8e-4519-810e-71033c155c42.Text: "No! They will be saved and you can't stop it! Attack!"

f642e488-500c-46d5-81aa-a3a245108925.Text: {n}The old woman rises from her knees and approaches her husband.{/n} "I know you were trying to save us. But {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Raycad_Early}there's still a way to set things right{/d}."

bbbe8cdb-f642-4761-96d3-fed2fc5ff0da.Text: "There's {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Raycad_Late}no washing{/d} the blood from your hands. But you could at least let us go, Aryld! The ones you haven't mutilated yet."

8c0e18dd-280e-4e12-a08a-b28db8f167cd.Text: "All of my adopted and blood children are here. I raised them all as my own. And now I must protect them. Help them see."

5010bad5-35ba-4bf0-9349-0a520bd1d218.Text: "At Aurora's behest! Aurora is a great prophet and a great warrior. Their face is shrouded, but their gaze pierces the veil of time and sees into the future! I always knew the governor's dogs were hiding the truth from us, and now, the day has come: a prophet has come to Rykad Minoris and opened our eyes! The end of the world is coming — the Final Dawn. And only those who accept Aurora's truth will survive it!"

e891574b-5ec7-471d-b850-fc424e873ced.Text: "I remember when the Vizsier used to sew our eyes shut so that His young spinners would see the truth." {n}Kibellah's voice sounds hollow, but there are glowing embers of fury in her eyes.{/n} "Our ritual was one of service to Him. It tempered and prepared us for our duty. What you are working here is despicable heresy, a blasphemous mockery of our sacred disciplines."

d5031e4e-172a-47ac-89f8-2c115f8376db.Text: {n}The hostages begin to leave and soon the group disappears around one of the bends. The old man looks away from them and walks in the opposite direction. His shoulders shake with sobs every now and then.{/n}

573612c7-ed4d-4019-86fa-af0ceb2d8baa.Text: "Those who lack faith cannot grasp the truth and will not be saved!" {n}The old man is obstinate, but you sense that the confidence in his voice has diminished.{/n}

eb7d7f53-2767-424d-a2ef-bd44d1bf7680.Text: "You will not lead me astray from the true path! I will save you, my children!"

33b21f16-c308-43cc-8f8d-76e8badf0cae.Text: "His mind and soul are pierced by shards of a colourful deception. Hues once twisted by despair and the Immaterium's influence can never be the same again."

82de3c37-d6f4-40b3-a472-22a84a5a28b2.Text: "But... all I wanted was to save... I..." {n}The man drops his weapon and covers his face with his hands in desperation. You hear several short sobs.{/n}

de4e8c28-2918-4a2a-9483-d085fc1bbf81.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox hisses furiously,{/n} "Layperson, cognition is not your primary function. You are saving your kin by holding them at gunpoint and believe that burning their eyes will grant them sight. It is evident that the author of the demagogic teaching that confused you meant to make a mockery of your deplorable intellect."

d1d6c36a-b4ed-489f-bb62-d25693863147.Text: "But... they said the end was near! They promised salvation! I wanted nothing else!" {n}The man's weapon falls from his hands to the ground. He clutches his head.{/n}

7d45166c-1fb5-4921-af9d-51bb51279386.Text: {n}Abelard's face turns a deep red.{/n} "To cast your own children into the thrall of heresy... To drown your progeny in this filth with your own hands!"

02b90bdb-dd41-4f9c-acda-dec00af2f02a.Text:
"It's coming! It's coming!
It's drawing ever nearer!
Heed the word of Aurora! Abandon all your mundane affairs. Ambition is but dust. Desire is but rust upon the metal of the soul.
The Final Dawn is coming! It will put an end to all worldly vanities!"

65e75009-3092-4373-ae43-067ca6a0844d.Text: The jumbled symbols on the paper look like a code or password.

cbcccca7-0464-40c8-8e61-5d9a9a10773f.Text: "A Harbinger reports: Brother Twilight and his people were unsuccessful. A dangerous enemy, {name} von Valancius, foiled his plans. The duty is now upon us, Aurora's followers, to succeed where Twilight failed."

3de1c34b-ab27-4b68-827e-28ee6c0817ca.Text: Message from the Cache on Rykad Minoris

b42270d5-09b5-4827-aa6b-8e4dbc0222ec.Text: [Turn to the soldier] "Camille. Do you recognise this vox-caster?"

a05b0b55-da3f-45bc-96a3-dcaa92963701.Text: "The investigation will establish if it was so. For now, you still stand accused."

4117c226-994f-4aa0-b8ac-18302b871b7b.Text: "So we have taken back the caster and now we are going to return it to the governor. You will not be spied on anymore."

f1bb78f0-cef9-405b-8058-3ca51dafcdd3.Text: [Enter the code from the found note]

176f4e03-a672-4eaa-9d42-c728947b0e88.Text: "Now I see you were not responsible for the ambushes."

5923a765-5e24-4440-b6d2-52762b2ba2a3.Text: "Those who allowed this vox-caster to end up in the wrong hands are guilty of criminal negligence."

674e07f9-1e05-47e8-800a-bf0abe4b4c23.Text: {n}The cogitator screen glows with a soft green light.{/n}

115d4882-1a40-4a62-9abc-62a404b1d1b8.Text: {n}New missive: "Aurora's Harbingers wish you to know, comrades, that the von Valancius ship is heading for the Navigators' station. You've got {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Raycad_Late}time{/d} to prepare a warm welcome for the enemy."{/n}

c8ae2ee2-513c-48f7-959d-e1cad8fa2b3c.Text: {n}New missive: "Von Valancius's ship has set off for Rykadi Philia. We pray that our comrades there manage to vanquish Aurora's enemy on their own. But you must anticipate the worst and do everything to make sure von Valancius's path definitively {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Raycad_Late}ends{/d} on Rykad Minoris."{/n}

f857485a-d214-4ecf-af82-a41a72f7077e.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} look favourably upon you. You overcome the cogitator's defences.{/n}

a5830d0b-049b-4f7c-831d-e10f139d8ec6.Text: {n}This time, the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} are apathetic toward your cause. You fail to overcome the cogitator's defences.{/n}

25095e14-0a53-44f7-87e7-f674632fae93.Text: "If you say so, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. But I'd imagine those folks are goners already. You can't exactly call them to account now."

eed212e8-963e-4f3e-83a3-6c33ff05c1b2.Text: "Yes... looks like one of ours — all our squads use them... So, does this mean those bastards could have been eavesdropping on us all this time? That was why my squad got ambushed!"

a8ad7f41-970a-49e3-aab8-1b556e1e1e91.Text: {n}A message archive loads up. Judging by the accompanying notes, the messages were meticulously transferred from paper to the sacred machine storage.{/n}

3cabfbad-b45e-41b1-9e72-4c63dd60df63.Text: "Good. That means at least my comrades didn't die for nothing... There won't be any more ambushes thanks to them — and you!"

b17dc0f6-f121-4a41-a7f9-4fff2b0ce45c.Text: "Looks like? Are you blind, layperson? Every vox-caster is unique! The distinct defects on the cover, the number signature on the antenna, the scintillating spectrum of the vid-screen! How can you possibly mistake one for another?" {n}Rasping indignantly, the Tech-Priest pokes a finger at the vox-caster, which looks completely indistinguishable from any other vox-caster you have ever seen.{/n}

2b1d51e6-cda1-4dbf-bf0e-e2001dd5d7af.Text:
{n}"Tell the Harbingers we've intercepted a convoy of the governor's underlings who were supposed to meet that von Valancius {mf|bloke|lass}. Only one out of the whole convoy got away, but he's not long for this world. No one's making it to the governor's hole — not that youngster or the ones he's supposed to meet. Our comrades have got their hands on a guard's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-caster{/g}, and these fools have no clue we can hear all their comms! We know their every movement and we're going to throw them a fine welcome party. Aurora must have no doubts that we'll do whatever it takes to stop her enemies.
Let the Final Dawn come!"{/n}

bc459316-d50c-4e17-8de6-0bd89d68ec3a.Text: "Like I'd expect anything different... Accusations is all you nobles ever do..."

dc28cff3-f4ea-4840-821d-f986c515037a.Text: "Phew... thank you, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! I'm telling you — I would never — I'm no rat!"

c1ac5bfc-91b3-403d-8964-946f4996bdd3.Text: "Enough talking. Let's go to the command centre."

730f5797-7f23-4672-b756-be9b1d76c2d7.Text: "What is it, soldier? Why are you so nervous?"

d9f75a08-149c-4808-aab9-63f05502f880.Text: "Your uniform looks odd on you, soldier. As if it belongs to someone else."

86289dc2-34a9-4230-a44f-5912118c51a6.Text: "Has the governor tried negotiating with the insurgents? Offering them aid? Tax relief?"

58608e10-e997-4d5a-9386-f38a09eb6217.Text: "How did you make it out alive if your entire convoy perished?"

45cebcca-a0a4-459d-8c74-30030be2e293.Text: "What can you tell me about the insurgency?"

784c55c7-d86c-4f6d-8a5e-7878ce67c081.Text: "I do not require an escort. I can get there on my own."

90aafd3a-e270-4a21-a057-e85548905658.Text: "Are you implying that it is the governor's fault and he has been failing in his duties?"

78b8dc83-4c88-4e87-b801-1ca332048c24.Text: "Do not dare badmouth your lawful governor, let alone justify the rebellion, in the presence of a Rogue Trader."

c85383ea-fa7e-4f98-aeae-83c2db09e9fa.Text: "There's not a lot to tell... We were taught that the ungrateful rabble often rebels against the lawful authorities," {n}comes Camille's rote answer. But then he continues in a slightly different tone.{/n} "For the past couple of years, we... er... haven't been doing very well."

92b6513b-3984-4db6-9079-e1b343104405.Text: "The ungrateful rabble rose in rebellion against the planet's lawful governor and His Lordship Calligos Winterscale, our ruler by the will of the Emperor! They are all heretics deserving of a most terrible death. Order will be restored. The guilty will be punished!"

466567af-8b85-4efe-b763-d33fde703b04.Text: "Two major earthquakes in both hemispheres, with lots of casualties and destruction. Then the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} tinkered with something they shouldn't have, and we had lives lost to a series of substation explosions. Then, on top of all that, there were the new taxes. The governor needed to be able to report to His Lordship Calligos that the army's numbers and equipment supplies had increased as planned..." {n}The young man falls silent and looks at you with apprehension.{/n}

71a76bea-e9f0-46cc-8111-c8ed230079a4.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g}'s words make Private Regias grow pale and instinctively pull his helmet down tighter.{/n}

baaee9df-2f07-4524-a4e0-7a112eb06d5e.Text: {n}The soldier grows paler still.{/n} "Please forgive me, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! I... was left all alone... and it's been scary, waiting for you. That's why..."

2e801489-4f15-4fae-9447-d2baab841948.Text: "Apologies, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship!" {n}The soldier draws himself up and goes to adjust his gear.{/n} "It's a new uniform. The guards are in a difficult situation right now, so we often get issued whatever's left... and it isn't always the right size."

0033587f-a1a0-43e2-b1e7-614a5b447052.Text: "I beg of you, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, I'm not implying anything! Why would I? I'm just... telling you what's been happening."

372a71b4-fe02-440d-bc6f-3ecb35a4accf.Text: "I don't know, I just... did somehow? There was an ambush, everything was going boom and bang around me, and I kept firing back till I saw our commander lying there with a hole in his head, and everybody else, too... I was alive, and the enemy had retreated."

c30d4fe3-d1f5-428d-9960-2af4d3a3b94d.Text: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} protected me!" {n}the soldier replies with confidence.{/n} "I didn't run, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, if that's what you're thinking! I was by my commander's side until the very end. I shot the last rebel from the gang that attacked us. But alas... the captain succumbed to his wounds, and the others had already died. The Emperor rest their souls!"

1adfdbfb-c726-4d3f-b424-f688836713d3.Text: "I don't know when they first began to appear but they've definitely been out there for at least a year. Some got caught and burned, of course. But heretic burnings aren't exactly rare. They catch someone every month. That's why nobody noticed the new ones for a while. But as soon as the rebellion started, there were hundreds of them coming out of the woodwork. Wandering about, muttering away... and none of them had eyes. You'll see for yourself, there's plenty of them on this highway. So that's that. You can't tell anymore if the rebellion's just because of the taxes and the disasters or... if the end of the world really is coming."

dc8b4cd9-4227-4ab4-a07b-42c829bdfabb.Text: "Your mouth is full of mud, soldier. You are hiding something behind beaming hues of faith and loyalty... What is it?"

cb2dd42d-5533-4ed5-93b0-3ecfe57e2645.Text: {n}The soldier gulps nervously under the stern gaze of Cassia's ruby eyes.{/n} "F-fear, I guess? In times like these, if you give in to weakness, you're done for. And I'm not done with life just yet."

0c1a634f-e265-47be-b68d-aa240c9540ff.Text: {n}Idira winces, glances at you, then shakes her head.{/n}

74891c3d-4342-46c8-93ff-8829489f53d3.Text: "So, about the rebellion — where was I... well, there were rumours that it was all happening for a reason. The earthquakes, the red robes' problems... And then there were those weird prophets. No eyes — scratched them out themselves, by the looks of it — and they kept going on about the Final Dawn. You know, the end of the world is near, repent or you'll be doomed, that sort of thing."

de84bc18-da60-4434-bbe8-92dd3c469e8e.Text: "Yes, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! The command centre is a straight walk from the starport. It's at the end of the Upperway, not too far from here. But we must proceed carefully. Emperor forbid we get ambushed again..."

84c4d755-1d11-4797-9810-85debc52ec25.Text: "Yes, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. We have to take this avenue: it leads from the starport right to the command centre. It's a short walk!"

5abf225c-29b9-437d-806d-0cb3d13ff454.Text: "The success-to-failure ratio of combat objectives completion for this world's military speaks to its subpar efficiency. I will advise the local ruler to seek my fraternity's aid in upgrading their troops to servitor maniples."

ddc8b961-7bc1-4e69-94be-2787270d656f.Text: "I have my orders, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. I obviously can't forbid you to do as you please. But it's my duty to follow you."

6822c2b3-fea7-407d-b348-ca8ebbc57f90.Text: {n}The soldier sinks his head into his shoulders.{/n} "Understood, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! Apologies, {mf|sir|ma'am}!"

c1511f07-3de9-46e0-8d6e-9b3dbfb3b4f5.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, it's very dangerous up ahead! I'm going to have to follow you for your own protection."

0ff9f711-f839-405d-91d7-129fb89983b9.Text: "Ha! When has any noble ever tried negotiating with riffraff?" {n}The soldier bites his tongue.{/n} "Which is to say no, he hasn't. And to tell you the truth... I don't think it would've helped. There's more to this rebellion than meets the eye..."

5ebcd66e-bc51-48d6-9013-6454ab356eae.Text: {n}The young man in a planetary guard uniform looks very pale. There is a feverish gleam in his eyes.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship? At last! Private Camille Regias at your command! I—" {n}He hesitates.{/n} "I was in the convoy the governor sent out to meet you. The convoy was ambushed by rebels! I'm the only survivor. Nevertheless, I'm ready to show you the way to the command centre where the governor is awaiting you!"

d24c45b7-0701-4bea-a68b-03ab3606666e.Text: {n}A young man in a planetary guard uniform salutes you.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! Private Camille Regias, ready to escort you to the command centre for your meeting with the governor! I regret to say that the convoy sent to meet you was ambushed and took critical losses in heavy fighting against the rebels. In other words, I'm the only survivor. However, the rebel force was destroyed as well. We can set out for the command centre!"

6116f584-5e60-4452-8866-682463ae57e2.Text: "Cowardice is shameful for a soldier of the Emperor."

ffcc72f7-f719-4116-a651-51290decda4c.Text: "The battlefield looks highly suspicious. Half of your comrades never even had the chance to draw their weapons. And the direction of the shots, as well — the attackers knew exactly what path the group would take and how large it would be."

e35332e5-0d21-4f78-8ec7-7afac56f07e2.Text: [Aim your weapon at the private] "Too many parts of your story fail to add up. I am beginning to wonder if you are a traitor."

16207042-45dd-433f-b98b-81608ab53511.Text: "Glory to the fallen warriors! They will not be forgotten. Let's keep walking."

1ed94015-d090-4f67-9bfd-b2a13ff55c89.Text: "Is that what your gift of prophecy is telling you?"

59db2f85-fc17-4948-861b-44c3ed992324.Text: "So, you are the traitor. You led your convoy into an ambush, didn't you?"

0de0de48-e8b0-44d7-9234-fb81b75059f9.Text: "Who is Aurora? What is the Final Dawn?"

28281edb-a208-437b-b724-66014acaaf03.Text: [Finish the wounded man] "Death to heretics and traitors."

395b0519-48e4-4925-8d65-ecde41f54202.Text: [Kill the private] "In times of war, it is better to execute an innocent than to have a mole in one's ranks!"

411e326b-6142-487f-998e-26169092a68a.Text: "How curious. That is the second squad under your lead that ended up in a rebel ambush. Do you have anything to say in your defence, private?"

4b02ab0f-794e-4295-a832-fd64ea83e95e.Text: [Help the wounded man] "It is all right. We're going to bandage you up and continue on our way."

50134025-d89e-447c-a5c1-56d80c9c986c.Text: [Help the wounded man] "I shall help you now, but as soon as we reach the governor, you are going into custody."

0d039ff5-ce00-4eeb-925d-1f4c9c419e28.Text: [Finish the wounded man] "Enough. I cannot afford the risk of dragging a potential rebel spy along."

87a31f65-5dfa-4dbc-865a-0bbeeef65a35.Text: "Watch your tongue, Tlass. Say another word and you will be next."

556a88a9-29ee-4814-a7ed-99cda96d19f5.Text: "Let's go. Now is no time for grief."

f9d25f87-a9cb-4817-b8bd-8a0eea01ab51.Text: "Our poor lads... they deserve proper last honours... not to be lying here like this..." {n}Camille looks away from the bodies.{/n}

6b23ce48-0d78-4ebd-9b5f-feaf1a017c3e.Text: {n}The young man sighs.{/n} "The remains of my squad. Once we've put down the rebellion, they'll be given the last honours they deserve as soldiers fallen in a righteous battle."

558d3d43-64d8-4e7c-9dbf-75f7ce1ce844.Text: {n}The soldier looks around, a little dazed. He is pressing his hand down on a fresh wound.{/n} "How is this possible..."

e7125fce-d451-4ea3-a960-0f787c3cc8da.Text: {n}The wounded young man looks at you spitefully and hisses,{/n} "Your victory means nothing! Aurora will come for you... and even if she doesn't — no one will escape the Final Dawn!"

d1471f91-93c6-4fc1-84ab-580fea49230a.Text: {n}The young man looks at you in slight confusion.{/n} "I don't know what you're talking about... Yes, we were ambushed... but it was all over so quickly. It's a miracle I survived. I was lucky to be behind cover when it began."

9e6117e9-efc1-4544-8b93-de9b84a67026.Text: "The enemy is smart and cunning. Perhaps they were watching us? I must report this to the governor!"

8e62b7a8-6bfa-431c-b8fb-a7990def916d.Text: "Warped if I know. With this cacophony in my head there's no damn telling if it's their voices or my gut feeling. Either way, my instinct tells me that he's innocent."

b7b36ad1-a1e9-4cd0-97dc-be2856dbb99e.Text: "Ha ha ha... no! Your entire convoy's gone. I took that whining pup Camille's uniform. Six months with the governor's underlings taught me their ways. I had no trouble posing as one of them. I had to make sure you scum didn't decide to turn around and fly home, instead of walking straight into the ambush." {n}The young man rasps and spits bloody foam.{/n} "Don't let it go to your head that you took us down. My comrades are many and they are coming for you. And if they are not... Anyway, you'll see for yourself!"

c30fdb0e-698a-41df-80e2-9ec709291205.Text: {n}A spark of madness flashes through the young man's eyes.{/n} "Aurora is the hidden truth. No one is worthy of seeing her face! But those who are loyal to her will stand by her side at the hour of the Final Dawn that will consume all! They will, but not you. You are an enemy of Aurora, and so you will be vanquished."

f00a40cc-b8f0-4655-89eb-f7e025734afc.Text: "I do not fear death at the hands of filthy dogs mired in their own lies! Take my soul, Aurora!"

b7be6627-84dc-4eab-9382-093254a90719.Text: {n}The guard opens his eyes widely, incredulous to the last that this is the end.{/n}

1478df1d-2584-4ab9-a3e9-def1b38a7417.Text: "Blast you, scum! Aurora will get you all the same! Aurora and the Final Dawn!"

2fd17c63-7a83-4f76-b1aa-320be054fff0.Text: "Uh-huh," {n}the guard says gloomily and looks away.{/n}

12ae0190-a6c9-4723-bc11-2bfae9069ad7.Text: "What? No! I'm— I'm not a traitor! I'd never lead my fellows into the line of fire... Never!"

098c0cbc-198f-42fd-bec3-8e45ecc6d815.Text: {n}The young man's eyes widen. Until his very last moment, they are filled with shock and disbelief at the crushing reality he is facing.{/n}

6c37f83f-e5cd-453d-b916-2d681703a3e9.Text: "Why, what did I do? Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, they won't even bother to look into the matter, they'll just march me to the wall and shoot me!" {n}The soldier lowers his head glumly, accepting his fate.{/n}

78f4fd49-e403-4303-a51a-bf0a2db1db20.Text: "I swear, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! I may've gotten a few things mixed up from inexperience, and that's why they don't add up. Please, let's walk to the governor's command centre. I must carry out my orders. Once we get there, you can have the intelligence run a check on me if you wish. I'm a loyal soldier and that's the truth!"

605019c6-8927-4097-87be-4ef36148fed1.Text: {n}Idira opens and closes her mouth several times as if struggling to say something, but in the end merely bites her lip, drawing blood, and nods glumly.{/n}

9c8daed1-c588-4555-9272-d9c4fb1021ec.Text: {n}In your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}past life{/d}, the ability to tell whether someone was trustworthy or a rat often marked the line between life and death. Under your scrutiny, the trooper seems far too calm — a sure sign the wretch is labouring to mislead you.{/n}

926d04e8-90ff-4a52-804f-6ac76e353188.Text: "Of course, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Please, let's make a move — the sooner we get there, the better!"

c67cb557-4d0e-4141-9ecc-604acf03296b.Text: {n}Idira sniffs and says gently,{/n} "Reconsider, Lord Captain, have mercy on the boy. He's been so awfully stressed, it's a wonder he can even talk. Bit of a simpleton, that's all. I sense no cunning in him."

2f6965c1-a58b-4511-b74d-327256a07b94.Text: "It certainly is, but if he were a coward, he'd have chucked his lasgun in a ditch long ago and taken to his heels. Yet there he is, leading you and doing his duty, never mind his chattering teeth."

e651e43e-13c7-4cfa-9525-ef27b26fb992.Text: "Do not believe him, Lord Captain! Pale green is seeping from his every word, and I know this colour of deceit well. I once mistook Felek's words, so humble and full of sweetness, for sincerity. In truth, they were... poison."

111f9942-e10a-4697-ad22-32a8ea198012.Text: "Updating data catalogue. The characteristic tendency of the planetary defence forces of Rykad Minoris to run into ambushes is not a consequence of chance or negligence. It can only be explained as some twisted variation of combat tactics. This phenomenon is depressing."

3330dfad-9b6c-42a5-a917-33993d828ca9.Text: {n}In your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}former life{/d}, your ability to tell a soldier from a rat often meant the difference between life and death. The private is a poor actor — you know he is not trying to trick you.{/n}

76d0eb0f-18ae-4f6c-ae46-2d1b1fc2bb7c.Text: "What? No! What doesn't add up? I'm the only survivor out of my entire squad, do you understand? All of my friends are dead — they're lying over there! I could have fled or hidden, but I chose to come all the way here to warn you... and you..."

cb98a97c-c0dd-489f-82fb-08fbc883c22a.Text: "Does anyone have any idea what just happened?"

5278bbbf-7834-4638-9610-17f6e16d4fb1.Text: "All we can do now is try to make it to the starport."

8a1666e1-b7f6-45ad-99a2-ddad4231ee51.Text: Allowed the terrified citizens to follow you when darkness fell on Rykad Minoris.

bb1e78c0-c06f-4602-a895-d19cff0885c1.Text: "We're not abandoning people in distress. Everyone can come with us."

ef9f393f-da1c-47e8-bfd7-3e14b6ae71cf.Text: Abandoned the terrified citizens to their fate when darkness fell on Rykad Minoris.

7469ebbf-6821-49be-9aaf-f6aa9a447a8e.Text: "I am under no obligation to save anyone. It is every man for himself."

7c906593-834f-4915-b329-cf6264f49208.Text: {n}Your {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g} comes alive. Vigdis's voice struggles to get through the thundering static.{/n} "Lord... tain, this is... x Master! Please sta... ll immed... ly send a..."

537e6305-b1b0-4d89-bfa8-c5af99256570.Text: {n}Heinrix removes his hands and shakes his head as if trying to drive away whatever is assailing him. His voice trembles when he says,{/n} "A simple solution to stabilise your condition. Keep it together. Do not give in to the force trying to take hold of you."

cb0a3916-4896-4b5a-96c5-9c1b3981b41c.Text: {n}Camille runs up to you, his weapon still in hand.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! What are your orders? We have no idea what's going on! Civilians are fleeing in panic and we can't get through to the governor or our senior officers!"

62647b3a-df26-4b8a-bb3b-a2f3c75ae5c6.Text: {n}The old man peers at you gloomily.{/n} "You told me my faith was false. You made me turn away from Aurora. Now what do you say, {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}? Who was right? Here it is — the Final Dawn!" {n}He makes a sweeping gesture with his hand.{/n}

3029b77b-9685-4b0c-ba49-65e32442308c.Text: "Hold your tongue, Aryld! Dawn or no dawn, I'll die before I let those eyeless freaks maim me! So keep quiet and do as {mf|His Lord|Her Lady}ship says! {mf|He|She}'ll tell us what to do!"

c7d00a93-ad38-473e-8c0d-f9aee8b2c85e.Text: {n}Jaspar clasps his fiancée's hand firmly.{/n} "To the abyss with this masquerade! The whole place's gone insane and here I am, dressed in civvies and without my vox-caster! What do we do, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship? Raquel says we have to fight our way to the starport. That's where her shuttle is, and yours as well, I suppose."

46737e1d-a76d-4a9e-8e50-71ca371e2184.Text: "Less talk, more action! What's Vigdis saying, Lord Captain? Are they going to send a shuttle for us?"

1d137661-cf16-49d3-8409-be389f31c538.Text: "Friendly... agents... of th-the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Inquisition{/g}... make me so n-nervous!"

c42d97ae-6689-4f03-9b98-cb2395184c49.Text: "Pull yourself together, Lady Tlass. And do not resist. It's a simple technique that will bring you relief." {n}Heinrix leans over Idira and puts his hands on her temples.{/n}

ec717fe3-8ce2-4787-a5b3-e2b39842844c.Text: "I'm not being friendly. What's happening is beyond normal cultist scheming. We can't afford to lose a single fighter."

97cc0e84-ff72-4028-a184-e7b4d8da1e55.Text: "...pening... ve observ... sappearance of the star from... vacuate..."

26c16543-8395-45c6-9b4e-1b014e5fdc27.Text: "Red, black, red, black... and lots of blinding white fear. The whole city's quaking! No — the whole world!"

fced80a7-3a57-4719-b6fe-aa5aa7e72ab5.Text: "I shall fear no darkness, for light is within me, the light of my faith in {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Thee{/g}. I shall flee before no enemy, for there is no enemy more terrible than cowardice, and I shall overpower it..." {n}Argenta prays aloud, all the while checking her equipment with deft fingers.{/n}

32d42e81-375f-4b9b-acb4-dafd4c5dfbd1.Text: "We must move out toward the starport at once. The shuttles aren't going to find us here even if the comm link stabilises. Which it won't."

ba29fc5c-9cac-4ad7-a590-bdec52a31338.Text: {n}The red-haired ex-rebel sits down on the pavement, tears running down her face.{/n} "When will this end already... when... I wanna go hooome!"

84feb51f-3a20-4486-ac21-fab42be4176d.Text: {n}The comm falls silent. Many eyes stare at you.{/n}

6d9516d7-94da-483f-8941-4c0698b461b8.Text: "Only an incomplete picture." {n}Heinrix sounds deadly serious.{/n} "Every warp-active person on this planet is sensing the presence of sorcery... It's rising like a tsunami. I have hardly ever encountered anything like it in {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}realspace{/g}. And, most remarkably, the sorcery is still growing. I cannot, however, say what set off this reaction or where the light has gone."

8e4843e8-b562-46df-96fd-5433fd976f52.Text: {n}Idira is holding her nose, trickling with blood.{/n} "I saw blurry shadows reaching for a ball of bright fire and pulling it away. And another shadow, much larger and more terrifying, that followed them. It opened its colossal eye when the others were gone with their loot. I saw no connections, no complicity... it was like a loop catching on a hook. A small terror made another, greater one, crawl out of its lair and act. That's the best I can explain it."

8f25bda5-e1a9-49fd-9311-4e8ba589757c.Text: "But what I can say is that I only see death in Rykad Minoris's future. Death and nothing else. And I mean its immediate future! In other words, it's time to leg it."

bb248d22-a5ea-4a9e-9900-ea9db9c1b766.Text: {n}Idira looks askance at Argenta.{/n} "Patience, everybody. Holy sis here is almost done powdering her nose..."

e40ec695-00af-4d51-9412-05ac72c51cf8.Text: "The Final Dawn!" {n}Argenta says furiously.{/n} "We stopped short of puzzling out the enemy's entire plan... O Emperor, forgive us for this negligence. I swear we will find a way to right it!"

a8e60521-2076-4d8b-b200-2367dc1eeb2e.Text: "We'll follow behind you, keeping a bit of distance. We must escort the remaining civilians. Without the guard's help, they'll scatter or fall into the enemy's hands."

b5ba7cc0-ab4d-43b9-be99-816bb40df9c5.Text: "Jaspar and I must get weapons — any weapons. We'll catch up with you at the starport. We might even pick up some people from the garrison or civilians along the way."

379de64b-a21e-4cae-a2b0-75aa1beaa4cd.Text: "And us? What about us? Can we go with you, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship? Please, don't leave us behind!"

2a2a668f-4603-4e26-8af8-0c9e3466f639.Text: {n}The old woman looks at you, not particularly hopeful and a little distrustful, as if she is reluctant to ask her question.{/n}

27da55ac-103b-4fab-ad1f-652983951680.Text: {n}The sense of alarm keeps growing stronger. As does the sensation of an intent gaze fixed upon you.{/n}

0cb1a4c2-252b-4f87-b39a-30eb5a9322a3.Text: "I'm no fast walker. But I'll hobble after you. If you get into a fight, it's not like you'll want an old woman to get in your way anyway. And I think there will be more fighting..."

f8fe6797-1839-435f-b22a-3df06d62b1cd.Text: "Th-thank you, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! I'll walk behind you... yes..."

06feea97-1435-4479-b3fe-aa5897455725.Text: "There sure will be. It looks like some of my former comrades are still on the loose." {n}The old man's voice sounds lethargic and almost robotic.{/n}

a285d3d9-9f5b-4649-aba3-753ba28e660c.Text: "Rogue Trader! We must help these people evacuate. The Emperor Himself has entrusted their fate to us."

414ff58f-fbfc-429b-ab31-ce5751f63c05.Text: {n}Camille frowns but salutes nonetheless.{/n} "Good luck, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship!"

d360efcc-1150-44c1-b837-ddd1739d8f1f.Text: "You, soldier! Care to help a lone, exploited civilian save herself?" {n}The red-haired woman hooks her arm through the soldier's resolutely.{/n}

91729485-88ac-4eaf-93f8-01d41ad35c76.Text: "I won't run off. I promise!" {n}The red-haired woman hooks her arm through the soldier's resolutely.{/n} "It's so good to have someone who'll protect you and take you to safety..."

0021fe4b-8bbc-47e6-801a-c30ea4b0e28f.Text: "Let's go, Aryld." {n}The old woman takes her husband by the hand wearily.{/n} "Perhaps we'll find our grandchildren and sit with them one last time. And if we don't... then it'll just be the two of us."

37e9ae38-5837-4938-9ec2-e79feac28c15.Text: {n}The sense of alarm is now almost physically drilling through your temples. The fleeting little whispers at the edge of your hearing are sinister and gleeful.{/n}

80ae3fd5-9ed3-4069-9236-a8bdfc79c7e0.Text: {n}A chill runs down your spine. You seem to feel Aurora's gaze upon you once again... only it is not coming from her corpse any longer, but from everywhere.{/n}

9fa14ee3-2490-4fe3-a6ba-9dde03a36b3b.Text: {n}An otherworldly cacophony, which until now resembled the rumbling of distant cannons, suddenly swallows you with its full intensity — the warp energies seemingly bursting out of thin air, rushing inside your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}exposed mind{/d} like an unstoppable wave of filth. For a moment it feels like your head might explode... but then the sensation retreats, leaving in its wake a different one — that of someone's touch on your temples.{/n}

092930cd-1a89-4230-ad40-965f44edcb27.Text: {n}Kibellah gives you a faint smile and whispers,{/n} "A great dance begins. But I am still with you, Domin. Fear not, for I will not let your soul fall into the clutches of the unclean. If it comes to it... I will be quicker than them."

54a84562-c555-4ffb-8837-e21953182512.Text: "I have won, and you have perished along with your plans."

b074c409-a254-4e78-901b-abf04cf546b7.Text: "I will hunt down all of your accomplices, wherever they may be. And they will all follow you into the fire."

716bc23b-fe0c-4d10-b8d5-58b501ef5309.Text: "I wish I could learn your secrets, Aurora. You died too soon and never revealed them to me."

ba40532b-1d84-4ccd-9996-321b11232a6f.Text: {n}Surrounded by evil-repelling emblems, Aurora's corpse looks like a tiny island of gloom in the glorious ocean of your impending Triumph. The governor's people must have put a lot of work into protecting the body from decay as well as sawing off the grim iron face mask.{/n}

456f9375-5403-4c95-bf32-e09527fcaecc.Text: {n}Not a sound comes in response. But as soon as you blink, the corner of the corpse's mouth seems to move upward by a hair's breadth. Or is it just your imagination?{/n}

5b1ae549-6b76-4d0e-a2bb-a23e6f3f84c4.Text: {n}The dead prophet has the weary, unremarkable face of an utterly nondescript commoner. The one aberration of her appearance is the many small mouths on her cheeks and forehead. They have been painstakingly sewn shut with a thick thread and plastered over with a layer of face powder. The cosmetics transform the heretic's face into an eerie mask. The corner of her mouth is frozen in a hint of a grin, wryly mirrored by her lesser mouths. "Are you pleased, enemy mine?" the grin seems to ask.{/n}

45f38ca7-162d-4e66-9886-d237403850af.Text: [Greet the people] "It is my pleasure to protect an Imperium world and its honest inhabitants! May the light of the eternal Terra shine on us all!"

55994375-aa8d-48ad-921b-61392593ada5.Text: [Address the soldiers in the cordon] "Stop the ceremony! Take the people away! Something terrible is about to happen!"

4355f803-008b-478e-acde-53e9893d782b.Text: [Turn around and look at Aurora's corpse]

031a31a1-ded6-43ec-bc53-8663b4ab7d12.Text: "Make way! Make way! Let us greet the {mf|hero|heroine}!" {n}A small group of {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_Noble}festively dressed people{/d} rushes toward you.{/n}

2ec75692-51a1-494e-9dcb-4dae58b11cad.Text: "Er... hello, Y'{mf|Lord|Lady}ship! Glory to you! Glory!" {n}A motley group of {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_Commoners}modestly dressed people{/d} hurries toward you.{/n}

45d07f98-af85-44ad-8833-61788f3b52e7.Text: "Ahem... Glory to Your thrice-praised {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! We're, er... very, very grateful to you, we really are! Neither I nor my grandchildren would've probably been {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_OldPeopleSurvived}alive now if not for you{/d}... Oi! Aryld! Move your old bones! Get over here and greet {mf|His Lord|Her Lady}ship!"

522919c2-6546-49d2-862f-58e55d4860b4.Text: "I'm coming, I'm coming..." {n}The old man trailing his wife is the one whose life you spared despite his links to Aurora's cultists. He casts an apprehensive sideways glance at the prophet's corpse, but quickly looks away and bows to you.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship!"

52a66418-94ea-4b13-a50b-03a53f91cc80.Text: {n}Among the guards in the security cordon you recognise Camille, the young scout who {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_KamilSaved}led you{/d} to the command centre. When he meets your eye, he smiles and salutes.{/n}

1bacaa08-b020-4239-b6ea-986d24b435b8.Text: "Glory to the von Valancius dynasty! Glory to {name}, a {mf|hero|heroine} of Rykad Minoris!" {n}A stately, beautiful, and finely dressed woman calls out your name in a sonorous voice. It isn't until you take a closer look at her face that you recognise her as Captain Raquel, the pilot you {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_RakelHelped}met{/d} on Rykadi Philia.{/n}

7e0c7753-3b40-4d46-845d-d19bb1c9e75d.Text: {n}Standing next to her is her fiancé, Jaspar, the vox operator you {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_JasperSurvived}rescued{/d} at the starport during your first visit to the planet. He, too, is wearing civilian clothes.{/n}

70cc897a-4c0d-4bad-a84c-a4eccb413817.Text: "Rykad Minoris honours the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} and bows to His most loyal servants, the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Traders{/g}!"

0f4f8ec0-202d-4d03-95e8-8e8659b69d38.Text: {n}The soldiers in the cordon exchange perplexed glances, but their trained discipline prevails and they turn toward the spectators, preparing to lead the crowd away.{/n}

da6db0c9-29ce-4a7b-9891-4d83d89fa4c2.Text: {n}Nothing. Nothing strange. The crowd's salutatory clamour; the prophet's motionless corpse. Only the air is oddly still, as before a thunderstorm.{/n}

45366f8c-a8a5-4ee6-aeec-3782256d1578.Text: "What... what... they're coming out of the darkness, they're stealing the light... the darkness is insatiable... and behind them, behind these thieves, an ineffable eye follows, watching, watching... aargh!"

918b3fdd-6444-40fd-a26e-24b8cbf05cdf.Text: "I— I'm... sensing something. Boundless. Blue... golden... dark..."

09f20e8a-1005-4206-9757-51ad001831f7.Text: {n}A grimace contorts Heinrix's face. The Interrogator lifts a hand to his temple, as though struck by a sudden migraine.{/n} "What..."

cdb1fabd-5bdb-4098-8682-c0ede6b3ea08.Text: "The grateful citizens wish to present gifts to their redeemer!" {n}The master of ceremonies' sugary voice almost brings a taste of honey to your mouth.{/n}

5277646f-430d-4c13-a1e9-bf2c2f03b538.Text: "What was the point of herding us here? Celebrating? I could've just as well celebrated at home..." {n}An elderly woman — the one you {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_OldPeopleSurvived}saved{/d} along with other hostages from her crazed husband — shuffles toward you.{/n}

ecf3c635-dd36-4d6e-88de-174f32fa92ec.Text: {n}For whatever reason, you know for certain that right at this moment, the "gaze" of Aurora's dead, empty eye sockets is fixed upon the back of your head. A thought surfaces in your mind, not a voice inside your head, no, a mere thought: "They are all going to die. Befuddled, deprived, never having seen the Truth. And it is all because of you, enemy mine."{/n}

e728abc3-947a-4cee-8500-801035764ecc.Text: "Something is coming, Domin. An unholy death contrary to His will." {n}Kibellah's eyes are blank as she digs a steel claw into an unhealed wound.{/n}

d56d3f79-b39d-4d25-ba5a-9ba68ed4e690.Text: "Thank you to our protector! Our benefactor!" {n}The spirited red-headed woman is jumping up and down and waving her hands. However, once she gets close enough to see your face, her eyes widen with shock.{/n} "Uh-oh. Uh... oh. Weren't you the one the Chief sent to {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_RedLiedTo}take over{/d} from us? Err... I mean... I'm really glad to see you alive and well!"

438d8a04-94c1-410f-8ec8-ed5e0a1dd450.Text: "Thank you to our protector! Our benefactor!" {n}The spirited {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Triumph_RedSurvived}red-headed woman{/d} is jumping up and down and waving her hands.{/n} "Thank you for being merciful!"

a12f981f-7558-44db-abff-4405bb694cc1.Text: "I wish to start the Triumph at once. Give the order!"

2a323ce7-dac7-456c-a583-07aabde66118.Text: "This is disgusting. I do not want a staged show of 'gratitude.' Allow the ordinary people of Rykad Minoris to speak to me or skip this farce altogether!"

b6392abb-4f63-4199-91fa-098ade00da25.Text: "An excellent plan. I am ready to start the Triumph!"

096a1d7d-30b3-41ff-a00f-31bf67cba5bf.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, peerless {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius! I am the master of ceremonies of Rykad Minoris. Everything is in place for your Triumph. Allow me to give you a brief summary of the upcoming event."

3b1309a1-c041-4cf1-935d-7e9b6542b5f1.Text: "You will take the road, now familiar to you, from here to the starport. You will be accompanied by your comrades-in-arms and a guard of honour. The body of the heretic known as 'the prophet Aurora' will be pulled in your wake as a battle trophy. A stop is planned in the middle of the road. There, grateful citizens will rush toward you, praising you for their salvation."

d55bd4d3-17dd-4f24-9299-39fff5797003.Text: "Once they have said their praise, the procession will move on. Governor Medineh will await you by the starport. It is also where the pyre has been built for burning the body of the heretic known as Aurora. You will be handed a flamer blessed by a representative of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorum}Ecclesiarchy{/g}. You can choose to personally perform the burning. But if you wish to underscore the amicable alliance between House von Valancius and House Winterscale, it will be fitting to pass the honour of the burning to Governor Medineh. However, the choice is yours!"

45562b3f-fc3c-4a62-ad44-e2e2d9ab1ac0.Text: "Not to worry: this is a thoroughly choreographed interlude! The group of the grateful people will be composed exclusively of loyal citizens vetted by us. Members of the military. Young people, attractive and physically fit. A few healthy children."

07ed15a6-3279-4af6-8b5c-6d17a8ae1bd1.Text: {n}The master of ceremonies' eyes widen.{/n} "My sincerest apologies, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! No thought could be further from my mind than incurring your anger! Let the, er, ordinary people through, you say? I'll see what can be done!"

dc09ed47-b567-4bff-b2a4-01716cec3a5e.Text: "Where is the venerable Governor Drivestem? Is he hiding from the Rogue Trader?"

eff1f78d-37fe-41c0-b5a1-6551148ec12a.Text: "Urbend would not have dared to be so insolent. He proceeded to the courtyard for some fresh air with the Lord Inquisitor."

307717a0-1fb0-4261-82cb-42a1681c9a9c.Text: "Then we should be there too. I'm sure the blessed head of the von Valancius dynasty will also join us in time."

852d62e5-e134-4667-bd02-57a683341f67.Text: The ancient chronicle contains a long list of pirate dens annihilated by the von Valancius dynasty, and planets it brought into Imperial Compliance.

582a3e65-4c65-4856-bcd3-42cfb6dac25d.Text: The Drukhari captive is muttering something angrily in its unnatural tongue.

77890bfa-46bb-40bf-adb5-d7e2b16f0158.Text: The Drukhari captive is angrily muttering curses directed at the "detestable mon-keigh," promising horrible torture for everyone present.

bedcfc9a-0371-4d35-a2d7-5d1cae69c920.Text: The severed head of the machine mutilated by Chaos has its grotesque teeth bared menacingly.

21275926-617d-4a04-880b-b8919d472a81.Text: Judging by the melted spots on its armour, this mighty Leman Russ, decorated with the von Valancius coat of arms, has fought in a number of battles against the enemies of the Rogue Trader.

fe0b8359-e883-4f5f-bc13-946062a165fe.Text: This venerable Leman Russ is known as the Skipian Punisher and it has served the von Valancius dynasty for two centuries. It was hit in the battle with the xenos that inhabited Skipia II, but it heroically destroyed sixty-three enemy vehicles and brought victory to its comrades, securing its status as a relic blessed by the Emperor.

b9fdb9dd-8ad8-45f6-a365-ef130ce1ca05.Text: Obscura, somna, Black Lethe — the guests of the Rogue Trader can enjoy the most exclusive and refined varieties of intoxicants.

674c41e2-7c1b-418f-a49d-b38b91be791c.Text: "Does Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship wish to proceed into the courtyard?"

19af5bcf-7979-46f6-bf32-c9d9f86731dd.Text: The skull of the legendary pirate Lakshim the Freak, who terrorised the Koronus Expanse three centuries ago. It was claimed in a boarding attack by the esteemed Theodora von Valancius.

675178eb-370e-400d-9256-8331fc39bb5f.Text: Exceptional amasec of the highest quality has been poured into a drum, the kind from which regular soldiers drink water and recaf.

50cdf445-2755-410f-953a-4b4f0e15bb4c.Text: This fountain of priceless wine quenches one's thirst by the sheer sight of its abundance.

974264c2-b1f3-4b95-8151-c558c7e6c073.Text: The refined features of these statues demonstrate the beauty and perfection of Humanity's genetic purity.

f4c5a707-2023-455c-bbcd-57b90171f861.Text: "Young Gaprak is right. The xenos are not just a threat — they are also an opportunity."

ab70e7a3-bc00-4693-a245-9431897bd889.Text: [Yawn] "For you, perhaps. For me, it is just another day."

41ea3bea-2149-4038-b0dd-6a4aca1c8e83.Text: [Pointedly gaze at Drivestem with animosity and say nothing]

38162f73-0595-4623-9104-f8534dd72306.Text: [Smile graciously] "I welcome you to my palace, honoured guests!"

5981960b-50ed-4506-8b0d-353d0237100e.Text: [Talk to young Sauerback] "I see you hate xenos with all your heart."

3b9ceef1-65d9-4b2b-a298-645e7ccacb24.Text: "It pleases me to see such earnest faith. I must commend you."

3082d007-fa55-4590-b2af-59a4e264c8d7.Text: [Smile venomously] "And how many xenos have you killed personally, Sauerback?"

7a0216ee-56d4-48e7-9877-3b9d852b851b.Text: [Nod to the Inquisitor] "My greetings to the member of the Holy Inquisition."

49f39364-1710-4ae0-bfcc-e0c6a826e4b5.Text: "Well said, Sauerback. Since you have already promised it, I will accept your support. I hereby impose a duty on your house — you are to provide me with soldiers. And you, young man, are to lead them."

76ad2819-b35f-434f-b927-a9f8c8bb1d7d.Text: "Since young Gaprak is so inspired by the thought of conducting business with xenos, I shall take him into my service as a trade representative. His house shall see to it that he makes himself useful and that his service is beyond reproach."

303c9143-ad24-4513-94e4-33ebefc883cd.Text: "And who is this member of the honourable priesthood of the Adeptus Mechanicus?"

bb964500-70b1-4a7e-8261-cdcb04020cdb.Text: [Look at Abelard's young relative] "What is your name?"

12ffbf1c-9ff9-4aab-b3a6-ba68681664de.Text: "Where are the rest of your kin, Abelard?"

7343ac5b-381d-4664-9697-a01b5d4a2213.Text: "Where are Abelard himself and the rest of your kin?"

203a2874-f714-411f-bc76-7f02c043f9f6.Text: "So you wish to become my servant as well?"

28798ccd-c27e-4dde-b2eb-69d364494268.Text: "I hope the Werserian family gives Abelard the credit he deserves?"

beb523ab-5118-4a46-aa6d-e2b431825cd4.Text: "It's quite true, I really am not interested."

2e692413-c647-4454-a478-fab0c5668fcb.Text: "Hold your tongue, Urbend. I decide who may speak and who may not. Please continue, Astartia."

2a2648ac-dddc-4b9f-ab61-b2df41ad704a.Text: "I am ready to accept your congratulations."

1c0259fd-62d6-43d4-914f-7d48dac950a5.Text: [Take a guess at who is allied with whom in this tangle of snakes]

5644797c-08e4-4d1c-810f-5cb036757b27.Text: "May I enquire after Heinrix van Calox?"

d92295de-e9f2-454b-b35c-10852dfd9e19.Text: Astutely gauged the relations between the noble houses of Dargonus.

f319306d-6fe4-4381-bf88-ec8e571e1f11.Text: [Study the faces of the nobles in attendance]

c050949e-50d3-4256-87aa-cd1184f67241.Text: {n}Governor Urbend Drivestem stands surrounded by highborn guests like a planet orbited by many moons. All of his charm is directed at a man in resplendent power armour adorned with the sigil of the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Inquisition{/g}. But as soon as you approach, Drivestem is the first to give you an elegant bow, getting ahead of the rest in the expression of loyalty.{/n} "This is a great day, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"

99bc06f1-1bb3-4c5b-99fa-f37dea4f4fe8.Text: {n}Young Gaprak regards the magnificent trophies you have collected on xenoworlds, then answers seriously and without servility,{/n} "Thank you for this honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I will prove myself a devoted and diligent servant."

31dc812e-df9b-4d8c-a46b-8126de78efd5.Text: {n}The Lord Inquisitor's relaxed expression radiates an odd sense of menace. He is akin to a predator on the prowl, content to hide in the brush of fake smiles and elegant conversation — for now.{/n}

66f7d145-fc81-4820-a710-6c9c1fec70de.Text: {n}Your haughty words produce the desired effect — the heads bow a little lower, and the faces shine with eagerness to oblige the glorious {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}.{/n}

99193085-3d9c-4a42-90a2-3372d4af4d92.Text: {n}Your disfavour has been noticed by the guests. Drivestem pales and bows his head in contrition.{/n}

0f47b0aa-1575-42bd-aa30-b14a35e41bdf.Text: {n}You are buffeted by a salvo of congratulations and compliments.{/n}

a7a5f002-e7e9-4f62-8093-3e78dbc1fa40.Text: {n}The guests around the governor fall into a deferential hush at your approach. Judging by the last bit of their conversation, they were just discussing someone's horrible poisoning that took place at the last society gathering.{/n}

c7f7f140-8c01-4bb4-ade3-fb3c87c327f4.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g}'s {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmentations{/g} seem unfamiliar and bizarre. Implants such as these are only available to members of the blessed hierarchy of the Adeptus Mechanicus, and one would not come upon such sacred relics even at the highest echelons of the nobility.{/n}

ea33eb2d-4eda-4354-80f6-3ba89b8c2ef5.Text: {n}Among the aristocrats surrounding the opulently dressed Drivestem, you notice a couple of young nobles in Sauerback and Gaprak colours. It would seem that the major noble families of Dargonus have decided to introduce their younger members to high society.{/n}

f6f3260e-8fab-4b5f-adb1-b39739a4f331.Text: {n}The tall man in grey power armour adorned with a column with a skull is undoubtedly a high-ranking Inquisitor. He keeps to the periphery of the conversation, seldom deigning to comment. Next to him is his entourage — a rangy warrior in black armour and a {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} dressed in red, whose face is hidden behind a brass mask.{/n}

82bc7ed4-f3cc-4028-befe-ad5e8ab6588d.Text: {n}Abelard stands somewhat apart from the others, as if reluctant to approach Drivestem. Next to him is a young woman, and you notice a family resemblance between them.{/n}

d3c67f39-2636-45cb-805e-08c111479339.Text: {n}To the side, keeping some distance from Drivestem, stands a young woman whose face bears an uncanny resemblance to that of Abelard Werserian.{/n}

f7151a49-dafe-44d9-8fe3-d71f3e2d9403.Text: "We were talking about the brutal {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} raid on our fair Dargonus. So many victims, so much damage to our industries..."

79a98b9d-2072-4a22-8352-77c279a60467.Text: "Thank the Emperor that you are our protector. If it weren't for you, the cursed invaders would have obliterated the whole planet." {n}He offers you a thin and obsequious smile.{/n}

3b4d9447-79b3-4b1e-93ad-b49826dbf44d.Text: "Such a terrible shame it is that the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} currents delayed our protector's arrival..." {n}There is an acidic hint to his words, but it is too faint for you to call him to account. Judging by young Sauerback's unpleasant smile, it is not just your imagination.{/n}

6fdfbc0e-1666-4b69-8a96-5d87c947b26f.Text: "Sharing the sector with the blasted xenos is impossible! I hope we respond to their raid on Dargonus with a punitive campaign!" {n}Young Sauerback's smile is conceited and bloodthirsty.{/n}

6ab78032-3ba1-44b7-97d5-556aa72441e3.Text: "I do! This pestilence against the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} must be exterminated!" {n}He talks ardently and smoothly, like a Commissar. He places his hand on the hilt of his finely adorned sword, his pale face ablaze with noble fury.{/n}

4ec0f8be-c18b-4269-b615-8b6d0ba8f10b.Text: "Or they must be forced into servitude. Many xenos are more useful alive and obedient than dead." {n}The young man in Gaprak colours speaks with sagacity and gravity, but his opinion seems to carry little weight in this circle.{/n}

d85fab86-6a36-4676-9547-6d1f724eaf98.Text: {n}Sauerback blushes and raises his chin.{/n} "House Sauerback is stalwart in its faith, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"

95631f41-833d-4e2e-bfc4-15321c9ae681.Text: {n}Sauerback flushes and mumbles incoherently,{/n} "The honourable Macharius... forbade... but I wanted... did not let me go to battle..."

7ff722be-6cde-49f1-9a20-aba6679d83f6.Text: {n}The Inquisitor standing among the guests offers a thin smile.{/n} "It must have been difficult for this youth to foster such bloodlust toward enemies of the Imperium without ever having seen one at a blade's distance."

4db2c693-dd16-417d-a2d0-d6e9a7ee0687.Text: {n}Sauerback raises his chin proudly and glances at the austere decorations in the palace — the weapons, the sacred banners, and the glorious trophies. By the looks of it, some youthful dream of his is coming true.{/n} "It is an honour for me to serve you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I swear it before the Emperor, I won't let you down!"

f51f982b-0334-4cc5-be4d-17b68213ab8c.Text: {n}Young Gaprak accepts your praise calmly and with dignity, as befits a smart boy lauded by his mother and father for his prudence.{/n}

e311c70f-df74-4d01-bbd7-d8b5db65ae03.Text: {n}The Inquisitor standing among the guests clears his throat — quietly, but Gaprak's face instantly pales and sours.{/n}

c6019225-93ac-479f-8161-186f51724cc8.Text: {n}The Inquisitor standing among the guests smiles faintly and leans toward you. He whispers,{/n} "I congratulate you on procuring a highborn hostage. Bravo."

c8c31832-a40b-4912-af73-66c8e2b47909.Text: {n}Are you imagining things, or did you just notice a mocking glint in the eye of the Inquisitor standing among the guests?{/n}

826a66a7-5440-418e-8d9f-77b8fb03dff5.Text: {n}He responds with a dignified bow, his proud face calm and unfaltering.{/n} "And my greetings to you, esteemed {name} von Valancius. May shadows never darken the light of the {g|Encyclopedia:Astronomican}Astronomican{/g} that guides you."

f5ffeec8-5185-46b6-a0eb-11f6ce3dfa15.Text: "I, however, have been told all about you." {n}The Inquisitor's face is impenetrable, but behind this mask you detect a hint of mockery.{/n}

2e0411dd-40cf-47e3-9ee9-f5645db2473a.Text: "An oversight, to be sure. My name is Xavier Calcazar, and I have the honour of serving as a member of the illustrious Ordo Xenos, the head of the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} Conclave, and the Lord Inquisitor of this region. It is my unending task to ensure this sector's readiness to meet external threats and resist internal corruption."

3d51b6ed-e32f-497c-80ce-06ee47dec0a6.Text: {n}The Inquisitor's companion, a crimson-robed member of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}, bows to you. From behind the brass mask mounted with dozens of augmetics comes a metallic rasp,{/n} "Glory to the von Valancius heir."

93a5596d-545d-4c6f-8844-bd30938b1bc8.Text: "This is Brasswhisper, which, naturally, is not his real name. The esteemed {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g} is a member of my retinue — there are times when I am forced by my duty to the Emperor to deal with {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenotechnology{/g}, and Brasswhisper ensures my safety in such moments."

c357485b-c157-4c3f-84e6-52a0d866ac56.Text: "Works that have been desecrated by xenos are dangerous. They warrant—" {n}His whispering cuts off, replaced by heavy, ragged breathing. It seems that the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g}'s quiet voice is not an extravagant quirk, but rather a consequence of some injury. After catching his breath, Brasswhisper continues,{/n} "...warrant due caution."

b022a3b3-96ac-4007-80b0-288646bc884f.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, allow me to introduce the daughter of Chancellor Clementia Werserian and my great-granddaughter, Astartia." {n}Abelard looks solemnly upon the young woman with barely concealed pride.{/n}

3da35e71-b9e5-402d-9370-152d35690bb7.Text: "I am delighted to witness you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Astartia bows, keeping her observant and intelligent eyes trained on you.{/n}

ede621af-55d2-4dcc-b6c8-514a4fb26e42.Text: "Astartia Werserian, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I am the daughter of Chancellor Clementia Werserian and the great-granddaughter of your loyal servant Abelard. Delighted to witness you." {n}She bows, her observant and intelligent eyes trained on you.{/n}

991080da-2f41-43c6-83af-93ee42f13dc1.Text: "It is difficult to put into words, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Never before have I seen such a grand and striking ceremony." {n}Astartia's voice sounds passionate and inspired, and her eyes shine with barely contained excitement.{/n}

f5460812-c515-4241-9825-d48a9037d63a.Text: "They are in the city, preoccupied with running the festivities and watching over some of the more crucial services. No incidents can be allowed to ruin your ceremony."

a1d106a6-e8ed-4261-bf7f-cf35993ecc6d.Text: "They are in the city. My dear forebear is watching over the festivities being organised for the people, and the rest of my kin are overseeing the most important services. We do not want some mishap to darken this glorious day."

2dda340c-e99c-4b8d-aa12-92af2489d2f7.Text: {n}Astartia frowns and adds peevishly,{/n} "I asked the esteemed Abelard to put me to some important task too, but he bid me to attend the reception, where I can do nothing to serve Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

e7426623-c7c8-43a0-ac1c-fe1058f5c9bf.Text: {n}Young Gaprak keeps staring at Astartia curiously and a little bashfully. It seems the boy likes her.{/n}

cf420c6b-fc30-4391-b440-9adfb78d7da3.Text: {n}Sauerback smirks.{/n} "If I had known, I too would have asked Abelard to let you miss the party."

83779ecb-9f7b-48e1-a34d-a7b94a916a8a.Text: {n}Astartia flushes and starts talking quickly and with fire in her voice — it would seem that she finds work-related conversations far more interesting than court gossip.{/n} "Of course! I've been working on a project for the last four years. We could set up—"

c0cf427f-8626-4319-9f21-9ff811d3092c.Text: "Enough, Astartia. I highly doubt that {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} is interested in listening to the fantasies of a young woman about how to run {mf|his|her} protectorate."

a2ec178d-cde7-41e2-b391-36007738aa7a.Text: {n}Abelard shoots Drivestem a glare so dark and bloodthirsty that the latter instinctively starts looking for the nearest warden.{/n}

a998e475-d0d3-4c5c-ad22-9b2b1bf021b7.Text: "Absolutely, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We greatly respect him for his wisdom, and he repays us with attention and kindness," {n}she says warmly.{/n}

f10c2390-9b03-4351-b6cb-30cbe2ac0f65.Text: "I am... obliged, dear Astartia." {n}It looks like Abelard is somewhat embarrassed by the turn this conversion has taken.{/n}

1eb1829e-d215-458d-9540-bd2c654df604.Text: "Absolutely, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We greatly respect him for his wisdom, and he repays us with attention and kindness," {n}she says warmly, but then her voice takes on an accusing tone.{/n} "I wish others appreciated him as much as we do. It was a terrible blow to my esteemed forebear when he was ordered to leave your retinue."

9415314b-5a2a-4aff-be31-7e0dedcb2010.Text: {n}Governor Drivestem hisses quietly and menacingly,{/n} "If you think, girl, that you are entitled to dispute the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}'s orders, then your family has been allowed to live in liberty for too long."

0b59f9de-ceb4-4dc0-bd39-dadac9c97002.Text: {n}Heartened, Astartia continues in the tone of a seasoned {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} clerk,{/n} "Our suggestion is to set up a chain of stations in the void — plasma beacons that would signal the passing ships. By placing them in logistically sound locations, we could simplify our ships' routes so that they may split long {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} jumps into a series of safer, shorter jumps from one beacon to another. This would have a positive effect on the overall safety of journeys and the accessibility of colonies."
