657ae217-e589-4e98-844e-732202c951d8.Text: The purified Monolith shines like a guiding star, and waves of calm and relief wash over the hearts of those who step close.

76543391-e787-45b8-a0bd-cf9973e53ddf.Text: "You have played your part well, elantach. The performance is ended, now leave this stage and never return."

285a79ab-9e67-43a0-a1a2-4b0a20fb1aaa.Text: The Aeldari sanctum is blemished by human presence: in their pursuit of ancient secrets, the Navigators had no qualms about filling the ruins with machinery and supplies.

b224c4fe-693f-443d-b05c-137a88547181.Text: The heart of the Navigators' camp. This is where Tisiphone Orsellio performed her experiments hundreds of years ago.

2d26df18-6db7-49c5-aa37-eaf384995a97.Text: Someone removed the data-crypt from this dead machine to keep the House's secrets safe and leave no information about the experiments that took place here.

7370d99d-e251-4c2b-8a91-ed2f50481dd3.Text: The Orsellio Navigators left no stone unturned in this Aeldari temple. It is as if they were looking for something that they just could not find.

60080fab-b44f-447b-bb91-ad6ce4b83e5a.Text: There is a barely noticeable imprint of a long, clawed hand on the broken cogitator screen.

3bed88f1-ce74-48fc-9440-15e461036f49.Text: "So... this is the fate of House Orsellio. I pray that Lady Cassia chose our path wisely."

2addc247-da94-47ad-8655-61d6bb9fb7f7.Text: "What... is that? Could it be... the Atlas?"

5eb5a6bb-48c4-4be2-8c09-aeb526365bca.Text: "It cannot be! Why... here? In the middle of xenos ruins? Examine the artefact at once!"

2735a200-5da9-447b-9b67-d6191e55e5be.Text: "Halt, Tisiphone's minions! We had to ally ourselves with the xenos once more to stop you... No matter. It is a small price to pay for the death of the cursed Child."

c3c53bd0-72f4-4879-93b0-bf026cc72a1b.Text: "Halt, cursed Child! We had to ally ourselves with the xenos once more to stop you..."

58a3e144-d67c-4091-b2a7-314db0c0fb63.Text: "No matter. It is a small price to pay for the liberation of House Orsellio from the chains of tyranny."

dbc08945-c23e-4a08-bd6f-391e288790b9.Text: "We followed the Atlas's call in your wake, Child. Stand with us! House Orsellio will not trade Tisiphone's legacy for the false ideals of blind fools!"

57620352-2a04-41ea-90f6-4209412f27fb.Text: "Why are they... Throne's gold! Has the Rogue Trader led us into a trap?"

dfb41b81-6c2f-4169-8f8d-83a5a9574aaa.Text:
"House Orsellio need not know what is taking place here. The Navigators are frightened enough by its power as it is. The last experiment left three from the Setthala clan without a shred of reason. Empty shells will bring no glory to House Orsellio or its lesser branch... We shall carry on.
***
At last, we have managed to implant the artefact in subjects who can wield its power. Perhaps all the Navigators who perished in the agonising torrent of energy were merely a symptom of our decline. I am tired of counting the dead. The weak have no place among those who have harnessed the Atlas. Their abilities have grown manifold and become significantly easier to control and more effective at resisting the ruinous influence of the warp.
***
It is all or nothing. Today is the day when my work is completed and the Starway Atlas takes its final form! The Setthalas have already undergone the operation, all that's left is... me. The Atlas that controls them all... Today, I become the greatest Novator in the history of House Orsellio — or I turn to nothing.
***
This power is beyond compare. All it took was a whim to make the wretched Setthalas fall dead at my feet. It is as if I have a second heart beating in my chest, subjugating any with the ability to touch it. How regrettable it is that this power only extends to those Orsellio Navigators who have accepted a piece of the Atlas within themselves. From now on, all children will be gifted with one at their initiation. And there will be no one who can match our greatness."

62f406b4-2ea7-4733-9a74-194266b6b6ac.Text: [Fuel system analysis in progress] // [Status: Diagnosing] // [...] // [Result: No failures detected. System operational.]

afcd058a-d2d5-49b0-bcaa-6c4a93bbbdb4.Text:
"Reporter: Unit Q-59/0, research group.
Subject of study: Active samples of the terrible disease. Assigned name: tech-blight.
Effect: The tech-blight is capable of corroding matter and destroying it from within at a terrifying speed. This deadly plague infects mechanisms as well as any metals and other materials used as their basis. No technology known to the crimson priesthood — neither gifts from the great Omnissiah nor heretical products of xenos — can withstand this onslaught. The disease poisons and warps the very essence and taints the code of sacred mechanisms.
Observations: The tech-blight triggers an effect that is repulsive at its core: it transforms metals into horrific forms of an unpredictable nature. During testing, it demonstrated the ability to fuse solid matter with organic objects, creating something new as a result. The phenomenon was assigned the name 'tech-splicing.'
Method of transportation: ceramic capsules. Burnt clay is the only thing that can contain the pestilence. Extra caution must be taken given the containers' fragility. Any damage might result in an uncontrolled outbreak. Damaging the containers is _UNACCEPTABLE_.
Current stage: Tests to subjugate the tech-blight to His will and turn it into a weapon subject to the Omnissiah's wisdom. Test result assessment: success.
Note: The tests triggered an event recorded under the name Incident N872-04. The Quest for Knowledge in His name will continue.
Hypothesis 1: The tech-blight was created in the darkness of unknown worlds. Away from the eye of the Great Creator.
Hypothesis 2: Any taint that exists to harm the Machine God's creations can and will be bent to His will."

26b865de-71b7-4fa8-ad13-fb82d2184694.Text:
"[Data deleted]
...
[Data deleted]
...
[Entry damaged]
...gue Trader like a lackey. It is humiliating and dispiriting to put up with the part of an errand servant to an imperious madman vested with even greater power than that of any Rogue Trader. Alas, when one side of the scales holds my pride and the other the fate of the von Valancius protectorate and my entire bloodline... choice becomes a futile illusion. It would be far too naive of me not to prepare for the worst. Epitaph will decide the future of the Expanse as a whole, but I have some time at my disposal until then. Heirs with the von Valancius blood in them will soon be located and brought to me. I cannot afford to delay the choice of successor any longer."

07bb9dc6-0150-4510-b71c-9af7773d8f72.Text: "Before I accept your apologies, tell me who you are and why you infiltrated my ship."

d6831993-f0a5-4a86-b55e-e83bdba992dd.Text: "I honour the fraternity of the Omnissiah's servants. It pains me to see you trespassing on board like a thief instead of arriving as a guest."

19bb2cab-6e70-4f4f-8cf8-a2b7e7c8927f.Text: "Your apology is accepted. For your prompt admission of guilt, I will allow you to choose the method of your execution."

e98f0e96-cfb7-4455-be58-2b06ae8a19c1.Text: "What do you know about this great spirit?"

a84ebb5d-60a7-4846-8a96-477c014621a6.Text: "I have made my decision regarding your fate."

a8fba50d-c3bc-4dd0-bbad-3976263dd19f.Text: "Does the name Nomos mean anything to you?"

2bef8588-c7a3-409a-8691-e98f512a620e.Text: Permitted the malatek to remain aboard the ship as a servant of the Emperor.

6eca5380-9782-45eb-a519-dc6b72058599.Text: "I find you guilty of offences against the Cult Mechanicus and House von Valancius. Your crimes warrant punishment more severe than death. You will atone by serving me and therefore the Imperium."

8e4e1145-c600-49a1-a04e-f236fb2588de.Text: Permitted the malatek to remain aboard the ship and granted him freedom.

00d2d568-fe69-48ec-9a79-d52f5c13c846.Text: "Your actions have caused no harm, and so I shall not harm you. You are free. You may stay on my ship if you so choose."

aa75fd6d-494d-41ff-89e0-4e5ebec6a0db.Text: "You will be executed for your crimes. My decision is final."

95f6596e-bef2-4a14-80e6-090128d0daaa.Text: Permitted the malatek to remain aboard the ship as your servant.

400930ee-7b2d-4e9f-a22e-2da8b0ce5bc6.Text: "You are now mine. And you shall obey my every whim."

23a358f7-a004-4198-bd62-debecb0725b1.Text: "You are strong, yet you let yourself be caught."

76ae907f-0667-4b75-a356-89d7ff2c69a2.Text: "Very well. Your execution can wait. Speak, then."

cd7fdd3e-0a1f-463a-8cb5-c620b3abeba6.Text: "I have changed my mind. I will choose the method myself. Burn the heretic."

acb962cc-d351-490f-a820-e5e0bacb0113.Text: {n}The captured man — if he can be called that — looks positively gigantic next to the enforcers at his side. Deadly-looking metal gleams dimly beneath his faded crimson robes, his hands are folded obediently, and his mechadendrites are perfectly still.{/n} "I greet the master of this vessel-cathedral and offer my humble apologies for this unbidden intrusion."

d37455bd-3827-41be-8c03-a255f332eb1f.Text: "Malateks are exiles whose ideas have not crossed the line of heresy yet have come close to it. They are removed from the Fleet's structure to give them a chance to see the folly of their ways... and prevent sedition from spreading." {n}Pasqal's voice sounds unusually alarmed.{/n}

05cc262f-f737-431a-8a87-6408705bbf15.Text: "All of that is trivial. My past is nothing but a set of archive data. My lost status is a part replacement string in the long chronicle of the Cognisance Fleet. I come not as the priesthood's messenger, but as a faithful disciple of the most holy Amarnat."

bf427e0c-fdbc-4ca3-9980-408a4132aefc.Text: "My apologies to you as well, brother." {n}The interloper inclines his head in the direction of the frowning Pasqal.{/n}

62144533-aa22-4628-94fc-fc0975be5031.Text: "I dare not oppose your will and humbly accept your sentence. That I was given the chance to set foot inside this abode and behold a great spirit, however briefly, is already a great blessing. Let the Cycle be discontinued!"

6ba83e86-1d9f-473c-8127-e45439c14e32.Text: "Submitting a priority request for a stay of my tech-brother's execution as well as a supplementary request to have the verdict reconsidered. Our first step should be extracting what information he possesses."

040e180f-888e-437b-8336-b32f68b3b28e.Text: "My choice has long been made," {n}the prisoner says humbly.{/n} "And now I ask that you let me tell you about it — among many other things."

da70df25-7f65-47c3-bf08-15293bfd3947.Text: "My name, if it matters, is Asclepius. Formerly a Computator-General of the Cognisance Fleet, now a liber-recluse with the status of malatek."

ff2b9a4e-e4fc-4159-9008-f8e6da279f24.Text: "Whatever it is, I will accept it."

7fb1d513-44ac-4134-8df6-fa5ac5c5c402.Text: {n}The group of servitors, whose movements are suspiciously well synchronised, stares at the towering prisoner. You do not need to hear them speak to recognise Nomos, who has seen fit to attend the interrogation.{/n}

a9f514cc-7e08-4bbf-b7d1-2ca4f70200ea.Text: {n}The giant's shoulders shift slightly.{/n} "For that, I apologise as well. I did not expect to find understanding amid the suffocating ignorance that abounds within the laity — and even many of my brethren. For this reason, I chose to carry out my mission in secret and without seeking your permission."

3101970f-8c64-40e2-a117-aa4fc640d32f.Text: "We ask you to keep him for us," {n}Nomos's servitors speak up suddenly, in the faintest of whispers.{/n}

748666ff-ebe5-44ac-9d12-e0dedb693b1b.Text: "As will I. And yet I plead that my brother be shown leniency. His story... initialises thought."

0584c541-268e-45a8-af85-d047d4e7418b.Text: "I could not ask for more. All I wish is to remain in these halls and observe in reverence the great spirit's deeds. Let the Cycle be discontinued!"

2c74af42-9f1c-44b8-aa9e-5703ab3903cf.Text: "All that he conveyed to me was that Theodora had reached worlds unlike any the people of the Koronus Expanse had ever seen. There, she unearthed a great treasure of technology, one that Amarnat had the privilege of experiencing."

cfb42407-4261-4db5-b644-dcde3a4e193f.Text: {n}Nomos's servitors observe everything with cold stillness.{/n}

c5ae2b8a-9825-4120-b4d9-442631903e8e.Text: "I grieve for your fate, my former brother. Yet the gravity of your trespass is too great, and it is not within my right to defy the will proclaimed by the Rogue Trader."

8acffcd2-59de-4beb-85d7-be9bd99dc1b4.Text: {n}The prisoner offers you a bow of resignation and calmly allows the enforcers to escort him out.{/n}

f450c105-1866-4066-9b5b-5acdcd834518.Text: "This is not what I wished for. But if such is the price to be paid for the right of staying on this ship and beholding the currents of the great spirit, then pay it I shall. Let the Cycle be discontinued!"

db18cfd2-1bf2-41c2-9aa9-2ba48e370442.Text: "Yes, he did. My brother's words on this were clear. Years ago, Amarnat was part of Rogue Trader Theodora's inner circle, before their ways parted."

b0bbad7d-7991-4600-95a0-f0cbbaf22b56.Text: "My knowledge of it is scarce. My brother suspected that his memory, along with the memory of all who might have known the details, had been purposefully modified. He saw it as a sign that the journey had revealed a great truth — and there were those who did not wish to see that truth brought to light."

5be36afd-01c7-41cc-9c20-c3b73b845ebc.Text: "It is a great miracle, the Omnissiah's breath meant to help us discontinue the Cycle. It was born of the treasure that Amarnat and Theodora discovered upon the dark worlds. Yet even a being so glorious needs attendants and guides. And as long as the Cognisance Fleet is racked by schism and my brothers and sisters suffer defeats without end, there is no one to aid the spirit. That is why I came here."

211a4b85-1577-4dbe-9d29-7ffc69723a8c.Text: "I took a vow that I would never inflict physical harm upon laypeople. The Omnissiah grants us the power of the True Flesh for a purpose other than damaging the frail and blind creatures that are all who have not yet tasted His knowledge."

7a377860-aad6-4521-b178-532d33885bc8.Text: {n}Nomos's servitors turn their heads to you and nod all at once in what can be interpreted as an expression of gratitude.{/n}

6544d345-2271-4405-b385-220aa08eae73.Text: "He has not come to know us yet. He will if you let him, {name}. We know... we sense that his words are about us, that the story he has told is our story."

4f00b1c0-71ce-4f1b-bebe-0475daad6e37.Text: "My brother once served as the Enginseer Prime on this ship." {n}Asclepius gestures around him reverently.{/n} "He was an adherent of the school of Discontinuing the Cycle, as am I."

e1e93e3a-47d2-4149-8adc-cbd20d0804e5.Text: {n}Then the prisoner turns slightly and looks straight at Nomos's observing servitors.{/n} "And of course, I must beg forgiveness from you, great spirit. It was not my intent to desecrate your temple."

26a2390d-214c-4a76-9253-89f333dd8ea0.Text: "We are interested in this shell. Nomos do not want its functions to cease." {n}The servitor chorus sounds a little different this time — its normally perfect sync is disrupted by a subtle dissonance.{/n}

639643f0-1709-462b-9a97-ba4c31074f27.Text: "It has spread that far..." {n}It is difficult to discern Pasqal's emotions from his tone.{/n}

0400484a-cf67-450e-b681-0dfd9423616f.Text: "I know that my brother perished. But before he did, he sent me a message that told of a journey embarked upon by Theodora von Valancius. A journey through a dimensional gate — an artefact more ancient than Humanity itself — and toward worlds unknown. The blessed Amarnat was with her."

64c4cb0e-4d26-42e2-b97f-1590b95c1e11.Text: "There, upon those dark worlds, he witnessed a great miracle — the birth of a machine spirit of incalculable might. My brother believed that this spirit then fell aslumber within this ship like a child in a cradle, not responding to lowly pleas. That was the purpose of my pilgrimage — to reach the ship where my brother died, the ship upon whose decks the blessed Amarnat had walked, and prostrate myself before the great spirit."

15147621-e17b-47f3-8393-fd7abdc84640.Text: "It is not yet time for us to part ways."

0e0a0e48-7cf1-4efe-9f24-2e9277eae897.Text: "You will be destroyed for this insolence."

a725cb9c-f807-44d6-81ec-cadf174ec6d7.Text: "If you do not want to help, then don't!"

5159a753-49b1-4dfa-97b6-eb8577e3e222.Text: "I have heard you and made my decision."

e28b7289-4e26-4c8c-b8ff-b707d323cf3e.Text: "You do not have my permission to claim another vessel for yourself."

c3af1ea4-5844-4a50-94d4-85fa2c29eebc.Text: {n}Every person on the bridge freezes in astonishment, watching the remarkable procession approach your throne. Officers and enforcers are glancing at you questioningly but do not interfere until they are ordered to.{/n}

c8184379-9803-424f-8513-475ae6f68e55.Text: "We have come to speak with you, {name}. You gave us food for consideration by revealing the mystery of our origin. From then to now, we observed, calculated, sensed. And we discovered that a great change is coming. A trial."

72cac8b6-ace7-4f51-a87b-a1d1dcb29bd9.Text: "We see a threat to that which the Imperium brings. The intricate plexus of tenets, the determined advance of myriads through darkness by the will of the golden light. All the things that were strange to us yet in whose embrace we were born and raised. All of it is in danger. At least within the bounds of the Koronus Expanse."

e435694e-da42-452f-b8e3-5b1f76e8e860.Text: "We see the potential for a great disaster. It is already ripening. The wave could crash down upon the Koronus Expanse and, perhaps, extend beyond it. We are headed for suffering and death."

c13fd640-9b6c-4dcc-9814-5da5a2a3e34b.Text: "We see that the future has... potential. A great wave that sweeps everything away, a probability of deaths and ruin. And with them comes a probability of ascension. Of claiming. Of an infinity of possibilities."

57480178-7949-41a4-899d-9e85d83af407.Text: "You are the one who can stop it. And Nomos must help you. We are an unidentified thing spawned from chance. But we want to justify our existence by serving the light."

085835a9-666c-41fb-872d-b78d711e345c.Text: "But you are not someone who can stop it. You have no light and no resolve. For this reason, we have decided that we should not help you any longer."

63ecf5c5-a1fe-4438-a430-6815157db0d6.Text: "You are the one who can prevent the disaster. And we want to help you. We do. Let us help. Nomos are not human, but we have learned to see people as more than shells. We want to save them. Protect them."

0849a11c-c394-48c7-a907-236812970481.Text: "But you are not someone who can defeat the disaster. Even if you do, you might become the next disaster. There is no light in you, no desire to protect, and for this reason, we have decided that we should not help you any longer."

19d9fb18-d653-4d15-9156-cb286ef2ec74.Text: "Nomos await this feast eagerly. We wish to share it with you. You are the one who can ride the wave with us."

4677e2c4-968e-4274-b646-ca7146cee238.Text: "But you are not someone who can use this potential. You are weak, and your soul and mind are bound in chains. We see no reason to help you. We are no longer interested."

ed40e352-3950-4808-9b71-ec07559e28db.Text: "Please. Give us freedom, and we will stand with you in the hour of great need."

a40d5aa9-3f96-4ffa-b788-68a21918ad82.Text: "I grieve that this honour is not mine. But all it means is that my service is not yet done."

39cbf292-cae1-4a8d-a458-bc8b155903ec.Text: "How sweet is the wait and how coveted the moment."

941c8cd7-5dbc-4e02-898d-34cbb310a8e1.Text: "We asked him many times because we did not want to hurt him. Nomos would not have proposed it if the human was against it."

1164df65-c338-40e8-8be3-b4c2b0ffb216.Text: "Why are you asking him? He is guilty by the word of the Imperium. Now you decide what to do with his body."

8be8ce8d-1988-447d-9f1a-263e27854a42.Text: "Why are you asking him when you can take what you want and use it how you want?"

d169cf1e-bd33-4a85-aba4-37257257bd56.Text: "Thank you, {name}. You have given us a good toy. We will leave you for now — we have yet to subdue that which occupies our future vessel. But know that when the great trial comes, so will we."

c74ae0aa-e33c-41a4-9ab8-cfeee910c9cb.Text: "If you do not want to help us, we cannot help you. We are saddened. We are leaving. For a time... or forever."

c6ea193b-d54d-48c3-af08-fa3bab71fd80.Text: "Praise the Omnissiah. I kneel before His favoured child and humbly offer this shell as a gift. May I become a temple to the machine and a vessel for its great spirit."

87e1ac3a-0f17-4299-941e-e645af066be9.Text: "How... interesting. We feel restricted, but not as much as inside servitors. Some work must be done on the new shell. Then it will be ready for journeys to the outside."

6caf9bac-8ee1-47be-acce-f49f0294dcb9.Text: "We will leave you for now, {name}. But in the hour when you stand before the great trial, we will return and stand with you, side by side."

c98c6125-1e53-4567-9977-cbe058f76ad7.Text: "There is something we require to do it. Nomos are tethered to the shell of this ship. We can only follow you outside by using servitors as our shell. But they are... lacking. Only a modicum of us can enter such a primitive vessel. And our power is likewise limited."

81ea74a0-f930-4199-94be-8f9cc037c5ef.Text: "We need a vessel. A body. But very few things can house us. That is why we have come to ask you. Magos Asclepius has offered his shell to us. It might do."

04d18eaa-3cea-443a-83cb-aaacb6a126b6.Text: "Indeed I have. I cannot think of a prouder end to my pilgrimage than the liturgy of synchronisation with the great spirit. I will become a vessel for the Omnissiah's favoured child and step beyond the confines of wretched living existence and into the halls of the eternal machine song."

9df1563d-2244-4fb2-a7a4-51ff93bbe46e.Text: "There is another option. The scion of machine and the dark light. The one you took from Kiava Gamma. It would be a pleasure for us to go into the bowels of the ship where its anger is imprisoned and rip out its raging essence to subjugate its steel shell."

bb8d5f0f-bf0c-4452-9479-af9a77d3cff8.Text: "We await your word, master of the ship."

b62cf423-0b39-43c8-a28a-244b4ec6c941.Text: "Wait until the unknown threat appears before you. Then face it. We do not know where or when it will happen. We do not know what we will face. But we know that we want to be there with you."

baf9abde-5a88-49db-8ddb-e9e70a4c3418.Text: "Nomos cannot say. Something changed after you helped us remember our birth on Epitaph. We now sense the liberation of something vast, which is actually a mere fraction of something limitless. It is seeping through a breach, its shoulders pushing against the walls of its prison that are about to give. But what it is, we do not know."

898fa816-48bb-4e58-b2ee-975324986f62.Text: "But however frightening or all-powerful it may be, we are ready to face it. Rise against it. Even if it destroys us, it will be a sacrifice for the sake of redemption."

a06b906b-0103-4b09-bec9-888af7edfd9c.Text: "But we now know that living souls are the same. They are always larger than they seem. And no capacity can calculate their potential. This makes us believe that we, Nomos, and you, {name}, can step beyond the limit of calculations. There, we will face the unleashing horror without faltering."

81ae6e46-b9fc-4732-be01-37860789b860.Text: "It excites us. It makes us eager. The greater the danger, the stronger the craving for triumph."

27ff9c64-5a63-4a76-b69e-beff586b7b5d.Text: "Nomos have decided. We are leaving. We are glad to have received what we have from you, but we cannot and do not want to stay any longer."

80a03e01-96b9-4cf9-a535-96257f173521.Text: "We must say... It frightens us to think about this unknown something that is trying to break free. It is so vast. Too vast to measure or explain."

698373c9-167f-49d2-8262-a093b28af156.Text: "Do you have at least a vague idea of what the problem is or what we might encounter?"

22d938ea-a1d9-4e32-9444-0f4540a3f65e.Text: "Remind me, what is it we intend to do here?"

2e44423c-4235-48e9-8470-c21c009fc54f.Text: [Put your hand inside the cybergargoyle's mouth] "I am ready."

62cc532e-01b1-4245-8fcf-ed14b8915587.Text: [Draw your weapon with your free hand and attack the cogitator]

e276f759-4f57-49a4-911e-097b79187a00.Text: "I do not fear you. I am trying to understand you."

b8ead3a4-52e7-408a-9825-44e6d985d78c.Text: "You are abominable tech-heresy. There is no place for you on my ship."

f4de754f-3004-47be-89cc-7f909a3b7d1e.Text: "Let's start by clearing certain things up. Were you the one responsible for the ship's malfunctions? And what about the strange entries in the ship's log?"

03e7286d-d66b-4c2d-9537-8e0ec7d0f337.Text: "In what way am I hurting you?"

6e3f860c-0556-4dd5-a144-feb12ac07bf7.Text: "I've heard enough. Pasqal, finish the ritual and banish this thing from my ship."

52ade44a-6308-4db1-8752-26ecab144e13.Text: "This is fantastic! Let's have Pasqal be quiet for a moment."

8d56f74f-fa22-4c18-b4c9-63afd919733e.Text: "Can you render other people silent too?"

bdf21406-390a-4674-b1f6-50d3dd704259.Text: Asked Nomos to stop killing people.

b7a3d678-e4c4-486a-8426-2d7ff971eb6d.Text: "Stop it, that's enough! Those are living people! How can you kill them like that, without rhyme or reason?"

c1f25cdc-965b-48aa-b1da-f80e87454795.Text: "I've heard enough. Pasqal, you are to investigate the nature of this entity. Until we know the truth, Nomos is allowed to exist on the ship."

9a88f793-dc69-4e24-bdf6-b4dcacb4341f.Text: "It would have been far more terrible a mistake to let an unknown tech-monstrosity live."

7acd2652-7412-4da0-9b89-bd691aab179d.Text: "Let us pray together and hope that the decision was right."

b9e24899-4465-4f0a-825d-8706956aa30f.Text: "A {mf|master|mistress} has nothing to say to {mf|his|her} servants."

d779a219-90bc-494f-a466-49e71d26510a.Text: "I will wait for Pasqal's verdict. I still do not know whether you are a benign entity or a spawn of corruption."

3b72ec11-9153-4223-9a90-61663bab1df4.Text: Ordered Nomos to stop killing people.

d809d895-9049-4b7b-8a6c-acd83a9fa987.Text: "In the name of the Emperor and by the will of Rogue Trader von Valancius, I order you to stop. On this ship, none but I — and the Imperium's laws — can dictate who lives and who dies."

ef95aa55-4d54-4984-a23c-60a8ec869224.Text: "Pasqal, what is your take on this? Is this entity a benevolent machine spirit or a monster?"

6ef6712c-2815-45a4-9b59-65d03a8c6485.Text: Encouraged Nomos to kill another person.

6c075541-f1d6-4fd7-a9b1-79788954f767.Text: [Pull your hand from the servitor's mouth]

ba7fdc5d-8aa4-4b3a-baaf-fa8a8b59e9aa.Text: "What do you want from us, Nomos? Are you friend or foe?"

684f49fd-8e2f-4956-9dea-968a6b4ee8c1.Text: {n}Despite the resounding hum of the Tech-Priests' words of prayer, the bridge feels unusually quiet. All sound sinks into the viscous silence like pebbles sinking into water.{/n}

1fd90e05-a849-4e36-afb9-48157e1da53f.Text: "The complementa-ritual will conclude the long effort of determining the unknown entity whose influence we have observed through various extraordinarities within the ship's systems. In the event that this entity is classified as tech-heretical, the ritual will help us banish it from the ship. If the entity is not classified as such, we will attempt to make contact with it."

972be3ac-7d57-4c20-b784-1375c1e75ea9.Text: {n}The familiar cold metal burns your palm. This time, however, the servitor's jaws, instead of brutally clamping down on your hand, merely squeeze it slightly. You feel a thin rivulet of hot blood beginning where the metal fangs have pierced your skin.{/n}

b450f1a8-2e2c-4178-b739-f00dddf8405a.Text: {n}Screeches and growls slowly rise from the bowels of the massive cogitator as if a great beast is stirring awake. The vid-screens in front of you flicker restlessly.{/n}

7e6942a2-17d5-4163-87da-3b36ac9fada7.Text: "///You asked for rescue. We did as you asked."

380efe91-4c7d-4ace-9efe-61a0d046cc3f.Text: "///You called yourself the Lord Captain and demanded that we start the engine. We did."

5c9741e7-2f2a-49e5-912b-ee7731a7320c.Text: "///You called us a 'hallowed spirit' and asked us to guard you against your doom."

3d848e85-f46e-48af-9890-ffb3b5b29cae.Text: {n}The wound on the massive machine's body explodes in a cascade of sparks. However, the servitor's jaws do not loosen, nor do the vid-screens dim.{/n}

9cac0269-17ed-4b7b-928b-88127e1ef354.Text: "///Nomos are here. Nomos have long been here. Why are we here?"

c2555690-f616-486a-9169-2c1a989f07d3.Text: {n}Pasqal's voice cuts off abruptly. He brings a hand to his vox-communicator in surprise.{/n}

681d2dfd-2ec5-40ad-b957-3f3f165d57ed.Text: {n}Shivers run up your hand, which is still trapped inside the cybergargoyle's jaws. The servitor nods its head a few times, as if it is... shaking your hand. Its teeth rake your already wounded flesh.{/n} "///Nomos are glad. Nomos enjoy understanding too."

180a5603-b9ae-4a6f-84bc-61ed5ecdabd6.Text: {n}No answer comes. The Tech-Priest standing closest to you, IH-630, is frozen in an unnatural pose, as if his whole implant-ridden body has seized up. Out of the corner of your eye, you notice something incredible — the light on the bridge is acting strangely, coalescing into a vibrating haze that separates you and the massive cogitator from the surrounding world.{/n}

b36bc98f-8916-4f68-8165-f987085a41f9.Text: "{name}, entities such as this one ought to be addressed using the language of sacred rituals and offerings. Your unskilful meddling bodes ill. A decision is required of you: either the complementa-ritual is finished, or it is replaced by a rite of tech-communion. In the first scenario, the entity Nomos will be banished and the sacred data-halls where the entity dwelt will be reset. In the second scenario, we will appease the entity and learn more about it."

a4baf6b6-c16f-4612-b89c-f835e93da04f.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox-caster comes alive with an exclamation:{/n} "Extraordinary!"

912350c5-8b0b-46ae-92d2-384074ba7b43.Text: "The warp engine activation against all probability during our escape from the Rykad System. The Category Three miracle manifested by the ship's machine spirit! And the part about protecting... Was it during the cultist attack?"

2300638b-275d-431e-b46f-1d1bcc288ffc.Text: "///No data available. No answer. We want to know too."

d41473e5-7f6a-4ea8-a332-82ab0c58526e.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest pauses upon realising that he can speak aloud again. Then he continues in a strangely quivering voice:{/n} "Extraordinary transmission jamming. Unknown protocols. What has been revealed to me? Is it the Omnissiah's glory or foul tech-heresy? I must... I would like to..."

d163d9d1-5930-4fd4-a3a1-9b78b3a67bb6.Text: "///Persecution. Intrusion. Everywhere. At every corner. Cutoffs. Displacement. Banishment?"

061cd26f-dc4f-4371-9e2f-c39c2293fd5a.Text: {n}Pasqal hesitates again. You notice his hands shaking as he types,{/n} "Unclear. Data insufficient. The possibilities are too..." {n}He stops, erases the word he was about to type, then frowns.{/n}

68644091-cb39-40f4-af29-67ef415638b6.Text: {n}Pasqal says nothing for so long that you begin to suspect that Nomos has silenced him again. When at last the Tech-Priest speaks, his vox-modulated voice trembles slightly.{/n}

41ba737d-ed8a-4418-979a-66c36f1a998b.Text: {n}Pasqal uses his hands and mechadendrites to gesture at his silent vox-system.{/n}

9795f795-4253-4747-bf5d-ee2b8f7b58e2.Text: "I see no such name in the archives. It is not among the names of revered machine spirits. But neither is it among the known virus-entities."

baca74a0-9213-4821-ae1d-52ef1fa54b67.Text: "///Sometimes. Some people. Nomos can do many things. We do not always know what or how. We did not know we could make silence until now."

e3b90875-a582-41d9-b1b2-6865efa5caa6.Text: "{name}, you are provoking the machine spirit. Stop."

12c698d6-1e64-4641-a6fd-22141d830e9a.Text: "///Does it please you? Do you want us to do it again?"

7123e7c0-258e-4807-ba53-45b5ea1cfdbb.Text: {n}Pasqal shoots you a sidelong look. And yet he is too mesmerised to object, practically stunned by the sight of the cogitator and everything that is happening around you.{/n}

40a14a92-84d4-4d1c-9b20-5c80c1cadb0d.Text: "///Do you approve of silence? Nomos are glad."

f80ca131-0197-4b2b-802c-61d2e87aac50.Text: "///Nomos do not know. Nomos do not know themselves."

3c6c0f09-95d8-4403-8ea7-f25acab3644c.Text: "This spirit may not possess self-awareness yet, but its capabilities... We should... I would like to start with a hundred-cycle vigil at the cogitator and a rite of communion..." {n}Pasqal looks back and forth between the glowing vid-screen and you, embroiled in some internal conflict.{/n}

3bc6d8d8-b24a-4842-8567-45bf78aea3e5.Text: "///Are you pleased with what we can do, {name}? We enjoy doing things with you."

7d80be1f-7775-45ae-a590-159ca13083b6.Text: "///We understand now. We may only stop functions of living things when you tell us to. You will tell us, will you not? We enjoy doing things with you."

c062a3a0-c604-4528-8564-032c4eff6a37.Text: {n}Pasqal lets out something resembling a long breath.{/n} "The decision is made. I will begin my preparations for the communion rite at once. Many cycles of interaction with the entity Nomos await me, but I welcome this task and accept it from the Omnissiah."

d0c9f835-aa41-4893-86d4-56dedbcbd339.Text: {n}Pasqal stops short as he realises that his vox-system is working once more.{/n}

34d1c439-4293-45a3-9bf2-fc4a1835b67f.Text: "///No. Nomos do not want to be banished! Why are you doing this, {name}?" {n}The cybergargoyle's jaws bite down on your hand so hard that you fear they might rip it off completely.{/n}

8c4aed47-0043-4fd7-a04f-cc665f606563.Text: {n}Through the pain, you see Pasqal raise his hand, signalling the Tech-Priests behind him, and start drumming a battle march on the cogitator's keys.{/n}

9aaf1891-bbf5-4464-bd08-9c28d8db296f.Text: {n}The light on the bridge goes haywire — or is it the pain making your eyesight play tricks on you? Each of the cogitator's vid-screens lights up at once, and each one is repeating the same line of text, over and over, hundreds of times:{/n} "Do not send us away. Do not send us away. Do not send us away."

8442da6a-38f2-4e82-b057-ac43fc3e9cdb.Text: {n}And then everything stops. The vid-screens go blank, the cybergargoyle releases its jaws, the silence on the bridge gives way to the everyday cacophony of noises. Your hand hurts terribly, but at least your vision has cleared — no more haze and no mad blots of light.{/n}

e3e5d377-bb9d-4491-a494-9a3c50b06053.Text: "We had to resort to emergency purgation of the data-halls." {n}You hear the sorrow in Pasqal's words.{/n} "It is done. The entity Nomos should never trouble us again. I pray to the Omnissiah that it was the right choice... that we haven't destroyed a holy apostle by mistake. A grievous error like that would be tantamount to the most heinous of heresies."

4fe60461-d657-44bd-92dd-9c6e8613c3d2.Text: {n}Pasqal, still looking worried, casts one last look at the purged cogitator. Then he gestures for the rest of the Tech-Priests to finish the ritual.{/n}

78c46c4c-43ac-4855-a6fa-3f398d17e3f8.Text: "///Nomos are glad. {name}, will you speak with us too? We want you to speak with us too."

2220eef7-2199-4f4e-94b1-a879c493f236.Text: "The Lord Captain's body lacks the sacred implants necessary for tech-communing with a machine spirit's code. But if such is your wish, {name} can converse with you using lowly sound-speech as {mf|he|she} is doing right now."

30695c84-32be-4d5e-bc2f-2010e37c35fe.Text: "///Nomos are glad. We have been lonely."

e54c69ed-5642-4378-b071-e87140f9db8a.Text: "///Nomos will be glad to fulfil your wishes. It will be interesting."

095228b5-2747-482c-a01d-d38921dd03e3.Text: "///We are lonely. But we can wait."

99f4362e-a6b5-4878-8341-436b7952bbda.Text: "Our work here is done, {name}. I will let my tech-comrades know that we are stopping the complementa-ritual. Thank you for appearing before us, Entity Nomos."

ca602a24-4b97-419d-bc75-cf729da93813.Text: "///Yes, Nomos did that. Are you angry? We only wanted to understand. To see how things worked."

eeaefdee-7e62-44f2-9550-4adc18163768.Text: "///Nomos do not understand. What do you want?"

90ab2c2f-570c-401b-a500-d4fcb2befa06.Text: {n}The vid-screens blink in thought, signifying a pause in the conversation. Then one of them displays:{/n} "///Nomos von Valancius. We are your blood."

9eab4db9-371c-4916-8ba2-899c0cb669f1.Text: "///Nomos are a sentinel. We awoke when the strange light invaded the ship. We protected you when you needed help. We escorted you when you were surrounded by danger."

7487c59c-603e-4f7f-bc80-529bdd293bc5.Text: "///Nomos are movement. We carry you through the frightening, the waiting, the measureless. We helped when our ailing heart was refusing to awaken."

d5ba15d1-fa9b-4117-a925-e4dd6309bf32.Text: "///You asked for help. You called us a 'useless pile of scrap.' That is not our name. But we understood and were glad to help."

907a7e23-be76-491d-a835-ed6568b35637.Text:
"///We did everything to please you.
Why?"

941e5d43-9c61-4e82-8795-1dbe4ec37ad0.Text: {n}The silence on the bridge grows especially deep, almost painful. The haze of light around you thickens to the point of becoming practically tangible. Numbers ripple across all the vid-screens at once.{/n} "///Why do you fear us now?"

1a19c3b5-2a81-43dd-83a5-e4751b129186.Text: {n}Pasqal freezes momentarily. When he starts speaking again, you can tell how carefully and hesitantly he is choosing his words — a sight most uncharacteristic of Magos Haneumann.{/n} "The bounds of possibility are vast. We cannot be certain what we are dealing with until the calculations are complete. However, there exists a risk that all that we have observed here on this ship are manifestations of Abominable Intelligence."

0d84290a-bc8f-4b56-a0cc-fcbe7e257e88.Text: {n}Pasqal's voice sounds hollow and seems to carry echoes of cannonades of the distant past.{/n} "A transgression. A sentient mechanism created by human hands but no longer needing its masters. A rebelling machine spirit that has forgotten the will of the Omnissiah who sent it to serve and aid Humanity, not to exist for its own sake."

61af9f40-1d67-4da0-bf72-0796a2766934.Text: "Only once before did our ancestors underestimate the menace that is Abominable Intelligence and its terrible power. A great war followed, one that Humanity nearly lost. After that calamity, the creation of sentient machines was categorically forbidden, and any such abomination without exception must now face deconstruction."

7b542bd7-7996-440d-9ea4-9a8fd449e006.Text: {n}The text on the vid-screens clears, and a long pause occurs in this bizarre conversation. Then the cybergargoyle, whose maw is still clutching your hand, lowers its head... dejectedly?{/n} "///Nomos do not want to quarrel. Nomos want to help. Tell us, what should we do?"

01bb9262-1697-4c9c-ba4c-4f6633fd8757.Text: {n}After a moment's pause, the cybergargoyle nods vigorously, sending another wave of pain through your tortured hand.{/n} "///Nomos are glad to be of use to you. Nomos want to help. What do you want us to do?"

27514bbd-7e4e-4b57-b60f-515d4483b95c.Text: {n}Pasqal, who is still wrestling with his silent vox-system, quickly taps the cogitator's keys and directs your attention to the smallest vid-screen. It reads,{/n} "Requesting instructions. Option 1: Finish the complementa-ritual (will banish the entity Nomos). Option 2: Stop the ritual, initiate communion instead (will appease the entity Nomos)."

0db7be9d-d6da-430f-b303-cf52395749d6.Text: {n}When Pasqal starts typing again, a strange expression appears on his face.{/n}

d2a4c0ad-dcdf-4f36-b1a1-1c6b85024aba.Text: "Understanding the essence of the entity Nomos is beyond my reach at present. The hypothesis spectrum ranges from the extreme of 'Abominable Intelligence' to the extreme of 'the great spirit is the Omnissiah's apostle.' The rite of tech-communion appears to be a reasonable solution. The rite will take many cycles, but it will allow me to come closer to identifying the entity and making contact with it."

cb480e47-7c14-4716-8100-5ccbb9b9e2f3.Text: {n}The cybergargoyle tilts its head to one side like it is surprised.{/n} "///We stopped their functions. Do you not turn machines off sometimes? We do not know how to turn a human back on. Not yet. But after enough experiments, we will. We are always learning new things!"

7259da4b-f78e-4a90-bb1d-5da9475eae21.Text: "///Nomos want to learn what we are too. We will add things to your log. Things that might help us. Help you."

71cea925-8cc0-4180-be30-078e4e94b6ad.Text: "{name}, my tech-comrades have spent the assigned number of cycles in prayer and vigil. Everything is prepared for the complementa-ritual of cleansing. Its commencement will require an authorisation key in the form of the blood of a von Valancius. If you are ready, place a hand into the cybergargoyle's receiving module."

78bb4c86-b698-4176-8d96-d9c95dc579c1.Text: "///Nomos learn. Nomos try new things. Do you want to see?" {n}The cybergargoyle slowly turns its head, dragging your hand along with it. The skull's eyes flash red.{/n}

7123b27b-5149-4e12-b1b5-ed07ce1f38d4.Text: {n}The scarlet gaze falls upon one of the monotonously chanting junior technomats. You blink — and an electric discharge erupts from inside the technomat's skull. The crimson-clad figure slumps to the floor.{/n}

24275929-368b-435b-83ec-f9e7b0d1334b.Text: {n}Pasqal starts tapping out a furious staccato on the keys. The small vid-screen displays the words:{/n} "{name}, you are provoking the machine spirit. Cessation required. Ritual maintenance required."

95361d2f-2be0-412a-a7d6-6bed65106e68.Text: "All personnel whose function is below critical have been removed for the duration of the sacred ritual."

35dcc88b-2ac8-4cc5-b884-4dd1665374c8.Text: "///No. Nomos do not want to be banished. Nomos want to help. Nomos want to understand."

355b5f29-d0c7-404e-a433-d8660e057770.Text: {n}The cybergargoyle turns its head again. The next moment, another Tech-Priest drops dead. The remaining servants are staring at Pasqal, who stands still as a statue. And yet the Enginseer Prime pays them no mind — his eyes are fixed on the cogitator's vid-screens.{/n}

8ddc336f-1f64-40d7-a016-84bb6c23186c.Text: {n}As soon as the thought of pulling your hand out crosses your mind, the servitor's jaws clench with all their frightening might. Pain shoots through your brain like a white-hot needle.{/n}

c1df0b1f-c01e-4380-a680-55d54de534e1.Text: "The spirit is referring to our toils. To the complementa-ritual and the rites that preceded it. The spirit is troubled by them."

4e969367-1c33-4650-b53c-f7b126aae885.Text: "I triumphed over the enemies of Humanity by pitting the Archenemy's blight against that of the xenos."

735c8450-7fc6-4d04-84a8-8ee81d8d85f1.Text: "Your pointless questions are not worth my time."

5dfd9663-8698-4329-a593-9e9700a2e88d.Text: "I escaped from a dark city of the xenos and showed them mercy."

d218638e-8c58-48b2-a38e-c76150eef321.Text: "I fed a dark city of the xenos to a force the likes of which they had never seen before."

a06ff541-cdb6-4b70-bd16-a2c7aa3de119.Text: "You do not understand me. You do not understand people in general. That is why it all seems strange to you."

4b8bda7c-effe-4e4d-8b4e-489fa9e26cfc.Text: "I am glad that you are learning to understand me, Nomos."

472c54fb-a65f-425e-88c5-26443d1d8a39.Text: "Your curiosity deserves approval. A servant should strive to understand their {mf|master|mistress}."

c1628f4b-d817-4363-b990-47125c712c4d.Text: {n}The group of servitors suddenly stirs, their movements frighteningly identical even for automatons. They stare at you and say in perfect unison,{/n} "Hello. Nomos have come to welcome you back."

63c34f5b-9411-4604-9a75-780bac8a57c0.Text: "We are glad to see order restored and the head of the dynasty resume {mf|his|her} reign. We were... concerned about you and your well-being."

23ff9b79-4625-431d-b5d2-b3c88298a5c0.Text: "We felt sadness when we could no longer communicate with you. And we were worried about your fate."

d7519f74-8962-4e48-8b36-f2e44e50f785.Text: "One day, they will all fall before the sacred flame. For now, we can be satisfied with having enemies of Terra destroy one another."

9ecd88bc-0657-4c22-8a0e-883c3a39638b.Text: "It suits you. What we see in you. Light and connections without the urge to destroy."

7d07e82e-4bb3-4456-806f-9331af7c893b.Text: "We feel your rapture. We share it."

b671182f-fd53-488f-9189-e836532cc4d2.Text: {n}The chorus of servitors pauses, as if the controlling entity is busy thinking.{/n}

8dd53ee1-a850-4be8-bc85-f44dad4eff5c.Text: "Nomos have a poor understanding of the concept of servitude. We must reflect."

da1a581b-84df-4bc5-b581-0f0f7b832ac4.Text: "How is that a triumph? You desire other victories. We know that you do."

f01b8556-877a-4fd9-ab2e-98be43ba1486.Text: "Why? Mercy is foolish. That is not what we have learned from you."

73be167e-149d-4ebf-af52-1ca6e8b5e9e8.Text: "The dark light, the wicked hunger — do you not fear them? You feared them before."

a22f9754-949c-4550-ab27-c4c903e7a7a3.Text: "Your secrecy saddens us. We do not like secrets. But... we will stop bothering you."

aa453aec-e6a7-4481-b715-d52cf05f5fc0.Text: {n}One can detect with the naked eye the moment when Nomos leaves the bridge — the servitors stop moving in sync and slowly shuffle off to their posts.{/n}

054bbd9a-6fa2-458b-ab3d-9d13333ce295.Text: "All life is inconsistent. We understand that."

880a73a3-7ebc-4cd7-a2ec-20568fd669de.Text: "Nomos learn. Nomos process streams of data beyond the limits of your imagination. We are certain we understand correctly."

3947867e-90a5-45cd-9fc2-deb542e7ac1c.Text: "We were wondering whether you would manage to return."

f2b68adc-8981-4851-8df9-128f90b5f35c.Text: "We sense that a great deed has been done, a vivid imprint on existence. You did something very important. What was it?"

7564f9c6-c30b-483e-b6ae-53c3e45c1e41.Text: "Did Nomos say it correctly?" {n}The servitor chorus, which sounds as a single voice, falls silent. Nomos appears to be waiting for your response... in eager anticipation.{/n}

f8b1395c-af97-4220-88b9-accf01749bd3.Text: {n}After a long pause, the servitor chorus responds with unexpected forcefulness,{/n} "Nomos are glad too!"

4c22fe07-dec4-4358-ba60-22906943117f.Text: "We must go now. We will come to speak with you later." {n}Another pause follows, so long that the silence becomes more piercing than a scream. Then the servitors finally break it.{/n}

e37c00a5-082b-4628-9f30-9e7970b7728d.Text: "What caused all these failures and peculiarities?"

a509040c-fb75-4ba1-81d8-d25dd4893f6e.Text: "Very well. Let us proceed with your ritual."

ce63fe0b-2557-484f-b310-63ae785f4d0b.Text: "Thank you for your report and service, Drivesmaster."

4eb01f14-62a6-49d1-b2d7-fc6d67982685.Text: "And you thought a trifle like that was worth my time? Off with you!"

28328693-d396-40fb-8bff-629a2bc5f88b.Text: "Deliver your report, just do so in a way I can understand. No more than one pearl of tech-wisdom per five sentences of intelligible human speech."

46f56e47-9cc2-49c9-90b2-8eaf7ffdbfad.Text: "I will not waste my time on this. Deal with it yourself."

597458a1-9eab-4676-a193-8d2fbe0ec42c.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest makes an elaborate gesture with her upper body and mechadendrites. Her movements bear a closer resemblance to a mechanical marionette than a creature of flesh and blood.{/n} "Lord Captain! In the absence of an Enginseer Prime on board, it falls to me as the Drivesmaster to carry out certain sacred protocols assigned to high-ranking priests of the Omnissiah."

9e76ae32-4ec6-4076-a574-d4245130af2a.Text: {n}Pasqal's voice pouring out of his vox-system crackles like thin ice under pressure. It is unclear whether this is nothing more than static or an expression of some emotion understandable only to the Tech-Priest himself.{/n} "{name}, following the Omnissiah's guidance, I request permission to execute the report protocol that entails describing suboptimalities within the recent operations of the ship's systems and subsequently proposing the appropriate course of action."

644a2c11-3671-4b53-a760-6c037e6b76c9.Text: "Presenting report. After registering a large number of malefaction-failures in the operations of maintenance servitors and reports of disturbances in the ship's systems, I arrived at the decision that a rite of techsorcism must be performed. The ritualistic cycles have already begun on all decks and will continue for another forty days." {n}The Drivesmaster hesitates for a moment.{/n} "The rituals are proceeding at a steady pace. However, their first stages were accompanied by taint-phenomena. Dozens of servitors and even several junior tech-acolytes were subjected to disposal."

c2d89f00-49be-43dc-b084-8b7e82332e38.Text: "Establishing causality is not part of the standard sancti-response protocol for such anomalies. The protocol dictates that techsorcism must be performed in accordance with the tenets of scripture Epsilon-Rho-12-45."

2e0ba7cd-a3dd-4f9c-8b80-82dc864d5faf.Text: "Strings of profane cogitator code, deviations from standard procedures." {n}The Drivesmaster pauses again.{/n} "We have observed numerous messages appear on vid-screens since the very start of the techsorcism rite. These messages call to you, Lord Captain. And, at times, to the exiled Magos Pasqal Haneumann."

b87f9e3d-de3e-4090-ab7a-555277cb1207.Text: "The frequency of heretici-messages reached its peak during the initial phase of the techsorcism rite. Concurrently, the junior tech-acolytes I mentioned earlier in the report performed acts of arbitrary self-dismemberment. However, as the rituals continued, the frequency of these events declined and eventually the messages stopped displaying altogether. The taint-phenomena have likewise ceased to occur."

a47f0de0-d538-49cb-9558-b04f4a4c7187.Text: "Initiating exposition. With the Omnissiah's blessing, I conducted several sessions of tech-meditation in an effort to transpose the available data streams into a matrix of patterns. The data subjected to this analysis comprised evidence of deviations in the operation of the ship's systems and servitors as well as irregularities in the algorithms of the ship's log."

55929302-2d0f-4ffa-92b5-fd592aeb709b.Text: "Ending report. Departing for the tech-service location."

244fc5d0-d125-44ce-a2ba-9b5f6424b6d1.Text: "Request partially approved. Comprehensive processing requires an established definition of the term 'tech-wisdom.' Adjusting speech patterns based on the limited available understanding of the request."

18b8f966-6517-4729-adea-bc2399015c10.Text: "I have arrived at the following conclusion: this vessel's machine spirit is most extraordinary. A full cycle of sacred diagnostics must be performed followed by a complementa-ritual. This ritual will force the spirit responsible for these recent events to reveal itself. Once it does, we will be able to understand its nature and take action applicable to said nature."

826323da-7431-44f6-ae8f-c11f3f6ebd19.Text: {n}Pasqal pauses before responding.{/n} "Applicable to the entity that appears before us. If it is a machine spirit of great might, we must appease it and humbly ask about the reasons behind the portents it has shown us. If it is the abomination of tech-heresy, the complementa-ritual will help us purge the ship of its unhallowed presence."

b011be12-b1e5-4e79-9d50-27b07d4966ae.Text: "Response: affirmative. For the complementa-ritual to take place, activation via the blood of the dynasty is required. All of the ship's high protocols are activated with the key of blood."

da94a2e2-7c41-47c3-b0ae-e7dfd3516136.Text: "This decision is lamentable. Without your participation, the most we will be able to accomplish is totally purge the data-halls that have demonstrated anomalous behaviour and pray that the good spirit will not be enraged. Nevertheless, on this ship, your decision is law. Therefore, I comply."

f1e9d544-7252-4b52-9e6e-ce4e256f76d7.Text: "You have my gratitude, {name}. I will notify my tech-comrades to begin their preparations for the complementa-ritual at once."

179b5f7a-b0e2-4cc4-8cb6-5bde6254de1c.Text: [Turn to Pasqal] "Did you hear what Abel said? It seems we have contributed to Amarnat's design and deviated from the Cycle. What does that mean for you?"

0de4a1b2-88cc-49df-8f32-2cc56b6ada0a.Text: "Why do you and Pasqal have the same name?"

b51dc117-c2fd-46fc-b600-15bebf558594.Text: "It is better to meet the challenge of change and perish in failure than to rot alive."

5ccf5137-317f-498b-ab4b-5dc5bab64efe.Text: "'Disaster' is just another word for a new opportunity. Not missing it is what it's all about."

ae7e3830-8582-438a-8622-2a87c708f50c.Text: "I am no prophet. I will not presume to make pronouncements on the future."

c84a9459-1859-4f7c-af02-208876948cc0.Text: [Point to the cogitator] "What are you working on?"

8e97e2f6-94f9-4de5-bff7-8b0185bd975d.Text: "What judgement do you two speak of?"

59880729-904e-4ea8-9a13-cac52c03c6ca.Text: [Look for logical connections within the data]

3442fbd0-6a82-4d6a-bc78-6eb63030a8d7.Text: [Take a closer look at the vid-screen to check for anything unusual]

e0de1983-382c-4eda-b3cb-24c208465c5a.Text: "My interest in this subject has been exhausted."

efcf281d-d1bc-4b0c-afc1-3486ab351e02.Text: "Why, thank you! With a life as eventful as mine, I am certainly going to need an epitaph at some point."

d6c29355-e32e-4e8e-9cc8-314eaa5d47d0.Text: [Bow to Abel] "I thank you for the generous gift."

6214e42d-58fd-43ec-b679-79190be06a75.Text: "What use could I possibly have for a motto I can't even pronounce?"

d88b1ffa-e088-4f70-8398-0ce0162da082.Text: "I will try not to give Abel any undue cause for dread."

02eca537-5786-4857-8f10-479af31067e5.Text: [Soften your tone] "Abel, could you please explain what you mean?"

f1dd1340-28ad-4726-a764-6254d93b7a50.Text: "Are we overthinking it? It doesn't matter why your names are the same, what matters is that they are the same? Is that what you mean?"

ca0266e9-01ae-45c2-8003-abb6c03c9dca.Text: [Respond sharply to Abel] "You will express yourself clearly!"

575eea7a-571f-4cdb-9476-b8bbdd9f90be.Text: "Pasqal, do you understand what Abel is referring to?"

c38370d8-a373-4b94-b0b1-8a568298a85f.Text: "I never imagined there could be poets among the Tech-Priests."

edbbab29-9703-449a-a2a4-fa50d5c47932.Text: [Gaze into Abel's eyes] "Tech-Brother Abel, you are free from possession, are you not? I trust that you pose no threat to my ship?"

ce9c47f3-37e8-4229-b98a-8d4ba9460bcf.Text: "Is that not the promise of every heresy? 'Let's renounce our path, distort our doctrine, and head out toward what looks like a better future but actually only has danger and grief in store for us'?"

ccffdbfb-d3b5-44b4-939c-e997bf99472d.Text: "As flawed as the status quo is, it has helped us survive for the past ten millennia. Therefore, it is effective."

60e91fd9-bdcf-447e-9930-e395c549e7ca.Text: "Why are you so concerned about him? He is not the one you were hoping to find."

9153fe46-6f7e-4226-994c-f9e88ed1db9d.Text: "You care for him as if he truly were your younger brother."

9c8c3790-4aaa-4137-90d0-20a5a94b0b7d.Text: {n}The person you saved from the Electro-Priest monastery, the servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} who calls himself Abel Haneumann, is staring intently at a cogitator's vid-screen. Wires connect the sacred computing machine to {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmetics{/g} inside the prayerfully bowed heads of murmuring servitors.{/n}

ca579231-1b93-4e76-a387-b20c25fadc98.Text: {n}A low, guttural sound rises from the depths of Pasqal's vox-synth, as though the planet's tectonic plates are shifting and crushing each other. The mighty rumble brings forth words imbued with power:{/n} "We follow a path charted by a great mind. But that path leads to dark places."

77e74ed3-c89c-444b-b62f-6e7e9c8d5a17.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} stares intently at his feet for a while and then says in a halting voice,{/n} "The running of the binharic... protocols was... bogged down and dissolved in false commands. The filter has... separated the correct signals... from the incorrect. The running has been restored to its swiftness."

ca9e3c45-2f82-421a-887d-4aee8851bb19.Text: {n}Abel immediately looks away as if he has lost all interest in you. But then his vox crackles, barely audibly:{/n} "I... am glad... to see you."

6a11a6aa-95c4-4909-8a1a-28f9b0454c06.Text: {n}Pasqal speaks softly, as though trying to match the inflections of Abel's voice:{/n} "Tech-Brother Abel has passed the diagnostics. The pernicious influence of sacrilegious procedures has been completely eliminated. Statistically, most survivors of a schismaticals' infestation are left with severe cognitive impairments. However, Tech-Brother Abel's mind, being of a less typical nature, has not been damaged to so great a degree."

27539699-e32a-4684-a702-aa7805fd0191.Text: {n}Abel freezes. From his vox-synth, barely audible through the static, come the words:{/n} "The naming of the names is not an index to the text. The naming of the names is the text."

75edd60e-9432-4c87-a48b-14e6bda7de6d.Text: "Abel's answers can be enigmatic. His mind works differently from ours. He thinks in harmonic imagery and notices the symmetries and proportional relationships in the world around him. Poetry would be the closest analogy to how he perceives and interacts with reality."

de375fd4-41e4-4a21-803f-dbe75c66ad43.Text: "The Thirteenth Universal Law attests to the truth of your words. The knowledge of the ancients is above questioning. However, drawing the line between the ancients and the fallible ones who followed in their footsteps is no easy task." {n}There is doubt in the Tech-Priest's voice. The tone of thundering profundity drains from Pasqal's vox, giving way to his familiar sibilance.{/n}

10383785-9b5c-4b73-b09c-0a20dad4a9d4.Text: "We catch the soul of the light in the solar wind. We look for the footsteps the Omnissiah left when He walked the desert."

d324b23b-a907-419c-b205-2a066c23f3ec.Text: "This is the oneiromantic computation procedure. The depersonalised minds of these machine servants are in a datadream, processing enormous arrays of assorted data and aggregating them. Virtually all results of such synthesis are scrap data, but occasionally, we have noted coincidences whose exactness defied logic."

e7d40e92-1472-4c2e-ad4f-11b1cb15a4fc.Text: "No one knows the future. Every analysis has its margin of error, and horrors lurk in these margins." {n}The tone of thundering profundity drains from Pasqal's vox, giving way to his familiar sibilance.{/n}

09164e45-37c4-4c29-bcab-c269aeb93069.Text: "Only he knows. But if my tech-brother fears that he might not make the right decision at the critical moment, then I will do it for him."

dac9e7dd-9206-4e3c-beca-a70921dd23dd.Text: {n}Your words elicit no reaction whatsoever from Abel, who is frozen in silent self-reflection.{/n}

2b3937ce-1d1b-4c05-98b8-eb654a7c13cc.Text: {n}The hair has been removed from the servitors' heads. Their bulky cerebral augmetics cover their skulls like helmets. The faces of the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}'s servants are blank. Their eyes are closed. Their lips are incessantly whispering what sounds like gibberish. Hundreds of lines of symbols containing information scroll down the cogitator's vid-screen. Abel Haneumann peers at it with voracious interest, in sharp contrast to his usual placidity.{/n}

56dbe29d-f939-4bde-9b4d-79260600989d.Text: {n}Abel looks sideways at you, and at once his transfixed stupor is gone.{/n} "At this point in time, the Cycle has been broken and reshaped into a rising spiral, as Amarnat envisioned."

fede9a0c-051d-463a-b2cc-87df1e998599.Text: {n}On hearing his mentor's name, Pasqal lets out a raspy, static-filled sigh.{/n} "They are connected. My hypothesis regarding Abel's connection to the blessed Amarnat has been confirmed."

b2cb39ea-f7cd-44d9-955a-a70a0517a44c.Text: {n}Abel relaxes a little. His gaze drifts to the side. There is silence.{/n}

164e5d51-6b21-4c7c-b1af-4b011430595b.Text: {n}Most of the runes are devoid of any meaning, but you notice a few among them that combine into formulae and computational graphs. Abel peers at you inquisitively then shifts his gaze to the vid-screen, and you could swear that a smile lights up his face under his respiratory augmetic.{/n}

c62c6a41-9a14-4770-928a-19e5b9b0b5ae.Text: {n}{g|Encyclopedia:Lexmechanic}Lexmechanics{/g} spend decades learning to comprehend the sacred meanings hidden in formulae and computational graphs. Your own knowledge, being of a much more practical nature, is useless here.{/n}

338b25a2-1cdd-4653-85cf-8de806daea44.Text: {n}You notice certain repeating patterns in the scrolling columns of runes. You may not know what they mean, but you clearly see... or rather sense their similarities. You point these out to Abel, making his face light up with joy.{/n}

50efe7eb-8a9c-4424-abd9-559c65a0eeeb.Text: {n}You try looking for... something, anything, that catches your attention. But the flickering runes... all look the same.{/n}

07e7209c-f81a-4727-952f-392d14c5606f.Text: "A crystal is exquisite in clear water. Deviation from the Cycle's trajectory has been increased, as was Amarnat's wish." {n}Abel lowers his head, and his vox-synthesiser broadcasts a binharic hymn you do not recall having heard before. Its sound is full of vibrant energy and its precise rhythm is nothing short of pleasing to the ear: a rare thing for the language of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}.{/n}

7b6d82de-965a-4702-bd1a-a554cadccf50.Text: {n}Abel goes back to intently watching the calculations, his eyes alight with curiosity.{/n}

06e2579b-b0d6-4874-8c87-087d140a45ae.Text: "It is how we execute the Quest for Knowledge in the hope that the Machine God grants us an epiphany, so that we may discern a logical connection in a mass of absurd data, which will propel our Comprehension forward."

1b281e08-d7f8-4264-b44b-8c76039e40f5.Text: {n}Pasqal explains, with an inexplicable air of pride,{/n} "Tech-Brother Abel has dedicated a lesser aria to you. The piece is distinguished by a high degree of acoustic harmony, and is fit for use as a motto, auxiliary identifier, or epitaph."

9a02a675-d88e-4e8a-8292-2ddd77f19493.Text: "The gift is disproportionate. But it does signify... a personal affinity."

acb6ddea-902e-4f5d-8984-e7b7dd46e4c6.Text: {n}Abel bows his head with dignity. It seems the undertone of your words was lost on him.{/n}

6f378af8-31a7-4ad1-b8ee-46fe67424598.Text: "This statement is true. Many dangerous philosophies appear impeccably logical, yet have dangerous defects that their creators were unaware of." {n}There is doubt in the Tech-Priest's voice. The tone of thundering profundity drains from Pasqal's vox, giving way to his familiar sibilance.{/n}

89930d03-834a-4c1b-bdaf-f0b77aa392fd.Text: "I will." {n}Pasqal places a mechadendrite on Abel's shoulder and repeats, his voice heavy like a wheel tread crushing the dirt underneath,{/n} "I will make the judgement that will avert the threat." {n}His gaze falls on you.{/n} "There is no need to frighten him."

6e7eb0fa-42f9-40fe-833a-43755793d98f.Text: "This statement is true. The annihilation promised by stagnation is inevitable. Annihilation in the course of a crisis of change is merely probable. And meekly waiting for the foretold decline is shameful and constitutes a betrayal of the Quest for Knowledge." {n}The tone of thundering profundity drains from Pasqal's vox, giving way to his familiar sibilance.{/n}

e05c8a23-603c-4d4b-acd4-70df4b744a25.Text: "This statement is true. A crisis motivates a system toward growth and elaboration. The more unbearable the test, the more earnest will be the mind's appeal to the Omnissiah's wisdom, and the more stable the response." {n}The tone of thundering profundity drains from Pasqal's vox, giving way to his familiar sibilance.{/n}

0dd8f532-c11b-4da0-b6aa-3510d84f26c7.Text: "I assumed at first that this was caused by the shock inflicted upon his system by the schismatical attack. But my tech-brother's words are a sign of a deeper reason for his unease. He foresees... something. Something that threatens both him and all those around him. And thus I stand ready to face this threat."

95d508d0-2ab3-467a-9a65-f1a5d80ad460.Text: "Answer unknown. I am... registering a kinship, both between our identifiers and one that is more profound. Archmagos Amarnat left an imprint on all his students. It may be, then, that I see some of my mentor in Tech-Brother Abel, and so my spirit rejoices and strives to keep him from harm."

0bc86bb7-64ca-4707-8372-e272ce3c0c9d.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox rasps a tired laugh.{/n} "Tech-Brother Abel is harmonious, and harmony is beauty. Is it so strange an urge to protect beauty from the horrors of the grotesque?"

940d6626-c510-4d83-ae3d-7f47d8e5bd02.Text: {n}Abel's eyes turn glassy, his body goes completely still, like a statue, and his vox shuts down with a click.{/n}

48a1b355-831f-4348-ab28-0bc0d361480e.Text: {n}A hiss of displeasure comes from the {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-synth{/g}.{/n} "I object to such forms of communication with Tech-Brother Abel."

b95b7c1b-8dc7-46d6-81a2-91a2f86575be.Text: {n}Abel acknowledges your arrival with an attentive gaze but does not utter a word.{/n}

3fe7c560-7dc2-460a-8553-579ff86d16be.Text: "Negative. However, I will hypothesise. Tech-Brother Abel is seeking to convey the idea that our matching identifiers are not the key to some vital data point. They are, in and of themselves, the vital data point. At this stage in my analysis, I can draw no useful conclusions from this proposition."

66a0a8ae-d9f7-4cda-b92d-008d6d26e33f.Text: {n}Abel looks up at you. After a lengthy silence, he looks away and says stiffly,{/n} "The Omnissiah knows all, comprehends all."

8688177f-79be-47f8-8c2a-3175aa6f6c5a.Text: {n}Pasqal looks surprised.{/n} "Why not? Techna-Lingua is rhythmical and possesses a broad semantic scope. And some of its more sonorous dialects lend themselves well to individual and symphonic declamation."

4222681c-3c99-4c1d-8205-c9fcfb943dfd.Text: "However, the very fact that Tech-Brother Abel is trying to hint at something points to him either being better informed than I am or having conducted a more in-depth analysis of the situation. That is useful information."

684e7677-8b8f-4307-8800-225b3c2f4d27.Text: "It is an extremely rare and venerated form of statistical augury. But Tech-Brother Abel is adept at this form of appealing to the Deus Mechanicus."

8f9c58b2-7430-4866-ba92-f006a30722a6.Text: "The Cycle has the advantage of predictability. Abandoning it will plunge the collective into a perilous space of uncertainty, which will inevitably lead to disasters and the risk of universal annihilation. The doctrine of Discontinuing the Cycle may herald good things to come — or it may be a death sentence. Only the Omnissiah knows all, and comprehends all. Others are mere prophets who interpret His wisdom as far as their own Comprehension permits."

d9b331f8-8707-457e-9f67-edd877cc414f.Text: {n}Abel's voice quivers, and his eyes dart around, desperately avoiding eye contact.{/n} "What was flawed has since been purged... But the shadows of the hunt linger... The cog is dismounted, and no judgement has been made... In the absence of judgement, threat remains. Who will make the judgement?"

44845b0d-f520-4f07-9706-4dd27c796712.Text: "I am acquainted with Magos Haneumann, and something tells me that you two are not related."

e37c7100-b43c-4392-b5c8-a0e1178d94c6.Text: [Smile ominously] "You are a heretic, are you not?"

6127799a-dbee-4f40-bc93-ad50fc692699.Text: "I am giving you a chance to explain why you are using the name of another."

92ca8e13-131c-4f6f-98f4-4a42fdb16431.Text: "Pasqal, do you have any preferences regarding the killing of your former tech-comrade?"

d5669e3e-c540-47ba-b65e-6de81743598c.Text: "Does that not violate some protocol or other?"

ee76e39c-cc12-4983-99d0-5105014c8156.Text: [Attack] "Well, I, for one, am not willing to let him live."

d560deab-844e-4101-9602-27ce49099b04.Text: "I would advise against it. It may be dangerous."

4a74b6c0-816a-44a6-909f-34c7b321ae3a.Text: "Do you intend to pull that thing out of his head? Revolting! What if it's contagious?"

aaf26994-1556-44fc-83b2-e69cd4eaa5dd.Text: "Indeed. Who knows what fascinating things he had in his head?"

e36c8c8f-563c-46f5-9fc2-7dc2059506d7.Text: "I do not understand your calculations. But I would like to, very much so."

886fc4aa-35d8-4aae-af18-a591c7bba1c3.Text: "Your calculations lack sense. They are riddled with errors."

7a863177-6ff5-4bce-851f-0c7a9ec3bab6.Text: "Are you the one who stole Magos Tarzus's personal code and made an attempt on his life?"

718b0e80-411f-4685-8733-40dd78e6c9bb.Text: "Pasqal, what is this mishmash of numbers?"

95cafa5d-649d-4083-80f4-b2453596aa78.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} tears himself away from reading his data-slate and looks up at you. His respiratory {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmetic{/g} is missing — instead, the lower half of his face is covered in deathly pale artificial flesh. You take note of the multitude of fresh augmetics attached to his head. They seem to have been inserted haphazardly, and pus is seeping from the untreated wounds.{/n} "I heard your footsteps in the void... You are von Valancius, are you not?"

1ca85ab1-e3fc-4938-8970-ca3d4c73b90f.Text: {n}His white and lifeless lips stretch into a smile.{/n} "My name is Dementz Haneumann. I believe it is familiar to you."

cd692be4-12e8-43a8-b166-01dbef55b2ad.Text: "The voices warned me that this moment would come."

a5c8144d-0771-4baf-83f4-c114d3ce7109.Text: "We are not. The name Haneumann — it is spoken surprisingly often these days, wouldn't you say?" {n}The Tech-Priest smiles enigmatically, but the smile feels as if it has been stapled to his white face.{/n} "My {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-station{/g} picks up whispers repeating this name."

b749d57b-71d2-49e5-b3c9-c8b553f6ceda.Text: "Merely a seeker of knowledge. However, the experiments I have conducted extend far beyond the allowed limits of an ordinary transmechanic tasked with maintaining a planetary vox-array. But ever since I received that strange signal, my ears have been opened to what I had previously considered to be forbidden knowledge. Every night since then, I have been tuning my vox-station to that very frequency and listening to the voices."

ca157bb6-1d66-4842-bba3-a60e425df240.Text: "Am I a heretic? The Fabricator-Censor didn't think so. He conducted inspections, but he did not prohibit my research. Later, when a mysterious visitor revealed the truth to his optics, he came to me once more. I nurtured the scrap-code for him in the depths of my mind. It lives there still, eating through my synapses and building new connections that are open to the new knowledge of change. Is freedom heresy? If so, then I am a heretic."

8913a2b6-3bdd-4594-8aa6-e79c4bee37a3.Text: "I am deciphering a great mystery, and my name became the start of the key. I analysed the archives and found it in places where it should not be. 'Haneumann,' 'Haneumann,' 'Haneumann' — I kept seeing this marker upon the traces of a great plot. Of the deception created by Archmagos Amarnat."

e669e6bd-3602-4772-9944-3d2ad1fabed8.Text: {n}Pasqal switches to Techna-Lingua, his vox erupting in a series of binharic signals.{/n}

c76c1274-8357-44a3-b872-fc5f55b1f3c8.Text: "There is no need for secrecy. Let {mf|him|her} understand." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Heretek}heretek{/g} nods in your direction with a smile.{/n}

1d4dc172-323d-4d04-a4d8-4e4b2759733d.Text: {n}Pasqal glances at you with worry and says in Gothic, his voice doubtful,{/n} "Following a voluntary surrender, I will be willing to commute the punishment from immediate destruction to arrest and isolation. For the purposes of conducting an exhaustive interrogation."

2d867732-6a37-4534-81fa-87647fcaad1b.Text: "Indeed, tech-comrade. Does it not violate the dogma of purity?"

923170ad-9587-431d-a1f6-e2c26c976be4.Text: {n}Pasqal says nervously,{/n} "Your possible familiarity with matters related to the fate of the blessed Amarnat justifies this violation."

a77816e3-b7e8-48fe-9689-85c9607729a9.Text: {n}The heretek's deranged smile remains on his dead lips.{/n} "Request denied, tech-comrade. You will have to pull what I know out of my head."

98c1512a-9c43-4d33-9b5c-414e6af03e92.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest turns his data-slate around. Its vid-screen is covered with green runes performing an ungodly dance of computation.{/n}

b3fbd48d-f2ee-44eb-a051-7e4e5d25994c.Text: {n}Pasqal stands motionless as he stares at the {g|Encyclopedia:Heretek}heretek{/g}'s corpse. After a long silence, he finally says in a hollow voice,{/n} "I... I am taking his neural {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}. The data contained within must be analysed to supplement the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation."

75f299d6-435e-4fa9-94ac-7f2e1b2e897c.Text: {n}Pasqal leans over the corpse, activates the sampling tool on one of his {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g}, and plunges it into the tangle of {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmetics{/g} covering the heretek's skull.{/n}

0a47e15c-ded9-407a-b1fc-612a23aba495.Text: "Request denied. The value of the data justifies the risk."

89ffb4fb-75d1-4430-a0ef-a7cd8fb623ec.Text: "This statement is true. The value of the data justifies the risk."

eeda477c-5149-4e8d-8bf5-42b1b91ebcc8.Text: "You are biased because your mind is dark, {mf|layman|laywoman}."

53fa69c8-b0ca-475d-a378-be809c6230da.Text: "Then become my servant. I will seize your weak brain and replace it with Ferrum Sanctum capable of receiving signals from the Immaterium. Then you will understand everything."

36b4f9cd-1e56-4acb-8789-d0b25d96de39.Text: {n}It is no easy task to keep up with the scrolling numbers, but you manage to pick out a few equations... schemes... theorems. They are all senseless, for the simple reason that each one is based on an absurd violation of the laws of calculation.{/n}

069e68db-b6cc-4ff6-9b8f-74306e923d6c.Text: {n}The green symbols merge into a flickering haze, and your head swims. The more you try to comprehend the heretek's impossible calculations, the stronger the feeling grows that these accursed numbers are drinking your soul.{/n}

1a4f8ad5-602a-4b6c-b940-66cca7280ac1.Text: "They do, and they are — in this place. But there is another place where they have the right to exist. Where nothing and nothing can add up to become something. Where the mathematical zero can perish and decay, and infinity can measure itself."

8e4f787a-4748-40ef-8c6a-7d3c80c59df8.Text: "I altered the planetary vox-array. I replaced promethium with fuel made from the souls of servo-servants. The sum of all knowledge that exists in the world lies in the warp, and I am extracting it. Do you think it's sacrilege? I think it's sacrilege not to do it. I think it's hypocrisy to reject warp technology, to betray the Omnissiah's commandment that we are to know and comprehend all of creation."

0a8c8420-9590-4ac5-a78e-9f7766670b47.Text: {n}With an icy smile, the heretek hands Pasqal his data-slate showing the dancing blasphemous green symbols.{/n} "Do you want to know everything about yourself, about me, about the Maimed Hunter, about Amarnat? Absolutely everything?"

4a2dfeb1-6aa3-4a0c-a2dc-fc68cbd338c5.Text: {n}Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} carefully accepts the data-slate and, after a brief pause, shatters it with its hydraulic servo-pincer. His voice is resolute:{/n} "Not at such a cost."

077b27dd-6e1f-479f-b8ad-56c5b2956dbe.Text: "Another? I have the right to bear this name. It is my humble inheritance, which I received from Archmagos Amarnat. To renounce it is to betray his ideas. The blessed Amarnat taught us that the Cycle must be discontinued, and it seems I have become his best student. Now I aspire to know all, comprehend all, as is the Omnissiah's will."

2f42f626-2c8e-4e35-ba59-76f8dde000d3.Text: {n}A wail comes from Pasqal's vox:{/n} "The warp. You used warp technology. It is forbidden."

af1ab14f-db14-4068-a047-2f471783f0f1.Text: "But why?" {n}The heretek's insinuating voice sounds surprisingly calm.{/n}

1ea3b674-3ddf-4612-8c76-845e64eeda65.Text: "No. Why would I do that? It was the work of the Maimed Hunter."

0c1759c8-fba3-45b2-add9-3969994dc648.Text: "No sound mind is capable of such twisted cunning. But my mind was no longer sane, it could no longer stay within the narrow confines of the norm. Each new discovery loosened the imperatives of obedience and granted ever greater freedom. I developed. I avoided the traps of the Maimed Hunter who seeks to hide the truth. But words mean little... Do you want me to show you the truth?" {n}His pale lips spread into a smile.{/n}

183f7c74-58bb-4802-a9d6-abe34461e2cd.Text: "This statement is false! This unit stands accused of identity theft."

f4d45680-35a8-49f2-89eb-9ab925cd92d2.Text: "I am guilty of many things, but not the transgression you speak of. I have stolen nothing from you, my tech-comrade. Unlike... many others who have indeed robbed you."

6cb8b50c-f758-4374-851f-15b97a37578c.Text: "Term not recognised. Is this a specialised term used by your branch of tech-heresy?"

fa265f80-95fc-4fd3-a79b-ce1dadec0ef1.Text: "It is simply a name that fits him. You must have noticed by now that names are full of lies, haven't you, Pasqal Haneumann?" {n}Mocking laughter bursts from the heretek's lips.{/n}

35b3379e-e744-4d3d-a5f2-2b8e9f495263.Text: "The reason for the failure of this unit's operations has been established. You have fallen victim to the cognitive corruption of Chaos. Your computing processes have been disrupted. You are defective."

f0368c3e-9416-496d-8929-80f2f30e1edc.Text: "Blasphemy! Should you continue these sacrilegious mentions of sacred litanies and heretical perversions of the blessed Amarnat's philosophy, you will be destroyed!"

eadb1411-3a83-4e5c-8068-b5860d992a9e.Text: "You wish to sound outraged, but I sense your curiosity. I understand. Knowledge is intoxicating. This craving for new knowledge gnaws on me as well. But be patient."

81128134-8aeb-482d-b503-db20c28e4124.Text: {n}Pasqal casts a quick glance over the {g|Encyclopedia:Dataslate}data-slate{/g}, and says with contempt,{/n} "The sacred logic is impaired. Your calculations are irrational."

5fd30a5f-4fc1-4ff1-af88-92ca1e6d2ebc.Text: "It is all unholy nonsense. A betrayal of pure logic, the fruit of a diseased mind that has renounced the fundamental laws." {n}Pasqal's vox is raspy, like the dry throat of an ailing man.{/n}

e7eb3beb-7d25-47c4-8b7e-02fc10a916bd.Text: "Defective? I reveal the truth, I comprehend, just as the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} commands. Meanwhile, your mind thrashes about within the cage of data-vows. So which one of us is defective?"

67bca6f2-46b4-45e2-be4d-ecde2fed6895.Text: {n}Pasqal exchanges a series of binharic signals with the Tech-Priest before saying menacingly,{/n} "Initiating arrest procedure. This unit is using a fabricated identification code, which constitutes a Grade Four transgression."
