f708e6aa-0357-4787-bb7e-671c4231b163.Text: "If you speak of our souls' ability to overcome hardship... then the experience of suffering does indeed become a symbol of our abiding strength and inner growth. And it gives hope that we can overcome life's trials."

4c84a125-503f-4bca-8ac9-6af08b223d59.Text: "I can follow the line of your thoughts, elantach. Every form, colour, creature, and being possesses its own charm and capacity to stir our emotions. Millions of stars in the darkness. The inimitability of void crystals. The plethora of intelligent and primitive life forms that inhabit the galaxy... The world manifests itself in endless diversity — and in that lies its true magnificence."

97c69b3c-fd30-43d4-9195-1f0eb4e2b279.Text: "And what does that mean?" {n}Yrliet asks, with all her attention focused on your words.{/n}

8169fc24-e81f-4c3d-a3bc-0eeedf315d69.Text: {n}Yrliet goes still and looks at you intently as if seeing you for the first time.{/n} "It seems there are many facets of your soul that I have not considered, elantach. Interesting... I accept your answer and thank you for speaking with me. This is the first conversation on board this vessel that has truly brought serenity and joy to my soul."

96afb967-b195-4a46-a095-c5d04c902b50.Text: "Lack of understanding between our kinds is to be expected, elantach. I did not assume that you would grasp all of what was said... Nevertheless, I did hope that your mind would be capable of more."

3e3d0689-d443-4b13-a7ab-235c5f9716c3.Text: "I understand. There are times when something sublime can arise from the accidental combination of colours on the celestial palette. Or from the tangled threads of fate of two souls weaving together at a particular moment. In this unexpected and elusive instant, the world acquires a particular allure."

44c4d390-77b1-4d21-9b5e-d07fdbd6c1fb.Text: {n}Yrliet says nothing for a time, silently watching you from under her half-lowered lids.{/n} "Now that we have each shared our truth about this world... I would like to know if your thoughts about me align with those of your kin, elantach, or if you see me differently."

1d035978-079c-4cfd-9bd8-6bf2a8799906.Text: "Your words do not trouble my soul. On the contrary, they bring only relief. And now that this conversation is over, I will leave you to return to guiding your steel-winged bird." {n}Yrliet nods curtly and melts into the shadows of the bridge.{/n}

ad7ce725-5dbb-4ce6-a34a-5998c034a4c2.Text: {n}Guarded interest gleams in Yrliet's eyes when your gazes meet again.{/n}

3d8c20ea-beb2-4106-9131-c0ae0fab4245.Text: "That is enough, mon-keigh. Did I not warn you about the consequences?"

844921b1-da89-42f4-b488-a1262ee4e858.Text: "I accept your answer, elantach. As long as you do not attempt to get under my skin or demand... something else... of me." {n}She places particular emphasis on the last few words.{/n} "I will go now, elantach. Guide your steel-winged bird."

ede09fd3-e437-4a6e-a2fa-ab247bcb7694.Text: "If your words are sincere, elantach... then you are capable of seeing more than you do now."

cb8b523e-da24-49af-b10e-5f1f817d9f5e.Text: "That will be best, I think. The less conspicuous my presence is on your ship, the more at peace my soul will be. I will go now, elantach. Guide your steel-winged bird." {n}Yrliet nods curtly and melts into the shadows of the bridge.{/n}

8fe292d7-436e-435a-9514-eca4f65405a1.Text: "Mon-keigh lives pass so swiftly. You rush through them for the sake of a chosen goal, but thoughts of transience and loss frighten you, and so you drive such thoughts away and drown yourselves in the daily tumult. But it is from fleeting moments, which enter our lives and quickly vanish from them, that the soul's fortress grows. A moment's blooming, an hour's wilting — the splendour of each lies in its ephemerality. So too the memories of those who have left our side and no longer walk the path with us."

751d08fd-8638-45e4-a3d2-58682defe0af.Text: "Think of the Lilaethan, the world on which our paths crossed. What is it truly? What is its essence? The Lilaethan's magnificence comes not from the green of its vast forests, or from the depths of its waters. Its beauty is in the word. In the way it dances on the tongue. And even you, elantach, can sense it. Try — say the word, slowly, delicately, casting aside all stray thoughts. Feel. Perhaps then you will see."

9d0ebc45-65a4-4298-91ed-3f60749cc036.Text: "Mon-keigh grow angry when they do not receive an answer. And when they do receive an answer, they grow angry then, too." {n}Yrliet steps back and looks away from you.{/n} "Let us leave this conversation in the past, and move on."

1c6d57c1-910b-40ff-8788-f73cb9bb3882.Text: {n}The world around you fades and your perception instantly narrows, coming to a single point of focus on the tip of your tongue. "Li" — your tongue delicately tickles the roof of your mouth, and the sound slips along your throat with incredible silkiness, warming as it goes like a sip of fresh recaf. "Lae" — the tip of your tongue touches the same place again and air softly rushes from your chest, the sound like the susurration of leaves as the wind weaves through a forest canopy. "Than" — your tongue taps your front teeth and a gentle vibration spreads through your body, sending a shiver along your spine.{/n}

9bb289f9-c731-4585-a935-ef95ffccffc1.Text: "Still, it was fascinating to observe your reaction. Now I am curious to know how you see this world."

6fd701b4-5549-415b-96cc-e2a1018bc410.Text: "Perhaps I was too hasty in my judgement of you. Perhaps your essence is only emptiness inside a colourful shell." {n}A stifled sigh escapes Yrliet's lips.{/n} "I warn you, elantach, one more insinuation and any chance of understanding between us will be forever lost to you."

71c0fed6-7b5d-413e-a7fa-24473d3f0dcb.Text: "Are you all right? You look different somehow."

71006fc8-8cec-455f-b2bf-fc379ef766c9.Text: "The Farseer said you underwent a rite of rebirth. Is that true?"

951392d5-2070-4d4c-a37a-e0cffbc61c8c.Text: [Wait for the rite to be completed]

09a95664-3b66-448a-84eb-e1b539b8b207.Text: [Stop the rite] "Get out of my way! If you won't help her, then I will do so myself!"

4942b92a-282d-4de5-83ac-ce7e1ee07998.Text: "Yrliet, did you manage to complete the rite?"

46bd3754-c0e7-4064-83f6-ae8385f17b7a.Text: "You were calling my name, Yrliet. I thought you needed my help."

94b245ef-e97f-454e-9c62-5550996eacee.Text: "We have to get out of here, while your body is still holding on outside."

b947fb44-5338-4c9e-ad9a-3e9b06dd26a6.Text: "It is so beautiful and quiet here. A stark contrast to my own world."

bd130424-1fe3-4e87-a588-147627121829.Text: "So, do all Aeldari souls look like this?"

93cb468b-9ec5-4acc-b3d5-a6d3b5ba8a12.Text: "You are now alone, without your kin or your spirit stone. If you want to survive — then be my sanctioned pet."

9ee2a37b-cc1a-4ca4-b3ae-c451f06f3aef.Text: "We're both safe. That's what matters most."

6d0a3991-1dd1-48b3-9649-c291a77f9c50.Text: "But I don't know how to get out of here! I don't even know how I got here."

199fd05d-0184-47ed-a288-397a84345ee5.Text: "Hurry, help me get out of here!"

7595fe66-7c85-4445-9004-2d941095ea5c.Text: "Yrliet, what will happen to you now?"

38b4d886-c2ef-49e0-91b1-2f61e42c4a81.Text: "What does this mean? Has Yrliet forgotten everything we've been through together?"

24a24c0b-1ee0-4227-8733-e52c5bec6dfd.Text: "You saved me. Shielded me with your soul."

cd745577-4f3e-44a0-b360-c6b2d62d13d1.Text: "Since when was the life of a mon-keigh more precious to you than your own?"

8190b0f2-dc3e-42ef-a4b6-add21c207e41.Text: "Nothing is over yet! I will stay by your side and help you find a new spirit stone."

32bcc0cc-e6bc-420b-b357-a43f7126af58.Text: "Forget about the arrogant Aeldari. I will grant you food and shelter — anything you could ever wish for!"

dc53bfa7-ab16-49a1-8bf5-141e62d13fad.Text: [Leave Yrliet in the forest] "It is said that revenge is a dish best served cold. Now you are all alone and this cursed forest shall be your grave."

85624a3f-4804-4f0e-b065-5de2d19d6fad.Text: "Stop the rite! Can't you see she is suffering?"

7ef2933c-f042-4ee1-9b52-0bb90408b283.Text: "You collapsed, screaming in pain. What happened?"

1b8291ca-b04c-47c4-8f84-17201416aa3c.Text: "I will never go near vile Aeldari magic ever again!"

6d638bc7-aed3-4ae7-946a-bc7e77cb357c.Text: "You have started calling me 'mon-keigh' again. Why?"

890466a7-03c2-4abe-8bc5-777e26d5c5af.Text: "But you have called me 'elantach' ever since we first met."

1711ddf3-7f18-46bd-b07f-110a4a4fd43d.Text: "Why are you standing there gawping? Fix it! There must be a way!"

0f1654f9-1847-4a81-8392-e8afb85481cf.Text: {n}Yrliet is on her knees, clinging to the spirit stone like a lifeline with both her hands. Her eyes are dim, her breath is uneven, and her body is trembling. The rite has definitely gone awry.{/n}

d2d2a26e-82d9-4eb6-9b59-9a8d18323a77.Text: {n}Yrliet looks down at her breastplate in astonishment, seeing her shattered spirit stone.{/n} "O merciful Isha..."

44523334-ee3f-42a7-b2f3-006ee1290fa9.Text: "Stop, elantach! This is... the very heart of my world. Too fragile for you to touch. You cannot come here. You... should not even be here!"

566b9ca1-9e6b-449a-8974-5d1c4a5d746c.Text: {n}The foreign world spits you out like waste. Your head is spinning, your entire body aches, and every muscle burns with the strain. It feels as if the thousands of gazes that were following you in Yrliet's world continue to watch you, evaluate you, judge you...{/n}

11b90674-66e4-4f83-b545-69399049b245.Text: "Welcome back to our world, child. Do you remember what happened? Do you know what will be?"

230fb70f-231e-43f9-b4e8-a579665312db.Text: "Or your ancestors decided to relieve you of them. When you first came, I saw dark spots in your soul, diminishing its glow. But now... now your soul is crystal clear."

83bea931-3ab1-457b-bb07-8a64c1c28667.Text: {n}Strange, subtle changes in her emerald eyes make your heart sink. Inexplicable anxiety crawls up your spine to whisper in your ear: something is wrong. Something is missing.{/n}

2403de94-221a-499d-8976-1f35f236cbd1.Text: {n}Yrliet's gaze radiates serenity and warmth, as if the screams and pain from a few moments ago were just your imagination.{/n}

280ac843-e9f9-460f-8e2f-4d6d7f6e0182.Text: {n}Several minutes pass before Yrliet shudders and... falls silent. Her arms hang limply at her sides, her gaze is turned toward the sky, and on her trembling lips appears the shadow of a smile.{/n}

6c2ed545-db9f-46f4-ad92-cfca59accb45.Text: {n}Yrliet shrugs, looking surprised.{/n} "I spoke with the souls of Alaitoc's ancestors. I remember a bright glow and hundreds of observant gazes piercing my soul. And then... I do not remember anything. I just woke up, mon-keigh."

ba431dd8-b9b0-4d42-bfac-c19e938e9b83.Text: {n}Yrliet slowly comes to awareness, turns her head, and looks into your eyes.{/n} "I spoke with them, mon-keigh."

a3be85c7-07e0-4210-bdd8-3d16edb1cfb4.Text: "I... do not know, {name}. I do not know." {n}Yrliet's gaze absently travels over her kin's faces, but they turn away from her in fear and disgust.{/n}

5cd170fb-fa1a-4950-aee8-20586b0ff322.Text: "I told you that everything comes with a price, Outcast. You have shielded mon-keigh from danger with your soul and ended up coming under the attack of our ancestors." {n}Shairenkhei sorrowfully shakes his head.{/n} "At least you survived the rite. Tell me — were your words heard?"

1610355b-41fb-4188-acf5-33c5321d273c.Text: "Oh, elantach, what have I done?" {n}Yrliet shakes her head in regret.{/n} "I am still connected to the souls of my ancestors. It is dangerous for you to be here. Leave!"

ccc08832-0a14-4119-a55f-d6b44ab9616d.Text: "My ancestors beheld the wounds inflicted on my soul during the search for Crudarach and the Drukhari's torture. The wounds that did not heal for many weeks while I was unable to meditate and immerse myself in my world. And they are somewhere here now — healing, patching, mending. And you, {name}... They also think you are one of the wounds bleeding inside my soul." {n}Yrliet looks at you with a gloomy, guilty look.{/n} "Let's try to do as we have done before — try and pull you out of my world with medita—"

ffadf79e-d95b-4365-a275-2a9528bd771b.Text: "We should not compare our worlds, elantach. Mine is a blossoming garden that I have tended and cherished for years. Yours is still young and ungraceful — as it should be."

add9d095-f8f2-4287-b199-ef8e802280f0.Text: "An inner world is just a reflection of how we see our soul. Everyone shapes it differently and each one is unique."

bcdcbfc6-2b16-41c9-8993-d1b20276b335.Text: "My body will endure, elantach. Because I—"

962d8742-dc1e-4057-a7a4-137ef88dece5.Text: {n}Yrliet anxiously looks around, and shadows of doubt start to weave their way into the corners of her beautiful world.{/n} "Do not worry, {name}. I will protect you, whatever happens."

679070f2-37d5-4dcc-a68e-13f68c515228.Text: "Yes, that might work. Do you remember our meditation? Let go of everything, elantach. Doubts. Fears. Anxie—"

78af1a34-250b-400a-8704-25ce74b9eeff.Text: {n}You feel a strange prickling sensation starting from the tips of your ears all the way to your toes. A wave of warmth and calm crushes over you, giant and inescapable — and with it, the sense of someone watching you. As if thousands of eyes are trained upon you at the same time. You do not belong here. You should not be here.{/n}

caf51053-f00c-4102-ae6e-223d0013ef28.Text: "{name}, are you all right?" {n}Yrliet kneels over you, peering into your eyes with a worried expression.{/n} "Yes... yes, I see. You are unharmed."

ef391e6e-fefd-4059-b022-1a88d88c7be4.Text: {n}The Crudarach Aeldari, shocked by your sudden return from the depths of another's world, approach slowly, observing you and Yrliet, who has just awoken.{/n}

06cfd3cd-e938-4620-8ce8-a722b00fce68.Text: {n}The Aeldari warrior nods at your question.{/n} "We are eager to know as well, sister. Asuryan was merciful toward you, as were our ancestors from Alaitoc's Infinity Circuit. Tell us — what was their answer?"

980f9323-12b5-4aaa-910a-145c4e59d59b.Text: {n}Yrliet shrugs, looking surprised.{/n} "I do not think it is so, mon-keigh. I spoke with the souls of Alaitoc's ancestors. I remember a bright glow and hundreds of observant gazes piercing my soul. And then... I do not remember anything. I just woke up."

a7df8cdd-b3b7-4559-9c30-2e9f14d41c8f.Text: "Because you are one of them, mon—" {n}Yrliet blinks, confused.{/n} "Yes... my memory is slowly returning. For ones like you, we use the word 'elantach.'"

141a1802-ec4b-4058-9c28-1f2a9fbbb5fd.Text: "Even if we wanted to, mon-keigh, it is impossible to recreate a spirit stone so easily. But I will not let you into the secrets of my kin, for you are also at fault for what has happened to the Outcast."

439fce66-5623-4b7b-8fba-77781589f5f1.Text: "The ancestors from Alaitoc beheld the wounds inflicted on my soul during the search for Crudarach and the Drukhari's torture. The wounds that did not heal for many weeks while I was unable to meditate and immerse myself in my world. And they decided to help me — to heal me, patch me up, mend me. But you, {name}... They also thought you were one of the wounds bleeding inside my soul." {n}Yrliet looks at you with a gloomy, guilty look.{/n}

6a3481be-9534-48a9-a533-58fb9a591aaf.Text: "I do not understand... Why would Alaitoc's souls do something like this?"

c1ecbc5e-4f3c-459a-9474-a35ea2846e48.Text: {n}The Farseer stumbles back in horror.{/n} "Oh, this is your punishment, Outcast! For your betrayal of your own kind!"

91727d72-2948-4a1d-8dae-5f2364acdb05.Text: "You became imprisoned in my world, {name}. And when the souls of my ancestors targeted you to rid my world of everything that did not belong there, I..." {n}Yrliet stammers.{/n}

9f5f1b9f-86cb-4d73-80b3-fff22492ac37.Text: "It seems that you became part of the rite when you drew too close. That is why I did not sense you straight away and why you could not leave." {n}With a trembling hand, Yrliet strokes the spirit stone shards, then jerks her hand away with a cry, staring at a cut on her finger.{/n}

48ba04c5-408c-4a4c-8459-73d69c01a13e.Text: "They would have healed my soul and made you disappear. But I did not want that. I... will decide for myself when to walk side by side with you and when our ways will part. The freedom to choose, even if the choice is dangerous and wrong — that is my Path, {name}. That is what I live and fight for."

0cbf2e90-022e-446f-a5f0-79e49c3e3af6.Text: "Wait! If you change the rite, you could make everything even worse for Yrliet!"

bf20963a-54de-422f-bcee-185be8b990a9.Text: {n}Shairenkhei signals his warriors, and they start to gather.{/n} "Our ways part here, Outcast."

266c70ce-255d-4c0d-847f-d5308b3605ec.Text: {n}Avoiding Yrliet as best they can, the Aeldari scatter across the meadow and disappear into the shadows of the forest. She watches them leave, her fists clenched so hard that her knuckles have turned white.{/n} "So ended the Path of the Outcast."

6052e8cb-a14e-4924-a577-b5b9ed474d17.Text: {n}Your words make Yrliet smile slightly.{/n} "If only it were that easy, elantach. One must know how to bond an empty spirit stone with a soul, intertwine it with one's inner world, and be able to contain it. Only the Farseer castes are capable of such a feat, but now my kin have turned their backs on me... and not for the first time."

601c5bd9-cd6a-43dc-94a3-06ee46bd84b6.Text: {n}Gripping the broken stone out of habit, Yrliet backs away.{/n} "No, {name}. You cannot do this to me. Y-you cannot..." {n}Fear and despair grow in her eyes, and, without waiting for an answer, Yrliet turns around and runs — to get away from you.{/n}

aadf2d59-ca95-4902-8834-240ca0df7a0a.Text: "Kae-morag, they are already here! Run... run away now, {name}!"

183a3dc2-61c0-4f8e-8e7d-e32c32957864.Text: "I..." {n}Yrliet looks around, lost, but there is no one left to help her. You can see the fear clawing at her from the inside, and she nods curtly without saying a single word.{/n}

09d3840a-fc4a-4dd3-8a56-773f18f28c28.Text: "All I ever wanted was to be free" {n}Yrliet shakes her head in grief.{/n} "And instead I have become a pet. Well, at least I will feel more comfortable in your ship than in the forests of this world."

cd622ccf-0a81-4b30-a7d2-a01d8c3dfcf7.Text: "Let us go, elantach. Let us leave this graveyard of doubts, unfulfilled hopes, and newfound fears. Together."

d048fe52-bb39-43be-9ad9-db3576be4986.Text: "Elantach, I understand that..." {n}Yrliet stops mid-sentence and looks down at her breastplate in astonishment, seeing her shattered spirit stone.{/n} "O merciful Isha..."

5c4bf91c-5088-4604-a145-bf31d1e8be7f.Text: {n}Yrliet's body keeps trembling in pain, but her face is inscrutable — her thin lips are whispering something in the Aeldari language, her hands relentlessly forming ornate gestures.{/n}

ed880d1d-1861-4a19-840b-95b0768bfdc9.Text: "Now that Yrliet's soul is left without protection, the insatiable gaze of She Who Thirsts will forever be trained upon her. And if the Outcast dies, her soul will never be able to join her ancestors in the Infinity Circuit — Sai'lanthresh will devour it in that very moment."

40c4b51a-ed67-4c23-8570-8c03fdef5701.Text: "No. At least I do not remember anything like that."

4880955c-b4f0-4269-b3bd-90b5780d34a0.Text: {n}Yrliet thinks for a moment.{/n} "It... is possible. But I remember little of that time and of you, elantach. Perhaps I lost some of my memories during the rite."

6c2a1f78-19bf-4bfd-ba95-87d0250cceab.Text: "I think many of her memories will eventually return. But something in her soul has irrevocably changed."

f9ce82cb-f36e-4d3b-bac7-2c4335f167a4.Text: "The Rite of Bonding is dangerous, and the Outcast knew the price. I do not know what she sees, hears, and feels. But there is one truth — the Outcast's soul is impure and the Alaitoc ancestors have noticed this. Most likely, the Outcast will go through the Rite of Rebirth... or perish."

ad7aabfd-2a7e-4a3e-95d6-e8a7054be10e.Text: "Your faith in me? Did I hear that right?"

bba3bd87-68e6-4efc-9e5a-47a68420e9ea.Text: "I cannot help with meditation, but I am prepared to stay with you and share the silence. That way, you will be able to forget about the horrors of Commorragh, if only for a little while."

04a4a0e0-37cf-4153-89a7-c1392b41ee62.Text: "I do not think I will ever be able to completely trust you."

4f281867-936e-4ff8-bad8-a1c85faebb48.Text: "I understand why you did that. And I forgive you."

70ea184c-80b1-46cb-b0de-484bee951167.Text: "I have always been honest with you, Yrliet. You, however, lied to me from the start."

5f86747a-d484-46be-b145-88a34907f333.Text: "How are you going to regain your powers now?"

8562dbbb-c840-4c66-bc61-c6b5a996d9e7.Text: "I wish I could embrace you and give you comfort, but you cannot bear human touch."

b147bc0d-caae-40d2-8037-a82680e32dae.Text: "I hope you find a way to deal with that."

cc45e6f9-a3cc-42cc-8a31-f0a90dc17307.Text: "I already told you that I know nothing about the shard. That trophy belonged to Theodora, my predecessor."

a58d5004-ab97-41a6-b8a4-eb0faac412a7.Text: "You are unable to meditate? Can that happen?"

2f6832f7-cbe6-4099-a13e-13948416b9f9.Text: "{name}, I..." {n}Yrliet's usual pride and arrogance give way to awkwardness and confusion.{/n} "This is my first time ever having to explain myself like this. But you... more than anyone... deserve to know the truth."

67e5d9d2-3399-4ad9-9f8b-b8e964bf029d.Text: {n}Yrliet looks you straight in the eye.{/n} "The time I spent with you, our conversations, the glow of your soul that only I can see... Yes, faith. With you, I..." {n}She stammers, at a loss for words.{/n}

53970d47-1116-47bc-b201-b49966cf3040.Text: {n}Yrliet freezes for a second, then gestures for you to take a seat nearby.{/n} "We had a saying on Crudarach: in silence you can hear a heartbeat — the music of the soul trying to burst out. Please, share this wordless song with me, {name}. And may it bring peace to us both."

89de8adf-4123-436a-9370-998be3f3c7d1.Text: {n}Yrliet lowers her head in shame.{/n} "There is indisputable truth to your words. I should have realised sooner that you were worthy of more than what I offered you. You are worthy... of my trust. Forgive me my arrogance, {name}."

8e2ce088-670a-4d37-ab39-f3788601e002.Text: "I understand, elantach. You have forgiven me and reminded me of the Path I walk. For that alone, I am endlessly grateful to you."

3cc4494d-e3bc-4ab5-994c-7e42b3a9d02a.Text: {n}Yrliet makes an elegant gesture and nods curtly.{/n} "I would love to talk for longer, but any respite in the Dark City does not last long. When you are cornered prey, you must remain vigilant and expect to be tested at any moment. I will prepare for what awaits us."

a790a6db-b73e-4993-a03f-427cac63e028.Text: {n}Yrliet's eyes widen in surprise.{/n} "I give you my word, {name}, I will never betray your trust ever again. You have shown great compassion by accepting me and forgiving my deed. I do not know if I would have been able to do the same."

a53c01bf-b472-44ee-904e-bc2a18fc818b.Text: "It pains me to know the hardships you had to endure because of me. And you still suffer — in this cursed arena, in this cursed city. I also..." {n}Yrliet pauses as if hesitant to continue.{/n} "My soul is crushed, elantach. The loss of Crudarach, the horrors of Commorragh, and the Drukhari's attempts to re-educate me... I have fully paid the price. I have lost my Path and can no longer... meditate. My body and my soul know no peace now. And that means that She Who Thirsts will soon turn her predatory gaze on me."

5ee58316-b380-4534-af78-ec937e0e2d4f.Text: {n}Yrliet shudders and ponders your words for a long while as she battles silently with herself. But then she shakes her head.{/n} "No. I cannot bear it, elantach. But the fact that you remember this and respect my feelings means a great deal to me."

f282d2c5-40ab-49d4-8116-1a88a5f01cfb.Text: "Asuryan will not abandon his child in such a dark hour, elantach. I am sure of it."

89fc6585-f29f-4dd8-9756-bdf92d44889a.Text: "I... I do not know." {n}Sincere hopelessness rings in Yrliet's voice.{/n}

6f0b09a9-380f-4f76-81da-43589152d52e.Text: "I understand how unworthy I am in your eyes. This may sound like a ridiculous excuse, but... I did not want to betray you, {name}. I only wished to learn the truth about Crudarach's demise and find my kin. And when I saw the shard of my world in your dwelling, that trophy mounted on the wall, I was beside myself with fear and rage. And when my dark cousin whispered in my ear that he knew the answers to my questions... I made a mistake. I trusted my kin. And, fearing that you might refuse me if you knew where I had been getting my orders from, I simply asked you to direct your ship to the particular system."

ce967682-0d4f-4da1-b470-17e30f44ee11.Text: "Did I trust Marazhai? No, of course not. I thought he spoke of my kin's location to crush my soul — that he wanted me to go there and find only death instead of them. But hope... hope for the better... prevailed over my faith in you, elantach." {n}Yrliet sighs awkwardly, avoiding your gaze.{/n} "Filled with hope, the thought never even crossed my mind that this single thread, forever slipping from my grasp, would lead us to the very heart of the Dark City. I am sorry, {name}. And I wanted you to know that."

38797b1d-1a91-451a-9512-a7865c3831d8.Text: "So you are not the one to blame for the destruction of Crudarach, but your blood is?" {n}Yrliet purses her thin lips.{/n} "No, I will not condemn you and your blood. No more. My accusations have already cost us too much."

828d7d97-51be-4651-a5fc-864dd30155d8.Text: "I have heard stories about Aeldari unable to reach their inner world because of anguish or madness. And every story had a tragic ending."

c17f76ac-18e1-4782-8936-c6ba05f7c6ab.Text: {n}A bitter smile touches Yrliet's lips.{/n} "But you are here too, elantach?"

13878856-7046-45bb-8992-7d72cea05e24.Text: "I am somewhat surprised, but I am not opposed to such visits. You may come here any time you like."

67b180fd-ba5a-4f4d-99e1-42bfeecf1a75.Text: "Why are you in my chambers? And uninvited, at that?"

294cf2bc-d235-4926-b529-cb77c439fd63.Text: [Draw your weapon] "Are you spying on me, xenos? Or are you plotting something even more sinister?"

6ac79071-1fd2-4e6c-845e-f978af2805b4.Text: "You do understand how suspicious this looks, yes?"

08dd9b3b-516f-46ec-a9da-9f5f7e78eda8.Text: "Do the Aeldari not teach their children that barging into others' rooms is improper?"

af800f4d-fda0-40cd-9b6d-592581ebc45e.Text: "I remember our agreement and will fulfil it, just as I promised."

650f737b-b02f-4e0d-a8ce-0ec0c7ec8cb8.Text: "Before I leap to any conclusions, explain what you are doing here."

d74b9280-76ab-407b-9486-f7a4c7347476.Text: "Something has changed. It is as though you have cut yourself off from me. Yrliet, what is going on?"

fb569681-a033-495f-9f55-3ccf68ededd9.Text: "I inherited this trophy from my predecessor."

6728c825-986d-419c-9b72-dde00b976d87.Text: "Is it... a piece of something Aeldari?"

ed76bfcb-19c4-4c42-a4d6-9ba41a428602.Text: "If you truly did not come here with nefarious intent, then simply apologise for your intrusion."

46409a68-88c6-4796-baa9-53ada258c164.Text: "I think you know something about this trophy."

18170379-410f-4df5-b4f9-f15a7bb2d226.Text: "Do not tell me what to do or how to behave."

6acb9692-6d20-4b44-a77e-325fe81f34a4.Text: "Do not give up. You will find what you are looking for."

43889b53-e4e0-4391-95e2-d3570411e88a.Text: "I stand by my actions. Your kin got nothing less than what they deserved."

423ce5cd-dae5-46e1-8581-fa2241de1709.Text: "If something displeases you, you are to leave my ship at any time."

3ddab40b-611c-4230-a126-a96ad76ad4cf.Text: "How did you manage to slip past the enforcers?"

e16103d0-6549-4f42-bc2a-4fe2327d2f0b.Text: "Yrliet? What a pleasant surprise to see you here."

da098601-ce94-4b3f-8fc1-6e9146f2a2c0.Text: [Attack] "I don't believe a single word, xenos!"

364e376c-41e2-4167-931e-ac771f05673e.Text: "Watch your tone, Aeldari, or you will regret speaking to me in such a manner."

faf183fc-5bfc-4708-a9cb-78b4d804d817.Text: "For humans, trespassing is akin to an insult."

e464300a-4646-48da-82db-5e9cb29f85a7.Text: {n}Taking careful steps, almost without a sound, Yrliet examines the study's interior, raising her brows in surprise and muttering something to herself in the Aeldari tongue.{/n}

59a3018a-ac2e-4ac8-899b-99bf12b19968.Text: "You know I avoid your kin and their obsessive attention. It was fairly easy to distract a couple of mon-keigh and slip past them..." {n}Meeting your eyes, Yrliet nods in understanding.{/n} "I suppose this is not pleasant news to hear."

c222fdb3-103a-4b0d-a9d9-b950005c9eb6.Text: "I was not wrong to think so, was I?" {n}For a moment, a sad smile flickers on Yrliet's face, and her voice rings with agonising doubt.{/n} "No matter what, you... tried to keep your promise. Even if your species loves to stamp out any life form they find undesirable..."

1dc49a5a-8ebc-4d13-a5da-6ddb4d97c800.Text: {n}Yrliet shrugs her shoulders, unfazed.{/n} "Curb your ire, elantach. You think I would attempt to scout out your secrets like this? No. I have merely been exploring the belly of the steel-winged bird — as ugly and awkward as it may be, it is nevertheless carrying through the darkness, the stars, and the depths of the warp. I had no idea this was your dwelling until I entered it."

c56cb3d2-b95d-4844-aec1-63362e2fdb50.Text: "Only in your eyes, elantach. But knowing how fearful and mistrustful your species is, I suppose I should have foreseen such a reaction."

489d9f05-4131-4453-8b51-a38aca2aac2a.Text: {n}Yrliet tilts her head in confusion.{/n} "Do I need permission to do so?"

0cbdc881-1dc7-43af-931c-f4cdc3792b30.Text: "I had no idea this was your dwelling until I entered it." {n}The Aeldari turns her emerald gaze on you — it seems she is completely unfazed by your sudden appearance.{/n}

d8d10805-78f8-4860-947d-68a7d360e996.Text: "On my craftworld, we all held to a simple custom — you may set your foot wherever your Path requires. Sacred ground was the only exception to this rule. Is there something sacred in this room, elantach?" {n}Yrliet looks around the room.{/n} "I do not think so."

80f93140-8b36-4315-b46d-3d676f2066a8.Text: {n}Yrliet's words are interrupted by a strange sound similar to a stifled sigh, her gaze trained upon something past you. Turning around, you see what has caught her attention — an odd, unsightly shard of porous material, mounted on the wall like a trophy. An entire kaleidoscope of emotions plays across her face, changing too quickly to catch. She sighs once more... and then her feelings are concealed behind an impenetrable, impersonal mask.{/n} "What is this, mon-keigh?" {n}Yrliet's voice sounds unusually cold.{/n}

0be233a4-3838-4054-86bc-ccca4408a07d.Text: "What is this, elantach? Consolation? What do you—"

e846629d-1a32-478c-851e-ad75d98afc0e.Text: {n}The strange shard has been here since at least the day of your ascension to the Rogue Trader's throne. Looking closely, an odd thought nags at your mind: it may be disfigured and corroded by some unknown power, but it vaguely resembles wraithbone, a material crafted by the Aeldari.{/n}

5d45dbbf-b989-4376-9625-b8f578952165.Text: {n}The strange shard has been here since at least the day of your ascension to the Rogue Trader's throne. Whatever it is, you cannot possibly guess at its provenance or purpose.{/n}

d6d7e40b-886a-4169-8d7e-e2c4af20ed95.Text:
{n}Yrliet looks at you — her eyes devoid of every emotion, every shred of life and warmth that you previously beheld in them.{/n}
"You are observant, elantach. How unusual. But there is no need to trouble your mind with conjecture. I have inflicted enough of my unbridled feelings upon you, but I am in control again."

a29bceee-9de6-43c3-be47-435a3a5220e5.Text: "So you do not even care enough to know what objects adorn your dwelling? Truly?" {n}Yrliet lets out a thin, sorrowful sound, then cuts herself short, going as still as a statue.{/n}

3dce45d2-ffcd-4a8e-bdc2-7a4b08323106.Text: "So that is it? You are proud of the victories and violence of your blood while being ignorant of their true nature?" {n}The usually verbose Yrliet now speaks in short, clipped sentences.{/n}

f5c6bb68-2d21-4315-80d2-750587785893.Text: {n}Yrliet glares at you, her eyes full of naked rage.{/n} "Enough! I will not listen to your webs of words that are trying to shroud my mind!"

c08ad872-4d63-47b2-982c-7852c4d45ff3.Text: "This shard... is but a small part of something much larger. Something great... now reduced to a trophy on a mon-keigh's wall..." {n}A kaleidoscope of emotions rages on Yrliet's face for a few moments before she lets out a ragged sigh.{/n}

364511a2-86e6-4bc6-a2ba-67361a0bda28.Text: "Enough. I have lingered here too long. From now on, I... will avoid entering places you would prefer to keep hidden from me."

d93ebb85-04e8-4ab3-9a4b-0fbde25048ad.Text: "Did I ever think I would encounter this again after Crudarach?" {n}Yrliet laughs sorrowfully.{/n} "Stiff, meaningless rules... and condemnation for overstepping lifeless boundaries. It weighed so heavily upon me. Back then."

9abfa5e0-5af9-49f8-b71f-6259f26552c4.Text: {n}Yrliet gives you a barely visible nod. Her face is clouded with emotion, but you cannot read her expression.{/n} "Your words, elantach — they are something that still gives me ho—"

ef2d8c4c-ea40-40ae-ae79-45088deac36a.Text: "Then make haste and prove that your words have at least some—"

301caf51-a414-44b2-8b91-39c6fb059e83.Text: "But the direction of your thought eludes me, elantach. With one hand, you bestow mercy upon my kin, yet take their lives with the other. What is it? A flaw of your soul... or of the blood that flows in your veins? I am... frightened by your fickleness."

ecbe1e07-397a-4233-a742-48d6d7913b8b.Text: {n}Yrliet turns to you.{/n} "Why are you asking me this, elantach? Is this place forbidden?"

7b7e01a4-d82c-4021-b075-206cf90148db.Text: "But is your entire world contained within this tiny metal cage, elantach? Your ship, these chambers — they are but a speck of dust. An island. A temporary shelter in a world that is far bigger and more expansive than... Well, enough of that. Now that you are here, I wish to speak with you... about our agreement."

d990676c-b74b-4c87-b261-091e33bf76c1.Text: "I do not understand why your soul is burning with anger. This room is no different from any other." {n}There is no flicker of surprise in the Aeldari's calm gaze, suggesting she has been aware of your presence — and scrutiny — since you entered.{/n}

f0b573a5-92eb-4724-ac6e-529dd5cfc767.Text: "And for what?" {n}Yrliet jerks her head, rage burning in her eyes.{/n} "My kin, the reason why I agreed to travel with you, have not been found! Why have you not focused all your efforts on searching for them? To save them from burning in the fires of hatred between our species? I put my faith in you, elantach!"

91e5c7f7-e282-4feb-9746-6d35612ccb67.Text: "And we... we have managed to find some of the children of Crudarach. Find and bear witness to their horrifying fate." {n}Yrliet half-closes her eyes.{/n} "I think that every step I take to discover Crudarach's fate brings nothing but doom to my brothers and sisters. And still... I ask you not to stop. With every cycle, those still hidden in the darkness of the cosmos draw closer to their demise... and obscurity. Out of all the mon-keigh I have met... I thought... that you — you, elantach — might be able to understand me and my pain."

08f0fc15-9806-4537-b97f-2337ce8e5dd4.Text: "We found everyone we could, elantach, and all of them... were dead." {n}Hopelessness and despair gleam in Yrliet's eyes, and her voice breaks treacherously.{/n} "But the thread of fate is broken and I no longer know how to help my people. I failed to save anyone. And I failed to learn the truth about Crudarach's demise. I... have lost my way. And I thought you were the only person on this entire ship who might understand."

0d745762-1036-428c-950e-63ad9292337d.Text: "But I was mistaken." {n}You see disdain in the Aeldari's face when you lock eyes again,{/n} "Like the other mon-keigh, you treat my kin with wanton hatred and cruelty. You did not even try to save them! Perhaps... trusting you was a mistake. Now I am like a hostage trapped on your ship, chained by debt and hopelessness."

dd8e0fff-e2a8-44df-a378-cb8739787d2e.Text: "I have travelled through the veil many times inside your steel-winged bird, and every time Her voice torments me, trying to drive me mad..." {n}Yrliet stares through you, unconsciously touching the spirit stone on her chest with a trembling hand.{/n} "Her whispers fill my ears each time I enter the warp. Inescapable and incessant, poisoning and inflaming every single emotion and thought, making them uncontrollable. I have... learned to shut myself off. As best I can. Just so that I might have the chance to... search for what I have lost."

5ea68a8d-9c7d-45fc-89ee-40b99f94f0db.Text: "Heinrix, what punishment awaits him who failed to realise his own acolyte was a traitor?"

96e8fe9f-b479-43aa-8114-cbe94bd04fad.Text: [Execute Yrliet] "Kibellah, enact the will of the Undying Emperor."

ed1280f4-422b-46e3-ae06-668c43e89603.Text: [Give Yrliet to Heinrix] "I keep my promises, van Calox."

939ab4f6-1086-4050-8d61-852b7e7353ff.Text: "Saints' blood, what manner of farce is this?"

91191225-48b6-4ab1-8809-3241c3d8863f.Text: [Execute Yrliet] "I have been waiting for this moment ever since I woke up on the streets of Commorragh."

4a428dad-1c66-4733-941b-bf6f5a6e5e99.Text: [Give Yrliet to Heinrix] "Do me a favour, Heinrix."

05b960c6-ff63-4300-a29f-3d5d40d7f6a5.Text: [Execute Yrliet] "Would you be so kind, Sister Argenta?"

14a3c2dc-2dc4-4429-af8c-1fc84d932e28.Text: "Yrliet will receive corporal punishment — as many lashes as her body can endure without expiring."

6295a648-9ad2-4b33-b241-f94acf0ce69c.Text: "I would have never left you at their mercy."

7b48ac67-3b74-4f21-af99-8e2a0d9d530d.Text: "I think you may have forgotten who gives the orders on this ship. How dare you burst onto the bridge and make demands of me?"

88721fa2-b6f9-479b-8606-81fadc297471.Text: "If you shared with them what you shared with me in Commorragh, they would surely understand your actions."

37779bb2-d308-44af-a90d-2b51d7aa3f20.Text: "Anyone else want to share their thoughts?"

21fbb0cf-a755-46a5-886d-b272b7abbacd.Text: "Yrliet is here to stay as part of my retinue. Get used to it."

5d4884c6-679e-4f5c-8ffd-43522792d60d.Text: "They will forgive you. Not all of them, and not right away, but they will."

53e84bea-225c-4177-b878-0e41d05180e1.Text: "Do you really not care about what happened? Or are you trying to conceal your true feelings again?"

324d51d5-ca94-4487-a840-9c5badb79376.Text: "Yrliet will now apologise to everyone who was harmed by her deed. And that will be enough."

66901420-4f6e-4dab-8ce6-819e3e73c854.Text: "It is time to get back to work."

36083610-e478-4793-b69c-c0a4847ae37d.Text: "Let the past stay in the past."

4288601a-2eff-4cf3-bb10-ae7e07bc5d19.Text: "I only know that everyone makes mistakes. And everyone hides the parts of their personalities they are not proud of. That is true of both humans and Aeldari."

05547ae1-332b-4902-8ef5-83a132d6bc57.Text: "You have already become part of my world. You may have done something disagreeable in my eyes, but that does not make you a stranger."

e4d3ca82-02ec-4399-977e-6f06bceaeca0.Text: {n}The bridge is enveloped in an unusual silence — the officers on duty are huddling in the corners, looking on curiously at what is transpiring in the centre.{/n}

658d41bf-1bd1-48c8-8d81-5ff226bce124.Text: "For how long are you going to tolerate this filth on your ship, {name}? This foul traitor, who has already dragged you into the darkness once and who almost left your protectorate without its sovereign!"

9f1dfd59-8604-4f58-b819-ec26792e7418.Text: "Rogue Trader." {n}Heinrix's voice makes your blood run cold.{/n} "Has Aeldari heresy clouded your judgement? Treachery always means death — either for the traitor or the one betrayed. You almost died in Commorragh. Your retinue... you know what became of them. Is it not high time that justice was done?"

3fdba8bf-13bc-4b33-bc57-00691cc811d5.Text: {n}Those present nod wordlessly but do not dare to interfere.{/n}

19036c27-1972-43bd-8ca3-fa68d62e737c.Text: "You promised to give me the Aeldari as soon as we escaped that accursed nest of xenos. It is time."

2cf1e0fa-c083-44fa-986c-e142f121e795.Text: "Now this is a fine spectacle — the inhuman gets what she deserves! Let us all watch and laugh."

e05086de-3b85-441a-91fa-161bc91fbcd3.Text: "Your wonderful Path has led you into a rather thorny situation, cousin. You refused to beg for mercy in Commorragh, and now you will have to lick the boots of mon-keigh."

eb75f02a-a241-4e41-8d4b-7fbeae4fad19.Text: {n}Yrliet does not react to the curses being slung at her. With an imperturbable expression, she watches the crowd before her, then turns her gaze to you.{/n}

15fbdada-44c5-4ee7-8410-fa60fff0b6a7.Text: {n}Catching sight of you, the curious crew members dash to their posts, leaving only the senior officers in the middle of the bridge.{/n}

65bdf1fd-cf8d-4a95-8566-7db629927911.Text: {n}Van Calox turns his gaze to Marazhai, who glances at you and the Interrogator with mocking hope on his face.{/n} "A lesson that will fully sink in."

c9c626ed-0c59-421e-9312-7ea6c80c6b55.Text: {n}Heinrix gives a vague shrug.{/n} "That is not enough. But at least the xenos will be taught a lesson."

b86ac56f-626a-40a4-ba33-dea7e37f27d7.Text: "Pain can heal a human soul, but what about a xenos? I have no answer for that."

605d672a-47a4-49eb-acb7-8158b5eaf014.Text: {n}A predatory grin spreads across the Interrogator's face.{/n} "With great pleasure."

d2a095c1-f033-4842-8319-98f90de046be.Text: {n}Realising her impending death, Yrliet simply closes her eyes.{/n} "O Asuryan, have mercy upon your child's soul..."

506e021b-803e-43d2-951b-f68a04564828.Text: {n}Yrliet shudders, but then quickly frowns slightly and shrugs her shoulders nonchalantly.{/n} "I do not think mon-keigh whips are more fearsome than the torture of the Dark City."

6a6d844e-ddce-4b9e-af59-9abf28d4fcf9.Text: {n}Yrliet smiles slightly.{/n} "Of course not. You are you."

1f93094d-6237-4f35-81fc-252707e60f50.Text: {n}Heinrix narrows his eyes, disappointed.{/n} "Deplorable indulgence of the enemies of Humanity, Rogue Trader. And of your own weak will."

d5ba90ab-1500-4317-914c-4556928cfea5.Text: "The one who points out a mistake shall be rewarded for the truth. But if you do not wish to see the truth, remain among the blind."

bb87324d-d7a5-4929-9f5a-ea6cce734aa1.Text: {n}Everyone present timidly averts their eyes. Speaking up against you definitely was not part of the plan.{/n}

6d8dbbdf-6923-4fbd-834a-32f0e036c54a.Text: "You know, Lord Captain. I will support any order you give, but to keep the xenos in the retinue, especially after everything..." {n}Abelard casts a tense look at the lower bridge.{/n} "...after everything that has transpired because of her — it would not be wise."

7f58db51-3a19-4592-ab30-9e6a8ac12c2c.Text: "The enemies of Humanity have no place among humans. You know this." {n}Cassia's hands shake a little and she clenches her fists.{/n} "But death is far too merciful a sentence. What I endured... was far more terrible."

c12faa09-aff2-4f93-851a-a7825e25c536.Text: "I don't know, Lord Captain." {n}Idira is unusually subdued.{/n} "You can punish her, but, you know, death is... permanent. It's not like we were stuck in Commorragh forever, you know?"

887e04f4-5f0a-43a8-8837-cdb417535678.Text: "You know, shereen, when a pet refuses to obey their master, they are usually put in a cage at best or turned into a lovely piece of taxidermy at worst."

3b893b0a-543b-4188-9002-b0e757f86f05.Text: "The heinous behaviour pattern of the xeno-entity and of specimens similar to her statistically leads to unfavourable and unpredictable outcomes."

f4531b95-44ba-45a8-b7b5-55dbdea603c2.Text: {n}After whispering about the terrifying punishment awaiting the Aeldari, the officers present slowly return to their duties.{/n}

459c8630-f657-44dd-862e-ab2b848d69e9.Text: "Humility is not one of your virtues, xenos. The Rogue Trader may have stood up for you, but... one wrong glance, one slip of the tongue, one suspicious gesture — and your life is over."

42d88f1e-603e-4f1e-b06a-4e7a80e65ee3.Text: "Easy forgiveness is a sign of impending weakness, Rogue Trader. Think on this." {n}Argenta reluctantly lifts her hand from her weapon.{/n}

91be7bd0-58d4-4d79-b117-cb603cf87204.Text: {n}Disappointed by the outcome of the confrontation, the officers present slowly return to their duties.{/n}

de31ef34-d648-45b6-9666-056e31ab3841.Text: "Words. Will not fix. What has been done." {n}The Interrogator grips his weapon, but he hesitates, shifting his intense gaze from you to the xenos, and then back.{/n}

e2cf0dab-5562-4e8d-ab7c-1f01477937d0.Text: "The xenos's apologies ring hollow. There is neither repentance nor truth to them."

accec2b2-707f-48e3-b936-ef1e2cd027b5.Text: {n}Yrliet's face contorts in a mix of emotions — from anger and hatred to dejection and despair. But soon, she musters her courage and in a stilted, barely audible voice, says,{/n} "My words will not heal the wounds on your bodies. And still, I regret what you had to endure. Because of me."

2b408fe4-4458-44c9-9884-51f4e09030ef.Text: {n}Marazhai laughs airily.{/n} "And now the Asuryani will walk on her hind legs before the mon-keigh. I am glad I decided to drop by to see what all the fuss was about..."

102e4df1-3ba8-4aeb-9d45-2c54723c0aff.Text: {n}Yrliet shrugs uncertainly.{/n} "Your mon-keigh have had it worse. I will live, and the wounds of my soul will eventually heal. They will live, too, but their souls... their souls will forever bleed painful memories."

571099f2-5854-4347-8fe2-4bec0fae693f.Text: "Stop it. You cannot believe that, elantach. I do not need words of comfort — the words of these mon-keigh do not touch my soul. Only your thoughts matter. Yours and mine."

7b1ce90d-658e-45b3-aabd-2897aa9fd05c.Text: "Do not leave just yet, elantach. Before you do... answer my question. I know we have talked a great deal, and you have even accepted what I did. But I also know that the mind and the emotions are not always in accordance. Now that the raging waves of danger have died down and Commorragh has been left far behind... What are your thoughts of me?"

60bac81e-ba59-4f8d-82ab-f903f6546eb8.Text: {n}Yrliet nods and gestures elegantly before leaving.{/n} "Until we meet again, elantach. May the darkness scatter into a myriad of new stars before you."

38fe3d5e-ffed-4c38-88bc-847b9430360b.Text: {n}Yrliet frowns distrustfully{/n} "These words are full of joy, but soon they will flow into a river of doubt and guilt. Bitter grass may never become a fragrant flower. Do not pretend that it never happened."

7d0a1f6d-e393-42be-a631-d865d1af3842.Text: {n}Yrliet smiles timidly in return.{/n} "Neither do I, elantach. The unknown... A conflicted state of the soul... It is bright, exciting, illogical. I like this feeling, but it also frightens me. I am glad that I can share this feeling with you while we walk the same road."

2d9db62a-d550-48bd-89ae-a42b2493b745.Text: {n}Heinrix shakes off his hands in disgust.{/n} "Before putting the xenos to sleep, I will interrogate her. I still... have many questions that need answers."

2f1105c9-261f-47df-9b80-d2c66890b02f.Text: "Lies and slander from the enemies of Humanity, Rogue Trader. Spare me... that."

980ea402-0bda-4dfb-a98d-7b19252e0048.Text: "Vil'Yrliet does not deserve death. For her, it would be a release from her sorrowful lot of being an unclean xenos." {n}Murderous rage flashes in Kibellah's black eyes.{/n} "But we... we do deserve her death. As payment for what we have endured."

534b5d5d-7233-432e-9d85-5ad2366324ee.Text: "This moment was predetermined by your unholy nature, Vil'Yrliet."

285d8cc9-7086-4d02-8945-dd686fe113db.Text: "I am... sorry that my mistake led anyone along the paths of the Dark City. I can see their pain and rage. I understand. But words and pity will not help them. Only time, and, perhaps, revenge, which will dull their pain for a little while. But you have taken away their chance for revenge, elantach. And all we can do now is wait."

33d7f00f-a933-4635-a322-ba88be1069d4.Text: "If this is your forgiveness, mon-keigh, I will face it with dignity. And I will never approach you alone again, to ease the fears of your servants." {n}Yrliet's voice sounds lifeless and dull. She no longer meets your eyes.{/n}

da57b28b-70e3-4bf9-b36e-3903446062e4.Text: "She serves as a clear example that the great powers bestowed by the Warrant must also be used with great caution. That is the end of her usefulness."

da6521a2-5bfa-493c-ad82-591d5b562aff.Text: {n}Yrliet shakes her head.{/n} "Those words were meant only for you, elantach. You are the only one I can trust with my feelings. Only to you can I bare my mental wounds. We have a... special history and a special bond, {name}. I do not care about the others."

227cad45-47bd-48fb-b39b-7ea3bc733b8d.Text: "I wish I could argue otherwise." {n}A short laugh escapes Yrliet's lips.{/n} "But I made a mistake. And I concealed my feelings and emotions from you. Perhaps you have done the same. But as long as we walk the same road, we have a chance to become better than we were before."

7040b726-37d0-46ab-8edc-5de0bba0f0a3.Text: "Enough, xenos. Justice will be done — one way or another." {n}Heinrix's voice drips with venom.{/n}

a6baf545-1097-47bd-afe4-a0357750c189.Text: "Slither all you like, heretic spawn, but you will never leave this ship unscathed."

07c729c2-0234-4d57-bf4b-885d4d37e8d5.Text: "I have seen your inner world, elantach. Aren't you letting too much into the very heart of you?" {n}A short laugh escapes Yrliet's lips.{/n} "Still, it is good to know that you have not locked your soul away from me."

c06e7b4b-6350-4a98-8074-4c08da297ccc.Text: {n}Upon hearing your words, the Interrogator stiffens and he grits his teeth in anger.{/n} "Achilleas died after receiving due punishment, even if it was not at the hands of the Inquisition. I will hear no more about it."

63594fae-ebd1-428c-9163-979d983901aa.Text: "Very well." {n}Without further ado, Heinrix raises his hand. You feel the echo of otherworldly cold.{/n}

9864edeb-8550-42e7-83f1-2a7f16fefbcb.Text: {n}Contempt smoulders in Yrliet's eyes, and a bitter smile twists her lips as she turns to face you.{/n}

2206ccbb-b055-436f-be3c-096aa26979bc.Text: "We both know your words are empty, mon-keigh. You will not disobey the elantach's orders, for you see no point in paying for my death with your own."

8457ec9b-4c73-4dbd-992e-cb09704c2d0a.Text: "I understand that this incident was unpleasant for you. But it does not mean that all humans are animals."

12caaf65-3dfd-4f4f-ab40-dd0f22e887ec.Text: "If you dislike how my people behave, try to spend your time somewhere more out of the way."

be288dea-f477-4aac-9563-8a3e960d4337.Text: "Fraternising with a xenos? Unspeakable heresy! Show me to this madwoman, and I shall see that she is suitably punished!"

104e336e-6359-4842-908a-7ac8d3ceba8c.Text: "I do not think you fully understand human thoughts and actions. It will take time, but I can help you make sense of them."

618a2ed0-7290-442d-8180-edb3c4ac3bac.Text: "You are an exotic animal to my people. Get used to it if you want to continue travelling on this ship."

f3534031-f390-407e-a7ad-f77480e6eb45.Text: "So I don't have a chance either, then?"

6df88aaa-59e9-4551-a725-2599617749ac.Text: "I am also repelled by the thought of a human desiring an Aeldari."

4e496e45-d7d7-4e5f-902a-10e2927f89a3.Text: "All humans are different. My people's interest in you was not intended to be an insult."

dc6205ac-8244-48d6-9557-3afc43ba847d.Text: "Next time, ask me before you decide to take justice into your own hands."

65cf1c76-9cb7-497c-bea9-47fec569170b.Text: "Let this be a lesson to all the other fools."

079d2a86-e8d7-4198-8728-be08fb944398.Text: "Do not ever kill my subjects, Yrliet. This is your first and last warning."

c0563d15-269d-4e90-8edf-bd4e68bcf50d.Text: "Sometimes we struggle to understand the motives behind our own actions."

146f8b78-08c3-403e-8ad6-db054aabbb56.Text: "And what do you see in the world around us that I do not?"

0d6d9956-a241-4650-8680-a9dc45a332c5.Text: "I think we will never be able to understand one another. Let's not discuss this any further."

bf9b8c43-f75b-4409-997f-c2859ebd5619.Text: "For you, I am willing to become a wild animal, or a docile pet."

48047d0b-3efd-4032-b239-0de82558b37b.Text: "I shall speak to my subjects. You will not be bothered again."

a1bf5f7a-0e74-4fea-aa30-3535ec32dd7f.Text: "I wouldn't mind going somewhere private with you either."

cbe0b864-e636-4dc6-88f3-95763a787757.Text: "Were you truly so offended by it?"

0df79f2e-c65f-4fd3-a89d-877285e8c9f8.Text: "You are a xenos, a strange and unknown creature. And humans strive to understand the unknown, for the unknown is the most frightening thing of all."

841ebebf-d4f5-4244-9ac2-e41ad740ba8d.Text: "Perhaps you would stop insulting the human race at every turn?"

8bc58c69-7395-40b3-b6ae-4a7ec1ad1a34.Text: "My people have behaved contemptibly, and I apologise for it."

dbe830f6-7bdd-4667-b5bd-999056171f34.Text: "Please spare me a brief moment of your time, elantach." {n}Yrliet quietly appears beside the throne, exhaustion and anger set upon her brow.{/n}

fe384829-df20-45cb-b4a8-7bb5587de3a0.Text: "No. Your kind's simple souls and narrow minds are the root of all these flaws."

838331de-814b-4b07-9869-167c53daf97b.Text: "Asuryan knows that I do not care about the curious glances of mon-keigh — I grew inured to them back in the blossoming gardens of the Lilaethan. They curse me from afar, they follow my every move, they ward themselves against me... Let them. After all, what can be done with such weak-minded, primitive creatures?"

925bbd7c-8fcb-4140-b951-818fd6870a89.Text: {n}Yrliet is so overwhelmed with emotion that her body starts to tremble.{/n} "Try to imagine, elantach, being lusted after by a wild beast. It is... foul. Disgusting. So vile that it makes your very soul shudder."

c3173ee9-a61f-4a0b-abc3-dbfa438e30f4.Text: "She is already dead, elantach. I could not let the offence go unpunished, so I took her life myself."

26e7900e-b36a-4b52-83d9-be8accb98fcc.Text: "I have walked the Path of Awakening, elantach, and learned to see that which is hidden and hear that which is unspoken. When I found myself on the Lilaethan, I watched your kind long enough to understand the true nature of mon-keigh. I do not think you can tell me anything I do not already know." {n}Casting a fleeting gaze at the officers on the bridge, she lets out a weary sigh.{/n} "Nevertheless, I will not protest. Conversations with you are the only thing on this ship that can ease my solitude."

835b3469-eab2-4e86-a3e9-8b5820726a49.Text: "As you should be. You, at least, have some faint understanding of my feelings, elantach... which cannot be said for your primitive kin."

a3dbee92-60f0-46b0-aa58-8963ef53b4d7.Text: "I have given you a chance by travelling with you, elantach. If you were having... other thoughts about me..." {n}Yrliet wrinkles her nose.{/n} "Cast them out of your mind."

538182fa-f0fb-4f32-a2a4-5de5770fc8c8.Text: "Then keep your servants on a shorter leash, mon-keigh."

0b8ca0d4-804c-4cc7-8921-3ea5fc80b91a.Text: "I am standing before you now precisely to avoid a repeat occurrence."

5650c0ca-20f5-4fae-ac72-83c93facb629.Text: {n}Yrliet nods slowly.{/n} "Mon-keigh usually grow angry when their property is damaged. I am glad that we have come to an understanding."

528c342c-d6fe-4e5f-925f-10fe53566070.Text: "Elantach, please understand that I do not find mon-keigh attractive. The mere thought of being intimate with one of your kind..." {n}Yrliet breathes out heavily, trying to maintain her composure.{/n}

401b39c9-a75c-4c29-a39c-0c19cdf468f4.Text: {n}After thinking for a moment, she nods.{/n} "I will need time to put the entire truth of this world into the meagre language to which your ears are accustomed. When I find my answer, I will pay you a visit."

df781859-57aa-412f-baa7-8ff2d5700d1a.Text: {n}Her slender fingers make a gesture as if she is untwisting an invisible thread.{/n} "Our conversation has only proved my point, elantach, that mon-keigh and the Children of Asuryan are as different as night and day. Aeldari do not simply see the world differently — they see more than any mon-keigh can ever comprehend."

2ef15e92-f1f7-49a3-ac8d-04fbfc31c029.Text: {n}Yrliet does not seem surprised. Perhaps a tad disappointed?{/n} "Then what of my request, elantach? Will you allow your kin to continue bothering me?"

f24b20dc-de87-47ef-98ad-8c62ce6fee20.Text: {n}Yrliet frowns as she looks at you, but only slightly.{/n} "I was wrong to expect your help. If my words have fallen on deaf ears, then I will deal with my problem myself."

f91d173e-862c-41d3-a056-b05eba5c9916.Text: {n}Yrliet tilts her head to the side, as if she cannot believe what she has just heard, and looks intently into your eyes.{/n} "I... accept your words, elantach. And still..."

c72cbd99-1673-421f-a34b-91c69de71d6d.Text: "And still..." {n}Yrliet touches her spirit stone and her face twists with genuine disgust.{/n} "One mon-keigh's stunt has caused the cup of my patience to spill over. She dared to approach me... to speak to me... and, touching my hand, she... she suggested that we withdraw somewhere private. She wanted... wanted... Kae-morag! The mere memory of it stirs up a tempest in my soul!"

f1c153bc-55a5-4139-aed8-1bc1db98c7a4.Text: "It was emotions that once brought down my kind, elantach, toppling us from our pedestal as rulers of the galaxy. Indulging your weaknesses — or whims — does not make your species any more attractive."

acc7a8b3-bac9-44f0-a5f2-40f4f3fd0ba2.Text: "Your words warm my soul." {n}Yrliet nods and is briefly lost in thought.{/n} "Very well, I will leave now. Do not forget your promise."

05e1353c-7539-41c5-a886-82ccdafe2c51.Text: "Narrow minds and simple souls... Every day, I feel as if I am caught in a trap, surrounded by a pack of wild animals." {n}Half-closing her eyes, she adds, her words barely audible,{/n} "I am prepared to pay this price to find my kin. But everything has its limit."

074d90fe-b6ef-4968-9cf7-d523dad53713.Text: {n}Half-closing her eyes, she adds, her words barely audible,{/n} "For the minuscule chance of saving my kin... I am prepared to pay this price. But everything has its limit."

35825ffa-3023-49e0-99c6-bc7f6c277bd8.Text: "Had any of them wished to understand my nature, they would have already run away in fear from one who walks the Path of the Outcast. But they are just trying to provoke me. Hurt me. No. Mon-keigh are driven by their instincts — to survive, to breed, to ensure the preservation of their species and the annihilation of those who threaten them... It is neither good nor bad. It simply is."

531e73a2-3d51-41a9-acde-981c206ad63f.Text: {n}Yrliet freezes in involuntary surprise.{/n} "The rotting core spells doom for the whole. Now I can see where the ugly nature of your servants originates. There is no sense in discussing this with you any further."

f187dc3b-9f38-4f4b-9917-f79d510d2a86.Text: {n}Yrliet considers this, then nods — more to herself than to you.{/n} "Your species is sensitive to the truth. I will have to remember that."

6c240f5e-6c80-4f4f-a82d-decd9d387e46.Text: "What do I see?" {n}Yrliet gives you a thoughtful look.{/n} "Your words ring with the desire to know the soul of another. But will you be able to comprehend my answer?"

bdb3713e-91c9-4987-8b0a-3f10caf63863.Text: "I just c-can't escape this cold... I've tried holding my hand over a candle, but the fire was like ice."

8598fff2-efc7-4474-9808-a02a72b0c4c4.Text: "Emperor's mercy! Your hands... Don't the blisters hurt?"

2fbb3717-7d23-4c57-8a6f-b8d184a486b1.Text: "N-no, it's just so cold. I'd give anything... to feel warm again."

da5ff4c8-4a1d-4232-b238-f9baedd87c31.Text: "He's having another breakdown! Isn't it time we told the enforcers? This might end badly otherwise."

d167c59e-105d-4780-bc16-f9fc0b0f1c79.Text: "Don't tell them just yet. He's had two already, he can pull through again. Besides, this could happen to anyone these days."

aecb7a5f-df4f-42a4-b0ed-a933285ea8b6.Text: "If I start to lose myself, just give me His Peace. I don't want to suffer, and I don't want to drag you all into the warp with me either."

92067370-f498-4126-9dcc-90e09e9efc07.Text: "You have taught us everything and we will not fail you. We are ready!"

8fc5af3a-7fbf-40e4-9b90-a2de35c6149f.Text: "I have prepared you well, Zacchary. My Choir will live up to my name."

aadb5e06-6c35-461d-8f63-7708069390f8.Text: "You are a failure of a teacher. You have taught them nothing."

6a8d62ad-1fd9-4422-9e1f-18d426ddc4b7.Text: "The God-Emperor is a lie! The Astronomican is a lie! We are all going to perish!"

13b423ac-0fd1-4a0e-90dc-a0ebd3f68f13.Text: "I call to you, O Prince of Pleasure, I entrust you with my puny soul and beseech you for your protection..."

a835fc15-98fd-4258-8dd5-7f1bf08cf5c0.Text: "O God-Emperor, protect us from the horrors of the Empyrean, shield us from the Immaterium's corruption, be our shield..."

b6fb27cf-706b-492f-bd62-8c65526702c4.Text: An otherworldly being is draining the Astropath's life force.

743f75e4-f78e-488f-8718-89de2e4800e0.Text: "I'll gladly give my last for you, Teacher!"

48290d9a-261a-44df-b56e-c036201f40f2.Text: The Astropath's energy is dissipating around him.

74a715e6-b4a8-4a22-9449-f773c6355e8b.Text: "When he drained my life, it felt so sweet! Oh, sweet duty!"

06fd23a2-9671-4949-8ab6-437a92e28cae.Text: Standing next to the Astropath on the pedestal is another figure in identical vestments, which seems to be draining the life force from him.

f53c5a68-aa7a-4423-8027-097768a41323.Text: "I did not give up my life and energy willingly. He took control of my will, he made me drain myself dry..."

9b8131a3-de63-4d98-9c55-bc771a10765e.Text: "I find you guilty of arrogance and betrayal of your Choir! You will be sentenced!"

dbb35e84-818c-40fa-b19a-be53fbfafee3.Text: "Let us kill him for the glory of the Dark Gods! He cannot stand against us alone!"

59f0ac6b-db40-43c2-83f3-f84796fecd8f.Text: "Master, please, wake up! I'm here by your side!"

584f7cb5-2940-43c9-8158-ae29dc6bb999.Text: "I didn't think you would do that... with your own hands..."

8a4fe5d8-a128-4c72-96ce-f4972522409e.Text: "Stop! My mind is boiling! Teacher, please stop!"

b5799e19-d110-4edf-a681-bf2fcb9d16ce.Text: "No! Please, Teacher, anything but that! Better to kill me than turn me into one of those mindless things!"

a7cbae17-4565-43da-83ec-d8314fb65817.Text: "What is inside him is not for your eyes to see."

50771884-45d4-46c0-9c7b-60d9a10d898f.Text: "The soul of another is a maze with no way out."

ea7f83d9-1f2c-492b-8b6a-07878e909735.Text: "Go. Give me some time alone with him..."

788c6d8c-01e9-48cd-ba05-64aaf5f2dcdd.Text: "Lord Captain, I distinctly recall this spectre being a trap."

2f5b948f-fa4c-4a1d-82b8-280b07baed73.Text: "Spend no more time on this abomination, Rogue Trader. It has already revealed its lying nature to us."

870f302a-9ae5-40dd-83e7-01c371db8874.Text: "Please, let us not touch... that... again. It only brought us pain the last time."

497d9e04-caf4-4454-b7ba-6e439ccdb1fd.Text: "We have already established that this entity is not our target, {name}. We need to keep looking."

023147fc-0658-408f-98c2-a8e061d3f820.Text: "Didn't you check this one already, Lord Captain?"

cc74a7ba-50d5-4e41-9cdc-ad1c2b02b602.Text: "This azhi has burned us once before. Shall we continue our search, shereen?"

766b9f96-2990-47d3-9ae8-f7a4642ff3b9.Text: "This ghost was sent to confound us. Direct your steps away from it, Domin."

7b34830f-2f39-45b9-96cf-a1ee7d141ff7.Text: "Did you enjoy the pain, {name}? Then do not let me stop you."

e9778164-df89-4b24-95e0-548922cb96dc.Text: "It has been determined through empirical evidence that this entity is a false one. The predicted outcome of repeat contact is unsatisfactory."

eb159320-2963-4ced-b9f9-dfed309cbd49.Text: "This is a false trail. These things are messing with our heads — we should look elsewhere, Rogue Trader."

121c92ec-bc7e-4998-98d6-17fb0169a5cd.Text: "Blasted trickery! Do not let it fool you again, Aett-Vater."

27a2d659-be2b-41a9-87ee-00264bea1fed.Text: "Do not touch this spawn of the veil. It is a delusion, elantach."

e1999b93-4f0b-49d5-903d-f6799baae412.Text: There are no marks of physical violence on the servant's body. The victim's eyeless face is contorted in a frozen expression of horror.

9d4e94a5-0b88-4c88-8f3d-abc95e37ecc9.Text: The corpse is clutching a knife. There are numerous wounds around the eyes and ears. The molten remains of the brain show through the empty eye sockets.

89cf12fd-8937-4c3a-989d-5b5447f5957c.Text: "An excellent battle, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Even the warp's apparitions are no match for you."

4236cfca-be03-400b-a24b-2b5575069386.Text: "Well... it has been an honour serving... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}..."

41fb9303-898a-4774-8f8f-7905031aa46a.Text: "Worry not, Master Weisz. For as long as I live, the barrier will hold."

660c3a5b-113b-45b2-8f92-15ee471f9b8d.Text: "That's a lie... A LIE! Those... aren't my paths. They aren't my lives. There's only one me, the real me... Go away!"

0101dde4-c54f-4833-b20b-b501fd6e8b42.Text: "Well now, let's take a peek behind the door and meet those who are so anxious to see us."

61bddc93-47c9-4c7f-b8eb-70676f182fd5.Text: "I looked up to you. I followed every word you said. If I had only had the foresight to defy you at that fateful moment..."

b7446787-a35b-4bcf-8280-647a557e1f14.Text: "I had warned you that the ritual was a mistake, and for that, you turned me into a monster! You failed even at that, you miserable fool..."

29c5c691-e969-4f1b-b42a-29fc43692dd0.Text: "When you were soaking up my power... killing me... What did you feel? Did you enjoy it?"

c3c38c05-2e97-4869-a239-5e816f16d956.Text: "All I wanted to do was help. I was trying to save you. And you — what have you done to me?"

a6382595-505d-47f7-98ae-4b6cb6e3178e.Text: "You were useless as a mentor. Your failure merely confirmed my expectations. You should have known your place..."

498caea1-03b6-4c78-828b-cafb08ade53f.Text: "You had always believed in yourself, not in Him. Well, He disbelieved in you too."

d4d8ca52-2544-442b-adf9-47c86a9c771d.Text: "Look at yourself. At what you have become. Pathetic. They said we were destined for greatness, but you have chosen to wallow in self-pity and lies."

89ec4679-2f60-4b7e-8602-5ae91886499f.Text: "Many thanks for this opportunity to be of service, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It was quite riveting!"

15d73b25-9c24-4b2d-bd0a-41b9b68e17e4.Text: "How can this be... You— you promised..."

a402daff-c4e3-4172-81ae-e5cb4b0f2c7e.Text: "Please stay still, Master Weisz. It will only hurt at first..."

f0fa6868-8081-4b6e-b9cf-914edbeb30e2.Text: "Lord Captain, we have cross-referenced the key characteristics of the system with our astronautical chart data. The planet Vheabos VI is located here. The problem is, the augurs detect an unusual change in the atmosphere not unlike a massive release of toxins. It appears that something unfortunate has happened to the planet's underground storage facilities."

ceb98457-1eea-4cb1-8936-c6e750ea0671.Text: "It is impossible to land safely on the planet just now: unknown ships are cruising in the system. Hmm... No need for any cog to analyse it, I can decipher this telemetry easily: xenos. The armoury and artillery crews are standing by."

53bc52ef-dde0-40a4-a0a2-b60da7670431.Text: "Lord Captain, our Astropaths received a message from Achilleas Scalander on Dargonus. He closely studied the data from the incursion on Vheabos VI, including the mention of the xenos leaders. He promised to direct the efforts of his aides to identify those enemies of Humanity so their location can be determined."

31cd3d79-4804-45e6-a4f6-ecc10469ca94.Text: "Master Scalander is also reporting the {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g} are getting ready for more attacks on your territory. Information from his aides continues to arrive, and Achilleas will personally report to you the moment the target for the upcoming raid becomes clear. The Drukhari excel at catching their opponents off guard, and there will be little time to mount a response. According to Master Scalander, your personal participation in the defence would be the best strategy, given the circumstances."

6f057444-0adb-43eb-aff6-c2b25bc2efe1.Text: "A new message from Master Scalander, Lord Captain. This time he is not reporting yet another attack but the alleged location of one of the xenos leaders. Achilleas's aides have reported that said leader will be heading an attack on the paradise world Grantis. There is one catch — the planet belongs to Calligos Winterscale, another Rogue Trader."

d54638e0-d9ed-4bfc-b60e-aeffc0938348.Text: "Master Scalander noted in his message that responding to a distress call is unlikely to be considered an incursion into somebody else's territory. The governor of Grantis will most likely send out a call for aid the moment the raid begins — and if your voidship happens to be nearby, no one will question your reasons for landing."

926e1b78-8c17-4b87-97d1-0277ec757b76.Text: "An unidentified object has been located in the system. The artefact reacts to our transmissions by releasing unknown radiation — most likely of xeno-origin, the cogs are reporting. If you want to get a closer look, we need to close the distance between the vessel and the object."

769bd149-c4c0-4236-9af0-b0353d0cba84.Text: "Lord Captain! We have dealt with the voidships of these beasts, but a xenos boarding party has landed on the ship — they are advancing steadily toward the plasma drive. The enforcers are being overrun, they are asking for reinforcements — if we do not help them, this filth will destroy our vessel from the inside!"

b598a0eb-531f-483c-a2af-14f938a9b8f1.Text: "I have an urgent message from Dargonus, Lord Captain! Our Astropaths are receiving numerous transmissions... But no, these aren't ordinary messages — each and every one is a plea for help! Dargonus is reporting a massive xenos raid, and every mental image transmitted is wreathed in flame!"

287ffb0a-9794-43a7-972b-d08afe7c6598.Text: "The Astropathic Choirmaster is struggling to determine when exactly the invasion began, but all signs point to it happening shortly after your departure to the Cinerus Maleficum. Any delay condemns the world to even greater suffering — your people are begging for immediate aid!"

6e583d06-8db2-49c2-a4c6-411a6c85bec0.Text: Ordered the remnants of the Black Ship be destroyed by bombardment.

e3b4e881-1b8f-440d-bd10-45868ea34574.Text: "Bombard the vessel. Let the dead follow the dead."

5e2038c9-a595-47de-868f-55cf66c8dbd0.Text: Ordered the remnants of the Black Ship be destroyed by sending in a boarding team.

506a8344-9063-4865-9ac5-871b9cf14182.Text: "Send out a boarding party. Let them destroy this unholy site."

9c36916b-c51d-4867-80cc-5c28aa0b33ce.Text: Ordered tech-priests be sent to the wreck of the Black Ship to recover all that was worth taking.

f25c221e-2e35-4aa1-9a5a-fc6f134eb1c5.Text: "Send out the technicians to strip the vessel of anything valuable. And make sure they keep quiet about what they are about to see."

ca2ac84a-04c0-4282-a960-fa64f11a1093.Text: "I am no longer interested in this vessel. Leave it to rot."

ca9c80a1-f2aa-4ea7-8689-e6dc32752add.Text: "Lord Captain, this is Vox Master Vigdis Surri Otta Toliman speaking. I hope your heroic expedition was a success. What will be your further instructions?"

8eacc94f-9a53-44b7-a26c-503004de1e73.Text: "The machine spirit of this vessel is dead and defiled. It should be sent to the Omnissiah in a proper nuclear funeral rite."

c7f13548-bdd8-411b-93eb-28a58314538d.Text: "As you wish, Lord Captain. The power of our main battery should be enough to penetrate the glacier and evaporate the vessel completely."

1fff665c-53da-4539-8cec-95b3666c56fb.Text: "It is with regret that I report our main battery will not be enough to fully destroy the vessel. The hull goes deep into the glacier, shielding the target against our strike."

2adbe36c-a71a-483a-8b9e-2f093d1e83b5.Text: "It will be done, Lord Captain. A boarding party will immediately be dispatched to the provided coordinates. They will be equipped with cutters so they can penetrate the ship's hull, get to the reactor, and initiate a cascading overload that will destroy the vessel. The losses incurred by the operation should be negligible."

3fb6a6fa-07db-4161-82ed-219957fc4a80.Text: "It will be done, Lord Captain, I will inform the ship's steward about the need to provide a secure storage space for your discoveries as well as an armed squad of discreet and well-trained wardens to protect them."

bde17f31-41a0-484d-8f2a-8dc6f9c41175.Text: "It will be done, Lord Captain. An entry detailing your glorious expedition will be added to the ship's archive."

d1f46820-c115-42da-ba12-af628f7c4dfc.Text: Do not disturb the dead voidsmen. And steer clear from the affairs of the Inquisition.

89b025aa-081c-4abc-80b1-53aedd660977.Text: The augurs detected the remains of an Imperium vessel down on the surface of this planet. Judging by the emblems on the hull, it once belonged to the Inquisition and crashed many centuries ago. The reasons are unknown and there is no way to tell what might lie in wait. The bulk of the ship has sunk into a glacier, which makes further analysis difficult.

c966cac3-6a11-4008-8748-013e87335b46.Text: The technician crew is preparing the Lord Captain's landing shuttle.

f6050a55-c018-406e-8be9-b7bc07366bfa.Text: Any mention of the discovery was removed from the vessel's archives just in case.

643b7b94-42cd-48fe-aaca-586cf234dcae.Text: "Permission to report, Lord Captain. I keep receiving messages about strange behaviours in certain ship systems. All decks report the uncontrollable opening and closing of doors, gates, and airlocks. They behave erratically and do not obey the operators' commands. Regrettably, this has led to casualties among the crew. The Tech-Priests have explained that these phenomena are being caused by the machine spirits' irascibility and have spent hours chanting litanies to soothe their anger. Unfortunately, many crew members were badly injured before the prayers could stabilise the systems."

04fa6602-1d67-4ac5-b303-cda344982a4f.Text: "Lord Captain, I keep receiving reports about malfunctions among the various ship systems. This time we are dealing with inexplicable temperature fluctuations. Thermal control failures were observed not only in individual compartments but even in the soldiers' protective equipment. Several crew members have suffered from burns and frostbite."

00931c61-9243-47c8-8d0b-1c54ca51e0cc.Text: "The Tech-Priests are performing the rites of machine spirit pacification and remain convinced that the issues were caused by the spirits' obstinacy and defiance. Their reports claim the incidents remain well within the scope of expected performance parameters. Over the last few days, complaints about the malfunctioning thermal controls have dwindled, but the crew members have started whispering that our vessel is haunted. The Tech-Priests' assurances that only the machine spirits' tempers are to blame are doing nothing to dissuade these ridiculous rumours."

d26ee938-a3a3-40d5-8654-a4f4bfc4d426.Text: "Lord Cap'n, this is Master Helmsman Ravor. The crew is grumbling again, but they've a right reason this time — our analytics systems have gone totally bonkers. The red robes... excuse me, Tech-Priests are blaming the anger of the machine spirits. Allegedly, this is how they profess their displeasure at the crew not being worshipful. We have largely managed to stabilise the output of the augurs and auspexes across the ship, but you should know there is something awfully sketchy about the machines these days."

0399056c-3116-49e0-8073-75808961b595.Text: "I can confirm, Lord Captain. The vessel's analytics systems were behaving incorrectly for a time. The cogitators could not produce statistical data and displayed meaningless numeric combinations instead, the augurs failed to correctly analyse matter and mistook solids for liquids and vice versa. Thanks to the Tech-Priests' efforts, standard operation of the ship's mechanisms has been restored. I am still registering sporadic reports of similar malfunctions, but we should now be able to handle them."

c47c21ea-9a12-4347-a306-afadf6dfcab0.Text: "Lock onto the Wasteland Wayfarer and open fire."

20a44bac-653c-477a-856f-8640b894e49f.Text: "We're leaving. There's nothing more for us to do here."

4051b059-13cf-48e7-9dd2-1bd330f38be5.Text: "Lord Captain, I am glad to see you are in good health. As soon as you entered the Wasteland Wayfarer, the vox-link was affected by interference. The augurs recorded a flicker of movement on the ark, and our Astropaths reported the presence of psyches aboard that were not entirely human."

c1d4f28c-6543-4b82-bca0-7cc6b1621817.Text: "The colony gripped by this foulness was unable to put a ship into orbit and set off to wreak new villainy. The only thing they could do is set a trap for good-hearted subjects of the Emperor. Or for pirates intending to rob the 'defenceless pilgrims.'"

fada6c03-bfac-4dd6-90d7-285407809ec7.Text: "Corporaptor Hominis. They possess exceptional infiltration capabilities, they are adaptive, highly organised, and their intellects are advanced. Observed in parasitic infection of individuals of other species with subsequent reconfiguration of the host's genetic structure."

d59fc4c3-02b1-4874-98a0-349e255ebc51.Text: "Blasphemous inhuman wretches. They must have entered the vessel alongside the pilgrims and eventually took over, or they may have even been waiting on the planet itself. One way or another, they doomed the bodies and the souls of everyone who set foot on the surface of this world."

7cf5ef97-239e-4a69-8b5e-8864bbcbaad6.Text: "Menace 3T, the Genestealers. Spies of a hostile xenos race sent to infiltrate the Imperium. I will report this to the Lord Inquisitor the first chance I get. To underestimate this threat or its psychic potential would be folly. Now that they are no longer hiding, I can hear their disgusting mental cries with disturbing clarity."

559ffb52-5b0d-44bb-8fe6-b9c610adb257.Text: "We call them 'the False Among Us.' Pilferers of our bloodlines. These spawn of the Great Devourer silenced the voices of several of my people's enclaves. Their stinging bites steal souls just as their flesh steals the shapes of the nobler races. Abominations!"

4bfae415-00c1-4cf4-9bca-6a8068a801f5.Text: "Outrageous perfidy. I assume the ungodly creatures from this ship are unable to raise the Wasteland Wayfarer from the surface. Hardly surprising, the most old and worn-down transports are often sent on one-ways trips so they can then become the centre of the fledging colony after landing, and their reactor — the energy core of the new settlement."
