6387985f-7045-4c00-8662-cff78dc99b18.Text: "Only a little longer before this iron dolt is completely fried."

e4a657bd-cd03-4529-b85d-05fc513a9cce.Text: "Hey! I'm trying to say a prayer here."

7e4dda5c-2825-4705-bcbf-dfe3bbcda604.Text: "I'm not satisfied with that answer. I will repeat my question again — the last Electro-Priest you killed, where did you find him?"

d85fe127-1488-47fc-b528-de4aa5aeac64.Text: "Burn in the fire of Dawn, servant of the corpse emperor! Aah!"

372c9143-3781-46a3-a737-c22fdf3684d0.Text: "And another one meets the limit of his utility. The last of them."

615b71a5-7b24-47bd-aef4-fe685ef9db37.Text: Judging by the positions of the bodies, the soldiers walked into sniper fire and died before they knew where it was coming from.

6fde3820-0e2c-48e3-862e-9d470bcf287a.Text: The turret was placed in a great hurry but the technomat never had the chance to activate it.

58b530e2-5c92-4f60-98e6-146bfccd004b.Text: The insurgents walked in a crowd right across the mine barriers — seemingly oblivious to the fear of death.

6f6141eb-b21c-4e93-8933-1116e2665354.Text: In violation of all security vows, the promethium tanks have been left open and unattended. It would only take a single spark to ignite them.

13dde3d0-c6eb-4c0f-8844-ee3f91e0d889.Text: "The end is near! But you will not witness it!"

53f118f5-c37a-4fcb-9778-d68957741f8e.Text: Obscure glyphs have been scrawled on the rockcrete. Their unnatural shapes are physically repulsive.

5efdc557-9ac2-4900-a1e9-62f5f9385e40.Text: Every one of the dead have had their eyes ruthlessly burned.

c3530134-6cb0-4421-85bd-1342bf6fde7b.Text: "Darkness is coming... And in it, there will shine a spark of dawn... The Final Dawn..."

d07a1c5e-95f4-4b10-a35d-4f78fbe745dc.Text: An eight-rayed sun has been crudely scratched into one of the walls.

71cc2964-ba03-4820-a61a-7131026d72ea.Text: In violation of the Rite of Operation, the shuttle's promethium tanks have been abandoned and left open: someone interrupted the fuelling sacrament.

724debd5-84b7-404e-a0cd-96258bc3e563.Text: An entire procession of cargo servitors was destroyed by gunfire, and not a single one of them attempted to flee.

e98fcb9e-5a5a-4a32-9c64-a169ceb9a13f.Text: The tithe collector's post has been trashed with particular malicious delight, and there is no telling whether it was the rebels or the soldiers who did it.

668ecd30-d058-45f0-bd58-305f60ebffc6.Text: "Esteemed spirit of the mine, I beseech you, allow me to arm your fuse and tear me not into shreds."

b91de02a-58f4-40ec-9891-e9f5cf6f56d4.Text: "Artillery! Do you copy? Requesting a barrage on launch pad three!"

fa0507ca-6a17-4fa3-b4c8-c203fd6d3a65.Text: The blood in the puddle seems to be bubbling and, defying the laws of nature, refuses to coagulate.

fe5758ef-8483-440f-9f09-18dff18bd6c9.Text: Black glassy sand trickles out of the corpse's eyes.

a5a965e0-b3cd-4fe5-b472-fc763bbaaea8.Text: Ghostly lights hang suspended in midair. Their shimmering is mesmerising.

923c56e9-af2b-4769-a37c-e7902521459b.Text: These people were trampled to death by the frenzied mob that stormed the starport.

c0e1cc3c-a9ec-4355-b32f-3552dcb69f28.Text: The checkpoint was swept away by a stampede of refugees who could not be stopped by gunfire and explosions.

910836c9-4b94-4872-9179-d28d61c6cdae.Text: Someone tossed a frag grenade right into the thick of the crowd, where shrapnel caused true carnage.

f5f294b6-3be5-4cf2-ab3d-454f7e90d156.Text: This shuttle was overcrowded and failed to take off.

d20bbcac-c25e-4178-bce2-dc6a14a124bf.Text: "May the Emperor keep you, {name}! A great day!"

bc320667-7d38-41cc-bc94-68487bb7428f.Text: "Can you make it so that the guests stop walking up to me and asking me to open my third eye? I can certainly do it, but they will regret it."

35afb4c3-2be5-42f8-9fd6-ed8d6ebd3c7b.Text: "This is pure chaos! How can people think so much, and so haphazardly?"

7fd3d630-8e3e-4362-b5f2-34b1cda01146.Text: "I hope at least this celebration in your honour won't end in a shootout."

35667837-6a60-481c-b1e9-95e6e7df2450.Text: "Your gatherings look odd and unusual. I will remember this."

217fe0d2-908d-4ed9-acd0-c4105037d30a.Text: "It is my hope that the von Valancius dynasty will serve the Imperium faithfully."

9a488b9c-5c7e-4166-9d01-f5b4dd21a48c.Text: "A splendid reception! One worthy of a Rogue Trader!"

344bbfb2-e561-4ff0-841f-eafba976282a.Text: "Allow me to congratulate you on claiming your inheritance."

efb0a00c-1e63-45e9-b7c8-a1f667c9954b.Text: "The Emperor protects the von Valancius dynasty — it sent Theodora a worthy successor."

284723bd-3385-4320-bf5f-dd45077b0e22.Text: Arthur is silent and avoids looking at you.

ae000011-0c23-4dd5-9fc6-979517e17fb8.Text: "We would do well to discuss the situation without any witnesses."

345f5f67-2eec-4004-8253-6f735ed43f76.Text: "The ceremony is not half bad, but the new von Valancius can only be tested in action."

b57aafa2-2b9e-4d02-acd8-f3418a6708c3.Text: The servant speaks in an unknown tongue, melodious and exotic.

74bc8ac9-3373-45dc-9f74-87178fe34cbc.Text: "Glory to the von Valancius dynasty, conquerors of stars uncharted!"

b19639bb-221f-48ec-94b7-10a14d414689.Text: "Glory to the Emperor and the von Valancius dynasty!"

6e41b28c-8ec6-4c73-a070-7a18544e1fcb.Text: The servant gives you an alluring smile.

aa15f33b-b576-4221-ae50-b09080f80eca.Text: The stinking pile of smouldering corpses has grown larger, topped with the bodies of Chorda dynasty soldiers.

87c1e50f-84a1-4cbd-8425-3c17888bc19f.Text: A tiny insect runs across Incendia's pale face and disappears into her half-open mouth. The air around the crucifix is saturated with a nauseating, rotten stench.

00788b4f-e627-4db7-a485-602ecc2c881d.Text: [Attack] "Do you know what I see? Heresy. These 'exhibits' must burn... and you will burn along with them!"

0327cdf3-7d87-4a21-a52e-04ea25cfeccb.Text: "These aren't xenos, they're mutants in makeup."

d99fb8ba-9069-41e7-aeaf-c2084de1c228.Text: "Do you have any Aeldari in your collection?"

8d146a2c-fcdc-4152-aaed-9808a6b47d78.Text: "Lad, there's a real xenos standing right in front of you, and you can't even tell."

0d0815f4-f7da-46bb-a4b5-f0716f8d7393.Text: Demanded that the "xenos" be released from their cages on Footfall.

63e967e6-3d23-4159-964d-59bef5714a05.Text: "I demand that this abuse be stopped and all the captives freed."

cb97abf5-bd11-4ff8-bcda-2e857208380e.Text: "I will buy all the captives from you."

423d3a31-4b38-4b23-b4c5-b5d03d664428.Text: "Why are you back? I already freed your 'exhibits'."

45a318a9-6a31-4ad3-90a7-0924ed373338.Text: [Attack] "Come to think of it, you have disappointed me just as much."

3c3278d3-c683-4a67-b38c-0e14363c159c.Text: "The burning was mediocre, and the volume of the screams was sorely lacking. Fix it by the time of my next visit, or you shall be next in the cage."

cb03eb15-4ef2-48f9-963c-7a182a07f4be.Text: "It seems, Yrliet, that you have more in common with humans than one might think."

cc78c9bf-9880-4f48-b2ac-8ed16c4f149b.Text: "I have enjoyed this exhibition. I shall visit it again."

0b322481-f730-4a10-ad97-322286f93159.Text: "I would be interested to hear the opinion of my resident xeno-expert."

aefa7a2e-e179-4f01-be84-f099eb2304f8.Text: "A dangerous form of entertainment... Xenos have no place among humans! Kill them all!"

c9fc30e8-d08f-4381-ad85-4e5386ed2bef.Text: [Press and hold the button that sends a jolt to the "exhibits"]

511e6479-e352-4817-ab93-d887002791f4.Text: [Release the button] "Those are good specimens. Nice and loud."

00fed1b6-87ca-48f2-b518-d1f2ca5e254b.Text: {n}This young man is clearly making every effort to look dapper — his fashionable clothes are practically new and his hair is well groomed. What ruins this impression is the poorly scrubbed-off oil stains from his leaky {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g} and the fit of the jacket, which was clearly made for someone else. He gives you a beaming smile and says, his voice ringing,{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallOfficial}Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}{/d}, what an incredible honour! This humble collection is hardly likely to impress you, a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, conqueror of stars. But it is the best one on Footfall!"

4b6c2a89-2350-4f77-9903-33e96ad82ef0.Text: "Oh, shereen, where do I begin? With this wretched voidborn they're trying to pass off as an Aeldari? Or maybe this hapless mutant — I think they're covered in industrial paint... Truly this exhibit is a testament to the resourcefulness of the human mind, but it's certainly not a xenos exhibition."

48cfe2ba-1026-4b37-b88a-713d9e7eea99.Text: "Oh, enough of your scowling! Let us delight our shereen with a generous display of wisdom. Let's start with this villainous eyesore..." {n}Jae points at the nearest cage.{/n} "If I may so bold as to presume, this 'xenos' was spawned by three bottles of spectacularly awful rotgut and one lost scuffle with a door frame."

075ccfae-530e-4709-9306-d84277dc9f70.Text: {n}This young man is clearly making every effort to look dapper — his fashionable clothes are practically new and his hair is well groomed. What ruins this impression is the poorly scrubbed-off oil stains from his leaky {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g} and the fit of the jacket, which was clearly made for someone else.{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallIncognito}Come one, come all{/d}! See for yourself the best collection of live {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} on Footfall!"

18642125-902e-4d35-b687-6da0a67695ff.Text: "Dangerous, vicious, ruthless xenobeasts, caught red-handed as they were attempting to commit evil against the Imperium! But right now, they're harmless. Our cages can withstand their rage. But I wouldn't recommend getting too close, ha ha!"

2ef1f787-2aec-4a05-8e7e-375a92a6f6c0.Text: {n}The man's smile dims, but only for a moment.{/n} "Not xenos, you say? I'm sure there must be some mistake! I will check the shipping list myself, rest assured."

5e75c7c2-4d92-4f75-9f5c-21dcf893180f.Text: {n}The captives' screams become utterly unintelligible, at times giving way to guttural, gurgling sounds — some of the exhibits bite off their tongues and begin to choke on the bloody foam pouring out of their mouths. A few moments later, the charred bodies slump to the bottoms of their cages with a sickening snap.{/n}

701c2024-d640-4f7d-9583-97c8dc104ee7.Text: {n}The exhibition owner just stands there, mouth agape and wide-eyed, swivelling his head back and forth between you and the smouldering remains of his collection.{/n}

97f97ae5-0a59-4a04-a30e-2ad45d14b449.Text: {n}Jae, chortling quietly, says to Yrliet through the tears,{/n} "Well, I'll be, this Aeldari is the real deal! Long ears? Check! Five rows of sharp teeth? Check! Bloodthirsty stare? Just like the one you're giving right now! Cousins! As the Exalted One is my witness, you're cousins!"

35bf2cbe-a808-47b6-94df-594496d7e26a.Text: {n}The man's cheerfulness fades a little, but he instantly offers you a respectful bow.{/n} "As Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} wishes. No need to fret — I will release them all immediately!"

5c9841e6-9309-4afd-b3fa-8a0b7751c9b5.Text: "Apologies, {mf|sir|ma'am}, that is simply impossible. Private property. Legitimate business. Licensed by the Liege. Last but not least, it's a noble cause — to help the citizens of Footfall foster a proper attitude toward enemies of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}." {n}With a guilty look, he makes a helpless gesture.{/n}

b984a872-ef53-411a-8353-a56c6f407140.Text: {n}He thinks for a moment.{/n} "That can be done. Very much so. The entire collection will cost you a tidy sum, but you're free to take them away right now!"

fd9dd766-e8be-46e8-b6e0-a2487c415bdb.Text: "I knew {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} were not overly bright. But this place... is thoroughly steeped in stupidity mixed with your kind's worst vices."

371c7086-ba6a-4989-a5a2-8a83b731cad2.Text: "His words are oozing with greenish-yellow hues... I do not think the promise will be kept. Such entertainment is lucrative precisely because billions of Imperium subjects have never encountered a xenos in their life. Ignorance and curiosity create colossal demand... that's what I was taught. And I can see that the lesson was truthful."

eddfbcaf-b86e-4b00-b7fb-0e8075077af8.Text: {n}The young man quails under your stare.{/n} "You can't! We're performing a valuable service here — teaching the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}'s subjects to recognise His enemies on sight!"

8aa5a2c6-5e72-4821-8561-b487e28b33f8.Text: {n}A buzzing electrical discharge pierces the captives' bodies, making them shake convulsively and scream in maddening pain. The man watches with approval at first, but when the smell of burnt meat begins to spread through the air, he glances at you with worry.{/n}

98ec4838-9709-4f11-a2df-9e472308fdbc.Text: "Um, pardon me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but you will... damage my exhibits if you keep doing that."

81fba978-1a13-4bf0-838b-c54f0ea5bec9.Text: "O-of course we do! Here it is, a common Yaldaree, caught just for our collection. Six faithful Imperium subjects died to catch this beastie!" {n}He confidently jabs his thumb in the direction of one of the cages.{/n}

fecc4ef8-ccd0-4be7-9cf4-391ae9fa5bc8.Text: "A x-x-xenos?" {n}The man pales before your eyes, his gaze jumping between Yrliet and you.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} preserve me, w-why is this monstrosity walking around freely on F-Footfall?"

c9ec0ee0-84de-4e8b-8e90-41664407dcdc.Text: {n}The man eyes Yrliet from top to bottom, unconvinced.{/n} "Forgive my saying so, but, as far as I know, our small enterprise is the only one on Footfall with the permission to own xenos. Besides, have you ever seen a xenos that's not caged?" {n}He pauses to think, then lowers his voice in a conspiratorial manner.{/n} "Still, with such an... exotic appearance... your companion could very well become the star of my humble collection."

c2a443dc-42a3-4d99-976c-3e52b14abad0.Text: "My dear {mf|sir|ma'am}, everything in moderation! Please kindly leave other citizens a chance to punish these xenos for educational purposes!"

9b4ad820-a121-4c5a-a9cb-8caec54d7f72.Text: {n}He laughs nervously, glancing at the captives, who are barely alive.{/n} "Y-yes, we made sure to catch the ones that were the most... um... vocal!"

1fc282ff-d5fc-453f-b00a-1b646e919919.Text: {n}He gulps and forces a pale smile.{/n} "C-certainly, glad to oblige..."

a387121e-d722-4181-bdb5-0f3b844545e5.Text: {n}He does not even have a chance to object. His body crumples into a garish heap next to the cages.{/n}

c757c8d4-4e6f-4ca3-a86f-cffefae6463d.Text: "Indeed you did. But how long do you think it'll take me to catch some new ones?" {n}He smiles innocently.{/n}

eb4113ad-0681-4b74-8e56-50ece1414bc8.Text: {n}Heinrix arches an eyebrow and gives you a look that could sour milk.{/n} "Are you being serious, {name}? Do you actually want me to give an opinion on this buffoonery?" {n}Instead of his usual impassiveness, he sounds offended.{/n}

70e25657-7424-4228-87cd-3e7ec0f687d5.Text: {n}Glancing at the nearest cages, Yrliet frowns, her expression puzzled.{/n} "It is known to me that your kin tremble at the mere mention of outsiders from distant stars, elantach. But what is this? A protection ritual of sorts, where mon-keigh take on the guises of the creatures from their nightmares so that they can sleep better at night?"

60c8a0f7-24d7-4ea5-ac07-3492c949fd58.Text: {n}Yrliet spits out a string of words accompanied by a series of elaborate gestures, but the {g|Encyclopedia:Elucidator}Elucidator{/g} is powerless to convey their exact meaning. All the translation device is able to muster is a mishmash of words that includes "long and agonising."{/n}

08151e1b-c790-434a-a6a3-b75532069bcc.Text: "A keen observation, Mistress Heydari. Note the unusual colouration of this xenos's skin. Of course, one might suppose that this is some unnatural mimicry that's helping it blend in with its surroundings, but I would still bet on it being the result of poisoning. Young man, if you don't want your precious xeno-exhibit to expire right here on this chain, I suggest you find a chirurgeon, quickly."

7e137ab5-504d-4c02-ad56-f0fb67c6ec1d.Text: "As if a duplicitous smuggler and a snoop from the Inquisition weren't trying enough on their own — now they're attempting to find a rapport..." {n}Abelard mutters.{/n}

8ad95421-872f-4f80-9da0-f5ee594b5b78.Text: {n}The man puffs out his chest and turns up his nose, his pride clearly wounded.{/n} "What guises, lady? I'm telling you, these are {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} — dangerous, merciless, vicious beasts! If they aren't your area of expertise, please kindly refrain from misinforming my audience!"

50962d37-c866-4192-aa6f-197de1ba67fe.Text: {n}The man bows his head respectfully, still shooting glances at Yrliet.{/n}

9d44b3e5-a2ee-46fb-b9d5-99fe1e040181.Text: "You must have me confused with someone else. I am {name}, envoy of the von Valancius dynasty."

121a3db2-84ba-45f6-93c4-eede4df4a8c1.Text: "I wonder who this Fidelio is, and why they cannot start proceedings until he or she appears."

e39cd3d3-d608-4377-abfb-e6243c873628.Text: "What is this place and what is going on here?"

92e6aac6-5c49-42c4-901d-538fb031bc7e.Text: [Join the attendees] "I want to see what this is about."

2da25b0c-23f1-47c9-9b4a-d95ce766e69a.Text: [Leave] "I don't want to get involved in this."

8ad064c5-a815-4ee4-9935-3f729764874c.Text: {n}The low hum of voices quiets, and a dozen gazes shift to you.{/n}

6583a209-4a6e-4b43-811a-cf132b3cc001.Text: {n}The tall man with a shaved head is rubbing his hands together nervously. His opulent clothes are nearly bursting at the seams on his muscular body, and his expression is forbiddingly grim. Still, he's trying to put on an air of friendliness.{/n} "Greetings! You must be..."

4a641099-bff6-4140-8de3-eac19bffeffc.Text: {n}The gathering you've found yourself at seems refined and respectable at first glance. The decorations and the attendees' clothes speak of wealth, and so does the location, which isn't far from the Liege's residence. But you notice that most of those gathered are of rather imposing physique. Many of them have scars and military-grade {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g}. Several of the guests look like they are covering the exit. A few are clearly carrying concealed weapons...{/n}

02141444-0fbe-43cc-873e-9eca1c1b0ce3.Text: {n}Your appearance has definitely attracted everyone's attention. Just about every guest here keeps glancing at you, and some are clearly watching your every move, even though they are trying not to show it.{/n}

e0617f0f-fac0-4f9c-900f-288247d0ff62.Text: {n}Judging by the expensive clothing worn by the people here and the proximity to Footfall's administrative centre, you have found yourself attending some kind of high society event.{/n}

d1fdbc15-b560-4ea6-ada9-97aaa536919c.Text: {n}He puts on a broad smile, but then catches himself and quickly frowns once more.{/n} "Please. Ahem. We can talk later. Chaplain is about to begin..."

32edeb4e-a75b-485e-bfa6-3319c35745ca.Text: "I sense neither sorcery nor {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} influence... However... every other attendee has military-grade {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g}. Almost all of them are armed. See those two? They act like they're just strolling about, but they're really covering the exit... and so is that pair over there. We shouldn't let our guard down at this gathering — something is afoot."

97878474-93bc-44bc-b8a9-fd71b4f04e14.Text: {n}He rubs his hands together anxiously.{/n} "Von Valancius? You're not on the list. But that hardly matters — all doors on Footfall are open to a representative of Lady Theodora! Please, come right in — Chaplain is about to begin. Now where is that last attendee, Fidelio..."

8b3f3e22-877d-4360-88df-8ee944311326.Text: "Judging by the way that fellow with the list was talking about this individual — it's someone very important. But it's not a name I've heard before."

06188d72-ff21-4607-8476-bd72e95fb311.Text: {n}You catch sight of something odd — before stepping away from you, the man gestures subtly to a nearby {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}, giving it some kind of command. The servitor quickly removes the bottles of {g|Encyclopedia:Amasec}amasec{/g} and glasses set out for the attendees from a nearby table.{/n}

9cc7948c-fdd6-4091-88ed-b6be6c8dfb97.Text: {n}Your appearance seems to have perturbed the man, but no more than should be expected when a distinguished guest arrives at an event without invitation.{/n}

593e5662-8761-4871-a7af-ef4a23501e2e.Text: "And the danger's a whole lot greater," {n}she finishes grimly.{/n}

1515342d-6322-4654-9d8a-b3c32fdf3637.Text: "That is, a little danger, but a big opportunity."

19288fb5-4094-4d78-8c51-0084bad52bb2.Text: "What is this tomfoolery..." {n}Abelard grumbles, but not before making sure that the man is out of earshot.{/n}

c1d38cab-deeb-42a7-8b09-dce7646d1968.Text: "A curious habit, introducing yourself with the first name offered to you." {n}Heinrix glances around with pointed nonchalance.{/n} "Let's see how long you can keep up the ruse."

425cb048-9ae5-4b44-9252-9576d6d4029a.Text: "I know nothing about the place, but I can feel that something's in the works here. I sense danger and opportunity..."

3a121303-7ce4-438c-a0f4-e0f1e128f41a.Text: "Neither have I, my sweet angel, neither have I! But then again, I've barely heard your name, and I regret that fate didn't bring us together sooner..."

cedfa4b8-8602-4365-b549-0e1d8311c683.Text: "...because you wished to embark upon the path of redemption and become an upstanding citizen of the Imperium, of course?"

4246ea58-8191-4a94-9746-c102b3896c4c.Text: "Are you telling me you can recall the name of every wanted criminal in the Expanse?"

2840ed05-b114-4f40-acc8-934bbe57cafd.Text: {n}Abelard casts a sidelong glance at Jae and says with forced courtesy,{/n} "Mistress Heydari, you are familiar with the Footfall crowd. Does the name Fidelio mean anything to you?"

e5927dbc-6ee8-489d-9e98-0b980ffbbd7e.Text: "Nothing at all, my esteemed Master Werserian," {n}Jae says in a honeyed voice.{/n} "Alas, the name doesn't ring any bells. Colour me intrigued!"

df75a3c4-a2a3-41da-ab8d-9eaaa4db0906.Text: "Only those who have violated the Lex Imperialis, their accomplices, and possible contacts — their names, features, and the locations of potential hideouts. An Arbitrator who cannot instantly identify a dangerous criminal or their associates is useless."

0bc4237e-eefb-438d-a798-0c07c9ca1393.Text: {n}Chaplain looks at you and gives a slight nod.{/n} "I wasn't referring to {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio — at least Denz himself wanted to see {mf|him|her} at his funeral. But the rest? I know every one of you, and I would be astonished to discover anyone here who truly mourns this loss."

c9d7fa6f-0898-46cd-ab6c-ea412766caa6.Text: {n}Chaplain looks at you and gives a slight nod.{/n} "I wasn't referring to our esteemed guest. But the rest of you I know all too well."

7db7e602-933a-4b1c-adbf-a7abb59d1394.Text: "So go ahead, pray for Bellardo's soul. Soon the flames will take him. A fitting end for a life like his. May the Emperor keep his soul!" {n}Without another word, Chaplain makes the sign of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g} and pointedly turns away from the attendees.{/n}

ddd1db7a-e19b-4086-9856-c72a4190e9af.Text: "This place? Hmm... Right by darling Vladaym's residence, fifth circle... Some guys I know are operating around here, I know what their takings are and who they work for. But the place itself — I'm drawing a blank!"

4c0e824f-1b92-491e-a0ed-ce645b1b4a77.Text: "Oh, what a terrible, sorrowful day! We pay our respects to the life and soul of Footfall society, a loyal servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}, a generous benefactor who spared no expense to keep the fire of faith burning, and an example to all future generations — the most noble and unforgettable Master Bellardo! This loss..." {n}The fussy {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} clerk speaks in a strained voice — and keeps peeking at a paper with text on it. His speech drags on and on, blending into a monotonous cascade of praises of the late Master Bellardo.{/n}

81ddf236-56d6-4aea-b831-8008eb02e42f.Text: "So let us offer a prayer to the Emperor for the repose of Master Bellardo's soul and the prosperity of his heirs! I now pass you over to our most reverend Chaplain."

e619b719-ac78-4eb4-bda4-b53e22b5e16e.Text: "{mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius! Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I heard about your arrival on Footfall, of course... and about Lady Theodora's passing... but I wasn't told... you're not on the list..." {n}He stops.{/n} "But that's not a problem, of course! Please, come on in — Chaplain is about to begin! Ah, but we're waiting for one more attendee to arrive, Fidelio... without Fidelio, it's all been for nothing..." {n}Mumbling, the man excuses himself and joins the other attendees.{/n}

6d1ef6c4-dbbb-4802-9a0d-1d493bc78a1e.Text: {n}He glances at the scroll in his mechanical hand {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g}.{/n} "{mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio? All the guests have arrived, you're the last on the list, and we couldn't well start without you. Your presence is absolutely vital!"

bb58c63a-de51-4e40-aff8-c463f27a493f.Text: {n}Solomorne rubs his chin in thought.{/n} "Fidelio... I can say with certainty that there is no such name on the wanted list, and that the Arbitrators posted on Footfall have sent out no special reports on this person."

91a61b33-e0bc-433b-bae8-df0f8d54de42.Text: {n}A formidable-looking man dressed in the attire of an {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorum}Ecclesiarchy{/g} missionary glares at the gathered crowd.{/n} "And here you all are, you vultures. Let's offer a prayer, then. But if you think that the Emperor — or the messenger of His will, in other words, myself — does not see into your vile souls, you are sorely mistaken!"

48d89f85-e99b-45c8-b971-87733bcbda17.Text: "I have never heard the name before either."

b622c1a3-afb6-40cf-b226-f27f275615c2.Text: "This is very grand for a pirate's funeral. Is this normal for Footfall?"

9bcdfb57-2ba1-403e-9c75-eaf6f9789149.Text: [Take a good look at the deceased]

0649bb64-eaa9-4f13-ab82-d768105add56.Text: {n}Whoever prepared the body of the grey-haired man lying in the coffin, they did a good job — even in death he looks majestic.{/n}

969f6e74-ae60-4b33-8d37-4bb2afd50c7a.Text: {n}Solomorne looks at the dead man's face and says sternly,{/n} "Jerrycan Denz, a pirate. Wanted for countless robberies and attacks on trade vessels. He was never caught assaulting tithe ships, but the Arbites still added his name to the list of high-risk suspects, with a note stating, 'Elimination recommended.'"

755a037e-dca0-49d6-a450-dfce0104e2ad.Text: "Now I remember. Reverend Hieronymus mentioned the name Master Bellardo as one of the biggest donors to the temple."

ca125a8e-0794-4bea-9bec-d1f9868c4d2c.Text: "Folks on Footfall are known to turn a blind eye to many things, but even the locals aren't so unscrupulous as to honour pirate scum a few paces away from the Liege's residence. But no one has heard of Denz for so many decades... I barely recognised him myself, and I've seen his face on picts a fair few times back then. I assume he retired and started a more or less honest life under a new name. What was it they were calling him? Master Bellardo?"

7d2226f8-7b4f-4228-8639-ea35c64f1d40.Text: {n}Abelard maintains a grave expression befitting the occasion — until he sees the face of the deceased. He frowns. He peers at it with suspicion. Then he gasps, astonished, almost dazed.{/n} "I'll be! This is quite the meeting... if it can be called such, under the circumstances."

c50a9fc1-db68-4b07-ad0a-fd56e9a84b71.Text: "Do I! I would tell you all about this man, but the words I'd use would be improper for a funeral! This, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, is Jerrycan Denz, known back in the day as one of the most notorious pirates in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}."

a4325e97-e37b-4631-bae2-973486825819.Text: "They nicknamed him 'Jerrycan' for his habit of having a jug or two of {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g} on hand — he did love burning things. Oh yes, he was a menace back then... how long ago was it? Sixty years ago? I was serving my last days in the Navy when news came of his latest attack..."

04509f4c-86fd-4f32-a648-53a3688bd3a4.Text: {n}It's hard to glean anything from the deceased's appearance apart from the fact that he must have been wealthy — his clothes look expensive, and his {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} are new and rare.{/n}

e1879f68-d33b-420a-90f2-8012e0b9272b.Text: {n}Abelard distractedly runs a hand through his hair.{/n} "Well, well... There was a time when the sight of Jerrycan in a coffin would have been enough to make me dance. Quite literally! By the Throne, I would have danced a jig on the spot! But now... I don't know. No more jumping into the warp right from under the cruiser's nose, eh, you old beast? Who would've thought I'd be at your funeral..."

68aa28c5-4fd6-4fa4-bf09-6747331fffa5.Text: {n}His face seems unfamiliar at first... but then a realisation strikes you. Age has greatly changed this man's features, but you've seen him before — on picts and posters saying, "Wanted: Highly Dangerous Pirate." Decades ago, the one who is currently lying before you in a coffin used to go by the name Jerrycan Denz and was known as one of the most infamous pirates in the Koronus Expanse.{/n}

87e27a08-9acc-4e75-ae2e-2c24f4df3a4c.Text: {n}After a pause, he adds, with feeling,{/n} "The bastard escaped justice after all."

4eb7814f-8efb-4aba-b60f-cd40cb43c69f.Text: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} left in the deceased's body speak of his high standing — expensive tech is typically extracted from the dead, and only the most prominent and wealthy avoid this fate upon their death.{/n}

705786f0-d37a-4b7d-a681-46e5a45a14b4.Text: The lid of the container automatically opens when touched. It is completely empty.

d652ff08-e49e-469a-947e-c8c263978a70.Text: Heavy plasteel door to the furnace

034d9251-1db2-4c1b-b2d5-7be96879d58f.Text: This is where the fire for burning the bodies comes from.

d72d5481-6fd0-47ee-a22a-487c42567791.Text: It looks like they repurposed the nozzle of an ancient station engine for the needs of the crematorium.

0b77026a-7077-46e1-8fc8-684065675fd7.Text: Some young lad smiles as he uses a nail to poke teeth out of a broken jawbone, saying, "She loves me... She loves me not..."

fa19a755-394e-44f6-8163-afc3d5de52dd.Text: "Don't interrupt me! They're coming from extra corners. I need to count everything in case there are new ones!"

5ba1908b-d3ed-4314-9252-bd34e8aa4179.Text: "Eh, I was a hardened voidsman, and now... Now I only surf the streams of sewage and raid bottles of amasec..."

f0a969a5-5592-42c6-a990-9ad7e21ac387.Text: "Oh, what a nice soup it was... what a soup!"

94457d41-1f06-420b-b02b-5cccdd2170fb.Text: "It's squalid here, sure... but there's never a dull moment!"

9e4ebe67-f45c-4042-984b-c32f53886c41.Text: "A shoe's a wonderful thing. It's your shoe, and your plate, and your pillow... You can even chew on the sole if you're desperate!"

6dbc602c-d24b-4512-949c-c32d655b2690.Text: "Fancy a crispy finger? Just a couple of thrones... I'll cut it off my right hand, that's the juicier one!"

50e13aac-0671-4db6-a3e9-dfedd5b43b50.Text: Whistling carelessly, the man squeezes the gunge out of the purulent abscesses on his face and with great care collects it in some kind of jar.

d3a508f0-415a-4773-a4e0-6c39a71203a6.Text: Moaning and sobbing incessantly, a dishevelled old woman cradles and kisses a small human skull wrapped in a diaper.

4477b0eb-12af-4c9a-8cb0-a03f5f960782.Text: "Sometimes prayers reach us through the ventilation. In those moments, you really feel that the Emperor is with us."

8e160c8e-059e-4e77-baad-b6920e409e8d.Text: A haggard vagrant fearfully hides the stub of a mouldy protein bar.

ec835284-8d3c-46d5-acfa-7911ba8770c1.Text: Sticking out her tongue with the effort, the woman patiently draws on a piece of paper the letters from the label of the bottle of rotgut.

5f849dff-f069-476b-9f62-df78e11374cd.Text: The heavy containers are firmly blocking the door.

aeb82bfe-ed6a-45f5-ae29-d50fa8a06ec3.Text: The warehouse's visitor record. There are different dates, but only two names.

45f15851-b1fc-40c1-aa32-167ba753c44f.Text: An assortment of parts for void shield arrays. They look used but still too new to be replaced.

682690ba-c12c-4920-928b-cdbb8da1da1e.Text: "Water purification unit." A device like this is supposed to be used for the needs of the station instead of gathering dust in a warehouse.

56eda1db-0bb1-45ef-a001-07ca911ac029.Text: The sound in this spot is suspicious, like there's a large cavity somewhere beneath the floor.

7b9110d0-bf18-4f8c-9771-41a51b5e94c9.Text: After making a few holes in the tunnel's plating, you find no cavity on the other side.

86bce665-a38b-4ca7-9836-9a9cbd531467.Text: The cavity contains... a staggering mound of packed trash. It appears it's been gathering here for decades, if not centuries.

fa80f81a-eb5c-4e57-bad8-a01a6bf0eb4a.Text: Digging through the trash yields no results.

da1ede1a-6067-4025-bd2d-1e235a29423e.Text: Under the rubble, you find a small hollow — presumably some worker's cache from the time of the station's founding.

ad8906ab-f715-4746-9188-32e105f9e985.Text: [Try to break through to the cavity]

b8664c47-4655-4293-845b-610749e61ae8.Text: "People care too much about things that don't matter. Yes, you do too. Not me, though — I transcend."

db6873dd-a3d9-4b8e-8e4a-8096340cecc2.Text: "The rest may see me as a homeless slob who lives underground. But my mind houses thousands of worlds and lives!"

82309017-d006-4cf0-8f2e-008acecc92c5.Text: There's a word scribbled on the side of the tent: "Library."

73361982-35f3-4baa-bc5e-bb0025ea0041.Text: The tent has half a dozen books titled, "Life of Saint Drusus," "High Gothic Alphabet," "Properties of Real-Valued Sequences and Functions: An Advanced Lecture Course."

724775fc-637c-46ab-a659-7edc063ce9c5.Text: The word on the tent reads, "Infirmary." There's a snoring body inside without any signs of illness or wounds, but it does hit you with an unbearable wave of stale alcohol.

cf3d2214-5a78-4746-b5ac-40f5efe7b177.Text: The word on the tent reads, "Temple." Inside is a tiny makeshift altar with candles on it — the cleanest and most well-kept structure in the vicinity.

6e827e47-62e4-4b9a-892c-31bfccbd14ab.Text: "Bloody Throne, we're gonna burn! Guns out, we gotta shoot our way out!"

35320dbd-3362-4f81-9b5b-80bb770ca5ef.Text: "To arms! Aim for the walls or the floor — we won't get through the outer door quickly enough!"

fe8a66f1-bd96-48ac-a3a6-3530c73f5442.Text: "Aah! Come on, Idira, look harder... The floor! We've got to shoot through the floor! Quickly!"

fcfec95d-1cf5-48aa-bbfd-cf6ee7f2ff94.Text: "Damn it, open fire! Shoot! Shoot the walls and the floor — the door's fortified!"

c846e060-6c9b-40af-8001-f7796559cb8c.Text: "Quickly! We need to fight our way out! Emperor, protect us!"

470a14b9-9205-400a-afff-8a8798a6fbf3.Text: "Not long before his death, Denz mentioned something about 'dead eyes' looking at him."

b92153dc-68e9-4335-9dfd-1b3a917b1ffc.Text: "Given your speech during the ceremony, I take it you're not fond of the other attendees."

8faa635b-984f-40a5-811c-24b8a8e3baea.Text: "So you think this woman is our Fidelio?"

7f27882f-ede4-4fee-8f5b-45c9d08cafa2.Text: "A question, if I may — how was it that an Ecclesiarchy missionary came to be a friend and associate of a famous pirate?"

f0f2193f-3368-4837-a04d-29512aa45d2b.Text: "The esteemed Master Bellardo was a pirate..."

795395b8-f450-43a8-b49e-0552ea62941d.Text: "There's an entry in the book of remembrance about repentance. The writing looks fresh. Could Fidelio have left it?"

fd4553e4-14d7-4ac4-a414-9c4358a496cb.Text: "I have serious reason to suspect that someone here wanted to kill Fidelio."

3723b278-4e36-4818-92b7-e61049fd7f08.Text: "Call all the parties involved. It is time to discuss the matter of the will."

b38ce860-794a-4dc2-8dd9-e9c1469cff18.Text: "I think I need more time. I'll get back to you."

88b3f86f-0d30-40a7-acac-1301412a8223.Text: "So Bellardo has left all his worldly possessions to a certain Fidelio. Who is this mysterious person?"

80250783-3813-4a7a-81ab-2a05af1766b7.Text: "I have a strong suspicion that someone here wants me dead."

1675db99-cc27-49af-b1c8-dd738e535e2f.Text: "Maybe Fidelio will make themselves known once Denz's will is made public?"

b7adce43-7f94-444b-a09f-7c2669772692.Text: "Truth be told, I don't even know myself."

f57dd405-1bb4-4785-a572-c0d262862161.Text: [Attack] "You know what? All of you pirate scum disgust me. You should not be allowed to walk freely on an Imperium station!"

b6f9d351-a5fc-4b22-8852-9ac9b87f9134.Text: "Thank you for speaking with me. I must go."

18d56f6c-d350-4803-a7ac-5ef3df044920.Text: "On the matter of the inheritance... when can I claim it?"

538f1f5a-84f5-4bcc-95ed-3c10772cea53.Text: "No, I did not. I came here by chance."

d6411518-51b3-41e5-b4df-cceb11879417.Text: "It's an item of some sort, and probably one of great value. A weapon, possibly."

5725e8cd-4e72-48dd-96e3-936a40567c38.Text: "Let's go over everything we know. Denz supposedly left his possessions to Fidelio — a woman who wanted to take revenge on him for killing the captain of the ship Repentance. The word Repentance is written in the book of remembrance, and the entry is new. Does this mean that our Fidelio is somewhere close by?"

2c962434-f6b8-41ba-943b-3a99db818b06.Text: "It could be a name — the name of a ship, for example."

9c94cb17-1dac-4d74-a6e4-3ac3b2800927.Text: "I think I might know the answer."

6ccc9cbf-26d5-4f72-a179-bccc1ac68868.Text: "Clearly it's his desire to atone for his past."

98ec327e-851d-4c93-8de4-e5f43a9743a5.Text: "The influence of a warp entity. It settled in Denz's home and poisoned his mind."

c4d3ddc0-a3c7-4eef-9797-1391971b5b19.Text: "I wish to intervene in the matter of the inheritance left by Master Bellardo."

fd70aa48-237a-4f32-a89b-ee7166e13389.Text: "I would like to discuss with you what I've been able to uncover in regard to the mysterious Fidelio."

4d9d3dd3-369c-48fe-919b-0cb16512b3dc.Text: "That is all I've been able to learn so far."

ac72b6bf-1cdd-4601-b10d-a48870550858.Text: "Well, it looks like we've cleared up the Repentance part."

5e67bc2b-9987-4b07-a840-6b0151f956bf.Text: {n}Up close, Chaplain leaves an even stronger impression — a tall, burly man, whose face and hands bear numerous scars. His entire visage seems to tell the story of many heretics who met their end upon their encounter with this adept of true faith.{/n}

34571ffa-fb76-4ad6-abe2-4e386e3e0219.Text: {n}Chaplain gives you a friendly nod, but his gaze is intense, like he's trying to get a sense of who you are.{/n} "Pleasure to meet you, {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio. I prefer to go by Chaplain — it is both my name and my occupation."

c11fd44e-d9a7-47f7-8539-4e93878f2c36.Text: {n}Chaplain gives you a respectful nod.{/n} "May Saint Drusus protect you from illness and misfortune. I'm surprised to see a noble figure such as yourself here. Did you know Denz? I mean, Master Bellardo."

d6bd2b79-812b-487e-ad3c-b2358f0a8a7d.Text: "I didn't, that's for sure. I can't imagine what he meant by it."

152b997a-ee64-4964-9c37-0a8f3132d0ef.Text: {n}Chaplain chuckles. The scars on his face grow even more prominent.{/n} "Do you know why they call me Chaplain? It's because I was the priest on Denz's ship in his wilder days."

3baa9373-9e3e-480f-b0ef-1577429d55bf.Text: "I'm a missionary of Saint Drusus, and the truth of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} speaks through me. So I see no point in pretence. All who have gathered here have one goal — to bite a chunk out of Denz's estate. Ambition and aspirations of wealth are not immoral in and of themselves, but..." {n}Chaplain grimaces.{/n}

e79f019a-8650-4d30-b2b4-127bc381c3dc.Text: "It's just that I'm sickened by the thought that such a great man has left behind nothing but a pile of human refuse. His son is a drunk and a weakling. His 'friend' Daggen — the one who greeted you at the entrance — is a dim-witted brute with an incredibly bloated ego. His widow made off on the family yacht in the direction of the Maw while his body was still warm — with an entourage of five brawny, good-looking young fellows."

aad5fbb9-d3ad-437b-9382-598a5ad987d3.Text: {n}Chaplain peers at you once more.{/n} "I'd like to believe that he didn't choose you as his heir on a whim, {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio. At least you had the guts to come here, into a nest of vipers who despise you because Denz's money and property slipped through their fingers. I respect that kind of audacity — and so did he."

79f3e510-3f95-4d95-863a-740acf5aa597.Text: "If you're surprised, you shouldn't be. There are plenty of heretic scum among the pirates of the Expanse, but Denz wasn't one of them. He was a true believer. And he shared more of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}'s ideals than some of those stiff-necked officers. A leader with an iron fist and an iron will — don't we owe our conquest of thousands of star systems to people like that?"

0b4278dd-cd60-4a5a-a5c2-7753a1398545.Text: {n}Jae's eyes light up at the word "inheritance." But she quickly checks herself and summons up a mournful expression.{/n}

9dc6b428-bfd9-4af9-8089-3af37e9ab945.Text: "You know, it's funny how, despite being Denz's — that is to say, Master Bellardo's — closest associate and confessor, I've never heard of you — the {mf|man|woman} he chose to be his sole heir. I'm glad, of course, that the inheritance didn't go to any of the others, the vultures. But I'm still curious — why you?"

9133461a-d39a-4f66-9170-b7bd2a507bc3.Text: {n}Chaplain grins.{/n} "You don't say! How can this be? Someone wants the sole heir of a tremendous fortune dead, in the place where the other contenders, deprived of these riches, have gathered?"

b216c0f0-357c-4bb0-a317-cfbed7cacb0f.Text: "If you, {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio, really are worthy of Denz's name — you will deal with these minor vicissitudes. Consider this my blessing. The Emperor protects. Anyone who deserves it, that is."

dffdde0d-e954-4a44-a3b0-faca3195dfef.Text: {n}Chaplain's eyes flash momentarily.{/n} "Hmm... A ship called the Repentance... I'm not sure, but you might be right. Now that you've said that, I've remembered an interesting detail."

02099c4d-e545-49fa-bc73-53cca9d042ad.Text: "You just can't wait, can you?" {n}Chaplain scoffs.{/n} "After the funeral. Denz will be delivered into the flames, then we will announce his last will and testament, and you will officially come into your inheritance."

35280263-cfd6-4e43-9fb0-134c8ac561b5.Text: "Then I will consider this a stroke of good luck. Denz would be chuffed to have someone of your standing at his funeral."

2b5fbc4e-3c3c-4112-b748-42dc316ccc70.Text: "Interesting. I knew he kept secrets even from me, his friend and confessor. Then again, meeting you is not the only secret I've discovered. I still don't know who this Fidelio is, the person who Denz made his heir."

395c5cf1-30f7-45d6-8f30-8149fb4662aa.Text: "Interesting. I've never heard about you from Denz, and an acquaintance of such standing is no small thing..." {n}Chaplain doesn't look ready to risk openly accusing you of lying, but he doesn't seem to be buying your answer either.{/n} "Then again, meeting you is not the only secret I've discovered — I still don't know who this Fidelio is, the person who Denz made his heir."

4aec9603-3132-464d-8ef3-e79b32630dd4.Text: {n}Chaplain nods.{/n} "Unsurprising. Denz did like remarkable people. And he knew how to get people to like him."

16f01cca-572c-4332-a9c4-c8855344c8a4.Text: "Of course." {n}Chaplain gives you a tiny, crooked smile.{/n}

b548c402-3d48-4442-b4fd-80e0854cb01d.Text: "Interesting... Denz was full of mysteries, and it looks like even I didn't know everything about him."

69bb8950-5605-430f-ba5c-47cf3285df3a.Text: {n}Not wasting time on words, Chaplain grabs the flamer.{/n}

7133ff2c-908b-494c-82b2-9b13446e8b0f.Text: "Ha! That's odd. I've been watching the guests, and I know everyone here. If you're not Fidelio, then no one here is Fidelio. Well, unless they were able to get in undetected..."

4fe0056a-0d9c-4df2-ac4c-daf434451c58.Text: "Of course they did. And they still do. And they will keep trying. The inheritance is no trifle, after all. And the claimants are not exactly the placid types." {n}Chaplain shrugs, as if he's talking about something mundane.{/n}

cb551713-4f6d-44e3-a4ba-6adb3a971e50.Text: {n}Chaplain gives you a less than friendly look, but nods.{/n} "You represent House von Valancius, you can certainly try to call the will into question if you so wish."

b9416d2d-f239-4c21-a4c1-08c8119411e2.Text: "And the ones he robbed were mostly types that no true subject of the Imperium would shed a tear over. {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}Xenos{/g}, heretics. Not all of them, of course... but the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} will judge if Denz was a decent man."

a6aa949e-6507-49ba-9fb8-eaa163bcb8bf.Text: "Let me just ask you — are you sure you're ready to resolve everything now? Maybe you'd like to talk to all sides, form your own opinion of the claimants?"

ced4462e-ea25-49b1-b0d1-e0fc969e6e12.Text: "Let me just ask you — are you sure you're ready to resolve everything now? Maybe you'd like to talk to all sides, form your own opinion of the claimants? Find out who Fidelio is, if nothing else?"

b559039d-a5bb-4efa-b4a2-8e4c9ee0175a.Text: "Maybe they will. But I would like to know for certain. If they don't make an appearance, we might never find out who Denz wanted to bequeath his fortune to."

3d35916e-e948-4898-b9de-10d48a8b13e7.Text: "Do you intend to try every idea that pops into your head? That doesn't seem like the best solution. I would suggest doing some thinking and gathering more information."

181ced79-39e5-4d24-a867-172a1a6845de.Text: "About twelve years back, there was an attempt on Denz's life. Not many could have even got close to him, let alone wounded him, but that assassin was a master of her craft. Denz always was a hardy fellow, and that's what saved him. That and his trusty implants. But the medics pretty much had to put him back together from scratch."

13131baf-0a2b-4452-80d5-f5d55998fc04.Text: "When he finally emerged from the hands of the sawbones — months after the attempted assassination — he kept chuckling about her being a sharp one. And that she was real angry with him for burning her father, or her husband, I don't recall... and he was a ship captain. I vaguely remember that conversation, but I'm almost certain that the ship was called the Repentance. And that Denz even knew the names of that captain and the proud would-be avenger. The woman's name was Leona or something like that, and her last name... I wouldn't be surprised if it sounded similar to Fidelio."

e309c354-b4a6-4e42-a1ca-2e345ec32459.Text: "Anything is possible, I suppose. It was rough for him when he went. His body rejected medicine and implants, and he was raving on and off... These things can break even the strongest person, make them regret and repent. But even if you're right, this answer brings us no closer to solving the mystery of Fidelio."

2bd2c391-8caf-43d1-b1da-0c743eade1b2.Text: "She got away after the attempt, but I know that Denz sent mercenaries after her almost immediately. Whether he found her or not — that I do not know. It seems unlikely he did, because if he had settled the score with her, he wouldn't then go and put her in his will, would he?"

62d2f95b-a8cf-4cc3-ab02-23fdb410f6c8.Text: "You know, there's a saying that no lair is big enough for two beasts," {n}Chaplain says warmly, almost affectionately.{/n} "What I mean is, if Denz and some daemon from the warp happened to share the same house — the one who'd run or wind up dead would be the daemon. Not the other way around."

2ae6bef6-dafb-48a0-bb46-8af312ad1b01.Text: "Seems so. If we've guessed right, all that's left is Fidelio and the will..."

bd3a28e4-b75e-44ea-937d-5098264f9a63.Text: "Denz did love his toys, but the names he gave them were simpler than that. He called his favourite rifle Shooty Pew-Pew — I doubt he would call another thing 'Repentance.'"

a3c64010-c5f3-42a0-8e8b-586d79839553.Text: "It's my best guess. Let me remind you what he said, 'I owe Fidelio. If not for the Repentance...' Who else could he have been indebted to if not a vengeful daughter — or lover, or whoever she was — of a captain he'd killed? It would be a very Denz thing to do — to leave all the money not to his wimp of a son, not to his idiot first mate, but to the cunning lass who almost killed him."

d68d19cf-40e0-4bac-845e-133bfd604a75.Text: "We also know something about 'dead eyes' and the fact that the courtyard is completely open — I don't think an unknown person could've gotten in here and left those words in the book."

78cbd2fa-794a-4aca-b72c-5b4cd68bb98b.Text: "Well, {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius, now it's all in your hands. I'm no sleuth and don't know what to do with all these clues. If you have some thoughts about Fidelio's whereabouts — find her. If not, come back to me. We still need to send Denz on his way — and deal with the matter of his estate."

1583a5e7-bcdb-4407-be24-147c3c0ec3d0.Text: {n}The area around the book is completely open. If Chaplain is telling the truth and he really does know all the guests by sight, then the words could only have been left by someone with free run of the courtyard, someone who wouldn't attract attention...{/n}

cf45bfac-6170-4aaf-bc15-d80530c29121.Text: {n}You still don't have a good enough grasp of the situation to be theorising about the possibility of unseen infiltration. Perhaps someone other than Fidelio wrote that line in the book, and it's as simple as that?{/n}

2cd27ace-0609-42a4-9991-61d2e5d34b92.Text: "I haven't the faintest idea. And I think that no one present knows either, or two dozen hired killers would have already begun a manhunt for this Fidelio, wherever they may be hiding. This is, after all, a significant inheritance. And the other claimants are not exactly pleased at being left out of the will."

8d51d4ae-cda8-484e-8202-47ace16985dc.Text: "Hmph. That is strange. Who could have looked at him like that in his own home? Some errant servo-skull that was passing by? Maybe it was nothing more than a dying man's delusion?"

0d861cb7-0e6f-4ea4-8b67-f0e29001477a.Text: {n}Chaplain's eyes narrow a little.{/n} "I can see that you're intrigued. I must say I am too. Ever since I heard of my friend's death, I couldn't stop thinking about the mystery of his will. You have the von Valancius name and title, perhaps you can pull more out of the guests here than I could? Here is the only clue I've got: Denz mentioned the name Fidelio to me only once. It was a long time ago, he was very drunk — he latched onto my robe and said... I hope that these are his exact words... 'I owe Fidelio. If not for the repentance...'"

149cc3cf-445d-4f0c-b904-9b4d5d97546f.Text: "You are a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} and Denz's friend. If you want to intervene, then do so. Name the heir yourself, if you like, I won't voice a word of protest. There might be issues with the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g}, but... I know which palms to grease to make them go away."

f05d5d8f-8f4d-4999-b982-dd3ac14cb982.Text: "How strange... aren't you Master Bellardo's confessor, Chaplain? How could anyone other than you have told him to repent?"

edf1f017-722e-4d3b-bbaa-a7d023dbadf1.Text: "Return to me if you find out more. Maybe we can work this out together."

70b46f18-f59b-4c42-9a19-656bcf1ffeac.Text: {n}Chaplain gives you a less than friendly look, but nods.{/n} "You're a Rogue Trader, it is your right. You want to call the will into question? Name another heir on your own authority? I don't think even the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} would dare to object."

61342c09-d689-4877-96b4-a334d7996ca1.Text: "You are an envoy of the von Valancius dynasty and Denz's friend. I will support you even if you use your authority to name the heir yourself. There might be issues with the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g}, but... I know which palms to grease to make them go away."

a7099b56-9b9a-433c-9a99-0cb178e8e4fc.Text: "Did Bellardo ever mention repentance to you?"

df7351c1-eb4e-469b-9ffc-394a511a4c90.Text: "What did you wish to speak about?"

5f76713f-87ae-4b75-b655-c921c00d6416.Text: "The amasec that you ordered your servitor to remove was poisoned. What a fascinating coincidence."

9de51025-4cd9-4d38-8f4c-177ee5cea484.Text: "Given the deceased's former occupation, I have a good idea what role you played under his command."

58cd2e22-da7a-45bb-a4ba-79ebac3f32c3.Text: "Why did Denz leave you out of his will?"

ebe5620b-b495-45b1-9520-788d39566273.Text: "I refuse to have any part in this."

83dea76f-e284-48b1-a8a3-a70bcf99094e.Text: {n}The tall man who welcomed you at the entrance is shifting from foot to foot and keeps glancing around with a gloomy expression.{/n}

a69a45d5-855f-4fe5-a4a3-d2551e90b7c0.Text: "This is an honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, such an honour... Could you spare a minute of your time? I have a request to make..."

0049fc03-0578-43e1-89d8-c636820fb374.Text: "{mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius! Could you spare a minute of your time? I'd very much like to talk to you!"

ccbe6165-56c2-40c1-8275-a1cd306e0649.Text: "Here's the thing, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I'll just give it to you straight — I'm sorry, I don't know how to talk to lofty folk..."

c14f5e25-a17d-46fa-a0dd-d1336b3ee310.Text: "Well, Denz — that is, Bellardo — my old friend and boss, died. And he left all he had — and he had a lot, mind you — to this Fidelio. That was kind of rude of him, that's no way to treat your friends. I get it, he left his useless son high and dry, and a good thing too, but his old friend?"

1b0f706d-e508-439e-903e-ddf513751403.Text: "So I'm thinking... maybe you can step in and set things right? Intervene in the matter of the inheritance... or I don't know..."

efde0813-c9d4-47d2-bd9a-6f44735678c4.Text: {n}He looks you in the eye.{/n} "Poisoned? No, it can't be! Must've been a bad batch."

e8f40e4a-b032-4805-8b6a-fa88bfb15e3d.Text: {n}Daggen smirks.{/n} "They used to call me Torch. He's Jerrycan, I'm Torch... those were the days!"

ce685c1b-bded-4fa8-8c28-105b5a18c28a.Text: "Old age, you know, his head wasn't the same anymore... Yeah, that's got to be it. It was just too unfair. To fly with him for ten years and then get nothing for it?"

1282d0d7-7142-440f-a6d4-3f87044708f8.Text: {n}Daggen winces like he has a toothache.{/n} "I wish I knew! I first heard the name when Denz kicked it. Maybe Fidelio's a whore who put a smile on his face in his golden years? And so Denz decided to give them the whole kit and caboodle."

51af08c7-3e2e-43d7-8a2d-edf71cd0992a.Text: "You're a distinguished sort, you can muscle in on this. You can talk to Chaplain — he's Denz's executor — and ask about the will. Or maybe you can find Fidelio and have a talk with them too? I mean, who'd want an inheritance that's not rightfully theirs? More trouble than it's worth, if you ask me. And trust me, old Daggen can be of service to you if you need anything. I know lots about Footfall and other things, I can help with information, get you some solid lads for a job... You can use a guy like me!"

40fd7210-fb6d-47e0-bb23-5bbececce0c4.Text: "I wouldn't dare to insist, of course. But if you happen to change your mind..."

ff5f2104-3b82-47f2-8f2a-e93359e10b61.Text: "Oh, all kinds of things happened, my girl! Things going flying, people dying, too — servants, that is. Whenever we felt like remembering our glory days and got sloshed on half a jug of the good stuff... that's when it would happen. I remember one time we decided to see who could carve open servitors in the dark the quickest..." {n}Daggen grins, then catches himself and glances at you.{/n} "All right, serious talk — nah, nothing like that in his house. Nothing sorcerous apart from the writing. As for when it began... xenos knows. Ten, twelve years ago?"

b9c2565b-23c0-4368-9c86-17bbac7a0644.Text: "No, but I know what you're talking about. The scribbles in his home, right? Yeah, it happened, all right — that writing just appeared out of nowhere. On the walls, the mirrors — and always the same word: 'Repentance.' I told him to get a {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} to check his house for sorcery, but he said no. Too pricey, I guess — he said something about that, how he had already paid too much for repentance. Not a lot of psykers around, and a single one of them will cost you as much as a team of top-notch bruisers..."

e14205f0-548e-419e-a755-8694ef411cd0.Text: "Hey, listen, friend — how long did that go on? The writing? Anything else strange happen in the household? Flying knickknacks, furniture growing tentacles, people dying for no reason?"

4475fc7b-7e8e-48d0-9015-00acb6d59158.Text: "I'm Daggen Otheo, I was first mate on Denz's ship, I mean, Master Bellardo."

6996f4d9-4b9f-414e-8f76-da35de61e35a.Text: "Badly. He went downhill real fast — just a year ago, he was still living it up, storming the slum asteroids to shoot riffraff and mutants, and then all of a sudden, he was done. His old wounds had caught up with him... And he had plenty of those, both from the old days and more recent ones, like when somebody tried to bump him off... twelve years back, I think it was."

a23e9449-aef9-4cd5-9c7c-c182ce60622c.Text: "{mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio, are you leaving already? I'm afraid you'll have to wait... wait, yes... It's Footfall Station Services, see, they're carrying out a scheduled inspection of the life support systems. It won't take long! An hour, maybe two..."

b0cda066-1a6c-45c9-b13b-e884773a3fcd.Text: "To arms, lads! Just like the good old days!"

1c802124-892c-4489-a0d5-7f98c62a168d.Text: {n}Idira turns to you and shakes her head.{/n} "It'd be good to take a look at that writing, but if I had to guess — it doesn't sound like {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} influence to me. If something really did take up residence in that house, it would've made a bigger splash in ten years. Like a dozen corpses big."

f1eec522-5916-4356-a348-22c4a183bc65.Text: "And what is it that you've heard about me?"

0649ab3d-c992-4748-9c9a-a3a8ef5193e5.Text: "You don't seem particularly grief-stricken over your father's death."

281a8828-d33e-4ba7-b650-d2b2df860a05.Text: "And what is this 'injustice' that I'm supposed to prevent from occurring?"

e7032311-708a-4ef9-bf0f-4f6a0cc57ae5.Text: "Thank you for speaking with me. Goodbye!"

3e226975-ed89-4257-beb3-1c5e339e0bb9.Text: "What kind of assistance do you seek from me?"

c069eb47-9289-482a-9da6-c0e75cd88b41.Text: "I want nothing to do with this."

c336f395-bbec-4036-830c-27e13290c5c2.Text: "Did your father ever talk to you about repentance?"

b5161918-5721-4675-8bba-406b72845a01.Text: {n}A man of indeterminate age turns to you and sighs loudly. You can tell by his breath that he came to the ceremony after indulging in one or two glasses of strong drink.{/n}

f9a54933-4852-4c4b-bea6-a21d27f99b1f.Text: "Ah, {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio! I've heard so much about you — and here you are at last, in the flesh."

1360c3c1-9a68-4870-8ebf-439eaf822085.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, it must have been the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}'s providence that brought you here! Surely a figure as great as yourself won't allow for a terrible injustice to happen!" {n}The man grimaces — it appears that obsequiousness does not come easily to him.{/n}

22f9febd-12ce-4568-877d-ede5e4eabc12.Text: "Good {mf|sir|lady} of House von Valancius! I'm ever so glad to see at least one decent person in this crowd..." {n}His eyes narrow.{/n} "Can we talk? Support from an envoy of an esteemed dynasty could very much help... to prevent a terrible injustice from happening."

e14c6df9-593c-4157-ae2a-dce69345efd0.Text: "If I was the one lying in that box, he wouldn't be crying his eyes out either," {n}Kas bites out with sudden acidity. He takes a moment to calm himself.{/n} "A son's feelings are complicated. I wasn't a good son; old Denz wasn't a good father. But I do miss him in my own way, yes. He always seemed timeless to me, not just a bag of meat and ugly ambitions like the rest of us are."

650215be-8076-4c54-ad90-c54316ee4c4d.Text: "Well..." {n}He grimaces.{/n} "The lawful heir is being robbed of his inheritance. My dear father left his entire fortune, down to the last coin, to some nobody — a certain Fidelio, who hasn't even bothered to come to his funeral. And I'm left with nothing. Do you think it's fair?"

e62718d3-0f5a-40b6-b0cd-24037061147e.Text: "You're nobility — you, of all people, must realise just how wrong and unacceptable this situation is. So I thought — maybe you could lend me a hand somehow? For the sake of friendship with the future keeper of the Bellardo fortune — me. And for the sake of justice, of course!"

8d003b27-902e-46bb-af9a-f161aaa7e13a.Text: "As if I know! The old man wasn't a heart-to-heart sort of person. Right up until the announcement of his last will and testament, I had no idea he'd put me in the doghouse."

7876734c-1075-430c-8cf6-b0b7a30751f7.Text: "I have absolutely no idea. Zero. There's a will, there's a name — that's it. Maybe they're my father's by-blow, some brother or sister I never knew I had? Maybe they're a whore who brightened his final days? I get the feeling that old louse Chaplain knows, he's always known more about Father's business than any of us. But he's keeping quiet."

07751b4a-841a-4ed9-bdde-d5b52478b52c.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I've never even been in the presence of a person of your status, let alone talked to one! But I just thought — maybe you can impose your will on the matter of the inheritance? It would be great to find out who this Fidelio is too, true, but that's nothing, that's just my curiosity..."

48b5f5cc-e9fd-4384-a790-28c2c0b1ca3a.Text: "Put a word in for me, suggest that they go over the will one more time... You're an envoy of House von Valancius, after all, and Footfall respects that name. And, well, it would be nice to find out who this Fidelio is too."

6bc2c436-cacc-499b-abc4-7644e8b6b2b9.Text: {n}He bows.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, thank you! I don't know how to thank you for your kindness — but I'll definitely try if it all works out!"

d0edabdd-e0f4-4926-8591-cad3aa9e95be.Text: "Much obliged! And know that I'll make it worth your while. If I get the inheritance, I'll express my gratitude in whatever way I can."

6d8c3f99-88a9-4c59-ac2d-587a9320ee7d.Text: {n}He slumps a little.{/n} "That's that, then... It's just not my day. When is it ever?"

b43839ee-33f4-4b05-9e93-14cc7b413342.Text: "To turn a funeral rite into a stepping stone for one's covetous desires is blasphemy. To dispute the will of the dead is doubly blasphemous." {n}Kibellah's dark eyes seem to burn right through the man, making him swallow nervously and avert his gaze.{/n}

5f04084b-e168-4888-b747-1b3b449030a2.Text: "My dear Fidelio, leaving already? And you won't even stay to see the old man burn — I mean, laid to rest?"

a91c84a0-26c6-4b0b-b401-767eae859d45.Text: "Pardon me. Kas Bellardo. I have the honour of being the only child of the deceased." {n}He sends a mocking salute in the direction of the coffin.{/n}

fd6274ae-37c7-41fd-bc7a-ed63f00e54ad.Text: "Ha ha, ha ha ha, that's hilarious. Even good old Chaplain doesn't tell me to repent — he gave up on me long ago. And my old dad, he gave up on me long before that!" {n}He laughs nervously.{/n} "Wait... you mean that 'repentance'? Those stupid ghosts or whatever it was? I'm pretty sure my father did it himself, the senile old kook, or maybe it was my daughter messing around. Where else could those words have come from?"

abffd5db-1525-4d17-a44a-0b088e51e616.Text: {n}He forces a smile.{/n} "That you were... very close with... ah, forget it! I didn't mean anything by it. Just making conversation."

5696ae6a-6f03-4dad-bed1-3641d786a99d.Text: "Oh, you don't know? Out of the blue, writing started appearing on a wall in our house, just one word — 'Repentance.' Big, sprawling scribbles, like a child's handwriting. The first one appeared about ten or so years back. The help kept whispering about it being the work of ghosts, woooh! But for some reason the old man didn't want to do anything about it, and he told me not to. The writing amused him somehow. Whenever he'd see 'Repentance' scratched on the wall, he'd just grin."

cd979250-3020-4095-aaab-f54621ee0036.Text: "Age. Debauchery. Old wounds. By the end, my old dad was more {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g} than man. Especially after the assassination attempt — people tried to kill him, you see, about twelve years ago."

69ceea37-fa34-42fa-a2a3-bf651c6f36e4.Text: "What, am I supposed to die... at my own father's funeral? Ha ha. No, I don't think I will!"

c36380ec-2a32-43c0-93d3-fe039d83e97e.Text: "Chaplain? Is everything clear to you now?"

98776305-81f5-46e0-a306-9d1407c9db34.Text: "Summon everyone. It is time to decide the fate of Bellardo's estate — and that of the heirs."

54ba6d6e-4cfe-46d8-a136-948361c837aa.Text: {n}If you didn't know what to look for, it would be easy to overlook this {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}, which may have once been a woman. The servitor's implants, the mechanical nature of its movements, the empty gaze — it's all there. But...{/n}

76421d07-4363-4ffb-90f6-69e189b78af5.Text: {n}That single word causes the servitor's body to twist in a violent spasm. Something akin to a sob or a growl builds in its throat, and its mechanical appendages jerk convulsively.{/n}

e59ac849-a19d-49b0-b260-715140ed9147.Text: "Servitors are the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s stepchildren. That's what they say in my homeland. Shouldn't the inheritance go to the parent? Their representative, to be specific." {n}Jae somehow manages to cast Pasqal a glance that is both conspiratorial and pleading.{/n}

853564c8-462e-41ec-86a9-8c1d2bb901b3.Text: "I have not encountered this statement before and I am unwilling to endorse it. Poetic platitudes, though they may seem innocuous, can be a false visage for perverse interpretations of His tenets." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-synthesiser suddenly starts malfunctioning, causing Pasqal's timbre to jump like a fooling jester.{/n}

f74fe43b-3f80-41e0-8044-7a8ebe56cda3.Text: {n}Chaplain's tall figure appears next to you.{/n} "So this is our heir! Right?" {n}He pauses, mulling it over, then gestures for the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} clerk who gave the opening speech to approach.{/n} "The inventory of Denz's possessions, what does it say about this servitor?"

ab64791d-3fe0-472c-b822-f9fe0d958228.Text: "Let's see here, let's see... one moment... mmhmm, mmhmm... Section B17/40, 'Personal Effects of the Deceased,' subsection 'Servitors'... Here it is!"

90ed4434-19dd-453e-b998-b8fdc0312179.Text: "I believe so. Didn't I tell you that Denz, after he survived the assassination attempt, sent a whole squad of mercenaries to hunt down the woman who tried to kill him? Looks like he found her." {n}Chaplain nods at the servitor.{/n}

9b7ad32a-05b2-4666-8091-51c366ae5ad4.Text: {n}Silence. The servitor's eyelids flutter slightly, its gaze staring off into space. Deep inside its single human eye, dark as a well, a spark seems to flicker... or is it just your imagination?{/n}

8ee0d5f9-3cc6-49ae-b3c2-96bc1f9e3939.Text: "She was allowed to keep her memory and some semblance of awareness, so I suppose the mysterious writing of 'Repentance' both here in the book and back at Denz's home was done by her. The question that remains, of course, is why would Denz decide to make a servitor his heir? This is either his last and cruellest joke — or an incredibly ham-fisted attempt to make amends on his deathbed. I'd like to believe that it's the former."

46ce76e5-c6c2-4e1b-9b5b-b6b90e1ec139.Text: "Or — we could ask {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius to settle the matter in the name of {mf|his|her} dynasty. This is Footfall, after all. If a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} says that a servitor can inherit — then that's how it's going to be."

c50984ff-18f1-4fa7-92ce-d01471b3bf23.Text: "Oh, this is a rare, one-of-a-kind unit! Commissioned personally by Master Bellardo twelve years ago! The main function of this servitor is cleaning the house, bedrooms, vestibules, bathrooms... In accordance with Master Bellardo's wishes, its free will was completely eradicated, and the parts of its brain that regulated pleasure responses were destroyed... but to a large extent, its memory and awareness were preserved!"

9af53db4-db6d-4905-9674-508a4ef982fa.Text: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Chaplain chuckles.{/n} "This ought to be good."

2d77a593-db61-45b5-a4e3-d39bd845fd39.Text: "Th-this matter requires further investigation... We will have to go over the codices, bylaws, statutes, regulations... from the last four hundred years or so." {n}The clerk pales a little.{/n} "But we'll find the answer sooner or later!"

f241b5ed-4e13-44dc-b6a5-024bdeb62c55.Text: "Were this not a gathering of criminal rabble, maybe I'd make an effort to recall the inheritance laws in effect on Footfall. But seeing as that is what you are..." {n}Solomorne cracks his neck.{/n} "...you're fresh out of luck."

ac82b83a-ed8f-4528-a38f-f8488422780d.Text: "Have you ever heard the name Fidelio?"

766cae5f-9520-4509-9399-96f54a73ed25.Text: "Who are you and what are you doing here?"

fb614433-0a2d-4651-8869-fe16d047ea1b.Text: "Someone left some strange words in the book of remembrance, as if they were from Fidelio. That wasn't your doing by any chance?"

0660a16b-07e9-4220-b906-095213e8842a.Text: "Did your grandfather ever mention the word repentance to you?"

a081583f-619a-4871-8c9b-d9f2afa3100a.Text: {n}The girl dressed in expensive clothes raises her sad little face to you and says in a serious voice,{/n} "Hello."

cc2542f9-2a0a-41d2-80dd-453fb9b44950.Text: "He did. That word kept appearing in our house, and nobody knew who wrote it. It used to make Grandpa happy when I was little. He always smiled when he saw it! But then... later, when I was a little bigger and Grandpa was already old... it stopped making him happy. He was sad. He would just sit there and stare at nothing. And after that, when he got sick..." {n}She stops, her big eyes glistening with tears.{/n}

7d1547f0-591b-483e-a4db-0dff7ed6c9b0.Text: "When he got sick, the writing started to scare him. More and more of it appeared. 'Repentance, repentance, repentance.' Even in his bedroom! One time, he pointed at that word... and said something... something very weird... About dead eyes. And about cobras going to class."

07cc1f9e-f1b4-4d8a-b094-1cc7af04d7c5.Text: {n}Adelia tries to smile, then just nods seriously.{/n}

add0b426-41e9-4bff-8375-111e58af498b.Text: "Hiding." {n}She hesitates for a moment.{/n} "I thought I was going to cry, and I didn't want anyone to see. I... my name is Adelia Bellardo. It's my grandpa in there, in the box."

6b5c3963-a3d0-45bf-99a8-6b205e222b88.Text: {n}Abelard, who was looking at her with sympathy, narrows his eyes.{/n} "What did you say? Cobras going to class? Are you sure this is what your grandfather said?"

1c0cdd35-9ce1-42d9-ab25-c4d69e81005d.Text: {n}The girl raises her serious and sad eyes to you.{/n}

997f9942-3442-4aa9-a4e2-6df99ce9331f.Text: {n}Abelard strokes his beard.{/n} "Perhaps this is the old {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialNavy}Navy{/g} officer in me talking, but I am almost certain he wasn't talking about a snake, but a Cobra-class destroyer. 'Cobra' going to 'class,' you see?"

60dfba18-200c-4fe0-b383-20b1d59f3351.Text: "It's someone my dad is very mad at. But Dad is always mad at everyone — at Grandpa, Mum, Daggen, Chaplain..."

c8200106-a58c-4f79-97f0-7bbf297f2013.Text: "Ha. That would've been a funny prank!" {n}Her eyes light up a little.{/n} "But I don't play pranks. It was someone else. Maybe Fidelio did it, very quietly? Or maybe it was someone who's not on the list, but also someone nobody would suspect?"

86d9d04e-8010-42e1-8edd-5f1f8489440d.Text: "My dad is Kas Bellardo. He's with the guests. And my mum ran away, they told me she hates Dad and Grandpa. I guess she hates me too, I don't know. It was a long time ago, I don't even miss her anymore. I miss Grandpa... He was the nicest." {n}She presses her lips together and lets out a quiet, very unchildlike sigh.{/n}

7ee5bac7-8731-4fba-84cc-962947794e11.Text: {n}Her last phrase stirs your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}memories{/d}. No, this naive child's tale has nothing to do with reptiles... "Class," "cobras"... It seems her mind has distorted her late grandfather's words — he must have been talking about a voidship. More specifically, about a Cobra-class destroyer.{/n}

197c89ca-f1fb-440f-bdd8-8af7328243e7.Text: "If you do not wish to be parted from your forefather, then sever his head, embalm it, and put it in your bed." {n}Kibellah's voice sounds mundane, like she is explaining the most basic things.{/n} "Speak to him before you go to sleep and after you wake up, and that way he will stay with you."

820a1700-2f61-4724-a593-aa6f261ce621.Text: {n}Argenta's face softens. She reaches out and gently strokes Adelia's head.{/n} "The tears will pass, Adelia. The tears will pass, the strength will return, and your courage will never leave you."

f95a466e-c9f2-4f73-badb-e23ab2109a9c.Text: "Wh-what?" {n}Adelia shrinks away fearfully, looking to you for protection.{/n}

c537b011-108a-4ee6-a65b-e88916a4c1c9.Text: "Don't listen to the lady. The lady is nuts. Like, properly off her rocker. Listen to your elders, eat your breakfast, and don't cut off your grandpa's head."

526ed3d4-3a06-456b-84d3-551ea9ae41b6.Text: "Of course I'm sure. When Grandpa was ill, I sat with him, and this one time he just started talking about cobras. I was sad, but it was also a little funny. 'Cobra, get to class!' he said."

701be5aa-afc9-4aba-a10a-639a908ad715.Text: "Daddy, what are you doing? I'm sorry, I promise I'll be good, I'll give you all of Grandpa's money!"

d9ac2baa-7c12-4750-b652-ace7f931d392.Text: "Shut your hole, brat! Listen up, all of you: either the inheritance goes to me or I blow this one's brains out. I'm gonna count to three! One... Two..."

914980e2-fe39-4085-a545-f6df0b0f7279.Text: "Pasqal, matters of technology are your forte. Which means you're going for that lever."

378e07ed-a850-4299-bdc2-bd4e06fd36d2.Text: "Argenta, how about a stroll through this delightful muck?"

2291917f-c32f-46a3-b180-0b62d645c10e.Text: [Enter the malodorous sludge yourself] "Hard choices are the lot of any leader."

6a1f8a79-527b-4c1a-be17-3b405638c293.Text: "Yrliet, the honour of pulling the lever falls to you."

741c622f-37c6-4782-bbaa-cc2c12b62fc0.Text: "Cassia, even delicate nobles can benefit from learning of the darker sides of life. Please proceed to the lever."

b14a6335-2fa9-4fb0-b002-16787956feda.Text: "As everyone knows, the person who does all the dirty work for the Rogue Trader is {mf|his|her} Seneschal..."

cfb312f1-d8b3-423d-b3fb-e2a79f7ecd2f.Text: "Kibellah, you are my shield. My shadow. My blade. My puller of levers."

1b3bb908-e1ab-4d3c-b521-74a129b334b7.Text: "Solomorne, could Glaito jump far enough to reach the lever?"

c4ade83e-4932-4614-af5a-2c51789efa35.Text: "Idira, I have a mission for you!"

49daa1b6-d87d-47e6-b063-3d784df18b41.Text: {n}A horrible stench reaches your nostrils long before you see its source — a corridor where punctured pipes are disgorging streams of murky sludge. In the distance, you see the lever that opens the doors leading outside. The only way to reach it is by submerging yourself in the sludge.{/n}

fa5b19e9-542f-49f7-a4e4-24129950c168.Text: "Do I understand the reason for this deliberation correctly: we are deciding which one of us should plunge into the mire to open the door?"

ff4a73ae-32c0-49c6-9f63-69fb8d741a14.Text: "I'm too old for this sh— ahem."

5411ea8e-fc63-4c51-93a0-5184e3f82ee6.Text: "Is this filth somehow unusual for mon-keigh settlements?"

7a7768b7-b5b5-46f7-8ffa-7fc35506955e.Text: {n}Cassia brings the corner of a perfumed shawl to her nose.{/n} "I think I am going to be sick."

e9a0e666-cdf9-461d-9c31-dbb4123d60e6.Text: "Looks like the utility folks have really let themselves go; they've got shi— ahem, sewage spilling out right under the central square, but they just — eugh, so that's what I smelled last time I was in Vladaym's palace! Ha ha, the stench suits him."

5673fa7e-eec5-4250-a878-381de4411706.Text: "Someone's gotta go and pull the lever, right? I propose our holy sister as a candidate! A seeker after spiritual purity shouldn't be put off by a little bit of ordinary muck, after all."

0bcca29a-f27c-48f2-8d2a-bb6d88d2c320.Text: {n}Yrliet shrugs and silently enters the stream.{/n}

3168b4e0-fc65-42e8-b21e-9e30077d70c7.Text: {n}With a slight bow, Heinrix departs for the murky waters with a stoic expression.{/n}

07435bc6-2065-42b0-a0c7-a75f600b4623.Text: "What if I told you there was a sunken stash of smuggled xenodevices in there?"

1a9fcb1c-ed15-489f-9e1e-be8fcc3bf7f9.Text: {n}Pasqal hesitates briefly before responding,{/n} "I reject this hypothesis."

014a45d3-f668-4d50-b164-04e093c236a7.Text: {n}Kibellah shrugs and gracefully wades into the current of filth.{/n}

8dbe5446-df3d-4638-8686-b5409b2aa545.Text: "It's slippery, he might fall in the sewage. I'd better go myself." {n}And the Proctor stoically sets out to assail the stinking stream.{/n}

f6941f57-3f9c-4208-9bcf-b94ae5995a6c.Text: {n}Cassia looks at you like she cannot believe in such villainy.{/n} "I... I... very well! I will go learn... of the darker sides..."

5a00608e-5b9a-4b33-b88c-94fcc7243298.Text: "I serve House von Valancius!" {n}Abelard salutes you and marches onward with dignity.{/n}

b0beb122-628f-4289-9925-18dd3fd6c544.Text: "Sure thing, shereen! And I just finished scrubbing off the last bits of the soup!"

8f143c50-b5a0-402f-8254-368f21e4520c.Text: "I'm no prissy noble afraid to get her hands dirty!" {n}Argenta advances through the putrid waters like a voidship.{/n}

21c16959-4638-433b-b428-981cc55d36be.Text: {n}After studying the substance closely, Pasqal says firmly,{/n} "Request denied. I cannot defile my Ferrum Sanctum by making contact with this substance."

81a0a041-4cff-4360-bccc-1cd88bc5d5a7.Text: "It doesn't take a fortune-teller to figure out the specifics of that mission..."

4f948acc-eece-47e9-8b65-816aa1ba35ec.Text: "Hang on, you can just say no?"

81165fbe-bf98-46a0-8c4c-89df7f2c33c0.Text: "Wait, so you hid valuables in the crematorium's furnace?"

9c8fd3b7-d573-47d7-9b05-e5743dcdc739.Text: "I refuse to have any part in this."

2b91ae5f-e569-4f9f-89ca-240292b71b0d.Text: "I will help you on the following condition. You see, I am — most definitely — {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio. I'm afraid I've misplaced some of my documents. If you make me a copy of everything you can find in the archives that has my name on it — you'll get your contraband."

c27236cf-6ac3-41e8-8eaf-6cce0a91aae3.Text: "Why did you decide to ask me specifically for help?"

54cd6e4c-e58a-47c3-a91a-38f0a8d78bf2.Text: "What do you need from me and what are you offering in return?"

569ed06d-d03d-4afb-8ea1-fdd328799227.Text: {n}You hear someone delicately clearing their throat.
