5d7cd347-431b-4903-80f4-c46e6372bdd0.Text: {n}Marazhai snorts.{/n} "None of us are going to bend our backs out of compassion for the weak, {name}."

379d8988-9112-40ec-b659-a359944ace02.Text: {n}The Drukhari stays silent. You see the jaw muscles working in his hollow cheeks. Finally, he speaks with reluctance:{/n} "I need time."

fb2dfc1c-3fd9-45ea-bef1-316df2659b18.Text: "But of course. What else could such a gracious invitation to rule be?" {n}Marazhai stares into Kharael's eyes intently. He does not look away.{/n}

cbe9f1fc-0136-49c3-8bc7-3989177d0708.Text: {n}Kharael casts an appraising glance at you, but his response is addressed to Marazhai.{/n} "The Kabal is on the verge of destruction. We require assistance."

83bd898b-d974-41a0-ade9-9f2ad2e9a217.Text: {n}The Drukhari hisses furiously.{/n} "You dare speak of this to me, mon-keigh?"

e151d1f8-32b9-4c37-bf59-3831478c9a36.Text: "So what do you want from me?" {n}Marazhai speaks with feigned indolence.{/n} "From a Dracon cast down from his post and banished from the ranks of the Reaving Tempest? From a Drukhari banned from Commorragh itself?"

562d6a28-88f3-4612-8a92-dd962efb20b0.Text: "We need a leader. We need a symbol of the power that led the Kabal to might and prosperity for centuries. The lineage of the Aezyrraesh has not yet faded, which means it is destined to return... The Reaving Tempest is calling out to you."

dfe718b9-bfc4-4230-8c7c-abb779ff94c3.Text: {n}Marazhai regards you with a look of smouldering hunger and replies to Kharael with contempt.{/n} "The mon-keigh is my property, Kharael. Be careful when you are looking at {mf|him|her}, I may misinterpret your intentions."

31dd873a-d76d-4d0c-ad21-7670961e01fe.Text: "Answer the summons. Attend the meeting, look at the faces of those who have gathered there. And start rebuilding the Kabal. The Reaving Tempest is not dead while I still breathe, and I will make the Dark City tremble when we return there in full force."

f84f757f-0ab7-4045-93dc-27321f82b265.Text: {n}Marazhai sneers.{/n} "Have some fun. The Drukhari forced to hide in realspace? I suppose it will be an amusing sight. We will get there, find out what ridiculous ambush they have set up for me, and then we will cut them down. To the last warrior. If the Reaving Tempest has truly fallen... so be it. By my right as an Aezyrraesh, I will end it."

6e315702-905b-410f-b4cf-01193322f3d2.Text: {n}Marazhai looks at you askance, then shakes himself and turns away.{/n} "Then this conversation is over."

4eed828f-a393-46df-85c1-eed78a39c29f.Text: {n}Marazhai's eyes narrow as a smile spreads across his lips.{/n} "We will go there and get what we want. You will acquire trophies and new playthings, and I will derive pleasure from trampling all over those who turned their backs on me... Power over my Kabal, too, if I manage to make them bow down before me."

c943345f-3cf3-4589-b352-cd4e128a2d83.Text: {n}Kharael appears to be choking with rage.{/n} "What? You... you've become the plaything of a mon-keigh? How far you have fall—"

0a85f80e-fd7f-4617-83a5-e0574339b58d.Text: {n}Marazhai nods.{/n} "Excellent. We have the coordinates. We know what to expect. I will sharpen my blades — they will obviously be needed when I reunite with my kin. At least, I hope so."

e0066321-3665-4b7b-8c3a-bb1b58138c62.Text: "Forgetting your place?" {n}Kharael's voice is ringing with scorn.{/n} "This mon-keigh has the nerve to talk to you like that? How low you must have fallen to—"

4d389246-daaa-4d31-b661-968d39e1b464.Text: {n}Marazhai gives you another look, this time one of disappointment.{/n}

c442d9d1-4b67-4c02-ba2d-e021c1f3d557.Text: {n}Kharael smirks but does avert his gaze.{/n}

33c12969-26ba-4c2f-b598-e3008fb17fa5.Text: {n}Marazhai snaps his fingers pensively.{/n} "Get back to your ships. I need time to contemplate my answer to the plea of the Reaving Tempest."

451305f5-7ed0-4291-8b74-24f541a8d423.Text: "No, no... Did you not see how Kharael spoke to me? The incline of his head, the tone... He yearns for my return. Perhaps the Reaving Tempest... can still be reborn." {n}Marazhai stares off to the side, immersed in thought.{/n}

b7bad514-3b8f-4a12-95a8-316d9068c3ea.Text: {n}Kharael cocks his head slightly.{/n} "Ever since you were deposed... there has been a lot of talk about you. Much of it... casts shade even on the scions of the Aezyrraesh. Not all Kabalites are convinced that serving you is a worthy future for the Reaving Tempest."

aaa0fb1a-7673-4629-b7b5-2c2a6e616a1a.Text: {n}The xenos shrugs nonchalantly.{/n} "I think Kharael found a way to gain access to my spies, the ones left or abandoned as sleeper agents on your ship. My downfall was so sudden I never had the time to cover my tracks."

2ac2a459-4cd8-4298-9e93-79866d530675.Text: {n}Kharael looks at Marazhai with distrust.{/n} "Despite being open to the lusts of Sai'lanthresh, not even realspace could break an Aezyrraesh... Your appearance suggests you have plenty of prey at your disposal."

9870aae9-3add-46b1-99c2-b6a11f961be9.Text: "We cannot wait long for your decision. Those who have found refuge in realspace have been here... too long." {n}Kharael's voice rings with genuine fear.{/n} "We are forced to fight one another. Forced to seek torment in the blood of our kin. Do not tarry, find our base in a neighbouring star system where our raid is hiding from the scheming of other Kabals. You should hurry — the voice of Sai'lanthresh in the minds of our companions grows louder with every passing day."

36aca3c4-ef04-4fc7-8d6f-b4e6b6d8967a.Text: {n}Marazhai turns to you with an intrigued smile.{/n} "The Kabal wants me back? Hmm. How very curious..."

a8b83a19-0c4b-440e-afef-a6fc5a0dabae.Text: {n}Marazhai turns toward you, and Kharael flinches, noticing the brand on his neck. The Drukhari's voice becomes a hiss:{/n} "You... let yourself be branded with a mark other than the tattoos of the Reaving Tempest?" {n}Kharael's gaze swings toward you.{/n} "Who does it belong to? This mon-keigh here?"

69e72367-c70c-43f1-92b6-b33b3e47f5c6.Text: {n}Kharael's gaze lingers on you, or more specifically, on the brand on your neck. Suddenly he snorts.{/n} "Did you get bored away from home, Marazhai? You found yourself a toy?"

c7fcdf29-5860-4758-a29b-4992d7e43670.Text: "It is not. A trap is what I prepared for you, an unexpected and exquisite creation of a sophisticated mind. This is an invitation to a slaughter." {n}Marazhai's lip curls in contempt.{/n} "Kharael did not even try to hide how much the Reaving Tempest hates me."

2552d698-af3a-47b9-ad4d-378580fdc927.Text: {n}Marazhai gives you a look of smouldering hunger and nonchalantly replies to Kharael over his shoulder.{/n} "You mean this burn? It is but a mark from a mon-keigh laser charge."

ed855ac2-3988-495c-94f2-97ca54f54689.Text: "...and that's not to mention the fact that our shelter has become a new dysjunction point." {n}Kharael literally spits the words.{/n} "The warp rages in the spire, flooding the city with daemon hordes. It is no secret how the rift came to appear in the very abode of the Reaving Tempest..."

133d888a-2e98-44ba-93f3-ac895db88c14.Text: "Careful, Kharael." {n}Marazhai's voice drops to a rumbling purr.{/n} "You are about to insult the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest by claiming that the Drukhari whose aid you begged on bended knee is unworthy of such a request. Are you sure you wish to do that?"

bd6d8c58-4148-4d96-8c68-4c38e8ccf537.Text: {n}Kharael takes a few moments to catch his breath, choking on his own rage. At last, he manages to get his emotions under control and whispers,{/n} "I will remain silent, Aezyrraesh."

685d6428-b728-4dca-88a6-79d84cd3451d.Text: "...and that is punishment enough for my kin who broke the laws of Commorragh." {n}Marazhai's voice oozes lazy malevolence.{/n} "Was it not my sister who flouted the ban by gathering Farseers with the gift of sorcery in our abode? Was it not she who patronised the Haemonculus who was experimenting on creatures with psyker powers? What does that have to do with me, Kharael? Fling your accusations at a different target if you want them to stick."

f318176c-cdeb-4725-b554-39049b383c4c.Text: {n}Kharael looks over Marazhai appraisingly, not even hiding the disgust in his gaze and the falsity in his voice.{/n} "Though the surviving scion reeks of desperation and thirst... We are denied the luxury of a choice."

e1f1e9fa-f45a-49af-a684-af4f039a9ef1.Text: {n}Marazhai narrows his eyes.{/n} "Let us say I accept your offer. What use do I have for the handful of Drukhari huddling behind you, Kharael? Answer me — does the Reaving Tempest still live? Or is this the death rattle of the fallen?"

642086f6-12dc-4552-941b-2ed4550b6284.Text: {n}Marazhai is silent for a few moments.{/n} "I do not like your tone, Kharael. You are too insolent. You are forgetting your place if you truly are going to serve me as the new Archon."

f9494f9a-7fc1-49c2-a5ab-009e13bd40ea.Text: {n}Marazhai laughs.{/n} "You must think very poorly of me if you expect me to believe a single word you said about my 'long-awaited' return to the Kabal... But I will indulge you. Let us pretend I am blind and deaf, and therefore will consider your offer."

7f5529bb-d85c-478c-ac87-b8afbd28c177.Text: {n}Kharael leans forward.{/n} "Two raids managed to hide in the tangle of the Webway and are awaiting the chosen hour. There are Kabal troops hiding in the bowels of Commorragh itself. We are biding our time. When these forces come together, they will be enough to take over another spire and absorb several smaller Kabals who will serve us..."

a922735b-949e-4281-b227-b793ea2213f7.Text: {n}Marazhai makes a warning gesture.{/n} "I have not yet decided, {name}."

a6b0a350-7f12-4797-a730-dfaa9ab62068.Text: [Look around] "They have been fighting, and for a long time."

ae1fce62-92fa-4e0c-b1b3-2703a9aea7ed.Text: "It is time for us to go."

a306eb8c-c8df-4096-9058-85bbe71a8cfe.Text: {n}The convulsing xenos is dressed in Reaving Tempest armour that has been pierced by weapons in several places. The dying warrior raises his head and stares at you. He sees Marazhai and opens his bloody mouth wide.{/n} "You..."

4d49891e-87f7-46c6-8171-03744a2d6d51.Text: "...my Dracon." {n}The bloodied lips twist in an ugly smile.{/n} "Now that you are here... the Tempest will be avenged. Make them choke on their own blood."

0f3f3620-c681-41c5-be1c-75d73e4ecc20.Text: "...Marazhai?" {n}The bloodied face twists into a grimace of surprise.{/n} "You are alive..."

c6b358dd-f729-4e05-aca1-4641fd155bad.Text: "...you." {n}The bloodied face twists into a grimace of disgust.{/n} "Refuse of the arena..."

e6d4bef6-1567-423a-bfff-8c7b711cbfa4.Text: {n}Marazhai narrows his eyes.{/n} "You doubt my ability to survive? After I managed to escape the Dark City? You should not."

ae51d845-1d61-433a-a50d-49a5103a6632.Text: {n}Marazhai's movements are swift and precise, making the dying Drukhari gurgle and fall silent forever. The Dracon pensively wipes the blood off his blade.{/n} "They must be taught to worship me anew."

b7cfdcf7-6c7c-4202-b374-e4c61d063681.Text: {n}Marazhai watches impassively as you dispatch the xenos.{/n} "Had enough fun yet? We need to move on, straight into the maw of those who think they can outwit us."

d3dd0bfa-5e02-4d2f-b193-3b46222cf6f6.Text: {n}The wounded Drukhari chokes and wheezes, trying to get up.{/n} "I am..."

60b4393c-ca2e-426e-a117-7ae521edc92a.Text: {n}Marazhai grins.{/n} "Indeed. My weapons have been sheathed for too long."

4e2aeb70-c65b-4a13-9c53-95aa4ac9a5ee.Text: {n}You barely notice the swift blow — the dying xenos falls silent. Marazhai wipes the blood off his blade.{/n} "This one was already drained. Let us find another, someone full of pain and vitality."

7351631f-29e8-4aea-9540-777ac23bf350.Text: "What if... what if the Reaving Tempest is not feuding with the Black Heart, which tracked my Kabal down here? What if they joined forces? For reasons that currently elude me. Then everything points to the fact that these warriors from my Kabal were not killed in a battle, but butchered like cattle after being brought to the front lines." {n}Marazhai looks around and grimaces.{/n}

082feae6-581c-4491-95a6-a10691997875.Text: "We are... destroying one another... going insane since we left Commorragh hoping to find... find..." {n}The Drukhari's voice fades to an unintelligible hiss.{/n}

5f2df3a6-7893-49c5-853b-98468a425835.Text: "Carnage. Killing enemies, or each other — it does not matter. They suffer as I have suffered, driven insane by the voice of Sai'lanthresh. In realspace it can only be drowned out by the whistling of blades and the moans of the dying."

901c9e15-3e49-45bd-b569-c6c5d720a510.Text: "You cannot see it, {name}, but... the very battlefield is strange. Clashes between Kabals are different from raids on mon-keigh worlds. I can draw attack vectors in my head as much as I want, picture the squad locations and so on... but it does not make sense. Nothing about this makes sense." {n}The xenos flexes his fingers in obvious irritation.{/n}

b6eb9cfb-eb37-4031-ba91-759f112b7b52.Text: "A heavy ordeal for Drukhari. Protracted battles in realspace require... particular dedication and ferocity." {n}Marazhai gazes around the battlefield with a look of confusion on his face.{/n} "Hmm. Strange."

141d3a34-a04a-4381-a7cd-535c78085412.Text: "Although..." {n}Marazhai seems to recall something, and a look of satisfaction appears on his face.{/n} "Forget it. In fact, this is just a confirmation of what kind of spectacle awaits us."

0a384ff4-def2-407d-9e14-7257d12ed8f1.Text: {n}Marazhai stops you, his eyes burning with barely restrained anger.{/n} "The life of my property is not yours to take."

7eeb1f0f-33be-4b43-a058-3e5983a7f700.Text: "Has Marazhai been questioned about the incident?"

aff67b45-3c7b-4d38-85dc-1ecaeda4ee87.Text: "I will immediately talk to the xenos and find out what happened."

cba6614a-3457-476d-9398-6104b93acdc3.Text: "They were Mandrakes. They could have infiltrated the ship through the shadows."

bf76eb2f-8268-4328-a70a-ebea1c48e73d.Text: "A report from the middle decks, Lord Captain. Immediately after our translation from the warp, there were reports on the vox-channels about black creatures appearing all over the place. The witness accounts claim they emerged straight from the shadows, and it was your pet xenos Marazhai they were interested in."

ad3ee006-9ee7-480d-9327-3e0eb3656999.Text: "Several enforcers perished in the battle, but we managed to avoid significant casualties. Your... xenos took out the aggressors. I would not be bothering you with this if we had determined how the creatures got onto the ship. Until we know for sure, we won't be able to stop future incursions."

031fd30f-fc02-4d28-b624-aea0c3a3a0de.Text: {n}A pregnant pause fills the vox-channel.{/n} "In that case... guarding the decks against every shadow will not be possible. We will strengthen the security detail at key points on the vessel and hope the incident does not happen again."

c1f312d8-bec3-4c55-b514-86d074092ac4.Text: "No. Since the incident on the officers' deck, everyone has been giving him a wide berth." {n}Vigdis's voice is trembling slightly. It appears that even she is afraid of approaching the xenos.{/n}

4b655a0f-a9eb-4aea-890f-ecafe7ff6901.Text: [Produce a weapon] "Enough, Marazhai! Let us just kill them all, is that not what we came here for?"

02557b16-c8aa-488d-8641-624d68bb3192.Text: [Nod toward the female Drukhari next to Nazrakhei] "Who is that?"

6ceea1c5-80aa-4a40-b314-a2556bb63c76.Text: "You claim all the work was done for you, xenos, but why, then, are you behaving as though you have been stuck in realspace for too long?"

d788cbdf-ce46-4db9-a0be-b0368f3d77eb.Text: "Wait. I did not understand any of that."

5c2910a4-a233-4dfa-92d9-614579059005.Text: "I am so tired of your confusing xenos intrigues..."

8086a68c-520f-4a75-8b0c-b86560f6d508.Text: "Even I can clearly see that the offer to join the Black Heart is a ploy — a false lifeline tossed out to desperate souls. And I am just a mon-keigh!"

b4e65b96-78a6-497f-9eb2-70588458eac9.Text: "So the remains of the Reaving Tempest have joined a different Kabal?"

bd99f262-9873-426e-a329-1008392da33a.Text: "Impressive, Marazhai. They sent an entire cavalcade of highborn xenos after you."

d8131f99-d856-4c36-919a-9ee9788fe37b.Text: "So the Reaving Tempest was doomed from the start?"

a54b877c-0d06-42af-823e-ea8dded2e286.Text: [Betray Marazhai] "Hey, xenos! Collect your rubbish, I have no use for it."

026d7986-9f50-4894-bd9d-dc59ea8911fd.Text: "A deal? No, just a token gift will suffice. You did not even have to get your hands dirty with Marazhai."

f37f443e-bb27-4005-a41f-bc6e8ca22fc6.Text: "Consider this, Archon. You may find it useful to have agents of your own among the mon-keigh. There are entire worlds under my command, filled with millions of victims..."

edc65b3c-c36f-4288-8468-34bec8c4e81b.Text: [Lie] "Still smarting from the Arebennian interrupting your trial, Nazrakhei? Are you making the Reaving Tempest do your dirty work and go against the Arebennian's will, even though it was he who helped Marazhai escape Commorragh?"

536ace95-1ff6-4390-8861-58dfdbc49965.Text: "The carnage behind us... The Reaving Tempest are not allies of the Black Heart, but cattle slaughtered to keep Nazrakhei alive!"

cda4491e-066b-4870-8f35-fb81d4860ef5.Text: "So the invitation was a trap after all. By the stars, you Drukhari are so predictable!"

1e506128-7b72-4f25-8090-0f70d508f744.Text: "What about Nocturne of Oblivion? What part did he play during the trial?"

a32299c9-3398-4182-8ab9-bfe28ff1582a.Text: "What are all these Drukhari leaders doing here?"

b8c83a66-3b5a-454b-b217-e2680e844d91.Text: "Marazhai... you knew. There is no way you could not have known."

cec612d4-2247-484e-a726-315b43696600.Text: "The betrayer is betrayed. What pleasing irony!"

8a9173f1-08e7-410c-8553-5422a7580209.Text: {n}The Drukhari look foreign against the background of the gorge, long black figures that stir into motion when you appear. One after the other, the warriors of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest turn, and you can almost physically feel their eyes land on you. It is surprising, but none of them raises their weapon.{/n}

7a84b5d2-c52e-474c-8d9a-b20ab84b3b24.Text: {n}The Drukhari look foreign against the background of the gorge, long black figures that watch you closely and grip their weapons. The warriors of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest are tracking your every move, apparently ready for anything.{/n}

b1e1bfb6-2c1e-4544-b71f-4a53866d54a4.Text: {n}The Drukhari look foreign against the background of the gorge, long black figures that brandish their weapons when you approach. An angry whisper runs through the ranks of the xenos — it seems they can barely restrain themselves from lunging at you.{/n}

09a30207-ac4c-4ca0-ac98-715397dc7f1a.Text: {n}Marazhai answers the unkind rumbling with contemptuous laughter.{/n} "Excellent! I expected nothing less! Do you hear how much anger my mere appearance provokes? Oh, how I will cherish this slaug—"

b3e798bd-93da-46a9-94c9-f87aacc8844c.Text: "The warm welcome of my kin." {n}Marazhai's mouth twists in contempt.{/n} "But I can feel their fear. It is a good si—"

7a1d91f1-7ada-4951-a94d-a518188ff918.Text: {n}Marazhai casts a glance at the xenos and hisses in satisfaction.{/n} "Look, {name}. Can you see their poses? The incline of their heads? And most importantly, they are more numerous than I expected to see after all Commorragh rallied against the Ka—"

518d9040-d319-49a4-a011-32a5000468bc.Text: {n}You know the xenos in the split golden mask. The figure who presided over your fake inquisitorial trial emerges from the haze of anguished memory, shrouded in the parasite-induced gloom.{/n}

676cd9a2-22a2-4a1a-9679-6616adabbde8.Text: "Nazrakhei. Archon of the Black Heart. In the flesh. What a surprise." {n}Marazhai's voice is deliberately calm, but you catch a note of genuine surprise, even amazement. This is the last thing he was expecting.{/n}

c2e53eaa-64f9-45ed-86f5-2f7ff2773628.Text: {n}Kharael fixes you with a stare that holds the promise of pain and torment. Your jeering has obviously struck a nerve.{/n}

5f724ad9-371b-41c5-b53e-a4535aa43889.Text: "You are right, Kabalite. I have heard enough. Seize Aezyrraesh this instant!"

477f2e79-146d-4d36-ab0c-e2cff2bed163.Text: {n}Marazhai shrugs, clearly mimicking the human gesture.{/n} "So neither of us had any doubt about what was going to happen here."

18cefe21-e45f-4b8a-b2ac-4847c9baaf7a.Text: {n}You hear the creaking of gloves as Marazhai's hands clutch his blade grips, a telltale sign that he is not merely annoyed but beside himself with fury.{/n}

8ad72b83-7036-42a0-ac09-ec53b81272ee.Text: {n}Marazhai's face is a complex mask of emotions — rage, astonishment and realisation. He begins to speak, his voice unusually hoarse and quiet, the words meant only for Nazrakhei's ears.{/n} "You... were not planning to overthrow Yremeryss. You did not plan to make me the new Archon of the Reaving Tempest. From the beginning... you only wanted to destroy my Kabal."

f4c7305d-dc53-436d-ad47-3cd9c57c831a.Text: "Kill them! Kill everyone except the whelp, I need him alive!"

830d714d-fc58-48a5-a236-74afd3f0d7bb.Text: "Your mon-keigh {mf|master|mistress} does not even let you speak without permission, whelp?" {n}Nazrakhei's voice drips with venom.{/n} "You are pathetic, Marazhai. Perhaps you should think of your impending doom... as deliverance."

4b0a4f96-23ff-41b8-a92b-dbbd0c1c2004.Text: {n}The Succubus next to Nazrakhei looks at you.{/n} "The Aezyrraesh betrayed and offended their Kabal. One by her weakness and irreverence, the other by his pathetic performance at the Obsidian Court and an alliance with the mon-keigh. To call oneself of the Reaving Tempest these days is to be dishonoured. Its former members may pass into death or into servitude to a different master. Archon Nazrakhei granted his favour to the scum who once served the Aezyrraesh."

7a43a989-9f2d-4641-b244-df8f7fb49e17.Text: {n}The Kabalites of the Reaving Tempest are in no hurry to carry out the will of their new patron. You notice the looks directed at Marazhai — it seems his arrival has made some of the turncoats question their choices.{/n}

74308a63-6c67-41da-b44f-40c8059581b5.Text: {n}The Drukhari hesitates, then exchanges glances with the nearby Kabalites, slowly unsheathes the weapon, and raises it.{/n} "Enough grovelling before the doomed... Better to die free and on my own terms than to remain a dead man's plaything."

b025fffd-f202-442d-952e-efa52803fbe2.Text: {n}A blow aimed between the plates of Marazhai's armour catches him off guard and causes him to lose his balance. In the next instant, Sinisthoria vanishes from her position and reappears next to you, her Wych's blade slicing through the air and cleaving Marazhai's backbone.{/n}

7ae6c38f-4992-4ba8-bbd6-48ae511ce6c4.Text: "The outcome was known long before the story began. One Aezyrraesh brought the wrath of the Black Heart upon her Kabal, the other became the first pillar to fall at my command. And now... the remnants of the Kabalites still loyal to Vect will put an end to the history of the departed Kabal. They brought me to you, and they will drag you back to Commorragh in chains."

2bf58dd3-dc1c-4412-be73-3caed9142130.Text: "Do not think I will let you die easily, my pet." {n}The Succubus grabs the wheezing Marazhai by the hair and roughly pulls his head back.{/n} "We have many, many hours to spend together... perhaps I will not find it in me to part with you, and you will become my favourite sentient lounge chair, Aezyrraesh. Only time will tell."

cf8a7b8f-1ee5-4010-b155-35d253d713fb.Text: {n}Nazrakhei glances at the Wyches dragging Marazhai's body away and turns to you.{/n} "Hmm. Why did you do it, mon-keigh? Do you really think I would stoop to making a deal with your kind?"

dcaf0e84-a1c8-4690-87d2-95278fbf641c.Text: "I was not talking to you, living corpse." {n}The Drukhari's burning gaze is directed past Nazrakhei — at Marazhai.{/n}

54453f70-78d0-4294-ae38-1e814429da2a.Text: "Temper your hubris, mon-keigh. I will not listen to the whimpering of prey!"

a76b2a5f-2c56-41fe-80f8-e5ec916aa18d.Text: {n}Nazrakhei chuckles.{/n} "Fair enough. Very well... here is your reward, mon-keigh. Now get out of here, and wait for another visit. The Black Heart will soon come to exact tribute from your kin, so you had better be ready."

4a22ee9d-033e-4351-b5d0-55e9c4e9f338.Text: {n}Nazrakhei narrows his eyes.{/n} "A servant of the Kabal... perhaps, mon-keigh, perhaps. I will send you an envoy when the time comes. Until then, you had better be ready for the arrival of my raiding parties, if you value your life."

3fb2d98f-1ca4-478d-bcdd-3f488e944ae8.Text: {n}The Archon of the Black Heart makes a dismissive gesture, and the Drukhari melt away among the debris and shadows of the ravine. Xenos engines start roaring in the distance as the black voidships begin their ascent into the sky.{/n}

add8587a-7cd7-4c81-9938-ee9987c07799.Text: {n}Kharael freezes. There is genuine terror in his gaze directed at Marazhai.{/n} "The mad servants of Cegorach... have allied themselves with the Aezyrraesh?" {n}He looks back at his companions, clearly distraught at the mention of the Harlequins.{/n}

98ba6c38-571d-496b-a8b9-14a0ee1cab84.Text: {n}Nazrakhei looks at Kharael.{/n} "That is enough. Your life was spared for a purpose — it is time to fulfil it."

82ecfbea-8686-455b-a467-f41c27a5d0c2.Text: {n}Marazhai grins back.{/n} "Well spotted, {name}. An entire cavalcade... What happened, Nazrakhei? What is the reason for all this attention?"

aa55ca31-0962-4d00-bb03-a2f07d6dc689.Text: {n}Nazrakhei is in no hurry to reply, running a finger along the edge of his blade and gazing intently at Marazhai.{/n} "I have come to teach you a lesson, whelp. To make an example out of you in the presence of the rest of your wretched Kabal, which the Black Heart has graciously accepted into its ranks."

dff9d58b-6a60-442b-b73d-730042490931.Text: "The Reaving Tempest... Such a grand name for a pile of rubbish led by a haughty bitch. The snivelling wretch thought she could bend the laws of Commorragh to extract the Kabal from the protection of the Black Heart. No one rejects our favour without consequence."

04da0679-846a-4de4-80e4-725ab53690f0.Text: {n}Kharael, the Drukhari negotiator, casts a glance at you.{/n} "You don't say?" {n}An unkind smile crosses his face.{/n}

17480fa0-25d8-477a-a5e6-4f9771d4fe59.Text: {n}There is something familiar about Nazrakhei's face and movements... until you understand you have seen the same lurching gestures, the same twitching in Marazhai after he withered and was driven insane by the unceasing whispering of the warp. It seems the Archon has spent too long in realspace.{/n}

d47fa369-808d-4908-a7e6-7ffd53fc2566.Text: {n}You find your attention drawn to Kharael. When he looks at Nazrakhei, there is no reverence or subservience in his gaze, only grim amusement.{/n} "I would argue with that statement, but we are talking too much as it is. What are your orders, Archon?"

7cbf3ac2-618b-462a-a24c-4682867990f8.Text: "I had just begun planning raids on the spire... when who should come to me? You. The Kabal's Dracon, who longed to regain the favour of the Black Heart. You asked for an alliance to bolster the loyalty of the Reaving Tempest. You pledged your allegiance. I confess, for a moment I even entertained the thought of installing you as Archon... but that moment melted away at the thought of tearing the Reaving Tempest apart from the inside without having to lift a finger."

5686c3be-292c-46cf-b447-c0d6c17dae03.Text: {n}Nazrakhei speaks slowly, savouring every word. It is obvious that getting to Marazhai is a long-held ardent desire that has finally been realised.{/n}

81f2ca44-96f7-4c2d-b6ce-36b03b868875.Text: {n}Marazhai blinks in confusion, tilts his head, and lets out an amazed chuckle.{/n} "By the suns' light, you are not wrong! You are withered! What happened, Nazrakhei? Why did the mighty Archon of the Black Heart not remain lurking in the Webway, but instead chose to crawl out into Sai'lanthresh's hunting grounds? Has he been... driven out?"

9f3115ea-0742-4ccc-ad66-06ba24dd5aed.Text: "You were the one to suggest holding a fake trial for Yremeryss. No matter the outcome, you promised to condemn her in the name of the Black Heart, your voice being second only to that of Asdrubael Vect himself. You let me set the stage with my own hands..." {n}Marazhai's voice trembles with admiration and rage.{/n} "And then you delivered the verdict, stripping the Reaving Tempest of its Dracon and showing the others that the Kabal had made a mistake and grown weak."

031ddf5b-14e5-4361-844f-4afda82dd0a2.Text: {n}Nazrakhei gives you an exasperated look but does not deign to reply.{/n}

b7f97463-14cb-46cd-8789-33b7dbb94630.Text: "He does not know, {name}." {n}Marazhai answers you mockingly.{/n} "The great Archon of the Black Heart does not have the slightest idea what the Arebennian was doing at his little trial."

28773a38-3a4e-4f45-97e6-f10973174041.Text: {n}The mask of calm vanishes from Nazrakhei's face, revealing the countenance of a raging maniac.{/n} "Another word, Aezyrraesh, and your future torment will multiply a hund—"

625c3be2-b291-4dc8-8b69-68394cf9ec50.Text: "You forget yourself, whelp." {n}For a brief moment, a spark of rage surfaces from under Nazrakhei's mask of arrogant tranquillity.{/n}

074f822d-02f3-48aa-8252-b5797919d390.Text: "Did you really think we would just bow before the Black Heart, Nazrakhei? The same Kabal that tried to dispose of us?" {n}The Drukhari tilts his head mockingly.{/n} "It was foolish to expect us to grovel before a feeble corpse, crumbling under the burden of years, unable to endure the call of Sai'lanthresh with dignity."

cc679b66-31e4-4e5d-b427-e7e674a5ffec.Text: "Who are you to interrupt me, outcast?" {n}Marazhai hurls each word into the air like a well-calculated blow.{/n} "You, head of the Obsidian Court, are too old and decrepit to risk wasting your life force out in realspace! And yet you are here, Nazrakhei, because of a lowly gladiator from the arena? Or perhaps because of a Kabalite who escaped the Dark City with his life in spite of your sentence, and who thus made a mockery of Asdrubael Vect's Kabal? You have been cast out of Commorragh until you correct your blunder!"

c9fb4306-9b2f-407c-8bae-d8314da54399.Text: "Well, meat?" {n}Marazhai looks around, his lips curving.{/n} "How does it feel to be the attack dogs of an Archon who has fallen out of favour with Vect himself? How long have you all been kept here, huddled together with your crumbling overseer? Do you still believe they will not feed you to Sai'lanthresh when you are no longer needed, most likely alongside Nazrakhei?"

1481fed6-82b8-4cfa-98a7-3867e0ce8204.Text: "You came, you foolish whelp." {n}The mere sound of Nazrakhei's voice gives you an itchy feeling in your head where the brain-eating maggot was once nestled.{/n} "Kharael was not lying when he claimed you would be stupid enough, or brazen enough, to show yourself before the Reaving Tempest again... or rather, before the new ranks of the Black Heart."

ddbe9a62-d758-4b76-bcbc-dca47ecc3868.Text: {n}A wave of voices ripples through the ranks of the Kabalites of the Reaving Tempest. Sinisthoria, who is watching the altercation, grins reflexively, and Nazrakhei freezes like a statue.{/n}

55c20761-b996-43b6-819c-d7f7e902ef3f.Text: {n}Nazrakhei's voice resembles a snake's hiss:{/n} "Vect will not forgive those who dared challenge the Black Heart!"

7635d2aa-1355-4744-b011-55e137de027f.Text: {n}Marazhai laughs mockingly.{/n} "Vect will not care about a massacre with no survivors. Have at them, sisters and brothers!"

922ad71d-b4e4-4ebd-a6a5-9aa3e7ef8cc2.Text: "WHAT?" {n}Nazrakhei seems to be trying to incinerate you with his glare.{/n}

9508f3da-a3f6-4973-9efa-3c879c78035c.Text: {n}Marazhai turns to you, looking even more puzzled than the Archon... but recovers in time to don an arrogant expression.{/n} "How cunning! The rabble can be fed to the angry Harlequins, and you can reap the fruits of their labours..."

30f18fd0-7635-4a00-9a36-dbf426ce7d66.Text: "{name} is right, is {mf|he|she} not?" {n}Marazhai shifts his gaze to Kharael.{/n} "How long have you been trying to convince yourself that handing over your brothers-in-arms to this decrepit wreck is the only way to survive, hmm? Hoping to buy mercy by degrading yourself to a mere plaything? Cowardice and sycophancy are your new names, envoy of the Reaving Tempest!"

7fb9fd5d-312b-4fff-a3bc-04a7e0d03b39.Text: "Enough, mon-keigh. No one here is interested in your pathetic speculations."

d5aa71b0-eaa7-4c50-9be2-744ed5f65951.Text: {n}Kharael's voice is devoid of any emotion.{/n} "The Aezyrraesh have lost the right to be considered the first among us. If the Black Heart wills it, we will destroy those who have dishonoured the Kabal."

ee5e426e-b37a-4e70-a8f4-5501f92e9ac1.Text: "Hmm." {n}Marazhai pierces Kharael with his gaze before shifting it back to Nazrakhei.{/n} "Then why did you serve me so well by bringing my sworn enemy here, Kharael? Both he and the remnants of the Reaving Tempest will be mine..." {n}Marazhai slaps the Soul-Trap hanging from his belt and laughs derisively.{/n} "...and I will forever listen to your agony!"

0871177a-4ed3-44c6-afda-8f4018519ad4.Text: "I..." {n}Kharael is clearly taken aback by this statement. He draws back, glancing at the Kabalites around him.{/n}

5af8ca20-ec1c-4eb9-8519-a6d6b6564d97.Text: {n}Marazhai's gleeful smile provides you with a conclusive answer.{/n}

68f3acb4-e13f-43f6-a5e8-901b02ecc6f6.Text: {n}Marazhai hisses through his teeth.{/n} "Settle down. You were not expected to understand."

fadce2ec-d177-4e5c-85f7-c7e2912b449e.Text: {n}Marazhai casts a glance at you and shrugs in a contrived gesture he has clearly adopted from humans.{/n}

0cfb9c24-36fd-4997-8a2c-af5a360e2179.Text: {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "I have grown tired of all this chatter... but..." {n}He casts a rapturous glance at Nazrakhei and grabs his weapon.{/n} "If I cut out the heart of that decrepit wreck myself, it will have been worth it!"

d87706ad-514f-4825-85ac-ca842ad90a02.Text: "The Archon would hardly deny himself the pleasure of taking part in a raid..."

28486579-c019-4d32-8df2-a535068a1f56.Text: "A raid, mon-keigh. Not a hunt for a single fugitive."

aa762a90-d6b0-428c-a2b2-b923c259f6f0.Text: "You're a bit late. He's playing with someone else these days..."

39a59235-1429-4546-a18b-1bbb0436de57.Text: {n}Yrliet almost recoils under Nazrakhei's gaze, either out of fear or disgust.{/n} "I... remember him. It was to him that I answered in that trial in Commorragh..." {n}She trails off and grimaces in anger.{/n}

8ab4e807-9d18-4ce2-a148-4babb15f3020.Text: {n}Abelard rubs his temple.{/n} "Do I understand correctly that one xenos gang devoured another xenos gang... just to indulge the maniacal whims of one xenos ringleader?"

dd012815-d7fa-49d1-ab1b-a0751a215104.Text: "It baffles me how these enemies of Humanity did not wipe each other out centuries ago..."

56d31c51-d6dd-4327-98f5-3c03ec71c8e5.Text: "Honestly, sometimes I just can't tell if I should be scared of the sheer cheek of our skinny xenos or impressed by it..."

bf97a85e-1827-42f1-848a-7e3bf5ced760.Text: "My rebellious toy." {n}Sinisthoria's voice rings with every imaginable shade of cruelty.{/n} "You did not honestly think your ridiculous escape from the Cult that had graciously given you refuge would be forgiven, did you?"

269e4db9-6ef5-4109-bcd3-3edd86116dc5.Text: "Well, Rogue Trader? Why are we wasting time... when all our targets are out in the open? Give... the order..." {n}Argenta is shaking with the desire to raise her weapon.{/n}

299160d4-d1ec-4cef-a1c7-cd9fb4c67d4a.Text: {n}Yrliet looks as if she intends to say something, but she stops herself in time, hiding a smile.{/n}

3b6196a3-daa4-4c6f-adb1-4601d8ff5cec.Text: "Sinisthoria. The last Succubus from the Cult of the Fatal Thirst that ruled the arena." {n}Marazhai responds without taking his eyes off his kin.{/n} "It was she who suggested I join the Bloodstained Proselytes instead of decorating her chambers with my innards."

0e39afd9-d78b-4925-b39c-9e77ad920783.Text: "You have spoiled your pet, Marazhai. A mon-keigh that dares to speak in the presence of Aeldari... You could have at least sewn its mouth shut so as not to offend your ears with its ceaseless yapping."

49de2f21-f9a1-4115-b2d8-5ac4bc9e1766.Text: "Indeed, Nazrakhei." {n}Marazhai's voice is dull and almost bored.{/n} "What are the Great Archon and his pet Succubus doing here?"

8cfc040f-91c4-44e0-9c01-4af0d29163d2.Text: "I gave them the privilege of joining the Black Heart, the greatest Kabal of glorious Commorragh. But only if they tracked down and brought back the last surviving member of the former Archon's line, the last living Aezyrraesh. Your former warriors have done their part, though not without assistance from the Wyches of the Fatal Thirst. But that is no reason to deny them credit."

ec79520c-2cdd-4784-ace0-0ea4c6ec8412.Text: "And now explain to me what happened, xenos."

eb42e9da-b8b6-489e-8c10-d36040e1f3d6.Text: "Will you leave me now? Just like that?"

d5530839-d7a8-4275-b880-98ec44cc5c5c.Text: "You think Marazhai could return to Commorragh?"

db2322f1-0ca9-45d6-b92b-5b2886931d38.Text: "Does this mean there is no one left to threaten you?"

a01d3835-f0b9-42e9-a742-c24a4c6ea3f8.Text: "The fun is over. It is time to return."

e578fab5-6f9e-46e2-af3d-dffb114413b5.Text: "What of me? I still have need of your aid, Marazhai!"

604e059c-ae04-4435-97c5-63308fdd071b.Text: "You are not going anywhere until the terms of our deal are met!"

e6301d14-31f9-4dbc-92d1-9050d09ac5ca.Text: "We must go. Let us not linger here."

477aa63f-c44b-48d3-86b6-7e4aae8a269e.Text: {n}Marazhai shakes the blood off the blade and turns to the surviving Drukhari. His voice booms like thunder.{/n} "Who else dares to question my right?"

c02232b3-6bd1-46f9-8551-8609eae3b0e3.Text: {n}Marazhai looks around the battlefield.{/n} "Nazrakhei is dead. Sinisthoria is dead. And all those cowards and sycophants are dead, every last one of them!"

edab64a1-5f6e-462f-8a9d-633a655f5ea1.Text: {n}Kharael lowers his head.{/n} "No, Archon Marazhai. The Aezyrraesh family has been chosen to lead the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest."

2045df4c-f563-4e4b-ac78-599912910cd6.Text: {n}Marazhai laughs wickedly.{/n} "Yes, I remember. You still have plenty of enemies in need of my personal attention."

40f2e452-4db6-42d1-8142-a6ad0af31485.Text: {n}Kharael shifts his gaze to Marazhai.{/n} "Archon Yremeryss. Archon Nazrakhei. The Cult of the Fatal Thirst. These are compelling reasons to make any who doubt the Aezyrraesh or wish to hinder this line bite their tongues, lest they become its next victims. Compelling enough to force Commorragh into accepting Archon Marazhai."

7db6ca71-8741-4828-b5be-8083221f1753.Text: "Your Kabal has been crushed and nearly wiped out completely. Commorragh is a death trap for your kin. So tell me, Dark One, are you purposefully luring the fallen Dracon back so you have something to bargain with when the minions of your supreme overlord come for your head?"

d7875c13-57a5-45ca-85cb-f32f159dd37d.Text: "I have no need of spineless, disloyal scum who were tested by circumstance and found wanting. The ones who cast me down I have ground to dust. What is there to regret?" {n}His gaze is directed somewhere else, past you, past the bloody remains beneath your feet, toward something only he can see.{/n} "I will find a purpose for myself. I will find whoever is pursuing me, even if that means tracking them here and not in the Webway."

558d20d0-cb03-4b9b-83c8-7be64c7450d8.Text: {n}Kharael hesitates before muttering a reply, unable to tear his gaze away from the burning eyes of his overlord.{/n} "Your instructions will be carried out to the letter, Archon Marazhai."

701ca7d1-c2b5-4d43-ba7c-961a894fa6b5.Text: "Mandrakes. Nazrakhei's followers. The remains of the Reaving Tempest... No, I am still in danger. But will they risk hunting me, a Drukhari who lives in realspace and has destroyed all of his enemies? I doubt it."

3b375ba6-689a-494c-92ba-58543d9c3bd4.Text: {n}Marazhai turns to Kharael.{/n} "You must act swiftly. Gather the survivors. Go back to Commorragh and find those loyal to the Tempest. Eliminate the traitors and renegades. Find a weak Kabal that can be consumed and start preparations for the raid. When I return... we will strike."

b8230dcb-8f17-43b9-91c4-82275e870978.Text: {n}One by one, the Drukhari silently disappear amidst the devastation and traces of battle. You hear the roar of engines in the distance as the predatory silhouettes of the xenos ships start rising into the sky.{/n}

5ff0d824-3e3c-4458-bae7-a904f352dbfd.Text: {n}Marazhai turns his gaze on you, a satisfied grin adorning his face.{/n} "I have had enough of this rock, {name}. Let us go back to the ship as soon as we collect our trophies. Later... you and I will have a talk."

bacae18c-fba7-4698-91fe-d7fa4bc376bc.Text: {n}Marazhai nods grimly.{/n} "Indeed. And once we are back... you and I will have a talk. But for now... let us collect the trophies."

4e5f2403-c424-46ab-a146-1d56d092a9be.Text: {n}Marazhai chuckles and seizes Kharael by the chin in a fluid motion, the deceptively gentle act causing the white-haired Drukhari to flinch and then go still.{/n} "Patience, my pet. Concentrate on your duties... and I will be back with you before you know it."

2032e1f8-e5f9-44f9-8aa6-68b5ff6b1021.Text: "Fallen, risen..." {n}Kharael shakes his head condescendingly.{/n} "Those who now fear to raise their head against our enemies will follow the Aezyrraesh. And there are many, as many as Yremeryss once had — and her army of lackeys drove out most who wished to overthrow her. We will see who comes for the Reaving Tempest reborn. We will see who comes to die."

20a544d3-ea8c-44a5-827b-a0a5736f664c.Text: "Oh, please let the xenos slink off to his Webway and leave us and our crew in peace..." {n}Abelard's voice rings with disappointment.{/n}

17fbb2cd-7e6f-4e33-a71f-52f1274eda97.Text: {n}Argenta's dark gaze follows the xenos as they leave — you can tell that she cannot bear to let so many enemies of Humanity walk away with their lives.{/n}

1323efa7-a53e-4d76-849b-18ccc503c83c.Text: {n}Kibellah starts frenziedly renewing the marks on her arm. Without looking away from the bloody pattern, she whispers,{/n} "You are my Domin still, but your decision... offends my soul."

e35e3558-8c3c-4830-9917-3ba8cb3c16e6.Text: {n}Kharael looks at you with revulsion, but he notices Marazhai's narrowed eyes and answers:{/n} "The news that the Dracon survived and is in realspace was first brought to me by the old spies aboard your vessel. Nazrakhei was beside himself hoping to find the one who had turned him into the laughingstock of Commorragh first by escaping from the arena, then by fleeing the Dark City, and finally by surviving the Mandrakes' wrath. When the Archon found me, he demanded I bring him to Marazhai."

0d5acc94-9c5b-45ff-b4e4-2250b4fb6378.Text: "He must have decided that I would repeat Marazhai's same mistake and trust him. I did not, and besides, grovelling before an Archon that has fallen into disfavour is even more dangerous than resurrecting a fallen Kabal. Pretending that I was carrying out Nazrakhei's orders was easy, he became noticeably more stupid after his time in realspace. Conspiring with Marazhai via one of the unseen servants on your ship was more challenging... but not impossible."

bc77bed6-57b0-4b93-a4f1-8fef6ca1eded.Text: "{name}... you do realise, listening to this xenos's revelations, that your crew and ship are in for a long — very long — investigation and purge..."

273f9a6d-b262-4bc2-92a8-0b4fa0fe845a.Text: {n}Marazhai narrows his eyes.{/n} "Do not play coy, mon-keigh. It will happen, {name}. One day." {n}He gently caresses your face with his fingers clad in his clawed metal glove, smiling.{/n} "But not just yet."

e221e7ab-a4ea-4af5-b67e-ba0290e94d26.Text: {n}Kharael hisses furiously.{/n} "What? You are not coming with us? You are going to stay with..." {n}He shoots you a look that is part disgust and part anger.{/n}

9191ef61-9789-44f4-8205-0f4470f06d04.Text: {n}Marazhai narrows his eyes.{/n} "Be quiet, or I will make you so. Are you starting off your service to the new Archon by challenging his decisions?"

f78a398b-ac16-4e59-a10b-7e15f89809b3.Text: "Would you mind telling me why you needed one hundred species of bird and what you used them for?"

6c0a51e5-ab19-4c22-a837-7ecbfc5a848e.Text: "You have been wilfully changing entries in the ship's logbook and forbidding officers from reporting it to Abelard."

8d8217c6-c959-4a7b-ab35-59845fc5b30c.Text: "You must have had quite the falling-out with Jae if she is threatening to kill you."

81e55051-c2b5-40b8-8d73-a36d513d348d.Text: "The officers are reluctant to be quartered next to your chambers because of the constant emotional outbursts it causes them. Some even maim themselves and others."

67a80cf5-d6da-4e26-9e9b-7d43d3ab48df.Text: "Your interpretation of this classical text is not entirely correct. If the subjects have grown accustomed to the ruling house, all the sovereign must do is refrain from breaching longstanding traditions. Adjust unwanted laws as gradually as you would shift the bed of a flooded river, and no one will ever take your power from you."

078cac66-c34f-4110-8ded-2cd7a9b39ae6.Text: "On the contrary, the loyalty of subjects can be bought at a pittance — lower a tax, throw them a festival, or feed the needy — a gracious gesture once every cycle will exalt you in the eyes of the rabble as if it were His own blessing."

4aa7ede8-9338-40c8-b62f-cf1ce204f991.Text: "This inner turmoil is clouding your mind. My protectorate, my subjects, my title are mere resources that I am using solely for my own ends."

825583d9-466d-4bd6-8d04-0c020485ec32.Text: "It is my duty whether I like it or not."

234755bd-ee0a-40eb-9aa2-3576c61226d5.Text: "Enough talk, Lady Cassia! You have pushed me to my limit. Dismissed."

d00a4faa-54ca-4fb3-a25b-71e8d937a37c.Text: "I am not afraid of acquiring a reputation for ruthlessness. I would rather crush a rebellion than condone one — is that not the greater mercy, in the end?"

748a6c7e-1171-4f4a-b19f-a66682e54adb.Text: "I will exercise restraint and lenience in my actions. Excessive suspicion and mistrust harden the hearts of the people and turn them against each other."

c81f7cd1-54bb-42a2-8756-52491bf19cee.Text: "Oh, it has always been my opinion that subjects expect two things from their sovereign — to abuse power and to bless their babies. Succeed at both, and boring essays become unnecessary."

83646e25-88d2-4586-9a78-77a68d8fc59d.Text: "I beg your pardon, Oystach who? Is reading your only pastime?"

90aa3662-4d9d-4880-957c-b3e9796b75c9.Text: "I am afraid I do not have an answer — I am not familiar with the works of this... scholar."

feff6078-2a88-42fc-a1fd-d5ac45b2154b.Text: "You have done terrible things, but I would not presume to lecture a person of noble blood."

42771206-d91b-4624-be87-2f6472bb4b9a.Text: "Woes dog your steps, but we will find a way to defeat them. I promise."

d8385b26-7261-4850-99d8-3746a9000f1d.Text: "It is not always easy, but I try to lead the dynasty toward prosperity by worthy means."

d3a3062f-87d2-49ea-9fcb-38ca6be7d560.Text: "I never promised I would give you an answer. Let's end it at that."

16a23d39-7c43-401c-b3c0-ac54784145a4.Text: "The messenger you rebuked butchered his own family and then killed himself."

c1b2d897-8aa8-420b-99fb-2dc9e4195d2e.Text: "During the warp voyage you gave the wrong orders, which led to the vessel shifting off course and the service bay being destroyed."

4e0939c5-6023-4db3-a700-9a0fec9df323.Text: "My crew has good reason to fear you — you truly are a monster. From now on I forbid you to leave your chambers unless absolutely necessary."

2aa00ccf-fe56-4a1e-991d-54a452c49e3f.Text: "You have a kind soul but have difficulty reaching out to people. I could teach you the art of communication, if you like."

44abb233-2026-475a-bfb8-7c953bcedf65.Text: "Everyone who has dared to slander you will be punished. There is nothing reprehensible about your actions."

20daafbb-2cc0-45d6-9699-efb9b53aed16.Text: "Forgive my temerity, Lady Cassia. I was looking into your eyes and completely forgot your question."

75f6d81b-14d8-4207-a9e8-16b95ba11a13.Text: "One must be a tyrant, a friend, and a jester to one's subjects. What matters is that to clearly discern which role is required at a given moment."

734fae5e-6015-449c-a198-1b5ac6c8ccfc.Text: "What is it you wanted to talk about, Lord Captain? I have nothing to say to your unfounded accusations about my conflicts with the crew — I cannot recall my having a single quarrel with any of your people during my entire time aboard!"

12b557b8-051f-44e5-b646-4b11813ac9c1.Text: "Admittedly, I am at a loss myself. The day we arrived on {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g} I sent a request to the ship's quartermaster and asked him to get me a songbird. But he never asked for clarification, and shortly before we left I had a countless number of cages delivered to me, all wrapped in bright red panic with flickering tints of fear. There was a bird in every one!"

8f6a818a-98c2-444a-a317-f727766ab176.Text: "I haven't rebuked a single errand boy on this ship." {n}Cassia ponders this for a moment.{/n} "Ah, I think I remember! A kind young man with a shy smile and skilful fingers with too much rotten ochre on his shoulders. I grew tired of the disgusting colour and advised him to lighten his burden by casting the weight off his shoulders. He did not come the next day. Or ever again."

df3bbdd0-600b-45f9-89be-1f4d78f7bbbd.Text: "I beg to differ! I read numerous books on Astra Nataris and can swear on House Orsellio's honour that your officers are entering data in complete contravention of regulation! False terms, random distances between lines, spelling mistakes in even the simplest of words. I have spent the last few cycles correcting the latest log entries, and I thought it would please Master Abelard, as he is so fond of order."

5991aa02-8d28-42d6-84ba-d818a9552c54.Text: {n}Cassia's ruby eyes become round and an unbidden flush suffuses her pale face with a rosy tint.{/n} "We didn't... I didn't... That is our private business — the issue was between me and Lady Jae. Lord Captain, please pay it no heed. We made our peace long ago. And I will have you know — no one threatened me. Your information is incorrect."

1f7ef019-e52d-4f36-9d07-d4eb4a489c42.Text: "Very well. Since we are done with this... misunderstanding, I would like to change the subject. It would only be fair for me to ask you a few questions now, wouldn't it?" {n}Cassia hesitates and continues in a less confident tone.{/n} "Do not mistake me, I am not going to accuse you of anything! It's just that... you are the most worthy interlocutor on the entire ship. And you are always so busy..."

8b86bee4-220c-4aae-ab0b-a34e1393f975.Text: "You are sending me away? Now?" {n}Cassia's look makes you wince as though you've just tasted sour citrus.{/n} "Although... Never mind. I dare not take up any more of your time, Lord Captain."

6cbc114e-dc57-40d9-bb99-8320c08580bb.Text: "I admit I was afraid we were too different. And yet... You helped me realise that I can be candid with you."

8a1b5928-72e2-4006-9b7d-b0fa4094d572.Text: "Thank you for the conversation, Lord Captain. It was... fascinating."

0cd96257-e8a4-4bf6-9508-136cc2d8103b.Text: "There is so much power in your words — power that makes me want to join you. I understand now why your subjects are eager to follow you."

f1f191c8-3615-47a8-a4d6-896600822068.Text: "I must confess that sometimes I can hardly bear the burden the House has placed upon me. I feel I am not doing my best... Tell me how you, heir to a protectorate, can bear the responsibility for billions of lives day after day and not stoop under all the weight?"

96b2e220-001a-450b-8a0e-626e656254b1.Text: {n}Cassia cannot help but smile a little.{/n} "Please don't, Lord Captain. I was expecting a serious conversation, but you are joking. I hope you will give a proper answer to my second question."

f333a2b5-25d0-4a5b-8c46-ff6252a0fb5a.Text: "Thank you for your patience, {name}. You are helping me to see the world in different colours... a novel experience for me. Our conversations hold a special place in my heart. Allow me to bid you farewell for now. I am heading back to my chambers to consider today's conversation."

5ef18b3e-0a54-4c18-8eac-c39fc38d854b.Text: "And yet the Seneschal did not appreciate my efforts and for some reason called them an outrage. Even though mere days before he had been swaddling me in warm yellow words — I noticed all your people do this when they are expressing sympathy. I merely wanted to repay the Seneschal with the same courtesy. Perhaps he finds my friendliness off-putting?"

8d8ec663-694b-4d62-a14e-802d9f4c4364.Text: "Will you share your thoughts with me?"

69d6aaa7-aef3-4fdb-9fc5-98c7abe9d597.Text: "According to the twenty tomes penned by the preacher Oystach-Istafan the Forgotten, mercy and cruelty go through the world hand in hand, but people flock only to one pan of the scales. Would you rather inspire fear in your followers, or be magnanimous and choose awe?"

81bc92fa-492e-43e2-812d-4de26acd77ce.Text: "You... are saying strange things. I do not understand how you can even... A jester? Stuff and nonsense!"

b80a38e0-5cd1-4aab-a4cc-2754c1b02fb0.Text: "My ey—" {n}Cassia's cheeks flush.{/n} "Lord Captain, we do not know each other well enough for such talk. I forgive you... this time. Please try to listen to my second question."

eaed651c-4a08-45c0-a43a-6ef27ae94e59.Text: {n}Cassia thinks for a moment and then smiles.{/n} "Indeed. I was not wrong about your merits, or your ability to hold a conversation. I hope my second question does not confound you either."

bc629e8c-429e-4db0-be8d-a1ce8b52e444.Text: "Perhaps I was mistaken about the vastness of your knowledge. I hope you will be able to answer my other question with more grace."

f51222d7-31fb-48e3-987f-62f25f577d95.Text: "We may not think alike, and I do not always understand your motives, and yet... May I be candid with you?"

e76ce4d6-e734-4029-bd90-013ad79a9c9a.Text: {n}Cassia shakes her head in disapproval.{/n} I was expecting a serious conversation, but you are laughing in my face? I do hope you will give a proper answer to my second question."

7e20380b-0ff7-4b32-baa5-bc975d1076af.Text: {n}Cassia regards you with an icy glare.{/n} "I also enjoy art. Painting. Singing. Writing poetry. But I fear those subjects would equally alien to you."

30da7e20-28dd-417a-87f4-bc42fb9ea8cd.Text: "You may be right..." {n}It seems that Cassia did not appreciate your words.{/n}

0f5bd5f8-58ed-46a4-8720-4e527a90d06a.Text: "Your kindness knows no bounds, {name}." {n}Cassia lowers her silver eyelashes.{/n} "I will endeavour not to cause you any more trouble..."

f825fdde-29f9-41ff-b805-98e5f1b0068c.Text: "Lord... Lord Captain! I presume that you haven't yet read the book that I recommended to you. Or perhaps you already have and are simply ridiculing me?" {n}Your heart grows hotter in your chest, you lose your breath, and warmth rushes to your cheeks. Cassia, her face flush with colour, cannot bring herself to raise her snow-white eyelashes.{/n} "Just this once, I shall forgive you your... absent-mindedness. Please do try to concentrate when I ask you this next question."

00f42fab-4b24-43a8-9392-2daa8ae4b25d.Text: "I already told you I cannot control my abilities! What else do you want from me? Will I be assigned a Pariah chaperone? Or will you put me in suppressing shackles?"

fc37eca9-2bae-43c0-a461-4aa41df2dcd0.Text: "That... would be wonderful! My education on Eurac V was cut short, but I had realised by then that the wisdom of books is a poor substitute for the wisdom of experience."

79c58b92-647a-4d9e-9f7d-6c83d4169906.Text: {n}Cassia purses her lips.{/n} "So this is what you've decided."

9cdd5aee-344f-45ff-b752-b83ab7aaad53.Text: "I saw something in the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g}. Something... vast. Predatory. Shimmering with indescribable colours. It came from nowhere and stared at the ship with hundreds of hungry eyes, right there in our path. I decided to change the course while it was still possible but did not want to sow panic. Would it have been better to tell the crew we were heading straight into a monster's gaping maw?"

fd08735e-1548-4ff1-89bb-1a34308a1634.Text: "Thank you, Lord Captain. I hope your people won't soon forget the coming lesson in humility — their stinging backs will help to remind them."

40423eaa-e2a3-4515-8ccf-f1b34a012d02.Text: "I read a treatise by Paisius de Mobbius very recently, who claimed that subjects would never believe their new ruler was better than the old one unless the old one had been a tyrant. No matter the circumstances, the lowborn rabble become deluded about their prospects and rebel in favour of their base desires. What do you make of that?"

a1a1a525-6ee1-48a1-b100-c2d50334a40f.Text: "This lack of manners is unbecoming of a Rogue Trader. And yet you are the master of this ship, and I am but a humble guest who abides by your rules."

6c5743f9-1871-433b-b931-cb74d77c3bc0.Text: "I was so excited, I thought I would have a hundred friends instead of just one! They were squeaking so piteously I let the poor things out. I even fed them my breakfast and dinner... But the stupid birds would not stop chittering even after bedtime! They were dashing about the room, smacking me in the face with their wings... and defecating! I became angry, and suddenly they started pecking at each other's eyes and attacking me! Then I became afraid — and they fell over dead... I do not think I want to keep pets anymore."

b1c9a12d-e25e-496e-bd9f-5720538ad069.Text: "In accordance with your current contract, you will serve as Navigator Primaris on this vessel for another 600 turns."

1d9d2abd-1585-46ef-ba30-a8593d1b1b5c.Text: "I would be honoured to do the Lady Navigator a favour. The Astropathic Choir will contact Regent Aaronto and arrange a formal reception on the capital world of Dargonus."

35f2bc22-87d0-4832-ba42-cec0c1724dff.Text: "Don't even think about it. A Navis Nobilite House can take care of itself without you. Your place is aboard my ship."

dc8f3b07-71e0-4c44-82a0-f606f8f39696.Text: "I apologise for the sudden request for an audience, Rogue Trader. {name}. We need to discuss the future of our rela— our cooperation."

eff5a057-c552-4ed4-bb2b-d460b505e70e.Text: "Your words are oozing with virid green, Rogue Trader. They are choking people like a leash wrapped around their necks. But if you wish to make prisoners instead of allies, I have no choice but to become one of them."

3dee96f3-ca0c-4b6f-9d6b-8035a6a2e3a6.Text: "I cannot wait that long!" {n}Cassia's usually quiet voice rises, sending a wave of heat toward you — and you instinctively clench your teeth, reflecting her anger.{/n} "The regent must be told that I am alive. The House must be told I am alive! Or the Orsellio dynasty will tear itself apart from the inside. I am begging you, Rogue Trader. Aid me. I am sure Regent Aaronto will reward you most generously."

12c7fb31-3687-4659-8eb6-33c94b92ef09.Text: "The events on Eurac V destroyed the world I knew. Words cannot describe the depth of my gratitude for rescuing me. But I dare not impose upon your goodwill any longer — and therefore I am asking for a favour. Help me contact Regent Aaronto. I wish to return to the fold of House Orsellio as soon as possible so that I can complete my education. The first thing I need to do is... Well, a meeting with House Orsellio will be enough."

abf55715-777e-45e3-8552-3ce7a4b6d725.Text: "You cannot imagine how badly I wanted to hear these words. Rogue Trader, you have my gratitude. I will continue to honour our agreements until we arrive on Dargonus."

f0f209fc-8b45-4183-8cfa-42bc5bb4362e.Text: "They are madmen who seek to destroy the centuries-old traditions of our great House, so carefully nurtured by the previous {g|Encyclopedia:Novator}Novator{/g} Tisiphone Orsellio. They deem the century of her rule a tyranny, and our most sacred relic a curse that must be destroyed. Fools! If the Atlas were to be destroyed, the whole of House Orsellio would follow it into oblivion!"

8425ae0d-a8fc-40f4-a42f-4d899cfe37dd.Text: "They dread its power, for only a {g|Encyclopedia:Novator}Novator{/g} can fully grasp the mysteries and harness the power of the Starway Atlas! What the renegades call a leash, we call a guiding star."

b9ab395f-b678-4a11-be51-2352ae1b447c.Text: "Everyone in the House knows the child is the keeper of the one true Starway Atlas, which once belonged to our great {g|Encyclopedia:Novator}Novator{/g} Tisiphone Orsellio. The ungrateful wretches secretly hated Her Grace, and when... Tisiphone abdicated her responsibilities and set off for parts unknown, they staged a revolt to destroy her successor."

e16a6ff3-e554-4828-8c92-9ab45d39e2c1.Text: "We believe it with all our heart! The Novator spent many cycles on the world where the child was born. It is said that everyone who witnessed the miracle of her birth simultaneously departed for a destination known only to the {g|Encyclopedia:Novator}Novator{/g}. Tisiphone gave the order and followed them soon after, leaving her precious gift, the Atlas, to Cassia and therefore marking her as her successor."

b3cf20c2-81f5-46b9-8590-5941e9927cd3.Text: {n}The regent stays silent and then replies.{/n} "To call your statement false would be a lie. For many years, we managed to maintain the fragile balance within our House, but then... The {g|Encyclopedia:Novator}Novator{/g}'s departure shook the faith of many."

a185a2ce-b38a-4b92-91a6-7e44e09ae081.Text: "The treasury is empty, the Navigators are scattered, the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} routes are scrambled, and many of our allies cannot be reached. Which is why it is so important to complete the child's education — it is Cassia's duty to take Tisiphone's place and lead the House to prosperity. Such is her great destiny!"

7185e77a-97bb-466b-8aec-cf571484b8f5.Text: "A special gift for a special child. She was born with it and grew up under its influence. The instability... sometimes hampered her education, but we learned to prevent most outbursts. As long as the child remains calm and remains in seclusion, the powers cannot take hold of her mind."

1857b84e-02f6-4a78-9173-69e3a1234cd0.Text: "As long as the Lady Navigator remains under my protection, I will speak on her behalf."

bf736cc9-5ac2-4d3d-bdba-06aff4abc52f.Text: "I would like to discuss the Lady Navigator's future now."

0e34560d-6399-431a-86ea-2a374943947f.Text: "I dare not refuse the will of House Orsellio's regent."

d371f040-99d2-4478-98a2-c9e4013cbcdb.Text: "Cassia, I would be honoured if you decided to stay."

7d3fa69f-a6a6-426a-8d6d-84452ca11d3f.Text: "Lady Elina, what do you have to say in your defence?"

3abfcb61-32c0-41ac-bc41-be493bfa3130.Text: "I would like to speak to the regent again."

1491c44b-ad46-4c65-9dc0-ced9eb41d05a.Text: "Lady Elina and her men are free to depart Dargonus as they wish."

ee974426-3a80-45c5-904e-43ca3c689ac5.Text: "The station was caught in an internal war between your Navigators, but that's not all. They attacked me and my companions!"

64cc4f31-7087-4e80-a760-cd11322d2bf8.Text: "The renegades among your people seized control of the station and tried to kill the Lady Navigator. They didn't get away with it."

9bd1dea8-6806-4822-aaa0-18333b0042bb.Text: "The station was full of madmen. I butchered everyone who dared threaten my life."

7e0f8f8e-4e97-43e6-962e-295f0bddd176.Text: "I hereby dismiss all charges against Lady Elina-Hatteria."

d202d9b9-e991-4e10-949d-db1e68a00418.Text: "I hereby proclaim Regent Aaronto Orsellio guilty of what happened."

daa75cdc-66c2-4101-8f59-82e127501ac2.Text: "I no longer wish to do business with House Orsellio. Take Cassia and get off my world."

8f6e8a2a-363b-4793-93fc-476673fb841c.Text: "I accept Lady Cassia's offer — we will sign the contract and the Navigators will be free to leave Dargonus."

04db45c1-c910-4013-a4bd-89ca50ed8c03.Text: "I accept Lady Cassia's offer — the instigator of the attack will be executed, and House Orsellio will pay compensation to the von Valancius dynasty."

42c36796-fe94-478e-9dea-094554217eb3.Text: "I wish to help House Orsellio solve their current problems."

d2be9b54-c85a-41ab-8354-0941cec932ad.Text: "Lady Cassia, you too are an injured party in this. What would you do in my place?"

5e41c49b-8070-4145-ba96-99b50000282a.Text: "I will accept the compensation you have offered."

015ac69e-5c3c-4ec7-8bb3-5046fc1bf501.Text: "I am ready to deliver my judgement."

7b1369b0-2cef-4805-852d-b969858f818e.Text: "However, I still hold House Orsellio and you, Regent, personally responsible."

a31c61aa-9705-4427-855c-16f073d761df.Text: "I find both sides of House Orsellio guilty and hereby sentence you to death."

a63ce6db-7da5-44ba-83ea-d750a4b7ecd5.Text: "I will personally decide when the Lady Navigator leaves my crew. If you object, we can settle the matter with a duel."

17f3b40f-e8fe-415a-9e5f-db85fbd03e20.Text: "I will personally decide when the Lady Navigator leaves my crew. If you object, we can settle the dispute with a duel."

efb533cb-8aec-4f37-97c5-8bb6e5e3de07.Text: "Cassia has no need of your tutelage. As the future Novator, she will handle the issues her House is facing on her own."

3fe3b5be-9f0b-4dc1-9d19-38aa4ed00f35.Text: "Allow me to decline the compensation. House Orsellio needs its resources now more than ever."

a5504d94-d429-4d89-8fa7-c35597434934.Text: "Is this not what your years of training were preparing you for? Now is the time to make your own decisions."

ffcaa0e4-b124-4fb7-a71e-a1b9482c2dac.Text: "Of course, you cannot do it alone. But if you listen to my instructions, everything will be fine."

96f35d09-521e-41f2-ae89-5beaf1ee2002.Text: "Lady Elina will be publicly executed — I will personally carry out the sentence."

68d0653b-9a53-4d3b-b26a-ee0717237663.Text: "What are you going to do to Lady Elina?"

fbc2072b-70f4-44a2-81ed-c1fb1f71d73d.Text: "Thank you for your input, Lady Cassia. I will consider whether I should accept your offer."

624831fe-a419-4c0b-94af-93280f6e98f2.Text: "What about an exchange of culture and technology?"

2550e28e-220e-4594-a20c-5e9c15c981c1.Text: "Henceforth, representatives of House Orsellio are forbidden to navigate ships within the limits of the von Valancius protectorate."

0e99af9b-45a1-4a41-a27c-616295b7162d.Text: "Share information about the influential persons your House is working with, and I will turn a blind eye to what happened."

2e37605d-a26f-456d-aae7-c24b69ae66e3.Text: "I hereby sentence your delegation to death — let this be a lesson to all in House Orsellio."

26fac0ae-84f1-4980-968b-e49e6a2061ce.Text: "Be that as it may, you are responsible for the actions of your people. Give me one good reason not to execute you on the spot."

750218bc-a96e-4a7d-ad79-6d7821a2d5d5.Text: "You stood aside as your people — these so-called renegades — attacked! How is that not treason?"

9eca6ca5-ebef-48fe-83db-e9988919a16e.Text: "I hereby dismiss all charges against Regent Aaronto."

8d3ae10b-db40-4f68-827e-cda1f13b22cf.Text: "I find Lady Elina-Hatteria guilty of the attempted murder of Lady Cassia and the attack on the Rogue Trader."

5d1e8902-457f-4ea1-bee1-f1844cdc257f.Text: "Lady Cassia, I ask you to do your duty as the custodian of the Atlas of House Orsellio."

6221a7c4-3519-4eea-bea8-3bf5559029e4.Text: "I sentence Lady Elina to two thousand years' imprisonment in the dungeon of the von Valancius dynasty."

a9689c49-41b8-4f66-945c-1ad0ccb94620.Text: "Lady Elina will be the first Navigator to be transformed into a servitor."

0ee38702-8f18-4ca6-86fa-a678e03fcedf.Text: "I understand Tisiphone's transgressions. But what does any of that have to do with Lady Cassia?"

1250a743-a2a9-4733-8c7a-84bf9825cd89.Text: "What else is Tisiphone Orsellio guilty of?"

d8398a0a-e203-45c0-a1e0-c16e97f4cfca.Text: "Your people attacked me in my home. Give me one good reason not to execute you on the spot."

58a0bf04-ee99-4483-b702-a9026421e4f3.Text: "Why didn't you attack before? Why now?"

f3e7bb9a-49af-4b95-9566-4e281633c170.Text: "So you admit Regent Aaronto was not aware of the assassination attempt?

630c1634-7000-4be6-ac30-53c3076c9ce9.Text: "You called Cassia a monster because of Tisiphone's Atlas?"

27a982c6-92d0-4f09-989c-43593b236ef6.Text: "House Orsellio must be purged. I am surrendering Cassia to Lady Elina's custody."

24c888ec-3d7a-464b-b13d-32de78e0475f.Text: "I will help Lady Elina to fight the tyranny of House Orsellio, but Cassia will live."

4ed3012d-a31e-4c08-accf-af8ae81e9704.Text: "You are sorely mistaken if you think you're getting away with only compensation."

ee17beb6-bdd3-4372-87b2-c68dc13259a2.Text: [Execute them] "Enough! I have no desire to listen to anyone. The punishment will befall each member of House Orsellio here and now."

8a2457cd-b9f7-461f-b951-e672e6949f70.Text: "I am not interested in your pathetic excuses. Wardens! Get the House Orsellio delegation out of my palace and off my world!"

459ef43f-8e16-426e-8d4e-d5b9eeef7c3d.Text: "Who said Cassia is coming with you?"

79a546f1-8320-446e-b25b-49ff86e4f9a5.Text: "Lady Elina will make a remarkable servo-skull."

a8236605-df25-4ace-9bf1-6b1d850802d1.Text: "I could forget about what happened if House Orsellio publicly proclaimed an alliance between our dynasties."

bbf1e13b-2e16-45f9-afb8-36625a6819cc.Text: "You were given a chance to resolve the issue amicably, Regent."

1dc14864-c609-4fc4-8c67-40dda76419be.Text: "I wish to help House Orsellio solve their problems."

56e62517-c1e1-4ced-bf87-7c07b40fa4c8.Text: "I knew this would be the best you could do."

36810865-7fbd-4e4e-ab66-abb6ec24550b.Text: "Lady Cassia, who told you that you were needed aboard my ship?"

839aacc0-90e9-4e23-b99c-b6c62a077f53.Text: "Regent Aaronto, representatives of your House made an attempt on Lady Cassia's life and attacked a Rogue Trader."

d3e250f5-429b-44f9-92ea-7a3c00f4b392.Text: "Let us sign a treaty of friendship and alliance between our dynasties."

9b526b4b-6ccb-4fe5-b937-9c298325c5fa.Text: "I do not care for your pitiful compensation! House Orsellio will pay for this insolence in blood!"

6b8d2936-67f3-4835-ace5-0830b29d8a64.Text: "Come now, Regent. You proved your innocence."

edc9fd0e-7354-444a-b27a-aa59ae56a150.Text: "How do I know your words are not just another trap?"

1e220ec7-8105-4c8f-be45-66a608388470.Text: "I believe you, Regent Aaronto. And yet this is now the second attempt that has been made on Cassia's life. I need answers."

cbdca80a-6fcc-4307-8d9b-98035ce031d7.Text: "Why do the renegades seek to destroy the House's relic?"

fb2c0327-090b-48e6-9cba-05da8a08ae3c.Text: "Why are people trying to kill Lady Cassia?"

ae925e87-d7dd-499b-88f6-8e30a985958b.Text: "It looks like House Orsellio has fallen on hard times."

2d44e924-13b2-429b-94ae-9152da4fa6d7.Text: "What do you know about Cassia's unbridled power?"

0cb14272-c540-46da-96f5-ad4e758db409.Text: "Rogue Trader, I... will occasionally permit myself to reminisce about our voyages shrouded in azure mists and pink sparkles. Farewell."

b8d402e6-b1d3-4dbb-9663-9fab4423a3ef.Text: "I feared this moment would never come. Farewell, Rogue Trader. I will never forget the {mf|man|woman} so tightly clad in steel and silver."

6114a06e-691b-402b-86bc-0283fe7d1a6f.Text: "If this is what Rogue Trader wants..." {n}Cassia falters but a moment later squares her shoulders.{/n} "I will gladly resume my duties in House Orsellio. Farewell, {name}."

8df1862c-b53a-4562-acae-5690ab4ec105.Text: "There are traitors in your midst. Would the Lady Navigator not be safer under my protection?"

94de0051-6750-4e14-9cc8-5941b7d8f992.Text: {n}There is a pregnant pause. The regent stares at you as if trying to peer through the skin, muscle, and bone and see the darkest corners of your heart.{/n} "You are not wrong, Rogue Trader. If you are willing to take care of the child while we deal with our... problem — so be it."

e707f588-47eb-40d3-9fd5-87b1d3d0702a.Text: "Though House Orsellio may have suffered the pain of a schism, only we can protect the child from our brethren and lead her along the paths of enlightenment to the {g|Encyclopedia:Novator}Novator{/g}'s throne."

fd0678f5-7873-44f0-bccb-387ac321a14e.Text: "And now we must bid you farewell." {n}Regent Aaronto gives Cassia one final look and then, with a trembling hand, directs the servants to head toward the exit.{/n}

3b9d5193-b121-4344-ac7d-44f4d4443cec.Text: "Under pirate law, Rogue Trader! We thought you a {mf|man|woman} of honour!"

8411e915-fb51-4efc-b349-1b44b92aae02.Text: "I will give my consent if I am furnished with another Navigator. Otherwise, Cassia will remain until her contract expires."

7fcfe8f4-8cda-400c-b500-ad38a58f8818.Text: "Calderon," {n}says the regent, vaguely gesturing at his entourage,{/n} "is henceforth bound to you under a new contract on behalf of House Orsellio."

6c576c56-5415-49bc-9844-f428bf20a5a6.Text: {n}Cassia smiles — you have never seen her so open or so radiant.{/n} "Thank you, {name}... I mean, Rogue Trader."

7383ed00-dd3c-4bd4-a942-50ef188e9f53.Text: {n}A tall, wizened old man proudly stares at you with milky, unblinking eyes. Loose skin sways with his every move, as if the {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}'s flesh has detached from his bones. An unsightly hole mars the regent's face where his nose should be, and the old man's skull is covered with spiky growths.{/n}

5f702773-0483-46ef-8c6f-778a08afaf78.Text: "And yet this is not why we are here. Our Grace is obliged to note how much the Rogue Trader has done for House Orsellio by protecting its beloved child. We waited for many turns to behold her radiant visage." {n}The regent shifts his unblinking gaze to Cassia.{/n} "Come now, child. There is much we need to discuss."

720d6e11-4976-463c-bcbe-c075bc24e62e.Text: "Paranoia was slowly driving Tisiphone insane, and one day she created the Starway Atlas — a relic that is implanted in our bodies at birth. A noose around our necks. Our gift and our damnation. Tisiphone used the Atlas to control us, subdue our will, and mould our thoughts. If anyone put a toe out of line, she killed them with a glance."

dfe83330-1864-4842-aaa7-d5d43410307d.Text: "I..." {n}Cassia steps forward, but then stops and looks at you.{/n}

ec0c72ec-e3fa-4b35-aebe-93799ddd2228.Text: "Unthinkable! It would be a disgrace for House Orsellio! We urge the Rogue Trader to reconsider the sentence — how is this not a grave insult to the {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobilite}Navis Nobilite{/g}?"

42566d1f-dcf4-4b09-9fa5-090901ac1646.Text: {n}Cassia smiles faintly and addresses the regent:{/n} "Esteemed Regent, it pleases me to see the gleaming sheen of gold and turquoise above your brow. It is thanks to the efforts of the Rogue Trader that I stand here today, and there is so much I want to tell you... But what is it you desire to hear most?"

b4897267-3f7f-4f50-b357-f2ff48f13480.Text: "We know what happened at the station, child. Your connection to the Atlas has grown so strong, we felt the turmoil in your soul — and the events that transpired... have shaken us."

623cd747-533b-4573-a6b7-51a050edd364.Text: "Come, child. The House is awaiting your return."

c4b654ac-0b2f-4981-91e8-28a1a463adca.Text: {n}The regent pensively scratches his scant beard with webbed fingers.{/n} "I suppose we can tolerate that. After all, it was you who rescued the child. If so, tell us — what exactly happened on Eurac V?"

3b8ae556-6fe8-4dc2-b5a3-c7002ce7d223.Text: "Rogue Trader, we are now bound by the terms of the contract. Your representatives may contact House Orsellio at any time, and we will respond. And one more thing... Protect the child like the apple of your eye. Remember that you have the future Novator of a {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobilite}Navis Nobilite{/g} House aboard your vessel."

2b7b8280-279c-4c86-9b61-2f1a31e32b83.Text: "Without the girl? I guess we are alive, which is something. Thank you, Rogue Trader. House Orsellio will not forget your wisdom and generosity."

5e3d4281-6990-4cc9-aab7-65fd5a7d62ca.Text: "It pleases us to know that the enemies' schemes failed to harm relations between our dynasties. But tell us, what future awaits House Orsellio and the von Valancius protectorate?"

e0384374-679a-496f-a27a-b29991994ff5.Text: "House Orsellio is deeply grateful to the Rogue Trader for the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Cassia_HelpedNaviTraditionalists}destruction of the saboteurs{/d}, and we are willing to reciprocate such a magnanimous gesture. We trust that a treaty of friendship and alliance underpinned by the transfer of several artefacts of exceeding rarity will suffice. Now come, child, it is time we depart for your new home so that we may finish what we started."

47b187c0-db88-4341-9962-ffb7b688e584.Text: "The tedium of waiting for this moment, you cannot imagine."

cd8eb0eb-3607-4211-8097-cf2253d006b6.Text: "Esteemed Regent, perhaps I could continue my education while still accompanying the Rogue Trader on {mf|his|her} travels? Just imagine how much I could learn beyond the bounds of..." {n}Cassia notices the regent's furious glare and falls short{/n}.

3c922e00-6387-4671-a8a1-74be8f14e696.Text: "You are correct, it is time for me to do my duty to the House." {n}Cassia gives you an uncertain look, as if seeking your approval.{/n}

d9496862-7893-47af-9e10-d0f041979672.Text: "It is settled, then." {n}Aaronto shifts his unblinking gaze to Cassia.{/n}

160617a6-b1df-49b7-9d44-87e431cf8064.Text: "We are loath to flout the laws of honour, but having you as an adversary is something we would enjoy even less. For the sake of neutrality between our dynasties, we agree to your terms."

c818122f-59dc-4d89-8c58-31841bca5260.Text: "And yet there is still one matter we need to discuss, Rogue Trader. As we said earlier, the child must return to the fold of her House. We hope you will be gracious enough to acquiesce."

9b3cf5fe-2441-4635-b175-ee394e8034d7.Text: "We would be honoured to hear your thoughts on the matter."

1f9cf411-506a-4f12-aea0-93f0ecd1a52e.Text: "Don't you dare! This is my House, my family!"

2ab19f42-6376-47f4-9de2-0f24ad71e65d.Text: "Allow us to offer you compensation worthy of a Rogue Trader, as a gesture of friendship and an apology for any unpleasantness."

4cd8b0b2-d3ba-4ca5-a749-d287ac653e64.Text: "Hide behind us, child, and we will protect the future of our House! Onward, descendants of Orsellio! For the child, for Tisiphone, for our dynasty!"

e19e0445-fc48-40f3-9440-8fe4a438f227.Text: "I think I am ill-prepared to make judgements of this kind..." {n}Cassia lowers her eyelashes and continues in a barely perceptible whisper,{/n} "I am sure the Rogue Trader knows what to do better than I."

38db6263-251c-45c5-adf8-a4d492bed59a.Text: "As for the esteemed regent and his people — I do not think they are guilty of the traitors' trespasses. But they are responsible for bringing them here, and therefore it would be fair to ask House Orsellio for compensation for this negligence."

c397ddf5-e4b0-4c32-85a0-ea6fa094e122.Text: "N-no, I would never... Forgive me, Rogue Trader, but I refuse. I am a Navigator, not an executioner."
