1c580d46-7fbd-4277-b81c-dd96e3a9380b.Text: "There is no need to spill noble blood, Rogue Trader. We are outnumbered and understand our position all too well. We will take our leave of you for now... only for now. But try to hide the child from us in the future, and there will be trouble."

e799cf67-a5c5-4baf-802d-692d99fd5442.Text: "We will not move an inch until the child is returned to the House. To battle!"

13c8d458-451b-40a3-acd9-e42bba1e92bc.Text: {n}Unhurriedly, the regent turns to Cassia and beckons:{/n} "Come, child. The destiny prepared for you by the stars must be fulfilled."

1effe641-d0c1-4a07-a3a1-b5be226a58b2.Text: "May the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}God-Emperor{/g} watch over your protectorate, Rogue Trader. Farewell, for now we take our leave."

bf752fce-9741-4712-966f-9d6dee7463af.Text: "What are you saying, Rogue Trader? How could I—? I have never done anything like that!" {n}Cassia's usually pale face flushes so deeply that even her ears turn red.{/n}

f0f5e2fd-65c3-4792-8f76-584b1f271f6d.Text: "And then another two to get into the regent's good graces and reach Eurac V. Now Cassia is in the spotlight and the House council is about to put her on the throne — surely there is no better time to cut off the serpent's head?"

3e14808d-4530-4015-9651-7da4651db2d9.Text: "I, Elina-Hatteria of House Orsellio, swear to tell the Rogue Trader nothing but the truth, may the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}God-Emperor{/g} be my witness."

8bc2c1e3-c537-4e6c-9ba4-a857a7d75f53.Text: "I implore you... To settle this conflict, I offer the Rogue Trader a hundred-year contract with House Orsellio, committing us to charting the shortest and safest routes for the von Valancius protectorate within the Koronus Expanse. I will also remain aboard the Rogue Trader's vessel and assist {mf|him|her} until {mf|he|she} decides otherwise. Or until duty to the House summons me to the Novator's seat."

e76da514-9616-44c2-8d78-db8dbe735239.Text: "Silence! With all due respect, House Orsellio has hardly covered itself in glory thus far today. It is time its representatives answered before the Rogue Trader."

49cf3fec-0ef1-456a-b137-da7585050c04.Text: {n}The regent nods curtly.{/n} "We will arrange for the items to be delivered as soon as possible."

4d35a1d5-0daa-4906-8441-1f1d07d0e860.Text: "The esteemed regent will put Lady Elina and her people in one of our family gaols. She is a House Orsellio Navigator, after all. There is no need for our precious blood to be spilt."

87752036-4de3-46ea-ad9a-de701b642156.Text: "Rogue Trader, allow me to ask what fate awaits the esteemed regent and the other members of my House."

f385a591-0e86-46b5-85c9-b6eae1ef8b42.Text: "I... Esteemed Regent, I will be staying with the Rogue Trader. It is time we moved from theory to practice, don't you think?"

cedba873-2fcf-44ab-94af-97257ff2d158.Text: "Your demands are outrageous, but we cannot claim they are ill-founded. We accept your terms, but the treaty of friendship we previously offered is hereby withdrawn."

77efd178-6491-4e36-b348-fed638551a48.Text: "Theodora von Valancius was a very open-minded woman, but sagacious Tisiphone did not support many of her... endeavours. And neither should we. We are afraid House Orsellio will have to refuse the Rogue Trader's offer."

4b3c1d18-3095-4645-88d2-922020bf6c6b.Text: "We fear that honour will not allow us to betray our allies in such a contemptible manner."

77496969-af72-4899-ad2f-453aa92c2c5e.Text: "There can be no doubt the traitors must be executed. All their complaints about Tisiphone's tyranny are merely a cover for their self-interest and their desire to seize power over the House. Did they hate Tisiphone? Perhaps. But I did not wrong them, and neither did your people."

16188841-6852-4264-a228-dd4a1e7bcda2.Text: "As we said earlier, the child must return to the fold of her House. We hope you will be gracious enough to acquiesce."

a7bf8ae9-4390-45cc-851d-19a63496b962.Text: "{g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}," {n}the regent's piercing voice cuts through the silence,{/n} "on behalf of House Orsellio, we would like to express our immense satisfaction at this meeting — and our gratitude for the {d|Encyclopedia:CassiaQ1_GrandWelcome}warm welcome{/d}. It pleases us to know there are still {mf|lords|ladies} in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} who observe etiquette and the traditions of hospitality."

0d8b6924-66d0-4a75-bbbc-d85074ea68e4.Text: "Say your farewells, child. Should you ever see the Rogue Trader again, it will be as the Novator of House Orsellio."

dc136ebe-c4ff-4e74-9f7d-f434fbc0ef5c.Text: "{g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}." {n}The regent's sagging lips twist in a condescending sneer.{/n} "We hope the von Valancius protectorate finds its bearings soon and you astound us with {d|Encyclopedia:CassiaQ1_HumbleWelcome}functions every bit as grand as those of your peers{/d}."

dec20ae8-4990-4315-9486-5acec4abdf03.Text: "If I may speak, so many dirty colours have poured from the mouths of those present that I feel covered in filth from head to toe. I... As the future Novator, I want to bleach them, purify them, and let them go! Heed me — I am the one to blame for what happened today! And I accept full responsibility for the actions of my House." {n}Cassia speaks bravely and openly, though her hands are shaking a little.{/n}

b989973b-36f4-4c17-809b-796787930938.Text: "I... I thought you needed a {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}. If you do not," {n}Cassia says, her face hardening in an instant,{/n} "it will be my pleasure to leave with the esteemed regent."

1b6cfd13-58fa-4cea-9ae1-378e8d16846a.Text: {n}Regent Aaronto remains silent for a long while.{/n} "So be it. We failed to notice that our child had grown up and become strong. You may stay with the Rogue Trader until the House summons you — {mf|his|her} influence is... anomalous, but it has served to bring out blessed Tisiphone's most precious talent — the talent of leadership."

e3cde762-4a5a-4366-be84-8c0c5338fcaa.Text: {n}Lady Elina stares at Cassia incredulously with bulging eyes but remains silent. Her hand restlessly caresses the spot where her Atlas is embedded.{/n}

887e4127-5b48-4c5a-9d51-7068ad201a73.Text: {n}Cassia watches you closely, holding her hands in a gesture of prayer.{/n}

33f16ebc-8be3-4f42-8a3b-822411b246b4.Text: {n}Regent Aaronto nods slowly.{/n} "In that case, House Orsellio is deeply indebted to the Rogue Trader, and we are willing to reciprocate such a magnanimous gesture. We trust that a treaty of friendship and alliance underpinned by the transfer of several artefacts of exceeding rarity will suffice."

f42cbe16-af22-4458-8323-20d4f41d8cdb.Text: "You call this a fair trial? Ridiculous! Everyone here is rotten to the core. All of you are heretics and madmen! Curse you! Curse you!"

8263b2ae-2a8e-42ea-8ece-d7f87f53b566.Text: {n}An unkindly light glints in Cassia's eyes:{/n} "Very well... Considering the circumstances, I will use the power..."

1cdfcfe3-39e4-4523-a480-d45d64669642.Text: "What does this mean, Rogue Trader? Did she not admit her guilt?"

2c9f3790-9c06-4063-9674-946329bdaec3.Text: "Tisiphone always had plenty of opponents, but we were afraid to trust one another — any of us could be spying for her followers. We saved our strength and dealt the first blow five years after the heir was born, striking at one of the estates on Ir-T-Vi. But the girl survived, and Regent Aaronto hid her so far away and guarded so thoroughly it took us another thirteen years to find her."

61646591-4314-4ab5-a052-52fe2bc0755b.Text: {n}Elina watches you with hatred, unable to change her fate in any way.{/n}

70cc777f-ea5c-483a-8265-efd44c9b9cdc.Text: "Tisiphone's madness weakened the dynasty, and not long ago the {g|Encyclopedia:Novator}Novator{/g} vanished — indeed, her loyal followers lie when they say she chose to retire. The truth is that nobody knows the truth. I hope she is rotting away on one of her secret worlds," {n}Elina finishes with a sneer.{/n}

bd014239-4e40-4ab5-a8ae-1037a93d472d.Text: "What an honour. I must give credit where credit is due, at least you bothered to listen to me. Good luck with the monster, Rogue Trader."

03c9ca33-a1ac-433a-b5cc-f00f690ba67e.Text: "Now come, child, it is time we departed for your new home, so that we may finish what we started." {n}He stretches out his withered hand, covered with translucent leathery membranes, toward Cassia.{/n}

4942e7f9-79bb-4d67-bd18-0ffd320b5b5c.Text: "I do not know what it is you wish to learn, but I will start from the very beginning. A long time ago, Tisiphone ascended to the throne of Orsellio — she was a daring Novator who brought part of the House to the Expanse, hoping to strengthen our position in the Imperium. The House prospered but Tisiphone was never satisfied — she went mad in her pursuit of power, seeking more influence, more control, and she saw enemies everywhere, even among her loyal followers."

b473bb56-13fb-4083-ab59-370beda7523e.Text: "At first many branches of House Orsellio tried to resist her tyranny — and Tisiphone cut them down with extreme brutality. For example, the entire Setthala branch was destroyed simply because its leaders asked too many questions about the Atlas and wanted to know the truth about its creation."

d839659e-98af-4e0a-b4e8-cb90dd2bb8a9.Text: "Tisiphone passed her Atlas on to her successor before fleeing the House — to a newborn child! We could not surrender the throne to the tyrant's creature. Tisiphone was cunning and treacherous, she must have hatched the entire plan beforehand — her disappearance, the child, the transfer of the leash. We feared that one day she would be reborn in Cassia's body. And we could not let that happen."

178355c0-e1e8-4683-ad91-ed9f113721f8.Text: {n}Elina clicks her tongue loudly.{/n} "Regent Aaronto is guilty of mass killings, intimidation, inhuman torture, abetting Tisiphone, and raising her heir. His crimes are many, but this one is not among them. I'd love to see his head on the chopping block, but honour prohibits me from slandering him in a trial before the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}."

b603a461-41f2-45c9-bcbf-a03c1771d733.Text: "The Rogue Trader now knows about the regent's atrocities — and the girl's corruption. I hope I succeeded in warning you about the danger that lurks within Cassia Orsellio."

1e44d9d3-8dfc-4657-971e-1ec7baffe44d.Text: "Largely yes, but there is more. Have you never felt pure, unadulterated disgust while standing close to her? Or perhaps fury, or fear? Who but a monster would manipulate the minds and feelings of others? Even more so than Tisiphone herself did?"

7686a542-2abd-4582-b198-cc4c84b11534.Text: "I swore to tell nothing but the truth."

6576869c-0c75-4b66-91f2-d2852b475f03.Text: "Thank you, Rogue Trader. We will contact your representative as soon as we return to the base and discuss what has transpired with the other branches of the House."

71d898c1-e001-47a5-bbeb-7dae38d39d08.Text: {n}The unnaturally bulbous eyes of the {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} constantly shift between you and Cassia. Black secretions run down her cheeks instead of tears, leaving unsightly streaks.{/n}

c7d7e03d-da49-466c-8cf5-fe0767446654.Text: "I... I am not sure my Atlas truly is the one that once belonged to Her Ladyship Tisiphone."

77b5a198-83ba-4ddc-a093-f8a5ac8b0ebb.Text: "House Orsellio is deeply saddened by the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Cassia_KilledBothNavis}passing of Theobald Thrice-Pioneer Orsellio{/d} — and at the hand of the Rogue Trader, no less! It is regrettable that the holder of a sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} chose to deprive the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} of one Navigator's eye." {n}The regent grimaces.{/n} "Now come, child, it is time we departed for your new home, so that we may finish what we started."

8f9b235f-f124-422d-806a-188e607a10c4.Text: {n}Reddish brown splotches cover the regent's face.{/n} "We do not wish to discuss the transgressions of the Rogue Trader — this is not the time or the place. That {name} von Valancius chose to {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Cassia_HelpedNaviRadicals}side with the most despicable renegades{/d} among the {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobilite}Navis Nobilite{/g} and caused the demise of our brother Theobald Thrice-Pioneer... Well, we will overlook that in exchange for your rescue, child. Now come, it is time we departed for your new home, so that we may finish what we started."

bb6835d1-a9b7-4a48-8ccb-f77ff72f987e.Text: "A ridiculous claim! In the heat of battle, your servants would not have paused to consider who was truly to blame! We would have been cut down next to the traitors if we'd so much as reached for our weapons!"

2e43b6be-8a2a-41dd-89d0-c994e7f4bc75.Text: {n}Elina gives a satisfied chuckle.{/n} "At least Felek did one thing right."

f439014a-f140-4221-9cdd-044b558eb75a.Text: "What are you saying, child? Isn't that what we, the Great Regent, have taught you since the very day of your birth?"

e694bd2e-c9ef-4eec-a3e2-d882fc5ecebd.Text: {n}Cassia frowns and touches the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_CassiaAmuletOn}stone{/d} that is heating up under her skin.{/n} "Even if I wanted to carry out the execution personally... The traitor's artefact is limiting my powers."

9316e35a-9695-459a-be8b-5c9053f0e657.Text: "Lord Captain, ending the trial like this goes against every law and custom!"

8e377d3d-6f46-4937-824d-1f2e12ca9cc6.Text: {n}Cassia's expression remains calm, but her lips tremble when she turns around to look at you for the last time.{/n}

cd0b6e34-7498-42de-b729-4ac7bf4a4889.Text: "If you are truly letting me go... There is no need to say it twice. I will no longer cause any trouble. Not to you, at least." {n}Elina glares at Cassia and Aaronto.{/n}

e4734c52-557a-42c2-a574-450fbe3bf6a7.Text: "Hear us, child. This burden is too heavy for you to shoulder alone. You are not yet ready..."

1def1ce0-7a18-4bf3-8301-faa9ab302ecd.Text: "This is unthinkable! We, the Great Regent, were hoping for a fair trial and proper decorum from Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} in accordance with the laws of the Koronus Expanse! Therefore... we are deeply disappointed, Rogue Trader."

bf46ce09-657a-40ea-a83d-4deb509345a5.Text: "Kindly explain what you mean by that!"

a7116b54-e6e6-4447-a92e-8704c7ad8483.Text: {n}The Navigator cocks his head.{/n} "I am afraid we, the Great Regent Aaronto, must respectfully decline your offer. House Orsellio has enough... problems of its own. I am afraid adding allies' troubles would be too great a burden for us at present."

b4876bad-5e78-4464-b2f8-4e537962da37.Text: "Nevertheless, we must remind you that this is a... turbulent time for House Orsellio. We are delighted to be allies of the Rogue Trader, but until our internal and external conflicts are resolved, our capacity for assisting you will be limited."

c1fbe5dc-59ea-4e48-9c03-cfad4ac64786.Text: "As for the treaty of friendship between our dynasties... Our emissary will contact yours and deliver the scrolls for your signature and seal. And may the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} bless this new alliance!"

3741521c-021e-438d-9c10-7557a5bf2b15.Text: {n}Regent Aaronto stares through you unblinkingly as though you have not spoken.{/n}

4a7be69d-b301-4102-b23b-3f59684f05a9.Text: "Keep your mouth shut, Regent. Your House is guilty of attempting to take the life of a Rogue Trader — the accused will speak only when graciously permitted to do so." {n}The Proctor's hand slams into his chest with a thud.{/n} "Let judgement begin."

0969d6fd-c0dc-4d71-be48-d5b66313b60f.Text: "With great pleasure. Our emissary will contact yours and deliver the scrolls for your signature and seal. May the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} bless this new alliance!"

461f5327-e215-4ff3-871d-c99b095a62bb.Text: "Hmmm." {n}The regent's sagging skin quivers when he sighs.{/n} "It would be highly disrespectful of us to refuse the aid of a Rogue Trader. We, Aaronto Orsellio, do hereby accept your offer. If you will allow, we shall discuss the details later."

0d82d892-086f-448c-b392-88803aa4bf71.Text: "Under the Expanse law, the payment for rescuing the Lady Navigator was a contract obliging her to serve on my ship."

96a9f507-0ab8-46ea-aece-41b2642a63ff.Text: "I will dismiss the charges against House Orsellio for what transpired."

0954db81-7c29-45af-88f5-1e4c00d17a50.Text: {n}Lady Elina bursts into hysterical laughter that is now utterly bereft of reason.{/n}

d078a154-915e-4037-a498-f5a8841b4d59.Text: "Come, child. You should not stay where you are not welcome." {n}The regent's eyes move from Cassia to you and he bids you farewell with a curt nod.{/n}

fb2acc3a-d965-4e44-9426-8a07b1c9017c.Text: {n}Air whistles out of the dark holes in the regent's face. His bulging eyes dart furiously between you and Cassia.{/n} "This time we are compelled to agree with you, child. But do not forget your duty — your burden will forever remain with you. We will allow you to gain experience in the company of {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}... for now. We must now take our leave. May the Emperor watch over your path."

939121b5-a56a-4ff9-b8fb-fa8f2cd00a8e.Text: {n}The regent acknowledges your words with a nod and waits for you to continue.{/n}

2c7c1ce0-64dd-4b12-a958-cefa43fbc8f4.Text: "Rogue Trader, House Orsellio humbly asks for your lenience and forgiveness. We could not even imagine these... vile rats could be scurrying among our ranks. As for them sneaking into the Rogue Trader's palace and staging an unthinkable crime... God-Emperor be our witness, the accursed renegades seek to spark a feud between our houses!"

9f54d853-0098-4e74-b8c1-4d184b21c185.Text: "You do not want a war with a {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobilite}Navis Nobilite{/g} House, Rogue Trader. We could achieve much more as allies. House Orsellio is an injured party in this, just as you are. The renegades infiltrated our ranks, weakened us, implicated us before the Rogue Trader, and almost killed the most precious thing we have — our noble child! Do you really think we wished death upon the one who is destined to lead our House to greatness?"

8f6084ae-6428-4670-8053-9b3edb22bd02.Text: "We are ready to tell you everything we know so that this misunderstanding can be remedied as quickly as possible."

b1cf4fe7-11f8-4ff8-8523-36322a7383fd.Text: "Vile wretch! Who do you think you are? Will you now start killing those who have displeased you as Tisiphone did before you?" {n}The fury on Elina's face gives way to desperation once she realises what she just said. She slowly reaches for the Atlas embedded in her chest, looking at Cassia with obvious fear.{/n}

9107f58d-2035-4432-8939-f200334532e9.Text: {n}Aaronto Orsellio stands as tall as his aged, crooked spine will allow and looks at you with a proud unblinking gaze.{/n} "What does this mean for us, Rogue Trader?"

51f47b61-a104-4a04-a122-b7d17a23a834.Text: "You must be insane if you think we will allow this. Close ranks!"

7deb121c-ad50-4e2c-9546-1feab0a8b17d.Text: "I sentence you to death for your crimes against a Rogue Trader and Lady Navigator Cassia. Any last words?"

0c646516-7f66-49e0-9f5e-5ffa7a3f9d1d.Text: "Your fate will be decided during the trial, Lady Elina. I will hear what you wish to tell me."

95b08595-d8c0-4ae9-8669-bb438f54b9ba.Text: "Mercy!" {n}The Lady {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} covers her face with her disfigured scaly hands, each with an extra finger and conjoined phalangeal bones. Her clothes are covered in blood, mostly that of your servants, and several unexploded bolts are sticking out of her chest plate.{/n}

37347213-b0f9-4c1c-a16a-3e51d208b553.Text: "Tisiphone's heir be damned! I know that House Orsellio will cast off the tyrant's shackles someday, though not here and now. Others will come after me — and may our enemies tremble!"

856946b8-50a2-4dec-a480-699bb0ca0bb1.Text: "Thank you for your lenience, Rogue Trader."

b5bfd28a-1bed-49e4-a507-da640584f166.Text: "{g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, whether on purpose or out of ignorance, you are harbouring a monster that is cunningly pretending to be an innocent maid! Spare me, and I, Elina-Hatteria Orsellio, will swear to tell you the whole truth about the madness that is devouring House Orsellio like a malignant tumour. Do not let the regent deceive you with honeyed lies lest the cursed child ruin your protectorate as well!" {n}You see rage and despair in the Lady Navigator's face, but neither is directed at you.{/n}

1bdc8764-89e3-4dca-85cc-fcbddcb29c35.Text: The memory was gone, and {name} once again found {mf|himself|herself} plummeting into the maroon abyss of roiling visions.

33245134-43f4-4ec2-b542-2f2dcfe84570.Text: ...gave the order to shoot at the window, thus drawing Lady Cassia's attention.

2bc9366e-7159-4df1-8a4c-cb91ea0d7001.Text: ...snatched a dagger from the floor and started hacking at the hands reaching from inside the painting.

980ef8a1-ed89-484b-bb5d-4b9823ee6283.Text: ...tried to escape from the Sanctum Navis.

9adb0200-9276-420b-82d9-dc73e1a17aa4.Text: ...followed {mf|his|her} intuition and jabbed the cogita-brush's catheter into {mf|his|her} own vein.

95ab2d78-144f-42ec-b20a-32dd5e53eeba.Text: ...closed {mf|his|her} eyes and remained adrift in the weightlessness.

724d575f-0fb8-4814-8685-3405b48ac631.Text: ...descended into the abyss. Toward the screams.

29023132-ef2b-4ff9-8547-21c07b3333a7.Text: ...urged the Lady Navigator to fight the monster to the bitter end.

4ff534ed-f184-4637-8d0f-2dd4d6d2e438.Text: ...attacked the dead Navigator with {mf|his|her} bare hands.

27ce5e87-862b-4850-bfe3-ccc731ae0386.Text: ...grabbed Lady Navigator's hand to try to pull her back out.

d56f0fe1-c1c2-4043-ab6e-4214053b652a.Text: ...drew closer to look at the figures.

b19ff66f-a321-4bdc-85d7-4923581f9349.Text: ...stabbed Tisiphone Orsellio with the ritual dagger.

33037acd-813d-47da-a6f0-c7628801609e.Text: Cassia took the Rogue Trader's hand and guided {mf|him|her} through the maroon mist and out of the painting. Their unconscious bodies were discovered in the Sanctum Navis 20 Terran days after their disappearance: as soon as the Rogue Trader's voidship had emerged from the warp in an unknown system.

a06952d8-62c7-4454-b7d9-5bbe85021344.Text: When the Lady Navigator opened her eyes, the space around her changed: bright colours drove the mists away and the faintest light somewhere very high above reminded the Rogue Trader of the world {mf|he|she} had left on the other side of the canvas.

8fea2c13-ac36-4f09-ade6-575e133d78f0.Text: The Lady Navigator graced the Lord Captain with a tired smile. The abortive ritual had turned out to be a trap set for Lady Cassia by the previous Novator of her House. But the Rogue Trader had ensured that her plan fell to ruin. And now it was time to desert that accursed place.

76a0edc1-f8b8-4c58-ad6b-f501fb5ad88f.Text:
Tisiphone Orsellio sank her claws into Cassia's drained body, her hand passing right through Cassia's Navigator armour like it was nothing. The entity clutched something inside and let out a deafening, triumphant howl.
Cassia's eyes shot open wide from the pain and she grabbed the hand that was constricting the Atlas within her chest.
"I am so... sick... of submission..."

56382ca9-172f-4379-988c-62c329ade6a0.Text: Tisiphone Orsellio clutched her skull, which had been chipped by Cassia's claws, let out a horrible howl, and flew into the air... but it did not save her from the Lady Navigator's all-seeing gaze.

751e4e02-add1-40bf-9275-06504992f0a8.Text: Servant: "No, please! Not the fingers!" Enforcer: "I'm gonna break one for every word of a lie I hear coming from your mouth. Now talk!" Servant: "P-please, you have to believe me! All we did was prepare the canvas and mix the Lady Navigator's blood into the paints! Then we were told to lock open the shutters so that the Lord Captain could see everything that was going on inside the Sanctum Navis from the observation chambers, and—"

1679bb47-5a22-4c40-aadd-9217b9c5e96c.Text: Enforcer: "I escorted the Lord Captain to the observation chambers and yelled at the servant for leaving the shutters open, but then I was told it was on the Rogue Trader's orders.

397b0688-1e5c-4c80-b157-64e63cec56dc.Text: We could see the Lady Navigator clearly through the armaglass. She was nervous, flicking through some manuscripts over and over. Her anxiety was passed on to the servants, and because of it, they just couldn't do anything right.

c025fc77-1e63-450a-b0a6-e6684596bd37.Text: We could see the Lady Navigator clearly through the armaglass. She was vexed, pacing around the room, overseeing preparation for a ritual of some sort. Even to me, the look in her eyes felt like a lead weight around my neck.

8c174a71-0584-491f-ade8-482a324806cc.Text: We could see the Lady Navigator clearly through the armaglass. She was lost in thought, staring at the canvas in front of her. She looked like she was completely unaware of the world around her.

a7e945c0-714b-4280-a03d-dcec55c2ab34.Text: Soon the servants were ordered to leave the Sanctum Navis, and the Lady Navigator picked up her brush. Entranced, she started dragging it across the canvas, painting one image over another, and another one over the last, and another... And then the Lord Captain noticed it. There was a thing... on the other side... The picture, covered in a layer of fresh blood, was coming to life, but the Lady Navigator was oblivious. That is when the Lord Captain..."

919aaf51-b0af-409a-b295-716fb2b813d7.Text: The ritual dagger of House Orsellio cleaved the billowing shadows, and yet, the painted hand re-formed itself the moment after the blade passed through it. Cassia went limp in the clutches of her horrific creation and was immediately pulled to the other side of the painting. A moment later, {name}, still clutching the dagger, was likewise plunged into the depths of the world the Lady Navigator had created.

fc0b44a6-54c5-42dc-8c82-6508b21efc1d.Text: The Lord Captain's efforts to free the Lady Navigator were to no avail: her body was drowning in the roiling blood on the canvas. And as soon as Cassia's outstretched hand had fully vanished inside the painting, dozens of hands emerged from the canvas, wrapped themselves around the Lord Captain's body, and dragged their second victim into the world of the Lady Navigator's creation.

9031cc49-e194-476d-bd83-3e360057bfae.Text: Ignoring Cassia's pleas for help, the Lord Captain dashed for the exit but immediately slipped on a pool of the Lady Navigator's blood and fell, cutting {mf|his|her} hand on shards of glass. Something dug its claws into the Lord Captain's leg and the creatures from the painting, having already consumed Cassia whole, dragged their second victim into the dark abyss.

a72268c3-ccd5-4ef5-ba9f-135e941a59af.Text: {name} awoke, finding {mf|himself|herself} in the middle of a gigantic, boundless, billowing... nothingness. {mf|His|Her} body felt weightless, floating in a void strewn with hundreds of the Lady Navigator's colours — some of them bright, warm, and alluring... others morose, cold, and heavy.

2d51bd24-f78a-4739-8322-67e1399d99cd.Text: {name} plunged into a river of bright hues, and flashes of rosy sunset and lilac carried {mf|him|her} down the dazzling stream. Before long, the Lord Captain was standing in an idyllic garden permeated with the fragrance of flowers and the singing of birds. Servants in purple livery darted back and forth, attending to a withered old woman in a Navigator's mask. Sitting on her lap and smiling coyly to everyone was a little girl with ruby eyes and white hair.

4e4d319c-0b45-4e65-a9c7-f9c69d4a34e9.Text:
Greyish-blue waves swallowed the Lord Captain and the feeling of lightness disappeared as {mf|his|her} limbs grew heavy again. {name} fell on the hard floor of a laboratory cluttered with vats as tall as a human. Inside them were dozens, hundreds, even, of repulsive mutants. Some had no arms, or no legs, or two heads, or no face, or their innards turned inside out... but each had white skin. White hair. Long clawed limbs. And ruby eyes.
"My lady! The child... the child is born!"

42085487-deb5-4dce-ad4e-3e6c610ea078.Text: "Be a good little girl, my Child. Until the day we meet again." With trembling hands, the woman handed the girl to a Navigator in laboratory attire. "I am... out of time. Prepare the Child for the Atlas transfer. And destroy all records and mentions of the world of Ir-T-Vi. None must learn of that which took place here. And remember, her body must grow strong for it to accept my power. And once I have returned... loyalty will be rewarded."

6de7d439-2af8-4844-b805-c3477b90329f.Text: The Rogue Trader's blood stained the brush in {mf|his|her} hands with unnatural speed, but there was no pain. Instead, the blood continued to flow, taking on the vague form of...

5c26071e-5fbc-4292-952c-19e61c8d59cd.Text:
The tall old woman slowly approached one of the vats. "Readings?"
"Stable."
"Mutations?"
"None were detected at any of the stages."
"Genes?"
"Identical, my lady."
"Hmm... Chances of survival?"
"A hundred times higher than any of the previous experiments."
"How long will it take to grow this... child?"
"I fear accelerating the process might cause the body to fail. The only one after years of—"
"Silence. I understand the situation. Natural growth... I do not have that much time. We will have to go with the backup plan."
"Yes, Novator. It will be done."

860861ba-2bad-462b-9f27-40cf89bc94f5.Text: The Lord Captain charged at the entity and Tisiphone Orsellio finally noticed the presence of a living creature in that bizarre world. Enraged by the impudence of this uninvited guest, she lunged at the Lord Captain.

a30a6bd3-0e3e-4be8-9897-b26eaed0f355.Text: {name} stayed in the ocean of nothingness, devoid of any sensation or emotion...

569563d7-3be8-424f-99be-8b834a1a994f.Text:
Someone's scream broke the delicate equilibrium of the Lord Captain's motionless body and the weightlessness released {mf|him|her}. {mf|He|She} plummeted into the maroon abyss of roiling illusions, but was now in full control of {mf|his|her} body again.
Then {name}...

f6742b51-3c7c-4d5c-aa2a-e6db43c4aaad.Text: Cassia noticed the Lord Captain's presence, albeit barely. But {name}'s words were completely drowned out by the entity's ghastly howl, and the Lady Navigator had to turn her attention back to the monster.

ae8b0055-f823-4d73-8524-153096ea6c02.Text: The Lord Captain's words attracted not just Lady Cassia's attention —- Tisiphone Orsellio, finally noticing the presence of a living creature in that bizarre world, turned to face the interloper and lunged forward, seething with rage.

b9e26199-bea1-40cd-a7cd-c0892600fd2e.Text: ...until a persistent pulsation in {mf|his|her} right side reminded {mf|him|her} of a world that once seemed more real than this one.

28f636c2-4e4f-4ebb-a24f-4476f3250ff1.Text: ...until an ornate ritual dagger floated before {mf|his|her} eyes and reminded {mf|him|her} of a world that once seemed more real than this one.

64efdb41-15be-429f-a91c-5f8555c2c8ee.Text: ...until a slight smile upon someone's lips surfaced in {mf|his|her} mind. The warmth of her skin, the silk of her snow-white hair... Cassia! She was there, somewhere amid that seething nothingness, all alone...

e230ef46-b91c-4836-91f3-96b83557e30c.Text: The Lord Captain crashed from an immeasurable height to the bottom of a roiling abyss. In the next moment, {name} saw two figures amid the billowing maroon mist. One of the figures, unnaturally gaunt and tall, was clutching the other, smaller one in its claws, screaming furiously.

42ce668e-47c7-4576-b1eb-121945a875e3.Text: A single plasma shot liquefied Tisiphone Orsellio's skull. Then her entire body, bone by bone, crumbled into ash... And with that, it was all over at last.

5f4960db-861d-41f2-8417-9ba18ff0c352.Text: The power hammer slammed into Tisiphone's ancient bones and instantly shattered her frame into tiny particles... And with that, it was all over at last.

a20d39d3-c324-45ae-9467-577ea5f833b0.Text: The bizarre laws of that place breathed life into whatever was painted on the canvas. The weapon instantly formed in the Lord Captain's hands and {mf|he|she} charged into battle.

fd43d5ba-4e0e-46f3-ab8d-111c8ccec932.Text: The Lady Navigator opened her third eye and a wave of unbridled warp energy obliterated Tisiphone's spectre before she realised what was happening. Then the exhausted Cassia collapsed.

6f9b0556-d4e9-4aef-a48c-0bb00832ea91.Text: When the entity's claws were millimetres from the Rogue Trader's throat, Cassia opened her Navigator's eye, and a wave of unbridled warp energy obliterated Tisiphone's spectre before she realised what was happening.

6261d27c-835d-4d4d-8f20-5176e5e1bb06.Text: Senior Enforcer: "We performed an emergency warp jump, barely activated the Geller field in time, and are now being dragged to Throne knows where by an unknown force! The Lady Navigator and the Lord Captain are still unaccounted for. Now tell me. One. More. Time. What transpired in the Sanctum Navis?"

c20175e9-e320-44e2-82b5-1b0866b347cf.Text: Enforcer: "Startled by the Lord Captain's cry, the Lady Navigator answered! That's when I realised it. The armaglass between us and the Sanctum Navis was... gone. And the things in the painting, they broke free!"

dbed1842-2f61-4cc2-b81b-9893e4e46131.Text: Enforcer: "To my horror, the shots instantly shattered the armaglass and a few bolts passed dangerously close to the Lady Navigator. Startled, Lady Cassia turned around... and then the horrors in her painting broke free!"

44ff16e8-2c22-4d37-b865-bfcb9c9cd315.Text:
Sector: [no data]
Region: [no data]
Location: [no data]
Material: Relation of the Lord Captain's personal account, recorded by: [no data]
Note: Strictly classified
Access protocol holder: {name} von Valancius

f51460e8-f73c-4876-a4d3-5245adfa3651.Text: Enforcer: "Sir?" Senior Enforcer: "Mistress Vox Master, I have a report that needs to be delivered to the senior officers. The Lord Captain and the Lady Navigator... were lost during the emergency warp jump. Their whereabouts are still unknown. I am sending you the interrogation reports. End of recording."

06f4fd14-f896-44ca-a0d4-780294379f59.Text: Enforcer: "I didn't dare to stop {mf|him|her}... I just watched, bolter at the ready. The machine spirits went mad, the doors and the shutters started opening and closing at random, but the Rogue Trader managed to dart inside. Startled by all the noise, the Lady Navigator turned around... and then those horrors in her painting, they broke free!"

de2cb23d-a8e0-412c-9955-ddf4125731e3.Text: Enforcer: "I... I barely remember a thing. There was a bright flash, a purple blur... I remember feeling so scared that my knees were shaking. I remember my legs carrying me away like they had a mind of their own... As I ran, I heard screams behind me... The Lord Captain and Lady Cassia... they... oh, God-Emperor, the creatures, they pulled them both inside the painting!"

dda16a79-cc55-47f3-8726-7c222926c7b7.Text: Tisiphone Orsellio's ritual did not go as planned. The warp disturbance triggered by the Lady Navigator's trance washed over the Sanctum Navis. The voidship's machine spirits reacted to the surge of the Immaterium and interpreted it as a call to action. Thus did the emergency jump into the unknown begin.

77f40c81-940c-4868-96cd-167dbc5b0a51.Text: Amid the shrieks of sirens, the clanging of shutters, and the distant hum of the warp engine, some unknown will pulled the Lord Captain into the Sanctum Navis, toward the creatures from the living canvas that had already gripped the Lady Navigator's throat. Horrified, almost out of breath, and struggling to scream, Cassia stretched out her hand... and began slowly sinking into her own painting.

b2d0a621-f54a-4add-b8fd-f316308ce352.Text:
There was horror and desperation in her eyes.
"You lie, Tisiphone! I cannot be you! I am me—"
Cassia's voice cracked and crimson tears started down her cheeks.
"You know you are lying to yourself, Child." The chilling voice made {name}'s ears ring. "You saw everything. I created you. You are the Child. You are me. And so it must be."
"I... Yes, I am the Child. You are me. And so it must be..." Cassia went limp in Tisiphone Orsellio's merciless grasp and closed her eyes.

61003547-84fa-444e-a112-61cf75f14002.Text: The Lord Captain pulled the Lady Navigator closer. After a while, the creatures eased their onslaught and Cassia crashed into the Lord Captain, knocking {mf|him|her} off {mf|his|her} feet. The Lord Captain felt a sharp pain in {mf|his|her} side as Cassia's cogita-brush pierced {mf|his|her} flesh during the fall. A moment later, Cassia was sucked into the air and pulled inside the canvas. Instants later, the Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself} was plunged into the depths of the world the Lady Navigator had created...

8ffedf80-98a3-4c90-8779-6b09fc4a368e.Text:
And yet, there was hatred and contempt in her eyes.
"I know what you crave, Tisiphone Orsellio. But you will never have it. You want my soul? My body? You claim that I am you? No. Get out... of... my... head..."
Cassia freed a hand from Tisiphone's grasp and struck Tisiphone's cadaverous face with all her might, shattering the old woman's skull into white spatters of paint.

072b6089-8949-4401-a0c6-237ef037f840.Text:
Yet, there was steadfast resolve in her eyes.
"I know who you are, Tisiphone Orsellio. I know what you crave... I saw it in the visions that you sent me again and again. I won't allow you... I will never allow you to become me..."
Cassia's fatigued voice quivered, but she was not about to yield in this battle.

c1e1b65f-b330-4420-9780-15984a491b28.Text: One step was all it took for some unknown force to notice the Lord Captain, seize {mf|him|her}, and drag {mf|him|her} through the painting's twisted space. Now the Lord Captain could clearly see the dark shade of the long-dead Navigator leaning over Cassia. Clutching her neck in its clawed fingers, the shade screamed,

b58d4b1b-a87e-4c1f-99e0-d70c2b60ac7d.Text: The crimson swirls confused the Rogue Trader's thoughts and emotions. {mf|He|She} could hear whispers and moans coming from the depths. If {mf|he|she} were to take one step, {mf|he|she} would be forever lost in that violent mist and join the wretched chorus... But there was also a voice, so desperately pleading for mercy. Yet, whose voice it was, {name} could not tell.

5d1875ea-4a0f-4f9f-9695-5cdde2665f58.Text: In the swirling mist all around {mf|him|her}, {name} could make out human faces stricken with torment... and not just human faces! There were xenos, Aeldari, their features fused together with those of humans, which made the crimson spectres look all the more abominable. Their gazes and their rage were directed at the two unmoving figures facing each other.

586e0dfa-9bd2-4e95-8465-b72c0427253a.Text: "You were given life because of me. You survived because of me! And here you are now — because I have willed it so. Bow before me! Tell me what I wish to hear, and your suffering will end. Go on, Child... I have waited for so long. Submit to me!"

912fe4ac-ee50-418c-bb75-c49e7120a54b.Text: The fight that followed was short. The moment Tisiphone realised she did not have the strength to overpower Cassia, she flew into the air with a scream of despair and tried to flee... but there was no escape.

ffa6dede-f75e-43de-b9f0-d072c4c56178.Text: Cassia looked exhausted, her body covered in hundreds of thin cuts, her lips lacerated, claw marks on her cheeks.

c355898a-de2b-4c7c-834b-8c32166dab53.Text: The silvery blade whistled through the air — and Tisiphone let out a horrible howl as her skeletal figure flew upward and scattered into black ash... And with that, it was all over at last.

66eabe86-108d-4bdd-bfc1-d68adae55716.Text: The Lord Captain charged at the entity but passed right through Tisiphone Orsellio's body. The entity growled and gave the Rogue Trader a furious sidelong glance, but did not deem {mf|him|her} a threat and instead focused her attention on the Lady Navigator.

6aeca46c-9916-4fc4-9163-2124bf62eaf3.Text: The sharp teeth of the chainsword shredded Tisiphone's ancient bones until the spectre let out a horrible scream of despair and scattered into black ash... And with that, it was all over at last.

549c42b6-d728-4647-ad76-40f403036ae5.Text:
Sector: Koronus Expanse
Region: Orsellio Prophecy System
Location: Sanctum Navis, exterior observation chambers
Material: Witness interrogation vox-records conducted by upper deck enforcers

df956576-1ba3-4154-b8c1-d14abb3cfe06.Text: Entry A-201.48.66. 10 chronometer turns since the incident.

5b27126f-4412-41a6-8be5-afc7abf30d6c.Text: Enforcer: "Witness Hideh-On-00110101, you claim that you left the Sanctum Navis on the Lady Navigator's orders?" Hideh-On-00110101: "Affirmative. This unit acted in accordance with Maintenance Protocol TRN-08353. Step one: cense the sacred mechanisms for the duration of 15 chronometer turns. Step two—"

3c737e8e-9c6f-4eb5-823d-c2944e1dac72.Text: Enforcer: "You failed to inform the bridge about the imminent jump. I want to know why." Hideh-On-00110101: "Data... unavailable. The Lady Navigator ordered that she be connected to the voidship, but she did not order the preparation of the machine spirits for warp translation. Cause: a ritual that cannot be identified by this unit's capabilities. This unit received the command to interrupt Protocol TRN-08353 and exit the Sanctum Navis."

5c3a5328-857a-44cc-9791-dd8d2e584ab6.Text: Entry M-001.87.23. 30 chronometer turns since the incident.

94d2c37e-ee8d-4363-9f65-dd6e43b68c0e.Text: Enforcer: "Groxshit! Armaglass can't shield you from warp horrors!" Servant: "I-I swear it on my soul and the Golden Throne, master enforcer, the Lady Navigator only wanted to paint a picture for a ritual or some such, that's all I know! She wasn't g-going to use the power in her eye but I still got as far away from there as I could. That's all I saw, I'm telling you!"

5c44576e-343e-4420-a970-63e5b464eed2.Text: Entry H-905.00.80. 50 chronometer turns since the incident.

81a7f5e7-03b3-4a36-b62d-a332e47ca2f4.Text: Approving groans came from within the maroon mist and the faces of humans and Aeldari slowly evaporated along with the dead Novator.

b1cfa01a-d2b2-4a78-a146-7f7cce507b74.Text: The memory dissipated and a gust of silvery wind hurled the Lord Captain back into the ocean of nothingness. But this time, the nothingness felt dismal — instead of bright hues, all it contained was shadows of invisible monsters swimming by, shrouded by a nebulous veil of unfathomableness.

e43df404-1d4c-440c-9513-09bb74f3797a.Text: "Like any heresy, House Orsellio's Atlas must be destroyed."

b5de2f82-60d3-4549-9bae-7a7d58fbffa5.Text: "You are right... I should consider this one more time."

5295fb52-646d-4337-a7c7-d08d06bf6642.Text: "I too wish to be enlightened about what is happening here."

63c67ca9-1de8-495c-8e59-559a3fe74b7d.Text: "House Orsellio can never hope to redeem themselves before the God-Emperor. Serve your justice, xenos."

8532b2b7-0940-4618-92ec-04ee7ba37517.Text: "I will not stand here and let some duplicitous xenos slaughter Navigators of the Imperium!"

0117ce4d-66af-496d-b1b0-4aeb66599ccb.Text: [Address the renegades' envoy] "How did you get here before us? No one but Cassia knew the way."

97facfce-9245-4817-9452-64bd40033c1d.Text: "An ambush... How ignoble! Yet so typical of xenos."

c18d85a7-2d4d-4a00-8a20-9500c32d33b9.Text: "Is it possible to perform the ritual to cleanse the Atlas without the xenos' help?"

1c27c372-86f4-4da7-9505-e0e056fa9293.Text: "Cassia is the inheritor of the one who bound the Spirit Monolith to the Navigators' bodies. Listen to whatever she has to say. She is not the woman her predecessor was."

9ec3ce50-5723-4511-aebe-17920b57db44.Text: [Execute Cassia] "Enough! I hereby sentence House Orsellio to oblivion!"

57255d6e-af4b-4ad7-8f01-9d3bcca3b177.Text: "If you think I shouldn't, I won't."

92526881-836b-42e0-81ae-399503a13bec.Text: "The Atlas is a heretical artefact of a madwoman's creation. Wouldn't it be better to get rid of it?"

c45d3c02-83f5-4599-a093-774e6994b04b.Text: "How did the Navigators of House Orsellio taint the Spirit Monolith?"

3afecdfc-e490-4b81-9001-8811567b713d.Text: "You are free to act as you see fit."

508c44e8-3e01-41a9-8685-cd607d5f30af.Text: "You can't just cast me aside like that!"

c36a1f95-c548-4d82-b3d9-a8c986f516cc.Text: "I see that you have made up your mind. Then there is no point in discussing it."

ac848e74-d86b-4f69-8eb7-333f4bd85fc2.Text: "What will happen to House Orsellio if the Atlas is destroyed?"

f8d57c85-f150-49a4-9de2-b15b07688fb8.Text: [Address Yrliet] "What was that about? What answer have you always known?"

8ec85e99-cad3-419b-9c83-4c7eca077aca.Text: "I hereby sentence House Orsellio to oblivion."

a41a2cae-f448-427a-bd85-72e914b0a638.Text: [Address the Harlequin] "Get to the point before I put a hole in your hideous mask."

88fb7ea4-4c30-4906-bb23-027c7cffa0e7.Text: "Seldom do humans and xenos get the chance to resolve their conflicts without violence. I second Lady Cassia's proposal."

1db6cb69-a875-467a-9fd9-b49584e38da9.Text: "Let us deal with the Atlas issue after we have destroyed the xenos."

5d30bd51-a47b-4a71-8ad9-6844d55b188f.Text: "Neither Theodora von Valancius nor Tisiphone was infallible. But that doesn't mean we are powerless to rectify the errors of our ancestors."

15555d7d-0da2-4d8b-8aba-1403f04571fb.Text: "This is appalling. House Orsellio's deeds... cannot be forgiven."

2363dcf2-da30-462f-ae13-ac6a628ab0e1.Text: "There is no shame in using xenos powers for the good of the Imperium."

909939c4-1281-4c18-b69a-eb935031f73f.Text: [Address Cassia] "What do you say to this xenos's assertions?"

20eb1501-6d63-4846-b878-9dd3261d09fd.Text: "How dare you lump us together? I never would have stooped to something like this!"

a61cc9e1-3eb9-482a-bc84-974465e8351f.Text: "Save the Navigators from death, and you will gain a powerful ally among humans."

b8977e71-467c-4162-add6-5594e3b17654.Text: "Cassia can bring death to her entire House with but a thought. What would become of the Monolith if the souls of the Orsellio Navigators were to leave their bodies all at once?"

eeb0ee53-b996-4908-b3fb-9b2f415a2d5b.Text: "The fate of House Orsellio is being decided as we speak. You cannot stand idly by!"

e7d2cc23-58aa-4fd1-bd3b-bb6a32ec2c8d.Text: "Losing the Atlas will weaken House Orsellio and, in turn, the Imperium. That cannot be allowed to come to pass!"

c50a338d-0ccf-41af-936c-ee083737530d.Text: "What future do you see for your House, Cassia?"

dc40d811-5099-46ce-936a-a0b02b37d629.Text: "It is high time House Orsellio paid for Tisiphone's error."

d12eadc4-70fd-4331-a3da-033f592c6e74.Text: "I won't let the xenos have the Atlas."

7ca5b16f-214d-408c-b7f3-17b7c2649eac.Text: "I will have no part in this conflict."

c4d9797c-11ab-4e14-8c29-9fc570367050.Text: [Attack the Harlequins] "I will not let the God-Emperor's servants be sullied by this heresy further."

d175fd16-d0e2-45d3-99ce-a1a2f3f6c12d.Text: "What is this taint you speak of, xenos?"

2dba8886-5f97-4007-a082-3ab4603440a4.Text: "Why shouldn't I simply kill you all where you stand?"

17ee8d2b-c684-4653-baab-8299f7caf470.Text: "If I were in your position, I would not risk losing the House's great relic. I would leave things as they were."

ea01eb56-0743-4c99-9732-b29fabbf7a3f.Text: [Address Cassia] "What experiments did Tisiphone conduct here?"

3158fc20-6b88-487a-97d9-32d59d734e45.Text: [Address the Harlequin] "And what does all this mean, exactly?"

c92030af-ec59-4850-95f8-ce1453672e5a.Text: "I see... So you think you can reject me? Then perish along with the rest of the Orsellios!"

c4976422-80dc-4d33-8201-9e782707423d.Text: [Address the Great Regent's envoy] "How did you get here?"

43aad13b-3cf1-43e9-a6f4-4a751e988bce.Text: [Address the renegades' envoy] "I suggest you explain yourself immediately. And you had better be very persuasive."

e5b7228a-8542-4729-bf76-de6705fe60f2.Text: "Is there no way whatsoever to separate the Navigators' souls from those of the Aeldari without killing one or the other?"

12e2580d-e5ba-4a84-8dc8-fab36f840507.Text: "The Atlas must certainly be destroyed. But surely the entire House cannot be expected to serve penance for Tisiphone's crimes?"

84e6368d-b26a-4e17-9eec-7c41315b72bb.Text: "What? Perish the thought! The Starway Atlas is the foundation of House Orsellio's power. Whence do you suppose we draw the strength to fare the Sea of Souls? Is this not the greatest library of Navis Nobilite knowledge across the Koronus Expanse and Calixis Sector? Should the Atlas be destroyed, House Orsellio will face oblivion!"

13934f42-a09a-4819-ab04-aa30026914e6.Text: "Nonsense! Tisiphone created the Atlas only a few centuries ago, whereas the history of House Orsellio dates back to the last millennium! We have always been a House to be reckoned with, but when Tisiphone arrived in the Expanse, she set her sights on acquiring power that could let her family branch dominate the rest. And where has that left us? Our bodies are corrupted with xenoheresy! God-Emperor, forgive Your children for committing a trespass so heinous..."

eff4954c-53b9-4292-b985-95674e172c45.Text: {n}The xenos thinks for a moment.{/n} "I do not believe there is. The three-eyed mon-keigh have desecrated this place, and I will not put the Spirit Monolith at risk just to help them avoid the consequences of a lamentable performance."

55e776e6-d8cd-4fb8-a773-cc8ebcb64fd3.Text: "Cassia, are you really capable of this?"

633e966a-b914-4d1c-b66b-28f11fe890c2.Text: "Wait!" {n}Cassia's appeal is addressed both to you and the Aeldari surrounding you.{/n} "I cannot change the past, it is true. Nor can I change the fact that my House is forever tainted with disgrace born of Tisiphone Orsellio's hubris. Yet, all of us here today have the power to change the future and halt the unending suffering that is drowning both your kin and mine!"

c88a76ee-a7e5-4297-95c0-5d4dc8600d73.Text: "It was unwise of Tisiphone to use an artefact of the xenos for her experiments, but we cannot afford to destroy the Atlas. Not at this time. House Orsellio is weakening along with this stone. Who can say what will happen to us all if we destroy it? I shall delve into our House's ancient documents and reach out to the memories of the Setthala clan... I am certain that we will find a way to rid ourselves of this curse that was once called a blessing. All in due time."

1da918ad-cfe5-4f7b-bb54-59aa2dd89310.Text: {n}Cassia sighs quietly.{/n} "It was unwise of Tisiphone to use an artefact of the xenos for her experiments. House Orsellio will have to do whatever it takes to make up for her shortcomings in the eyes of the Emperor. Which is why I cannot allow you to destroy the Atlas. Not only will it weaken us, the whole of Humanity will suffer as well!"

5168860b-2251-4671-9aeb-7fa65004a080.Text: "Y-yes, indeed! And if the Koronus Expanse loses a Navigator House, turmoil will engulf worlds and stations that cannot exist without the seeing eye of the Navis Nobilite, and Rogue Traders' fleets will fare no better. Your dynasty too will feel the effects, {name} von Valancius. So I am asking you now: whose side are you on?"

9cd7a5aa-8220-4987-a7d3-849e6b3af1a0.Text: {n}The envoy's eyes widen in horror as her body instantly bends in half.{/n} "F-forgive my outburst, my lady. You truly are my Novator, whether or not you have been crowned as one! House Orsellio was always loyal to Novator Tisiphone. Henceforth, it will be loyal to her successor, even if you see fit to lead us down a different path!"

f7bced01-ece9-4fee-a5f1-fedc55491c84.Text: "You address the future Novator of House Orsellio. One who survived the massacre of Eurac V. Who has lived following an attempt on her life at the palace of Dargonus. Who has restored her House's stability in what scant time she has been free while you — all of you — have spent years destroying it from within! You address one who has passed through the tempest of the Sea of Souls to the true Atlas as a Rogue Trader's ally. Yet, still you call me unworthy, don't you? Young? Inexperienced? Kneel before me, and I shall forgive you your insolence."

a9f66b1a-3cd5-43a3-a1ca-96a53cec8a4c.Text: "Your travels at the Rogue Trader's side have confused your mind, Child. Let us return to the Great Regent, and then—"

80998a75-e07d-4164-86f4-be2da0b0cdfa.Text: "House Orsellio was always loyal to Novator Tisiphone. Henceforth, it will be loyal to her successor, even if you see fit to lead us down a different path, my lady!" {n}The Navigator's voice trembles with reverence.{/n}

ad6f6bdf-594d-478e-8bab-2a5744547761.Text: "Then... I will simply make you do it." {n}Cassia closes her eyes for a moment and brings a hand to her Atlas.{/n}

ea0b5d82-cf54-4f96-bbb6-732590185cc4.Text: "Stop, xenos! Didn't you promise that you would kill the girl along with her protectors and spare the rest?"

3a723f5b-fc60-4926-9e0b-57a93f255193.Text: "What... what does this mean? Has the Rogue Trader stooped so low as to lure the Child and us into a trap?" {n}The envoy's lips curl in fury.{/n} "Great Regent Aaronto was wrong to {d|Encyclopedia:CassiaQ1_RegenAlive}trust you{/d}!"

e6912e69-21bf-4c76-8636-b624d237c652.Text: "What... what does this mean? Has the Rogue Trader stooped so low as to lure the Child and us into a trap?" {n}The envoy's lips curl in fury.{/n} "We should not have trusted you again after the {d|Encyclopedia:CassiaQ1_RegenExecuted}murder of Great Regent Aaronto{/d}!"

e45fc432-149c-4f8b-a5a3-3e28770fb7df.Text: "What is this? The Rogue Trader and the traitors to the House have lured the Child into a trap set by xenos? I wish my eyes were deceiving me. But now I can see clearly that {d|Encyclopedia:CassiaQ1_RegenAlive}Great Regent Aaronto{/d} was right to send us after your vessel." {n}The sturdily built woman is armed with a pistol, and yet, there are signs of exhaustion in her posture. Her face is hidden behind a gem-encrusted three-eyed mask and her elaborate Navis Nobilite vestments are stained with dried blood and other evidence of recent combat.{/n}

e13272c7-80a5-4507-a3ec-4f3286acbedb.Text: "You will stop defiling the remains of the hallowed ground of our ancestors with your semblance of speech, mon-keigh." {n}The Harlequin's bright clothes glimmer faintly in the dim light of the system's star, and the sinister grin on his mask only adds to his menacing and aloof presence.{/n} "The final act will soon unfold where you will pay for the deeds of your ancestors. Stay put and wait for the puppeteer to pull at your strings."

32c44668-d2f0-4530-be98-21073979c0f3.Text: "Silence, traitor! The Atlas is the sacred relic of House Orsellio, it is what elevates us above the rest! How dare you—" {n}The regent's envoy abruptly loses her breath with a groan and she clutches her chest where her Atlas is implanted.{/n} "I refuse... to accept this... Impossible..."

ee0b964a-e779-416f-8dc6-a3b8533f78a4.Text: "It was not easy to follow you through the raging storm. However, the connection to the Child's Atlas works both ways. We braved the tempest with nothing but the call of the Atlas to guide us. And we made it. It doesn't matter if it cost us many lives to do so."

6b98a135-5496-4ddb-8738-8a6c625af9f1.Text: {n}The Harlequin draws his blade and slashes the air right by Cassia's neck. The {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_CassiaAmuletOn}stone that was fused with her body{/d} tears through her skin and falls at the Harlequin's feet.{/n} "I am touched that the desperate mon-keigh with darkness in his eyes passed my gift to you, after all. But I no longer see the need for it."

776888c7-9034-4195-8a0b-cb46398499a2.Text: "Then it is time for the closing scene, mon-keigh. Dance like never before!" {n}The Harlequin bows theatrically as he presses and holds a button on the strange device in his hands.{/n}

abf1a8ea-8d27-4d15-a19c-34fd77e131b4.Text: "You dare threaten me, xenos?" {n}Cassia's ice-cold voice is completely unrecognisable. Cruel. Ruthless. Resentful.{/n} "Why are there xenos ruins where the Palace of the Atlas should be? Why is this place coated in an impenetrable black mist? Answer me!"

c0d5d97e-d551-4dea-8539-e994cc7fa0da.Text: "Why... why are there xenos ruins where the Palace of the Atlas should be? Why is this place coated in an impenetrable black mist? I... I'm... suffocating..." {n}Cassia clutches her breastplate near where her Atlas is, her voice feeble and trembling.{/n}

02f2d6c0-2746-49f9-a412-b86fdff72640.Text: {n}The Harlequin's mask laughs in your face.{/n} "You will have your cue yet, mon-keigh. Have patience — the denouement is nigh."

9b4ed250-e860-4843-afb9-69bda73d3863.Text: {n}He points his thin finger at the remarkable crystal floating behind his back, and the Harlequins around you tighten the grips on their weapons.{/n}

ca132cf6-4a1a-4871-a33c-4ffc6179d9c9.Text: {n}Cassia clutches her breastplate and {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_CassiaAmuletOff}stifles a cry of pain{/d}.{/n} "How... can you control my Atlas, xenos?"

34edc1ba-1abb-45c9-9fd3-06fc08dea714.Text: {n}Cassia clutches her breastplate around where her Atlas is embedded and {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_CassiaAmuletOn}thin rivulets of blood trickle from her mouth, nose, and eyes{/d}. Felek's stone on her neck tears through the skin and falls at the Harlequin's feet.{/n} "What... was that? The pain... The colours are swirling before my eyes..."

bafa7188-8b15-4b7c-b4f4-b5815734d4d3.Text: "Yours? Kae-morag! The star of our play is even more brazen than I thought!" {n}The Harlequin chuckles and draws his weapon.{/n} "Begin your last dance, three-eyed one!"

d65da526-241f-4845-8c1b-57a016b4e117.Text: "What's this I am seeing? Our leading lady did receive my gift, after all. Good. At least not all mon-keigh are without use." {n}The Harlequin laughs and draws his weapon.{/n} "Dance, then! Dance, three-eyed one!"

183e52e9-e7f5-4df5-9ca5-d48bedd990c1.Text: "No... It is not possible! To consort with xenos is to violate the word of the God-Emperor! It is known to all that Tisiphone Orsellio executed anyone who showed any interest in the enemies of Humanity!"

53329fec-f7e2-4c59-9981-460e0abff413.Text: "Is that so? Then why is it that every piece of metal or fabric in this place bears our House's coat of arms? Open your eyes!"

4f4ff27f-6936-4b65-a57b-0f0f69bc8022.Text: "Despite all her flaws, Tisiphone was a great Navigator who served the Imperium faithfully for many years, and so has House Orsellio. I shall make up for her misdeeds and rid the bodies of my subjects of xenoheresy... and only the Novator's Atlas will be left to remind our scions of the price we had to pay."

dd49bc8c-71ef-4b93-acbb-560bb7546709.Text: "Your bickering ends now! I can see the truth behind your every word. One's exclamations are woven from gold and silver, but one good look between the threads reveals her green venom and deep red thirst. The other is using his scarlet veil of hatred to conceal an ocean of purple and amber powdered with ashes. I no longer wish to hear from either of you. Today, your Novator herself will decide the future of House Orsellio."

57d5a9a8-c9ec-4a79-b213-657d085ca125.Text: "I am so sick of the muddy colours of your words that entangle the soul like sticky webs. No more regents! No more Novators! I just... want to wrap myself in pallid silence..."

37c4e0dd-9334-4868-b00b-80c871f1cf9e.Text: "Come. I shall guide you back to the Koronus Expanse, the cradle of House Orsellio. And then we shall part ways. Forever."

99f27bc7-1667-4948-bc0f-ebc6f9a28f4a.Text: "Very well, mon-keigh. I will play the role of executioner for your three-eyed kin. But do not think that you are welcome on the Crone World. You will walk away as soon as the dirge is sung. And only because {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}some of my brothers and sisters find you amusing{/d}." {n}The Harlequin bows theatrically and presses a button on the strange device in his hands.{/n} "And now... it is time for the closing scene."

4e6159a3-7e7e-4b80-9b62-7e1243f95e17.Text: "I doubt if your primitive notion of 'justice' can convey the nuances of what our souls demand when we behold the torment of the Spirit Monolith, mon-keigh."

b37320c5-11e9-43bc-b6c8-229d3300f7e6.Text: "So be it, {name}." {n}An exhausted smile flickers on the Lady Navigator's lips.{/n}

d923c105-b322-4d06-bf1f-df53c3d79d61.Text: {n}Cassia gives you a grateful nod and turns to the Harlequin Troupe.{/n} "I cannot change the past, it is true. Nor can I change the fact that my House is forever tainted with disgrace born of Tisiphone Orsellio's hubris. Yet, all of us here today have the power to change the future and halt the unending suffering that is drowning both your kin and mine!"

f2897477-c8c9-4173-93e0-9f5b42b9f303.Text: "You? You suggest that the mon-keigh and the Aeldari change the future together?" {n}The Harlequin leans forward curiously.{/n} "I must admit, my leading lady, I am confounded by your... audacity. Go on."

56d40f7d-801c-4b3b-8458-169149e51667.Text: "My Atlas..." {n}Cassia places a hand on her gilded breastplate.{/n} "If you can free the phantoms of my House from the Spirit Monolith, guide them to enter my Atlas! Their experience and wisdom will help steer House Orsellio onto the path of truth and allow future generations to avoid the calamitous pitfalls of their forebears."

45cdf416-b079-498b-b70f-44b5b68dd57a.Text: "Kae-morag, my leading lady, the shards of the Monolith are lodged inside the chest of every mon-keigh bound to you by ties of blood. How exactly do you intend to return them?"

a94c9c22-7a7d-4259-b090-ba03a05fbf95.Text: "I never wished to learn such harsh truths about my own House..." {n}Cassia buries her face in her hands and you feel waves of despair spreading from her lithe frame, which suddenly appears as fragile as glass.{/n}

dcea0e01-2824-47dd-8398-c958394c7c42.Text: "The ancestors of the three-eyed mon-keigh sought to command the power of the Spirit Monolith and, yet, suffered failure time and again. Eventually, they discovered a way to harness this power: a terrible way, torturous and unforgivable. They shattered the Monolith into many shards and weakened the souls within. And then..." {n}The Harlequin trembles with fury.{/n} "Then they placed the shards inside their bodies to empower their abilities."

78571f20-541f-4f27-9401-b2288dc5de5e.Text: {n}The renegade Navigator stares at Cassia in shock.{/n} "You... you are more than just a tyrant's heir! You are a successor to a mad heretic. A betrayer of the faith! You must be destroyed. You and the Atlas. Once and for all!"

0f03e04b-4add-4f7a-a21e-b329b0009e12.Text: "Yet another aggressive mon-keigh specimen." {n}The Harlequin scoffs.{/n}

1daee8f6-dc1d-40a6-a905-226400057bfb.Text: {n}The Harlequin remains as still as a garish statue for several minutes. Then the mellifluous voice behind the mask says,{/n} "For the sake of returning all of the Monolith shards... I am willing to go along with this impromptu performance, mon-keigh. But for a bird to fly, it first needs to be unshackled."

8bc36ec5-c2a2-493d-a963-d38659cd889e.Text: "No!" {n}The regent's envoy draws her pistol.{/n} "I won't let you destroy the Atlas! Even if it is the Child's wish. Lady Orsellio, you are too... young. Inexperienced. You simply cannot comprehend—"

b4b55ffe-47a2-4321-9506-008408885b9c.Text: "We have reached an understanding at last." {n}The regent's envoy offers Cassia a respectful nod.{/n} "House Orsellio welcomes its mistress, Lady Cassia, our Novator. Thanks to you, both the Atlas and our bloodline are saved. What happens next, only the stars know."

aeeeeae4-6a50-4cc3-a5b3-686f5feff67e.Text: "Are you done with your performance, mon-keigh? Then stand aside and do not interrupt."

966649bf-72d6-4acc-904a-b7e763b8941f.Text: "I..." {n}Cassia freezes hesitantly, only for her frightened gaze to harden.{/n} "You truly intend to betray me, Rogue Trader? After all that we have been through?"

71ac0bcf-3113-4d7e-9a97-b9e796648912.Text: "You say that only because you wish to soothe me." {n}She smiles faintly.{/n}

2543eba5-1efe-4b65-90e9-34b62277886a.Text: "You say so now, but had you been in Tisiphone's shoes... would you have passed up a chance like that? You cannot know for certain. I can see your soul's colours all too well and there are plenty of darker shades within."

33446958-a63f-4af2-962e-a2367230a519.Text: {n}Cassia looks up at you with sorrow in her eyes.{/n} "So you... don't believe that we can make up for the faults of those who came before us?"

4912693c-03a3-4398-9326-43e9916c6448.Text: "My whole life, I have been taught to honour the Emperor and His light that illuminates our way in the darkness of the Sea of Souls, a place of horror and torment. I have been told that all heresy must be eradicated lest its weeds spread deep inside human souls. I am one such weed, Lord Captain. And... so is all of House Orsellio."

09bf7c44-268d-4645-919c-ca42494fdb77.Text: "And now... begone from our world, mon-keigh."

aee6bc69-7c3b-4347-bbff-8ca9622aaac7.Text: "Lady Orsellio! Rogue Trader! Praise be to the God-Emperor, you have saved the Atlas from the detestable xenos. We must inform the Great Regent of all this at once!"

9f18c826-bdff-4edd-870b-2186e9144dd8.Text: "No! The xenos threat may have been eliminated, but the Atlas is still the fruit of Tisiphone's heretical experiments. As long as it survives, House Orsellio will remain a prisoner to its own miserable state and continue to suffer from its Novator's tyranny."

eb14b611-2f7a-4dcf-b5ed-738a6d63a7ed.Text: "What good is an ally who heedlessly seeks self-destruction?" {n}The Harlequin shrugs indifferently.{/n} "Your kind is weak and your memory is short. A puppet's fate suits your nature better."

2002b59f-e835-48ab-ac7e-8173e21216a9.Text: "An ugly plot, to be sure. As the one who directs this play... I would be deeply offended by such a resolution." {n}The Harlequin lowers his head in thought.{/n} "Your words are harmonious, mon-keigh. But what will your companions say?"

6440eaa4-4958-4d04-9350-aa85c253b1a8.Text: "I do not believe the protagonist of our play is quite capable of that. I do sense ancestral echoes and hidden menace within her... but she could not become the death of her House. And thus, mon-keigh, you have failed to daunt me."

1c4b9921-00eb-4e48-b501-4bf841033d39.Text: "I won't let the Atlas be destroyed! Even if it is the Child's wish. Lady Orsellio, you are too... young. Inexperienced. You simply cannot comprehend—"

58650b7d-e912-4f4d-99a0-c7d2803ed39a.Text: "I never expected to hear such words coming from the cursed Child." {n}The renegade interrupts the regent's envoy with a wave of his hand.{/n} "If such is Lady Cassia's decision, House Orsellio accepts it. And you will not stand in our way!"

986e72a7-cf0e-4985-9fa7-61b5ce8ecb95.Text: {n}Utterly drained, Cassia admires the result of her efforts.{/n} "The flashes of scarlet and the poisonous black are gone — now there is only an azure summer sky. The xenos spirits are at rest, and as for my ancestors... it is so odd to feel their warmth in my chest. They no longer intrude upon my thoughts and no longer hide in shadows like ghosts. And yet, they answer my call as soon as I close my eyes and reach out to their wisdom..." {n}She sighs wearily.{/n} "Forgive me, this journey has taken a heavy toll on me. Let us continue our conversation on board the ship once I have had a chance to recuperate in my chambers."

ff83316e-f539-4e5d-8a1a-fe72897bc90f.Text: {n}Cassia nods to the Navigator and beckons him to approach.{/n} "It is just the two of us now, so focus. Peer inward. Heed the ancestors' call through the Atlas as I do. Look through my eyes upon all that I have seen. Lend me your strength, and together... together, we shall deliver House Orsellio from its plights."

a1e41ac4-9b8e-4435-a154-39b07786d02f.Text: "Then... peer inward. Heed the ancestors' call through the Atlas as I do. Look through my eyes upon all that I have seen. Lend me your strength, and together... together, we shall deliver House Orsellio from its plights."

fd76dda6-7b27-4ece-b5d3-9b5836338d82.Text: "Not you too, Rogue Trader! Are you all so blind that you cannot see the truth? The heresy of the xenos has seeped into the very heart—"

64476f0d-fec5-475a-9ebd-d300ddcc0124.Text: "Naturally, the Atlas must be preserved and used for the good of the Imperium. The Setthala clan, Tisiphone, and many of my subjects have already paid for House Orsellio's power with their lives. It behoves me to prove that their sacrifices were not in vain."

b075cd72-73bb-4434-a70e-3c9ae8ca54a4.Text: "I cannot change the past. Nor can I change the fact that my House is forever tainted with disgrace born of Tisiphone's hubris. And yet, I now hold the power to change the future and halt the unending suffering that is drowning my people." {n}Cassia straightens her shoulders and looks at the surviving Navigators.{/n}

6172cb6f-d815-4354-83df-9275792c7557.Text: "Oh, now you are interested in my opinion, {name} von Valancius?" {n}Cassia's voice quivers with fury.{/n} "Well, then, my House has suffered long enough, both from Tisiphone's mistakes and its 'alliance' with you. It is high time we disposed of the Atlas for good and finally freed ourselves."

76da44d3-c6eb-479c-85a2-47cf2669504e.Text: "If I only had the courage to tear this curse out of my chest with my own hands." {n}Cassia gazes at the Harlequin sadly.{/n} "Do it. Free my House from its bane. Break the chains that are tightening around the necks of our ancestors whatever the cost may be. If House Orsellio is destined to perish for Tisiphone's malefactions, so be it."

51744adf-9773-44a5-93e5-99d507575f0c.Text: "Damn you, {name}! I hate you, I hate you!" {n}Cassia's fear and rage burn your lungs. Your knees buckle, tears swell in your throat, and your head is in utter disarray. You feel nauseous, but then... the sensations suddenly ease.{/n}

37381095-7ffd-41df-a2f9-c777b38b502e.Text: "Silence, void cur! You do not deserve to be called a Navigator of House Orsellio if you permit yourself to address your Novator with such insolence." {n}The regent's envoy offers Cassia a respectful nod.{/n} "House Orsellio welcomes its mistress, Lady Cassia. Thanks to you, both the Atlas and our bloodline are saved. What happens next, only the stars know."

334d09c1-85d0-4c4d-836f-97ac940cde28.Text: {n}Cassia nods tiredly.{/n} "We should return to the Koronus Expanse and inform the House of all that took place here. I see no reason to hide the truth any longer. It is high time we began learning from our mistakes."

0db9b0b5-985c-407b-a57b-2bdd21454635.Text: {n}The renegade interrupts the regent's envoy with a wave of his hand.{/n} "If such is Lady Cassia's decision, House Orsellio accepts it. And you will not stand in our way!"

3954f820-5839-4bf0-ac75-f24b74d8e5d6.Text: "Lady Orsellio! Rogue Trader! Praise be to the God-Emperor, you have saved the Atlas from the detestable xenos. We must inform the Great Regent of all this at once!" {n}The envoy has regained consciousness and Cassia's attention shifts to her.{/n}

5ec260c9-b0a1-4a87-a666-776f6586f795.Text: {n}The Harlequin presses and holds a button on the strange device in his hands and says to you,{/n} "It will be my pleasure to satisfy your request. But do not think that you are any more welcome on the Crone World than the three-eyed mon-keigh. You will walk away as soon as the dirge is sung. And only because {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}some of my brothers and sisters find you amusing{/d}."

e18f7e3e-4f1f-48c4-a045-caa0ae7d53ba.Text: "I shall use the Atlas to sever my subjects' connection to the Spirit Monolith and then I shall extract its shards from every Navigator of House Orsellio. This artefact is implanted at birth, but that does not mean that the ritual cannot be reversed. I witnessed its creation through Tisiphone's eyes in my visions. I lived it, over and over again, through the memories of the Setthala clan. I... I can recreate the ritual that will return the souls of your kin to you and save my people's lives."

da54bdf9-a21d-4a02-b452-60c9002d5339.Text: "The Aeldari souls nourished House Orsellio with their strength for nearly three centuries. I... want to do this right, {name}. No more blood need be shed."

afd01f3e-0e5b-4186-9e44-f6bb13063fcb.Text: "Ah, I can feel it again... the tranquillity. The ancestral souls have found peace, and corruption no longer endangers the Monolith or this world." {n}The Harlequin's narrow shoulders now look completely relaxed.{/n} "Remember our agreement, Cassia Orsellio. We will soon meet in this place again so that you can give us the shards."

c65c4ec8-60cc-4000-b78e-9b9123ff9e9e.Text: {n}The renegade tilts his head.{/n} "Wasn't your {d|Encyclopedia:CassiaQ1_RadicalsWithUs}invitation{/d} a sign of your consent to our bargain? The Grand Council would not have taken place without the Child, so you found another way to respond to our message: by taking House Orsellio to Tisiphone's secret hideout so that we could finally destroy her legacy... and her successor."

d5823b37-99a1-42a3-a64a-49fb12bb8afe.Text: "Rogue Traders are not the only ones who know how to find allies." {n}The renegade scoffs and looks at the Aeldari standing beside him.{/n} "Saying that, we should have rid ourselves of this 'alliance' the moment we crossed the Webway Gate. You can trust no one. Least of all the vile xenos."

c136f70e-893d-4af4-8512-8400a628eafe.Text: "Do you not see it?" {n}The Harlequin's voice booms throughout the ruined temple.{/n} "When you mon-keigh discovered this Crone World, you tainted it with your crude technology. Despoiled it of its relics. Ruined all there was to the last stone. But worst of all, you sullied the souls of our ancestors reposed in their sacred vessel, the Spirit Monolith!"

0b2ab4bc-ae8c-4394-9e23-c4bc966bd025.Text: "Your primitive language has no words to convey the true nature of this place, but I will venture a try. Some call it a World Beneath the First Stars. Others know it as a Crone World or an Unblighted World. It was our ancestors' home before we became prey to She Who Thirsts."

f21cbfd9-80df-4479-96b3-80f7e0714ab4.Text: "We call planets such as this one Crone Worlds. They came to be long before my time, back when all of the Aeldari were a united people whose empire stretched from one edge of the galaxy to the other. It is a World Beneath the First Stars. An Unblighted World. I never thought that I would come to find one."

85b5d538-6592-4105-90a1-fa23483696ce.Text: "I have nothing to add to the Outcast's words. Other than my eternal astonishment at your... curious troupe, mon-keigh."

c59b90fb-4611-49d4-a1d4-eb9c16e8a963.Text: {n}This enormous translucent stone shares a strange resonance with this place. You can sense the energy emanating from it: mysterious, restless, coagulated... It resembles a giant heart that has been plucked out of its owner's chest. Its crystal clarity is pierced by hundreds of dark veins that have taken root within like a terrible illness.{/n}

0e2b3e9e-e2b1-421c-84bf-b43285288477.Text: "Like... a sea of bottomless blue..." {n}Cassia looks around her with a stunned expression, her gaze shifting from one xenos to another.{/n} "I... I did not know that living things could exude such saturated hues. I wish I could paint this ocean a different colour."

c798a88b-fc46-4283-89eb-145166f52515.Text: "Quiet." {n}The Harlequin's tone is mild, but it is not a request.{/n} "I am unsurprised that the truth is hidden from your gazes, three-eyed mon-keigh who see into Sha'eil. I realised it the moment I met the first of you. Wretched. Begging us to help you destroy your own kin. I sensed it within you: our ancestors' call. Their pleas. Their endless torment. I knew that what you found was a Crone World. And I humbly waited for the day you would lead me to it."

a0ea9a64-36e6-4ce7-b1f6-dfdaef712ca9.Text: "The experiments..." {n}Cassia covers her mouth in horror.{/n} "This is where she conducted her experiments. Tisiphone..."

69d219d8-8b3b-4353-8e0e-dcd1e5e84d9b.Text: "What is the meaning behind your words, Athair, Troupe Master?"

6c05f13a-86c8-4e8c-86bc-29976b571fec.Text: "{name}..." {n}Cassia's pleading look causes your throat to seize up with despair and sadness, and yet, you can feel her powers waning rapidly.{/n}

125945bb-f30d-4598-ae92-a5c16e494be8.Text: "You know the answer already, Outcast. You have always known."

35584dff-e9b3-4eb4-b687-7f24919535de.Text: "I witnessed the Atlas's creation through Tisiphone's eyes. I watched it happen through the memories of the Setthala clan. I... can create a ritual that will sever our connection to the Aeldari artefact. I can move the House's ancestors to my Atlas, the only one that the Orsellios will keep so it may serve future Novators. The ancient wisdom within the Atlas will help steer House Orsellio onto the path of truth. And allow future generations to avoid the calamitous pitfalls of the past."

77289ce0-5fa1-4be6-a7e5-2ffa9998de27.Text: "You think you can restrain the entire might of the Atlas on your own, Child? Hold it in your own two hands? No... No, I don't think so! Even the strongest of Orsellio Navigators could not have shouldered such a burden. Worse still, even Tisiphone herself couldn't have, Throne smite her! The Atlas must be destroyed. All of it, for good. Even if it means we have to pay with our ancestors' souls that are trapped within."

8f8b58fb-dbd0-443d-8607-d6459caebc11.Text: {n}Yrliet glowers at Cassia.{/n} "So that is why... that is why your presence makes my soul shrink to the size of a river pearl and my throat choke in a collar of thorns. That is why your words seep into my soul like poison, leaving wounds that will not heal. There is a shard of the Spirit Monolith inside you, mon-keigh! Twisted. Perverted. Invigorating you by making my ancestors suffer."

00074f46-4e59-4dcd-b118-d535a7673eba.Text: {n}Cassia offers you a reticent smile.{/n} "I foresaw this answer within the golden sparks of your thoughts."

65099b63-79ee-4cb7-b687-1d706bdef7ec.Text: "With all due respect, {name}, you already have a position of your own, that of a Rogue Trader. I am... heir to a Novator's throne. And it is for me to decide the fate that awaits House Orsellio."

9e184051-a58d-4d4c-8cd7-a817850e89ec.Text: {n}Cassia closes her eyes and speaks as if in a trance:{/n} "There was such power locked within this stone, such possibilities... It would make our Navigators' abilities several times stronger. No. It would magnify them by a factor of dozens! But the price was too high. After mere hours of use, the stone would always burn the minds of its hosts. So it was decided to break the Monolith into many shards, which were far easier for a human will to control."

2b3111db-20cd-4b0e-92ad-2099dc0f7a11.Text: "I-I cannot say where this memory sprang from. Perhaps I saw visions of Tisiphone in my dreams, and yet... I have seen all this so clearly... There was such power locked within this stone, such opportunities... It would make our Navigators' abilities several times stronger. No, it would magnify them by a factor of dozens! But the price was too high. After mere hours of use, the stone would always burn the minds of its hosts. That is why Tisiphone broke the Monolith into many shards, which were far easier for a human will to control."

61521522-a6fb-45d0-bdf8-a47f979c9c72.Text: "It means, mon-keigh, that your companion's ancestors sought to command the power of the Spirit Monolith and, yet, suffered failure time and again. Eventually, they discovered a way to harness this power: a terrible way, torturous and unforgivable. They shattered the Monolith into many shards and weakened the souls within.
