And then..." {n}The Harlequin trembles with fury.{/n} "Then they placed the shards inside their bodies to empower their abilities."

09b41721-daee-488f-ae75-9dc1900fdf1b.Text: "Who can say? The mere thought of it makes my heart skip a beat. Attempting to remove the Atlas surgically from a Navigator's body will end in their immediate demise the moment it is separated from their flesh. And if we were to destroy the Aeldari crystal on this world... I assume few would survive such an ordeal."

e5d9f0bb-b987-4dbe-a73c-1fca1352493b.Text: "The Atlas must be preserved and used for the good of the Imperium. To squander such a formidable artefact would be outrageous idiocy." {n}Cassia's red eyes are full of contempt, and her voice is uncharacteristically harsh.{/n} "The Setthala clan, myself... Tisiphone, and many subjects of mine have already paid for House Orsellio's power with their lives. I will prove that their sacrifices were not in vain."

e7a5a290-43df-481c-a3cb-9246968803d3.Text: "Alas, you are right, Outcast. The ancestors of the three-eyed mon-keigh sought to command the power of the Spirit Monolith, and yet they suffered failure time and again. Eventually, they discovered a way to harness this power: a terrible way, torturous and unforgivable. They shattered the Monolith into many shards and weakened the souls within. And then..." {n}The Harlequin trembles with fury.{/n} "Then they placed the shards of the Spirit Monolith inside their bodies to empower their abilities."

06366c88-a18d-4fa8-878e-1ccdde3428c5.Text: "No, your ancestors went further than that." {n}The Harlequin trembles with fury.{/n} "They placed the shards of the Spirit Monolith inside their bodies to empower their abilities."

7f12531b-e89a-4f21-b29a-f45281ac473e.Text: "You think the solution is so easy, don't you, mon-keigh? When you die, your souls become captives inside the Spirit Monolith. This process is deranging to our ancestors, who have served as the Monolith's guardians for aeons. It is equally agonising to the souls of your dead. And the more mon-keigh souls the Monolith absorbs... the more volatile it becomes. The Aeldari and the mon-keigh have spent many a dance battling for supremacy within the Monolith, and its integrity is waning. You sense it too."

827e3d33-53fb-4459-93a2-8a5d5f3df7cc.Text: "Rogue Trader! How dare you?" {n}Cassia frowns indignantly.{/n} "All this time, you guided me, you taught me by example that I have to learn to make difficult decisions on my own. Yet, today you intervened in my conversation with the Aeldari and put them all to death. That was... dishonourable of you!"

6f79719a-906b-49fe-92d1-4d82f5bd272b.Text: "You do love throwing other people's lives away, {name}, don't you?" {n}Cassia's voice quivers with fury.{/n} "But, as much as it pains me to admit it, House Orsellio has suffered long enough, both from Tisiphone's mistakes and its 'alliance' with you. You are right. It is high time we disposed of the Atlas for good and finally freed ourselves."

4a07dec5-9436-444e-8dee-f5036a76f172.Text: "Silence!" {n}Cassia's voice quivers with fury.{/n} "House Orsellio has suffered long enough, both from Tisiphone's mistakes and its 'alliance' with the Rogue Trader. It is time we decided our fate for ourselves, put an end to the Atlas once and for all... and freed ourselves."

ba351837-8608-4930-b6c7-014d9a00ac50.Text: "Enough!" {n}Cassia's red eyes are full of contempt and her voice is uncharacteristically harsh. The Navigator cannot help but shrink into a quivering ball under her gaze.{/n} "The Atlas must be preserved and used for the good of the Imperium! The Setthala clan, myself... Tisiphone, and many subjects of mine have already paid for House Orsellio's power with their lives. And I will prove that their sacrifices were not in vain."

4c33e58c-7321-48fb-a461-d80461f506cb.Text: "I..." {n}The regent's envoy hesitates, her long fingers with clear burn scars twitching nervously.{/n} "I understand. The Great Regent is not here, but I saw everything for myself. You are right. The time has come to put an end to Tisiphone's legacy. Long have we followed her instructions, too blind to notice how the Atlas was destroying the House and our very souls."

2e9b05ee-49db-4b27-88f5-93f85ad84eb1.Text: "Is it not true that everyone in this world is after power?" {n}Cassia's face is exceedingly untroubled and her gaze is distant and cold.{/n} "The Rogue Trader makes every effort to strengthen the von Valancius dynasty and trample the opposition. Then why wouldn't House Orsellio make use of a xeno-artefact for the sake of its blood and the Imperium itself?"

11e57e3d-eaef-4196-9705-c82d14dfbe9e.Text: "What disgrace..." {n}Cassia covers her eyes, and you feel your heart become gripped by her rage.{/n} "All this time, House Orsellio's grandeur has been built on lies and betrayal of its blood and the Imperium itself!"

2c8639cb-cf59-4bbf-b23b-72bc451733ad.Text: "Lady Cassia, will you do me a favour?"

a664ebd3-99c6-48fb-a0b1-8a88e674ac0e.Text: "I don't think that it will be easy for Tisiphone's opponents to accept the truth of what transpired here, even though I saw it for myself, saw in the Child a hope for the future and a reign that was not Tisiphone's. I will strive to convince my associates to give Lady Cassia a chance, for a reunited House Orsellio will grow twice as strong."

b15c5af4-7c87-4925-be72-406aad34839f.Text: "I came here to see the truth with my own eyes. And I have seen enough. Tisiphone was a monster, and you are worse than—"

1f86c789-e9b0-4dd7-82a3-a0a2968cec6b.Text: "What is this? The Rogue Trader and the traitors to the House have lured the Child into a trap set by xenos? I wish my eyes were deceiving me. But now I can see clearly that {d|Encyclopedia:CassiaQ1_RegenExecuted}Great Regent Ciretta{/d} was right to send us after your vessel." {n}The sturdily built woman is armed with a pistol, and yet, there are signs of exhaustion in her posture. Her face is hidden behind an encrusted three-eyed mask and her elaborate Navis Nobilite vestments are marred by dried blood and other evidence of recent combat.{/n}

7cc0af6b-b885-47bd-8453-44a2fe15c741.Text: "How dare you oppose me?" {n}Cassia's calm voice makes the Navigator flinch but she does not notice, for she only has eyes for you.{/n} "I do not want to be afraid anymore, {name}. Or to serve the House that has betrayed me time and again. That has used me as a soulless puppet. As Tisiphone's obedient substitute. I am... leaving. Leaving with you, {name}. I renounce my Novator's title."

bc63c04a-afbc-4387-82c4-556fcaf4524f.Text: "You think you can threaten us, foolish mon-keigh? The three-eyed one cannot break the Spirit Monolith. She does not possess the pow—"

66e33800-19ea-4346-804b-c9a6d666209f.Text: "I do. As you are well aware. It is what you all fear." {n}Cassia's calm voice causes the Harlequin Troupe to tense, but she does not notice, for she only has eyes for you.{/n} "I do not want to be afraid anymore, {name}. Or to serve the House that has betrayed me time and again. That has used me as a soulless puppet. As Tisiphone's obedient substitute. I am... leaving. Leaving with you, {name}. I renounce my Novator's title."

3f7cf01f-910f-4b52-a829-297142335bc6.Text: "Quite right." {n}An eerie smile brightens Cassia's face.{/n} "I knew you would understand me."

2706db9d-c853-4725-aa4d-8a698932f38c.Text: "You are ill-qualified to judge the merits of my House, {name} von Valancius. I can see your soul's colours all too well and there are plenty of darker shades within."

09411d4e-5938-4c4e-8278-1788f1388c63.Text: "The only way to free our ancestors from the pain is to separate the mon-keigh taint from the Spirit Monolith. My Troupe is here to perform just that. We all will play our parts today, and when the final act of this age-long tragedy begins, the mon-keigh players will exit this world's stage." {n}Sinister shadows dance on the Harlequin's mask as he draws an unknown device from his sleeve.{/n}

0ef49b53-3b93-4dbc-ad56-0ee2cd3c7d5d.Text: {n}Cassia nods curtly and looks back at the Navigators.{/n}

98d1ee38-b0b7-4f3d-af29-ffc6b9788c68.Text: {n}The Harlequin flinches reflexively but then his body instantly eases back.{/n} "Three-eyed mon-keigh who sees into Sha'eil, the taint of your ancestors has begun to consume your body and soul. Pathetic fools with an insatiable lust for power that is not yours. Ending your misery will be merciful."

6ea6d049-51dc-468b-810b-43bb73ce1ef3.Text: {n}The xenos thinks for a moment.{/n} "You mon-keigh have desecrated our ancient world. I see no reason to assist you with the final dance."

0a6d4528-5655-4989-b956-052b56b55d77.Text: {n}Surrounded by the Navigators' groans, the Harlequin presses and holds a button on the strange device in his hands.{/n} "This play has dragged on long enough. It is time for the closing scene, mon-keigh. For too long have we searched for this world and the shard within the three-eyed one's chest, the first of the tainted shards. And we will give this world back to the souls of our ancestors."

bec47b02-d285-4a17-8c81-ff592acc79fe.Text: "It is true, {name}. I..." {n}Cassia lowers her lashes, desperately trying to hide the tears welling in her eyes.{/n} "I wish to say yes, but it is not within my gift to do so. Not after what we learned about the Atlas. Not after what Tisiphone did."

7cef7d67-c306-45b7-97fa-764ec65fe641.Text: "And what... are we supposed to do now?"

de34abc7-adaf-4c2a-a521-24440381ac98.Text: "In the time since we met, you have taught me many heartless yet valuable lessons, Lord Captain. And I am grateful to you, I truly am. You have opened my eyes to many truths. Life isn't a book, not someone's imagined and beautifully told story. And now it is time for me, the Novator of House Orsellio, to take care of my family. A relationship with you... will only distract me from performing my duty."

b35d8c1d-0dc6-4159-bcad-4395969ca5ed.Text: "You can't. We are in the middle of a warp storm. Without a Navigator who knows the way back, you are doomed." {n}Cassia's smile is cold and cruel. Just like yours is whenever you decide the fate of others.{/n}

ca29a002-7ae6-4a9a-bee1-1d962976c35f.Text: "Perhaps... the three-eyed mon-keigh who see into Sha'eil could be of use to the Troupe. They do not fear the realm of She Who Thirsts — they cut through it on their steel-winged birds. They even found their way to a Crone World that was hidden from our sight." {n}The Harlequin lowers his head in thought.{/n} "Your words are harmonious, mon-keigh. But what will your companions say?"

e721e470-6d6d-4271-bc35-8c4f76a188a0.Text: {n}Her gaze, tender and full of sorrow, comes to rest on you.{/n} "Let us discuss our relationship away from this place. Assuming, of course, that we survive the day."

5932a36b-f58b-43b6-b1c4-e129e18e3eec.Text: {n}Cassia shrugs.{/n} "The tyrant's heiress you loathe so much no longer has a claim to the throne. You have your freedom. Isn't that what you have all craved for so long? Elect a worthy Novator for yourselves. Pave a new path for House Orsellio. Restore the concord between the inner clans... But don't even think of harming me or the Rogue Trader — or you will face the wrath of my Atlas."

c283a3e0-1648-434b-a6e7-e4799a101ff9.Text: {n}The Navigators are staring at you, at Cassia, and at each other, incapable of processing what has just happened.{/n}

223e153d-4911-4c0a-9fdd-a4f06df1054d.Text: "Three-eyed mon-keigh who sees into Sha'eil, the taint of your ancestors has begun to consume your body and soul. Pathetic fools with an insatiable lust for power that is not yours. Ending your misery will be merciful."

7bf0cccf-5a47-4138-8537-8df5f66705aa.Text: "I..." {n}Cassia freezes hesitantly, only for her frightened gaze to harden.{/n} "I shan't explain myself to a xenos. Do you wish to know what I think? The Atlas must be saved, and we must continue using it for the good of Humanity, and not that of ghastly creatures such as these. Now then, whose side are you on, Rogue Trader?"

6470a4c3-e938-4e20-9e88-5c0f9dd6c9fb.Text: "If I only had the courage to tear this curse out of my chest with my own hands, I would have done so already." {n}Cassia looks at the Harlequin defiantly.{/n} "Heed my wish, xenos: do it. Free my House from its bane. Break the chains that are tightening around the necks of our ancestors, whatever the cost may be. If House Orsellio is destined to perish for Tisiphone's malefactions, so be it."

d71eba60-ad92-42a7-ad1a-700cc0f3f2a8.Text: "Taint? Do you... mean the Atlas... xenos traitor?"

c9c1c097-6222-47a0-b973-edcd83831773.Text: "No! I won't allow that to happen! Rogue Trader, pray, make them see reason! If the Koronus Expanse loses a Navigator House, turmoil will engulf worlds and stations that cannot exist without the seeing eye of the Navis Nobilite, and Rogue Traders' fleets will fare no better. Your dynasty too will be affected!"

789484dd-477f-4d48-bae6-78b566fbfad3.Text: "It is too late, mon-keigh. All the characters have already taken their places upon the stage and you have a major role to play."

9c6b7ad0-07f1-498c-9513-728ee2a052ce.Text: {n}The Harlequin remains as still as a garish statue for several minutes. Then the mellifluous voice behind the mask says,{/n} "I am willing to try, mon-keigh."

a5d69218-cf9c-4722-b485-73c6f9a967cc.Text: {n}The Harlequin tilts his head in surprise, looks at you and Cassia in turn, and then stifles a chuckle.{/n} "What makes you mon-keigh think that I will do your bidding? I am not the executioner of three-eyed mon-keigh who see into Sha'eil, oh no. I am the bane of all who have tainted this Crone World with their presence. Let the final dance begin!" {n}The Harlequin bows theatrically as he presses and holds a button on the strange device in his hands.{/n}

15785624-f19c-423b-ad77-cd2d7e63ced9.Text: "I need to think this through one more time."

47a6e2ff-a5a3-46c4-b291-27efa02bf24d.Text: "A cloud of mottled hues surrounds you, making you lose focus. You mustn't let them cloud your reason."

97a49231-3264-45e7-be36-8c8185ff9cea.Text: "There is another path, my lady. Here and now. Cast your House's troubles aside. Be with me for as long as the stars allow us."

fff059e1-9921-42f4-8e83-c4a4e919b50b.Text: "The time is exactly right. Renounce your House that sees you as nothing but a spiritless 'child' and an enemy. Let the Atlas act as your shield, for neither the xenos nor the Navigators will risk threatening you, knowing that you can destroy the Spirit Monolith with your mind."

d540ce27-fdbd-4ea0-9dd2-17a607eec183.Text: {n}Cassia raises her eyebrows and suddenly bursts into mirthless laughter.{/n} "Oh, {name}, do you truly believe that you and I have a future? I see your colours. I always have. The whiteness of your gentle words fades in the face of your cruelty, which you seldom make any effort to conceal."

b01906c9-12ef-4b01-b93d-04c6df27554d.Text: "You are a frightening and ruthless person, {name}. You always have your way, it's true, but I am terrified. And sometimes... sometimes I hate you. In spite of the feelings that your presence awakens in my heart... No. I will never be yours. This is it, Rogue Trader. Accept my rejection with dignity."

8cda9531-aa3b-48f4-a6fb-5830ad3c0184.Text: "{name}, what are you... Not at a time like this..."

39d12b80-e07d-4000-9c8f-e8484f46402c.Text: "What drivel! You are the sacred Child, you cannot desert our House—"

96d9052e-3847-415d-a8a3-3f86f2699c7f.Text: "I never expected to hear such words from the mouth of the cursed Child." {n}The Navigator slowly bows his head.{/n} "Child... no, Lady Cassia. If such is your decision, House Orsellio will follow you. The time has come for us to do away with the dark pages of our House's history."

16e3c508-2f72-47ca-97a4-b9f60932c70b.Text: "Damned xenos! This was not the bargain we struck, Throne smite you!" {n}The Navigator whose skin is so thin that it reveals the muscles, bones, and innards underneath clenches his augmented gold jaw in contempt.{/n}

0be0f207-95c2-4e6b-9ab2-ebb32459beaf.Text: "I am confident in my abilities. More so than ever before."

68d1a1d8-d043-438f-9877-778c35427024.Text: "If you attack my people, elantach, you can abolish all memory of our alliance." {n}Yrliet clutches the spirit stone on her chest.{/n} "You mon-keigh ruin all that you touch."

1bffac51-3b51-4678-9f73-d823d5a1849d.Text: "You are both part of my retinue. I will not choose between you."

fb76871e-0b46-4773-81e8-981d2bf893fe.Text: "You will have to, elantach, or else I will make the choice for you. And it will not be to your liking."

7e234d67-0db4-4e97-8dd8-62173f9a21f5.Text: "So many red flames have just burst from your heart, Yrliet." {n}Cassia's gaze is full of sympathy for the Aeldari.{/n} "I never meant to harm you or your kin. But if it is my death you desire, I will not go down without a fight."

13c1525e-0a4b-4a62-bf52-829855ebaea9.Text: "Well, elantach. Our paths have diverged at last."

58975e81-8fa3-42c5-b3ab-42d03bdf9aef.Text: "Rogue Trader, surely you do not consider this a difficult choice? A Navigator of the Imperium and a xenos rogue despised even by her own kind?"

73325396-a0f7-43fd-9fe5-1b9f64b73a1d.Text:
"There was a time when I believed that I would lead my House to prosperity. In truth, fortune and blessings have long since been passing us by, as if the Koronus Expanse itself is trying to oust the Orsellio children from its bounds. If nothing changes in the near future, all of us will wither like night flowers at dawn — or perhaps, face our ultimate fall.
***
Upon my word, the Sea of Souls itself must favour me! During the last jump, I saw into the eye of a vicious storm. Within it, amid the ruins of a xenos world, was a treasure, mighty and dangerous, not unlike our own power. And I found a way to reach it! I drive away the memory of our journey and the cost that our House suffered. The ritual alone was... No matter! The goal will be worth the price, and due effort is all that is needed of us.
***
By the grace of the Emperor, we made it through that terrible tempest! However, the Aeldari ruins appear to have dampened the crew's spirits. Those pitiful commoners talk too much. Tensions in the camp are rising... I should cut out the tongues of those who witnessed the first experiments — this information cannot be allowed to reach the ship. No, not just them. I shall have the Setthala clan dock the tongue of every lowborn."

a0dffbac-d6c1-4b7f-b72e-93246317ca16.Text: "You have made great strides in learning how to keep them at bay. I commend your perseverance."

74457100-45ef-4735-b155-b6c573ad7a79.Text: "Your efforts are lacking. I suggest you try harder, because my patience is bound to run out eventually."

3b87bb7f-3de5-4578-93b3-c653c1d19013.Text: "And why, pray tell, should I go on this suicidal escapade to Throne knows where?"

4630806f-c85f-42e0-acee-9d7be719b9d2.Text: "What else did the visions tell you?"

0e486bb9-9f6b-41af-851e-372dc56f5b43.Text: "What makes you so sure that you will find the way to this physical manifestation of the Atlas?"

551304d9-5574-47d2-a4c0-a3d7272e53b3.Text: "Has the warp twisted your mind? How can you trust visions of such dubious origin?"

237ab0e1-6afa-49fa-8761-8509f949180d.Text: "I have had enough of these Navigator troubles. These are your House's matters to deal with, and I no longer wish to have anything to do with them."

6148e9a9-a452-45a8-8ad9-f7ea61f14484.Text: "I need time to think it over."

4cc60a4d-b623-4c7a-aeb9-adecd99d8622.Text: "Was there something you wished to tell me?"

5127e1f6-f268-4cb8-80ca-2a470f725441.Text: "You are standing on the cusp of a great discovery for all of House Orsellio. Inviting the regent seems like the sensible thing to do."

6b14d1af-ee3b-4f7f-92dc-ba833eedce31.Text: "If you wish to show the House your strength and undauntable spirit, invite the renegades to be the first to touch the secrets of the Atlas they loathe so much."

c5a411c2-809a-407a-9beb-301c43a4e36f.Text: "You are asking me to cast my lot with renegades and murderers?" {n}Cassia frowns, and you can feel her unease as if it were your own.{/n} "Only three in ten suicidal expeditions meet with success, and only if the followers have undying loyalty to their leadership. Of those with divided crew, however, none survive."

e6d3f820-b902-420d-9973-1d6c5bf02723.Text: "Then it is best that we go alone."

5039eb61-33df-4459-9ecc-d34e772b3bce.Text: "Trust me. I shall stay by your side and let no harm come to you."

ea7dd15f-875d-4922-ba84-601c5c278108.Text: "Show the renegades your resolve! And if something goes wrong, my people will blast their heads off."

c014fb32-d3d2-452d-96b2-71cd9e5e6b68.Text: "Burdens ought to be shared with your loyal followers, not shouldered on your own."

3e4743e1-bd77-407f-b957-cedf8493de49.Text: "And what about my crew? Do you concern yourself with their lives at all? I urge you to think twice before answering."

5d187785-e0ae-44db-b490-20d3d24c7a53.Text: {n}Cassia tiredly rubs her breastplate where it conceals the Atlas, then nods.{/n} "I will pass on the invitation to the regent, but it would be unreasonable to hope that the incumbent leader will join this expedition. After the events on Dargonus, all of House Orsellio trembles before you, and I doubt my family will take the risk."

4a8df1f2-d1f8-4ae8-8050-dc73ea2c29a7.Text: "It is my duty as the head of the House to carry such burdens. Why are you trying to convince me to imperil my subjects?"

5b834a25-4f22-447f-8ec9-5900d0e148d4.Text: "I..." {n}Cassia looks around helplessly but cannot give you an answer. She bows her head in shame.{/n} "I am sorry... It is the only way."

87ad995b-003c-4175-9bd3-ff3d08dc7634.Text: {n}Cassia breathes a sigh of relief, but the look in her ruby eyes quickly darkens again.{/n} "The House is still watching me. Both the renegades and the loyalists. I doubt that any of them will agree even to a brief armistice for the sake of learning the truth about the Atlas's origins. And I... do not wish to see House Orsellio lose even one more life to another fratricidal skirmish. No. I shall go after the answers about our past on my own."

3f9eabf2-e4d0-4a47-a3a1-16472da1ff2d.Text: "I do not think any of them will agree even to a brief armistice. They abhor each other with such vehemence, they would rather spill every drop of Orsellio blood than see the Novator's throne go to the other side."

6face91b-4d54-4e4a-b586-cfe49653ed0b.Text: "I have already told you that I do not wish to imperil the Orsellio Navigators further. It is possible that they will still take on this terrible risk and follow us, listening to the echoes of my Atlas for guidance... And yet, I do hope that my subjects are not that senseless. No, Lord Captain, I must tread this path myself."

331c9df0-adab-4bbb-b1d1-877847f0ebaa.Text: {n}Cassia's shoulders relax a little.{/n} "Thank you for your understanding, Rogue Trader. And now permit me to take my leave. I must start preparing for the journey. From what I have been able to glean, we must first travel to the—" {n}Her ruby-red eyes widen in astonishment.{/n} "—the Orsellio Prophecy System. Odd that. Could it be that the historical records are lying? And Kaleyn Orsellio is not whom the star system is named after? Either way, that was the system from which Tisiphone embarked on her journey, and we are going to follow in her long-forgotten footsteps."

9e3bbb82-96c8-478f-a476-fbfa272c30b9.Text: "The renegades will do anything to kill the cursed Child. To kill me. I do not want traitors to sabotage our voyage across the Sea of Souls and forever bury us amid the horrors of the warp. That would leave both our dynasties leaderless, wouldn't you agree?"

273f8ae3-84cf-4e71-aa8e-8984cb47e74a.Text: "If I were to turn my enemies into allies... it would help House Orsellio heal its wounds. Some of them, at least." {n}Cassia tiredly rubs her breastplate where it conceals the Atlas.{/n} "Let it be as you say, Rogue Trader. I will pass on the invitation to the renegades' leader. But even if the head of the rebellion agrees to this, they will never join the expedition in person. After the events on Dargonus, all of House Orsellio trembles before you, and I doubt the traitors are eager to take unnecessary risks."

b9e67fa2-9005-48fc-a038-a29ab25bffe0.Text: "And now permit me to take my leave. I must start preparing for the journey. From what I have been able to glean, we must first travel to the—" {n}Her ruby-red eyes widen in astonishment.{/n} "—the Orsellio Prophecy System. Odd that. Could it be that the historical records are lying? And Kaleyn Orsellio is not whom the star system is named after? Either way, that was the system from which Tisiphone embarked on her journey, and we are going to follow in her long-forgotten footsteps."

bada96f1-d2ee-4356-a50a-2dac00836e64.Text: "I cannot understand the reason for your persistence, {name}. Why put the safety of your crew on the line for a band of traitors from a Navigator House? They hardly wish to see my resolve — they would rather see my heart ripped out of my chest."

88a1648f-600b-4a20-bb15-03517e6c2632.Text: "{name}! How wonderful it is that I've found you here." {n}Uncontrollable anxiety washes over your body, causing you to lose your breath. Cassia notices this, closes her eyes, and you are released from the grip of emotions that are not your own.{/n} "Please forgive me. My powers... are sometimes too insistent in their attempts to break free from my control."

00c07a48-2f48-42b2-841e-be0c012b5f01.Text: "But the visions told me an altogether different story, one where the Setthalas helped Tisiphone create the Atlas! And they vanished immediately after the experiments were done with. Perhaps I can... no, I know I can find the way to the Palace of the Atlas if I recreate Tisiphone's journey from my visions. A real palace, not the psychophysical illusion to which the Orsellio Navigators can reach out. I have always had a feeling that it truly exists in our world. Now, however... I know it with absolute certainty."

dfa90710-a8da-475a-b5ed-e8b992711a01.Text: "I... My House has nothing more to offer you, {name}." {n}Cassia bows her head much lower than what the dignity of one of the Navis Nobilite would normally allow.{/n} "Perhaps the Palace of the Atlas holds a reward that will surpass all our expectations. Perhaps we will discover nothing more than the grey ash of disappointment. And yet, we have walked a long road together, side by side. I surrender myself to your magnanimity... for the last time."

c6e2886a-82d1-4952-9e24-06be44a9917b.Text: "I saw Tisiphone experience an epiphany in a dream — just like my visions came to me on our travels through the warp. She... beheld a planet hidden behind roiling warp storms. The world promised her great power, so Tisiphone gathered the Setthalas, her most devout followers, to go on a suicidal journey through the tempest. I know not the details of what happened on that planet, but it was there that the Setthalas sacrificed themselves for an experiment of some kind, and it was there that House Orsellio obtained its Starway Atlas."

c98393f2-2bd9-4cc9-bc44-c56efbff0e9c.Text: {n}Cassia shrugs coldly.{/n} "I have spoken with the House's Navigators through the Atlas. These days, I can feel with increasing clarity how our connection is growing stronger. The renegades have destroyed several more void estates, and internal skirmishes with fatal consequences are occurring on an alarmingly regular basis. Sacred Orsellio blood is being spilt... That is utterly lamentable. But unsurprising, considering your {d|Encyclopedia:Ch1_Cassia_KilledBothNavis}fit of bloodlust on Eurac V{/d} and your merciless actions that {d|Encyclopedia:CassiaQ1_AllExecuted}left not one but two leaders of the feuding sides decapitated{/d} at the official reception on Dargonus."

a28b44ca-8d26-47ad-8515-9db3403a11f7.Text: "I came to deliver good tidings. I have spoken with the House's Navigators through the Atlas. Of late, I can feel with increasing clarity how our connection is growing stronger. Despite the dissent in its midst, House Orsellio has been able to keep a precarious equilibrium, thanks in part to your unexpected arrival on Eurac V and the resolution of the conflict at the Dargonus reception. Not all Orsellios concur with your decisions, but none can deny the impact that you, and no one else, have had on the House's present state of affairs."

221e26e5-0ca0-43cf-bb04-d6fe936b69fe.Text: "For the first time ever, I have an opportunity to find answers to the questions my mentors so deftly avoided. Why did Tisiphone choose me? What is the Atlas? Is it true that House Orsellio's past is drenched in blood? Please, {name}, do not snap this tautly drawn string of destiny — my destiny! Journey with me in Tisiphone's wake to the distant stars!"

70418e86-a8d1-45b8-8403-2d8e45ed3d16.Text: "In that case... I shall humbly await your decision. You know where you can find me."

f27519e4-5483-441b-9bb8-b5a95c3f9188.Text: {n}Cassia clenches her fists, her claws cutting into her palms, and a few ruby droplets stain the hem of her garb.{/n} "I see. I... I shall never disturb you again, Rogue Trader."

fee4b18a-f223-4d99-905a-a4c123f3c84c.Text: {n}Cassia's silvery eyelashes are stained with scarlet.{/n} "Rogue Trader, please..."

a0221b92-e5be-4b61-ba24-86c52f41c491.Text: "Rogue Trader? More often than not, whenever I find myself in your presence, greyish-blue mist surrounds me soon afterward." {n}Despondency. Irritation. Disappointment. The moment Cassia enters the room, you feel a wave of emotions that are not your own.{/n} "Ah, I beg your forgiveness. My powers cannot stop trying to break free from my control."

fc7750e5-15b8-4081-9a60-7ebcad002263.Text: {n}Cassia nods gratefully, lowers her gaze, and clasps her hands together.{/n} "There is more I wish to tell you. It is about... the visions that I have come to experience at an increasing rate during warp jumps. The same visions come to me again, and again, and again... It is as if I am going mad. For you see, these visions are about me, the Atlas, and Tisiphone Orsellio, the House's previous Novator. I have seen Tisiphone's experiments, the ones that involved the Navigators from the Setthala branch, which she was rumoured to have destroyed for disobedience."

dd80594e-1009-4a58-bce1-163342ce2108.Text: "However, I am not here to reproach you for the deeds of yore. Instead, I wish to tell you of the visions that I have come to experience at an increasing rate during warp jumps. The same visions come to me again, and again, and again... It is as if I am going mad. For you see, these visions are about me, the Atlas, and Tisiphone Orsellio, the House's previous Novator. I have seen Tisiphone's experiments, the ones that involved the Navigators from the Setthala branch, which she was rumoured to have destroyed for disobedience."

5ea606b4-330f-4035-ad43-e15ab8c1bb20.Text: "Yes... I bring good tidings! Because of House von Valancius's support, House Orsellio has survived, despite the dissent within. On behalf of the Orsellio Navigators and myself, please accept our sincerest gratitude."

1f47f0c4-2030-40a1-9555-a2bd0808cedb.Text: "I shan't beg you." {n}Cassia's eyes remain impassive, but she cannot stop her pale lips from trembling.{/n} "Should the anthracite vice around your heart ever change to... lighter shades... you know where you can find me."

0e028023-2cec-4f4f-982f-0b73c0bfe3a5.Text: {n}Cassia frowns warily.{/n} "If that is your opinion... I will heed your words."

85a5578e-734b-4854-aed7-5139418f7747.Text: "I have been informed that House Orsellio will soon convene its Grand Council. Would it not be better to wait for it to finish first?"

e2acc81f-18bc-48c7-abcf-adaff53e1805.Text: "I cannot shake a certain foreboding about the upcoming meeting in the incorporeal Palace of the Atlas. Troubling mirages have plagued my mind for many nights now. Voices calling and cursing my name. And the more I use the Atlas, the clearer the visions become and the louder the voices grow... and the further my powers wane. I am certain that all of the House is experiencing the same, for all of us are connected. I can sense my family's fear. House Orsellio is doomed to perish in darkness should I fail to discover the reason why the Atlas is weakening. And that reason... I believe it is hidden somewhere in my visions of Tisiphone."

d4f0927a-0ef7-449d-98cb-f5790291b459.Text: "I cannot shake a certain foreboding about the upcoming meeting in the incorporeal Palace of the Atlas. Troubling mirages have plagued my mind for many nights now. Voices calling and cursing my name. And the more I use the Atlas, the clearer the visions become and the louder the voices grow... and the further my powers wane. I am certain that all of the House is experiencing the same, for all of us are connected. I can sense my family's fear. House Orsellio is doomed to perish in darkness should I fail to discover the reason why the Atlas is weakening. And that reason... I believe it is hidden somewhere in my visions of Tisiphone."

cf5c5cd9-3527-4405-a0cf-b086c2482c63.Text: "Estimated probability of conflict: inevitable. Initiating //retreat//confrontation avoidance//redeployment// protocol."

1c3eab03-97bd-49fe-997f-6c136798523e.Text: "Heretek Pasqal, I will wreak punishment upon you in the name of the Deus Mechanicus!"

6537686f-7f9f-4b7d-a71a-5c44f4a2c009.Text: "Abel, why did you decide to come with us?"

dc02bae6-d28d-452e-bdaf-4fd267de2c14.Text: "What do you make of this camp?"

3cbd2a40-5c01-4aff-8e98-f190f17a0220.Text: "What do you think happened to this ship?"

1f8389e0-f248-4fd5-bbe9-8d389ab5093c.Text: "Do you understand what is going on here?"

5e0f5fd3-f566-4ae7-9da7-3899047eaa25.Text: {n}Quiet and mysterious as always, Abel Haneumann's demeanour is a mixture of cautiousness and curiosity as he inspects the ship's ruined interior. When you approach him, he acknowledges you by saying softly,{/n} "Death's footsteps were heard here."

a00bc4dc-7b9c-4a0b-9a79-66294497585f.Text: "The Cycle is on the verge of being discontinued. Doubt has opened its maw wide, bidding us enter."

a45d8115-848a-43a4-9078-57372c1ad324.Text: {n}Abel looks upon the tech-barbarians with a moderate degree of curiosity, without attempting to approach or interact with them. Occasionally his gaze rests on some sacred item covered in tribal imagery or otherwise desecrated, and he raises his eyebrows, evidently pained.{/n}

e934f03f-337c-417b-b22f-8e4d45a3c99c.Text: {n}Abel averts his eyes in embarrassment and says, almost shyly,{/n} "A hunt. The hunter is coming."

dbfefe07-d0d9-462b-8148-5ac3a51c3307.Text: {n}Abel shakes his head in shame and hastens to break eye contact with you.{/n}

c5358d25-b623-4df5-9837-7101c20f1168.Text: "The hunter? The Maimed Hunter?" {n}Pasqal places a mechadendrite claw on Abel's shoulder, demanding an answer. Abel nods.{/n} "The Maimed Hunter. That persona occurred in the data I decrypted. Unfortunately, the sum total of information on it is very near zero."

b9f3ecb2-5002-4b9b-90ef-a14a043e3e36.Text: "The sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Archeotech}Archeotech{/g} and the profane have mixed, like tainted water and sacred unguent."

4d58a6bd-90b4-4fc3-9679-8e917f75fd65.Text: {n}Suddenly a smile appears on his face.{/n} "This has happened before. The spirit transcends the body. The matter in which it manifests itself is transformed into something more spirit-like."

81564dbb-20dd-4874-9214-cc218bd4f9f6.Text: "An epiphany. Followed by doubt. Followed by debate. Followed by Judgement— no, a lack of Judgement." {n}Abel's speech becomes fragmentary.{/n} "A contradiction. A dilemma, resulting in antagonism..."

9dc4ae9a-f82f-482b-a59c-0addb58ca56f.Text: "My tech-comrade insisted on taking part in this excursion. This is as much of a priority mission for him as it is for me. We are both expecting to meet our mentor, Amarnat."

c410b456-1a78-42ec-948b-f6bd19083b8c.Text: "Now everything is clear. A battle was fought here, and during preparations for it, Amarnat declared the observatorium off-limits. Even to fellow servants of the Omnissiah, the Explorators. It was an internal conflict, and he expected his erstwhile tech-comrades to become his enemies."

a2e516d8-ff7d-46ba-85a2-f12c8a76b49f.Text: "A conflict. There was a conflict here."

43799173-3d53-4aca-9367-4f21908089de.Text: "I am registering residual traces of paper combustion inside this cogitator's casing. Did they... fuel this repository of knowledge with books?"

3bfd8584-8847-4cc8-a1d2-5dca52b8ea17.Text: "Something simply ordered the spirit of this machine to die."

6db71ca3-15fb-4714-afbc-79fe2273d6dc.Text: "I recognise the pattern of the chant. They are imitating a reactor shutdown vigil."

81d62524-8a9c-40ce-9edb-6a069265cef8.Text: "I am registering a deviation from the rite. Orderly procedure was not followed during sacred unguent replacement."

286ed381-dbee-4c1e-967e-712428e21c66.Text: The ventilation shaft feeding air onto the decks is surrounded by generous offerings.

a8a523ab-f09d-40d5-adca-2dcd419c5216.Text: "How dare they set up camp right in the heart of the sacred machine! This is a sacrilege against the blessed remains!"

47dd22ad-89c6-43a9-a1c9-23c38963973b.Text: The handprints and footprints indicate that the locals have turned the sacred unguent tank into something like a ritual font.

27c3d86b-597a-479d-9673-167e84df3956.Text: Primitive amulets with decorative carvings hang from the vox-antenna.

a52a6ff0-d234-4d7d-aa4a-176aeb68f847.Text: "This cogitator's pattern is so old and sacred I have never seen the like of it before. I have only heard about them from fragments of legend."

8aad0775-0560-46bb-bca4-9b2350587dd2.Text: "These barbarians are pillaging the ship's supplies. I am registering a Category Nine blasphemy."

04127996-9273-44c0-b78c-b4988533c763.Text: "The barbaric inscriptions blasphemously profaning the flesh of this sacred machine echo the words of the requiem of reverent shutdown."

1dbf2c1a-1752-463c-bd05-86be630de4e4.Text: "This noble warrior's armour and augmetics are undamaged, and yet they are dead. What killed them?"

c4abc271-bbfa-4841-99ad-65dc10b7a5a7.Text: The cogitator's screen glows faintly. You take a closer look and realise it has been gutted, its innards replaced with candles that cast glints on the black plex-glass.

83f6f8a1-b5f4-4580-8462-f506691e5ab6.Text: Someone tried to lubricate the cog with blood, only for it to form a dry crust that bound the mechanism forever.

f2a5e2a6-a6b2-49be-a61a-698a6d07d23b.Text: "I will not let you win! I will destroy this ship! I—"

be255681-52f0-469f-b826-41afc859b21b.Text: "Your defeat is predetermined! No other outcome is possible!"

a8f13f07-72a2-4fe8-9035-773f1b2ecf2c.Text: "This marking does not follow fleet protocol. This constitutes a Category Ten blasphemy."

964fc88c-2771-4f08-b35f-1e76d9d1cd66.Text: "The halls of this holy ship feel strangely familiar to me."

088c0da7-b9f0-4bb5-acd4-b5db1f441016.Text: "I feel as though I am walking through a crime scene."

535ed4bb-38ec-48cb-9f32-7795027dd2b9.Text: "This holy ship's deplorable condition is an unacceptable heresy!"

4b0042f0-7a68-44c6-9b21-2a0257131565.Text: "This vessel is furnished throughout with extraordinarily ancient and sacred mechanisms! What a great temple it used to be!"

3320b823-a7a2-40a1-a792-2326075b80b4.Text: The majestic metal statue is frozen in a menacing combative pose.

b3677cfb-2d35-4e63-98fe-454132554147.Text: This ancient warrior's flesh was once enhanced with priceless augmetics, but they are dormant now.

18b60dc8-03b1-40fd-950c-1162d749aa9d.Text: The tribesman avoids your gaze and makes a strange gesture — probably some kind of ritual — as you approach.

d73ba59c-ae68-461f-89e4-dd90a0f95870.Text: "This is odd. I see scratch marks from a servo-claw on this venerable Skitarius's armour."

31c6c722-74bf-496c-b699-bb8a3a655234.Text: A thick layer of candle snuff covers the mechanisms, paralysing the formidable weapon.

a0dfc031-f657-4db5-8c74-ef47c8c62482.Text: "What kind of paranoia drove the crew to place the cannon platform here, in the very heart of the ship?"

bae340b0-58c9-47b7-8639-17a58a0fe25d.Text: "I am registering evidence that a volkite carbine was fired here. I am registering a protocol violation: use of weapons by Adeptus Mechanicus soldiers inside one of the ship's bays."

126ca150-cc70-47f8-9aab-795df00566ef.Text: "The bay was breached from the inside. Traces of scaling suggest the use of a melta charge."

7142cd30-a326-47dd-aeae-e1d41967049d.Text: "Now everything is clear. A battle was fought here, and during preparations for it, Amarnat declared the observatorium off-limits."

28efd915-c561-4514-926f-62b5754cb581.Text: "Even to fellow servants of the Omnissiah, the Explorators. It was an internal conflict, and he expected his erstwhile tech-comrades to become his enemies."

e639da94-9561-433a-9713-06a70f7d65cd.Text: [Smile at Nihel] "This is my companion, Pasqal Haneumann. And you made a mistake in meddling with him."

28f4a4ed-b8ec-4a19-a362-e4e9aa7fed83.Text: "We are looking for Archmagos Amarnat. And we want answers."

e4681ca4-5a8e-4460-8ea9-4ecbd67b1b5f.Text: "Locals spoke of a ghost without a face. Did they mean you?"

5632ade2-d73f-4c87-8e5c-5b2f0f1cf96d.Text: "Are you saying Pasqal is part of that hivemind?"

d8bfc8cc-c618-4a9d-b2eb-113606e2ddc7.Text: "So the Tech-Priests of the name Haneumann are all parts of Amarnat?"

818d1e05-7a43-431a-b4cf-4081063e02a8.Text: "Did Amarnat believe he could form again? The plan sounds... risky."

990b6677-b3e3-4ff5-bcdb-f64243c1f098.Text: "You are the Maimed Hunter. You tried to kill the other Haneumanns."

0c464786-27f4-42e5-bcc4-fdda049a1302.Text: "Idiot. Calcazar was harbouring Axiomantha the whole time. She was working for him."

c037c0e3-67ea-4e15-9f55-ec8c7e0cb303.Text: "You betrayed your brothers and sisters. Such an act is unforgivable."

21101ac9-0937-4108-9b42-72125ee487fc.Text: "Yours was a grim duty. But you were unflinching in fulfilling it."

1da9e4f6-c229-4884-8edb-02ffefa4e848.Text: "You must not fight! We are surrounded by enemies. Enough blood has been shed."

d51be0f1-4c36-4d27-8da2-d97d6073df9f.Text: "You are right, Pasqal. You are the decision maker."

08729564-e899-4a28-b8ee-331d2e530a87.Text: "If anyone cares to hear a Rogue Trader's opinion on the matter, I—"

de2dbb91-dde5-40a3-b9d9-d65820f066b4.Text: "Think about what she said, Pasqal. Your secret is dangerous."

c5be56b9-d531-4ad8-84fa-77d8ba822e49.Text: "You are from Calcazar's retinue. Does he have anything to do with this?"

8a94cdc0-a939-4006-b620-44ae52238f30.Text: "That is your problem. You have always been too sceptical."

fa557f00-06e4-4319-bd86-c7d23350035d.Text: "The salutatory procedure will be performed, and the identification codes verified after the priority request has been executed — tell me where the blessed Amarnat is!" {n}Pasqal's voice clangs like steel.{/n}

6548d76a-2882-4faa-867c-b75eee985885.Text: {n}The face of the Tech-Priest standing opposite is hidden behind a brass mask. Rather than being one piece, it is assembled from the fragments of many augmetics. You have met this man before. He is called Brasswhisper, a member of Lord Inquisitor Calcazar's retinue.{/n}

1b584e13-e685-4d0f-b689-d490ad96a1f6.Text: {n}A cracked chuckle comes from behind the mask.{/n} "You still don't understand..."

421c3c47-e9f0-4619-b131-abbb9d48c398.Text: {n}The green energy entangles Nihel like a net, burning her True Flesh, draining the life force from her augmetics and mechanical components. But she focuses her will and strikes back at Pasqal with a pulse of her own. The rattling voice, no longer human, rages and roars like a forest fire:{/n} "I refuse to recognise you as the Messiah! I do not believe in you!"

d53a382e-2e2a-4fb9-b433-6413a4c05396.Text: {n}Nihel's disfigured lips twist, and seeds of dismay sprout in her voice:{/n} "I lured you here for a reason, Pasqal. I wanted you to see what our followers had become. This is what deviation from dogma ends in! Breach of canon begets ignorance. Ignorance begets blasphemy!"

090f0fb1-57eb-4656-ab8b-d524e9e05c08.Text: {n}Pasqal's reply sweeps Nihel's words away like a gust of wind. His optical visor turns a blinding blue.{/n} "No, tech-sister. Refraining from resistance was never our way. I am an Explorator, a reconnoitrer of Knowledge. I have brought fire to a hundred worlds. I have gleaned a thousand secrets in the darkness. I am an agent of unbridled will! I will not yield to oblivion, for oblivion itself fears me."

bd6557ce-5b4b-4d09-be43-bf7c308c9001.Text: "Response: affirmative. In order to move the Hermetico out of the Procession of the Damned, we had to disturb the pitiful locals."

6e088ca7-7c76-44e9-85ff-c76fd5094c0b.Text: "You wanted me to awaken, tech-sister. Here I am. Holding you to account."

516b287e-2fd2-4e16-a9be-07bc24295ab6.Text: Pasqal disagrees. What do you want

2ca15eb9-5361-4b4b-8e93-119650d1e24a.Text: {n}Pasqal interrupts you with an extremely commanding gesture of his mechadendrite.{/n} "There is no need for that. This debate, this dilemma, is ours alone."

729b7940-1e8a-49fb-8ad9-b8a1f12a55a9.Text: "All knowledge is dangerous. The peril in knowledge is the price of it. It is a sacred fee for a rite, not a prohibition."

54fb1ab4-4f12-4aea-ac87-965d1b9108ad.Text: {n}The hollow, pained laughter from behind the brass mask is amplified by its echo.{/n} "I know everything."

baa130da-4a32-48c6-88f2-b6657d9d8b8d.Text: "You are looking for Archmagos Amarnat, you say?" {n}Something clicks inside Brasswhisper's mask, and his voice becomes louder and harsher as if coated in liquid metal.{/n} "He has been by your side all this time."

a9ec0a81-05d7-46f4-accf-f3925f0e6c27.Text: {n}Pasqal turns his gaze to you, his pupils burning bright with celestial fire. A single word escapes from his vox:{/n} "Restoration."

758c2263-650d-46d6-85cd-eb48987ae165.Text: "The Amarnat Collective was designed to be a philosopher and a researcher. The concepts he produced were so powerful that they almost destroyed the Cognisance Fleet. But then he faced an unsolvable dilemma. And that was when Amarnat came apart."

73038ac1-6f71-4980-9216-dc3548226cd1.Text: "Cognitive reconstruction mechanism activated. The memory is awakening inside you." {n}Brasswhisper is shaken by a violent coughing fit, then he shouts ferociously,{/n} "Remember!"

d6904d59-0a68-4a8c-8cd6-b76e9c07700e.Text: "The six constituent servants of the Omnissiah hid their own memories from themselves behind false personas and were sent off to various parts of the Koronus Expanse. They went into hiding. Each had to live in solitude for many decades, accumulating individual observations before eventually bringing that experience back to a reunited Amarnat, who would then tackle the dilemma once more. That would be the Restoration."

6d35fcc2-5201-465d-905f-f8b650cca290.Text: {n}Sorrow echoes in Pasqal's inhuman voice:{/n} "The years have slipped through my fingers like sand. It was such a long time ago." {n}Your companion looks overwhelmed and pensive.{/n}

67f64b25-3165-4bc4-9fe2-4a517e867c44.Text: "Yes. Six mental keynotes. Dementz was Paranoia. After the separation, he sensed that his memory was a web of lies, and that feeling drove him to the depths of madness. Tarzus was Faith, fiery and unyielding. Axiomantha was Logic, unclouded by emotion or value judgements."

e5427edf-2e04-4161-a521-6bc972033013.Text: "The Restoration was statistically calculated on a level beyond your comprehension, lay{mf||wo}man. Billions of variables were taken into account. Countless scenarios went into the development of optimal strategies. Two Amarnat units meeting each other was an inevitable certainty. The matching identifiers were to be a spark that would start a chain reaction. And that was precisely what happened."

e60a4068-4522-4e8f-b55a-f4e4fbedb157.Text: "Abel was her good twin, Imagination. He did not know his past, just like the others, but he felt more than they did. He was always different. That was why he was the first to get close to the Restoration... one of the first."

eaa1b78b-1248-4ea7-b9f1-a2a4dfbe9dba.Text: "Pasqal was Judgement. The moderator of the cognitive process. The one who makes the decision." {n}Pasqal's voice rises to the vault of the observatorium and rumbles beneath it like thunder.{/n}

7d6fe78a-4ca0-4766-9b01-143470950853.Text: "And Nihel." {n}The brass mask starts to unlock with a hissing sound. The augmetics bend back, revealing a face disfigured by burns. A woman's face with a pair of darkly radiant, vibrant eyes.{/n} "Scepticism. The one who doubts."

ee493da1-db61-497b-b653-b1606f3a7e1d.Text: {n}A ringing brittleness enters Pasqal's voice:{/n} "We were motivated by the perfect stimuli. Curiosity, anxiety... shame. Each part of us was hostage to the legend of a betrayal it had committed, for suffering drove us to search and strive."

823dfe15-ad2e-4c6a-98be-acb6e646ff49.Text: "Its name was Eschatos. The secret to the rite of putting a machine spirit to death. A technology embodying the Discontinuing of the Cycle. Was it meant to exist? Or was it the acme of profanity against the Omnissiah and His creation?"

ee7dd65a-fff6-4a20-b364-a5e7061959fa.Text: {n}Pasqal continues Brasswhisper's speech in a lofty tone:{/n} "Eschatos was the perfect weapon against creations of the Omnissiah that had been corrupted by enemies... but also against His faithful servants. Its spread could bring victory to the Imperium, or it could destroy it. Eschatos could spell the end of the Adeptus Mechanicus, for it was the perfect answer to the power wielded by the Cult of the Machine God. Was it a blessing or a curse?"

e3174076-2219-47a0-8ad9-c70970391e31.Text: "There was no answer. Protraction was unacceptable. And so a way was found... to shelve the issue." {n}Brasswhisper gives a raspy sigh.{/n} "And I found the answer. Eschatos should not exist. We will correct our mistake."

d8029e8e-2a9d-41da-b994-cb9f0a95f9df.Text: "The power of machine negation. A Noospheric signal that interrupts any and all life created by the Omnissiah." {n}A green flash runs along the crack in Pasqal's respirator.{/n} "The power that I used to tap into... unconsciously."

b392a2f2-cb64-49e9-9f0f-efa19a12c7bc.Text: "This statement is true. I was admitted into the Lord Inquisitor's retinue and authorised to study a dangerous artefact taken from Amarnat. It tried to exert some kind of influence on me, but my data-vows protected me..." {n}Nihel Haneumann touches her scarred face.{/n} "A short circuit awakened some of my memories. I conducted an analysis, solved the Eschatos dilemma, and began to act."

b21cf52b-e883-4121-a945-1630959822f4.Text: "My agents all but terminated Tarzus, but he hid under an armour of martyrdom and insanity. An attempt to intercept Pasqal on Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17 failed because Abel had summoned him. The assassins caught up to him at the Rykad Minoris starport, but he was able to escape again. Another group went after Abel, only to perish at an Electro-Priest monastery."

d954da81-298b-4b83-a6a4-2685e126f863.Text: "You dispatched Dementz, who had lapsed into heresy. Axiomantha... simply disappeared until she suddenly turned up dead on Eufrates II. I have no idea how she managed to hide from me..."

2471ec48-6ce5-42ab-af65-5b86675af093.Text: "I am registering a lie! The Lord Inquisitor shared my conviction that Amarnat's legacy had to be destroyed. He was summoned to the Koronus Expanse by loyal members of the Cognisance Fleet in order to depose Amarnat. It was his troops that attacked the Hermetico in an attempt to obliterate our schismatic creation!"

e40238a0-3450-4ce5-8ade-f401a0eb4f16.Text: "So that was how you got on board the ship and into the observatorium, Nihel. Our traitorous tech-comrades gave Calcazar the access codes to the bridge. And he gave them to you." {n}Acute conviction vibrates in Pasqal's voice as he makes these quiet statements of fact. He is not asking questions; he is passing Judgement.{/n}

b2731fc9-9e86-45cf-a46a-31871fe4fb55.Text: "Lies!" {n}Something you have not heard before creeps into Nihel's voice: a note of... fear.{/n}

ac1f409d-8557-49b8-a79c-4fc382803eeb.Text: "Shared knowledge lay dormant inside the mind of every Amarnat unit. You tried to decrypt the other Haneumanns' neurocogitators, did you not? But to no avail. It was you who created the cipher that locked Amarnat's memory."

5aa10a9c-15f2-4b2d-b14b-5db840e0a1dc.Text: {n}With a mixture of pain and pride, Brasswhisper replies,{/n} "We all chose the path of martyrdom. I merely helped them reach the supreme goal at the end of that path."

29b774ef-d122-4ae3-9be4-d25d257ae4f3.Text: "The decision is his to make." {n}Nihel points to Pasqal.{/n} "As always."

ab6d3736-dbcb-4cac-9fc9-31dee9460083.Text: {n}Nihel's voice is imperiously metallic:{/n} "Tech-brother, I offer you the chance to yield peacefully to a fate that will please the Omnissiah. Do not resist your termination, and you will pass into oblivion as my friend and fellow believer."

1b8c6371-5a60-4d13-8f98-ce08216eb2b6.Text: {n}Pasqal looks thoughtful as he touches the crack running across his armoured respirator. A green spark runs through the deep gash left by an enemy's weapon in the metal.{/n}

41413b75-e683-44fd-a132-763bc8d36987.Text: "And it sufficed for you to merely show up in the Expanse again for the schism to rear its head once more. The Cognisance Fleet is already being torn apart by a fratricidal war! Is this what we wanted? Let us finish this... Let us discontinue the Cycle!" {n}Now the words of the one who once called herself Brasswhisper sound more like a plea.{/n}

e0d3292b-bb9d-4ac8-967d-9284a0e65ab3.Text: {n}The voice that answers her is no human voice. It could belong to a giant voidship or forge world, if they could speak.{/n} "You violated procedure, Scepticism. You usurped the function of another. You challenge only; you do not make decisions. I do."

26c6b70e-ad42-4bf9-aa1d-81c14370b074.Text: {n}Pasqal extends a mechadendrite toward Nihel and pronounces,{/n} "Tech-sister, my Judgement of you and your actions is one of condemnation. Tampering with procedure is unacceptable. Sabotaging the experiment is apostasy. For your betrayal, your vital functions will be terminated in the name of the Messiah of Discontinuing." {n}A greenish pulse of energy is born inside Pasqal's augmetics and darts toward Nihel like a furious lightning bolt.{/n}

66408628-9539-46ae-a607-0b732de26e97.Text: {n}Nihel rasps a sigh and gives Pasqal a look of despair.{/n} "The decision is his to make."

f5772d6e-4084-4955-a03f-e04ab260ee4d.Text: "Only I can decide who deserves to be destroyed, {name}. And I have made my decision."

8b20a2a5-8bf1-46f9-aca4-a09e96a6d2ec.Text: "Marginally. He used to play a major part in this story. Not anymore. This meeting is held upon my initiative." {n}Brasswhisper surveys the Inquisition soldiers and warriors of the Omnissiah standing motionless.{/n} "That said, I am still under the protection of the Lord Inquisitor and the Cognisance Fleet. Keep that in mind."

df02302f-3590-4a81-b819-9cae8e1d64ba.Text: "You were deceived, sister. Calcazar appropriated our work. He continued our research, no longer bound by the Omnissiah's canon. And you enabled him by destroying those who could return and reclaim his bloodied prize."

23f798a6-c77d-4253-a6de-06550bfeb3f1.Text: "We intend to discontinue the Cycle. Is that not obvious?" {n}There is a note of sarcasm in Brasswhisper's croaking voice.{/n}

5e05e232-3365-4a7c-8712-03aa5dfd0612.Text: "Speak or I will rip your memories out along with the Ferrum Sanctum implanted in your brain." {n}Pasqal enunciates each word as he activates his drilling mechadendrite.{/n} "What do you know of Amarnat?"

58ff7dfd-b5c1-4197-80aa-0bfba04e46d4.Text: "This statement is false. The hypothesis is without mer—"

0c43bab0-b882-42af-b093-39631334f071.Text: "Looking? How absurd. You lack the very concept of what you are looking for, lay{mf||wo}man. You expect to find a man, and Amarnat never was one... he was never one person."

8f14bb4f-083d-4650-8517-d96114fcbc79.Text: "The Amarnat Collective was created by a group of Tech-Priests who renounced individuality and merged into a hivemind. A mind that reasoned algorithmically but was guided by the principles and convictions of a righteous spirit. A superego that brought them one step closer to the Omnissiah."

b2786660-c227-4258-86c9-2b89b93822b7.Text: "...and locks us in a cage of data-vows!" {n}Pasqal shudders as if struck by the Motive Force itself. Mechadendrites rise like steel wings behind his shoulders. The voice from his vox-speaker takes on an otherworldly profundity and power:{/n} "And therefore the Cycle must be discontinued."

cdc3326e-49dd-4deb-9fca-0c55f245ba0b.Text: {n}Brasswhisper interrupts him with a forceful shout:{/n} "As the Cycle coils in multitudinous loops, it intersects with itself..."

48d31edd-e788-4184-8579-7b581344b152.Text: "All we did was breed corruption! Schism! Remember when they came to depose us? We resisted them and destroyed this ship! A sacred relic! An Ark Mechanicus older than our priesthood itself! Here in this hall, we released Eschatos and allowed an unconscionable heresy to happen! Do you remember? Do you remember how you got your cleft jaw?"

ad5634f7-90b6-45e9-bd90-7d4648d7b8a3.Text: "There you are, tech-brother." {n}Brasswhisper's voice is raspy and punctuated. His gaze is turned toward Pasqal.{/n}

318bc491-c6c1-4681-abd4-d3f99b2f5144.Text: "Your guesses are amazingly spot on, Pasqal."

58536275-b1c3-4ed0-98ba-7dce93207200.Text: "Pasqal, explain to the commoner that I do not care what tribe he is from, and that he should kneel in the presence of the Rogue Trader."

beae3d5e-6a4c-4a65-995c-1a1b34dafac7.Text: "We are here to look for someone."

6bcb04f1-067b-420b-b903-c52c98bb8716.Text: "You talk to us, your kinfolk do not. Why?"

a5712650-c072-4cec-b096-2cca3f11cd3d.Text: "Is that why you call us ghosts?"

072a8fb5-552b-4aa7-a1fa-d4b66bb04208.Text: "Do you believe the world has perished?"

cb94a9f0-822c-46ae-a57a-12086444ced9.Text: "What do you think destroyed the universe?"

87a66e80-810b-496f-94af-9102f9c98888.Text: [Take a closer look at the man]

adf92e7d-ec61-4c38-aa72-5770bc199b4c.Text: "So how did the faceless ghost get in?"

9fa5f645-044a-402c-a186-b76ee5a87210.Text: "Who or what is the great entity?"

e3cad152-a685-4f01-8bcf-a276234bb8e5.Text: "I greet your tribe. We come in peace."

fc697a6f-4159-4459-918a-6c661caebd43.Text: "Pasqal, what do you make of these people?"

a7369fca-feef-41ef-938c-f46ec1c1803b.Text: "How do you survive here and what do you do?"

a67ac0f1-c00b-4946-8d2c-3dd1280e0589.Text: {n}The lean, hunchbacked man studies you with his piercing gaze. One of his eyes looks you up and down, the other has been replaced by a bulky augmetic, ancient and adorned with gold but is deactivated for some reason. He states in a dry voice,{/n} "The ghosts of nothingness have entered the deck of the Acgen tribe."

5813aa7a-b437-4434-a5d2-8693bdd0734e.Text: "What draws you here, ghost of nothingness?"

7d9183c1-1f53-421f-be52-1b5e3775d717.Text: "The supreme deity. The spirit of wisdom and revelations. It bears the name Marnat."

4d66264c-4924-4dbb-b91d-8dab568897ea.Text: {n}The name grabs Pasqal's attention. He says sternly,{/n} "I am registering a meaningful linguistic pattern. Requesting all available information on Am— on Marnat."

fc3149b5-0ec2-4f87-90bd-3647949ffd09.Text: "Abandon this thought. Your kind can't go in there. The great tube was made for the travels of gods, not mortals. Only one who has the blessing of Pref, the great spirit who rules this deck, may approach the great tube. But even such a one will have tried in vain, for the great tube's spirits have sealed its gate and will only open it to those who know the divine word. And the rust wraiths ensure that humans don't steal the word. They'll make short work of any thief."

65aaad35-4371-4f6c-acaf-be9fe8f5844d.Text: "Hypothesis: this primitive community is made up of descendants of low-ranking technomats who once serviced this deck. The name 'Acgen' derives from Category Ac-Gen. 'Ac' stood for the Acolyte category, which serviced the main decks. 'Gen' referred to service staff who were assigned general, as opposed to specialised, maintenance duties."

9306c411-13de-40b2-b782-c7ed607686fd.Text: {n}Pasqal clicks his mechadendrite's claw, points to the tattoos covering the man's neck, and says,{/n} "Based on these markings, the unit has been identified as a member of Category 17 auxiliary staff. Requesting performance of appropriate salutatory ritual." {n}A binharic trill accompanies the stern words.{/n}

8a84e51f-5b45-4e23-96c9-15878cd2ebea.Text: "The undertakers of the world that expired in the Great Discontinuing of the Cycle. The mourners holding an eternal requiem for the universe."

c2f6a7ae-6a20-4865-8297-f4f9dcc20a62.Text: {n}The man looks at you and Pasqal with indifference. He does not seem to have understood a single word.{/n}

0ba1344a-cd4d-48b0-ba30-2a157d8d5bed.Text: "Yes. There is only nothingness outside this ship. Sometimes it spits out ghosts born out of the world's ashes, and they wander in. The sight of you saddens us, for we mourn you. Alas, there is nothing we can do to help you, since you do not exist."

068baa38-b8bc-4ee2-9327-935bbd9fb271.Text: {n}The man nods with a grimace of tragic sentiment.{/n}

d064bb51-c678-4c56-b2b7-328989d7105e.Text: {n}Pasqal lowers his head and says quietly,{/n} "That is him. My mentor. Amarnat."

6445c3bf-7105-4a39-b828-238710a27c25.Text: "This statement is true. The world ceased to exist a very long time ago. It turned to nothingness. To ashes. All that's left are these ruins. The last shard of the universe. Its cenotaph."

f9262f6b-34ab-4e31-92b7-8c97aa24cb47.Text: "The unthinkable was wrought. The Cycle was discontinued."

c758de55-371c-46bf-9bc7-5a0b05cb37fb.Text: "Farewell, ghost. I hope nothingness summons you back into its embrace soon."

e33b3386-d8f9-4dcd-8c77-0828347fde0d.Text: {n}The middle-aged man carries a potentia coil on his shoulders, after the manner of Tech-Priests. It is held in place by straps and is not connected to anything. Its weight has given him a hunched back. One of his arms has been replaced by an exquisite tech-scribe augmetic, but the quills and styli are incredibly dull as though they have been scraped against bare rock, and the limb's servo motor is dormant.{/n}

e3131e70-7f85-490d-8fe8-6ef45813c56a.Text: {n}The sight of the mangled augmetic elicits a pained grimace from Pasqal.{/n} "I am registering evidence of precious True Flesh being operated in unacceptable conditions. The markings indicate that this sacred metal was fashioned many centuries ago on blessed Mars. Putting it to such crude and careless use is an insult to the Omnissiah."

1402e733-bbe9-41ea-9bcd-8bfa1424bd1c.Text: {n}A wan, condescending smile graces the man's lips.{/n} "It was discontinued a long time ago."

c90579b2-f9ce-4426-9e93-f9915b240b27.Text: "Neither. It just happened. But it was a grievous event. And we grieve."

086a7b22-747d-4f5b-9fd4-21fbabdfebc6.Text: {n}The man shakes his head.{/n} "You find this hard to fathom, being ghosts born out of nothingness. I can understand. That is why we try to avoid talking to ghosts."

91dd17da-3f95-41da-9240-cf74170f388c.Text: "The master of this deck, the second most important god after Marnat. Mortals cruelly betrayed his trust once, and he hasn't talked to them or protected them since. Pref only ever answers the shaman's invocations, and only occasionally at that."

834f26f0-3bb5-45a1-9d13-00b288fb7795.Text: "We hold a vigil for all of existence, and the spirits of the mechanisms give us water, food, and nutrient mix. We thank them for that with rites of machine servicing and maintenance. So commands the great entity."

9601bb12-a84f-42e6-8da1-d5d60fd4fb7d.Text: "The tribesman's profane speculations most likely describe an important machine spirit that remains awake. Requesting a conversation with the unit identified as 'the shaman.'"

2db7c54b-f351-44b2-bc2b-dbe0b5b30076.Text: "I am the Fabricator General. My shoulders bear the sacred burden of leadership." {n}The man shifts his shoulders, bent under the potentia coil resting upon them.{/n} "The others fear you, as ghosts can carry the living away into nothingness. But I am protected by Marnat's grace."

8f2cde19-77c2-4ea6-98fd-4dd0fffe9efd.Text: "This tribesman's mind is full of the most unenlightened superstition. Why does this unit seemingly know less than some primitive barbarian?"

eb2f51d1-28e3-40e5-8bdf-aed80a1ab974.Text: {n}The sound of Techna-Lingua makes the man kneel humbly and whistle a reply as if imitating the language of the servants of the Omnissiah.{/n}

86b29c61-6e7a-4e3b-9316-1bf57401e205.Text: {n}Pasqal turns to you and remarks quietly,{/n} "That reply was in a binharic dialect. Primitive and crude... but correct."

53093e9e-9af8-4969-b758-2537c49a2678.Text: "Marnat is a divine being of great wisdom. It was this great wisdom that discontinued the Cycle, and all who had partaken of it lapsed into nothingness. We never partook of the wisdom, which is why we exist. And I have nothing to tell you about it, ghost."

afbe9db8-75bd-49b0-be26-62887eaaeaf3.Text: {n}Pasqal's roar is like the blaring alarm of an extractor.{/n} "Fabricator General? I am registering heresy!"

55ba7260-9a4f-4800-a032-8b1209cf1937.Text: {n}The man listens to the Tech-Priest's outburst without flinching.{/n} "The universe must have a Fabricator General — the supreme priest of the Omnissiah. There is none other to hold that title. Therefore, it is mine."

ce646e98-c147-4e49-a609-eb964f95a9a4.Text: "Hypothesis: the term 'divine word' refers to a command litany. A thorough understanding of the situation aboard the Hermetico will allow me to select the correct litany and recite it to the mechanisms that are still operational."

4b121e27-e996-46a0-852d-cf7c656537e6.Text: "The echo of an old crime was heard beneath the arching vaults of our home." {n}The tribesman nods at you gloomily.{/n} "A ghost of nothingness walked among us, of like appearance to you but without a face. He spoke words that must not be spoken, and then penetrated the Chamber of Observus. And our abode was shaken by the wrath of the gods for days, and we felt as though we were drifting through nothingness."

e555de8d-60e9-4da2-84a5-f20d37cc55a4.Text: "His brow bore the mark of sorrow and past misdeeds, and his voice was like seeping sand."

95428b69-8abc-446c-81f8-0c81d123b1d1.Text: "An abode of deities and mighty spirits, secluded from mortals." {n}The man points toward the entrance to the lift shaft.{/n} "Down this great tube, they used to descend to the mortals. Now they have all retired to the house of Observus, the calm and keen-sighted, there to remember and mourn the world that once was."

c9de6855-9cb6-4ee0-92df-794adac73aee.Text: {n}Pasqal hesitates, then adds worriedly,{/n} "Correction: this data is a hypothesis. An archive search yielded no confirmation of this data. My possession of it is an anomalous cognitive fluctuation."

2e4607c3-7be8-4ecd-9f94-505a460428f0.Text: "He knew the secret. The spell was not of divine origin — its power surpassed that of the gods. It was born in the mysterious depths of irregularity, and soon after a mortal first uttered it, the world was no more."

e71564f4-4fbe-4f91-a88b-8928149756cd.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest is taken aback. He pauses to think, then says with no great confidence,{/n} "This statement is false. Each of the hypotheses was logically deduced from our present situation."

bb9cdb8e-e384-4e89-8594-159deb6f9d0c.Text: {n}The man sighs and makes a sign with his hand that is vaguely reminiscent of a Tech-Priest gesture to ward off evil.{/n}

5f5a557b-cd8b-46b6-b075-6a99233ea952.Text: "Good. Don't seek to enter the gods' abode, ghost. It is no place for you."

662c6294-fa68-4417-bac3-e58e537a7f0f.Text: {n}The man points at one of the motionless statues.{/n} "The ancient ones, the servants of the gods. They used to be the gods' great warriors; now they guard the peace of this universal cemetery and see to it that mortals don't challenge the divine order."

0396a09c-3a54-4e9e-969f-cff429d2921c.Text: "Words command all of existence. The gods ruled the universe using words of power. There was a time when mortals, too, were granted knowledge of them, but that time died along with the world."

1a6adcb6-c349-4920-b52d-5d7224393686.Text: "The Skitarii, the deck guard. These immortal servants are an elite detachment of the crew blessed with the most ancient and wondrous augmetic enhancements. They could survive in a sleeping state for centuries even." {n}After a brief pause, a whisper comes from his vox:{/n} "Their presence here is unusual. Typically, the immortals only leave their storage chapel on special orders from the bridge."

9463bf84-c066-4654-b64e-e7af907e08a3.Text: {n}Fascinated by the answer, Pasqal says quietly,{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued."

288f5c1e-0b9a-49bc-91e7-139fb06c3d9c.Text: "I am registering multiple deviations from the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation in the actions of these units. Hypothesis: the breaches of sacred instructions do not stem from a malicious lapse into heresy. They are a consequence of the rite having been lost to memory. A grave heresy but not as profane." {n}The voice from the vox is full of sorrow and reproach.{/n}

8faab023-06ac-47d9-9eef-ff7c5b3ebc90.Text: "No, other ghosts walked with him, but he alone had a mind and a will. The others did his bidding."

fcf46246-6ed5-49a2-8eb5-1c16a0396a53.Text: "The unit has given us a distorted description of the observatorium — the bay that housed the Hermetico's bridge. There, under a grand dome of glasscrete, the wisest hierarchs of the Adeptus Mechanicus would spend time in reflection and strive to discern the Omnissiah's guiding signs in the glitter of the stars."

8fbe3594-aeaf-4ac0-8f95-fef5b5015a5a.Text: {n}The man shrugs indifferently. His voice is tinged with sympathy:{/n} "It does not matter. You are ghosts."

116f62c7-122f-43a8-b9c0-f59e809aeb8f.Text: {n}Pasqal waves a mechadendrite at him in annoyed dismissal and says impatiently,{/n} "The blessed Amarnat can command any mechanism on his ship. The indoctrinal heresy uttered by the unit is unworthy of attention."

0dbdd219-e7b8-40b8-9218-0c7d78c4e1d8.Text: "What are you? Or what were you?"

37861721-07f5-428e-8be5-4e20ba0546ec.Text: "We need Amarnat and the power he wields."

9ded4b67-ac79-4fab-b0c0-3a33a6f43435.Text: "We need Eschatos. But we also need Pasqal."

4b81d5e1-1372-4d3a-8bb4-599e03784754.Text: "Your secret reeks of heresy. Do the right thing and destroy it."

d7f9027c-1077-42d6-a192-ccce7b13ddc3.Text: "What will the destruction of Eschatos mean for you?"

fe475f3d-3487-413f-8a35-b51b9dd45d67.Text: [Address Abel] "What are your thoughts on this dilemma?"

df3096b6-337f-4529-a230-5c4592abb9a4.Text: "I think Abel means that your experiment has caused too much destruction and bloodshed."

86607eef-dd26-406e-88c9-ce84d9da8032.Text: "It is obvious. If we reject Amarnat's knowledge now, all the sacrifice will have been in vain."

d4245ef2-299a-4958-8764-fbc295449a4f.Text: "Do what you have decided to do."

9116d50d-f3e4-4059-9570-b508307dcc71.Text: "What next? What is the general algorithm?"

9f75d0df-169c-419c-b807-afb98a1d4584.Text: [Draw your weapon] "I will not let it happen!"

7b844236-3278-415e-83ef-350aa0f3e1e3.Text: "Perhaps he means that your bold attempt at ascension has earned you the right to this power."

447848bb-5b15-45cc-9127-3deda273c37d.Text: "I am sorry about the death of your tech-sister."

ae8215c2-a6b7-447a-9c8f-6858bd11e0e9.Text: "You did the right thing. She deserved it."

cc85ee47-ffb6-43c3-b41c-f46f853e7711.Text: "Amarnat was a union of six Tech-Priests. All but a few of them are dead now. How does Amarnat still exist?"

97f662a9-168e-43c4-b5e3-7d185394f218.Text: "A Judgement must be passed. Should the secret of Eschatos exist or be shunned as a false path?"

e6b2da73-8814-481a-b8e5-46d023162865.Text: "Nihel reinforced our union with the prudence of Dementz, a meticulous and reserved auditor, a danger-seeker. I strengthened our genius with the fiery faith of the warrior Tarzus, in order to banish the shadows of false ideas. Axiomantha, who teetered on the brink of becoming a malatek, was chosen by us for her loyalty to ruthless logic and her cold scrutiny, or indeed dissection, of our theories."

05b0acc2-0869-49b4-a24c-8cf96368c2ae.Text: {n}Arrogance creeps into Pasqal's voice as he gazes at Nihel's body:{/n} "The Amarnat Collective's experiment has demonstrated that a shared consciousness is as prone to flaws as an individual one. We failed to put our power to the right use. We destroyed ourselves. But that does not mean our power was bad. We were bad... most of us."

d57fde4c-64f1-4af4-a843-8b110984c9f2.Text: "The Collective can be replenished with worthy minds from among those aboard the Hermetico. Sincerity is present in their motives and faith. They are intuitively capable of comprehending the notion of Discontinuing the Cycle. Our collective memory can compensate for their lack of knowledge and memory of the rites. Restoration is possible." {n}Pasqal — or what used to be known as Pasqal — makes a sacred gesture, and green sparks run down his mechanical arm.{/n} "But the Judgement must be passed first."

058fbe46-6394-45e5-a4b3-473d9b8b7315.Text: {n}The ghostlike figure in red approaches you cautiously. Enormous sad eyes look at you from his ascetic face.{/n} "Doubt has been shunned. The dominate of prejudice has ended." {n}Abel's voice resonates with the same otherworldly profundity that has filled Pasqal's vox.{/n}

860b39e0-25bc-4c25-adc1-ddbf911e571b.Text: "Now I see just how poisonous is the fruit Eschatos bore. It sowed schism and strife among the Cognisance Fleet and my closest tech-brothers and tech-sisters with whom I shared my thoughts. And therefore, my verdict is harsh: the knowledge of Eschatos comes not from the Omnissiah but from perverse forces inimical to Him."

60ad3946-59d7-44bb-89a1-57601b60da15.Text: {n}Jealously creeps into the god's voice:{/n} "Am I to become part of a compromised project again? I have seen the paths chosen by my tech-comrades, and I cannot put my trust in anyone anymore. I alone will decide for myself. Since I can neither carry the burden of Eschatos nor divide it, let it lapse into oblivion."

1ec7fb62-7143-498b-8a06-be908520dee5.Text: {n}A pained sigh comes from Pasqal's vox. When he turns to you, his eyes crease slightly, as if he is smiling weakly behind his respirator unit.{/n} "I think it is over. I did what was right."

c5690a46-e2ab-454f-ab52-28f07b999931.Text: {n}There are grating overtones of pain in the god's voice:{/n} "So great is the temptation... To preserve my personhood and yet hold on to the power of Eschatos... My own thirst to yield to that temptation is what allows me to pass the Judgement. Eschatos must be forgone. One cannot possess it without one's mind becoming depraved, and the existence of the Amarnat Collective will sooner or later lead to its destruction and the concentration of the innermost secret in the hands of one. This is unacceptable."

12d074ed-905a-4a52-8c52-283985128d49.Text: {n}The god's voice is thunderous and mournful:{/n} "Eschatos is not to blame for the schism and bloodshed that followed its creation. The blame lies with us. The innermost secret must not be lost because of our imperfection. We recognise that the Amarnat Collective has proved itself incapable of solving the dilemma and does not deserve rebirth. So let the dilemma henceforth be solved by Pasqal Haneumann. Alone."

8f322664-8033-43f4-962d-8b5a450ade78.Text: {n}The god's voice now echoes with the very familiar overtones of another voice. That of Pasqal Haneumann. And it is full of grief.{/n} "The Collective means a new schism, and a return to schism is unacceptable. However, the innermost secret is truly useful to the servants of the Omnissiah. The old method has proved itself inadequate, and so I renounce Amarnat... but not his legacy. Let us see if Pasqal Haneumann can humbly carry the burden that proved too great for his overproud... creator."

59d099bd-adaf-45b7-aa09-362cd623e73b.Text: {n}The god's voice grows despondent:{/n} "Wielding the power single-handedly... An unacceptable temptation. If this universe needs Eschatos, then Eschatos needs a steward. Alas, only Amarnat is up to that task. Therefore, let him live again."

2a566b9d-7344-4cdd-b3f5-05077a5296f5.Text: {n}The god's voice thunders with righteous indignation and the venom of wounded pride:{/n} "To shun this great power? To renounce the right to forge the future? Such a path is shameful for a servant of the Omnissiah!"

861cacae-7f59-4c38-9776-232d47404c40.Text: {n}Pasqal throws back his head, and the power brimming in his voice rushes forth like a flood. The Tech-Priest's booming voice is heard throughout the ship, echoed by every vox-speaker on every deck.{/n} "I peered into the vortex of time and saw dark omens. I saw that my tech-comrades and I were trapped in the Cycle, spiralling toward nothingness. I saw inevitable doom at the end of that trajectory and rebelled against it."

5be00599-7b03-48ce-81e5-897dd8e490b4.Text: {n}Pasqal throws back his head, and the power brimming in his voice rushes forth like a flood. The Tech-Priest's booming voice is heard throughout the ship, echoed by every vox-speaker on every deck.{/n} "I was once part of a great whole. I was once but one of many. We gleaned the horror that lay ahead, and we rebelled against it. Yet we proved unworthy of the knowledge revealed to us."

440ad55b-43c6-4ff0-a70e-b2b9d855560f.Text: {n}Pasqal throws back his head, and the power brimming in his voice rushes forth like a flood. The Tech-Priest's booming voice is heard throughout the ship, echoed by every vox-speaker on every deck.{/n} "I once broke the Omnissiah's tenets. I overstepped the limits placed on knowledge. I was guilty of a transgression. We all were."

e7a5a201-81ef-40cd-93b4-57c0fbc440c1.Text: {n}Abel gives you a sideways glance and says ruefully,{/n} "So much loss."

b6325231-3948-4283-87f5-5eb3dfa404a8.Text: "Your Judgement is accepted. Farewell, {name}." {n}Pasqal closes his eyes and calmly receives your blow.{/n} "The unit Pasqal Haneumann's service has ended."

8efb72b5-1555-475c-9890-8982d99fa941.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest looks the same as before... yet different. His morbid aura of martyrdom has given way to a calm and powerful halo of purposefulness. His mechadendrites move with the grace of an inscrutable dance. The scars left by loss and doubt have turned into dark threads on a radiant body confident in its next step.{/n}

05953a7e-a9b8-492a-a5c8-7be23311f2c1.Text: "Thank you for the path we have walked." {n}As Pasqal bows, his thin shoulders seem to take an eternity to descend from the heights that his mind has soared to.{/n} "And I am sorry about what happened to Theodora."

ca40321d-0af3-4e87-b8d4-bbda220a802b.Text: {n}The otherworldly force drains from his vox like water. Pasqal turns to look at you, and you see the familiar features showing through the higher form of intelligence. In a strange voice that could equally be frightened, pleading, or indifferent, he enquires,{/n} "Are you going to kill me?"

76f7c063-8b9a-410b-8fd7-960d8239effa.Text: {n}The voice from the vox is like the tolling of bells summoning a host of angels:{/n} "I declare the period of ignorance over and will resume execution of the general algorithm.
