Integrity has been rehabilitated to a satisfactory degree. Memory access has been restored. I remember everything." {n}Pasqal turns to you and gives you a long look brimming with quiet elation.{/n}

1d6b97fd-6991-4329-a54c-719f678fc35d.Text: "This statement is true. Only Imagination and Judgement are left. Our directive is to conceptualise the future we desire and bring it into being."

db78bb6b-540f-4db9-b769-b1d3b780464e.Text: "May the shattered mirror reassembled reflect light wholly anew."

0523953e-3883-4fa1-9675-79cd9ae2f69b.Text: "This statement is true." {n}Pasqal's stock phrase sounds more complex and more... human than before.{/n} "I carry within me his memory and his logical foundation. I am us; I am Amarnat."

9c09b2d1-92ef-4ae4-b708-b8f025861afd.Text: {n}Abel points to Pasqal's mechadendrites and says softly,{/n} "They have always remembered. They have always preserved."

3faf5210-07ba-45f1-8da8-aa58eceaea02.Text: "We were allies. She entrusted me with studying a trophy she had obtained." {n}The voice from the vox grows quiet and hoarse, as though coming from a distant past:{/n} "We, Amarnat, discovered the basic ways of communicating with it. We developed a weapons-grade strain of tech-blight for her. It terrified me. So I developed its antidote — Eschatos. The concept for the ultimate interruption of machine life."

6f38c62b-0b89-4551-acce-971947f91251.Text: "Abel..." {n}Pasqal turns his gaze toward his last surviving tech-comrade.{/n} "Our quiet genius. The caged genius of imagination. The abstract artist of code. His talent completed the Collective and made it a whole."

5a7aa779-2ec4-4d6f-830b-a291569c836c.Text: "That was why every one of our shards was located so close to you and to the von Valancius domain. We were counting on her finding us. And extending us her aid and protection."

ad0d2b6a-35ff-4762-8e8e-983b639e5bb5.Text: "Abel..." {n}Grief fills Pasqal's voice.{/n} "Our quiet genius. The caged genius of imagination. The abstract artist of code. His talent completed the Collective and made it a whole."

da9de634-f5ca-4dd9-9400-936d09c6bca0.Text: {n}As Pasqal gazes upon the body of his fallen tech-sister, his voice sounds stern and... mournful:{/n} "Nihel violated the procedure, and thus her functions had to be terminated. But that does not mean she was wrong. What I see... The destructive power of Eschatos, the entropic energy this secret emanates... I cannot guarantee that Eschatos remains controllable. I cannot guarantee that its existence pleases the Omnissiah."

dfaa926e-42f6-421b-9bc6-e0c369d2bcec.Text: {n}A soft binharic melody, full of sadness and solemn resolve, pours from Abel's vox. You have not heard it before. You would never have thought the binharic language could be so... comprehensible to one who does not bear the mark of the Omnissiah's iron blessing.{/n}

4962bcaa-5076-49b5-861b-200a3c4c267e.Text: "If I bid you to follow, will you come with me, tech-comrade?" {n}Pasqal waits for an affirmative nod and says,{/n} "We will be the core."

1d3e107c-0fa8-4511-9791-29a630a30875.Text: "A higher form of intelligence. A Collective of computational tools freed from the limitations of individualism and the aberrations that stem from having a distinct personality. And at the same time, a Collective bound by a single set of principles that are of equal importance to all: being pure of faith in the Omnissiah and acting for the benefit of Humanity."

b86bf6a9-f30b-4be0-a8af-6e37128307e3.Text: {n}Abel lowers his eyes and is silent for a while, then says,{/n} "We have made great sacrifices."

4dc110b9-8715-4dd3-aca8-17b9d782522a.Text: "And should I exist? That is, we. Amarnat."

944f9dc1-f980-4341-9cf0-3ab771b2f685.Text: {n}With a sad sigh, Abel adds quietly,{/n} "Great power has its own answers to the question of who is worthy of it."

071ab0f1-9cd0-4170-9b8b-493c56ff1669.Text: {n}Abel gives you a sideways glance and says sorrowfully,{/n} "Self-sacrifice must not be in vain."

eee7e098-cca9-4fe8-a235-18485660a56b.Text: {n}Without waiting for an answer, Pasqal says gravely,{/n} "You have always been inscrutable, tech-comrade."

0eff2e2a-2b8d-4f30-93f1-67168af1f4fd.Text: {n}Pasqal nods with an air of authority and says,{/n} "I thank you both. The information has been noted and submitted for analysis."

a1d78eff-297d-4885-b9c4-3d883840773e.Text: {n}Pasqal casts a sorrowful gaze at Nihel's body. His voice is full of wisdom and... weariness:{/n} "We have seen many things over the decades. We have seen true corruption. The distortion of the Omnissiah's design. Kiava Gamma, Eufrates II... the planets of xenos passed into oblivion. Our own crimes. The darkness grows. There must be a fire to burn it away."

cfa77f7f-45c8-410b-a7d2-1596295aa45f.Text: {n}Like the hand of a deity, the mechadendrite extends over Nihel lying convulsing on the deck.{/n} "I did not want this, tech-sister. But the procedure must be completed. Farewell." {n}His claw carefully removes a mangled, soot-covered neural cogitator from Brasswhisper's head. The Tech-Priest shudders, and peace descends over her disfigured face.{/n}

184d816e-f5f1-49a6-ad1c-f82a46cd4d37.Text: {n}The graceful dance of the mechadendrites takes on a more comprehensible, symmetrical pattern.{/n} "I am leaning toward the idea that both Eschatos and Amarnat must cease to exist."

d182678f-fb27-4d55-9ce0-974043a5f5f5.Text: {n}A shower of sparks bursts from the power unit on Pasqal's shoulders, burning holes in his scarlet hood.{/n} "An act of self-sacrifice. I will destroy the data concerning this technology and the methods of reproducing it. I will burn it out of my neural circuits. Along with everything that led to its creation. Amarnat will be no more. Only a damaged and incomplete shard of him will remain: Pasqal Haneumann."

75a46ebd-468a-4743-aa82-5c75f088c0d3.Text: {n}The graceful dance of the mechadendrites takes on a more chaotic and unpredictable pattern.{/n} "I am leaning toward the idea that Eschatos must exist. But not in the hands of the Amarnat Collective. In mine alone."

62cafd90-e222-4a15-911b-7581e98fb714.Text: {n}The graceful dance of the mechadendrites takes on a more energetic, wilder pattern.{/n} "I am leaning toward the idea that Eschatos is necessary. That Amarnat is necessary. That the Cycle must be discontinued."

79da1251-e77b-4adb-b8ea-832e858ed491.Text: "This statement is enigmatic. I request an expanded interpretation." {n}Pasqal looks demandingly into Abel's eyes, but he turns away.{/n}

a1b3b89e-bfab-4490-86c3-6816d6f92563.Text: "In accordance with the Machine God's commandment, I have crafted a tool with which to implement my design. In accordance with His commandment, I have developed a plan and analysed it. Now I will act. By my power as an Archmagos, I hereby effect a Restoration and revive the Amarnat Collective. The servants of the Omnissiah need a Messiah who will discontinue their Cycle, and I will be that Messiah. I am Him."

a3a07b5b-fead-48a2-9e5b-92d0758bf623.Text: {n}You hear echoes of other voices in Pasqal's: a touch of Dementz's anxiety, of Tarzus's zeal, of Axiomantha's pensiveness. They all fuse into a new voice, full of wisdom and confidence in his prerogative to lead — the voice of Archmagos Amarnat. And this voice takes hold of the lips of your companion's new brothers and sisters. The ancient Tech-Priest turns his gaze toward you and says, with gravitas,{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued."

f6c9abb5-4b00-4633-b9f7-9fcf3d8208b6.Text: {n}The Acgen tribesfolk, the ignorant fosterlings of the Omnissiah, slip into the observatorium hall like silent shadows. Led by an intuitive grasp of the significance of the moment, they automatically gather in a circle, heeding Pasqal's summons... or perhaps, at this point, someone else's.{/n}

c96bcbaf-5525-4657-b1cb-1c3f9ba9f16b.Text: "Self-doubt drained our strength and made us hesitate, just as the elders, whose testaments we were following, hesitated. Our fear of change drove us to dogma, paralysed us, and made us waste precious moments when we could have altered destiny's course. We fell apart, helplessly fleeing the dilemma. And in scattering we exposed our weakness to the world."

314fd997-dabb-469b-a1da-046a9f19c0e8.Text: "We were consumed by madness and fanaticism, by depravity and paranoia. The old mistake will not be repeated. I, Pasqal Haneumann, will take the entirety of the power and shoulder the entirety of the burden. I alone will preserve the great knowledge of Eschatos and decide the fate of the Cycle that will be discontinued."

a41bd8a2-27d4-4e71-b362-52088675aead.Text: "Stop... Thou shalt not create... a Schism... Thou shalt not suffer... a heretek..."

920021b9-7c03-4091-a729-2fe371066b47.Text: "Though our fate is implacable, I, Pasqal Haneumann, will follow my sense of duty and become a protector to my tech-brethren, leading them into the future. Alone."

fff81137-2c7d-4866-956c-3cd575423772.Text: {n}Cold steel cuts through the fire in his voice.{/n} "But you are right — the danger of heresy is great. I can feel the gift of Eschatos gnawing away at my principles. It is indeed forbidden to possess it... alone. Therefore, I will place chains upon my mind that will bind it with the doubts of the many but protect it from corruption. Let the Amarnat Collective be revived, so the steadfastness of the many may balance out the vulnerability of the individual."

794a3d4c-09b2-4cc7-abe2-f1efb5a2f53a.Text: "I sentence it to oblivion. I curse the fruit of every labour ever undertaken in its name, and I reformat every particle of memory that contains its knowledge. May the Rite be unshakeable. May the Adeptus Mechanicus priesthood be as one. May Amarnat and the heresy of Discontinuing the Cycle lapse into oblivion forever." {n}The green lightning bolts produced by Pasqal's vox strike his cogitator and turn white-hot. Then... they subside and fade away like ghosts.{/n}

1cb213d8-9dd8-4854-ba55-24fd76c87760.Text: {n}And his voice. A voice born in the nuclear font of a star and hardened in the cold of the interplanetary void.{/n}

7abffc3a-69f2-45ce-a1e6-3e656c42a3b2.Text: "We were different. Each one of us considered the prospects of such an experiment, but I was the first to gain the resolve to attempt it. Nihel joined the project to effect control over it: she regarded the experiment as dangerously close to a blasphemous act of creation. The conclave had ordered her to end my research, but she became convinced of the possibility of its success."

46a08d58-7d3e-43da-8e9c-8afe6c50aac9.Text: "Everything Amarnat was at the moment of the disconnection has now awoken in my mind. We are at the point where we stopped. But the Amarnat Collective was envisioned as a dynamic structure. We need new minds."

2a04d043-a906-4749-a0f3-b9e27b100647.Text: {n}Pasqal remains motionless. Only a short binharic aria comes from his vox. You feel oddly confident that your gesture of respect has been appreciated and received favourably.{/n}

481ba7f3-379e-4e76-b1c2-2e6674559e49.Text: "So am I." {n}The Tech-Priest's inscrutable gaze is fixed upon the body once inhabited by Pasqal's shared mind.{/n}

42243d2d-ac6c-4e1d-b3ba-c5e128a59701.Text: "Whether she deserved it does not matter. I did what was right because it was right."

4917a625-5d16-4499-b3f0-c3216b1f1a4b.Text: [Point at the surrounding ruins] "Are you sure this is not a compelling reason?"

6f338f1d-94b0-4cb4-9690-f6e16729181c.Text: "We have come to plead for Pref's benevolence."

e5f3a539-fd64-4f97-be58-d25cb47e3c1d.Text: "Tell it something profound and spiritual and invoke the Omnissiah."

48bf8d2d-b9b1-42fa-8db6-44565a50c232.Text: "I think a show of force is in order, to show this machine its place."

71739c89-3c6f-4ae0-a7b9-313aea2eef7c.Text: "If the machine spirit speaks a Tech-Priest language, do we even need the old man?"

146ef14b-d56d-4995-9db5-1ac014a02b8f.Text: "Volunteering too much information to an unknown entity is not a good idea. Lie and say that you are an authorised inspector from the Fleet's conclave."

0bdc641d-0cd5-4468-b544-0aa620f7b235.Text: "Tell him you are the Messiah of Discontinuing."

a9e6ede1-a7d0-4497-8aaa-d27cec78384f.Text: "You are an eminent and venerable Magos. It cannot ask for more than that. It wouldn't dare."

762c3e3e-69a3-4162-8c7e-d2898e9865fa.Text: "Tell it you are on a mission from Amarnat. Perhaps the spirit knows who he is."

3f9de6d1-615d-46dc-837f-79254cc6bb53.Text: {n}The elderly tech-shaman looks up at you with dim eyes. He smells strongly of exhaust fumes.{/n} "Have you come to speak to the Great Pref, ghosts? Pref will not speak your lesser tongue. But I can help. I can interpret."

11135e64-76ce-4135-a847-a4fbe8272b21.Text: {n}The ageing barbarian's skin is covered in tattoos of mechanisms — as if the ink drawings of cogs could pass for actual augmetics. Wires and scraps of flex tubing are braided into his hair, as well as shards from a broken data-slate screen. Cogitator circuit boards hang on threads from his large ceremonial drum.{/n}

ce3fdb6a-9294-4d34-9809-632c4ed463b2.Text: "This statement is true." {n}Pasqal extends a hand toward the machine, which is enveloped in showers of sparks. The crack in the Tech-Priest's armoured respirator shines a bright green. There is steel in his voice:{/n} "My power is my authorisation. Acknowledge it or you will regret it, wayward spirit!"

f4c52f91-8944-408e-af7e-7c3b804e9049.Text: "This statement is false. I am not registering any veneration."

cd86e828-0aad-4988-8151-f7783e50b04f.Text: "Pref... Hypothesis: the barbarian is using this debased designation to refer to a Prefect Enumerator. An especially sacred cogitator served by all of the deck's junior machine spirits. I am registering a Category Six blasphemy. The tribesman claims to communicate with it. Only enlightened adepts of the Omnissiah are permitted to interact directly with a Prefect Enumerator."

56637b81-0e4e-4532-84eb-c7f8a1fc513f.Text: {n}Machine spirits can be capricious and undisciplined. After years without sanctified maintenance, this one may have forgotten all about obedience. Normally, in cases like these, a Tech-Priest would bring the wayward spirit to its senses with a shock from an electric prod or a blow from a wrench, accompanied by the litany of uninterruptible obedience.{/n}

65e19b3f-5ca2-4c90-944a-6856098890fe.Text: "I am registering Category Six, Seven, and Eight blasphemies in this tribesman's vestments. Only enlightened Tech-Priests are authorised to dismantle and interact with the bodies of sacred machines. And painting the skin in crude imitation of True Flesh is a profane mockery."

03df362f-498c-4c54-ab1a-29d7380e90c2.Text: {n}The tech-shaman raises the roaring mechanical censer and inhales a lungful of its aromatic exhaust fumes. The tribesman's eyes grow dim, and he puts his hands on his drum. His fingers strike the taut synthetic leather with remarkable deftness and rhythm.{/n} "Like this."

0f744e74-9075-41c7-84c2-6412e867af8e.Text: {n}Pasqal frowns and says darkly,{/n} "I am registering a Categ— blast it, layman, this blessed smoke is meant for the sacred machines, not your lungs." {n}Then the Tech-Priest falls silent and listens carefully, before uttering in astonishment,{/n} "This primitive melody... is a language. Our language. A variety of rhythm-based tech-vernacular in which meaning is created by the lengths of pauses between the signals."

cab89cb8-7b6c-4461-bf34-ddc6bcf01e5e.Text: {n}Every word you say is accompanied by a series of quick drum taps in a complex, choppy rhythm. Crackling comes in response from a vox hidden somewhere inside the wall. The tech-shaman tilts his head and says,{/n} "The Great Pref would like to know who is speaking to him."

98ecc455-04b6-4322-b266-584903459ef0.Text: {n}Pasqal looks at you disapprovingly and says, with evident reluctance,{/n} "This unit is a Tech-Nuncio sent by the Supreme Conclave of the Cognisance Fleet to investigate. Presenting code regalia." {n}The indicator on Pasqal's neural cogitator glows. His Noospheric aura lights up with new data as fake credentials are generated in the deep recesses of the cogitator's circuitry.{/n}

f4ec204f-27af-43b5-8b1b-ef92a8c3afab.Text: "This unit is Magos Pasqal Haneumann." {n}He hesitates a little, then adds,{/n} "Some identify him as the Messiah of Discontinuing, although that statement is false."

8043efb1-3935-443f-a448-77e089b91fc2.Text: "This statement is false. The idiom is a distinctive vernacular most likely only used by the ship's crew. It is intuitively familiar to this unit, but not intelligible."

61abb9f8-3d3b-4bf5-a5ee-02d45d7ee61d.Text: "The Prefect Enumerator is running an identification procedure."

146cbc9b-87dc-4ecd-91cc-de6e1ace5949.Text: "I am fulfilling my sacred duty of service to the Machine God. I intend to protect this blessed ship and the servants of the Omnissiah aboard it."

7f60c2d9-1ba9-4581-968f-06be616a4a66.Text: "Hypothesis: the part of the legend that speaks of 'disowning' the mortals and forgetting their faces describes the removal of access rights from authorised units. For reasons unknown, the Prefect Enumerator was ordered to cease accepting commands from outsiders."

fed665d0-39c9-44b5-a374-9d1ea783ceab.Text: "I have come to discontinue the Cycle."

eca1312f-cb6c-4452-99b7-ce27990e018d.Text: {n}Pasqal's vox hisses angrily, and he shakes his head.{/n} "The Prefect Enumerator's reaction is anomalous. Such disregard for regalia can only be explained by... a protocol signifying an extreme degree of danger to the vessel."

5d09030a-a1c3-497c-9611-3c133f7c4094.Text: {n}Pasqal looks at you and adds with slight surprise,{/n} "I remember this language now. Or more precisely... this unit used to know it. And now it remembers having known it." {n}The Tech-Priest turns toward the wall with the sacred mechanisms concealed inside it, and says doubtfully,{/n} "I am registering an anomaly. The data exchange deviated from the standard registration procedure."

d6c7c388-d6cf-4dde-9fae-88a93e59c1b7.Text: {n}Pasqal's voice becomes dry and bristly:{/n} "The machine spirit is requesting to know this unit's access privileges. It refuses to submit to a stranger's will without a compelling reason."

e9d0345c-6461-47ef-b825-4b1ea730b311.Text: "This unit is Magos Explorator Pasqal Haneumann, a member of the Cognisance Fleet. Presenting doctrinal compliance and algorithmic obedience certificates." {n}The indicator on Pasqal's neural cogitator glows. New data lights up Pasqal's Noospheric aura that no layperson can see.{/n}

8afa8eab-3e9c-43b6-958d-bc6b8374eaf5.Text: {n}The tech-shaman shouts out in fear and shakes his drum frantically.{/n} "Pref acknowledges your power, ghost! He does! He asks why you seek his friendship!"

6fb0db4b-45cf-4542-be00-75455e7ed27d.Text: {n}A pained rattle comes from Pasqal's vox as he touches the crack in his armour, which is no longer glowing. He looks as though he has a sudden toothache, then says with effort,{/n} "Hypothesis: the Prefect Enumerator's request is to be interpreted as 'What is the purpose of your visit?'"

0e5cd438-75a4-4ea1-b21b-8968f49ec58a.Text: "It is how I venerate the iron spirits who have done their duty and passed into nothingness, ghost. I do this in the hope that I might gain some of their wisdom."

0977f887-5590-4a6d-a70e-d49b55d39cde.Text: "Given existing data on the machine spirit's refusal to follow orders within the chain of command, I predict that standard identifiers will be assigned a low priority."

d66d5891-3c2b-4d80-a278-ceadb646ad8b.Text: {n}The tech-shaman listens to the crackling coming from the hidden vox in response and shakes his head contritely.{/n} "The Great Pref does not recognise your name or your face. He will not grant you his friendship and bids you to leave."

e2c91793-85b8-4a51-b055-a550287a48d5.Text: {n}The tech-shaman listens to the crackling that comes in response and opens his mouth to say something, only for Pasqal to interrupt him in a tone of authority:{/n} "The Prefect Enumerator has stated that he knows my name and is familiar with my power. He respects my mission and grants me a place within the crew's chain of command. Your work here is done, binharic interpreter."

af49dfbb-83d5-42a8-b8c7-3e9bfded6b31.Text: "I am following the orders of my mentor, Archmagos Amarnat, and correcting a mistake made decades ago."

843b6459-5551-4416-bc05-1b539f9c493f.Text: "The Prefect Enumerator was commanded to limit the number of people who have clearance to issue orders, including even high-ranking Tech-Priests from other ships. It was tasked with defending the observatorium as if it were under siege. Our mutual introduction rather resembled an exchange of secret passwords."

7aea44c1-906b-4e0a-8b76-1dfcfac9de73.Text: {n}The tech-shaman bows his head, sneers, and rasps much like the crackling vox,{/n} "You speak, but the Great Pref isn't convinced that he should listen. He chooses to remain deaf and indifferent."

5d60214a-5b0e-43e5-ae61-7aa213a42581.Text: {n}The tech-shaman throws up his hands and interprets the volley of crackles emitted by the machine.{/n} "The Great Pref does not honour your reason for seeking his friendship. He wants you to leave."

a7401318-5d06-410b-bfdf-42c227abb847.Text: "The Iron Priests of Fenris can speak binharic using flutes, drums, and bone rattles. Some of the rituals they used to appease machine spirits loathe the sound of the vox."

ca6d8a07-33b8-438d-ae16-3e85482d6f85.Text: {n}Ulfar clutches his charm with one hand and his battle-ready weapon with the other. You hear him whisper tensely,{/n} "Spirit Wolf, shield my soul from the terrors of the warp and the ire of angered spirits."

52a40910-f248-477d-a480-1204caab8a69.Text: "Initiating reactivation of the access protocol, Lord Captain. A different combination of input data for the Prefect-Calculator may bypass the lock. This crippled machine-spirit is unlikely to retain the cogni-programmes required to track repeated attempts from a single unit, nor the counter to limit them."

b762ea2a-a757-4e66-a2c0-bfc009cea683.Text: "What do you seek from him who has Pref's ear, ghost?"

3a82ef62-3c94-475d-a2ec-2d7de70afe9c.Text: {n}The tech-shaman translates Pasqal's words into quick taps on his drum, its dangling circuit boards jingling dramatically. He inhales the aromatic exhaust of his roaring censer, listens carefully, and says in a strained voice,{/n} "Pref asks why he should treat your words with respect and not scorn them."

3c0b6925-d8e9-4e65-a92a-bc1fd022488d.Text: {n}Pasqal nods and enunciates,{/n} "By my power as a Magos Explorator decorated with four one-grade promotions and an entitlement to Category Three sacred augmentation, as well as likely the only active ordained Tech-Priest of the Adeptus Mechanicus aboard this voidship, I appoint myself this vessel's supreme hierarch."

6260ec73-1e24-43dc-bf1d-f1bd3bcaf700.Text: "Our deck's great patron spirit, who protects it and watches over everything that happens on it. Pref used to be a kind father to us until wicked people tricked him. That was when he disowned the mortals who lived here. He wiped the names of everyone who used to be under his patronage from his memory and no longer recognised their faces. Since then, Pref has been a harsh and cruel-hearted master who is deaf to our prayers."

0be185d4-88e9-43a5-863d-6f2e35daae98.Text: "The hypothesis is of merit. This unit is conducting a rescue mission in which the safety of an Archmagos-rank unit is at stake. Requesting emergency authorisation."

4f58c04c-71ae-40d8-b811-2a276381baf7.Text: {n}The tech-shaman translates Pasqal's words into a sharp staccato of drum taps, then nods with an important air and says,{/n} "Pref enquires why you are seeking his friendship."

ad88ddde-537c-4964-a06e-8f06ea27c724.Text: {n}Perhaps Pasqal's distinguished regalia will satisfy the exacting machine spirit.{/n}

f7959ca6-6e46-4fc7-9349-bee3a80ddd61.Text: "Hypothesis: the Prefect Enumerator's request is to be interpreted as 'What is the purpose of your visit?'"

7e8b8291-74cf-4e95-bfdf-a617514d8065.Text: "Pasqal, show him the Prefect Enumerator's authorisation that confirms your right to give orders."

f3e49178-848b-444c-a5eb-4f0a4e846fcf.Text: "We would like to go up to the observatorium."

8883f876-fc58-4712-b0cd-3aa181576300.Text: "A wise precaution. Give me a few minutes to prepare."

825d1c35-0fb6-46f2-b24a-b6532a806cb2.Text: {n}The ancient servitor seems dead. The infrequent twitching of his head is the only glimmer of life left in him. The numerous augmetic regalia embedded in the body of this servant of the Omnissiah speak to his high standing and devoutness.{/n}

8b465f79-83f0-415c-a495-96780bc7fff2.Text: {n}Raising his voice, the Tech-Priest solemnly repeats his command to the servitor.{/n}

47798c71-9caf-4fe5-a835-6fd0eceaca89.Text: "This statement is false. My archive has no record of any encounters with this unit or any archive requests concerning it. I... just know. And I grieve." {n}Pasqal touches the servitor's pale skin covered in inky cacography.{/n} "The tribespeople inscribed his body with the blessed Manual of Maintenance and Repair. Hypothesis: ignorant as to the true purpose of this litany, they perceived it as a health-replenishing magic spell."

c38e8953-c985-4eda-b308-d146025d4cb2.Text: "An Obscuratoria is a complete ban on holy ministry within the compound. Any and all sacred maintenance procedures are deferred until after the ban is lifted. An Obscuratoria is declared when a temple has been compromised by suspected corruption, before a battle, or in the event of a major critical incident..."

4c726d04-dd63-4ddb-8b81-67f71ee02dd6.Text: {n}An intricate, monumental, and piercing binharic aria pours from Pasqal's vox. Encoded in its signals is Haneumann's authority to give orders on this ship. The servitor stares at Pasqal with visored eyes and bows his head awkwardly.{/n} "Regalia identified. I greet the venerable Magos and will execute the order presently. Lift system activated."

5c673734-5630-4263-b365-e3101a63d162.Text: {n}The servitor's last words are drowned out by a harrowing screech that rolls across the deck as several shrill voices wail, "SssecuUrrRrity perRrrImmmeter brREeeach! FfForTheOmnissSsiah!"{/n}

2e67efea-2be4-4d19-a9c7-8afae5138e3a.Text: {n}The servitor gives a jolt, raises his head, and fixes his augmented eyes on you. The large black circles of his visors are cloudy and covered in scratches. A pained moan comes from the speaker on the servant's throat.{/n} "Un— un— unit status... operational. Unit ident— ident— identifies itself... as? No data available. Error... Error... Malfunction. The Omnissiah knows... what?"

7592d54f-ceea-4476-9f01-1b47fe0f1ce2.Text: {n}Pasqal enunciates solemnly, accompanying each word with binharic commands,{/n} "As its first pronouncement, this unit declares that no security threat to the high observatorium is present. As its second pronouncement, this unit orders the operation of the lift system to be restored. As its third pronouncement, this unit confirms its authorisation to issue that order."

b8258301-8ac5-442a-9f2c-678855ded0b6.Text: {n}The servitor's jerky movement is accompanied by a shower of sparks from his mouth. His optical visor makes a series of clicks.{/n} "Unit's hierarchical rank... not recognised. Authorisation to give orders... unconfirmed. Awaiting... confirmation."

65523f06-0b7d-49ec-b0ae-12a119da3b32.Text: "This unit is not part of the Hermetico chain of command. It must... introduce itself to the ship's system for confirmation of its authority."

d0000505-e1d3-4c62-9d33-58263a74d9d6.Text: "This unit cannot select the appropriate countermanding order without knowing the exact reason Obscuratoria was declared."

4847d10f-5a18-43ae-bc94-7d73390659e9.Text: {n}Pasqal sighs heavily.{/n} "He is suffering. This unit is long past its operational life expectancy, but the particularly ancient and sacred True Flesh it was awarded for its outstanding service to the fleet is still prolonging its years."

e4727944-4a8b-44e8-aca6-756140a282fe.Text: {n}A spasm in the servitor's neck makes his chin twitch.{/n}

7360844d-08c2-4db0-9d24-b9dc26e92d12.Text: "Tech-Brother Hectodon-XI, this unit identifies itself as Pasqal Haneumann. Can you hear me? Do you know me? Can you tell me what happened here?"

ebe0baf7-a9bd-4eac-bc97-41e25db09478.Text: {n}A jumble of sounds comes from the servitor's speaker, as if a very old man, who has outlived his faculty of speech, is trying to utter once-familiar words now strange to him. Then suddenly, a spark lights up his visors, and he utters with great strain,{/n} "Executing... function... all reserve capacities... engaged... in executing primary function."

86330f2e-e870-498b-8c53-f45f63f984c1.Text: "Hypothesis: as soon as the lift going up to the observatorium is operational, we will be attacked. The deck guard will activate and attack us. Requesting confirmation of readiness for combat."

b3915d21-b5b3-4612-9cb9-fedfec4ec84b.Text: "Hypothesis: Obscuratoria was declared ahead of a battle in order to hinder a hostile infiltration of the observatorium. Knowing the reason enables this unit to deactivate the containment protocol."

108129ce-20c0-4b1f-b93e-3b41d258cc00.Text: "Request denied!" {n}The rattle in the servitor's voice could be easily mistaken for indignation.{/n} "Access to the lift system denied! Service is in Obscuratoria mode."

ed6b1852-d0e6-486e-8024-400b25b90180.Text: {n}The Tech-Priest carefully touches the servitor's withered body with his mechadendrites. Data-spikes slide out of them and sink into the servitor's augmetics. Pasqal's vox sounds thoughtful and slightly puzzled.{/n} "I identify this unit as Magos Logis Hectodon-XI. The unit received seven commendations for advances in astrography recorded in the fleet archive. The unit... he liked watching the stars. He called them beacons left for us by the Omnissiah."

ed7ccea9-9716-4c17-9259-443b7db6eef7.Text: Laboured, stuttering growls and periodic rattling comes from beneath the casing.

dfc1c076-991e-41e7-abc8-9bc8d952ae63.Text: The cogitator by the door is no different from the others in the bay, but when you glance at the screen, a strange feeling of wrongness washes over you.

372b3e23-dff4-4ca9-955b-360591a51c93.Text: The lines on the screen look fuzzy, as though the cogitator's readout system or data storage has been damaged.

e43f8ce4-9989-4a5a-81ef-ec87ac6860d9.Text: The cogitators regularly display reports on the screens — endless chains of symbols, many of which only high-ranking Tech-Priests can likely understand.

d7f4e508-e7ae-4d1b-b23e-1f602352ba85.Text: An unfamiliar machine, barely visible in the flickering candlelight, hums quietly.

b1d30b57-41a8-4234-8d5a-71b8de472286.Text: The instrument terminal, an important part of the compartment's internal infrastructure, appears to be in working order.

775017e2-3fbe-401f-83e4-a9e0265e7b8a.Text: Instead of regular symbols and numbers, the screens display slanted script, almost resembling handwriting, in an unknown language.

fd690891-7177-4e1c-abce-1c48c23cb9cf.Text: The dead person's hands are stained red with blood, and strips of skin dangle from their flayed face.

f425768f-3baf-4f5d-b3f3-6a9ff98b4484.Text: A huge shell ready to be loaded into the macro-cannon breech.

78357d98-4e5f-451d-91d6-019e7656c723.Text: Only darkness can be seen in the open breech of the macro-cannon.

82ec90d1-d116-4eed-8fd2-8c5ff6cc31fc.Text: "The Lord Captain herself has come down to us... What a blessing..."

bfdd9fc6-92f3-46f8-bbf3-ca3156f54cc0.Text: "Hurry, hurry, before the Lord Captain gets angry..."

fc1d2491-1060-4f6e-bfc2-31b3bc822a14.Text: "But where did it go? I saw it right here..."

898beac3-99ee-4a31-a1e8-3c9f3dbb1199.Text: Something shifts and rolls under the mutant's skin.

b742387e-30d5-448b-b1c1-586130b4de3c.Text: The mutants are wearing defaced but still recognisable void suits, those typically worn by technomats in the ship's operational sections.

5658568c-9d66-418e-bd94-fb55df639973.Text: The mutant does not notice you — his blind eyes are coated in a cloudy iridescent film.

839753db-1991-4267-a282-b66681d4a4cc.Text: "Attack! The Lord Captain is with us!"

fd844bba-9e90-45af-8836-f0e4b748f067.Text: A spilt liquid, cloudy and carrying a strong chemical smell. It is the coolant used to stabilise the major cogitator systems.

6b9365f1-8d52-4acc-bcd1-c723b795fb14.Text: The people's remains have been hideously mutilated. The flesh seems to have melted at the edges and is thickly coated in stinking mucus.

25cd1cb8-fb6b-4b4a-ad90-51a74945af19.Text: "Ah, there you are, my little coward... Why won't you look at your captain, Idira?"

25ac5770-a084-448a-ab27-45590af63546.Text: "Look at her, {mf|boy|girl}. My little Idira is utterly trapped in her visions."

1b0fdac6-b571-4d63-a348-a5d3f0e31f2c.Text: "No matter... I will allay your doubts."

f92a099a-dc3a-47d9-adbd-0d40c64cc7a2.Text: "See? I have already begun assembling my new crew. These dregs proved themselves to be traitors, alas, but I have also found those who remained loyal to me!"

469b96c3-94d2-4d80-b2b0-ad7e48d52817.Text: "This is what servants loyal to their suzerain look like! Go forth, my subjects, protect your Lord Captain!"

36d61c87-1f15-49af-ae5c-28d8aeead70f.Text: "Where is she? I clearly remember her being around here somewhere..."

20f8fbe6-f601-4896-92c6-20754f12a6a1.Text: The wall lining is dented, as though someone tried to break their way out.

a4d0d363-639b-4551-80ce-5a0783671179.Text: "Idira, snap out of it. For Vigdis. She is going out of her mind with worry about you."

f6465afa-0a34-4198-a17e-60e309a84a95.Text: "Idira! Snap out of it, or I'll shoot you myself!"

aa8df8e1-bb97-421b-9b4c-5cb40e2a3851.Text: Allowed Argenta to execute the possessed Idira.

3c3f8098-57bb-453a-a886-57ee49dd2c8c.Text: Stopped Argenta from executing the possessed Idira.

c43eda5d-1f46-4ddf-9b92-56aee8203b11.Text: "Idira! I am your captain, not her! Listen to me and snap out of it!"

016b1474-9267-4a40-a115-6841f174db65.Text: {n}"Theodora" clucks her tongue in sympathy, reaching out to tenderly stroke Idira's hair.{/n} "Poor little Idira... There, there... How could I not come? You were crying for me so desperately, your pleas carried to the very depths of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} itself..."

75d601cb-3917-4553-9a24-8182fe7e4da6.Text: {n}Argenta wordlessly swings her weapon up and aims it at Idira, who is struggling in the monster's hold. The Sister of Battle looks at her without an ounce of doubt or mercy.{/n}

5428004e-d6b5-4f1c-949b-50b73d3fccea.Text: {n}One second — and Idira's body sags to the floor. At the same moment, you hear a terrifying sound — shrill and piercing laughter.{/n}

18e0d5ab-7cb3-4a62-9847-875f8382165f.Text: {n}Argenta wrinkles her nose at your shouted command and lowers the weapon by a few centimetres — but she does not put it away.{/n}

cb9183f8-fd7a-4def-b1cf-e08908734335.Text: {n}Idira lets out a soul-chilling howl and tries to grab the hand tearing into her, but her fingers pass through the monster's flesh.{/n} "I didn't hear anything! I didn't hear anything that could have had anything to do with you... I'm sorry, Lord Captain, I failed... Aaaah!" {n}Idira breaks into a strangled scream and you feel the air around you grow rapidly colder.{/n}

96f5a36b-3862-4897-bc5e-0ba6afd24aef.Text: {n}Your blow passes through the illusion. "Theodora" does not react to your shout, but continues to deliberately force her fingers under the {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g}'s skin. Black rivulets of blood seep from the wounds, streaking down Idira's contorted, shrieking face.{/n}

2b3f5d3a-5025-4722-aa02-b2a6f2d6e3a8.Text: {n}Idira stills for a moment, and then she pleads in a piteous, almost childlike voice,{/n} "Lord Captain... Help me..."

a324504e-f6df-4268-bf60-9b2c22a5b4fc.Text: "Oh, that would have been a real gift to our little Idira... Except her life belongs to me, not you!"

ce6dd6e9-8662-41b9-b9d6-fc5e1e9aec92.Text: {n}Idira shudders and goes limp. Then she blinks, disoriented, and looks at you.{/n} "L-Lord Captain..."

6736db84-ef6a-46b2-ac2b-023ffdf26b8f.Text: "Damn it!" {n}"Theodora" shoves the psyker away with a low snarl. The Rogue Trader's body begins to change, losing its human shape.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} will devour you! It will devour everyone responsible for my death! Die! Die for the delectation of my lord!"

04a3b2de-1b4d-499b-8eff-b7a59406be63.Text: "Don't even bother. She cannot hear you, little {mf|boy|girl}. She doesn't hear anyone but me."

d4763cee-5548-4f45-b90f-4377e42aab4d.Text: {n}Idira's body slides from "Theodora's" claws and sags to the floor. Piercing and shrill laughter suddenly fills the air.{/n}

1fa8731a-1e88-4b50-8046-c529637ae958.Text: "Lord Captain?" {n}Idira turns her head to you, but her demented gaze only rests briefly on your face before sliding away. Up close you can see that the base of one of Idira's temple {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} has blackened and melted.{/n} "No... Wait... Lord Captain... Lady von Valancius!" {n}Idira raises her eyes to "Theodora," who stands before her. Tears stream down Idira's cheeks.{/n} "You... you came back..."

d1c6e0a3-a911-40a0-a73e-a2c421a34992.Text: {n}"Theodora's" hands swell before your eyes, a dull liquid pulsating under the skin. A moment later, it streaks toward her fingers, which are driven deep under Idira's scalp. Idira convulses and shrieks in agony. A sound wave hits you in the face, leaving behind the tang of blood and the smell of decaying flesh.{/n}

34e38aff-aeb2-4d39-9cb4-ce91d0293006.Text: {n}The smile suddenly drops from her mutilated face.{/n} "Why didn't you save me? Why didn't you warn me? Answer me, you insignificant wretch, or I'll drag the answer out of you myself!" {n}"Theodora's" fingers dig into Idira's scalp, meeting no resistance.{/n}

0943118b-ec87-4b3f-adf0-8dcc9e6cd169.Text: {n}The figure of the cackling Theodora von Valancius shudders and begins to change form.{/n} "At last you begin to understand how important it is to promptly dispose of trash! But you've learned your lesson too late. Too late."

a6d1f5da-ec55-4b48-9896-11db64bfcb14.Text: "Has anything like this ever happened to you before?"

edf43f21-3b07-439b-ba62-7a1e067a8690.Text: "I eliminated the problem. Neither Idira nor the ghost of the departed Theodora will trouble us again. Once I'm finished here, make arrangements for the disposal of the bodies."

a3c5f9b7-93c9-47b5-834a-7ac930591ac3.Text: "I got rid of the warp's illusions. Idira is alive — bring her to the chirurgeons and have them see to her."

dea28a23-9bd2-41ea-af6d-69a9a35fe18e.Text: "You hear the warp whispering in your head, and you answered? Are you insane?"

05e1607d-5a58-4cd7-b754-629a76c287c6.Text: "The warp tricked you. It played upon your feelings. I can understand why, but that is no excuse for what you did."

b06e4d05-f871-4b27-af59-63df996a9081.Text: "Enough. Sister Argenta, carry out the Emperor's will and destroy this heretic."

70584a95-62e7-4cde-a3f9-627b3cd8015c.Text: "This abomination claims that you called her. Is this true?"

2da87797-426f-49ee-a4ec-65deb7b18789.Text: "Your worries do not interest me, but as long as you keep yourself under control and remain useful, you will live."

8b43c4e0-da06-40e8-82c8-dc384ef2ed2f.Text: "I'm not going to kill you, but keeping you in the crew is dangerous. You'll be put under guard and escorted from the ship at the first orbital stop we come to."

154187a2-cf6b-4ab8-bf34-56c1def79ba6.Text: "I want to help you, Idira. We'll think of something."

f7a863cf-210f-42ff-bfd8-6ec66a49b0e6.Text: "The previous Rogue Trader has been seen on the ship recently. Was that your doing?"

cdca13c3-ff30-40fd-bf6d-2fa11c8929c5.Text: "What will happen to my crew while we look for this 'remedy'?"

cf672e1e-c1d4-4c94-8554-971d3e6ec906.Text: "So what am I supposed to do with you now?"

917a52e5-ada9-437f-8f98-ab2b870d9a42.Text: Ordered Argenta to execute Idira after she summoned "Theodora."

e36071c2-b8fe-4694-81cb-3bff47164885.Text: "I got rid of the psyker's creations. Idira is alive — see that she gets medical attention, and then put a guard on her. If she succumbs to the warp's influence again — shoot her without warning."

273585f8-b7c5-499d-ae20-dacfdaf45d70.Text: Personally executed Idira after she summoned "Theodora."

f7ef9dd0-ff09-4da6-a508-c12b3ef4a536.Text: [Kill Idira] "Your weakness will be the death of us all. I will not allow it."

78db5113-e925-4170-9547-4e6d8868aa6d.Text: "I handled the problems in the bay, although there is one matter outstanding: see to it that Idira Tlass leaves the ship at the next port. I cannot risk keeping her in my crew."

8a640420-7d33-4e26-978a-3e85dc8ecdde.Text: "Everyone who was on the deck is dead, including the attackers. What happened was entirely the fault of Idira Tlass. Dispatch servitors here and put her out through an airlock, I am sick of her antics."

87c5f976-32d4-4ad1-aef6-77c8c257d871.Text: {n}Idira stares at you with crazed eyes while clutching the wounds on her head. At first, no sound comes out of her moving lips, then she coughs weakly and whispers,{/n} "Lord Captain, is it... really you?"

8329815e-7ebf-4b23-b8d2-f4712968bd6d.Text: "Sometimes a psyker's first manifestation leads to their death and the deaths of many others. But if a psyker possesses inordinate willpower and discipline, they can stave off their fall for some time. Idira has been alive many years already — a laudable achievement and a stroke of incredibly good fortune — but the forces of the warp will ultimately devour any psyker deprived of the Emperor's protection. The fact that these manifestations are growing more powerful is a clear sign that the end is near."

1ffad7c5-2c12-4ce6-892d-2556e5dce5eb.Text: {n}Argenta trains her weapon on Idira and watches you closely.{/n}

6c067f0c-ea6e-4c1a-9924-fa93392441e0.Text: {n}For a moment the airwaves are filled with something that sounds somewhat like breathing, somewhat like ordinary interference.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain."

935bd989-c1ac-49e8-aee5-f09b54a5693c.Text: {n}You hear unconcealed relief in the Vox Master's voice.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain. As you command."

321fe26f-c502-4821-ba42-3b492304bac8.Text: "You don't know what it's like — the most important person in your life, who's now gone forever, suddenly starts talking to you inside your head! How could I not try to reach her? I had to!"

e361e471-117e-4b95-aad7-b47596723ade.Text: {n}Idira lets out a plaintive scream — and then sags to the ground like a broken toy.{/n}

921e10ef-5183-4b6e-bb57-fb44b52664e0.Text: "I... can barely remember. The voices, my old, good whispers, they suddenly turned red... sharp... They started cutting, tearing, ripping me to pieces. I cried out, I called for help... and she came." {n}Idira groans and clutches her head.{/n} "Damn it, why are the voices making so much noise now? Shut up! Shut UP!"

ccadd10b-a58c-4eaf-8d01-14264fc890a0.Text: {n}Idira nods and with visible effort forces herself to smile.{/n} "Understood, {name}. I swear I'll be more useful than ever before."

45bcd8cd-74c6-4b1f-87ea-95b12b7e5f50.Text: {n}Idira covers her face with her hands and tries to hold back her sobs.{/n} "Th-Thank you... Thank you, {name}! I won't let you down!"

09ddc696-b561-4a43-8e08-cae7b622fd10.Text: {n}Idira shudders in fear and reluctantly nods.{/n} "I... understand. Of course. Thank you, {name}. Forgive me... and farewell."

4554c153-f876-452b-b43d-513c135e5f32.Text: "Me? Did I...? Yes, Lord Captain... I think it was me who called her."

75c0343b-1039-4cb0-b594-c5062aff1d9e.Text: "Like this — never! Well, there was something... but it was different. It wasn't as strong, or as terrifying. Apparitions appeared. Mechanisms malfunctioned. The crew lost their minds..." {n}Idira breaks off.{/n} "But Lady von Valancius knew about that. She said it was a small price to pay, an acceptable expense! No {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} is immune to it! But what happened here... it was just a mistake. I won't do it again!" {n}Idira stretches her lips in a helpless smile, looking past you.{/n} "There will be no more mistakes, Lord Captain."

0958bb27-5d99-493b-82bb-15536504cc6c.Text: {n}Argenta grits her teeth.{/n} "This is not the first time this... heretic has caused the death of her crew. Do you remember the incident on the mid-deck, Idira? What did those honest souls ever do to deserve such a fate? To be turned into mutants and attack their own families? You are a monster. A heretic. If you have any humanity left in you, admit what you are!"

92a21aeb-a0af-47da-bc76-492adb66453f.Text: "Yes, {name}. I did it a couple of times, when I'd had too much to drink... At the time, I thought I heard her voice among all the whispers in my head. The voice was so sad, so clear... I couldn't help myself — I answered. I hoped I could reach her... there."

7f3918b6-cd12-471f-8865-e2bfa1532511.Text: {n}Idira turns sharply to face you.{/n} "{name}... I know after everything I've done, you have no faith in my willpower or my strength, but I can fix everything. It's just I'm not at my best, you see, but maybe we can find a way? To replace my {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g}. Or some other remedy, a better one. Lady von Valancius said that such a thing could be found — if not here, then elsewhere. I just didn't need it before, but... We just need to find it. We need to figure out where to look for it, and we'll get it! And until then, I'll keep myself on a tight leash!"

13d79026-d500-4cd6-bc88-15819e85a02c.Text: {n}Idira lets out a desperate shriek and tries to hide from the inevitable, but the Sister of Battle's strike finds its target. The {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g}'s body slowly sags to the floor.{/n}

6f6a3c8e-e32e-47f3-9f80-62dc80104667.Text: {n}Idira removes her hand from her head and tries to wipe away her tears, leaving bloody marks on her face. Then she touches her burnt-out {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g}, frowning.{/n} "I... don't know. It should be quiet... but in my head... the whispering's louder. It shouldn't be... like that."

f8b3294b-2dcc-4937-bf59-9ff1b9abf4b9.Text: {n}Idira swallows and straightens.{/n} "I'll pull myself together, Lord Captain. The death of Lady von Valancius knocked me for six — I'll get myself under control. No more booze, no more obscura, nothing. And I'll stop walking around the lower decks. I'll be stone-cold sober." {n}She determinedly wipes the tears and blood from her face.{/n}

f72ae1a2-78ee-46a0-9437-8db08c065d13.Text: "Why? I've heard enough stories about ways of extending a psyker's life. But I don't think you'll like all of them."

1cd7aee4-5ada-4beb-890b-14b44a497754.Text: {n}Idira bites her lip.{/n} "Ever since she died... Since I first heard her voice in my head... the whispers have gotten louder. Clearer. Harder to resist."

3152a94c-e339-4cb9-b85c-9248908cc52f.Text: "You did the right thing, Lord Captain. There is no way back for a fallen psyker."

ae669c08-945c-468e-9830-8f088b8b03cd.Text: "You are making a mistake, Lord Captain. Perhaps you will find something to slow the decline, but it will not stop it. Only a miracle can save Idira Tlass now."

549a9fb4-5728-4134-8b1c-10f6f817b90f.Text: {n}Idira awkwardly shakes out her stained clothing.{/n} "I... I think I'd better... With your permission, Lord Captain..." {n}She sways, takes a step back — and faints.{/n}

48f28b79-825b-4b70-b212-b2b3af9207a0.Text: "Forgive me, {name}. I know I let you down. I let everybody down... But it started off well, didn't it? You didn't shoot me or chase me off... All I had to do was keep control of myself and the two of us would have gotten along fine! I threw away my chance!"

081dd739-78d7-4d26-8b82-afcbfa1d3785.Text: "Lord Captain... Of course. Consider it done."

955a7c8d-2f25-452e-8263-d589473c218b.Text: "Shut up..." {n}Idira moans.{/n} "Quit your preaching, you're the worst out of everyone here!"

bfbde0ef-6bc9-421b-8dc8-7026ba01af25.Text: "Lord Captain?" {n}The Vox Master's shaking voice comes over the comm-bead.{/n} "I received a report that the shooting on the lower deck had stopped. I presume you have brought the situation under control. Awaiting further instructions."

2d64a171-4b5c-4ddf-85ac-76e3b3a84291.Text: "{g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} grant her—" {n}Abelard stops short, staring at the body unblinkingly for a few seconds, before turning away.{/n}

87a77a87-ef02-493b-9623-70ea4cd90464.Text: {n}She falls silent for a moment. When she next begins to speak, it is in a barely audible whisper.{/n} "I know what you're thinking. During the warp jump, when Lady Theodora came out toward us... I keep thinking about that meeting. I keep blaming myself... Why didn't I divine it? Why didn't I stop her killer? These thoughts have been playing at the back of my mind, day after day... choking me with guilt... and do you know what? The one... on the officers' deck... I don't know what that was. But this time... here... this was the product of my guilt. An accuser straight out of my own mind."

549cfcf2-44dd-4a65-a316-a8b422f46f15.Text: {n}Wielding a sampling tool, a {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} carefully reaches out toward the bloody mess that used to be Idira's brain and dips the tip into it.{/n} "I will preserve an organic specimen for future study."

856acecb-915a-463d-81aa-84dd1c18c6df.Text: "If you are Theodora, then tell me — who really killed you?"

bd60168e-2b06-490c-817b-0ad858a8751c.Text: "Where's Idira? What have you done with her?"

8d720e83-e3ef-4807-b114-01ac50038454.Text: "You are not Theodora. Theodora is dead. There is no coming back from that."

dba1261c-9242-4bf9-9a08-80f65ca6a9e3.Text: "I'm sorry we could not help you, but you do not belong here."

b873c60f-9492-4ccc-9dc1-7acd2c25e974.Text: "I will send you back into the abyss you crawled out of."

164f0b9a-cb81-4b59-9476-787206d57e2e.Text: "What do you want with me? Why were you waiting for me?"

3874b645-e464-4d7c-8e85-2537b5847426.Text: {n}Theodora von Valancius is before you, and she looks grotesque: a hole yawns wide in her chest, rusted hooks protrude from beneath her skin, and a lumpen, inflamed scar cuts across her throat. The figure flickers, as though it is dropping in and out of this reality. She looks at you with the whitish eyes of a corpse and smiles venomously.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}! We meet at last! I had grown tired of waiting for you to pay me a visit." {n}"Theodora's" look is appraising, and her mocking tone turns to one of distaste.{/n} "Indeed, centuries of selfless toil and effort, and everything I left behind has gone to this nonentity."

ddf8bd62-9d03-4379-bbda-985c19b98c61.Text: "Argenta, my dear, there's no need to make such a fuss. Why don't we sit down over a cup of {g|Encyclopedia:Recaf}recaf{/g} like we used to? I'll listen to your rapturous tales of sacred relics, portents, and your special path. You must have been so lonely without me here — no one else is willing to listen to your ravings, or help you with your childish treasure hunt..." {n}"Theodora" laughs melodiously, almost without mockery.{/n}

bfe47a42-4849-41e9-af32-3169a2f01dc3.Text: {n}At the sight of the terrifying "Theodora," Abelard's face turns sickly pale.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Throne{/g} spare us from the cursed apparitions of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}..."

3c523ce3-7046-4fd7-aa77-fceeb0ad3cc1.Text: "Is that what you are truly praying for? I can hear how fast your heart is pounding, Werserian — I think deep down you hope this apparition never ends."

98939605-ef10-45fc-8a1d-f7ab92d72544.Text: {n}"Theodora's" lips curl in a malevolent smile.{/n} "'What', you ask? You dare say that to me, little {mf|boy|girl}? I am Theodora von Valancius Massimo af Scarus, Rogue Trader of the Imperium and commander of this voidship."

b10acb1b-c024-464e-b5eb-ce666fce0457.Text: {n}"Theodora" wearily rolls her eyes.{/n} "Matters are so dire that the pleas of one of my servants breached death's veil to reach my ears — how could I ignore such a desperate cry for help, and from my little Idira, no less? And, once I appeared here, of course I had to meet the pretender who has allowed this deplorable state of affairs."

1265a40d-5920-40c0-9d55-e6810426dd77.Text: "Me? What have I done with Idira?" {n}"Theodora" laughs mockingly.{/n} "All I did was turn that little mutt from the fringes into a true servant of the Imperium. I gave her toys, I cleaned up after her antics, I provided her with everything she could ever dream of. Oh, I had great plans for poor little Idira!"

96589b5c-6870-49c6-9d23-c2bff69375d3.Text: "I truly am Theodora — the remnants of herself that she left behind in this world. I am an echo of her memories preserved in the minds of those who cared for her. I am the taste of tears spilt for the unsaid and the undone. I am the terror of she who failed to turn the tide of fate and who refuses to look truth in the face. I am as real as the human passions that bring worlds to ruin."

ac6050a8-7d37-499c-996d-2f880e975b97.Text: "Oh, wouldn't you like to know the answer to that question! I don't even know which would be more satisfying — to give you an honest answer or leave you to languish in your ignorance. Hmm... we'll see how you conduct yourself, little {mf|boy|girl}."

57f20b59-f742-4170-864a-920050556d89.Text: "Alas, my glorious voyage through life was ended in the dullest possible way — by death. A nuisance I staved off as long as I could. But do not weep for me, my {mf|boy|girl}: I am still keeping an eye on my property. And punishing all those who failed me." {n}"Theodora" bares her rotten teeth in a snarl, her laughter piercing.{/n}

c315f36e-6811-47e9-a52e-7a6f4bcba21a.Text: {n}"Theodora" tosses her head back and laughs. The scar on her throat opens with a wet sucking noise, curving into a horrible facsimile of a smile.{/n} "{mf|He|She} feels sorry for me! Wretched, spineless creature! No, the only one worthy of pity here is you, {mf|boy|girl}. But do not expect any. I am not here to console you, oh no!"

ec8688fc-4b0a-4615-b286-deb5397f0830.Text: {n}The strike passes through "Theodora," who simply laughs scornfully.{/n} "So that's how you greet your great predecessor, {mf|boy|girl}? Bonds stronger than the laws of life and nature are holding me in this world. You will find it somewhat harder to get rid of me a second time."

079322a5-0609-46c6-8ff1-dd6ccf8c1de6.Text: "I am here to seek retribution against all who failed me. My brainless crew. My useless officers. My pathetic servants, who turned their backs on their mistress in her darkest hour. And worst of all — you, my dear heir. You, who have undeservedly claimed the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} and everything else that is mine. I will drag it all to the warp with me — including you!"

00ca2587-3356-4a5f-bbae-924c7cf265b3.Text: "You? Of all the people to ever threaten me, you are the most pathetic, {mf|boy|girl}. All that you possess now was given to you in error. You are unworthy of such a generous gift and you are incapable of holding onto it."

9b9a8aa9-73eb-42c6-ba44-45475c39acf1.Text: "And who now deigns to grace us with their presence? Another gaggle of heretics and traitors thirsting to get their due for what they've done? Or is it the leader {mf|himself|herself}, who has finally grown tired of hiding behind others?"

ccd2a51d-ac80-498d-84fd-31559af1b673.Text: "I'm dead? How is that? I am no different from those who have not yet crossed the divide between reality and eternity. I see. I speak. I remember the wrongs you all committed against me. And for all those who failed me — I have already begun exacting my retribution."

b6909bd4-b8ef-4e2b-8e93-f58287a344a9.Text: {n}Argenta's eyes spark with fury.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Warp}Warp{/g} illusion! Begone!"

b3481a41-bbb7-440d-b0dd-dc6aa755e4ea.Text: "Of course, {mf|boy|girl}, for it was I who gave the order to bring you here, to my ship. Oh, how I rue that decision now! And how I regret heeding the advice of my Seneschal!"

831d3461-2748-4ae5-8be9-42d8c5565b01.Text: {n}Abelard whispers hurriedly to you,{/n} "How can this be? It is the same vision as on the officers' deck... and yet entirely different. Why does it not remember that meeting? And... why does it remember what the real Lady Theodora did?"

7b890730-58ee-4990-aace-7060ba4883c4.Text: "You are not Domin'Theodora!" {n}Kibellah's eyes blaze with fury.{/n} "The Undying One does not relinquish the souls that come to Him — such is the absolute truth! You are a thief of names!"

d75b9508-d3c7-4b07-9f89-b83a2bb71d08.Text: "Foolish child. Your world is limited to the darkness of the lower decks and the words of your Vizsier. You know nothing of truth or death. You do not even know the first thing about yourself." {n}"Theodora's" voice is dripping with venomous condescension.{/n}

54e01f87-1e34-48de-9119-d9a0ba03c0d7.Text: "Everything is in order. We will not be seeing any more ghosts. But Idira has had a rough time of it. Send a cleanup team to the hold and call a chirurgeon for Idira. She needs time to recover."

b6036b14-6006-4635-8e14-d3775df4be1c.Text: "I eliminated the problem. Neither Idira nor the ghost of the departed Theodora will trouble us again. See to it that the bodies on the lower deck are disposed of."

e58d95e9-01d2-4c77-8f38-c0190903e6a1.Text: "Everything is under control. The rebels have been pacified, and the ghost of Theodora won't trouble us again. Idira won't cause us any more problems either — see to the disposal of the bodies."

6990d30d-15c6-4396-a8ad-d9433c34c035.Text: "The situation is under control. Put a guard on Idira Tlass. If she tries anything else — shoot her without warning."

74f69ca5-12e5-4bb9-875b-eec3e023e340.Text: "The rebels have been dealt with, but I will not tolerate another stunt like that from anyone on board. Have Idira Tlass tossed out of an airlock."

13e6b3f7-01fe-48b6-8d36-4f365543d498.Text: "See to it that Idira Tlass leaves the ship at the next port. I cannot risk keeping her in my crew."

033894ec-75ed-40eb-b39e-16d08ef429aa.Text: "What happened was entirely the fault of Idira Tlass. Put her out through an airlock, I am sick of her antics."

0e31f9b8-f8ff-4cfe-818e-6eb209abb0da.Text: "Everything is in order. Have Idira taken to her cabin and assign a chirurgeon to her."

9cb67ad2-ce9c-4702-b675-f63d1008c8a6.Text: "You were right. Idira summoned the 'ghost' of Theodora. Keeping her in the crew is out of the question — she cannot control her abilities. See to it that she leaves the ship at the nearest port. Give her some money if she asks for it."

51613fcb-05d1-4650-a29f-432a43771f4b.Text: "The 'ghost' of my predecessor was the work of Idira. She needs medical attention. See to that, and have her put under constant guard. I'll decide what to do with her later."

2aa655cb-8aea-4ef7-a5e8-3efb2cefcd4e.Text: "Lord Captain?" {n}The Vox Master's voice, usually calm and reserved, shakes traitorously, fighting through the low-level static.{/n} "I saw a message about shooting in the bay. What happened? Did you manage to restore order? And what condition is Idira in?"

9a07cc51-f3b8-498f-8f10-ce333bf7e2a6.Text: "Lord Captain?" {n}The Vox Master's voice, usually calm and reserved, shakes traitorously, fighting through the low-level static.{/n} "I received a message about shooting on the lower deck. Did you manage to restore order? What condition is Idira in?"

251fd7d6-c65d-40a3-b406-7d5f81b6ca7f.Text: "Lord Captain?" {n}The Vox Master's voice shakes traitorously.{/n} "I received a report that the shooting on the lower deck had stopped. I presume you have brought the situation under control. Awaiting further instructions."

5d533a8a-d144-4f15-8c87-396b1a6b2535.Text: {n}You detect unconcealed relief in the Vox Master's voice.{/n} "As you command, Lord Captain."

ae9da08d-12c3-499c-b525-a582276cea6b.Text: {n}For a moment the airwaves are filled with something that sounds somewhat like breathing, somewhat like ordinary interference.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain."

abb37056-15e4-4743-8884-e99363b21c8f.Text: {n}You hear unconcealed relief in the Vox Master's voice.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain. As you command."

aa35547b-5b72-4efc-ad4f-eb95100fbda3.Text: "Lord Captain... Of course. Consider it done."

cb3b5122-a792-4828-a740-c95746f47a5f.Text: {n}It is difficult to say if what you hear is a gasp of surprise or simply an uptick in interference. But the Vox Master answers you with only the slightest hesitation.{/n} "As you command, Lord Captain. I will send the cleanup team to you right away."

85622501-a680-45f1-a314-fa5f336f01bb.Text: "Lord Captain, the voices are so noisy, they're calling me — the door must be around here! We need to go farther, deeper..."

c22bc5d8-dfa3-456d-9530-e4274b8b2666.Text: "We're close! I can almost feel the door handle in my hand... What? Yes, yes, I hear you, my sweet whispers, just guide us, please!"

c36c4dbd-e6c9-4b74-8744-f8feeaff0081.Text: "I've seen this corridor before. We should turn right, we're almost there. Is this a dream? No? Who cares anyway, only one way to go... Yes, it's to the right!"

918ceefa-3472-42a6-861d-d9528dbe21b1.Text: "Well, that takes care of that freak. So, uh, Lord Captain, will you take me to the door?"

6d5348d2-98fd-4c79-a113-1702f9ef1ce7.Text: [Draw your weapon] "It will be my pleasure to end a vile xenos!"

36a6e806-ec72-4024-b6f1-905b658345ad.Text: "I shall grant you a swift death."

419564a7-7cb2-4b36-8a86-f48faa971cf1.Text: "I shall kill you for the sole reason that I enjoy killing xenos."

d34fc1f5-d011-4ae1-98ed-d1472aaca8d0.Text: "The Haemonculus is dead. You are free."

c7af77ba-5bc3-40bc-9e53-99330f629b9a.Text: "All I need is the implant on your head. Give it to me, and I shall set you free."

a6fd1d6d-d270-4b26-880c-fb10bac4f8b1.Text: "I will not take your life. Farewell."

df99ef58-1039-4966-a81a-12db56974ffe.Text: [Draw your weapon] "I cannot deny the request of one who is in torment."

22f656b9-d8d7-4342-9623-2d46196c4a9a.Text: {n}You see a contorted, agony-racked Aeldari — or, more accurately, something that resembles one. Dozens of scars and sutures cover its face, the sight of its misaligned joints moving under its skin makes your stomach turn, and its singular eye looks devoid of sanity. And yet, as you examine the creature's tattered clothes, you can still recognise, albeit with some difficulty, the ceremonial raiment of a Farseer.{/n}

f429eaef-5ed2-4768-b3d8-715c151ecd21.Text: "A hollow shell forced into servitude. Every thread of my being calls out to me, urging me to claim your lives, only stopped by the fading remnants of my former self. Quickly. I demand that you give my death to me and break the shackles of this nightmare." {n}The Farseer's crooked fingers reach for his temples — and now you notice the sinister-looking device on his head.{/n}

a241ded4-03fd-4247-b277-65e624314551.Text: "I have never been merciful to xenos. I have no desire to start now. Let him suffer until death claims him."

5a7a4d9d-0b61-406c-902e-6599f46d054a.Text: "I have no reason to lie to you, mon-keigh. However, your beliefs are of no matter. You are already here, which means I will finally die."

86cd8488-d815-48a6-95f4-149dae892272.Text: {n}Yrliet takes a quivering breath.{/n} "Who are you? I do not recognise you, but your vestments..."

ae195bc5-3358-43b1-ba78-c45aa658da0a.Text: "A child... of our dead home? I do not remember you. But it gladdens me on the cusp of death to behold a spark... of the Asuryani."

b1b8fef1-5b3a-4db2-aa93-0ed06f5acd52.Text: "No. It's not fair. Is this my salvation? Are you telling me I escaped bloody Commorragh just to put that thing back on my head willingly?" {n}Dismayed, she keeps looking between you and the xenos.{/n}

2ee0fd6e-d183-4ea8-b1f8-44495417dca2.Text: "I... spent aeons harnessing my gift. I guided... an entire world. My gaze... pierced the future, looking epochs ahead. And even I am... at my limit, clinging desperately to the meagre relics of what I once called my soul just to speak another word. Who gave you the audacity to think you will fare any better?"

fe46a559-9c3f-4cb0-bb32-39afc517f500.Text: "I will not give you another choice, mon-keigh."

ec49e509-6546-4509-8f5a-603671bcc5c1.Text: {n}The xenos tries to let out a laugh.{/n} "I have not been given permission. The master is dead? Then I am compelled to kill his executioners."

4ae94705-3d75-491e-8fd8-9ccf17c39153.Text: {n}The Aeldari hisses and howls, his crooked fingers tearing his ragged robes apart.{/n} "It is too late! My mind is poisoned. My soul is marred. I do not know for what purpose you need this cursed machine, mon-keigh, but if your mind carries a shred of reason, then destroy it along with me."

1103b294-f059-42e1-8e79-1f656ece7bbd.Text: {n}Idira suddenly leans forward. Anger and desperation are written all over her face.{/n} "Not a chance, xenos! That thing, that... psy-stifler, it will save my life! You... you're just weak, that's why you can't handle it!"

c252a99d-4a9f-4a63-9150-ec287f59f995.Text: "Naive child. You would condemn yourself to a fate of true horror. Heed me when I say there are things far worse than death."

a27ec4b2-928b-4798-89b7-9dcaa1f22cfe.Text: "It hides the soul within the warp from the spawn of Chaos without severing its connection to realspace. And it slowly consumes the soul. Day after day the soul erodes and withers until nothing remains but emptiness."

c4ab0ccd-49ff-4cf6-82c9-a44ce2ff641f.Text: {n}Idira bursts out laughing, her voice hoarse and hysterical.{/n} "Oh, this half-baked guff is killing me. What, does that mean it wasn't my own salvation I saw in my dreams, it was this half-dead xenos's 'deliverance'? Come off it! Don't you buy any of this crap, Lord Captain, he's just trying to mess with our heads!"

2d43958c-3810-4831-b7c5-0dfc21b97647.Text: "He was tortured by the same xenos who held you captive and brutally murdered your friends. You are comrades in misfortune in a way. Don't you have any sympathy for him at all?"

aae970b9-3c6c-4ac6-9958-fb8a46605c06.Text: {n}Idira interposes herself between you and the xenos.{/n} "No, Lord Captain, wait! Look!" {n}She points a shaking hand at the Aeldari's head.{/n}

b8fd4086-fe10-46d6-bfb2-b6faf1f545b4.Text: {n}The Farseer rises from his knees in a jerking motion, like a broken marionette, and takes a step toward you with glassy eyes. His frail fingers move as if tugged by invisible strings, and the mutilated bodies of the twisted creatures in the tanks start convulsing synchronously. In frightening unison, their unblinking eyes shift to you.{/n}

3e79bafc-ec2c-4171-9739-2e04db45c674.Text: "Comrades? What in the kraken's arsehole are you talking about?" {n}Ulfar shakes his head, perplexed.{/n} "I am a descendant of the Allfather, and he is a vile inhuman. Compare me with a knife made of honest plasteel, broken in the Haemonculus's hand, and you will find more similarities than I have with this wretch. He can suffer — you can see that he is no commoner, so he has no doubt done his share of vile deeds in his life."

d2582f54-2472-4977-b7dc-82496d002cfa.Text: "At last... my deliverance. Mon-keigh? The disgrace. The humiliation of falling at the hand of a lesser creature... Enough. The anticipation of this moment is all that has allowed me to retain a vestige of reason. End me now."

c1b5ec3d-a8d7-4098-b814-4068ed377746.Text: "Tervantias's plaything. The master used me... by means of that which now entangles my mind and bends me and my powers to its will. I am the tool that conceals this lair from prying eyes with the energies of the veil. Had the mon-keigh seer not heard my pleas for help... you never would have found me."

3451c2f3-b59e-4384-b22e-ffe238265176.Text: {n}Idira freezes, her eyes locked on the familiar translucent threads of the psy-stifler coiled in sickening patterns around the Aeldari's temples like a crystal vice.{/n}

8fd8907b-4bb3-45bc-93e1-bf786ecf3e45.Text: {n}Translucent threads coil in strange, sickening patterns around the Aeldari's temples, sinking into the skin on his face, neck, and clavicles. In the dim, cold light of the laboratory, the device resembles glistening carrion worms that are mercilessly drinking the xenos's mind dry.{/n}

5ad57473-66bb-4d03-ada0-c9f9b9bd7702.Text: {n}Idira gives you a puzzled glance.{/n} "I think... that's what we're here for. I can barely see this xenos's aura in the warp. Must be the work of that thing on his head."

22ccf2c3-3c63-44f9-adb8-a3e6ea09eaf2.Text: "Is that right? You certainly talk a lot for someone who's supposed to be empty. Before all this, you must have never shut up!"

7bbc3828-c245-4d17-b053-4395841b73dc.Text: {n}The Aeldari doubles over in an anguished paroxysm, his voice ringing like a taut string.{/n} "My silent cries pierced the veil and sent visions of this prison beyond its walls. They carried with them all my dreams of deliverance and liberation. Is that not the reason for your coming?"

6bbc7c6b-3aef-487b-a3dc-795491e0a846.Text: "Then you should trust your feelings. Go ahead, try to open it."

bbeafc45-596b-4fc3-bf1d-36b7f5f96078.Text: "Are you sure you are not mistaken? We can search for a while longer."

a45754f3-bf43-4cb4-ad03-f6863d304cbd.Text: "I knew you were delusional. Come. We have wasted enough time on this."

1e39849a-a090-4539-84a5-7e76c03bbd0d.Text: "As long as we are together, we will get through this, Idira. Trust me."

50063f68-a088-4718-8c7d-35df55e2dd01.Text: "My faith in the Emperor is stronger than any warp trickery. He protects us."

136ce41a-63a0-4edf-831f-0cf21d104148.Text: "This sounds like a challenge! I was just thinking about acquiring a new skull for my collection."

f5e1ed34-6c9e-4c71-9322-6bdb18e38b1c.Text: {n}Idira stares intently at the solid wall in front of her, shifting from foot to foot and biting her nails. The wall looks like an ordinary plasteel and rockcrete surface, no different from any other in here.{/n}

b096d14b-44ac-4fa6-9c09-d715a1f4ccee.Text: "Lord Captain... This is it. The place from my visions, even the scratches on the walls are the same. Except for one thing." {n}She points at the wall.{/n} "That's where the door is supposed to be. The one I keep opening in my dreams every night. I've seen this moment so many times it feels more real to me than I am. My visions couldn't have lied to me..."

5240a9e5-9fcd-4e9c-9e43-5c4c4e797ac0.Text: {n}Heinrix looks at Idira without blinking.{/n} "A trap, then. You've been played, Idira. A cruel trick, one that could only have come from the warp's twisted will."

5a4404df-c0a5-415e-af2f-7c02ba417165.Text: "Open a door that doesn't exist? Ha, the things you say sometimes, Lord Captain! Well, it wouldn't be the strangest thing we've ever done. Oh, what the warp, what have I got to lose? Here goes..."

dc9c965c-3984-4016-8a7d-ab7a00144df0.Text: "I've never been more sure in my life. This is the spot. Hmm, what if I just..."

b11984df-1f97-400b-92c0-812f830672e6.Text: "No! It must be here, it can't not be here! Please, just let me try something. Maybe I am delusional, but it's still my last hope."

79609a1e-17de-4a76-a5dd-e8e34da3a12f.Text: {n}Idira steps closer to the wall and reaches out toward the non-existent door. As if in a trance, she clenches her fingers as if gripping an invisible handle and slowly turns it. You hear a click.{/n}

529a7408-e2d0-47d4-8dd5-7b7e105502a4.Text: {n}A violent ripple tears through the space around the wall. A cacophony of whispers makes your skin crawl from head to toe like an unseen wave emanating from twisted, broken reality. Uneven rays of impossible, nauseating light break through the rockcrete, forming the silhouette of a doorway. Eventually, the vision passes, and you clearly see a door where a blank wall used to be.{/n}

b3c54b9e-6fe4-4f09-98d2-377f11608644.Text: {n}Idira turns to you with a wide and somewhat deranged smile.{/n} "Lord Captain, we found it — it's the door! Exactly like the one in my visions, which means my salvation is close."

d960992d-5545-482a-9104-f358ad55eb39.Text: {n}Idira looks somewhat emboldened by your words. She smiles.{/n} "Well, you're not wrong — we've been through worse, haven't we? Thanks, Lord Captain! I won't let you down!"

2b8413e0-540d-4eec-a8dc-9b644eee75e9.Text: {n}Idira awkwardly clears her throat and nods, not looking too convinced.{/n} "I hope you're right, Lord Captain. Taking a lightning bolt to the gut is something I'd like to avoid, so here's hoping the Emperor doesn't have anything more important to protect right now."

e869f97c-0f6e-44f5-ba42-4c6cd4183a72.Text: "Just, while you're busy lopping off heads, please try not to break whatever or whoever it is we're looking for! I don't think we'll ever get another chance like this."

57d90847-e354-4f14-bdde-3846719c4b15.Text: {n}Idira rolls her eyes theatrically.{/n} "Of course, no one ever takes pity on the witch! Any excuse to get rid of her!"

ebc7d0d0-e4fd-4266-8eae-f3fdecf04ba9.Text: "Except..." {n}She frowns in concern.{/n} "Except it wasn't hidden by some force field contraption, it was a powerful warp barrier. I could never have removed something like that. It's like our arrival was expected, and now they're inviting us in. We best be ready — someone who knows their witchcraft is waiting inside."

a71e26e2-0a67-4755-9d65-4e6d3cd7dd6b.Text: {n}Marazhai grimaces slightly.{/n} "Whoever is waiting inside, I hope warp sorcery has not sapped them of their ability to feel fear. Or pain."

55e298c5-832f-4a58-b9ba-f2e20990e4c2.Text: "I will not tolerate a psyker on the verge of eruption in my retinue. Neutralise yourself at once or die."

b8bac40c-238c-4b53-8ef1-548a517736db.Text: Convinced Idira that her only salvation was to become one with the voices.

8a689b67-a610-4fcb-b849-bea05a414e24.Text: "I know of another way to help you. One that will spare you from having to fight the voices ever again. Become one with them."

82b73d50-3414-4f86-8a58-06164003f151.Text: "You are two steps away from becoming a portal. It pains me to say this, but the psy-stifler is our only chance of preventing that."

e21c6c46-2f29-42be-ae19-f2bd6e76e69b.Text: "I command you to open the door inside your head!"

1e6241a9-ccf9-45dc-b2d4-fcb91f25f081.Text: [Kill her] "You have left me no choice."

f4f079e7-aef3-4019-a9d4-4f07eaf667bc.Text: [Point at the xenos's body] "He was one of the most powerful psykers of all. Look at what the psy-stifler did to him. Don't do it, Idira."

dfe3979d-69b7-4223-b19b-6ecad2d9a38f.Text: "Are you all right? How are you feeling?"

50f13229-f413-4644-bbdf-0107240fce09.Text: "I am glad that the problem has been solved."

52085eed-d235-4f68-bdcf-7ef208c4c66d.Text: "Mistress Tlass, I demand a status report."

3792d2e2-b93f-4f5b-af43-55ace235d3c0.Text: "Break that abominable device. Robbing yourself of your soul is never the way."

d797711e-013f-4b05-b9d1-aefb00521476.Text: "Put on the implant. Do not waste another moment. You must survive no matter the cost."

538c1916-2aae-416c-8969-1a13902035ad.Text: "If it means betraying yourself and changing the essence of who you are, then what sense is there in living such a life?"

8359980b-2e4b-4afa-94eb-150cf5970478.Text: [Destroy the psy-stifler] "You can thank me later."

08b004fe-2f1d-42af-8e4a-01cf6cc39d35.Text: "You are right. Do as you see fit."

8392bb1b-2895-44f7-a94d-29ee8b3c2546.Text: "Trust me, it will be better this way."

fcce798c-7c46-40c0-8bf6-18a06ee31c71.Text: [Kill her] "You were doomed the moment you were born."

4830af86-c6f0-43f7-868d-6c1d235dde03.Text: "Your life is not the only one at stake here. Sentiment has no place in this discussion — you must put on the psy-stifler."

3d0073cf-9fa5-457f-9983-396b83bfb17b.Text: "You are right. Do as you see fit."

028678e5-9a51-4f8e-9c6d-9150bc0eac15.Text: [Put the psy-stifler on her head by force] "You can thank me later."

cc2f3d18-262b-4241-ae30-ea136b3b83a3.Text: "For the last time. Open. The door."

95447e06-e9b9-437e-949b-d94dfbfcd5b9.Text: [Kill Idira] "A psyker with a xeno-artefact in her head? I don't think so. I will rid myself of this menace."

467364f6-cf1c-49a4-97e5-e91fde20d0ad.Text: "All your life, you have hated the voices, feared them. Don't. After all, they are part of you. Let them in, all of them. Open the door."

a0bb8560-d77f-4638-aad7-c3e978ee4676.Text: "Nothing is more important than the Rogue Trader's safety."

7363bdfe-91ee-4d1e-a0f6-59fefd463f11.Text: "I will put my trust in you. I pray that it is not misplaced."

2a018673-1f0e-47c1-b35e-45b4ea671a83.Text: "Or maybe you will finally become yourself? You won't know until you try."

67030c91-0900-49c0-b259-ec0874400aeb.Text: "I won't let them hurt you. I know how. Put your trust in your Lord Captain."

054add6d-81db-40e8-85ee-8cc003fe7b4d.Text: {n}Idira gives you a confused look.{/n} "Become one? What... do you mean?"

a42c877a-21aa-4f1c-b83d-cb773190d4be.Text: {n}The moment the psy-stifler touches Idira's temples, dozens of wriggling crystal threads shoot out of the device and sink into her skin. She screams in pain, clutching her head as the squirming contacts bore into her flesh. Eventually it passes, and all you can hear is Idira's heavy breathing.{/n}

20007039-6333-4e2b-9654-b2c269973469.Text: "Well... that's it done. It's so quiet. The voices... they're still here, but it's nothing like the clamour I lived in before. They were so loud I couldn't even drown them out with the best obscura. And now I... I can silence them whenever I want."

829de294-5717-41e4-9b08-7e3c0a487f20.Text: "Lord Captain, you can't joke about these things. This device, this psy-stifler, it can help... I think. But if I open the door, if I really let the whispers inside me, then will I... will I just be gone? Or worse?"

a05f2db2-52cb-429f-92c6-b086e8ff70a0.Text: {n}Idira smiles bitterly.{/n} "Yeah. The witch is no longer a threat, life can go on — who cares what she wants? Fine. You've won. I'm just an obedient tool in your hands. When was it ever any other way?"

a64215bf-d724-43b1-ad91-b1e084f3cbc1.Text: "No. I want to tell you not to make the mistake of using this device. Drukhari technology is designed to mutilate and torture — you have witnessed this yourself. Are you sure you are willing to part with your soul, just so you can live without fear of the curse that you and I share?"

9e76ccd1-3f60-41d2-ada4-00d4eab860da.Text: "Our... curse?" {n}Idira falls silent, unsure what to say to that.{/n}

5cd497e6-1398-4095-a9ef-c84924d9b30b.Text: {n}She shrinks. She is torn between her fear of the consequences of your proposed solution and her absolute loyalty to you. But you know that she would never dare to defy you.{/n}

5825771e-3606-43ea-9e1f-25eaacf94e5f.Text: {n}Your insinuating voice has her spellbound. You know that she trusts your honeyed words simply because she wants to trust them. To trust you. After all, the Lord Captain would never let something horrible happen to {mf|his|her} pet witch, would {mf|he|she}?{/n}

40f66c59-28dc-4205-ae52-532f6d59a8c8.Text: {n}It is rather entertaining to observe the battle between hope and doubt play out on her face. But then again, the outcome is already known to you.{/n}

6116395b-a4e5-4553-92d6-a312bef58f8d.Text: {n}Idira drops the psy-stifler on the floor, where it shatters into a million tiny pieces.{/n} "I'll... I'll do it. Lord Captain. I'll let the whispers in. You better step back in case... well, in case you-know-what."

8a801c27-c562-4059-9faf-56b9497bfc47.Text: "I'm perfectly fine. I don't remember the last time I felt so good." {n}Idira looks focused and somewhat puzzled, as if still trying to process what exactly just happened.{/n} "I'm fine, really, except... I feel like something's missing. This thing probably just takes some getting used to.
