My pals behind the door threw a fit when I put it on, they started whispering all kinds of horror stories, as per usual... Well, I just shut them up and closed the door a little. It's the first time in my whole life that I've been able to do that."

dfb6bc81-c493-427f-92d9-76414907c556.Text: "Let's keep going, then, Lord Captain? Not much else to do here. Once we get back to the ship, please let me know when you've got time so we can talk properly."

2ae1a55b-efbc-4176-8b4c-bb2e18f9912d.Text: {n}Idira nods.{/n} "Now I'll be useful and efficient to a fault. I'm no longer a burden. Except I feel like something's missing. This thing probably just takes some getting used to. My pals behind the door threw a fit when I put it on, they started whispering all kinds of horror stories, as per usual... Well, I just shut them up and closed the door a little. It's the first time in my whole life that I've been able to do that."

3b8167eb-d92e-49ec-9ae8-d2f71154ab3b.Text: "We are one. I am inseparable from what is beyond me. I am the door. I am the threshold. I am the key, and the keyhole, and the void in between. Am I their voice? Is the void my voice? Forgive me, it is so difficult, we are confused... But we will learn. I am no longer afraid." {n}Different inflections and undertones weave into the psyker's every phrase, like a thousand voices at once are forcing their way out to have their say.{/n}

a6741f7b-4010-49b7-8c64-cbefa972f6ee.Text: {n}Idira looks at you with unfocused eyes and smiles weakly, as if trying to remember how to use her muscles to form a facial expression.{/n} "We thank... I thank? You, Lord Captain. I... we feel better. But it will take time. Let's leave. Find me on the ship later, I think me and them will be better acquainted by then."

f5bfb2f6-a46a-4959-8280-758098832045.Text: {n}Idira carefully pulls the threads of the psy-stifler out of the Farseer's breathless body. The strange device glimmers ominously in her hands, and it is difficult to tell in the dim light if its threads are moving on their own or if it is because her whole body is trembling.{/n}

9273e119-8c33-40ba-8d13-a2b6f202e5ea.Text: "Lo and behold, there was no cure-all miracle — no secret chemicals of the Inquisition, no {g|Encyclopedia:Archeotech}archeotech{/g}. Just this damn Drukhari gizmo. What did I even expect to find? But, well, a mad dog has to be kept muzzled or else somebody will put it down. And I don't want to be put down. Then again, I don't want to wind up like him either... What do you think, Lord Captain?"

46d4052b-ec93-41da-8eb7-cb0969193d2e.Text: {n}Terrified and confused, Idira looks at the device, then at you, then at the dead Aeldari.{/n} "That xenos... {name}, did you see his eyes right before he attacked us? It was like there was no light left in them. And it's all because of this thing? I don't want to die, but... I don't want to live like that either. If it means I'll stop being myself, then what's the point?"

60645ee2-f714-4a5b-b5ad-05182e828476.Text: {n}Idira spits on the Farseer's corpse.{/n} "Weakling. All you could do was make excuses for yourself, and that's why you're dead. What do I need a soul for if I'm gonna die either with or without one? I'll sell a dozen souls if it means I get to live a minute longer. Don't you agree, Lord Captain? You do want your {d|Encyclopedia:CompIdira_NoTrust}pet psyker{/d} to go on serving you, don't you?"

34aaebe2-e372-4e92-8808-6c678922c61a.Text: "My... decision?" {n}Idira bites her lip and looks down at the xeno-artefact in her hands. Her expression betrays an intense struggle, the burden of a terrible choice. A few moments pass before she raises her head and nods.{/n}

ed44e5fb-b7da-4882-8c49-91177cccb3af.Text: "Yes. Yes, you're right. This crap isn't worth it. Time to accept the inevitable. I can entertain these fantasies of a nice, long life all I like, but... that's all they'll ever be — fantasies. Pretty tales to tell over a glass of amasec to make real life seem less shitty."

4a9b4500-3040-4ffc-ad34-8079503a4250.Text: "And what IS the way, then? You'd rather have me curl up and die? After all we've done? No, {name}. I don't deserve that crap. I want to live. You keep telling me I need to make myself useful, that I'm a burden and a menace. Well, here I am, defusing myself so I can dutifully serve you for years to come! Once you get tired of me, you can push me onto your heir, and I'll follow them around, chewing their ear off, just like Abelard."

c31cb28b-044d-4481-bf54-aeda0387e97f.Text: "Must I? What if I become like him, a soulless puppet that doesn't care about anything or anybody anymore? Lord Captain... I think it's time I accepted it. Nothing can save me, and that's... that's okay. I'm scared, I'm absolutely terrified, but I don't need any whispers to understand that the right thing to do is to break this thing and stop chasing phantoms."

ad14af89-4123-45c2-b1f3-5cea31944a86.Text: "Yes, of course. I don't deserve to die. Why would I doubt myself when the solution to all my problems is right here? We've come such a long way for this... Well, my dear little whisperers, time for you to leave me alone for a while and sit quietly behind your favourite door."

892a0da6-6250-484d-b64c-fbbfffa8994b.Text: {n}Idira's expression shows a desperate internal struggle that lasts a few long moments. Eventually, her eyes clear, and she looks at you in confusion.{/n} "I think I nearly made a terrible mistake..."

1116da8b-41eb-48ac-8b35-0f93a5d88ff5.Text: "How hypocritical. Easy for you to pontificate about the meaning of life when it's not your own. You have no idea what you're trying to consign me to. If you don't want to help me, then I'll help myself."

7d178036-08e7-44dc-991c-78b8c6de4dc0.Text: "What... what have you done? This was my only chance, the only way I could live, and you... you've doomed me." {n}Tears stream down her cheeks, but there is no rage or resentment in her eyes — only detachment from reality.{/n}

77ab1d22-089f-4614-a538-2df991baa78e.Text: {n}The crystal shards of the device form a glinting, jagged line on the cold metal floor between you and Idira, reflecting a thousandfold her expression of overwhelming horror.{/n}

0a17a484-9533-4256-8f0a-b667e47ddd7c.Text: "Better for who? That's right, you're not the one who's in for a horrible death. Never mind the death — the rest of my life will be horrible, every void-damn moment of it. The only thing you care about is getting as much use out of your witchy little puppet before it breaks completely. Am I wrong? Fine. I'll be of use to you. You can use me however you want, I don't even care anymore." {n}Idira glances one last time at the shards of the psy-stifler, angrily wipes her tears with her sleeve, and looks past you.{/n} "Can we go?"

a7f982cc-b932-4ccf-9a94-06d364336573.Text: "No, wait, I don't want to! I don't—"

a29bc9f9-702a-432e-8a14-3642dd0bbb36.Text: "Good point... What if I blow up when I'm right next to you or someone else I care about? I've been so focused on saving my own selfish soul that I completely forgot. You're right. I have to stop being a danger to those around me."

5b5abf63-0973-4019-bb15-e24d48cbce9d.Text: "Lord Captain, I must refuse. I promise, as soon as I realise my time has come, you'll be the first to know. I'll give you enough time to throw me out the airlock or blast a hole in my brain — I won't put up a fight. But I'd rather drop dead here and now than become... like this poor sod."

a8877058-ca76-48d5-936f-41a885300466.Text: {n}Idira's body falls to the floor with a dull thud. The crystal shards of the psy-stifler resemble horrifying needle-sharp teeth, their reflection glinting nauseatingly in the slowly growing pool of blood. It is by your hand that Idira's door has been closed forever.{/n}

b44df510-95fb-4977-a0e1-4e60ea8ba823.Text: "Lord Captain, since you've robbed me of my last hope, you might as well kill me here and now. I can't go on like this. You don't know what it's like to wait day in and day out for your body to burst into pieces only to spawn a horde of daemons. When none of your thoughts are your own, when you can't tell a vision of the future from a normal nightmare. Just... just end it. Please. I'm... tired."

ed04db23-1a78-431b-994e-557d30d0b0ba.Text: "Maybe he was lying through his teeth! Maybe he wasn't a Farseer at all! Besides, who knows what xenos brains are like? Yes, he withered and died, but I'm not weak like him! No, I have to do this. Anything is better than ending up as daemon food..."

dee2fec9-c6ef-4c15-9da8-a6abbe0885d7.Text: {n}Heinrix gazes at the Drukhari device, pressing his lips into a thin line. Then he shifts his gaze to Idira.{/n} "Mistress Tlass..."

91fd9734-68b4-4f42-9a2b-e3b55d52b2bf.Text: "What is it, iceman? Want to hurry me along? Can't wait for the blasted unsanctioned witch to muzzle herself?"

9f7cbec3-b2d4-4295-9c2f-827f3238bd29.Text: {n}She closes her eyes, takes a deep breath, and extends her arm out as if reaching for a handle. In an instant, she begins screaming. One voice, then another, then a dozen more — hundreds of unhallowed voices replace one another in a drawn-out howl. Purple light bursts out of her eyes and mouth.{/n}

1d5287d8-8d5f-42f3-88e6-b44f8003c53a.Text: {n}You invoke the power of your patrons from beyond the veil and whisper the forbidden words — unseen marks that forever bind the psyker's tortured soul to your service. As the final sound escapes your lips, the screams stop. Idira, swaying back and forth, looks up at you.{/n}

fcd48129-ebfa-46fa-a346-4ece6240b1f9.Text: "The reality of the situation is ugly and merciless. I'm a psyker. My abilities are getting more and more out of control by the day. Which means I'll go out like any psyker should — it'll be ugly and merciless. Best I can hope for is that it'll be so fragging awesome and heroic that you'll be telling stories of it to your grandchildren for ages, hah! Thank you for helping me realise this, {name}."

8fb639fd-0d9a-425f-981f-e9e5565e4171.Text: {n}Idira sniffles and casually drops the psy-stifler on the floor, where it shatters into a million tiny pieces.{/n} "I'm pretty sure we're done here. Lord Captain, mind letting me know when you have some time once we're back on the ship? I want to talk to you about plans for the future in private. Can we go now? I've still got a whole life to get on with!"

869d2658-136e-4083-95d4-31154bb0d7ec.Text: "Lord Captain... what have you done? I asked you... I feel strange somehow. I can... make the voices stop. I can hear myself think. And... I can't shake the feeling of some irreplaceable loss. I think I'm still me, but something is missing. Something important."

2f2fc9b9-f350-45ff-a179-336b9b3f860c.Text: {n}Yrliet is warily observing Idira from under her lowered lids.{/n} "You do not have to resort to... a solution like this. There are other ways... My kind have other technology, devices not designed purely to scourge the soul..."

f4d156aa-cc86-4ecf-968e-8225b85b382c.Text: "Oh yeah, Red, I'm sure they do. And as soon as I visit your nearest and dearest, I'm sure they'll welcome me with open arms and spoil me with gifts... Look, Yrliet, if you're not on great terms with them, then what chance does a mon-keigh witch have?"

b1549314-0873-4d1b-9317-534889febbfc.Text: "Command me. It's all the same to me now. I'll go wherever you want."

50744b01-bdaa-4bbc-b774-0a9e9568b490.Text: "Thank you, Lord Captain. I won't let you down. Now, if you'll excuse me..."

f961b13b-b285-4724-949a-252e6be0be62.Text: "Very well. We will go there at once."

87a4f5d3-00df-45d7-b71c-5e3692159cb2.Text: "I will take you there later. I need to assess the situation first."

d6fc88fe-2231-4b74-b67d-1fff6865c6f6.Text: "Your request is denied. I am taking only those I trust with me."

fa137c49-6143-4a70-a892-7e490828b984.Text: "Remind me, what is it you want to find there?"

a251331f-4644-4499-9578-76a47a8f8441.Text: {n}You can hear the anxiety in Idira's voice even over the vox-connection.{/n} "Lord Captain, we've found it! The door is so close I can practically feel its metal handle in my hand."

d35dea81-c0bb-454c-b239-87a5bf88c173.Text: "The voices are whispering over each other in both my ears, I can barely make out what they're saying. Please, take me with you. They keep telling me I won't get another chance, and I believe them. It's now or never."

053ceda1-ae36-4910-b21a-e4e9e6c609bc.Text: {n}The vox goes silent for such a long time that you begin to suspect a malfunction. But then the silence is shattered by Idira's utterly lifeless voice:{/n} "But doesn't that mean... I'm going to die?"

5e284d89-d8cd-4d16-9b03-bdf5be9d630f.Text: "No. No, of course I won't die. I'm stronger than that. Yes... yes, you're probably right, the voices must be leading me into a trap — why would they want to shut themselves out, right? We'll... we'll find another way, won't we, Lord Captain? Of course we will..." {n}Idira's voice wilts with every word she speaks, turning into incoherent mumbling and eventually fading away completely. The connection cuts off.{/n}

9afee4b4-3918-4ee0-a488-3c1ab4a912fd.Text: {n}There is a pause — some kind of internal struggle must be happening within Idira.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain. But please don't forget about it! My fate is on the line here."

7e6f6d41-9f2e-4adf-91dc-ed4b7f135682.Text: "Thank you, thank you, Lord Captain! I'll owe you until the day I die, you can hold me to that! Well, door, I'll see you soon."

4b472391-fb27-4c83-a5d4-1c2d9baf98b3.Text: "The door. From my visions. There's something behind it, something that can help me deal with my powers for good. I can't even find the words to express how important it is to me, and I've got plenty of words in my head right now, believe you me!"

845e8244-e9be-4fe1-ace2-0d47d7c77471.Text: "Do your visions contain any clues on where to start looking?"

21387d8f-4871-4db5-a4a8-1f37971dba96.Text: "Before I make my decision, I have questions to ask you."

6a4418e1-d886-4844-a32d-9d011f712c03.Text: "Is the door you describe similar to the door your whispers come from?"

204089a7-1dfc-43e9-964f-04bcb3ea6726.Text: "I find it difficult to believe that suppressing your abilities is safe."

94c586b9-df2e-40cb-a1e2-898b6bc0e965.Text: "We will find this door. I give you my word."

769a0d0a-5e83-449e-8a8a-55ba987d0fa9.Text: "We have to find that door. You are too unstable."

df5d6741-ff4f-4ae3-92bb-9621a9ef439d.Text: "Out of the question. I will not indulge your sorcerous visions."

21b5537f-bab6-40f2-92da-e8d41bd35292.Text: "What do you think is behind the door?"

bfb9085a-6cb8-420b-9aa3-d6aa8eb6b672.Text: {n}Idira hurriedly enters the study, sniffling and hunching her shoulders. She looks haggard — there are bags under her eyes, her hair is dishevelled, and her hands quiver slightly every few moments. With some effort, she focuses her eyes on you and forces a crooked smile.{/n}

f5db4a27-6a2f-4596-8c18-c6e56c11661a.Text: "Lord Captain, I wanted to thank you for not leaving me with that sick Haemonculus. And I'm sorry if I said a bunch of things I shouldn't have said. I was... pretty out of it. You just don't know what it's like to finally be alone with your own thoughts. It wasn't easy to give that up and believe it was just another trap set by a xenos."

a76cb32b-537b-4518-a8d5-9bdad556fc32.Text: "I actually came to talk about something important. It's about my whispers, in fact." {n}Idira bites her lip and looks at you with hope.{/n} "I've been having some interesting visions... And I feel like how we deal with those visions is going to decide my fate. I know it sounds dramatic, but I'm being dead serious. When you have a moment, call me over on the bridge, all right?"

2cdddf1b-83aa-4286-bf74-bf3f172b8058.Text: "Absolutely, Lord Captain! Ask me anything and I'll try my best to answer!"

9eb839e7-dcdb-4a0a-9e38-eba85cb7a043.Text: "Thank you for agreeing to hear me out, Lord Captain! Here's the deal: after all that happened recently, the voices in my head suddenly flared up and started gabbling worse than before. Don't get the wrong idea, I'm handling them just fine. But I think I know of a way I can get them to settle down a bit."

ec7b827e-b8b6-4759-8bcc-d7752b8068c5.Text: "I keep having the same vision over and over again. I'm walking down a corridor, and there's this door at the end. And I just know that right behind that door is blissful silence — all I've got to do is reach out and open it. So I touch it with my fingers, I can feel the cold, rough metal... and then I suddenly snap out of it and always find myself staring at a wall in some compartment or other. I look behind me, and all the doors on the way are open, but I have no memory of how I got there."

c5335195-b1b1-4fe0-b4d1-d090e2188e40.Text: "Vague ones, as usual. I think I can hear the muffled cries of some weird birds, and my head is sweating like it's somewhere hot. I'm surrounded by rockcrete, your everyday Imperium stuff, except it reeks of burnt flesh, fried cables, and chemicals."

11bee414-0356-4806-8c9d-906e8841a2de.Text: "Lord Captain, I'll cut to the chase: please help me find that door. I'm not joking, this is a matter of life and death. My gut tells me it's my last chance to deal with my powers, and if I don't..." {n}She trails off.{/n}

db439981-f36a-4c74-b5f9-8a9da95e687c.Text: "Besides, you don't need stories to remember what happened to me when Tervantias blocked my powers. Just a bit longer, and my brains would've been mush."

44097c20-b8b0-49ba-ba5b-e1da0b8a98b4.Text: "I've no idea! Maybe it's some incredible implant from the Tech-Priests' secret stores? Or, I don't know, a serum kept in the Inquisition's vault? There's such a thing as {g|Encyclopedia:Archeotech}archeotech{/g}, right? Plenty of it lying around, maybe some of it could help me." {n}Idira is trying to maintain a facade of confidence while simultaneously pulling at a hangnail so hard her finger begins to bleed.{/n}

dcec93a3-9a20-4888-ad50-84b06664be63.Text: "No... Well, I don't know. It feels different. The one from the visions feels very, I don't know, real? I can even touch it. It's definitely not an illusion, it really does exist somewhere. And trust me, neither of us wants to open the other door, the whispering one."

6f535b28-f2a7-441f-91c7-41f90d9f1f86.Text: {n}Idira snorts.{/n} "Oh, it's really, really not! I'm sure you've heard stories about how people tried to lock psykers' abilities away for good, and how those psykers would then eventually go insane and explode into little pieces."

b232fe47-9623-464f-ab4d-ae6c52371bbb.Text: "But if there's a way — no, not to shut my door completely, but to make it so a tiny little crack remains... now that's a different story. I can just feel it: if we find this thing, whatever it is, it'll all be all right!"

f84a0e15-f17f-4c01-b9b7-75f81893ed53.Text: "No way! It can't be! Whatever, I'll go in alone if you like, just please help me get there..."

773e7ff9-7d04-4519-bf33-a7b3fb9b0178.Text: {n}Some of the darkness in Idira's eyes clears, and her smile widens slightly.{/n} "Thank you, Lord Captain! I knew you wouldn't leave me in a bind! As soon as I sense we're close, I'll let you know right away."

632ebbec-5b4c-49f3-8d49-1fef8c4e08da.Text: {n}Idira gives a reserved nod.{/n} "Yes, Lord Captain. I'll prove to you that I deserve a place aboard this ship. As soon as I sense we're close, I'll let you know right away."

e5705d69-36e5-4372-81d7-a1094bffb1e6.Text: {n}Idira hugs herself and looks at you with eyes filled with despair. Silence falls. Then it is shattered by her utterly lifeless voice:{/n} "B-but, Lord Captain... I... Doesn't that mean... I'm going to die?"

15fc9774-da64-42ba-978b-ee1237be3dfa.Text: "Lord Captain, I'm so glad to see you! I nearly lost it when you up and disappeared on me. I was getting by on stimulants and recaf, I barely slept, all so I could keep listening to the whispers for any clue on how to find you. The only other time I felt so powerless was when Lady Theodora..." {n}She stops.{/n} "Pardon me, Lord Captain, I'm talking nonsense."

0d35e0e5-bbd5-476e-a967-297df7f3375c.Text: "Lord Captain, I'm real glad to see you're fine and well! When you disappeared, I thought, that's it, I'd lost you just like I did Lady Theodora. Left without a Lord Captain again. I did everything I could to make myself useful in some small way, I listened to the whispers day and night trying to fish out something, anything about you."

6252856b-c083-4f54-ae25-a3ea7fa7b9c0.Text: "And... it gives off a sense of despair. Suffering, thick like tar, hangs in the air, gets into your nose and throat, makes you sick. I've only been to one other place that felt like that — the Haemonculus's lair." {n}Idira flinches.{/n}

36c12fe2-85cb-41d7-b5de-a70d49b92c4b.Text: "No. No, of course I won't die. I'm stronger than that. Yes... yes, you're probably right, the voices must be leading me into a trap — why would they want to shut themselves out, right? We'll... we'll find another way, won't we, Lord Captain? Of course we will..." {n}Idira's voice wilts with every word she speaks, turning into incoherent mumbling and eventually fading away completely.{/n}

c4b7cf76-9021-4e7a-a283-ee43e20cc729.Text: "Lord Captain, I'm sorry for barging in like this, but I just saw... no, heard! Sensed? Anyway, it's close. My salvation, it's close. It's somewhere in this system. Remember I told you about having new visions? Well, thanks to those visions, I now know of a way I can get them to settle down a bit. Wait, I'm jumping ahead! I'll just start from the beginning."

fce5bfae-15fd-4e17-9184-bd4e825a8e2b.Text: "Well, thanks to you, things are back to the way they've always been — the door's cracked open again, and my dear old whisperers are back to torture me, the rascals." {n}She chuckles bitterly.{/n} "You know, I didn't come here just to get all teary-eyed and grateful on you. It's something important, something about my whispers. See, I've been having some interesting visions... And I feel like how we deal with those visions is going to decide my fate. I know it sounds dramatic, but I'm being dead serious."

266c6331-4654-49bb-92da-0440daaba316.Text: "Sorry, that's about it. Nothing more concrete. But I think, if we get close enough, I'll sense it immediately."

329ef43f-ea9c-412c-b551-cd92c587cb73.Text: {n}Idira nods and looks at you anxiously.{/n}

e01967bd-573d-4c96-9691-f57fad6ddc5d.Text: "Why are you so angry? I solved the problem."

6146bc28-4425-43f3-82b3-9a52e9c85305.Text: "Give me a reason why I should continue listening to your advice and trusting your judgement. Right now I don't see any."

afb6ba90-314b-4962-96ec-0c59896dd361.Text: "Do not speak to your Lord Captain in that tone."

7d3002b9-79c7-4b4b-9a6c-4ee7d4c4a67d.Text: "Let's talk about your role in all this instead. You allowed this revolt to happen, your actions practically guaranteed it would."

2c9f6e57-81ed-4b54-ad7e-3f242f866f0c.Text: "Maybe if Theodora had spent more time on 'trifling' matters, she wouldn't have wound up dead. There is a new Lord Captain aboard this ship now, and I will not repeat her mistake."

4246aa08-7d5c-410c-a628-b954dd795097.Text: "I would be only too willing to trust in my Seneschal and not fill my head with such matters, but the situation had spiralled out of your control, Abelard."

00ba0779-d01a-4b11-a7fb-0fda8a2c0fc3.Text: "I have seen plenty of sentiment and handwringing in recent days, but very little competence. I have no plans to rely on your judgement or your 'tried and tested procedures' in the future."

9340d6b9-6efa-4c08-8b41-c6fa6ae07811.Text: "Theodora trusted in established procedures — and she died. I won't make the same mistake. If you want to keep building the future of the von Valancius protectorate with me — stop living in the past."

295fc80e-3f0e-4dca-b60f-cd16285c756e.Text: "The prosperity of the von Valancius protectorate is just as important to me. You are the only person who has comprehensive knowledge of how things are run on this ship. I think in the future I will follow your recommendations."

66fd7591-38a0-4664-9b73-3db24dd6f150.Text: "I understand, but you need to learn how to respect me as your Lord Captain and Rogue Trader. Accept it and start living in the new world — a world where Theodora is gone and where you and I have new decisions to make."

45707d6b-1f80-447b-8794-47b6402faf1a.Text: "I value what Theodora created and I trust that this situation is an aberration in the ship's otherwise smooth operation. Since the established procedures are working, I see no reason to change them."

045a98a5-54ed-4288-900f-c86746384743.Text: "There is some truth to your criticism."

95db9c81-6059-4e8b-af6a-f919f5fc6166.Text: {n}Stopping unexpectedly, Abelard imperiously dismisses the unit to stand at a distance, and addresses your other companions, saying,{/n} "I have an urgent matter to discuss with the Lord Captain. Please give us a moment."

e71bde0b-c950-482f-8396-61044b36db9a.Text: {n}Abelard looks at you, and his last vestiges of restraint vanish.{/n} "Well, are you pleased with your 'investigation,' Lord Captain?"

6bc65056-9372-4cc8-8718-2148165d58e6.Text: "You kowtowed to the disloyal rabble. You believed their lies and showed them leniency. Next time the ship is attacked by cultists, that rabble will welcome them in with open arms and allow them to wreak whatever havoc they like, because they see you as a weak leader."

68b5f658-e841-4365-9420-910f63233c32.Text: "You kowtowed to the disloyal rabble — worse still, you put weapons into their hands. Now we do not simply have an untrustworthy mob in the hold, we have a mob that is armed. Next time they decide to start an uprising, it will be far bloodier — that is, of course, if they don't accidentally wipe themselves out first."

5f32c025-96d3-4508-917a-0e4af6c2c667.Text: "You made a harsh but necessary decision. But before that, you danced to the tune of a panicking junior officer. You put your life at unnecessary risk in the midst of a potential uprising. And your actions triggered everything that followed. If you hadn't given Lieutenant Vent false hope and then snatched it away again, she wouldn't have snapped! You had no business going anywhere near the lower decks."

7ae26b7a-e999-4c7c-a00d-e8d14697680b.Text: "I would have handled the situation myself had you not decided to intervene," {n}Abelard says irascibly.{/n} "Remember Lord Captain Theodora. Do you think she ever set one slippered foot on the lower decks? No. She did not. Such matters were left to myself and the junior officers while she dedicated herself to her grand designs for the protectorate — as any true strategist and {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} ought."

c67f290a-d4ce-483b-98dd-d625747505d2.Text: {n}Abelard looks at you, stunned, and exhales loudly. Then he nods curtly.{/n} "I... commend your decisiveness, but I am uncomfortable with introducing new protocols in the midst of a crisis."

bf1dfca2-681c-4f02-b218-b309d417a589.Text: {n}Abelard's face relaxes slightly.{/n} "You're... right. At least as concerns junior officers making complaints directly to you."

01fcd5b2-d5fb-4128-8df5-c15f03408d52.Text: {n}The Seneschal's thick brows loom over his darkening eyes like thunder clouds.{/n} "Yes, Lord Captain. You will not hear anything from me apart from reports on my direct duties." {n}Abelard is silent for a few seconds.{/n} "I suppose my presence in your retinue will be extremely short-lived. But for now, let us leave this cesspit."

c567bcdd-77f1-4d31-8f06-76edc9fb6b2f.Text: "And..." {n}Abelard stands straight at attention.{/n} "I lost my temper, Lord Captain. And I believe I ought to explain myself."

96b2d8c8-0dc2-4e8f-a0cb-d70901ee812a.Text:
{n}Abelard solemnly inclines his head.{/n} "Yes, Lord Captain."
{n}After a moment's silence, he adds, looking at you with interest,{/n} "Your resolve is admirable and demonstrates strong leadership. I shall remember this moment, should my old habits ever begin to creep back in."

0b38ca4d-5a6b-425f-9e08-a3725ef8899f.Text: "I should say so!" {n}Abelard heaves a sigh, but he visibly relaxes.{/n} "You simply needed to trust me."

58540a93-ff38-4dfb-b989-03c5db9880ae.Text: "But why did you have to be the one to do it? And did you consider what it might cost you?"

f34b205e-dfb0-420a-b925-182a31730b33.Text: "Is that how you see your future at the helm of the von Valancius protectorate?"

7cef54a6-873e-4193-96eb-b65c9a635ea0.Text: "And now, please, let us leave the lower decks. If the Rogue Trader desires to stretch {mf|his|her} legs, there are far more suitable places."

04659af5-7f37-4422-b4ff-2fd037120b73.Text: {n}Abelard frowns, his affronted dignity clearly at war with his military training, but the latter wins out. He shrugs slightly, juts out his chin, and speaks in a calmer, graver voice,{/n} "I never expected to hear such words after all my years of service. But I suppose I have brought this on myself. Allow me to explain."

e9f19031-e3b3-40f8-8377-82851f565455.Text: {n}Abelard speaks slowly, the words not coming easily to him.{/n} "The prosperity of the von Valancius protectorate is not just an empty phrase to me. I left the Imperial Navy for the chance to see it flourish. It was the most momentous decision of my life. I did it because I saw in Lord Captain Theodora's deeds the sign of true greatness. Rogue Traders do not simply forge new routes and capture worlds — they create order out of anarchy. That creative impulse was entirely lacking during my time in the military."

2ca09339-95d6-4ca5-876e-7da507a25996.Text: "I am obliged to speak thus. Who else can point out your errors and offer you counsel?"

e3e7eaeb-21d6-451b-9a26-8e88af066e42.Text: "So I left behind everything I had known, everything my family had known — I come from a long line of officers — and I embarked upon this incredibly reckless venture. Lord Captain Theodora entrusted me with all the concerns she had no time for. She would go off on her flagship for long periods, to distant frontiers, on scouting voyages, and the advancement of the entire protectorate rested on my shoulders. And then suddenly, everything that had been built over years and years began to quake, rattling like a flimsy hangar on a seismically active world."

7e74c008-ca81-4f1c-9b85-6ebe032e25fb.Text: "One of the senior officers betrayed us all, the Rogue Trader was killed, and who knows what is happening on the planets. I tell you this honestly, without fear of appearing weak. All this has come as a grievous blow to me. I am not panicking or grieving because I cannot allow myself to panic or grieve. I am duty-bound to aid the new Rogue Trader — to aid you — to find your footing as quickly as possible. And to do that, I must insulate you from problems that in the past have been dealt with by tried and tested procedures set out in the ship's regulations. Procedures that were established long ago and have functioned smoothly for decades cannot suddenly be deemed excess to requirements!"

9d1fd039-45bd-4930-9e1b-f7773cf4feed.Text: {n}Abelard dips his head in a sign of assent. The shadow of incredible strain, which evidently had been wearing on him for some time, finally lifts from his face.{/n} "I am glad you see the value in the foundations laid down by your illustrious predecessor. Why fix what isn't broken? As for me, I shall endeavour not to cause you any further consternation, Lord Captain."

f1e0cee0-bb56-4d58-ad5b-7a6a1c548f18.Text: "I appreciate your efforts, but there is no need to 'insulate' me from all problems. This is my ship, and these are my people."

a4d92a73-0588-4a30-be85-f03229761bb5.Text: "Did you hear? They were shouting your name."

f4876687-0325-4721-acee-896856838c32.Text: "The people dared to disrespect a senior officer."

d4ccebc6-bd5d-4510-afd6-cfac33598651.Text: "Let's keep moving. We need to get to the bottom of this."

c51344fa-616b-4218-935d-79523431cbf0.Text: "Making hard choices often means becoming the enemy in the eyes of one's subordinates. I understand."

233058de-a82e-4d19-9f49-3635771ba9e2.Text: "We will discuss your work later. I want to know what is going on with the strikers."

05e907b8-84b3-41bc-ba79-3558eb554282.Text: {n}Abelard reflexively wipes the sweat from his brow in a startlingly human gesture, and a telling one — a rare moment where he allows his age and weariness to show through his armour-like veneer of self-assurance.{/n} "The lower decks are a source of endless problems. Sometimes I dearly regret that we cannot replace all the locals with {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitors{/g}."

4df97e95-3cd1-465e-90da-1024a2110284.Text: {n}Abelard nods with an air of forbearance.{/n} "The zeal of the newly appointed. Many commanders and leaders experience it. Wait another five or ten years and you will see that trying to solve every minor issue yourself is ineffectual."

56296bd7-4d7a-4ef5-8806-08fcc8fdf90c.Text: "Of course they were. The organisation of the daily, routine life of the ship rests upon my shoulders. The mountain of challenges and problems from which I endeavour to insulate you, Lord Captain. The situation on the lower decks has been a cause for concern, and I have intervened personally on more than one occasion. That must be why they remember me. They do not know your face. To them, you are akin to a creature of legend, one who has stood on the steps of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}, no less. Whereas I am the man whose name is attached to every order docking rations or lowering a bay's heating."

a00a2d1e-5044-47dc-9a1a-8fb1a2af2ac3.Text: "They would not have the chance to express such disrespect if we were not here, and if the situation had been dealt with by the relevant officers." {n}Abelard grimaces.{/n} "It is a junior officer's worst failing, to pass problems up the chain of command. I have never been able to abide it. I shall say it again — it was a mistake to come here on Lieutenant Vent's whim, Lord Captain."

d5dd4564-7c19-48fb-a493-17cddeefc108.Text: "I must admit that the lieutenant is by no means the worst material for an officer," {n}Abelard adds peevishly.{/n} "But, in the name of Terra, the girl is the same age as my eldest great-granddaughter! And she has the gall to tell me how to manage the lower decks and hunt down cultists. It will be another twenty years at least before she can be trusted to act without oversight."

fabaf4fc-594c-4e7c-9be6-d98967670411.Text: {n}Abelard looks at you in slight surprise, but says with genuine approval,{/n} "Wise words, Lord Captain. And very true ones."

02bcb38e-f284-4124-aec1-df284db7ea45.Text: "What troubles me is that you are putting your life at risk — no matter how negligible the danger may be. But as you wish."

f54cf039-8bf6-4759-a489-9bad3b2d4145.Text: "Look who it is! This is all his fault! All of it!"

3759a19f-8796-412e-a5bb-15a5cd0660d7.Text: "Get lost, torturer! Take that! That's for Depot 4!"

93421b8d-cc7c-4551-82cf-acce66a047c0.Text: "So what — are we being disbanded? Are we going to be transferred?"

824ae5e0-2a00-492d-bfc4-359907ed61d1.Text: "Turns out upstairs hasn't forgotten us lower-deckers after all..."

8a747513-74c1-4df5-99b9-3c12c0fba014.Text: "This day will be celebrated as a holiday in Depot 4 for years to come!"

38e082c5-f30f-4b06-90cb-fc1fae89836d.Text: "Can it be? Things are really going to change for the better?"

67877257-9b82-4b01-8861-858c97702e9b.Text: "Wow! Nobles from the upper decks, down here to see us!"

86c24f69-968d-4299-bc61-a1cd4c34a502.Text: "They showed mercy on us, I can't believe it."

c1026cb7-a151-4ce8-afb6-f3d41278a298.Text: "It's not clear if anything will change for us. But at least we've been shown mercy..."

318325ff-dacb-41da-9d12-f3fbf1c0a7d4.Text: Something resembling a nest made out of thermal insulation material. This must be where the workers sleep between shifts.

fd7de41c-6c9d-4612-ab57-785f3096a417.Text: Huge pipes — the arteries of the ship — run through many bays, delivering air, water, heat, and the propulsive force of steam.

42fee1d7-0e42-4713-a4bb-49f419c0342c.Text: The carved Aquila on the door has been polished to a shine — either through special cleaning or as a result of frequent rubbing for good luck, as is the practice among common people.

c1953996-86ee-4e52-b696-04246eac4bae.Text: Inside the box, a string of scratched letters runs along the edge — different first names but the same surname. It looks like this box has been passed down in the family from generation to generation.

e83ed4e5-6455-4e84-8b31-085cf168b55e.Text: This page is where the start of each shift is marked. The last mark is missing — the workers went on strike.

adf8e1cf-692e-4df0-922b-da1a0ef7a452.Text: The heat sink warms the air around it to a scorching temperature. This is the warmest part of the bay — the workers have even dragged deck chairs here.

4eb6f69e-d9bb-4d78-a564-7d5d04401673.Text: "Third shift — you're free to go. Fourth shift — get to work."

ed1962bc-f78c-403b-b246-4b6dbfe33816.Text: "The children of the Imperium shall fear unrighteousness and bend the knee before the throne of Terra."

a35300f4-6617-469d-9546-3b646e0c9acb.Text: "Remember: toil is your devotion. Idleness and laxity are transgressions in the eyes of the Emperor."

981d5ef6-081d-4ab1-b3aa-acd61fa61530.Text: "Honour the Lord Captain, for {mf|he|she} is the Emperor's anointed. Honour the officers, for they are the bearers of the Lord Captain's will!"

a4079a1d-f8f8-4f0c-a4fe-969cf28f7325.Text: "Emperor save us and keep us, this is depressing..."

839acabd-5f4d-41d0-9403-277671e92ef9.Text: "I'd love to see how they live on the upper decks, even just once..."

07b06eb2-0c30-4586-b11c-7c18dd987cad.Text: "I was born in this sector, and it looks like I'll die here too."

6384250e-a0c4-40f2-ac19-07ac2b2f5622.Text: "No one spares a thought for us down here... We're just supposed to work and keep our mouths shut..."

fe01f1e9-7679-45be-9fe9-76afdd90d861.Text: "We're innocent, Lord Captain! It's those wretched enforcers... but we're honest people!"

068ee1fc-b29d-4e81-88b3-24cdbc15c40e.Text: "Our children are freezing! We've done nothing wrong, and we're being punished!"

9d68dd1d-9bb6-4077-8074-888118e9b6e9.Text: "This is complete bedlam... Are you satisfied, Lord Captain? Then, may I suggest we leave this circus and discuss everything en route."

3004cb06-f75e-4a20-8f9c-4040c7c236ab.Text: A container can be seen beyond the massive bars. Perhaps examining the pipe will allow you to reach it.

6a6133d9-7105-40fe-9dd3-c9d824c7f7af.Text: The gauge shows that the steam pressure in this pipe is close to the maximum. However, it does not reach the bars at the other end.

a1e1d434-bb20-4542-a291-d336f11c4495.Text: Nothing is happening. Perhaps turning a different valve will work.

528652f2-caf1-451c-a275-d52d32570114.Text: "We encountered some locals on our way here. Their conduct was outrageous — they even tried to throw things at us."

bc3d5482-c3ae-41e7-8a39-a8d1b0500d7c.Text: "We were attacked on the way here. How do you explain that?"

dc141f5d-cd69-42b9-a2ee-f05526164a8d.Text: "I want to speak to the strikers."

53a4fa27-8f59-4f09-bc5b-774607ac1389.Text: "I give the assault unit permission to open fire. We will crush the seeds of insurrection with full force."

4f1846f8-40f3-451a-915f-0159c0c8cb49.Text: "Tell me what is troubling you. Why are you striking?"

ce71f033-6e23-4443-adc2-2d38ebe4b345.Text: "The persecution started apropos of nothing, you say? I was told that one of you was found in possession of a cultist amulet, and that there are heretics hiding here."

3a4e6574-3a03-4ed0-81dd-75b3f794750f.Text: "Abelard, do you have anything to add?"

1f04290e-d56d-422e-bfdd-73579cc588c9.Text: "Spreading anarchy on the ship is the first step toward embracing Chaos. Putting weapons into untrained hands would be even worse. What's more, the enforcers are needed to maintain oversight and order. Withdraw those demands and we will consider the rest."

a95406d0-acd4-4db7-a33e-d1b4a4fcb5c3.Text: "Fine. I'll give the order for the enforcers to be withdrawn from this sector. And you will be given weapons. Let's see how you cope governing yourselves and what difference it makes."

3e0b8bec-583c-4ce4-8d6b-a802f3a77273.Text: "You have failed to convince me of your trustworthiness. This unrest ends now. Everyone who was involved will be eliminated."

76a2a706-f267-4c89-a2f5-cbec81e0f1d3.Text: "Then it's decided. The persecution will stop. And I will expect you to assist in locating any remaining amulets or weapons left by the cultists."

92cc689b-b7d8-48c5-9c97-e95fd302df73.Text: "Then it's decided. The harassment will end. I will expect the clans who have agreed here to assist in locating cultist amulets and weapons. Anyone who refuses will be punished."

1e102aab-30f2-4ab9-aa64-6adc863e23e8.Text: "Is that all you have to say? Are you sure you're worthy of an officer's rank, Lieutenant Vent?"

2a9e1d75-fe25-45d1-a78c-bbf0e2a40345.Text: "Sauerback, was it really necessary to torture these people with cold?"

c39d5d5d-81bf-4ffd-8043-0e85ec6a7d09.Text: {n}The sounds of a heated discussion reverberate through the ship's bays. Lieutenant Avrilla Vent of the ship's enforcers is barring the path of her superior, Master-at-Arms Jocasta Sauerback, who has arrived clad in armour. Judging by their expressions and tone, the standoff has dragged on for some time already and has now reached boiling point.{/n}

ad7df03c-0f46-4d01-a6e3-859eceff2a22.Text: {n}A dozen pairs of eyes stare apprehensively at you. The people before you are typical inhabitants of the lower decks — you take in their simple clothing, crude weapons, and faces that display varying levels of mutation, from the barely discernible, to the strange, to the outright grotesque.{/n}

e9d81b17-d6fd-48c5-8e76-dc2f73345816.Text: "Shut up, Rivet," {n}snaps the old woman, who turns her hostile dark eyes on you.{/n} "Here's the deal, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Your damned enforcers are all over us down here. They say they're looking for 'cultists.' One wrong word and they're reaching for their batons. If they want to punish someone — they turn off the heating to whole bays for a week at a time, so we get sick and freeze! In my clan, two little ones died from inflammation in their lungs, all because of those enforcers." {n}The old woman spits on the floor and rubs at the spittle with the toe of her worn-out shoe.{/n}

82c00efa-8583-4b1a-b672-9ff987972403.Text: {n}Abelard frowns and pitches his voice low so that his words do not reach the other officers:{/n} "And it was worth leaving the bridge for this? You could have issued the order from there..."

e14a408d-4715-4c2f-a191-0e5c401da5eb.Text: "A cultist amulet? What's that? The gewgaw they found on the dead drunkard? If it was something evil or forbidden, we sure didn't know... The enforcers just said they were looking for heretics among us, and anyone obstructing their investigation would be punished. But how could there be heretics here? We know our own people, there have been no new faces around."

73b111e7-7cc2-4fe1-87c0-246fd778151b.Text: "Definitely not! And if there were, we'd be the first to report them!"

d060d2ea-27c8-4389-bc1a-3e6b1614f3f3.Text: {n}Abelard's mouth twists, but he restrains himself and says nothing.{/n}

278649c8-b87a-4bf8-9fc6-13e020652ff0.Text: "Right you are, Lord Captain! Allow me to wish you good luck!" {n}Hope gleams in Lieutenant Vent's eyes.{/n}

47f66c49-b69e-44fc-bbf6-e007ab283a2e.Text: "Sorry. I've let everybody down." {n}It's not clear who her words refer to — Abelard, her comrades, or the striking workers who are now doomed to die. Vent reaches forward and grabs the barrel of the weapon aimed at the crowd.{/n}

09f62c53-6070-4070-92a9-d7a43913138d.Text: {n}A whisper passes through the crowd, and you detect a mixture of fear, astonishment, and joy in their reactions. Finally, three people break away from the crowd — an elderly woman and two men. These must be the leaders. They bow clumsily before you.{/n} "L-Lord Captain! You have come down to us!"

a8c33fc9-3f05-4bc7-bfc2-d6292b2ac3b6.Text: "Our clans are all inside the bay that's been sealed off. But the lower decks are big — I'm sure there are some people who've had just about enough. We're getting it from all sides, the soldiers have encircled the ones who've risen up, a death squad has just arrived... it's no wonder folks are lashing out."

c334094d-8bef-458d-a7b2-2908cda9c2e8.Text: "Would you look at this, the exalted Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} is asking us bilge rats what we want. Well, here's what — we want you to rein in your damned enforcers, to quit turning off the heat, and to stop battering everything that moves. No, that's not it. We want the enforcers gone from here, and we want to be armed! Give us arms, and we'll govern ourselves, we'll defend ourselves if these cultists do show their faces. I've been leader of my clan for twenty years now, getting rid of these club-wielding thugs can only improve things around here."

2deb8044-5e64-4174-ab4d-fef8de8c2c3a.Text: "You've gone too far, Old Nan. They'll never let the maggots on the lower decks live without the enforcers breathing down their necks. They probably even insist on enforcers on the upper decks too. As for weapons — what do we need them for? Before the first day's out, we'll have someone shooting their neighbour out of stupidity or drunkenness. We don't need that — if the enforcers stop hassling us, that'll be enough. In return, we'll find the scavengers who robbed the cultists' bodies, and we'll talk to them, one lower-decker to another. If there are any more of those damned amulets about, we'll hand them over to the enforcers ourselves."

71146fb5-0698-48fb-b776-764cf7f9cd32.Text: "You speak for yourself and your clan, and I'll speak for me and mine. I don't want empty gestures — I want real change. They'll promise us the world now, but as soon as the anointed one turns {mf|his|her} back, these brutes will be on us even harder than before. All because we dared to speak out!"

2eafc276-cd6e-4470-84a0-307e4ba1e6a9.Text: {n}The tall worker's eyes dart between the two arguing leaders. Every few seconds, he opens his mouth as if planning to agree, but each time he falls silent, simply making a few vague noises of approval.{/n}

6919f2c9-2b54-4138-a35d-260bf8394e27.Text: {n}The tall worker they call Rivet shrugs and casts a sidelong look at the old woman.{/n} "Old Nan, listen! Listen! The Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} has come down to us and is offering concessions! And I don't know a single person in the whole of Depot 4 who's ever stood next to the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, let alone talked to them! Back down — now's no time for you to be a stubborn old crone!"

1740999b-5e78-4714-a9df-f08f082be047.Text: {n}The tall worker they call Rivet flinches nervously under your gaze, but he casts a glance at the old woman and says nothing.{/n}

2ad30a22-5b43-4f88-ad24-a233a05b35a0.Text: "The story about going scavenging for boots and 'accidentally picking up a heretical amulet' doesn't convince me. These people were moments away from rebelling and, possibly, becoming minions of the Archenemy. We must not give them what they want. Even if they did acquire something innocently, purely out of their own stupidity, that does not mean they are not tainted with corruption."

64aec65b-5823-4fc1-9c63-f3fa63bfdfb5.Text: {n}The old woman's hand cuts through the air.{/n} "I'd rather be gunned down by the enforcers than back down now! They'll have us all killed anyway, sooner or later."

7fa61628-dbcd-45f0-92c1-3eb372cf377d.Text: "I don't like seeing the clans of Depot 4 at odds with each other. But I agree with the Lord Captain — I won't demand the disbanding of the enforcers."

f33f2e87-d212-4ce0-b6dd-fb8249c17906.Text: "Listen to us, Old Nan. The three clans of Depot 4 ought to act as one. We've made our minds up, it's your turn to decide. Don't ask them to disband the enforcers or give us weapons — we don't need any of that."

d82b6b1e-6548-46d5-b64d-6cb2f3e21c6a.Text: {n}The old woman hisses in dissatisfaction.{/n} "You two are ganging up on me, is that it? So brave you are against an old woman! But I'll shut up. I will, indeed. I won't go against two clan leaders on my own. If you want to make peace with the enforcers — make your peace."

6fa1aa01-7fb0-45db-9fa7-814f028c7453.Text: "That's great, just fantastic! Lord Captain, we're all agreed!"

92a53598-9e45-411f-bb43-45dd459085c6.Text: "I authorised the use of all necessary measures to locate Chaos worshippers hiding in this sector. The specific steps taken by the officers were not reported to me." {n}Abelard frowns, clearly disgruntled at having to explain himself in the workers' presence.{/n} "Nevertheless, I am certain that their actions were justified. Cultists are no drunken stevedores — they are the enemy and a threat to the ship. Neutralising them demands decisive action."

46c08c25-2861-431d-8831-7a690cb508b1.Text: "Here's an explanation for you — the people have been pushed to their limit, and now they're lashing out. As if we don't know why these top deck units are being sent down here, like that one there that the lieutenant won't let past."

2bfe119d-cfd2-4864-92b4-7c99668c7f5e.Text: "We are most, most eager to assist! We'll get right to it, Lord Captain!"

f3459188-6a15-4a2f-bcd1-be63e03b8142.Text: "Of course, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We'll root out any nasty business faster than the enforcers, and we'll leave no stone unturned."

dff923fb-bec4-4b48-b396-5f22fb23efe5.Text: {n}Abelard's face turns stony and he clenches his jaw. He looks at you, his narrowed eyes glittering with anger.{/n}

c4c6273a-77bf-4c75-8597-528eaaec4c2b.Text: {n}The old woman raises her arms triumphantly.{/n} "Good riddance to the executioners! Freedom for Depot 4!"

39fbe467-554f-49ef-8f01-9ae2c9e1cd9d.Text: "You can count on us, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We'll find the cultist foulness, if any of our people have taken possession of it."

3e27c7b1-b19c-42cc-8d90-e62f1b39590f.Text: "No! Lord Captain! I swear my loyalty to you! I beg you! Have mercy!"

6d62f493-66b6-49a0-82ca-944d3f7b711a.Text: {n}The old woman spits in your face.{/n} "Curse you!"

5324956a-93bb-4c48-a42b-cfab7a8962a8.Text: {n}Vent's gaze is full of worry — and regret.{/n} "The people are getting desperate, clearly... They saw the assault unit and they decided they had nothing left to lose. I mean, I apologise, Lord Captain. It is outrageous. I'm sure the people simply didn't recognise you — it wouldn't have occurred otherwise. We will deal with them — once the current situation is resolved..."

10acaf22-b064-4ea1-a7d6-1fb2071fbbf8.Text: {n}Their words seem sincere to you. Their body language and the glances traded between them reveal that the news of the attack has shocked them.{/n}

45caf3e9-baaf-4c37-b546-33b5886fe071.Text: {n}They are too tense and frightened for you to easily read their intentions. They could be telling the truth, but they could also be lying to protect themselves.{/n}

fbfe0731-4f3c-47e3-abe1-519af715d222.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, thank you! You have not abandoned us lower-deckers! You came yourself and settled everything! I'll tell my grandchildren about this!"

af095442-9838-43c1-be11-4d60ea128ca7.Text: "All hail the Lord Captain! All hail!"

e0cc51b8-1642-44a1-8792-08206006d645.Text: "Lieutenant Vent, my patience is wearing thin. I have given you an order. Now get out of my way."

0ccfa842-7a44-4776-b23a-eae3805784fe.Text: "I cannot comply with that order, ma'am!" {n}Vent looks shaken, but there is fire in her eyes.{/n} "This is my deck and my sector. So long as this area remains under the Lord Captain's special oversight, no action can be taken without my express permission. There are only three people who are authorised to make me stand down — the first officer, the Rogue Trader, and the Emperor Himself!"

4fb0b0da-523a-4dc4-a22e-5c0800cab79d.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, my people have locked down the bay where the strikers are, including their leaders. We have the situation under control as far as resources allow."

47989d6a-6c3b-4cff-bec3-0adee0533148.Text: {n}Sauerback gives the signal and is the first to raise her weapon.{/n} "Yes, Lord Captain!"

f91ef55e-f4c3-4544-896e-af208454ac99.Text: "I confirm the information regarding the proper tending of the machine spirits in this sector. {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}Servitors{/g} indicate that these commoners are performing the sacraments they are permitted to know."

88eff5b9-7094-4c09-9ded-66707cd2d697.Text: {n}Suddenly, Lieutenant Vent stands in the executioners' path once again. Her face resembles a wax mask and her eyes are wide with fear, but her lips are clamped into a firm line.{/n} "If you want to mow down everyone in Depot 4, you can start with me!"

46acbee6-c27f-4456-aa5e-b9afdcfb24ce.Text: "S-striking? That's news to us, Y-Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}," {n}says a tall, thin man in worker's garb.{/n} "All we're doing is... asking questions... saying what we think..."

6f81e563-1c61-4762-8188-28ac2bc88d01.Text: "What begins as petty thievery can turn into a far graver problem. I have seen it before." {n}Abelard's face darkens momentarily.{/n} "In my second war, there was a sergeant in the {g|Encyclopedia:AstraMilitarum}Imperial Guard{/g} regiment that was stationed nearby. The sergeant took an ordinary pocket knife from the body of a heretic, and his whole unit lost their lives for it. When they finally managed to break into the barracks, they found not a single survivor — only the pocket knife, which had grown through all the rows of beds like a metal choking vine. So, when it comes to scavengers, malcontents, strikers, or whatever they'll turn into next, my verdict is simple — give them no quarter."

f13d8f37-2ef0-485e-a5ce-5a78cce51472.Text: {n}For a split second, Vent freezes in fear, but she pulls herself together, straightens, and clips out,{/n} "Forgive me, Lord Captain. I will take steps to ensure such a thing does not happen again."

df68546e-7ccb-47b9-a114-4e1fdfc7de40.Text: "Naive children! Weren't you taught from an early age about the dangers of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}'s creations? Weren't you warned that any unfamiliar object could be one of them?"

734cc22f-027a-4e3c-aed6-220c8cb46ca4.Text: "We were told, holy sister. But it was long ago. The last time we saw a confessor in our sector, it was just after I'd had my third little one."

b7adff8c-e232-4cb8-aabe-6494c710801b.Text: "That is regrettable. But you cannot lay the burden of leading a righteous life on the shoulders of the holy fathers. Who will you blame when beasts crawl out of those amulets you stole from the heretics? The holy father who was not there, or the scavenger who brought evil down on himself and his neighbours?"

3fea1e09-817f-4f07-bd2b-926fca9c459d.Text: {n}Argenta does not interrupt the workers, but you see the sadness well in her eyes when the children's deaths are mentioned. She quietly whispers a requiem prayer and makes a sign over herself.{/n}

ab71a75f-db29-4db8-ad3b-7819464fb280.Text: {n}Lieutenant Vent turns deathly pale. Her eyes are wide with fear, but her lips are clamped into a firm line.{/n} "If you want to mow down everyone in Depot 4, you'll have to start with me!"

67dee46d-8cf4-4a9b-a994-04cd141320a7.Text: "Under control, Lieutenant? I came here to lead an investigative unit, and what do I see? The rabble is on the verge of mutiny! There is nothing to investigate — this simply calls for immediate repressions and firing squads! And you, Vent, are a step away from facing charges yourself!"

8eea84ea-03db-47f5-b684-88802ec2a7a9.Text: "Give the rabble a grox, and they will take an agri-world, Lord Captain. They only understand brute force and will interpret any concession as a sign of weakness. Giving them weapons and recalling the enforcers would be folly. It would only be a matter of time before we had a full-scale mutiny on our hands!"

5ef72ef0-1993-4da4-bee2-879f5b52ae66.Text: "So not all my lessons fall on deaf ears..." {n}Abelard mutters in crabby approval. He does not clarify whether he means Vent, Sauerback looming over her, or both.{/n}

8bfe2101-d1bc-4a62-a97c-8cf9c80dd390.Text: "The rabble understands only one language, Lord Captain: that of violence. As per regulations, should the labourers persist in their unwillingness to cooperate, the next step is limiting air supply and cutting off water, which is almost certain to restore order. The peasants can grumble all they want, but in the end, they are the source of their own misery — all they have to do is bow their heads and fall in line, and the need for punitive measures will disappear."

dba7cb48-737a-45ca-a5b2-dbf873247cd1.Text: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}Noticing you, the two officers snap to attention and salute, their subordinates following suit a moment later.{/n}

626d5dce-990f-4a08-b184-fb5566c0e3e1.Text: "It's all true. Vent is the only enforcer officer who's stood up for us. It's clear as day who had a mother from the lower decks, and who grew up amidships and has no fellow feeling toward us!" {n}The grim man with a scarred face throws up his arms.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, we're no villains here, we're honest workers, your servants. We've plotted no disorder, we went on strike openly, and now we've got guns pointed at us. All we're doing is asking to be allowed to work in peace, without being harassed."

b3cc66b3-b6a7-46ce-b2da-826c71ab1a8a.Text: {n}The old woman's face pales, but she merely grits her teeth and spits on the floor again.{/n}

7bed0467-85c8-4036-b298-957925f8764b.Text: "Sorry, Old Nan. I'm not putting my life and my whole clan's lives on the line because of your stubbornness."

8a730b2e-b802-4b49-a879-24ee28b94268.Text: "And as for this amulet, or whatever it is — they took it off a dead body. There are no cultists still breathing in our sector, that's for sure. But when that fight broke out, some enterprising folks looted the bodies. The boots they came back with — nobody's ever tread these decks in boots so fine, I can tell you that. Seems to me these cultists have better commanders than us."

eacc740d-20ac-464f-8755-ad082aa8727c.Text: "Oh, yeah! Those boots really were fine! And there was no harm in taking them, right? As for the amulet... it must have been pocketed by someone who didn't know any better. We don't need any amulets around here. We all worship the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}, and when we're working we bow down before the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} of the Large and Small Transformers and the Servo-Motor — the same way my grandfather was taught a hundred years ago by a Tech-Priest who came calling! Believe us, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} — we are people of faith."

a7c08fa0-69df-424f-80ec-57a00f0dc9fc.Text: "Where does Seneschal Werserian come into all this?"

6154301d-47b0-433e-a94f-cc3f2b168b3b.Text: "I will listen to what you have to say. Speak, Lieutenant."

fca750cc-330b-4580-8d02-3d4a1425a763.Text: "You may speak, but I want to hear a report, not a shouting match. Having two officers bickering in full view of the bridge is unacceptable."

c615e363-e542-445a-858e-2ea398f60550.Text: "I will not tolerate this kind of conduct on my ship. Abelard, assign the lieutenant an appropriate punishment. Lieutenant, you have one minute to state your business!"

3c9b217b-d08f-4492-b98f-0efca43d3258.Text: "It appears I have unearthed an old squabble. I would prefer to be left out of it."

aad177b3-69a2-42e7-9707-3b227a29c21e.Text: "Lieutenant Vent, would you say the Seneschal has singled you out from your peers in any way?"

6c3897fb-36cf-43bd-bc35-edec883168d2.Text: "There's an insurrection in the making aboard my ship, and no one has informed me?"

ba86bdc6-6f36-48d5-b57f-1a94d10b89a8.Text: "I've heard enough. I will go down to the lower decks and deal with the problem personally."

d6a30288-19d8-4e72-89e6-0dd2423e7c36.Text: "This matter is not worth the Rogue Trader's time. Abelard, you have acted with staggering incompetence. From now on, you will sort out your own problems. Get out, and take that upstart with you."

09875d02-292d-46e6-8e8f-5f302434f390.Text: "I am certain the Seneschal was acting within his authority, but I will verify the soundness of his decisions for myself."

42a171fb-170b-4cc7-a0c0-c7314622aee0.Text: "Master-at-Arms, the ship's enforcers report to you, and yet, you seem hesitant to provide your own perspective."

69d6ef4f-f0c6-4678-b9de-684086456576.Text: "Abelard, what do you have to say to all this?"

61896cf5-2945-438a-8731-5d2056e6db8e.Text: {n}The everyday sounds of the bridge are disrupted by voices raised in anger, Abelard's voice the loudest of all:{/n} "This is not the conduct of an officer! These are the antics of a highborn brat out on a lark! Explain yourself, Lieutenant!"

deba900d-f644-4b7f-a061-7fc0dba12fe7.Text: {n}The young woman standing before Abelard strives with all her might not to quail under the onslaught of her superior's anger. She falters but then manages to look him in the eye and say,{/n} "I... I apologise, sir. But I must speak to the Lord Captain."

5811c25a-2645-40f8-af79-6c7ba71e659e.Text: "Very well, Lieutenant. You may address the Lord Captain, not least because I see you have already seen fit to disturb {mf|him|her}. Your unauthorised appearance on the bridge and display of belligerence toward a higher-ranking officer will be logged on your personal file without delay."

f4a62053-5def-4ce8-90d2-7f2783f0e155.Text: "Lord Captain! Lieutenant Avrilla Vent, requesting permission to speak." {n}Vent falls silent, and then adds rashly,{/n} "On a matter of extreme importance and urgency!"

e48e4399-2aaf-4257-9a39-51659fa8a744.Text: "The situation could boil over at any minute, so I'll give you the condensed version... It all began when the enforcers found a cultist amulet on the body of someone who'd been killed in a drunken brawl. We reported it up the chain immediately, arranged for a cleansing rite to be performed, and opened an investigation. No heretics have been found alive. But the search has brought tensions between enforcers and workers to a head."

ea5a11b1-b0ab-4859-a0b5-173a5a1e2442.Text: "Mistress Sauerback, can you recall an occasion where I would encourage an officer to disobey their superior? Or one where I would overrule their order? Or show favouritism to those who merited none?"

fc6b2a90-b143-439e-b092-9efe7389aa00.Text: "But on this ship, the word of the Lord Captain carries more weight than a salvo from a hundred bolters. I'm sure that if the Rogue Trader addresses the malcontents directly, {mf|he|she} will quell the unrest."

7dcb919f-7ce8-47ab-8f43-baf93d93b65c.Text: "Depot 4 is poor and troubled. But at worst that means drunken fights and illegal rotgut brewing. We have handled the workers of Depot 4 in the past. We would have done so again, if the crackdown on Depot 4 hadn't been so harsh. And another important point to bear in mind: the problem is not limited to this sector. It is located on one of the most populated lower decks, and everything that happens there has a knock-on effect on all the neighbouring sectors."

51f0a607-1b55-47ce-8a3c-c9000cec075e.Text: "I am sorry, Lord Captain. I... I thought that drastic times called for drastic measures!" {n}Vent exclaims hotly.{/n}

4725640f-62eb-4250-86e2-6e1b5339c69c.Text: {n}Flushed with anger and embarrassment, the Seneschal bellows,{/n} "Enough! Lieutenant, you know where the exit is. You and I will discuss the brewing rebellion, as well as your egregious breach of protocol here today."

9a9aa383-16d0-42df-a9d9-f07497dbd871.Text: "This matter cannot wait. Any minute now, an assault unit will be dispatched to the lower decks on orders to crush the workers' strike by any means necessary. But I am convinced that this step is unwarranted, and that the crisis itself was provoked... by the actions of one of the senior officers." {n}Vent is almost trembling with tension as she delivers her speech, her face extremely pale.{/n}

3102bec2-8af0-4384-8d44-9cb7fec455ab.Text: {n}Abelard, in no hurry to intervene, lets out a sceptical huff. He glances at Sauerback, who is standing not far from him, but she maintains a stony expression.{/n}

5b601456-656f-4946-aed3-b78dd68d875a.Text: "Lord Captain! I urge you to investigate the actions of Seneschal Werserian. And to intervene in what's happening on the lower decks, because very soon we will have a mutiny or a massacre on our hands." {n}Vent reels off the last words as though she knows them by heart — she has clearly been preparing to say them for some time. When she is finished, she casts an anxious glance at Abelard, then at you.{/n}

e6c33ee8-0d12-4c4d-b931-2ab286848c9f.Text: "I would not deem it a problem worthy of the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}'s attention. The lower decks, as it so happens, are in revolt. Thirty-some years ago, we even had a revolutionary leader rise up who dared to establish workers' rule across the entire ship. It took a month to restore order, but even eight years later, we were still battling rumours that the 'hero' had survived his execution and was on the verge of gathering people to fight against tyranny once more." {n}Abelard scoffs.{/n} "Needless to say, the rumours were baseless. As for the current situation, we have sufficient enforcers to deal with it."

4d673ff9-71f3-45c9-86b6-0eacd21802bd.Text: {n}Abelard grits his teeth slightly.{/n} "An enterprise bordering on the sophomoric, but please yourself, Lord Captain. However, I categorically insist that I escort you."

7583b292-6634-43c1-8e7f-0235224a4c76.Text: "I dread to think what problem you will disturb the Rogue Trader with next. Perhaps you will ask the Lord Captain to break up brawls in the messroom? I have already given you the means to resolve this problem — you simply need to use them."

1f4c1adc-707a-4e3c-b10e-450f0aa48f3b.Text: "Throne preserve you, Lord Captain! I thank you for your support!"

8793a8d4-2aef-4567-ad77-0da5ad1911c9.Text: "I will not hurry — since my competence is under scrutiny, I shall speak for as long as I see fit. There is an established order to the way things are done on this ship, and one of the pillars of that system is that the Rogue Trader's attention is not distracted by trivial matters. It is the Seneschal's role to ensure that. I have always handled internal problems myself, so, of course, when I received information about cultists hiding on the lower decks, I took the matter in hand. So long as I live, not one of the vermin who murdered Theodora von Valancius will find refuge on her ship."

c118124d-f416-4c84-9215-9842ee9bb193.Text: "The ship's regulations state that the Master-at-Arms is responsible for resolving all matters related to the ship's enforcers. And yet it is no secret that the Seneschal has a tendency to... show partiality. Those enforcers and officers whom he has deemed particularly promising are at times given permission to approach him for tutelage."

51b052ad-486a-4fd9-b7bd-312a74b10369.Text: "Lord Captain, I regret that the enforcers were unable to handle the situation, which then led to your and the Seneschal's involvement. I consider it my duty to go to Depot 4 myself and see to the expedient resolution of this incident."

cd8dd691-e34e-4ca3-ad6e-47e3f5e8377f.Text: "Lord Captain, unlike Lieutenant Vent, I respect the chain of command and realise that it is not within my right to challenge my superiors." {n}Sauerback bows her head in Abelard's direction. However, a moment later, a serpentine smile appears on her lips.{/n} "That being said, while I entirely share Master Werserian's opinion on what fate Depot 4 deserves, I must note that this insubordination is a direct consequence of practices that he himself has introduced."

9d4dfc8c-4600-447b-91a2-722fed09b655.Text: "Mistress Sauerback, I see you have decided to follow the lieutenant's example after all. Such behaviour does you no credit."

7de26770-b8c2-4c2a-a0d4-fe7087424251.Text: "I cannot deny Master Werserian's experience and insight — the Seneschal has a record of fostering students who have indeed achieved much and demonstrated impeccable performance. However, extending such patronage over the head of their immediate superior encourages disregard for hierarchy among Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s servants. Today, an enforcer goes to the Seneschal to report an order from the Master-at-Arms that they happen to disagree with. Tomorrow, they will go to the Lord Captain to object to the Seneschal's order. I notice a pattern in these actions."

e075c339-b43c-43c5-9ed3-36f6a9727840.Text: "None, Seneschal, for there have been no such cases in the entire time I have served aboard this ship. If anyone were to claim otherwise, I would have them pay for insulting your honour with blood. Your conduct in this regard have always been spotless. Nevertheless, given your eminent position, a simple show of attention on your part is enough to erode the propriety of junior officers, inflate their sense of self-importance, and undermine discipline."

50f17599-356e-4dfb-a570-c5098a65371c.Text: "I dare not waste your time with such trivial matters, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

fcecdb69-5351-41b3-8c18-2c3ebfa7d97c.Text: "Evidently, my officers are anything but a shining example of unity and adherence today. I have only myself to blame, I suppose."

91c1088f-f285-46d3-a4f2-8e5cb3c9774b.Text: "Lord Captain, I swear that Seneschal Werserian has never granted me any privileges, never once advocated for me, nor facilitated my promotions. Although... He is the man who convinced me to become an officer in the first place. He has offered me extensive guidance in my service, for which I am grateful to him. And while not all my fellows receive such attention, I know of at least a dozen fine officers whom the Seneschal keeps in his sights to ensure that they continue to strive."

7dfa05c0-fc42-4439-9e83-ae9f1f11f594.Text: "That you distinguish some of them and know them by name is tantamount to walking around the officers' deck handing out gifts to officers who have caught your eye. It fills those you set apart with ambition and audacity, makes them stand out among the rest. Enforcers are meant to be faceless servants, fighters ready to die, their fate entrusted to their commander and no one else. That is the sole foundation of order."

26e86d85-0e0e-41b1-bba8-71841f5d7e74.Text: "To prepare new generations of the dynasty's servants, to instruct them, and to separate those with potential from those who have exhausted it — that is my duty as Seneschal. This ship has bays worth of pilots, enforcers, officers, technicians, and stewards whom I have raised personally. By the Throne, every third person standing on this bridge right now was my student at one point."

b0544137-96dc-4b25-9418-0da2293688d3.Text: "You were far too heavy-handed, Seneschal Werserian! Arrests, interrogations, mass punishments for entire sectors... It has driven the people to the brink!" {n}Vent says bitterly.{/n} "Now there is a strike on the lower decks — in Depot 4, to be precise. Three worker clans are involved, but many more are passively supporting them. The situation could degenerate into an all-out insurrection. But when I reported my concerns, the only response I received was an order to dispatch an assault unit and crush the strike with maximum force."

fa1eae3e-c39c-4dfd-ab35-617f65baf5e3.Text: "If I may, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, sending a hit squad to crush the rebellion is a means of ignoring the problem, not solving it."

5163db6f-55e4-479d-b7d9-cdd3cf449bce.Text: "Depot 4 is one of the poorest sectors on the lower decks. It is home to clans of general labourers. They are not as valuable to the ship as the families who have served its specialised systems for generations. They are an easily replaceable resource — and one which is now, more besides, giving succour to cultists and minions of the Archenemy."

eda5b9da-33d0-4ff7-833f-8cc910352057.Text: "I beg you to hurry. Time is running out..."

3e1f3d11-a7e5-4de1-bef6-0703a2fbac2a.Text: "Praise the Emperor!" {n}Vent cannot contain her relief.{/n} "Thank you, Lord Captain!"

82828249-5527-485e-91b2-8fbb91e9291c.Text: "Yes, Lord Captain! Listen to my report and punish me as you wish, but all that matters is that you hear me out!" {n}says Vent, a pleading note entering her voice.{/n}

a91a6cc8-100a-445b-809b-af0157635a6a.Text: "I see no need to add anything. I acted within the remit of my authority, guided exclusively by the best interests of your protectorate and your personal safety. If you wish to confirm the rectitude of my actions for yourself, I have no objections."

397b9048-cd7f-449a-ade7-a9609cbb4c74.Text: "For my part, I urge the Lord Captain to go down to the lower decks, stop the assault unit, and speak directly to the people. You will see that they are not lying, or harbouring heretics! That way, you will stop the uprising before it begins."

b282b0a1-41a4-40f8-a2a8-de60a88b965d.Text: "What are the charges against House Werserian?"

12251af8-e771-41c2-8c1b-cd2fd45c5e72.Text: "Why are there dead bodies at the entrance to my palace?"

f563bc8a-3a0c-4956-ac5e-c8fadbc3504f.Text: "Clementia, I wish to hear your account."

890b8a07-3c5f-4eab-82d7-f03e67cf5440.Text: "Your words alone are not enough to make me doubt the loyalty of House Werserian. As the Rogue Trader, I order you to release them from custody at once."

eb6f445f-518f-4d07-87fa-e4e17ebe1229.Text: "Drivestem, you aren't accusing one of Dargonus's leading noble houses of treason without airtight evidence, are you?"

83ff69a5-ad28-4ccd-b462-970c4c605136.Text: [Speak to the heads of houses present] "Do you support the governor's accusations?"

594fcbc2-fa1d-4f27-bdce-3c9e2a7947dd.Text: "What happened on Dargonus in my absence?"

52ab0dac-ad95-4def-b6c7-d64d7bdf043e.Text: "Sabotaging logistics, riots, conspiracy... The case appears to be flimsy. I wish to learn more before I make my final decision."

51c391c6-4adc-46fa-a792-3f1f36a7719f.Text: "I do not have time to deal with this. Drivestem, I accept the findings of your investigation and find the Werserians guilty."

e633fdd1-c13c-4d91-bdd8-b16e59d7b108.Text: {n}Clementia tries to take a step toward you, but the warden nearby stops her. Her face is veiled with fear and weariness.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! You are here. Please, you must hear us out."

e5124387-a883-4c13-8888-1915c5318045.Text: "Under different circumstances, I would not have dared disobey your word, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but I am afraid that this situation demands that the guilty receive their due punishment. This sabotage of logistical chains perpetrated on the capital world of your dynasty has naturally had an effect on tithe collection. The Marshal himself is certain to arrive here sooner or later to investigate the matter. Alas, his attention puts both you personally and the entire protectorate at risk. However, we still have a chance to alleviate his displeasure by resolving this incident ourselves and punishing the culprits."

b504a801-c1fc-4fd2-8075-3557c57e07cc.Text: "We have known each other for many decades now and we have had our fair share of disagreements, but... do you really think my flesh and blood would trample upon the very definition of honour and loyalty?" {n}Abelard's voice is quivering with rage.{/n}

503feed8-e03b-460a-af6e-9d446dee22bf.Text: {n}The governor sweeps his gaze over Abelard, then replies, a faint shadow of a doubt in his voice:{/n} "We have evidence implicating them, Abelard... I am sure that {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} will arrive at a fair ruling."

85318d61-fd06-4558-866b-587babdf97c2.Text: "So this is how it is." {n}Abelard stares at you for a few moments, then turns away and looks at Clementia's pale, exhausted face. The Seneschal tries to say something but only manages to cough out:{/n} "Pray, Clementia. Do not let them see you demeaned."

d4a8f927-0a37-48db-82df-eb5964f1c635.Text: {n}Clementia opens her mouth as if trying to speak up in defence of her family but failing to find the right words. The young Astartia next to her visibly swoons, seemingly about to faint, but manages to steady herself.{/n}

3eb518d6-2239-4809-883d-09f7ed8f47c5.Text: "Thank you for your trust, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The governor bows low to you.{/n} "The Werserian family is guilty of rebellion against {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} the Rogue Trader and is hereby sentenced to death. Immediately!"

701b6598-f237-4b7a-8540-006949727965.Text: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}..." {n}The governor inclines his head in a stiff bow.{/n} "Speak to me when you are ready to announce your verdict."

b96376b4-a5f2-41b4-a7c4-56f9bf3c4ead.Text: "Thank you for your willingness to help, Lord Captain. I am certain that all the charges are false and I would be grateful for your help in exposing them as such. I think you should speak to everyone present... the noble lords and ladies."

5fc42e77-fb05-4271-adbc-aa0c0203cf97.Text: "When we caught wind of the rumours of your disappearance, we patiently awaited news of your return, but then Dargonus was struck by a series of terrible events. The first was the sabotage of logistics that hampered shipments. Then mass unrest spread across the entire planet, and the minor noble houses began squabbling among themselves, trying to pin the blame on their rivals... We took great pains to calm them down and managed to quash the revolt, though not without some outside help, unfortunately."

1ee6fabc-f2d4-4377-8b18-e1ec4bc4250b.Text: "Of course I have evidence, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The investigation has established that members of the Werserian family, which is responsible for both Dargonus's fleet and its logistics, used their contacts and influence to forge a host of documents in order to undermine the planet's supply routes and economy, thus fomenting unrest among the inhabitants."

4f6e4f75-bd30-49c7-838d-edfaaecd9c28.Text: "This young man is shrouded in a mist of grey and blue. Sickly shadows of fear are fluttering around him." {n}Cassia speaks so quietly that only you can hear her.{/n}

17e5b294-827d-4f9b-9a76-ce7821d7dab5.Text: {n}Noticing the close attention of the Rogue Trader, the young man averts his gaze. His long face is sweating and he presses his dry lips together tightly into a thin line. He seems to be afraid of something.{/n}

acc97cae-fdb1-4ad5-8fe6-5403cabc1fc1.Text: {n}Noticing the close attention of the Rogue Trader, the young man averts his gaze.{/n}

cc494988-963e-4ed5-aa55-8f009fa020cd.Text: "These events have also been overshadowed by the... I am ashamed to even say it aloud in front of you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... the rumours circulating among the higher houses..." {n}The governor stammers, then takes a deep breath.{/n} "Some were calling for Theodora's true heir to be installed as head of your house... Kunrad Voigtvir. Not all of your subjects have forgotten his past efforts for the benefit of the trade protectorate." {n}Drivestem stops talking, watching you with a tense expression.{/n} "When the investigation was launched... the evidence led us to the Werserians."

b80ed824-977b-4059-9e6b-8e42e1576a23.Text: "I remind you that House Werserian has hardly covered itself in glory in the past — it allowed xenos to attack the planet." {n}Governor Drivestem throws a quick, arrogant glance at a red-faced Clementia.{/n}

33ae0442-037c-4438-a50e-36d9cc663298.Text: {n}The aristocrats in attendance exchange glances, the noble lords averting their gazes and the noble ladies hiding behind the fans — no one is willing to be the first to answer.{/n}
