c921f94e-08c0-47a5-a16b-720354be77cb.Text: "We may not have agreed on everything, but at least you tried to reach out to me. As a thank you, I will share the coordinates of my kinspeople's cache with you as I promised. You will be given a reward worthy of your efforts."

fde66bd0-0e5e-4836-8cd1-b394db08e6e6.Text: "Lord Captain, we have received a report from the augur crew. The situation is... unusual. The xenos ship displays no biological or energetical signatures, even though it appears to be intact. According to the scanners... there is nobody on board."

42f03cf5-2692-48b1-908e-162767a45e32.Text: {n}The Vox Master relays the order to the Tech-Priests and promptly receives a reply.{/n} "Lord Captain, I am reporting that the hull fragments belong to the Drukhari xenos race, but the presence of their ships in the system at this time has not been confirmed."

9458fa0f-286c-4aae-b40a-26a934974994.Text: "However, survivors are believed to be hiding in one of the compartments of the damaged vessel of the Imperium. We have also spotted some drifting plating remains that belong to a third, unidentified vessel."

a63bbb85-cb14-4170-8077-8c099e1ed7b0.Text: {n}After several hours of tedious waiting, Vigdis gets back on air.{/n} "Lord Captain, the scouts confirm our earlier report. The xenos ship is intact. Many valuable artefacts have been found inside, but neither the Aeldari nor their bodies were discovered."

208c98cc-9552-4357-8b5f-24e37076e8c2.Text: "It will be done." {n}Vigdis flips the switches on the vox-system's cogitator, and the transmission goes quiet for a while.{/n}

f1b521f7-ccf4-40e0-a061-055f6294fe7b.Text: "We... are late again, elantach." {n}Yrliet's voice sounds faint and almost listless.{/n}

7083fc24-fc2d-4ad5-973e-8655e31f6d78.Text: "Kae-morag!" {n}A strangled cry interrupts the broadcast on the captain's bridge.{/n} "I came with you hoping to find my surviving kinspeople, elantach. And all I found were corpses buried by human hatred. Even when you could have helped my people, you stubbornly followed the same path as the rest of the mon-keigh, breaching our treaty. Do not expect gratitude from me."

07eaad87-7014-4f4c-95ef-47c4864edcbc.Text: "The xenos joined forces to eliminate a vessel of the Imperium? Hmm. An alliance between the Aeldari and the Drukhari is an unusual sight, and yet such an outcome... is hardly surprising."

0a535de3-c8af-46bf-8cdd-f98cbcb536e5.Text: "Why, Master Interrogator, I was thinking exactly the same thing! At last, you and I can finally agree on something."

090d22b4-eaae-4e02-9292-4735104a7633.Text: "Looks very much like a conspiracy between the charming xenos cousins, azhi condemn them thrice over. An uncommon occurrence for the Aeldari and the Drukhari... But far from impossible."

10571896-5542-4317-8363-5fb0cdbfe63c.Text: "How blind are the mon-keigh to the vices of their own kind. Humans attack a ship of the Children of Asuryan sailing peacefully by, but it is my kinspeople who are to blame?" {n}Yrliet is beside herself with contempt and rage.{/n} "No, my kind would not willingly take part in a massacre orchestrated by the Dark Ones and then abandon their ship. Something else happened here, something I am afraid to even consider."

70a2001d-ef86-4e77-bd80-9605bf714e62.Text: "Lord Captain, the scouts managed to rescue several emaciated officers from the wrecked ship. Despite their wounds, they were able to tell us what had happened: during a patrol, the frigate discovered an Aeldari ship crossing the system and decided to immediately attack the enemies of Humanity. The xenos vessel proved too fast and skittish, but at one point its engines failed, giving the frigate a chance to attack."

c44911e6-6c59-4125-9e0b-a6285b3d1518.Text: "When the guns were aimed, several Drukhari ships suddenly pounced from the darkness. At first they attacked from a distance, but soon boarded the frigate and wreaked a bloody massacre on the decks. It is only by sheer miracle that the surviving officers managed to escape, locking themselves up in a hidden technical compartment the xenos had no use for. The survivors claim that the xenos conspired and deliberately led the ship into a trap, where it met its doom."

d5b51787-ac35-4394-bfde-bcf731585700.Text: "How blind are the mon-keigh to the vices of their own kind. Humans attack a ship of the Children of Asuryan sailing peacefully by, but it is my kinspeople who are to blame for the tragedy that befell them for their deeds?" {n}Yrliet is beside herself with contempt and rage.{/n} "No, my kind would not willingly take part in a massacre orchestrated by the Dark Ones and then abandon their ship. Something else happened here, something I am afraid to even consider."

69a478aa-740a-4fb3-8da3-beef6b2fb9e3.Text: "I know that you have tried your best to keep your promise, elantach. And there are not enough colours and undertones in your language to describe how much that means to my kind. How much it means to me..." {n}For a brief moment, Yrliet's voice is drowned in silence.{/n} "I'm grateful. And I will fulfil my end of the bargain by sharing the coordinates of my kinspeople's cache. You will be given a reward worthy of your efforts, elantach."

05e296f3-0763-45e6-84d5-3050283ccb6f.Text: "Elantach, has..." {n}The comm-bead in your ear delivers a stifled gasp.{/n} "Has my search come to a dead end? I ventured into the darkness of space with the mon-keigh, hoping to find my kin... But all I found were corpses buried by human hatred." {n}Yrliet's voice trembles either with desperation or anger.{/n}

7a8763a7-a8f4-474b-b434-89831f13e249.Text: Achilleas Scalander has reported new information about the planned attack. The xenos are already preparing to strike — the Rogue Trader must act immediately.

9a4d32a8-3b24-4945-ae7c-fe1aa22700ae.Text: "Where is the scum that cut off my hand? I'm coming for you, and I'll rip out your heart!"

ef7e2aa2-ec4a-421e-9684-049c0808d269.Text: "Ungrateful scum. We guard them, and they dance on our bones! I will remember that face, and I will come back."

49638d14-5c40-475a-8826-4491ec1115a9.Text: "Damn it, why did it have to be Godierda? I don't know why the Emperor ordered you to kill her, but we must see to it that she did not die in vain."

fa054a85-afcd-4b48-b619-53bf0ae16272.Text: "And just like that, she's gone. She will never even know what she died for. Meanwhile, the spinners go on passing whatever judgement they please."

d9cdf688-f040-4e87-a04a-a544d3ad2dba.Text: "Throne! Did you see that 'forcer get roasted? She had it coming, I say! At least we'll get a few hours without any more beatings."

98b4bcfc-b655-4bea-aee8-bd2b49c4cbc2.Text: "Godierda is dead? Hah! Something to celebrate, until they assign a new 'forcer!"

f2a18cb7-4fcf-49de-9c62-8953660a7b57.Text: "Did the enforcer just up and die or did she... have a little help? Eh, who cares. I just wish they'd take the body away soon. Last time, the stench made me sick for the entire shift."

349f5baa-3e28-4592-ac70-c0d699085fd9.Text: "A death cultist? I knew I should have switched shifts today."

f788846c-ff5b-4360-ae9d-e9a82c4452c5.Text: "You... didn't come here for me, did you? I've done nothing wrong!"

33df5409-88dc-4bc4-98a7-71917ffdf58b.Text: "I don't know why you're here, but I hope it's not to take me away..."

9e241c32-551b-4e17-a32f-b35cc0b92513.Text: "You know, I look at you, but I'm not scared at all. I guess I've seen too many disasters to be afraid of death."

0be1e7c0-d57f-4b2c-9aa8-8c5c60f5f063.Text: "My friend from the foundry bay is still looking for his daughter after that enforcer raid."

5da38107-d7de-42f5-8d11-c9b69fb57ebc.Text: "Should have told him she ended up in the shredder."

0ffc73d8-ad7d-4d15-a317-1293b120a8cf.Text: "Why are you shaking, kid? Did the shift siren spook you?"

a824777e-daf2-48e5-8bc7-54a23efb5a73.Text: "Leave him be. If you had lived through what those bloody upper-deckers did in the foundry bay, you'd be afraid of your own shadow, too."

b32e705a-88c0-451d-a03a-07f22b339386.Text: "The foundry workers were given rations and medicine for free, and we're barely making the ends meet here! Where is the justice in that?"

5ac4d48b-1a1c-4b41-bf19-353f3370fc3b.Text: "Guess the upper-deckers only understand strength. We should follow suit and kill a big officer, too."

2c2a380d-b93f-4a01-8dd0-8f3fbe38c3a5.Text: "What does Nemesite have against the Rogue Trader, anyway? {rt_mf|He|She} gave the foundry clans presents instead of breaking all their bones."

734dd9d9-f507-4d06-893b-9308d6152bae.Text: "Why should we be happy with handouts? {rt_mf|He|She}'s feeling generous today, but what's that gonna change? They were eating scraps and dying of disease yesterday, and they will be again tomorrow."

d81bf68c-156c-4340-8957-f26adbafa9d1.Text: "Don't bother hiding that pretty badge of dishonour, foundryman. Everybody knows you sold your brother to the enforcers for a ration pack."

ec690ebe-9055-4906-94c7-9947900387cd.Text: "That moron was yelling that he was Nemesite! Our entire family could have been shot! I... did what I had to."

0938d07c-71b8-41bf-841b-861518178fb7.Text: "I heard they strung up thirty-three 'Nemesites' in the foundry after all that snitching."

60f9cacd-dc4f-44eb-b9ab-77456ad3a006.Text: "And I heard that half of the snitches never even made it to the middle decks, thanks to the work of a few kind people."

cbdbaeae-68bd-40ae-bd3b-13be83e2351d.Text: "Death to the sellouts. And a plague upon the devious upper-deckers!"

dd3a1430-b341-4703-9473-8db97b253909.Text: A cable thrumming with the power of the conductive charge. A single swing of the blade will send the enforcer's soul to the Undying One.

c4d45680-e9df-43d8-845f-8f5a491f64c7.Text: Carry out the will of the Undying One

58fbb94b-6cf6-49a8-b04f-0586ca46bf8d.Text: Become a shadow and heed the voice of the crowd

b5bde4e3-99bb-4478-9cae-365938ee88ae.Text: It is too early. The quarry must not see the hunter set the snare.

ed896270-628c-4376-b91f-b0d04d8d778c.Text: Wait. Observe. Prepare. She sees you. The moment has not yet come.

dba0835b-26ae-409f-bf21-b2be376ea110.Text: "I see you lot have all taken off your red scarves. No longer feel like playing Nemesite, do you?"

3d9bc6eb-76c6-4a2e-b350-a38d787553bd.Text: "If you don't put on a scarf, you become someone's enemy. The same goes if you do."

059e3398-a437-450d-8897-8eb88877ea24.Text: "Listen, listen! Boy, do I have a story to tell!"

389c62c1-b303-4dff-bcb2-a629d8eda06c.Text: "How come the enforcers haven't flogged you stupid for all your 'stories' yet?"

07ef7af2-27e9-4bd3-9f89-978d43e917a5.Text: Set up a trap by spilling the liquid

9de53cc8-0fc1-48d0-8375-bd008446e2b0.Text: A reservoir of technical fluid. If it leaks, the power of the conductive charge will spread imperceptibly across the floor.

3c198979-2810-476a-8d18-3e422eec4d3c.Text: "You know that feeling when you're being stared at, but you can't tell who by or where from? I have that feeling right now."

96331b1a-d1bc-43a2-985c-834c68b509c1.Text: "I'm not sure, but I don't like the way the locals are staring at us. Maybe it's your captivating charisma, but I much more suspect that the enforcer's armour is to blame."

161b1eeb-bf41-42e5-bbec-3c811eee351c.Text: "Where is the Second Spinner? We were supposed to meet here."

3fe084ea-ada5-42c2-98f2-64dc2bb58681.Text: "Spindle! That son of a grox! His mouth is like a sieve, and I'm not talking about his missing teeth."

845ecba2-a5e5-4d1e-a69a-684166b2d1c0.Text: "Someone hit the upper decks hard and all the clues lead straight down into the chambers! The 'forcers are coming to butcher us!"

4569f754-a235-453f-ad5c-eb3577441737.Text: "I heard Nemesite hurt a big shot, so the enforcers are preparing to raid the chambers. We should run! They won't bother figuring out who's really guilty and who's not!"

aa6e6544-9c04-4d7a-a466-59b3394d9b8b.Text: "Someone from the chambers attacked the temple? Then turn them over to the enforcers! I don't want to die for somebody else's crimes!"

46b7b1ea-efb6-4888-b022-c5c02f28736f.Text: "Do you believe yourself fit to serve on the flagship?"

aa96975a-23ef-4de5-bb2d-256ebd1c1d1c.Text: "So your reasons are your unflinching courage and your love of the stars?"

c16914b0-e0af-4a75-a7cc-4256a4d6cefa.Text: "Very well. I accept you into my service."

ed5fb276-3fc4-4142-a08f-94f7c75c7b90.Text: "I appreciate your fervour, but my ship has no shortage of skilful warriors."

57150bc1-9405-441c-92c6-7ea1e8aa3ab9.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! Senior Lieutenant Mattis Erebis, at your service!" {n}The tall, dark-haired young man enunciates sharply as he salutes you with great fervour. Breathless from his own audacity, he blurts out,{/n} "I hope I don't sound too bold if I say I've always dreamt of serving on your flagship. Would it be too much for a modest servant of the dynasty to hope that the Lord Captain might graciously make him part of {mf|his|her} crew?"

e84deece-956b-4cc8-8078-b6d9e363221a.Text: {n}Mattis looks away first.{/n} "Pardon my tactlessness, Mistress..." {n}He clears his throat.{/n} "I have the strangest feeling that we have met before."

89a7fe81-8436-4be9-8c62-6b6d07d48393.Text: "I have served dutifully in the planetary forces, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Governor Drivestem even awarded me a medal for defending the southern hive against the xenos. I may have been born on a gravity-bound world, but my heart belongs to the void!"

9debb998-f156-419d-af2b-2b3ab8f5394d.Text: "There is... another reason, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, but I am afraid you will find it laughable. You see, I have always known my destiny awaits me on the flagship. Because ever since I was a child, I've had the same dream over and over: a dark-haired young woman walking barefoot along the decks, and me following in her footsteps. I would run but could never catch up to her."

11d23be3-3707-439a-9e72-6079138eb0ca.Text: {n}Kibellah soundlessly appears at your side. Her face is reflected in Mattis's dark eyes. As their gazes meet, they both freeze in astonishment and lower their heads.{/n}

bf81fa14-67aa-4e82-8c9f-62f8f6338627.Text: "This is truly an honour for me, Lord Captain! I will not let you down! Glory to House von Valancius!"

290bf6d3-b716-482b-b2e4-58b4218badd2.Text: {n}The spark fades from the young lieutenant's eyes.{/n} "Of course, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Thank you for hearing out my request. Glory to the dynasty!"

2d2e74b5-383b-4ffb-a610-d50e9ffe3f46.Text: "Let us go," {n}Kibellah whispers softly.{/n} "I have heard... and seen... all I needed to."

626c091d-870e-4b13-ab33-10f948105983.Text: "My father told me he had felt something of the sort when he met my mother." {n}Mattis's eyes take in Kibellah's features. He smiles sadly.{/n} "I believe my future awaits me there."

557384a1-e054-44ae-949a-a39b0d00d392.Text: {n}Kibellah takes her time to reply.{/n} "You... were born on a world and absorbed a hive's scents. I would have remembered someone who smelled like that. I do not know you."

0868f0bc-b41e-49ae-ad4d-b8f7a7dbf427.Text: {n}If Kibellah had had enough to eat growing up, if she had not put her body through gruelling trials, if she had not used intoxicants during the cult's rituals... You might have said the two bore quite the resemblance to each other.{/n}

7284187d-4fe6-4f03-a7ee-c4e5387cc3e8.Text: "That scrap of parchment must be incredibly special. I see no other reason for your brother and sister to be ignoring the Rogue Trader."

55776ab3-35df-46e4-a101-963ba10fbaca.Text: "That dark shape in the portrait. You drew it in, did you not, Lorna? Who is it?"

28793c8e-cad7-4568-abd9-81f9b8379863.Text: "You're pressing down too hard on your quill, Lumi. Look how thick your lines are! And the ink hasn't dried! Mother will be livid when she sees this stain on my cuff..."

4e5bf0a9-fb86-490a-9910-5121975fc9c7.Text: "And to the Rogue Trader, ruler of a thousand stars!"

814dc76f-80c0-4a1a-a86c-293f82093e5d.Text: "Why don't you watch what you're doing instead of lecturing me again! How many times has Master Rogbard said: apply the base colours first, then the darker shades." {n}The Erebis children are leaning over a sheet of parchment, arguing passionately. A small, finely made box next to them contains quills and a few bottles of ink.{/n}

9da6c899-cf7c-48fc-9359-a7fbded6980d.Text: "That is proper. That is honourable." {n}Kibellah barges into the conversation, winces, then whispers softly,{/n} "Come, Domin. Let us frighten them no more."

d9f29633-6bd3-4ada-b7c7-8061656d082e.Text: "Our family was once renowned for their courage, but Dargonus has no need for boarding teams. So our parents enrolled Rono and Lumi in the scriptorium to study religious painting."

9f79c4df-3df3-4e9f-99f5-023420a8cefb.Text: {n}The parchment is an unfinished family portrait showing the Erebis parents and their four children. The young artists' skill is impressive.{/n}

13b3f239-23e1-4abc-9548-ef7e72158c65.Text: {n}Lorna grabs her younger siblings' collars and makes them bow, looking guilty.{/n} "M-my apologies, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! I am to blame! Lumi and Rono tend to get far too engrossed in their work, but I will see to it that they do not forget their manners again."

5b67211d-845b-4a6a-a18d-45e76699a601.Text: {n}Kibellah's shadow hangs over the younger Erebises. Her unblinking gaze carefully studies the unfinished drawing, and grows gloomier still.{/n}

6e588801-ab69-4a0f-92f3-970f7cb55316.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! We are honoured to be at the von Valancius palace. I am Lorna Erebis." {n}A pale young woman, slightly shorter than Kibellah, smooths a lock of her dark hair nervously as she stands between her younger siblings and the spinner.{/n}

e1fdb6fe-aa10-42c8-a961-a1d0cce65e85.Text: {n}Kibellah casts a final glance at the portrait, then quietly walks away.{/n}

933d4781-c45f-4c19-b991-5f6d049a5f55.Text: {n}Lorna purses her lips and looks away.{/n} "Mother says the Erebis clan has a secret guardian that protects us from the shadows. And I thought... It would be unfair to draw all of us but not them. Silly, I know..."

45d62eb0-fe89-4abd-965b-d44e5fa60779.Text: {n}But your attention is drawn not to the fine lines and shading, but the sketch of a dark figure added in by a still more masterful hand.{/n}

83681c9c-8586-4c76-9f19-d191007b1486.Text: "Then why did you name your daughter Lorna and not Naaki? Did you not want her to become great?"

ff05c5e5-8f36-444e-bd52-eeed461ced5d.Text: "I am looking for a Naaki Erebis. The ship's archives mention several of your ancestors, but the one I need is a living person."

590a106b-c0c7-4bfa-8b7d-78c476b5495d.Text: "The Undying Emperor? You were followers of the Bloodspun Web?"

141c30f7-7168-41f4-854f-63b84ee37301.Text: "Is there currently anyone named Naaki in your household?"

cae00a9a-b53a-4c17-9eb8-311cab9f9959.Text: "From this point forward, Mattis will serve on my ship."

bf5292be-6bea-4f36-94f3-45e1603dcada.Text: "He is the pride of the Erebis family. Its blood. Its essence. We are delighted for him to serve you as we used to serve Lady Theodora."

b42fd4d6-d021-40c7-a06b-771adaf0240c.Text: {n}The couple exchange glances again.{/n} "Our clan had... has a tradition. We name our children in honour of our past heroes: Mattis and Naaki Erebis, the twin founders of our family. A great warrior and a keeper of knowledge."

4508952e-3819-4f4a-adce-05f98785a555.Text: {n}Xioni Erebis nods slowly in response, a sad smile upon her lips.{/n} "We did. But the Emperor took her from us. The Undying Emperor."

fa7c5b71-98c9-42ec-a15f-9777382d19c8.Text: "We realise that your attention to House Erebis was brought on by some manner of circumstances. Please let us know how we can be of service to you, and we will do what you require."

89d04276-89b2-4e87-ad0c-11bc94a1cac8.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, allow us to thank you once again for this honour. Though we left the flagship a long time ago, it is a pleasure to be in the presence of a Lord Captain again." {n}Xioni looks at you with a pensive, unblinking gaze, her eyes darker than the night sky.{/n}

50d89b3a-a785-4c7f-b5a3-f2d583324e3d.Text: "Our eldest son, Mattis, is on the planetary guard. So is Lorna, our eldest daughter, though she has devoted herself to medicine. And to my great surprise and elation, our younger children, Rono and Lumi, have found their vocation in serving the God-Emperor and the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Ecclesiarchy{/g}."

8ff6a965-6050-478f-a945-1d732bba0792.Text: "Sadly, we are but a shadow of what was once a much more numerous clan. Most of our kinspeople fell in combat, but we believe the Erebises' last battle is yet to be fought. We raise cohorts of successors. We teach new recruits — and our own children — the ins and outs of void service before they even set foot on board. The new generation... are learning to serve in their own way."

a7cd5656-066a-4182-9c2d-518fd275ba13.Text: "No... No one has borne that name for many years now."

e30303e9-e1cb-4128-ac8c-1922a236acaa.Text: "No, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Randor and I, we have always been stalwart in our faith, and we revered the spinners' service, but their sacred path was too dark and frightening for us."

76aab640-27b0-4dde-a3e6-d54f7bf5e07a.Text: "We may not have understood the deeds of the Bloodspun Web, but we never doubted that the spinners carried out His will, for they gave their all to their duty. It is a heavy duty, but a true duty always is."

192ac6de-2c91-4942-8aa2-2ec386b6d21b.Text: {n}Randor laughs.{/n} "What can I say... I have always wanted to raise a great person."

eac70a16-3528-4714-b4f2-906d6ef04e63.Text: "I won't lie, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, we never saw her in person. We did not have the rank. Even her favour was bestowed on us in the form of a document penned and delivered by a scribe. But we remember her orders, and they were reflective of all the courage and fervour of a true Rogue Trader."

6558ece9-b48f-4561-a2e3-d3d1f03554a0.Text: "They did name a daughter Naaki." {n}Kibellah's words hang heavy in the air.{/n}

ba5fd8c9-6268-4b97-9eb6-cb6e866f18c1.Text: "Enough." {n}Kibellah's cold, raspy voice sends a shiver down your spine.{/n}

7bb085ed-0b47-41d2-8565-568bf3e03b93.Text: "A keen observation." {n}Randor's eyes meet Kibellah's as she speaks, but he is not intimidated. On the contrary, the corner of his mouth curves upward slightly, and he gives a respectful nod.{/n}

736aea82-80bb-4898-9e19-faa87b4dce1c.Text: "Legend had it that a great future awaited bearers of those names. Every Mattis or Naaki Erebis would add to the clan's renown, and they would prove faithful assistants to any Lord Captain they served. But legends are just that, legends. It is not names that give people strength but the faith inside their hearts."

27cebd33-2576-4f78-9cf9-ca30e6bac296.Text: "I am ready to receive the Arbites delegation."

d341bda5-7ab0-468d-925b-1b51e06330ff.Text: "I am ready to receive the Arbites delegation."

2dacea7b-6cc7-4057-8bab-e9dc63b0dfdc.Text: "I remember you. You were in charge of the proceedings at my Magnae Accessio."

121a4bd9-9cb9-479a-97e0-739476e24b82.Text: "I will have the audience arranged immediately, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

3e5071a2-0b55-4fe7-afb7-3e22be95a3b2.Text: "I will have the audience arranged immediately, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

3fd972f8-275b-49b1-bbf5-de1d8277d2ee.Text: {n}The man's face lights up with a smile, and he bows deeply.{/n} "I was, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! And now, per the High Factotum's orders, I have assumed the role of your acting chancellor!"

72e11cc6-c888-410b-85c8-68328796cbc6.Text: "After Chancellor Werserian was forced to leave office, and Secretary Scalander..." {n}He clears his throat, clearly considering a change of subject.{/n} "Well, I must admit, I expected the worst. But my predecessors served the dynasty dutifully, which is why everything is currently as stable as it can be here on the capital world."

6981b14b-219b-4e23-9b7c-d4ab43c003b8.Text: "You mentioned a guardian in the shadows, did you not, Lorna?"

caf1b2c3-223c-4dc4-8941-3df0c5c48175.Text: "Naaki is of the past. When those who remember her die, she will die too."

1bce64b8-6269-49cb-889a-100772947aab.Text: "You are Naaki Erebis. The Emperor's will is clear."

a96f0da3-7c07-40e3-b49f-ecd84ceea565.Text: [Let the Erebis family reunion proceed undisturbed]

313c96c3-81ed-461d-832f-704c4e7f7b07.Text: "You still have the dexterity of your former profession, Xioni."

444e0471-7c2e-4057-82f4-af0304bcacc4.Text: "I do not kill on others' orders. Neither should you kill Naaki."

a280665a-814e-4fc1-a303-74e0ffef553e.Text: "Perhaps you would like to bid your family farewell?"

5ddeb673-ee4e-4396-9df2-4559d8732ce5.Text: "You cannot kill your past. You can destroy the people who are connected to it, but are you truly prepared to murder innocent people just to cut yourself free?"

fa81f9c4-72f4-4457-afed-2942d6403414.Text: "Killing your family will not bring you peace but only shatter your soul still further."

562c597d-ce4c-4584-80b3-4a6d59ea0aa6.Text: "If you must kill innocents to vanquish your doubts, then you are not a spinner but a common murderer. You should fear the bloodlust you feel!"

f59e15ab-4e40-43bc-8c5b-8dcf2adaf208.Text: "You admit your mind is clouded. Do the Tenets of the Web permit you to do His will with tangled thoughts?"

2d0f9320-d52d-49f2-aa46-0d4e5c90785d.Text: "If killing your family will relieve you of your doubts, then do it."

d03b2ea4-46f3-4947-92c3-bea45d3138d1.Text: "The choice is yours and yours alone. You are the Undying One's spinner."

5813f4ed-37d4-45e4-89ea-6c32db880220.Text: "Reckon with the past by spilling the blood of those who betrayed you. Do they still hold Naaki in their hearts? Then tear them out."

71c3c4c9-2546-451b-91e8-f480d09f9f54.Text: "So all this time, Mattis, your dreams were showing you..."

5ea70d68-1717-489c-b628-6b25972671ef.Text: "You lied when you said the Emperor had taken Naaki."

6b2ab70d-80a4-49f2-b8c0-768fec357db2.Text: "What were you thinking, giving your daughter away to the death cultists?"

5847739c-ee44-4253-aa9a-8b378f3d185a.Text: "A difficult choice, but a righteous and devout one."

2448473e-64a9-419f-a58f-8cf33d365dca.Text: {n}Kibellah's cry brings the Erebis family back together. Six alarmed faces. Six people standing shoulder to shoulder like a fortress wall. And one lone, grim figure opposite them. The shadow peers into their dark eyes... The same as her own. Their pale lips, the same as her own. She clenches her fists, ignoring the steel claws that pierce her palms.{/n}

d13dda25-61a7-4c3d-bfc2-4b3e1793a4b6.Text: "A few years before Lady Theodora sent our clan's survivors to Dargonus, the Bloodspun Web's Vizsier came to our bay. He said the Emperor demanded the next firstborn of the Erebis clan. That He needed a new spinner."

4fff1c5d-da73-4f61-a03e-2bc7e30909d1.Text: {n}Kibellah senses your lie and smiles bitterly.{/n}

1009e12b-4025-4b9a-afc3-5936505bb12e.Text: {n}Kibellah turns to you sharply.{/n} "We are here to settle our debt to the Undying One. We now have the name, the person, and the explanation. I... know what must be done. So why do I feel pain from an unseen wound in my heart? Why am I, for the first time in my life, hesitant to sever a thread? All this time, I have been wandering in the labyrinth of my mind, but the answer never came to me. What must I do, Domin? How do I end Naaki Erebis?"

414d8d47-7b81-43e2-b346-dfba0246109c.Text: "We thought of the sacrifice we had to make, and... of the sacrifice the Emperor makes for all. It was hard for us, but we did not doubt His will. It was our sacrifice and our service."

bd9ebc24-7a45-4e44-8577-05ac3540d868.Text: "The most difficult one in our lives, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. But we knew our daughter was alive and serving the faith. And, as mysterious and bloody as the ways of this service were, they were ways that pleased the Emperor."

d4d2bd87-9763-4740-86dc-a563d7c95f0f.Text: "The ritual of releasing the burden." {n}Kibellah steps up to her brother, who is so completely like her... and yet so thoroughly different.{/n} "New Bloodspun Web recruits undergo it in order to forget their past and devote themselves to the Undying One. And so that their souls do not suffer. Tell me, Mattis... is your soul in pain?"

37531b38-a7bc-47f8-bf03-7fca9ab64c6e.Text: "I could have had a family and a future full of righteous service. A chance for a different life. That was taken from me. Who I would be and how I would serve was decided for me."

f8afe980-8ed9-4eaf-97d4-395f3ee4a88c.Text: "The Vizsier. The Bloodspun Web. These... people. They had the audacity to decide who I was and what I existed for. I was but a tool for them." {n}Kibellah's lips twist in contempt.{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:CompKibellah_Distortion}But no longer{/d}. Now I am the Domin's shadow. I am greatness and power. I am the fear and fury of {mf|his|her} foes. The infinite universe lies open before me..."

d45b14fd-4eee-4a98-80f7-2fc242032779.Text: {n}Her eyes grow colder than the void itself.{/n} "You are right, Domin'{name}. Forgive my insolence, but you and the guests should leave the hall. I have... personal business to settle." {n}The Erebises start to edge back in terror, but freeze in place at one gesture from Kibellah.{/n}

3fbb87d6-ca86-4b9a-81f6-38138b1360ba.Text: {n}Kibellah flinches, goes even paler... And then her eyes widen. She clutches her chest with a pained rasp and collapses to the floor like a broken doll.{/n}

e0fdb484-06f4-4080-a163-88e18916053c.Text: {n}Kibellah's lifeless body convulses in death throes. You cannot feel her heartbeat. The Erebis family surrounds her, panic and fear crossing their faces for only a brief moment before their rigorous voidsman training takes over.{/n}

864cd804-94b3-4676-b241-70a90b812e79.Text: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Some things are never forgotten."

9e6fe21f-a801-4d42-9388-246fe823799d.Text: {n}Kibellah, dismayed, looks first at the Erebis family, then at you, then at her own reflection in the steel of her dagger.{/n} "I... will not kill... Must I follow my orders when my entire nature shrinks from it and my heart screams it is wrong? This is not my will."

8d2f3c31-8b8f-4d14-ad23-9bd60b908de2.Text: {n}Shaken and devastated, the Erebises can only watch helplessly as Kibellah walks out of the throne room.{/n}

7ff856ff-989b-415c-902e-04edd1438266.Text: "My family abandoned me many years ago."

a396ffdb-36b1-40e3-92df-e214a82e8142.Text: "My family... is waiting for me on the flagship."

7350805e-5665-4fea-aa44-d273a8d1c4b7.Text: "Farewell. Naaki... spent all these years missing you. But I will not."

22ae80cf-caf0-41f8-a98b-6314e9782990.Text: "I remember what I am permitted to remember. The Tenets of the Web. Prayers to the Undying One. The names of poisons and intoxicants. The name the Vizsier gave me. But you... No. I do not remember you. I do not know you."

deb4bf5b-62fd-4cc1-8c90-686f6a2ef06e.Text: "Whispered... The God-Emperor demands a great sacrifice, yet it makes serving Him all the more honourable." {n}Xioni's voice trembles, and she turns to her husband for strength and support.{/n}

26ea57db-158b-4140-90af-1f8fad5bd128.Text: "Six months later, we had twins. A boy and a girl with eyes darker than darkness itself." {n}Xioni smiles tenderly at Kibellah.{/n} "You were born first, Naaki. And with sorrow and pride, we gave the Vizsier our most precious treasure. For that is how one honours the God-Emperor."

b86451ea-dcaf-4ee8-8076-9b28e068d34a.Text: "We did not lie. We would never have dared." {n}Randor looks over at Kibellah, her dark hair, her scars.{/n} "Naaki..."

ccfb4464-2050-40d0-b465-64dc201b6739.Text: "So if I had been born a minute earlier, that animated corpse standing before you today would have been me?" {n}Mattis recoils from his parents.{/n} "But why doesn't she remember anything? Why was she never told?"

0b289ea6-ceba-4437-861e-dfdbec4f65dd.Text: "It only hurts because I never knew you all these years."

a366bb22-1733-4634-8565-d231501b46e3.Text: {n}She clenches her fist.{/n} "The Vizsier forged me into a weapon and stained it with blood. He named a mark. He gave a mission. Come, Domin. We must descend into the temple of death, where I will report on my task. And ask the Vizsier a single question. 'Why me?'"

d44373ad-938d-43c4-b8aa-1730fa34ae7d.Text: "You have grown into a fine woman, Naaki. And though you may be lost now, I know the Emperor will point you right. We are... proud of you."

77c9c905-fd27-4c5b-aebc-57b02187f5a0.Text: {n}The corners of her eyes twitch, as though she is in pain.{/n} "My name is Kibellah."

74640e42-1be1-418c-bd04-c8f151a39f66.Text: {n}Xioni leans over and puts an ear to her daughter's unmoving chest.{/n} "Her heart isn't beating! I must restart it! Step back!" {n}She lays her palms on Kibellah's breastbone and pushes — once, twice, thrice... ten times... thirty times...{/n}

80a2345e-0907-43a2-9891-71ecedf7aca1.Text: {n}A heavy, raspy sigh escapes Kibellah's chest.{/n}

48e16924-c99f-4780-9c08-87a7cf8f5f24.Text: "Naaki Erebis... is dead. Only... Kibellah remains."

e93a43e0-d708-4bd7-ab23-94ebb77584e6.Text: {n}Xioni touches Kibellah's cheek.{/n} "Naaki... The Emperor is merciful! He has not parted us!" {n}Kibellah carefully moves Xioni's hand aside.{/n}

71ca2b38-f206-4313-a833-7b4a7b7102ab.Text: "I was weak. Reluctant to be taken in His hands. But then a haze clouded my eyes... And I saw her. A frightened girl. Naaki. The part of me even the ritual of releasing the burden had failed to erase. And I knew that a part of me had always clung to a past I did not even remember. My fear of death subsided. I let Naaki go, for the Undying One had been waiting to take her. And what was broken became whole. Naaki is gone. Only Kibellah remains."

86e489be-15b5-4ace-8b79-0579c2f56a82.Text: {n}Kibellah nods and casts a strange glance at those who, in another life, would have been her family.{/n} "Naaki Erebis is no more. Death's dues are paid. There is... one last thing to be done."

133edbe6-bf3f-4fb1-b1f0-92d82ca6170a.Text: "Enough. I... I know who Naaki Erebis is." {n}Her unblinking gaze turns to you.{/n}

b4588512-2c40-4f1a-abe9-521a534a3037.Text: {n}Kibellah shakes her head.{/n} "You are wrong, Domin. I hear your words, but I also... {d|Encyclopedia:CompKibellah_StillDoubts}hear the whispers of monsters{/d} wandering through my mind. And they are glad that the Erebis will not die. For these people are the source of my doubts — empty hopes, the ghosts of attachments. Weaknesses that displease the Undying One. Only by cutting their threads will I prove that I am ready to serve Him fully."

8f15eedc-2de9-45b5-9eda-4c9080dcb35f.Text: {n}She closes her eyes and exhales convulsively.{/n} "You... may be right. Perhaps I am making a mistake. I will trust you."

d656aef6-cc5a-42f4-80b7-1de9f19fb517.Text: {n}The look in her dark eyes grows colder than the void itself.{/n} "These deaths please the Undying One. They are not for me, but for Him. I am but a blade that must be sharp if it is to serve. And I will cut the threads."

5dcebd4b-c1c2-4363-b0a6-4140887380eb.Text: {n}The Erebis family recoils in horror, but a gesture from Kibellah freezes them on the spot.{/n} "I ask you and your guests to leave the room — let only the Undying One witness my return to the thread."

272b383c-a144-4267-aa6b-0ed685822a68.Text: "Death called the name... and my mind could not take in the will of the Undying One. The shock extinguished all thought, but there remained a hardness in my heart that my consciousness lacked. It... simply stopped. It did what I could not do by my own hand."

4ae24cbb-741b-42eb-8519-73fce6dccb41.Text: "Naaki..." {n}Xioni Erebis looks at Kibellah with scarcely concealed fear, but her husband notices her reaction and shakes his head in warning.{/n}

a6b460d3-06b4-4384-9d54-c89ee8bc9fde.Text: "No!" {n}Mattis screams.{/n} "How could you keep something like that to yourselves? How could you... How could you!"

32ec5db3-827f-4788-9c96-4661c9d0500b.Text: {n}Lorna hugs her younger brother and sister, who cast frightened glances at their parents and the sinister woman with the wry smile.{/n}

570dec50-fe7a-4bcc-be22-b651df56bd5f.Text: "The woman who was destined for me. Not the love of my life, but... my sister?" {n}Mattis shudders and stares intently at Kibellah.{/n} "I didn't know. Do you... remember me?"

dcd2e753-f3bc-4179-a357-790a9ed27250.Text: "An unseen shadow. A servant of death... Mother called her Naaki, but I knew she was talking to... someone she knew."

cf4d0be3-7057-49fc-8bba-1de0efc3c6d6.Text: "Naaki Erebis..." {n}Kibellah throws her head back, and her laughter resonates through the hall.{/n} "Naaki Erebis is me!"

b9fb3a72-060f-42ee-8981-7791391faafb.Text: "You said the Undying One had taken Naaki. But death whispered her name only a short while ago."

971c5591-aa26-4323-b2ae-2e3564493f97.Text: "Let us enjoy the evening! Join the guests. We will talk later."

672df4df-86f1-483b-a8fc-f4fa26a5ab7f.Text: "How is House Erebis faring on Dargonus?"

2db909bd-521d-443e-8658-ef16c84a47e6.Text: "Are you finding the reception to your liking?"

9dba9f8e-86fc-4b5c-b8b8-dac9e5a8cfd2.Text: {n}Officers Randor and Xioni Erebis both make the sign of the Aquila, reverent expressions on their battle-scarred faces. Beside them are their children. Raised to love the God-Emperor, they are mild-mannered but fascinated by their new surroundings. Judging by their uniforms, the two eldest children are already members of the Dargonus planetary guard.{/n}

560423c5-bf5b-491c-99ed-6fd28c6abd53.Text: {n}Xioni touches her husband's palm ever so slightly, gives him a reassuring nod, then addresses you:{/n} "As a token of our greatest reverence for the von Valancius dynasty, allow me to present you with a modest family relic of the Erebis clan. May it serve you faithfully."

7ace7eb8-4a7c-46cf-88af-4541265f2e83.Text: "Of course, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. We are available for you at any time."

2ff886a7-2317-442b-9c69-b95c0b73bbf5.Text: "We are delighted by the favour shown to us, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship! Life in the capital is much calmer and slower compared to the ship. And I have almost gotten used to the gravity." {n}The prosthetic supporting Randor's spine creaks under his clothes as he attempts an awkward bow.{/n}

0cf35765-11ed-4efb-9385-fdcf81b42a5b.Text: "It is beyond all our expectations! We... could not have dreamt of something like this, to be honest. Even just permission to settle on Dargonus and continue our service on the dynasty's capital world was a most gracious gesture on Lady Theodora's part. We did not expect any further attention." {n}Xioni smiles gently, but her fingers are fidgeting with her heirloom pendant.{/n}

91ebddcd-3c6d-4f79-adf9-cc3ac7406252.Text: {n}As the Erebis parents notice a Bloodspun Web cultist at your side, they exchange glances. An almost imperceptible tension hangs in the air.{/n}

2a6b0087-84bd-49e6-b8dc-78465c9306d6.Text: {n}Kibellah whispers, just barely audibly,{/n} "A crowd, the Domin's attention, and this being their first visit to the palace... They are nervous. You must give these people time. Let them get accustomed to these surroundings... and to your presence. Let them wander around the hall and taste the food. We will talk to each one individually."

56e0e043-389e-4c81-8a70-d5e32d9fab81.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, it is a great honour for House Erebis to be invited to your palace." {n}There is a glimpse of distinct anxiety in Randor Erebis's eyes.{/n}

3b7a9457-2e95-494b-8ec4-ca688a19be64.Text: "You immediately donned the Vizsier's armour — is it helping you to embrace your new role?"

66da3824-2b12-4fd5-a33d-c14391f6b929.Text: "I know this is a ridiculous question to ask, but... how are you doing?"

4a2f58cd-7216-49ff-804b-4e96314a0a42.Text: "Did I just see the God-Emperor? In the flesh?"

9360659e-cf87-46ae-823d-ef0202df1072.Text: "What will become of the Bloodspun Web now?"

bd0b720a-f91e-4711-b5f8-09340fa7122f.Text: "I am sorry. Losing a mentor is hard."

45a25d1c-fe3b-495d-a50f-8b391aabd00a.Text: "You have done your duty to the God-Emperor. It was his wish, as well."

9d876a84-e935-461c-82e3-bb85a567daa2.Text: "He was a crazed old man who lied to you and used you. Do not feel sorry for him."

253b0dd1-0c85-4a34-8cd7-2d75b62f205a.Text: "What did the Vizsier look like to you?"

0d54898b-336d-41cb-b114-11f4dbe513c6.Text: {n}Clad in the Vizsier's armour, Kibellah is staring at the spot where, just a short time ago, lay the body of the man who raised her. Her shoulders are shaking and her head hangs low, but no tears are to be seen and no sobs come from behind her mask of dark gold. Suddenly, she throws her head back, and a desperate cry full of pain, fury, and regret echoes around the temple. This is not the Vizsier, nor a spinner you see before you. Just a daughter who has lost her father.{/n}

cdbf8c45-60ae-420c-ba03-8eeaf8ac9e82.Text: {n}Yrliet shakes her head and whispers quietly,{/n} "To foster a bond just to sacrifice it in the end. To kill your father just to assume his place. Your kind's fear of what you perceive as weakness is, in truth, your greatest weakness of all — one that leads your spirit into a trap with no escape."

ff058c50-cac9-4405-bb7e-dd1c6fc829fa.Text: "Did you two have visions? All I saw was the old man himself... Though he did fight with a strength that is beyond mere mortals. Swift and deadly, he was. He chose himself a good death, even if it was bleak." {n}Ulfar looks at Kibellah pensively.{/n}

ae9db7d5-c2ec-4821-b9ac-6b7e1b1c198b.Text: "The Tenets of the Web teach us never to regret or hesitate. But I could never have imagined that I would one day have to make a choice this painful. I did what had to be done... But that does not quell the pain. I know he is in the Undying One's hands, but that does not soothe the grief."

6fb0e013-849f-4746-b9ed-29c977f4b203.Text: "Was that how you saw the Vizsier, Domin'{name}? You saw an image of Death in him, but it was only an image. Fumes of the sacred intoxicant blessed our ritual, but what you saw, and killed, was a mere man. The Undying One does not come to the living. We come to Him."

acf3a330-7673-4bee-aec6-29514f109cba.Text: "Change lies ahead." {n}Kibellah cuts the air with her palm.{/n} "Travelling with you has given me {d|Encyclopedia:CompKibellah_Fanatic}many insights{/d}. We have been lurking in the shadows for too long! That was why we failed to prevent Nemesite's crimes or foil the abominations' plot. That was why we failed to protect Domin'Theodora. And I will not let anything like that happen to you! The Bloodspun Web will stretch its threads from out of the shadows and absorb new blood."

3c0695d7-3085-4543-ad56-892ea12d05aa.Text: {n}Kibellah raises her head to peer into the Undying Emperor's dark eye sockets.{/n} "We will not stray from the Tenets. We {d|Encyclopedia:CompKibellah_Humility}will not forget{/d} our predecessors' sacrifices and our Vizsiers' teachings. Service to the Undying One is our life. For He is duty. He is death."

06c34da3-d797-4904-9468-593e07d7cf61.Text: {n}Kibellah tosses her head back proudly.{/n} "For too long, we have languished amid the dereliction of the lower decks, concealing ourselves and enacting His will in secrecy. No longer! Henceforth, we will be a scarlet hand guiding trembling souls. As His holy servants, we will vest ourselves in gold and the veneration we {d|Encyclopedia:CompKibellah_Distortion}deserve{/d}, for to despise us is to despise Him! And we will serve you, Domin'{name}, not from the shadows but bathed in radiance. Such is the new Bloodspun Web."

67fc9499-6e23-4402-a4ce-632a4fa6e667.Text: "He was... more than that. He was both a friend and..." {n}Kibellah's voice drops, her next words barely audible:{/n} "...a father."

cfc96a2a-9e52-493f-aac8-e1c0ab23e2b0.Text: "It was his duty. But he... was reluctant to leave me to the very end. I saw it as his eyes went dim."

0fe8998e-a436-48c5-90d9-2e834fd19c21.Text: {n}Kibellah whispers softly,{/n} "He was an old man who lied to me and used me... But he was. And now he is no more."

06a70285-f8bc-4003-8212-17a3361124c2.Text: "Younger. The way he was when I first saw him. I was younger, too. It was as though we were facing each other in a training match like we used to."

43d60d71-f89e-4684-aa3b-99e3ae93366b.Text: "I do not want to lose my name as my mentor lost his. But no spinner will ever speak it again, for I am their Vizsier. Yet you are my Domin. And I am your shadow. Let me remain Kibellah to you, at the very least."

a4a6272d-5caf-4fc3-b9e2-1e60b71af4d3.Text: "We will open the temple to those among our congregation who wish to serve the flagship and the Undying One. We will grow our numbers. We will train fighters. We will share the enforcers' duty and fortify them with our skills. We will shun defending our grounds in confinement, and go on the offensive. We will no longer be unseen guardians, but will become His soldiers. And yours, Domin'{name}."

4c0ee970-7f84-4be5-be8b-1b8c9804d97b.Text: {n}Kibellah studies the spinners. Her voice thunders under the temple's vaults:{/n} "Bow now before your new Vizsier." {n}And a hundred whispers reply, "Death salutes you!"{/n}

5fed893e-c0f6-43e6-a3ca-074f6de93f27.Text: "I know I sought vengeance against him, but... I feel his absence already."

3d6f959a-5086-48a8-8a24-faec695ad43a.Text: "I think so, yes." {n}Kibellah reverentially touches a drop of blood on the dark gold.{/n} "I... sense the weight of this sacred vestment. The weight of the Vizsier's burden and the decisions I must make. From this day forth — my burden." {n}Her voice is full of sombre pride.{/n}

a1f7450b-6fbd-46cb-9c3d-5826c51b27fe.Text: "A fight worthy of Commorragh's arenas. I recall spectacles where members of the same family were forced to kill one another. What a treat it is to watch some mon-keigh patricide again."

07c2aedf-b1a2-4bc9-a83e-418dffa16c94.Text: "We have learned how Kibellah came to be part of the Bloodspun Web. We have met her family."

a3d0d847-ae40-44de-aac3-60d9af8a8d04.Text: "You greet us clad in armour. Are you preparing for battle?"

eb3d2ffc-b4d4-4933-91c1-cccafd60c8a2.Text: "Sacrament? Are we being dragged into another ritual?"

c9d81b5d-86aa-4bb4-b989-f202e399f7c7.Text: "What do you mean, 'the affliction you nurtured'? Was it you who doomed Kibellah to her suffering?"

87092cd0-99a2-4058-a7c5-1b1e4a2b606a.Text: "It seems your plan has failed. Kibellah did not carry out her last order."

d5737918-5f3c-473d-9b30-5023504314ca.Text: "Let that which must be done, be done."

14dea27b-c0d1-4e68-986b-927d3de37647.Text: "Is a simple transition of power not possible? Why must there be bloodshed?"

5e47da0e-e354-43fd-a355-5618a5c69edc.Text: "Do not demand yet another sacrifice from her, Vizsier!"

f0f1f3aa-bfe4-4f07-a9dc-26fb501151c0.Text: "You snatched her from her family. Do not call her your daughter."

1cae3b7b-f07d-4311-ae56-9a574cf9266e.Text: "Kibellah has been cured of her affliction."

9d3d5a1e-824a-438e-97be-9ca6f078881a.Text: {n}The Vizsier whispers a prayer, his masked face turned toward the Undying One's image. Instead of his usual threadbare clothes, he is wearing elegant armour of bone and dark gold, marked with purity seals. He turns as he hears you approach.{/n} "Kibellah... I have been hearing your footsteps for a long time. In His whispers."

ac4d7fd1-c4d9-4389-ab7c-a3567303ebac.Text: {n}The Vizsier's voice becomes astonishingly gentle.{/n} "My daughter, do you believe you have only served Him because I set you on the thread of the Web? Do you believe you have no faith in Him? You know that is not true."

acd7744a-36c2-48f4-b2a5-f65f7ec11e73.Text: "I grieve for her. And I am proud of you, Second Spinner. Your faith is beyond doubt."

652a1b48-422d-4607-9c65-9c9913e1a5e6.Text: "And the feelings that exist between you. Those supersede all else, perhaps. Could I have prevented them from springing up? Smothered them while they were still weak? I could have. But I chose not to."

3e161d6d-02b6-4279-9c8d-4cfd54852d23.Text: "Yes. It is difficult to be cruel to someone you love. Have you come to know that, Domin?"

8d0abcdd-a4e8-4b2c-989d-2a9395aa0d37.Text: "Do not call it love, Mentor. I was loyal to you and I deserved... better."

425f7579-e6ec-4e14-99ea-c703581c1d01.Text: "I... forgive you for your cruelty, Mentor."

874c9e4e-be3f-4e3f-9027-4298c6291f08.Text: "This is my final report, Mentor. I no longer wish to serve you."

9b259fe8-df07-41c5-b07c-b03e3a208752.Text: "Kibellah will be the new Vizsier. Her journey to the Undying One and the choice she made will be reflected in the Bloodspun Web's new pattern. As for me... I will go to Him, as I have long awaited."

df2dc785-8e27-452e-ab10-ac201c2a9c2c.Text: {n}The confusion and alarm in Kibellah's face gives way to anger and horror. Her face distorts like a crumbling paper mask as the emotions wash over her. Too many emotions for one whose soul has gone dead.{/n} "I— I have not yet done all that you expect me to, have I?"

c81f2fea-6786-47fa-a891-4cdcb93e0bd3.Text: "It has not failed. The choice has been made. Certainly, the new Vizsier of the Bloodspun Web will bring more change than I imagined. The threads will be more intertwined. The pattern will be different. But... the service to Him will continue."

b9842f0a-b4bb-44f5-8957-50389bad1b8c.Text: "That is correct, my daughter. Can you feel it? The proper way this burden must be passed?"

9db482d4-8a61-4b45-9ceb-4820acec399e.Text: {n}Agony distorts Kibellah's features, but she clenches her fists and nods.{/n} "We must summon death to these halls. And glorify Him."

fd4b4431-a2cb-40f7-a8fb-42b4d248880a.Text: "Still, it is... unfair." {n}Kibellah's face has become a death mask.{/n}

4265589a-f0dd-4b5c-afdd-d170db7f27cf.Text: "Because great things are not achieved in small ways. Because if you worship Him, your sacrifice to Him must be great as well."

be8605fb-6b7f-4693-9a3b-7d8e763bb731.Text: {n}The Vizsier's voice is full of sorrow and humility.{/n} "Yes. For I am stronger than you. And my high spinners stand with me, those who swore an oath to protect me and not outlive me. And He, too, stands with me. His face will emerge out of mine. And may those you chose when you set out along the threads of the Web, your comrades, your Domin — may they stand with you. Fight. Fight with no regret." {n}A bitter sigh falls from the old man's lips.{/n} "Farewell, my daughter. Let us honour the Undying One."

6e67c8a5-c904-4dde-88f2-ab0e533f41ee.Text: {n}Kibellah's voice falters. She clenches her teeth, trying to keep herself from bursting into tears.{/n} "I don't want to kill you!"

c7c782b0-977c-4b23-8f4d-810a7385f818.Text: {n}Kibellah's face dissolves into a cruel and bitter smile.{/n} "And still you steal from me. Even my vengeance has become part of your ritual."

3b4a12fa-e36e-4a64-afd2-858323868d3e.Text: "I was her family. I raised her and taught her. I gave her everything I had. Did I not, my daughter?"

a4c9a09b-964b-480d-b461-0d5c28126848.Text: "Your words are dishonest. The ritual of releasing the burden erased me. Made me hollow. What will of my own I had... you took from me. And filled me with yours instead."

77a1b780-f267-4941-a3dc-a40ec32febdb.Text: "This is true. No longer do I see anguish in her soul... Second Spinner, I am ready to receive your report. Have you accomplished the task the Undying One Himself set you?"

fb73a6bb-48c4-4e4b-8065-d30b242f383e.Text: "Everyone the name of Naaki Erebis ever meant anything to is dead. Naaki is no longer among the living."

8c303e51-c7e3-438e-9ae7-23be4b10cd86.Text: "Yes, Mentor. My mission has been accomplished. The Undying One revealed a name to me, and I found my mark."

92445aa4-e7c2-4e9f-99cb-8b0870ed8079.Text: "Everyone the name of Naaki Erebis ever meant anything to has forgotten her... and themselves. Naaki is no longer among the living."

db66bac0-8271-4871-982e-a4433ad75a30.Text: "Naaki Erebis died the moment she realised the Undying One wanted her to come to Him. Her body was wrested away from death, but... That which was once Naaki is now dead."

42c89dcf-88d2-46ac-ac3d-ca8c4584c09a.Text: "The task remains undone. I refuse to complete it! Condemning a life to oblivion is wrong for those who worship death. No one will hurt my family! No one will hurt me! Let the Undying One punish me if He so wills!"

a71c487b-a50d-4f0e-9a1d-96d1d533e775.Text: "This was difficult for you to do, my daughter. I understand, and I am sorry. But such was the Undying One's wish."

a8d4c0cc-f3f0-48a5-a4d1-c51a5c7a725b.Text: {n}Silence falls for what feels like an eternity. At last, the Vizsier responds with the sadness of an all-forgiving father,{/n} "That... is one of the threads as well, my daughter. I understand you."

2f915cc4-1031-4cb6-80f2-5fce6166a6a0.Text: {n}A tired sigh escapes the Vizsier's chest.{/n} "A harrowing sacrament. A ruthless ritual... I am relieved that it is nearing the end. Everything is coming together just as He revealed to me. Perfection has been sculpted. The affliction I nurtured has been vanquished. The choice has been made... So whence all the sadness, my daughter?" {n}The Vizsier shakes his head, suddenly looking very human. His shoulders droop, and he extends a hand toward Kibellah.{/n}

430f0342-0b10-4914-a934-2ab9a4dc9dc6.Text: "A great ritual. Many decades ago, the Undying One revealed through a {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialTarotGlossary}Tarot{/g} reading what must come to pass, and I heeded. The Bloodspun Web's path toward gaining its new Vizsier was then conceived. A path of discovery, devotion, dying, and resurrection in purity. Kibellah's predecessor stumbled on that path. So did the next one. I waited. I have lived long past my due time. The Undying One has been waiting for me for so long..."

beaff5db-417f-4608-a320-fd19b9113b4a.Text: "The Undying One laid the thread, and I served as guide. The meeting with you and your world, Domin. The hunt for Nemesite, her grim and ghastly doppelganger. The comprehension of her flock's pain... My assignments stirred anxiety in my daughter's soul. As they were meant to."

fb1180ff-36a5-4fc2-a65b-220115a3c667.Text: "You... were my family, Mentor. You and the Bloodspun Web. I will not defile myself with a lie."

50e5661a-7a27-4d73-a98d-c36fa3812f22.Text: "Blood is our gift. The only thing that is truly ours. The only worthy way to worship and honour Him."

0b84e49c-e801-444e-9e76-6ea5209148ea.Text: "Domin'{name}, {mf|Lord|Lady} of the Ark. It is good that you are here with her. It is right. The Undying One has blessed this union of light and shadow."

c22ef059-eb99-4e4c-94d7-1c3a0ca20523.Text: "Today is a special day. I have only donned this armour once before, when I was Second Spinner. That day... I ceased to be second. But I have remembered the weight of this gold on my shoulders and chest through all the years since." {n}Kibellah opens her mouth, but the Vizsier stops her with a gesture.{/n} "You will understand, my daughter. You will understand soon."

30079909-5110-444f-ac1d-140a93c52f02.Text: {n}The Vizsier looks away for a brief moment and nods to empty space.{/n} "The Undying One's congregation sacrifices the blood of its blood. That is how spinners are brought into this temple. But only those who would serve Him of their own volition stay and spin the Bloodspun Web. As Kibellah did."

244b7159-9611-4f93-9c95-f24ee2731485.Text: {n}Kibellah grits her teeth hissing,{/n} "You used my trust to make me your tool! Of course I see no other destiny for myself now. But that does not mean it was preordained!"

460e806b-f207-489a-a180-5d9ce598fc99.Text: "You... are right, Mentor. The path I walk is mine. And I thank you for setting me on it."

bf2d7e63-24e6-4f6a-8153-4427bae4818c.Text: {n}Kibellah's brow furrows in anguish.{/n} "Perhaps I could have served Him differently... Now I will never know. You took that away from me."

6d31c294-685a-4df5-8baf-43e9855ae148.Text: [Leave] "I tried to help her. But some ailments are incurable."

7291385a-77e1-4f51-820b-c7456286ac9c.Text: {n}Breathing heavily, the Choirmaster covers his face and whispers,{/n} "It is... over, Lord Captain. We are in the world of flesh again."

00dd1331-e277-4242-89e7-29e4b9c8ed5f.Text: {n}As the shock of another mind's jumbled thoughts stops constricting your throat and the rippling haze falls from your eyes, you find yourself facing empty space. Kibellah's body, or indeed any trace of her, is nowhere to be seen: it is as if she was never in the chapel.{/n}

f2d7a09d-374f-4136-848e-a1591038f132.Text: "I... do not know, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. We were in the trance together, and we came out of it together. Perhaps she fled. Or perhaps... you left her for Death to collect — and Death collected her?"

d36c8494-5308-4dbe-84a6-71ec6f4a684d.Text: {n}The Choirmaster nods gloomily.{/n} "Our inner horrors are our burdens. Praised be the God-Emperor that you were able to leave her tormented mind."

2f799724-a810-4a89-88b1-85eb35417a5a.Text: "That was not the Emperor, Lord Captain. It was merely Mistress Kibellah's vision of Him. A figment born out of her imagination. Alas, none among my fellows are powerful enough to bring you the voice of the Protector of Mankind."

412b15b8-7073-4275-9d58-985aa5f45ce4.Text: "I looked away for one second, and that kaskha was gone! O Exalted One, I hope You really did collect her — because if You didn't, then this ship now has a mad murderer on the loose."

71642b8d-a9c3-49de-a083-d5887fd07879.Text: "Can you put me in a trance with Kibellah? I need to get inside her mind."

fb9602e1-0cd9-480b-a7d6-0cd9828c666b.Text: "I am not yet prepared for that."

60ecd642-9e71-40fe-a5cb-6b5b7d49267c.Text: "I am prepared for the risk. Put us in a trance."

e1412977-1685-4bc5-b359-e4e1ad2de3c5.Text: "Is the Choir managing to fulfil its duties without Weisz?"

6b543f26-a732-4de4-ad88-e142ed2b5068.Text: {n}A slender young man, his eyes hidden behind sacred manuscripts, adjusts the augmetic on his temple. He notices you and starts.{/n} "L-Lord Captain! How can I be of service?"

529cb6e2-16b5-498e-a376-28622af7f24b.Text: {n}As you approach, the Choirmaster's blindfold lights up with a bluish glow.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship seldom comes here without a reason. How can I be of service to you today?"

4bf7b11e-c4dc-4350-add1-e226f497c9c7.Text: "I will stay in the chapel, {name}, to hold a vigil in prayer. May the Emperor help you return this lost soul to the righteous path."

834cc765-3d28-4a81-816b-ddad3d63c2e8.Text: "I fear I am not in any way familiar with the ship's supply procedures or the lives of its children, so I cannot give you an answer, Lord Captain."

3b9f8501-be30-4f5d-af22-c286d0a1dea9.Text: "Your words... They so remind me of what the late Master Weisz used to say. For reasons I will never know, this thought always troubled him." {n}The Choirmaster's brow furrows.{/n} "After some reflection of my own, I concluded that tormenting myself with such questions would only make said death in the warp arrive that much sooner."

b5922895-6981-401a-8cfa-bc90b3675288.Text: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Did you... ask for help? My apologies. I have only a vague recollection of what I was doing and whom I was talking to when Adeline appeared." {n}Weisz's face is sunken, but the undying spark behind the time-worn scrolls is still there.{/n}

9a84d52a-5716-44ed-874a-7cc45ef13711.Text: "Monalic Qadd, acting Choirmaster of the Astropathic Choir, elected following Master Weisz's death until such time as a new Choirmaster is assigned to the flagship by decree of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAstraTelepathicaGlossary}Adeptus Astra Telepathica{/g}."

f34bb781-1971-4387-b0e8-e60bfed398ba.Text: {n}The Choirmaster looks away, embarrassed.{/n} "The mistakes of the past no longer haunt me, not in my dreams or in reality. But I still remember. I remember every single one of them."

09724c67-4db5-43ba-a3a7-64f8fbaf6d32.Text: "A synchronised trance is a complex telepathic practice. Things can go awry unless both participants trust each other and have a... strong spiritual connection. However, I can sense that you do. I would be honoured to be your guide during the ritual, Lord Captain. But remember: it is easy to get lost in another person's thoughts. And the fears of others... house monsters."

90b3970e-0573-4e26-9c16-c49a152eb426.Text: "May the God-Emperor aid you, Lord Captain."

71a50fd6-1356-424a-b453-df6800ebe6a8.Text: "To tell the truth, I have simply been too short on time lately. Running the Choir consumes all of my attention."

ebf47eb9-5bd7-496c-b08e-f88e02e647d3.Text: "Despite all the difficulties — yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Master Weisz was the strongest voice in the Choir, and it is not easy for us without him. Sending and deciphering messages is harder now, but every Astropath is doing their utmost not to let the dynasty down."

6a202cd2-f19d-4959-b93d-0794890bf739.Text: "Are you well, Kibellah? Do you remember what happened? How we met... Death?"

d79e4c02-b111-4d1a-921e-32b0e6021b8e.Text: "It was not you I saw inside Kibellah's mind. It was... Zacchary Weisz."

d01c41d5-bb39-43fe-999a-1c3d8e83cfae.Text: {n}As the shock of another mind's jumbled thoughts stops constricting your throat, you find yourself staring at Kibellah's pale face. It has settled into a strange expression.{/n} "Domin... {name}?"

8ab0967f-010f-45d6-9a4d-ed4b030e34da.Text: "I saw him, too. Our mentor's spirit has found no rest. He is still here, yearning for redemption. Yearning to be useful, to be... a saviour."

ffaa9690-2cad-4bf5-97c7-a65c489a6ee4.Text: "But you have reminded me of who I am. And that my shameful weakness must be extinguished."

3fed483c-a5b9-4dc5-bf98-2cda8e16f4bf.Text: "And I am still filled with doubt. Is the Vizsier leading the Bloodspun Web down the right path? Do I hear truth in His whisper, or am I distorting it with my own wishes? That doubt must be extinguished."

a74906c1-fb6e-4131-b4fb-716dc4028560.Text: {n}Kibellah looks away.{/n} "This 'Naaki Erebis' is the payment the Undying One demands. The price of redemption. The price of freedom. Who is this person? Where are they from? I do not know. Help me find them, Domin. Your Factotum oversees archives that contain many names. Let him find the one that Death has spoken. And I will pay the price that was set. For I know... I feel with all my essence... The death of Naaki Erebis is the key. The answer to my questions."

68d546db-c945-4e41-9997-2a9d50eb4ca9.Text: "I remember... stumbling. I remember my doubt in the truth of the Tenets throwing me off my feet. I remember deciding to kill... and not because I had heard His whisper, but because I deemed it to be right. Death whispered my name. For a spinner without a thread is like a sky without stars. They would drown in their own soul's darkness."

20b65d7d-a8e6-4379-9fae-1110459c1422.Text: "I must attempt to save her, at the very least."

c18e6550-1e3a-4873-afc5-b5e979d3f9b0.Text: "Why is a Requiescator speaking for the late Forius? Does the man not have a family?"

50f8e0bc-9d17-45a0-b528-87413ebac188.Text: "Tell me about the circumstances of the murder."

fb2240f2-3039-4978-9b94-530d9a131254.Text: "Grant her grim soul mercy, Vizsier. Let her die."

a4256d9d-71d3-412d-8ff7-480919ec07b9.Text: "There must be a way to help her."

2ccc2d39-61ec-4be9-911b-b8b5449d6c7d.Text: "What is happening to her? She is not herself."

6b2d2b02-eb8b-471d-a891-1af4f2400527.Text: "Kibellah is not subject to ordinary justice. She serves the Emperor through death, and as such cannot be convicted for a death."

b1f7768a-9063-4bde-bd18-a2030f088d2d.Text: "Forius deserved to die, and I am not going to punish Kibellah for that murder. As for his practices, they are henceforth banned on this ship."

f41e72e3-aa6a-48a8-90ec-c5e6d3190b1d.Text: "You have violated the prohibition on killing that I issued to the Bloodspun Web."

eb5c04dd-cf54-4f2f-b6a0-419092945126.Text: "Let us hear from the victim's representative."

aa55a860-ce23-46ab-a0d3-603d41576a1a.Text: "I find Kibellah guilty. But she will receive a more lenient penalty than death."

d686deb0-3698-4fed-ba41-60f4f898afc8.Text: "My companion is within her rights to kill anyone on this ship. Her accusers, on the other hand, are naught but dust. Do not touch her. Is that clear?"

0bf14fb4-4ff0-4432-ab38-58aaf0e92090.Text: "Let us see just how well he knows the deceased. Tell me, Requiescator, what did Forius like and dislike about his work?"

eb52ae67-a7a2-4df8-b5cc-273d1dc87996.Text: "The Forius clan will be awarded a generous indemnity for their loss, to be paid by me."

c12a2f4b-5ae8-4ef6-8893-ef1f4e5d50e1.Text: "The blame for what happened lies not with Kibellah, but with your entire perverse philosophy. Enforcers, I order you to cull every member of the Bloodspun Web on my ship!"

c8735d37-8ddd-495a-8cdf-55b5baad9e76.Text: "I never gave you permission to harm my servant, Vizsier."

b65ebfe6-c8cc-4894-b418-4fd1bd2d1fcc.Text: "She must die — not because anyone's beliefs demand it, but because such is the will of the Lex Imperialis. Kibellah, for the murder of a servant of the Imperium, your sentence is death. Vizsier, carry out the execution."

77ac264e-5694-4afe-a66c-de7e518b836f.Text: "A murder was committed. The punishment for that is clear. Let the law triumph. Commence preparations for the execution."

e52404c2-ef17-4dc5-8ad5-d6e49f292c4c.Text: "Is it true that you killed him, Kibellah?"

12342efd-c2c1-4c2e-b353-2f25c78408d1.Text: "Forius's nonchalant disregard for common humanity is worthy of respect!"

59c8b53f-91a0-4019-9f41-261bc7ece609.Text: "Lord Captain, a murder has been committed on this ship. The victim is one Lettard Forius, Chirurgeon Majoris. The perpetrator was apprehended at the scene of the crime, admitted her guilt, and did not resist arrest."

0f8b7ff9-6022-42d5-af32-1e5c97c9d6c9.Text: "How would one heal the soul of another, Domin? She is fighting a losing battle inside her mind... One she has all but lost. We cannot enter her mind. We cannot reach out a hand to her... Although..."

b4418b81-48f6-4930-9f3f-b35be1b2fd0e.Text: "The eyewitness accounts didn't give us much. The deceased and the murderer had a brief conversation, following which Mistress Kibellah beheaded the Chirurgeon Majoris. The witnesses did not overhear any details of the conversation."

c178d7c3-a97b-4f17-8085-d5ec1a279fd0.Text: "The clan to which the deceased belonged are wary of bringing accusations against the Lord Captain's companion. And the esteemed Lettard never made any courageous friends in his life, having always preferred his work to the company of others."

c9ff3ac5-fc0f-4388-8e81-57eae3a7535d.Text: "The Heartless Man imagined himself to be above others. He believed his trade had uplifted him. He {d|Encyclopedia:CompKibellah_Distortion}did not even avert his gaze{/d} before a servant of the Undying One. It was... brazen. Unjustifiable."

e6275bc7-f53d-4207-8205-ad8600e6e8f5.Text: "The Heartless Man enjoyed what he did. His work should have been a {d|Encyclopedia:CompKibellah_Fanatic}holy mission of service{/d}. The pain of thousands should have been a solemn sacrifice. Yet he derived pleasure from it. It was... repulsive."

9383f0ea-7753-44f5-9e3b-7415b56cd167.Text: "The Heartless Man took on a burden that was not his to bear. His duty was to heal, but instead he sent people to the Undying One, people whose time had not yet come. He was... {d|Encyclopedia:CompKibellah_Humility}cruel{/d}. And had no intention of ever stopping."

23f594cc-64ec-471c-9f90-dcd984cdadd0.Text: "I— I don't want to die, Domin!"

4da2e1af-9160-48c9-b46c-9b0ab9427a84.Text: "The Second Spinner is in the throes of a spiritual ailment that we call doubt. This most terrible ailment, though harmless to layfolk, is deadly to us. For a doubtful spinner will stray from their destined thread and into bloodthirsty madness. Doubt brings them to the Undying One before their time."

00b6e8bf-49dd-4b65-ac3c-769b0525caa1.Text: "Enforcers! The Bloodspun Web is now outlawed! Execute the undesirables!"

d4dec85b-acd4-4db8-a797-7d7c44fa76a6.Text: {n}Kibellah appears cold and apathetic. Her unblinking eyes stare vacantly, her expression odd.{/n}

34490da7-efe9-4fa0-9f7b-6783318da37f.Text: "Mentor... Why me? Do you truly think the greatest danger to your flock is... me?" {n}Kibellah's voice trembles with pain.{/n}

74d7d46c-ce64-481f-8aeb-3f95aa4fa97f.Text: "Unimportant people. Common people. Doomed people." {n}The Requiescator shakes drops of imaginary blood from his hands with disgust.{/n} "This was the esteemed Lettard's way of thinking: does a doomed leper care whether the disease or the knife is causing them pain? Is the formula for a medicine that would cure distinguished officers not worth the lives of a few dozen commoners turned test subjects? With the knowledge he gained, he invented a multitude of balms, antidotes, and treatment methods that went on to save thousands of lives."

4e50ad73-9206-4d1d-afe6-0acc8a737332.Text: "Yes." {n}Neither the chirurgeon's death nor her own impending punishment seem to trouble Kibellah. Her pensive dark gaze wanders around the bridge.{/n} "It was me."

381f1c9f-5979-41cd-ad89-5b8f957d7daf.Text: {n}Though the Vizsier's eyes are sewn shut, one can still read the grief that permeates his wrinkled features. He whispers in a sorrowful voice,{/n} "You have strayed from the thread. You have doomed the Tenets of the Bloodspun Web to oblivion. What a sorry end — for me, not for you. For I am compelled to usher my apprentice's soul to the other side before it is my own time to go."

47d08146-04b2-4708-ad27-a5245f46fa6f.Text: "The Undying One... never whispered his name. I myself decided to sever his thread."

1d45324f-6437-4918-b3a2-07f76f2165e3.Text: "The Heartless Man did more than heal people. He maimed them, too. Tortured them. Killed them slowly. And observed."

e04c0a5e-9880-42a0-859b-728899bb18fb.Text: "Second Spinner Kibellah, the Undying One has spoken. It is your time."

661a04b6-1623-43e1-ada4-558ff1af308f.Text: {n}The Vizsier turns his face toward Kibellah, who seems withdrawn, her spark snuffed out. He whispers,{/n} "Then seek a steward of souls. An artisan who will put you both in a psyker's trance, allowing your minds to become one. You have a chapel full of Astropaths, Domin. One of them will surely do you that service. See that their guidance is strong, for inside her soul, you will encounter... monsters. A doubt-ridden mind is a dangerous place."

203ebe47-2bc8-479e-a1ce-7c970d643553.Text: "When there is no one to speak for a deceased person in court, their representative is entitled to seek assistance from a member of the Requiescators' Guild. Their duty is to know and remember each and every person on this ship so that they can defend the interests of the deceased and represent them in court. They study the victim's entire life history to gain the most detailed impression of their personality, deeds, and aspirations. The guild was founded by one of your distant ancestors and, to my knowledge, the Requiescators only exist on our glorious flagship."

4319aeca-a56c-41fe-aa50-dd96c7a15562.Text: "We humbly await your verdict, Lord Captain."

cb7d6131-2789-4dd8-9c04-a8132ff2cbee.Text: {n}The masked man's voice is unpleasantly creaky.{/n} "The esteemed Lettard served this voidship and this dynasty for many years. He treated the sick and gained new knowledge as his trade commanded. He saved many, but he himself was not saved. He caused Mistress Kibellah no grievance. He never offended her. He merely answered her questions regarding his work, whereupon he was attacked. And so he has the right to demand a reckoning. The death of his murderer would be lawful and proportionate retribution."

a274306c-0c3d-4f07-a0fe-8ea66c3e60b5.Text: "His methods were efficient. Only one who has never lain upon an operating table would prefer a principled healer to a competent one."

ada1b216-97ca-4884-8324-379634d9f43a.Text: "The esteemed Lettard would be grateful for this judgement. He was a man of logic and practicality."

78d3ba6a-1442-4401-9655-e3e64558b1d3.Text: "I cannot be put on trial." {n}Kibellah's words are barely louder than a whisper, but everyone hears them. She raises her head, face deathly pale, as if she is asleep with her eyes open.{/n} "None have the right to judge a spinner of death."

d09be47f-234b-47cb-b5b3-437521d94a8a.Text: {n}A single voice cuts through the ensuing silence.{/n} "That is the Lord Captain's will. But the deceased would not call it justice."

e48443ad-05ee-48e2-9bfb-8131de557b3c.Text: {n}She points at the masked man and smiles wryly. Her grim whisper is chilling:{/n} "I am going to kill you too."

65aa37ca-5da0-4de3-b1e2-2a318a5a3d86.Text: "I am fine." {n}Kibellah turns her face toward you slightly. A whisper escapes her lips:{/n} "This is just hollow ceremony. Pointless."

879293bb-ae31-4fd8-8416-fda743dbffdf.Text: {n}The masked head lowers, and the man strokes his chin contemplatively.{/n} "He was fascinated by diseases. Injuries. Pathogens. Complications. The part he disliked was... the patients. They would not let him concentrate on that which was killing them."

7b5ac8e5-eeac-48da-92cf-92a82d1bb610.Text: {n}Frowning, Kibellah adds,{/n} "There was another like the Heartless Man. A xenos from the Dark City who lorded over flesh and oversaw {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_KibellahWasInCommoragh}unholy resurrections{/d}. They were both touched by the same corruption, that of hubris."

43907cc3-dde8-45f8-bea6-434c0d5da2cc.Text: "To take the one who no longer sees the Tenets. To give her to Him. She is dangerous. To pacify her forever — such is my duty, and so it must be."

8b07e67c-be87-4fd5-bcac-15dabcfd8c16.Text: "But if you saw her the way I see her, you would. She is tempest. She is woe. You do not want this by your side, Domin. Believe me."

445a89a6-f9cf-437c-a94e-530bf3525861.Text: "Did He whisper my name to you? I— I do not believe you, Mentor. I am loyal to Him. You must have been confused and misread His signs."

6805a241-0473-418f-83ff-e5660fa241e0.Text: {n}The masked man bows, stiffly and decorously.{/n}

8efe65bd-0745-4a10-bf95-bc197f8ad530.Text: "What makes you think you are fit to judge me, Mentor? You are not Him!"

43ffc087-ca16-48ea-b9f5-1d799aad1373.Text: {n}Kibellah fixes you with a long stare, as though struggling to comprehend what you have just said. Then she sighs.{/n} "That matters little. You cannot prevent death from taking. It simply takes."

fcd20d76-0199-4707-9834-04e663e88d3e.Text: "I humbly declare that the esteemed Lettard was indifferent to the fortunes, good or otherwise, of his estranged kinspeople whom you have made rich. And that he would not be satisfied with this ruling."

b208e4e1-5703-48c7-afec-f2f5a46c3ee7.Text: "He treated the sick and he gained knowledge." {n}The masked head jerks up haughtily.{/n} "The boots of those who walk the path of wisdom leave bloodied footprints. It is a rule that existed long before the esteemed Lettard did."

dacb31ec-ac80-43cc-9090-c92792b01410.Text: "Our service is demanding. It requires clarity and a sense of purpose that she no longer possesses. Long have I sensed the seeds of anxiety in her, but I hoped her reason would prove stronger and prevail. Alas, now I see the mark of despondence on her. Alas, I know that I am not mistaken."

1fca546f-3d06-4709-9946-7c95ca1051e7.Text: "You could. A thread binds the Domin and {mf|his|her} shadow together. A rare thread, a shared thread. Will that connection be enough for your souls to enter into harmony?"

e3130d6e-8093-4f7f-9d99-af6df4a3c993.Text: {n}Marazhai shrugs.{/n} "So she felt like killing some servant. Why do they all take such offence? Is every corpse going to cause such a stir from now on?"

9f66cdf9-3ffc-4a1c-b6c4-e38c4b2b6e55.Text: "I told you it would end like this. But why should anyone listen to little old Jae?" {n}She shakes her head sullenly.{/n}

8f60d62f-353c-4a1c-91c5-48c27933d768.Text: "Her colours have changed. The scarlet and the gold are drowning in the rage of muddled crimson, the misty blues of sorrow, and the impenetrable greens of doubt. These shades are all in conflict, melding together in a frenetic tapestry..."

0785157c-9a88-4106-b7d5-14708c95aa7d.Text: "You walked a narrow, dark path across a yawning abyss — it is small wonder that you stumbled. This soul, already mangled by bloody and frightening service, has fractured further still. Can it still be saved?" {n}Yrliet falls silent, leaving her own question unanswered.{/n}

ba0350c1-09db-4fbd-b6ad-2cf410dc5eb6.Text: "She was never sane to begin with. Judging lunatics is a thankless duty. The more important thing to address is that her cult is guilty of having drilled the notion of chosenness into her head — the whole sect must answer for this incident."

55710eb2-57b2-449e-9bdc-e41b51ccd29e.Text: "No contradicting the Lord Captain, convict." {n}The enforcer lays a firm hand on Kibellah's shoulder.{/n}

ce71aa70-22e3-4bef-a2a2-13842deffaba.Text: {n}The bridge is suddenly filled with a furious clamour, until an old man's whisper cuts through the noise.{/n} "Enough, my daughter."

f56bd223-98da-4029-b105-d1b0e6397de9.Text: "Do. Not. Touch me!" {n}Her hissing whisper turns into a ferocious cry. Out of nowhere, a dagger appears in her grasp and flashes across the enforcer's hand. His bloodied fingers fall to the floor.{/n}

85271326-a9a3-49d0-bc5c-a924aae4630e.Text: "The Forius clan invoked a ship's tradition and summoned a Requiescator to testify on behalf of the deceased."

426ff73c-1072-44ce-bc6f-d84b437890ca.Text: "When you were brought in and placed on his table, burned by the {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentThroughFire}fire you had passed through{/d}, he saved you. The methods he used to keep your body alive had been tested on inhabitants of Loading Bay 8. As had the scar-removing techniques. Were their lives worth yours? The esteemed Lettard thought that they were."

279030e1-64a7-4f91-943e-c96cbbc4ff4d.Text: At the start of combat, mercenaries select their targets. Until they suffer {g|Encyclopedia:DamageGlossary}damage{/g} from the designated target, the mercenary suffers −80% less damage from other sources.
